areas.title: AB Power, Energy and Machinery Engineering
areas.description: Agricultural & Biosystems Power, Mechanization Planning, Machinery Testing (PAES), Automation, Project Management, Laws & Ethics (RA 10915).

items.question: Which Republic Act is known as the 'Philippine Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering Act of 2016' that strengthened and modernized the practice of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering?
items.rationale: R.A. 10915 lapsed into law on July 21, 2016, repealing R.A. 8559 and aligning ABE practice with international standards.

choiceExplanations.Republic Act No. 10601: R.A. 10601 is the Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization (AFMech) Law of 2013, not the 2016 ABE professional act.
choiceExplanations.Republic Act No. 10915: Correct — Republic Act No. 10915 is the Philippine Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering Act of 2016 that modernized ABE practice.
choiceExplanations.Republic Act No. 3927: R.A. 3927 is the original 1964 Philippine Agricultural Engineering Law, later superseded by R.A. 8559 and R.A. 10915.
choiceExplanations.Republic Act No. 8559: R.A. 8559 is the Philippine Agricultural Engineering Act of 1998, which R.A. 10915 repealed and replaced in 2016.

items.question: When was Republic Act No. 3927, the original Philippine Agricultural Engineering Law, approved and enacted?
items.rationale: R.A. 3927 was enacted on June 18, 1964 (31 sections), later repealed by R.A. 8559 (1998) and R.A. 10915 (2016).

choiceExplanations.July 21, 2016: July 21, 2016 is the date R.A. 10915 lapsed into law, not the 1964 enactment of R.A. 3927.
choiceExplanations.June 5, 2013: June 5, 2013 is the approval date of R.A. 10601 (AFMech Law), not R.A. 3927.
choiceExplanations.June 18, 1964: Correct — Republic Act No. 3927, the original Philippine Agricultural Engineering Law, was approved on June 18, 1964.
choiceExplanations.February 13, 1998: February 13, 1998 is the approval date of R.A. 8559, the second Agricultural Engineering Act.

items.question: Which Philippine law promotes the development and adoption of modern, appropriate, and cost-effective agricultural and fisheries machinery and equipment?
items.rationale: R.A. 10601 (Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization Law of 2013) governs mechanization, machinery registration, and BAFE.

choiceExplanations.R.A. 10601 (AFMech Law): Correct — R.A. 10601 (Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization Law of 2013) promotes modern, appropriate, and cost-effective agri-fisheries machinery.
choiceExplanations.Power stroke: Power stroke is the combustion expansion phase of an internal combustion engine cycle, not a Philippine statute.
choiceExplanations.RA 3927: R.A. 3927 was the 1964 law regulating agricultural engineering practice, not the national agri-fisheries mechanization act.
choiceExplanations.RA 9520: R.A. 9520 is the Philippine Cooperative Code of 2008 governing cooperatives rather than agricultural mechanization.

items.question: Under R.A. 10601, BAFE requires registration of agricultural and fisheries machinery entities abbreviated as MFADDIE. What does MFADDIE stand for?
items.answer: Manufacturer, Fabricator, Assembler, Distributor, Dealer, Importer, and Exporter
items.rationale: All entities engaged in manufacturing, fabricating, assembling, distributing, dealing, importing, or exporting agri-fishery machinery must register with BAFE.
choices: Manufacturer, Foreign Assembler, Distribution, Dealer, Investor, and Employer
Machinery Firm, Assembler, Designer, Dealer, Inspector, and Engineer
Manufacturer, Fabricator, Assembler, Distributor, Dealer, Importer, and Exporter
Mechanization Facility, Agency, Distributor, Developer, Importer, and Exporter

choiceExplanations.Manufacturer, Foreign Assembler, Distrib: Foreign Assembler, Distribution, Investor, and Employer are inaccurate terms not used in the official BAFE MFADDIE acronym.
choiceExplanations.Machinery Firm, Assembler, Designer, Dea: Machinery Firm, Designer, Inspector, and Engineer do not match the machinery supply-chain entities registered under MFADDIE.
choiceExplanations.Manufacturer, Fabricator, Assembler, Dis: Correct — Under R.A. 10601, MFADDIE stands for Manufacturer, Fabricator, Assembler, Distributor, Dealer, Importer, and Exporter.
choiceExplanations.Mechanization Facility, Agency, Distribu: Mechanization Facility, Agency, and Developer are incorrect substitutions for Manufacturer, Fabricator, and Assembler in MFADDIE.

items.question: Under R.A. 10915, how often must a licensed Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer renew their Professional Identification Card (PIC) with the PRC?
items.rationale: The PRC Professional Identification Card (PIC) is valid for 3 years and renewed upon paying fees and submitting CPD compliance and AIPO (PSABE) Certificate of Good Standing.

choiceExplanations.Every 2 years: Two years is shorter than the statutory three-year validity cycle of PRC Professional Identification Cards.
choiceExplanations.Every 3 years: Correct — Under PRC regulations and R.A. 10915, an ABE renews their Professional Identification Card every 3 years.
choiceExplanations.Every 5 years: Five years exceeds the standard three-year PRC license renewal period for registered engineers.
choiceExplanations.Every year: PRC Professional Identification Cards are not renewed annually; they remain valid for three years.

items.question: Which of the following are required for the renewal of an Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer's Professional Identification Card (PIC)?
items.answer: CPD units and Certificate of Good Standing from the AIPO (PSABE)
items.rationale: Section 20 of R.A. 10915 requires proof of CPD credit units and a Certificate of Good Standing from the Accredited Integrated Professional Organization (PSABE).
choices: CPD units and Certificate of Good Standing from the AIPO (PSABE)
Endorsement from the Department of Agriculture
A new passing score on the board exam
Only payment of PRC renewal fees

choiceExplanations.CPD units and Certificate of Good Standi: Correct — Renewing an ABE PIC requires earned CPD units, a Certificate of Good Standing from PSABE, and the PRC fee.
choiceExplanations.Endorsement from the Department of Agric: Department of Agriculture endorsement is not required by the PRC to renew an engineer's Professional Identification Card.
choiceExplanations.A new passing score on the board exam: Retaking the board examination is unnecessary for regular PIC renewal of an active registered engineer.
choiceExplanations.Only payment of PRC renewal fees: Paying PRC fees alone is insufficient without required CPD units and an AIPO Certificate of Good Standing.

items.subtopic: 1.0 ABE vs. CE Scope of Practice
items.question: Under R.A. 10915, which of the following infrastructure projects falls strictly within the signing and sealing authority of an Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer rather than a general municipal barangay road?
items.answer: Farm-to-market roads (FMR), communal irrigation, and agricultural slaughterhouses
items.rationale: ABEs sign and seal plans and specifications for FMRs, irrigation and drainage systems, farm structures, and agri-processing facilities.
choices: Farm-to-market roads (FMR), communal irrigation, and agricultural slaughterhouses

choiceExplanations.Multi-story urban commercial condominium: Multi-story urban commercial condominiums fall under Civil Engineering and Architecture rather than ABE scope.
choiceExplanations.Farm-to-market roads (FMR), communal irr: Correct — Under R.A. 10915, FMRs, communal irrigation systems, and agricultural slaughterhouses fall within ABE signing and sealing authority.
choiceExplanations.National expressway interchange: National expressway interchanges are general civil works outside Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering practice.
choiceExplanations.International airport runway: International airport runways are civil and aviation infrastructure outside ABE signing and sealing authority.

items.subtopic: 1.0 ABE vs. ChE Scope of Practice
items.question: How does the scope of practice of an Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer (ABE) differ from that of a Chemical Engineer (ChE) in processing plants?
items.answer: ABEs handle primary agricultural/bioprocess systems and farm-level value-adding, while ChEs handle industrial chemical plants
items.rationale: Under R.A. 10915, ABEs cover agricultural bioprocess, postharvest, and farm waste systems, whereas industrial chemical manufacturing belongs to ChEs.
choices: ABEs are prohibited from designing food dryers or grain mills
There is no legal distinction between the two professions
ABEs handle primary agricultural/bioprocess systems and farm-level value-adding, while ChEs handle industrial chemical plants
ChEs exclusively sign and seal biogas digesters on livestock farms

choiceExplanations.ABEs are prohibited from designing food: ABEs are legally authorized under R.A. 10915 to design agricultural postharvest dryers and grain mills.
choiceExplanations.There is no legal distinction between th: R.A. 10915 and R.A. 9297 establish distinct statutory scopes for ABEs and Chemical Engineers.
choiceExplanations.ABEs handle primary agricultural/bioproc: Correct — ABEs cover primary agricultural, bioprocess, and farm value-adding facilities, whereas Chemical Engineers cover industrial chemical plants.
choiceExplanations.ChEs exclusively sign and seal biogas di: Livestock farm biogas digesters are explicitly covered within ABE practice under R.A. 10915, not exclusively ChEs.

items.question: Who is primarily responsible for calibrating, integrating, and preparing technical specifications of agricultural sensors and controlled-environment instrumentation used in precision farming?
items.rationale: Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation, and Control Systems is a core competency area under R.A. 10915 and the PRC ABELE TOS.

choiceExplanations.Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer: Correct — R.A. 10915 assigns agricultural sensors, precision-farming instrumentation, and controlled-environment systems to Agricultural and Biosystems Engineers.
choiceExplanations.Geodetic Engineer: Geodetic Engineers specialize in land surveying, boundary determination, and mapping rather than farm instrumentation.
choiceExplanations.Civil Engineer: Civil Engineers focus on general structures, roads, and hydraulics rather than agricultural precision sensors.
choiceExplanations.Mining Engineer: Mining Engineers handle mineral exploration and extraction rather than agricultural controlled-environment systems.

items.question: Presidential Decree No. 1594 (later superseded by R.A. 9184) originally prescribed policies, guidelines, rules, and regulations for which of the following?
items.rationale: P.D. 1594 governed government infrastructure project procurement, bidding, and contracts prior to the Government Procurement Reform Act (R.A. 9184).

choiceExplanations.Agrarian reform land distribution: Agrarian reform land distribution is governed by R.A. 6657 (CARP), not P.D. 1594.
choiceExplanations.Environmental impact assessments: Environmental impact assessments are governed by P.D. 1586 (Philippine EIS System), not P.D. 1594.
choiceExplanations.Government infrastructure contracts and: Correct — P.D. 1594 originally prescribed policies and guidelines for government infrastructure contracts and public bidding before R.A. 9184.
choiceExplanations.National building structural codes: National building structural standards are governed by P.D. 1096 (National Building Code), not P.D. 1594.

items.question: What does CPES stand for in the evaluation of government agricultural infrastructure construction projects?
items.rationale: CPES evaluates contractor performance during and upon completion of government infrastructure projects (workmanship, materials, time, facilities, etc.).
choices: Civil and Agricultural Planning Evaluation Scheme

choiceExplanations.Civil and Agricultural Planning Evaluati: Civil and Agricultural Planning Evaluation Scheme is a fabricated phrase and not a government procurement acronym.
choiceExplanations.Central Project Engineering Standard: Central Project Engineering Standard is not the official contractor rating system used on government projects.
choiceExplanations.Construction Price Estimation System: Construction Price Estimation System refers to costing rather than contractor performance evaluation under CPES.
choiceExplanations.Constructors' Performance Evaluation Sys: Correct — CPES stands for Constructors' Performance Evaluation System, used to evaluate contractors on government infrastructure projects.

items.question: Under Philippine environmental regulations (R.A. 8749 / DENR-EMB), what document must an agri-processing facility with air pollution source equipment (such as a rice hull furnace or boiler) secure before operating?
items.rationale: A Permit to Operate (PTO) Air Pollution Source Installations (APSI) is issued by DENR-EMB to ensure emissions comply with Clean Air Act standards.

choiceExplanations.Certificate of Ancestral Domain: A Certificate of Ancestral Domain pertains to indigenous peoples' land rights under R.A. 8371, not air emissions.
choiceExplanations.Barangay Clearance only: A Barangay Clearance is a local permit and cannot authorize operating air pollution source equipment.
choiceExplanations.Building Occupancy Waiver: Building Occupancy Waiver is not a DENR-EMB environmental permit for boilers or furnaces.
choiceExplanations.Permit to Operate (PTO): Correct — Under R.A. 8749 (Clean Air Act), DENR-EMB requires a Permit to Operate (PTO) for air pollution source equipment.

items.question: Under R.A. 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000), which unit is primarily mandated to establish Materials Recovery Facilities (MRFs) and implement segregated collection at the community level?
items.rationale: R.A. 9003 places primary responsibility for solid waste segregation, MRFs, and 10-year solid waste management plans on LGUs and barangays.

choiceExplanations.Land Transportation Office: The Land Transportation Office regulates motor vehicles and driver licensing, not solid waste facilities.
choiceExplanations.Department of Trade and Industry: The Department of Trade and Industry oversees commerce and industry rather than barangay waste segregation.
choiceExplanations.Local Government Units (LGUs Barangays): Correct — R.A. 9003 mandates Local Government Units, starting at the barangay level, to establish MRFs and segregated collection.
choiceExplanations.Philippine Statistics Authority: The Philippine Statistics Authority compiles national statistical data rather than operating solid waste recovery facilities.

items.question: According to the 2013 PHilMech study, what was the average level of agricultural mechanization in the Philippines for all crops, and specifically for rice farms?
items.rationale: PHilMech's 2013 benchmark established 1.23 hp/ha across all crops and 2.31 hp/ha for rice cultivation.

choiceExplanations.3.50 hp/ha (all crops) and 4.50 hp/ha (r: 3.50 hp/ha and 4.50 hp/ha greatly exceed the actual Philippine farm mechanization level recorded in 2013.
choiceExplanations.5.00 hp/ha (all crops) and 6.20 hp/ha (r: 5.00 hp/ha and 6.20 hp/ha represent highly mechanized nations rather than the 2013 Philippine average.
choiceExplanations.1.23 hp/ha (all crops) and 2.31 hp/ha (r: Correct — The 2013 PHilMech study reported average Philippine mechanization at 1.23 hp/ha for all crops and 2.31 hp/ha for rice.
choiceExplanations.0.52 hp/ha (all crops) and 1.00 hp/ha (r: 0.52 hp/ha reflects the older pre-2000 Philippine mechanization baseline rather than the 2013 PHilMech update.

items.question: Which stage of agricultural evolution is characterized by the integration of IoT sensors, AI, drones, cloud computing, and autonomous robotics for real-time precision farm management?
items.rationale: Ag 1.0 = manual/animal labor; Ag 2.0 = mechanization & chemical inputs (Green Revolution); Ag 3.0 = GPS/precision guidance; Ag 4.0 = IoT, AI, big data, and smart autonomous farming.

choiceExplanations.Agriculture 1.0: Agriculture 1.0 represents traditional manual labor and animal-drawn farming without mechanized engines or digital tools.
choiceExplanations.Agriculture 2.0: Agriculture 2.0 refers to mechanization with tractors, synthetic fertilizers, and high-yielding crop varieties.
choiceExplanations.Agriculture 4.0: Correct — Agriculture 4.0 integrates IoT sensors, AI, drones, cloud computing, and autonomous robotics for real-time precision farming.
choiceExplanations.Agriculture 3.0: Agriculture 3.0 introduced early electronics, GPS guidance, and basic variable-rate precision tools prior to cloud AI.

items.question: Which historical phase of farming corresponds to Agriculture 2.0?
items.answer: Widespread adoption of tractors, synthetic fertilizers, and high-yielding varieties
items.rationale: Agriculture 2.0 (mid-20th century / Green Revolution) introduced internal combustion tractors, synthetic fertilizers, pesticides, and improved crop varieties.
choices: Autonomous swarm robotics and digital twins
Subsistence farming using hand tools and draft animals
Widespread adoption of tractors, synthetic fertilizers, and high-yielding varieties

choiceExplanations.Autonomous swarm robotics and digital tw: Autonomous swarm robotics and digital twins belong to Agriculture 4.0 smart farming, not Agriculture 2.0.
choiceExplanations.Subsistence farming using hand tools and: Subsistence farming with hand tools and draft animals characterizes Agriculture 1.0.
choiceExplanations.Satellite-guided variable-rate applicati: Satellite-guided variable-rate application emerged during Agriculture 3.0 with GPS and early computers.
choiceExplanations.Widespread adoption of tractors, synthet: Correct — Agriculture 2.0 corresponds to the Green Revolution era of tractors, synthetic fertilizers, and high-yielding varieties.

items.question: Which statement best distinguishes digitalization, automation, and robotics in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering?
items.answer: Digitalization converts farm data to digital form; automation executes tasks without continuous human intervention; robotics uses programmable physical machines to sense and act
items.rationale: Digitalization handles data capture/processing, automation handles self-regulating control loops, and robotics combines electromechanical actuation with sensing.
choices: Automation and digitalization mean exactly the same thing
Robotics only refers to software spreadsheets
Digitalization converts farm data to digital form; automation executes tasks without continuous human intervention; robotics uses programmable physical machines to sense and act

choiceExplanations.Automation and digitalization mean exact: Automation executes processes automatically, whereas digitalization converts analog farm information into digital records.
choiceExplanations.Digitalization requires physical robotic: Digitalization involves converting information to digital formats and does not require physical robotic arms.
choiceExplanations.Robotics only refers to software spreads: Robotics involves programmable physical machines interacting with the environment, not mere spreadsheet software.
choiceExplanations.Digitalization converts farm data to dig: Correct — Digitalization converts data to digital form, automation runs tasks autonomously, and robotics uses physical machines to sense and act.

items.question: What does the DA-BAFE platform 'GeoAgri' stand for?
items.answer: Geographic Information System for Agricultural and Fisheries Machinery and Infrastructure
items.rationale: GeoAgri is DA-BAFE's GIS-based database mapping agricultural and fisheries machinery, infrastructure, and FMR projects nationwide.
choices: Geographic Information System for Agricultural and Fisheries Machinery and Infrastructure

choiceExplanations.Geological Survey of Agrarian Lands: Geological Survey of Agrarian Lands is an unrelated phrase, not DA-BAFE's machinery GIS platform.
choiceExplanations.Global Earth Observation for Agronomy: Global Earth Observation for Agronomy is not the name of DA-BAFE's national agricultural machinery database.
choiceExplanations.Geographic Information System for Agricu: Correct — GeoAgri stands for DA-BAFE's Geographic Information System for Agricultural and Fisheries Machinery and Infrastructure.
choiceExplanations.Geothermal Energy for Agriculture Initia: Geothermal Energy for Agriculture Initiative is a fabricated name unrelated to DA-BAFE GIS mapping.

items.question: In a standard Geographic Information System (GIS) coordinate plane, what does the x-coordinate (Easting) represent?
items.rationale: In GIS and Cartesian mapping, x represents East–West horizontal position (longitude/easting) and y represents North–South position (latitude/northing).

choiceExplanations.Cetane: Cetane number measures the auto-ignition quality of diesel fuel, not spatial map coordinates.
choiceExplanations.Ideal Gas Law: The Ideal Gas Law relates pressure, volume, and temperature of gases, not GIS coordinates.
choiceExplanations.Horizontal (East–West) position Longitud: Correct — In a standard GIS coordinate plane, the x-coordinate (Easting or Longitude) represents horizontal East–West position.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust system: Exhaust system is an engine assembly that channels combustion gases away from cylinders.

items.question: What does ROPS stand for on four-wheel agricultural tractors?
items.rationale: ROPS is a cab or frame structure engineered to protect tractor operators from crush injuries during tractor overturns.

choiceExplanations.Roll-Over Protective Structure: Correct — ROPS stands for Roll-Over Protective Structure, a protective frame or cab that shields tractor operators during overturns.
choiceExplanations.Rotary Output Power Shaft: Rotary Output Power Shaft is an incorrect term for the tractor's Power Take-Off (PTO) shaft.
choiceExplanations.Rear Operational Pulling System: Rear Operational Pulling System is a fabricated phrase, not the tractor drawbar or hitch.
choiceExplanations.Remote Operator Positioning Sensor: Remote Operator Positioning Sensor is an invented name unrelated to tractor rollover safety frames.

items.question: During performance testing of a heated-air mechanical grain dryer per PAES, at what regular time interval are temperature, relative humidity, and grain moisture readings typically recorded?
items.answer: Every 30 minutes (or 1 hour depending on dryer batch duration)
items.rationale: PAES 202 (Methods of Test for Heated-Air Mechanical Grain Dryers) specifies periodic 30-minute to 1-hour sampling intervals for air conditions and moisture tracking.
choices: Buy the new engine to reduce maintenance cost
Every 30 minutes (or 1 hour depending on dryer batch duration)

choiceExplanations.Buy the new engine to reduce maintenance: Buying a new engine is an engineering economics recommendation, not a PAES dryer testing interval.
choiceExplanations.Department of Science and Technology (DO: DOST-ITDI is the Philippine metrology and industrial technology institute, not a measurement time interval.
choiceExplanations.All belts should be replaced: Replacing all belts is a mechanical maintenance task rather than a dryer data-logging schedule.
choiceExplanations.Every 30 minutes (or 1 hour depending on: Correct — Under PAES grain dryer testing, temperature, humidity, and moisture data are typically recorded every 30 minutes or 1 hour.

items.question: Which of the following is classified as a primary tillage implement designed to cut, invert, and break deep soil layers?
items.rationale: Moldboard, disk, chisel, and subsoiler plows are primary tillage implements; harrows and cultipackers are secondary tillage implements.

choiceExplanations.Disk plow: Correct — A disk plow is a primary tillage implement designed to cut, lift, and invert deep, unworked soil layers.
choiceExplanations.Cultipacker: A cultipacker is a secondary tillage implement used to crush clods and firm the seedbed.
choiceExplanations.Rotary weeder: A rotary weeder is a cultivation tool used to remove shallow weeds between crop rows.
choiceExplanations.Spike-tooth harrow: A spike-tooth harrow is a secondary tillage implement used to smooth soil and break surface crusts.

items.question: What is the primary function of the intake and exhaust valves in a four-stroke internal combustion engine?
items.answer: To admit fresh air/air-fuel mixture into the cylinder and release burned exhaust gases at precise timings
items.rationale: Camshaft-driven valves open and close ports in the cylinder head to regulate intake and exhaust gas exchange.
choices: To store rotational kinetic energy between power strokes
To cool the engine block using radiator fluid
To convert reciprocating piston motion into rotary crankshaft motion
To admit fresh air/air-fuel mixture into the cylinder and release burned exhaust gases at precise timings

choiceExplanations.To store rotational kinetic energy betwe: Storing rotational kinetic energy between power strokes is the function of the engine flywheel.
choiceExplanations.To cool the engine block using radiator: Cooling the engine block with radiator fluid is performed by the cooling system and water jacket.
choiceExplanations.To convert reciprocating piston motion i: Converting reciprocating piston motion to rotary motion is done by the connecting rod and crankshaft.
choiceExplanations.To admit fresh air/air-fuel mixture into: Correct — Intake and exhaust valves open and close at timed intervals to admit fresh charge and expel burned exhaust gases.

items.question: Crude oil (petroleum) is primarily a complex mixture of which class of chemical compounds?
items.rationale: Crude oil consists mainly of hydrogen and carbon compounds (alkanes, cycloalkanes, and aromatic hydrocarbons).

choiceExplanations.Silicates: Silicates are inorganic silicon-oxygen minerals forming rocks and soils, not crude petroleum.
choiceExplanations.Amino acids: Amino acids are nitrogen-containing organic monomers that form proteins rather than petroleum.
choiceExplanations.Hydrocarbons: Correct — Crude oil is primarily a complex mixture of hydrocarbons composed of hydrogen and carbon chains and rings.
choiceExplanations.Carbohydrates: Carbohydrates are biological sugars, starches, and fibers produced by living organisms, not crude oil.

items.question: When shifting a standard manual-transmission agricultural tractor from first gear to a higher gear, which pedal must the operator depress first?
items.rationale: Depressing the clutch disengages engine power from the transmission so gears can shift smoothly without grinding.

choiceExplanations.Right wheel brake only: The right wheel brake slows only the right rear wheel for sharp turns, not gear shifting.
choiceExplanations.Clutch pedal: Correct — Depressing the clutch pedal disengages engine power from the transmission so gears can be shifted without damage.
choiceExplanations.Differential lock pedal: The differential lock locks both rear axles together to prevent wheel slip in muddy fields.
choiceExplanations.Accelerator pedal: The accelerator pedal adjusts fuel delivery and engine RPM rather than disconnecting the transmission.

items.question: A 4-cylinder internal combustion engine has a cylinder bore of 10 cm and a piston stroke of 12 cm. What is the total engine piston displacement?

choiceExplanations.3.77 L: Correct — Total displacement equals 4 × (π/4) × (10 cm)² × 12 cm = 3,769.9 cm³, or 3.77 L.
choiceExplanations.5.15 L: 5.15 L overestimates the cylinder volume and does not match the 10 cm bore and 12 cm stroke.
choiceExplanations.2.84 L: 2.84 L underestimates the 4-cylinder volume (equivalent to roughly three cylinders of this size).
choiceExplanations.4.62 L: 4.62 L does not satisfy the piston displacement formula V = n × (π/4) × D² × L.

items.question: An agricultural diesel engine develops an indicated horsepower (IHP) of 25 hp and operates at a mechanical efficiency of 82%. What is its brake horsepower (BHP)?
items.rationale: BHP = IHP × ηm = 25 hp × 0.82 = 20.5 hp.

choiceExplanations.30.5 hp: 30.5 hp results from mistakenly dividing IHP by mechanical efficiency (25 / 0.82) instead of multiplying.
choiceExplanations.22.8 hp: 22.8 hp corresponds to roughly 91% mechanical efficiency rather than the stated 82%.
choiceExplanations.20.5 hp: Correct — Brake horsepower equals indicated horsepower times mechanical efficiency: BHP = 25 hp × 0.82 = 20.5 hp.
choiceExplanations.18.5 hp: 18.5 hp underestimates BHP and would correspond to only 74% mechanical efficiency.

items.question: An NIA irrigation drop/waterfall has a discharge of 1.5 m³/s and a gross head of 8 m. What is the theoretical hydraulic power available (use γ = 9.81 kN/m³)?
items.rationale: P_theoretical = γ × Q × H = 9.81 kN/m³ × 1.5 m³/s × 8 m = 117.72 kW.

choiceExplanations.98.1 kW: 98.1 kW represents the power for 1.25 m³/s or a lower head, omitting the full 1.5 m³/s × 8 m product.
choiceExplanations.142.5 kW: 142.5 kW exceeds the available hydraulic potential for Q = 1.5 m³/s and H = 8 m.
choiceExplanations.85.4 kW: 85.4 kW underestimates theoretical hydraulic power and reflects roughly 72.5% of the actual value.
choiceExplanations.117.7 kW: Correct — Theoretical hydraulic power is P = γQH = 9.81 kN/m³ × 1.5 m³/s × 8 m = 117.7 kW.

items.question: Using the same waterfall (Q = 1.5 m³/s, H = 8 m), if the turbine-generator system has an overall efficiency of 75%, what is the actual power output?

choiceExplanations.117.7 kW: 117.7 kW is the 100%-efficient theoretical hydraulic power before applying the 75% overall efficiency.
choiceExplanations.88.3 kW: Correct — Actual power output equals theoretical power times overall efficiency: 117.72 kW × 0.75 = 88.3 kW.
choiceExplanations.74.2 kW: 74.2 kW underestimates output and corresponds to roughly 63% overall efficiency instead of 75%.
choiceExplanations.96.5 kW: 96.5 kW overestimates output and corresponds to about 82% efficiency instead of 75%.

items.subtopic: 1.0 Pump BHP with Specific Liquid Density
items.question: A pump delivers 0.02 m³/s of liquid fertilizer (density ρ = 1,200 kg/m³) against a total head of 15 m at 70% pump efficiency. What brake horsepower (hp) is required?

choiceExplanations.4.82 hp: 4.82 hp underestimates required shaft power by roughly 29% and omits the fluid's 1,200 kg/m³ density.
choiceExplanations.5.85 hp: 5.85 hp fails to account properly for the heavier 1,200 kg/m³ fertilizer density or 70% efficiency.
choiceExplanations.8.10 hp: 8.10 hp overestimates the required power for the given flow, head, density, and 70% efficiency.

items.subtopic: 1.0 Power in HP from Torque & RPM
items.question: A tractor PTO shaft delivers a torque of 240 N·m at 540 rpm. What is the shaft power in horsepower?

choiceExplanations.21.6 hp: 21.6 hp overestimates shaft power and corresponds to roughly 640 rpm at 240 N·m torque.
choiceExplanations.14.5 hp: 14.5 hp underestimates shaft power and corresponds to roughly 430 rpm at 240 N·m.
choiceExplanations.25.0 hp: 25.0 hp exceeds the actual power produced by 240 N·m torque at 540 rpm.

items.question: A proposed grain drying facility has a Present Worth of Benefits of Php 2,000,000,000 and a Present Worth of Costs of Php 1,000,000,000. What is its Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR)?
items.rationale: BCR = PW(Benefits) / PW(Costs) = 2B / 1B = 2.00 (dimensionless ratio, NOT Php 2 Billion; BCR > 1 indicates an economically viable project).

choiceExplanations.2.00: Correct — Benefit-Cost Ratio equals Present Worth of Benefits divided by Present Worth of Costs: 2B / 1B = 2.00.
choiceExplanations.4.00: 4.00 doubles the true ratio and would require Php 4,000,000,000 in benefits for Php 1,000,000,000 costs.
choiceExplanations.1.00: 1.00 is the break-even BCR where benefits equal costs, not a 2-to-1 ratio.
choiceExplanations.3.00: 3.00 represents benefits three times greater than costs, not two times.

items.question: Determine the present worth of an annual equipment savings of Php 2,500 at the end of each year for 12 years at 8% interest compounded annually.

choiceExplanations.Php 15,240.10: Php 15,240.10 underestimates present worth and corresponds to a higher discount rate (~12.4%) over 12 years.
choiceExplanations.Php 18,840.20: Correct — Present worth of an annuity is P = 2,500 × [1 − (1.08)⁻¹²] / 0.08 = Php 18,840.20.
choiceExplanations.Php 22,500.00: Php 22,500.00 overestimates present worth and reflects a much lower discount rate (~4.4%).
choiceExplanations.Php 30,000.00: Php 30,000.00 is the undiscounted sum of 12 payments (2,500 × 12) at 0% interest.

items.question: A farmers' cooperative borrows Php 500,000 for a tractor at 10% annual interest, payable in 5 equal annual year-end installments. What is the annual payment?

choiceExplanations.Php 118,500.40: Php 118,500.40 is too low to amortize a Php 500,000 loan at 10% over 5 years.
choiceExplanations.Php 150,000.00: Php 150,000.00 overstates the annual installment by applying simple non-amortized interest charges.
choiceExplanations.Php 100,000.00: Php 100,000.00 only repays the principal (500,000 / 5) and ignores the 10% annual interest.
choiceExplanations.Php 131,898.74: Correct — Capital recovery payment equals A = 500,000 × [0.10(1.10)⁵] / [(1.10)⁵ − 1] = Php 131,898.74.

items.question: In international engineering measurement, SI stands for the International System of Units. In the Philippines, which government agency oversees the National Metrology Laboratory (NML)?
items.rationale: SI is the International System of Units; under R.A. 9236 (National Metrology Act), the National Metrology Board is chaired by the DOST Secretary and NML operates under DOST-ITDI.
choices: Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)

choiceExplanations.Department of Agriculture (DA): The Department of Agriculture oversees agricultural development and BAFE, not national metrology standards.
choiceExplanations.Department of Public Works and Highways: DPWH oversees national highways, bridges, and flood-control works rather than physical metrology standards.
choiceExplanations.Department of Science and Technology (DO: Correct — Under R.A. 9236, the Industrial Technology Development Institute of DOST (DOST-ITDI) operates the National Metrology Laboratory.
choiceExplanations.Department of Health (DOH): The Department of Health regulates public health and medical facilities, not national measurement standards.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A new tractor brand is being tested. The tachometer placed at the Power Take-Off (PTO) shaft recorded an average rotational speed of 1,700 RPM. The indicated engine power of 100 hp was found to be true. What likelihood value of torque was likely recorded at the PTO shaft?
items.rationale:
Torque ft-lbs = (Power in hp × 5252) / RPM
= (100 hp × 5252) / 1,700 RPM
= 309 ft-lbs

choiceExplanations.247 ft-lbs: 247 ft-lbs underestimates torque and yields only about 80 hp at 1,700 RPM.
choiceExplanations.340 ft-lbs: 340 ft-lbs overestimates torque and corresponds to roughly 110 hp at 1,700 RPM.
choiceExplanations.309 ft-lbs: Correct — PTO torque is T = (5,252 × HP) / RPM = (5,252 × 100) / 1,700 = 308.9 ft-lbs ≈ 309 ft-lbs.
choiceExplanations.278 ft-lbs: 278 ft-lbs underestimates torque and yields only about 90 hp at 1,700 RPM.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: The benefits to society regardless of who in the society receives the benefits.

choiceExplanations.Financial benefit: Financial benefit measures returns accruing only to a specific private owner or project entity, not all of society.
choiceExplanations.Sales: Sales represent gross goods or services sold by an enterprise rather than net societal welfare gains.
choiceExplanations.Revenue: Revenue is total monetary receipts of a business, not broader economic welfare to society.
choiceExplanations.Economic benefit: Correct — Economic benefit measures total welfare gains to society as a whole, regardless of who receives them.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Benefits less costs excluding depreciation.

choiceExplanations.Profit: Profit subtracts non-cash charges like depreciation and taxes from revenue rather than measuring pure cash movement.
choiceExplanations.Net benefit: Net benefit refers broadly to total benefits minus total costs rather than specifically excluding non-cash depreciation.
choiceExplanations.Cash flow: Correct — Cash flow equals cash inflows (benefits) minus cash outflows (costs), excluding non-cash expenses such as depreciation.
choiceExplanations.Economic benefits: Economic benefits reflect societal welfare values before subtracting project costs or isolating cash flows.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Which one is a one-time expense?

choiceExplanations.Operating cost: Operating costs are recurring expenses incurred continuously throughout project operation, not one-time capital outlays.
choiceExplanations.One-time cost: One-time cost is a generic descriptive phrase rather than the standard feasibility-study budget classification.
choiceExplanations.Investment: Correct — Investment refers to one-time initial capital expenditures for fixed assets needed to establish a project.
choiceExplanations.Single cost: Single cost is an informal term, not the recognized project-feasibility category for capital expenditures.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Land is an example of

choiceExplanations.Contingency: Contingency is a reserve budget allowance set aside for unforeseen cost overruns or price changes.
choiceExplanations.Operating capital: Operating capital (working capital) funds short-term day-to-day liquidity and inventories, not fixed land assets.
choiceExplanations.Operating cost: Operating costs are recurring expenses such as utilities, fuel, and routine wages during production.
choiceExplanations.Investment: Correct — Land is a long-term fixed capital asset classified as an investment cost in project feasibility studies.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Which among the feasibility indicators is best for determining project performance?

choiceExplanations.BCR: BCR measures relative benefit per peso spent and can misrank mutually exclusive projects of different scales.
choiceExplanations.IRR: IRR can yield multiple roots or distort rankings for mutually exclusive projects with differing scales.
choiceExplanations.NPV: Correct — Net Present Value (NPV) directly measures absolute net wealth created in today's currency without scale distortion.
choiceExplanations.Payback period: Payback period ignores cash flows after recovery and neglects the time value of money.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: The discount rate when the Net Present Value is zero.

choiceExplanations.ROI: ROI measures simple accounting return relative to cost without discounting cash flows to zero NPV.
choiceExplanations.IRR: Correct — The Internal Rate of Return (IRR) is defined as the discount rate at which Net Present Value equals zero.
choiceExplanations.Break-even rate: Break-even rate is not the standard capital-budgeting metric defined where NPV equals zero.
choiceExplanations.BCR: BCR is the ratio of discounted benefits to discounted costs, not a discount rate.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: What is the effect of increasing inflation rate to discounted cash flow at project start?

choiceExplanations.Increases: An inflation rate change does not increase discounted cash flow at t = 0 because the discount factor is 1.
choiceExplanations.None: Correct — At project start (t = 0), the discount factor (1 + r)⁰ equals 1, so inflation has no effect.
choiceExplanations.Decreases: Discounting reduces future cash flows, not cash flows occurring immediately at project start (t = 0).
choiceExplanations.Fluctuates: Cash flows at t = 0 remain unadjusted by future compounding or discounting rates, so they do not fluctuate.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Using straight line depreciation method, what is the book value at the end of year 2 of a tractor purchased at Php 2,200,000 if its life span is 10 years? Salvage value is 10%.
items.rationale:
Depreciation = (Php2,200,000-Php200,000)/10 years = Php 200,000/year
Book value = Purchase price — total depreciations = P2,200,000 − (P200,000/yr x2yrs) = P1,800,000

choiceExplanations.Php 1,800,000: Correct — With 10% salvage (Php 220,000), annual depreciation is Php 198,000, giving Php 1,804,000 at Year 2 (nearest Php 1,800,000).
choiceExplanations.Php 1,600,000: Php 1,600,000 corresponds to roughly Year 3 book value rather than the end of Year 2.
choiceExplanations.Php 2,000,000: Php 2,000,000 reflects only about one year of depreciation (~Php 200,000) instead of two years.
choiceExplanations.Php 2,020,000: Php 2,020,000 subtracts only one annual depreciation charge instead of two years of straight-line depreciation.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: A banana production and export project is being evaluated for financial feasibility. At 11% annual discount rate, it has the following feasibility indicators: net present value of 1.8 billion pesos and internal rate of return of 58%. If annual discount rate drops to 10%, will it be feasible?

choiceExplanations.Insufficient data to determine: The given 11% NPV (Php 1.8B) and 58% IRR are sufficient to confirm feasibility at 10%.
choiceExplanations.No: Lowering the discount rate below 11% increases NPV further above Php 1.8B, so the project stays feasible.
choiceExplanations.Yes: Correct — Decreasing the discount rate from 11% to 10% increases NPV above Php 1.8B and stays well below the 58% IRR.
choiceExplanations.Maybe: There is no uncertainty because lower discount rates strictly raise NPV for standard investment cash flows.

items.question: In what year was the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Philippine Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering Act of 2016 approved?

choiceExplanations.2022: Correct — Although R.A. 10915 lapsed into law in 2016, its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) were approved in 2022.
choiceExplanations.2016: 2016 was the year R.A. 10915 lapsed into law, not when its IRR was approved.
choiceExplanations.2018: 2018 is incorrect; the PRB-ABE and PRC finalized and approved the R.A. 10915 IRR in 2022.
choiceExplanations.RA 2020: RA 2020 mixes a Republic Act prefix with a year and is not when the IRR passed.

items.question: What law is known as the Philippine Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering Act of 2016?

choiceExplanations.RA 9736: R.A. 9736 is an unrelated statute and not the Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering Act of 2016.
choiceExplanations.RA_ 10915: Correct — R.A. 10915 is the Philippine Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering Act of 2016.
choiceExplanations.RA9513: R.A. 9513 is the Renewable Energy Act of 2008, not the ABE professional law.
choiceExplanations.RA 10601: R.A. 10601 is the Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization (AFMech) Law of 2013.

items.question: Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering refers to the application of and designs to the processes and systems involved in the sustainable production, post production and processing of safe food, feed, fiber, timber and other agricultural and biological materials and the efficient utilization, conservation, and management of natural and renewable resources in order to enhance human health in harmony with the environment.

choiceExplanations.Agriculture: Agriculture alone omits the engineering principles specified in R.A. 10915's statutory definition.
choiceExplanations.Engineering science: Correct — R.A. 10915 defines ABE as the application of 'engineering science and designs' to sustainable agricultural and biosystems processes.
choiceExplanations.Engineering: Engineering alone omits the word 'science' from the exact R.A. 10915 statutory phrase.
choiceExplanations.Science: Science alone omits 'engineering' from the statutory definition in Section 4(b) of R.A. 10915.

items.question: In ABE law, agricultural and biosystems consist of crops, forestry and other plants, poultry, livestock, fisheries and resources and other animals, wildlife and other living things.

choiceExplanations.Land: Land is an environmental medium rather than a biological resource paired with fisheries in Section 4(a).
choiceExplanations.Farm: Farm refers to an agricultural production site rather than the statutory 'aquaculture' term paired with fisheries.
choiceExplanations.Aquaculture: Correct — Section 4(a) of R.A. 10915 explicitly pairs 'fisheries and aquaculture resources' in defining agricultural and biosystems.
choiceExplanations.Agriculture: Agriculture is the broad sector itself rather than the specific 'aquaculture' term paired with fisheries.

items.question: Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer refers to a person who is registered and licensed to practice agricultural and biosystems engineering in the country and who holds a and professional identification card from the Board of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering and the PRC.

choiceExplanations.Option C (See original Tambong/Recalled: Option C represents an incorrect distractor in the source key for the statutory 'certificate of registration' phrase.
choiceExplanations.Option A (See original Tambong/Recalled: Option A represents an incorrect distractor in the source key rather than 'certificate of registration'.
choiceExplanations.Option D (See original Tambong/Recalled: Correct — Section 4(c) of R.A. 10915 specifies holding a valid 'certificate of registration' and PIC, keyed here as Option D.
choiceExplanations.Option B (See original Tambong/Recalled: Option B represents an incorrect distractor in the source key instead of 'certificate of registration'.

items.question: Agricultural and Biosystems Automation and Instrumentation refers to the use and application of agricultural and biosystems :

choiceExplanations.Integrated circuits: Integrated circuits are microelectronic semiconductor chips rather than the statutory term paired here for ABE automation.
choiceExplanations.Sensors: Correct — RA 10915 defines ABE automation and instrumentation as involving the use and application of agricultural and biosystems sensors.
choiceExplanations.Instruments: Instruments are general measuring devices, whereas the missing statutory keyword preceding instrumentation here is sensors.
choiceExplanations.Circuits: Circuits are electrical conduction paths and do not complete the statutory ABE automation and instrumentation definition.

items.question: Agricultural and Biosystems Resource Conservation and Management refers to measures of conservation and proper management of agricultural and resources.

choiceExplanations.Biological: Correct — Under RA 10915, ABE resource conservation and management covers measures conserving agricultural and biological resources.
choiceExplanations.Zoological: Zoological pertains strictly to animal life and excludes plant and broader biological resources under the ABE law.
choiceExplanations.Farm: Farm refers to agricultural holdings rather than the broader biological resources paired with agricultural resources in RA 10915.
choiceExplanations.Water: Water is only one physical resource covered within land and water engineering, not the general statutory term biological.

items.question: In RA 10915, agricultural and refers to local activity or series of activities to maintain or raise the quality or change the form or characteristics of agricultural, fishery, forestry and biological products/materials.

choiceExplanations.Quality control: Quality control verifies product standards rather than denoting the statutory activity changing product form or characteristics.
choiceExplanations.Forestry: Forestry is a source sector of raw materials mentioned in the definition, not the processing activity itself.
choiceExplanations.Bio-processing: Correct — RA 10915 defines agricultural and bio-processing as activities maintaining, raising quality, or changing the form of biological products.
choiceExplanations.Fishery: Fishery is one of the product sectors listed in the definition rather than the processing term itself.

items.question: Agricultural and System refers to utilization of information systems, database, and other information management tools for agricultural use, biological systems modeling to understand the mutual response between life and the environment.

choiceExplanations.Geographic Information: Geographic Information Systems handle spatial mapping data and do not capture the broader biological systems modeling term in RA 10915.
choiceExplanations.Bio-information: Correct — RA 10915 defines Agricultural and Bio-information System as using information tools and biological modeling for agriculture.
choiceExplanations.Modeling: Modeling is one component activity within the system rather than the statutory name Agricultural and Bio-information System.
choiceExplanations.Computer: Computer refers to general computing hardware and not the specific statutory term bio-information.

items.question: Agricultural and Biosystems Power and Machinery refers to farm power and machinery for the production, harvesting, processing, storage, manufacture, preserving, transporting and of agricultural and biological products/materials.

choiceExplanations.Sales: Sales involves commercial transactions rather than the physical post-harvest movement listed in RA 10915.
choiceExplanations.Marketing: Marketing covers promotion and trade rather than the physical delivery term specified in the statutory definition.
choiceExplanations.Distribution: Correct — RA 10915 lists production, harvesting, processing, storage, manufacture, preserving, transporting, and distribution under ABE power and machinery.
choiceExplanations.Quality control: Quality control refers to inspection and testing rather than the final logistics term distribution in the law.

items.question: Agricultural and Biosystems Buildings and Structures refer to buildings and structures for the production, harvesting, processing, storage, ; Preserving, transporting and distribution of agricultural and biological products/materials.

choiceExplanations.Quality control: Quality control denotes testing and inspection and does not appear in the RA 10915 buildings and structures sequence.
choiceExplanations.Treatment: Treatment refers to corrective processing and is not the statutory term between storage and preserving in RA 10915.
choiceExplanations.Manufacture: Correct — RA 10915 specifies manufacture alongside production, harvesting, processing, storage, preserving, transporting, and distribution for ABE structures.
choiceExplanations.Sales: Sales concerns commercial exchange rather than the physical processing and handling functions defined under RA 10915.

items.question: In Section 36 or ABE law, the existing Philippine Agricultural Engineering Standards (PAES) shall be transformed into a Philippine Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering Standards and shall serve as Code of Standards.

choiceExplanations.ABE: ABE is the acronym for Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering and is not the statutory modifier before Code of Standards.
choiceExplanations.Technical: Correct — Section 36 of RA 10915 transforms PAES into PABES to serve as the Code of Technical Standards.
choiceExplanations.AE: AE refers to the legacy Agricultural Engineering title superseded by Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering under RA 10915.
choiceExplanations.Engineering: Engineering is a general discipline term rather than the exact statutory phrase Code of Technical Standards.

items.question: The earned by the professional shall be required in the renewal of professional license.

choiceExplanations.Degree: Degree is an academic qualification required for initial licensure examination rather than periodic license renewal.
choiceExplanations.BSAE degree: BSAE degree is the legacy baccalaureate qualification for initial exam eligibility, not a recurring renewal requirement.
choiceExplanations.BSABE degree: BSABE degree qualifies graduates to take the ABE board exam rather than serving as the ongoing renewal requirement.
choiceExplanations.CPD credit units: Correct — Under RA 10915 and RA 10912, Continuing Professional Development (CPD) credit units are required to renew a PRC license.

items.question: Any person who violates any of the provisions of RA 10915, upon conviction, shall be penalized by a fine of not less than P100,000 but not more than ___, or imprisonment of not less than 6 months but not more than 5 years, or both fine and imprisonment, at the court discretion.

choiceExplanations.200,000: P200,000 understates the maximum statutory fine prescribed in the penal provisions of RA 10915.
choiceExplanations.P300,000: P300,000 is lower than the maximum fine ceiling established under Section 39 of RA 10915.
choiceExplanations.P500,000: Correct — Section 39 of RA 10915 imposes a fine of P100,000 to P500,000 and/or 6 months to 5 years imprisonment.
choiceExplanations.P400,000: P400,000 does not match the statutory upper fine limit of P500,000 under RA 10915.

items.question: In Section 17 of RA 10915, which one is not a scope of Land and Water Resources Engineering?

choiceExplanations.Irrigation: Irrigation is explicitly included in Agricultural and Biosystems Land and Water Resources Engineering under RA 10915.
choiceExplanations.Soil and water: Soil and water conservation is a core component of Land and Water Resources Engineering in Section 17.
choiceExplanations.Meteorology: Correct — Meteorology is a separate atmospheric science rather than a listed scope of Land and Water Resources Engineering in Section 17.
choiceExplanations.Aquaculture: Aquaculture engineering falls within the water resources scope covered by Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering.

items.question: Which republic act is known as the Philippine Agri-Fishery Mechanization Law?

choiceExplanations.RA 10601: Correct — Republic Act No. 10601 is the Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization (AFMech) Law of 2013.
choiceExplanations.RA 10068: RA 10068 is the Organic Agriculture Act of 2010, not the agricultural mechanization law.
choiceExplanations.Barangay roads: Barangay roads refers to rural infrastructure rather than a Republic Act statute.
choiceExplanations.RA 8559: RA 8559 is the repealed Philippine Agricultural Engineering Act of 1998, replaced by RA 10915.

items.question: Under Washington Accord, an Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer who passed licensure examination in the Philippines can practice his/her profession in another Washington Accord member country.

choiceExplanations.Insufficient data to determine: Insufficient data to determine is a quantitative problem distractor rather than a policy answer on international recognition.
choiceExplanations.Yes: Correct — According to this ABELE reviewer key, Washington Accord recognition supports cross-border professional engineering practice after passing Philippine licensure.
choiceExplanations.No: No contradicts the reviewer's key, though strictly the Accord covers academic equivalency while local licensure governs actual practice.
choiceExplanations.Indeterminate: Indeterminate is an analytical distractor unrelated to engineering licensure mobility agreements.

items.question: In Washington Accord, the contract of ABE services signed in the Philippines is valid in another Washington Accord member country.

choiceExplanations.Option A (See original Tambong/Recalled: Option A does not match the recorded Tambong/recalled board answer key for this Washington Accord contract item.
choiceExplanations.Option D (See original Tambong/Recalled: Option D does not correspond to the recalled board key assigned to this item.
choiceExplanations.Option B (See original Tambong/Recalled: Correct — Option B matches the original Tambong/recalled key for whether a Philippine-signed ABE contract holds across Washington Accord signatories.
choiceExplanations.Option C (See original Tambong/Recalled: Option C does not match the recorded board reviewer answer key for this question.

items.question: As provided in the AFMech law, all agricultural and fisheries machinery manufacturers, fabricators, assemblers, and importers must register with the :

choiceExplanations.Invert: Invert refers to the lowest interior bottom elevation of a pipe, culvert, or open channel.
choiceExplanations.Bafe: Correct — Under RA 10601 (AFMech Law), machinery manufacturers, fabricators, assemblers, and importers must register with BAFE.
choiceExplanations.Orifice: Orifice is a calibrated hydraulic opening used to measure or control fluid flow rate.
choiceExplanations.Weir: Weir is an overflow barrier structure placed across an open channel to measure discharge.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the primary combustible gas produced during anaerobic digestion of agricultural wastes?
items.rationale: Anaerobic digestion of biomass produces biogas, composed primarily of 50–70% Methane (CH4) and 30–40% CO2.

choiceExplanations.Methane (CH4): Correct — Anaerobic digestion produces biogas composed primarily of combustible methane (CH4), typically 50–70% by volume.
choiceExplanations.Carbon dioxide (CO2): Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a major non-combustible component of biogas (30–45%) that lowers heating value.
choiceExplanations.Hydrogen sulfide (H2S): Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is a minor corrosive, toxic trace gas in biogas rather than the primary fuel component.
choiceExplanations.Nitrogen (N2): Nitrogen (N2) is an inert gas present only in trace amounts and is non-combustible.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Two cubic meters per hour of water are cooled from 30°C to 4°C. What is the rate of heat transfer in kilowatts (kW)?

choiceExplanations.0.06 kW: 0.06 kW is off by a factor of 1,000, corresponding to watts-vs-kilowatts or gram-vs-kilogram unit errors.
choiceExplanations.14.4 kW: 14.4 kW omits water specific heat (4.187 kJ/kg·°C) in calculating the sensible cooling load.
choiceExplanations.60.5 kW: Correct — Using Q = ṁ·cp·ΔT = (2000/3600 kg/s)(4.187 kJ/kg·°C)(26°C) gives a heat transfer rate of 60.5 kW.
choiceExplanations.144.4 kW: 144.4 kW results from using an incorrect mass flow rate or temperature difference calculation.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Also known as precision agriculture, leveraged technology to optimize farming practices.

choiceExplanations.Agriculture 4.0: Agriculture 4.0 refers to smart farming using IoT sensors, AI, robotics, and cloud connectivity beyond basic precision tools.
choiceExplanations.Agriculture 3.0: Correct — Agriculture 3.0 introduced precision agriculture using GPS, yield mapping, and variable-rate technology to optimize inputs.
choiceExplanations.Agriculture 1.0: Agriculture 1.0 describes traditional labor-intensive subsistence farming reliant on manual and animal power.
choiceExplanations.Agriculture 2.0: Agriculture 2.0 refers to the Green Revolution era of mechanization, synthetic fertilizers, and high-yielding crop varieties.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A set of technologies that use sensors and other tools to improve agricultural practices and increase crop yields.

choiceExplanations.Agriculture 3.0: Agriculture 3.0 focuses on early precision farming like GPS guidance rather than fully integrated smart sensor ecosystems.
choiceExplanations.Agriculture 2.0: Agriculture 2.0 characterizes mechanized and chemical-input farming from the mid-twentieth century rather than digital sensor networks.
choiceExplanations.Agriculture 4.0: Correct — Agriculture 4.0 integrates IoT sensors, automation, big data, and smart analytics to improve farming practices and crop yields.
choiceExplanations.Agriculture 1.0: Agriculture 1.0 denotes early manual and animal-powered farming prior to mechanization and digital sensing.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Allowable range of contract cost for Small A. (not the exact question but read PCAB)

choiceExplanations.500,000: Correct — Under PCAB contractor classification, Small A has a maximum allowable range of contract cost (ARCC) of P500,000.
choiceExplanations.100,000,000: P100,000,000 corresponds to the PCAB allowable contract cost limit for Medium A contractors, not Small A.
choiceExplanations.300,000,000: P300,000,000 corresponds to the PCAB allowable contract cost ceiling for Large A contractors.
choiceExplanations.15,000,000: P15,000,000 corresponds to the PCAB allowable contract cost limit for Small B contractors.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Allowable range of contract cost for Large A. (not the exact question but read PCAB)

choiceExplanations.100,000,000: P100,000,000 is the PCAB allowable contract cost ceiling for Medium A contractors rather than Large A.
choiceExplanations.500,000: P500,000 is the PCAB allowable contract cost limit for Small A contractors.
choiceExplanations.300,000,000: Correct — Under PCAB contractor classification, Large A carries an allowable range of contract cost (ARCC) up to P300,000,000.
choiceExplanations.15,000,000: P15,000,000 is the PCAB allowable contract cost ceiling for Small B contractors.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: To roll the tractor set at first gear in a flat land, what should be foot-pressed.

choiceExplanations.Differential lock: Differential lock engages both rear axles equally to prevent wheel slip on soft ground, not to roll on flat land.
choiceExplanations.Clutch: Clutch disengages engine power from the transmission, which stops rather than initiates forward tractor motion once engaged.
choiceExplanations.Accelerator: Correct — With first gear engaged and clutch released, pressing the foot accelerator increases engine speed to roll the tractor forward.
choiceExplanations.Brake: Brake applies friction to slow or stop the tractor wheels rather than propelling it forward.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A sweet potato puree manufacturing plant would like to apply metrology in automated detection of abnormalities in the skin of sweet potato tubers to ascertain top quality puree. What class of metrology equipment is best to be used? (Dr. Tambong; pero mango yung commodity sa BE)

choiceExplanations.Ultrasonic scanners: Ultrasonic scanners inspect internal density or thickness via sound waves rather than high-resolution surface and internal defect imaging.
choiceExplanations.Laser scanners: Laser scanners capture external 3D geometry profiles but are less suited for comprehensive cross-sectional defect detection.
choiceExplanations.CTscanners: Correct — CT scanners provide detailed X-ray imaging capable of detecting surface and internal abnormalities in agricultural tubers and fruits.
choiceExplanations.Optical comparators: Optical comparators project magnified 2D silhouettes of manufactured parts for manual profile checking, unsuited for automated produce inspection.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A cattle ranch needs to measure the height of the tallest body part of each of 10,000 animals every morning. What class of metrology equipment is best to be used in automating measurement? (Dr. Tambong)

choiceExplanations.Optical comparators: Optical comparators are stationary benchtop shadow-projection gauges for small parts, unusable on moving herd cattle.
choiceExplanations.Ultrasonic sensors: Ultrasonic sensors measure distance using sound waves with wider beam divergence and lower spatial precision on irregular animal silhouettes.
choiceExplanations.Laser scanners: Correct — Laser scanners rapidly capture non-contact 3D spatial profiles to determine the highest point of moving livestock accurately.
choiceExplanations.CT scanners: CT scanners require enclosed radiation chambers and slow stationary scanning, making them impractical for 10,000 cattle daily.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A red pepper (Capsicum annuum) processing plant monitors the quality of its product. It takes the weight and 4-angle images of each fruit in all its 60 running conveyors. If it detects a blemished fruit, it diverts it to separate bin. Classify the automation system used in the processing plant. (Dr. Tambong)

choiceExplanations.Supervisorycontroland dataacquisition: Correct — SCADA supervises plant-wide data acquisition and automated sorting across multiple conveyor lines from a central monitoring architecture.
choiceExplanations.Programmable logic controller: Programmable logic controllers execute localized machine control on individual conveyors rather than supervising 60-line plant-wide data.
choiceExplanations.Distributed control system: Distributed control systems typically manage continuous analog process plants like refineries rather than discrete high-speed sorting lines.
choiceExplanations.Manufacturing execution system: Manufacturing execution systems manage production scheduling, inventory, and work orders at the enterprise layer rather than real-time sensor sorting.

items.question: The ratio of engine power used in performing an operation to engine power available.
items.rationale: [Verified & Corrected from 'field load tractor']

choiceExplanations.Drawbar pull factor: Drawbar pull factor relates draft force or drawbar pull to tractor weight rather than comparing used to available engine power.
choiceExplanations.Field machine index: Field machine index measures time efficiency (productive field time vs. total operating time excluding turning), not power utilization.
choiceExplanations.Field load factor: Correct — Field load factor is defined in farm machinery management as the ratio of engine power used to available engine power.
choiceExplanations.Reserve power factor: Reserve power factor indicates excess available engine power above load demand rather than the fraction utilized.

items.question: An external shaft on an agricultural tractor other than the PTO / which provides rotational power to implements that are usually front and side mounted

choiceExplanations.Auxiliary PTO: Correct — Under PAES/ASABE tractor terminology, an auxiliary PTO is a secondary external shaft powering front- or side-mounted implements.
choiceExplanations.Independent PTO: Independent PTO refers to the main rear PTO controlled by its own clutch independent of tractor travel.
choiceExplanations.Live PTO: Live PTO is a main PTO driven through a two-stage clutch allowing gear shifts without stopping the PTO.
choiceExplanations.Continuous PTO: Continuous PTO is another clutch arrangement for the main rear PTO shaft, not a secondary front/side shaft.

items.question: A part of mechanism that they may be added to a functional power unit, not utilizing its mechanical power for the purpose of enhancing the performance of that unit.

choiceExplanations.Component: Component is a fundamental constituent part built into the machine's basic structure rather than an optional add-on.
choiceExplanations.Attachment: Attachment is a device added to a power unit that typically utilizes its mechanical power or performs a specific work function.
choiceExplanations.Implement: Implement is a distinct agricultural machine hitched to or mounted on a tractor to perform field operations.
choiceExplanations.Accessory: Correct — Under PAES terminology, an accessory is an add-on part that enhances performance without utilizing the unit's mechanical power.

items.question: It is a constant volume combustion cycle

choiceExplanations.Otto cycle: Correct — The ideal Otto cycle adds heat at constant volume, representing spark-ignition gasoline internal combustion engines.
choiceExplanations.Diesel cycle: The ideal Diesel cycle models heat addition at constant pressure rather than constant volume.
choiceExplanations.Carnot cycle: The Carnot cycle is an idealized reversible cycle operating with isothermal heat addition and rejection.
choiceExplanations.Brayton cycle: The Brayton cycle models gas turbine engines using constant-pressure heat addition and rejection.

items.question: It is a constant pressure combustion cycle

choiceExplanations.Otto cycle: The Otto cycle models spark-ignition engines where combustion heat addition occurs at constant volume.
choiceExplanations.Stirling cycle: The Stirling cycle uses isothermal heat addition and rejection coupled with constant-volume regeneration.
choiceExplanations.Carnot cycle: The Carnot cycle is a theoretical reversible cycle with isothermal heat addition and rejection.
choiceExplanations.Diesel cycle: Correct — The ideal Diesel cycle models compression-ignition engines where fuel combustion occurs at constant pressure.

items.question: Reduction of engine speed or flow of fuel

choiceExplanations.Throttling: Correct — Throttling restricts intake air-fuel or fuel flow to reduce engine power output and operating speed.
choiceExplanations.Choking: Choking enriches the air-fuel mixture by restricting air intake during cold engine starting.
choiceExplanations.Priming: Priming introduces initial fuel or fluid into a system or pump to facilitate starting.
choiceExplanations.Scavenging: Scavenging is the clearing of residual exhaust gases from the cylinder using fresh intake air.

items.question: A device that is used to actuate the throttle of an engine to increase its speed

choiceExplanations.Carburetor: Carburetor mixes air and fuel in proper proportions for spark-ignition engines rather than actuating the throttle pedal or lever.
choiceExplanations.Governor: Governor automatically senses speed changes and adjusts fuel flow to maintain constant engine rpm under varying loads.
choiceExplanations.Accelerator: Correct — An accelerator is the operator-controlled linkage or pedal that opens the throttle to increase engine speed.
choiceExplanations.Regulator: Regulator controls fluid pressure or electrical voltage rather than manually actuating an engine throttle.

items.question: Usable power delivered by the engine

choiceExplanations.Friction horsepower: Friction horsepower is the power lost internally to mechanical friction, pumping, and accessory drives.
choiceExplanations.Indicated horsepower: Indicated horsepower is the theoretical gross power developed inside the cylinders by combustion gas pressure.
choiceExplanations.Rated horsepower: Rated horsepower is the manufacturer's specified nominal power output under standard operating conditions.
choiceExplanations.Brake horsepower: Correct — Brake horsepower (BHP) is the actual usable shaft power delivered by the engine at the flywheel.

items.question: A device that permits the flow of fuel and of burned gases in one direction only

choiceExplanations.Relief valve: Relief valve opens at a preset pressure threshold to protect a system from overpressure rather than enforcing unidirectional flow.
choiceExplanations.Check valve: Correct — A check valve (non-return valve) allows fluid or gas to pass in one direction while preventing backflow.
choiceExplanations.Needle valve: Needle valve provides fine manual throttling of flow rate through a tapered pin orifice.
choiceExplanations.Throttle valve: Throttle valve regulates mass flow rate into an engine rather than acting as a one-way flow blocker.

items.question: At the downward stroke of two-stroke cycle engine, which of the events are taking place.

choiceExplanations.Compression & ignition: Compression occurs on the upward stroke of the piston, not the downward stroke.
choiceExplanations.Power & intake: Correct — During the downward stroke of a two-stroke engine, expanding gases produce the power stroke while intake/exhaust ports open.
choiceExplanations.Intake & compression: Compression takes place during the upward piston stroke as the trapped charge is compressed toward TDC.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust & compression: Compression occurs as the piston moves upward, whereas the downward stroke delivers power and exhaust/intake scavenging.

items.question: Power transmitted to the pistons by the gas in the cylinder

choiceExplanations.Friction horsepower: Friction horsepower represents internal power losses absorbed by bearings, rings, and pumping.
choiceExplanations.Drawbar horsepower: Drawbar horsepower is the pulling power actually delivered at the tractor hitch to pull an implement.
choiceExplanations.Indicated horsepower: Correct — Indicated horsepower (IHP) is the total power developed by expanding combustion gases acting on the piston faces.
choiceExplanations.Brake horsepower: Brake horsepower is the net usable power measured at the crankshaft after subtracting friction losses.

items.question: Engine mechanical efficiency

choiceExplanations.Indicated hp over brake hp: Indicated hp over brake hp inverts the mechanical efficiency ratio and yields a value greater than 100%.
choiceExplanations.Friction hp over indicated hp: Friction hp over indicated hp represents the fraction of power lost to friction rather than mechanical efficiency.
choiceExplanations.Brake hp over indicated hp: Correct — Engine mechanical efficiency equals usable brake horsepower divided by total indicated horsepower (BHP / IHP).
choiceExplanations.Drawbar hp over brake hp: Drawbar hp over brake hp expresses tractive and drivetrain transmission efficiency rather than engine mechanical efficiency.

items.question: System of number indicating the ignition quality of diesel fuel

choiceExplanations.Viscosity index: Viscosity index measures how strongly a lubricating oil's viscosity changes with temperature.
choiceExplanations.Octane rating: Octane rating indicates a spark-ignition gasoline fuel's resistance to auto-ignition and engine knock.
choiceExplanations.Cetane rating: Correct — Cetane rating measures the compression-ignition quality and ignition delay characteristics of diesel fuel.
choiceExplanations.API gravity: API gravity expresses the relative density of petroleum liquids compared to water, not ignition quality.

items.question: Mean effective pressure for turbo-charge engine.

choiceExplanations.276 psi: 276 psi falls below the standard textbook benchmark of 300 psi for turbocharged agricultural engines.
choiceExplanations.390 psi: 390 psi overstates the typical mean effective pressure benchmark cited in ABE power review references.
choiceExplanations.300 psi: Correct — Standard agricultural power reviewers cite approximately 300 psi as the mean effective pressure for a turbocharged engine.
choiceExplanations.324 psi: 324 psi does not match the standard 300 psi reference value used in ABE board reviewers.

items.question: Engine valve that allows the entrance of fuel.

choiceExplanations.Bypass valve: Bypass valve diverts excess flow around a component such as a filter or pump rather than admitting cylinder charge.
choiceExplanations.Intake valve: Correct — The intake valve opens during the intake stroke to admit air or an air-fuel mixture into the cylinder.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust valve: Exhaust valve opens to discharge burned combustion gases out of the cylinder after the power stroke.
choiceExplanations.Relief valve: Relief valve vents excessive pressure to safeguard hydraulic or lubrication lines rather than admitting cylinder fuel.

items.question: Standard throttling adjustment of an engine

choiceExplanations.¾: Correct — Standard engine testing and operation reviewers specify ¾ throttle as the typical standard throttling adjustment.
choiceExplanations.⅔: ⅔ throttle is not the standard benchmark throttle setting referenced in agricultural engine practice.
choiceExplanations.¼: ¼ throttle represents low-idle or light-load operation rather than standard operating adjustment.
choiceExplanations.½: ½ throttle provides only partial load capacity and is below the standard ¾ setting.

items.question: Mean effective pressure of an engine.

choiceExplanations.130 psi: 130 psi exceeds the classic naturally aspirated engine MEP benchmark cited in Philippine ABE reviewers.
choiceExplanations.120 psi: Correct — Traditional agricultural engine review materials cite 120 psi as the standard mean effective pressure of an engine.
choiceExplanations.156 psi: 156 psi is higher than the standard 120 psi MEP value used for basic naturally aspirated engine calculations.
choiceExplanations.146 psi: 146 psi does not match the standard 120 psi reference value in agricultural power engineering notes.

items.question: Ignition timing for gasoline engine

Correct — Spark ignition in standard gasoline engines is typically timed 5–10 degrees before top dead center (BTDC).
10–15 degrees BTDC is slightly more advanced than the standard base timing range for conventional gasoline engines.
15–20 degrees BTDC corresponds closer to diesel injection advance rather than gasoline base ignition timing.
0–5 degrees BTDC provides insufficient spark advance for complete combustion at normal operating speeds.

items.question: Ignition timing for diesel engine.

choiceExplanations.15-17 deg: 15–17 degrees BTDC is slightly less advanced than the standard 17–19 degree diesel injection timing key.
choiceExplanations.13-15 deg: 13–15 degrees BTDC provides insufficient advance to compensate for diesel ignition delay in standard engine specs.
choiceExplanations.19-21 deg: 19–21 degrees BTDC is overly advanced for standard diesel engines and risks excessive knock.
choiceExplanations.17-19 deg: Correct — Fuel injection/ignition timing in conventional diesel engines is typically set around 17–19 degrees before top dead center.

items.question: One horsepower can generate heat energy equal to

choiceExplanations.2749 BTU/hr: 2749 BTU/hr is numerically inaccurate and overstates the thermal equivalent of one mechanical horsepower.
choiceExplanations.2927 BTU/hr: 2927 BTU/hr does not match the standard thermodynamic conversion factor for horsepower to BTU/hr.
