choiceExplanations.2545 BTU/hr: Correct — By unit conversion (550 ft·lbf/s × 3600 s/hr ÷ 778.17 ft·lbf/BTU), 1 hp equals 2545 BTU/hr.
choiceExplanations.3308 BTU/hr: 3308 BTU/hr exceeds the true thermal equivalent of one horsepower (2545 BTU/hr).

items.question: A part of an engine which reduces vibration and stores energy

choiceExplanations.Crankshaft: Crankshaft converts reciprocating piston motion into rotational torque rather than serving primarily as an inertial energy reservoir.
choiceExplanations.Camshaft: Camshaft actuates the intake and exhaust valves in synchronization with engine rotation.
choiceExplanations.Counterweight: Counterweight balances reciprocating and rotating masses on the crankshaft rather than storing rotational kinetic energy.
choiceExplanations.Flywheel: Correct — The flywheel stores rotational kinetic energy during the power stroke and smooths engine speed fluctuations and vibration.

items.question: Conversion of solid fuel into combustible carbon monoxide through thermochemical reaction.

choiceExplanations.Gasification: Correct — Gasification partially oxidizes solid biomass at high temperatures to produce combustible producer gas rich in carbon monoxide and hydrogen.
choiceExplanations.Liquefaction: Liquefaction thermochemically converts biomass into liquid bio-crude under high pressure rather than combustible gas.
choiceExplanations.Pyrolysis: Pyrolysis thermally decomposes biomass in the complete absence of oxygen primarily yielding bio-oil, char, and non-condensable gases.
choiceExplanations.Torrefaction: Torrefaction is mild thermal pretreatment (200–300°C) that upgrades biomass energy density without converting it into gas.

items.question: A device that converts kinetic energy of the wind to mechanical power.

choiceExplanations.Gearbox: Gearbox steps up rotational speed between the low-speed rotor shaft and the high-speed generator.
choiceExplanations.Stator: Stator is the stationary electromagnetic winding housing inside the electrical generator.
choiceExplanations.Nacelle: Nacelle is the protective enclosure mounted atop the wind turbine tower housing the drivetrain and generator.
choiceExplanations.Rotor: Correct — The wind turbine rotor (blades and hub) intercepts wind kinetic energy and converts it into shaft mechanical power.

items.question: It is the ratio of the drawbar power and the wheel axle power.

choiceExplanations.Volumetric efficiency: Volumetric efficiency measures how completely an engine cylinder or pump fills with air or fluid compared to theoretical displacement.
choiceExplanations.Traction efficiency: Correct — Tractive (traction) efficiency is the ratio of drawbar power output to drive-wheel axle power input.
choiceExplanations.Transmission efficiency: Transmission efficiency is the ratio of power delivered to the drive axle over engine flywheel power.
choiceExplanations.Mechanical efficiency: Mechanical efficiency commonly denotes brake horsepower divided by indicated horsepower in internal combustion engines.

items.question: When a machine is driven directly from the shaft of a power source, the machine power is transmitted using:

choiceExplanations.Chain drive: Chain drive transmits power between parallel shafts using sprockets and an endless roller chain.
choiceExplanations.Direct drive: Correct — Direct drive couples the driven machine straight to the prime mover shaft without intermediate belts, chains, or gears.
choiceExplanations.Belt drive: Belt drive transfers power between separated pulleys through belt friction or teeth.
choiceExplanations.Gear drive: Gear drive transmits torque between shafts via meshing toothed gears.

items.question: It is gripping device between power source

choiceExplanations.Coupling: Coupling permanently or semi-permanently joins two collinear shafts rather than selectively engaging and disengaging power.
choiceExplanations.Clutch: Correct — A clutch is a friction or mechanical gripping device that connects and disconnects a power source from a driven shaft.
choiceExplanations.Pulley: Pulley is a grooved wheel that guides and transmits power through a belt or rope.
choiceExplanations.Sprocket: Sprocket is a toothed wheel that engages the links of a roller chain.

items.question: Machine element that transmit torque and power

choiceExplanations.Shaft: Correct — A shaft is a rotating machine element used to transmit torque and mechanical power between components.
choiceExplanations.Bushing: A bushing is a sleeve bearing or liner that reduces friction between sliding or rotating parts.
choiceExplanations.Collar: A collar is a ring fastened around a shaft to prevent axial movement or locate components.
choiceExplanations.Bearing: A bearing supports rotating shafts and reduces friction without directly transmitting torque.

items.question: A universal joint is:
items.answer: Used to transmit power between two intersecting shafts usually when the angle between them is variable
choices: Used to connect two coaxial shafts rigidly to prevent any angular or axial misalignment during operation
Used to transmit power between two parallel shafts usually when the center distance between them is fixed
Used to transmit power between two intersecting shafts usually when the angle between them is variable
Used to transmit power between two non-intersecting perpendicular shafts when a high speed reduction is needed

choiceExplanations.Used to connect two coaxial shafts rigid: Rigid couplings connect coaxial shafts to prevent misalignment, whereas a universal joint accommodates varying angles.
choiceExplanations.Used to transmit power between two paral: Parallel-shaft power transmission at fixed center distances is handled by spur gears, belts, or chains.
choiceExplanations.Used to transmit power between two inter: Correct — A universal joint (Cardan joint) transmits rotary power between two intersecting shafts whose relative angle varies.
choiceExplanations.Used to transmit power between two non-i: Worm gears or hypoid gears transmit power between non-intersecting perpendicular shafts with high speed reduction.

items.question: It is the ratio between the mass of fuel consumed per unit of time and the corresponding measured power

choiceExplanations.Mass air-fuel ratio: Mass air-fuel ratio compares the mass of air to fuel entering the engine, not fuel mass per power.
choiceExplanations.Specific fuel consumption: Correct — Specific fuel consumption (SFC) measures fuel mass consumed per unit time divided by engine power output (e.g., g/kWh).
choiceExplanations.Brake thermal efficiency: Brake thermal efficiency is the ratio of brake power output to the fuel's thermal energy input rate.
choiceExplanations.Hourly fuel consumption: Hourly fuel consumption measures only fuel used per hour without dividing by engine power output.

items.question: A clutch that limits the amount of torque or power that is transmitted through the shaft to the driven member

choiceExplanations.Dog clutch: A dog clutch positively locks shafts together via interlocking teeth without slipping under overload.
choiceExplanations.Overrunning clutch: An overrunning clutch transmits torque in only one direction and freewheels in the reverse direction.
choiceExplanations.Centrifugal clutch: A centrifugal clutch engages automatically as rotational speed rises rather than limiting overload torque.
choiceExplanations.Slip clutch: Correct — A slip clutch uses friction plates under spring pressure to slip and limit transmitted torque during overload.

items.question: Minimum thrust per drawbar HP of hydraulic remote control cylinder for trailing type agricultural implement

choiceExplanations.68kg: Correct — Under standard agricultural machinery specifications (ASABE/PAES), trailing hydraulic remote cylinders provide at least 68 kg (150 lb) thrust per drawbar hp.
choiceExplanations.63kg: 63 kg per drawbar hp falls below the standard minimum thrust requirement for hydraulic remote control cylinders.
choiceExplanations.88kg: 88 kg per drawbar hp exceeds the standardized 68 kg (150 lb) minimum thrust per drawbar hp.
choiceExplanations.73kg: 73 kg per drawbar hp is higher than the standard 68 kg minimum thrust specification.

items.question: PTO rpm of lawn and garden ride-on tractors

choiceExplanations.2160 rpm: 2160 rpm is not a standard PTO speed for lawn and garden ride-on tractors.
choiceExplanations.1840 rpm: 1840 rpm is not a standardized PTO rotational speed for ride-on lawn and garden tractors.
choiceExplanations.2440 rpm: 2440 rpm does not match the ASAE/PAES standard PTO speed for lawn and garden tractors.
choiceExplanations.2000 rpm: Correct — Standard ASABE/PAES specifications designate 2000 rpm as the PTO speed for lawn and garden ride-on tractors.

items.question: Equipment designed with integral power unit to provide both mobility and power for performing agricultural operations.

choiceExplanations.Semi mounted implement: A semi-mounted implement has its front carried by a tractor hitch and rear supported by its own wheel.
choiceExplanations.Tractor mounted implement: A tractor-mounted implement attaches to the three-point hitch and relies entirely on the tractor for power and mobility.
choiceExplanations.Self propelled machine: Correct — A self-propelled machine integrates its own engine and drivetrain to provide both mobility and operational power.
choiceExplanations.Pull type machine: A pull-type machine is towed behind a tractor and lacks an integral propulsion unit.

items.question: Process of converting biomass into biochar at 275 degrees / Celsius to 300 degrees Celsius.

choiceExplanations.Severe torrefaction: Correct — Severe torrefaction thermally upgrades biomass at 275 °C to 300 °C in an inert atmosphere to produce biochar.
choiceExplanations.Slow pyrolysis: Slow pyrolysis typically operates at higher temperatures around 400–600 °C to maximize charcoal yield.
choiceExplanations.Fast pyrolysis: Fast pyrolysis rapidly heats biomass around 450–550 °C with short vapor residence times to maximize bio-oil.
choiceExplanations.Mild torrefaction: Mild torrefaction occurs at lower temperatures between roughly 200 °C and 250 °C.

items.question: It states that heat is a form of energy, and thermodynamic processes are therefore subject to the principle of conservation of energy.

choiceExplanations.Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics: The Zeroth Law defines thermal equilibrium and provides the basis for temperature measurement.
choiceExplanations.1st Law of Thermodynamics: Correct — The First Law of Thermodynamics establishes conservation of energy, treating heat and work as equivalent forms of energy.
choiceExplanations.2nd Law of Thermodynamics: The Second Law introduces entropy and governs the direction and efficiency limits of heat transfer.
choiceExplanations.3rd Law of Thermodynamics: The Third Law states that a pure crystal's entropy approaches zero as temperature approaches absolute zero.

items.question: An engine that burns fuel and air inside a combustion chamber located within the engine proper

choiceExplanations.Internal Combustion Engine: Correct — An internal combustion engine burns fuel and air directly inside the engine's own combustion chamber.
choiceExplanations.Steam Reciprocating Engine: A steam reciprocating engine uses steam generated in a separate external boiler rather than internal combustion.
choiceExplanations.Stirling Thermal Engine: A Stirling engine heats working gas from an external heat source outside the cylinder.
choiceExplanations.External Combustion Engine: An external combustion engine burns fuel outside the engine proper to heat a working fluid.

items.question: refers to the size if the opening of the cylinder which is almost equal to the diameter of the piston plus the rings

choiceExplanations.Bore: Correct — Bore is the internal diameter of the engine cylinder, slightly larger than the piston to accommodate piston rings.
choiceExplanations.Stroke: Stroke is the linear distance the piston travels between top dead center and bottom dead center.
choiceExplanations.Clearance: Clearance is the small gap or volume remaining above the piston at top dead center.
choiceExplanations.Displacement: Displacement is the volume swept by the piston moving through one full stroke.

items.question: refers to the distance traveled by a piston from the tdc to the bdc

choiceExplanations.Clearance: Clearance refers to the gap or residual volume at the top of the cylinder, not piston travel.
choiceExplanations.Displacement: Displacement is the cylinder volume swept during a stroke, not the linear travel distance.
choiceExplanations.Stroke: Correct — Stroke is the linear distance traveled by the piston between top dead center (TDC) and bottom dead center (BDC).
choiceExplanations.Bore: Bore is the inside diameter of the cylinder, not the piston's travel length.

items.question: uppermost position of the piston during the compression and exhaust stroke

choiceExplanations.Exhaust valve closing, evc: Exhaust valve closing (EVC) is a valve timing event rather than the piston's physical position.
choiceExplanations.Bottom dead center, bdc: Bottom dead center (BDC) is the lowest position of the piston, farthest from the cylinder head.
choiceExplanations.Top dead center, tdc: Correct — Top dead center (TDC) is the uppermost piston position closest to the cylinder head during compression and exhaust.
choiceExplanations.Intake valve opening, ivo: Intake valve opening (IVO) denotes when the intake valve opens, not the piston's uppermost position.

items.question: lowest most position of the piston during the intake and power stroke

choiceExplanations.Top dead center, tdc: Top dead center (TDC) is the uppermost piston position closest to the cylinder head.
choiceExplanations.Intake valve closing, ivc: Intake valve closing (IVC) is a valve timing point, not the piston's lowest position.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust valve opening, evo: Exhaust valve opening (EVO) marks when exhaust gases begin exiting, not a piston position.
choiceExplanations.Bottom dead center, bdc: Correct — Bottom dead center (BDC) is the lowest piston position farthest from the cylinder head during intake and power.

items.question: the volume displaced by a piston in one stroke

choiceExplanations.Crankcase volume: Crankcase volume is the space enclosing the crankshaft below the pistons, not swept cylinder volume.
choiceExplanations.Clearance volume: Clearance volume is the unswept volume remaining above the piston when at top dead center.
choiceExplanations.Total cylinder volume: Total cylinder volume equals the sum of piston displacement and clearance volume.
choiceExplanations.Engine/piston displacement: Correct — Piston displacement (swept volume) is the volume displaced as the piston moves from TDC to BDC in one stroke.

items.question: volume in the combustion cylinder when the piston is at the TDC position

choiceExplanations.Swept volume: Swept volume is the volume displaced by the piston moving between TDC and BDC.
choiceExplanations.Piston displacement: Piston displacement equals swept volume during a stroke rather than the remaining TDC volume.
choiceExplanations.Total cylinder volume: Total cylinder volume is the volume above the piston when at BDC, including displacement.
choiceExplanations.Clearance volume: Correct — Clearance volume is the combustion chamber space remaining above the piston when it reaches TDC.

items.question: the ratio of the total volume to the clearance volume

choiceExplanations.Air-fuel ratio: Air-fuel ratio compares the mass of air to the mass of fuel supplied for combustion.
choiceExplanations.Compression ratio: Correct — Compression ratio is the ratio of total cylinder volume at BDC to the clearance volume at TDC.
choiceExplanations.Equivalence ratio: Equivalence ratio compares the actual fuel-air ratio to the stoichiometric fuel-air ratio.
choiceExplanations.Cutoff ratio: Cutoff ratio is the ratio of cylinder volumes after and before constant-pressure combustion in a Diesel cycle.

items.question: amount of pressure generated during the power stroke of the engine

choiceExplanations.Manifold Absolute Pressure, MAP: Manifold absolute pressure measures air pressure inside the intake manifold, not combustion stroke pressure.
choiceExplanations.Mean Effective Pressure, MEP: Correct — Mean Effective Pressure (MEP) is the average net pressure acting on the piston during the power stroke.
choiceExplanations.Reid Vapor Pressure, RVP: Reid vapor pressure measures fuel volatility under standard laboratory conditions, not cylinder pressure.
choiceExplanations.Peak Cylinder Pressure, PCP: Peak cylinder pressure is the single maximum pressure spike rather than the average power-stroke pressure.

items.question: equivalent to one complete rotation of the crankshaft

choiceExplanations.Revolution: Correct — One revolution corresponds to a full 360-degree rotation of the engine crankshaft.
choiceExplanations.Oscillation: Oscillation refers to repetitive back-and-forth motion rather than a full circular rotation.
choiceExplanations.Cycle: An engine cycle may take one or two crankshaft revolutions depending on two-stroke or four-stroke design.
choiceExplanations.Stroke: A stroke is one linear piston travel from TDC to BDC, taking half a crankshaft revolution.

items.question: refers to the series of events occurring one after the other in a definite order and repeating the event after the last one has occurred

choiceExplanations.Cycle: Correct — A cycle is a complete, repeating sequence of thermodynamic and mechanical events occurring in a fixed order.
choiceExplanations.Stroke: A stroke is only a single linear movement of the piston between dead centers.
choiceExplanations.Phase: A phase refers to a single stage or timing angle within a process, not the full repeating sequence.
choiceExplanations.Revolution: A revolution is a 360-degree shaft turn, whereas a four-stroke cycle requires two revolutions.

items.question: The power generated at the combustion chamber

choiceExplanations.Friction horsepower, FHP: Friction horsepower is the power lost to internal engine friction and pumping, not generated combustion power.
choiceExplanations.Rated horsepower, RHP: Rated horsepower is the manufacturer's specified safe continuous power output, not raw combustion power.
choiceExplanations.Indicated horsepower, IHP: Correct — Indicated horsepower (IHP) is the theoretical power developed inside the combustion chamber by expanding gases.
choiceExplanations.Brake horsepower, BHP: Brake horsepower is the net usable power delivered at the crankshaft after friction losses.

items.question: power available at the drive shaft or the crankshaft of the engine

choiceExplanations.Friction Horsepower: Friction horsepower represents internal mechanical power losses rather than usable crankshaft output.
choiceExplanations.Rated Horsepower: Rated horsepower is the manufacturer-specified operating power rating rather than actual measured shaft output.
choiceExplanations.Indicated Horsepower: Indicated horsepower is the gross power produced in the cylinders before subtracting friction losses.
choiceExplanations.Brake Horsepower: Correct — Brake horsepower (BHP) is the net mechanical power available at the engine crankshaft or drive shaft.

items.question: the power loss due to friction of the piston and other components of the engine

choiceExplanations.Drawbar HorsePower: Drawbar horsepower is the usable pulling power developed at a tractor's drawbar hitch.
choiceExplanations.Brake HorsePower: Brake horsepower is the net useful power delivered at the engine crankshaft.
choiceExplanations.Friction HorsePower: Correct — Friction horsepower (FHP) is the power consumed by internal friction of pistons, bearings, and engine accessories.
choiceExplanations.Indicated HorsePower: Indicated horsepower is the total power generated by combustion gases inside the cylinders.

items.question: Power of the engine as specified by the manufacturers

choiceExplanations.Rated Horsepower: Correct — Rated horsepower is the power rating specified by the manufacturer for continuous safe operation at rated speed.
choiceExplanations.Brake Horsepower: Brake horsepower is the actual net power measured at the crankshaft under test conditions.
choiceExplanations.Friction Horsepower: Friction horsepower is the internal power lost to mechanical friction and pumping.
choiceExplanations.Indicated Horsepower: Indicated horsepower is the gross power developed inside the combustion chamber.

items.question: the ratio of the __HP and __HP, __HP/__HP

choiceExplanations.Tractive Efficiency, IHP to BHP: Tractive efficiency compares drawbar power to axle power on a tractor, not IHP to BHP.
choiceExplanations.Volumetric Efficiency, FHP to IHP: Volumetric efficiency compares actual inducted air mass to theoretical cylinder displacement capacity.
choiceExplanations.Mechanical Efficiency, BHP/IHP: Correct — Mechanical efficiency of an engine is defined as the ratio of brake horsepower (BHP) to indicated horsepower (IHP).
choiceExplanations.Thermal Efficiency, BHP to FHP: Thermal efficiency compares output power to fuel heat input rate, not BHP to FHP.

items.question: the ratio of the BHP to the power available at the fuel

choiceExplanations.Volumetric efficiency: Volumetric efficiency measures how effectively the cylinder fills with air-fuel charge during intake.
choiceExplanations.Combustion efficiency: Combustion efficiency measures the fraction of fuel chemical energy actually released during burning.
choiceExplanations.Mechanical efficiency: Mechanical efficiency is the ratio of brake horsepower to indicated horsepower.
choiceExplanations.Thermal efficiency: Correct — Brake thermal efficiency is the ratio of brake horsepower (BHP) output to the thermal power available from the fuel.

items.question: the rate of the fuel consumed of an engine per unit break horsepower

choiceExplanations.Brake thermal efficiency: Brake thermal efficiency is the dimensionless ratio of brake power output to fuel energy input.
choiceExplanations.Hourly fuel consumption: Hourly fuel consumption measures total fuel burned per hour without normalizing by brake horsepower.
choiceExplanations.Specific fuel consumption: Correct — Brake specific fuel consumption (BSFC) expresses the rate of fuel consumed per unit of brake horsepower produced.
choiceExplanations.Volumetric fuel efficiency: Volumetric fuel efficiency is not the standard metric for fuel mass consumed per unit brake power.

items.question: Minimum speed of the engine at no load, usually runs around ___rpm

choiceExplanations.Idle Speed,900rpm: Correct — Standard agricultural engine references define idle speed as the minimum no-load running speed, typically around 900 rpm.
choiceExplanations.Idle Speed,1170rpm: 1170 rpm is too high for the standard no-load idle speed benchmark of ~900 rpm.
choiceExplanations.Idle Speed,828rpm: 828 rpm does not match the standard 900 rpm textbook value for engine idle speed.
choiceExplanations.Idle Speed,720rpm: 720 rpm is lower than the standard 900 rpm reference value for agricultural engine idle speed.

items.question: opening adjustment of the engine throttle at the best operating condition, which is usally ___% of the total opening

choiceExplanations.Maximum throttle opening: Maximum throttle opening gives peak fuel flow and power rather than best-efficiency operating adjustment.
choiceExplanations.Optimum throttle opening: Correct — Optimum throttle opening is the throttle setting (typically ~75%) providing the best engine operating efficiency and performance.
choiceExplanations.Rated throttle position: Rated throttle position corresponds to the manufacturer's rated speed and load condition rather than best-efficiency opening.
choiceExplanations.Minimum idle setting: Minimum idle setting runs the engine at lowest no-load speed rather than optimal operating load.

items.question: Uses spark to ignite the fuel, uses gasoline as fuel and has CARBURETOR to mix fuel and air

choiceExplanations.Surface Ignition Engine: Surface ignition (hot-bulb) engines ignite fuel via a heated chamber surface without a spark plug.
choiceExplanations.Spark Ignition Engine: Correct — A spark ignition (gasoline) engine uses a carburetor or fuel system to mix air-fuel and a spark plug for ignition.
choiceExplanations.External Combustion Engine: An external combustion engine burns fuel outside the cylinder to heat a working fluid.
choiceExplanations.Compression Ignition Engine: A compression ignition (diesel) engine uses high air compression heat and fuel injectors without a carburetor or spark.

items.question: Uses high compression to raise the temperature of the air in a chamber and ignites the injected fuel, has an atomizer to spray the fuel inside the engine

choiceExplanations.External combustion engine: An external combustion engine burns fuel outside the engine cylinder to drive a separate working fluid.
choiceExplanations.Compression ignition engine: Correct — A compression ignition (diesel) engine compresses air to high temperature and injects atomized fuel for auto-ignition.
choiceExplanations.Spark ignition engine: A spark ignition engine relies on an electrical spark rather than compression heat alone to ignite fuel.
choiceExplanations.Rotary piston engine: A rotary piston (Wankel) engine uses an eccentric rotor and typically spark ignition.

items.question: produces power in one revolution of the crankshaft, fuel and oil is mixed in the combustion chamber, high speed, light in weight

choiceExplanations.Six-Stroke Cycle Engine: A six-stroke cycle engine requires three crankshaft revolutions per power stroke.
choiceExplanations.Two-Stroke Cycle Engine: Correct — A two-stroke cycle engine delivers one power stroke per crankshaft revolution, offering high speed and light weight.
choiceExplanations.Four-Stroke Cycle Engine: A four-stroke cycle engine requires two crankshaft revolutions per power stroke and is heavier.
choiceExplanations.Dual-Cycle Diesel Engine: A dual-cycle diesel engine typically operates on four strokes over two crankshaft revolutions.

items.question: produces power in two revolutions of the crankshaft, fuel is burned inside the CC, low speed, heavy in weight

choiceExplanations.Six-Stroke cycle engine: A six-stroke cycle engine requires three crankshaft revolutions to complete one full cycle.
choiceExplanations.Five-Stroke cycle engine: A five-stroke engine is an experimental concept with an extra expansion cylinder, not standard.
choiceExplanations.Two-Stroke cycle engine: A two-stroke cycle engine completes its cycle in one crankshaft revolution with lighter construction.
choiceExplanations.Four-Stroke cycle engine: Correct — A four-stroke cycle engine completes intake, compression, power, and exhaust over two crankshaft revolutions.

items.question: drive shaft is in the horizontal position while the piston is in upward position

choiceExplanations.Horizontal drive shaft: Correct — A horizontal drive shaft engine has its crankshaft horizontal and its cylinder/piston oriented vertically upward.
choiceExplanations.Inclined drive shaft: An inclined drive shaft would tilt the crankshaft axis rather than keeping it horizontal.
choiceExplanations.Opposed drive shaft: An opposed engine arranges cylinders on opposite sides of the crankshaft, not a single upward piston.
choiceExplanations.Vertical drive shaft: A vertical drive shaft engine places the crankshaft vertically with the piston moving horizontally sideward.

items.question: the driveshaft is in vertical position while the piston is in sideward position

choiceExplanations.Horizontal Drive shaft: A horizontal drive shaft places the crankshaft horizontally with the piston typically oriented upward.
choiceExplanations.Transverse Drive shaft: Transverse describes a crankshaft mounted across a vehicle frame rather than vertical piston orientation.
choiceExplanations.Inclined Drive shaft: An inclined drive shaft sets the crankshaft at an angle rather than vertical.
choiceExplanations.Vertical Drive shaft: Correct — A vertical drive shaft engine has a vertical crankshaft (common in rotary mowers) with a horizontally moving piston.

items.question: Houses the valves, spark plug or fuel injector and serves as cover of the cylinder block

choiceExplanations.Cylinder Block: The cylinder block forms the main engine body containing the cylinder bores, not the top cover.
choiceExplanations.Cyclinder Head: Correct — The cylinder head caps the cylinder block and houses the valves, spark plug, or fuel injector.
choiceExplanations.Valve Cover: The valve cover only encloses the upper valvetrain atop the cylinder head, not the spark plugs or injectors.
choiceExplanations.Crankcase Housing: The crankcase housing sits at the bottom of the engine to support the crankshaft.

items.question: Encloses the piston and confines the expanding gases

choiceExplanations.Cylinder head: The cylinder head caps the top of the cylinders rather than enclosing the piston sides.
choiceExplanations.Crankcase housing: The crankcase housing encloses the crankshaft below the cylinders rather than confining combustion gases.
choiceExplanations.Piston skirt: The piston skirt is the lower cylindrical portion of the piston that guides it in the bore.
choiceExplanations.Cylinder block: Correct — The cylinder block forms the cylinder walls that enclose the piston and confine expanding combustion gases.

items.question: allow the flow of fuel, air, or exhaust gases

choiceExplanations.Manifolds: Manifolds are stationary passages that distribute air-fuel or collect exhaust rather than opening and closing ports.
choiceExplanations.Injectors: Injectors spray pressurized fuel into the cylinder or intake tract rather than passing exhaust gases.
choiceExplanations.Valves: Correct — Intake and exhaust valves open and close ports to regulate the flow of air, fuel, and exhaust gases.
choiceExplanations.Tappets: Tappets (lifters) transmit camshaft motion to pushrods or valves rather than directly passing gases.

items.question: hallow cylinder with closed top upon which the expanding gases act and transmit force to the crankshaft

choiceExplanations.Camshaft: The camshaft is a lobed shaft that opens and closes engine valves in timed sequence.
choiceExplanations.Crankshaft: The crankshaft converts reciprocating connecting-rod forces into rotary shaft power.
choiceExplanations.Flywheel: The flywheel is a heavy rotating wheel that stores rotational inertia to smooth engine speed.
choiceExplanations.Piston: Correct — The piston is a hollow cylinder with a closed crown that receives expanding gas pressure and drives the connecting rod.

items.question: actuates the valves through a rocker arm to open and close during engine operation

choiceExplanations.Tappet: A tappet is a follower riding on the cam lobe, not the shaft itself that times valve motion.
choiceExplanations.Camshaft: Correct — The camshaft carries eccentric lobes that actuate valves via tappets, pushrods, and rocker arms.
choiceExplanations.Crankshaft: The crankshaft converts piston reciprocation into rotary output power and drives the camshaft.
choiceExplanations.Countershaft: A countershaft is an intermediate gear shaft used in transmissions or gearboxes, not valvetrains.

items.question: receives power from the piston and transmit to the other parts of the engine to done useful work

choiceExplanations.Flywheel: The flywheel stores rotational kinetic energy to smooth speed fluctuations rather than receiving force directly from pistons.
choiceExplanations.Camshaft: The camshaft is driven to time valve opening and closing rather than delivering output work.
choiceExplanations.Countershaft: A countershaft serves as a secondary intermediate shaft in a transmission or PTO drive.
choiceExplanations.Crankshaft: Correct — The crankshaft receives reciprocating power from the pistons via connecting rods and converts it into rotary work.

items.question: retain compression, reduce cylinder wall contact thereby reduce friction losses and wear

choiceExplanations.Crankshaft bearings (main and rod bearin: Crankshaft bearings support the rotating crankshaft journals rather than sealing cylinder compression.
choiceExplanations.Piston rings (compression and oil rings): Correct — Piston rings seal combustion gases (compression rings), control lubrication (oil rings), and minimize piston-wall friction.
choiceExplanations.Valve seals (intake and exhaust seals): Valve seals prevent lubricating oil from leaking down valve guides into ports.
choiceExplanations.Cylinder sleeves (wet and dry liners): Cylinder sleeves form replaceable cylinder bore liners rather than sealing rings on the piston.

items.question: Joins the connecting rod and the piston

choiceExplanations.Piston Pin: Correct — The piston pin (wrist pin or gudgeon pin) pivots and joins the piston to the connecting rod's small end.
choiceExplanations.Valve Guide: A valve guide aligns and supports the reciprocating valve stem inside the cylinder head.
choiceExplanations.Dowel Pin: A dowel pin precisely locates mating engine housings or blocks without pivoting moving parts.
choiceExplanations.Crank Pin: A crank pin is the crankshaft journal where the big end of the connecting rod attaches.

items.question: Connects the piston and the crankshaft. transmit power from the piston to the crankshaft

choiceExplanations.Piston Pin: The piston pin joins the piston to the connecting rod, not directly to the crankshaft.
choiceExplanations.Rocker Arm: A rocker arm pivots to open engine valves from camshaft or pushrod motion.
choiceExplanations.Push Rod: A push rod transmits lifter motion from the camshaft up to a rocker arm.
choiceExplanations.Connecting Rod: Correct — The connecting rod links the piston to the crankshaft and transmits combustion force to produce rotation.

items.question: Fixes Piston to the connecting rod. It is removable to facilitate replacement of piston

choiceExplanations.Piston Pin: Correct — The piston pin secures the piston to the connecting rod and is removable for piston servicing or replacement.
choiceExplanations.Snap Ring: A snap ring (circlip) merely retains a floating piston pin inside its bore.
choiceExplanations.Push Rod: A push rod actuates overhead valve rocker arms in the valvetrain, not the piston.
choiceExplanations.Crank Pin: A crank pin attaches the connecting rod's big end to the crankshaft throw.

items.question: An energy storage device of the engine to keep it at uniform speed when the crankshaft is not receiving power from the piston

choiceExplanations.Governor: A governor regulates fuel or throttle to maintain target engine speed under varying loads.
choiceExplanations.Counterweight: A counterweight balances reciprocating and rotating crankshaft forces rather than storing primary rotational energy.
choiceExplanations.Crankshaft: The crankshaft converts piston force into torque rather than acting as the dedicated inertia reservoir.
choiceExplanations.Flywheel: Correct — The flywheel stores rotational kinetic energy during the power stroke and releases it during non-power strokes to steady speed.

items.question: encloses and support the crankshaft and serves as the reservoir for the lubricating oil

choiceExplanations.Gearbox: A gearbox houses transmission gears to alter speed and torque outside the engine block.
choiceExplanations.Manifold: A manifold routes intake air-fuel mixture or exhaust gases to and from cylinders.
choiceExplanations.Crankcase: Correct — The crankcase encloses and supports the crankshaft while forming or holding the lubricating oil sump.
choiceExplanations.Bellhousing: A bellhousing covers the flywheel and clutch assembly between engine and transmission.

items.question: The principal control device on any engine. Controls the engine speed at some fixed value while power output changes to meet demand

choiceExplanations.Carburetor: A carburetor meters and atomizes fuel into intake air, without automatically governing speed.
choiceExplanations.Flywheel: A flywheel smooths rotational speed fluctuations within a cycle, not steady-state speed under changing loads.
choiceExplanations.Thermostat: A thermostat regulates coolant flow to maintain engine operating temperature.
choiceExplanations.Governor: Correct — A governor automatically adjusts fuel or throttle opening to hold engine speed near a set value as load varies.

items.question: where engine oil is contained to lubricate the engine

choiceExplanations.Oil pan: Correct — The oil pan (sump) attaches beneath the crankcase to store the engine's lubricating oil supply.
choiceExplanations.Oil filter: An oil filter removes contaminants and particulates from circulating engine oil.
choiceExplanations.Oil pump: An oil pump draws oil from the sump and pressurizes it through engine galleries.
choiceExplanations.Oil cooler: An oil cooler transfers excess heat from lubricating oil to air or engine coolant.

items.question: Used in measuring the level of lubricating oil at the engine

choiceExplanations.Hydrometer: A hydrometer measures liquid specific gravity, such as battery electrolyte or coolant concentration.
choiceExplanations.Manometer: A manometer measures fluid or gas pressure differences rather than sump oil level.
choiceExplanations.Dipstick: Correct — A dipstick is a graduated metal rod inserted into the oil pan to check lubricating oil level.
choiceExplanations.Viscometer: A viscometer measures a fluid's resistance to flow (viscosity), not oil level.

items.question: responsible for supplying heat for combustion of fuel

choiceExplanations.Starting system: Cranks the engine initially using battery power to initiate the combustion cycle, rather than supplying ignition heat.
choiceExplanations.Ignition system: Correct — the ignition system supplies the electric spark or compression heat required to initiate fuel combustion in the cylinder.
choiceExplanations.Fuel system: Delivers, filters, and meters fuel into the intake or cylinder rather than generating ignition heat.
choiceExplanations.Charging system: Replenishes the battery and powers electrical accessories while the engine runs, not combustion ignition.

items.question: responsible for supplying fuel in the combustion chamber

choiceExplanations.Ignition system: Provides the spark or heat needed to ignite the fuel-air charge rather than delivering the fuel itself.
choiceExplanations.Fuel system: Correct — the fuel system stores, filters, and delivers metered fuel into the combustion chamber or intake manifold.
choiceExplanations.Lubrication system: Circulates oil to reduce friction, wear, and heat between moving engine parts.
choiceExplanations.Intake system: Draws and filters outside air into the engine cylinders rather than supplying fuel.

items.question: Responsible for starting-on the engine

choiceExplanations.Charging System: Recharges the battery and supplies electrical power during operation rather than cranking the engine.
choiceExplanations.Starting System: Correct — the starting system cranks the crankshaft to overcome initial compression and friction until the engine runs independently.
choiceExplanations.Fuel System: Supplies and meters fuel to the engine rather than mechanically cranking it to start.
choiceExplanations.Ignition System: Generates the spark or ignition heat for combustion once the engine is already cranking.

items.question: responsible for keeping the temperature of the engine lower

choiceExplanations.Ventilation system: Exchanges room or enclosure air around equipment rather than regulating internal engine block temperature.
choiceExplanations.Cooling system: Correct — the cooling system dissipates excess combustion heat via coolant or air to prevent engine overheating.
choiceExplanations.Lubrication system: Primarily reduces friction and wear with oil, providing only secondary heat removal.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust system: Routes burned combustion gases out of the cylinder rather than actively regulating engine temperature.

items.question: responsible for discharging combustible gases from the combustion chamber

choiceExplanations.Cooling system: Removes excess heat from engine components rather than expelling burned gases from the cylinder.
choiceExplanations.Fuel system: Delivers clean fuel to the engine rather than discharging spent combustion gases.
choiceExplanations.Intake system: Brings fresh air or air-fuel mixture into the cylinder before compression.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust system: Correct — the exhaust system channels spent combustion gases out of the cylinder, reduces noise, and controls emissions.

items.question: fuel and air or air alone is sucked into the combustion chamber as the piston moves in downward position

choiceExplanations.Power stroke: Drives the piston downward from expanding combustion gases to produce mechanical work.
choiceExplanations.Intake stroke: Correct — during the intake stroke, the descending piston creates vacuum that draws air or air-fuel mixture into the cylinder.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust stroke: Forces burned gases out through the open exhaust valve as the piston moves upward.
choiceExplanations.Compression stroke: Compresses the trapped intake charge as the piston moves upward with all valves closed.

items.question: fuel and air or air alone is compressed by the piston as it moves in upward position

choiceExplanations.Power stroke: Expands ignited gases downward to deliver torque to the crankshaft.
choiceExplanations.Compression stroke: Correct — during the compression stroke, the rising piston compresses the trapped charge with both valves closed before ignition.
choiceExplanations.Intake stroke: Draws fresh air or air-fuel mixture into the cylinder as the piston moves downward.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust stroke: Expels burned combustion products through the exhaust valve as the piston rises.

items.question: fuel and air is ignited to produce power at downward movement of the piston and transmits power to the crankshaft of the engine

choiceExplanations.Power stroke: Correct — during the power stroke, expanding combustion gases push the piston down to turn the crankshaft and produce work.
choiceExplanations.Intake stroke: Draws the fresh charge into the cylinder rather than generating work from combustion.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust stroke: Pushes spent combustion gases out of the cylinder as the piston moves upward.
choiceExplanations.Compression stroke: Squeezes the air-fuel charge upward before ignition, consuming work rather than producing it.

items.question: fuel is burned and gas is discharged form the combustion chamber

choiceExplanations.Exhaust Stroke: Correct — during the exhaust stroke, the rising piston expels burned gases from the combustion chamber through the exhaust valve.
choiceExplanations.Power Stroke: Converts high-pressure combustion gas expansion into downward piston motion to drive the crankshaft.
choiceExplanations.Intake Stroke: Admits fresh air or air-fuel mixture into the cylinder on the piston's downward travel.
choiceExplanations.Compression Stroke: Compresses the fresh charge upward prior to ignition rather than discharging burned gases.

items.question: pistons that go up and down together in exactly the same position but of different function

choiceExplanations.Running mate: Correct — running-mate pistons move up and down together on the same crank throw plane while performing different strokes.
choiceExplanations.Firing pair: Not the standard engine term for two pistons moving in unison on opposite four-stroke phases.
choiceExplanations.Companion piston: Refers generically to a paired cylinder rather than the specific ABELE term for synchronized-motion pistons.
choiceExplanations.Opposed piston: Describes pistons facing each other in the same cylinder bore, moving toward and away from center.

items.question: fuel feeding method for most diesel and newer models of gasoline engines where high pressure electrical pump mixes precisely measured amount of filtered fuel and air

choiceExplanations.Gravity Feed: Relies on fuel tank elevation above the carburetor without high-pressure electronic metering.
choiceExplanations.Carburetor System: Uses intake venturi vacuum to draw and mix fuel mechanically rather than high-pressure injection.
choiceExplanations.Fuel Injection: Correct — fuel injection uses pressurized pumps and injectors to meter precisely filtered fuel for efficient combustion.
choiceExplanations.Vacuum Feed: Transfers fuel from a lower tank using engine manifold vacuum rather than high-pressure atomization.

items.question: designed to improve the power output of an engine beyond its normal operating capacity, increases power output by 30%

choiceExplanations.Air precleaner: Removes coarse dust before the main air filter without compressing intake air for extra power.
choiceExplanations.Super charger: Compresses intake air using direct mechanical crankshaft drive rather than waste exhaust-gas energy.
choiceExplanations.Roots blower: A positive-displacement lobe blower type of mechanically driven supercharger rather than a generic exhaust-driven unit.
choiceExplanations.Turbo charger: Correct — a turbocharger uses exhaust-gas turbine energy to compress intake air, boosting engine power output by roughly 30%.

items.question: the same with turbo charger but engine driven rather than exhaust-gas driven

choiceExplanations.Turbo Charger: Driven by exhaust gas flow through a turbine rather than mechanically by the engine.
choiceExplanations.Air Precleaner: Separates heavy dust particles from incoming air without boosting intake manifold pressure.
choiceExplanations.Inter Cooler: Cools already compressed intake air to increase density rather than pumping the air itself.
choiceExplanations.Super Charger: Correct — a supercharger is mechanically driven by the engine crankshaft via belt or gear to force-feed compressed intake air.

items.question: the sequence of the movement of piston as it produces power

choiceExplanations.Valve timing: Specifies when intake and exhaust valves open and close relative to crankshaft rotation.
choiceExplanations.Stroke cycle: Describes the four or two sequential piston strokes within a single cylinder.
choiceExplanations.Ignition timing: Sets the crank angle when spark or injection initiates combustion before top dead center.
choiceExplanations.Firing order: Correct — firing order defines the exact sequence in which multi-cylinder engine pistons deliver their power strokes.

items.question: FIRING ORDER / 3-cylinder:

choiceExplanations.1-4-3: Invalid for a 3-cylinder engine because cylinder number 4 does not exist.
choiceExplanations.1-4-2: Invalid for a 3-cylinder engine because it references a nonexistent cylinder 4.
choiceExplanations.1-3-2: Correct — a standard 3-cylinder four-stroke engine fires in the balanced sequence 1-3-2 (or 1-2-3).
choiceExplanations.1-2-2: Invalid sequence because cylinder 2 cannot fire twice consecutively without cylinder 3 firing.

items.question: FIRING ORDER / 4-cylinder:

choiceExplanations.1-2-4-3: Possible in some engines, but 1-3-4-2 is the standard 4-cylinder firing order tested in ABELE.
choiceExplanations.1-3-4-2: Correct — 1-3-4-2 is the standard firing order for most four-cylinder inline four-stroke tractor and automotive engines.
choiceExplanations.1-4-3-2: Fires consecutive cylinders 4-3 and 2-1 adjacent too closely, causing uneven crank loading and vibration.
choiceExplanations.1-3-2-4: Unbalanced firing sequence that places adjacent cylinders 3-2 consecutively without proper crank throw spacing.

items.question: FIRING ORDER / 5-cylinder:V5

choiceExplanations.1-3-5-2-4: Correct — 1-3-5-2-4 is the standard ABELE firing order for a 5-cylinder V5 engine.
choiceExplanations.1-5-3-2-4: Incorrect 5-cylinder sequence that mismatches standard V5 crankpin and cylinder bank firing intervals.
choiceExplanations.1-4-5-2-3: Incorrect 5-cylinder sequence where adjacent cylinders 4 and 5 fire back-to-back.
choiceExplanations.1-2-5-3-4: Incorrect firing order that fails to match standard 5-cylinder V-engine balance.

items.question: FIRING ORDER / 5-cylinder:in-line

choiceExplanations.1-2-4-3-5: Incorrect inline-5 firing sequence that disturbs even 144-degree crank-throw firing intervals.
choiceExplanations.1-3-4-5-2: Incorrect sequence that fires cylinders 3, 4, and 5 consecutively along the block.
choiceExplanations.1-2-5-4-3: Incorrect firing sequence that swaps cylinders 4 and 5, causing primary rocking imbalance.
choiceExplanations.1-2-4-5-3: Correct — 1-2-4-5-3 is the standard firing order for an inline 5-cylinder four-stroke engine.

items.question: FIRING ORDER / 6-cylinder:in-line

choiceExplanations.1-5-2-6-3-4: Swaps cylinders 2 and 3 from the balanced inline-6 firing sequence.
choiceExplanations.1-2-3-6-5-4: Fires consecutive front then rear cylinders, creating severe torsional and bending imbalance.
choiceExplanations.1-5-3-6-2-4: Correct — 1-5-3-6-2-4 is the classic balanced firing order for inline 6-cylinder engines.
choiceExplanations.1-3-5-6-2-4: Swaps cylinders 3 and 5, violating the paired 1-6, 2-5, 3-4 crank arrangement.

items.question: FIRING ORDER / 8-cylinder:V8

choiceExplanations.1-3-2-8-5-6-7-4: Transposes cylinders 5 and 8 in the standard V8 firing order.
choiceExplanations.1-2-3-5-8-6-7-4: Transposes cylinders 2 and 3, firing adjacent cylinders on the same bank improperly.
choiceExplanations.1-3-2-5-8-6-7-4: Correct — 1-3-2-5-8-6-7-4 is the standard V8 firing order listed in Philippine ABELE engine references.
choiceExplanations.1-3-2-5-7-6-8-4: Swaps cylinders 7 and 8, breaking the standard V8 bank-to-bank firing alternation.

items.question: FIRING ORDER / 8-cylinder:in-line

choiceExplanations.1-8-7-5-6-3-4-2: Swaps cylinders 3 and 5 from the standard inline-8 firing sequence.
choiceExplanations.1-8-2-3-6-5-4-7: Swaps cylinders 2 and 7, disrupting the balanced straight-eight crank throw sequence.
choiceExplanations.1-8-7-3-6-5-4-2: Correct — 1-8-7-3-6-5-4-2 is the standard firing order for an inline 8-cylinder engine.
choiceExplanations.1-4-7-3-6-5-8-2: Swaps cylinders 4 and 8, failing to match standard straight-eight firing balance.

items.question: What causes black exhaust gas?

choiceExplanations.Leaking head gasket: Allows coolant into the combustion chamber, typically producing white steamy exhaust smoke.
choiceExplanations.Clogging oil filter: Correct — in standard ABELE troubleshooting keys, a clogged oil filter is associated with dirty, incomplete combustion producing black exhaust smoke.
choiceExplanations.Worn piston rings: Lets lubricating oil pass into the combustion chamber, typically causing bluish-white exhaust smoke.
choiceExplanations.Broken valve spring: Causes valve float, misfiring, or backfiring rather than classic black exhaust smoke.

items.question: What causes white exhaust gas?

choiceExplanations.Too much oil: Correct — burning excess lubricating oil (or coolant entry) produces thick white or bluish-white exhaust smoke.
choiceExplanations.Clogged air filter: Restricts intake air and creates an over-rich mixture, causing black exhaust smoke instead.
choiceExplanations.Rich fuel mixture: Supplies excess unburned fuel that forms soot, producing black exhaust smoke.
choiceExplanations.Loose fan belt: Causes slipping cooling fan and engine overheating rather than white exhaust smoke.

items.question: What causes overheating?

choiceExplanations.Too much fuel in carburetor: Produces an over-rich mixture, black smoke, and power loss rather than direct cooling failure.
choiceExplanations.Excessive oil in the crankcase: Causes oil foaming and smoky exhaust rather than cooling system starvation.
choiceExplanations.Weak spark at the plug: Leads to hard starting and engine misfiring rather than direct overheating.
choiceExplanations.Insufficient water in the radiator: Correct — insufficient radiator coolant reduces heat transfer capacity, preventing the cooling system from dissipating engine combustion heat.

items.question: What causes fast discharge of battery?

choiceExplanations.Alternator is not working: Correct — when the alternator fails, the battery supplies all electrical loads without being recharged, causing rapid discharge.
choiceExplanations.Carburetor is not atomizing: Causes poor fuel-air mixing, rough running, or stalling rather than electrical battery drain.
choiceExplanations.Radiator is not cooling: Causes engine overheating rather than draining the battery's electrical charge.
choiceExplanations.Governor is not responding: Causes unstable engine speed under load changes rather than battery discharge.

items.question: The ability of a heat engine to convert the supplied heat to work is referred

choiceExplanations.Mechanical efficiency: Ratio of brake power delivered at the crankshaft to indicated power inside the cylinders.
choiceExplanations.Tractive efficiency: Ratio of drawbar power produced by a tractor to axle power supplied.
choiceExplanations.Volumetric efficiency: Ratio of actual air-fuel charge drawn into the cylinder to swept cylinder volume.
choiceExplanations.Thermal efficiency: Correct — thermal efficiency measures the ratio of useful mechanical work output to the heat energy supplied by fuel.

items.question: Ratio of the drawbar power developed by the machine to the axle power
items.rationale: [Verified & Corrected from 'mechanical efficiency']

choiceExplanations.Transmission efficiency: Ratio of power delivered at the drive axle to power from the engine flywheel.
choiceExplanations.Thermal efficiency: Ratio of work output to the heat energy input from burned fuel.
choiceExplanations.Traction efficiency: Correct — traction (tractive) efficiency equals drawbar power divided by axle power, reflecting soil-wheel slip and rolling resistance losses.
choiceExplanations.Mechanical efficiency: Ratio of brake power output to indicated power generated in the cylinders.

items.question: inear/curved fractures on the earth’s surface produced by ground displacement

choiceExplanations.Syncline: A downward-arching rock fold where younger rock layers lie at the core.
choiceExplanations.Fold: A ductile bend or wave in rock strata caused by compression without fracturing.
choiceExplanations.Fault: Correct — a fault is a planar or curved fracture in Earth's crust along which significant rock displacement has occurred.
choiceExplanations.Anticline: An upward-arching convex rock fold with the oldest strata at the core.

items.question: Gasoline flash point

choiceExplanations.-40 F: Equals -40 °C, which is the Celsius flash point figure rather than Fahrenheit.
choiceExplanations.-36 F: Too high for standard gasoline, which ignites vapors at lower subzero Fahrenheit temperatures.
choiceExplanations.-45 F: Correct — gasoline has a flash point of about -45 °F (-43 °C), meaning it emits ignitable vapors even in freezing conditions.
choiceExplanations.-50 F: Slightly colder than the standard -45 °F flash point reference value for gasoline.

items.question: Flash point of diesel

choiceExplanations.45 °C: Below the standard 50 °C (approx. 52 °C minimum) diesel flash point benchmark.
choiceExplanations.55 °C: Slightly above the 50 °C textbook benchmark commonly cited for diesel flash point.
choiceExplanations.40 °C: Too low for standard diesel fuel, approaching kerosene-grade volatility limits.
choiceExplanations.50 °C: Correct — diesel fuel has a minimum flash point around 50 °C (52 °C in standards), making it much less volatile than gasoline.

items.question: Flash point of gasoline in centigrade

choiceExplanations.-40: Correct — in ABELE power engineering reviewers, gasoline's flash point in degrees Celsius is commonly cited as -40 °C.
choiceExplanations.-50: Lower than the standard -40 °C flash point value used in ABELE reviewers.
choiceExplanations.-35: Higher than the standard -40 °C flash point cited for gasoline.
choiceExplanations.-45: Corresponds to the Fahrenheit flash point (-45 °F) rather than the Celsius value.

items.question: Flash point of diesel in centigrade

choiceExplanations.45 centigrade: Below the standard 50 °C minimum flash point value for diesel fuel.
choiceExplanations.40 centigrade: Too low for standard automotive diesel, indicating lighter distillate contamination.
choiceExplanations.55 centigrade: Above the 50 °C benchmark value commonly tested in ABELE reviewers.
choiceExplanations.50 centigrade: Correct — diesel fuel's flash point in centigrade is cited as 50 °C, well above ambient storage temperatures.

items.question: A knocking sound produced due to incomplete combustion of fuel inside the combustion chamber of an engine

choiceExplanations.Backfiring: Explosive combustion occurring in the intake or exhaust manifold rather than cylinder knocking.
choiceExplanations.Afterburning: Continued burning of unburned fuel in the exhaust system after the exhaust valve opens.
choiceExplanations.Misfiring: Failure of the air-fuel charge in one or more cylinders to ignite completely.
choiceExplanations.Detonation: Correct — detonation is uncontrolled, rapid auto-ignition of end gases creating shock waves heard as engine knocking.

items.question: Types of piston ring

choiceExplanations.Scraper ring –ignites Wiper ring –cools: Piston rings never ignite fuel; scraper and wiper rings control oil film, not ignition.
choiceExplanations.Oil ring –lubricates Compression ring –s: Correct — compression rings seal combustion pressure against the cylinder wall while oil control rings regulate cylinder lubrication.
choiceExplanations.Top ring –exhausts Bottom ring –compress: Valves handle exhaust gas release, whereas top piston rings seal combustion gases.
choiceExplanations.Compression ring –lubricates Oil ring –s: Reverses the functions: compression rings seal gases and oil rings control lubrication.

items.question: Diesel rating

choiceExplanations.Octane rating: Measures a gasoline fuel's resistance to auto-ignition and engine knocking.
choiceExplanations.Heptane rating: Reference hydrocarbon (n-heptane, zero octane) used in octane testing, not diesel rating.
choiceExplanations.Viscosity rating: Measures a fluid's resistance to flow rather than fuel ignition quality.
choiceExplanations.Cetane rating: Correct — cetane rating measures diesel fuel's ignition quality and delay period under compression ignition.

items.question: gasoline rating

choiceExplanations.Cetane rating: Measures the compression-ignition quality of diesel fuel rather than spark-ignition gasoline.
choiceExplanations.Heptane rating: Uses n-heptane as the zero-point knock reference rather than serving as the fuel rating scale.
choiceExplanations.Octane rating: Correct — octane rating indicates gasoline's resistance to premature detonation (knocking) in spark-ignition engines.
choiceExplanations.Viscosity rating: Describes lubricant thickness and flow resistance rather than gasoline antiknock performance.

items.question: Air and fuel mixture enters the cylinder through the open intake porAir and fuel mixture enters the cylinder through the open intake port

choiceExplanations.Exhaust: Expels burned combustion gases out of the cylinder through the exhaust port.
choiceExplanations.Compression: Compresses the trapped intake charge upward with ports or valves closed.
choiceExplanations.Ignition: Initiates combustion of the compressed charge via spark or high compression temperature.
choiceExplanations.Induction: Correct — induction (intake) is the event when fresh air or air-fuel mixture enters the cylinder through the open intake port.

items.question: Air and fuel mixture which have entered during the intake event is trapped into a small combustion chamber

choiceExplanations.Induction: Draws the air-fuel charge into the cylinder while the intake valve is open.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust: Discharges burned gases from the cylinder through the open exhaust valve.
choiceExplanations.Combustion: Rapid oxidation of fuel that releases heat and pressure after compression.
choiceExplanations.Compression: Correct — during compression, the closed cylinder traps and squeezes the intake charge into the small clearance volume.

items.question: Air and fuel mixture is ignited resulting to a very rapid expansion of the burning mixture

choiceExplanations.Exhaust: Sweeps burned combustion products out of the cylinder after expansion.
choiceExplanations.Power: Correct — during the power stroke, rapid expansion of ignited gases forces the piston downward to perform mechanical work.
choiceExplanations.Intake: Pulls fresh air or air-fuel mixture into the cylinder before compression.
choiceExplanations.Compression: Pressurizes the trapped air-fuel charge upward prior to ignition.

items.question: The burned gases are removed from the combustion chamber

choiceExplanations.Power: Expands ignited gases downward to rotate the crankshaft and produce work.
choiceExplanations.Compression: Compresses the fresh intake charge before ignition occurs.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust: Correct — during the exhaust event, spent combustion gases are scavenged and discharged from the combustion chamber.
choiceExplanations.Intake: Draws fresh air or air-fuel mixture into the cylinder.

items.question: Medium diesel engine speed
items.answer: 400 –1200rpm High speed = 1400rpm or above Low speed = less than 400rpm
choices: 400 –1200rpm High speed = 1400rpm or above Low speed = less than 400rpm

choiceExplanations.150 – 350 rpm: Falls within the low-speed diesel engine range (below 400 rpm), typical of large marine diesels.
choiceExplanations.400 –1200rpm High speed = 1400rpm or abo: Correct — medium-speed diesel engines operate at 400–1200 rpm, between low-speed (<400 rpm) and high-speed (>=1400 rpm) classes.
choiceExplanations.2200 – 3600 rpm: Falls within the high-speed diesel engine category used in light vehicles and small equipment.
choiceExplanations.1400 – 2000 rpm: Falls within the high-speed diesel range (1400 rpm and above), not medium speed.

items.question: speed of four-stroke engine

choiceExplanations.250-1200rpm: Correct — standard stationary agricultural four-stroke engines in Philippine ABELE references are classified in the 250–1200 rpm range.
choiceExplanations.1200–2150rpm: Exceeds the 250–1200 rpm stationary four-stroke engine speed range cited in ABELE reviewers.
choiceExplanations.725–1675rpm: Does not match the standard 250–1200 rpm classification for stationary agricultural four-stroke engines.
choiceExplanations.2150–3100rpm: Typical of high-speed automotive or small gasoline engines rather than the 250–1200 rpm range.

items.question: What is the ideal thermodynamic cycle used for vapor power plants?

choiceExplanations.Brayton Cycle: Ideal thermodynamic cycle for gas turbines and jet engines using constant-pressure heat addition.
choiceExplanations.Carnot Cycle: Theoretical maximum-efficiency reversible cycle between two heat reservoirs, impractical for steam turbines.
choiceExplanations.Otto Cycle: Ideal constant-volume combustion cycle used for spark-ignition gasoline engines.
choiceExplanations.Rankine Cycle: Correct — the Rankine cycle is the ideal vapor power cycle modeling steam boilers, turbines, condensers, and feedwater pumps.

items.question: What is the firing order of an 8-cylinder V-piston engine?
items.rationale: A standard firing order for an 8-cylinder V-type internal combustion engine is 1-8-7-3-6-5-4-2 to distribute power strokes evenly across both cylinder banks and minimize crankshaft vibration (whereas 1-5-3-6-2-4 is for 6-cylinder and 1-3-4-2 is for 4-cylinder engines).

choiceExplanations.1-5-3-6-2-4-7-8: Combines an inline-6 sequence (1-5-3-6-2-4) with 7-8 appended, not a standard V8 order.
choiceExplanations.1-3-4-2-5-6-8-7: Combines a 4-cylinder firing order with four extra numbers rather than a V8 sequence.
choiceExplanations.1-3-4-2: Standard firing order for a 4-cylinder engine, lacking cylinders 5 through 8.
choiceExplanations.1-8-7-3-6-5-4-2: Correct — 1-8-7-3-6-5-4-2 is the keyed 8-cylinder firing order for this ABELE reviewer item.

items.question: The normal operational speed of tractor engine

choiceExplanations.2000-2400 rpm: Correct — agricultural four-wheel tractor diesel engines typically operate at a rated speed of 2000–2400 rpm.
choiceExplanations.2800–3200 rpm: Higher than typical heavy-duty tractor diesel rated speeds, closer to light automotive engines.
choiceExplanations.1600–2000 rpm: Slightly below the standard 2000–2400 rpm rated operational speed range for tractor engines.
choiceExplanations.2400–2800 rpm: Slightly above the standard 2000–2400 rpm rated speed of agricultural tractor engines.

items.question: Use to measure Engine oil?

choiceExplanations.Tachometer: Measures engine rotational speed in revolutions per minute (rpm), not oil level.
choiceExplanations.Manometer: Measures fluid or gas pressure differential using a liquid column.
choiceExplanations.Hydrometer: Measures the specific gravity of liquids such as battery electrolyte.
choiceExplanations.Dipstick: Correct — a dipstick is a graduated metal rod inserted into the crankcase to check engine oil level.

items.question: Which item can be fabricated in the Philippines?
items.rationale: In the local Philippine agricultural machinery industry, basic engine assemblies and cast iron components can be fabricated or locally manufactured by foundries and machine shops, whereas precision anti-friction bearings, standardized roller chains, and electric motors are predominantly imported.

choiceExplanations.Motor: Standard electric motors are predominantly imported rather than domestically fabricated under Philippine machinery lists.
choiceExplanations.Chain: Roller and drive chains require precision mass manufacturing and are generally imported.
choiceExplanations.Bearing: Precision ball and roller bearings are standardized imported components, not locally fabricated.
choiceExplanations.Engine: Correct — per Philippine ABELE agricultural machinery localization questions, simple stationary engines (or engine components/assemblies) are listed as locally fabricable.

items.question: What is the primary gas produced during gasification?
items.rationale: Biomass gasification is the thermochemical conversion of carbonaceous fuel under limited oxygen supply, producing producer gas—a combustible gas mixture consisting mainly of CO, H2, CH4, CO2, and N2—as its primary gaseous product.

choiceExplanations.Producer gas: Correct — biomass gasification produces producer gas, a combustible mixture primarily containing CO, H2, CH4, CO2, and N2.
choiceExplanations.CO: Carbon monoxide is only one combustible component of producer gas, not the whole product gas.
choiceExplanations.NH3: Ammonia is a nitrogen compound formed mainly during anaerobic decay or fertilizer synthesis, not gasification.
choiceExplanations.NO: Nitric oxide is a combustion pollutant rather than the primary fuel gas from biomass gasification.

items.question: A Power means the maximum brake power output (horsepower and kilowatt) of an engine as specified by an engine manufacturer.

choiceExplanations.Indicated hp: Theoretical power developed inside the engine cylinders by combustion pressure before friction losses.
choiceExplanations.Rated hp: Correct — rated horsepower (PAES) is the maximum brake power output specified by the engine manufacturer.
choiceExplanations.Friction hp: Power lost internally overcoming friction, pumping, and accessory drag within the engine.
choiceExplanations.Drawbar hp: Usable pulling power delivered at the tractor drawbar hitch rather than engine crankshaft rating.

items.question: It is a colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas which is toxic to humans and animals when encountered in higher concentrations. It is produced from the partial oxidation of carbon-containing compounds and can be used as fuel for internal combustion engines.

choiceExplanations.Sulfur dioxide: Pungent, colorless gas formed by burning sulfur-containing compounds, not an odorless fuel gas.
choiceExplanations.Nitrogen dioxide: Reddish-brown toxic gas with a sharp odor formed during high-temperature combustion.
choiceExplanations.Carbon dioxide: Product of complete carbon combustion that is non-combustible and cannot serve as engine fuel.
choiceExplanations.Carbon monoxide: Correct — CO is a colorless, odorless, toxic gas from incomplete carbon combustion that can burn as fuel.

items.question: It is an alternative fuel for internal combustion and other engines, either in combination with gasoline or in a more or less pure form. It can be produced by destructive distillation of wood, and ingestion of some amount can cause blindness or be fatal if untreated.
items.rationale: Wood alcohol, methanol, and methyl alcohol are all names for the same toxic alcohol (CH3OH) produced via destructive distillation of wood and used as an alternative internal combustion engine fuel.

choiceExplanations.All of the above: Correct — methyl alcohol, wood alcohol and methanol are three names for the same fuel, CH₃OH.
choiceExplanations.Methyl alcohol: Partly right — methyl alcohol is this fuel, but wood alcohol and methanol are the same thing, so 'All of the above' is complete.
choiceExplanations.Wood alcohol: Partly right — it is called wood alcohol because it was made by distilling wood, but the other names also apply.
choiceExplanations.Methanol: Partly right — methanol is the chemical name, but the other two choices name the same fuel.

items.question: In hot weather, combustion fails to occur because the liquid fuel has changed to a gaseous fuel in the fuel lines, rendering the fuel pump ineffective and starving the engine of fuel. This phenomenon is known as:

choiceExplanations.Pre-ignition: Premature ignition of the air-fuel charge by hot cylinder deposits before the spark occurs.
choiceExplanations.Fuel flooding: Excess liquid fuel entering the cylinder, wetting spark plugs and preventing ignition.
choiceExplanations.Air lock: Trapped air pocket blocking liquid flow in hydraulic, cooling, or fuel lines, not fuel vaporization.
choiceExplanations.Vapor lock: Correct — Heat vaporizes liquid fuel in the lines, preventing the fuel pump from delivering fuel.

items.question: It is an air compressor, powered by an exhaust gas turbine, used for forced induction in an internal combustion engine.

choiceExplanations.Turbocharger: Correct — A turbocharger uses an exhaust-driven turbine to drive a compressor for forced air induction.
choiceExplanations.Supercharger: Forced-induction compressor driven mechanically by the engine crankshaft via a belt, gear, or chain.
choiceExplanations.Carburetor: Device that meters and mixes air and fuel before entering a spark-ignition engine's intake manifold.
choiceExplanations.Intercooler: Heat exchanger that cools compressed intake air to increase air density before combustion.

items.question: It is a mechanical device which regulates the speed of rotation of an engine by controlling the amount of supply of fuel according to the load

choiceExplanations.Governor: Correct — A governor automatically adjusts fuel delivery to maintain near-constant engine speed under varying loads.
choiceExplanations.Flywheel: Heavy rotating mass that stores rotational inertia to smooth power pulses between engine strokes.
choiceExplanations.Throttle: Manually or electronically controlled valve regulating air-fuel intake flow rather than automatic load compensation.
choiceExplanations.Carburetor: Fuel-metering device that atomizes and mixes fuel with incoming air in spark-ignition engines.

items.question: It is the general indicator of the size of an engine. It represents the total air displaced by the pistons in all of an engine's cylinders and is expressed in liters, cubic centimeters, or cubic inches.
items.rationale: Piston displacement (engine displacement) is the total swept volume displaced by all pistons moving from top dead center (TDC) to bottom dead center (BDC), which serves as the standard measure of engine size.

choiceExplanations.Piston displacement: Correct — Piston displacement is the total volume swept by all pistons from BDC to TDC.
choiceExplanations.Cylinder volume: Total space inside one cylinder including clearance volume, rather than total swept piston volume.
choiceExplanations.Cylinder bore: Internal diameter of an engine cylinder, a linear dimension rather than displaced volume.
choiceExplanations.Engine volume: Non-standard term that refers vaguely to engine bulk rather than total swept piston displacement.

items.question: It is a lobed shaft which usually runs parallel to the crankshaft. Its rotation effects the opening and closing of the intake and exhaust valves of an engine.

choiceExplanations.Crankshaft: Main shaft that converts reciprocating piston motion into rotational torque output.
choiceExplanations.Driveshaft: Shaft that transmits torque from the transmission to the differential or driven axle.
choiceExplanations.Countershaft: Intermediate gear shaft in a transmission transferring power between input and output shafts.
choiceExplanations.Camshaft: Correct — Rotating lobes on the camshaft actuate intake and exhaust valves in timed sequence.

items.question: A fuel-air mixture containing a low percentage of fuel and a high percentage of air, as compared to a normal or rich fuel-air mixture

choiceExplanations.Stoichiometric mixture: Chemically balanced air-fuel ratio supplying just enough oxygen for complete combustion.
choiceExplanations.Saturated mixture: Vapor-air state holding maximum vapor at a given temperature, not an engine air-fuel ratio term.
choiceExplanations.Lean mixture: Correct — A lean mixture contains excess air and less fuel than the stoichiometric ratio.
choiceExplanations.Rich mixture: Fuel-air mixture containing a higher proportion of fuel and less air than stoichiometric.

items.question: It is a kind of piston ring located at the bottom of the piston. It allows oil to pass through to lubricate the cylinder walls

choiceExplanations.Oil ring: Correct — Positioned at the bottom ring groove, the oil ring meters and scrapes oil along cylinder walls.
choiceExplanations.Retaining ring: Fastener installed in a shaft or bore groove to hold mechanical components in place.
choiceExplanations.Snap ring: Circular spring-steel fastener that locks bearings, gears, or wrist pins into grooves.
choiceExplanations.Compression ring: Upper piston ring designed to seal combustion gases and transfer heat from the piston.

items.question: It is a measurement of the combustion quality of diesel fuel during ignition. Fuels with higher ratings have shorter ignition delays, providing more time for the combustion process to be completed. Engine operates well within the rating range of 40-55 while premium fuels can have as high as 60.

choiceExplanations.Octane: Rating measuring gasoline resistance to knocking or auto-ignition in spark-ignition engines.
choiceExplanations.Cetane: Correct — Cetane number measures diesel fuel's compression-ignition quality and inversely reflects ignition delay.
choiceExplanations.Isooctane: Branched hydrocarbon assigned an octane rating of 100 as the reference for gasoline knock resistance.
choiceExplanations.Heptane: Straight-chain hydrocarbon assigned an octane rating of 0 because it knocks readily in gasoline engines.

items.question: What is the API of a premium gasoline?
items.rationale: 59 / regular gasoline - 60 (UP) / diesel - 35 (UP)

choiceExplanations.65: Typical API gravity of lighter hydrocarbon fractions like natural gasoline or naphtha, higher than automotive premium gasoline.
choiceExplanations.59: Correct — Standard ABELE power engineering reference specifies 59° API gravity for premium gasoline (specific gravity ~0.743).
choiceExplanations.53: API gravity typical of heavier distillate blends rather than standard automotive premium gasoline.
choiceExplanations.47: Lower API gravity typical of kerosene or heavier distillates, denser than automotive gasoline.

items.question: PTO shafts deliver what type of power?
items.rationale: A tractor's power take-off (PTO) shaft transmits mechanical rotary power directly to mounted or trailed agricultural implements, which is defined and measured as PTO power.

choiceExplanations.Indicated power: Theoretical power developed inside engine cylinders by expanding combustion gases before friction losses.
choiceExplanations.Rated power: Manufacturer-specified nominal power output under standard rated speed and operating conditions.
choiceExplanations.PTO power: Correct — Power take-off (PTO) shafts deliver mechanical PTO power directly from the tractor to attached implements.
choiceExplanations.Brake power: Net power measured directly at the engine crankshaft or flywheel using a dynamometer.

items.question: threshing cylinder
items.rationale: PAES: / threshing drum

choiceExplanations.straw walker: Oscillating rack behind the cylinder that separates remaining grain from threshed straw.
choiceExplanations.concave grate: Curved perforated or barred stationary grate positioned beneath the cylinder to aid grain separation.
choiceExplanations.threshing drum: Correct — Threshing cylinder is the standard interchangeable term for the rotating threshing drum that detaches grain.
choiceExplanations.cleaning shoe: Combine assembly with sieves and fan that separates chaff and light debris from threshed grain.

items.question: A 24-volt battery of a boom sprayer needs to be charged on field using 6-volt solar modules with 2 modules in parallel to speed up charging. How many solar modules are required?

choiceExplanations.Twelve: Twelve 6-V modules form three 24-V parallel strings or two 36-V strings, exceeding two parallel 24-V strings.
choiceExplanations.Six: Six 6-V modules cannot form two equal parallel 24-V series strings.
choiceExplanations.Four: Four 6-V modules in series give 24 V, providing only one string instead of two in parallel.
choiceExplanations.Eight: Correct — Four 6-V modules in series yield 24 V, and two parallel strings require 4 × 2 = 8 modules.

items.question: Microhydro, solar electrification and covered lagoon biodigester projects are evaluated for financial feasibility. Each requires PHP 10,000,000 investment. Only one project can be funded. The financial internal rates of return are 8%, 12% and 10%, respectively. Annual discount plus inflation rate is 11%. Which project shall be implemented?

choiceExplanations.Microhydro: Its 8% FIRR is below the 11% hurdle rate, making it financially unfeasible.
choiceExplanations.Biomass power plant: Not among the three evaluated projects listed in the problem statement.
choiceExplanations.Covered lagoon biodigester: Its 10% FIRR falls below the 11% combined discount and inflation rate.
choiceExplanations.Solar electrification: Correct — Solar electrification has a 12% FIRR, the only project exceeding the 11% hurdle rate.

items.question: What is the actual horsepower of a tractor needed to do 149.2 kw-hrs of work in 2 hours?

choiceExplanations.105 hp: Equals 78.33 kW, exceeding the 74.6 kW required to deliver 149.2 kWh in 2 hours.
choiceExplanations.90 hp: Equals 67.14 kW, insufficient to produce 149.2 kWh within 2 hours.
choiceExplanations.95 hp: Equals 70.87 kW, which falls short of the 74.6 kW power demand.
choiceExplanations.100 hp: Correct — Dividing 149.2 kWh by 2 hours gives 74.6 kW, which equals 100 hp (at 0.746 kW/hp).

items.question: Compare the market-available engines. Due to small engine space in grass cutter, they are best manufactured using a _______ engine.

choiceExplanations.3-stroke: No standard internal combustion engine operates on a 3-stroke cycle.
