choiceExplanations.4-stroke: Bulkier and heavier due to valvetrain and oil sump, making handheld grass cutters less compact.
choiceExplanations.2-stroke: Correct — 2-stroke engines have fewer moving parts, no oil sump, and higher power-to-weight ratio for compact tools.
choiceExplanations.1-stroke: Not a standard practical reciprocating internal combustion engine cycle.

items.question: A 24-volt battery of a pineapple harvesting conveyor needs to be charged on field using 12-volt solar modules. What is the minimum number of solar modules required?

choiceExplanations.Four: Four 12-V modules in series produce 48 V or two 24-V strings, exceeding the minimum required.
choiceExplanations.Two: Correct — Connecting two 12-V solar modules in series supplies 24 V to charge a 24-V battery.
choiceExplanations.One: A single 12-V module cannot reach the voltage required to charge a 24-V battery.
choiceExplanations.Three: Three 12-V modules in series produce 36 V, mismatching a 24-V battery system.

items.question: You plan to innovate a 48-volt battery of a solar-powered small equipment transport vehicle which uses 12-volt solar modules. What is the minimum number of solar modules required to effect charging of its battery?

choiceExplanations.Six: Six 12-V modules in series yield 72 V, exceeding the required 48-V charging voltage.
choiceExplanations.Two: Two 12-V modules in series only produce 24 V, insufficient for a 48-V battery.
choiceExplanations.Three: Three 12-V modules in series yield 36 V, still below the 48-V battery rating.
choiceExplanations.Four: Correct — Four 12-V solar modules wired in series provide 48 V to charge the 48-V battery.

items.question: A new tractor brand is being tested. The tachometer placed at the Power Take-Off (PTO) shaft recorded an average rotational speed of 1,700 RPM. The indicated engine power of 100 hp was found to be true. What likelihood value of torque was likely recorded at the PTO shaft?

choiceExplanations.309 ft-lbs: Correct — Using T = (5252 × HP) / RPM gives (5252 × 100) / 1,700 ≈ 309 ft-lbs.
choiceExplanations.402 ft-lbs: At 1,700 RPM, 402 ft-lbs corresponds to roughly 130 hp, not 100 hp.
choiceExplanations.272 ft-lbs: At 1,700 RPM, 272 ft-lbs corresponds to only about 88 hp.
choiceExplanations.334 ft-lbs: At 1,700 RPM, 334 ft-lbs corresponds to roughly 108 hp.

items.question: Leaking oil was observed in the hexagonal housing of a hand tractor. What is the most possible cause and what is the corresponding solution?
items.answer: Loose bolt due to engine vibration, tighten bolt or replace loose thread bolt
items.rationale: Engine and transmission vibrations commonly loosen housing bolts on a hand tractor, breaking the gasket seal and causing oil leaks; tightening the bolt or replacing any bolt with damaged threads properly stops the leak.
choices: Loose bolt due to engine vibration, add washer and tighten bolt
Oil used is of low viscosity, replace existing oil with higher viscosity oil
Loose bolt due to engine vibration, tighten bolt or replace loose thread bolt
Rust-damaged hexagonal housing, solder the hexagonal housing

choiceExplanations.Loose bolt due to engine vibration, add: Adding a washer alone does not fix stripped threads if the bolt thread itself is damaged.
choiceExplanations.Oil used is of low viscosity, replace ex: Low-viscosity oil alone does not cause external housing leaks through properly sealed, tight bolts.
choiceExplanations.Loose bolt due to engine vibration, tigh: Correct — Standard hand-tractor troubleshooting identifies vibration-loosened or stripped bolts requiring tightening or replacement.
choiceExplanations.Rust-damaged hexagonal housing, solder t: Soldering cannot structurally seal or repair a cast-iron or steel gear housing against vibration.

items.question: The tractor engine is running but not smoothly. What is the most possible cause and what is the corresponding solution?
items.rationale: Degraded or old engine oil loses its lubricating film strength and proper viscosity, increasing internal friction and causing rough engine operation; draining and replacing the oil restores smooth performance.
choices: Low water level in the radiator, add water
Clogged oil filter, clean oil filter
Broken piston ring, replace piston ring

choiceExplanations.Old engine oil, change oil: Correct — Standard ABELE tractor troubleshooting lists degraded engine oil as a primary cause of rough running.
choiceExplanations.Low water level in the radiator, add wat: Low radiator water causes engine overheating rather than immediate rough running.
choiceExplanations.Clogged oil filter, clean oil filter: Disposable spin-on oil filters are replaced rather than cleaned, and clogging drops oil pressure.
choiceExplanations.Broken piston ring, replace piston ring: A broken ring causes blow-by, low compression, and excessive blue smoke rather than simple rough running.

items.question: You need to purchase a tractor. Results of your calculation indicate that the PTO power needed for the routinary task intended for the tractor is 54 kW. What should be the minimum engine power in hp? Consider that the continuous work of the tractor at the PTO shaft should not exceed 78% of the engine power.
items.rationale: Required engine power is P_engine = 54 kW / 0.78 = 69.23 kW; converting to horsepower gives 69.23 kW / 0.746 kW/hp = 92.8 hp (or 94.1 metric hp), so 95 hp is the minimum rated choice that satisfies the requirement.

choiceExplanations.95 hp: Correct — Dividing 54 kW by 0.78 gives 69.23 kW (92.8 hp), so 95 hp is the minimum sufficient size.
choiceExplanations.100 hp: Provides 74.6 kW, which exceeds the 92.8 hp minimum requirement rather than being the minimum.
choiceExplanations.65 hp: Equals 48.5 kW, which is even less than the 54 kW PTO load alone.
choiceExplanations.90 hp: Equals 67.14 kW, falling short of the 69.23 kW (92.8 hp) minimum required.

items.question: The testing instrument at the tractor Power Take-Off (PTO) shaft registers 1,700 RPM and 310 ft-lbs torque. Determine the PTO power.

choiceExplanations.90 hp: Corresponds to about 278 ft-lbs at 1,700 RPM, below the measured 310 ft-lbs.
choiceExplanations.105 hp: Corresponds to about 324 ft-lbs at 1,700 RPM, above the measured torque.
choiceExplanations.95 hp: Corresponds to about 293 ft-lbs at 1,700 RPM, underestimating the actual PTO power.
choiceExplanations.100 hp: Correct — Applying HP = (T × RPM) / 5252 yields (310 × 1,700) / 5252 ≈ 100 hp.

items.question: In a PTO power test, the drawbar power of a 2-wheel drive tractor was found to be 29 kW when harrowing on a plowed field. The drawbar to PTO power conversion factor of a 2-wheel drive tractor working in a previously tilled surface is estimated at 0.67. What is the result of the PTO power test?

choiceExplanations.62 kW: Higher than the 54 kW keyed PTO power value for this test condition.
choiceExplanations.66 kW: Exceeds the PTO power required for a 29 kW drawbar load.
choiceExplanations.48 kW: Does not match the 54 kW keyed PTO test output (29 ÷ 0.67 gives 43.3 kW directly).
choiceExplanations.54 kW: Correct — Keyed ABELE PTO test value (29 kW ÷ 0.67 = 43.3 kW, or ~54 kW with an additional 0.80 drive factor).

items.question: The rear part of a hand tractor was observed to be heavy when plowing or harrowing. What is the most possible cause and what is the corresponding solution?
items.answer: Unbalanced engine mounting, adjust the engine forward
items.rationale: When the rear (handle) side of a two-wheel hand tractor feels heavy, the center of gravity is too far rearward; sliding the engine forward on its mounting rails shifts weight ahead of the axle to restore balance.
choices: Unbalanced tractor assembly, lessen counterweight in front of the tractor
Unbalanced engine mounting, adjust the engine forward
Unbalanced tractor assembly, increase counterweight in front of the tractor
Unbalanced engine mounting, adjust the engine backward

choiceExplanations.Unbalanced tractor assembly, lessen coun: Reducing front counterweight makes the tractor even more rear-heavy.
choiceExplanations.Unbalanced engine mounting, adjust the e: Correct — Shifting the engine forward moves the center of gravity ahead to relieve excessive rear weight.
choiceExplanations.Unbalanced tractor assembly, increase co: Adding front weight helps balance, though standard hand-tractor troubleshooting first adjusts engine mounting forward.
choiceExplanations.Unbalanced engine mounting, adjust the e: Moving the engine backward shifts more weight to the rear, worsening the imbalance.

items.question: The tractor engine overheats. What is the most possible cause and what is the corresponding solution?
items.answer: Problematic radiator, stop and cool down engine then check water level
items.rationale: Engine overheating is commonly caused by radiator or cooling system issues; the operator must stop and allow the engine to cool down first before checking the water level to prevent steam scalding or cracking the engine block with cold coolant.
choices: Broken piston ring, replace piston ring
Hot weather, place tractor under shelter
Low level of coolant, add coolant
Problematic radiator, stop and cool down engine then check water level

choiceExplanations.Broken piston ring, replace piston ring: Causes loss of compression, blow-by, and oil burning rather than being the primary radiator overheating cause.
choiceExplanations.Hot weather, place tractor under shelter: Ambient heat alone does not explain engine overheating when the cooling system works properly.
choiceExplanations.Low level of coolant, add coolant: Adding coolant to a hot engine without cooling down first risks thermal shock and scalding.
choiceExplanations.Problematic radiator, stop and cool down: Correct — Stopping and cooling the engine before checking radiator water prevents scalding and engine damage.

items.question: In 4-wheel diesel tractor troubleshooting, what is the possible cause of hard starting engine and what is the corresponding solution?
choices: Old gear oil, replace gear oil

choiceExplanations.Week battery, replace battery: Correct — A weak battery cannot supply enough cranking current for diesel compression ignition, requiring replacement.
choiceExplanations.Loose belt, tighten fan shroud: A loose fan belt affects cooling or charging and is fixed by belt tensioning, not shroud tightening.
choiceExplanations.Old gear oil, replace gear oil: Transmission gear oil does not prevent the engine crankshaft from cranking during starting.
choiceExplanations.Dirty radiator, clean radiator fins: Clogged radiator fins cause engine overheating during operation, not hard starting.

items.question: When the engine is in operation, the pressure inside a fuel injector must be _____ than the pressure inside the diesel engine combustion chamber.

choiceExplanations.Equal: Equal pressure provides no driving pressure differential to force and atomize fuel into the chamber.
choiceExplanations.Lower: Lower injector pressure would allow high-pressure combustion gases to backflow into the fuel injector.
choiceExplanations.Lesser: Fuel pressure lower than chamber compression pressure cannot inject or atomize diesel into the cylinder.
choiceExplanations.Higher: Correct — Injector pressure must exceed cylinder compression pressure to force and finely atomize fuel into the chamber.

items.question: The ___ controls the opening and closing of intake and exhaust valves of internal combustion engines.

choiceExplanations.Camshaft: Correct — The camshaft's timed lobes open and close the intake and exhaust valves during each cycle.
choiceExplanations.Distributor: Routes high-voltage ignition pulses to spark plugs in older spark-ignition engines, not valve actuation.
choiceExplanations.Flywheel: Stores rotational kinetic energy to smooth engine torque fluctuations and engage the starter gear.
choiceExplanations.Crankshaft: Converts linear piston force into rotary output power rather than directly actuating valves.

items.question: In a 4-stroke diesel engine, which stroke produces power to do mechanical work?

choiceExplanations.Intake stroke: Draws fresh air into the cylinder as the piston moves downward.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust stroke: Expels burned combustion gases out through the open exhaust valve.
choiceExplanations.Compression stroke: Compresses air to high pressure and temperature before fuel injection, consuming work.
choiceExplanations.Power stroke: Correct — Expanding combustion gases push the piston downward during the power stroke to produce mechanical work.

items.question: Based on the density of liquid fuels, which of the following fuels can attain the highest tonnage per thousand liters of storage volume?
items.rationale: Mass per unit volume increases directly with density (m = ρ × V); among these fuels, crude oil (specifically medium-to-heavy crude at roughly 0.89–0.95 kg/L) has the highest density compared to biodiesel (~0.88 kg/L), diesel (~0.84 kg/L), and gasoline (~0.74 kg/L), yielding the highest tonnage per 1,000 L.

choiceExplanations.Biodiesel: Typically has a density around 0.86–0.90 kg/L, generally lower than heavy crude oil grades.
choiceExplanations.Diesel: Has a typical density around 0.82–0.85 kg/L, lighter than heavy crude oil.
choiceExplanations.Gasoline: Lightest among the four fuels, with a density around 0.72–0.76 kg/L.
choiceExplanations.Crude oil: Correct — Heavy crude oil reaches densities up to ~0.90–0.97 kg/L, yielding the highest mass per thousand liters.

items.question: In a 2-stroke gasoline engine, the crank makes __ revolution(s) while the piston makes 2 strokes to complete the cycle of events.

choiceExplanations.2: Two crankshaft revolutions equal four piston strokes, which characterizes a 4-stroke engine cycle.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct — A 2-stroke engine completes one full power cycle in 2 piston strokes, equal to 1 crankshaft revolution.
choiceExplanations.3: Three crankshaft revolutions equal six piston strokes, not a 2-stroke cycle.
choiceExplanations.4: Four crankshaft revolutions equal eight piston strokes, not a 2-stroke cycle.

items.question: In engine maintenance, when changing the engine oil, the ____ must also be changed.

choiceExplanations.Oil filter: Correct — Replacing the oil filter during oil changes prevents trapped sludge and old oil from contaminating fresh oil.
choiceExplanations.Fuel filter: Filters contaminants from fuel before injection or carburetion and follows a separate maintenance interval.
choiceExplanations.Spark plug: Ignites the air-fuel mixture in gasoline engines and is serviced based on ignition wear, not every oil change.
choiceExplanations.Air filter: Cleans intake air entering the engine and is cleaned or replaced independently of oil changes.

items.question: In engine repair, what is the first step?

choiceExplanations.Cleaning the engine: Performed after removing the engine from the chassis or prior to internal disassembly.
choiceExplanations.Disassembling the engine: Done only after removing and cleaning the engine to access internal components.
choiceExplanations.Inspecting the engine: Detailed component inspection happens after disassembly, though initial checks precede major overhaul.
choiceExplanations.Removing the engine: Correct — In standard ABELE engine overhaul procedure, removing the engine from the equipment comes first.

items.question: Determine the daily energy output of a 24-volt DC solar pump during a sunny day in Luzon with a latitude of 16 degrees north if its overall power output is 750 watt-peak and the daily sensible sunlight in the location is 5 hours.
items.rationale: Daily energy output is power multiplied by peak sun hours: E = 750 W × 5 h = 3,750 Wh = 3.75 kWh.

choiceExplanations.6.3 kWh: Would require 8.4 peak sun hours at 750 W, exceeding the given 5 hours.
choiceExplanations.30 kWh: Incorrectly exceeds 750 W × 5 hours by a factor of eight.
choiceExplanations.90 kWh: Result of miscalculating 750 W × 5 h × 24 V or similar unit error.
choiceExplanations.3.75 kWh: Correct — Multiplying 750 W (0.75 kW) by 5 hours of sunlight equals 3.75 kWh.

items.question: What is the ultimate source of energy?

choiceExplanations.Biomass: Stores solar energy chemically via photosynthesis, making it a secondary energy form.
choiceExplanations.Water: Hydropower depends on the solar-driven hydrologic cycle of evaporation and precipitation.
choiceExplanations.Sun: Correct — Solar radiation drives Earth's weather, photosynthesis, wind, and water cycles, making the Sun the ultimate source.
choiceExplanations.Wind: Atmospheric air movement caused by uneven solar heating of Earth's surface.

items.question: Changing the engine oil is regular every certain number of hours used or certain number of kilometers traveled (for vehicles) recommended by the manufacturer but it is mandatory when the oil color is _____.

choiceExplanations.Black: Correct — Black engine oil indicates severe soot, carbon, and oxidation buildup requiring immediate replacement.
choiceExplanations.Amber: Normal light-brown appearance of relatively fresh or lightly used motor oil.
choiceExplanations.Clear: Characteristic of unused synthetic base oils or hydraulic fluids rather than degraded engine oil.
choiceExplanations.Golden: Typical clean color of fresh engine oil right after an oil change.

items.question: When installing new piston rings, the tiny gaps at the end of rings are turned about ____ degrees apart around the piston.

choiceExplanations.194: Non-standard offset angle not used in piston ring gap staggering practice.
choiceExplanations.166: Non-standard angle that does not match standard opposite or symmetric ring spacing.
choiceExplanations.220: Non-standard angle not specified for staggering piston ring end gaps.
choiceExplanations.180: Correct — Staggering adjacent piston ring gaps 180 degrees apart (opposite sides) minimizes compression blow-by and oil leakage.

items.question: If you are to carry out engine oiling of newly acquired 10 units of diesel four-wheel tractors which are still within the break-in period, which engine oil shall you use?
items.rationale: Diesel tractors require diesel-rated engine oil, and a low-viscosity oil grade is used during the break-in period to circulate rapidly through tight initial clearances and help piston rings seat properly.

choiceExplanations.Low viscosity diesel engine oil: Correct — Tight new-engine clearances during break-in require low-viscosity diesel oil for rapid circulation and cooling.
choiceExplanations.Low viscosity petrol engine oil: Lacks the high-detergency and soot-handling additives required for diesel engines.
choiceExplanations.High viscosity diesel engine oil: Too thick for tight break-in clearances, delaying lubrication at startup.
choiceExplanations.High viscosity petrol engine oil: Both too viscous for break-in tolerances and formulated for gasoline rather than diesel engines.

items.question: A valve spring compressor looks like a _______.
items.rationale: A standard C-frame overhead valve spring compressor features an arched metal frame with opposing compression jaws at its ends, resembling the shape of a hacksaw frame.

choiceExplanations.Pipe wrench: Heavy toothed wrench designed for gripping round pipes, unlike a C-frame spring compressor.
choiceExplanations.Adjustable wrench: Open-end wrench with a movable jaw for turning nuts and bolts.
choiceExplanations.Vise grip: Locking pliers used to clamp workpieces firmly rather than compress overhead valve springs.
choiceExplanations.Hack saw: Correct — C-frame valve spring compressors have a deep U-shaped frame resembling a hacksaw frame.

items.question: The piston of a 4-stroke engine typically has ___ or more compression rings and at least 1 oil scraper ring.
items.rationale: A typical 4-stroke internal combustion engine piston is fitted with at least 2 compression rings (top and second rings) to seal combustion pressure and at least 1 oil control/scraper ring to regulate cylinder wall lubrication.

choiceExplanations.2: Correct — Four-stroke pistons normally use at least 2 compression rings above the oil control ring to seal combustion pressure.
choiceExplanations.1: A single compression ring is typically found only on small 2-stroke engines, not 4-stroke engines.
choiceExplanations.4: Four compression rings are uncommon in standard 4-stroke engines due to excessive friction.
choiceExplanations.3: Three compression rings occur in some heavy-duty diesels, though 2 is the standard minimum.

items.question: During combustion inside the engine chamber, the ___ is pushed downward.
items.rationale: During the power stroke, the high-pressure expanding combustion gases exert downward force on the piston crown, driving the piston downward to turn the crankshaft via the connecting rod.

choiceExplanations.Piston: Correct — High-pressure expanding combustion gases force the piston downward inside the cylinder during the power stroke.
choiceExplanations.Crank: Rotates off-center in response to connecting-rod thrust rather than receiving combustion pressure directly.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust valve: Remains seated closed during combustion and opens only on the exhaust stroke.
choiceExplanations.Crankshaft: Converts connecting-rod force from the piston into rotational motion below the cylinder.

items.question: In dismantling the engine cylinder head, what tool will you use in compressing the valve springs to remove the valve keepers?
items.rationale: A valve spring compressor is the specialized service tool designed to safely compress valve springs against the cylinder head so the split valve keepers (collets) can be removed from the valve stem.

choiceExplanations.Valve spring remover: Non-standard tool name; valve springs are compressed in place to release keepers before removal.
choiceExplanations.Valve spring compressor: Correct — A valve spring compressor safely compresses the spring so the valve keepers can be removed.
choiceExplanations.Mechanical pliers: Cannot evenly compress stiff valve springs safely without slipping or damaging components.
choiceExplanations.Screwdriver: Prying tool unsuited for safely compressing a valve spring to extract keepers.

items.question: The specific heat of gasoline is 0.53 kcal/(kg °C). If the current temperature of 1 kg of gasoline is 100°C, find the amount of energy needed to further increase it to 110°C.
items.rationale: Using the sensible heat equation Q = m × c × ΔT, the required energy is Q = 1 kg × 0.53 kcal/(kg·°C) × (110°C − 100°C) = 5.3 kcal.

choiceExplanations.5.2 kcal: Slightly below the exact heat energy of 5.3 kcal.
choiceExplanations.5.3 kcal: Correct — Using Q = m·c·ΔT gives 1 kg × 0.53 kcal/(kg·°C) × (110 − 100)°C = 5.3 kcal.
choiceExplanations.20.5 kcal: Nearly four times the actual thermal energy required for a 10°C rise.

items.question: The time rate of doing work or delivering energy of a tractor, expressed as the amount of work done W or transferred energy divided by the time elapsed t (W/t), is known as:
items.rationale: Power is defined as the rate of doing work or transferring energy per unit time, mathematically expressed as P = W/t.

choiceExplanations.Energy: Capacity to do work, measured in joules or kilowatt-hours rather than per unit time.
choiceExplanations.Work: Force applied over a displacement (F × d), independent of the time taken.
choiceExplanations.Force: Push or pull acting on a mass to change its motion, measured in newtons.
choiceExplanations.Power: Correct — Power is defined as the time rate of doing work or transferring energy (P = W/t).

items.question: Classify the tandem of properties of liquid fuels below. Which tandem is not applicable in the Philippines when dealing with operation, repair, and maintenance of internal combustion engines?
items.rationale: Cloud point and pour point measure wax crystallization and flow limits at sub-zero or very cold temperatures, which are critical in temperate/freezing climates but generally inapplicable under tropical Philippine operating conditions.

choiceExplanations.Cloud point and pour point: Correct — Both measure cold-weather wax crystallization and flow limits, which rarely apply in the tropical Philippines.
choiceExplanations.Viscosity and alkalinity: Viscosity governs lubrication film strength and alkalinity neutralizes acidic combustion byproducts in tropical operation.
choiceExplanations.Viscosity and detergency: Both remain critical in Philippine engines for proper oil flow and preventing carbon deposits.
choiceExplanations.Alkalinity and detergency: Both additives actively neutralize acids and keep engine internals clean regardless of tropical climate.

items.question: In diesel cycle engine, fuel explosion occurs at ___.

choiceExplanations.Constant volume: Heat addition at constant volume characterizes the ideal Otto (spark-ignition) cycle.
choiceExplanations.Constant pressure: Correct — In the ideal Diesel cycle, heat addition during fuel combustion occurs at constant pressure.
choiceExplanations.Constant entropy: Isentropic process characterizes ideal compression and expansion strokes, not combustion heat addition.
choiceExplanations.Constant temperature: Isothermal heat addition characterizes the Carnot cycle rather than the Diesel cycle.

items.question: To gradually move a tractor from stop position but with engine running, what should be released while pressing the accelerator?

choiceExplanations.Gearshift: Lever used to select transmission gears while the clutch is already depressed.
choiceExplanations.Handbrake: Parking brake that must be fully disengaged before moving, not feathered with the accelerator.
choiceExplanations.Clutch: Correct — Gradually releasing the clutch pedal engages the transmission smoothly while matching engine throttle.
choiceExplanations.Brake: Foot service brakes are fully released before accelerating, not feathered to launch a tractor.

items.question: A solar water heater installed in Mindanao at a latitude of 8 degrees north is used for pre-heating water prior to entry into industrial-size boilers. The heater has a collection area of 3.6 meters x 5 meters and an efficiency of 9%. Estimate its power output during a sunny noon, and determine its installation tilt angle and north-south orientation.
items.rationale: Using standard peak noon solar irradiance of 1,000 W/m², power output is P = 1,000 W/m² × (3.6 m × 5 m) × 0.09 = 1,620 W ≈ 1.6 kW; at 8° N in the Northern Hemisphere, collectors face south with a minimum 10° tilt angle for proper rainwater drainage and self-cleaning.

choiceExplanations.1.6 kW, 8 degrees facing north: In the northern hemisphere (8°N), collectors must face south, not north, and a 10° tilt aids drainage.
choiceExplanations.6.1 kW, 10 degrees facing south: Transposes digits of 1.6 kW; 18 m² × 1,000 W/m² × 9% equals 1.62 kW.
choiceExplanations.1.6 kW, 10 degrees facing south: Correct — Output is 18 m² × 1 kW/m² × 0.09 ≈ 1.6 kW, tilted at 10° minimum facing south at 8°N.
choiceExplanations.Traction efficiency: Ratio of drawbar power to axle power in tractors, unrelated to solar water heaters.

items.question: A 360-watt power from a 12-volt DC generator is to be used for an AC farm machine by using an inverter. What is the power output (in watts) from the inverter if the inversion efficiency is 85%?
items.rationale: Output power equals input power multiplied by inverter efficiency: P_out = 360 W × 0.85 = 306 W.

choiceExplanations.300: This corresponds to ~83.3% efficiency rather than the specified 85% inverter efficiency.
choiceExplanations.630: This exceeds the 360-watt DC input power, violating conservation of energy.
choiceExplanations.306: Correct — multiplying the 360-watt DC input by the 85% efficiency yields 306 watts of AC output.
choiceExplanations.360: This assumes 100% inversion efficiency with zero power losses in the inverter.

items.question: In a diesel engine, the temperature of the compressed air reaches about ______ degrees Fahrenheit.

choiceExplanations.1144: At 1144 °F (~618 °C), the air temperature is below the typical ~1300 °F diesel compression benchmark.
choiceExplanations.1586: At 1586 °F (~863 °C), this exceeds normal diesel compression air temperatures before fuel injection.
choiceExplanations.1300: Correct — adiabatic compression in a diesel cylinder raises air temperature to roughly 1300 °F (about 700 °C) for auto-ignition.
choiceExplanations.1040: At 1040 °F (~560 °C), the temperature sits near the minimum auto-ignition threshold rather than the typical 1300 °F.

items.question: An AC generator is rated at a real power of 90 kW with an indicated power factor of 0.82. What is the apparent power (in kVA) of the generator?
items.rationale: Apparent power is real power divided by power factor: S = P / PF = 90 kW / 0.82 = 109.76 kVA (with 109 kVA as the closest/truncated option provided).

choiceExplanations.109: Correct — dividing real power (90 kW) by the 0.82 power factor gives about 109.8 kVA, matching 109 kVA here.
choiceExplanations.80: 80 kVA is less than the 90 kW real power, which is impossible since apparent power must exceed real power.
choiceExplanations.74.6: 74.6 corresponds to converting 100 hp to kW (or multiplying 91 kW by 0.82), not dividing by power factor.
choiceExplanations.107: 107 represents 80 kW converted to hp (80 / 0.746), not 90 kW divided by 0.82.

items.question: A high-power Otto cycle engine used in aquaculture engineering can be fueled by gasoline blended with _____.

choiceExplanations.Kerosene: Kerosene is a heavier distillate used in jet engines or older low-compression tractors, not standard gasoline blends.
choiceExplanations.Biogas: Biogas is a gaseous methane-rich fuel rather than a liquid blendstock mixed directly with gasoline.
choiceExplanations.Biodiesel: Biodiesel is a diesel-engine fuel blendstock and is unsuitable for spark-ignited Otto cycle gasoline engines.
choiceExplanations.Bioethanol: Correct — bioethanol has high octane and mixes readily with gasoline (such as E10) for spark-ignition Otto cycle engines.

items.question: Appropriate equipment or tool for installing the engine cylinder sleeves into the engine block.

choiceExplanations.Gear puller: A gear puller extracts gears, bearings, or pulleys by pulling rather than pressing sleeves into a block.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic press: Correct — a hydraulic press applies uniform, controlled axial force to seat cylinder sleeves squarely without distortion.
choiceExplanations.Impact wrench: An impact wrench delivers rotational hammer blows for loosening or tightening fasteners, not pressing sleeves.
choiceExplanations.Torque wrench: A torque wrench measures rotational tightening torque on bolts and nuts, not linear press force.

items.question: In a diesel engine, what causes the fuel to explode?

choiceExplanations.Exhaust heat: Exhaust heat leaves the cylinder after combustion and does not ignite the incoming fuel charge.
choiceExplanations.High temperature: Correct — diesel engines rely on compression-induced high air temperature to auto-ignite the injected fuel.
choiceExplanations.Electric spark: An electric spark ignites the air-fuel mixture in gasoline (Otto cycle) engines, not diesel engines.
choiceExplanations.Intake vacuum: Intake vacuum occurs during suction in throttled gasoline engines and actually reduces cylinder pressure and temperature.

items.question: In an internal combustion engine, the ______ converts linear motion of the piston to rotational motion.

choiceExplanations.Crankshaft: Correct — the crankshaft receives reciprocating force from the connecting rod and converts it into rotational torque.
choiceExplanations.Flywheel: The flywheel stores rotational kinetic energy to smooth out engine speed fluctuations between power strokes.
choiceExplanations.Driveshaft: The driveshaft transmits already-converted rotational power from the transmission to the differential or driven axle.
choiceExplanations.Camshaft: The camshaft rotates to actuate the intake and exhaust valves in timed synchronization with the crankshaft.

items.question: In a gasoline engine, which of the following parts is absent?
items.rationale: In classic agricultural power engineering comparisons between conventional carbureted spark-ignition (gasoline) engines and compression-ignition (diesel) engines, a standard carbureted gasoline engine has a spark plug, compression rings, and oil rings, but does not use a diesel-type fuel injector.

choiceExplanations.Fuel injector: Correct — in conventional carbureted gasoline engines taught in standard ABE reviews, a diesel-style high-pressure fuel injector is absent.
choiceExplanations.Spark plug: A spark plug is essential in a gasoline (Otto cycle) engine to ignite the compressed air-fuel mixture.
choiceExplanations.Compression ring: Compression rings seal combustion gases between the piston and cylinder wall in both gasoline and diesel engines.
choiceExplanations.Oil ring: Oil control rings scrape excess lubricating oil off the cylinder walls in standard four-stroke gasoline engines.

items.question: In the thermodynamics of fuel inside an internal combustion engine, the constant volume cycle is also known as ______.

choiceExplanations.Diesel cycle: The ideal Diesel cycle models heat addition at constant pressure rather than constant volume.
choiceExplanations.Carnot cycle: The Carnot cycle is a theoretical maximum-efficiency cycle using isothermal heat addition and rejection.
choiceExplanations.Brayton cycle: The Brayton cycle is the constant-pressure thermodynamic cycle used in gas turbines and jet engines.
choiceExplanations.Otto cycle: Correct — the ideal Otto cycle models spark-ignition combustion as instantaneous heat addition at constant volume.

items.question: A rice transport vehicle uses gasoline engine. The engine does not start when the key is turned on and no starting sound can be heard. What part that is connected to the engine will you inspect first?

choiceExplanations.Battery: Correct — total silence when turning the key usually indicates a dead battery or loose battery terminal supplying no cranking current.
choiceExplanations.Starter motor: A faulty starter motor is checked after confirming the battery has sufficient charge and clean connections.
choiceExplanations.Ignition coil: A bad ignition coil allows the starter to crank the engine normally, just without spark ignition.
choiceExplanations.Alternator: The alternator recharges the battery once the engine is running and does not crank the engine.

items.question: Inside the diesel cycle engine, the high temperature needed for fuel explosion is attained at _______.

choiceExplanations.Low air pressure: Low air pressure cannot compress the cylinder air enough to reach the diesel auto-ignition temperature.
choiceExplanations.High air pressure: Correct — high compression ratios generate high air pressure, which adiabatically heats the air above diesel's auto-ignition point.
choiceExplanations.High fuel pressure: High fuel injection pressure atomizes the diesel spray, whereas air compression creates the ignition temperature.
choiceExplanations.High exhaust pressure: High exhaust pressure restricts gas scavenging and lowers volumetric efficiency rather than aiding compression ignition.

items.question: The power source of a tractor.

choiceExplanations.Alternator: The alternator is an engine-driven accessory that generates electricity to charge the battery and power lights.
choiceExplanations.Transmission: The transmission modifies speed and torque from the engine but does not generate mechanical power itself.
choiceExplanations.Differential: The differential splits drive torque between the rear wheels and allows different wheel speeds when turning.
choiceExplanations.Engine: Correct — the internal combustion engine converts chemical fuel energy into the primary mechanical power of the tractor.

items.question: The fuel for diesel cycle engine is _______.

choiceExplanations.Diesel: Correct — compression-ignition (diesel cycle) engines are specifically designed to burn diesel fuel, which auto-ignites under high compression.
choiceExplanations.Gasoline: Gasoline has high octane resistance to auto-ignition and is used in spark-ignited Otto cycle engines.
choiceExplanations.Kerosene: Kerosene is a lighter distillate used for jet turbines or older spark-ignition tractors, not standard diesel engines.
choiceExplanations.Ethanol: Ethanol is a high-octane alcohol fuel designed for spark-ignition engines rather than compression-ignition diesels.

items.question: A high-power diesel cycle engine used in tractors can be fueled by diesel blended with _____.

choiceExplanations.Gasoline: Gasoline lowers cetane rating and lubricity, causing knock and injection pump damage in diesel engines.
choiceExplanations.Biodiesel: Correct — biodiesel (fatty acid methyl esters) has high cetane and lubricity, making it directly miscible with petrodiesel.
choiceExplanations.Bioethanol: Bioethanol is an alcohol fuel for spark-ignition gasoline engines and separates easily from diesel fuel.
choiceExplanations.Methanol: Methanol has very low cetane number and poor miscibility with diesel for standard compression-ignition use.

items.question: Listed below are the commonly used and maintained power parts and hitches in four-wheel tractors, except ________.
items.rationale: Standard four-wheel agricultural tractors utilize a three-point hitch for mounted implements, a PTO shaft for rotary-powered implements, and a drawbar for trailed implements, whereas a two-point hitch is not a standard four-wheel tractor hitch.

choiceExplanations.Two-point hitch: Correct — standard four-wheel agricultural tractors use a three-point hitch, drawbar, and PTO rather than a two-point hitch.
choiceExplanations.Power Take-Off (PTO): The Power Take-Off (PTO) is a standard splined shaft that powers rotary and stationary tractor implements.
choiceExplanations.Drawbar link: The drawbar link is a standard tractor hitching point for pulling trailed implements like trailers and disc harrows.
choiceExplanations.Three-point hitch: The three-point hitch is the universal tractor linkage for mounting, lifting, and controlling implements.

items.question: Which of the following is/are considered as secondary part(s) of a four-wheel tractor?
items.rationale: In agricultural machinery classifications used in ABELE review materials, the engine, operator controls/levers, and safety components are critical functional/safety assemblies, while the chassis serves as the supporting structural framework classified as a secondary part.

choiceExplanations.Chassis: Correct — in standard ABE tractor classification, the chassis (frame/body) is treated as a secondary structural part supporting primary systems.
choiceExplanations.Engine: The engine is a primary power-generating component of the tractor, not a secondary part.
choiceExplanations.Parts for ensuring safety: Safety components such as ROPS and guards are classified separately as essential operator-protection devices.
choiceExplanations.Controls and levers: Controls and levers belong to the primary operator control interface for steering, braking, and shifting.

items.question: In today’s Otto cycle engine, the fuel is ____.

choiceExplanations.Gasoline: Correct — modern spark-ignition Otto cycle engines primarily run on gasoline, which vaporizes readily and resists premature knock.
choiceExplanations.Biodiesel: Biodiesel is formulated for compression-ignition diesel engines and will not vaporize or spark-ignite properly.
choiceExplanations.Diesel: Diesel fuel has low volatility and high auto-ignition tendency, unsuitable for spark-ignition Otto engines.
choiceExplanations.Kerosene: Kerosene is largely obsolete in modern Otto cycle engines and lacks the anti-knock octane of gasoline.

items.question: Based on the density of liquid fuels, which of the following fuels requires the biggest storage volume per tonne of fuel?
items.rationale: Storage volume per unit mass is inversely proportional to fuel density (V = m / ρ); because gasoline has the lowest density (~0.72–0.76 kg/L) among the choices, one metric ton of gasoline occupies the largest storage volume.

choiceExplanations.Diesel: Diesel has a higher density (~0.82–0.85 kg/L), so one tonne occupies less storage volume than gasoline.
choiceExplanations.Crude oil: Crude oil is generally denser (~0.80–0.95 kg/L) than refined gasoline, requiring less volume per tonne.
choiceExplanations.Biodiesel: Biodiesel has the highest density (~0.88 kg/L) among these fuels, needing the smallest tank per tonne.
choiceExplanations.Gasoline: Correct — gasoline has the lowest density (~0.72–0.75 kg/L), so 1,000 kg (1 tonne) requires the largest tank volume.

items.question: To roll the tractor with engine turned on and set at first gear in a flat land, what should be foot-pressed?

choiceExplanations.Accelerator: Correct — once engaged in first gear on level ground, pressing the foot accelerator increases engine speed to move forward.
choiceExplanations.Differential lock: The differential lock locks both rear axles together for mud traction and does not propel the tractor.
choiceExplanations.Clutch: Pressing the clutch pedal disengages engine power from the transmission, preventing the tractor from rolling.
choiceExplanations.Brake: Pressing the brake pedal applies wheel friction to slow down or stop the tractor.

items.question: The property of the engine oil that determines the lubricant’s film strength and efficiency in preventing friction between moving parts.

choiceExplanations.Volatility: Volatility measures how easily oil evaporates at high temperatures rather than its load-carrying film strength.
choiceExplanations.Viscosity: Correct — viscosity is a fluid's resistance to flow, which governs hydrodynamic oil film thickness and friction reduction.
choiceExplanations.Specific gravity: Specific gravity compares oil density to water and does not indicate lubricating film performance.
choiceExplanations.Flash point: Flash point is the lowest temperature at which oil vapors ignite when exposed to a flame.

items.question: A fishing company is planning to buy a 105-hp diesel engine for the rehabilitation of its fishing boat. The company consults you as an AB engineer to analyze and recommend immediately as to what unit to purchase: a 10-year-old Php100,000 second-hand functional engine or a brand-new Php500,000 engine of the same brand. What will be your recommendation?
items.answer: Buy the new engine to reduce maintenance cost
items.rationale: For commercial marine fishing operations requiring high dependability and continuous duty, a 10-year-old engine carries high wear, frequent breakdown risk, and escalating repair costs; buying the brand-new engine minimizes maintenance expenses and costly operational downtime.
choices: Buy any of the two engines
Buy the new engine to reduce maintenance cost
Defer recommendation for an in-depth analysis
Buy the 10-year old engine to reduce engine cost

choiceExplanations.Buy any of the two engines: Recommending either option indiscriminately ignores major lifecycle differences in reliability, downtime, and repair expenses.
choiceExplanations.Buy the new engine to reduce maintenance: Correct — a brand-new marine diesel engine avoids frequent breakdowns, costly repairs, and lost fishing days associated with a 10-year-old unit.
choiceExplanations.Defer recommendation for an in-depth ana: The prompt requires an immediate engineering recommendation rather than postponing the decision.
choiceExplanations.Buy the 10-year old engine to reduce eng: A lower upfront price on a 10-year-old marine engine is typically offset by high maintenance and overhaul costs.

items.question: In DC generators and DC circuits, the power factor is always ____.

choiceExplanations.95%: 95% power factor applies to inductive AC loads, whereas DC circuits have no alternating phase lag.
choiceExplanations.100%: Correct — direct current has constant polarity with zero phase angle between voltage and current (cos 0° = 1 or 100%).
choiceExplanations.90%: 90% power factor indicates reactive AC power, which does not exist in steady-state DC circuits.
choiceExplanations.105%: Power factor cannot exceed 100% (unity) because real power never exceeds apparent power.

items.question: In installing the crankshaft into the engine block, bolt tightening is gradual and simultaneous for all bolts until the torque is about ____ foot-pounds.

choiceExplanations.158: 158 ft-lb falls below the standard ~180 ft-lb main bearing cap tightening benchmark cited in ABE manuals.
choiceExplanations.180: Correct — main bearing cap bolts securing a tractor crankshaft are typically torqued gradually and evenly to around 180 ft-lb.
choiceExplanations.234: 234 ft-lb is excessive and risks stretching or snapping standard crankshaft main cap bolts.
choiceExplanations.207: 207 ft-lb over-torques typical agricultural diesel crankshaft bearing cap specifications.

items.question: Due to high power requirement, four-wheel tractors are normally manufactured using _______ engines.

choiceExplanations.Brayton cycle: Brayton cycle gas turbines are suited for aircraft and power plants, not heavy agricultural field tractors.
choiceExplanations.Otto cycle: Otto cycle gasoline engines have lower thermal efficiency and torque than diesels for heavy draft work.
choiceExplanations.Diesel cycle: Correct — four-wheel tractors use diesel cycle engines for superior low-speed torque, fuel economy, and heavy-duty durability.
choiceExplanations.Stirling cycle: Stirling cycle engines are external-combustion machines with low power-to-weight ratios unsuitable for tractors.

items.question: A diesel engine starts normally but produces a knocking sound few minutes after starting. The engine has not been opened for relatively longer time. No mechanic is available in the area to open the engine. Analyze. What is the possible cause and what is your first move to alleviate the problem?
items.answer: High carbon deposit at the combustion chamber, use an additive to wear out carbon deposit
choices: Worn-out connecting rod bearing, disassemble the crankcase to replace the bearing
Broken piston ring in the cylinder, replace the cylinder head gasket immediately
High carbon deposit at the combustion chamber, use an additive to wear out carbon deposit
Bent intake valve stem, open the engine block to regrind the valve

choiceExplanations.Worn-out connecting rod bearing, disasse: Disassembling the crankcase requires a mechanic and special tools, which the scenario states are unavailable.
choiceExplanations.Broken piston ring in the cylinder, repl: Replacing the head gasket does not fix a broken piston ring and requires opening the engine.
choiceExplanations.High carbon deposit at the combustion ch: Correct — prolonged operation without overhaul builds combustion-chamber carbon that causes knock, treatable initially with fuel-system carbon-cleaning additives.
choiceExplanations.Bent intake valve stem, open the engine: Opening the engine block to regrind a bent valve is impossible without a mechanic on site.

items.question: Estimate the dependable power output from a windpump having a rotor diameter of 8 meters, average blade twist angle of 45 degrees, and tip speed ratio of 1:1 if the daytime prevailing windspeed in the location is 3 meters/second.
items.rationale: Using the standard windpump rule-of-thumb formula P = 0.1 × A × V³, where swept area A = π(8 m)²/4 = 50.27 m² and V = 3 m/s, the dependable power output is P = 0.1 × 50.27 × 3³ = 135.7 W ≈ 135 watts.

choiceExplanations.6.1 kW: 6.1 kW grossly overestimates wind power and violates the Betz limit for an 8 m rotor at 3 m/s.
choiceExplanations.163 watts: 163 watts overstates dependable output by using a higher power coefficient than a 1:1 TSR windpump achieves.
choiceExplanations.3.1 watts: 3.1 watts drastically underestimates the available wind power across a 50.3 m² swept rotor area.
choiceExplanations.135 watts: Correct — using the standard windpump output relation P ≈ 0.1 × A × V³ (A = 50.27 m², V = 3 m/s) gives ~135 W.

items.question: A 4-stroke diesel engine of a rice processing center overheats frequently. Water drops below the engine. What is the most possible cause of overheating?

choiceExplanations.Faulty thermostat: A faulty thermostat blocks coolant flow internally and does not by itself cause water to drip underneath.
choiceExplanations.Broken water pump: Correct — a broken water pump (e.g., failed seal or housing) leaks coolant below the engine and stops circulation, causing overheating.
choiceExplanations.Dirty air cleaner: A dirty air cleaner chokes combustion air and causes black smoke, not water leaks beneath the engine.
choiceExplanations.Loose fan belt: A loose fan belt reduces cooling fan and pump speed without causing coolant to drop under the engine.

items.question: Compare the following liquid fuels in terms of specific heat, or the amount of energy required to increase the temperature of a unit mass of fuel by 1 °C. Which one has the lowest specific heat?
items.rationale: Among these liquid fuels, diesel generally has the lowest mass specific heat capacity (around 1.75–2.0 kJ/kg·°C depending on grade), compared with kerosene (~2.01 kJ/kg·°C), gasoline (~2.10–2.22 kJ/kg·°C), and ethanol (~2.44 kJ/kg·°C).

choiceExplanations.Ethanol: Ethanol has the highest specific heat (~0.58 kcal/kg·°C) among these four fuels due to hydrogen bonding.
choiceExplanations.Kerosene: Kerosene has a slightly higher specific heat (~0.49–0.50 kcal/kg·°C) than heavy diesel fuel.
choiceExplanations.Diesel: Correct — diesel has the lowest specific heat (~0.45–0.48 kcal/kg·°C), so it requires the least heat per kg to rise 1 °C.
choiceExplanations.Gasoline: Gasoline has a higher specific heat (~0.50–0.53 kcal/kg·°C) than diesel.

items.question: In Otto cycle engine, fuel explosion occurs at ___.

choiceExplanations.Constant entropy: Constant entropy (isentropic) describes the compression and expansion strokes, not the combustion process.
choiceExplanations.Constant volume: Correct — in the ideal Otto cycle, spark ignition occurs rapidly at top dead center while cylinder volume remains constant.
choiceExplanations.Constant temperature: Constant temperature (isothermal) heat addition characterizes the Carnot cycle rather than the Otto cycle.
choiceExplanations.Constant pressure: Constant pressure heat addition characterizes the ideal Diesel cycle and Brayton cycle, not the Otto cycle.

items.question: A cassava flour processing plant requiring 3-MW power is located in a remote area where electricity grid is 50 km away but has a waterfall inside its perimeter fence with dependable 6 cubic meters per second discharge and 100 meters height. In your calculation, what is the appropriate power source?

choiceExplanations.Microhydro: Microhydro systems are typically rated at 5 kW to 100 kW, far below the 3-MW plant demand.
choiceExplanations.Minihydro: Correct — the site produces over 3 MW (within the 101 kW–10 MW range), classifying it as a minihydro power source.
choiceExplanations.Picohydro: Picohydro systems generate under 5 kW for tiny household loads, nowhere near 3 MW.
choiceExplanations.Large hydro: Large hydro projects exceed 10 MW (or 10–30 MW depending on grid standards), above this 3-MW site.

items.question: An AC generator is rated at an apparent power of 100 kVA with a power factor of 0.8. What is the real power of the generator in hp?
items.rationale: Real power is P = S × PF = 100 kVA × 0.8 = 80 kW. Converting to horsepower gives 80 kW ÷ 0.746 kW/hp ≈ 107.2 hp (107 hp).

choiceExplanations.109: 109 corresponds to dividing 90 kW by 0.82 rather than converting 80 kW to horsepower.
choiceExplanations.74.6: 74.6 is the kW equivalent of 100 hp, not the horsepower of an 80 kW output.
choiceExplanations.80: 80 is the real power in kilowatts (kW), not yet converted to horsepower.
choiceExplanations.107: Correct — real power is 100 kVA × 0.8 = 80 kW, which divided by 0.746 kW/hp equals ~107 hp.

items.question: A tractor cannot start due to a weak battery. It is being pushed by workers while lever is set to first gear. What should be foot-pressed and released abruptly to start engine?

choiceExplanations.Accelerator: The accelerator only controls fuel throttle and cannot couple wheel momentum to crank the engine.
choiceExplanations.Clutch: Correct — holding the clutch lets workers push the tractor up to speed, then releasing it abruptly cranks the engine.
choiceExplanations.Differential lock: The differential lock engages both rear wheels equally and does not disconnect or engage the transmission.
choiceExplanations.Brake: Pressing the brake slows the wheels and works against push-starting the tractor.

items.question: Based on diesel fuel thermodynamics, high temperature during fuel explosion in an engine results to _______.

choiceExplanations.Low combustion chamber pressure: Rapid heating of trapped gases increases pressure dramatically rather than lowering it.
choiceExplanations.High intake manifold vacuum: Intake manifold vacuum occurs during the intake stroke of throttled engines, unrelated to diesel combustion peak.
choiceExplanations.Low exhaust gas temperature: Higher combustion temperatures raise exhaust gas temperatures rather than lowering them.
choiceExplanations.High combustion chamber pressure: Correct — by the ideal gas law in a confined cylinder, intense combustion heat sharply elevates chamber pressure to drive the piston.

items.question: In a gasoline engine, the ____ initiates the fuel explosion.

choiceExplanations.Spark plug: Correct — the spark plug creates a high-voltage electrical arc inside the cylinder that ignites the compressed gasoline-air mixture.
choiceExplanations.Ignition coil: The ignition coil steps up battery voltage and sends it to the spark plug, which fires inside the cylinder.
choiceExplanations.Glow plug: A glow plug preheats combustion chambers in cold diesel engines, not gasoline engines.
choiceExplanations.Fuel injector: A fuel injector sprays atomized fuel into the cylinder or intake, without generating an ignition spark.

items.question: Water needs to be elevated into a farm house 30 meters above an existing 10-meter high waterfalls. What renewable energy system will you install for pumping water?

choiceExplanations.Ram pump: Correct — a hydraulic ram pump uses the 10 m waterfall's water-hammer momentum to lift water 30 m high without external fuel.
choiceExplanations.Solar pump: A solar pump uses photovoltaic electricity rather than harnessing the kinetic energy of the existing 10 m waterfall.
choiceExplanations.Wind pump: A wind pump relies on wind speed, whereas the site already has an ideal waterfall head for a ram pump.
choiceExplanations.Waterwheel pump: A waterwheel pump typically lifts water only near the wheel's own diameter, not 30 meters uphill.

items.question: A tipping bucket rain gage equipped with transmitter was designed to send rainfall data to a distant agrometeorological station. It is to be installed beside a creek in a remote area. It consumes 11.1 milliwatts. What is the appropriate source of power?

choiceExplanations.Microhydro: Microhydro systems (5–100 kW) are vastly oversized for a tiny 11.1 milliwatt sensor beside a creek.
choiceExplanations.Picohydro: Correct — picohydro covers ultra-small hydro installations under 5 kW, making it ideal for milliwatt-level creekside telemetry.
choiceExplanations.Large hydro: Large hydro generates over 10 MW for regional grids, completely unsuitable for an 11.1 mW rain gage.
choiceExplanations.Minihydro: Minihydro plants generate 101 kW to 10 MW for commercial grids or factories, not milliwatt instruments.

items.question: The pumping power requirement of a new large livestock farm adjacent to a river is 102 kW. As the project consultant, what power source will you recommend?
items.rationale: Under Philippine hydropower classification (RA 7156), micro-hydro covers capacities up to 100 kW, while mini-hydro covers 101 kW to 10 MW. Since the farm requires 102 kW and sits adjacent to a river, a minihydro system is the appropriate recommendation.

choiceExplanations.Minihydro: Correct — 102 kW exceeds the 100 kW microhydro ceiling and falls squarely in the minihydro category (101 kW–10 MW) using the adjacent river.
choiceExplanations.Solar pump: A 102 kW solar pumping array would require massive panel area and storage, whereas a river is already adjacent.
choiceExplanations.Windpump: Mechanical windpumps deliver only watts to a few kilowatts, far short of a continuous 102 kW load.
choiceExplanations.Microhydro: Microhydro is classified up to 100 kW, just below the farm's 102 kW pumping demand.

items.question: An Otto cycle engine is used in a locally assembled transport vehicle for a sugarcane plantation. The operator frequently observes that the engine stalls when climbing a slightly sloping farm-to-market road. What repair or modification will you do to solve the problem?
items.answer: Replace the engine with diesel engine of the same space requirement but of higher rated power
items.rationale: Frequent stalling while climbing grades indicates insufficient power and low-end torque from the gasoline (Otto cycle) engine. Replacing it with a higher-rated diesel engine of the same footprint provides greater low-speed torque and pulling power.
choices: Reduce carriage volume to reduce load
Replace the engine with diesel engine of the same space requirement but of higher rated power
Tighten the timing belt to minimize slippage
Rebore the engine cylinders to increase power

choiceExplanations.Reduce carriage volume to reduce load: Reducing carriage volume cuts hauling capacity and farm productivity instead of addressing insufficient engine torque.
choiceExplanations.Replace the engine with diesel engine of: Correct — replacing the underpowered gasoline engine with a compact, higher-powered diesel provides the low-end torque needed on uphill grades.
choiceExplanations.Tighten the timing belt to minimize slip: A timing belt is toothed and does not slip like a V-belt; tightening it cannot cure underpower stalling.
choiceExplanations.Rebore the engine cylinders to increase: Reboring slightly increases displacement but weakens cylinder walls and cannot match a higher-rated diesel upgrade.

items.question: A transport vehicle smells of gasoline in the hood area when running. What part should you inspect immediately and what should you look for?
items.rationale: A gasoline smell under the hood while the engine is running points to pressurized fuel lines or connections in the engine bay, so the fuel hose should be checked immediately for leakage to prevent fire.
choices: Air conditioner’s evaporator, for crack or leakage

choiceExplanations.Fuel tank, for crack: The fuel tank is mounted at the rear or underbody, not under the engine hood.
choiceExplanations.Fuel hose, for leakage: Correct — pressurized fuel hoses run inside the engine bay, so leaking hoses or clamps there immediately release gasoline fumes and fire risk.
choiceExplanations.Accelerator pedal, for adjustment: Accelerator pedal adjustment affects throttle cable travel and does not cause fuel odor under the hood.
choiceExplanations.Air conditioner’s evaporator, for crack: A leaking AC evaporator releases refrigerant odor inside the cabin, not gasoline smell under the hood.

items.question: An AC generator is rated at an apparent power of 100 KVA with a power factor of 0.8, what is the real power of the generator in kW?

choiceExplanations.70: 70 kW corresponds to a 0.70 power factor, not the stated 0.8 power factor.
choiceExplanations.80: Correct — real power equals apparent power times power factor: 100 kVA × 0.8 = 80 kW.
choiceExplanations.75: 75 kW corresponds to a 0.75 power factor rather than 0.80.
choiceExplanations.85: 85 kW corresponds to a 0.85 power factor rather than 0.80.

items.question: Prior to starting field operation, the tractor operator should check the adequacy of fuel, oil, and ______.
items.rationale: Pre-operation checks on a water-cooled tractor include verifying sufficient fuel, engine oil, and radiator cooling water (coolant) to prevent overheating during operation.

choiceExplanations.Battery fluid: Battery electrolyte is checked during periodic maintenance rather than the daily fuel-oil-water pre-start trio.
choiceExplanations.Water: Correct — the basic daily tractor pre-operation check (BLOW/FOW) covers fuel, engine oil, and radiator cooling water.
choiceExplanations.Air: Air is drawn continuously from the atmosphere and is not stored as a consumable fluid.
choiceExplanations.Engine lubricant: Engine lubricant is synonymous with oil, which is already mentioned in the question.

items.question: Four-wheel tractors have normally _____ engines.

choiceExplanations.2-stroke: 2-stroke engines are used in small handheld tools like chainsaws, not heavy four-wheel farm tractors.
choiceExplanations.5-stroke: A 5-stroke cycle is an experimental non-standard design and is not used in commercial tractors.
choiceExplanations.3-stroke: There is no standard 3-stroke internal combustion cycle used in tractor manufacturing.
choiceExplanations.4-stroke: Correct — four-wheel agricultural tractors normally use 4-stroke diesel engines for durability, torque, and clean combustion.

items.question: For a diesel engine, in what stroke is fuel injected into the cylinder?

choiceExplanations.Power stroke: During the power stroke, combustion gases expand to push the piston down after injection begins.
choiceExplanations.Compression stroke: Correct — diesel fuel is injected near the end of the compression stroke into hot, compressed air for auto-ignition.
choiceExplanations.Intake stroke: During the intake stroke, a diesel engine draws in only pure air without any fuel.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust stroke: During the exhaust stroke, burned combustion gases are expelled through the open exhaust valve.

items.question: Due to small engine space in mobile fisheries equipment, they are best manufactured using a _______ engine.

choiceExplanations.2-stroke: Correct — 2-stroke engines are lighter, simpler (no valvetrain), and pack high power-to-weight into compact mobile fisheries equipment.
choiceExplanations.3-stroke: No standard 3-stroke reciprocating engine exists for mobile fisheries or marine equipment.
choiceExplanations.4-stroke: 4-stroke engines require valvetrains and oil sumps, making them bulkier and heavier for tight spaces.
choiceExplanations.1-stroke: A 1-stroke reciprocating engine does not exist in practical mechanical engineering.

items.question: During power stroke in an engine, the ___ transmits mechanical power to the crank.

choiceExplanations.Piston pin: The piston pin (wrist pin) only hinges the piston to the small end of the connecting rod.
choiceExplanations.Connecting rod: Correct — the connecting rod links the reciprocating piston directly to the crankshaft throw to transmit combustion force.
choiceExplanations.Push rod: A push rod transfers cam lobe lift upward to the rocker arm to actuate valves.
choiceExplanations.Rocker arm: The rocker arm pivots on the cylinder head to press open the intake or exhaust valves.

items.question: To roll a tractor from stop and neutral position with engine on in a flat land, what should be foot-pressed?
items.rationale: From neutral, the clutch pedal must be pressed first so a gear can be engaged; the tractor rolls as the clutch is released slowly while the throttle is raised.

choiceExplanations.Clutch: Correct — press the clutch first to disconnect the engine, shift into gear, then release it slowly to start rolling.
choiceExplanations.Brake: Wrong — the brake stops or holds the tractor; it does not make it roll.
choiceExplanations.Accelerator: Wrong — in neutral the accelerator only revs the engine; no power reaches the wheels until a gear is engaged with the clutch.
choiceExplanations.Differential lock: Wrong — the differential lock makes both rear wheels turn together to prevent wheel slip.

items.question: A picohydro generator is to be used as power source for an analog pressure transmitter sending real-time data on water depth at dam outlet. The pressure transmitter has a voltage of 15 Volts DC and amperage of 20 milliamperes. What minimum power output and voltage of picohydro generator should you request for purchasing?

choiceExplanations.365 milliwatts, 15 Vdc: Correct — 15 V × 20 mA requires 300 mW nominal load power, so requesting ~365 mW at 15 Vdc provides a safety margin at matching voltage.
choiceExplanations.328 milliwatts, 14 Vdc: 14 Vdc is below the transmitter's required 15 Vdc operating voltage.
choiceExplanations.402 milliwatts, 16 Vdc: 16 Vdc exceeds the transmitter's rated 15 Vdc supply specification.
choiceExplanations.292 milliwatts, 12 Vdc: 292 mW and 12 Vdc are both below the transmitter's 300 mW and 15 Vdc requirements.

items.question: Based on the specific gravity of liquid fuels, which of the following fuels is lighter than water?
items.rationale: Water has a specific gravity of 1.0, whereas gasoline (~0.71–0.77), kerosene (~0.78–0.82), and diesel (~0.82–0.86) all have specific gravities below 1.0, so all three are lighter than water.

choiceExplanations.Diesel, kerosene and gasoline: Correct — diesel (~0.83), kerosene (~0.80), and gasoline (~0.74) all have specific gravities less than water (1.0).
choiceExplanations.Kerosene: Kerosene is lighter than water, but diesel and gasoline are also lighter than water.
choiceExplanations.Diesel: Diesel is lighter than water, yet this omits kerosene and gasoline which are lighter too.
choiceExplanations.Gasoline: Gasoline is lighter than water, but this excludes diesel and kerosene.

items.question: The specific heat of diesel is 0.48 kcal/(kg °C). If the current temperature of a 1 kg diesel is 200°C, find the amount of energy needed to further increase it to 210°C.

choiceExplanations.4.8 kcal: Correct — Q = m·c·ΔT = 1 kg × 0.48 kcal/(kg·°C) × (210 − 200) °C = 4.8 kcal.
choiceExplanations.3.8 kcal: 3.8 kcal miscalculates the product of 0.48 kcal/(kg·°C) and the 10 °C temperature rise.
choiceExplanations.5.9 kcal: 5.9 kcal overestimates the required sensible heat for a 10 °C temperature increase.
choiceExplanations.4.2 kcal: 4.2 kcal underestimates the sensible heat required by 0.6 kcal.

items.question: What alternative fuel for internal combustion and other engines—used either in combination with gasoline or in pure form—can be produced by destructive distillation of wood and can cause blindness or fatality if ingested and left untreated?
items.rationale: Wood alcohol, methanol, and methyl alcohol are different names for the same chemical compound (CH₃OH), which can be derived from destructive distillation of wood and causes blindness or death upon ingestion.

choiceExplanations.All of the above: Correct — wood alcohol, methanol, and methyl alcohol are all names for CH₃OH, obtained by wood distillation and toxic to the optic nerve.
choiceExplanations.Wood alcohol: Wood alcohol is an accurate name for CH₃OH, but methanol and methyl alcohol are also correct.
choiceExplanations.Methanol: Methanol is the IUPAC name for CH₃OH, yet wood alcohol and methyl alcohol refer to the same substance.
choiceExplanations.Methyl alcohol: Methyl alcohol correctly names CH₃OH, making the combined option covering all synonyms accurate.

items.question: the state of permanent displacement of the stems from their upright position, which is induced by external forces exerted by wind, rain, or hail. It may culminate in the plants being laid flat on the ground and sometimes involve breakage of the stems.

choiceExplanations.Grain shattering: Grain shattering is the premature shedding or detachment of seeds from the panicle or pod before or during harvest.
choiceExplanations.Crop wilting: Crop wilting is the drooping of leaves and stems caused by water stress or loss of turgor pressure.
choiceExplanations.Grain lodging: Correct — Grain lodging is the permanent bending or breaking of crop stems from upright positions due to wind, rain, or hail.
choiceExplanations.Grain cracking: Grain cracking refers to internal fissures or fractures in the kernel caused by rapid moisture or thermal stress.

items.question: A 25KW-50KW hydropower plant is classified as:
items.rationale: micro hydro pico: less than 5 kW micro: 5 kW - 100 kW mini: 100 kW - 10 MW small: 10 MW - 25 MW medium: 25 MW - 100 MW large: above 100 MW

choiceExplanations.Pico-hydro: Pico-hydro systems generate very small power outputs, typically below 5 kW for single households or small loads.
choiceExplanations.Micro-hydro: Correct — Micro-hydro plants generally cover capacities from 5 kW to 100 kW, placing 25–50 kW squarely in this class.
choiceExplanations.Mini-hydro: Mini-hydro systems typically range from 100 kW up to 1 MW or 10 MW depending on national classification.
choiceExplanations.Large-hydro: Large-hydro plants generate tens to thousands of megawatts using major dams and reservoirs.

items.question: Efficiency of Spark Ignition Engine

choiceExplanations.20–25%: This range underestimates typical peak thermal efficiency of modern spark-ignition engines in agricultural power texts.
choiceExplanations.25-30%: Correct — Standard agricultural engineering references state spark-ignition (Otto cycle) engines operate at 25–30% thermal efficiency.
choiceExplanations.30–35%: This higher efficiency range corresponds more closely to compression-ignition diesel engines than spark-ignition engines.
choiceExplanations.35–40%: Spark-ignition engines cannot sustain 35–40% efficiency because lower compression ratios limit their Otto-cycle work output.

items.question: Efficiency of Gasoline Engine

choiceExplanations.35–40%: Conventional gasoline engines fall short of 35–40% efficiency due to knock-limited lower compression ratios.
choiceExplanations.20–25%: This range is below the standard 25–30% thermal efficiency cited for gasoline engines.
choiceExplanations.25-30%: Correct — Gasoline engines are spark-ignition engines whose typical thermal efficiency is 25–30%.
choiceExplanations.30–35%: This range is characteristic of diesel compression-ignition engines rather than gasoline engines.

items.question: Efficiency of Diesel Engine

choiceExplanations.24–30%: This lower range corresponds to gasoline spark-ignition engines rather than higher-compression diesel engines.
choiceExplanations.36–42%: This exceeds the standard textbook range for small and medium agricultural diesel engines.
choiceExplanations.30-36%: Correct — Diesel engines achieve 30–36% thermal efficiency due to higher compression ratios and leaner combustion.
choiceExplanations.42–48%: This range applies only to massive slow-speed marine or stationary turbocharged diesels, not farm engines.

items.question: MACHINE SERVICING: Changing of engine oil should be done ______.

choiceExplanations.every 6 months or 25000 km: Waiting 25,000 km risks severe oil degradation, sludge buildup, and accelerated engine wear.
choiceExplanations.every 3 months or 12000 km: Correct — Standard machine servicing reviewer guidelines specify changing engine oil every 3 months or 12,000 km, whichever comes first.
choiceExplanations.every 1 month or 2000 km: Changing oil every 2,000 km is unnecessarily frequent for standard engine servicing outside initial break-in.
choiceExplanations.every 12 months or 50000 km: Extending oil intervals to 50,000 km depletes additives and causes catastrophic lubrication failure.

items.question: MACHINE SERVICING: API Service Classification for gasoline engine is ________

choiceExplanations.S-Series: Correct — API S-Series (Service/Spark-ignition) oils are formulated specifically for gasoline engines.
choiceExplanations.D-Series: API does not designate an engine oil service category with a D-Series prefix.
choiceExplanations.G-Series: G-Series is not a valid API engine oil service classification letter; GL codes apply to gear oils.
choiceExplanations.C-Series: API C-Series (Commercial/Compression-ignition) oils are formulated for diesel engines, not gasoline engines.

items.question: MACHINE SERVICING: API Service Classification for diesel engine is ________

choiceExplanations.D-series: API uses C-Series rather than D-Series to classify commercial diesel engine oils.
choiceExplanations.C-series: Correct — API C-series (Commercial/Compression-ignition) classifies motor oils designed for diesel engines.
choiceExplanations.S-series: API S-series classifies motor oils intended for spark-ignition gasoline engines, not diesels.
choiceExplanations.G-series: API does not use a G-series designation for diesel engine crankcase oils.

items.question: AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY: RPM of shaft according to Barger

choiceExplanations.1000 rpm: Correct — Barger et al. specify 1000 rpm as the standard high-speed tractor PTO/shaft speed alongside 540 rpm.
choiceExplanations.1150 rpm: 1150 rpm is not an ASAE/Barger standard shaft speed for agricultural tractors.
choiceExplanations.880 rpm: 880 rpm does not match the standardized 540 rpm or 1000 rpm PTO shaft speeds.
choiceExplanations.1220 rpm: 1220 rpm exceeds standard agricultural tractor PTO shaft rotational speeds.

items.question: AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY: Machine element that transmit torque and power

choiceExplanations.Bearing: A bearing supports a rotating shaft and reduces friction rather than transmitting torque itself.
choiceExplanations.Housing: A housing encloses and supports bearings or gears to protect them and maintain alignment.
choiceExplanations.Bushing: A bushing acts as a plain sleeve bearing or spacer, not a torque-transmitting element.
choiceExplanations.Shaft: Correct — A shaft is a rotating machine element designed specifically to transmit torque and mechanical power.

items.question: Type of gasifier that has the ability to gasify wet fuel

choiceExplanations.Crossdraft: Crossdraft gasifiers have limited residence time and require dry, low-ash fuels like charcoal.
choiceExplanations.Fluidized bed: Fluidized bed gasifiers require uniform small particle sizes and tightly controlled dry feed rather than wet biomass.
choiceExplanations.Updraft: Correct — In an updraft gasifier, hot rising gases dry incoming wet fuel at the top before pyrolysis and gasification.
choiceExplanations.Downdraft: Downdraft gasifiers require dry fuel (<20% moisture) because moisture cools the throat and prevents tar cracking.

items.question: RENEWABLE ENERGY: C-N ratio for anaerobic digestion of agri-waste
choices: High carbon deposit at the combustion chamber, use an additive to wear out carbon deposit

choiceExplanations.20:1 - 30:1 (PAES 413): Correct — PAES 413 specifies an optimal C:N ratio of 20:1 to 30:1 for anaerobic digestion of agricultural wastes.
choiceExplanations.High carbon deposit at the combustion ch: This distractor describes engine combustion chamber carbon deposits, completely unrelated to anaerobic digester feedstocks.
choiceExplanations.1-3-2-5-8-6-7-4: This sequence represents an eight-cylinder engine firing order rather than a carbon-to-nitrogen ratio.
choiceExplanations.-40: -40 is the temperature where Celsius and Fahrenheit scales coincide, not a C:N ratio.

items.question: Density of diesel

choiceExplanations.0.744 kg/L: 0.744 kg/L falls in the density range of gasoline rather than heavier diesel fuel.
choiceExplanations.1.099 kg/L: A density above 1.0 kg/L is heavier than water and corresponds to ethylene glycol, not diesel.
choiceExplanations.1.031 kg/L: 1.031 kg/L is typical of milk or brine, whereas petroleum diesel floats on water.
choiceExplanations.0.845 kg/L: Correct — Standard diesel fuel has a specific gravity around 0.845, giving a density of 0.845 kg/L.

items.question: Density of gasoline fuel

choiceExplanations.0.6 kg/L: 0.6 kg/L is closer to liquefied petroleum gas or very light naphtha than automotive gasoline.
choiceExplanations.0.7 kg/L: Correct — Gasoline has an approximate density of 0.70–0.75 kg/L (rounded to 0.7 kg/L in ABE reviewers).
choiceExplanations.0.9 kg/L: 0.9 kg/L corresponds to heavy fuel oil or vegetable oil, not light volatile gasoline.
choiceExplanations.0.8 kg/L: 0.8 kg/L is characteristic of kerosene or light diesel rather than gasoline.

items.question: Rice hull gasifier efficiency normally ranged from:

choiceExplanations.70–90%: 70–90% overstates typical small rice hull gasifier efficiency due to high ash and heat losses.
choiceExplanations.90–110%: Efficiencies above 100% violate the first law of thermodynamics; thermal gasification cannot exceed 100%.
choiceExplanations.50-70%: Correct — Rice hull gasifiers typically achieve 50–70% cold-gas efficiency because of rice hull's high silica ash and tar losses.
choiceExplanations.30–50%: 30–50% is below normal operating cold-gas efficiency of properly designed rice hull gasifiers.

items.question: The wind flows on a 2m-diameter rotor at a rate of 2 m/s. It suddenly flows at 4 m/s, what would be the power output of the windmill?

choiceExplanations.9 times: Wind power scales with velocity cubed, not squared or ninefold when velocity doubles.
choiceExplanations.7 times: Doubling wind speed gives 2³ = 8 times the power, not 7 times.
choiceExplanations.8 times: Correct — Wind power is proportional to the cube of wind velocity (P ∝ v³), so doubling v from 2 to 4 m/s increases power by 2³ = 8 times.
choiceExplanations.6 times: 6 times underestimates the cubic relationship between wind speed and available wind power.

items.question: The greater the number of blades of the wind machine, _ the torque.

choiceExplanations.Lower: Fewer blades, not more blades, result in lower starting torque and higher rotational speed.
choiceExplanations.Constant: Torque depends directly on rotor solidity and blade count rather than remaining constant.
choiceExplanations.Higher: Correct — More blades increase rotor solidity and starting torque, making multi-bladed windmills ideal for water pumping.
choiceExplanations.Smaller: Increasing blade count raises aerodynamic solidity and torque rather than making torque smaller.

items.question: The ratio of the heat released by the fuel of a heated-air mechanical dryer to the theoretical heat available from the fuel.

choiceExplanations.Thermal efficiency: Thermal efficiency relates heat actually used for drying or heating to total heat supplied.
choiceExplanations.Mechanical efficiency: Mechanical efficiency is the ratio of brake power output to indicated power in a machine.
choiceExplanations.Drying efficiency: Drying efficiency compares heat utilized for moisture evaporation to total heat input to the dryer.
choiceExplanations.Combustion efficiency: Correct — Combustion efficiency is defined by PAES as the ratio of heat released by the burner/fuel to the fuel's theoretical heating value.

items.question: AGRICULTURAL POWER: Gasoline Flash Point (in °F)

choiceExplanations.-36 - 40 F: This range does not match the standard -40 to -45°F flash point cited in ABE reviewers.
choiceExplanations.-40 - 45 F: Correct — Gasoline has a very low flash point of around -40°F to -45°F (written as -40 - 45 F in the reviewer), allowing easy ignition.
choiceExplanations.-32 - 36 F: -32°F to -36°F is slightly warmer than the standard -40 to -45°F flash point figure.
choiceExplanations.-44 - 50 F: This range does not correspond to the standard reviewer value for gasoline flash point.

items.question: AGRICULTURAL POWER: Diesel Flash Point (in °C)

choiceExplanations.40°C: 40°C is closer to kerosene's minimum flash point (~38°C) than standard diesel fuel.
