choiceExplanations.50°C: Correct — Standard automotive/agricultural diesel has a minimum flash point around 50°C (typically 52°C+ in specs), making it safer to handle than gasoline.
choiceExplanations.55°C: While some heavy diesels exceed 55°C, 50°C is the standard reviewer benchmark value.
choiceExplanations.45°C: 45°C is below the minimum ~50°C flash point threshold specified for diesel fuel.

items.question: Highly Mechanized Farm have ________ hp/ha

choiceExplanations.2-2: "2-2" collapses to a single number and is not a standard mechanization power range.
choiceExplanations.3-4: 3–4 hp/ha exceeds the 2–3 hp/ha threshold traditionally defining highly mechanized agriculture.
choiceExplanations.2-3: Correct — In ABE mechanization classifications, a highly mechanized farm typically utilizes 2–3 hp/ha of available power.
choiceExplanations.2-4: 2–4 hp/ha widens the upper bound beyond the standard 2–3 hp/ha benchmark.

items.question: measure direct solar radiation

choiceExplanations.Pyranometer: A pyranometer measures total global (direct plus diffuse) solar radiation on a horizontal surface.
choiceExplanations.Albedometer: An albedometer measures surface albedo by comparing incoming global radiation and reflected solar radiation.
choiceExplanations.Pyrheliometer: Correct — A pyrheliometer tracks the sun at normal incidence to measure direct-beam solar radiation.
choiceExplanations.Photometer: A photometer measures visible light intensity (illuminance or luminance) rather than total solar irradiance.

items.question: measures general solar radiation

choiceExplanations.Albedometer: An albedometer measures the ratio of reflected to incident solar radiation (surface albedo).
choiceExplanations.Pyrheliometer: A pyrheliometer measures only direct-beam solar radiation using a narrow-field-of-view collimated tube.
choiceExplanations.Pyranometer: Correct — A pyranometer measures global (general) solar radiation, combining both direct and diffuse components over a hemisphere.
choiceExplanations.Luxmeter: A luxmeter measures visible illuminance in lux rather than broadband solar radiation energy.

items.question: The standard length of stroke of hydraulic remote-control cylinders for trailing-type agricultural implement is:

choiceExplanations.8-16 inches: Correct — ASAE S201/S316 standards specify 8 inches (203 mm) and 16 inches (406 mm) as standard cylinder stroke lengths.
choiceExplanations.16-24 inches: 24-inch strokes exceed standard ASAE remote-control hydraulic cylinder specifications for trailing implements.
choiceExplanations.0-8 inches: 0–8 inches omits the standard 16-inch stroke and includes zero stroke.
choiceExplanations.24-32 inches: 24–32 inches is far longer than ASAE standard remote hydraulic cylinders for farm implements.

items.question: The inherent characteristics of tractors to maintain or to produce increased drawbar pull even if the speed is reduced.

choiceExplanations.Tractive efficiency: Tractive efficiency is the ratio of drawbar power output to axle power input.
choiceExplanations.Slippage ratio: Slippage ratio measures wheel travel reduction under load relative to zero-load travel.
choiceExplanations.Lugging ability: Correct — Lugging ability is a tractor engine's capacity to increase torque and pull as engine speed drops under heavy load.
choiceExplanations.Rolling resistance: Rolling resistance is the opposing force required to move wheels across soil or ground surfaces.

items.question: The force utilized in multi-bladed windmill

choiceExplanations.Lift force: Correct — Modern and multi-bladed airfoil-section wind rotors primarily harness aerodynamic lift force perpendicular to the wind flow.
choiceExplanations.Drag force: Drag force acts parallel to wind flow and drives low-efficiency cup anemometers or Savonius rotors.
choiceExplanations.Centrifugal force: Centrifugal force is an outward inertial force on rotating blades, not the driving wind force.
choiceExplanations.Thrust force: Axial thrust force pushes against the rotor tower rather than turning the rotor shaft.

items.question: Average power density of solar heat striking the earth surface.
items.rationale: 0.58kW/m² / Peak 1kW/m² / entering earth atmosphere(solar constant) - 1.355 kW/m2 / striking earth surface - 0.89 kW/m2

choiceExplanations.0.58kW/m²: Correct — Standard ABE solar energy references give 0.58 kW/m² (~500 kcal/h·m²) as the average solar power density reaching Earth's surface.
choiceExplanations.0.68kW/m²: 0.68 kW/m² is higher than the standard average surface solar power density cited in ABE texts.
choiceExplanations.0.48kW/m²: 0.48 kW/m² underestimates the standard 0.58 kW/m² average solar power density value.
choiceExplanations.0.38kW/m²: 0.38 kW/m² is significantly below the standard 0.58 kW/m² figure used in Philippine ABE reviewers.

items.question: Determine the rotor speed of a windmill with a wind tip-speed ratio of 1:1 and a wind velocity of 2m/s.

choiceExplanations.1m/s: A 1 m/s blade tip speed with 2 m/s wind yields a 0.5:1 ratio, not 1:1.
choiceExplanations.2m/s: Correct — Tip-speed ratio equals rotor tip speed divided by wind velocity; at 1:1 with 2 m/s wind, tip speed is 2 m/s.
choiceExplanations.4m/s: A 4 m/s tip speed with 2 m/s wind corresponds to a 2:1 tip-speed ratio.
choiceExplanations.3m/s: A 3 m/s tip speed with 2 m/s wind gives a 1.5:1 tip-speed ratio.

items.question: API

choiceExplanations.Agricultural Power Institute: Agricultural Power Institute is a fabricated expansion; API sets petroleum and lubricant standards.
choiceExplanations.American Petroleum Institute: Correct — API stands for the American Petroleum Institute, which sets engine oil and fuel classification standards.
choiceExplanations.American Power Institute: American Power Institute is not the oil and fuel standards organization known as API.
choiceExplanations.American Pipe Institute: API stands for American Petroleum Institute, though it also publishes oilfield pipe standards.

items.question: Minimum efficiency of a heated air mechanical grain dryer.
items.rationale: 75% / 90% (heating eff, petroleum, direct) / 75% (heating eff, petroleum, indirect) / 65% (heating eff, biomass, direct) / 50% (heating eff, biomass, indirect)

choiceExplanations.82%: 82% exceeds the minimum heated-air mechanical grain dryer efficiency required under PAES standards.
choiceExplanations.68%: 68% falls below the PAES 201 minimum thermal/heating efficiency requirement of 75%.
choiceExplanations.75%: Correct — PAES 201 specifies a minimum heating/burner efficiency of 75% for heated-air mechanical grain dryers.
choiceExplanations.60%: 60% is well below the 75% minimum efficiency standard for heated-air grain dryers.

items.question: An engine with no load is in what condition

choiceExplanations.Idle condition: Correct — An engine running with zero external load at minimum stable speed is in idle condition.
choiceExplanations.Peak condition: Peak condition refers to maximum torque or maximum power output under full load.
choiceExplanations.Rated condition: Rated condition is operation at the manufacturer's specified rated speed and full continuous load.
choiceExplanations.Stall condition: Stall condition occurs when excessive load overwhelms engine torque and stops the crankshaft.

items.question: The process of converting an energy from one form to another

choiceExplanations.Induction: Induction is generating voltage or magnetism via a changing magnetic field, not general energy conversion.
choiceExplanations.Transduction: Correct — Transduction is the general process of converting energy from one form into another.
choiceExplanations.Conduction: Conduction is heat or electrical transfer through a medium without converting energy forms.
choiceExplanations.Convection: Convection is thermal energy transfer through bulk movement of a fluid.

items.question: Direction of solar panels

choiceExplanations.East: Facing East captures only morning sunlight and misses peak midday and afternoon solar radiation.
choiceExplanations.West: Facing West favors afternoon sun and reduces overall daily energy yield in the Philippines.
choiceExplanations.North: In the Northern Hemisphere (including the Philippines), north-facing panels receive minimal direct annual sunlight.
choiceExplanations.South: Correct — In the Northern Hemisphere, solar panels should face true South to maximize year-round solar energy capture.

items.question: refers to the quantity of solar radiation energy received on a surface during an amount of time, expressed in kWh/ m²

choiceExplanations.Solar constant: Solar constant is the average solar power flux (~1361 W/m²) just outside Earth's atmosphere.
choiceExplanations.Solar insolation: Correct — Solar insolation is the cumulative solar radiation energy received per unit area over a given time, expressed in kWh/m².
choiceExplanations.Solar reflectance: Solar reflectance is the fraction of incident solar energy reflected by a surface (albedo).
choiceExplanations.Solar irradiance: Solar irradiance is instantaneous power per unit area (kW/m² or W/m²), not cumulative energy.

items.question: It is the power per unit area (surface power density) received from the Sun. (kW/m2)

choiceExplanations.Solar irradiance: Correct — Solar irradiance is the instantaneous solar power received per unit surface area, measured in W/m² or kW/m².
choiceExplanations.Solar constant: Solar constant is the fixed mean irradiance outside Earth's atmosphere (~1.36 kW/m²), not general surface power density.
choiceExplanations.Solar insolation: Solar insolation is energy accumulated over time per unit area (kWh/m²), not instantaneous power.
choiceExplanations.Solar emittance: Emittance describes radiant power emitted by a surface rather than power received from the Sun.

items.question: The total radiant energy leaving a unit of surface area per unit time, emitted and reflected energy is called___

choiceExplanations.Reflectance: Reflectance is the dimensionless fraction of incident radiation reflected by a surface.
choiceExplanations.Radiosity: Correct — Radiosity (J) is the total radiant flux leaving a unit surface area per unit time, combining emitted and reflected energy.
choiceExplanations.Irradiation: Irradiation (G) is the total radiant energy incident upon a surface per unit area and time.
choiceExplanations.Emittance: Emittance refers only to radiation emitted by a surface, excluding reflected incident radiation.

items.question: it is radiation energy leaving a surface

choiceExplanations.Absorptive power: Absorptive power refers to radiant energy absorbed by a surface rather than emitted outward.
choiceExplanations.Emmissive power: Correct — Emissive power is the thermal radiation energy emitted and leaving per unit surface area per unit time.
choiceExplanations.Radiant intensity: Radiant intensity measures radiant power emitted per unit solid angle (W/sr), not total surface flux.
choiceExplanations.Reflective flux: Reflective flux accounts only for bounced incident light rather than radiation emitted by the surface.

items.question: A process from one form of energy to another.

choiceExplanations.Conduction: Conduction transfers heat or electric charge through a material without changing its energy form.
choiceExplanations.Transduction: Correct — Transduction is the conversion of energy from one form to another (e.g., mechanical to electrical).
choiceExplanations.Dissipation: Dissipation is the irreversible loss of useful energy, typically wasted as low-grade heat.
choiceExplanations.Induction: Induction specifically refers to generating electric current or voltage via a changing magnetic field.

items.question: Main cause of engine’s leak is due to ___.

choiceExplanations.High oil viscosity: High oil viscosity thickens oil flow and resists leakage rather than causing oil leaks.
choiceExplanations.Low oil pressure: Correct — In ABE engine troubleshooting reviewers, an external or internal engine oil leak manifests as or is associated with low oil pressure.
choiceExplanations.Lean air mixture: A lean mixture affects combustion temperature and power, not engine oil sealing or leaks.
choiceExplanations.Low fuel pressure: Low fuel pressure causes starving or misfiring in the fuel system, not oil leaks.

items.question: Component that converts animal power to mechanical power

choiceExplanations.Drawbar: A drawbar is a hitch bar on a tractor or implement, not worn by draft animals.
choiceExplanations.Singletree: A singletree is the pivoted wooden or metal bar attached behind the traces to equalize pull.
choiceExplanations.Evener: An evener (doubletree) distributes draft pull evenly between two or more harnessed animals.
choiceExplanations.Harness: Correct — A harness fits onto the draft animal's body (collar, hames, traces) to convert muscular draft effort into mechanical pull.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A device at the header of a combine for severing the plant stalk

choiceExplanations.Conveying mechanism: The conveying mechanism (auger or draper) moves cut stalks toward the feeder house.
choiceExplanations.Cutting mechanism: Correct — The cutting mechanism (reciprocating sickle cutterbar) at the combine header severs the standing plant stalks.
choiceExplanations.Gathering mechanism: The gathering mechanism (reel) guides and holds standing stalks toward the cutterbar without cutting them.
choiceExplanations.Threshing mechanism: The threshing mechanism (cylinder and concave) separates grains from stalks inside the combine body.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In ASAE, safety code for laboratory equipment and typical application, the safety yellow color stands for

choiceExplanations.Warning: Under safety color codes, Warning uses orange to indicate moderate-to-serious potential hazards.
choiceExplanations.Danger: Danger uses safety red to signify immediate hazards that will cause death or serious injury.
choiceExplanations.Notice: Notice uses safety blue for general instructions or equipment care without personal injury risk.
choiceExplanations.Caution: Correct — Under ASAE/ANSI safety color codes, safety yellow designates Caution for minor or moderate potential hazards.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: ASAE stands for

choiceExplanations.American Society of Agricultural Enginee: Correct — ASAE stands for the American Society of Agricultural Engineers (now ASABE, adding Biological Engineers).
choiceExplanations.American Society of Automotive Engineers: The automotive engineering society is SAE (Society of Automotive Engineers), not ASAE.
choiceExplanations.American Society of Agronomy Engineers: No such organization exists; agronomy professionals belong to the American Society of Agronomy (ASA).
choiceExplanations.American Society of Applied Engineers: American Society of Applied Engineers is a fabricated distractor acronym.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The minimum number of hours required in testing rice thresher based on PAE standards.

choiceExplanations.2 hour: 2 hours exceeds the minimum continuous test duration mandated by PAES for rice threshers.
choiceExplanations.4 hour: 4 hours is four times longer than the PAES minimum rice thresher test run.
choiceExplanations.1 hour: Correct — PAES 205 (Test Methods for Rice Thresher) requires a minimum continuous testing period of 1 hour.
choiceExplanations.3 hour: 3 hours exceeds the 1-hour minimum continuous test requirement in PAES rice thresher standards.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A drive where shafts are operating on a counter clockwise directions

choiceExplanations.Sprockets: Sprockets connected by a chain rotate both shafts in the same direction.
choiceExplanations.Belts: Open belt drives rotate both pulleys in the same direction (only crossed belts reverse).
choiceExplanations.Chains: Chain drives transmit power with both sprockets rotating in the same direction.
choiceExplanations.Gears: Correct — Two externally meshing gears reverse rotation, causing adjacent shafts to turn in opposite (clockwise/counterclockwise) directions.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is a kind of steel used in making disk plow bottom

choiceExplanations.Soft-centered steel: Correct — Soft-centered steel combines hard high-carbon outer layers for wear resistance/scouring with a tough low-carbon core to absorb shock.
choiceExplanations.Cold-rolled steel: Cold-rolled steel lacks the hard-faced outer wear surface and shock-absorbing core needed for plow bottoms.
choiceExplanations.Medium-carbon steel: Medium-carbon steel wears faster on the surface and is less specialized than laminated soft-centered steel.
choiceExplanations.Low-carbon steel: Low-carbon steel is too soft and wears out rapidly in abrasive soil tillage.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: When welding deposit is applied to strengthen peg-tooth of a rice thresher, this method of treating metal is used.

choiceExplanations.Surface annealing: Annealing softens metal through heating and slow cooling rather than strengthening wear surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Flame hardening: Flame hardening heats and quenches existing high-carbon steel without adding a weld metal deposit.
choiceExplanations.Case hardening: Case hardening diffuses carbon or nitrogen into steel surface layers without welding filler metal.
choiceExplanations.Hard facing: Correct — Hard facing deposits a wear-resistant weld alloy onto metal parts like thresher peg-teeth to extend service life.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Cost of machine including shipment

choiceExplanations.Free alongside ship: Free alongside ship (FAS) covers delivery beside the vessel, excluding main ocean freight charges.
choiceExplanations.Free on board: Free on board (FOB) transfers cost and risk once loaded; buyer pays main freight.
choiceExplanations.Cash on delivery: Cash on delivery (COD) is a payment-upon-receipt term, not a freight-inclusive pricing term.
choiceExplanations.Cost in freight: Correct — Cost and/in freight (C&F or CIF without insurance) includes the machine's price plus shipment freight cost to destination.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A substance commonly used as coating to protect iron against corrosion

choiceExplanations.Manganese: Manganese is an alloying element in steel for strength and toughness, not a galvanic coating.
choiceExplanations.Zinc: Correct — Zinc is applied via galvanizing to protect iron and steel through barrier and sacrificial cathodic protection.
choiceExplanations.Silicon: Silicon is used as a deoxidizer and alloying element in steel, not a corrosion-protective coating.
choiceExplanations.Tungsten: Tungsten is a high-melting alloying metal for tool steels, not an anti-corrosion iron coating.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The smallest gears that are meshing together.

choiceExplanations.Rack: A rack is a straight, flat toothed bar that converts rotary gear motion to linear motion.
choiceExplanations.Worm: A worm is a screw-like helical shaft that meshes with a worm wheel at right angles.
choiceExplanations.Idler: An idler gear sits between driver and driven gears to change direction or span distance.
choiceExplanations.Pinion: Correct — In any pair of meshing gears, the smaller gear is called the pinion while the larger is the gear.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: If a large factor of safety is used in the design, product would tend to be

choiceExplanations.Compact: A large factor of safety requires thicker, heavier sections, making the product bulkier rather than compact.
choiceExplanations.Expensive: Correct — a large factor of safety increases material volume, size, and manufacturing cost, making the product expensive.
choiceExplanations.Lighter: A high safety factor adds extra material for strength, making the component heavier instead of lighter.
choiceExplanations.Economical: Oversizing parts with a large safety factor raises material and production costs, reducing cost economy.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A metal sheet with gauge number equal to 14 means

choiceExplanations.14 sheets per square foot area: Sheet gauge measures thickness rather than the number of sheets covering one square foot.
choiceExplanations.14 hundredths of an inch thickness: Gauge 14 steel is roughly 0.075 to 0.078 inches thick, not 0.14 inches.
choiceExplanations.14 pieces in one inch thickness: Correct — historically, sheet metal gauge indicated roughly how many stacked sheets equaled one inch in total thickness.
choiceExplanations.14 pounds per square foot weight: Metal weight per square foot defines plate poundage, not standard sheet gauge numbers.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A 4 feet wide x 8 feet long with 1/8-in. thick is

choiceExplanations.Metal plate: Correct — flat-rolled steel stock measuring 4 ft by 8 ft with 1/8 inch thickness is classified as a metal plate.
choiceExplanations.Metal strip: Metal strip refers to narrow flat-rolled stock, typically much narrower than a 4 ft by 8 ft panel.
choiceExplanations.Metal sheet: Metal sheet generally refers to thinner flat stock below 1/8 inch (or 3/16 inch depending on standard), lighter than plate.
choiceExplanations.Metal bar: Metal bar is narrow solid stock in round, square, hex, or flat cross-sections rather than wide 4x8 panels.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is a welding process that uses an electrode.

choiceExplanations.Arc welding: Correct — arc welding uses a consumable or non-consumable electrode to strike an electric arc that melts and joins metals.
choiceExplanations.Gas welding: Gas welding melts metals using a fuel-gas and oxygen flame from a torch rather than an electrical electrode.
choiceExplanations.Forge welding: Forge welding joins heated metals by hammering or pressing them together without an electrode.
choiceExplanations.Friction welding: Friction welding generates heat through mechanical rubbing between workpieces under pressure without an electrode.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The higher is the gauge number of a metal sheet, the lower is the

choiceExplanations.Hardness: Sheet hardness depends on alloy composition and heat treatment, not its gauge number.
choiceExplanations.Thickness: Correct — standard sheet metal gauge numbers increase inversely as the sheet thickness decreases.
choiceExplanations.Length: Sheet length is an independent cut dimension unrelated to the metal gauge number.
choiceExplanations.Density: Material density is an intrinsic physical property of the metal, unaffected by sheet gauge.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A welding process commonly used for thin sheets of metal.

choiceExplanations.Riveting: Riveting mechanically fastens sheets using metal pins rather than a thermal joining or welding process.
choiceExplanations.Forging: Forging shapes solid metal by compressive hammering or pressing rather than joining thin sheets.
choiceExplanations.Casting: Casting pours molten metal into a mold to form parts instead of joining thin sheets.
choiceExplanations.Soldering: Correct — soldering joins thin metal sheets at low temperatures using a melted filler alloy without melting the base sheets.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A machine tool used to reduce the diameter of a metal

choiceExplanations.Shaper: A shaper uses a reciprocating ram to cut flat surfaces rather than turning cylindrical diameters.
choiceExplanations.Lathe: Correct — a lathe rotates the cylindrical workpiece against a cutting tool to turn and reduce its outer diameter.
choiceExplanations.Planer: A planer reciprocates a large workpiece beneath a stationary tool to machine flat surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Slotter: A slotter uses a vertically reciprocating tool to cut internal keyways, slots, and grooves.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is the process of cutting hole to a material by means of shearing process

choiceExplanations.Reaming: Reaming uses a multi-flute rotary cutter to finish and size an existing drilled hole accurately.
choiceExplanations.Punching: Correct — punching cuts a hole through sheet or plate metal by applying compressive shear force between a punch and die.
choiceExplanations.Drilling: Drilling creates round holes by rotating a multi-edge cutting bit rather than shearing out a slug.
choiceExplanations.Boring: Boring enlarges and trues an existing hole using a single-point rotating or stationary cutting tool.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A screw used to fix metal parts together.

choiceExplanations.Flat-head drywall screw: Drywall screws are designed to fasten gypsum board to studs rather than joining metal parts.
choiceExplanations.Self-tapping screw: Correct — a self-tapping screw cuts or forms its own mating threads as it is driven into metal parts.
choiceExplanations.Coarse-thread wood screw: Coarse-thread wood screws are engineered to grip fibrous wood rather than dense metal sheets.
choiceExplanations.Lag-thread timber screw: Lag-thread timber screws are heavy fasteners designed for structural wood framing, not sheet or machine metal.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: If a metal has a thickness of 1/8 inch it is called as

choiceExplanations.Plate: Correct — flat metal stock starting at 1/8 inch thickness (or thicker depending on standard) is commonly classified as plate.
choiceExplanations.Foil: Metal foil is ultra-thin rolled metal, typically less than 0.006 inches thick.
choiceExplanations.Sheet: Metal sheet refers to thinner flat stock below plate thickness, generally under 1/8 inch.
choiceExplanations.Strip: Metal strip refers to narrow flat-rolled metal coils or lengths rather than thickness classification alone.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Filing is classified as

choiceExplanations.Hot working: Hot working deforms metal plastically above its recrystallization temperature rather than filing at room temperature.
choiceExplanations.Warm working: Warm working shapes metal at intermediate temperatures below recrystallization, unlike ambient hand filing.
choiceExplanations.Heat treating: Heat treating uses controlled heating and cooling cycles to alter metal microstructure and properties.
choiceExplanations.Cold working: Correct — filing removes and shapes metal at room temperature below recrystallization, placing it under cold working shop operations.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Ability of material to resist indention

choiceExplanations.Toughness: Toughness is the ability of a material to absorb energy and resist fracture under impact.
choiceExplanations.Malleability: Malleability is the ability to deform plastically under compressive forces like hammering or rolling.
choiceExplanations.Ductility: Ductility is the capacity to stretch into wire under tensile stress without breaking.
choiceExplanations.Hardness: Correct — hardness measures a material's resistance to localized plastic deformation such as indentation, scratching, or abrasion.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Property of material to join together with other metal at liquid state

choiceExplanations.Fusibility: Correct — fusibility is the property of a metal to melt easily and coalesce with another metal in the liquid state.
choiceExplanations.Machinability: Machinability indicates how easily a material can be cut, turned, or milled with machine tools.
choiceExplanations.Malleability: Malleability is the ability to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets without cracking.
choiceExplanations.Hardenability: Hardenability is a steel's ability to form martensite to a given depth upon quenching.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A machine element used to tighten bolt

choiceExplanations.Rivet: A rivet is a permanent unthreaded fastener deformed on one end to join plates.
choiceExplanations.Stud: A stud is an externally threaded headless rod rather than the internally threaded tightening piece.
choiceExplanations.Nut: Correct — a nut has internal threads that mate with a bolt's external threads to clamp and tighten joints.
choiceExplanations.Washer: A washer is a flat or spring ring placed beneath a nut or bolt head to distribute load.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is used to keep castellated nut from loosening

choiceExplanations.Dowel pin: A dowel pin is a solid cylindrical pin used for precise component alignment rather than nut locking.
choiceExplanations.Clevis pin: A clevis pin passes through a yoke or clevis to form a hinged joint, secured by a cotter.
choiceExplanations.Cotter pin: Correct — a split cotter pin passes through a bolt hole and the slots of a castellated nut to lock it.
choiceExplanations.Taper pin: A taper pin is a conical solid pin driven into tapered holes to align and fasten hubs.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is used to prevent bolt and nut from loosening

choiceExplanations.Gasket: A gasket seals mating flanges against fluid or gas leaks rather than locking fasteners.
choiceExplanations.Washer: Correct — lock washers and spring washers maintain bolt tension and bite into surfaces to prevent nuts and bolts from loosening.
choiceExplanations.Rivet: A rivet is a permanent unthreaded pin fastener, not an anti-loosening device for bolts.
choiceExplanations.Bushing: A bushing is a cylindrical sleeve lining a bore to reduce friction or size a shaft.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A device usually used to connect two shafts on a direct drive system

choiceExplanations.Bearing: A bearing supports a rotating shaft and reduces friction rather than connecting two collinear shafts.
choiceExplanations.Coupler: Correct — a coupler (shaft coupling) joins two collinear shafts end-to-end to transmit torque directly.
choiceExplanations.Sprocket: A sprocket is a toothed wheel that drives or is driven by a roller chain.
choiceExplanations.Pulley: A pulley is a grooved or crowned wheel used with belts or ropes for indirect drive.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Domesticated animals used as power for agriculture.

choiceExplanations.Fattening animals: Fattening animals are livestock raised specifically to gain body weight for meat production.
choiceExplanations.Draft animals: Correct — draft animals such as carabaos, oxen, and horses are domesticated animals trained to pull farm loads and implements.
choiceExplanations.Breeding animals: Breeding animals are kept primarily for reproduction and herd improvement rather than farm traction.
choiceExplanations.Dairy animals: Dairy animals are livestock raised mainly for milk production rather than mechanical draft work.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A gas that produces putrefactive bacteria that breaks down organic material under airless condition consisting mainly of methane and carbon dioxide.

choiceExplanations.Biogas: Correct — biogas is produced by anaerobic bacterial digestion of organic matter, yielding primarily methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2).
choiceExplanations.Propane: Propane is a petroleum-derived liquefied hydrocarbon gas rather than an anaerobic fermentation product.
choiceExplanations.Syngas: Syngas is a hydrogen and carbon monoxide mixture generated by high-temperature thermochemical gasification.
choiceExplanations.Ethane: Ethane is a minor natural-gas hydrocarbon component, not the main product of anaerobic digesters.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A substance that is added to the tractor for the purpose of changing traction and stability.

choiceExplanations.Lubricant: A lubricant reduces friction and wear between moving engine or transmission parts.
choiceExplanations.Ballast: Correct — ballast is added weight (cast iron weights or liquid in tires) placed on a tractor to improve traction and stability.
choiceExplanations.Coolant: Coolant circulates through the engine cooling system to dissipate combustion heat.
choiceExplanations.Antifreeze: Antifreeze lowers coolant freezing point and raises boiling point inside an engine radiator.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Dimensions of flat belts are designated by its

choiceExplanations.Width and diameter: Belt size does not include pulley diameter; flat belt cross-section uses width and thickness.
choiceExplanations.Pitch and angle: Pitch line and included groove angle characterize V-belts rather than flat belts.
choiceExplanations.Length and pitch: Pitch length and tooth pitch specify synchronous timing belts or chain drives.
choiceExplanations.Width and thickness: Correct — flat belt cross-sectional dimensions are standardized and specified by belt width and thickness (or ply count).

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A hand operated tractor which is suitable for both primary and secondary tillage used when field has been soaked for at least half a day to soften the soil

choiceExplanations.Traction-type walking tractor: Traction-type walking tractors pull mounted implements using wheels rather than floating on mud.
choiceExplanations.Rotary-type power tiller: Standard rotary power tillers rely on soil-engaging wheels or skids and sink in deep mud.
choiceExplanations.Standard-type two-wheel tractor: Standard two-wheel tractors use pneumatic or cage wheels that bog down in deeply soaked paddy mud.
choiceExplanations.Puddling-type floating tiller: Correct — per PAES standards, a puddling-type floating tiller rides on a float board over soaked soil for primary and secondary tillage.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Optimum axle speed for puddling-type floating tiller

choiceExplanations.305 rpm: Exceeding the 250 rpm optimum axle speed wastes power and splashes mud excessively.
choiceExplanations.200 rpm: Running at 200 rpm produces insufficient puddling and churning action on soaked paddy soil.
choiceExplanations.250 rpm: Correct — Philippine agricultural engineering standards specify 250 rpm as the optimum axle speed for a puddling-type floating tiller.
choiceExplanations.230 rpm: An axle speed of 230 rpm falls below the standard 250 rpm design value.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The sum of all resistance acting on the tractor

choiceExplanations.Rolling resistance: Rolling resistance is only the soil and tire deformation component resisting forward travel.
choiceExplanations.Air resistance: Air resistance is solely the aerodynamic drag acting against the moving tractor body.
choiceExplanations.Slope resistance: Slope resistance is only the gravitational component opposing motion when climbing an incline.
choiceExplanations.Running resistance: Correct — running resistance is the total sum of rolling, air, acceleration, and slope resistances opposing tractor movement.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Running resistance of a tractor includes
items.answer: Rolling, air and acceleration, and slope resistance
choices: Tractive, brake and steering, and hitch resistance
Rolling, air and acceleration, and slope resistance
Soil, tire and implement, and drawbar resistance
Draft, wheel and transmission, and axle resistance

choiceExplanations.Tractive, brake and steering, and hitch: Tractive force propels the tractor while braking and hitch loads are separate from running resistance.
choiceExplanations.Rolling, air and acceleration, and slope: Correct — tractor running resistance sums rolling resistance, aerodynamic/inertial (air and acceleration) resistance, and grade or slope resistance.
choiceExplanations.Soil, tire and implement, and drawbar re: Implement and drawbar loads represent external draft rather than tractor running resistance components.
choiceExplanations.Draft, wheel and transmission, and axle: Transmission and axle losses are internal drivetrain losses, not external running resistance.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: To shift implements weight to the tractors drive wheel in order to improve traction

choiceExplanations.Weight transfer means: Correct — weight transfer shifts part of the implement and front-axle load onto the rear drive wheels to boost traction.
choiceExplanations.Depth control mechanism: A depth control mechanism maintains a preset tillage depth rather than specifically shifting weight for traction.
choiceExplanations.Ballast distribution method: Ballasting adds dead weights to the tractor rather than transferring dynamic implement weight.
choiceExplanations.Draft control system: Draft control automatically raises or lowers the three-point hitch to keep implement draft constant.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: An international testing center for tractor

choiceExplanations.California: California does not house the internationally recognized OECD-accredited Nebraska Tractor Test Laboratory.
choiceExplanations.Nebraska: Correct — the Nebraska Tractor Test Laboratory (University of Nebraska–Lincoln) is the official US and international tractor testing center.
choiceExplanations.Michigan: Michigan State conducts agricultural research, not the official statutory US tractor testing program.
choiceExplanations.Iowa: Iowa State hosts agricultural engineering programs rather than the official Nebraska Tractor Test Lab.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A tillage implement consisting of two or four gangs of concave disks

choiceExplanations.Rotary tiller: A rotary tiller uses L-shaped or C-shaped blades on a PTO-driven horizontal rotor.
choiceExplanations.Moldboard plow: A moldboard plow uses curved bottom shares and moldboards rather than gangs of disks.
choiceExplanations.Disk harrow: Correct — a disk harrow arranges concave steel disks on common shafts into two (single-action) or four (tandem) gangs.
choiceExplanations.Disk plow: A disk plow mounts large individual concave disks on separate standards rather than common gang shafts.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A procedure in which planting is made directly into an essentially unprepared seedbed

choiceExplanations.Strip tillage: Strip tillage tills narrow bands along crop rows while leaving inter-row areas undisturbed.
choiceExplanations.Conventional tillage: Conventional tillage performs full-width primary and secondary operations to prepare a clean seedbed.
choiceExplanations.Minimum tillage: Minimum tillage reduces the number of passes but still disturbs more soil than direct seeding.
choiceExplanations.Zero tillage: Correct — zero tillage (no-till) plants seeds directly into an essentially undisturbed seedbed covered with previous crop residue.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A tillage and land forming operation using a tool which splits the soil and turns two furrows laterally in opposite directions, thereby providing a ridge and furrow soil configurations

choiceExplanations.Listing: Correct — listing uses a double-moldboard lister or middlebuster to split soil laterally in opposite directions, forming ridges and furrows.
choiceExplanations.Subsoiling: Subsoiling shatters deep compacted hardpans vertically without turning soil into ridges and furrows.
choiceExplanations.Chiseling: Chiseling loosens soil with narrow rigid or spring shanks without inverting or ridging furrows.
choiceExplanations.Harrowing: Harrowing breaks clods, levels the surface, and kills weeds during secondary tillage.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The angle, in a vertical plane perpendicular to the direction of travel, between a centralized tool or reference axis and the soil surface

choiceExplanations.Disk angle: Disk angle is measured in the horizontal plane between the disk face and the direction of travel.
choiceExplanations.Tilt angle: Correct — per ASABE tillage terminology, tilt angle lies in a vertical plane perpendicular to travel between the tool axis and soil surface.
choiceExplanations.Rake angle: Rake angle lies in a vertical plane parallel to travel between the tool face and horizontal.
choiceExplanations.Clearance angle: Clearance angle prevents the tool heel from rubbing the cut soil surface behind the cutting edge.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Dit is a part of the plow button which helps to counteract the side pressure exerted by the furrow slice

choiceExplanations.Landside: Correct — the landside is the flat side plate of a moldboard plow bottom that slides against the furrow wall to counter side thrust.
choiceExplanations.Moldboard: The moldboard is the curved upper plate that lifts, pulverizes, and inverts the cut furrow slice.
choiceExplanations.Frog: The frog is the central structural casting to which the share, moldboard, and landside bolt.
choiceExplanations.Share: The share is the sharp lower wedge that cuts the furrow slice horizontally from the subsoil.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A type of plow which has two sets of bodies mounted symmetrically on a share frame that can be rotated over 180 degrees along the longitudinal axis

choiceExplanations.Reversible plow: Correct — a reversible (two-way) plow carries opposed left- and right-hand bodies rotated 180 degrees at headlands to throw all furrows one way.
choiceExplanations.Subsoil plow: A subsoil plow uses deep vertical shanks to fracture hardpans rather than rotating opposed plow bodies.
choiceExplanations.Moldboard plow: A standard one-way moldboard plow turns furrows to only one side and lacks a 180-degree turnover frame.
choiceExplanations.Chisel plow: A chisel plow uses narrow curved shanks for non-inversion tillage without symmetric rotatable bodies.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Percentage of work done in pulling an average plow

choiceExplanations.16%: Standard agricultural machinery references allocate 18%, not 16%, of plow draft work to pulling the plow.
choiceExplanations.22%: Allocating 22% overestimates the friction/pulling share relative to the classic 48%-34%-18% plow energy breakdown.
choiceExplanations.18%: Correct — classic moldboard plow draft energy studies attribute about 18% of total work to overcoming friction and pulling the plow.
choiceExplanations.20%: A 20% value slightly overstates the classic 18% portion used in pulling an average plow.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Percentage of work of plow used in cutting furrow slice

choiceExplanations.40%: A 40% share underestimates the standard reviewer figure of 43% for cutting the furrow slice.
choiceExplanations.38%: Cutting the slice takes the largest single share of plow draft, higher than 38%.
choiceExplanations.43%: Correct — standard agricultural power references cite 43% (approx. 43–48%) of plow work for cutting the furrow slice.
choiceExplanations.52%: A 52% share overstates the cutting fraction when combined with turning and pulling losses.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Percentage of work of plow used in turning slice of soil

choiceExplanations.44%: Turning the slice consumes less power than cutting, making 44% too high.
choiceExplanations.34%: Correct — standard tillage references attribute about 34% of total moldboard plow work to lifting and turning the furrow slice.
choiceExplanations.31%: A 31% share underestimates the classic 34% energy fraction spent turning the furrow slice.
choiceExplanations.30%: A 30% figure falls below the established 34% energy share for turning soil.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A point in which all the horizontal and vertical forces in the plow meets

choiceExplanations.Center of mass: Center of mass is the geometric balance point of the plow's material weight, not soil forces.
choiceExplanations.Center of pressure: Center of pressure applies mainly to fluid or aerodynamic pressure distributions on submerged surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Center of resistance: Correct — the center of resistance is the point on a plow bottom where resultant horizontal and vertical soil forces converge.
choiceExplanations.Center of gravity: Center of gravity is where gravitational weight acts, distinct from resultant soil reaction forces.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A type of plow designed to reduced friction by making a rolling bottom instead of slides along the furrow

choiceExplanations.Rotary plow: A rotary plow uses rotating blades driven by the tractor PTO rather than rolling disk bottoms.
choiceExplanations.Disk plow: Correct — a disk plow uses freely rotating concave disks that roll through soil, reducing sliding friction in sticky or rocky ground.
choiceExplanations.Moldboard plow: A moldboard plow slides along the furrow bottom and wall, creating higher sliding friction.
choiceExplanations.Chisel plow: A chisel plow drags stationary rigid or spring shanks through soil rather than rolling bottoms.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A primary tillage plow for rice farming that is attached in replacement to the cage wheel of a power tiller

choiceExplanations.Chisel: A chisel plow is a tractor-drawn shank implement, not mounted in place of cage wheels.
choiceExplanations.Moldboard: A moldboard plow attaches behind a power tiller via a hitch rather than replacing cage wheels.
choiceExplanations.Rotary: A rotary tiller mounts at the rear PTO or gearbox rather than replacing traction cage wheels.
choiceExplanations.Spiral: Correct — a spiral plow mounts directly onto the power tiller axle in place of cage wheels to till and propel in wetland rice.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: An angle of the disc plow in reference to the vertical plane.

choiceExplanations.Disk angle: Disk angle is the angle of the disk plane relative to the forward direction of travel.
choiceExplanations.Lead angle: Lead angle describes helix or gear tooth inclination, not standard disk plow geometry.
choiceExplanations.Pitch angle: Pitch angle refers to blade or propeller inclination rather than vertical disk plow tilt.
choiceExplanations.Tilt angle: Correct — disk plow tilt angle is the inclination of the disk face measured from the vertical plane (typically 15–25 degrees).

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: An angle of the disk plow in reference to the direction of travel of the plow

choiceExplanations.Tilt angle: Tilt angle is measured relative to the vertical plane rather than the direction of travel.
choiceExplanations.Lead angle: Lead angle describes screw thread or gear helix geometry, not disk plow travel alignment.
choiceExplanations.Disk angle: Correct — disk angle is the horizontal angle between the disk plane and the direction of travel (commonly 42–45 degrees).
choiceExplanations.Pitch angle: Pitch angle denotes fore-and-aft rotation or blade inclination rather than horizontal disk angle.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A plow that combines the primary and secondary tillage at the same time. It is used to cut and to pulverize the soil

choiceExplanations.Disk plow: A disk plow cuts and turns soil in primary tillage without powered pulverization.
choiceExplanations.Chisel plow: A chisel plow fractures deep soil without inverting or finely pulverizing the seedbed.
choiceExplanations.Moldboard plow: A moldboard plow turns furrow slices in primary tillage, requiring secondary harrowing to pulverize clods.
choiceExplanations.Rotary plow: Correct — a rotary plow (rotavator) uses PTO-driven rotating blades to cut, invert, and pulverize soil in one pass.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The power requirement of a rotary tiller for primary tillage

choiceExplanations.30kw/m: Correct — standard farm machinery references cite approximately 30 kW per meter of working width for primary rotary tillage.
choiceExplanations.25kw/m: A 25 kW/m figure underestimates the heavy PTO power demand of primary rotary tilling.
choiceExplanations.20kw/m: A 20 kW/m power rating is typical of lighter secondary tillage rather than deep primary tilling.
choiceExplanations.35kw/m: A 35 kW/m figure exceeds the standard 30 kW/m rule-of-thumb requirement for primary rotary tillage.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A plow primarily for loosening the soil

choiceExplanations.Disk plow: A disk plow cuts and partially inverts soil slices rather than simply loosening them.
choiceExplanations.Moldboard plow: A moldboard plow cuts and completely inverts the furrow slice to bury surface residue.
choiceExplanations.Rotary plow: A rotary plow aggressively chops and pulverizes soil using powered rotating tines.
choiceExplanations.Chisel plow: Correct — a chisel plow pulls narrow curved shanks through soil to shatter and loosen it without inversion.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A plow that is used to break up plow sole

choiceExplanations.Subsoiler: Correct — a subsoiler operates below normal plowing depth (typically 40–70 cm) to shatter dense plow soles and hardpans.
choiceExplanations.Cultivator: A cultivator performs shallow secondary tillage between crop rows to control weeds.
choiceExplanations.Middlebuster: A middlebuster splits topsoil laterally to form ridges and furrows rather than breaking deep hardpans.
choiceExplanations.Rotavator: A rotavator pulverizes shallow topsoil layers and can actually contribute to plow pan formation.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A gang arrangement often called as "tandem harrow"

choiceExplanations.Offset gang: An offset disk harrow uses two opposing gangs arranged one behind the other, throwing soil opposite ways.
choiceExplanations.Double action: Correct — a double-action (tandem) disk harrow has four gangs: two front gangs throwing soil outward and two rear gangs inward.
choiceExplanations.Triple action: Triple-action is not a standard disk harrow gang classification in agricultural machinery.
choiceExplanations.Single action: A single-action disk harrow has only two opposing gangs positioned side-by-side in a single row.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The actual coverage rate by an implement based on the total field tiime

choiceExplanations.Rated field capacity: Rated capacity is a nominal manufacturer specification rather than actual measured field coverage.
choiceExplanations.Material field capacity: Material capacity measures mass harvested or processed per hour (t/h), not area per hour.
choiceExplanations.Effective field capacity: Correct — effective field capacity is the actual area covered per unit time, accounting for turns, stops, and overlap over total field time.
choiceExplanations.Theoretical field capacity: Theoretical field capacity assumes continuous operation at full width and speed with zero lost time.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The disk angle that will give the minimum draft for a disk plow for a given width of cut is

A 30–35 degree disk angle provides too narrow a cut and excessive side draft.
Exceeding 45 degrees increases soil throwing and draft unnecessarily for a given cut width.
Angles of 35–40 degrees require higher draft per unit cut width than 40–45 degrees.
Correct — disk plow tests show minimum draft per unit width occurs at a disk angle of 40–45 degrees (typically 42–45°).

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Seeding directly into previously undisturbed soil

choiceExplanations.Mulch-till: Mulch-till disturbs the entire soil surface before planting while leaving residue mixed near the surface.
choiceExplanations.Ridge-till: Ridge-till scrapes ridge tops and plants seeds on preformed ridges rather than undisturbed flat soil.
choiceExplanations.No-till: Correct — no-till (zero tillage) places seeds directly into previously undisturbed soil through narrow planter slots.
choiceExplanations.Strip-till: Strip-till cultivates narrow 15–25 cm bands along future seed rows before planting.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The strip of the land at the ends of the field used for turning by field machinery

choiceExplanations.Border strip is: Border strips are parallel diked strips used in surface border irrigation, not turning strips.
choiceExplanations.Dead furrow is: A dead furrow is the open trench left where two plow slices are turned away from each other.
choiceExplanations.Back furrow is: A back furrow is the raised ridge formed where two first-pass furrow slices overlap.
choiceExplanations.Headland is: Correct — the headland is the unplowed or turning strip at each end of a field reserved for machinery maneuvers.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A machine that prepares the soil, meters the seed, and positions the seed in one operation

choiceExplanations.Broadcaster: A spreader that scatters seeds or granular materials randomly over the soil surface without metering into furrows.
choiceExplanations.Planter: A seeding machine designed primarily for row-crop precision hill or single-seed spacing rather than continuous drill metering.
choiceExplanations.Drill: Correct — A seed drill opens furrows, meters seeds continuously, and covers them in a single pass.
choiceExplanations.Transplanter: A machine that places pre-grown seedlings rather than raw seeds into prepared soil.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A machine which is cylindrical in shape designed for planting a pre-germinated rice seed in rows

choiceExplanations.Grain drill: A tractor-drawn or animal-drawn drill using furrow openers and fluted or double-run meters for dryland small grains.
choiceExplanations.Drum seeder: Correct — A drum seeder uses perforated cylindrical hoppers pulled across puddled soil to drop pre-germinated rice seeds in rows.
choiceExplanations.Rotary seeder: A seeder with a rotating disk or impeller mechanism rather than cylindrical perforated drums for puddled rice.
choiceExplanations.Punch planter: A planter that punches discrete holes through soil or mulch and drops seeds into hills.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A scattering of seeds on the surface of prepared soil

choiceExplanations.Dibbling: Placing seeds manually or mechanically into individual holes made at specific intervals in the soil.
choiceExplanations.Drilling: Depositing seeds continuously in furrows at a controlled depth and covering them with soil.
choiceExplanations.Transplanting: Moving established seedlings from a nursery bed and setting them into the main field.
choiceExplanations.Broadcasting: Correct — Broadcasting scatters seeds uniformly across the prepared soil surface without forming discrete rows or holes.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is a planting method wherein seeds are deposited, either singly or in group, in a water soluble tape under controlled condition

choiceExplanations.Check-row planting: Planting seeds in hills aligned in two perpendicular directions to permit cross-cultivation.
choiceExplanations.Hill-drop planting: Dropping groups of two or more seeds together at fixed intervals along a row.
choiceExplanations.Furrow-band planting: Placing seeds or chemicals in a narrow strip or band inside an opened furrow.
choiceExplanations.Seed-tape planting: Correct — Seed-tape planting embeds single or grouped seeds in water-soluble tape under controlled conditions before laying in soil.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A mechanical or thermal device that produces a liquid dispersion having a volume median diameter of less that 50 um

choiceExplanations.Mist blower: An air-carrier sprayer that produces larger mist droplets typically around 50 to 100 micrometers in diameter.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic atomizer: A nozzle using liquid pressure alone to break spray into relatively coarse droplets above 100 micrometers.
choiceExplanations.Aerosol generator: Correct — An aerosol generator mechanically or thermally atomizes liquid into fine droplets with volume median diameter under 50 micrometers.
choiceExplanations.Pneumatic sprayer: A compressed-air sprayer that forces liquid through a nozzle, generally producing coarser sprays than aerosols.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The ratio of knife velocity to forward velocity of rice reaper

choiceExplanations.1.08: This velocity ratio is too low for clean cutting and causes excessive stalk bending in rice reapers.
choiceExplanations.1.35: Correct — PAES standards specify a knife-to-forward velocity ratio around 1.35 for efficient cutting performance in rice reapers.
choiceExplanations.1.55: Higher than the standard 1.35 design ratio used for typical walking-type rice reapers.
choiceExplanations.1.46: Exceeds the standard 1.35 knife-to-forward speed ratio specified for rice reaper cutting mechanisms.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A steel containing 0.035-0.4% carbon and is widely used for production of steel plate, structural steel, bars, etc

choiceExplanations.High-carbon steel: Steel containing roughly 0.6% to 1.5% carbon, used for springs, cutting edges, and wear parts.
choiceExplanations.Mild steel: Correct — Mild (low-carbon) steel contains roughly 0.035% to 0.4% carbon and is standard for plates, bars, and structural members.
choiceExplanations.Tool steel: High-alloy, high-carbon steel formulated for high hardness and wear resistance in dies and cutting tools.
choiceExplanations.Medium-carbon steel: Steel with roughly 0.3% to 0.6% carbon, favored for shafts, gears, and forged parts needing higher strength.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The center to center distance between overlapping broadcast applications

choiceExplanations.Spacing: The center-to-center distance between adjacent crop rows, nozzles, or planting hills rather than broadcast passes.
choiceExplanations.Drift: Unintended off-target movement of spray droplets or particles carried away by wind during application.
choiceExplanations.Overlap: The width by which adjacent application passes intersect to ensure uniform coverage across edges.
choiceExplanations.Swath: Correct — Effective swath width is the center-to-center distance between successive overlapping passes in broadcast application.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The portion of combine comprising the mechanism for gathering crops

choiceExplanations.Star wheel: Correct — In PAES/ASABE rice harvesting terminology, the star wheel mechanism gathers standing stalks toward the cutter bar.
choiceExplanations.Cutter bar: The reciprocating sickle-bar assembly that severs crop stalks rather than gathering them into the header.
choiceExplanations.Gathering chain: A lugged chain used primarily on row-crop headers like corn heads rather than general crop-gathering combine reels.
choiceExplanations.Pickup reel: A rotating reel with spring tines used specifically to lift lodged or windrowed crops off the ground.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A gas, a liquid , or a solid used to propel or transport chemical

choiceExplanations.Surfactant: A surface-active agent added to reduce surface tension and improve wetting, spreading, or emulsification.
choiceExplanations.Diluent: An inert liquid or solid added to reduce active-ingredient concentration rather than specifically propel the chemical.
choiceExplanations.Carrier: Correct — A carrier is the gas, liquid, or solid medium used to transport or propel the active chemical to its target.
choiceExplanations.Adjuvant: Any additive mixed with a pesticide formulation to modify spray characteristics or enhance biological effectiveness.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The draft of implement in terms of force per unit area of tilled cross-section

choiceExplanations.Side draft: The lateral horizontal force component perpendicular to the direction of travel caused by asymmetrical implement loading.
choiceExplanations.Horizontal draft: The total horizontal component of pull parallel to the line of travel, not divided by cross-sectional area.
choiceExplanations.Unit draft: Draft expressed per unit width of the implement or per plow bottom rather than per cross-sectional area.
choiceExplanations.Specific draft: Correct — Specific draft is the implement draft divided by the cross-sectional area of the tilled soil furrow.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A clutch that is used to drive a machine element in only one direction is

choiceExplanations.Friction clutch: A clutch that transmits torque in either direction through clamping pressure between friction plates.
choiceExplanations.Overrunning clutch: Correct — An overrunning (one-way) clutch transmits torque in only one rotational direction and freewheels when driven faster from the load.
choiceExplanations.Centrifugal clutch: A clutch that engages automatically above a threshold rotational speed via centrifugal weights, regardless of direction.
choiceExplanations.Slip clutch: An overload protection clutch that slips when torque exceeds a preset limit rather than restricting rotation direction.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The unbroken side off furrow is called

choiceExplanations.Furrow crown: The rounded top ridge formed by the inverted soil slice turned over by the moldboard.
choiceExplanations.Furrow wall: Correct — The furrow wall is the vertical, undisturbed side of the furrow left after the plow share cuts the slice.
choiceExplanations.Furrow sole: The horizontal bottom surface of the open furrow left beneath the cut furrow slice.
choiceExplanations.Furrow slice: The ribbon of soil severed, lifted, and inverted by the plow bottom during tillage.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: When 30% or less of the soil surface is tilled, the tillage operation employed is

choiceExplanations.Minimum tillage: A broad conservation approach reducing tillage passes to preserve residue, not defined specifically by a 30% tilled limit.
choiceExplanations.Ridge tillage: Planting crops on preformed permanent or semi-permanent ridges while leaving inter-row residue undisturbed.
choiceExplanations.Mulch tillage: Full-width soil loosening with sweep or chisel implements that leaves crop residue on the surface.
choiceExplanations.Strip tillage: Correct — Strip tillage disturbs only narrow planting bands covering 30% or less of the soil surface, leaving middles untilled.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A soil tool reaction in which soil slides over the surface of the tillage tool without significant adhesion

choiceExplanations.Pulverizing: Breaking soil clods into finer aggregates through impact, crushing, or secondary tillage action.
choiceExplanations.Scouring: Correct — Scouring occurs when soil flows smoothly across a polished moldboard or blade without sticking to the metal.
choiceExplanations.Shattering: Fracturing compacted soil into irregular blocks and cracks along natural planes of weakness.
choiceExplanations.Shearing: Cutting or sliding soil along a failure plane under applied normal and tangential stress.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A booklet provided by manufacturers in which steb by step procedure for repair or disassembly of parts are given

choiceExplanations.Parts manual: An illustrated catalog listing part numbers, exploded assemblies, and component names for ordering replacements.
choiceExplanations.Owners manual: General ownership documentation covering basic operation, warranty, and routine care rather than detailed repair disassembly.
choiceExplanations.Technical manual: Correct — A technical (service/shop) manual provides step-by-step disassembly, troubleshooting, tolerances, and repair procedures for technicians.
choiceExplanations.Operators manual: A field-oriented booklet detailing safe operation, adjustments, and daily maintenance rather than full shop disassembly.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A booklet form provided by manufacturers in which adjustment, care and maintenance procedure, and safety of the machine are

choiceExplanations.Parts manual: A catalog of exploded diagrams and part numbers used to identify and order replacement components.
choiceExplanations.Assembly manual: Instructions focused on putting together shipped machine components before initial delivery or field use.
choiceExplanations.Operators manual: Correct — An operator's manual instructs the user on machine adjustments, routine care, maintenance schedules, and safe operation.
choiceExplanations.Technical manual: A service publication intended for mechanics covering detailed overhaul, teardown, and diagnostic repair procedures.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is the line of pull that is straight from center of load through the point where the drawbar of the draft is attached to the drawbar of the tractor

choiceExplanations.Horizontal line draft: The top-view projection of the line of pull relating lateral hitch alignment to the center of resistance.
choiceExplanations.Vertical line draft: Correct — The vertical line of draft is the side-view line from center of load through the implement-to-tractor drawbar hitch point.
choiceExplanations.Lateral line draft: Refers to side-to-side force offset rather than the vertical-plane line through the drawbar hitch.
choiceExplanations.Resultant line draft: The three-dimensional combined force vector rather than the vertical-plane line of pull described here.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is the line of draft that is straight line from the center of resistance or load to the point where plow drawbar is attached to the tractor drawbar

choiceExplanations.Horizontal line draft: Correct — The horizontal line of draft is the plan-view straight line connecting the plow's center of resistance to the tractor drawbar hitch.
choiceExplanations.Lateral line draft: A non-standard term referring to sideways draft offset rather than the horizontal-plane hitch line.
choiceExplanations.Resultant line draft: The combined 3D pull vector rather than the horizontal plan-view line between resistance and drawbar.
choiceExplanations.Vertical line draft: The side-view line of pull governing hitch height and vertical weight transfer onto tractor wheels.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The rate of planting, or pounds of seeds planted per acre that gives a desired quality of plants without thinning is

choiceExplanations.Direct row seeding: Sowing seeds directly into field rows rather than transplanting, without implying zero thinning.
choiceExplanations.Precision hill planting: Placing exact seed counts into spaced hills, which may still require thinning depending on emergence.
choiceExplanations.Optimum seeding rate: The general seed rate maximizing yield, whereas this question specifies achieving final stand without thinning.
choiceExplanations.Planting to stand: Correct — Planting to stand meters seeds at the exact rate needed to establish the desired plant population without thinning.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Tractor tire used to propel as well as to provide good floatation is

choiceExplanations.Traction tire: A deep-lugged drive tire designed primarily to transmit high drawbar pull rather than steer and float.
choiceExplanations.Implement tire: A free-rolling tire built to carry trailed implement loads rather than propel or steer a tractor.
choiceExplanations.Drive tire: A rear or powered wheel tire optimized for maximum soil grip and torque transmission.
choiceExplanations.Steering tire: Correct — In standard ABE reviewer classification, the steering tire provides directional control, flotation, and propulsion support on tractors.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Bearings used for disk plow bottom are

choiceExplanations.Needle roller bearing: A compact radial bearing with thin rollers that cannot support the heavy thrust loads of a disk plow.
choiceExplanations.Tapered roller bearing: Correct — Tapered roller bearings withstand both the large radial and axial thrust loads generated by angled disk plow bottoms.
choiceExplanations.Cylindrical roller bearing: A bearing suited for heavy radial loads but offering little or no axial thrust capacity.
choiceExplanations.Spherical roller bearing: A self-aligning heavy-duty bearing used primarily for shaft misalignment rather than standard disk plow hubs.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A compartment provided for the harrow aid in penetration

choiceExplanations.Depth wheels: Gauge wheels that limit maximum working depth rather than adding ballast for deeper penetration.
choiceExplanations.Gang frames: Structural beams holding disk gangs together rather than compartments built specifically to hold ballast.
choiceExplanations.Trash guards: Shields or scrapers that prevent crop residue from wrapping around bearings and shafts.
choiceExplanations.Weight boxes: Correct — Weight boxes are trays or compartments mounted on harrows to hold ballast that increases soil penetration.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Substance added to spray as stickers, stabilizers and conditioning

choiceExplanations.Mineral oil: Refined petroleum oil often used directly as a spray oil or dormant insecticide rather than this reviewer key.
choiceExplanations.Petroleum gas: Correct — In standard PRC ABELE reviewer keys, petroleum gas is listed as the substance used as spray stickers, stabilizers, and conditioners.
choiceExplanations.Kerosene distillate: A light petroleum fraction formerly used as a solvent carrier rather than a sticker or conditioning additive.
choiceExplanations.Anhydrous ammonia: A pressurized nitrogen fertilizer injected into soil, not a pesticide spray sticker or stabilizer.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Pump recommended for a sprayer that is used for abrasive spray materials

choiceExplanations.Diaphragm pump: Correct — A diaphragm pump isolates moving mechanical parts behind flexible membranes, making it ideal for abrasive wettable powders.
choiceExplanations.Roller pump: A positive-displacement pump whose nylon or rubber rollers wear rapidly when pumping abrasive suspensions.
choiceExplanations.Gear pump: A metal-gear pump with tight clearances that quickly abrade when handling gritty or suspended spray materials.
choiceExplanations.Piston pump: Uses tight-fitting pistons and cylinders that suffer accelerated seal and liner wear from abrasive particles unless specially lined.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Approximate pressure used in spraying wedicide

choiceExplanations.10–25 psi: Too low for proper fan-pattern formation with standard hydraulic herbicide nozzles, causing uneven coverage.
choiceExplanations.25-40 psi: Correct — Weedicide (herbicide) spraying typically uses 25–40 psi to produce coarse droplets that minimize drift while covering weeds.
choiceExplanations.40–55 psi: Higher than typical herbicide pressures, increasing fine droplets and wind-drift hazard onto sensitive crops.
choiceExplanations.55–70 psi: Excessive pressure suited for high-pressure fungicide or insecticide penetration rather than herbicide application.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A machine used to kill weed seeds by microwave heating during weeding operation

choiceExplanations.Steamer: Uses pressurized hot steam rather than microwave electromagnetic energy to kill weeds and soil pests.
choiceExplanations.Zapper: Correct — A microwave weed zapper radiates high-frequency electromagnetic waves into soil to destroy weed seeds thermally.
choiceExplanations.Flamer: Burns LP gas or fuel to apply direct open flame for thermal weed control.
choiceExplanations.Scorcher: Relies on radiant or direct flame heat rather than microwave dielectric heating of weed seeds.
