items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A device used to hold spray nozzle close to the soil so those chemicals can be sprayed on young grass in plant row

choiceExplanations.Drift hood: A shroud enclosing a boom section primarily to block wind drift rather than position nozzles along rows.
choiceExplanations.Spray shield: Correct — A spray shield holds nozzles close to the ground and shields crop foliage during directed inter-row spraying.
choiceExplanations.Boom drop: A vertical extension tube lowering nozzles between tall crop rows without necessarily enclosing or shielding the spray.
choiceExplanations.Nozzle guard: A protective cage shielding nozzle tips from mechanical impact rather than directing low inter-row sprays.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is used between the cultivator sweep and the plant row to prevent soil from covering small young plants

choiceExplanations.Colter: A sharp rolling disk mounted ahead of a plow bottom to slice crop residue and furrow walls.
choiceExplanations.Shank: The vertical or curved structural leg connecting a cultivator tool to the toolbar frame.
choiceExplanations.Sweep: A V-shaped flat cutting blade attached to a cultivator shank to undercut weeds below the surface.
choiceExplanations.Fender: Correct — A fender (crop shield) rides between cultivator sweeps and young crop rows to keep thrown soil from burying seedlings.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: When the soil is thrown to the plant during cultivation, the operation is

choiceExplanations.Sub-soiling: Deep tillage below the normal plow pan to break compacted layers without mounding soil onto rows.
choiceExplanations.Side-dressing: Applying fertilizer alongside growing crop rows rather than specifically throwing soil toward plant bases.
choiceExplanations.Off-barring: Throwing soil away from the crop row toward the furrow middle during early cultivation.
choiceExplanations.Hilling-up: Correct — Hilling-up throws loose inter-row soil toward the base of growing plants to suppress weeds and support roots.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is the true point of hitch or center of pull of an implement

choiceExplanations.Center of power: Correct — The center of power is the true hitch point or effective line of pull from the tractor.
choiceExplanations.Center of resistance: The resultant point on the implement where all soil and operating resistances effectively act.
choiceExplanations.Center of gravity: The point where the entire weight of the tractor or implement is balanced.
choiceExplanations.Center of load: Another term for center of resistance on the implement rather than the tractor hitch point.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The effective drawbar pull of the tractor is reduced for every percent grade by

choiceExplanations.4%: Four times the actual drawbar pull loss, overestimating the gravity resistance per percent slope.
choiceExplanations.3%: Overestimates the drawbar pull reduction caused by lifting tractor and implement weight up a 1% grade.
choiceExplanations.2%: Double the standard rule of thumb of 1% drawbar pull reduction per 1% upward slope.
choiceExplanations.1%: Correct — Each 1% upward grade adds grade resistance equal to 1% of gross weight, reducing effective drawbar pull by about 1%.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: An instrument used to measure the draft of a plow

choiceExplanations.Tensiometer: A soil-moisture sensor measuring soil water matric tension in kilopascals or centibars.
choiceExplanations.Tachometer: An instrument that measures rotational speed in revolutions per minute of a shaft or engine.
choiceExplanations.Penetrometer: A cone-tipped probe used to measure soil penetration resistance or compaction rather than implement draft.
choiceExplanations.Dynamometer: Correct — A traction dynamometer is inserted at the hitch to directly measure the pulling force (draft) of a plow.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The maximum friction in the moldboard plow is

choiceExplanations.At the heel of landside: Experiences sliding contact against the furrow wall and sole, but lower normal pressure than the share point.
choiceExplanations.At the wing of moldboard: Turns the lifted furrow slice near the rear edge, where soil pressure and friction are lower.
choiceExplanations.At the rear of frog: Serves as an internal mounting bracket bolted behind the share, moldboard, and landside, not contacting soil directly.
choiceExplanations.At the point of share: Correct — The share point first penetrates and wedges into uncut soil, experiencing the highest soil pressure and friction.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A primary or secondary tillage implement used for broadcast or for strip tillage and also used as chemical incorporators prior to planting

choiceExplanations.Disk harrow: A secondary tillage implement with angled concave disks used to cut clods and residue, not specifically strip-till incorporation.
choiceExplanations.Rotary hoe: A high-speed crust-breaking and early-weeding tool with curved spoon tines rather than a primary/secondary strip tiller.
choiceExplanations.Roller tiller: Correct — A roller tiller performs broadcast or strip tillage and incorporates pre-plant chemicals uniformly ahead of planting.
choiceExplanations.Field cultivator: Uses spring-tine shanks for seedbed preparation and weed control without roller-tiller strip incorporation design.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is a plow consisting of a strongly constructed frame and a vertical leg drawn to a subsoil and the bullet shape attachment creates a tube like cavity acting as a drainage channel

choiceExplanations.Mole plow: Correct — A mole plow pulls a cylindrical bullet-shaped torpedo through clay subsoil to form unlined underground drainage channels.
choiceExplanations.Chisel plow: Uses narrow curved shanks to shatter soil deeply without inverting it or forming drainage tunnels.
choiceExplanations.Subsoil plow: Breaks deep compacted hardpans using heavy vertical shanks, typically without a bullet-shaped mole attachment for drainage.
choiceExplanations.Lister plow: A double-moldboard plow that throws soil both ways to form alternating ridges and surface furrows.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A kind of chemical used for spraying which form a finely-divided solid particles when mixed with water

choiceExplanations.Solution: A homogeneous liquid mixture where the chemical completely dissolves at the molecular level without solid particles.
choiceExplanations.Suspension: Correct — A suspension disperses finely divided solid pesticide particles (e.g., wettable powders) throughout water without dissolving.
choiceExplanations.Emulsion: A dispersion of tiny liquid droplets (such as oil) suspended inside an immiscible liquid like water.
choiceExplanations.Aerosol: Fine liquid or solid particles dispersed in a gas medium rather than mixed in water.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: An insecticide that kills insects when insects suck on plant tissues

choiceExplanations.Fumigant: A volatile chemical acting in the gaseous phase through the insect's respiratory system.
choiceExplanations.Repellent: A substance that deters pests from feeding or landing without directly killing them upon sap ingestion.
choiceExplanations.Systemic: Correct — A systemic insecticide is absorbed and translocated through plant sap, poisoning insects that pierce and suck plant tissues.
choiceExplanations.Contact: An insecticide that kills pests upon direct external body contact rather than through plant sap ingestion.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is the cultivation of one crop underneath a perennial crop

choiceExplanations.Inter-culture: Correct — Inter-culture is the practice of cultivating shorter-duration annual or understory crops beneath an established perennial crop canopy.
choiceExplanations.Relay-cropping: Planting a second crop into a standing first crop shortly before the first crop is harvested.
choiceExplanations.Strip-cropping: Growing different crops in alternating wide strips across a field, typically for erosion control.
choiceExplanations.Alley-cropping: Growing arable crops in open alleys between hedgerows of planted trees or shrubs rather than directly underneath a canopy.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Application of chemical to a small restricted area, usually to control the spread of pest

choiceExplanations.Broadcast treatment: Uniformly applying a chemical over an entire field or target area rather than restricted patches.
choiceExplanations.Band treatment: Applying chemical in narrow parallel strips along crop rows while leaving inter-row spaces untreated.
choiceExplanations.Spot treatment: Correct — Spot treatment targets chemicals onto localized infested patches or small restricted areas to halt pest spread.
choiceExplanations.Space treatment: Dispersing fog, mist, or vapor into an enclosed volume of air to contact flying or exposed pests.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Dispersion of liquid or dry particles in air in such a manner that target pest are exposed to chemical

choiceExplanations.Band treatment: Applying chemical in narrow linear strips along planted rows rather than dispersing particles in air.
choiceExplanations.Spot treatment: Targeting small localized ground or plant patches rather than filling an air volume with dispersed chemical.
choiceExplanations.Space treatment: Correct — Space treatment disperses fine droplets, dust, or aerosols into the air so airborne or exposed pests contact the chemical.
choiceExplanations.Foliar treatment: Applying spray directly onto plant leaves and stems rather than treating the surrounding airspace.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Application of chemical to a specific area such as row, bed, or at base of the plant

choiceExplanations.Aerial application: Applying agricultural chemicals from aircraft over broad fields rather than targeting specific row bases.
choiceExplanations.Foliar application: Spraying chemicals onto leaves and stems rather than targeting the soil bed or plant base.
choiceExplanations.Broadcast application: Spreading chemicals uniformly over the whole field surface without confining to rows or beds.
choiceExplanations.Direct application: Correct — Direct (directed) application places chemicals precisely onto targeted zones such as rows, beds, or plant bases.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Application of chemical to the stem, fruit, leaves, needles, or blades of a plant

choiceExplanations.Basal application: Applying chemical strictly to the lower trunk or base of trees and woody stems.
choiceExplanations.Band application: Applying chemical in narrow strips along rows rather than specifically targeting aerial plant foliage.
choiceExplanations.Foliar application: Correct — Foliar application delivers sprays or nutrients directly onto above-ground plant parts including leaves, stems, fruits, and needles.
choiceExplanations.Broadcast application: Treating an entire field area uniformly rather than targeting plant foliage specifically.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Application of chemical over entire area to be treated

choiceExplanations.Spot application: Restricting chemical delivery to small, isolated pest patches rather than treating the whole field.
choiceExplanations.Broadcast application: Correct — Broadcast application distributes a chemical uniformly over the entire target area without leaving untreated strips.
choiceExplanations.Band application: Applying chemical in narrow strips over or beside rows while leaving middles untreated.
choiceExplanations.Basal application: Confining chemical placement to the base or lower trunk of trees and shrubs.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Application of chemical to the base of a tree around the trunk or by injection into slasher or cuts

choiceExplanations.Broadcast application: Uniformly covering an entire field area rather than treating individual tree trunks.
choiceExplanations.Foliar application: Applying chemical to leaves and canopy stems rather than the lower trunk or bark cuts.
choiceExplanations.Basal application: Correct — Basal application treats the lower trunk collar of trees or introduces herbicide into bark frills and cuts.
choiceExplanations.Band application: Placing chemical in continuous parallel row strips rather than around individual tree bases.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Application of chemicals in parallel strips leaving the area between strips free of chemical

choiceExplanations.Spot application: Treating isolated patches of pests rather than continuous parallel strips across rows.
choiceExplanations.Broadcast application: Applying chemical across the entire surface without leaving untreated gaps between strips.
choiceExplanations.Band application: Correct — Band application applies chemicals in narrow parallel strips along rows while leaving inter-row spaces untreated.
choiceExplanations.Basal application: Treating only the lower trunk base or bark cuts of woody plants.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Soil blocks or masses that are cut, sheared or broken loose by tillage tool

choiceExplanations.Ped: A naturally formed soil aggregate bound together by natural pedogenic processes rather than tillage fracture.
choiceExplanations.Clod: Correct — A clod is a coherent mass of soil broken, sheared, or cut loose artificially by tillage implements.
choiceExplanations.Hardpan: A dense, compacted subsurface soil layer resistant to root and water penetration.
choiceExplanations.Crust: A thin, hard surface soil layer formed by raindrop impact and drying rather than tillage shearing.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The amount paid for hiring equipment and operating services to perform a certain task

choiceExplanations.Ownership cost: Annual fixed expenses of owning a machine, such as depreciation, interest, taxes, insurance, and housing.
choiceExplanations.Variable cost: Operating expenses incurred per hour of running owned machinery, including fuel, oil, repairs, and labor.
choiceExplanations.Custom cost: Correct — Custom cost is the contracted fee paid to hire both external equipment and an operator to perform a farm operation.
choiceExplanations.Fixed cost: Expenses that remain constant regardless of annual machine use, such as depreciation and insurance.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A sprayer designed to charge the spray droplet so that there is a powerful attraction between the plants and the charged droplet

choiceExplanations.Pneumatic sprayer: Uses compressed air to atomize and propel liquid spray without applying an electrical charge.
choiceExplanations.Electrostatic sprayer: Correct — An electrostatic sprayer imparts an electric charge to droplets so electrostatic attraction pulls them onto grounded plant surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic sprayer: Uses pressurized liquid forced through small nozzles to form droplets without electrostatic charging.
choiceExplanations.Air-blast sprayer: Uses a high-velocity fan airstream to carry hydraulic droplets into tree canopies without charging droplets.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is used to protect tractor operator from dust, noise, rain and heat

choiceExplanations.Shield: A guard covering moving machine parts or crop rows rather than enclosing the tractor operator.
choiceExplanations.Cab: Correct — A tractor cab is a fully enclosed operator compartment protecting against dust, noise, rain, and excessive heat.
choiceExplanations.Fender: A wheel cover protecting the operator from mud and debris thrown by tires, not enclosing against noise or heat.
choiceExplanations.Canopy: An overhead roof offering shade and rain shelter without enclosed walls against dust and noise.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A harvest residue discharged from cleaning devices of a combine

choiceExplanations.Chaffs: Correct — Chaff consists of light seed coverings and fine crop residues discharged from the combine's cleaning shoe.
choiceExplanations.Stalks: Stalks are the main upright structural stems of plants rather than fine material expelled by cleaning devices.
choiceExplanations.Straws: Straw refers to the coarser, longer stems discharged from the straw walkers or rotor, not the cleaning sieve.
choiceExplanations.Stubble: Stubble is the short base of crop stems left standing rooted in the field after harvesting.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The perpendicular distance between the upper hitch point and the common axis of the lower hitch point of a tractor

choiceExplanations.Drawbar height: Drawbar height is the vertical distance from the ground to the tractor's drawbar hitch plane.
choiceExplanations.Mast height: Correct — Mast height is the perpendicular distance between the upper hitch point and the common axis of the lower hitch points.
choiceExplanations.Lift height: Lift height is the maximum vertical distance an implement can be raised above the ground.
choiceExplanations.Transport height: Transport height is the ground clearance beneath a raised implement during road or field travel.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: ASAE: slow moving vehicle velocity

choiceExplanations.40kph: Correct — Under ASAE/ASABE S276, a slow-moving vehicle (SMV) is designed to operate at maximum speeds up to 40 km/h (25 mph).
choiceExplanations.45kph: 45 km/h exceeds the ASAE/ASABE S276 slow-moving vehicle emblem speed limit of 40 km/h.
choiceExplanations.30kph: 30 km/h falls below the 40 km/h (25 mph) upper threshold defined in ASAE S276.
choiceExplanations.35kph: 35 km/h is lower than the standard 40 km/h (25 mph) ASAE slow-moving vehicle limit.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Factor which consider the physical condition, heart beat ratio, and body weight of a person when operating a machine

choiceExplanations.Safety factor: Safety factor relates to machine guards, failure margins, and hazard prevention rather than physiological measurements.
choiceExplanations.Ergonomic factor: Correct — Ergonomic factors evaluate human physical condition, heart rate ratio, body weight, and operator comfort during machine operation.
choiceExplanations.Environmental factor: Environmental factors involve external ambient conditions like temperature, noise, dust, and terrain rather than operator physiology.
choiceExplanations.Operational factor: Operational factors concern field speed, turning time, and scheduling efficiency rather than human physical biometrics.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Maximum tire inflation pressure for agricultural implement

choiceExplanations.55psi: 55 psi is below the standard 60 psi maximum inflation pressure rating for agricultural implement tires.
choiceExplanations.50psi: 50 psi is lower than the typical 60 psi maximum allowable inflation pressure for implement tires.
choiceExplanations.65psi: 65 psi exceeds the 60 psi maximum inflation limit and risks tire damage or blowout.
choiceExplanations.60psi: Correct — Agricultural implement tires under standard PAES/ASABE guidelines have a maximum inflation pressure rating of 60 psi.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is structural member of an implement where tillage tool to be a beam attached

choiceExplanations.Coulter: A coulter is a rolling disk blade mounted ahead of the plow bottom to cut trash and soil.
choiceExplanations.Frog: A frog is the central casting or bracket of a moldboard plow bottom uniting share, moldboard, and landside.
choiceExplanations.Landside: A landside is the flat plate on a moldboard plow bottom that slides against the furrow wall for stability.
choiceExplanations.Shank: Correct — A shank is the structural member or standard connecting the soil-engaging tillage tool to the implement frame or beam.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Recommended material in the manufacture of pin sleeve and hitch pin for walking type power tiller

choiceExplanations.Stainless steel: Stainless steel is costly and unnecessary for standard PAES walking-type power tiller hitch pins and sleeves.
choiceExplanations.High-carbon steel: High-carbon steel is overly brittle for shock-loaded hitch pins compared to tougher cold-rolled steel.
choiceExplanations.Hot-rolled steel: Hot-rolled steel lacks the dimensional accuracy and surface finish specified by PAES for hitch pins and sleeves.
choiceExplanations.Cold-rolled steel: Correct — PAES 109 specifies cold-rolled steel for manufacturing the pin sleeve and hitch pin of walking-type power tillers.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A centrifugal pump that develops a vacuum sufficient enough for atmospheric pressure ro force the liquid though the suction pipes into the pump casing without initially feeding the pump to create suction

choiceExplanations.Self-priming pump: Correct — A self-priming centrifugal pump evacuates air from the suction line using retained casing liquid to create vacuum without manual priming.
choiceExplanations.Booster pump: A booster pump increases pressure in an already pressurized line rather than priming dry suction piping.
choiceExplanations.Multistage pump: A multistage pump uses multiple impellers in series to generate high head, requiring manual priming unless self-priming.
choiceExplanations.End-suction pump: A standard end-suction centrifugal pump requires its suction pipe and casing to be pre-filled before starting.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is a metallic or synthetic lining for a hole which reduces or prevents abrasion between components of a machine

choiceExplanations.Bushing: Correct — A bushing is a cylindrical metallic or synthetic sleeve lining a hole to reduce friction and prevent abrasion.
choiceExplanations.Bearing: A bearing is a broader assembly, often with rolling elements, supporting rotating shafts rather than simply lining a hole.
choiceExplanations.Collar: A collar is a ring clamped onto a shaft to locate components axially, not a hole lining.
choiceExplanations.Gasket: A gasket is a static deformable seal placed between mating flanges to prevent fluid leakage.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: When does a substance oxidized?

choiceExplanations.When it gains electrons: Gaining electrons corresponds to chemical reduction, not oxidation.
choiceExplanations.When it gains protons: Gaining protons changes an atom's atomic number or acidity (Brønsted base), not oxidation state.
choiceExplanations.When it loses protons: Losing protons reflects acid dissociation rather than an electron-transfer oxidation reaction.
choiceExplanations.When it loses electrons: Correct — Oxidation is the loss of electrons from an atom, ion, or molecule, increasing its oxidation state.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: How many significant figures are there in 100000.0000?

choiceExplanations.8: Counting only 8 omits two trailing zeros that are significant after the decimal point.
choiceExplanations.10: Correct — All 10 digits in 100000.0000 are significant because trailing zeros to the right of a decimal point are significant.
choiceExplanations.14: The number 100000.0000 only contains 10 total digits, so it cannot have 14 significant figures.
choiceExplanations.12: The number 100000.0000 has only 10 digits in total, making 12 significant figures impossible.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The two countries that established Massey Ferguson / Tractors were the

choiceExplanations.FRANCE and UNITED KINGDOM: Massey-Harris originated in Canada, not France, before merging with Britain's Harry Ferguson.
choiceExplanations.CANADA and UNITED STATES: Harry Ferguson was based in the United Kingdom rather than the United States during the 1953 merger.
choiceExplanations.CANADA and UNITED KINGDOM: Correct — Massey Ferguson formed in 1953 from the merger of Canadian manufacturer Massey-Harris and British tractor maker Ferguson.
choiceExplanations.UNITED STATES and GERMANY: Neither the United States nor Germany founded the 1953 Massey-Harris-Ferguson merger.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What component of force is used in savonius windmills?

choiceExplanations.Centrifugal Force: Centrifugal force acts radially outward on rotating blades and does not provide the driving torque.
choiceExplanations.Thrust Force: Thrust force pushes axially along the wind direction on a rotor rather than spinning a Savonius drum.
choiceExplanations.Drag Force: Correct — A Savonius vertical-axis wind turbine relies primarily on differential aerodynamic drag between its concave and convex scoops.
choiceExplanations.Lift Force: Lift force drives Darrieus and modern horizontal-axis propellers, whereas Savonius rotors are predominantly drag-driven.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In thermodynamics, it pertains to the region of study separate from the environment or surroundings.

choiceExplanations.Reservoir: A thermal reservoir is a large body with constant temperature that exchanges heat with a system.
choiceExplanations.Universe: The thermodynamic universe comprises both the system and its surroundings combined.
choiceExplanations.Boundary: A boundary is the real or imaginary surface separating the system from its surroundings.
choiceExplanations.System: Correct — In thermodynamics, a system is the specified quantity of matter or region in space chosen for study.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Food safety hazard that pertains to bacteria and viruses:

choiceExplanations.Biological hazard: Correct — Biological hazards in food safety encompass living microorganisms and pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites.
choiceExplanations.Radiological hazard: Radiological hazards involve ionizing radiation or radioactive isotopes contaminating food, not microorganisms.
choiceExplanations.Physical hazard: Physical hazards are foreign solid objects like glass, metal fragments, or stones inside food products.
choiceExplanations.Chemical hazard: Chemical hazards involve toxic substances like pesticides, heavy metals, allergens, or cleaning residues.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A system that automatically regulates the speed of an engine.

choiceExplanations.Lubrication system: The lubrication system reduces friction and cools moving engine parts using pressurized or splashed oil.
choiceExplanations.Governing system: Correct — The governing system automatically senses engine speed and adjusts fuel or throttle to maintain target rpm under varying loads.
choiceExplanations.Carburetion system: The carburetion system meters and atomizes fuel with intake air rather than autonomously regulating engine speed.
choiceExplanations.Ignition system: The ignition system provides the high-voltage spark to ignite the air-fuel mixture in spark-ignition engines.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Heart of the agricultural machinery manufacturing, marketing, and after-sales service in the Philippines:

choiceExplanations.AMTEC: AMTEC at UPLB focuses on testing and evaluating agricultural machinery rather than industry manufacturing and marketing.
choiceExplanations.BAFE: BAFE is the Department of Agriculture's regulatory and engineering bureau, not the machinery dealers' association.
choiceExplanations.AMMDA: Correct — The Agricultural Machinery Manufacturers and Distributors Association (AMMDA) represents the core of Philippine machinery manufacturing, marketing, and after-sales service.
choiceExplanations.PSAE: PSAE (now PSABE) is the professional society of agricultural and biosystems engineers, not a trade association.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The difference between the present values of the project benefits and project costs:

choiceExplanations.Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR): Benefit-Cost Ratio is the quotient of discounted benefits divided by discounted costs, not their difference.
choiceExplanations.Capitalized Cost (CC): Capitalized Cost is the present worth of an infinitely lived project or perpetual cost stream.
choiceExplanations.Net Present Value (NPV): Correct — Net Present Value (NPV) is calculated by subtracting the present value of costs from the present value of benefits.
choiceExplanations.Internal Rate of Return (IRR): Internal Rate of Return is the discount rate at which a project's Net Present Value equals zero.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Shall act as an advisory body to ensure the success of DA programs concerning agricultural and fisheries mechanization (RA 10601, Section 23):

choiceExplanations.AFMeC: Correct — Under RA 10601 Section 23, the Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization Committee (AFMeC) under PCAF advises DA on mechanization programs.
choiceExplanations.BAFE: BAFE implements engineering standards, infrastructure, and mechanization programs under DA rather than serving as the advisory committee.
choiceExplanations.PCAF: PCAF houses and provides secretariat support to AFMeC, whereas AFMeC itself is the mandated advisory committee.
choiceExplanations.PhilMech: PhilMech leads mechanization research, development, and extension under Section 7 rather than acting as the Section 23 advisory body.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In engineering economy, the formula F = P(F/P, i%, n) represents which factor?

choiceExplanations.Uniform series compound amount factor: The uniform series compound amount factor is (F/A, i%, n), converting equal periodic payments A to future worth F.
choiceExplanations.Single-payment compound amount factor: Correct — The factor (F/P, i%, n) = (1 + i)^n is the single-payment compound amount factor converting present P to future F.
choiceExplanations.Uniform series sinking fund factor: The sinking fund factor is (A/F, i%, n), finding equal periodic deposits A from a future sum F.
choiceExplanations.Single-payment present worth factor: The single-payment present worth factor is (P/F, i%, n), discounting a future amount F back to present P.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Seeds grown from SeedNet and selected accredited growers:

choiceExplanations.Registered seed: Correct — Registered seeds are the progeny of foundation seed, grown by SeedNet members and selected accredited seed growers.
choiceExplanations.Breeder seed: Breeder seed is the initial genetically pure seed produced directly by the originating plant breeder or institution.
choiceExplanations.Certified seed: Certified seed is the progeny of registered seed produced by general accredited growers for commercial farmer planting.
choiceExplanations.Foundation seed: Foundation seed is the direct progeny of breeder seed maintained under strict control by research institutions.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Hydropower plant with a capacity ranging from 5 kW to 300 kW:

choiceExplanations.Mini-hydro: Mini-hydro systems typically range above micro-hydro capacity (commonly 301 kW to 10 MW depending on classification).
choiceExplanations.Micro-hydro: Correct — Under Philippine Department of Energy classifications, micro-hydropower plants cover generating capacities from 5 kW to 300 kW.
choiceExplanations.Small-hydro: Small-hydro plants have larger capacities, typically ranging from 1 MW up to 10 MW or more.
choiceExplanations.Pico-hydro: Pico-hydro plants are the smallest class, generating less than 5 kW of electrical power.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A power tool with saw teeth on a continuous blade or band:

choiceExplanations.Scroll saw: A scroll saw uses a short, thin reciprocating blade for intricate curves rather than a continuous loop.
choiceExplanations.Miter saw: A miter saw uses a rigid circular blade mounted on a swing arm for angled crosscuts.
choiceExplanations.Circular saw: A circular saw cuts using a rotating toothed disc rather than a continuous flexible band.
choiceExplanations.Band saw: Correct — A band saw uses a long, continuous loop of toothed metal band stretched over two or more wheels.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In engineering economy, the formula P = A(P/A, i%, n) represents which factor?

choiceExplanations.Uniform series sinking fund factor: The sinking fund factor is (A/F, i%, n), calculating periodic payments A required to reach future sum F.
choiceExplanations.Uniform series compound amount factor: The uniform series compound amount factor is (F/A, i%, n), summing periodic payments A to future F.
choiceExplanations.Uniform series present worth factor: Correct — The factor (P/A, i%, n) is the uniform series present worth factor converting equal payments A into present value P.
choiceExplanations.Uniform series capital recovery factor: The capital recovery factor is (A/P, i%, n), converting a present sum P into equal periodic payments A.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In engineering economy, the formula A = P(A/P, i%, n) represents which factor?

choiceExplanations.Uniform series capital recovery factor: Correct — The factor (A/P, i%, n) is the uniform series capital recovery factor finding equal payments A from present value P.
choiceExplanations.Uniform series compound amount factor: The uniform series compound amount factor is (F/A, i%, n), finding future sum F from uniform series A.
choiceExplanations.Uniform series present worth factor: The uniform series present worth factor is (P/A, i%, n), finding present value P from uniform series A.
choiceExplanations.Uniform series sinking fund factor: The sinking fund factor is (A/F, i%, n), finding equal periodic deposits A from future value F.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Agency that primarily takes the lead in overall research, development, and extension (RDE) in farm and fisheries mechanization in the Philippines (RA 10601, Section 7):

choiceExplanations.PCAARRD: PCAARRD is a DOST sectoral council that coordinates agricultural R&D rather than leading DA's RDE mechanization mandate.
choiceExplanations.AMTEC: AMTEC at UPLB handles official agricultural and fisheries machinery testing and evaluation, not national RDE leadership.
choiceExplanations.BAFE: BAFE oversees engineering programs, regulation, and standards implementation under DA, rather than leading RDE under Section 7.
choiceExplanations.PhilMech: Correct — Under RA 10601 Section 7, PhilMech serves as the lead agency for agricultural and fisheries mechanization RDE.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Level of operation where the investment neither produces a profit nor incurs a loss:

choiceExplanations.Margin of safety: Margin of safety measures how far current or budgeted sales exceed the break-even sales level.
choiceExplanations.Break-even point: Correct — The break-even point is the output or revenue level where total revenues equal total costs, yielding zero profit or loss.
choiceExplanations.Shutdown point: The shutdown point is the minimum price or output below which a firm cannot even cover variable costs.
choiceExplanations.Payback period: Payback period is the time required for cumulative net cash inflows to recover an initial investment.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: University-based agency responsible for testing and evaluation of agricultural and fisheries machinery (UPLB):

choiceExplanations.PCAARRD: PCAARRD is a DOST R&D coordinating council, not a machinery testing center based at UPLB.
choiceExplanations.BAFE: BAFE is a bureau of the Department of Agriculture rather than a UPLB-based machinery testing agency.
choiceExplanations.PHILMECH: PHILMECH is a DA agency headquartered in Nueva Ecija focused on mechanization RDE, not UPLB testing.
choiceExplanations.AMTEC: Correct — Under RA 10601, the Agricultural Machinery Testing and Evaluation Center (AMTEC) at UPLB conducts official machinery testing.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It consists of the clutch, gearbox, differential, and brake system:

choiceExplanations.Fuel supply system: The fuel supply system stores, filters, and delivers fuel to the engine cylinders.
choiceExplanations.Power transmission system: Correct — The power transmission system includes the clutch, gearbox, differential, final drives, and brakes to control and transmit engine power.
choiceExplanations.Steering control system: The steering control system directs the front or articulated wheels to guide tractor travel.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic lift system: The hydraulic lift system uses pressurized fluid to raise, lower, and control mounted implements.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Type of food safety hazard when paralytic shellfish toxin is found in a food product:

choiceExplanations.Chemical hazard: Correct — Paralytic shellfish toxin (saxitoxin) is a naturally occurring marine biotoxin classified under chemical food safety hazards.
choiceExplanations.Biological hazard: Biological hazards involve living pathogens (bacteria, viruses, parasites), whereas toxins themselves are classified as chemical hazards.
choiceExplanations.Physical hazard: Physical hazards consist of solid foreign contaminants like glass shards, metal pieces, or bone fragments.
choiceExplanations.Radiological hazard: Radiological hazards involve radioactive materials or ionizing radiation, not marine algal toxins.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A thermodynamic system where both energy and matter can exchange with the surroundings:

choiceExplanations.Closed system: A closed system allows energy transfer across its boundary but prohibits mass exchange with surroundings.
choiceExplanations.Open system: Correct — An open thermodynamic system (control volume) permits both mass and energy to cross its boundary.
choiceExplanations.Isolated system: An isolated system prevents both matter and energy from crossing its boundary.
choiceExplanations.Adiabatic system: An adiabatic system is one thermally insulated so no heat crosses its boundary, regardless of mass flow.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Application fee for wastewater reuse according to the Department of Agriculture (DA):

choiceExplanations.₱500.00: ₱500.00 is not the prescribed DA Administrative Order No. 2007-26 fee for wastewater reuse applications.
choiceExplanations.₱600.00: Correct — Under DA Administrative Order No. 26 (Series of 2007), the application fee for wastewater reuse certification is ₱600.00.
choiceExplanations.₱1,000.00: ₱1,000.00 exceeds the ₱600.00 DA application fee for agricultural wastewater reuse.
choiceExplanations.₱300.00: ₱300.00 is half the official ₱600.00 DA application fee for wastewater reuse.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: For an ideal gas, the volume at constant pressure is directly proportional to the absolute temperature:

choiceExplanations.Gay-Lussac's Law: Gay-Lussac's Law states that pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature at constant volume.
choiceExplanations.Avogadro's Law: Avogadro's Law states that gas volume is proportional to number of moles at constant temperature and pressure.
choiceExplanations.Charles' Law: Correct — Charles' Law states that for a fixed mass of ideal gas at constant pressure, volume varies directly with absolute temperature.
choiceExplanations.Boyle's Law: Boyle's Law states that gas pressure is inversely proportional to volume at constant temperature.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Approximate number of G.I. rivets per kilogram:

choiceExplanations.180: Correct — Standard galvanized iron (G.I.) roofing rivets average approximately 180 pieces per kilogram in Philippine construction estimates.
choiceExplanations.120: 120 pieces per kilogram underestimates the standard count for G.I. roofing rivets.
choiceExplanations.150: 150 pieces per kilogram is lower than the standard 180 G.I. rivets per kilogram estimate.
choiceExplanations.220: 220 pieces per kilogram overestimates the typical count of standard G.I. roofing rivets.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Type of roadside ditch intended to convey large flows in areas with limited right-of-way:

choiceExplanations.Roadside rectangular ditch: Correct — Under PAES 421, rectangular roadside ditches carry large discharge volumes efficiently where right-of-way width is limited.
choiceExplanations.Roadside parabolic ditch: Parabolic ditches mimic natural channels and resist erosion, but require wider right-of-way for large flows.
choiceExplanations.Roadside trapezoidal ditch: Trapezoidal ditches have sloped sides requiring wider right-of-way compared to vertical-walled rectangular ditches.
choiceExplanations.Roadside triangular ditch: Triangular V-ditches carry smaller flows and require flatter side slopes that consume more lateral width.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Law of Thermodynamics stating that the total entropy of an isolated system can never decrease over time:

choiceExplanations.0th Law of Thermodynamics: The Zeroth Law defines thermal equilibrium and serves as the basis for temperature measurement.
choiceExplanations.1st Law of Thermodynamics: The First Law states the conservation of energy, meaning energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
choiceExplanations.3rd Law of Thermodynamics: The Third Law states that a pure crystal's entropy approaches zero as temperature approaches absolute zero.
choiceExplanations.2nd Law of Thermodynamics: Correct — The Second Law of Thermodynamics states that the total entropy of an isolated system always increases or remains constant.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Which of the following is a good electrical insulator?
items.rationale: Mica is a non-metallic silicate mineral with high dielectric strength and heat resistance, making it an effective electrical insulator, whereas brass, tin, and platinum are electrical conductors.

choiceExplanations.Mica: Correct — Mica is a silicate mineral with high dielectric strength and low conductivity, making it an excellent electrical insulator.
choiceExplanations.Platinum: Platinum is a precious metallic element and a good electrical conductor, not an insulator.
choiceExplanations.Brass: Brass is a copper-zinc metallic alloy widely used for electrical contacts and conductors.
choiceExplanations.Tin: Tin is a conductive metal commonly used in electrical solder alloys rather than insulation.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A side lapping width covering of 70 cm corrugated G.I sheet

choiceExplanations.1.5 inches: Correct — Standard corrugated G.I. sheet side lapping (1.5 corrugations) covers about 1.5 inches on a 70-cm effective width sheet.
choiceExplanations.1.7 inches: 1.7 inches does not match the standard 1.5-inch side-lapping allowance used for 70-cm corrugated G.I. sheets.
choiceExplanations.1.2 inches: 1.2 inches is narrower than the standard 1.5-inch side overlap for corrugated G.I. sheets.
choiceExplanations.1.4 inches: 1.4 inches slightly understates the standard 1.5-inch side-lap width for corrugated G.I. roofing sheets.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: MEMBERS OF THE BOARD
items.rationale: 1.ariodear c. rico (chairman) / 2.juana t. tapel (member) / 3.sherwin o valdez (member

choiceExplanations.baldwin g. jallorina (chairman): Engr. Baldwin G. Jallorina served as PhilMech Executive Director, not Chairman of the PRC ABE Board.
choiceExplanations.arnold r. elepano (chairman): Dr. Arnold R. Elepaño is a UPLB professor and ABE educator, not the PRC Board Chairman referenced here.
choiceExplanations.dionisio g. alvindia (chairman): Dr. Dionisio G. Alvindia served as PhilMech Executive Director, not Chairman of the PRC ABE Board.
choiceExplanations.1.ariodear c. rico (chairman): Correct — Engr. Ariodear C. Rico has served as the Chairman of the PRC Board of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the specific measure of pitot-tube?
items.source: RECALLED COMPRESS PART 2; area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Static head: Static head is measured by a wall piezometer tap perpendicular to flow, not a Pitot tube.
choiceExplanations.Total head: Correct — A Pitot tube facing into the fluid stream measures the stagnation (total) head, equal to static plus velocity head.
choiceExplanations.Elevation head: Elevation head is the vertical height of a fluid point above an arbitrary datum plane.
choiceExplanations.Velocity head: Velocity head is found using a Pitot-static differential tube by subtracting static pressure from total pressure.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A male or female ox under a year old?

choiceExplanations.Heifer: A heifer is a young female bovine that has not yet borne a calf, typically over one year old.
choiceExplanations.Steer: A steer is a castrated male bovine raised primarily for beef production.
choiceExplanations.Calf: Correct — A calf is a young male or female bovine (ox/cattle) under one year of age.
choiceExplanations.Yearling: A yearling is a young animal between one and two years of age.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: “Zero” is what kind of number?

choiceExplanations.Integer: Correct — Zero is an integer, belonging to the set of whole numbers {...,-2, -1, 0, 1, 2,...}.
choiceExplanations.Irrational number: Irrational numbers cannot be written as fractions of two integers, whereas zero equals 0/1.
choiceExplanations.Imaginary number: Imaginary numbers involve multiples of the imaginary unit i (√-1), whereas zero is a real number.
choiceExplanations.Prime number: Prime numbers are integers greater than 1 with exactly two positive divisors, excluding zero.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The power rating classification for the four wheel standard light tractor

choiceExplanations.66–83hp: 66 to 83 hp corresponds to a higher heavy/medium-heavy tractor class under PAES tractor classifications.
choiceExplanations.49–66hp: 49 to 66 hp falls into the standard medium tractor power rating classification.
choiceExplanations.32 to 49hp: Correct — Under PAES 118, a four-wheel standard light agricultural tractor has a rated power of 32 to 49 hp (24–37 kW).
choiceExplanations.15–32hp: 15 to 32 hp corresponds to the compact or mini four-wheel tractor category.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: a way of redesigning products and product systems so that they are in harmony with natural ecological cycles

choiceExplanations.End-of-pipe control: End-of-pipe control treats pollutants after generation rather than redesigning products to eliminate waste at source.
choiceExplanations.Clean production: Correct — Clean production redesigns products and processes to eliminate waste and align industrial systems with natural ecological cycles.
choiceExplanations.Linear production: Linear production follows a take-make-dispose model that depletes resources and accumulates waste.
choiceExplanations.Waste remediation: Waste remediation cleans up existing environmental contamination rather than preventing it through product redesign.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: inflow to a groundwater reservoir

choiceExplanations.Groundwater overdraft: Groundwater overdraft occurs when extraction exceeds natural recharge over time, depleting the aquifer.
choiceExplanations.Groundwater mining: Groundwater mining is the unsustainable pumping of non-renewable fossil water faster than it replenishes.
choiceExplanations.Groundwater recharge: Correct — Groundwater recharge is the downward infiltration and inflow of surface water into a groundwater aquifer.
choiceExplanations.Groundwater discharge: Groundwater discharge is the outflow of water from an aquifer to springs, streams, or wells.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: earthquakes produced by sudden movement along faults and plate boundaries

choiceExplanations.Tectonic: Correct — Tectonic earthquakes result from sudden slip and energy release along geological faults and tectonic plate boundaries.
choiceExplanations.Volcanic: Volcanic earthquakes are triggered specifically by magma movement and pressure changes beneath active volcanoes.
choiceExplanations.Collapse: Collapse earthquakes are small local tremors caused by underground cavern or mine roof failures.
choiceExplanations.Explosion: Explosion earthquakes are artificially induced seismic waves generated by chemical or nuclear detonations.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: earthquake produced by movement of magma beneath volcanoes

choiceExplanations.Explosion: Explosion earthquakes are man-made seismic events caused by detonating nuclear or chemical explosives.
choiceExplanations.Tectonic: Tectonic earthquakes occur from sudden movement along faults and plate boundaries, not magma intrusion.
choiceExplanations.Volcanic: Correct — Volcanic earthquakes are generated by the ascent, pressure buildup, and fracturing caused by moving magma beneath volcanoes.
choiceExplanations.Collapse: Collapse earthquakes result from the caving-in of underground mines or karst caves.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: is defined as a fault that has moved within the last 10,000 years.

choiceExplanations.Active fault: Correct — PHIVOLCS defines an active fault as a geological fault that has moved within the last 10,000 years (Holocene epoch).
choiceExplanations.Potentially active fault: A potentially active fault shows geological signs of past displacement without confirmed movement in the last 10,000 years.
choiceExplanations.Dormant fault: Dormant fault is a loose non-standard term for a fault showing no recent historic activity.
choiceExplanations.Inactive fault: An inactive fault has shown no displacement over millions of years and poses negligible seismic hazard.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is Field Efficiency of Rice Combine?

choiceExplanations.70%: 70% is below the standard 75% minimum field efficiency specified for rice combines under PAES.
choiceExplanations.75%: Correct — Under PAES 224 (Rice Combine Harvester specifications), the standard minimum field efficiency is 75%.
choiceExplanations.80%: 80% exceeds the 75% standard field efficiency benchmark typically assigned to rice combine harvesters.
choiceExplanations.65%: 65% is lower than the PAES-specified 75% field efficiency for self-propelled rice combines.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the color when it is stop in PAG-ASA?
items.answer: Answer: red Yellow means caution Green means go
choices: Answer: red Yellow means caution Green means go
Answer: orange Red means caution Green means go
Answer: yellow Red means caution Green means go
Answer: green Yellow means caution Red means go

choiceExplanations.Answer: red Yellow means caution Green m: Correct — In standard warning color coding (red-yellow-green), red signals stop/danger, yellow signals caution/alert, and green signals go/safe.
choiceExplanations.Answer: orange Red means caution Green m: Red indicates stop/evacuation rather than caution, while orange denotes a higher preparedness warning.
choiceExplanations.Answer: yellow Red means caution Green m: Yellow denotes caution or alert, not stop, whereas red signifies stop or danger.
choiceExplanations.Answer: green Yellow means caution Red m: Green indicates safe/go conditions, not stop, while red indicates stop or severe danger.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Difference between obtained value to true value

choiceExplanations.Tolerance: Tolerance is the permissible limit of variation in a physical dimension or specified measurement value.
choiceExplanations.Deviation: Deviation is the difference between a single observed value and the mean of measurements.
choiceExplanations.Uncertainty: Uncertainty is a quantitative parameter characterizing the dispersion of values reasonably attributed to a measurand.
choiceExplanations.Error: Correct — measurement error is defined as the difference between an obtained or measured value and the true value.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: a generation in a breeding experiment that is successive to a mating between parents of two distinctively different but usually relatively pure genotypes

choiceExplanations.Outcross generation: Outcross generation results from mating unrelated individuals, usually to introduce new genetic traits into a line.
choiceExplanations.Parental generation: Parental generation (P) consists of the original distinct pure-breeding individuals crossed at the start of an experiment.
choiceExplanations.Backcross generation: Backcross generation comes from crossing a hybrid progeny back to one of its original parental genotypes.
choiceExplanations.Filial generation: Correct — the filial generation (F1, F2, etc.) denotes successive offspring produced after crossing two distinct parental genotypes.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Typically defined as the difference in height between the high point and the low point on a landscape

choiceExplanations.Gradient: Gradient refers to the rate of elevation change per unit horizontal distance, or slope steepness.
choiceExplanations.Aspect: Aspect is the compass direction that a terrain slope faces, such as north or east.
choiceExplanations.Relief: Correct — topographic relief is the vertical elevation difference between the highest and lowest points on a landscape.
choiceExplanations.Elevation: Elevation is the vertical height of a single point relative to a reference datum like mean sea level.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A separate area for the emptying and cleansing of stomach and intestines and for the preparation of casings tripe or edible fat

choiceExplanations.Dressing area: Dressing area is where slaughtered carcasses undergo hide removal, evisceration, splitting, and washing.
choiceExplanations.Gut room/tripery: Correct — under slaughterhouse standards, the gut room or tripery handles stomach and intestine emptying, casings, tripe, and edible fat.
choiceExplanations.Chilling room: Chilling room is a refrigerated chamber used to rapidly cool dressed carcasses and prevent microbial spoilage.
choiceExplanations.Bleeding room: Bleeding room is the slaughter area where stunned animals are stuck and drained of blood.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Percentage of groundwater on the earth surface

choiceExplanations.0.35(Fresh) –0.62(saline): This range underestimates global groundwater share; fresh groundwater is about 0.76% and saline groundwater about 0.93% of total water.
choiceExplanations.0.54(Fresh) –0.81(saline): This range is lower than standard hydrologic estimates of 0.76% fresh and 0.93% saline groundwater.
choiceExplanations.0.76(Fresh) –0.93(saline): Correct — standard global water distribution estimates place fresh groundwater at 0.76% and saline groundwater at 0.93% of Earth's water.
choiceExplanations.1.15(Fresh) –1.38(saline): This range overstates global groundwater; actual shares are approximately 0.76% fresh and 0.93% saline.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Signal of typhoon which gives an 18 hours natural disturbance?
items.rationale: 3 / Note:1 –36hrs (30-60kph) / 2 –24hrs (61-120kph) / 3 –18hrs (at least 220kph) / 4 –12hrs (171-220kph)

choiceExplanations.1: Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 1 has a 36-hour lead time with 39–61 km/h winds.
choiceExplanations.4: Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 4 has a 12-hour lead time with 118–184 km/h winds.
choiceExplanations.2: Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 2 has a 24-hour lead time with 62–88 km/h winds.
choiceExplanations.3: Correct — PAGASA Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 3 carries an 18-hour lead time before storm-force winds arrive.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Most sold in Ph

choiceExplanations.Thresher Most manufactured-power tiller/: Correct — rice threshers are the most widely sold agricultural machines in the Philippines, while power tillers and dryers lead local manufacturing.
choiceExplanations.Combine harvester: Combine harvesters are mostly imported high-capacity units rather than the top-selling machine nationwide in unit volume.
choiceExplanations.Mechanical dryer: Mechanical dryers are commonly fabricated locally in the Philippines rather than leading total machinery unit sales.
choiceExplanations.Rice mill: Rice mills are stationary processing units with lower unit sales volume than portable threshers.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Pertains to farming activities utilizing fixed outlay of labor and capital to an increasing area ofland

choiceExplanations.Plantation farming: Plantation farming specializes in large-scale commercial monoculture crops like rubber, palm oil, or sugarcane.
choiceExplanations.Intensive farming: Intensive farming applies increasing labor and capital inputs per unit area to maximize yield on fixed land.
choiceExplanations.Extensive farming: Correct — extensive farming spreads a relatively fixed outlay of labor and capital over an expanding land area.
choiceExplanations.Subsistence farming: Subsistence farming focuses on producing enough food solely for the farm household's own consumption.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: is a method of farming which utilizes an increasing amount of labor and capital to the same area of land?

choiceExplanations.Subsistence farming: Subsistence farming produces crops primarily for family consumption with minimal surplus for sale.
choiceExplanations.Pastoral farming: Pastoral farming centers on raising livestock on grazing land rather than high-input crop production.
choiceExplanations.Intensive farming: Correct — intensive farming increases labor and capital inputs on a fixed land area to raise output per hectare.
choiceExplanations.Extensive farming: Extensive farming uses lower inputs per hectare across larger areas of land.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Is the income derived from the sale of goods?

choiceExplanations.Capital: Capital refers to financial funds or physical assets invested in a business to generate production.
choiceExplanations.Profit: Profit is the net financial gain remaining after deducting total expenses from revenue.
choiceExplanations.Revenue: Correct — revenue is the gross income earned from selling goods or services before subtracting costs.
choiceExplanations.Dividend: Dividend is a portion of corporate net profits distributed to shareholders.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Are those products or services that are directly used by people to satisfy their needs.

choiceExplanations.Capital goods and equipment: Capital goods are durable machinery and equipment used by businesses to manufacture other products.
choiceExplanations.Producer goods and services: Producer goods and services are inputs used by firms to produce finished goods rather than for direct consumption.
choiceExplanations.Consumer goods and products: Correct — consumer goods and products are final items or services purchased directly by people to satisfy their wants and needs.
choiceExplanations.Intermediate goods and materials: Intermediate goods are raw or semi-finished materials consumed during the production of final goods.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Are used to produce goods and services or other producer goods.

choiceExplanations.Luxury goods and services: Luxury goods are non-essential consumer items whose demand rises faster than income.
choiceExplanations.Producer goods and services: Correct — producer goods and services are inputs utilized by businesses to manufacture final goods or other producer goods.
choiceExplanations.Consumer goods and products: Consumer goods are finished products bought directly by end users for personal consumption.
choiceExplanations.Public goods and utilities: Public goods are non-excludable, non-rivalrous goods or utilities provided for collective public use.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Occurs when a decrease in selling price result in a greater than proportionate increase in sales

choiceExplanations.Inelastic demand: Inelastic demand occurs when a price change causes a less than proportionate change in quantity demanded.
choiceExplanations.Derived demand: Derived demand arises indirectly from the demand for another final good or service.
choiceExplanations.Elastic demand: Correct — elastic demand occurs when a decrease in price yields a more than proportionate increase in quantity demanded.
choiceExplanations.Unitary demand: Unitary demand occurs when the percentage change in quantity demanded equals the percentage change in price.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Occurs when a decrease in the selling price produces a less than proportionate increase in sale

choiceExplanations.Unitary demand: Unitary demand means quantity demanded changes in the exact same proportion as price.
choiceExplanations.Elastic demand: Elastic demand occurs when a price decrease causes a more than proportionate increase in sales volume.
choiceExplanations.Derived demand: Derived demand is demand for a production input driven by demand for its end product.
choiceExplanations.Inelastic demand: Correct — inelastic demand occurs when a price drop produces a smaller percentage increase in quantity demanded.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Exists when there are so few suppliers of a product or service that action by one will almost inevitably result in similar action by the others

choiceExplanations.Oligopoly: Correct — an oligopoly is a market dominated by a few interdependent sellers where one firm's actions trigger reactions from rivals.
choiceExplanations.Oligopsony: Oligopsony is a market structure with only a few dominant buyers facing many sellers.
choiceExplanations.Monopoly: Monopoly is a market served by a single seller with no close substitutes.
choiceExplanations.Monopsony: Monopsony is a market controlled by a single buyer of a good or service.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The quantity of a certain commodity that is offered for sale at a certain price at a given place an time

choiceExplanations.Demand: Demand is the quantity of a good consumers are willing and able to buy at a given price and time.
choiceExplanations.Surplus: Surplus is the excess quantity supplied over quantity demanded when price sits above equilibrium.
choiceExplanations.Supply: Correct — supply is the quantity of a commodity offered for sale at a specified price, place, and time.
choiceExplanations.Utility: Utility is the total satisfaction or value a consumer derives from consuming a good or service.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Protective device designed and fitted so that, aloe with other parts of the machine, it prevents contact with the dangerous part of all sides

choiceExplanations.Casing: Correct — under PAES 101, a casing is a protective enclosure that, alone or with machine parts, blocks contact from all sides.
choiceExplanations.Shield: A shield is a guard protecting operators from hazards primarily on one side or from flying debris.
choiceExplanations.Hood: A hood is a partial cover placed over rotating parts, discharge chutes, or dust-generating zones.
choiceExplanations.Barrier: A barrier is a physical rail or fence preventing unauthorized entry into a hazardous zone rather than enclosing all sides.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: obsolescence
items.answer: No longer being use or not useful anymore
choices: Gradual wearing out due to continuous physical use
No longer being use or not useful anymore
Loss of value due to natural resource exhaustion
Decrease in market value caused by price deflation

choiceExplanations.Gradual wearing out due to continuous ph: Gradual wearing out due to continuous physical use describes physical depreciation or wear and tear, not obsolescence.
choiceExplanations.No longer being use or not useful anymor: Correct — obsolescence is functional or economic outmodedness where an asset is no longer used or useful due to newer alternatives.
choiceExplanations.Loss of value due to natural resource ex: Loss of value due to natural resource exhaustion defines depletion rather than obsolescence.
choiceExplanations.Decrease in market value caused by price: Decrease in market value caused by price deflation is a macroeconomic price shift, not technological obsolescence.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A type of error where the hypotheses is false but is accepted

choiceExplanations.Type 1: A Type I error occurs when a true null hypothesis is incorrectly rejected.
choiceExplanations.Type 4: Type IV is not a standard hypothesis-testing error classification in classical statistics.
choiceExplanations.Type 2: Correct — a Type II error (false negative) occurs when a false null hypothesis is accepted or not rejected.
choiceExplanations.Type 3: Type III error refers to correctly rejecting a null hypothesis for the wrong reason or misidentifying direction.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: value that measures the degree of departure of the distribution from symmetry

choiceExplanations.Kurtosis: Kurtosis measures the tailedness or peakedness of a probability distribution rather than asymmetry.
choiceExplanations.Variance: Variance measures the average squared deviation of data points from the mean.
choiceExplanations.Skewness: Correct — skewness measures the asymmetry or degree of departure of a probability distribution from symmetry.
choiceExplanations.Covariance: Covariance measures the joint linear variability between two random variables.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: value that measures the flatness or peakedness of the distribution

choiceExplanations.Variance: Variance quantifies the spread of data points around their mean value.
choiceExplanations.Skewness: Skewness quantifies the asymmetry of a distribution around its mean.
choiceExplanations.Kurtosis: Correct — kurtosis measures the peakedness and tail heaviness of a frequency distribution relative to a normal distribution.
choiceExplanations.Dispersion: Dispersion refers generally to how widely data values are scattered across a range.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Is the process of selecting a sample using networks?

choiceExplanations.Convenience sampling: Convenience sampling selects participants who are easiest or fastest for the researcher to reach.
choiceExplanations.Snowball sampling: Correct — snowball sampling is a non-probability method where existing respondents recruit or refer future subjects through their social networks.
choiceExplanations.Purposive sampling: Purposive sampling selects subjects deliberately based on specific judgmental criteria or expertise.
choiceExplanations.Quota sampling: Quota sampling fills predetermined subgroup proportions using non-random selection.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Has the characteristics of both random and non-random sampling designs. In this sampling, the sampling frame is first divided into a number of segments called intervals.

choiceExplanations.Multistage sampling design: Multistage sampling draws samples sequentially from hierarchically nested groups such as regions, provinces, then households.
choiceExplanations.Stratified sampling design: Stratified sampling divides the population into homogeneous strata and draws random samples within each stratum.
choiceExplanations.Systematic sampling design: Correct — systematic sampling divides the ordered sampling frame into equal intervals and selects units at every kth step after a random start.
choiceExplanations.Cluster sampling design: Cluster sampling divides the population into clusters and randomly selects entire clusters for observation.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: any measure indicating the center of a set of data, arranged in an increasing or decreasing order of magnitude

choiceExplanations.Measure of statistical dispersion: Measures of statistical dispersion (such as range or standard deviation) quantify data spread, not central location.
choiceExplanations.Measure of central tendency: Correct — measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) indicate the typical center of an ordered data set.
choiceExplanations.Measure of relative position: Measures of relative position (such as percentiles or quartiles) locate a specific value within a distribution.
choiceExplanations.Measure of distribution symmetry: Measures of distribution symmetry (skewness) describe whether tails balance around the center.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the top agricultural export commodity of the Philippines?

choiceExplanations.Abaca fiber: Abaca fiber is a major Philippine specialty export, but its total export value trails coconut oil.
choiceExplanations.Coconut oil: Correct — coconut oil consistently ranks as the Philippines' top agricultural export commodity by value.
choiceExplanations.Canned pineapple: Canned pineapple is a leading Philippine fruit export but ranks below coconut oil in total export value.
choiceExplanations.Cavendish banana: Cavendish banana is a top fresh fruit export from the Philippines, though behind coconut oil overall.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Are those who take physical possession and ownership of products sold?

choiceExplanations.Agent: An agent represents a principal in transactions without taking legal title or ownership of the goods.
choiceExplanations.Merchant: Correct — a merchant takes physical possession and legal ownership of the products bought for resale.
choiceExplanations.Broker: A broker brings buyers and sellers together to negotiate deals without owning or possessing the goods.
choiceExplanations.Auctioneer: An auctioneer conducts public competitive bidding sales on behalf of sellers without taking ownership.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Those who carry several items and brands from varying sources and are not usually engaged in manufacture and fabrication of agricultural machines.

choiceExplanations.Distributor: A distributor typically holds exclusive or regional wholesale rights from specific manufacturers.
