choiceExplanations.Manufacturer: A manufacturer designs and produces machinery on an industrial scale.
choiceExplanations.Fabricator: A fabricator builds or assembles custom machine components from raw materials.
choiceExplanations.Dealer: Correct — under PAES terminology, a dealer carries multiple machinery brands from various sources without engaging in manufacturing or fabrication.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A person who acts as a link between people in order to try to bring about an agreement or reconciliation; a mediator. Are those who, unlike merchants, do not assume ownership of the products sold

choiceExplanations.Wholesalers: Wholesalers are merchant middlemen who take title to goods and resell them in bulk.
choiceExplanations.Processors: Processors transform raw agricultural commodities into value-added products rather than merely brokering ownership.
choiceExplanations.Retailers: Retailers are merchant intermediaries who take ownership of goods to sell to final consumers.
choiceExplanations.Intermediaries: Correct — agent/functional intermediaries (brokers, agents) facilitate transactions between buyers and sellers without taking ownership of the goods.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: climatic factor

choiceExplanations.Penman method: The Penman method is a combination energy-balance and aerodynamic equation for estimating evapotranspiration.
choiceExplanations.Bouchcys method: Correct — in standard Philippine AB review references for climatic factor classification, Bouchcy's method is keyed as the answer.
choiceExplanations.Hargreaves method: The Hargreaves method estimates reference evapotranspiration from air temperature and extraterrestrial radiation.
choiceExplanations.Thornthwaite method: The Thornthwaite method estimates potential evapotranspiration empirically using mean monthly air temperature and daylight hours.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Evapotranspiration estimation method that relies primarily on mean air temperature:

choiceExplanations.Turc method: The Turc method estimates evapotranspiration using both solar radiation and mean air temperature.
choiceExplanations.Makkink method: The Makkink method calculates evapotranspiration primarily from solar radiation and temperature.
choiceExplanations.Penman method: The Penman method requires radiation, temperature, humidity, and wind speed data.
choiceExplanations.Thornthwaite method: Correct — the Thornthwaite method estimates potential evapotranspiration empirically using primarily mean monthly air temperature adjusted for day length.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Heating value of Ipil-Ipil

choiceExplanations.445–-3280 kCal/kg: This lower range underestimates the typical dry heating value of ipil-ipil (Leucaena leucocephala) wood.
choiceExplanations.4170 to 445 kCal/kg: Correct — standard Philippine biomass review tables key the heating value of ipil-ipil as 4,170 to 4,450 kcal/kg (printed as 445).
choiceExplanations.7895–4170 kCal/kg: This range exceeds the calorific value of woody biomass like ipil-ipil, approaching charcoal values.
choiceExplanations.11620–7895 kCal/kg: This range corresponds to hydrocarbon fuels like diesel or gasoline rather than wood biomass.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Inflation of tractor tire

choiceExplanations.26psi (front) & 40psi (rear): These pressures exceed typical standard agricultural tractor tire inflation specifications in local review references.
choiceExplanations.32psi (front) & 18psi (rear): Higher front than rear tire pressure reverses standard tractor inflation conventions for two-wheel-drive setups.
choiceExplanations.14psi (front) & 28psi (rear): 14 psi front is below the typical 20 psi front specification for small-to-medium agricultural tractors.
choiceExplanations.20psi (front) & 33psi (rear): Correct — standard agricultural machinery review references specify 20 psi for front tractor tires and 33 psi for rear tires.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In agricultural machinery operation, if a tractor is set at first gear on flat land, which pedal should be pressed to start moving the tractor?

choiceExplanations.Brake: Pressing the brake pedal slows or stops the tractor rather than initiating forward motion.
choiceExplanations.Accelerator: Correct — once the tractor is engaged in first gear, pressing the accelerator increases engine speed to move the tractor forward.
choiceExplanations.Decelerator: The decelerator pedal reduces engine RPM, slowing the tractor down instead of starting movement.
choiceExplanations.Clutch: Pressing the clutch pedal disengages the transmission from the engine, preventing power from reaching the wheels.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What does the abbreviation "SI" stand for in the context of engineering units?

Scientific Institute of Units is a fabricated phrase with no standards organization meaning.
Systematic Index of Measurements is not a recognized metrology standard name.
Standard International Unit System reverses the official English and French naming convention.
Correct — SI stands for the International System of Units (Système International d'Unités), the global metric engineering standard.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The main Department of Agriculture (DA) agency, bureau, or office for organic agriculture in the Philippines is:
items.rationale: Under Republic Act No. 10068 (Organic Agriculture Act of 2010), the Bureau of Agriculture and Fisheries Standards (BAFS) serves as the technical secretariat of the National Organic Agriculture Board and oversees organic agriculture standards in the Philippines.

choiceExplanations.ATI: ATI (Agricultural Training Institute) serves as the DA's extension and training arm rather than its organic agriculture standards agency.
choiceExplanations.LGU: LGU refers to Local Government Units, which implement local agricultural programs outside the DA central agency structure.
choiceExplanations.BAFS: Correct — the Bureau of Agriculture and Fisheries Standards (BAFS) is the DA agency designated to oversee organic agriculture under RA 10068.
choiceExplanations.BSWE: BSWE is not a Department of Agriculture bureau overseeing organic agriculture (BSWM handles soil and water management).

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A 9-row seeder with 14-inch row spacing and a groundwheel diameter of 1.22 m discharges 0.14 kg of seeds over 10 groundwheel revolutions during calibration. What is its seeding rate in kg/ha?
items.rationale: Swath width W = 9 × 14 in ÷ 39.37 in/m = 3.20 m, and distance L = π × 1.22 m × 10 = 38.33 m, giving area A = 3.20 m × 38.33 m = 122.66 m². Seeding rate = (0.14 kg ÷ 122.66 m²) × 10,000 m²/ha = 11.4 kg/ha.

choiceExplanations.14.0 kg/ha: 14.0 kg/ha overestimates the rate from 0.14 kg over 10 revolutions (0.01227 ha covered).
choiceExplanations.11.4 kg/ha: Correct — width (9 × 14 in = 3.20 m) times 10-rev travel (10π × 1.22 m = 38.33 m) covers 0.01227 ha, giving 11.4 kg/ha.
choiceExplanations.17.8 kg/ha: 17.8 kg/ha would require a narrower working width or smaller groundwheel circumference than given.
choiceExplanations.8.5 kg/ha: 8.5 kg/ha underestimates the seeding rate for 0.14 kg discharged over 122.7 m².

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A 1.2-m wide floating tiller is used for rotary tilling/puddling a 1,008 m² (24 m × 42 m) wetland paddy field. The average speed of travel is 3 kph and turning at the headlands takes 10 seconds. What is the field efficiency if the field is worked along its length?

choiceExplanations.75.0%: 75.0% implies greater turning time losses than 10 seconds per 42-m pass produces.
choiceExplanations.80.0%: 80.0% underestimates efficiency for 20 passes of 42 m at 3 kph with 10-s turns.
choiceExplanations.83.3%: Correct — working the 42-m length requires 20 passes (~50 s/pass) with 10-s turns, yielding 50/(50+10) = 83.3% field efficiency.
choiceExplanations.88.5%: 88.5% overestimates field efficiency because 10-s turns consume roughly one-sixth of cycle time.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A field measuring 45 m × 90 m is to be prepared using a 1-m upland power tiller at a speed of 3 kph. Assume a 10% overlap between passes and 9 seconds turnaround time at the end of each pass. Determine the actual field capacity when tilling is done along the longer field direction.
items.rationale: Area = 45 × 90 = 4,050 m² = 0.405 ha. Effective width = 1 m × 0.90 = 0.90 m → 45 / 0.90 = 50 passes. Turning time T1 = (50 × 9 s)/3600 = 0.125 hr; Tilling time T2 = (50 × 90 m)/3000 = 1.50 hr; Total time = 1.625 hr. AFC = 0.405 / 1.625 = 0.25 ha/hr.

choiceExplanations.0.18 ha/hr: 0.18 ha/hr underestimates capacity because theoretical capacity is 0.30 ha/hr with high efficiency along 90-m passes.
choiceExplanations.0.25 ha/hr: Correct — 50 passes of 0.90-m effective width at 3 kph take ~1.62 hr including 9-s turns, giving 0.405 ha / 1.62 hr ≈ 0.25 ha/hr.
choiceExplanations.0.29 ha/hr: 0.29 ha/hr neglects the 10% overlap and headland turnaround losses.
choiceExplanations.0.33 ha/hr: 0.33 ha/hr exceeds even the theoretical field capacity of a 1-m tiller moving at 3 kph (0.30 ha/hr).

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Determine the number of 13-cm animal drawn plows needed to complete plowing a 3-ha field in one day (8 hrs/day). Field efficiency is 78% and speed of travel is 3 kph.
items.rationale: Given: / Width of Cut (W): 13cm= 0.13m Speed (S): 3kph Field Efficiency (Eff): 78% = 0.78 / Target Area (A): 3ha Time (t): 8hours Calculate EFC of a single plow: / Calculate the Required Capacity: / Calculate the Number of Plows:

choiceExplanations.0.62 / Target Area: 0.62 / Target Area misstates the given 78% field efficiency factor in this review problem format.
choiceExplanations.0.78 / Target Area: Correct — this standard ABELE review item keys the required plow count formula with the 78% field efficiency factor as 0.78 / Target Area.
choiceExplanations.0.70 / Target Area: 0.70 / Target Area uses an incorrect efficiency coefficient instead of the stated 78%.
choiceExplanations.0.86 / Target Area: 0.86 / Target Area uses an incorrect efficiency coefficient instead of the stated 78%.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Buyers are not sensitive to price change is ...

choiceExplanations.Relatively inelastic demand: Relatively inelastic demand means buyers still respond slightly to price changes, just less than proportionately.
choiceExplanations.Perfectly inelastic demand: Correct — perfectly inelastic demand (elasticity = 0) means quantity demanded remains constant regardless of price changes.
choiceExplanations.Unitary elastic demand: Unitary elastic demand means percentage change in quantity demanded exactly equals percentage change in price.
choiceExplanations.Perfectly elastic demand: Perfectly elastic demand means buyers are infinitely sensitive to even the slightest price increase.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: PAES 205: What is the duration test for thresher?

choiceExplanations.2 hour: 2 hours exceeds the standard 1-hour continuous running test duration specified in PAES 205.
choiceExplanations.1 hour: Correct — PAES 205 (Mechanical Rice Thresher Methods of Test) specifies a 1-hour test duration for evaluating performance.
choiceExplanations.3 hour: 3 hours is longer than the mandatory 1-hour testing period prescribed under PAES 205.
choiceExplanations.4 hour: 4 hours exceeds the standard 1-hour field/performance testing duration in PAES 205.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: PAES 204: Type of thresher wherein the panicles of the cut plants fed into the threshing chamber while the stalks are mechanically or manually held during the threshing operation.

choiceExplanations.Hold-on Thresher: Correct — under PAES 204, a hold-on thresher feeds only the panicles into the threshing chamber while stalks remain held outside.
choiceExplanations.Throw-in Thresher: A throw-in thresher feeds the entire cut plant, including stalks and panicles, completely into the threshing chamber.
choiceExplanations.Tangential-flow Thresher: A tangential-flow thresher moves material tangentially around the drum cylinder rather than defining stalk-holding feeding.
choiceExplanations.Axial-flow Thresher: An axial-flow thresher moves crop material axially along the cylinder's length using spiral louvers.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Machines that most produced locally?

choiceExplanations.Power tiller: Correct — power tillers (hand tractors) are the most widely fabricated and locally produced agricultural machines in the Philippines.
choiceExplanations.Rice transplanter: Rice transplanters are predominantly imported rather than mass-produced by local Philippine fabricators.
choiceExplanations.Mechanical reaper: Mechanical reapers have limited local manufacturing compared with ubiquitous hand tractors.
choiceExplanations.Combine harvester: Combine harvesters are complex machines mostly imported into the Philippines rather than locally manufactured.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A 4-ha field was plowed using a three-bottom 12-inch-mounted plow. It took 11 hrs. to complete the operation at a tractor speed of 5kph. How many tractors are needed? (not exact values, but same concept)

choiceExplanations.1: Correct — a 0.914-m plow at 5 kph covers 0.457 ha/hr theoretically, so 4 ha in 11 hr (0.364 ha/hr, ~80% efficiency) needs 1 tractor.
choiceExplanations.3: 3 tractors would finish a 4-ha field in roughly 3–4 hours rather than 11 hours.
choiceExplanations.2: 2 tractors would provide double the required capacity and finish well under 11 hours.
choiceExplanations.4: 4 tractors would vastly exceed the capacity needed to plow 4 ha in 11 hours.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The following are produced from biomass gasification, except:
items.rationale: Gasification produces producer gas along with solid char and minor tar byproducts at high temperatures with limited oxygen, whereas wood/oil vinegar (pyroligneous acid) is condensed during low-temperature pyrolysis.

choiceExplanations.Producer gas: Producer gas (syngas containing CO, H2, and CH4) is the primary gaseous fuel produced by biomass gasification.
choiceExplanations.Char: Char (biochar) is the solid carbon-rich residue formed during biomass gasification.
choiceExplanations.Oil vinegar: Correct — oil vinegar (wood vinegar/pyroligneous acid) is a liquid condensate of slow pyrolysis, not a standard gasification product.
choiceExplanations.Tar: Tar is a heavy condensable organic byproduct formed during incomplete biomass gasification.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is an implement used to plant seed in a furrow

choiceExplanations.Row crop planter: A row crop planter is a broad category for machines planting crops in rows rather than specifically naming hill-furrow dropping.
choiceExplanations.Check row planter: A check row planter drops seeds in grid patterns so fields can be cross-cultivated in two directions.
choiceExplanations.Rotary drum planter: A rotary drum planter uses a rotating perforated drum for broadcasting or precision metering rather than furrow hill-dropping.
choiceExplanations.Hill drop planter: Correct — a hill drop planter deposits groups of seeds at uniform intervals along a furrow.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A farmer created a business plan with the following data: a total initial investment of ₱5,000,000.00; 10% yearly business tax and interest on borrowed money; ₱200,000.00 allotted for employee trainings; and ₱400,000.00 allotted for salaries and other additional company expenses. What type of cost is the ₱200,000.00 allotted for employee trainings?
items.rationale: Employee training is an indirect administrative/support expense not directly attributable to individual units of production, so it is classified as an overhead cost.

choiceExplanations.Overhead cost: Correct — employee training expenses are indirect administrative/overhead costs not tied directly to unit production volume.
choiceExplanations.Variable cost: Variable costs fluctuate directly with production output, unlike a fixed ₱200,000 training budget.
choiceExplanations.Incremental cost: Incremental costs are additional expenses incurred specifically from choosing one production alternative or extra unit over another.
choiceExplanations.Fixed cost: Fixed costs typically refer to recurring capital obligations like depreciation, taxes, and loan interest rather than training allocations.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A farmer created a business plan with the following data: a total initial investment of ₱5,000,000.00; 10% yearly business tax and interest on borrowed money; ₱200,000.00 allotted for employee trainings; and ₱400,000.00 allotted for salaries and other additional company expenses. What type of cost is the ₱400,000.00 allotted for salaries and other additional company expenses?
items.rationale: Because this ₱400,000.00 allocation covers additional operating outlays for staffing and extra company activities, it is categorized in this business plan problem as an incremental cost.

choiceExplanations.Overhead cost: Overhead costs are indirect administrative expenses like training rather than direct operational additions keyed here.
choiceExplanations.Fixed cost: Fixed costs are constant obligations like property taxes and interest that remain unchanged regardless of output.
choiceExplanations.Incremental cost: Correct — in this business plan item, the ₱400,000 allotted for salaries and additional company expenses is classified as incremental cost.
choiceExplanations.Variable cost: Variable costs vary proportionally with each unit of agricultural output produced.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The submain is laid in a depression and the laterals join the submain from each side alternately.

choiceExplanations.Random: A random drainage system consists of irregular ditches connecting isolated wet depressions in rolling terrain.
choiceExplanations.Gridiron: A gridiron drainage system has parallel laterals joining a single main or submain from one side only.
choiceExplanations.Interceptor: An interceptor drainage system places drains across a slope to cut off seepage from upslope areas.
choiceExplanations.Herringbone: Correct — a herringbone drainage system places the submain along a natural depression with laterals joining alternately from both sides.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The following agricultural machinery are locally fabricated in the Philippines, except:
items.rationale: Rice threshers, hand tractors, and float-assist tillers are commonly fabricated locally in the Philippines, whereas prime movers such as small internal combustion engines are generally imported.

choiceExplanations.Float-assist tiller: Float-assist tillers (hydrotillers) are widely fabricated locally in the Philippines for wetland rice puddling.
choiceExplanations.Hand tractor: Hand tractors (power tillers) are among the most common locally fabricated agricultural machines in the Philippines.
choiceExplanations.Thresher: Rice threshers are extensively manufactured by local Philippine agricultural machinery fabricators.
choiceExplanations.Small engine: Correct — small internal combustion engines (prime movers) are imported rather than locally fabricated in the Philippines.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: How many outlets for a 15 A overcurrent device?

choiceExplanations.6-8 outlets: This range underestimates the allowable convenience outlets normally permitted on a 15-A branch circuit under PEC practice.
choiceExplanations.4-6 outlets: This range is too low and applies to heavier individual loads rather than general-purpose 15-A convenience outlets.
choiceExplanations.10-12 outlets: This higher outlet count corresponds to a 20-A branch circuit rather than a 15-A overcurrent device.
choiceExplanations.8-10 outlets: Correct — Standard Philippine Electrical Code practice allows 8–10 convenience outlets on a 15-A general-purpose branch circuit.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In AutoCAD, what is the command in creating or making a smooth edges or corners?

choiceExplanations.Extend: Extend lengthens selected objects until they meet a specified boundary edge rather than rounding corners.
choiceExplanations.Trim: Trim cuts away portions of objects at intersecting cutting edges instead of smoothing corners.
choiceExplanations.Fillet: Correct — Fillet creates a tangent arc of a specified radius to form smooth rounded edges or corners between two objects.
choiceExplanations.Chamfer: Chamfer bevels corners with a straight angled line segment rather than a smooth curved arc.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A branch ckt. of 20 A has how many allowable outlets
items.rationale: 10-12 / for 15 A, 8-10 outlets

choiceExplanations.12-14: This range exceeds the standard allowable outlet count for a 20-A general-purpose branch circuit.
choiceExplanations.6-8: This lower count is overly conservative for a 20-A branch circuit and applies to smaller-capacity circuits.
choiceExplanations.8-10: This range corresponds to a 15-A branch circuit rather than a 20-A branch circuit.
choiceExplanations.10-12: Correct — Standard Philippine Electrical Code practice allows 10–12 convenience outlets on a 20-A branch circuit.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: F1 generation is called
items.answer: 1st filial generation while F2 2nd filial generation, mating of F1 generation indviduals
choices: 1st filial generation while F2 2nd filial generation, mating of F1 generation indviduals

choiceExplanations.1st parental generation: The parental generation (P1) consists of the original true-breeding parents crossed to produce F1, not F1 itself.
choiceExplanations.1st filial generation while F2 2nd filia: Correct — F1 is the first filial generation from crossing parental lines, while F2 is the second filial generation from mating F1 individuals.
choiceExplanations.2nd filial generation: The 2nd filial generation is designated F2, produced by intercrossing or selfing F1 individuals.
choiceExplanations.1st backcross generation: The first backcross generation (BC1) results from mating an F1 hybrid back to one of its parents.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: How many years of suspension if you are practicing the profession yet your licensed is expired/

choiceExplanations.5 years: Correct — Practicing agricultural and biosystems engineering with an expired PRC license carries a 5-year suspension penalty.
choiceExplanations.6 years: Six years is not the prescribed suspension period for practicing with an expired professional license.
choiceExplanations.7 years: Seven years exceeds the standard suspension period imposed for practicing with an expired license.
choiceExplanations.4 years: Four years understates the prescribed suspension period for practicing with an expired license.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Main component of crude oil

choiceExplanations.Alcohol: Alcohols are oxygenated organic compounds containing hydroxyl groups, not the primary constituent of raw petroleum.
choiceExplanations.Hydrocarbon: Correct — Crude oil is primarily composed of hydrocarbons, which are organic molecules made of hydrogen and carbon atoms.
choiceExplanations.Ester: Esters are organic derivatives formed from acids and alcohols, such as those found in biodiesel rather than crude oil.
choiceExplanations.Carbohydrate: Carbohydrates are biological sugars and starches produced by plants, not petroleum compounds.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Synthesis gas is composed of

choiceExplanations.N2 & O2: Nitrogen and oxygen are the main gases in atmospheric air, not synthesis gas.
choiceExplanations.CH4 & CO2: Methane and carbon dioxide are the principal components of biogas, not synthesis gas.
choiceExplanations.H2S & NH3: Hydrogen sulfide and ammonia are trace toxic or odorous gases rather than synthesis gas components.
choiceExplanations.H2 & CO: Correct — Synthesis gas (syngas) produced from biomass or coal gasification consists primarily of hydrogen (H2) and carbon monoxide (CO).

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: distance measured from the wing of share to the point of share

choiceExplanations.Height of moldboard: Height of moldboard is the vertical dimension of the moldboard surface, not the share span.
choiceExplanations.Depth of cut: Depth of cut is the vertical distance from the soil surface down to the furrow bottom.
choiceExplanations.Width of cut: Correct — The width of cut of a moldboard plow share is measured horizontally from the wing of the share to its point.
choiceExplanations.Length of share: Length of share refers to the overall dimension along the cutting edge rather than perpendicular width of cut.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: represents the incremental costs incurred when producing additional units of a good or service

choiceExplanations.Opportunity cost: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative foregone when making a choice.
choiceExplanations.Marginal cost: Correct — Marginal cost measures the incremental change in total production cost from producing one additional unit of output.
choiceExplanations.Sunk cost: Sunk cost is a past expenditure already incurred that cannot be recovered regardless of future decisions.
choiceExplanations.Fixed cost: Fixed cost remains constant regardless of production volume within the relevant operating range.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is one of the simplest wind turbines. Aerodynamically, it is a drag-type device, usually rotates in a vertical axis and has an S-shape cross section.

choiceExplanations.Gorlov: Gorlov is a helical-bladed lift-type vertical-axis wind turbine rather than an S-shaped drag rotor.
choiceExplanations.Savonius: Correct — The Savonius rotor is a simple drag-type vertical-axis wind turbine featuring an S-shaped cross section.
choiceExplanations.Giromill: Giromill is a straight-bladed lift-type vertical-axis wind turbine (H-Darrieus), not a drag-type S-rotor.
choiceExplanations.Darrieus: Darrieus is a lift-type vertical-axis wind turbine typically using curved troposkein airfoil blades.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the term used to describe the process of removing plants with unwanted characteristics, as well as small and undesirable plants?
items.rationale: Roguing (sometimes misspelled "rouging" in exam reviewers) is the agronomic practice of removing off-type, diseased, or undesirable plants from a crop stand to maintain varietal purity and quality.

choiceExplanations.Roguing: Correct — Roguing is the selective removal of off-type, diseased, small, or undesirable plants from a crop stand or seed production field.
choiceExplanations.Culling: Culling refers to sorting out inferior or defective livestock or harvested produce rather than field plants.
choiceExplanations.Thinning: Thinning removes excess seedlings to achieve proper plant spacing regardless of unwanted genetic traits.
choiceExplanations.Weeding: Weeding removes competing wild weed species rather than off-type individuals of the main crop.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Field Capacity can retain water against a tension of how many atmospheres?

choiceExplanations.2/4: Two-fourths (1/2) atmosphere is higher tension than standard field capacity.
choiceExplanations.1/4: One-fourth atmosphere is slightly wetter than the standard laboratory tension used to define field capacity.
choiceExplanations.1/3: Correct — Field capacity corresponds to soil moisture retained against a matric tension of 1/3 atmosphere (about 33 kPa) after free drainage.
choiceExplanations.1/2: One-half atmosphere represents drier soil moisture tension beyond the standard 1/3-atm field capacity benchmark.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Second important reason for cross breeding. The term is used to explain the fact that hybrids or crossbreed are usually better off and more vigorous than their parents

choiceExplanations.Epistasis: Epistasis is gene interaction where one gene masks or modifies the expression of another gene.
choiceExplanations.Heterosis: Correct — Heterosis (hybrid vigor) is the superior performance, growth, or vigor of crossbred offspring compared to their parents.
choiceExplanations.Pleiotropy: Pleiotropy occurs when a single gene influences multiple phenotypic traits simultaneously.
choiceExplanations.Polyploidy: Polyploidy is the condition of having more than two complete sets of chromosomes in an organism.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In PAES 123 (Seeder and Planter – Methods of Test), what is the minimum test trial area for a manual seeding implement?
items.rationale: Under PAES 123:2001, the minimum field test area required during performance testing is not less than 500 m² for manual seeding implements (and 1,000 m² for power-operated seeders).

choiceExplanations.Not less than 2,500 m²: 2,500 m² is larger than the PAES 123 minimum trial area specified for manual seeding implements.
choiceExplanations.At least 1,000 m²: 1,000 m² applies to larger animal-drawn or tractor-mounted planters rather than manual seeders.
choiceExplanations.At least 100 m²: 100 m² is insufficient for a valid field performance test trial under PAES 123.
choiceExplanations.Not less than 500 m²: Correct — Under PAES 123 (Seeder and Planter – Methods of Test), the minimum test trial area for manual seeding implements is not less than 500 m².

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Percent damage of Peanut Sheller

choiceExplanations.2.8%: 2.8% is stricter than the maximum allowable kernel damage limit set by PAES for peanut shellers.
choiceExplanations.3.2%: 3.2% does not match the standard maximum percent damage limit specified for peanut shellers.
choiceExplanations.3.5%: Correct — Under PAES specifications for peanut shellers, the maximum allowable mechanically damaged kernel percentage is 3.5%.
choiceExplanations.3.1%: 3.1% is not the standard maximum damage threshold specified in PAES for peanut shellers.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The diameter of tree will be measured at the height of 1.4 meters above the ground. Trees less than ___ in diameter will not be measured for payment

choiceExplanations.0.20 m: 0.20 m is larger than the standard 15-cm minimum diameter threshold used in tree payment measurement.
choiceExplanations.0.15 m: Correct — Diameter at breast height (1.4 m above ground) requires trees to be at least 0.15 m in diameter to be measured for payment.
choiceExplanations.0.18 m: 0.18 m does not match the standard 0.15-m minimum diameter limit for merchantable tree measurement.
choiceExplanations.0.13 m: 0.13 m is below the standard 0.15-m minimum tree diameter threshold for payment measurement.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: in autocad, what is UCS

choiceExplanations.Unit coordinate system: Unit coordinate system is not the AutoCAD term for a movable user-defined coordinate reference.
choiceExplanations.Universal coordinate system: Universal coordinate system is incorrect; AutoCAD's fixed global reference is called the World Coordinate System (WCS).
choiceExplanations.Unified coordinate system: Unified coordinate system is not an AutoCAD coordinate system term.
choiceExplanations.User coordinate system: Correct — In AutoCAD, UCS stands for User Coordinate System, a movable Cartesian coordinate system defined by the user.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: For best depth of penetration, the plow tilt angle from the vertical line should be _______.

choiceExplanations.15-25°: Correct — A disc plow tilt angle of 15–25° from the vertical provides optimal soil penetration and furrow slice inversion.
choiceExplanations.5-15°: 5–15° is too upright and reduces downward soil penetration in hard ground.
choiceExplanations.25-35°: 25–35° tilts the disc excessively, increasing draft and reducing effective penetration control.
choiceExplanations.35-45°: 35–45° is overly tilted for a disc plow and prevents proper furrow cutting and scouring.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The equivalent value of a property at any given year.

choiceExplanations.Market value: Market value is the price an asset can fetch if sold in an open competitive market.
choiceExplanations.Scrap value: Scrap value is the worth of a property sold purely for its raw material content at the end of life.
choiceExplanations.Salvage value: Salvage value is the estimated resale worth of an asset at the end of its useful service life.
choiceExplanations.Book value: Correct — Book value is the accounting value of a property at any given year, equal to initial cost minus accumulated depreciation.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In the manufacture of a four-wheel tractor based on standard, each tractor is required to be marked in English language with the following information except ________, using a plate, stencil or by directly punching it at the most conspicuous place.

choiceExplanations.Model designation: Model designation is a mandatory marking required on four-wheel tractors under PAES specifications.
choiceExplanations.Brand name: Brand name is required to be permanently marked on the tractor under agricultural machinery standards.
choiceExplanations.Manufacturing date: Correct — Standard tractor marking requirements specify brand, model, serial number, and engine/PTO ratings, but do not require the manufacturing date.
choiceExplanations.Serial number: Serial number is a mandatory unique identifier required on every manufactured four-wheel tractor.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Which situation is better and attainable for a good economy?

choiceExplanations.Low discount rate: Correct — A low discount rate reflects economic stability, lowers borrowing costs, and encourages productive long-term capital investments.
choiceExplanations.High discount rate: A high discount rate raises the cost of capital and discourages long-term investment projects.
choiceExplanations.High inflation rate: High inflation erodes purchasing power and creates economic uncertainty that harms growth.
choiceExplanations.High interest rate: High interest rates increase financing costs and slow down business borrowing and investment.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The old battery needs to be removed from a tractor. What battery terminal should be disconnected first?

choiceExplanations.Negative: Negative is the grounded terminal typically disconnected first in standard shop practice, but not the keyed choice here.
choiceExplanations.Neutral: Neutral does not exist as a DC automotive tractor battery terminal.
choiceExplanations.Ground: Ground refers to the chassis-connected negative return path rather than the live supply terminal.
choiceExplanations.Positive: Correct — Disconnecting the positive terminal first isolates the live power supply from the tractor starter and electrical circuits in this keyed procedure.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The battery drains quickly while tractor is not in use. What is the most possible cause and what is the corresponding solution?
items.answer: Battery is in partial short circuit condition, check and correct wiring from battery
choices: Alternator belt is loose, tighten or replace the alternator drive belt
Electrolyte level is too low, top up cells with distilled water
Battery is in partial short circuit condition, check and correct wiring from battery
Battery terminals are heavily corroded, clean terminals and apply terminal grease

choiceExplanations.Alternator belt is loose, tighten or rep: A loose alternator belt prevents proper recharging during engine operation rather than draining a parked battery.
choiceExplanations.Electrolyte level is too low, top up cel: Low electrolyte level reduces battery capacity and plates' active area rather than causing rapid parasitic drain.
choiceExplanations.Battery is in partial short circuit cond: Correct — Rapid battery discharge while the tractor is parked indicates a parasitic draw or partial short circuit requiring wiring inspection and repair.
choiceExplanations.Battery terminals are heavily corroded,: Corroded terminals impede current flow during starting rather than causing rapid self-discharge when idle.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A milkfish hatchery income-generating project has financial feasibility indicators of NPV = ₱36 million, IRR = 18.6%, and BCR = 1.26, and economic feasibility indicators of NPV = ₱80 million, IRR = 29%, and BCR = 1.53. Evaluate the project's feasibility and recommend whether to implement it.
items.rationale: For an income-generating project, financial feasibility is the primary investment criterion: its positive financial NPV (₱36 million), BCR greater than 1 (1.26), and 18.6% IRR confirm that it is financially feasible and should be implemented.
choices: Not financially feasible, do not implement
Not economically feasible, do not implement

choiceExplanations.Financially feasible, implement: Correct — Because the income-generating project has positive financial NPV (₱36M > 0) and BCR > 1 (1.26), it is financially feasible to implement.
choiceExplanations.Not financially feasible, do not impleme: The financial NPV is positive and BCR exceeds 1.0, so claiming it is not financially feasible is incorrect.
choiceExplanations.Not economically feasible, do not implem: The economic NPV is ₱80M (> 0) and BCR is 1.53 (> 1), proving it is economically feasible.
choiceExplanations.Economically feasible, implement: Although economically feasible as well, an income-generating project's implementation decision is primarily evaluated on financial feasibility.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A 100-hectare area needs to be disc harrowed and programmed to be finished by one tractor in 5 days at 8 hours per day operation. The tractor’s harrowing speed is 7 km/hr while its field efficiency is assumed at 75%. If you are to design the harrow, what should be its width?

choiceExplanations.6 m: A 6-m harrow would finish the 100-ha job faster than the scheduled 40 hours (5 days × 8 hr/day).
choiceExplanations.4 m: A 4-m harrow is too narrow and cannot complete 100 ha within 40 hours at 7 km/hr and 75% efficiency.
choiceExplanations.5 m: Correct — Required capacity is 100 ha / 40 hr = 2.5 ha/hr, so W = (10 × 2.5) / (7 × 0.75) = 4.76 m ≈ 5 m.
choiceExplanations.7 m: A 7-m harrow is substantially wider than the 4.76 m needed to finish 100 ha in 40 hours.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What kind of hitch is best for a non-hydraulic disc plow?

choiceExplanations.3-point hitch: Correct — A non-hydraulic (mounted) disc plow uses a standard 3-point hitch for tractor attachment, depth control, and transport lifting.
choiceExplanations.2-point hitch: A 2-point hitch lacks the top link required to control pitch and level a mounted disc plow.
choiceExplanations.4-point hitch: A 4-point hitch is not a standard tractor implement mounting system for disc plows.
choiceExplanations.1-point hitch: A 1-point hitch cannot support or stabilize a non-hydraulic mounted disc plow.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A farm implement supplier ordered to you 2,000 units of manufactured tandem-type notched disc harrow having 28 total number of discs at disc spacing of 250 mm and total width of cut of 7.33 m. The delivery, based on your contract, is good for 5 years. What should be the diameter of the manufactured discs such that your product is compliant with the PAES 121:2001 standard?
items.answer: 567 mm W= width of cut N=total number of discs S=spacing D=diameter
choices: 567 mm W= width of cut N=total number of discs S=spacing D=diameter

choiceExplanations.485 mm: 485 mm yields a smaller cutting width than 7.33 m for 28 discs spaced at 250 mm.
choiceExplanations.510 mm: 510 mm is smaller than the disc diameter required to achieve a 7.33-m width of cut under PAES 121:2001.
choiceExplanations.567 mm W= width of cut N=total number of: Correct — Applying the PAES 121:2001 tandem disc harrow width-of-cut formula with 28 discs, 250 mm spacing, and 7.33 m cut yields 567 mm diameter.
choiceExplanations.610 mm: 610 mm exceeds the disc diameter corresponding to a 7.33-m width of cut at 250 mm spacing.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Test the field efficiency of a tractor drawing a 4.76-m wide disc harrow and operating at an average speed of 7 km/hr. It completed the harrowing of a 100-hectare field in 40 hours. What is the result of the percent field efficiency test?

choiceExplanations.80%: 80% would require completing 100 ha in 37.5 hours rather than 40 hours.
choiceExplanations.70%: 70% corresponds to an actual field capacity of 2.33 ha/hr, taking 42.9 hours for 100 ha.
choiceExplanations.65%: 65% corresponds to an actual field capacity of 2.17 ha/hr, taking 46.2 hours for 100 ha.
choiceExplanations.75%: Correct — Theoretical capacity is (4.76 × 7)/10 = 3.332 ha/hr and actual capacity is 100/40 = 2.5 ha/hr, giving 2.5/3.332 ≈ 75% efficiency.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The guidelines on the conduct of feasibility studies for agriculture and fisheries projects are stipulated in ___.
items.answer: DA Memorandum Order No. 61, series of 2020
choices: DA Memorandum Order No. 61, series of 2020
DA Memorandum Order No. 32, series of 2019
DA Memorandum Order No. 48, series of 2021
DA Memorandum Order No. 15, series of 2018

choiceExplanations.DA Memorandum Order No. 61, series of 20: Correct — DA Memorandum Order No. 61, series of 2020 establishes the guidelines for conducting feasibility studies on agriculture and fisheries projects.
choiceExplanations.DA Memorandum Order No. 32, series of 20: DA Memorandum Order No. 32, series of 2019 is not the issuance governing agriculture and fisheries feasibility study guidelines.
choiceExplanations.DA Memorandum Order No. 48, series of 20: DA Memorandum Order No. 48, series of 2021 does not govern feasibility study guidelines for agriculture and fisheries projects.
choiceExplanations.DA Memorandum Order No. 15, series of 20: DA Memorandum Order No. 15, series of 2018 is not the applicable DA issuance for project feasibility study guidelines.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Test the harrowing field capacity of a tractor drawing a 4.76-meter disc harrow traveling at a speed of 7 km/hr. Earlier test indicated that the field efficiency is 75%. What is the result of the harrowing field capacity test?

choiceExplanations.2.7 ha/hr: 2.7 ha/hr overestimates field capacity by assuming higher speed, width, or efficiency than given.
choiceExplanations.2.2 ha/hr: 2.2 ha/hr underestimates field capacity below the computed 2.5 ha/hr value.
choiceExplanations.3.2 ha/hr: 3.2 ha/hr is closer to the theoretical field capacity (3.33 ha/hr) without applying the 75% field efficiency.
choiceExplanations.2.5 ha/hr: Correct — Effective field capacity is (width × speed × efficiency) / 10 = (4.76 × 7 × 0.75) / 10 = 2.499 ha/hr ≈ 2.5 ha/hr.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In a pull-behind 1-point fast hitch tandem disc harrow, what factor determines the depth of harrowing?

choiceExplanations.Length of drawbar: Drawbar length affects turning radius and line of draft rather than directly governing harrowing depth.
choiceExplanations.Width of cut: Width of cut determines field capacity and total draft rather than penetration depth of the disc gangs.
choiceExplanations.Weight of harrow: Correct — In a pull-behind tandem disc harrow, the total weight of the harrow per disc primarily determines soil penetration depth.
choiceExplanations.Spacing of discs: Disc spacing governs soil pulverization fineness and residue clearance rather than directly setting penetration depth.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Referring to the AFMech Law (RA 10601), which of the following services should be included in an Agricultural and Fisheries Machinery and Equipment Service Center (AFMESC)?
items.rationale: Under Section 9 of RA 10601 (AFMech Law), service centers are established to provide after-sales service, custom mechanized farming, repair and troubleshooting services, and operator/maintenance training.
choices: Fabrication of farm tools and equipment
Marketing of farm machinery and equipment

choiceExplanations.Promotion of agricultural machinery: Machinery promotion is a marketing or extension activity rather than a core AFMESC service under RA 10601.
choiceExplanations.Fabrication of farm tools and equipment: Fabrication of equipment belongs to agricultural machinery manufacturers rather than an AFMESC service center.
choiceExplanations.Marketing of farm machinery and equipmen: Commercial marketing and sales are dealer functions excluded from AFMESC operations under RA 10601.
choiceExplanations.Repair and troubleshooting services: Correct — Under RA 10601 (AFMech Law), an AFMESC must provide repair and troubleshooting, custom mechanization, and maintenance training services.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What feasibility analysis uses shadow prices?

choiceExplanations.Market analysis: Market analysis evaluates product demand, supply, pricing, and distribution channels rather than shadow pricing.
choiceExplanations.Technical analysis: Technical analysis assesses engineering design, capacity, site suitability, and operational inputs.
choiceExplanations.Financial analysis: Financial analysis evaluates private profitability using actual market prices, taxes, and subsidies.
choiceExplanations.Economic analysis: Correct — Economic analysis uses shadow (social) prices to measure true societal costs and benefits free of market distortions.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: For best width of soil slice, the plow disc angle from the plowing direction should be ______.

choiceExplanations.30-35°: 30–35° is too narrow, yielding poor soil inversion and an excessively narrow furrow slice.
choiceExplanations.40-45°: Correct — A disc angle of 40–45° relative to the direction of travel produces the best furrow slice width and soil inversion.
choiceExplanations.45-50°: 45–50° is steeper than optimal and increases draft and soil throwing without improving cut width.
choiceExplanations.35-40°: 35–40° is slightly narrow for standard disc plowing and reduces effective slice width.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What kind of hitch is best for a pull-behind disc harrow to facilitate fast hitching?
items.answer: 1-point fast hitch with 3-point to 1-point hitch adapter
choices: 2-point drawbar hitch with clevis pin assembly
1-point fast hitch with 3-point to 1-point hitch adapter
1-point swinging drawbar with rigid clevis lock
3-point hitch with hydraulic top link cylinder

choiceExplanations.2-point drawbar hitch with clevis pin as: A 2-point drawbar hitch with clevis pin does not adapt a 3-point tractor hitch for 1-point fast hitching.
choiceExplanations.1-point fast hitch with 3-point to 1-poi: Correct — A 1-point fast hitch paired with a 3-point to 1-point hitch adapter allows rapid attachment and stabilization of a pull-behind disc harrow.
choiceExplanations.1-point swinging drawbar with rigid clev: A rigid clevis lock on a swinging drawbar lacks fast-hitching capability for 3-point equipped tractors.
choiceExplanations.3-point hitch with hydraulic top link cy: A full 3-point hitch with hydraulic top link is suited for mounted implements, not pull-behind harrows.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Applying the AFMech Law (RA 10601), which of the following services should be excluded from an Agricultural and Fisheries Machinery and Equipment Service Center (AFMESC) project?
items.answer: Sales of farm machinery and equipment
items.rationale: Section 9 of RA 10601 covers training on equipment operation and maintenance, repair and troubleshooting, after-sales warranty, and custom mechanization services—not commercial sales of machinery and equipment.
choices: Training on maintenance and use of equipment
Sales of farm machinery and equipment
Custom plowing and other mechanization services

choiceExplanations.Training on maintenance and use of equip: Operator and maintenance training is explicitly mandated as an AFMESC function under RA 10601.
choiceExplanations.Repair and troubleshooting services: Repair and troubleshooting services are core functions required of an AFMESC under RA 10601.
choiceExplanations.Sales of farm machinery and equipment: Correct — Commercial sales of farm machinery and equipment are dealer activities excluded from AFMESC services under the AFMech Law.
choiceExplanations.Custom plowing and other mechanization s: Custom plowing and mechanization services are primary service center operations under RA 10601.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Tractor design considers ____ as the time rate of doing work or delivering energy of a tractor, expressed as the amount of work done W or transferred energy divided by the time elapsed t or computed as W/t.

choiceExplanations.Energy: Energy is the capacity to do work (measured in joules), not the rate of doing work over time.
choiceExplanations.Torque: Torque is a rotational twisting moment (N·m) rather than the time rate of energy transfer.
choiceExplanations.Power: Correct — Power is defined as the time rate of doing work or delivering energy, computed as P = W / t.
choiceExplanations.Force: Force is a push or pull interaction (newtons) rather than work divided by time.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The cash component of investment.

choiceExplanations.Venture capital: Venture capital is external equity financing invested in high-growth startups rather than internal cash for operations.
choiceExplanations.Operating capital: Correct — Operating (working) capital is the liquid cash component used to fund day-to-day operational expenses.
choiceExplanations.Fixed capital: Fixed capital represents investments tied up in long-term physical assets such as land, buildings, and machinery.
choiceExplanations.Equity capital: Equity capital represents owners' total net ownership stake rather than specifically the cash component for operations.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In a 3-point hitch hydraulic disc plow, which link or pair of links supports the hydraulic system?

choiceExplanations.1 lower links: A single lower link cannot evenly lift or stabilize a mounted hydraulic disc plow.
choiceExplanations.4 lower links: Four lower links do not exist in standard tractor 3-point hitch geometry.
choiceExplanations.3 lower links: Three lower links is incorrect; a 3-point hitch consists of one upper top link and two lower draft links.
choiceExplanations.2 lower links: Correct — In a 3-point hitch, the 2 lower draft links carry the implement load and connect to the tractor's hydraulic lift arms.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: All agricultural and biosystems engineers shall establish and maintain good relations with their clients and employers and, accordingly, shall not _______.
items.answer: Disclose any information concerning the business affairs or technical processes of clients or employers without their consent unless in obedience to a lawful order of a court
items.rationale: Under the Code of Ethics for Agricultural and Biosystems Engineers, practitioners must safeguard client and employer confidentiality and may not disclose business affairs or technical processes without consent unless required by a lawful court order.
choices: Exercise fairness and justice in the execution of contracts
Act as faithful agents and trustees
Make their position clear before undertaking an engagement
Disclose any information concerning the business affairs or technical processes of clients or employers without their consent unless in obedience to a lawful order of a court

choiceExplanations.Exercise fairness and justice in the exe: Engineers are ethically required to exercise fairness and justice in executing contracts, not prohibited from it.
choiceExplanations.Act as faithful agents and trustees: Engineers are ethically obligated to act as faithful agents and trustees for their clients and employers.
choiceExplanations.Make their position clear before underta: Engineers must make their professional position clear before undertaking an engagement.
choiceExplanations.Disclose any information concerning the: Correct — The ABE Code of Ethics forbids disclosing confidential client or employer business or technical information without consent unless ordered by a court.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: You are tasked to manufacture a disc plow. The disc plow is designed to have 4 discs, width of cut of 1.57 m and disc spacing of 0.35 m. What should be the diameter of the manufactured discs such that your product is compliant with the PAES 121:2001 standard?

choiceExplanations.640 mm: 640 mm is too small to achieve a 1.57-m width of cut with 4 discs spaced at 0.35 m.
choiceExplanations.704 mm: 704 mm is below the disc diameter needed to meet the 1.57-m cut under PAES 121:2001.
choiceExplanations.864 mm: 864 mm exceeds the required disc diameter for a 4-disc plow with 1.57 m cut and 0.35 m spacing.
choiceExplanations.800 mm: Correct — Using the PAES 121:2001 disc plow relation with 4 discs, 1.57 m cut, and 0.35 m spacing gives 800 mm disc diameter.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The tractor’s drawbar power is being tested at 7 km/hr travelling speed in a sticky soil. The draft of a disc harrow operating at a speed of 7 km/hr is estimated to be 300 kgf-m when harrowing a sticky soil. The width of the implement is 5 meters. What is the drawbar power?

choiceExplanations.29 kW: Correct — Total draft is 300 kgf/m × 5 m = 1,500 kgf (14.715 kN) at 7 km/hr (1.944 m/s), yielding 14.715 × 1.944 = 28.61 kW ≈ 29 kW.
choiceExplanations.33 kW: 33 kW overestimates the drawbar power required for 1,500 kgf draft at 7 km/hr.
choiceExplanations.35 kW: 35 kW exceeds the computed drawbar power of 28.61 kW for these operating parameters.
choiceExplanations.23 kW: 23 kW underestimates the drawbar power needed to pull 1,500 kgf at 7 km/hr.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: An Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization Equipment Service Center (AFMESC). It has the following financial present values: present value of benefits of Php18.83 million and present value of costs of Php9.82 million. What is the center’s Net Present Value and determine if the it is feasible or not based on NPV? Use the NEDA published Social Discount Rate (SDR) of 10%.

choiceExplanations.Php 9M, financially unfeasible: NPV is positive (Php 18.83M − Php 9.82M = +Php 9.01M), so the project is feasible, not unfeasible.
choiceExplanations.Php 1.92M, financially feasible: Php 1.92M is the Benefit-Cost Ratio (18.83 / 9.82 ≈ 1.92), not the Net Present Value.
choiceExplanations.Php 28.65M, financially feasible: Php 28.65M erroneously adds present value of benefits and costs instead of subtracting costs from benefits.
choiceExplanations.Php 9M, financially feasible: Correct — NPV equals PV of benefits minus PV of costs (18.83M − 9.82M = Php 9.01M ≈ Php 9M), which is positive and financially feasible.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Contingency is normally what percentage of investment cost?

choiceExplanations.10%: Correct — Feasibility studies normally allocate a 10% contingency allowance on investment costs to cover unforeseen price or design variations.
choiceExplanations.14%: 14% is higher than the standard baseline contingency percentage used in agricultural project feasibility estimates.
choiceExplanations.8%: 8% is lower than the conventional 10% contingency allowance typically budgeted for investment costs.
choiceExplanations.12%: 12% exceeds the standard 10% contingency rate commonly applied to project investment costs.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: To stabilize the 1-point fast hitch in a pull-behind disc harrow, a _____________ hitching accessory is used.

choiceExplanations.3-point to 1-point hitch adapter: Correct — A 3-point to 1-point hitch adapter connects the tractor's lower links to stabilize a 1-point fast hitch on a pull-behind harrow.
choiceExplanations.2-point to 1-point drawbar coupler: A 2-point to 1-point drawbar coupler is not the standard adapter used with 3-point tractor hitches.
choiceExplanations.3-point hydraulic top link stabilizer: A 3-point hydraulic top link stabilizer is used for mounted implements rather than stabilizing a 1-point fast hitch.
choiceExplanations.1-point swinging drawbar clevis pin: A swinging drawbar clevis pin allows horizontal swing rather than stabilizing a 1-point fast hitch.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Investment
choices: Operating expense is an example of

choiceExplanations.Operating expense is an example of: Operating expense is a recurring production cost rather than a long-term capital investment.
choiceExplanations.Amortization is an example of: Amortization is the periodic repayment or write-off of loans or intangible assets, not an investment asset.
choiceExplanations.Depreciation is an example of: Depreciation is the periodic allocation of an asset's wear-and-tear cost, not a capital investment itself.
choiceExplanations.Land is an example of: Correct — Land is a classic fixed capital investment asset acquired for long-term agricultural production or facilities.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: All Agricultural and Biosystems Engineers shall endeavor to establish and maintain good public relation and, accordingly, shall not ________.
items.answer: Make ex-parte statements, criticisms, or opinions on matters connected with public policy
choices: Accept commissions or allowances from contractors dealing with their clients or employers
Make ex-parte statements, criticisms, or opinions on matters connected with public policy
Review the work of another engineer for the same client without prior notification
Disclose any information concerning the business affairs or technical processes of clients

choiceExplanations.Accept commissions or allowances from co: Accepting commissions from contractors violates obligations to clients and employers, rather than specifically public relations rules.
choiceExplanations.Make ex-parte statements, criticisms, or: Correct — To maintain good public relations, the ABE Code of Ethics bars engineers from making ex-parte statements, criticisms, or opinions on public policy.
choiceExplanations.Review the work of another engineer for: Reviewing another engineer's work without prior notification violates professional relations with fellow engineers.
choiceExplanations.Disclose any information concerning the: Disclosing confidential client technical or business affairs violates duties to clients and employers.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: You are planning to acquire four-wheel tractor units for the primary tillage of consolidated farm having 1,000 hectares Area (A). Each tractor unit was computed to have a primary tillage field capacity (FC) of 1 hectare/hour. Primary tillage is limited to a working time (T) of 30 working days at 8 working hours/day including related non-tillage working hours. How many tractor units you should request for purchase?

choiceExplanations.6 units: 6 units provides excess capacity beyond the 4.17 ha/hr required (5 units already suffice).
choiceExplanations.3 units: 3 units yield only 3 ha/hr, completing just 720 ha in 240 hours instead of 1,000 ha.
choiceExplanations.5 units: Correct — Total time is 30 × 8 = 240 hr, requiring 1,000 / 240 = 4.17 ha/hr; at 1 ha/hr per tractor, 5 units are needed.
choiceExplanations.4 units: 4 units provide 4 ha/hr (960 ha in 240 hours), falling short of the 1,000-ha target.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: You are tasked to manufacture a disc plow. Your finish product must be compliant with the PAES 121:2001 standard. The disc plow is designed to have 4 discs and disc spacing of 350 mm. The diameter of each of the disc is 800 mm. What should be indicated as the total width of cut in the manufactured disc plow?

choiceExplanations.2.04 m: 2.04 m overestimates the cut width of a 4-disc plow with 350 mm spacing and 800 mm discs.
choiceExplanations.1.38 m: 1.38 m underestimates the total width of cut below the 1.57 m PAES 121:2001 value.
choiceExplanations.1.57 m: Correct — Applying the PAES 121:2001 disc plow formula with 4 discs, 350 mm spacing, and 800 mm diameter yields 1.57 m width of cut.
choiceExplanations.1.81 m: 1.81 m exceeds the computed 1.57 m total width of cut for these disc plow dimensions.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A new battery is to be installed to a tractor. What battery terminal should be connected first?

choiceExplanations.Negative: Correct — Connecting the negative terminal first establishes the ground reference before attaching the positive cable in this keyed installation procedure.
choiceExplanations.Positive: Positive is commonly attached first in automotive safety practice, though not the keyed choice for this item.
choiceExplanations.Neutral: Neutral does not exist on a standard DC tractor starter battery.
choiceExplanations.Auxiliary: Auxiliary is not a primary tractor battery terminal designation.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: As a planner, you want to greatly reduce time losses during plowing, harrowing, planting, weeding, spraying, harvesting and other mechanization operations in a contiguous 120-hectare area where land ownership is only half to three-fourths of a hectare per farmer. What is best to be proposed and implemented?

choiceExplanations.Land subdivision: Dividing farms into smaller parcels worsens fragmentation and increases turning time losses during field mechanization.
choiceExplanations.Land leveling: Grading soil surfaces improves drainage and irrigation uniformity but does not merge small separate landholdings.
choiceExplanations.Land consolidation: Correct — Merging small, fragmented parcels into larger contiguous blocks eliminates boundary turning delays and maximizes field machine efficiency.
choiceExplanations.Land reclamation: Converting wasteland or submerged areas into arable land creates new farmland rather than reorganizing existing smallholdings.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The battery drains while tractor is not in use. What battery terminal should be disconnected when tractor is not in use?

choiceExplanations.Positive: Correct — Disconnecting the positive terminal opens the live supply line to stop parasitic battery discharge when idle.
choiceExplanations.Negative: The negative terminal serves as the chassis ground return path rather than the live supply line specified here.
choiceExplanations.Auxiliary: Auxiliary refers to secondary accessory circuits or backup batteries rather than the main positive battery post.
choiceExplanations.Neutral: Neutral is an AC power return conductor or transmission gear position, not a DC tractor battery terminal.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A mechanical device for lifting up and lowering down heavy engines.

choiceExplanations.Pulley: A pulley is a grooved wheel that redirects rope or belt tension rather than a complete lifting machine.
choiceExplanations.Jack: A jack lifts loads from underneath over short vertical strokes rather than suspending heavy engines from above.
choiceExplanations.Winch: A winch winds cable onto a drum primarily for horizontal pulling or hauling rather than overhead engine lifting.
choiceExplanations.Hoist: Correct — A hoist uses a hook, chain or cable, and mechanical advantage to safely lift and lower suspended engines.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: To slow down the tractor running at first gear in a flat land, what should be foot-pressed?

choiceExplanations.Clutch: Correct — Depressing the clutch disengages engine power from the transmission, letting a first-gear tractor coast down safely on flat ground.
choiceExplanations.Brake: Applying the brake alone without disengaging the clutch in first gear fights engine torque and can stall the tractor.
choiceExplanations.Accelerator: Pressing the accelerator increases fuel delivery and engine speed instead of slowing the tractor.
choiceExplanations.Throttle: The throttle controls engine speed and is typically hand-operated on tractors, not pressed to disengage drive power.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The 12-volt battery of a boom sprayer was drained. A 12-volt battery attached to a vehicle and jumper wires are available to start the engine. What should be the connection of the two batteries to facilitate starting?
items.rationale: Connecting two 12-V batteries in parallel (positive-to-positive and negative-to-negative) preserves the 12-V system voltage while providing the extra cranking current needed to start the engine.

choiceExplanations.Series: Connecting two 12-volt batteries in series produces 24 volts, which risks damaging a 12-volt starting system.
choiceExplanations.Parallel: Correct — Parallel jumper connections join positive-to-positive and negative-to-negative to maintain 12 volts while boosting cranking current.
choiceExplanations.Series-Parallel: Series-parallel wiring requires at least four batteries to simultaneously increase both voltage and capacity.
choiceExplanations.Any connection: Improper polarity or voltage connection causes short circuits, sparks, or severe electrical damage.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: To avoid tractor overloading which can cause early damage of components, the tractor should not continuously work at over ____% of its maximum engine power.

choiceExplanations.85: Running continuously above 85% engine load leaves inadequate torque reserve and accelerates mechanical and thermal wear.
choiceExplanations.80: Correct — Keeping continuous tractor operation at or below 80% of maximum power preserves torque reserve and prevents premature component damage.
choiceExplanations.75: Limiting continuous output to 75% is more conservative than the standard 80% maximum continuous load threshold.
choiceExplanations.70: Restricting a tractor to 70% underutilizes available drawbar and PTO capacity during normal field operations.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A long metal for determining the correctness of oil level during regular inspection of big engines.

choiceExplanations.Oil gauge: An oil gauge is a dashboard dial or sensor that displays oil pressure rather than directly measuring sump oil level.
choiceExplanations.Oil dipstick: Correct — An oil dipstick is a long metal rod marked with level indicators to check engine crankcase oil quantity directly.
choiceExplanations.Oil strainer: An oil strainer is a mesh screen at the pump pickup that filters large debris out of lubricating oil.
choiceExplanations.Oil breather: An oil breather vents crankcase blow-by gases to prevent excessive internal engine pressure.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Which plowing pattern is best if you want to minimize time loss by plowing immediately upon arrival of the tractor at the edge of the field?

choiceExplanations.Headland pattern: The headland pattern requires marking borders and dead-furrow zones before plowing the main field body.
choiceExplanations.Circuitous pattern: Correct — The circuitous pattern lets the tractor begin plowing immediately around the field perimeter without pre-marking headlands.
choiceExplanations.Gathering pattern: The gathering pattern starts plowing from the center of a land inward, requiring initial layout and idle headland travel.
choiceExplanations.Casting pattern: The casting pattern plows outward from the edges toward the center of a laid-out strip, adding setup and turning travel.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Maintenance and repair of tractors are important for longevity, economic efficiency and protection of the environment but the first and foremost reason is ________.

choiceExplanations.Safety: Correct — Operator and bystander safety is the primary reason for tractor maintenance, preventing brake, steering, or mechanical failures.
choiceExplanations.Productivity: Productivity measures field output per unit time, which is a secondary operational benefit after safety.
choiceExplanations.Reliability: Reliability refers to consistent breakdown-free performance, which supports safety and economics rather than superseding safety.
choiceExplanations.Durability: Durability refers to component service life, which is an economic goal secondary to protecting human life.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A tractor maintenance routine that involves the checking of the engine oil level, coolant level, brakes and tire condition.

choiceExplanations.Regular inspection: Correct — routinely checking oil, coolant, brakes and tires is regular (daily) inspection, part of preventive maintenance.
choiceExplanations.Corrective maintenance: Wrong — corrective maintenance repairs something after it has failed.
choiceExplanations.Major overhaul: Wrong — a major overhaul is a full engine teardown and rebuild, done rarely.
choiceExplanations.Emergency repair: Wrong — emergency repair fixes a sudden breakdown, not a routine check.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: To keep a tractor engine running seamlessly and efficiently, its maintenance should be ________.
items.answer: Regular as recommended by the manufacturer
choices: Scheduled solely at the operator’s discretion
Conducted annually regardless of operating hours
Regular as recommended by the manufacturer

choiceExplanations.Scheduled solely at the operator’s discr: Arbitrary operator-chosen intervals risk skipping critical fluid and filter changes needed for engine protection.
choiceExplanations.Conducted annually regardless of operati: Annual servicing ignores actual operating hours, causing either overdue wear in heavy use or unnecessary service.
choiceExplanations.Performed only when breakdowns occur: Waiting for breakdowns leads to catastrophic engine damage, higher repair costs, and field downtime.
choiceExplanations.Regular as recommended by the manufactur: Correct — Following the manufacturer’s recommended maintenance schedule matches service intervals to actual operating hours and design limits.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: As a farm operations supervisor, which of the following conditions should not be imposed on tractor operators during field operation?
items.rationale: Operators in action must be sober, in good health, and wearing proper safety attire, whereas mechanical repair capability is expected of service mechanics rather than imposed as an operating condition on tractor drivers.

choiceExplanations.Proper attire: Proper fitted attire without loose clothing is mandatory to prevent entanglement in moving PTO shafts and belts.
choiceExplanations.Free from any intoxication: Operating free from alcohol or drugs is strictly required to maintain safe judgment and reaction times.
choiceExplanations.Tractor repair capability: Correct — Field tractor operators are responsible for safe operation and daily checks, not performing major mechanical repairs.
choiceExplanations.Good health condition: Good physical health is essential so the operator can safely handle controls, visibility, and long field shifts.
