items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: ENGINEERING DRAWING: it is a geometrically represented image (visual image or figure) of an object obtained on a surface or plane

choiceExplanations.Elevation: A specific orthographic front, rear, or side view showing vertical height of a structure.
choiceExplanations.Development: Unfolded flat pattern of all surfaces of a 3D object for sheet-metal fabrication.
choiceExplanations.Projection: Correct — Projection is the geometric representation of an object formed on a projection plane using lines of sight.
choiceExplanations.Section: A cutaway view revealing internal features along an imaginary cutting plane.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: There should be provision for mosquito control such as mosquitofish stocking, vegetation management, application of chemical and biological control agents. Harvesting of the emergent vegetation should be practiced to maintain hydraulic capacity, promote active growth and avoid mosquito growth.

choiceExplanations.Facultative lagoon: A deep stabilization pond with aerobic upper and anaerobic lower layers, lacking emergent wetland plants.
choiceExplanations.Constructed wetland: Correct — PAES wastewater management specifies mosquitofish stocking and emergent vegetation harvesting for constructed wetlands to control mosquitoes.
choiceExplanations.Oxidation pond: A shallow open biological pond relying on algae and sunlight rather than emergent vegetation.
choiceExplanations.Aerated lagoon: A wastewater basin using mechanical aerators for oxygen transfer rather than emergent plants.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Grain to straw ratio requirement for testing a rice thresher range from _____.

choiceExplanations.0.4 to 0.52: Below the standard PAES grain-to-straw ratio range specified for testing mechanical rice threshers.
choiceExplanations.0.5 to 0.65: Correct — PAES rice thresher testing standards require a test crop grain-to-straw ratio between 0.50 and 0.65.
choiceExplanations.0.5 to 0.59: Truncates the upper limit of the 0.5 to 0.65 PAES rice thresher standard.
choiceExplanations.0.6 to 0.72: Exceeds the standard 0.50 to 0.65 grain-to-straw ratio required for rice thresher testing.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The term used for money that is used for future profit.

choiceExplanations.Dividend: A share of corporate earnings distributed periodically to stockholders rather than initial capital.
choiceExplanations.Investment: Correct — Investment is capital or money committed to an asset or venture with the expectation of generating future profit.
choiceExplanations.Annuity: A series of equal periodic payments made or received at fixed intervals.
choiceExplanations.Principal: The original sum of money borrowed or loaned on which interest is calculated.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: An open trench left between the adjacent strips of land after finishing the plowing operation

choiceExplanations.Headland furrow: A furrow plowed across the ends of a field to mark turning boundaries.
choiceExplanations.Back furrow: A raised ridge formed when two furrow slices are thrown together at the start.
choiceExplanations.Crown furrow: The center raised ridge of a plowed land, similar to a back furrow.
choiceExplanations.Dead furrow: Correct — A dead furrow is an open trench left when furrow slices are turned away from each other at finishing.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Many sellers are independently selling different types of products and/or services.

choiceExplanations.Pure monopoly: A market structure with only one seller controlling a unique product.
choiceExplanations.Bilateral monopoly: A market having a single seller facing a single buyer.
choiceExplanations.Pure oligopoly: A market dominated by only a few sellers offering identical products.
choiceExplanations.Perfect competition: Correct — In standard ABELE reviewer definitions, perfect competition describes a market with many independent sellers.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A type of proprietorship where there is an arrangement between two or more people to oversee business operations and share its profits and liabilities.

choiceExplanations.Partnership: Correct — A partnership is a business arrangement where two or more co-owners manage operations and share profits and liabilities.
choiceExplanations.Corporation: A distinct legal entity owned by shareholders with limited personal liability.
choiceExplanations.Franchise: A licensing arrangement allowing an operator to use an established brand and business model.
choiceExplanations.Cooperative: An autonomous member-owned association formed to meet shared economic, social, and cultural needs.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: an unincorporated business that has just one owner who pays personal income tax on profits earned from the business.

choiceExplanations.Stock corporation: An incorporated legal entity with capital divided into shares owned by multiple stockholders.
choiceExplanations.General partnership: An unincorporated business owned and managed jointly by two or more general partners.
choiceExplanations.Sole proprietorship: Correct — A sole proprietorship is an unincorporated business owned by one individual who reports profits on personal income tax.
choiceExplanations.Limited partnership: A partnership comprising at least one general partner and one limited-liability partner.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: is a member-owned entity that seeks to meet its members’ social, economic, and cultural needs.

choiceExplanations.Cooperative: Correct — Under RA 9520, a cooperative is an autonomous, member-owned association meeting members' economic, social, and cultural needs.
choiceExplanations.Partnership: A for-profit business owned by two or more partners sharing profits and liabilities.
choiceExplanations.Corporation: A legal entity owned by stockholders primarily focused on generating returns on equity.
choiceExplanations.Proprietorship: A business owned and operated solely by one individual for personal profit.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Time value of money and interest rate utilized together generate this concept which means that different sums of money at different times can be equal in economic value.

choiceExplanations.Equivalence: Correct — Economic equivalence means different cash amounts occurring at different times have equal value at a given interest rate.
choiceExplanations.Discounting: The specific calculation of finding the present value of a future cash amount.
choiceExplanations.Compounding: The specific calculation of growing a present sum to a future value via interest.
choiceExplanations.Amortization: Spreading loan repayment into scheduled periodic installments covering principal and interest.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A tillage equipment that cuts the soil to a depth of 6” to 18”.

choiceExplanations.Rotavator: A PTO-driven rotary tiller that pulverizes shallow topsoil typically 3 to 6 inches deep.
choiceExplanations.Moldboard: Correct — A moldboard plow is a primary tillage implement that cuts, lifts, and inverts soil at typical depths of 6–18 inches.
choiceExplanations.Subsoiler: A deep-tillage implement designed to shatter compacted hardpans 18 to 36 inches deep.
choiceExplanations.Cultivator: A secondary tillage implement used shallowly to control weeds and loosen surface crust.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A tillage equipment that cuts the soil to a depth of 3”-6”

choiceExplanations.Disc harrow: Correct — A disc harrow is a secondary tillage implement that cuts and pulverizes soil to a typical depth of 3–6 inches.
choiceExplanations.Moldboard plow: A primary tillage implement that cuts and inverts soil deeper, typically 6 to 18 inches.
choiceExplanations.Rotary tiller: Although shallow-working, standard ABELE classification keys 3–6 inches specifically to the disc harrow.
choiceExplanations.Chisel plow: A primary tillage implement using shanks to loosen soil deeper than 6 inches without inversion.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A tillage equipment that cuts the soil to a depth of less than 6”

choiceExplanations.Subsoil tillage: Deep fracturing of compacted soil layers below normal plow depth, typically over 18 inches.
choiceExplanations.Primary tillage: Initial deeper soil-breaking operations cutting 6 to 36 inches deep before seedbed refinement.
choiceExplanations.Deep tillage: Tillage operations penetrating well below 6 inches to break hardpan and improve drainage.
choiceExplanations.General purpose tillage: Correct — General purpose (or shallow/secondary) tillage cuts and works the soil at depths less than 6 inches.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A tillage equipment that cuts the soil to a depth of 6”-36"

choiceExplanations.Primary tillage: Correct — Primary tillage is the initial, aggressive soil-breaking operation reaching depths of 6 to 36 inches.
choiceExplanations.Zero tillage: Planting directly into undisturbed soil residue without prior mechanical soil inversion or loosening.
choiceExplanations.Secondary tillage: Shallow follow-up tillage under 6 inches used to refine the seedbed and control weeds.
choiceExplanations.Minimum tillage: Reduced-pass tillage practice limiting soil disturbance rather than specifying a 6–36 inch cut.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A sedimentary rock where clay is the main constituent

choiceExplanations.Limestone: A chemical or biochemical sedimentary rock composed predominantly of calcium carbonate minerals.
choiceExplanations.Conglomerate: A coarse-grained clastic sedimentary rock made of rounded gravel-sized pebbles cemented together.
choiceExplanations.Shale: Correct — Shale is a fine-grained clastic sedimentary rock formed mainly from compacted clay and silt particles.
choiceExplanations.Sandstone: A clastic sedimentary rock composed primarily of cemented sand-sized quartz or feldspar grains.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: 1° of Earth’s rotation is equivalent to _____.

choiceExplanations.5 minutes: Corresponds to 1.25° of rotation, since 360° takes 24 hours (1,440 minutes).
choiceExplanations.4 minutes: Correct — Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours (1,440 minutes), so 1° equals 1,440 ÷ 360 = 4 minutes.
choiceExplanations.3 minutes: Corresponds to 0.75° of Earth rotation rather than a full 1° longitude change.
choiceExplanations.2 minutes: Corresponds to 0.5° of Earth rotation, half the actual 4-minute rate per degree.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The elevation of line of sight of the instrument to a selected reference datum

choiceExplanations.Bench mark: A permanent fixed reference point with a known elevation above a datum.
choiceExplanations.Turning point: A temporary point used to transfer instrument elevation between consecutive leveling setups.
choiceExplanations.Height of instrument: Correct — Height of instrument (HI) is the elevation of the leveling instrument's line of sight above the reference datum.
choiceExplanations.Foresight reading: A rod reading taken on a point of unknown elevation to determine its height.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The transition in which gas transforms into solid without passing through the liquid phase

choiceExplanations.Vaporization: Phase transition where a liquid changes into a gas or vapor.
choiceExplanations.Sublimation: Phase transition directly from solid to gas, the reverse of deposition.
choiceExplanations.Deposition: Correct — Deposition (desublimation) is the direct phase transition from gas to solid without passing through the liquid state.
choiceExplanations.Condensation: Phase transition where a gas cools and transforms into a liquid.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: solid to gas

choiceExplanations.Sublimation: Correct — Sublimation is the direct phase change of a substance from solid to gas without becoming liquid.
choiceExplanations.Deposition: The reverse phase change where a gas transitions directly into a solid.
choiceExplanations.Vaporization: Phase change where a liquid transforms into a gas through boiling or evaporation.
choiceExplanations.Melting: Phase change where a solid absorbs heat and transforms into a liquid.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: solid to liquid

choiceExplanations.Sublimation: Direct phase transition from a solid straight into a gas.
choiceExplanations.Condensation: Phase transition from a gas into a liquid upon cooling.
choiceExplanations.Fusion: Correct — Fusion (melting) is the thermodynamic phase change from a solid to a liquid state.
choiceExplanations.Freezing: Phase transition where a liquid releases heat and solidifies into a solid.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: liquid to gas

choiceExplanations.Solidification: Phase change from a liquid into a solid, also known as freezing.
choiceExplanations.Condensation: Phase change from a gas into a liquid upon heat removal.
choiceExplanations.Vaporization: Correct — Vaporization (evaporation or boiling) is the phase transition of a substance from liquid to gas.
choiceExplanations.Sublimation: Direct phase change from a solid to a gas, bypassing the liquid phase.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: gas to liquid

choiceExplanations.Condensation: Correct — Condensation is the phase change in which a gas or vapor transforms into a liquid.
choiceExplanations.Vaporization: Phase change in which a liquid converts into a gas.
choiceExplanations.Sublimation: Direct phase change of a solid into a gas without melting.
choiceExplanations.Deposition: Direct phase change of a gas into a solid without becoming liquid.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Given a coordinate (5.9, -1.9). This type of coordinate is __________.

choiceExplanations.Cartesian: Correct — An ordered pair (x, y) such as (5.9, -1.9) specifies horizontal and vertical distances in the 2D Cartesian plane.
choiceExplanations.Cylindrical: Uses three parameters (r, θ, z) with an angle rather than two signed rectangular lengths.
choiceExplanations.Polar: Uses radius and angle (r, θ), typically written with an angular measure or degree symbol.
choiceExplanations.Spherical: Uses three parameters (ρ, θ, φ) to locate points in three-dimensional space.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In PAES 224 - Rice Combine – Specifications, what emblem shall be fitted in the rice combine?

choiceExplanations.Wide-Body Harvester: Not a standardized safety emblem specified in PAES 224 for rice combines.
choiceExplanations.Oversized Load Vehicle: Road transport signage for wide haulage, not the standard PAES 224 machine emblem.
choiceExplanations.Heavy-Duty Implement: Not an official safety emblem mandated by PAES 224 specifications.
choiceExplanations.Slow-Moving Vehicle: Correct — PAES 224 requires a triangular Slow-Moving Vehicle (SMV) emblem fitted on the rear of a rice combine.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the smallest computer language?

choiceExplanations.Kilobyte: Equals 1,024 bytes (or 1,000 bytes in decimal), far larger than a single bit.
choiceExplanations.Nibble: A group of four bits, half of a standard byte.
choiceExplanations.Bit: Correct — A bit (binary digit, 0 or 1) is the smallest unit of data in computing and machine language.
choiceExplanations.Byte: A group of eight bits used to encode a single character.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is the medium between human and the hardware.

choiceExplanations.Device driver: Low-level software enabling the OS to communicate with one specific hardware peripheral.
choiceExplanations.Operating system: Correct — The operating system acts as the core interface managing hardware resources and mediating between the user and computer hardware.
choiceExplanations.Application software: End-user programs such as word processors or CAD tools running atop the OS.
choiceExplanations.Utility program: Specialized maintenance software for tasks like disk cleanup, backup, or antivirus scanning.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Space requirements for boars
items.answer: 20 to 65 sq.ft Sow 48 to 80 sq. ft Pigs 3 to 6 sq. ft Fattening hogs 6 to 10 sq. ft Boars 20 to 65 sq. ft
choices: 20 to 65 sq.ft Sow 48 to 80 sq. ft Pigs 3 to 6 sq. ft Fattening hogs 6 to 10 sq. ft Boars 20 to 65 sq. ft

choiceExplanations.48 to 80 sq.ft: Standard floor space requirement for a sow (48 to 80 sq. ft), not a boar.
choiceExplanations.20 to 65 sq.ft Sow 48 to 80 sq. ft Pigs: Correct — Standard swine housing guidelines specify 20 to 65 sq. ft per boar (matching the reviewer's included swine space table).
choiceExplanations.6 to 10 sq.ft: Standard floor space requirement for fattening hogs (6 to 10 sq. ft), not boars.
choiceExplanations.3 to 6 sq.ft: Standard floor space requirement for young pigs (3 to 6 sq. ft), not boars.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In a frequency of 60Hz, there are __ cycles per second.

choiceExplanations.60: Correct — Hertz (Hz) is defined as cycles per second, so 60 Hz equals 60 cycles per second.
choiceExplanations.65: Would correspond to a frequency of 65 Hz, not 60 Hz.
choiceExplanations.50: Corresponds to 50 Hz electrical power systems, not 60 Hz.
choiceExplanations.55: Would correspond to a frequency of 55 Hz, not 60 Hz.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Instrument that measures the difference in pressure head

choiceExplanations.Manometer: Correct — A manometer (such as a U-tube or differential manometer) directly measures pressure or pressure head differences using a fluid column.
choiceExplanations.Barometer: Measures atmospheric air pressure rather than fluid pressure head difference.
choiceExplanations.Tensiometer: Measures soil moisture tension (matric potential) in agricultural soils.
choiceExplanations.Hydrometer: Measures the specific gravity or density of a liquid.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: One of the best ways of preserving endangered animal species.

choiceExplanations.Botanical garden: Conserves living plant collections rather than endangered animal genetic material.
choiceExplanations.Clonal orchard: Preserves vegetatively propagated fruit or forest trees, not animal species.
choiceExplanations.Gene bank: Correct — An animal gene bank preserves semen, embryos, oocytes, and DNA to conserve endangered animal species.
choiceExplanations.Seed bank: Stores plant seeds under controlled conditions for crop biodiversity, not animal germplasm.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is the exchange of goods and services measured in terms of money.

choiceExplanations.Barter: Direct exchange of goods or services for other goods without using money.
choiceExplanations.Capital: Wealth, machinery, or financial assets invested to produce further goods and services.
choiceExplanations.Utility: The total satisfaction or value a consumer derives from using a good.
choiceExplanations.Price Other reference: “commerce”: Correct — In ABELE economics reviewers, price (or commerce in alternate texts) denotes exchange value measured in terms of money.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Weight of a typical knapsack sprayer.
items.rationale: 22 kg (full) / 6 kg (empty)

choiceExplanations.22 kg (full): Correct — Standard PAES specifications limit a filled lever-operated knapsack sprayer's maximum total weight to 22 kg.
choiceExplanations.20 kg (full): Understates the 22 kg maximum full-weight standard specified for typical knapsack sprayers.
choiceExplanations.24 kg (full): Exceeds the 22 kg maximum full-weight limit ergonomically specified in PAES sprayer standards.
choiceExplanations.18 kg (full): Understates the 22 kg full-tank weight benchmark used in PAES knapsack sprayer specifications.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The primary factor that affects the performance of the sprayer

choiceExplanations.Operating-pressure level: An adjustable machine setting that influences droplet size and flow rate rather than the primary factor.
choiceExplanations.Spray-particle size: Correct — Spray-particle (droplet) size governs target coverage, penetration, evaporation loss, and drift, making it primary to sprayer performance.
choiceExplanations.Ground-travel speed: Controls application volume per hectare rather than directly defining spray droplet behavior.
choiceExplanations.Nozzle-orifice size: A nozzle dimension affecting flow rate and atomization, secondary to resulting droplet size.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Primary gas produced during gasification

choiceExplanations.Carbon dioxide: A product of complete combustion rather than the primary combustible gas in producer gas.
choiceExplanations.Nitrous oxide: A greenhouse gas emitted from nitrogenous soils, not a main biomass gasification product.
choiceExplanations.Hydrogen sulfide: A minor toxic impurity from sulfur-bearing feedstocks, not the primary gasification product.
choiceExplanations.Carbon monoxide: Correct — Biomass gasification produces producer gas whose primary combustible constituent is carbon monoxide (CO), alongside hydrogen and methane.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Stoichiometric air requirement for gasification.

choiceExplanations.26%-34%: Slightly below the standard 30%–40% stoichiometric air equivalence ratio typical of biomass gasification.
choiceExplanations.28%-37%: Does not match the standard 30%–40% stoichiometric air requirement cited for biomass gasifiers.
choiceExplanations.33%-44%: Exceeds the typical 30%–40% air-supply range before excessive combustion reduces gas heating value.
choiceExplanations.30%-40%: Correct — Gasification uses partial oxidation with typically 30%–40% of the stoichiometric air needed for complete combustion.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Robin engines are manufactured from?

choiceExplanations.Taiwan: Not the country of origin for Robin small engines (Fuji Heavy Industries/Subaru).
choiceExplanations.Germany: Not the manufacturing origin of Robin engines, which are Japanese-engineered.
choiceExplanations.China: Not the original manufacturing country of Robin engines, though knockoffs exist.
choiceExplanations.Japan: Correct — Robin small engines were originally developed and manufactured in Japan by Fuji Heavy Industries (later Subaru Robin).

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Changing of transmission oil for tractors should be done every

choiceExplanations.6 months or 22,080 km: Incorrect mileage figure that alters the standard 24,000 km maintenance benchmark.
choiceExplanations.5 months or 20,400 km: Incorrect interval differing from the standard 6 months or 24,000 km specification.
choiceExplanations.7 months or 26,400 km: Exceeds the standard 6-month or 24,000-km interval cited in the reviewer.
choiceExplanations.6 months or 24,000 km: Correct — Standard agricultural machinery maintenance reviewers cite changing transmission oil every 6 months or 24,000 km.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A process by which a farm manager looks ahead to the future and contemplates alternative courses of action for the farm.

choiceExplanations.Farm planning: Correct — Farm planning is the forward-looking management process of evaluating resources and selecting among alternative courses of farm action.
choiceExplanations.Farm organization: Arranging land, labor, and capital resources to execute an already chosen farm plan.
choiceExplanations.Farm budgeting: Estimating expected revenues, costs, and net returns for a specific farm plan.
choiceExplanations.Farm supervision: Overseeing daily farm operations and workers to ensure plans are carried out.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Involves converting inputs into outputs.

choiceExplanations.Distribution: Moving and delivering finished goods from producers to consumers or retail outlets.
choiceExplanations.Consumption: Using up finished goods and services by end users to satisfy needs.
choiceExplanations.Marketing: Promoting, pricing, and selling goods and services rather than transforming raw inputs.
choiceExplanations.Production: Correct — Production is the economic and engineering process of transforming resource inputs into valuable goods or service outputs.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is an increase in the production of economic goods and services

choiceExplanations.Economic growth: Correct — Economic growth is a sustained quantitative increase in an economy's output of goods and services (real GDP).
choiceExplanations.Economic development: Broader qualitative improvement in living standards, institutions, and human welfare beyond output growth.
choiceExplanations.Economic stability: Maintaining steady prices, low unemployment, and balanced macroeconomic fluctuations.
choiceExplanations.Economic efficiency: Producing maximum output from given inputs or allocating resources without waste.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: On what year does the profession Agricultural Engineering was introduced to the world. It’s also the year when US first offered BSAE course.
items.rationale: 1903 / 1907 - AE was recognized as a discipline, ASAE was formed / 1950 - year when PSAE was founded by Engr. Felix Maramba

choiceExplanations.1903: Correct — Iowa State College first offered the Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Engineering curriculum in 1903, marking the profession's formal birth.
choiceExplanations.1713: 1713 predates modern agricultural engineering and precedes the early nineteenth-century industrial mechanization era.
choiceExplanations.1522: 1522 falls in the sixteenth-century Renaissance period, centuries before university engineering curricula existed.
choiceExplanations.2093: 2093 is a future year well after the twentieth-century establishment of agricultural engineering.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Most abundant cell in organic material

choiceExplanations.Lignin: Lignin is a rigid aromatic polymer providing structural strength in woody plant cell walls, less abundant than cellulose.
choiceExplanations.Pectin: Pectin is a soluble polysaccharide cementing primary plant cell walls, present in much smaller proportions.
choiceExplanations.Cellulose: Correct — Cellulose is a linear glucose polymer forming plant cell walls and is the most abundant organic compound in biomass.
choiceExplanations.Hemicellulose: Hemicellulose consists of shorter branched polysaccharides cross-linking cellulose microfibrils, typically making up a smaller fraction.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Recommended gutter heights for multi span houses to allow machines to move freely.

choiceExplanations.3.8m-3m: 3.8 m to 3 m is an inverted, invalid range that exceeds standard multi-span greenhouse gutter clearance.
choiceExplanations.2.8m-3m: Correct — Multi-span greenhouses typically use 2.8 m to 3 m gutter heights to provide adequate clearance for machinery and ventilation.
choiceExplanations.1.8m-3m: A 1.8 m minimum gutter height is too low for tractors and standard greenhouse machinery to pass freely.
choiceExplanations.4.8m-3m: 4.8 m to 3 m is an inverted range and unnecessarily tall for standard multi-span greenhouse designs.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Mineral Content of paddy which can cause wear and tear of machine.

choiceExplanations.Silica: Correct — Rice hulls and paddy contain high levels of abrasive silica (SiO2) that rapidly wears milling and harvesting components.
choiceExplanations.Magnesium: Magnesium is an essential plant macronutrient found in chlorophyll and does not cause significant abrasive wear.
choiceExplanations.Alumina: Alumina (aluminum oxide) is an industrial ceramic abrasive, not a major mineral constituent of rice paddy.
choiceExplanations.Calcium: Calcium is a secondary plant nutrient in cell walls and does not cause major mechanical abrasion.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Time interval successive repetition of a periodic wave form:

choiceExplanations.Frequency: Frequency is the number of complete wave cycles occurring per unit time, measured in hertz.
choiceExplanations.Wavelength: Wavelength is the spatial distance between two consecutive identical points on a wave.
choiceExplanations.Period: Correct — The period is the time interval required for one complete cycle or successive repetition of a periodic waveform.
choiceExplanations.Amplitude: Amplitude is the maximum displacement or peak magnitude of a wave measured from its equilibrium position.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Panicles of the cut plants are fed into the threshing chamber while the stalks are mechanically or manually held during operation.

choiceExplanations.Through-flow thresher: In a through-flow thresher, whole cut stalks and panicles pass completely through the threshing cylinder.
choiceExplanations.Hold-on thresher: Correct — Per PAES rice thresher classification, a hold-on thresher feeds only the panicles into the chamber while holding the stalks.
choiceExplanations.Throw-in thresher: A throw-in thresher accepts entire harvested crop bundles directly into the threshing cylinder without holding the stalks.
choiceExplanations.Tangential-flow thresher: Tangential-flow describes crop movement perpendicular to the cylinder axis, not whether stalks are held during feeding.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Subsurface system wherein laterals join the submain on the both sides alternately.

choiceExplanations.Gridiron: In a gridiron subsurface drainage layout, parallel laterals enter only one side of the submain.
choiceExplanations.Herringbone: Correct — A herringbone subsurface drainage system places parallel laterals at acute angles entering both sides of a central submain.
choiceExplanations.Parallel: A parallel system arranges uniformly spaced laterals draining into a single main or submain along one side.
choiceExplanations.Interceptor: An interceptor drain sits across a slope to cut off and divert subsurface seepage water.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Drain layout for fields with relatively flat portions in the middle.

choiceExplanations.Parallel ditch: Parallel ditch systems use evenly spaced field ditches across uniform slopes rather than flanking a flat center.
choiceExplanations.Double main: Correct — A double main layout places two submains along the sides of a depression or flat middle area to drain adjacent slopes.
choiceExplanations.Single main: A single main system uses one central main line, suitable for narrow depressions rather than broad flat centers.
choiceExplanations.Cross slope: Cross-slope ditches run across sloping land to intercept surface runoff before it causes erosion.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Zone planning can be a useful tool, but it is most effective when planning a new farmstead. The farmstead is divided into different zones of 10 to 30 meters wide by concentric circles. The family living area is placed under

choiceExplanations.Zone 2: Zone 2 surrounds the living area and houses light machinery storage, garages, and farm workshops.
choiceExplanations.Zone 3: Zone 3 is located farther out for grain storage, feed processing, and heavy equipment sheds.
choiceExplanations.Zone 4: Zone 4 lies outermost from the house and accommodates livestock buildings, manure storage, and odors.
choiceExplanations.Zone 1: Correct — In concentric farmstead zone planning, Zone 1 is the innermost ring reserved for the family living area and farmhouse.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: It is a plan of action proposed by the constructor to the concerned agency’s implementing office which is aimed to prevent the recurrence of nonconforming findings on his on-going and/or future projects.

choiceExplanations.Remedial action plan: A remedial action plan fixes immediate defects or damage rather than preventing future nonconformities.
choiceExplanations.Preventive action plan: Correct — A preventive action plan outlines contractor measures to eliminate causes of potential nonconformities and prevent recurrence on ongoing or future work.
choiceExplanations.Corrective action plan: A corrective action plan addresses the root cause of an already detected nonconformity after it occurs.
choiceExplanations.Quality assurance plan: A quality assurance plan defines overall project quality standards and inspection procedures rather than nonconformity prevention.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: AutoCAD: It is used to restrict cursor movement to specific directions. It allows the cursor movement only in the vertical and horizontal direction.

choiceExplanations.Snap: Snap restricts cursor movement to specified grid increments or geometric object points.
choiceExplanations.Grid: Grid displays a visual reference pattern of dots or lines on the drawing area.
choiceExplanations.Polar: Polar tracking guides cursor movement along user-defined angular increments beyond horizontal and vertical axes.
choiceExplanations.Ortho: Correct — Ortho mode in AutoCAD constrains cursor movement strictly to horizontal and vertical directions.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Proportionate savings in costs gained by an increased level of production

choiceExplanations.Economy of scale: Correct — Economies of scale occur when unit production costs decrease proportionally as total output volume increases.
choiceExplanations.Economy of scope: Economy of scope refers to cost savings achieved by producing multiple different products together.
choiceExplanations.Cost of production: Cost of production is the total expense incurred to manufacture a good or provide a service.
choiceExplanations.Return on investment: Return on investment measures the financial gain or profitability relative to the capital invested.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: This refers to the decrease in price of goods/products/services

choiceExplanations.Inflation: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services over time.
choiceExplanations.Deflation: Correct — Deflation is a general decrease in the price level of goods, products, and services over time.
choiceExplanations.Depreciation: Depreciation is the reduction in book or market value of a physical asset due to wear or age.
choiceExplanations.Stagflation: Stagflation combines stagnant economic growth and high unemployment with rising price inflation.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: How many persons shall operate rice combine?

choiceExplanations.0-1 persons: Zero to one person cannot safely operate the combine while managing grain unloading and field support.
choiceExplanations.2-3 persons: Correct — Per PAES specifications for rice combine harvesters, normal operation requires 2 to 3 persons (operator plus bagging/hauling helpers).
choiceExplanations.4-5 persons: Four to five persons exceed the standard crew size specified for a mechanized rice combine.
choiceExplanations.6-7 persons: Six to seven persons are unnecessary for a rice combine, which integrates reaping and threshing.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Stoichiometric air requirement for pyrolysis

choiceExplanations.15–25%: 15 to 25 percent air approaches partial oxidation levels used in low-air gasification rather than pyrolysis.
choiceExplanations.10-20%: Correct — In biomass thermochemical conversion review standards, pyrolysis operates in an oxygen-starved environment with roughly 10–20% stoichiometric air.
choiceExplanations.20–30%: 20 to 30 percent stoichiometric air corresponds to biomass gasification rather than thermal pyrolysis.
choiceExplanations.30–40%: 30 to 40 percent stoichiometric air supports active gasification and partial combustion, not pyrolysis.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the least used machinery in the Philippines

choiceExplanations.Rotavator: Rotavators are widely adopted across Philippine farms via four-wheel tractors for rapid primary and secondary tillage.
choiceExplanations.Sprayer: Knapsack and power sprayers are among the most common tools used for crop protection nationwide.
choiceExplanations.Planter: Correct — Mechanical planters have the lowest adoption rate in the Philippines because manual transplanting and broadcasting still dominate crop establishment.
choiceExplanations.Thresher: Mechanical rice threshers have very high adoption rates across Philippine rice-producing regions.

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Moldboard Plow Depth of Cut

choiceExplanations.30-42 inches: 30 to 42 inches reaches deep subsoiling depths far beyond a standard moldboard plow's capacity.
choiceExplanations.42-54 inches: 42 to 54 inches is an extreme excavation depth unachievable by agricultural moldboard plows.
choiceExplanations.6-18 inches: Correct — Standard agricultural moldboard plows operate at primary tillage depths of roughly 6 to 18 inches depending on plow size.
choiceExplanations.18-30 inches: 18 to 30 inches requires specialized deep-tillage subsoilers or rippers rather than moldboard plows.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A ribbed type v-belt where the ribs are positioned along the belt length.

choiceExplanations.Double V-belt: A double V-belt (hexagonal belt) has V-shaped faces on both top and bottom for serpentine drives.
choiceExplanations.V-ribbed belt: Correct — A V-ribbed (poly-V) belt features multiple longitudinal V-shaped ribs running along the belt's inner length for high flexibility.
choiceExplanations.Cogged V-belt: A cogged V-belt has transverse notches on its underside to reduce bending resistance around small sheaves.
choiceExplanations.Banded V-belt: A banded V-belt joins several individual V-belts across their tops with a common backing band.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The minimum number of trial(s) required in testing heated air mechanical grain dryer as specified in PAES.

choiceExplanations.Two: Correct — PAES 202 (Methods of Test for Heated-Air Mechanical Grain Dryer) prescribes a minimum of two test trials.
choiceExplanations.Three: Three trials exceed the minimum two-trial requirement specified under PAES 202 for heated-air dryers.
choiceExplanations.Five: Five trials are not the minimum testing requirement under PAES 202.
choiceExplanations.Four: Four trials exceed the minimum number of runs mandated by PAES 202.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Holding capacity of mechanical dryer during testing as prescribed by PAES should be based on the _____ and other accompanying information such as moisture content and purity

choiceExplanations.Depth: Grain bed depth varies with bin geometry and does not directly define dryer holding capacity.
choiceExplanations.Density: Bulk density is a material property used to relate mass and volume, not holding capacity itself.
choiceExplanations.Volume: Volumetric capacity changes with grain moisture and compaction, whereas PAES specifies mass-based reporting.
choiceExplanations.Weight: Correct — Under PAES testing standards, mechanical dryer holding capacity is expressed by grain weight alongside moisture content and purity.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A type of bearing used to restrain endwise motion of a turning shaft or withstand axial load.

choiceExplanations.Needle bearing: A needle bearing uses long, thin cylindrical rollers mainly to support heavy radial loads in compact spaces.
choiceExplanations.Journal bearing: A journal bearing is a plain sleeve bearing designed primarily to carry radial shaft loads.
choiceExplanations.Radial bearing: A radial bearing supports forces acting perpendicular to the shaft axis rather than endwise axial loads.
choiceExplanations.Thrust bearing: Correct — A thrust bearing is specifically designed to resist axial forces and prevent endwise movement along a rotating shaft.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A drive where shafts are operating in a uni-direction

choiceExplanations.Belt and pulley: Belt drives can be crossed or twisted to reverse the driven shaft's direction of rotation.
choiceExplanations.Rack and pinion: A rack and pinion converts rotational motion into linear motion rather than driving parallel shafts.
choiceExplanations.Chain and sprocket: Correct — In a standard chain and sprocket drive, both the driver and driven sprockets rotate in the same (unidirectional) sense.
choiceExplanations.Gear and pinion: External meshing gear and pinion pairs rotate in opposite directions rather than the same direction.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A belt transmission suitable for cross-drive system

choiceExplanations.Ribbed belt: Ribbed belts have longitudinal grooves that must stay aligned with pulley grooves and resist twisting.
choiceExplanations.Timing belt: Timing belts are toothed positive-drive belts designed only for aligned parallel shafts.
choiceExplanations.V-belt: V-belts have a trapezoidal cross-section seated in deep grooves, making them unsuitable for crossed twisting.
choiceExplanations.Flat belt: Correct — Flat belts have a thin, uniform rectangular cross-section that easily twists 180 degrees for cross-drive belt systems.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: If the pulley to be driven requires to be turned in counterclockwise direction, what drive system would you recommend?

choiceExplanations.Mule-drive: A mule-drive uses idler pulleys to route power between shafts that are not parallel.
choiceExplanations.Open-drive: An open-drive belt turns both the driver and driven pulleys in the same rotational direction.
choiceExplanations.Compound-drive: A compound-drive uses multiple stages on an intermediate shaft to achieve higher speed ratios.
choiceExplanations.Cross-drive: Correct — A cross-drive belt configuration twists the belt between pulleys so the driven pulley rotates opposite to a clockwise driver.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: When one pulley is to be driven horizontally and the other pulley is to be driven vertically, what drive system would you

choiceExplanations.Quarter turn drive: Correct — A quarter-turn belt drive connects two non-intersecting shafts oriented at 90 degrees, such as horizontal to vertical pulleys.
choiceExplanations.Open belt drive: An open belt drive connects parallel shafts rotating in the same direction.
choiceExplanations.Crossed belt drive: A crossed belt drive connects parallel shafts rotating in opposite directions.
choiceExplanations.Compound belt drive: A compound belt drive connects parallel shafts through intermediate countershaft pulleys for speed changes.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: It is a power transmission device used to deliver misaligned shaft.

choiceExplanations.Friction clutch: A friction clutch engages and disengages power transmission between aligned shafts via friction surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Rigid coupling: A rigid coupling joins two collinear shafts solidly and cannot tolerate angular misalignment.
choiceExplanations.Flanged coupling: A flanged coupling bolts two shaft ends rigidly together and requires precise shaft alignment.
choiceExplanations.Universal joint: Correct — A universal joint (Hooke's joint) transmits torque reliably between two shafts whose axes are inclined or misaligned.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: If some belts on multiple v-belt drive are worn out, it is recommended that
choices: Only worn belts should be replaced

choiceExplanations.Only worn belts should be replaced: Replacing only worn belts causes uneven load sharing because new belts are shorter than stretched old ones.
choiceExplanations.All belts should be replaced: Correct — All belts in a multiple V-belt drive must be replaced as a matched set so every belt shares load equally.
choiceExplanations.Pulley speed should be reduced: Reducing pulley speed does not fix belt wear and alters the driven machine's operating speed.
choiceExplanations.Belt tension should be tightened: Over-tightening worn belts accelerates bearing failure and causes sudden belt snapping.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Commonly used V-belt for agricultural operation in the / Philippines.

choiceExplanations.Type B: Correct — Type B V-belts (17 mm top width) are the most common size for medium-duty agricultural machinery in the Philippines.
choiceExplanations.Type A: Type A V-belts (13 mm top width) are typically limited to light-duty drives and small appliances.
choiceExplanations.Type D: Type D V-belts (32 mm top width) are heavy-duty industrial belts rarely needed on small farm machines.
choiceExplanations.Type C: Type C V-belts (22 mm top width) are used for heavier stationary machinery rather than general farm implements.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: When buying flat belt, the common parameters used are

Tooth number applies to toothed timing belts, not smooth flat belts.
Correct — Flat belts are commercially specified and purchased by their belt width and number of fabric plies (thickness rating).
Diameter and groove count specify sheaves or pulleys rather than flat belts.
Angle and strand count do not apply to flat belt sizing.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A v-belt whose specification is B-32 means
items.answer: Type B with circumferential length of 32 inches
choices: Type B with circumferential length of 32 inches
Type B with center distance of 32 inches
Type B with top width of 32 millimeters
Type B with pitch diameter of 32 centimeters

choiceExplanations.Type B with circumferential length of 32: Correct — In standard V-belt nomenclature, B-32 denotes a B-section cross-profile with an inside circumferential length of 32 inches.
choiceExplanations.Type B with center distance of 32 inches: Belt designations specify the belt's own inside length, not the shaft center distance.
choiceExplanations.Type B with top width of 32 millimeters: A Type B V-belt has a fixed 17 mm top width, not 32 mm.
choiceExplanations.Type B with pitch diameter of 32 centime: Pitch diameter describes the pulley size, whereas 32 indicates the belt's inch length.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: In a variable-pitch sheaves, the recommended belts used are

choiceExplanations.Double angle belt: Double angle belts are hexagonal V-belts used for serpentine drives flexing in both directions.
choiceExplanations.Light duty belt: Light-duty V-belts are designed for fixed-pitch fractional-horsepower sheaves, not variable-pitch drives.
choiceExplanations.Positive drive belt: Positive drive (timing) belts have teeth and cannot ride up and down variable-pitch sheaves.
choiceExplanations.Adjustable speed belt: Correct — Adjustable (variable) speed belts have wide, thin profiles with high transverse rigidity to shift smoothly in variable-pitch sheaves.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A type of gear used for power-take off drive

choiceExplanations.Hypoid bevel gear: Hypoid bevel gears connect non-intersecting perpendicular shafts in automotive differentials, not standard PTO shafts.
choiceExplanations.Spline shaft gear: Correct — Tractor power take-off (PTO) drives use splined shafts with matching splined gears/couplings to transmit high torque reliably.
choiceExplanations.Double helical gear: Double helical (herringbone) gears are used in heavy stationary gearboxes to cancel axial thrust.
choiceExplanations.Internal ring gear: Internal ring gears are used inside planetary gear sets rather than standard PTO couplings.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: If the shaft of an engine rotates at the same speed with the shaft of the driven machine on the same axis, the transmission system is

choiceExplanations.Belt pulley drive: Belt and pulley drives transmit power between offset parallel shafts rather than collinear shafts.
choiceExplanations.Gear reduction drive: Gear reduction drives use meshing gears on separate shafts to alter speed and torque.
choiceExplanations.Direct couple drive: Correct — A direct-coupled drive joins collinear engine and machine shafts directly so both rotate at identical speed along one axis.
choiceExplanations.Chain sprocket drive: Chain and sprocket drives transfer power between parallel offset shafts using a roller chain.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A pulley that is used to tighten belt in a drive system

choiceExplanations.Driver pulley: The driver pulley is mounted on the power source shaft to transmit input motion.
choiceExplanations.Crowned pulley: A crowned pulley has a slightly convex face to keep flat belts centered during operation.
choiceExplanations.Driven pulley: The driven pulley receives power from the belt to operate the machine shaft.
choiceExplanations.Idler pulley: Correct — An idler pulley applies tension to a belt drive or guides the belt path without transmitting shaft power.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A grove that is placed on a shaft to prevent pulley from slippage

choiceExplanations.Keyway: Correct — A keyway is an axial slot machined into a shaft and hub to hold a key that prevents pulley rotation slippage.
choiceExplanations.Fillet: A fillet is a rounded inside corner machined on a shaft to reduce stress concentration.
choiceExplanations.Chamfer: A chamfer is a beveled edge cut at the end of a shaft for easier assembly.
choiceExplanations.Shoulder: A shaft shoulder is a stepped change in diameter used for axial positioning of bearings or hubs.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The standard length of bars available at the hardware is.

choiceExplanations.22 ft: 22 ft is not a standard commercial stock length for structural steel bars in Philippine hardware.
choiceExplanations.18 ft: 18 ft is not a standard stock length for hardware angle, flat, or reinforcing bars.
choiceExplanations.20 ft: Correct — Structural steel bars (flat, round, angle, and reinforcing bars) are commercially supplied in standard 20-foot (6-meter) lengths in Philippine hardware.
choiceExplanations.24 ft: 24 ft is longer than the standard 20-ft commercial bar length sold locally.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: When buying angle bars, the right specification is

choiceExplanations.Length and weight: Hardware angle bars come in standard lengths and are not specified by weight when ordering.
choiceExplanations.Gauge and pitch: Gauge and pitch are specifications for sheet metal thickness and screw or chain spacing.
choiceExplanations.Diameter and length: Diameter applies to round bars and pipes, not L-shaped structural angle bars.
choiceExplanations.Thickness and width: Correct — Angle bars are specified by leg widths and material thickness (e.g., 2" x 2" x 1/4" or 50 x 50 x 6 mm).

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Designation for standard V-belt are

choiceExplanations.Ha, hb, hc, hd, he: HA through HE designate agricultural double-V or specialized agricultural belt cross-sections, not standard industrial V-belts.
choiceExplanations.Ax, bx, cx, dx, ex: AX through EX designate notched/cogged raw-edge versions of standard V-belts rather than standard wrapped V-belts.
choiceExplanations.A, b, c, d, e: Correct — Classical standard V-belt cross-sections are designated by the letters A, B, C, D, and E in order of increasing size.
choiceExplanations.Aa, bb, cc, dd, ee: AA, BB, CC, DD designate double-angle (hexagonal) V-belts used in serpentine multi-pulley drives.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The length of chain usually expressed in

choiceExplanations.Meters: Meters express general SI length, whereas roller chain lengths are counted by link increments.
choiceExplanations.Inches: Inches measure pitch size or center distance, not the standard count used for chain length.
choiceExplanations.Strands: Strands indicate the number of parallel roller chains side-by-side, not the chain's length.
choiceExplanations.Pitches: Correct — Roller chain length is conventionally specified by the number of pitches (links) required to form the loop.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: AGMA stands for

choiceExplanations.American Gear Manufacturers Association: Correct — AGMA stands for the American Gear Manufacturers Association, the recognized standards body for gear design and rating.
choiceExplanations.Agricultural Gear Makers Association: Agricultural Gear Makers Association is a fabricated distractor and not a real standards body.
choiceExplanations.Association of Gear Manufacturing Agenci: Association of Gear Manufacturing Agencies is a fictional organization name.
choiceExplanations.American Grain Machinery Association: American Grain Machinery Association does not exist as a gear engineering standards group.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: It is the spacing of the gear teeth measured along the pitch circle

choiceExplanations.Diametral pitch: Diametral pitch is the ratio of the number of teeth to the pitch diameter.
choiceExplanations.Circular pitch: Correct — Circular pitch is the arc distance from one tooth point to the corresponding point on the next tooth along the pitch circle.
choiceExplanations.Base pitch: Base pitch is the tooth-to-tooth spacing measured along the base circle or line of action.
choiceExplanations.Chordal pitch: Chordal pitch is the straight-line chord distance between adjacent teeth rather than the arc along the pitch circle.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: It is the ratio of the input power and the output power in gears

choiceExplanations.Gear efficiency: Correct — Gear efficiency (output power divided by input power, conventionally tested as power ratio) measures mechanical power transmission effectiveness.
choiceExplanations.Velocity ratio: Velocity ratio is the ratio of the driver's angular speed to the driven gear's speed.
choiceExplanations.Gear ratio: Gear ratio is the ratio of tooth counts between the larger gear and the pinion.
choiceExplanations.Torque ratio: Torque ratio compares output torque to input torque rather than input and output power.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: It is the most common type of gear used in agricultural machinery with straight and parallel teeth to the shaft axis

choiceExplanations.Worm gear: Worm gears connect non-intersecting perpendicular shafts using a screw-like worm meshing with a gear.
choiceExplanations.Bevel gear: Bevel gears have conical pitch surfaces designed to connect intersecting shafts, usually at right angles.
choiceExplanations.Helical gear: Helical gears have teeth cut at an angle (helix) to the shaft axis rather than straight.
choiceExplanations.Spur gear: Correct — Spur gears have straight teeth cut parallel to the shaft axis and are the simplest, most common agricultural gear.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A gear commonly used for gear reducers or gear motors.

choiceExplanations.Worm gear: Correct — Worm gear sets provide very high single-stage speed reductions in compact housings, making them standard for gearmotors and reducers.
choiceExplanations.Hypoid gear: Hypoid gears are primarily used in vehicle rear axle differentials, not compact industrial gearmotors.
choiceExplanations.Miter gear: Miter gears are equal-sized bevel gears providing a 1:1 speed ratio at right angles, not speed reduction.
choiceExplanations.Herringbone gear: Herringbone gears are used in heavy high-torque parallel-shaft drives rather than compact gearmotors.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A gear used for intersecting shaft usually at right angles.

choiceExplanations.Helical gear: Helical gears typically connect parallel shafts or crossed non-intersecting shafts.
choiceExplanations.Spur gear: Spur gears connect parallel shafts and cannot transmit power between intersecting shafts.
choiceExplanations.Bevel gear: Correct — Bevel gears feature conical tooth profiles specifically designed to transmit motion between intersecting shafts, typically at 90 degrees.
choiceExplanations.Worm gear: Worm gears connect perpendicular shafts whose axes do not intersect.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Timing belt is commonly known as

choiceExplanations.Positive drive belt: Correct — Timing belts engage mating sprocket teeth with molded belt teeth, providing slip-free positive drive power transmission.
choiceExplanations.Variable speed belt: Variable speed belts are wide V-belts used in adjustable-pitch sheaves without teeth.
choiceExplanations.Friction drive belt: Friction drive belts (flat and V-belts) rely on belt-sheave friction rather than positive tooth engagement.
choiceExplanations.Double angle belt: Double angle belts are hexagonal V-belts designed to drive pulleys on both sides.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: It is commonly used belt drive for engine driven multi-pass rice mill

choiceExplanations.Flat belt: Correct — Traditional engine-driven multi-pass rice mills in the Philippines commonly use flat belts to drive line shafts and milling units.
choiceExplanations.Timing belt: Timing belts are synchronous toothed belts not typically used on heavy line-shaft rice mills.
choiceExplanations.Ribbed belt: Ribbed belts are mostly used in compact automotive and modern high-speed serpentine drives.
choiceExplanations.V-belt: While V-belts drive some compact mills, traditional multi-pass rice mills use flat-belt line-shaft transmissions.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: When ordering flat belt, the parameters need to be specified includes

Diameter and groove count specify grooved pulleys or sheaves, not flat belts.
Strand count applies to multiple V-belt or multi-strand chain drives, not flat belts.
Correct — Flat belts are ordered and specified primarily by belt width and number of fabric plies.
Rib count applies to longitudinal V-ribbed (poly-V) belts rather than flat belts.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: For slow speed operation, the recommended number of teeth for sprocket is

choiceExplanations.16 teeth: Correct — Machine design standards recommend a minimum of 16 teeth (typically 16–17) on the smaller sprocket for slow-speed chain drives.
choiceExplanations.14 teeth: 14 teeth fall below the recommended 16-tooth minimum, increasing chordal action and chain wear.
choiceExplanations.18 teeth: 18 teeth are typically recommended as the lower end for medium-to-high speed drives rather than slow speed.
choiceExplanations.13 teeth: 13 teeth cause severe polygonal chordal speed variation and rapid roller chain fatigue.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The recommended minimum number of sprocket teeth for high speed operation.

choiceExplanations.24-30 teeth: 24 to 30 teeth exceed the standard minimum range, unnecessarily enlarging drive size.
choiceExplanations.12-18 teeth: 12 to 18 teeth are too small for high-speed chain operation, causing excessive vibration and noise.
choiceExplanations.18-24 teeth: Correct — High-speed roller chain drives require at least 18 to 24 teeth on the smaller sprocket to minimize chordal pulsation and wear.
choiceExplanations.6-12 teeth: 6 to 12 teeth are far too few and produce extreme chordal impact at high speeds.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Gear oil is used for

choiceExplanations.Cooling radiator: Holds engine coolant (water-antifreeze mixture) to dissipate heat, not high-viscosity gear oil.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic reservoir: Stores low-viscosity hydraulic fluid used to transmit power in hydraulic cylinders and actuators.
choiceExplanations.Engine crankcase: Contains engine motor oil formulated for high-temperature combustion lubrication, not EP gear oil.
choiceExplanations.Transmission box: Correct — High-viscosity extreme-pressure gear oil lubricates transmission gears and bearings under heavy tooth loads.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: What is the formula for the length (L) of an open belt drive?
items.rationale: For an open belt drive with center distance C and pulley diameters D1 and D2: L = 2C + π(D1 + D2)/2 + (D2 - D1)²/(4C).

choiceExplanations.58%: Represents a dimensionless percentage value, not a belt-length formula.
choiceExplanations.L = C + π(D1 + D2) + (D2 - D1)² / (2C): Incorrectly halves the straight span (C instead of 2C) and doubles the arc and angle terms.
choiceExplanations.Cross-drive: Names a belt configuration where the belt crosses between pulleys, not an open-belt length equation.
choiceExplanations.L = 2C + π(D1 + D2)/2 + (D2 - D1)² / (4C: Correct — Standard open-belt length equals two center spans plus average pulley circumference and the squared diameter-difference correction.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Belt size designation for agricultural V belt is

choiceExplanations.Ax, bx, cx, dx, ex: Cogged (notched) classical industrial V-belt sections designed for smaller pulley diameters.
choiceExplanations.Aa, bb, cc, dd, ee: Double-sided (hexagonal) industrial V-belts used in serpentine drives driving from both faces.
choiceExplanations.Ha, hb, hc, hd, he: Correct — PAES and ASABE standards prefix agricultural V-belt cross-sections with H (HA, HB, HC, HD, HE).

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: It is used to fasten shaft pulleys and hubs of gears together

choiceExplanations.Lock washers: Spring or toothed washers placed under nuts or bolt heads to prevent loosening from vibration.
choiceExplanations.Retaining rings: Circlips seated in shaft or housing grooves to prevent axial movement of components.
choiceExplanations.Cotter pins: Split metal pins inserted through drilled holes to secure slotted nuts or clevis pins axially.
choiceExplanations.Keys: Correct — Machine keys fit into matching shaft and hub keyways to transmit torque and lock pulleys or gears rotationally.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The identification of the given tire with is maximum recommended load when used in specific type service

choiceExplanations.Rim diameter: Specifies the diameter of the wheel rim on which the tire mounts, not load capacity.
choiceExplanations.Ply rating: Correct — Ply rating identifies a tire's strength and maximum recommended load capacity for a specified service condition.
choiceExplanations.Aspect ratio: Expresses tire section height as a percentage of its section width.
choiceExplanations.Speed rating: Indicates the maximum safe operating speed of a tire under its rated load.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Time interval of measurement of test parameters in heated air mechanical dryer as specified in PAES Test Method

choiceExplanations.30mins: Correct — PAES heated-air mechanical grain dryer test methods specify recording test parameters at 30-minute intervals.
choiceExplanations.40mins: Exceeds the standard PAES 30-minute measurement interval during dryer performance testing.
choiceExplanations.20mins: Shorter than the 30-minute interval specified in the PAES mechanical dryer test method.
choiceExplanations.10mins: Too frequent compared to the standard 30-minute PAES interval for heated-air dryer testing.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: All rotating parts of agricultural machines as provided is the PAES should be

choiceExplanations.Statically balanced: Only ensures center of gravity lies on the axis at rest, without eliminating couple unbalance during rotation.
choiceExplanations.Axially aligned: Refers to shaft collinearity, not mass distribution across rotating elements.
choiceExplanations.Rigidly mounted: Describes structural fastening to a frame rather than rotational mass balance.
choiceExplanations.Dynamically balanced: Correct — PAES requires all rotating agricultural machine parts to be dynamically balanced to prevent vibration and bearing wear.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: What is the formula for the length (L) of a crossed belt drive?
items.rationale: For a crossed belt drive, the last term uses the sum of diameters squared: L = 2C + π(D1 + D2)/2 + (D2 + D1)²/(4C).

choiceExplanations.8%: Represents a percentage ratio rather than a belt-length formula.
choiceExplanations.L = C + π(D1 + D2)/2 + (D2 + D1)² / (4C): Uses only one center distance (C) instead of 2C for the two belt spans.
choiceExplanations.3%: Represents a percentage slope or loss figure, not a geometric belt-length equation.
choiceExplanations.L = 2C + π(D1 + D2)/2 + (D2 + D1)² / (4C: Correct — Crossed-belt length sums two center spans, average pulley circumference, and the squared sum-of-diameters correction over 4C.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: It is the Administrative Order by the / Philippine Department of Agriculture stating that only AB Engineers can inspect all FMR projects in accordance to PAES.

items.rationale: Department of Agriculture Administrative Order No. / 28,s.2009
choices: Department of Agriculture Memorandum Order No.
Department of Agriculture Department Order No.
Department of Agriculture Administrative Order No.
Department of Agriculture Memorandum Circular No.

choiceExplanations.Department of Agriculture Memorandum Ord: Internal DA directives on operational procedures, not the formal rule assigning AB Engineers to FMR inspection.
choiceExplanations.Department of Agriculture Department Ord: Nomenclature used by departments like DPWH or DOLE rather than DA Administrative Orders.
choiceExplanations.Department of Agriculture Administrative: Correct — DA Administrative Order (DAO) mandates that only licensed AB Engineers inspect FMR projects per PAES.
choiceExplanations.Department of Agriculture Memorandum Cir: Informational or clarificatory issuances, not the DA Administrative Order governing FMR inspection authority.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: It connects shaft with large misalignments

choiceExplanations.Universal Joint: Correct — A universal joint transmits rotary motion between shafts intersecting at large angular misalignments.
choiceExplanations.Flange Coupling: Rigidly bolts two shaft flanges together and requires near-perfect collinear alignment.
choiceExplanations.Muff Coupling: Rigid cylindrical sleeve coupling keyed to aligned shafts, allowing virtually no misalignment.
choiceExplanations.Sleeve Coupling: Rigid hollow cylinder coupling that joins collinear shafts without accommodating large angles.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: It accounts for the losses in an irrigation system from the water source and prior to delivery of water into field ditches

choiceExplanations.Storage Efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the root zone during irrigation to the water needed before irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Conveyance Efficiency: Correct — Conveyance efficiency measures water delivered to field ditches relative to water diverted from the source, capturing transit losses.
choiceExplanations.Application Efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the crop root zone to the total water delivered to the field.
choiceExplanations.Distribution Efficiency: Measures how uniformly irrigation water is spread across the irrigated field area.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: PAES 231 Types of Shallow in formations with very shallow water depths

choiceExplanations.Augered well: Correct — PAES 231 identifies augered (bored) wells as shallow wells suited for formations with very shallow water tables.
choiceExplanations.Jetted well: Constructed by high-velocity water jets washing out unconsolidated sand and silt to deeper shallow-well depths.
choiceExplanations.Drilled well: Constructed using rotary or percussion rigs capable of penetrating hard rock and deep aquifers.
choiceExplanations.Driven well: Formed by driving a pointed well screen into permeable sand or gravel rather than augering very shallow layers.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: PAES 401(housing for swine Production: Space requirements per animal m2/animal Adult pigs in groups

choiceExplanations.2.9: Exceeds the PAES 401 minimum floor space allowance of 2.5 m²/animal for adult pigs in groups.
choiceExplanations.2.3: Below the 2.5 m²/animal minimum group housing space specified in PAES 401 for adult pigs.
choiceExplanations.2.5: Correct — PAES 401 (Housing for Swine Production) specifies 2.5 m² per animal for adult pigs housed in groups.
choiceExplanations.2.7: Overstates the PAES 401 standard space requirement of 2.5 m²/animal for grouped adult pigs.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: An ordinary egg with a mass of 0.1 kg and specific heat of 3.32 kJ/kg-°C is dropped into boiling water at 95°C. If the initial temperature of the egg is 5°C, the maximum amount of heat transfer to the egg is

choiceExplanations.q = 0.1 x 4.18 x (95 - 5): Uses the specific heat of water (4.18 kJ/kg-°C) instead of the egg's 3.32 kJ/kg-°C.
choiceExplanations.30mins: Represents a time duration, not a sensible heat transfer calculation.
choiceExplanations.0.5%: Represents a dimensionless percentage rather than heat energy transferred in kilojoules.
choiceExplanations.q = 0.1 x 3.32 x (95 - 5): Correct — Maximum sensible heat transfer follows Q = m·c·ΔT using m = 0.1 kg, c = 3.32 kJ/kg-°C, and ΔT = 90°C.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Increase product efficiency and decrease hazard
items.source: RECALLED COMPRESS PART 2; area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Environmental management: Correct — Environmental management optimizes resource efficiency while reducing environmental and workplace hazards.
choiceExplanations.Quality assurance: Focuses on preventing product defects and meeting specifications rather than reducing environmental hazards.
choiceExplanations.Production planning: Schedules materials, labor, and equipment capacity to meet output targets.
choiceExplanations.Inventory management: Tracks stock levels and ordering cycles to balance holding costs and availability.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Contains less than or equal to 20% longitudinal streaks (PAES)

choiceExplanations.Over-milled rice: Rice milled beyond well-milled grade with practically all bran layers and germ removed (0% streaks).
choiceExplanations.Under-milled rice: Rice retaining a substantial portion of the bran layers and longitudinal streaks (>40% streaks).
choiceExplanations.Regular-milled rice: Rice with bran layers partially removed, having 21% to 40% longitudinal streaks under PAES.
choiceExplanations.Well-milled rice: Correct — Under PAES rice milling grades, well-milled rice contains less than or equal to 20% longitudinal bran streaks.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Standard thickness of concrete of trapezoidal ditch w/ riprap (PAES)
