choiceExplanations..20m: Thinner than the 0.25 m PAES standard thickness for trapezoidal ditches with riprap.
choiceExplanations..30m: Exceeds the 0.25 m PAES standard thickness specified for riprapped trapezoidal ditches.
choiceExplanations..15m: Insufficient compared to the 0.25 m PAES standard thickness for trapezoidal ditch with riprap.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: It is the ratio between the water delivered to the farm and water delivered from a source?

choiceExplanations.Water storage efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the root zone to the total water needed to reach field capacity.
choiceExplanations.Water distribution efficiency: Indicates uniformity of water depth infiltrated across different parts of the field.
choiceExplanations.Water application efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the root zone to water delivered into the field.
choiceExplanations.Water conveyance efficiency: Correct — Water conveyance efficiency is the ratio of water delivered to the farm to water diverted from the source.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: standard pressure of tire

choiceExplanations.90–120psi: Typical high-pressure range for heavy commercial truck tires, not standard agricultural or light vehicle tires.
choiceExplanations.45–75psi: Higher than the general 30–60 psi standard tire inflation range cited in ABELE reviewers.
choiceExplanations.30 - 60psi: Correct — Standard inflation pressure for typical utility/farm equipment tires falls within the 30–60 psi range.
choiceExplanations.60–90psi: Exceeds standard 30–60 psi tire pressure and applies mainly to heavy-duty load-range tires.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: For an earth dam of 15 meters maximum height, what should be the width of the crown?

choiceExplanations.2m: Below the 3 m minimum crown width required for a 15-meter-high earth dam.
choiceExplanations.4m: Wider than the 3 m standard minimum crown width for a 15-meter earth dam.

choiceExplanations.3m: Correct — Standard earth dam design criteria specify a minimum crest (crown) width of 3 m for dams up to 15 m high.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: the minimum fence height for cattle except for brahman cross and excotics breeds where the fence height shall be

choiceExplanations.1.2m for brahman 1.5 - 1.6m: Lower than the PAES cattle fencing minimum of 1.5 m (and 1.7–1.8 m for Brahman/exotics).
choiceExplanations.1.5m for brahman 1.7 - 1.8m: Correct — PAES cattle housing/fencing standards mandate a minimum fence height of 1.5 m, raised to 1.7–1.8 m for Brahman and exotic breeds.
choiceExplanations.1.8m for brahman 2.0 - 2.1m: Exceeds the PAES 1.5 m general cattle fence height and 1.7–1.8 m Brahman requirement.
choiceExplanations.1.4m for brahman 1.6 - 1.7m: Slightly below the PAES standard heights of 1.5 m and 1.7–1.8 m.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: What is the minimum slope of earth, gravel and bituminous roads from the center line towards the ditch to promote rapid runoff of surface water and minimize the amount of water which infiltrates into the roadways

choiceExplanations.4%: Exceeds the 3% minimum cross-slope specified by PAES for earth, gravel, and bituminous FMR surfaces.
choiceExplanations.3%: Correct — PAES farm-to-market road standards require a minimum 3% crown slope on earth, gravel, and bituminous roads for rapid drainage.
choiceExplanations.5%: Represents the typical maximum rather than the 3% minimum cross-slope for unpaved/bituminous roads.
choiceExplanations.2%: Insufficient cross-slope for earth and gravel FMRs, where PAES requires at least 3% from centerline to ditch.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: the power rating classification for four wheel standard light tractor

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Is the grouping together of farms in an area (initially forming a minimum of 50ha cluster) for synchronized farming operations from land preparation harvesting

choiceExplanations.Farm clustering: Correct — Under DA guidelines, farm clustering groups adjacent farms (minimum 50 ha) for synchronized production from land preparation to harvesting.
choiceExplanations.Contract farming: Agreement between farmers and a buyer specifying production quantities, quality, and purchase price.
choiceExplanations.Farm consolidation: Physically merging fragmented land parcels into larger single landholdings.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: In small farm reservoir, what is the maximum depth of water
items.answer: 3m and the maximum height of dike is 4m

choiceExplanations.2m and the maximum height of dike is 3m: Understates the PAES maximum limits of 3 m water depth and 4 m embankment height.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The burning efficiency of rice hull furnace

choiceExplanations.95%: Correct — PAES performance standards specify a minimum burning efficiency of 95% for rice hull furnaces.
choiceExplanations.100%: Ideal complete combustion unattainable in practical rice hull furnaces due to unburned carbon in ash.
choiceExplanations.90%: Below the 95% minimum burning efficiency required by PAES for rice hull furnaces.
choiceExplanations.85%: Falls well short of the PAES 95% burning efficiency standard for rice hull furnaces.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: In promoting operational efficiency, which scenario is acceptable?
items.answer: Both same input with more output and less input with same output
items.rationale: Efficiency equals output divided by input, so it improves whenever more output is achieved from the same input or the same output is achieved with less input.
choices: Both same input with more output and less input with same output

choiceExplanations.Same input, more output: Only covers one valid way to raise efficiency, excluding input reduction at constant output.
choiceExplanations.Less input, same output: Only captures input savings and omits increasing output from unchanged inputs.
choiceExplanations.Both same input with more output and les: Correct — Since efficiency equals output divided by input, increasing output at fixed input or cutting input at fixed output both improve efficiency.
choiceExplanations.More input, same output: Decreases efficiency because more resources are consumed without increasing output.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A farmer created a business plan with the following data: a total initial investment of ₱5,000,000.00; 10% yearly business tax and interest on borrowed money; ₱200,000.00 allotted for employee trainings; and ₱400,000.00 allotted for salaries and other additional company expenses. What type of cost is the ₱5,000,000.00 initial investment?
items.rationale: The ₱5,000,000.00 initial capital investment does not change with short-term production volume and is therefore classified as a fixed cost.

choiceExplanations.Fixed cost: Correct — Initial capital investment is a fixed cost because it does not vary with production volume once incurred.
choiceExplanations.Overhead cost: Ongoing indirect operating expenses (like utilities or admin salaries) rather than initial capital investment.
choiceExplanations.Variable cost: Expenses that change directly in proportion to the level of output or activity.
choiceExplanations.Incremental cost: Additional cost incurred from producing one extra unit or choosing one alternative over another.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A farmer created a business plan with the following data: a total initial investment of ₱5,000,000.00; 10% yearly business tax and interest on borrowed money; ₱200,000.00 allotted for employee trainings; and ₱400,000.00 allotted for salaries and other additional company expenses. What type of cost is the 10% yearly tax for the business and interest on borrowed money?
items.rationale: Since a percentage-based business tax (and interest tied to financed operating capital) varies with business activity and revenue levels, it is classified here as a variable cost.

choiceExplanations.Incremental cost: Marginal change in total cost between two discrete operational alternatives or output increments.
choiceExplanations.Variable cost: Correct — Percentage-based business taxes and interest tied to borrowed operating capital vary with revenue and financing levels.
choiceExplanations.Overhead cost: Indirect recurring administrative expenses not tied directly as a percentage of business revenue.
choiceExplanations.Fixed cost: Costs that remain constant regardless of output or business revenue changes.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Is a water bearing geologic formation or stratum capable of transmitting water through its pores at a rate sufficient for economic extractions by wells

choiceExplanations.Aquifer: Correct — An aquifer is a saturated permeable geologic formation that yields economically usable groundwater to wells.
choiceExplanations.Aquitard: A low-permeability bed that retards groundwater flow and cannot yield economical well supplies directly.
choiceExplanations.Aquiclude: A porous formation (such as clay) that stores water but is too impermeable to transmit it to wells.
choiceExplanations.Aquifuge: An impermeable geologic formation (such as unfractured granite) that neither contains nor transmits water.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: PAES: In farm-to-market roads, the minimum radius of curvature for flat, rolling and mountainous terrains, respectively, shall be

choiceExplanations.400, 120 & 40: Smaller than the PAES minimum horizontal curve radii for flat, rolling, and mountainous FMR terrain.
choiceExplanations.500, 150 & 50: Correct — PAES farm-to-market road standards specify minimum curve radii of 500 m (flat), 150 m (rolling), and 50 m (mountainous).
choiceExplanations.550, 165 & 55: Exceeds the PAES FMR minimum curvature radii of 500 m, 150 m, and 50 m.
choiceExplanations.450, 135 & 45: Below the PAES minimum radii of 500 m, 150 m, and 50 m for FMR alignment.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: 12,500m3 of water was delivered to a 10 ha farm for the month of June in which consumptive use is estimated at 8 mm/day. The effective rainfall for the period was 150 mm. what is the irrigation efficiency?

choiceExplanations.8mm/day x 30 days = 240mm: Correct — June has 30 days, so total consumptive use is 8 mm/day × 30 days = 240 mm (yielding 72% efficiency with 90 mm net irrigation need vs. 125 mm applied).
choiceExplanations.5mm/day x 30 days = 150mm: Uses 5 mm/day instead of the given 8 mm/day consumptive use rate.
choiceExplanations.8mm/day x 31 days = 248mm: Incorrectly assumes June has 31 days instead of 30 days.
choiceExplanations.8mm/day x 28 days = 224mm: Incorrectly uses 28 days (February) rather than June's 30 days.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: In FMR, the minimum hours before removal of forms is

choiceExplanations.21hrs: Shorter than the 24-hour minimum curing period before stripping concrete side forms in FMRs.
choiceExplanations.22hrs: Less than the 24-hour minimum form-removal time required under PAES/DPWH FMR concrete specifications.
choiceExplanations.24hrs: Correct — FMR concrete pavement specifications require at least 24 hours after placement before side forms may be removed.
choiceExplanations.31hrs: Exceeds the standard 24-hour minimum waiting period for concrete side-form removal in FMR construction.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: In PAES, what is the light intensity needed in the slaughter house inspection area

choiceExplanations.160lux: Below the 200 lux minimum illumination required by PAES for slaughterhouse inspection areas.
choiceExplanations.244lux: Not a standard PAES illumination threshold for slaughterhouse inspection zones.
choiceExplanations.260lux: Exceeds the 200 lux minimum requirement specified in PAES slaughterhouse lighting standards.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: What is the minimum wind design speed or wind gusts in constructing greenhouses?

choiceExplanations.195 kph: Higher than the 150 kph minimum wind gust speed specified in PAES 415 for greenhouses.
choiceExplanations.172 kph: Exceeds the PAES 415 minimum design wind speed of 150 kph for greenhouse structures.
choiceExplanations.138 kph: Below the 150 kph minimum wind-load design requirement for greenhouses under PAES 415.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: If it is desired to have a maximum flow of water at any depth, the best canal cross-section to be used is the:

choiceExplanations.Triangular: Suited for small discharges and roadside ditches, having higher wetted perimeter per unit area at large flows.
choiceExplanations.Parabolic: Approximates natural stable earth channels and grassed waterways rather than maximum-flow lined canals.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The ratio of the water diverted from the source to the water delivered to the farm

choiceExplanations.Conveyance efficiency: Correct — Conveyance efficiency compares water delivered to the farm turnout against total water diverted from the source.
choiceExplanations.Application efficiency: Ratio of water beneficially stored in the crop root zone to water applied at the farm.
choiceExplanations.Distribution efficiency: Quantifies spatial uniformity of irrigation water infiltrated across the field.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: It consists of filling the casing with water so that air trapped in the pump does not hinder its operation and reduce efficiency

choiceExplanations.Throttling: Partially closing a discharge valve to regulate flow rate and increase head loss.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: In PAES 204 (Mechanical Rice Thresher – Specifications), what is the minimum threshing efficiency?

choiceExplanations.97%: Below the stringent 99.8% minimum threshing efficiency mandated by PAES 204.
choiceExplanations.87%: Fails the PAES 204 threshing efficiency requirement of at least 99.8%.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation

choiceExplanations.Replacement value: Current cost to acquire a new asset providing equivalent capacity and function.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: You are to apply the standard for the manufacture of the knife for a spindle type locally manufactured abaca stripper. What kind of material shall you use?
items.answer: Stainless steel 304, mild steel or carbon steel
choices: Cast iron, aluminum alloy or brass

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Based on standard, the shelling recovery of a locally manufactured corn sheller should be minimum of ___ percent.

choiceExplanations.97: Correct — PAES corn sheller specifications require a minimum shelling recovery of 97%.
choiceExplanations.78: Unacceptably low recovery, falling well short of the 97% PAES standard.
choiceExplanations.105: Exceeds 100%, which is impossible for kernel shelling recovery.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: You are to test and evaluate the performance of a locally manufactured coffee huller based on standard. What should be the minimum hulling efficiency?

choiceExplanations.95%: Correct — PAES coffee huller specifications mandate a minimum hulling efficiency of 95%.
choiceExplanations.90%: Below the 95% minimum hulling efficiency required by PAES for coffee hullers.
choiceExplanations.85%: Fails the PAES 95% minimum hulling efficiency criterion for coffee hullers.
choiceExplanations.100%: Unrealistic perfection not required as the minimum PAES test threshold.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Manager’s salary is an example of

choiceExplanations.Operating cost: Correct — A manager's salary is a recurring day-to-day administrative expense classified as an operating cost.
choiceExplanations.Depreciation cost: Non-cash allocation of a fixed asset's purchase cost over its useful life.
choiceExplanations.Sunk cost: Past expenditure already incurred that cannot be recovered regardless of future decisions.
choiceExplanations.Capital cost: One-time expenditure for acquiring long-term fixed assets like land, buildings, or machinery.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The engine of a hand tractor suddenly stops while the tractor is running. What is the most possible cause and what is the corresponding solution? The tractor is still under warranty.
items.answer: Broken shafting or chain, report immediately to the supplier
items.rationale: A sudden engine stoppage can be caused by a jammed or broken drive shafting or chain, and because the hand tractor is still under warranty, the issue must be reported immediately to the supplier rather than repaired independently to avoid voiding the warranty.
choices: Broken shafting or chain, report immediately to the supplier
Broken shafting or chain, have it repaired in a shop

choiceExplanations.Defective engine, repair engine: Disassembling the engine prematurely violates warranty terms and misdiagnoses drivetrain failure.
choiceExplanations.Broken shafting or chain, report immedia: Correct — Sudden stop under load points to a broken shaft or chain, and active warranty requires immediate supplier reporting.
choiceExplanations.Broken shafting or chain, have it repair: Third-party shop repair voids an active manufacturer or supplier warranty.
choiceExplanations.Broken sprocket weld, weld sprocket: Unauthorized welding voids the warranty and does not address the supplier claim process.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Using simplest computation method, what is the annual depreciation of a tractor purchased at Php 2,200,000 if its life span is 10 years? Salvage value is 10%.

choiceExplanations.Php 158,400/year: Understates annual depreciation by applying an extra 20% reduction to Php 198,000.
choiceExplanations.Php 241,560/year: Exceeds even full purchase cost divided by 10 years (Php 220,000/year).
choiceExplanations.Php 198,000/year: Correct — Straight-line depreciation equals (₱2,200,000 − 10% salvage of ₱220,000) / 10 years = ₱198,000/year.
choiceExplanations.Php 213,840/year: Overstates the ₱198,000/year straight-line depreciation by failing to subtract the 10% salvage properly.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Annually recurring cost.

choiceExplanations.Sunk cost: Past, irrecoverable expenditure already incurred before the current decision.
choiceExplanations.Operating cost: Correct — Operating costs are expenses incurred repeatedly every year to run and maintain an enterprise or machine.
choiceExplanations.Capital cost: One-time investment required to purchase or construct fixed assets.
choiceExplanations.Initial cost: Upfront outlay paid at project start to acquire and install equipment.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The transmission of a hand tractor produces a cracking sound when turning direction to left or right. What is the most possible cause and what is the corresponding solution? The tractor is no longer under warranty.
items.answer: Broken bearing, remove bearing cap and replace bearing
items.rationale: A cracking sound in the transmission while turning left or right indicates a damaged steering/axle bearing, and since the hand tractor is out of warranty, the proper solution is to remove the bearing cap and replace the broken bearing.
choices: Broken shafting or chain, have it repaired in a shop
Broken shafting or chain, report immediately to the supplier
Broken bearing, remove bearing cap and replace bearing

choiceExplanations.Broken shafting or chain, have it repair: Causes complete loss of drive rather than a localized cracking noise only during turns.
choiceExplanations.Broken sprocket weld, weld sprocket: Causes chain slip or drive loss regardless of turning direction, not turning-specific cracking.
choiceExplanations.Broken shafting or chain, report immedia: Applicable only while under warranty and for broken drive shafts/chains, not post-warranty turning bearings.
choiceExplanations.Broken bearing, remove bearing cap and r: Correct — Cracking during turns indicates a damaged steering/axle bearing, which out-of-warranty requires removing the cap and replacing the bearing.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Using straight line depreciation method, what is the book value at the end of year 2 of a tractor purchased at Php2,200,000 if its life span is 10 years? Salvage value is estimated at Php200,000.

choiceExplanations.Php 2,196,000: Subtracts only ₱4,000 instead of two years of ₱200,000 annual depreciation (₱400,000).
choiceExplanations.Php 1,656,000: Overstates accumulated depreciation, falling below the straight-line year-2 book value of ₱1,800,000.
choiceExplanations.Php 2,070,000: Subtracts only ₱130,000 total instead of ₱400,000 over two years.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: As part of evaluating a feasibility study report, the evaluator sees to it that the software used is compliant with the international accounting standard or standards. Specify the standard or standards to comply.
items.rationale: Feasibility study financial evaluations must comply with both International Accounting Standards (IAS) and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), as active IAS standards remain in force alongside IFRS.

choiceExplanations.IFRS: International Financial Reporting Standards alone omits the earlier International Accounting Standards still in effect.
choiceExplanations.IAS: International Accounting Standards alone omits the newer International Financial Reporting Standards used in financial evaluation.
choiceExplanations.IAS and IFRS: Correct — Feasibility study accounting software must comply with both International Accounting Standards (IAS) and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).
choiceExplanations.IAS or IFRS: Complying with only one standard is insufficient because financial reporting requires adherence to both IAS and IFRS.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: What is the safest gear setting for a descending tractor in a 10% slope?
items.rationale: Descending a steep 10% slope in first gear provides maximum engine braking and speed control, preventing loss of control or runaway acceleration that occurs in neutral or higher gears.

choiceExplanations.First gear: Correct — First gear provides maximum engine braking and lowest ground speed to safely control a tractor descending a 10% slope.
choiceExplanations.Second gear: Higher gear ratio reduces engine braking resistance, increasing the risk of overspeeding downhill.
choiceExplanations.Third gear: Third gear allows excessive downhill speed with minimal engine braking, making tractor control unsafe.
choiceExplanations.Neutral: Coasting in neutral disconnects engine braking completely, creating a severe runaway hazard on slopes.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The generally accepted industry standard for power factor of generators.

choiceExplanations.70%: A 0.70 power factor under-rates the generator's real power output below standard industrial AC generator ratings.
choiceExplanations.85%: While some specialized synchronous machines operate at 0.85, standard commercial generators are rated at 0.80 lagging.
choiceExplanations.75%: A 0.75 power factor is lower than the standard 0.80 lagging rating used for AC generators.
choiceExplanations.80%: Correct — Standard three-phase AC generators are rated at an 80% (0.80) lagging power factor to convert kVA to kW.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: What is the minimum flash point of oil used in engines necessary to prevent fire?
items.rationale: Engine lubricating oil must have a flash point higher than 220 degrees Celsius so that it does not vaporize and ignite under high engine operating temperatures.

choiceExplanations.Lower than 220 degrees Celsius: Oil with a flash point below 220 °C can ignite easily under high engine operating temperatures.
choiceExplanations.Higher than 220 degrees Celsius: Correct — Engine lubricating oil requires a flash point above 220 °C to prevent vapor ignition during high-temperature operation.
choiceExplanations.220 degrees Fahrenheit: 220 °F (about 104 °C) is far too low and would cause severe fire hazards in hot engines.
choiceExplanations.220 degrees Celsius: Exactly 220 °C sits right at the minimum threshold rather than providing a safety margin above 220 °C.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Estimate the dependable power output and system efficiency of a microhydro having a gross head of 60 meters, minimum water discharge of 150 liters/second, and penstock water velocity of 12 meters/second.
items.rationale: Gross hydraulic power is P = ρgQH = 1000 × 9.81 × 0.15 m³/s × 60 m ≈ 88.3 kW; accounting for penstock head losses and a realistic 60% overall microhydro system efficiency gives approximately 52 kW.

choiceExplanations.635 kW, 60% efficiency: Overestimates power by an order of magnitude, exceeding even the theoretical hydraulic power of 88.3 kW.
choiceExplanations.52 kW, 60% efficiency: Correct — Using P = 9.81 × Q × H × η with Q = 0.15 m³/s, H = 60 m, and 60% efficiency gives about 52 kW.
choiceExplanations.75 kW, 85% efficiency: Assumes an unrealistically high 85% wire-to-water efficiency for a small microhydro system.
choiceExplanations.6.2 kW, 85% efficiency: Underestimates power by roughly a factor of ten and assumes an overstated 85% system efficiency.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: A 24-volt DC generator is to be acquired to support DC electrical loads including motors. The computed maximum amperage at peak load is 10 amperes. Surge current is assumed 25% higher than the computed peak load amperage. Load safety factor of 20% is to be used. If you are to carry out the acquisition, what minimum wattage of the generator should be selected?

choiceExplanations.360: Correct — Multiplying 10 A by 1.25 (surge) and 1.20 (safety factor) gives 15 A, which at 24 V equals 360 W.
choiceExplanations.414: Exceeds the required 360 W calculation by applying an extra 15% multiplier not specified in the problem.
choiceExplanations.468: Overstates the required wattage by adding an extra 30% margin beyond the 25% surge and 20% safety factor.
choiceExplanations.389: Incorrectly computes a 389 W rating instead of 24 V × 10 A × 1.25 × 1.20 = 360 W.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Quarter sawed lumber is best suited for finishing flooring because?

choiceExplanations.Minimum shrinkage: Correct — Quarter-sawn lumber aligns growth rings nearly perpendicular to the face, minimizing radial shrinkage, cupping, and warping.
choiceExplanations.Lower cost: Quarter sawing requires extra handling and wastes more wood, making it more expensive than plain-sawn lumber.
choiceExplanations.Faster drying: Quarter-sawn boards generally dry more slowly than plain-sawn lumber because moisture moves slower radially.
choiceExplanations.Higher yield: Quarter sawing produces lower volumetric lumber yield per log due to repeated log rotation during milling.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The minimum noise level outside the slaughterhouse during nighttime

choiceExplanations.45db: Correct — Under Philippine environmental and PAES slaughterhouse standards, the nighttime exterior noise threshold is 45 dB.
choiceExplanations.35db: 35 dB is overly restrictive and corresponds to quiet indoor library levels rather than exterior slaughterhouse limits.
choiceExplanations.50db: 50 dB corresponds to daytime or commercial limits rather than the stricter nighttime threshold outside a slaughterhouse.
choiceExplanations.40db: 40 dB is lower than the prescribed 45 dB nighttime noise standard for slaughterhouse surroundings.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: PAES 210:2000. Cornmill milled corn kernels with particle size between 0.86 mm to 1.09 mm

choiceExplanations.Grit #14: Under PAES 210:2000, Grit #14 is coarser, with milled corn particles larger than 1.20 mm to 1.40 mm.
choiceExplanations.Grit #18: Correct — PAES 210:2000 classifies milled corn kernels with particle sizes from 0.86 mm to 1.09 mm as Grit #18.
choiceExplanations.Grit #20: Under PAES 210:2000, Grit #20 refers to finer milled corn particles smaller than 0.86 mm.
choiceExplanations.Grit #16: Under PAES 210:2000, Grit #16 has coarser particle sizes ranging around 1.10 mm to 1.20 mm.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: SWIS maximum slope

choiceExplanations.16%: 16% is below the 18% maximum slope threshold set for Small Water Impounding System (SWIS) sites.
choiceExplanations.20%: 20% exceeds the 18% maximum slope limit for SWIS watershed and agricultural service areas.
choiceExplanations.18%: Correct — Small Water Impounding Systems (SWIS) are sited on areas with a maximum slope of 18% to prevent erosion.
choiceExplanations.22%: 22% is too steep for SWIS siting and poses excessive runoff velocity and embankment erosion risks.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Minimum space requirements per animal for boar pens.

choiceExplanations.6.5m²: 6.5 m² provides insufficient floor space for mature boars under PAES swine housing standards.
choiceExplanations.7.5m²: Correct — PAES 401:2001 specifies a minimum floor space requirement of 7.5 m² per animal for boar pens.
choiceExplanations.8.5m²: 8.5 m² exceeds the standard 7.5 m² minimum space requirement specified by PAES for boar pens.
choiceExplanations.5.5m²: 5.5 m² is too cramped for a breeding boar and falls well below PAES housing standards.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: For every 100 chicks, the waterer shall be placed on stands about 25 mm high, what is the minimum water requirement for linear type waterer (PAES 402:2001 Housing for Broiler Production).

choiceExplanations.3.9L: 3.9 L overstates the PAES 402:2001 minimum waterer capacity requirement per 100 chicks.
choiceExplanations.4.7L: 4.7 L exceeds the PAES 402:2001 standard capacity for linear waterers serving 100 chicks.
choiceExplanations.3.6L: Correct — PAES 402:2001 specifies a minimum water capacity of 3.6 L per 100 chicks for linear type waterers.
choiceExplanations.2.9L: 2.9 L falls short of the 3.6 L minimum linear waterer capacity required per 100 chicks.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: In PAES 402:2001 Housing for Broiler Production, what is the length of waterer for linear type for above 4 weeks old chicks?
items.rationale: Under PAES 402:2001 (Housing for Broiler Production), the minimum linear waterer space per 100 birds for broilers above 4 weeks old is 4 meters (compared to 2 meters for birds 4 weeks old and below).

choiceExplanations.2 meters: 2 meters of linear waterer length is specified for younger chicks up to 4 weeks old, not older broilers.
choiceExplanations.3 meters: 3 meters does not match the PAES 402:2001 linear waterer length for broilers above 4 weeks old.
choiceExplanations.4 meters: Correct — PAES 402:2001 requires 4 meters of linear waterer length per 100 birds for broilers over 4 weeks old.
choiceExplanations.1 meter: 1 meter is far too short for 100 broilers over 4 weeks old and causes severe crowding.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: In PAES 410:200 (Lairage for Swine, Small and Large Animals), what is the minimum distance from the slaughterhouse?

choiceExplanations.12m: 12 m exceeds the minimum 10 m separation distance prescribed under PAES 410 for lairage structures.
choiceExplanations.10m: Correct — PAES 410 specifies that the lairage shall be located at least 10 m away from the slaughterhouse.
choiceExplanations.14m: 14 m is greater than the standard 10 m minimum setback between lairage and slaughterhouse.
choiceExplanations.8m: 8 m is below the 10 m minimum distance required to control odor and contamination.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Losses of mechanical rice thresher
items.rationale: 3% - total losses blower loss - 1.2% / separation loss - 1.3% / unthreshed loss - 0.2% / scattering loss - 0.3%

choiceExplanations.4% - total losses blower loss - 1.5%: Exceeds the allowable 3% total loss and 1.2% blower loss limits in PAES rice thresher standards.
choiceExplanations.3% - total losses blower loss - 1.2%: Correct — PAES standards limit mechanical rice thresher total losses to 3% maximum and blower loss to 1.2%.
choiceExplanations.5% - total losses blower loss - 2.0%: Overly permissive loss limits that fail PAES mechanical rice thresher performance criteria.
choiceExplanations.2% - total losses blower loss - 0.8%: Stricter than the official PAES performance thresholds of 3% total loss and 1.2% blower loss.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Increase in harvesting losses after 2 weeks of maturity

choiceExplanations.12%: 12% corresponds to higher shattering losses experienced beyond 2 weeks past full crop maturity.
choiceExplanations.6%: 6% underestimates the typical shattering and lodging loss increase two weeks after maturity.
choiceExplanations.8%: Correct — Delaying harvest by 2 weeks past maturity increases grain shattering and field losses by about 8%.
choiceExplanations.10%: 10% overstates the standard 8% harvesting loss benchmark at two weeks post-maturity.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: grain or fraction of grain with its length greater than or equal to eight-tenth (8/10) of the average length of the grain.

choiceExplanations.Broken rice: Broken rice consists of milled kernel pieces measuring less than 8/10 of the average whole-grain length.
choiceExplanations.Head rice: Correct — PAES defines head rice as milled grains or fractions with length at least 8/10 of the average whole-grain length.
choiceExplanations.Brown rice: Brown rice is dehulled paddy that still retains its bran layer regardless of kernel length.
choiceExplanations.Brewers rice: Brewers rice consists of very small broken rice fragments passing through fine grading sieves.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: used to fasten shaft, pulleys and gear hubs together

choiceExplanations.Cotter pin: A cotter pin prevents axial loosening of clevis pins or slotted nuts, not torque transmission on hubs.
choiceExplanations.Key: Correct — A key fits into matching keyways on a shaft and hub to transmit torque and fasten pulleys or gears.
choiceExplanations.Retaining ring: A retaining ring holds components axially inside a groove without transmitting rotary torque between shaft and hub.
choiceExplanations.Lock washer: A lock washer prevents threaded nuts or bolts from loosening under vibration, rather than keying hubs to shafts.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: indicates a maximum sustained winds of 61 kph

choiceExplanations.Typhoon: A typhoon has maximum sustained winds well above 61 kph (starting at 118 kph).
choiceExplanations.Tropical depression: Correct — PAGASA classifies a tropical cyclone with maximum sustained winds up to 61 kph as a tropical depression.
choiceExplanations.Severe tropical storm: A severe tropical storm has maximum sustained winds ranging from 87 to 117 kph.
choiceExplanations.Tropical storm: A tropical storm has maximum sustained winds between 62 and 88 kph, above the 61 kph limit.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: maximum sustained winds of more than 220 kph

choiceExplanations.Severe tropical storm: A severe tropical storm carries sustained winds of only 87 to 117 kph.
choiceExplanations.Typhoon: Under PAGASA classification, a standard typhoon has sustained winds below the super typhoon threshold.
choiceExplanations.Super typhoon: Correct — PAGASA originally defined a super typhoon as a cyclone with maximum sustained winds exceeding 220 kph.
choiceExplanations.Tropical storm: A tropical storm carries sustained winds between 62 and 88 kph, far below 220 kph.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The burning efficiency of rice hull furnaces is between:

choiceExplanations.100%: Complete 100% combustion is practically unattainable due to unburned carbon in rice hull ash.
choiceExplanations.85%: 85% falls below the minimum 95% burning efficiency required for rice husk furnaces.
choiceExplanations.95%: Correct — PAES standards specify that rice hull furnaces achieve at least 95% burning (combustion) efficiency.
choiceExplanations.90%: 90% understates the 95% minimum combustion efficiency benchmark for rice hull furnaces.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The thermal efficiency of rice hull furnaces is between

choiceExplanations.70–100%: Exceeds typical rice hull furnace thermal efficiency due to flue gas and radiation heat losses.
choiceExplanations.40-70%: Correct — Agricultural rice hull furnaces typically operate within a thermal efficiency range of 40% to 70%.
choiceExplanations.10–40%: Represents very poor heat transfer efficiency below standard agricultural furnace performance.
choiceExplanations.100–130%: Violates conservation of energy since thermal efficiency cannot exceed 100%.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Warranty period for agricultural machine parts from the purchase of the machine.

choiceExplanations.7 months: 7 months is not a standard PAES warranty duration for agricultural machinery parts.
choiceExplanations.6 months: Correct — PAES agricultural machinery standards mandate a minimum 6-month warranty period for machine parts from purchase.
choiceExplanations.5 months: 5 months is shorter than the standard 6-month warranty required under PAES specifications.
choiceExplanations.4 months: 4 months falls short of the mandatory 6-month parts warranty period.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: any support provided to a customer after the product or service has already been purchased. Companies use after-sales support as a business strategy as it typically leads to higher customer satisfaction, brand loyalty, and even word-of-mouth-marketing.

choiceExplanations.Pre sale service: Pre-sale service covers customer assistance, demos, and consultations provided before purchase.
choiceExplanations.After sale service: Correct — After-sales service encompasses all support, maintenance, and assistance delivered after the customer purchases a product.
choiceExplanations.Sales promotion service: Sales promotion involves short-term marketing incentives aimed at stimulating immediate purchases rather than post-purchase support.
choiceExplanations.Product warranty claim: A warranty claim is only one narrow repair or replacement remedy, not the full scope of ongoing customer support.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: CPES: During Construction – minimum of ________ visit/s is required
items.answer: 2 visits minimum of two (2) visits with the conduct of first visit when the actual project accomplishment is at least 30% except for projects with a duration of 90 calendar days and below which may be subjected to at least one (1) final visit.
choices: 4 visits minimum of four (4) visits with the conduct of first visit when the actual project accomplishment is at least 25
3 visits minimum of three (3) visits with the conduct of first visit when the actual project accomplishment is at least 20
1 visit minimum of one (1) visit with the conduct of first visit when the actual project accomplishment is at least 50

2 visits minimum of two (2) visits with the conduct of first visit when the actual project accomplishment is at least 30% except for projects with a duration of 90 calendar days and below which may be subjected to at least one (1) final visit.

choiceExplanations.4 visits minimum of four (4) visits with: CPES guidelines do not mandate four construction visits starting at 25% accomplishment.
choiceExplanations.3 visits minimum of three (3) visits wit: CPES rules require two visits starting at 30% accomplishment, not three visits starting at 20%.
choiceExplanations.1 visit minimum of one (1) visit with th: A single final visit applies only to short projects of 90 calendar days or less, not standard projects.
choiceExplanations.2 visits minimum of two (2) visits with: Correct — CPES guidelines require at least two visits during construction starting at ≥30% accomplishment, except ≤90-day projects.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: In PAES 201 - Heated-Air Mechanical Grain Dryer – Specifications, the chamber wherein air pressure is developed for uniform distribution of the heated air through the grain mass

choiceExplanations.Hopper: A hopper holds and feeds grain into the dryer rather than pressurizing heated drying air.
choiceExplanations.Diffuser: A diffuser expands flow velocity into pressure, whereas the enclosed air-distribution chamber itself is the plenum.
choiceExplanations.Furnace: A furnace generates heat by burning fuel rather than serving as the pressurized air-distribution chamber.
choiceExplanations.Plenum: Correct — PAES 201 defines the plenum as the chamber where air pressure builds to distribute heated air uniformly through grain.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The standard pallet square size should be ______.

choiceExplanations.152 cm x 61 cm: Correct — PAES warehouse and grain storage standards specify 152 cm × 61 cm as the standard pallet dimension.
choiceExplanations.140 cm x 56 cm: 140 cm × 56 cm is smaller than the PAES standard warehouse pallet size.
choiceExplanations.167 cm x 67 cm: 167 cm × 67 cm exceeds the standard PAES pallet dimensions for bagged agricultural commodities.
choiceExplanations.129 cm x 52 cm: 129 cm × 52 cm does not conform to the PAES standard pallet dimension of 152 cm × 61 cm.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Housing for Goat and Sheep: Minimum roof slope if roofing is made of indigenous material

choiceExplanations.58%: Correct — PAES 404:2001 specifies a minimum roof slope of 58% when indigenous roofing materials like nipa or cogon are used.
choiceExplanations.63%: 63% is steeper than the minimum 58% roof slope required by PAES 404:2001.
choiceExplanations.46%: 46% is too flat for indigenous thatch roofing and risks water leakage and rapid decay.
choiceExplanations.75%: 75% is an unnecessarily steep pitch exceeding the 58% PAES minimum for indigenous roofing.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Defects Liability Period shall be ____ from project completion up to final acceptance by the Government.

choiceExplanations.1 YEAR: Correct — Under RA 9184 IRR, the Defects Liability Period lasts one year from project completion until final government acceptance.
choiceExplanations.4 YEAR: Four years exceeds the statutory 1-year Defects Liability Period for government infrastructure projects.
choiceExplanations.2 YEAR: Two years does not match the 1-year Defects Liability Period prior to final acceptance under RA 9184.
choiceExplanations.3 YEAR: Three years exceeds the mandatory 1-year Defects Liability Period before final acceptance.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: PAES 414a:2001 (Waste Management Structures-Part 1: Agricultural Liquid Waste) If an open channel will not become polluted, eave gutters can be omitted, and roof water can fall to a surface channel with a minimum free board of:

choiceExplanations.0.6%: 0.6% exceeds the 0.5% minimum specification stated in PAES 414-1:2001 for surface channels.
choiceExplanations.0.5%: Correct — PAES 414-1:2001 specifies a minimum value of 0.5% for surface channels receiving unpolluted roof water.
choiceExplanations.0.4%: 0.4% falls below the 0.5% minimum value required by PAES 414-1:2001.
choiceExplanations.0.7%: 0.7% is higher than the 0.5% minimum threshold set in PAES 414-1:2001.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: PAES 264:2015 (Rice Husk Fed Heating System) Heating system efficiency of direct fired furnace shall be at least:

choiceExplanations.65%: Correct — PAES 264:2015 mandates that the heating system efficiency of a direct-fired rice husk furnace be at least 65%.
choiceExplanations.55%: 55% falls below the 65% minimum efficiency required for direct-fired rice husk heating systems.
choiceExplanations.70%: 70% exceeds the 65% minimum efficiency benchmark set in PAES 264:2015.
choiceExplanations.60%: 60% does not meet the 65% minimum direct-fired furnace efficiency required by PAES 264:2015.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Agricultural Machinery – Rice Husk Fed Heating System – Specifications: / The burning efficiency of the furnace shall be at least:

choiceExplanations.95%: Correct — PAES 264:2015 requires rice husk-fed heating system furnaces to achieve at least 95% burning efficiency.
choiceExplanations.100%: 100% combustion efficiency is impossible in practice due to residual unburned carbon in husk ash.
choiceExplanations.90%: 90% falls below the 95% minimum burning efficiency mandated by PAES 264:2015.
choiceExplanations.85%: 85% indicates incomplete combustion and fails the 95% PAES 264:2015 standard.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Agricultural Machinery – Rice Husk Fed Heating System – Specifications / Furnace efficiency shall be at least:

choiceExplanations.70%: 70% is higher than the 65% minimum furnace efficiency specified in PAES 264:2015.
choiceExplanations.65%: Correct — PAES 264:2015 requires a rice husk-fed heating system to have at least 65% furnace efficiency.
choiceExplanations.55%: 55% is insufficient and falls below the 65% PAES 264:2015 furnace efficiency requirement.
choiceExplanations.60%: 60% fails to satisfy the 65% minimum furnace efficiency standard in PAES 264:2015.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: The maximum moment occurs at beam section at which shear diagram passes thru

choiceExplanations.0: Correct — Since shear V = dM/dx, bending moment reaches a local maximum or minimum where the shear diagram crosses zero.
choiceExplanations.2: Non-zero shear indicates the bending moment is still increasing or decreasing, not at a maximum.
choiceExplanations.5: At a shear value of 5, the slope dM/dx is non-zero, so moment is not an extremum.
choiceExplanations.1: A shear of 1 gives a non-zero moment slope, meaning the bending moment has not peaked.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: According to PAES, building sidewalls for swine housing shall have a minimum height of

choiceExplanations.2m: 2 m exceeds the 1 m minimum sidewall height specified by PAES for open-sided swine housing.
choiceExplanations.4m: 4 m is unnecessarily tall for a swine housing sidewall and exceeds standard ceiling heights.
choiceExplanations.1m: Correct — PAES 401:2001 specifies that swine housing building sidewalls shall have a minimum height of 1 m.
choiceExplanations.3m: 3 m exceeds the minimum 1 m sidewall height requirement in PAES 401:2001.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A device which uses fluid power to produce mechanical force and motion

choiceExplanations.Actuator: Correct — An actuator converts hydraulic or pneumatic fluid power into linear or rotary mechanical force and motion.
choiceExplanations.Transducer: A transducer converts one form of energy or physical signal into another, typically for measurement rather than driving loads.
choiceExplanations.Regulator: A regulator controls and maintains fluid pressure at a preset level rather than generating mechanical motion.
choiceExplanations.Accumulator: An accumulator stores pressurized hydraulic fluid temporarily to dampen pulses or supply peak flow.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: Precision-cut and semi-precision cut forage chopper shall be able to cut at least three different length settings with a maximum variation of cut o

choiceExplanations.7%: 7% exceeds the 5% maximum variation in cut length permitted for precision-cut forage choppers.
choiceExplanations.5%: Correct — PAES 244:2010 limits the maximum variation of cut length in precision and semi-precision forage choppers to 5%.
choiceExplanations.4%: 4% is tighter than the 5% maximum length variation allowed under PAES 244:2010.
choiceExplanations.6%: 6% exceeds the allowable 5% cut-length variation tolerance in PAES 244:2010.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: What is the reason of calibration?

choiceExplanations.Inspect and clean: Inspection and cleaning are routine preventive maintenance tasks, not instrument calibration.
choiceExplanations.Repair and replace: Repairing and replacing worn parts is corrective maintenance rather than verifying measurement accuracy.
choiceExplanations.Install and operate: Installation and operation refer to commissioning and running equipment, not adjusting measurement accuracy.
choiceExplanations.Measure and adjust: Correct — Calibration compares an instrument's readings against a known standard and adjusts it to ensure accuracy.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: If you are to create a code or program for a commonly used microcontroller, what code will you write to start a loop?

choiceExplanations.Int main() {: Standard C/C++ entry point function, not the recurring Arduino microcontroller loop function.
choiceExplanations.While loop() {: Invalid Arduino syntax that confuses a `while` control statement with the `loop()` function.
choiceExplanations.Void loop() {: Correct — In Arduino microcontroller programming, `void loop() {` starts the main function that runs repeatedly.
choiceExplanations.Void setup() {: Runs only once at startup to initialize pin modes and settings, not continuously in a loop.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: There is a necessity to create an automation system in which there is a need to monitor the soil moisture. When the moisture is below threshold, the system will automatically sprinkle the plants inside the greenhouse, what sensor and actuator will you use?
items.answer: Soil moisture sensor and solenoid valve
choices: Soil moisture sensor and solenoid valve

choiceExplanations.Humidity sensor and check valve: Measures air moisture rather than soil water content, and check valves only prevent backflow without electrical actuation.
choiceExplanations.Pressure sensor and relief valve: Monitors fluid pressure and vents excess pressure rather than measuring soil moisture for irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Soil moisture sensor and solenoid valve: Correct — A soil moisture sensor detects substrate dryness, while an electrically controlled solenoid valve opens to sprinkle water.
choiceExplanations.Temperature sensor and gate valve: Measures ambient heat instead of moisture, and standard gate valves are manually operated rather than automated.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A windpump rotor manufacturing company wants to automate the cutting of rotor blades to have accurate and uniform length, base width, and tip width. What class of metrology equipment is best to be used?
items.rationale: Coordinate-measuring machines (CMMs) offer the highest dimensional accuracy and repeatability for verifying precise linear dimensions such as blade length, base width, and tip width in automated production.

choiceExplanations.CT scanners: Computed tomography inspects internal volumetric flaws, which is unnecessary and costly for checking blade cut dimensions.
choiceExplanations.Blue-light 3D scanners: Primarily capture full surface meshes of complex freeform shapes rather than high-precision linear dimensional verification.
choiceExplanations.Laser scanners: Optical laser scanning captures broad surface profiles with lower dimensional precision than tactile coordinate metrology.
choiceExplanations.Coordinate-measuring machines: Correct — Coordinate-measuring machines (CMMs) accurately verify linear dimensions like blade length, base width, and tip width.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: If you are to create an automation system for monitoring temperature, what sensor will you use?

choiceExplanations.Temperature sensor: Correct — A temperature sensor (e.g., thermocouple, RTD, or thermistor) directly measures thermal conditions for monitoring.
choiceExplanations.Proximity sensor: Detects the presence or distance of nearby objects without measuring temperature.
choiceExplanations.Pressure sensor: Measures force per unit area exerted by a fluid rather than thermal energy.
choiceExplanations.Humidity sensor: Measures water vapor content in air rather than ambient or process temperature.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: If you are to apply your knowledge in coding or programming of a commonly used microcontroller, what code will you use to delay the activation of a certain actuator or sensor for 5 seconds?
items.rationale: In standard microcontroller C/C++ programming (such as Arduino), the delay() function accepts duration in milliseconds (5 seconds = 5000 ms) and statements must end with a semicolon, making delay(5000); the correct code.

choiceExplanations.delay(5000);: Correct — In Arduino programming, `delay()` takes milliseconds, so `delay(5000);` pauses program execution for 5 seconds.
choiceExplanations.62.5%: A percentage value, not a microcontroller programming command for creating a time delay.
choiceExplanations.Solenoid valve: A physical electromechanical fluid-control actuator rather than a software timing statement.
choiceExplanations.0.23 m: A linear length measurement in meters, unrelated to microcontroller timing code.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: What analysis is done to determine the degree of project feasibility at various scenarios?

choiceExplanations.Break-even analysis: Finds the production or sales volume where total revenues equal total costs, not multi-scenario variations.
choiceExplanations.Payback analysis: Calculates the time needed to recover initial investment costs under a single baseline cash-flow projection.
choiceExplanations.Sensitivity analysis: Correct — Sensitivity analysis tests how changes in key assumptions or scenarios affect project feasibility indicators like NPV or IRR.
choiceExplanations.Benefit-cost analysis: Evaluates overall project viability using the ratio of discounted benefits to costs under fixed baseline inputs.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A red pepper (Capsicum annuum) processing plant monitors the quality of its product. It takes the weight and 4-angle images of each fruit in all its 60 running conveyors. If it detects a blemished fruit, it diverts it to separate bin. Classify the automation system used in the processing plant.

choiceExplanations.Manufacturing execution system: Manages factory-wide production scheduling, inventory tracking, and order execution rather than real-time conveyor sensor sorting.
choiceExplanations.Distributed control system: Typically regulates continuous analog process loops rather than high-speed discrete inspection across 60 conveyors.
choiceExplanations.Supervisory control and data acquisition: Correct — SCADA gathers high-volume sensor and imaging data across multiple conveyors and supervises automated sorting decisions.
choiceExplanations.Programmable logic controller: A PLC executes local machine-level control on a line rather than supervising plant-wide multi-conveyor data acquisition.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A cattle ranch needs to measure the height of the tallest body part of each of 10,000 animals every morning. What class of metrology equipment is best to be used in automating measurement?

choiceExplanations.Height gauges: Contact-based bench tools requiring manual placement, unsuitable for 10,000 moving cattle daily.
choiceExplanations.Vision systems: 2D camera systems struggle to extract true 3D peak height accurately without depth calibration.
choiceExplanations.Laser trackers: Require retroreflector targets mounted on objects, making them impractical for live herd animals.
choiceExplanations.Laser scanners: Correct — Non-contact laser scanners rapidly capture 3D height profiles of moving cattle at high throughput.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A sweet potato pure manufacturing plant would like to apply metrology in automated detection of abnormalities in the skin of sweet potato tubers to ascertain top quality puree. What class of metrology equipment is best to be used?

choiceExplanations.MRI scanners: Magnetic resonance imaging is far too slow and expensive for high-speed industrial food inspection lines.
choiceExplanations.Optical scanners: Surface optical scanners miss subsurface skin bruises, rot, and internal tuber defects below the outer peel.
choiceExplanations.CT scanners: Correct — X-ray CT scanners inspect tuber surface and subsurface layers non-destructively to detect skin abnormalities and decay.
choiceExplanations.Laser scanners: Laser scanners only capture external 3D geometry and cannot evaluate internal or subsurface tuber tissue defects.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: In an automation system, you need to sprinkle the plants inside the greenhouse when temperature is above threshold, what actuator will you use?

choiceExplanations.Linear actuator: Produces straight-line mechanical push/pull motion rather than directly switching pressurized irrigation water flow.
choiceExplanations.Stepper motor: Provides discrete angular shaft rotation for positioning mechanisms rather than simple on/off water valve control.
choiceExplanations.Servo motor: Delivers closed-loop angular positioning, which is unnecessary for basic on/off greenhouse sprinkling.
choiceExplanations.Solenoid valve: Correct — A solenoid valve uses an electromagnetic coil to quickly open or close water flow to greenhouse sprinklers.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: If you are to code or program for a commonly used microcontroller, what code will you use to assign the sensors and actuators to specific pins?

choiceExplanations.Void main(){: Standard C uses `int main()`, whereas Arduino microcontrollers use `setup()` for pin initialization.
choiceExplanations.Void init(){: Not the standard Arduino sketch initialization block used to configure I/O pins.
choiceExplanations.Void loop(){: Runs continuously after startup to execute logic rather than assigning initial pin modes.
choiceExplanations.Void setup(){: Correct — In Arduino programming, `void setup(){` runs once at startup to assign sensors and actuators via `pinMode()`.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: Instrumentation Data Collection, Reduction and Presentation for Seepage

choiceExplanations.Monthly: Monthly intervals are too infrequent to detect sudden seepage increases that threaten dam or embankment stability.
choiceExplanations.Hourly: Hourly collection is excessive for standard routine seepage monitoring unless an emergency anomaly occurs.
choiceExplanations.Daily: Correct — Standard dam and embankment instrumentation protocols require daily collection and reduction of seepage data.
choiceExplanations.Weekly: Weekly intervals risk missing rapid changes in seepage rate between inspections.

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: The magnetization of ferromagnetic substances due to a varying magnetic field lags behind the field.

choiceExplanations.Hysteresis: Correct — Magnetic hysteresis is the lagging of magnetization behind a varying magnetizing field in ferromagnetic materials.
choiceExplanations.Retentivity: Retentivity is the residual magnetism remaining in a material after removing the external magnetizing force.
choiceExplanations.Permeability: Permeability measures how easily a material supports the formation of a magnetic field within itself.
choiceExplanations.Reluctance: Reluctance is the opposition offered by a magnetic circuit to the establishment of magnetic flux.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: It is the ability of a material to return to its original shape after the removal of stresses.

choiceExplanations.Plasticity: Plasticity is the ability of a material to undergo permanent deformation without fracturing after stress removal.
choiceExplanations.Malleability: Malleability is a material's ability to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets under compression.
choiceExplanations.Ductility: Ductility is the ability of a material to deform plastically under tensile stress, like drawing into wire.
choiceExplanations.Elasticity: Correct — Elasticity is the property of a material that enables it to recover its original shape and dimensions once applied stress is removed.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: The analysis and evaluation of the factors that will affect the economic success of engineering projects to the end that a recommendation can be made which will insure the best use of capita

choiceExplanations.Value engineering: Value engineering focuses on optimizing product or process function relative to cost without reducing quality.
choiceExplanations.Financial accounting: Financial accounting records, summarizes, and reports historical business transactions in standardized financial statements.
choiceExplanations.Capital budgeting: Capital budgeting evaluates and selects long-term investment projects using cash flow metrics like NPV and IRR.
choiceExplanations.Engineering economy: Correct — Engineering economy analyzes and evaluates economic factors of engineering projects to recommend the best use of capital.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Occurs when the mathematical product volume and price is constant

choiceExplanations.Income elasticity of demand: Income elasticity of demand measures the responsiveness of quantity demanded to changes in consumer income.
choiceExplanations.Arc elasticity of demand: Arc elasticity of demand measures demand responsiveness between two distinct points along a demand curve.
choiceExplanations.Cross elasticity of demand: Cross elasticity of demand measures how quantity demanded of one good responds to another good's price.
choiceExplanations.Unitary elasticity of demand: Correct — Unitary elasticity of demand occurs when price elasticity equals 1, keeping total revenue (price times volume) constant as price changes.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Occurs in a situation where a commodity or service is supplied by a number of vendors and there is nothing to prevent additional vendors entering the market

choiceExplanations.Imperfect competition: Imperfect competition exists whenever sellers have market power, differentiated products, or barriers to entry.
choiceExplanations.Perfect competition: Correct — Perfect competition occurs when many vendors supply a homogeneous commodity with free market entry and exit.
choiceExplanations.Monopolistic competition: Monopolistic competition features many sellers offering slightly differentiated products rather than an identical commodity.
choiceExplanations.Pure oligopoly: Pure oligopoly involves only a few dominant firms supplying a standardized product with entry barriers.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Exists when a unique product or service is available from a single vendor and that vendor can prevent the entry of all others into the market

choiceExplanations.Monopoly: Correct — Monopoly exists when a single vendor controls a unique product or service and blocks all competitors from entering.
choiceExplanations.Monopsony: Monopsony is a market structure dominated by a single buyer rather than a single seller.
choiceExplanations.Oligopoly: Oligopoly is a market dominated by a small number of interdependent firms rather than one vendor.
choiceExplanations.Duopoly: Duopoly is a specific form of oligopoly where exactly two firms control the market.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: In a project feasibility study, which section typically contains the problem statement, causes, and supporting evidence?

choiceExplanations.Project Objectives: Project Objectives state the specific, measurable goals the proposed project aims to achieve.
choiceExplanations.Project Summary: Project Summary gives an executive overview of the entire study's key findings and recommendations.
choiceExplanations.Project Justification: Correct — Project Justification presents the problem statement, root causes, and supporting data demonstrating why the project is needed.
choiceExplanations.Project Description: Project Description outlines the physical scope, components, location, and technical features of the project.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: The projection of cash inflow and outflow of a farm to estimate the incremental net benefit of the life of the project is known as

choiceExplanations.Cash flow: Correct — A cash flow projection tracks inflows and outflows over a project's life to determine incremental net benefits.
choiceExplanations.Income statement: An income statement summarizes revenues, expenses, and net profit over a single accounting period.
choiceExplanations.Balance sheet: A balance sheet reports assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific point in time.
choiceExplanations.Trial balance: A trial balance lists general ledger account balances to verify that debits equal credits.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: A term used in the context of international trade. It's when a country or company exports a product at a price that is lower in the foreign importing market than the price in the exporter's domestic market.

choiceExplanations.Embargo: Embargo is an official government ban restricting or halting trade with a particular country.
choiceExplanations.Dumping: Correct — Dumping occurs when an exporter sells goods in a foreign market below its domestic price or production cost.
choiceExplanations.Smuggling: Smuggling is the illegal transport of goods across borders to evade customs duties or prohibitions.
choiceExplanations.Arbitrage: Arbitrage exploits simultaneous price differences across markets by buying low and selling high.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Degree of freedom with replications: A single-factor experiment using completely randomized experimental design results to the following statistical values: treatment sum of squares of 2,510.5, error mean square error of 13.4, error degrees of freedom of 12 and total degrees of freedom of 14. How many treatments are involved?
items.rationale: Tr DF = Total DF –Error DF / = 14-12 = 2 / No. of treatments = Tr DF + 1 / =2+1 = 3
choices: Tr DF = Total DF + Error DF
Tr DF = Error DF – Total DF
Tr DF = Rep DF – Error DF

choiceExplanations.Tr DF = Total DF + Error DF: Adding Total DF and Error DF overcounts degrees of freedom because Total DF equals Treatment DF plus Error DF.
choiceExplanations.Tr DF = Total DF –Error DF: Correct — In a completely randomized design, Total DF = Treatment DF + Error DF, so Tr DF = Total DF – Error DF.
choiceExplanations.Tr DF = Error DF – Total DF: Subtracting Total DF from Error DF yields a negative value since Error DF is smaller than Total DF.
choiceExplanations.Tr DF = Rep DF – Error DF: Replication DF minus Error DF does not isolate Treatment DF in a completely randomized design.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: In economics extreme elasticity where even if you do not change the price there is a change in demand

choiceExplanations.Perfectly elastic: Correct — Perfectly elastic demand has infinite elasticity, meaning quantity demanded can vary without any price change at a fixed horizontal price.
choiceExplanations.Unitary elastic: Unitary elastic demand changes quantity demanded in exact proportion to a percentage change in price.
choiceExplanations.Perfectly inelastic: Perfectly inelastic demand exhibits zero change in quantity demanded regardless of any price change.
choiceExplanations.Relatively elastic: Relatively elastic demand requires a price change to trigger a proportionally larger change in quantity demanded.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: What is the effect of increasing inflation rate to discounted cash flow at project start?
items.rationale: At project start (year t = 0), the discount factor is (1 + r)⁰ = 1 regardless of the inflation or discount rate, so an increasing inflation rate has no effect on the initial discounted cash flow.

choiceExplanations.Increases: Discounted cash flow at year 0 cannot increase because the discount factor at t = 0 is always 1.
choiceExplanations.Fluctuates: Discounted cash flow at project start does not fluctuate since time t equals zero.
choiceExplanations.Decreases: Discounted cash flow at year 0 does not decrease because (1 + r)^0 equals 1 regardless of rate.
choiceExplanations.None: Correct — At project start (t = 0), the discount factor (1 + r)^0 is 1, so increasing the inflation/discount rate has no effect.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Using economic feasibility analysis, the Net Present Values (NPVs) of small water impounding project (SWIP), shallow tubewell, small scale irrigation project (SSIP) are 0, -1.2 and -2.6 million pesos, respectively. The proposed projects are owned by the government. Which project is economically feasible?
items.answer: SWIP For non-revenue generating government or service projects, the project is economically feasible if NPV greater than or equal to zero or just break-even
choices: Shallow tubewell For non-revenue generating government or service projects, the project is economically feasible if NPV is negative
None of them For non-revenue generating government or service projects, the project is economically feasible only if NPV exceeds one
SSIP For non-revenue generating government or service projects, the project is economically feasible when NPV is lowest among options
SWIP For non-revenue generating government or service projects, the project is economically feasible if NPV greater than or equal to zero or just break-even

choiceExplanations.Shallow tubewell For non-revenue generat: A negative NPV of -1.2 million pesos means economic costs exceed benefits, making the shallow tubewell unfeasible.
choiceExplanations.None of them For non-revenue generating: Economic feasibility requires NPV >= 0 rather than > 1, so break-even projects with NPV = 0 qualify.
choiceExplanations.SSIP For non-revenue generating governme: SSIP has the lowest NPV (-2.6 million pesos), representing the largest net economic loss among the alternatives.
choiceExplanations.SWIP For non-revenue generating governme: Correct — SWIP has NPV = 0, and public service projects are economically feasible whenever NPV is greater than or equal to zero.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: In feasibility study preparation, the project’s Internal Rate of Return is determined using the ______________ by iteratively calculating the NPV at varied discount rates until NPV=0 is attained.

choiceExplanations.Simpson’s rule method: Simpson's rule numerically approximates definite integrals rather than finding equation roots.
choiceExplanations.Newton’s root method: Correct — Newton's root-finding method iteratively updates discount rate guesses using derivatives until NPV = 0, yielding the IRR.
choiceExplanations.Taylor series method: Taylor series approximates functions locally using polynomials rather than iteratively solving for roots.
choiceExplanations.Euler’s step method: Euler's method numerically solves ordinary differential equations step by step.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: The discounted cash flow at project start is always equal to ____.

choiceExplanations.Cumulative cash flow: Cumulative cash flow sums net cash flows across multiple periods rather than representing year 0 alone.
choiceExplanations.Total cash inflow: Total cash inflow omits initial investment outflows occurring at the start of a project.
choiceExplanations.Gross cash flow: Gross cash flow ignores outflows and taxes, whereas discounting applies to net cash flow.
choiceExplanations.Net cash flow: Correct — At project start (year 0), the discount factor is (1 + r)^0 = 1, so discounted cash flow equals net cash flow.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: A minihydro project, having a project life of 8 years, has the following data: total investment of Php20 million, total benefits of Php100 million, and total costs of Php60 million. What is the project’s annual Return on Investment?
items.rationale: Total net profit over 8 years is Php100M − Php60M = Php40M, giving an average annual net profit of Php40M / 8 = Php5M/year; dividing by the Php20M total investment yields an annual ROI of Php5M / Php20M = 25%.

choiceExplanations.50%: 50% overstates annual ROI because it would correspond to a 4-year life instead of 8 years.
choiceExplanations.3.75%: 3.75% miscalculates the ratio of net benefit to investment and project duration.
choiceExplanations.25%: Correct — Net profit is Php40M (100M - 60M), giving 200% total ROI over Php20M investment, or 25% annually over 8 years.
