choiceExplanations.6.25%: 6.25% corresponds to dividing 50% rather than 200% across the 8-year project life.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: An AFMESC project, having a project life of 8 years, has a total investment of Php20 million, total benefits of Php100 million, and total costs of Php60 million. What is the project’s overall Return on Investment or ROI?

choiceExplanations.216%: 216% does not match the net benefit of Php40M divided by the Php20M investment.
choiceExplanations.184%: 184% underestimates overall ROI from Php40M net benefit on a Php20M investment.
choiceExplanations.200%: Correct — Overall ROI equals (Total Benefits - Total Costs) / Investment = (100M - 60M) / 20M = 200%.
choiceExplanations.230%: 230% overstates overall ROI relative to Php40M net profit on Php20M capital.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Your rice processing center has the following present values: present value of benefits of Php2.2B, present value of costs of Php1.1B. What is your processing center’s benefit-cost ratio?

choiceExplanations.1.6: 1.6 underestimates the ratio of Php2.2B present benefits to Php1.1B present costs.
choiceExplanations.2.6: 2.6 overstates the quotient of Php2.2B divided by Php1.1B.
choiceExplanations.1.8: 1.8 does not equal Php2.2B divided by Php1.1B.
choiceExplanations.2.0: Correct — Benefit-cost ratio (BCR) equals PV of benefits divided by PV of costs: Php2.2B / Php1.1B = 2.0.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Using financial feasibility analysis, the Net Present Values (NPVs) of farm-to-market road, irrigation and flood control projects are 18.2, 6.3 and -2.6 million pesos, while the Internal Rate of Returns (IRRs) are 9.6%, 12% and 3.5%, respectively. Annual discount plus inflation rate is 10%. Which project shall be implemented?
items.answer: Irrigation Since irrigation project has combined discount plus inflation rate higher than the country’s annual discount rate.
choices: Farm-to-market road Since it has the highest Net Present Value among all three proposed projects at 18.2 million pesos
All three projects Since infrastructure and agricultural projects always generate positive socio-economic net benefits
Flood control Since flood control project has the lowest Internal Rate of Return and a negative Net Present Value overall
Irrigation Since irrigation project has combined discount plus inflation rate higher than the country’s annual discount rate.

choiceExplanations.Farm-to-market road Since it has the hig: The farm-to-market road's IRR (9.6%) falls below the 10% hurdle rate, despite its reported NPV figure.
choiceExplanations.All three projects Since infrastructure: Not all infrastructure projects are feasible; flood control has negative NPV (-2.6M) and 3.5% IRR.
choiceExplanations.Flood control Since flood control projec: Flood control is financially unfeasible because its NPV is negative (-2.6M) and IRR (3.5%) is below 10%.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation Since irrigation project has: Correct — Irrigation is the only project whose IRR (12%) exceeds the 10% combined discount and inflation hurdle rate while keeping a positive NPV (6.3M).

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: A 15-year project has an overall Return on Investment (ROI) of 750%, what is its estimated ROI in any year within its project life?

choiceExplanations.55%: 55% over 15 years would yield 825% overall ROI rather than 750%.
choiceExplanations.50%: Correct — Dividing the 750% overall ROI evenly over the 15-year project life gives an estimated annual ROI of 50%.
choiceExplanations.45%: 45% over 15 years would yield only 675% overall ROI instead of 750%.
choiceExplanations.40%: 40% over 15 years would yield only 600% overall ROI instead of 750%.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: In feasibility study preparation, what analysis is required to determine the economic performance of the project at different scenarios?

choiceExplanations.Market demand analysis: Market demand analysis forecasts product demand and pricing rather than testing multiple project performance scenarios.
choiceExplanations.Financial ratio analysis: Financial ratio analysis evaluates liquidity, leverage, and profitability from accounting statements.
choiceExplanations.Technical feasibility analysis: Technical feasibility analysis assesses engineering design, technology, site suitability, and production capacity.
choiceExplanations.Economic sensitivity analysis: Correct — Economic sensitivity analysis evaluates how changes in key variables or scenarios affect project indicators like NPV, IRR, and BCR.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: The normal combined discount and inflation rate of the Philippines.

choiceExplanations.8-12%: Correct — In Philippine ABE feasibility evaluation, the normal combined discount and inflation rate falls within 8–12% around NEDA's 10% benchmark.
choiceExplanations.12–16%: 12–16% exceeds the typical Philippine feasibility study benchmark centered near NEDA's 10% rate.
choiceExplanations.16–20%: 16–20% is an unrealistically high hurdle rate compared to standard Philippine evaluation guidelines.
choiceExplanations.4–8%: 4–8% is below the standard Philippine combined discount and inflation benchmark near 10%.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: A farm-to-market road project in Isabela has these financial feasibility indicators: NPV of -P8M, IRR of 0.6% and BCR of 0.2. Its economic feasibility indicators are: NPV of P5M, IRR of 18% and BCR of 1.5. The social discount rate is 10%. Based on your evaluation, the project is ____________.

choiceExplanations.Economically unfeasible: Economic indicators show positive NPV (P5M), IRR (18% > 10%), and BCR (1.5 > 1), so it is not unfeasible.
choiceExplanations.Economically feasible: Correct — The project is economically feasible because its economic NPV is positive (P5M), IRR (18%) exceeds the 10% social discount rate, and BCR exceeds 1 (1.5).
choiceExplanations.Marginally feasible: With economic IRR (18%) well above 10% and BCR at 1.5, feasibility is solid rather than marginal.
choiceExplanations.Financially feasible: It is financially unfeasible because financial NPV is negative (-P8M), IRR (0.6%) < 10%, and BCR < 1.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: The following are covered in the scope of work of a feasibility study preparer, except _____.
items.rationale: A feasibility study evaluates financial and economic viability (including amortization, shadow prices, and salvage values) using preliminary engineering estimates, whereas detailed engineering design is conducted only after project approval.

choiceExplanations.Detailed engineering design: Correct — Detailed engineering design is performed after project approval during the DED phase, whereas a feasibility study only covers preliminary technical concepts.
choiceExplanations.Computation of periodic amortization val: Computing periodic loan amortization is part of the financial analysis in a feasibility study.
choiceExplanations.Estimation of salvage values: Estimating asset salvage values at project end is standard in feasibility cash flow projections.
choiceExplanations.Estimation of shadow prices: Estimating shadow prices is required for economic analysis in public feasibility studies.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Determine the Net Present Value of a 3-year root crops project with investment expenses at the start of the project of Php8.2M. The discounted cash flows for the end of years 1, 2, and 3 are -Php1.6M, Php 2.5M and Php8.8M.

choiceExplanations.Php1.3M: Php1.3M does not equal the sum of -8.2M, -1.6M, +2.5M, and +8.8M.
choiceExplanations.Php1.5M: Correct — Summing all discounted cash flows from year 0 to year 3 gives -8.2 - 1.6 + 2.5 + 8.8 = Php1.5M.
choiceExplanations.Php2.0M: Php2.0M overstates the sum of discounted inflows minus initial and year-1 outflows.
choiceExplanations.Php1.2M: Php1.2M underestimates the net sum of discounted cash flows across all four periods.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: What feasibility indicator is best for determining how fast the project recovers the investment?

choiceExplanations.Net present worth: Net present worth measures total discounted monetary gain rather than time to recover capital.
choiceExplanations.Payback period: Correct — Payback period directly measures the time required for cumulative net cash inflows to recover the initial investment.
choiceExplanations.Benefit-cost ratio: Benefit-cost ratio compares discounted benefits to discounted costs as a dimensionless ratio.
choiceExplanations.Break-even point: Break-even point determines the output or sales volume where total revenue equals total cost.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: What feasibility indicator is best for determining how much can you gain from a certain project?

choiceExplanations.BCR: BCR shows relative benefit per unit cost rather than total net monetary gain.
choiceExplanations.IRR: IRR gives a percentage rate of return rather than absolute monetary profit.
choiceExplanations.NPV: Correct — Net Present Value (NPV) measures the exact discounted net monetary gain a project generates above the required return.
choiceExplanations.PBP: Payback period (PBP) measures recovery time, not total net profit over the project life.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: What is the effect of increasing discount rate to discounted cash flow at year 10 of the project?

choiceExplanations.Unchanged: Future cash flows at year 10 change whenever the discount rate in 1/(1 + r)^10 changes.
choiceExplanations.Increases: A higher discount rate enlarges the denominator (1 + r)^10, reducing rather than increasing present value.
choiceExplanations.Decreases: Correct — Because discounted cash flow equals CF_10 / (1 + r)^10, increasing the discount rate r decreases the discounted value.
choiceExplanations.Fluctuates: Discounted cash flow decreases monotonically with a rising discount rate rather than fluctuating.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: What feasibility analysis uses market prices?

choiceExplanations.Technical analysis: Technical analysis evaluates engineering processes, machinery, site layout, and resource capacities rather than prices.
choiceExplanations.Financial analysis: Correct — Financial analysis evaluates project profitability from the investor's perspective using actual market prices, taxes, and subsidies.
choiceExplanations.Sensitivity analysis: Sensitivity analysis tests how variations in assumptions affect feasibility metrics rather than defining price bases.
choiceExplanations.Economic analysis: Economic analysis uses shadow prices adjusted for taxes, subsidies, and externalities instead of market prices.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: The ____ is equal to the discount rate when the Net Present Value is zero.

choiceExplanations.BCR: Benefit-cost ratio (BCR) equals 1.0 when NPV is zero, not the discount rate itself.
choiceExplanations.ROI: Return on investment (ROI) measures undiscounted profit over capital rather than the zero-NPV discount rate.
choiceExplanations.IRR: Correct — By definition, the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) is the discount rate at which a project's Net Present Value equals zero.
choiceExplanations.ARR: Accounting rate of return (ARR) uses undiscounted accounting income rather than discounted cash flows.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: The net cash flow of the cassava processing venture at project start is -10 million pesos due to loan at which revenue is not materialized yet. Discount rate is 10%. What is the value of the discounted cash flow in million pesos at project start?
items.rationale: -10 / The value of discounted cash flow at project start is the same as the net cash flow since discounting has not started yet

choiceExplanations.-9: -9 incorrectly discounts the year 0 cash flow by one year (10 / 1.1 ≈ 9.09).
choiceExplanations.-10: Correct — At project start (year 0), the discount factor is (1 + 0.10)^0 = 1, so the discounted cash flow remains -10 million pesos.
choiceExplanations.-11: -11 erroneously compounds the initial outflow by 10% instead of keeping year 0 undiscounted.
choiceExplanations.-12: -12 does not reflect the year 0 discount factor of unity.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: The price at which there is no loss or gain

choiceExplanations.Break-even price: Correct — Break-even price is the unit price at which total revenue exactly equals total cost, resulting in zero profit or loss.
choiceExplanations.Marginal price: Marginal price reflects the price or cost associated with producing or buying one additional unit.
choiceExplanations.Shadow price: Shadow price represents the true economic opportunity cost of a resource adjusted for market distortions.
choiceExplanations.Equilibrium price: Equilibrium price is the market price where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: As part of project planning, you need to estimate the discounted value of costs of a 3-year vegetable project. It has the following costs for years 0, 1, 2 and 3 in million Php: 5, 1, 2 and 3, respectively. What is its Present Value of Costs? Assume a combined discount and inflation rate of 10%.

choiceExplanations.Php 9.82M: Correct — Discounting each year's cost at 10% gives 5 + 1/1.1 + 2/1.1^2 + 3/1.1^3 = Php 9.82M.
choiceExplanations.Php 8.64M: Php 8.64M underestimates the present value of the cost stream at a 10% discount rate.
choiceExplanations.Php 9.03M: Php 9.03M omits or miscalculates part of the discounted cost terms across years 0 to 3.
choiceExplanations.Php 12.77M: Php 12.77M results from compounding costs forward rather than discounting future costs back to present.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: A banana production and export project is being evaluated for financial feasibility. At 11% annual discount rate, it has the following feasibility indicators: net present value of 1.8 billion pesos and internal rate of return of 58%. If annual discount rate drops to 10%, will it be feasible?
items.rationale: Reducing the discount rate from 11% to 10% increases the present value of net cash inflows above the existing Php 1.8 billion NPV, and 10% remains well below the 58% IRR, so the project remains feasible.

choiceExplanations.Yes: Correct — Lowering the discount rate from 11% to 10% increases NPV above Php1.8B, and IRR (58%) still exceeds 10%, so it remains feasible.
choiceExplanations.Insufficient data to determine: Sufficient data is given because NPV moves inversely with discount rate and IRR exceeds 10%.
choiceExplanations.No: Dropping the discount rate raises NPV above 1.8 billion pesos rather than making it negative.
choiceExplanations.Indeterminate: The outcome is determinate since a lower discount rate unambiguously improves NPV for standard cash flows.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: What is market price deducted by tax?

choiceExplanations.Border price: Border price is the international market value of a traded good at a country's border.
choiceExplanations.Equilibrium price: Equilibrium price is the market-clearing price where supply matches demand.
choiceExplanations.Shadow price: Correct — Shadow price reflects true economic resource value in economic analysis by stripping transfer payments such as taxes and subsidies from market prices.
choiceExplanations.Transfer price: Transfer price is the internal price charged between divisions of the same enterprise.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: In evaluating the sensitivity of a project using a standard compliant software, a Farm-to-Market Road (FMR) project generates an NPV of 29.53 million Php when discount rate is 10.62% and NPV of exactly zero when discount rate is set to 15.88%. What is the Internal Rate of Return of the project?

choiceExplanations.19.37%: 19.37% is not the rate where NPV equals zero.
choiceExplanations.20.64%: 20.64% does not produce a zero NPV as stated for the project.
choiceExplanations.18.26%: 18.26% does not correspond to the discount rate yielding NPV = 0.
choiceExplanations.15.88%: Correct — By definition, IRR is the discount rate where NPV equals zero, which is directly given as 15.88%.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Which among the feasibility indicators is best for determining project performance?
items.rationale: Net Present Value (NPV) is considered the best overall feasibility indicator because it measures absolute wealth added in present monetary terms and avoids the scale and multiple-root limitations of IRR.

choiceExplanations.IRR: IRR measures percentage yield but can give misleading rankings for mutually exclusive or differently scaled projects.
choiceExplanations.NPV: Correct — Net Present Value (NPV) is the preferred indicator of overall project performance because it directly measures net wealth added in currency terms.
choiceExplanations.BCR: BCR measures relative efficiency per peso spent without indicating the total scale of net benefits.
choiceExplanations.Payback period: Payback period ignores the time value of money and all cash flows after capital recovery.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: A solar powered irrigation project has the following values of its major financial feasibility indicators: NPV of Php62 million, IRR or 19.5% and BCR of 1.53. Evaluate and specify the projects feasibility.

choiceExplanations.Financially unfeasible: Positive NPV (Php62M), BCR > 1 (1.53), and IRR of 19.5% prove the project is financially viable.
choiceExplanations.Economically unfeasible: The given indicators are financial metrics, not economic metrics, and all exceed feasibility thresholds.
choiceExplanations.Financially feasible: Correct — The project is financially feasible because its financial NPV > 0 (Php62M), BCR > 1 (1.53), and IRR (19.5%) exceeds typical hurdle rates.
choiceExplanations.Marginally feasible: An IRR of 19.5% and BCR of 1.53 show strong profitability rather than marginal feasibility.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: If you are to create a feasibility study report for a 100,000-head layer chicken project, what is first chapter of your feasibility study report?

choiceExplanations.Market Aspect: Market Aspect follows the Project Summary and analyzes supply, demand, and marketing strategies.
choiceExplanations.Financial Aspect: Financial Aspect appears later in the report after market, technical, and organizational studies.
choiceExplanations.Project Summary: Correct — Project Summary (Executive Summary) is placed as the first chapter of a feasibility study to overview key findings and conclusions.
choiceExplanations.Technical Aspect: Technical Aspect follows the Market Aspect to specify production processes, equipment, and site requirements.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: A rice processing center has a total project cost of P45M. It has these financial feasibility indicators: NPV of P52M, IRR of 12.3% and BCR of 1.12. Its alternative cacao processing project needing the same investment cost has an IRR of 15.2%. Based on your evaluation, the project is ____________.

choiceExplanations.Marginally feasible: Having positive NPV (P52M), BCR > 1 (1.12), and IRR (12.3%) above 10% meets standard feasibility criteria.
choiceExplanations.Financially unfeasible: The rice processing center is financially feasible because its NPV is positive and BCR exceeds 1.
choiceExplanations.Economically unfeasible: Economic feasibility cannot be declared unfeasible from financial indicators alone, which are all positive.
choiceExplanations.Financially feasible: Correct — The rice processing center is financially feasible on its own because NPV > 0 (P52M), BCR > 1 (1.12), and IRR > 10% (12.3%).

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Which one is true when discount rate increases?
items.rationale: Since future net cash inflows are discounted by (1 + r)^t, increasing the discount rate r lowers the present value of future cash flows and therefore decreases the Net Present Value (NPV).

choiceExplanations.NPV decreases: Correct — Increasing the discount rate reduces the present value of future cash inflows, causing Net Present Value (NPV) to decrease.
choiceExplanations.Capital reduces: Initial capital investment at year 0 is unaffected by changes in the discount rate.
choiceExplanations.NPV increases: NPV moves inversely with the discount rate for conventional cash flows, so it cannot increase.
choiceExplanations.Risk decreases: A higher discount rate typically reflects higher perceived risk rather than decreasing risk.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: A non-revenue generating irrigation project has the following values of its major financial feasibility indicators: NPV of -Php2.6 million, IRR or 3.5% and BCR of 0.36. It has also the following values of major economic feasibility indicators: NPV of Php82 million, IRR or 28% and BCR of 3.51. Evaluate the projects feasibility then recommend whether to implement the project or not.

choiceExplanations.Economically feasible, implement: Correct — Non-revenue public irrigation projects are judged by economic indicators, and NPV = Php82M, IRR = 28%, and BCR = 3.51 justify implementation.
choiceExplanations.Financially unfeasible, reject: Public non-revenue projects are not rejected solely for negative financial NPV when economic returns are strong.
choiceExplanations.Economically unfeasible, defer: Economic indicators are strongly positive (NPV Php82M, IRR 28%, BCR 3.51), not unfeasible.
choiceExplanations.Financially feasible, implement: Financial NPV (-Php2.6M) and BCR (0.36) show it is financially unfeasible, though still economically viable.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: If you are to plan the National Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization Research, Development and Extension, which of the following agenda shall be excluded?
items.answer: Basic research on farm machinery engines
items.rationale: Under the AFMech Law (RA 10601), the National Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization RDE Agenda focuses on applied design, testing, pilot-testing, commercialization, and stakeholder training rather than basic research on farm machinery engines.
choices: Basic research on farm machinery engines
Design, testing of new machineries and equipment
Training of farmers, fisherfolk, manufacturers, extension workers and ABEs

choiceExplanations.Basic research on farm machinery engines: Correct — Under the AFMech Law (RA 10601), the national RDE agenda prioritizes applied machinery development, testing, commercialization, and training rather than basic engine research.
choiceExplanations.Development, pilot-testing and commercia: Development, pilot-testing, and commercialization of agri-fishery machinery are core components of the national RDE agenda.
choiceExplanations.Design, testing of new machineries and e: Designing and testing new agricultural and fisheries machinery is explicitly included in the RDE program.
choiceExplanations.Training of farmers, fisherfolk, manufac: Capacity building and training for farmers, fisherfolk, manufacturers, extension workers, and ABEs are mandated RDE activities.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: You are tasked to evaluate the financial feasibility of a 3-year AFMESC project. It has the following costs for years 0, 1, 2 and 3 in million Php: 5, 1, 2 and 3, respectively. Likewise, the same project has the following benefits for years 0, 1, 2 and 3 in million Php: 0, 6, 8 and 9, respectively. What is its Net Present Value and indicate if the project is feasible or not based on NPV? Use the NEDA published Social Discount Rate (SDR) of 10%.
items.rationale: Net cash flows (B − C) for years 0 to 3 are −5, +5, +6, and +6 million Php; discounting at 10% yields NPV = −5 + 5/1.1 + 6/1.1² + 6/1.1³ ≈ −5 + 4.55 + 4.96 + 4.51 = Php 9.01M (≈ Php 9M > 0), confirming the project is financially feasible.

choiceExplanations.Php -8M, not economically feasible: Php -8M is incorrect because discounted net cash flows sum to positive Php 9M.
choiceExplanations.Php 5M, economically feasible: Php 5M underestimates the discounted net cash flow sum of approximately Php 9.01M.
choiceExplanations.Php -10M, not financially feasible: Php -10M incorrectly yields a negative value; the project has a positive NPV of Php 9M.
choiceExplanations.Php 9M, financially feasible: Correct — Discounting net cash flows (-5, +5, +6, +6) at 10% yields NPV ≈ Php 9.01M (Php 9M), making the project financially feasible.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: A milkfish hatchery project has these financial feasibility indicators: NPV of P36M, IRR of 16.28% and BCR of 1.23. The combined inflation and discount rate is 10%. Based on your evaluation, the project is __________.

choiceExplanations.Financially unfeasible: All financial criteria are exceeded (NPV > 0, BCR > 1, IRR > 10%), so it is not unfeasible.
choiceExplanations.Economically unfeasible: Economic feasibility cannot be inferred directly as unfeasible when only positive financial indicators are provided.
choiceExplanations.Financially feasible: Correct — The project is financially feasible because NPV is positive (P36M), BCR exceeds 1 (1.23), and IRR (16.28%) surpasses the 10% hurdle rate.
choiceExplanations.Marginally feasible: An IRR of 16.28% well above 10% and BCR of 1.23 indicate solid rather than marginal feasibility.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: As part of feasibility study preparation, you need to find the discounted revenue of a 3-year fishery project. It has the following benefits for years 0, 1, 2 and 3 in million Php: 0, 6, 8 and 9, respectively. What is its present value of benefits? Discount plus inflation rate is stable at 10%.

choiceExplanations.Php 20.34M: Php 20.34M overstates the discounted sum of Php 6M, Php 8M, and Php 9M at 10%.
choiceExplanations.Php 17.32M: Php 17.32M underestimates the present value of benefits discounted at 10% over years 1 to 3.
choiceExplanations.Php 18.83M: Correct — Discounting future benefits at 10% gives 0 + 6/1.1 + 8/1.1^2 + 9/1.1^3 = Php 18.83M.
choiceExplanations.Php 15.06M: Php 15.06M corresponds to a higher discount rate than the specified 10%.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Monetary measure of the market value of final products within the country

choiceExplanations.GNP - gross national product: GNP measures total output produced by a country's residents and nationals regardless of geographic location.
choiceExplanations.GDP - gross domestic product: Correct — Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the monetary measure of the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders.
choiceExplanations.NDP - net domestic product: NDP equals GDP minus capital depreciation (consumption of fixed capital).
choiceExplanations.NNP - net national product: NNP equals GNP minus capital depreciation.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: an estimate of the total value of all goods and services produced by a country in a given period

choiceExplanations.CPI - consumer price index: CPI measures changes in the price level of a representative basket of consumer goods and services.
choiceExplanations.GDP - gross domestic product: GDP measures final goods and services produced strictly within domestic borders rather than by all national residents.
choiceExplanations.GNP - gross national product: Correct — Gross National Product (GNP) estimates the total value of all goods and services produced by a country's residents and businesses in a given period.
choiceExplanations.NNP - net national product: NNP subtracts depreciation from GNP rather than reporting gross output.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: ILLUMINATION: Equal intensity of light producing no shadow

choiceExplanations.Perfect diffusion: Correct — Perfect diffusion scatters light uniformly in all directions with equal intensity, eliminating harsh shadows.
choiceExplanations.Directional lighting: Directional lighting projects light predominantly from one angle, creating distinct highlights and sharp shadows.
choiceExplanations.Partial diffusion: Partial diffusion mixes diffused and directional light, still producing soft shadows.
choiceExplanations.Specular reflection: Specular reflection is mirror-like reflection where incident light bounces off a smooth surface at one angle.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Price elasticity of demand where a change in price does not lead to a change in demand.

choiceExplanations.Unitary elastic: Unitary elastic demand changes quantity demanded by the exact same percentage as price.
choiceExplanations.Perfectly elastic: Perfectly elastic demand exhibits infinite sensitivity, where any price increase drops demand to zero.
choiceExplanations.Perfectly inelastic: Correct — Perfectly inelastic demand has zero price elasticity, so quantity demanded remains completely unchanged regardless of price changes.
choiceExplanations.Relatively inelastic: Relatively inelastic demand still changes slightly when price changes, just proportionally less than price.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: diffusion in which flux is uniformly scattered in accordance with Lambert’s cosine law.

choiceExplanations.Incomplete diffusion: Partial scattering where luminous intensity varies with viewing angle rather than following Lambert's cosine law uniformly.
choiceExplanations.Specular reflection: Mirror-like reflection where the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence without uniform scattering.
choiceExplanations.Perfect diffusion: Correct — perfect diffusion scatters luminous flux uniformly in all directions according to Lambert's cosine law.
choiceExplanations.Mixed reflection: Combination of specular and diffuse reflection that produces directional highlights rather than uniform Lambertian scattering.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: It is an equal intensity of light crashing from all directions producing no shadows

choiceExplanations.Specular reflection: Mirror-like reflection from smooth surfaces that directs light along one angle and creates sharp shadows.
choiceExplanations.Perfect diffusion: Correct — perfect diffusion provides equal luminous intensity from all directions, eliminating harsh shadows.
choiceExplanations.Partial diffusion: Incomplete scattering of light that still retains directional bias and casts soft or partial shadows.
choiceExplanations.Direct illumination: Light traveling straight from a luminaire to a surface, creating strong directional brightness and distinct shadows.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: It is another term for delayed payment

choiceExplanations.Deferred annuity: Correct — a deferred annuity is a series of equal payments starting after an initial delay period.
choiceExplanations.Ordinary annuity: Equal periodic payments made at the end of each period starting immediately in the first period.
choiceExplanations.Perpetual annuity: A perpetuity whose equal periodic payments continue indefinitely without a scheduled end date.
choiceExplanations.Annuity due: Equal periodic payments made at the beginning of each period rather than after a delay.

items.question: Which Republic Act covers the institutionalization of Agricultural Engineer (AE) positions in the local government?
items.rationale: Republic Act No. 8559 (Philippine Agricultural Engineering Act of 1998) governed the practice and institutional recognition of Agricultural Engineer (AE) positions in government units prior to its repeal by RA 10915.

choiceExplanations.RA 8435: The Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Act (AFMA) of 1997, focused on agricultural modernization and competitiveness.
choiceExplanations.RA 7160: The Local Government Code of 1991, establishing general LGU powers without institutionalizing specific AE positions.
choiceExplanations.RA 10601: The Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization Law of 2013, which later required ABE divisions in LGUs.
choiceExplanations.RA 8559: Correct — RA 8559 (Philippine Agricultural Engineering Act of 1998) mandated AE positions in local governments.

items.question: Law that states / Pv=RT

choiceExplanations.Ideal Gas Law: Correct — the Ideal Gas Law relates pressure, specific volume, and absolute temperature as Pv = RT.
choiceExplanations.Charles’s Law: States that gas volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature at constant pressure (V/T = constant).
choiceExplanations.Boyle’s Law: States that gas pressure is inversely proportional to volume at constant temperature (PV = constant).
choiceExplanations.Combined Gas Law: Relates pressure, volume, and temperature between states (P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2) without specifying the gas constant R.

items.question: National Building Code: How many percent is the window in a certain room.

choiceExplanations.12%: Exceeds the 10% minimum window opening area required under PD 1096 for habitable rooms.
choiceExplanations.8%: Falls below the minimum 10% floor-area window opening requirement under the National Building Code.
choiceExplanations.14%: Exceeds the statutory 10% minimum window-to-floor area ratio specified in the National Building Code.
choiceExplanations.10%: Correct — Section 808 of PD 1096 requires habitable rooms to have windows totaling at least 10% of floor area.

items.question: the law of supply and demand defines that
items.answer: Under conditions of perfect competition the price at which a given product will be supplied and purchased is the price that will result in the supply and the demand being equal
choices: Under conditions of imperfect competition the cost of production directly determines the price without considering demand
Under conditions of perfect competition the price at which a given product is sold remains fixed regardless of consumer demand
Under conditions of pure monopoly the quantity supplied always exceeds the quantity demanded at the equilibrium market price
Under conditions of perfect competition the price at which a given product will be supplied and purchased is the price that will result in the supply and the demand being equal

choiceExplanations.Under conditions of imperfect competitio: Incorrect because competitive market prices depend on both supply and demand, not production cost alone.
choiceExplanations.Under conditions of perfect competition: Incorrect because competitive market prices adjust dynamically with shifts in consumer demand rather than staying fixed.
choiceExplanations.Under conditions of pure monopoly the qu: Incorrect because equilibrium occurs where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded, not under persistent surplus in a monopoly.
choiceExplanations.Under conditions of perfect competition: Correct — under perfect competition, equilibrium market price is established where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded.

items.question: Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization Law

choiceExplanations.RA 10601: Correct — RA 10601 is the Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization (AFMech) Law of 2013.
choiceExplanations.RA 11449: Does not designate the AFMech Law; agricultural and fisheries mechanization is governed by RA 10601.
choiceExplanations.RA 12933: Not the AFMech Law; agricultural and fisheries mechanization in the Philippines is enacted under RA 10601.

items.question: A 24-volt battery of a boom sprayer needs to be charged on field using 6-volt solar modules with 2 modules in parallel to speed up charging. How many solar modules are required?
items.rationale:
Given: Battery voltage = 24 V; Solar module voltage = 6 V; Parallel strings = 2.
Modules in series = V_battery / V_module = 24 V / 6 V = 4 modules.
Total modules = Series modules × Parallel strings = 4 × 2 = 8 modules (Eight).

items.question: What is the actual horsepower of a tractor needed to do 149.2 kW-hrs of work in 2 hours?
items.rationale:
Given: Work (W) = 149.2 kW-hr; Time (t) = 2 hr.
Power (P) = W / t = 149.2 kW-hr / 2 hr = 74.6 kW.
Convert to hp (1 hp = 0.746 kW): P = 74.6 kW / 0.746 kW/hp = 100 hp.

items.question: A 24-volt battery of a pineapple harvesting conveyor needs to be charged on field using 12-volt solar modules. What is the minimum number of solar modules required?
items.rationale:
Given: Battery voltage = 24 V; Solar module voltage = 12 V.
Minimum modules in series = V_battery / V_module = 24 V / 12 V = 2 modules (Two).

items.question: You plan to innovate a 48-volt battery of a solar-powered small equipment transport vehicle which uses 12-volt solar modules. What is the minimum number of solar modules required to effect charging of its battery?
items.rationale:
Given: Battery voltage = 48 V; Solar module voltage = 12 V.
Minimum modules in series = V_battery / V_module = 48 V / 12 V = 4 modules (Four).

items.question: A new tractor brand is being tested. The tachometer placed at the Power Take-Off (PTO) shaft recorded an average rotational speed of 1,700 RPM. The indicated engine power of 100 hp was found to be true. What likelihood value of torque was likely recorded at the PTO shaft?
items.rationale:
Given: Power (P) = 100 hp; Rotational speed (N) = 1,700 RPM.
Formula: T = (5,252 × P) / N
T = (5,252 × 100 hp) / 1,700 RPM = 308.94 ft-lbs ≈ 309 ft-lbs.

items.question: You need to purchase a tractor. Results of your calculation indicate that the PTO power needed for the routinary task intended for the tractor is 54 kW. What should be the minimum engine power in hp? Consider that the continuous work of the tractor at the PTO shaft should not exceed 78% of the engine power.
items.rationale:
Given: Required PTO power = 54 kW; Maximum continuous PTO ratio = 78% (0.78).
Engine power (kW) = 54 kW / 0.78 = 69.23 kW.
Convert to hp: 69.23 kW / 0.746 kW/hp = 92.80 hp.
Rounding up to the nearest standard rating that satisfies the minimum requirement gives 95 hp.

items.question: The testing instrument at the tractor Power Take-Off (PTO) shaft registers 1,700 RPM and 310 ft-lbs torque. Determine the PTO power.
items.rationale:
Given: Rotational speed (N) = 1,700 RPM; Torque (T) = 310 ft-lbs.
Formula: P = (T × N) / 5,252
P = (310 × 1,700) / 5,252 = 100.34 hp ≈ 100 hp.

items.question: In a PTO power test, the drawbar power of a 2-wheel drive tractor was found to be 29 kW when harrowing on a plowed field. The drawbar to PTO power conversion factor of a 2-wheel drive tractor working in a previously tilled surface is estimated at 0.67. What is the result of the PTO power test?
items.rationale:
Given: Drawbar power (P_DB) = 29 kW; Drawbar-to-PTO conversion factor = 0.67.
Formula: P_PTO = P_DB / Conversion Factor
P_PTO = 29 kW / 0.67 = 43.28 kW ≈ 43 kW.

items.question: Determine the daily energy output of a 24-volt DC solar pump during a sunny day in Luzon with latitude of 16 degrees north if its overall power output is 750 watt-peak and the daily sensible sunlight in the location is 5 hours. Choose only ONE best answer.
items.rationale:
Given: Power output (P) = 750 Wp = 0.75 kW; Daily sensible sunlight (t) = 5 hours.
Formula: E = P × t
E = 0.75 kW × 5 hr = 3.75 kWh.

items.question: The specific heat of gasoline is 0.53 kcal/(kg °C). If the current temperature of a 1 kg gasoline is 100°C, find the amount of energy needed to further increase it to 110°C. Choose only ONE best answer.
items.rationale:
Given: Specific heat (c) = 0.53 kcal/(kg °C); Mass (m) = 1 kg; ΔT = 110°C − 100°C = 10°C.
Formula: Q = m × c × ΔT
Q = 1 kg × 0.53 kcal/(kg °C) × 10°C = 5.3 kcal.

items.question: A solar water heater installed in Mindanao at latitude of 8 degrees north is used for pre-heating water prior to entry into industrial-size boilers. The heater has a collection area of 3.6 meters × 5 meters, and efficiency of 9%. Estimate its power output during a sunny noon and if you are tasked to carry out the installation, what is its installation tilt angle and north-south orientation.
items.rationale:
Given: Area (A) = 3.6 m × 5 m = 18 m²; Efficiency (η) = 9% = 0.09; Sunny noon solar irradiance (I) = 1,000 W/m² = 1 kW/m²; Latitude = 8° N.
Power output: P = A × I × η = 18 m² × 1 kW/m² × 0.09 = 1.62 kW ≈ 1.6 kW.
Orientation & Tilt: Since the site is in the Northern Hemisphere (8° N), the collector faces south with a practical minimum tilt angle of 10 degrees. Answer = 1.6 kW, 10 degrees facing south.

items.question: A 360-watt power from a 12-volt DC generator is to be used for AC farm machine by using an inverter. What is the power output from the inverter if inversion efficiency is 85%? Choose only ONE best answer.
items.rationale:
Given: Input power (P_in) = 360 watts; Inversion efficiency (η) = 85% = 0.85.
Formula: P_out = P_in × η
P_out = 360 watts × 0.85 = 306 watts.

items.question: An AC generator is rated at a real power of 90 kW with an indicated power factor of 0.82, what is the apparent power of the generator? Choose only ONE best answer.
items.rationale:
Given: Real power (P) = 90 kW; Power factor (pf) = 0.82.
Formula: Apparent power (S) = P / pf
S = 90 kW / 0.82 = 109.76 kVA ≈ 110 kVA.

items.question: Estimate the dependable power output from a windpump having a rotor diameter of 8 meters, average blade twist angle of 45 degrees, and tip speed ratio of 1:1 if the daytime prevailing windspeed in the location is 3 meters/second. Choose only ONE best answer.
items.rationale:
Given: Rotor diameter (D) = 8 m; Wind speed (V) = 3 m/s.
Swept area: A = (π / 4) D² = (π / 4)(8 m)² = 50.27 m² (≈ 50 m²).
Using the standard ABE dependable windpump power formula (P_d = 0.1 × A × V³):
P_d = 0.1 × 50.27 × 3³ = 135.7 W ≈ 135 watts.

items.question: An AC generator is rated at an apparent power of 100 kVA with a power factor of 0.8, what is the real power of the generator in hp? Choose only ONE best answer.
items.rationale:
Given: Apparent power (S) = 100 kVA; Power factor (pf) = 0.8.
Real power (kW): P = S × pf = 100 kVA × 0.8 = 80 kW.
Convert to hp: P = 80 kW / 0.746 kW/hp = 107.24 hp ≈ 107 hp.

items.question: An AC generator is rated at an apparent power of 100 kVA with a power factor of 0.8, what is the real power of the generator in kW?
items.rationale:
Given: Apparent power (S) = 100 kVA; Power factor (pf) = 0.8.
Formula: Real power (P) = S × pf
P = 100 kVA × 0.8 = 80 kW.

items.question: A picohydro generator is to be used as power source for an analog pressure transmitter sending real-time data on water depth at dam outlet. The pressure transmitter has a voltage of 15 Volts DC and amperage of 20 milliamperes. What minimum power output and voltage of picohydro generator should you request for purchasing?
items.rationale:
Given: Voltage (V) = 15 Vdc; Current (I) = 20 mA.
Formula: P = V × I
P = 15 V × 20 mA = 300 milliwatts (0.3 W) at 15 Vdc.
Answer = 300 milliwatts, 15 Vdc.

items.question: The specific heat of diesel is 0.48 kcal/(kg °C). If the current temperature of a 1 kg diesel is 200°C, find the amount of energy needed to further increase it to 210°C.
items.rationale:
Given: Specific heat (c) = 0.48 kcal/(kg °C); Mass (m) = 1 kg; ΔT = 210°C − 200°C = 10°C.
Formula: Q = m × c × ΔT
Q = 1 kg × 0.48 kcal/(kg °C) × 10°C = 4.8 kcal.

items.question: The wind flows on a 2m-diameter rotor at a rate of 2 m/s. It suddenly flows at 4 m/s, what would be the power output of the windmill?
items.rationale:
Given: V₁ = 2 m/s; V₂ = 4 m/s.
Wind power is proportional to the cube of wind velocity (P ∝ V³).
P₂ / P₁ = (V₂ / V₁)³ = (4 / 2)³ = 2³ = 8 times.

items.question: Determine the rotor speed of a windmill with a wind tip-speed ratio of 1:1 and a wind velocity of 2m/s.
items.rationale:
Given: Tip-speed ratio (TSR) = 1:1 = 1; Wind velocity (V_wind) = 2 m/s.
Formula: TSR = V_tip / V_wind
V_tip = TSR × V_wind = 1 × 2 m/s = 2 m/s (2m/s).

items.question: A diesel engine operating at 2500 rpm will be used to drive an irrigation pump operating at 1000 rpm. The pulley diameter for the pump is 4 inches. What is the recommended size of pulley for the engine?
items.rationale:
Given: N₁ = 2,500 rpm (engine); N₂ = 1,000 rpm (pump); D₂ = 4 in.
Formula: N₁ D₁ = N₂ D₂
D₁ = (N₂ × D₂) / N₁ = (1,000 rpm × 4 in.) / 2,500 rpm = 1.6 in (or use 2 in. standard pulley).

items.question: An irrigation pump is driven by a single cylinder engine. The set-up has the following specifications: engine rpm, 2200; pump rpm, 1800; and diameter of engine pulley, 25 cm. What should be the diameter of the pump pulley?
items.rationale:
Given: N₁ = 2,200 rpm; N₂ = 1,800 rpm; D₁ = 25 cm.
Formula: N₁ D₁ = N₂ D₂
D₂ = (N₁ × D₁) / N₂ = (2,200 rpm × 25 cm) / 1,800 rpm = 30.56 cm (30.55 cm).

items.question: The cylinder of a corn sheller will be driven by a 10-hp diesel engine using V-belt drive. The engine has a speed of 1800 rpm while the corn sheller requires an engine speed of 650 rpm. The effective diameter of the driver pulley is 12 inches. What should be the diameter of the driven pulley?
items.rationale:
Given: N₁ = 1,800 rpm (driver); N₂ = 650 rpm (driven); D₁ = 12 in.
Formula: N₁ D₁ = N₂ D₂
D₂ = (N₁ × D₁) / N₂ = (1,800 rpm × 12 in.) / 650 rpm = 33.23 in. ≈ 33 in.

items.question: A 10-hp diesel engine drives the cylinder of a corn sheller through a V-belt drive at an engine shaft speed of 1,800 rpm. What is the recommended shaft diameter for the engine drive? Assume a design stress of 6,000 psi.
items.rationale:
Given: Design power (P) = 10 hp; Shaft speed (N) = 1,800 rpm; Design stress (S_d) = 6,000 psi.
Torque: T = (63,025 × P) / N = (63,025 × 10) / 1,800 = 350.14 in-lb.
Shaft diameter: D = [16 T / (π S_d)]^(1/3) = [16 × 350.14 / (π × 6,000)]^(1/3) = 0.667 in. ≈ 0.66 in.

items.question: Compute the torque acting on a pulley rotating at 1800 rpm and delivering a power of 10 kW. If the pulley used in transmitting power runs at 1800 rpm has a diameter of 8 in., what is the force transmitted by the belt? Also, compute the actual load applied to the pulley shaft. If 6200 single-row deep-groove ball bearing will be used to drive the pulley, what would be the rating fatigue life of the bearing? What is the rated life in hours of the bearing?
items.rationale:
Given: N = 1,800 rpm; P = 10 kW; Pulley diameter D = 8 in. (r = 4 in. = 101.6 mm); Bearing = 6200 (basic dynamic load rating C = 400 kgf).
1. Torque: M = 974,000 × P / N = 974,000 × 10 / 1,800 = 5,411.1 kgf-mm.
2. Belt force: F = M / r = 5,411.1 / 101.6 = 53.26 kgf.
3. Actual shaft load (V-belt tension factor f_b = 2.25): K = 2.25 × 53.26 = 119.83 kgf.
4. Speed factor: f_n = (33.3 / 1,800)^(1/3) = 0.2645.
5. Fatigue life factor: f_h = f_n × (C / K) = 0.2645 × (400 / 119.83) = 0.883.
6. Rated life in hours: L_h = 500 × f_h³ = 500 × (0.8833)³ ≈ 344.62 hours.

items.question: Recommend a shaft size required for the main transmission shaft of a rice mill prime mover with the following specifications: Engine, Isuzu 8 PA; Hp rated, 225 Hp; and Engine Speed, 3600 rpm. Use 6,000-psi design stress for the shaft. Recommend a square-key size for the calculated shaft. Assume a size of key of ½" square.
items.rationale:
Given: P = 225 hp; N = 3,600 rpm; S_d = 6,000 psi; Square key width (w) = 0.5 in.; Allowable crushing stress (S_c) = 25,000 psi.
Torque: T = (63,025 × 225) / 3,600 = 3,939.06 in-lb.
Shaft diameter: D = [16 × 3,939.06 / (π × 6,000)]^(1/3) = 1.495 in. ≈ 1.5 in. (use 2-in. shaft, radius r = 1 in.).
Tangential force: F = T / r = 3,939.06 / 1 = 3,939 lb.
Required key length: L = F / (w × S_c) = 3,939 / (0.5 × 25,000) = 0.315 in. ≈ 0.32 in.

items.question: A shaft delivers 10 lbs at 10-cm crank radius. What is the torque delivered by the shaft? If the said shaft rotates at 80 rpm, what is the power delivered by the shaft?
items.rationale:
Given: Force (F) = 10 lbs; Crank radius (R) = 10 cm = 10 / 2.54 = 3.937 in.; Speed (N) = 80 rpm.
Torque: T = F × R = 10 lbs × 3.937 in. = 39.37 in-lb (or 45.45 kg-cm).
Power: Hp = (T × N) / 63,025 = (39.37 × 80) / 63,025 = 0.04997 Hp ≈ 0.05 Hp.

items.question: A solid shaft delivers 1000 in-lb torque at 800 rpm rotation, what shaft diameter would you recommend? Recommended design stress is 6,000 psi.
items.rationale:
Given: Torque (T) = 1,000 in-lb; Speed (N) = 800 rpm; Design stress (S_d) = 6,000 psi.
Formula: D = [16 T / (π S_d)]^(1/3)
D = [16 × 1,000 / (π × 6,000)]^(1/3) = 0.947 in. ≈ 0.9 in. (use 1" Ø standard shaft).
Answer = 0.9 in. use 1" Ø.

items.question: Compute the drawbar pull and drawbar horsepower of a 4-bottom moldboard plow on a clay loam soil having an effective width of cut of 0.3 m per bottom and a depth of cut of 0.15 m. The plowing speed is 10 kph. (Soil draft for clay loam soil is assumed at 8 psi).
items.rationale:
Given: Bottoms = 4; Width/bottom = 0.3 m; Depth = 0.15 m; Speed (V) = 10 kph = 2.778 m/s; Specific draft = 8 psi.
Total cross-sectional area: A = 4 × 0.3 m × 0.15 m = 0.18 m² = 279 in².
Drawbar pull (F): F = 8 lb/in² × 279 in² = 2,232 lb = 1,012.4 kgf.
Drawbar horsepower (using 1 hp = 76.2 kgf-m/s): DHP = (1,012.4 kgf × 2.778 m/s) / 76.2 = 36.9 hp.

items.question: What is the drawbar pull required for a 3-meter tractor-drawn offset-disk harrow. The implement specific draft is 89 kg/m. Also compute the drawbar horsepower of the implement if it is running at a speed of 20 kph.
items.rationale:
Given: Width (W) = 3 m; Specific draft = 89 kg/m; Speed (V) = 20 kph = 5.556 m/s.
Drawbar pull (F): F = W × specific draft = 3 m × 89 kg/m = 267 kgf.
Drawbar horsepower (using 1 hp = 76.2 kgf-m/s): DHP = (267 kgf × 5.556 m/s) / 76.2 = 19.47 hp ≈ 19.5 hp.

items.question: A 16-hp rotary tiller is tilling at a depth of 10 cm. Its rotating tiller has a width of 0.5 m. What is the specific power output of the machine if it is traveling at a speed of 0.5 m/sec? Assume a 0.80 power transmission efficiency for the tiller.
items.rationale:
Given: Power input = 16 hp, depth = 10 cm, width = 0.5 m = 50 cm, speed = 0.5 m/sec = 50 cm/sec, transmission efficiency = 0.80.
Formula: SPO = P_out / (W × D × V) = (P_in × η × 746 W/hp) / (W × D × V)
Substitution: SPO = (16 × 0.80 × 746 W) / (50 cm × 10 cm × 50 cm/sec) = 9,548.8 W / 25,000 cm³/sec = 0.382 Watts/cm³.
Answer = 0.382 Watts/cm³

items.question: Compute the drawbar pull of a plow on a power tiller with depth and width of cut of 10 cm × 8 cm. The number of plow bottom is 2. Soil draft is equal to 5 psi. If the plow is drawn at a speed of 10 km/hr, what is the drawbar horsepower of the plow?
items.rationale:
Given: Depth = 10 cm, width = 8 cm, n = 2 bottoms, soil draft = 5 psi, speed V = 10 km/hr.
Formula: A = D × W × n; F = A × Draft; DHP = (F × V) / 76.2 kg-m/sec-hp
Substitution: A = 10 cm × 8 cm × 2 = 160 cm². F = 160 cm² × (5 lb/in²) × (1 in / 2.54 cm)² × (1 kg / 2.2 lb) = 56.36 kg. Using V = 10 km/hr × (1000 m/km) / (3600 sec/hr) ≈ 2.77 m/sec (rounded): DHP = (56.36 kg × 2.77 m/sec) / 76.2 ≈ 2.04 Hp (exact unrounded = 2.05 Hp).
Answer = 2.04 Hp

items.question: Compute the force exerted by the hand tractor cage wheel with 0.8-m wheel diameter. The wheel is drawn by a 10-hp robin engine driving the cage wheel at 30 rpm. The transmission efficiency of the machine is 0.90.
items.rationale:
Given: Diameter D = 0.8 m (radius R = 0.4 m), engine power = 10 hp, wheel speed N = 30 rpm, transmission efficiency η = 0.90.
Formula: Axle power P = P_e × η × 4572 kg-m/min-hp; Tangential speed v = 2πRN = πDN; Force F = P / (2πRN)
Substitution: F = (10 × 0.90 × 4572 kg-m/min) / (2π × 0.4 m × 30 rpm) = 41,148 / 75.398 = 545.74 kg.
Answer = 545.74 kg

items.question: What is the drawbar horsepower of a plow requiring a drawbar pull of 253 kg if the plowing speed is 5 kph?
items.rationale:
Given: From the preceding problem, drawbar pull F = 253 kg; plowing speed V = 5 km/hr.
Formula: DHP = (F × V) / 76.2 kg-m/sec-hp
Substitution: V = 5 km/hr × (1000 m/km) / (3600 sec/hr) = 1.389 m/sec. DHP = (253 kg × 1.389 m/sec) / 76.2 = 4.61 hp ≈ 4.6 hp.
Answer = 4.6 hp

items.question: What is the required drawbar pull for a 5-meter tractor-drawn spike-tooth harrow with a specific draft of 89 kg/m? What is the drawbar horsepower of the implement if it is running at a speed of 6 kph?
items.rationale:
Given: Width W = 5 m, specific draft Ds = 89 kg/m, speed V = 6 km/hr.
Formula: F = Ds × W; DHP = (F × V) / 76.2 kg-m/sec-hp
Substitution: F = 89 kg/m × 5 m = 445 kg. DHP = (445 kg × 6 km/hr × 1000 m/km / 3600 sec/hr) / 76.2 = 741.67 / 76.2 = 9.73 hp ≈ 10 hp.
Answer = 10 hp

items.question: A water pump requires 64.75 hp to operate. If a diesel engine with an efficiency of 80% will be used to drive the pump, what is the recommended horsepower for the engine?
items.rationale:
Given: From Problem 38, pump horsepower PHP ≈ 64.75 hp (rounded to 64.8 hp); diesel engine efficiency η = 80% = 0.80.
Formula: EHP = PHP / η
Substitution: EHP = 64.75 hp / 0.80 = 80.9 hp (64.8 / 0.80 = 81.0 hp).
Answer = 80.9 hp

items.question: A water pump requires 64.75 hp to operate. If a gasoline engine with an efficiency of 70% will be used to drive the pump, what is the power requirement of the engine?
items.rationale:
Given: From Problem 38, pump horsepower PHP ≈ 64.75 hp (rounded to 64.8 hp); gasoline engine efficiency η = 70% = 0.70.
Formula: EHP = PHP / η
Substitution: EHP = 64.75 hp / 0.70 = 92.5 hp.
Answer = 92.5 hp

items.question: A tractor operating at 3.5 mph develops a drawbar pull of 3000 pounds. Estimate the required drawbar horsepower for the tractor.
items.rationale:
Given: Speed V = 3.5 mph, drawbar pull F = 3000 lb.
Formula: DHP = (F × V) / 375 = (F × V × 5280 ft/mi / 60 min/hr) / 33,000 ft-lb/min-hp
Substitution: DHP = (3000 lb × 3.5 mph) / 375 = 28 hp.
Answer = 28 hp

items.question: The specific fuel consumption of a tractor is 0.3 lbs per BHP-hour. If the heating value of the fuel is 19500 BTU/lb, what is the brake thermal efficiency?
items.rationale:
Given: Specific fuel consumption SFC = 0.3 lb/bhp-hr, heating value HV = 19,500 BTU/lb, thermal equivalent of 1 hp-hr = 2545 BTU.
Formula: BTE = [2545 / (SFC × HV)] × 100%
Substitution: BTE = [2545 / (0.3 × 19,500)] × 100% = (2545 / 5850) × 100% = 43.50% ≈ 43.5%.
Answer = 43.5%

items.question: Assume that you are the Agricultural Engineer of a 500-hectare corn farm with soil type that gives 10 psi draft when plowing at a speed of 4 km/hr. Compute the drawbar horsepower required to pull a three-disk plow with effective cut of 12 inches per disk at a plowing depth of 6 inches.
items.rationale:
Given: Draft = 10 psi, speed V = 4 km/hr, n = 3 disks, width per disk = 12 in, depth = 6 in.
Formula: F = n × W × D × Draft; DHP = (F × V) / 76.2 kg-m/sec-hp
Substitution: F = (3 × 12 in × 6 in) × 10 lb/in² = 2160 lb = 2160 / 2.2 = 981.82 kg. V = 4 km/hr × 1000 / 3600 = 1.111 m/sec. DHP = (981.82 kg × 1.111 m/sec) / 76.2 = 14.32 hp ≈ 14.3 hp.
Answer = 14.3 hp

items.question: Still referring to Problem 48, what is the amount of fuel consumed in liters per 16 hours day of one tractor unit if the specific fuel consumption is 1 lb/dhp-hr and the specific gravity of the fuel is 0.8?
items.rationale:
Given: From Problem 48, DHP = 14.3 hp, SFC = 1 lb/dhp-hr, SG = 0.8, operating time t = 16 hours/day, water density = 62.4 lb/ft³.
Formula: Fuel mass rate = SFC × DHP; Fuel volume rate = Mass rate / (SG × 62.4 lb/ft³) × 28.3168 L/ft³; Daily fuel = Volume rate × 16 hr
Substitution: Fuel rate = (1 × 14.3 lb/hr) / (0.8 × 62.4 lb/ft³) = 0.28646 ft³/hr × 28.3168 L/ft³ = 8.112 L/hr. Daily consumption = 8.112 L/hr × 16 hr = 129.79 liters.
Answer = 129.79 liters

items.question: The axle of a power tiller was tested on a Prony-brake dynamometer. The force delivered at 1-m brake arm was 300 kg at a speed of 25 rpm. Determine the torque and the shaft power of the machine. Also, compute the specific fuel consumption of the engine driving the power tiller if it consumes diesel at a rate of 0.9 liters per hour.
items.rationale:
Given: Force F = 300 kg, brake arm L = 1 m, speed N = 25 rpm, diesel consumption Fc = 0.9 L/hr, diesel density ρ = 0.84 kg/L.
Formula: T = F × L; Ps (kW) = (T × N) / 974; SFC = (Fc × ρ × 1000 g/kg) / Ps
Substitution: T = 300 kg × 1 m = 300 kg-m. Ps = (300 × 25) / 974 = 7.700 kW (or 10.32 hp). SFC = (0.9 L/hr × 0.84 kg/L × 1000 g/kg) / 7.700 kW = 756 / 7.700 = 98.18 g/kW-hr.
Answer = 98.18 g/kW-hr

items.question: A pump was installed with a suction head of 6 meter and a discharge head of 10 meters. The discharge rate of the pump is 60 liters per minute. What is the water horsepower of the pump?
items.rationale:
Given: Suction head = 6 m, discharge head = 10 m, discharge rate Q = 60 L/min = 1 L/sec.
Formula: TDH = Hs + Hd; Water Power (kW) = (TDH × Q) / 102; WHP = Water Power (kW) / 0.746 kW/hp
Substitution: TDH = 6 m + 10 m = 16 m. Water Power = (16 m × 1 L/sec) / 102 = 0.1569 kW. WHP = 0.1569 / 0.746 = 0.210 hp.
Answer = 0.210 hp

items.question: A pump, which discharges 4 liters per second at a head of 6 meters, is driven by an electric motor. The input current of the motor is 1.5 amp while the input voltage is 220 volt. What is the overall efficiency of the pump if the motor power factor is 0.98?
items.rationale:
Given: Q = 4 L/sec, TDH = 6 m, I = 1.5 A, V = 220 V, power factor cos φ = 0.98.
Formula: WP (kW) = (TDH × Q) / 102; Input Power IP = (V × I × cos φ) / 1000; η = (WP / IP) × 100%
Substitution: WP = (6 × 4) / 102 = 0.235 kW. IP = (220 × 1.5 × 0.98) / 1000 = 0.3234 kW. η = (0.235 / 0.3234) × 100% = 72.7 %.
Answer = 72.7 %

items.question: At 1200 rpm, a rotary pump is used to deliver milk at a head of 6 meters. The rate of flow of the pump is 0.01 m³/sec. What is the fluid and brake horsepower of the pump shaft if it has an efficiency of 75%. What is the motor horsepower if the transmission and motor efficiencies are 91% and 99%, respectively?
items.rationale:
Given: Q = 0.01 m³/sec, H = 6 m, specific gravity of milk ≈ 1.1 (ρ = 1100 kg/m³), η_p = 0.75, η_t = 0.91, η_m = 0.99.
Formula: FHP = (Q × H × ρ) / 76.2; BHP = FHP / η_p; MHP = BHP / (η_t × η_m)
Substitution: FHP = (0.01 × 6 × 1100) / 76.2 = 0.866 hp ≈ 0.87 hp. BHP = 0.87 / 0.75 = 1.16 hp. MHP = 1.16 / (0.91 × 0.99) = 1.288 hp ≈ 1.29 hp; select the next standard commercial motor size of 1-1/2 hp.
Answer = 1.29 hp therefore use 1 − 1/2 hp motor

items.question: At 1200 rpm, a rotary pump delivers milk at a flow rate of 0.01 m³/sec against a head of 6 meters with a fluid horsepower of 0.87 hp. What will be the flow rate, working head, and power requirement of the pump system if its speed is increased to 2100 rpm?
items.rationale:
Given: From the preceding pump system, N1 = 1200 rpm, Q1 = 0.01 m³/sec, H1 = 6 m, FHP1 = 0.87 hp, N2 = 2100 rpm.
Formula: Pump affinity laws: Q2 = Q1(N2/N1); H2 = H1(N2/N1)²; HP2 = HP1(N2/N1)³
Substitution: Q2 = 0.01 × (2100/1200) = 0.0175 m³/sec; H2 = 6 × (2100/1200)² = 18.38 m; HP2 = 0.87 × (2100/1200)³ = 0.87 × 5.359 = 4.66 hp.
Answer = 4.66 hp

items.question: Compute the amount of power that can be developed by a 600-kg draft animal pulling an 80-kg load at a speed of 0.9 m/sec.
items.rationale:
Given: Draft load F = 80 kg, speed V = 0.9 m/sec, metric conversion 1 hp = 75 kg-m/sec.
Formula: P = F × V; HP = P / 75
Substitution: P = 80 kg × 0.9 m/sec = 72 kg-m/sec. HP = 72 / 75 = 0.96 hp.
Answer = 72 kg-m/sec or 0.96 hp

items.question: Suppose a 4-cylinder engine has a bore of 3.5 in. and a stroke of 4.0 in, what is the piston displacement of the engine?
items.rationale:
Given: Number of cylinders n = 4, bore D = 3.5 in, stroke L = 4.0 in.
Formula: PD = (π/4) × D² × L × n
Substitution: PD = (π/4) × (3.5 in)² × 4.0 in × 4 = 153.94 in³ ≈ 153.9 in³.
Answer = 153.9 in³

items.question: Calculate the indicated horsepower of a six-cylinder engine, 4" bore and 4" stroke, 1500 rpm, 80 psi mean effective pressure.
items.rationale:
Given: n = 6 cylinders, bore D = 4 in, stroke L = 4 in = 4/12 ft, N = 1500 rpm, MEP P = 80 psi (assuming 4-stroke cycle, power strokes per rev = N/2).
Formula: A = (π/4) × D²; IHP = (P × L × A × N × n) / (33,000 × 2)
Substitution: A = (π/4) × 4² = 12.566 in². IHP = [80 × (4/12) × 12.566 × 1500 × 6] / (33,000 × 2) = 3,015,929 / 66,000 = 45.70 hp.
Answer = 45.70 hp

items.question: Suppose an engine has a piston displacement of 38.4 in³. If the clearance volume of the cylinder in 2.5 in³, what is its compression ratio?
items.rationale:
Given: Piston displacement PD = 38.4 in³, clearance volume CV = 2.5 in³.
Formula: CR = (PD + CV) / CV
Substitution: CR = (38.4 + 2.5) / 2.5 = 40.9 / 2.5 = 16.36 ≈ 16.4.
Answer = 16.4

items.question: Calculate the BHP of a 4-cylinder, 2-stroke cycle internal combustion engine with 4" diameter and 5" stroke piston. The mean effective pressure is 102 psi and the number of explosion per minute is 6600. The mechanical efficiency of the engine is 80 percent.
items.rationale:
Given: n = 4 cylinders, 2-stroke cycle (1 explosion/rev/cyl), D = 4 in, L = 5 in = 5/12 ft, P = 102 psi, total explosions/min = N × n = 6600 (so N = 1650 rpm), mechanical efficiency η_m = 0.80.
Formula: A = (π/4) × D²; IHP = (P × L × A × N × n) / 33,000; BHP = IHP × η_m
Substitution: A = (π/4) × 4² = 12.5664 in². IHP = [102 × (5/12) × 12.5664 × 6600] / 33,000 = 106.814 Hp. BHP = 106.814 × 0.80 = 85.45 Hp.
Answer = 85.45 Hp

items.question: The indicated power of an engine is 69 horsepower. The brake horsepower is 54. What is the mechanical or engine efficiency?
items.rationale:
Given: IHP = 69 hp, BHP = 54 hp.
Formula: Mechanical Efficiency = (BHP / IHP) × 100%
Substitution: Mechanical Efficiency = (54 / 69) × 100% = 78.26%.
Answer = 78.26%

items.question: A person is working for 4 hours in a farm harvesting. Estimate the power that can be generated by the person in doing the job.
items.rationale:
Given: Working duration t = 4 hours = 240 min.
Formula: Human power Pg = 0.35 − 0.092 log₁₀(t_min)
Substitution: Pg = 0.35 − 0.092 log₁₀(240) = 0.35 − 0.092(2.3802) = 0.131 hp ≈ 0.13 hp.
Answer = 0.13 hp

items.question: Two persons are doing the threshing operation by “Hampasan” method. What is the total human power generated by the two persons in one day if they work an average of 6 hours?
items.rationale:
Given: Number of persons = 2, working duration t = 6 hours = 360 min.
Formula: Pg = 0.35 − 0.092 log₁₀(t_min); Total power = Pg × number of persons
Substitution: Pg = 0.35 − 0.092 log₁₀(360) = 0.35 − 0.235 = 0.1148 hp/person ≈ 0.11 hp/person. Total power = 0.11 hp/person × 2 = 0.22 hp.
Answer = 0.22 hp

items.question: An engine was tested on a brake dynamometer at a speed of 2000 rpm. The brake arm of the machine is 1.2 meters and it registers a load of 5 kg. What is the shaft power of the engine?
items.rationale:
Given: Engine speed N = 2000 rpm, brake arm L = 1.2 m, load F = 5 kg.
Formula: T = F × L; Ps (kW) = (T × N) / 974; Ps (hp) = Ps (kW) / 0.746
Substitution: T = 5 kg × 1.2 m = 6.0 kg-m. Ps = (6.0 × 2000) / 974 = 12.320 kW. Ps (hp) = 12.320 / 0.746 = 16.51 hp.
Answer = 16.51 hp

items.question: The engine fuel tank was completely filled with gasoline before testing. After 4 hours of continuous test, 3.7 liters of fuel was used to reload the tank completely. Test has shown that the engine shaft power was 10 hp. What is the specific fuel consumption of the engine?
items.rationale:
Given: Time t = 4 hr, fuel consumed = 3.7 L, gasoline density ≈ 0.743 kg/L, shaft power Ps = 10 hp = 7.46 kW.
Formula: SFC = (Fuel volume × ρ × 1000 g/kg) / (t × Ps_kW)
Substitution: SFC = (3.7 L × 0.743 kg/L × 1000 g/kg) / (4 hr × 10 hp × 0.746 kW/hp) = 2749.1 g / 29.84 kW-hr = 92.13 g/kW-hr.
Answer = 92.13 g/kW-hr

items.question: A spark ignition engine was tested with BHP output of 9.6 horsepower. If the ambient condition during the test is 30°C ambient air temperature, what is the corrected BHP of the engine? The total atmospheric air condition is 1011 mbar.
items.rationale:
Given: Measured BHP = 9.6 hp, ambient temp T = 30°C, atmospheric pressure Pb = 1011 mbar.
Formula: Correction factor Kg = (1013 / Pb) × [(T + 273) / 293]^0.5; Corrected BHP = BHP × Kg
Substitution: Kg = (1013 / 1011) × [(30 + 273) / 293]^0.5 = 1.00198 × 1.01692 = 1.0189. Corrected BHP = 9.6 hp × 1.0189 = 9.78 hp.
Answer = 9.78 hp

items.question: A four-stroke naturally-aspirated diesel engine was tested on a prony brake dynamometer and gave a BHP output of 14.2 horsepower. During the test, the ambient air temperature was 27°C while the total atmospheric pressure was 1020 mb. What is the corrected brake horsepower of the engine?
items.rationale:
Given: Measured BHP = 14.2 hp, ambient temp T = 27°C, atmospheric pressure Pb = 1020 mb.
Formula: Correction factor Kd = (1013 / Pb)^0.65 × [(T + 273) / 293]^0.5; Corrected BHP = BHP × Kd
Substitution: Kd = (1013 / 1020)^0.65 × [(27 + 273) / 293]^0.5 = 0.9955 × 1.0119 = 1.0073. Corrected BHP = 14.2 hp × 1.0073 = 14.303 hp.
Answer = 14.303 hp

items.question: Compute the power that can be generated by a hydro-turbine with water input of 40 lps with a head of 20 m. The turbine efficiency is 70%.
items.rationale:
Given: Q = 40 L/sec = 0.04 m³/sec, head H = 20 m, efficiency η = 0.70, γ = 9810 N/m³.
Formula: P = γ × Q × H × η
Substitution: P = 9810 N/m³ × 0.04 m³/sec × 20 m × 0.70 = 5493.6 W ≈ 5494 watts or 5.5 kW.
Answer = 5494 watts or 5.5 kW

items.question: A hydro site offers a head of 50 m and a flow of 1.2 m³/s. With an alternator speed requirement of 1500 rpm in a direct-drive transmission, compute the specific speed of the turbine for the system. Assume a turbine efficiency of 70%.
items.rationale:
Given: Head H = 50 m, flow Q = 1.2 m³/s, speed N = 1500 rpm, turbine efficiency η = 0.70.
Formula: Po (kW) = η × 9810 × Q × H / 1000; Specific speed Ns = (N × √Po) / H^1.25
Substitution: Po = (0.70 × 9810 × 1.2 × 50) / 1000 = 412.02 kW ≈ 412 kW. Ns = (1500 × √412) / 50^1.25 = 30,446.7 / 132.96 = 229.0 ≈ 230.
Answer = 230

items.question: A wood charcoal stove consumes 0.5 kg of fuel per hour. If 95% is volatile matter, what is the design power of the stove? Assume a 6000 kcal/kg heating value for wood charcoal.
items.rationale: Given: FCR = 0.5 kg/hr, volatile matter fraction (VM) = 0.95, HV = 6000 kcal/kg. Formula: P_des = 0.7 * (1 + VM) * (FCR * HV) = 0.7 * (1 + 0.95) * (0.5 kg/hr * 6000 kcal/kg) = 0.7 * 1.95 * 3000 = 4095 kcal/hr. Answer = 4095 kcal/hr.

items.question: Compute the average power output of a stove with a fuel consumption rate of 5 kg of rice hull in 4 hours operation. The net calorific value of rice hull is 3000 kcal/kg.
items.rationale: Given: W_f = 5 kg, t = 4 hr, HV_net = 3000 kcal/kg. Formula: P_av = (W_f * HV_net) / t = (5 kg * 3000 kcal/kg) / 4 hr = 15000 / 4 = 3750 kcal/hr. Answer = 3750 kcal/hr.

items.question: What is the probable height of the flame in a step-grate stove with a power output of 1000 BTU/hr?
items.rationale: Given: P = 1000 BTU/hr = 1000 / 3414.43 = 0.2929 kW; for a step-grate (with-grate) stove, C_f = 75 mm/kW^0.4. Formula: h_f = C_f * P^(2/5) = 75 * (0.2929)^0.4 = 45.89 mm ≈ 45.9 mm. Answer = 45.9 mm.

items.question: Five hundred hectares of farm is to be plowed using 5-bottom moldboard plow. The cutting width of each plow bottom is 20 cm with a cutting depth of 15 cm. If three (3) tractors are pulling a plow at an average speed of 15 kph, how many days does the whole area be finished? Assume a plowing efficiency of 85% and a plowing operation per day of 6 hours. Also, compute the drawbar hp of the plow if the specific draft of soil is equal to 12 psi.
items.rationale: Given: Area = 500 ha, 5 bottoms at 20 cm width and 15 cm depth, 3 tractors, S = 15 kph, efficiency = 85%, 6 hr/day, specific draft = 12 psi. Part 1 (Days): Total width W = 5 * 0.20 m = 1.0 m; C_t = 0.1 * 1.0 * 15 = 1.5 ha/hr; C_e = 0.85 * 1.5 = 1.275 ha/hr per tractor; daily capacity for 3 tractors = 3 * 1.275 * 6 = 22.95 ha/day; Days = 500 / 22.95 = 21.8 days. Part 2 (Drawbar hp): Cross-sectional area A = 5 * 20 cm * 15 cm = 1500 cm² = 1500 / (2.54)^2 = 232.50 in². Draft force F = 232.50 in² * 12 psi = 2790 lb = 1268.18 kgf (at 2.2 lb/kg). Speed v = 15 kph = 4.1667 m/s. Formula: DHP = (F * v) / 76.2 = (1268.18 * 4.1667) / 76.2 = 69.34 hp ≈ 69.3 hp. Answer = 69.3 hp.

items.question: A tractor, shown at the right, has the following engine specifications: number of cylinders, 6; cylinder bore, 0.15 m; piston stroke, 0.20 m; engine speed, 2200 rpm; mean effective pressure, 180 psi; and number of stroke, 4. What is the indicated horsepower and brake horsepower of the engine, assuming an engine efficiency of 80%? What is the estimated PTO power, wheel axle power, and drawbar power of the tractor if its transmission efficiencies are 90%, 92%, and 81%, respectively.

During transport, a 3,500-kg tractor passes through an earth road at a speed of 15 kph. The rated brake power of the tractor is 125 horsepower while the transmission efficiency from the engine to the wheel axle is 80%. If the 2-m rear diameter wheel of the tractor, at 100 meter distance, can only rotate 11 revolutions during operation, determine the following: (1) percentage slip of the tractor wheel; (2) drawbar horsepower of the tractor; and (3) tractive efficiency of the tractor wheel.
items.rationale: Given: W = 3500 kg, V = 15 kph = 4.1667 m/s, BHP = 125 hp, trans eff = 80%, D = 2 m, D_a = 100 m, n = 11 rev, earth road C_rr = 0.07. (1) Theoretical distance D_t = pi * 2 * 11 = 69.115 m; Slip = (100 - 69.115) / 69.115 * 100% = 44.7%. (2) WAP = 125 * 0.80 = 100 hp; Slip loss P_s = 0.447 * 100 = 44.7 hp; Rolling resistance R = 0.07 * 3500 = 245 kgf; Rolling resistance loss P_rr = (245 * 4.1667) / 76.2 = 13.40 hp; DBP = 100 - 44.70 - 13.40 = 41.90 hp. (3) Tractive efficiency = (DBP / WAP) * 100% = (41.90 / 100) * 100% = 41.9%. Answer = 41.9%.

items.question: A 15-wheel axle hp tractor is running at a speed of 10 kph during harrowing in a deep mud soil. The tractor weighs 1500 kg. The wheel diameter of the tractor is 2 meters and is able to rotate at 14 revolutions in 100 meter distance. What is the speed of the tractor wheel in revolution per minute? What are the power losses of the tractor by wheel slip and rolling resistances?
items.rationale: Given: WAP = 15 hp, V = 10 kph = 166.67 m/min = 2.7778 m/s, W = 1500 kg, D = 2 m, 14 rev in 100 m, deep mud soil C_rr = 0.25. Wheel speed = 14 rev/100 m * 166.67 m/min = 23.3 rpm. Slip = (100 - pi * 2 * 14) / (pi * 2 * 14) * 100% = 13.68%, so slip power loss P_s = 15 * 0.1368 = 2.05 hp. Rolling resistance R = C_rr * W = 0.25 * 1500 = 375 kgf; rolling resistance power loss P_rr = (375 * 2.7778) / 76.2 = 13.67 hp ≈ 13.7 hp. Answer = 13.7 hp.

items.question: What is the wheel axle power of a four-wheel tractor whose engine power is equal to 150 Hp. The mechanical efficiency is 85%.
items.rationale: Given: Engine power P_e = 150 hp, mechanical efficiency eta_m = 85% = 0.85. Formula: P_w = eta_m * P_e = 0.85 * 150 hp = 127.5 hp. Answer = 127.5 hp.

items.question: What is the wheel axle torque of a four-wheel tractor with an engine power of 150 hp and a mechanical efficiency of 85% (wheel axle power of 127.5 hp or 95.115 kW) if its wheel rotates at 40 rpm?
items.rationale: Continuation of the preceding problem (P_w = 127.5 hp = 127.5 * 0.746 = 95.115 kW) with wheel speed N = 40 rpm = 40/60 rps. Formula: T = (1000 * P_w * 60) / (2 * pi * N) = (1000 * 95.115 * 60) / (2 * pi * 40) = 5,706,900 / 251.3274 = 22,707.03 N-m. Answer = 22,707.03 N-m.

items.question: An axial-flow biomass shredder is equipped with a 5-inch diameter double-groove V-belt at its cylinder axle. The engine used to drive the machine is rated at 2400 rpm at an optimum engine throttle opening. If the engine pulley is 4 inches, what is the speed of the shredder axle? What is the speed ratio of the engine and the shredder pulleys?
items.rationale: Given: D_1 (shredder) = 5 in, D_2 (engine) = 4 in, N_2 = 2400 rpm. Formula: N_1 * D_1 = N_2 * D_2 => N_1 = (2400 * 4) / 5 = 1920 rpm. Speed ratio N_r = N_2 / N_1 = 2400 / 1920 = 1.25. Answer = 1.25.

items.question: Design a water pump system required to supply water to 10,000 heads of broiler in a poultry farm. The source of water is 20 ft below the ground and is required to be elevated to 30-ft high into a water tank. The specific water requirement of the broiler is 0.025 m³/day-head. Assume a 20% friction head load from the suction and discharge head loss. Pump operating time is 20 hrs per day.
items.answer: 1.84 hp or use 2 hp electric motor
items.rationale: Given: 10,000 broilers, SWR = 0.025 m³/day-head, t = 20 hr/day, H_s = 20 ft, H_d = 30 ft, friction loss = 20%. Flow rate Q = (0.025 * 10,000) / 20 = 12.5 m³/hr = 0.003472 m³/s. Total head H = (20 + 30) * 1.20 = 60 ft = 18.288 m. WHP = (1000 * 9.8 * 0.003472 * 18.288) / 746 = 0.834 hp (≈ 0.83 hp). Assuming pump efficiency = 60% and motor/drive efficiency = 75%: Motor HP = 0.83 / (0.60 * 0.75) = 1.84 hp, so use a 2 hp electric motor. Answer = 1.84 hp or use 2 hp electric motor.
choices: 2.10 hp or use 3 hp electric motor
1.66 hp or use 2 hp electric motor
1.84 hp or use 2 hp electric motor
1.56 hp or use 2 hp electric motor

items.question: Design a water pump system required to supply water to a 5-hectare rice farm. The source of water is from a river 10 feet below, and discharges water 2 ft above the ground surface. Consider 25% friction head from the suction and from the discharge head of the piping system. Assume a crop requirement for rice of 10 mm/day and losses due to percolation and seepage of 2 mm/day. Conveyance losses is 10% of the irrigation requirement. Assume a 60% pump efficiency, an 80% transmission efficiency, and an 80% engine efficiency. Operating time per day is 8 hrs.
items.rationale: Given: Area = 5 ha = 50,000 m², H_s = 10 ft, H_d = 2 ft, H_f = 25%, CWR = 10 mm/day, P&S = 2 mm/day, conveyance loss = 10%, t = 8 hr/day, eta_p = 0.60, eta_t = 0.80, eta_e = 0.80. Irrigation requirement = (10 + 2)/1000 * 50,000 = 600 m³/day; with 10% conveyance loss, Q_day = 660 m³/day; Q = 660 / (8 * 3600) = 0.0229 m³/s. Total head H = (10 + 2) * 1.25 = 15 ft = 4.57 m. WHP = (1000 * 9.8 * 0.0229 * 4.57) / 746 = 1.375 hp; BHP = 1.375 / 0.60 = 2.29 hp; Engine HP = 2.29 / (0.80 * 0.80) ≈ 3.5 hp (standard PRC rounding), so use a 5 hp engine. Answer = 3.5 hp use 5 hp engine.

items.question: What is the wind power of a windpump having 5 meter diameter rotor at a wind speed of 4 m/sec?
items.rationale: Given: D = 5 m, V = 4 m/s, air density rho = 1.2 kg/m³. Rotor swept area A_r = pi * D² / 4 = 3.14 * 25 / 4 = 19.625 m². Formula: P_w = 0.5 * rho * A_r * V³ = 0.5 * 1.2 * 19.625 * 4³ = 753.6 watts. Answer = 753.6 watts.

items.question: What is the power of the rotor if the 3-meter windpump operates at 3 mps wind speed? Assume a power coefficient for the windpump rotor of 0.4.
items.rationale: Given: D = 3 m, V = 3 m/s, C_p = 0.4, air density rho = 1.2 kg/m³. Swept area A_r = pi * (3)² / 4 = 7.0686 m². Formula: P_r = C_p * 0.5 * rho * A_r * V³ = 0.4 * 0.5 * 1.2 * 7.0686 * 3³ = 45.80 watts ≈ 45.8 watts. Answer = 45.8 watts.

items.question: What is the rotor speed of a windpump having a rotor diameter of 4 m at a design speed of 3 m/s? The rotor will contain 12 blades with expected TSR of 2.
items.rationale: Given: D = 4 m, V_w = 3 m/s, TSR = 2. Formula: N_r = (TSR * V_w) / (pi * D) = (2 * 3) / (pi * 4) = 0.4775 rps. Converting to rpm: 0.4775 rps * 60 s/min = 28.65 rpm ≈ 28.7 rpm. Answer = 28.7 rpm.

items.question: What is the hydraulic power required by a windpump to deliver water at a rate of 15 m³/day with a head of 10 meters? Assume a 10 hours water pumping per day.
