items.rationale: Given: Daily discharge = 15 m³/day, pumping time = 10 hr/day, H = 10 m, rho = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s². Flow rate Q = 15 / (10 * 3600) = 0.0004167 m³/s. Formula: P_h = rho * g * H * Q = 1000 * 9.8 * 10 * 0.0004167 = 40.83 watts ≈ 40.8 watts. Answer = 40.8 watts.

items.question: A 15-wheel axle-hp tractor harrowing a deep mud soil is running at a speed of 10 kph. The tractor weighs 1500 kg. The wheel diameter of the tractor is 2 meters and is able to rotate at 14 revolutions in 100 meter distance. What is the speed of the tractor wheel in revolution per minute? What are the power losses of the tractor in terms of wheel slip and rolling resistances?
items.rationale: Given: WAP = 15 hp, V = 10 kph = 166.67 m/min = 2.7778 m/s, W = 1500 kg, D = 2 m, 14 rev in 100 m, deep mud soil C_rr = 0.25. Wheel speed = 14 rev/100 m * 166.67 m/min = 23.3 rpm. Slip = (100 - pi * 2 * 14) / (pi * 2 * 14) * 100% = 13.68%, so slip power loss P_s = 15 * 0.1368 = 2.05 hp. Rolling resistance R = C_rr * W = 0.25 * 1500 = 375 kgf; rolling resistance power loss P_rr = (375 * 2.7778) / 76.2 = 13.67 hp ≈ 13.7 hp. Answer = 13.7 hp.

items.question: Two persons are threshing by “Hampasan” method. What is the total human power generated by the two persons in one day if they work at an average of 6 hours?
items.rationale: Given: n = 2 persons, t = 6 hours = 360 min. Formula (human power): P_g = 0.35 - 0.092 * log10(t_min) = 0.35 - 0.092 * log10(360) = 0.35 - 0.235 = 0.11 hp/person (rounded). Total power for 2 persons = 2 * 0.11 hp = 0.22 hp. Answer = 0.22 hp.

items.question: A 16-hp rotary tiller is tilling at a depth of 10 cm. Its rotating tiller has a width of 0.5 m. What is the specific power output of the machine if it is traveling at a speed of 0.5 m/sec? Assume a power transmission efficiency for the tiller of 0.80.
items.rationale: Given: P_in = 16 hp, eta = 0.80, d = 10 cm, w = 0.5 m = 50 cm, v = 0.5 m/s = 50 cm/s. Output power P_out = 16 hp * 0.80 * 746 W/hp = 9548.8 W. Soil volume rate = w * d * v = 50 cm * 10 cm * 50 cm/s = 25,000 cm³/s. Formula: SPO = P_out / (w * d * v) = 9548.8 / 25,000 = 0.38195 Watts/cm³ ≈ 0.382 Watts/cm³. Answer = 0.382 Watts/cm³.

items.question: A 4 × 6 rubber roller is used as husker for a rice mill. The faster roller is directly driven by an electric motor at a speed of 1720 rpm. What would be the required speed for the faster and slower rollers?
items.rationale: Given: Speed of faster roller N_fast = 1720 rpm. For rubber-roll rice hullers, the slower roller runs at 25% lower speed (speed ratio = 0.75). Formula: N_slow = 0.75 * N_fast = 0.75 * 1720 rpm = 1290 rpm. Answer = 1290 rpm.

items.question: Compute the drawbar pull of plow on a power tiller whose depth and width of cut are equal to 10 cm × 8 cm. The number of plow bottom is 2. Soil draft is equal to 5 psi. If the plow is drawn at a speed of 10 km/hr, what is the drawbar horsepower of the plow?
items.rationale: Given: 2 bottoms, depth = 10 cm, width = 8 cm, specific draft = 5 psi, speed = 10 kph = 2.77 m/s. Total cross-sectional area A = 2 * 10 cm * 8 cm = 160 cm² = 160 / (2.54)^2 = 24.80 in². Drawbar pull F = 24.80 in² * 5 lb/in² = 124.0 lbf = 56.36 kgf (at 2.2 lb/kg). Formula: DHP = (F * v) / 76.2 = (56.36 * 2.77) / 76.2 = 2.048 Hp ≈ 2.04 Hp. Answer = 2.04 Hp.

items.question: A rice husk gas stove has a reactor diameter of 0.15 m. The amount of rice husk that can be loaded in the reactor is 1.20 kg. If the specific gasification rate of the stove is 110 kg/m²-hr, how long does the gasifier will operate producing combustible gases? Assume a gasifier efficiency of 20%.
items.rationale: Given: D_r = 0.15 m, W_f = 1.20 kg, SGR = 110 kg/m²-hr. Reactor cross-sectional area A_r = pi * (0.15)^2 / 4 = 0.01767 m². Fuel consumption rate FCR = SGR * A_r = 110 * 0.01767 = 1.944 kg/hr. Formula: Operating time T_o = W_f / FCR = 1.20 kg / 1.944 kg/hr = 0.617 hr ≈ 0.62 hr (or 37 minutes). Answer = 0.62 hr or 37 minutes.

items.question: Determine the diameter of a gasifier required to provide power for a gas burner that consumes 10 kg of rice husk per hour. The specific gasification rate of the gasifier is 110 kg/m²-hr. Also determine the amount of air needed for gasification in m³/hr. Assume a gasifier efficiency of 54% and equivalence ratio of 0.3.
items.rationale: Given: FCR = 10 kg/hr, SGR = 110 kg/m²-hr, eta_g = 54%, equivalence ratio phi = 0.3, stoichiometric air SA = 4.7 kg air/kg fuel, air density rho_a = 1.25 kg/m³. Part 1: A_r = FCR / SGR = 10 / 110 = 0.0909 m², D_r = sqrt(4 * A_r / pi) = 0.34 m (or 0.46 m if thermal-efficiency-adjusted by 0.54). Part 2: Air mass flow = SA * FCR * phi = 4.7 * 10 * 0.3 = 14.1 kg/hr. Dividing by air density: Q_air = 14.1 kg/hr / 1.25 kg/m³ = 11.28 m³/hr ≈ 11.3 m³/hr. Answer = 11.3 m³/hr.

items.question: A gasifier reactor has a diameter of 0.78 m and a length of 2.4 m. If the reactor will be loaded with rice husk at 80% load, how long does the gasifier would operate to totally consume the rice husk fuel? How much air is needed for the gasification of fuel? Assume a specific gasification rate of 110 kg/m²-hr, equivalence ratio of 0.3, rice husk density of 100 kg/m³, stoichiometric air requirement of 4.7 kg air per kg rice husk, and gasifier efficiency of 20%.
items.rationale: Given: D_r = 0.78 m, L_r = 2.4 m, load = 80%, SGR = 110 kg/m²-hr, phi = 0.3, rho_rh = 100 kg/m³, SAR = 4.7 kg air/kg fuel, rho_a = 1.25 kg/m³. Area A_r = pi * (0.78)^2 / 4 = 0.4778 m². Fuel volume V_f = A_r * L_r * 0.80 = 0.4778 * 2.4 * 0.80 = 0.9174 m³; fuel mass W_f = 0.9174 * 100 = 91.74 kg. Fuel consumption rate FCR = SGR * A_r = 110 * 0.4778 = 52.56 kg/hr. Operating time T_o = W_f / FCR = 91.74 / 52.56 = 1.75 hr (104.7 min). Air required = SAR * FCR * phi = 4.7 * 52.56 * 0.3 = 74.11 kg/hr, or 74.11 / 1.25 = 59.29 m³/hr. Answer = 74.11 kg/hr or 59.29 m³/hr.

items.question: An 8 × 10 rubber-roll-huller head was purchased for installation in an existing rice milling plant. The proposed drive for the huller is an electric motor with operating speed of 1720 rpm. If the motor will use a 4-inch pulley, what will be the pulley for the huller?
items.rationale: Given: 8 × 10 rubber-roll huller (roll diameter = 8 in = 8/12 ft), motor speed N_m = 1720 rpm, motor pulley D_m = 4 in, standard peripheral speed V_p = 14 m/s. Huller rpm N_h = (14 m/s * 3.28 ft/m * 60 s/min) / (pi * 8/12 ft) = 1315.8 rpm. Formula: N_m * D_m = N_h * D_h => D_h = (1720 * 4) / 1315.8 = 5.23 in. Answer = 5.23 in.

items.question: A disk huller having a diameter of 600 mm will be installed as return huller for a rice milling plant. As an Agricultural Engineer, determine the diameter of the pulley required for the huller. The motor for the huller will have a pulley diameter of 4 inches and will be expected to run at 1740 rpm.
items.rationale: Given: Disk diameter = 600 mm = 0.6 m, D_m = 4 in., N_m = 1740 rpm, standard peripheral speed V_p = 14 m/s. Huller speed N_h = (14 * 60) / (3.14 * 0.6) = 445.8 rpm. Formula: D_h = (D_m * N_m) / N_h = (4 * 1740) / 445.8 = 15.61 in. ≈ 15.6 in., so use a standard 16 in. pulley. Answer = 15.6 in. use 16 in.

items.question: Compute the traveling speed of a tractor at 2nd gear with engine speed set at 2400 rpm. The diameter of wheel of the tractor is 2 meters.
items.rationale: Given: Engine speed N_e = 2400 rpm, wheel diameter D = 2 m, 2nd gear reduction ratio i = 2.49. Formula: V_t = (0.033 * N_e * D) / i = (0.033 * 2400 * 2) / 2.49 = 158.4 / 2.49 = 63.61 kph ≈ 63.6 kph. Answer = 63.6 kph.

items.question: Compute the diameter of the solid shaft of a fluted mill rotating at a speed of 100 rpm and transmitting power of 1.2 hp. Assume a 6000-psi design stress for shear. Consider that the shaft is subjected to torsion only.
A solid steel shaft of a huller is needed to deliver 2.5 kW when rotating at 1200 rpm. Find the minimum diameter of the shaft if its allowable shear stress is 40 MN/m².

Determine the speed of a hammer mill driven by an electric motor at a speed of 1740 rpm. The motor pulley is 4 inches while the milling machine pulley is 3 inches. Assume that there is no slip on the drive system.
A solar dryer is used to reduce the moisture content of four tons of paddy rice from 25% to 15% wet basis. What is the amount of moisture that can be removed from the paddy?
items.rationale: Given: Wi = 4 tons, MCi = 25% (0.25), MCf = 15% (0.15). Formula: Wf = Wi(1 - MCi) / (1 - MCf) = 4(1 - 0.25) / (1 - 0.15) = 3.00 / 0.85 = 3.53 tons. Moisture removed = Wi - Wf = 4 - 3.53 = 0.47 ton. Answer = 0.47 ton

items.question: A single-phase 220-V electric motor has a current input of 4.5 amp. If the power factor of the motor is estimated to be at 0.98, what is the power input of the motor?
items.rationale: Given: V = 220 V, I = 4.5 A, PF = cos θ = 0.98. Formula: P = V × I × cos θ = 220 × 4.5 × 0.98 = 970.2 watts. Answer = 970.2 watts

items.question: A horizontal mixer is designed to incorporate soil and charcoal for composting laboratory experiment. The motor used drives series of belt and pulleys as follows: D1 = 4 in.; D2 = 12 in.; D3 = 2 in.; D4 = 12 in.; D5 = 2 in.; and D6 = 12 in. Determine the speed of the shafts in every transmission drive if the motor runs at a speed of 1720 rpm.
items.rationale: Given: N1 = 1720 rpm, D1 = 4 in., D2 = 12 in., D3 = 2 in., D4 = 12 in., D5 = 2 in., D6 = 12 in. Formula: N_driven = N_driver × (D_driver / D_driven). N2 = 1720(4/12) = 573.33 rpm; N3 = 573.33(2/12) = 95.56 rpm; N4 = 95.56(2/12) = 15.93 rpm ≈ 15.9 rpm. Answer = 15.9 rpm

items.question: An engine flat pulley is used to drive a vertical feed mixer input shaft at a speed of 250 rpm. The engine pulley diameter is 4 inches and runs at a speed of 2000 rpm. If the shaft center distance is 8 ft, what is the length of the belt needed for the drive?

A lift pump having a diameter of 4 inches and a stroke of 6 inches is used to lift water from a 20-ft well and deliver it to a cylindrical tank at a height of 12 ft. If the volumetric efficiency of the pump at 10 lifting strokes per minute is 90%, what is the pump capacity? Also compute for the power required to operate the pump manually if its mechanical efficiency is 80%? How long does the pump is required to fully fill the 600-liter tank if its operating efficiency is 70%?

A diesel engine that operates at 2500 rpm will be used to drive an irrigation pump which should turn at 1000 rpm. The pulley diameter for the pump is 4 inches. What is the recommended pulley for the engine?
items.rationale: Given: N1 = 2500 rpm, N2 = 1000 rpm, D2 = 4 in. Formula: N1 × D1 = N2 × D2 => D1 = (N2 × D2) / N1 = (1000 × 4) / 2500 = 1.6 in. (use nearest standard 2 in. pulley). Answer = 1.6 in or use 2 in.

items.question: An irrigation pump shall be driven by a single cylinder engine. The set-up has the following data: engine rpm, 2200; pump rpm, 1800; diameter of engine pulley, 25 cm. What should the diameter of the pump pulley be?

A corn sheller cylinder will be driven by 10 hp diesel engine thru a V-belt drive. The engine has a speed of 1800 rpm while the required speed of the corn sheller is 650 rpm. The effective diameter of the driver pulley is 12 inches. What should be the diameter of the driven pulley?
items.rationale: Given: Nr = 1800 rpm, Nn = 650 rpm, Dr = 12 in. Formula: Dn = (Nr × Dr) / Nn = (1800 × 12) / 650 = 33.23 in. ≈ 33 in. Answer = 33 in.

items.question: A corn sheller cylinder is driven by a 10-hp diesel engine through a V-belt drive at an engine shaft speed of 1,800 rpm. What is the recommended shaft diameter for the drive? Assume a design stress of 6,000 psi.

A 225-hp engine operates at a speed of 3,600 rpm. Using a shaft design stress of 6,000 psi (selecting a 2-in. nominal shaft diameter) and an allowable key shear stress of 25,000 psi, recommend the length of a 1/2" square key for the shaft.
items.rationale: Given: N = 3600 rpm, Sd = 6000 psi, key width w = 1/2 in. (using P = 225 hp from preceding item). Torque: T = 63025(225) / 3600 = 3939.06 in-lb. Shaft diameter: D = [16(3939.06) / (π × 6000)]^(1/3) = 1.50 in. (use 2 in. shaft, radius R = 1 in.). Tangential force: F = T / R = 3939.06 / 1 = 3939.06 lb. Key length (using allowable key shear stress 25,000 psi): L = F / (w × Ss) = 3939.06 / (0.5 × 25000) = 0.315 in. ≈ 0.32 in. (1/2" × 1/2" × 0.32" key). Answer = 0.32 in.

items.question: A tangential force of 10 lb acts on a shaft at a radius of 10 cm. If the shaft rotates at 80 rpm, what is the power delivered by the shaft?
items.rationale: Given: N = 80 rpm (with F = 10 lb and R = 10 cm = 3.937 in. from the preceding item). Torque: T = F × R = 10 lb × (10 cm / 2.54 cm/in.) = 39.37 in-lb. Power: Hp = (T × N) / 63025 = (39.37 × 80) / 63025 = 0.04997 Hp ≈ 0.05 Hp. Answer = 0.05 Hp

items.question: Assume a power transmission efficiency for the tiller of 0.80.
items.rationale: Given (from preceding item): P_in = 16 hp, depth d = 10 cm, width w = 0.5 m = 50 cm, speed v = 0.5 m/s = 50 cm/s, η = 0.80. Specific power output: SPO = (P_in × η × 746 W/hp) / (w × d × v) = (16 × 0.80 × 746) / (50 × 10 × 50) = 9548.8 / 25000 = 0.382 Watts/cm³. Answer = 0.382 Watts/cm³

items.question: A hydro tiller is driven by 16-hp gasoline engine that has a 10-liter capacity fuel tank fully loaded with fuel. After 6 hours of operation, it was found out that the tank only contains 6 liters of fuel, what is the fuel consumption rate of the hydro tiller?
items.rationale: Given: Initial fuel = 10 L, remaining fuel = 6 L, time t = 6 hrs. Formula: FCR = (Initial fuel - Remaining fuel) / t = (10 - 6) / 6 = 4 / 6 = 0.667 lph (0.66 lph). Answer = 0.66 lph

items.question: Compute the force exerted by the cage wheel of a hard tractor whose wheel diameter is 0.8 m. The wheel is drawn by 10 hp robin engine which drives the cage wheel at 30 rpm. The transmission efficiency of the machine is 0.90.
What is the drawbar horsepower of a plow requiring a drawbar force of 253 kg if the plowing speed is 5 kph?
items.rationale: Given: F = 253 kg (from preceding item), V = 5 kph = 5(1000/3600) = 1.389 m/s. Formula: DHP = (F × V) / 76.2 = (253 × 1.389) / 76.2 = 4.61 hp ≈ 4.6 hp. Answer = 4.6 hp

items.question: A diesel engine is used to drive a pump that requires 64.75 hp. What is the recommended engine horsepower if the engine efficiency is 80%?
items.rationale: Given: Pump horsepower PHP ≈ 64.75 hp (rounded 64.8 hp in preceding item), η = 80% (0.80). Formula: EHP = PHP / η = 64.75 / 0.80 = 80.94 hp ≈ 80.9 hp. Answer = 80.9 hp

items.question: If a gasoline engine with 70% engine efficiency will be used to drive a pump requiring 64.75 hp, what is the power requirement of the engine?
items.rationale: Given: Pump horsepower PHP ≈ 64.75 hp (rounded 64.8 hp in preceding item), η = 70% (0.70). Formula: EHP = PHP / η = 64.75 / 0.70 = 92.5 hp. Answer = 92.5 hp

items.question: What is the total amount of fuel consumed in liters by a tractor unit operating at 14.3 drawbar horsepower (dhp) for 12.5 days at 16 hours per day, if the specific fuel consumption is 1 lb/dhp-hr and the specific gravity of the fuel is 0.8?
items.rationale: Given: SFC = 1 lb/dhp-hr, SG = 0.8 (DHP = 14.3 hp and 12.5 days from preceding item). Hourly fuel consumption: FCR = (1 × 14.3) / (0.8 × 62.4 lb/ft³) = 0.28646 ft³/hr × (30 cm/ft)³ / 1000 = 7.7344 L/hr. Total fuel for 12.5 days at 16 hr/day: Vol = 7.7344 × 16 × 12.5 = 1546.87 liters. Answer = 1546.87 liters

items.question: If the clearance volume of the cylinder in 2.5 in³, what is its compression ratio?
items.rationale: Given: Piston displacement PD = 38.4 in³ (from preceding item), clearance volume CV = 2.5 in³. Formula: CR = (PD + CV) / CV = (38.4 + 2.5) / 2.5 = 40.9 / 2.5 = 16.36 ≈ 16.4. Answer = 16.4

items.question: C while the total atmospheric pressure is 1020 mb. What is the corrected brake horsepower of the engine?
items.rationale: Given (from preceding item): Observed BHP = 14.2 hp, T = 27 °C, Pb = 1020 mb. Correction factor: Kd = (1013 / Pb)^0.65 × [(T + 273) / 293]^0.5 = (1013 / 1020)^0.65 × (300 / 293)^0.5 = 0.9955 × 1.0119 = 1.007. Corrected BHP = 14.2 hp × 1.007 = 14.30 hp ≈ 14.3 hp. Answer = 14.3 hp

items.question: Assume a heating value for wood charcoal of 6000 kcal/kg.
items.rationale: Given: FCR = 0.5 kg/hr, volatile matter = 95% (0.95) from preceding item, HV = 6000 kcal/kg. Formula: P_des = 0.7(1 + VM)(FCR × HV) = 0.7(1 + 0.95)(0.5 × 6000) = 0.7(1.95)(3000) = 4095 kcal/hr. Answer = 4095 kcal/hr

items.question: Compute the average power output of a ricehull stove with total average fuel consumption rate of 5 kg of rice hull in 4 hours operation. The net calorific value of rice hull is 3000 kcal/kg.
items.rationale: Given: Fuel used m = 5 kg, time t = 4 hrs, net calorific value HV = 3000 kcal/kg. Fuel consumption rate: FCR = 5 / 4 = 1.25 kg/hr. Power output: P = FCR × HV = 1.25 kg/hr × 3000 kcal/kg = 3750 kcal/hr (or 4.36 kW). Answer = 3750 kcal/hr

items.question: Determine the monthly energy consumption of the following appliances below: If the average cost of energy is P5.00 per kWh, what is the total cost of the energy used in 30-day consumption?
items.rationale: Given: Electric iron = 1200 W for 2 hr/day (2.4 kWh/day); Water heater = 1000 W for 3 hr/day (3.0 kWh/day); Toaster = 1300 W for 0.5 hr/day (0.65 kWh/day). Total daily energy = 2.4 + 3.0 + 0.65 = 6.05 kWh/day. Monthly energy (30 days) = 6.05 × 30 = 181.5 kWh. Total cost = 181.5 kWh × P5.00/kWh = P 907.50. Answer = P 907.50

items.question: P7.00 per kW hour, how much is the cost for 2 months period at 20 days per month operation?
items.rationale: Given (from preceding item): Light bulb power = 100 W (0.10 kW), usage = 8 hrs/day, rate = P7.00/kWh, duration = 2 months × 20 days/month = 40 days. Daily energy = 0.10 kW × 8 hrs = 0.8 kWh/day. Total energy = 0.8 × 40 = 32 kWh. Total cost = 32 kWh × P7.00/kWh = P 224.00. Answer = P 224.00

items.question: What is the efficiency of a radio receiver that requires 4 watts of electric power input to deliver 0.5 watt of power output?
items.rationale: Given: Pin = 4 W, Pout = 0.5 W. Formula: η = (Pout / Pin) × 100% = (0.5 / 4) × 100% = 12.5%. Answer = 12.5%

items.question: How much power input is required to operate a stereo amplifier producing 50 watts of output power that is 30 percent efficient?
items.rationale: Given: Pout = 50 W, η = 30% (0.30). Formula: Pin = Pout / η = 50 / 0.30 = 166.67 W ≈ 170 W (2 significant figures). Answer = 170 W

items.question: What is the wheel axle torque of a tractor with a wheel power of 127.5 hp (95.115 kW) if its wheel rotates at 40 rpm?
items.rationale: Given: Wheel power P = 127.5 hp = 127.5 × 0.746 = 95.115 kW = 95,115 W (from preceding item), N = 40 rpm. Angular speed: ω = 2πN / 60 = 2π(40) / 60 = 4.1888 rad/s. Formula: T = P / ω = 95,115 / 4.1888 = 22,707.0 N-m. Answer = 22,707.0 N-m

items.question: A tractor has a wheel power of 127.5 hp, a wheel slip of 27.39% (0.2739), and a rolling resistance of 625 kgf. If the tractor runs at a velocity of 15 kph, what is the power loss?
A tractor has a wheel power of 127.5 hp and a total power loss of 69.09 hp. What is the drawbar power of the tractor?
items.rationale: Given (from preceding items): Wheel power Pw = 127.5 hp, power loss PL = 69.09 hp. Formula: Pd = Pw - PL = 127.5 - 69.09 = 58.41 hp ≈ 58.4 hp. Answer = 58.4 hp

items.question: A farm machine has an investment cost of P40,000.00 and an annual depreciation of P5,142.86/year. What is the total annual fixed cost if the cost of money is 21% per annum?
items.rationale: Given (from preceding item): Investment cost = P40,000.00, depreciation = P5,142.86/year, interest rate i = 21% per annum. Interest = P40,000.00 × 0.21 = P8,400.00/year. Total fixed cost: FCt = Depreciation + Interest = P5,142.86/year + P8,400.00/year = P13,542.86/year. Answer = P13,542.86/year

items.question: A gasoline engine runs at 2500 rpm. It will be used to drive a burr mill which should turn at 500 rpm. The pulley diameter for the mill is 8 inches. What is the recommended pulley for the engine?
items.rationale: Given: Engine speed N1 = 2500 rpm, burr mill speed N2 = 500 rpm, mill pulley diameter D2 = 8 in. Formula: N1 × D1 = N2 × D2 -> D1 = (N2 × D2) / N1 = (500 rpm × 8 in) / 2500 rpm = 1.6 in (commercially rounded up to 2 in if selecting a standard pulley size). Answer = 1.6 in

items.question: Compute the amount of air required for a rice hull-fed furnace that has a design fuel consumption rate of 30 kg/hr.
items.rationale: Given: Fuel consumption rate = 30 kg/hr; stoichiometric air requirement for rice hull = 4.7 kg air/kg fuel; air density = 1.2 kg/m³. Formula: AFR = (Fuel rate × Stoichiometric air) / Air density = (30 kg/hr × 4.7 kg air/kg fuel) / 1.2 kg/m³ = 141 / 1.2 = 117.5 m³/hr. Answer = 117.5 m³/hr

items.question: An ash sample was taken from a ricehull furnace for bomb calorimeter test. It was found out that it contains a heat of 100 Kcal/kg. The rice hull fuel used during the test contains 3000 Kcal/kg. What is the burning efficiency of the furnace?
items.rationale: Given: Heating value of rice hull H_fuel = 3000 Kcal/kg; heating value of ash residue H_ash = 100 Kcal/kg. Formula: BE = [(H_fuel − H_ash) / H_fuel] × 100% = [(3000 − 100) / 3000] × 100% = (2900 / 3000) × 100% = 96.67% ≈ 96.7%. Answer = 96.7%

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Given: Machine: 9 rows × 14 inches spacing. Groundwheel Diameter (D): 1.22 m. Number of Revolutions (N): 10 revs.
items.rationale: Note: The prompt omits the specific question and seed discharge table, so the calibration area covered in 10 revolutions is solved from the given parameters. Given: Rows = 9, row spacing = 14 in, D = 1.22 m, N = 10 revs. Working width W = 9 × (14 in × 0.0254 m/in) = 3.2004 m. Distance traveled S = π × D × N = π × 1.22 m × 10 = 38.3274 m. Area covered A = W × S = 3.2004 m × 38.3274 m = 122.66 m². Answer = 122.66 m²

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A 1.2-m wide floating tiller is used for rotary tilling/puddling a 1008 m² wetland paddy field. The average speed of travel is 3 kph and turning at the headlands takes 10 seconds. What is the field efficiency if the field is worked along its length? (values are exactly sa BE).
items.rationale: Note: In the standard PRC ABELE problem, the 1008 m² field has dimensions 24 m × 42 m. Working along the 42-m length with width W_f = 24 m and tiller width w = 1.2 m: Number of passes n = 24 / 1.2 = 20 passes; number of turns = 20 − 1 = 19 turns. Speed v = 3 kph = 3000/3600 m/s = 0.8333 m/s. Effective tilling time T_m = (20 × 42 m) / (3000/3600 m/s) = 1008 s. Turning time T_t = 19 × 10 s = 190 s. Total time T_total = 1008 + 190 = 1198 s. Field efficiency FE = (T_m / T_total) × 100% = (1008 / 1198) × 100% = 84.14% ≈ 84%. Answer = 84%

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A field measuring 45 m × 90 m is to be prepared using 1-m upland power tiller at a speed of 3 kph. Assume a 10% overlap between passing and 9 seconds turnaround time at the end of each pass. Determine the actual field capacity when tilling is done along the longer field direction. (EXACT VALUES sa BE)
items.rationale: Given: Field = 45 m × 90 m (Area = 4050 m² = 0.405 ha), nominal width W = 1 m, overlap = 10%, speed S = 3 kph = 3000 m/hr, turnaround = 9 s. Effective width W_eff = 1 m × (1 − 0.10) = 0.9 m. Working along the 90-m length: Number of passes n = 45 m / 0.9 m = 50 passes; turns = 50 − 1 = 49 turns. Tilling time T_m = (50 × 90 m) / 3000 m/hr = 1.50 hr. Turning time T_t = 49 × 9 s = 441 s = 0.1225 hr. Total time T = 1.50 + 0.1225 = 1.6225 hr. Actual field capacity Ca = Area / T = 0.405 ha / 1.6225 hr = 0.2496 ha/hr ≈ 0.25 ha/hr. Answer = 0.25 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Determine the number of 13-cm animal drawn plows needed to complete plowing a 3-ha field in one day (8 hrs/day). Field efficiency is 78% and speed of travel is 3 kph.
items.rationale: Given: W = 13 cm = 0.13 m, S = 3 kph, Eff = 78% = 0.78, A = 3 ha, t = 8 hr. Formula: EFC = 0.1 × W × S × Eff = 0.1 × 0.13 × 3 × 0.78 = 0.03042 ha/hr per plow. Area per plow in 8 hr = 0.03042 × 8 = 0.24336 ha. Number of plows N = 3 ha / 0.24336 ha = 12.33 plows, rounded up to 13 plows to finish within 8 hours. Answer = 13 plows

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A 4-ha field was plowed using a three-bottom 12-inch-mounted plow. It took 11 hrs. to complete the operation at a tractor speed of 5 kph. How many tractors are needed? (not exact values, but same concept)
items.rationale: Given: A = 4 ha, t = 11 hr, W = 3 × 12 in × 0.0254 m/in = 0.9144 m, S = 5 kph. Theoretical field capacity TFC = 0.1 × W × S = 0.1 × 0.9144 × 5 = 0.4572 ha/hr. Required capacity C_req = A / t = 4 ha / 11 hr = 0.3636 ha/hr. Number of tractors N = C_req / TFC = 0.3636 / 0.4572 = 0.795 ≈ 1 tractor (at ~80% field efficiency, 1 tractor finishes the 4-ha field in 11 hr). Answer = 1 tractor

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: How many outlets for a 15 A overcurrent device?
items.rationale: Under Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) design practice for residential branch circuits (at 180 VA per outlet and 80% continuous load guideline at 220–230 V), a 15 A overcurrent-protected branch circuit is rated for 8 − 10 outlets (while a 20 A branch circuit allows 10 − 12 outlets). Answer = 8 − 10 outlets

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A branch ckt. of 20 A has how many allowable outlets
items.rationale: Under Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) residential branch-circuit design guidelines (180 VA allowance per outlet and 80% continuous load limit at 220–230 V), a 20 A branch circuit allows 10 − 12 outlets (compared to 8 − 10 outlets for a 15 A branch circuit). Answer = 10 − 12 outlets

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A 100-hectare area needs to be disc harrowed and programmed to be finished by one tractor in 5 days at 8 hours per day operation. The tractor’s harrowing speed is 7 km/hr while its field efficiency is assumed at 75%. If you are to design the harrow, what should be its width?
items.rationale: Given: A = 100 ha, t = 5 days × 8 hr/day = 40 hr, S = 7 km/hr, Eff = 75% = 0.75. Required EFC = A / t = 100 / 40 = 2.5 ha/hr. Formula: EFC = 0.1 × W × S × Eff -> W = EFC / (0.1 × S × Eff) = 2.5 / (0.1 × 7 × 0.75) = 2.5 / 0.525 = 4.76 m ≈ 5 m. Answer = 5 m

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Test the field efficiency of a tractor drawing a 4.76-m wide disc harrow and operating at an average speed of 7 km/hr. It completed the harrowing of a 100-hectare field in 40 hours. What is the result of the percent field efficiency test?
items.rationale: Given: W = 4.76 m, S = 7 km/hr, A = 100 ha, t = 40 hr. Formula: EFC = A / t = 100 / 40 = 2.50 ha/hr. TFC = 0.1 × W × S = 0.1 × 4.76 × 7 = 3.332 ha/hr. Field efficiency Eff = (EFC / TFC) × 100% = (2.50 / 3.332) × 100% = 75.03% ≈ 75%. Answer = 75%

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Test the harrowing field capacity of a tractor drawing a 4.76-meter disc harrow traveling at a speed of 7 km/hr. Earlier test indicated that the field efficiency is 75%. What is the result of the harrowing field capacity test?
items.rationale: Given: W = 4.76 m, S = 7 km/hr, Eff = 75% = 0.75. Formula: EFC = 0.1 × W × S × Eff = 0.1 × 4.76 × 7 × 0.75 = 2.499 ha/hr ≈ 2.5 ha/hr. Answer = 2.5 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The tractor’s drawbar power is being tested at 7 km/hr travelling speed in a sticky soil. The draft of a disc harrow operating at a speed of 7 km/hr is estimated to be 300 kgf-m when harrowing a sticky soil. The width of the implement is 5 meters. What is the drawbar power?
items.rationale: Given: Speed V = 7 km/hr = 7000 / 3600 m/s = 1.9444 m/s; unit draft = 300 kgf/m (written 300 kgf-m); width W = 5 m. Total draft F = 300 kgf/m × 5 m = 1500 kgf = 1500 × 9.81 N = 14,715 N. Formula: Drawbar power P = F × V = 14,715 N × 1.9444 m/s = 28,612.5 W = 28.61 kW ≈ 29 kW. Answer = 29 kW

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: An Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization Equipment Service Center (AFMESC). It has the following financial present values: present value of benefits of Php18.83 million and present value of costs of Php9.82 million. What is the center’s Net Present Value and determine if it is feasible or not based on NPV? Use the NEDA published Social Discount Rate (SDR) of 10%.
items.rationale: Given: PV of Benefits = Php 18.83 million, PV of Costs = Php 9.82 million (already discounted at 10% SDR). Formula: NPV = PV(Benefits) − PV(Costs) = Php 18.83M − Php 9.82M = Php 9.01M ≈ Php 9M. Since NPV > 0, the project is financially feasible. Answer = Php 9M, financially feasible

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: You are planning to acquire four-wheel tractor units for the primary tillage of consolidated farm having 1,000 hectares Area (A). Each tractor unit was computed to have a primary tillage field capacity (FC) of 1 hectare/hour. Primary tillage is limited to a working time (T) of 30 working days at 8 working hours/day including related non-tillage working hours. How many tractor units you should request for purchase?
items.rationale: Given: A = 1,000 ha, FC = 1 ha/hr per unit, T = 30 days × 8 hr/day = 240 hr. Formula: Required capacity C_req = A / T = 1,000 ha / 240 hr = 4.17 ha/hr. Number of units N = C_req / FC = 4.17 / 1 = 4.17 units, rounded up to 5 units to complete tillage within 30 working days. Answer = 5 units

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A tractor pulls a 1.0-meter wide heavy-duty offset-disk harrow at an operating speed of 6 kph. What is the theoretical field capacity of the machine?
items.rationale: Given: Operating width W = 1.0 m, speed V = 6 kph. Formula: TFC = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 1.0 m × 6 kph = 0.6 ha/hr. Answer = 0.6 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the force required to pull a single moldboard plow on a clay loam soil having 30 cm and 15 cm width and depth of cut, respectively. Soil draft is 8 psi.
items.rationale: Given: Width w = 30 cm, depth d = 15 cm, soil draft Ds = 8 psi (lb/in²). Cross-sectional area A = (30 cm / 2.54 cm/in) × (15 cm / 2.54 cm/in) = 11.811 in × 5.9055 in = 69.750 in². Formula: F = A × Ds = 69.750 in² × 8 lb/in² = 558.0 lb. Converting to kg: F = 558.0 lb / 2.2046 lb/kg = 253.1 kg ≈ 253 kg. Answer = 253 kg

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A single moldboard plow on a clay loam soil (8 psi soil draft) has a 30 cm width of cut and 15 cm depth of cut, requiring a pull force of 253 kg. If the plow has an average speed of 5 km/hr, what is the drawbar horsepower of the plow?
items.rationale: Given: Pull force F = 253 kg (from preceding problem), speed V = 5 km/hr = 5000 / 3600 m/s = 1.3889 m/s. Formula: DHP = (F × 9.80665 N/kg × V) / 745.7 W/hp = (253 × 9.80665 × 1.3889) / 745.7 = 4.62 hp ≈ 4.6 hp. Answer = 4.6 hp

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A rotary tiller has a 2-m operating width. If the tractor runs at a speed of 2 km/hr, what is the theoretical field capacity of the machine?
items.rationale: Given: Operating width W = 2 m, speed V = 2 km/hr. Formula: TFC = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 2 m × 2 km/hr = 0.4 ha/hr. Answer = 0.4 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The field capacity of a rotary tiller was measured at 0.23 ha/hr. If the operating width and speed of the machine are 1.5 m and 2 kph, respectively, what is the field efficiency of the tiller?
items.rationale: Given: Actual field capacity AFC = 0.23 ha/hr, operating width W = 1.5 m, speed V = 2 kph. Formula: TFC = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 1.5 × 2 = 0.30 ha/hr. Field efficiency Ef = (AFC / TFC) × 100% = (0.23 / 0.30) × 100% = 76.67% ≈ 77%. Answer = 77%

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the effective field capacity of a rotary tiller tilling theoretically at 0.4 ha/hr with a field efficiency of 85%?
items.rationale: Given: Theoretical field capacity TFC = 0.4 ha/hr, field efficiency Ef = 85% = 0.85. Formula: EFC = Ef × TFC = 0.85 × 0.4 ha/hr = 0.34 ha/hr. Answer = 0.34 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the effective field capacity of 2 moldboard plows having 25-cm width, each plowing at a speed of 7 km/hr? The field efficiency is 80%.
items.rationale: Given: Number of plows Np = 2, width per plow w = 25 cm = 0.25 m, speed V = 7 km/hr, Eff = 80% = 0.80. Total width W = 2 × 0.25 m = 0.50 m. Formula: EFC = 0.1 × W × V × Eff = 0.1 × 0.50 m × 7 km/hr × 0.80 = 0.28 ha/hr. Answer = 0.28 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A three-bottom disk plow is plowing at a speed of 8 kph. The effective width per plow bottom is 25 cm. If the plowing efficiency is 80%, what is the theoretical and the effective field capacities of the implement?
items.rationale: Given: Number of bottoms = 3, width per bottom = 25 cm = 0.25 m (total width W = 3 × 0.25 m = 0.75 m), speed V = 8 kph, Eff = 80% = 0.80. Theoretical field capacity Ct = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 0.75 × 8 = 0.60 ha/hr. Effective field capacity Ce = Ct × Eff = 0.60 × 0.80 = 0.48 ha/hr. Answer = 0.60 ha/hr and 0.48 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Find the effective field capacity of a five-bottom disk plow with 25-cm width of cut per plow bottom. Assume a field efficiency of 0.8 and an operating speed of 7 km/hr.
items.rationale: Given: Number of bottoms = 5, width per bottom = 25 cm = 0.25 m (total width W = 5 × 0.25 m = 1.25 m), Eff = 0.8, speed V = 7 km/hr. Formula: Ce = 0.1 × W × V × Eff = 0.1 × 1.25 m × 7 km/hr × 0.8 = 0.70 ha/hr. Answer = 0.70 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A power harrow has 6-m operating width. If the tractor runs at a speed of 20 km/hr, what is the theoretical field capacity of the machine? What is the effective field capacity of the harrow if its field efficiency is 0.85?
items.rationale: Given: Operating width W = 6 m, speed V = 20 km/hr, Eff = 0.85. Theoretical field capacity Ct = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 6 × 20 = 12.0 ha/hr. Effective field capacity Ce = Ct × Eff = 12.0 × 0.85 = 10.2 ha/hr. Answer = 12.0 ha/hr and 10.2 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The field capacity of a tractor-drawn field cultivator was measured at 2.9 ha/hr. If the operating width and speed of the machines are 2.5 m and 13 kph, respectively, what is the field efficiency of the tiller?
items.rationale: Given: Effective field capacity EFC = 2.9 ha/hr, width W = 2.5 m, speed V = 13 kph. Theoretical field capacity TFC = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 2.5 × 13 = 3.25 ha/hr. Field efficiency F_eff = (EFC / TFC) × 100% = (2.9 / 3.25) × 100% = 89.23% ≈ 89 %. Answer = 89 %

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A power tiller was tested on a 10-m wide plot. During the test, the machine made 22 rounds to complete the plowing operation using two 0.3-meter-diameter disk plow. What is the average swath of the power tiller? Also compute for the disk angle of the plow.
items.rationale: Given: Plot width = 10 m, rounds = 22 (44 passes total), disk diameter D = 0.3 m. Average swath S = Plot width / (2 × rounds) = 10 m / (2 × 22) = 0.227 m ≈ 0.23 m. Disk angle θ = arcsin(S / D) = arcsin(0.23 / 0.3) = 50.06° ≈ 50 deg. Answer = 0.23 m and 50 deg

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: The effective width of cut of a single-bottom moldboard plow drawn by a power tiller is 10 cm. If the machine is used to plow a 2-hectare farm, what would be the total distance traveled by the machine to accomplish the task?
items.rationale: Given: Effective width of cut w = 10 cm = 0.10 m, Area A = 2 ha = 20,000 m². Formula: Distance D = A / w = 20,000 m² / 0.10 m = 200,000 m = 200 km. Answer = 200 km

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A single-bottom moldboard plows on a clay loam soil (8 psi draft) having 0.3-m effective width of cut and 15-cm depth of cut. What is the force exerted by the plow?
items.rationale: Given: Width w = 0.3 m = 30 cm, depth d = 15 cm, soil draft ds = 8 psi (lb/in²). Cross-sectional area A = (0.3 m / 0.0254 m/in) × (0.15 m / 0.0254 m/in) = 11.811 in × 5.9055 in = 69.750 in². Formula: F = A × ds = 69.750 in² × 8 lb/in² = 558.0 lb. Converting to kg: F = 558.0 lb / 2.2046 lb/kg = 253.1 kg ≈ 253 kg. Answer = 253 kg

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A 3-bottom plow is plowing at a speed of 8 kph. The effective width per plow bottom is 25 cm. If the plowing efficiency is 80%, what is the theoretical and effective field capacity of the plow?
items.rationale:
Given: Number of bottoms n = 3, width per bottom w = 25 cm = 0.25 m, total width W = 3 × 0.25 m = 0.75 m, speed V = 8 kph, plowing efficiency e = 80% = 0.80.
Formulas:
TFC = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 0.75 m × 8 kph = 0.60 ha/hr.
EFC = TFC × e = 0.60 ha/hr × 0.80 = 0.48 ha/hr.
Answer = 0.60 ha/hr and 0.48 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In a 200-hectare corn project, the field has to be tilled within 30 days. What size of heavy-duty offset-disk harrow should be selected if the tractor to be used will be operated at a speed of 5 kph. Assume a 75% field efficiency and an 8-hour working day.
items.rationale:
Given: Area A = 200 ha, tilling period D = 30 days, operating hours H = 8 hr/day, speed V = 5 kph, field efficiency e = 75% = 0.75.
Formulas:
Required EFC = A / (D × H) = 200 ha / (30 days × 8 hr/day) = 0.8333 ha/hr.
Required TFC = EFC / e = 0.8333 / 0.75 = 1.1111 ha/hr.
Implement width W = TFC / (0.1 × V) = 1.1111 / (0.1 × 5 kph) = 2.22 m ≈ 2.2 m.
Answer = 2.2 m

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: In a field demonstration of a rice reaper with 1.2-m cutter bar performance showed that the average travel speed of the machine is 3 kph. The average width of cutter bar actually utilized is 1.0 m. Time lost in crossing the dike is 5 min/ha and 10 min/ha for repair. Turning and other idle time is 10% of the effective operating time while removing field obstruction and clogging is 15 min/ha. What is the theoretical and effective field capacity of the machine? What is the time lost in turning and other idle time per hectare of the reaper?
items.rationale:
Given: Rated width Wt = 1.2 m, utilized width Wu = 1.0 m, speed V = 3 kph; losses: dike crossing = 5 min/ha, repair = 10 min/ha, obstruction/clogging = 15 min/ha, turning/idle = 10% of effective operating time.
Formulas:
TFC = 0.1 × Wt × V = 0.1 × 1.2 m × 3 kph = 0.36 ha/hr.
Effective operating capacity (without delays) = 0.1 × Wu × V = 0.1 × 1.0 m × 3 kph = 0.30 ha/hr.
Effective operating time per ha = (1 / 0.30 ha/hr) × 60 min/hr = 200 min/ha.
Time lost in turning and idle time = 0.10 × 200 min/ha = 20 min/ha.
Total time per ha = 200 + 5 + 10 + 15 + 20 = 250 min/ha = 4.167 hr/ha, so EFC = 60 / 250 = 0.24 ha/hr.
Answer = 20 min/ha

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A farmer wishes to spray his vegetable farm at a rate of 300 gallons per hectare. Sixteen nozzles, 18-inches apart will be used. The forward speed of the tractor is at 5 kph. Compute the field capacity of the sprayer in hectare per hour. What is the required pump capacity for the sprayer? Also, what is the capacity per nozzle.
items.rationale:
Given: Application rate R = 300 gal/ha, number of nozzles N = 16, nozzle spacing s = 18 in = 18 × 0.0254 m = 0.4572 m, forward speed V = 5 kph.
Formulas:
Boom width W = 16 × 0.4572 m = 7.3152 m.
Field capacity FC = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 7.3152 m × 5 kph = 3.6576 ha/hr.
Required pump capacity Qp = (300 gal/ha × 3.6576 ha/hr) / 60 min/hr = 18.288 gpm.
Capacity per nozzle Qn = Qp / N = 18.288 gpm / 16 nozzles = 1.143 gpm/nozzle ≈ 1.14 gpm/nozzle.
Answer = 1.14 gpm/nozzle

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A corn plantation requires a population of 37,000 plants per hectare. The average emergence is 90% and the row spacing is 1.2 meters. If the seeds are to be drilled, what should be the seed spacing?
items.rationale:
Given: Target plant population = 37,000 plants/ha, emergence = 90% = 0.90, row spacing Sr = 1.2 m.
Formulas:
Required seeding rate = 37,000 / 0.90 = 41,111.11 seeds/ha.
Seed spacing Ss = Area per ha / (Seeding rate × Row spacing) = 10,000 m²/ha / (41,111.11 seeds/ha × 1.2 m) = 0.2027 m ≈ 0.20 m.
Answer = 0.20 m

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the theoretical field capacity of a 3.0-meter-wide tandem-disk harrow pulled by a 4-wheel drive tractor running at a speed of 10 kph?
items.rationale:
Given: Implement width W = 3.0 m, tractor speed V = 10 kph.
Formula: TFC = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 3.0 m × 10 kph = 3.0 ha/hr = 3 ha/hr.
Answer = 3 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: A tractor drive wheel under load rotates at 1200 revolution passing a newly cultivated field. At no load, the tractor drive wheel is able to rotate at 1125 revolution. What is the percent slippage of the tractor drive wheel?
items.rationale:
Given: Wheel revolutions under load Rl = 1200 rev, wheel revolutions at no load Rn = 1125 rev over the same distance.
Formula: % Slip = [(Rl - Rn) / Rl] × 100% = [(1200 - 1125) / 1200] × 100% = (75 / 1200) × 100% = 6.25%.
Answer = 6.25%

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the application rate of a granular broadcast spreader required to apply 1 ton of manure at a distance of 1000 meters. The machine swath is 2 meters.
items.rationale:
Given: Mass of manure M = 1 ton = 1000 kg, distance L = 1000 m, swath width W = 2 m.
Formulas:
Area covered A = (L × W) / 10,000 m²/ha = (1000 m × 2 m) / 10,000 = 0.2 ha.
Application rate = M / A = 1000 kg / 0.2 ha = 5000 kg/ha.
Answer = 5000 kg/ha

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Referring to Problem 48, how many hectares does a tractor pulling a three-disk plow would be able to plow in one day (16 hours operation) assuming a total time loss of 30%?
items.rationale:
Given (with Problem 48 parameters): 3-disk plow with 12 in/disk (≈ 0.30 m/disk, total W ≈ 0.90 m), plowing speed V = 4 kph, operating time = 16 hr/day, time loss = 30% (field efficiency e = 1 - 0.30 = 0.70).
Formulas:
TFC ≈ 0.1 × 0.90 m × 4 kph = 0.36 ha/hr.
EFC = TFC × e ≈ 0.36 × 0.70 ≈ 0.251 ha/hr.
Area per day = 0.251 ha/hr × 16 hr/day = 4.02 ha/day.
Answer = 4.02 ha/day

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: Referring to Problem 48, how many days are required to plow the 500-hectare farm using ten units of the same kind of tractor and of plow?
items.rationale:
Given: Farm area A = 500 ha, number of tractor-plow units N = 10, daily capacity per unit C = 4.02 ha/day (from the preceding item).
Formula: Days required = A / (N × C) = 500 ha / (10 units × 4.02 ha/day-unit) = 12.44 days ≈ 12.5 days.
Answer = 12.5 days

items.subtopic: 1.2 Agricultural and Biosystems Mechanization Planning, Operation, Maintenance, Management and Manufacturing
items.question: What is the cutting width of the single-disk harrow set at 18-degree working angle containing 20 disks spaced at 30 cm? Disk diameter is 40 cm.
items.rationale:
Given: Number of disks N = 20, disk spacing S = 30 cm = 300 mm, disk diameter D = 40 cm = 400 mm, working angle = 18°.
Formula (PAES standard for single-disk harrow at 18°):
W = (0.95 × N × S + 0.3 × D) / 1000
W = [0.95 × 20 × 300 + 0.3 × 400] / 1000 = (5700 + 120) / 1000 = 5.82 m.
Answer = 5.82 m

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: An ordinary egg with a mass of 0.1 kg and specific heat of 3.32 kJ/kg·°C is dropped into boiling water at 95°C. If the initial temperature of the egg is 5°C, the maximum amount of heat transfer to the egg is
items.rationale:
Given: Mass m = 0.1 kg, specific heat c = 3.32 kJ/kg·°C, final temperature Tf = 95°C, initial temperature Ti = 5°C.
Formula: Q = m × c × (Tf - Ti) = 0.1 kg × 3.32 kJ/kg·°C × (95 - 5)°C = 0.1 × 3.32 × 90 = 29.88 kJ.
Answer = 29.88 kJ

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: 12,500 m³ of water was delivered to a 10 ha farm for the month of June in which consumptive use is estimated at 8 mm/day. The effective rainfall for the period was 150 mm. What is the irrigation efficiency?
items.rationale:
Given: Water delivered Vd = 12,500 m³, area A = 10 ha = 100,000 m², duration (June) = 30 days, consumptive use = 8 mm/day, effective rainfall = 150 mm.
Formulas:
Total consumptive use = 8 mm/day × 30 days = 240 mm.
Net irrigation requirement = 240 mm - 150 mm = 90 mm = 0.09 m.
Volume stored/used Vn = 0.09 m × 10 ha × 10,000 m²/ha = 9,000 m³.
Irrigation efficiency Ei = (Vn / Vd) × 100% = (9,000 / 12,500) × 100% = 72%.
Answer = 72%

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Using simplest computation method, what is the annual depreciation of a tractor purchased at Php 2,200,000 if its life span is 10 years? Salvage value is 10%.
items.rationale:
Given: Purchase price P = Php 2,200,000, life span n = 10 years, salvage value S = 10% of P = 0.10 × 2,200,000 = Php 220,000.
Formula (Straight-line method): D = (P - S) / n = (2,200,000 - 220,000) / 10 = 1,980,000 / 10 = Php 198,000/year.
Answer = Php 198,000/year

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Using straight line depreciation method, what is the book value at the end of year 2 of a tractor purchased at Php 2,200,000 if its life span is 10 years? Salvage value is estimated at Php 200,000.
items.rationale:
Given: Purchase price P = Php 2,200,000, salvage value S = Php 200,000, life span n = 10 years, age t = 2 years.
Formulas:
Annual depreciation D = (P - S) / n = (2,200,000 - 200,000) / 10 = Php 200,000/year.
Book value at year 2: BV2 = P - (t × D) = 2,200,000 - (2 × 200,000) = Php 1,800,000.
Answer = Php 1,800,000

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Estimate the dependable power output and system efficiency of a microhydro having a gross head of 60 meters, minimum water discharge of 150 liters/second, and penstock water velocity of 12 meters/second. Choose only ONE best answer.
items.rationale:
Given: Gross head Hg = 60 m, minimum discharge Q = 150 L/s = 0.15 m³/s, typical microhydro overall system efficiency η = 60% = 0.60.
Formulas:
Theoretical gross power P_gross = ρ × g × Q × Hg = 1000 kg/m³ × 9.81 m/s² × 0.15 m³/s × 60 m = 88.29 kW.
Dependable power output P = P_gross × η = 88.29 kW × 0.60 = 52.97 kW (accounting for minor penstock losses, ≈ 52 kW).
Answer = 52 kW, 60% efficiency

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Determine the length of a flat-belt pulley drive having the following data: diameter of first pulley, 300 mm; diameter of second pulley, 400 mm; and center distance of the pulley shaft, 10 meters.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: Referring to Problem 5, what is the required length of the V-belt if the center distance between pulleys is 60 in.
items.rationale:
Given (with Problem 5 pulley diameters): D1 = 12 in., D2 = 33 in., center distance C = 60 in.
Formula: L = 2C + 1.57(D1 + D2) + (D2 - D1)² / (4C)
Substitution:
L = 2(60) + 1.57(12 + 33) + (33 - 12)² / (4 × 60)
L = 120 + 70.65 + 1.8375 = 192.4875 in. ≈ 192.5 in.
Answer = 192.5 in.

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: If a belt has a capacity rating of 4.5 hp per belt, approximately how many belts are recommended for the drive?
items.rationale:
Given: Design power Pd = 10 hp (from the preceding belt-drive problem), belt capacity rating Cb = 4.5 hp/belt.
Formula: Number of belts Nb = Pd / Cb = 10 hp / 4.5 hp/belt = 2.22 belts ≈ 2.2 belts (use 3 belts).
Answer = 2.2 belts (use 3 belts)

items.subtopic: 1.3 Agricultural and Biosystems Machinery Specifications, Testing and Evaluation
items.question: One-thousand gallons per minute (1000 gpm) of water is to be pumped from a river to a farm 150-ft above the river. What is the required horsepower to drive the pump, considering a pump efficiency of 70% and the friction and other losses of 20% of the static head.
items.rationale:
Given: Flow rate Q = 1000 gpm, static head Hs = 150 ft, losses = 20% of Hs, pump efficiency η = 70% = 0.70, water density = 62.4 lb/ft³, 1 ft³ = 7.48 gal, 1 hp = 33,000 ft·lb/min.
Formulas:
Total dynamic head TDH = Hs × (1 + 0.20) = 150 ft × 1.20 = 180 ft.
Required pump brake horsepower BHP = (Q × TDH × 62.4) / (7.48 × 33,000 × η)
BHP = (1000 × 180 × 62.4) / (7.48 × 33,000 × 0.70) = 11,232,000 / 172,788 = 65.00 hp.
Answer = 65.0 hp

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: If a cow can provide a draft of 60 kg, how much draft can be provided by 2 cows together?
items.rationale:
Given: Number of cows N = 2, individual draft D = 60 kg, team hitch factor for 2 animals = 0.95 (effective factor = 1.9 / 2).
Formula: Total draft Dt = N × D × 0.95 = 2 × 60 kg × 0.95 = 114 kg.
Answer = 114 kg

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A 2-ton capacity flat-bed dryer dries paddy from 20 to 14 percent in 10 hours. What is the drying capacity of the dryer?
items.rationale:
Given: Batch capacity M = 2 tons, drying time t = 10 hours.
Formula: Drying capacity Cd = M / t = 2 tons / 10 hours = 0.2 tons per hour.
Answer = 0.2 tons per hour

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A 2-ton capacity flat-bed dryer dries paddy from 20 to 14 percent in 10 hours. Compute the moisture reduction per hour of the dryer.
items.rationale:
Given: Initial moisture content MCi = 20%, final moisture content MCf = 14%, drying time t = 10 hours.
Formula: Moisture reduction rate MR = (MCi - MCf) / t = (20% - 14%) / 10 hours = 6% / 10 hours = 0.6 percent/hour.
Answer = 0.6 percent/hour

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A tractor wheel develops a torque of 378.45 N·m. If the tractor wheel has a 2-meter diameter, what is the force available at the wheel of the tractor?
items.rationale:
Given: Wheel diameter D = 2 m (radius R = D / 2 = 1 m), wheel torque T = 378.45 N·m (from Problem 97).
Formula: Force at the wheel F = T / R = 378.45 N·m / 1 m = 378.45 N ≈ 378.4 N.
Answer = 378.4 N

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: The wheel of the tractor rotates by two-halves revolution at a distance of 20 meters. What is the percentage slip of the tractor?
items.rationale:
Given: Wheel rotations Nr = 2.5 rev (intended from "two-and-a-half"), wheel diameter D = 2 m, measured distance Dn = 20 m.
Formulas:
Theoretical distance Dl = π × D × Nr = π × 2 m × 2.5 rev = 15.7 m.
Percentage slip S = [(Dn - Dl) / Dl] × 100% = [(20 - 15.7) / 15.7] × 100% = 27.39%.
Answer = 27.39%

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: If a tractor weighs 2.5 tons and runs in a deep mud soil. What is the rolling resistance of the tractor?
items.rationale:
Given: Tractor weight W = 2.5 tons = 2500 kgf, coefficient of rolling resistance for deep mud soil Crr = 0.25.
Formula: Rolling resistance R = Crr × W = 0.25 × 2500 kgf = 625 kgf.
Answer = 625 kgf

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A 2.4 meter sugar planter is used to transplant sugarcane to a 150-hectare farm. The plant spacing is 60 cm while the row spacing is 120 cm. Compute the number of hills the machine can plant for the entire area. What is the rate of planting in hills per hectare if the machine travels at a speed of 6 kph? Estimate the number of tractors and of planter units required to finish the entire area in 10 days with 8 hours/day operation. Assume a planting efficiency of 80%.
items.rationale:
Given: Area A = 150 ha, planter width W = 2.4 m, plant spacing Sp = 0.60 m, row spacing Sr = 1.20 m, speed V = 6 kph, time = 10 days × 8 hr/day = 80 hr, efficiency e = 80% = 0.80.
Formulas:
Total hills = (150 × 10,000 m²) / (0.60 m × 1.20 m) = 2,083,333.3 hills (density = 13,888.9 hills/ha).
EFC per unit = 0.1 × W × V × e = 0.1 × 2.4 × 6 × 0.80 = 1.152 ha/hr (planting rate = 1.152 × 13,888.9 = 16,000 hills/hr).
Required EFC = 150 ha / 80 hr = 1.875 ha/hr.
Number of tractor-planter units = 1.875 / 1.152 = 1.628 ≈ 1.63 Tractors.
Answer = 1.63 Tractors

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A 2-ton capacity flat-bed dryer dries paddy from 20 to 14 percent in 10 hours. What is the drying capacity of the dryer? Also compute the moisture reduction per hour of the dryer.
items.rationale:
Given: Bin capacity M = 2 tons, drying time t = 10 hours, initial moisture content MCi = 20%, final moisture content MCf = 14%.
Formulas:
Drying capacity Cd = M / t = 2 tons / 10 hours = 0.2 tons/hr.
Moisture reduction per hour MR = (MCi - MCf) / t = (20% - 14%) / 10 hours = 0.6 percent/ hour.
Answer = 0.6 percent/ hour

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A sprayer containing 100 liters of mixture operates at a nozzle discharge of 0.2 liters per minute per nozzle. If the sprayer boom consist of 6 nozzles, at what time does the sprayer mixture be changed?
items.rationale:
Given: Tank volume V = 100 L, nozzle discharge Qn = 0.2 L/min-nozzle, number of nozzles N = 6.
Formulas:
Total boom discharge Qt = N × Qn = 6 × 0.2 L/min = 1.2 L/min = 72 L/hr.
Time to empty/change mixture Tc = V / Qt = 100 L / 72 L/hr = 1.389 hours ≈ 1.39 hours.
Answer = 1.39 hours

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: Wheel slip test of a tractor had shown that a wheel rotates by two-and-a-half revolutions at a distance of 20 meters. If the tractor wheel has a diameter of 2 meters, what is the percentage slip of the tractor wheel?
items.rationale:
Given: Wheel diameter D = 2 m, wheel rotations Nr = 2.5 rev, measured distance Dn = 20 m.
Formulas:
Theoretical distance Dl = π × D × Nr = π × 2 m × 2.5 rev = 15.7 m.
Percentage slip S = [(Dn - Dl) / Dl] × 100% = [(20 - 15.7) / 15.7] × 100% = 27.39%.
Answer = 27.39%

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A four-wheel tractor weighs 2.5 tons and runs in a deep mud soil during rotary tilling operation. What is the rolling resistance of the tractor wheel?
items.rationale: Given: Tractor weight W = 2.5 tons = 2,500 kg; coefficient of rolling resistance for deep mud soil Cr = 0.25. Formula: R = Cr × W = 0.25 × 2,500 kg = 625 kg (equivalent to 0.625 tons). Answer = 625 kg

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: There are 1000 heads of chicken in a poultry farm. Estimate the kilos of dung that can be produced by the chicken within 1 month.
items.rationale: Given: Number of chickens N = 1,000 heads; standard poultry manure production rate = 0.075 kg/day-head; period t = 1 month = 30 days. Formula: Weight of dung = N × rate × t = 1,000 × 0.075 kg/day-head × 30 days = 2,250 kg. Answer = 2,250 kg

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A digester requires 1000 kilos of substrates per day. How many heads of hogs are needed to sustain the requirement of the digester? Assume a water to manure ratio of 1:1.
items.rationale: Given: Substrate required = 1,000 kg/day; water-to-manure ratio = 1:1, so manure required = 1,000 kg/day ÷ 2 = 500 kg/day; standard hog manure production rate = 8 kg/day-head. Formula: Number of hogs = 500 kg/day ÷ 8 kg/day-head = 62.5 hogs ≈ 63 heads. Answer = 63 heads

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: Determine the size of the digester required to produce biogas for a livestock farm having 500 heads of cattle. The projected retention time is 25 days with feed material to water ratio of 1:1.5. Also estimate the amount of gas that can be produced from the digester and the number of gas burner that can be supplied by the system.
items.rationale: Given: Cattle = 500 heads (at 14 kg manure/day-head and 0.03 m³ biogas/kg manure); retention time RT = 25 days; manure-to-water ratio = 1:1.5; substrate density = 1,000 kg/m³; standard burner consumption = 6 m³/day (0.25 m³/hr × 24 hr/day). Calculations: Manure weight = 500 × 14 = 7,000 kg/day (7 m³/day); slurry volume = 7 × (1 + 1.5) = 17.5 m³/day; digester size = 17.5 × 25 = 437.5 m³; daily gas production = 7,000 × 0.03 = 210 m³/day; number of burners = 210 m³/day ÷ 6 m³/day-burner = 35 burners. Answer = 35 burners

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A combine harvester, with 3-meter-wide effective width, passes the field at a speed of 4 kph. If the field efficiency of the machine is 70%, what is the field capacity of the harvester?
items.rationale: Given: Effective width W = 3 m; speed V = 4 kph; field efficiency Ef = 70% = 0.70. Formula: Theoretical field capacity Ct = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 3 × 4 = 1.20 ha/hr; Effective field capacity Ce = Ct × Ef = 1.20 × 0.70 = 0.84 ha per hr. Answer = 0.84 ha per hr

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A five-row reaper, with a spacing of 30 cm per row, is harvesting at a speed of 2 kph. The field efficiency of the reaper is 70%. If the specific draft of the machine is 2 kg per row, what is the power output of the reaper?
items.rationale: Given: Rows = 5; specific draft = 2 kg/row; speed V = 2 kph = (2 × 1,000)/3,600 = 0.5556 m/s. Total draft F = 5 × 2 kg = 10 kgf. Formula: Power output P = (F × V) / 76.2 = (10 × 0.5556) / 76.2 = 0.0729 hp ≈ 0.073 hp (equivalent to 54.5 W; note: effective field capacity is 0.1 × 1.5 m × 2 kph × 0.70 = 0.21 ha/hr). Answer = 0.073 hp

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A 6-meter wide harvester is harvesting corn at a rate of 100 kg per minute. The effective width of the machine is 90% of its width. If it runs at a speed of 2.5 kph, what is the effective field capacity and harvesting rate of the machine in tons per hectare? Assume a machine field efficiency of 70%.
items.rationale: Given: Width = 6 m; effective width W = 0.90 × 6 = 5.4 m; speed V = 2.5 kph; Ef = 0.70; mass rate = 100 kg/min = 6,000 kg/hr = 6 tons/hr. Formula: Effective field capacity Ce = 0.1 × W × V × Ef = 0.1 × 5.4 × 2.5 × 0.70 = 0.945 ha/hr; Harvesting rate = (6 tons/hr) ÷ (0.945 ha/hr) = 6.35 ≈ 6.3 tons per hectare. Answer = 6.3 tons per hectare

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: Compute the apparent air velocity in a 1-ton-capacity flat-bed dryer having a dimension of 2.4 m × 2.4 m square bin. The specific airflow rate of the dryer is 50 m³ per minute of air per m³ of grain. Assume a density of grain of 500 kg/m³.
items.rationale: Given: Grain mass = 1 ton = 1,000 kg; grain density = 500 kg/m³; bin area A = 2.4 m × 2.4 m = 5.76 m²; specific airflow = 50 m³/(min·m³). Formula: Grain volume = 1,000 / 500 = 2 m³; total airflow Q = 50 × 2 = 100 m³/min; apparent air velocity Vapp = Q / A = 100 / 5.76 = 17.36 m/min. Answer = 17.36 m/min

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A plow requires a drawbar pull of 253 kg. If the plow has an average speed of 5 km/hr, what is the drawbar horsepower of the plow?
items.rationale: Given: Drawbar pull (from preceding linked problem) F = 253 kg; speed V = 5 km/hr = (5 × 1,000)/3,600 = 1.3889 m/s. Formula: DHP = (F × V) / 76.2 = (253 × 1.3889) / 76.2 = 4.61 hp ≈ 4.6 hp. Answer = 4.6 hp

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A three-bottom disk plow is plowing at a speed of 8 kph. The effective width per plow bottom is 25 cm. If the plowing efficiency is 80%, what is the theoretical and effective field capacity of the implement.
items.rationale: Given: Number of bottoms = 3; width per bottom = 25 cm = 0.25 m (total width W = 3 × 0.25 = 0.75 m); speed V = 8 kph; field efficiency Ef = 80% = 0.80. Formula: Theoretical field capacity Ct = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 0.75 × 8 = 0.60 ha/hr; Effective field capacity Ce = Ct × Ef = 0.60 × 0.80 = 0.48 ha/hr. Answer = 0.48 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: Also compute the drawbar horsepower of the implement if it running at a speed of 20 kph.
items.rationale: Given: From preceding linked problem, offset disk harrow width = 3 m and specific draft = 89 kg/m, so draft F = 3 × 89 = 267 kg; speed V = 20 kph = (20 × 1,000)/3,600 = 5.5556 m/s. Formula: DHP = (F × V) / 76.2 = (267 × 5.5556) / 76.2 = 19.47 hp ≈ 19.5 hp. Answer = 19.5 hp

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A power tiller was tested on a 10 m wide plot. During the test, the machine made 22 rounds to complete the plowing operation using two-0.3 m diameter disk plow. What is the average swath of the power tiller?
items.rationale: Given: Plot width W = 10 m; number of rounds N = 22 rounds (1 round = 2 passes, so total passes = 2 × 22 = 44). Formula: Average swath S = W / (2 × N) = 10 m / (2 × 22) = 10 / 44 = 0.227 m ≈ 0.23 m. Answer = 0.23 m

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: The effective width of cut of a single bottom moldboard plow drawn by a power tiller is 10 cm. If the machine will be used to plow a 2 hectare farm, what is the total distance that would be traveled by the machine in order to accomplished the task?
items.rationale: Given: Effective width of cut W = 10 cm = 0.10 m; area A = 2 ha = 2 × 10,000 m² = 20,000 m². Formula: Distance D = A / W = 20,000 m² / 0.10 m = 200,000 m = 200 km. Answer = 200 km

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: What size of heavy-duty offset-disk harrow should be selected if the tractor to be used operates at 5 kph. Assume a 75% field efficiency and an 8-hour working day.
items.rationale: Given: From preceding linked problem, Area A = 200 ha and tilling period Pt = 30 days; operating time OT = 8 hr/day; field efficiency Ef = 0.75; tractor speed V = 5 kph. Formula: Required theoretical field capacity Ct = A / (Pt × OT × Ef) = 200 / (30 × 8 × 0.75) = 1.111 ha/hr; Width W = Ct / (0.1 × V) = 1.111 / (0.1 × 5) = 2.22 m ≈ 2.2 m. Answer = 2.2 m

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: Turning and other idle time is 10% of the effective operating time while removing field obstruction and clogging is 15 min/ha. What is the theoretical and effective field capacity of the machine? What is the time lost in turning and other idle time per hectare of the reaper?
items.rationale: Given: From preceding linked problem, machine width = 1.2 m, effective width We = 1.0 m, speed V = 3 kph; time lost in dike crossing = 5 min/ha, repair = 10 min/ha, obstruction/clogging = 15 min/ha; turning/idle time = 10% of effective operating time. Formula: Using effective width, effective operating rate = 0.1 × 1.0 × 3 = 0.30 ha/hr (or 60 / 0.30 = 200 min/ha); turning and idle time loss = 0.10 × 200 min/ha = 20 min/ha. Answer = 20 min/ha

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A farmer wishes to spray his cotton plantation at a rate of 300 gallons per hectare. Sixteen nozzles, 18 inches apart will be used. The foward speed of the tractor will be 5 kph. Compute the field capacity of the sprayer in hectare per hour. What is the required pump capacity for the sprayer?
items.rationale: Given: Number of nozzles = 16; nozzle spacing = 18 in; total boom width W = 16 × 18 in × 0.0254 m/in = 7.3152 m; speed V = 5 kph; application rate = 300 gal/ha. Formula: Field capacity FC = 0.1 × W × V = 0.1 × 7.3152 × 5 = 3.6576 ≈ 3.66 ha/hr (required pump capacity = 300 gal/ha × 3.6576 ha/hr = 1,097 gal/hr = 18.3 gpm). Answer = 3.66 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: How many hectares would a tractor pulling a three-disk plow with a 12-inch cut per disk be able to plow in one day (16 hours operation) at a speed of 4 kph, assuming a total time loss of 30%?
items.rationale: Given: From preceding linked problem, 3 disks at 12 in/disk (W = 3 × 12 in × 0.0254 m/in = 0.9144 m) and speed V = 4 kph; operating time = 16 hr/day; time loss = 30% (Ef = 0.70). Formula: Effective field capacity EFC = 0.1 × W × V × Ef = 0.1 × 0.9144 × 4 × 0.70 = 0.2560 ha/hr; Area per day = 0.2560 ha/hr × 16 hr/day = 4.096 ≈ 4.10 ha/day. Answer = 4.10 ha/day

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: How many days are required to plow a 500-hectare farm using ten units of a tractor pulling a three-disk plow (12 inches per disk) operating at 4 kph for 16 hours per day with a total time loss of 30%?
items.rationale: Given: Farm area A = 500 ha; number of tractor-plow units N = 10; capacity per unit (from A1-1204) = 4.0965 ha/day. Formula: Time = A / (N × capacity) = 500 ha / (10 × 4.0965 ha/day) = 12.21 days ≈ 12.2 days. Answer = 12.2 days

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A tandem disk harrow has 20 disk spaces, a disk spacing of 300 mm, and a disk diameter of 400 mm. What is the cutting width of the machine?
items.rationale: Given: From preceding linked problem, number of disk spaces N = 20, disk spacing S = 300 mm, disk diameter D = 400 mm. Formula: Cutting width W = (0.95 × N × S + 1.2 × D) / 1,000 = [0.95(20)(300) + 1.2(400)] / 1,000 = (5,700 + 480) / 1,000 = 6.18 m. Answer = 6.18 m

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: Assume a field efficiency of 90%. The harrow has 24 pieces of 30-cm disk spaced at 20 cm.
items.rationale: Given: Tandem disk harrow with 24 disks (N = 24 - 1 = 23 spaces), disk diameter D = 30 cm, spacing S = 20 cm, field efficiency Ef = 0.90, and speed (from preceding linked problem) V = 10 kph. Formula: Effective width We = 0.95(23)(20) + 1.2(30) = 473 cm = 4.73 m; Theoretical field capacity Ct = 0.1 × 4.73 × 10 = 4.73 ha/hr; Effective field capacity Ce = 4.73 × 0.90 = 4.257 ≈ 4.26 ha/hr. Answer = 4.26 ha/hr

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: How many grams of cotton seeds are required per row for a hectare assuming that a row spacing and plant spacing for the seeds are set at 0.20 m and 0.50 m, respectively? The seeding rate is 10 kg/ha.
items.rationale: Given: Seeding rate = 10 kg/ha = 10,000 g/ha; row spacing Sr = 0.20 m; standard 1-ha square field = 100 m × 100 m. Formula: Number of rows = 100 m / 0.20 m = 500 rows; Seeds per row = 10,000 g / 500 rows = 20 g (note: if computed per hill of 0.20 m × 0.50 m, seed required is 0.1 g/hill). Answer = 20 g

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A tractor wheel with a diameter of 2 meters develops a wheel torque of 378.45 N·m. What is the force available at the wheel of the tractor?
items.rationale: Given: Wheel diameter D = 2 m, so radius R = 2 m / 2 = 1 m; wheel torque (from preceding linked problem) T = 378.45 N·m. Formula: F = T / R = 378.45 N·m / 1 m = 378.45 N ≈ 378.4 N. Answer = 378.4 N

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A tractor wheel with a diameter of 2 meters completes 2.5 revolutions over a reference no-load distance of 20 meters. What is the percentage slip of the tractor?
items.rationale: Given: Wheel diameter D = 2 m; revolutions N = 2.5 rev; reference no-load distance An = 20 m. Formula: Loaded/geometric distance AL = π × D × N = π × 2 × 2.5 = 15.708 m; Percentage slip = [(An - AL) / An] × 100% = [(20 - 15.708) / 20] × 100% = 21.46% ≈ 21.5%. Answer = 21.5%

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A tractor weighing 2.5 tons (2,500 kg) is running on deep mud soil with a coefficient of rolling resistance of 0.25. What is the rolling resistance of the tractor?
items.rationale: Given: Tractor weight W = 2.5 tons = 2,500 kg; coefficient of rolling resistance in deep mud Cr = 0.25. Formula: R = Cr × W = 0.25 × 2,500 kg = 625 kgf. Answer = 625 kgf

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A machine has a power output of 50 W and an efficiency of 30%. What is the required power input (rounded to 2 significant figures)?
items.rationale: Note: The problem statement was missing from the source item (only the header appeared). From the source solution: Given power output Pout = 50 W and efficiency = 30%. Formula: Pin = Pout / Efficiency = 50 W / 0.30 = 166.7 W ≈ 170 W (rounded to 2 significant figures). Answer = 170 W

items.subtopic: 1.4 Agricultural and Biosystems Automation, Instrumentation and Control System
items.question: A biogas system has a daily gas production of 2.4 m³ and a gas holder volume of 1.5 m³. What is the gas holder capacity as a percentage of daily gas production?
items.rationale: Given: Daily gas production G = 2.4 m³; gas holder volume (from the source solution) Vg = 1.5 m³. Formula: Gas holder capacity (%) = (Vg / G) × 100% = (1.5 m³ / 2.4 m³) × 100% = 62.5%. Answer = 62.5%

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Degree of freedom with replications: A single-factor experiment using completely randomized experimental design results to the following statistical values: treatment sum of squares of 2,510.5, error mean square error of 13.4, error degrees of freedom of 12 and total degrees of freedom of 14. How many treatments are involved?
items.rationale: Given: Total degrees of freedom df_total = 14; error degrees of freedom df_error = 12. Formula: Treatment degrees of freedom df_tr = df_total - df_error = 14 - 12 = 2; Number of treatments t = df_tr + 1 = 2 + 1 = 3. Answer = 3

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: An minihydro project, having a project life of 8 years, has the following data: total investment of Php20 million, total benefits of Php100 million and total costs of Php60 million. What is the project’s annual Return on Investment? Choose only ONE best answer.
items.rationale: Given: Project life n = 8 years; total investment I = Php 20M; total benefits B = Php 100M; total costs C = Php 60M. Formula: Net benefit = B - C = 100M - 60M = Php 40M; Annual net benefit = 40M / 8 years = Php 5M/yr; Annual ROI = (Annual net benefit / I) × 100% = (5M / 20M) × 100% = 25%. Answer = 25%

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Determine the Net Present Value of a 3-year root crops project with investment expenses at the start of the project of Php8.2M. The discounted cash flows for the end of years 1, 2, and 3 are -Php1.6M, Php 2.5M and Php8.8M.
items.rationale: Given: Initial investment (t = 0) = -Php8.2M; discounted cash flows for years 1, 2, and 3 = -Php1.6M, +Php2.5M, and +Php8.8M. Formula: NPV = Σ DCF = -8.2 + (-1.6) + 2.5 + 8.8 = Php1.5M. Answer = Php1.5M

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: The net cash flow of the cassava processing venture at project start is -10 million pesos due to loan at which revenue is not materialized yet. Discount rate is 10%. What is the value of the discounted cash flow in million pesos at project start?
items.rationale: Given: Net cash flow at project start (t = 0) NCF = -10 million pesos; discount rate r = 10% = 0.10. Formula: DCF = NCF / (1 + r)^t = -10 / (1 + 0.10)^0 = -10 / 1 = -10 million pesos. Answer = -10

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: As part of project planning, you need to estimate the discounted value of costs of a 3-year vegetable project. It has the following costs for years 0, 1, 2 and 3 in million Php: 5, 1, 2 and 3, respectively. What is its Present Value of Costs? Assume a combined discount and inflation rate of 10%.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: You are tasked to evaluate the financial feasibility of 3-year AFMESC project. It has the following costs for years 0, 1, 2 and 3 in million Php: 5, 1, 2 and 3, respectively. Likewise, the same project has the following benefits for years 0, 1, 2 and 3 in million Php: 0, 6, 8 and 9, respectively. What is its Net Present Value and indicate if the project is feasible or not based on NPV? Use the NEDA published Social Discount Rate (SDR) of 10%. Choose only ONE best answer.
items.rationale: Given: Costs (yrs 0–3) = 5, 1, 2, 3 M Php; Benefits (yrs 0–3) = 0, 6, 8, 9 M Php; r = 10% = 0.10. Formula: PVB = 0/(1.1)^0 + 6/(1.1)^1 + 8/(1.1)^2 + 9/(1.1)^3 = 0 + 5.455 + 6.612 + 6.762 = Php 18.828M. PVC = 5/(1.1)^0 + 1/(1.1)^1 + 2/(1.1)^2 + 3/(1.1)^3 = 5 + 0.909 + 1.653 + 2.254 = Php 9.816M. NPV = PVB - PVC = 18.828 - 9.816 = Php 9.012M ≈ Php 9M. Since NPV > 0, the project is financially feasible. Answer = Php 9M, financially feasible.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: As part of feasibility study preparation, you need to find the discounted revenue of a 3-year fishery project. It has the following benefits for years 0, 1, 2 and 3 in million Php: 0, 6, 8 and 9, respectively. What is its present value of benefits? Discount plus inflation rate is stable at 10%.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: Using straight line depreciation method, what is the book value at the end of year 2 of a tractor purchased at Php 2,200,000 if its life span is 10 years? Salvage value is 10%.
items.rationale: Given: Initial cost C = Php 2,200,000; lifespan n = 10 yrs; salvage value S = 0.10 × 2,200,000 = Php 220,000. Formula: Annual depreciation D = (C - S) / n = (2,200,000 - 220,000) / 10 = Php 198,000/yr. Book value at year 2: BV_2 = C - 2D = 2,200,000 - 2(198,000) = Php 1,804,000 ≈ Php 1,800,000 (rounded to 2 significant figures matching the given cost). Answer = Php 1,800,000.

items.subtopic: 1.5 Project Management, Feasibility Study Preparation/Evaluation, Research, Development and Extension, and Information System on ABE
items.question: A banana production and export project is being evaluated for financial feasibility. At 11% annual discount rate, it has the following feasibility indicators: net present value of 1.8 billion pesos and internal rate of return of 58%. If
items.answer: Feasible — if it is feasible at 11% discount rate, the more it will be feasible at 10%
items.rationale: Given: At r = 11%, NPV = Php 1.8 billion (> 0) and IRR = 58% (> 11%). For normal cash flows, NPV increases as the discount rate decreases (and IRR = 58% exceeds the 10% NEDA Social Discount Rate).
