Therefore, if the project is already feasible at 11%, it will be even more financially feasible at a lower discount rate of 10%. (Note: the original question stem is truncated at 'If', referring to evaluation at the 10% discount rate.) Answer = Feasible — if it is feasible at 11% discount rate, the more it will be feasible at 10%.
choices: Not feasible — lowering the discount rate from 11% to 10% makes NPV negative
Feasible — if it is feasible at 11% discount rate, the more it will be feasible at 10%
Feasible only at 11% — lowering the discount rate to 10% makes it less feasible
Indeterminate — IRR must be less than the 10% discount rate to be feasible

areas.title: Land and Water Resources Engineering
areas.description: Hydrology, Irrigation & Drainage Engineering, Soil & Water Conservation, Aquaculture Engineering, Agri/Fishery Sciences, Mathematics & Basic Engineering.

items.question: An irrigation centrifugal pump is rated at 150 gallons per minute (GPM). What is its equivalent discharge in liters per second (L/s)?
items.rationale: Q = 150 gal/min × 3.7854 L/gal ÷ 60 s/min = 9.46 L/s.

choiceExplanations.5.68 L/s: Corresponds to 90 GPM, not 150 GPM, under the 0.06309 L/s per GPM conversion factor.
choiceExplanations.9.46 L/s: Correct — Multiplying 150 GPM by 3.7854 L/gal and dividing by 60 s/min yields 9.46 L/s.
choiceExplanations.15.00 L/s: Incorrectly divides 150 GPM by 10 instead of applying the 0.06309 L/s per GPM factor.
choiceExplanations.12.62 L/s: Corresponds to 200 GPM (200 × 0.06309 L/s), overestimating the rated 150 GPM pump discharge.

items.question: Water flows through a rectangular irrigation canal 1.2 m wide and 0.6 m deep at a mean velocity of 0.85 m/s. What is the discharge Q?

choiceExplanations.0.72 m³/s: Represents the cross-sectional flow area (1.2 m × 0.6 m = 0.72 m²), omitting velocity.
choiceExplanations.0.61 m³/s: Correct — Using Q = A × V = (1.2 m × 0.6 m) × 0.85 m/s gives 0.612 m³/s, or 0.61 m³/s.
choiceExplanations.1.02 m³/s: Equals canal width times velocity (1.2 × 0.85), omitting the 0.6 m flow depth.
choiceExplanations.0.51 m³/s: Equals flow depth times velocity (0.6 × 0.85), omitting the 1.2 m canal width.

items.question: A trapezoidal canal has a bottom width b = 2.0 m, flow depth d = 1.0 m, and side slope z = 1.5 (H:V). What is its hydraulic radius R?

choiceExplanations.0.75 m: Overestimates hydraulic radius by using an incorrect wetted perimeter rather than 5.61 m.
choiceExplanations.0.91 m: Results from dividing area by top width (5.0 m) or using a mismatched rectangular perimeter.
choiceExplanations.0.48 m: Underestimates hydraulic radius, as 3.5 m² divided by 5.61 m wetted perimeter exceeds 0.48 m.
choiceExplanations.0.62 m: Correct — With area A = 3.5 m² and wetted perimeter P = 2 + 2√(1 + 1.5²) = 5.61 m, R = A/P = 0.62 m.

items.question: A concrete-lined canal (n = 0.015) has a hydraulic radius R = 0.64 m and bed slope S = 0.0009. Using Manning's equation, what is the mean flow velocity?

choiceExplanations.1.48 m/s: Correct — Using Manning's formula V = (1/n)R^(2/3)S^(1/2) with n = 0.015, R = 0.64 m, and S = 0.0009 yields 1.48 m/s.
choiceExplanations.0.95 m/s: Underestimates velocity, inconsistent with R^(2/3) = 0.743 and S^(1/2) = 0.03 divided by n = 0.015.
choiceExplanations.2.45 m/s: Overestimates velocity, as the 0.0009 bed slope and 0.015 roughness limit flow to ~1.48 m/s.
choiceExplanations.1.92 m/s: Results from omitting the 2/3 exponent on R or misapplying the slope term in Manning's equation.

items.question: What is the optimal bottom width b of the most hydraulically efficient rectangular open channel carrying a cross-sectional area of 8 m²?
items.rationale: For the most efficient rectangular channel, b = 2d, so A = 2d² = 8 → d = 2.0 m and b = 2(2.0) = 4.0 m.

choiceExplanations.2.83 m: Corresponds to a square cross-section (b = d = √8 ≈ 2.83 m), not the optimal b = 2d rectangle.
choiceExplanations.5.66 m: Corresponds to 2√8, mistakenly doubling a square's side length instead of setting b = 2d.
choiceExplanations.4.0 m: Correct — For a most efficient rectangular channel (b = 2d), A = 2d² = 8 m² gives d = 2 m and b = 4.0 m.
choiceExplanations.2.0 m: Represents the optimal flow depth d rather than the optimal bottom width b = 2d.

items.question: For the most hydraulically efficient trapezoidal channel (half-hexagon, θ = 60°), what is the relationship between hydraulic radius R and flow depth d?
items.rationale: In any most hydraulically efficient rectangular or trapezoidal open channel, R = d/2.

choiceExplanations.R = d / 2: Correct — In a most efficient trapezoidal (half-hexagon) channel, the hydraulic radius equals half the flow depth (R = d/2).
choiceExplanations.R = d / 3: Underestimates hydraulic radius; R = d/3 does not hold for a half-hexagon section.
choiceExplanations.R = d / 1: Overestimates hydraulic radius, as wetted perimeter always exceeds area divided by flow depth here.
choiceExplanations.R = d / 4: Half of the true hydraulic radius, underestimating the hydraulic efficiency of a half-hexagon section.

items.question: In sandy or very loose soils where embankment stability is critical, what is the flattest recommended side slope (H:V) commonly cited for unlined earth canals?
items.rationale: Very loose sand or peat soils require flat side slopes up to 3:1 or 4:1 (H:V) to prevent sloughing and bank collapse.

choiceExplanations.2:1: Suitable for ordinary loamy or firm soils, but too steep for very loose sandy embankments.
choiceExplanations.1:1: Recommended for stiff clay or stable earth, which would slump in loose sandy soils.
choiceExplanations.4:1: Correct — A 4:1 (4H:1V) side slope is the flattest recommended grade for unlined canals in very loose sandy soils.
choiceExplanations.0.5:1: Very steep slope reserved for rock or concrete-lined canals, unstable in unlined earth.

items.question: Which irrigation conveyance structure carries canal water under pressure beneath a road, railway, or natural depression?
items.rationale: An inverted siphon conveys water below an obstruction using closed conduit flow under hydrostatic head.

choiceExplanations.Flume: An elevated open channel supported on trestles to carry water above a depression or crossing.
choiceExplanations.Drop structure: A hydraulic structure that conveys canal water steeply downward to a lower elevation without erosion.
choiceExplanations.Inverted siphon: Correct — An inverted siphon is a closed pressure conduit carrying canal flow beneath roads, railways, or depressions.
choiceExplanations.Turnout: An intake or outlet structure that diverts controlled water from a main canal into lateral ditches.

items.question: A concrete gravity dam primarily resists horizontal hydrostatic water pressure through which mechanism?
items.answer: Its own massive weight acting downward
items.rationale: Gravity dams rely on their own self-weight to resist overturning and sliding forces from impounded water.
choices: Steel tension cables anchored in soil
Its own massive weight acting downward
Arch thrust transferred into canyon walls

choiceExplanations.Steel tension cables anchored in soil: Describes anchored or post-tensioned tiebacks, not the primary resisting mechanism of a gravity dam.
choiceExplanations.Its own massive weight acting downward: Correct — A concrete gravity dam relies primarily on its own dead weight to resist sliding and overturning from hydrostatic pressure.
choiceExplanations.Buttress piers only: Describes a buttress dam, which transfers water load through inclined slabs onto spaced piers.
choiceExplanations.Arch thrust transferred into canyon wall: Describes an arch dam, which transmits hydrostatic loads horizontally into solid canyon rock abutments.

items.question: What is the primary purpose of a Small Water Impounding Project (SWIP) in Philippine agricultural watersheds?
items.answer: Storing rainfall and runoff behind a small earth dam for supplemental irrigation, flood control, and aquaculture
items.rationale: SWIPs are earth-fill dams (typically 5–15 m high) serving 25–150 ha of upland/rainfed farms.
choices: Pumping deep geothermal steam for electricity
Storing rainfall and runoff behind a small earth dam for supplemental irrigation, flood control, and aquaculture

choiceExplanations.Desalinating seawater for coastal cities: Describes coastal desalination plants, unrelated to inland agricultural watershed SWIPs.
choiceExplanations.Draining peatlands for urban housing: Describes land reclamation drainage, opposite to impounding runoff for farm water storage.
choiceExplanations.Pumping deep geothermal steam for electr: Describes geothermal power generation, not surface water impoundment for agriculture.
choiceExplanations.Storing rainfall and runoff behind a sma: Correct — Under Philippine DA/BSWM programs, a SWIP impounds rainfall and runoff behind a small earth dam for irrigation, flood control, and aquaculture.

items.question: An aquifer bounded both above and below by impermeable confining layers (aquicludes) where groundwater is under pressure greater than atmospheric is called a:
items.rationale: In a confined aquifer, water rises above the top of the aquifer to the piezometric surface when tapped by a well.

choiceExplanations.Vadose zone: The unsaturated soil zone above the water table containing both air and water.
choiceExplanations.Unconfined aquifer: An aquifer with a free water table exposed to atmospheric pressure and no upper aquiclude.
choiceExplanations.Perched water table: A localized saturated zone held above the main water table by a small impermeable lens.
choiceExplanations.Confined (artesian) aquifer: Correct — A confined aquifer lies between upper and lower aquicludes, keeping its groundwater under pressure above atmospheric.

items.subtopic: 2.0 Orographic vs. Frontal vs. Convective Rainfall
items.question: Which rainfall lifting mechanism occurs when moist air masses are forced upward as they encounter a mountain barrier?
items.rationale: Orographic lifting is mountain-facilitated; convective lifting is caused by localized thermal heating; frontal lifting occurs along warm/cold air-mass boundaries.

choiceExplanations.Stratiform drizzle: Light, uniform precipitation from widespread layered stratus clouds rather than mountain lifting.
choiceExplanations.Frontal (cyclonic) precipitation: Rainfall formed when warm moist air rises over a cooler air mass along a weather front.
choiceExplanations.Orographic precipitation: Correct — Orographic precipitation occurs when moist air is forced upward over mountain barriers, cooling adiabatically and condensing.
choiceExplanations.Convective precipitation: Intense, localized rainfall caused by surface solar heating making warm air rise buoyantly.

items.question: A spillway is designed for a 25-year return period flood. What is the probability that this design flood will be equaled or exceeded in any single year?
items.rationale: Annual exceedance probability P = 1 / T = 1 / 25 = 0.04 = 4%.

choiceExplanations.2%: Corresponds to a 50-year return period flood (1/50), not a 25-year design flood.
choiceExplanations.10%: Corresponds to a 10-year return period flood (1/10), much more frequent than 25 years.
choiceExplanations.4%: Correct — Annual exceedance probability equals the reciprocal of the return period, P = 1/T = 1/25 = 4%.
choiceExplanations.25%: Corresponds to a 4-year return period flood (1/4), mistakenly equating T directly to percent.

items.question: Using the Rational Formula (Q = 0.00278 C I A), estimate the peak runoff from a 15-ha watershed with runoff coefficient C = 0.40 and rainfall intensity I = 50 mm/hr.

choiceExplanations.1.25 m³/s: Overestimates peak runoff, corresponding to C = 0.60 or an incorrect watershed area.
choiceExplanations.2.10 m³/s: Roughly equals Q without multiplying by the 0.40 runoff coefficient (0.00278 × 50 × 15 ≈ 2.09).
choiceExplanations.0.83 m³/s: Correct — Applying Q = 0.00278 C I A = 0.00278 × 0.40 × 50 × 15 yields 0.834 m³/s, or 0.83 m³/s.
choiceExplanations.0.42 m³/s: Half of the actual peak runoff, corresponding to half the area or half the C value.

items.question: If reference evapotranspiration (ETo) is 5.5 mm/day and a mid-season rice crop has a crop coefficient Kc = 1.20, what is the crop evapotranspiration (ETc)?
items.rationale: ETc = Kc × ETo = 1.20 × 5.5 mm/day = 6.60 mm/day.

choiceExplanations.4.58 mm/day: Erroneously divides ETo by Kc (5.5 / 1.20) instead of multiplying them.
choiceExplanations.5.50 mm/day: Equals the reference evapotranspiration (ETo) alone, ignoring the 1.20 crop coefficient.
choiceExplanations.7.20 mm/day: Overestimates ETc by assuming an ETo of 6.0 mm/day instead of 5.5 mm/day.
choiceExplanations.6.60 mm/day: Correct — Crop evapotranspiration equals Kc × ETo = 1.20 × 5.5 mm/day = 6.60 mm/day.

items.question: A soil has a Field Capacity (FC) of 24% and Permanent Wilting Point (PWP) of 16% by weight. What is its present moisture content if 25% of its available moisture (AM) has been used?
items.rationale: AM = FC − PWP = 24% − 16% = 8%; Moisture used = 0.25 × 8% = 2%; Present MC = 24% − 2% = 22%.

choiceExplanations.18%: Represents 75% available moisture depleted (24% − 6%), rather than 25% depleted.
choiceExplanations.23%: Represents only 12.5% available moisture depleted (24% − 1%), half the stated depletion.
choiceExplanations.22%: Correct — Available moisture is 24% − 16% = 8%, and depleting 25% (2%) leaves 24% − 2% = 22%.
choiceExplanations.20%: Represents 50% available moisture depleted (24% − 4%), twice the stated 25% depletion.

items.question: A moist soil sample weighs 140 g before oven drying and 112 g after oven drying at 105°C. What is its moisture content on a dry-weight basis?

choiceExplanations.20.0%: Calculates wet-basis moisture content (28 g / 140 g) instead of dry-weight basis.
choiceExplanations.25.0%: Correct — Dry-basis moisture content equals water mass divided by oven-dry soil mass: (140 − 112) / 112 = 25.0%.
choiceExplanations.28.0%: Represents the mass of evaporated water in grams (28 g), not the moisture percentage.
choiceExplanations.32.5%: Overestimates moisture content, inconsistent with 28 g of water over 112 g of dry soil.

items.question: What is the definition of Real Specific Gravity (particle density ratio) of soil?
items.answer: Ratio of the oven-dry weight of soil solids to the weight of an equal volume of water (excluding pore spaces)
items.rationale: Real specific gravity (typically ~2.65 for mineral soils) considers only the solid soil particles, whereas apparent specific gravity includes pore spaces.
choices: Ratio of water mass to dry soil mass
Ratio of pore volume to total soil volume
Ratio of bulk soil weight including pores to an equal volume of water
Ratio of the oven-dry weight of soil solids to the weight of an equal volume of water (excluding pore spaces)

choiceExplanations.Ratio of water mass to dry soil mass: Defines gravimetric soil moisture content on a dry-weight basis, not specific gravity.
choiceExplanations.Ratio of pore volume to total soil volum: Defines soil porosity, which measures void fraction rather than solid particle density.
choiceExplanations.Ratio of bulk soil weight including pore: Defines Apparent Specific Gravity (bulk specific gravity), which includes soil pore spaces.
choiceExplanations.Ratio of the oven-dry weight of soil sol: Correct — Real Specific Gravity compares the oven-dry weight of solid soil particles alone to an equal volume of water.

items.question: Which form of soil water drains downward freely under the pull of gravity between saturation and field capacity?
items.rationale: Gravitational water occupies macropores above field capacity (0 to 1/3 atm) and drains freely downward.

choiceExplanations.Chemically bound water: Water structurally combined within soil minerals, unavailable to plants and retained at 105°C.
choiceExplanations.Capillary water: Water held in soil micropores against gravity by surface tension, serving as plant-available water.
choiceExplanations.Gravitational water: Correct — Gravitational water occupies macropores between saturation and field capacity and drains freely downward under gravity.
choiceExplanations.Hygroscopic water: Tightly adsorbed thin water film around soil particles below wilting point, unavailable to plants.

items.question: If the readily available moisture (RAM) in a crop's root zone is 48 mm and the peak daily crop water use (ETc) is 6 mm/day, what is the irrigation interval?
items.rationale: Irrigation Interval = RAM / ETc = 48 mm ÷ 6 mm/day = 8 days.

choiceExplanations.12 days: Overestimates the interval, corresponding to an ETc of 4 mm/day rather than 6 mm/day.
choiceExplanations.6 days: Equals the daily crop water use rate numerically, not 48 mm divided by 6 mm/day.
choiceExplanations.8 days: Correct — Dividing readily available moisture by peak daily crop use gives 48 mm / (6 mm/day) = 8 days.
choiceExplanations.10 days: Exceeds the safe depletion interval, risking crop water stress after day 8.

items.question: A paddy field has ETc = 6 mm/day, percolation = 2 mm/day, effective rainfall = 1.5 mm/day, and application efficiency = 75%. What is the Farm Irrigation Requirement (FIR)?
items.rationale: NIR = ETc + P − ER = 6 + 2 − 1.5 = 6.5 mm/day; FIR = NIR / Ea = 6.5 / 0.75 = 8.67 mm/day.

choiceExplanations.10.67 mm/day: Omits subtracting the 1.5 mm/day effective rainfall before dividing by 0.75 efficiency ((6 + 2) / 0.75).
choiceExplanations.6.50 mm/day: Represents the net field irrigation requirement (6 + 2 − 1.5), ignoring the 75% application efficiency.
choiceExplanations.7.80 mm/day: Underestimates FIR, failing to match 6.50 mm/day divided by 0.75.
choiceExplanations.8.67 mm/day: Correct — Net requirement is 6 + 2 − 1.5 = 6.5 mm/day, and dividing by 0.75 efficiency yields 8.67 mm/day.

items.subtopic: 2.0 Sprinkler Radius of Throw & Staggered Layout
items.question: In a staggered (triangular) sprinkler layout, why is staggering sprinklers along adjacent laterals often preferred over a square layout in windy areas?
items.answer: It improves distribution uniformity and reduces dry spots between overlapping wetted circles
items.rationale: Staggered/triangular spacing provides more uniform overlap across the field compared to square spacing under wind drift.
choices: It eliminates the need for a pump
It improves distribution uniformity and reduces dry spots between overlapping wetted circles

choiceExplanations.It prevents water evaporation completely: Evaporation still occurs in all overhead sprinkler systems regardless of lateral spacing geometry.
choiceExplanations.It doubles the operating pressure: Operating pressure depends on pump head and nozzle hydraulics, not staggered spacing.
choiceExplanations.It eliminates the need for a pump: Sprinkler systems still require pressurized flow from a pump or high gravity head.
choiceExplanations.It improves distribution uniformity and: Correct — Staggering sprinklers in a triangular pattern creates more uniform overlap and minimizes dry gaps under wind distortion.

items.question: In the Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE), what does 'erosivity' (R factor) refer to?
items.answer: The potential ability of rainfall and runoff to cause soil erosion
items.rationale: Erosivity (R) is a property of rainfall energy and intensity; erodibility (K) is an inherent property of the soil.
choices: The protective effect of crop canopy
The steepness of the field slope
The inherent susceptibility of a soil to detach and wash away
The potential ability of rainfall and runoff to cause soil erosion

choiceExplanations.The protective effect of crop canopy: Refers to the cover and management factor (C factor) in the USLE.
choiceExplanations.The steepness of the field slope: Refers to the slope length and steepness factors (LS) in the USLE.
choiceExplanations.The inherent susceptibility of a soil to: Defines soil erodibility (K factor), not rainfall erosivity.
choiceExplanations.The potential ability of rainfall and ru: Correct — In USLE (A = R·K·L·S·C·P), the R factor quantifies the erosive power of rainfall and runoff.

items.question: Which soil and water conservation practice involves plowing, planting, and cultivating across the slope along lines of equal elevation?
items.rationale: Contour furrows act as miniature dams that slow surface runoff, increase infiltration, and reduce sheet/rill erosion.

choiceExplanations.Deep percolation: Downward movement of water below the crop root zone, not a tillage pattern.
choiceExplanations.Broadcast seeding: Scattering seed uniformly over a field surface rather than cultivating along elevation contours.
choiceExplanations.Contouring (contour farming): Correct — Contouring aligns tillage furrows and crop rows along constant-elevation lines across slopes to slow runoff and curb erosion.
choiceExplanations.Subsoiling: Deep tillage below the plow pan using chisel shanks to break compacted soil layers.

items.question: In a Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS), what is the primary role of a biological filter (biofilter) paired with mechanical aerators?
items.answer: Biofilters convert toxic ammonia (NH₃) into less toxic nitrate via nitrifying bacteria, while aerators maintain dissolved oxygen
items.rationale: Nitrification (NH₃ → NO₂⁻ → NO₃⁻) requires oxygen; aerators sustain DO levels (>5 mg/L) and strip CO₂.
choices: Problematic radiator, stop and cool down engine then check water level
Biofilters convert toxic ammonia (NH₃) into less toxic nitrate via nitrifying bacteria, while aerators maintain dissolved oxygen
Hydraulic gradient or hydraulic grade line

choiceExplanations.Problematic radiator, stop and cool down: Unrelated automotive engine overheating instruction, not an aquaculture RAS biofilter function.
choiceExplanations.Calculate the Weight of Water:: Unrelated engineering calculation prompt fragment, not a biological filtration process.
choiceExplanations.Biofilters convert toxic ammonia (NH₃) i: Correct — In RAS, aerobic nitrifying bacteria in biofilters oxidize toxic NH₃ to NO₂⁻ and NO₃⁻ while aerators supply dissolved oxygen.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic gradient or hydraulic grade li: Unrelated open-channel and pipe-flow hydraulics term, not an RAS water-treatment component.

items.question: Why is agricultural lime (CaCO₃) commonly applied to acidic fishponds before stocking?
items.answer: To raise water/soil pH, buffer alkalinity, and enhance natural plankton productivity
items.rationale: Optimal fishpond pH is 6.5–9.0; liming neutralizes acid sulfate soils and stabilizes alkalinity.
choices: To increase toxic unionized ammonia concentrations
To raise water/soil pH, buffer alkalinity, and enhance natural plankton productivity

choiceExplanations.To deplete dissolved oxygen rapidly: Lime does not strip oxygen; it stabilizes pH to support healthy respiration and plankton.
choiceExplanations.To increase toxic unionized ammonia conc: Raising pH increases toxic NH₃ fractions only when ammonia is elevated, which is not lime's goal.
choiceExplanations.To raise water/soil pH, buffer alkalinit: Correct — Agricultural lime neutralizes acidic pond soils, builds carbonate alkalinity, and frees nutrients to stimulate phytoplankton growth.
choiceExplanations.To sterilize the pond permanently: Agricultural lime adjusts pH gently rather than permanently sterilizing aquatic life.

items.question: In rice physiology, which stage marks the transition from the vegetative phase to the reproductive phase when the microscopic panicle begins forming at the stem tip?
items.rationale: Panicle initiation begins the reproductive phase (~60–65 days before harvest), when water stress is especially damaging; sorghum is noted as a drought-tolerant C4 cereal.

choiceExplanations.Panicle initiation (PI): Correct — Panicle initiation marks the shift from vegetative to reproductive growth as the microscopic panicle forms at the shoot apex.
choiceExplanations.Active tillering: An early-to-mid vegetative stage when new basal shoots (tillers) multiply rapidly before stem elongation.
choiceExplanations.Germination: The initial sprouting stage when the rice seed absorbs water and extends radicle and coleoptile.
choiceExplanations.Hard dough stage: A late ripening stage when grain starch hardens shortly before harvest maturity.

items.question: Which group of microorganisms is numerically the most abundant in agricultural soils, and what is the proper culinary term for meat from a goat?
items.rationale: Bacteria are the most numerous microorganisms in soil (millions to billions per gram); goat meat is called chevon (mutton = sheep, veal = calf).

choiceExplanations.Fungi; Veal: Fungi have high biomass but fewer numbers than bacteria; veal is meat from young calves.
choiceExplanations.Nematodes; Mutton: Nematodes are multicellular microfauna far less numerous than bacteria; mutton is meat from mature sheep.
choiceExplanations.Bacteria; Chevon: Correct — Bacteria are the most numerically abundant microorganisms in agricultural soils, and chevon is the culinary term for goat meat.
choiceExplanations.Protozoa; Venison: Protozoa are single-celled soil predators far fewer than bacteria; venison is meat from deer.

items.question: In differential leveling, a rod reading taken on a point of known elevation (such as a Benchmark) to establish the Height of Instrument (HI) is called a:
items.rationale: HI = Elevation(BM) + BS; Foresight (FS) is a reading taken on a point of unknown elevation.

choiceExplanations.Backsight (BS): Correct — A backsight is a rod reading on a point of known elevation (like a benchmark) used to find HI = Elev + BS.
choiceExplanations.Turning point (TP): An intermediate stable point on which both a foresight and subsequent backsight are taken.
choiceExplanations.Foresight (FS): A rod reading taken on a point of unknown elevation to subtract from HI and find its elevation.
choiceExplanations.Azimuth: A horizontal clockwise angle measured from a reference meridian (usually north), unrelated to vertical leveling.

items.question: What water pressure (in kPa) corresponds to a static pressure head of 12 meters of water (use γ = 9.81 kN/m³)?

choiceExplanations.117.7 kPa: Correct — Multiplying water specific weight γ = 9.81 kN/m³ by 12 m head gives P = 117.72 kPa (117.7 kPa).
choiceExplanations.120.0 kPa: Assumes an approximate unit weight of 10 kN/m³ instead of the specified 9.81 kN/m³.
choiceExplanations.147.2 kPa: Corresponds to a 15-meter pressure head (9.81 × 15), not 12 meters.
choiceExplanations.81.8 kPa: Underestimates hydrostatic pressure, corresponding to roughly an 8.3 m head rather than 12 m.

items.question: One pipe can fill an irrigation tank in 5 hours and a second pipe can fill it in 4 hours, while a drainpipe can empty the full tank in 20 hours. With all three open, how long will it take to fill the tank?

choiceExplanations.2.0 hours: Underestimates fill time by ignoring the drainpipe or overestimating combined inflow rate.
choiceExplanations.3.5 hours: Overestimates fill time, inconsistent with a net fill rate of 8/20 tank per hour.
choiceExplanations.2.5 hours: Correct — Net filling rate is 1/5 + 1/4 − 1/20 = 8/20 = 2/5 tank/hour, so filling takes 2.5 hours.
choiceExplanations.3.0 hours: Overestimates fill time; at 2/5 tank per hour, 3 hours would overflow to 1.2 tanks.

items.question: The sum of the ages of Ariodear and Caesar is 42. If Ariodear is 30 years older than Caesar, how old is Caesar?
items.rationale: Let C = Caesar's age; (C + 30) + C = 42 → 2C = 12 → C = 6 years old.

choiceExplanations.36 years old: Represents Ariodear's age (6 + 30 = 36), not Caesar's age.
choiceExplanations.12 years old: Represents 42 − 30 before dividing by 2 to solve for Caesar's age.
choiceExplanations.18 years old: Overestimates Caesar's age; if Caesar were 18, Ariodear would be 48 and their sum 66.
choiceExplanations.6 years old: Correct — Solving C + (C + 30) = 42 gives 2C = 12, so Caesar is 6 years old.

items.question: A right triangle has legs of 6 m and 8 m and a hypotenuse of 10 m. What is the radius r of the circle inscribed inside the triangle?
items.rationale: Semi-perimeter s = (6+8+10)/2 = 12 m; Area A = ½(6)(8) = 24 m²; Inradius r = A / s = 24 / 12 = 2.0 m.

choiceExplanations.2.5 m: Overestimates inradius; equals a quarter of the 10 m hypotenuse rather than (a + b − c)/2.
choiceExplanations.3.0 m: Equals half the shorter leg (6 m / 2), exceeding the true 2.0 m inradius.
choiceExplanations.1.5 m: Underestimates inradius, inconsistent with r = (a + b − c)/2 = (6 + 8 − 10)/2.
choiceExplanations.2.0 m: Correct — For a right triangle, inradius r = (a + b − c)/2 = (6 + 8 − 10)/2 = 2.0 m.

items.question: Evaluate the definite integral ∫₀^(π/2) sin⁴(x) dx using Wallis's formula.
items.rationale: For even n = 4, Wallis's formula gives [(3 × 1) / (4 × 2)] × (π/2) = (3/8)(π/2) = 3π/16.

choiceExplanations.2π / 13: Incorrect numerator and denominator not produced by Wallis's factorial-product formula for even powers.
choiceExplanations.3π / 14: Incorrect denominator; Wallis's formula yields 4 × 2 × 2 = 16, not 14.
choiceExplanations.3π / 18: Incorrect denominator from miscomputing 4 × 2 × 2 as 18 instead of 16.
choiceExplanations.3π / 16: Correct — By Wallis's formula for n = 4 (even), ∫₀^(π/2) sin⁴(x) dx = (3·1)/(4·2) · (π/2) = 3π/16.

items.question: Find the sample standard deviation of the soil infiltration measurements: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 mm/hr.
items.rationale: Mean = 8; sum of squared deviations = 16 + 4 + 0 + 4 + 16 = 40; s = √[40 / (5 − 1)] = √10 ≈ 3.16 mm/hr.

choiceExplanations.2.83 mm/hr: Represents the population standard deviation √(40/5) = √8, using N instead of N − 1.
choiceExplanations.4.00 mm/hr: Overestimates standard deviation, equal to half the total range (12 − 4) / 2.
choiceExplanations.8.00 mm/hr: Represents the sample mean (8.00 mm/hr) or population variance, not the standard deviation.
choiceExplanations.3.16 mm/hr: Correct — With mean 8 and sum of squared deviations 40, sample standard deviation is √(40/(5−1)) = √10 ≈ 3.16 mm/hr.

items.question: Area which contributes runoff or drains water into the reservoir (AMTEC, 2016 - PAES 609:2016).

choiceExplanations.Watershed: Correct — Under PAES 609:2016, a watershed is the land area that contributes runoff or drains water into a reservoir.
choiceExplanations.River basin: A larger regional drainage system composed of a main river and all its tributary watersheds.
choiceExplanations.Runoff reservoir: A storage impoundment that holds captured runoff rather than the contributing land area itself.
choiceExplanations.Drainage divide: The topographic ridge or boundary separating adjacent watersheds, not the contributing area itself.

items.question: The study of the biological, chemical, and physical features of lakes and other bodies of fresh water (Oxford Languages, 2022).

choiceExplanations.Meteorology: The atmospheric science studying weather processes and short-term atmospheric conditions.
choiceExplanations.Limnology: Correct — Limnology is the scientific study of the biological, chemical, and physical characteristics of lakes and other freshwater bodies.
choiceExplanations.Hydrometeorology: The interdisciplinary study of water and energy transfer between land surfaces and the lower atmosphere.
choiceExplanations.Hydrology: The broader science of Earth's water occurrence, distribution, movement, and properties across the hydrologic cycle.

items.question: A branch of meteorology and hydrology that studies the transfer of water and energy between the land surface and the lower atmosphere (Wikipedia, 2022).

choiceExplanations.Hydrology: Focuses broadly on terrestrial and subsurface water occurrence, circulation, and distribution rather than atmospheric exchange.
choiceExplanations.Meteorology: Focuses on atmospheric physics, weather systems, and forecasting rather than land-atmosphere water transfer.
choiceExplanations.Limnology: Studies the biological, chemical, and physical features of lakes and inland freshwater bodies.

items.question: Based on PhilMech’s 2011 and 2012 agricultural statistics of Asian countries, the Philippine farm mechanization showed an upswing trend which recorded an average mechanization level of 1.23 hp/ha; rice and corn farms registered the highest level of available farm power at 2.31 hp/ha (Philippine Official Gazette, 2013). items.question: rate of evapotranspiration equal to or smaller than predicted crop evapotranspiration as affected by the level of available soil water, salinity, field size or other causes

choiceExplanations.Standard crop evapotranspiration: Crop evapotranspiration under optimal, well-watered, disease-free conditions without environmental or management limitations.

choiceExplanations.Aquiclude: An impermeable or very low-permeability formation that may contain water but does not transmit it significantly.
choiceExplanations.Aquifer: Correct — An aquifer is a saturated permeable geologic formation that stores and transmits enough water for economic pumping.
choiceExplanations.Aquifuge: A dense, non-porous rock formation that neither contains nor transmits groundwater.

items.question: rate of water loss by evaporation from an open water surface of a pan

choiceExplanations.Pan evaporation: Correct — Pan evaporation directly measures the rate of water loss from the open water surface of an evaporation pan.
choiceExplanations.Lake evaporation: Water loss from a large natural or artificial reservoir, typically estimated by applying a coefficient to pan data.
choiceExplanations.Actual evaporation: The real-world water vapor loss occurring from soil or water surfaces under prevailing moisture limits.

items.question: rate of evapotranspiration from a reference surface which is a hypothetical reference crop with an assumed crop height of 0.2 m, a fixed surface resistance of 70 s/m and an albedo of 0.23

choiceExplanations.Actual crop evapotranspiration: Evapotranspiration reduced below potential rates by water stress, salinity, pests, or field conditions.

items.question: aquifer which has water table serving as upper surface of the zone of saturation

choiceExplanations.Leaky aquifer: A semi-confined aquifer overlain or underlain by an aquitard that transmits minor vertical seepage.

items.question: rainfall pattern with five wet months of more than 200 mm/month, five dry months of less than 100 mm/month, two transition months of 100mm to 200mm/month and total annual rainfall above 1500 mm.

choiceExplanations.Meteorological Drought: Correct — Meteorological drought is defined directly by a significant precipitation deficit (>25% below normal) over a region.
choiceExplanations.Agricultural Drought: Occurs when soil moisture becomes insufficient to support crop growth during critical developmental stages.
choiceExplanations.Socioeconomic Drought: Occurs when water shortages affect supply and demand of economic goods and human welfare.
choiceExplanations.Hydrological Drought: Reflects prolonged deficits in surface streamflow, reservoirs, and groundwater levels rather than initial rainfall deficit.

items.question: Type of climate that has two pronounced seasons: dry from / November to April and wet during the rest of the year.

choiceExplanations.TYPE 1: Correct — Under PAGASA's Corona climate classification, Type I has two pronounced seasons: dry from November to April and wet the rest of the year.
choiceExplanations.TYPE 3: Has no very pronounced maximum rain period, with a short dry season lasting only one to three months.
choiceExplanations.TYPE 2: Has no dry season, with a very pronounced maximum rainfall period from November to January.
choiceExplanations.TYPE 4: Features rainfall that is more or less evenly distributed throughout the entire year.

items.question: In discharge measurement, the readings in a staff gage are useless without this:
items.rationale: A staff gage only indicates water stage (elevation/depth), so a stage-discharge rating curve is required to convert stage readings into stream discharge rates.

choiceExplanations.Flow duration curve: Shows the percentage of time a given discharge is equaled or exceeded rather than converting stage to flow.
choiceExplanations.Synthetic hydrograph: Estimates runoff hydrographs for ungaged basins using basin parameters instead of translating staff gage readings.
choiceExplanations.Unit hydrograph matching curve: Not a standard stage-discharge tool for converting water level readings into streamflow rates.
choiceExplanations.Rating curve: Correct — A rating curve establishes the empirical relationship between stream stage (staff gage reading) and volumetric discharge.

items.question: The hydraulic process that reduces the rainfall erosivity is?

choiceExplanations.Transpiration: The release of water vapor through plant stomata, which occurs after root uptake rather than cushioning raindrop impact.
choiceExplanations.Percolation: The downward movement of infiltrated water through deeper soil layers toward the water table.
choiceExplanations.Infiltration: Entry of water into soil that reduces surface runoff volume rather than directly intercepting kinetic raindrop energy.
choiceExplanations.Interception: Correct — Vegetative canopy interception catches raindrops before impact, dissipating kinetic energy and lowering rainfall erosivity.

items.question: A soil Ph which below 7.0

choiceExplanations.Acidity: Correct — Soils with pH values below 7.0 have excess hydrogen ions and are classified as acidic.
choiceExplanations.Neutrality: Corresponds to a soil pH of 7.0 rather than values below 7.0.
choiceExplanations.Sodicity: Refers to excessive exchangeable sodium percentage (ESP > 15%), typically associated with high pH (>8.5).
choiceExplanations.Alkalinity: Describes basic soils with pH values above 7.0 rather than below 7.0.

items.question: GOOD SITES FOR DAMS
items.answer: 1.Supported by vegetated watershed of large river
items.rationale: 1.Supported by vegetated watershed of large river / 2.Outlet of large drainage basin / 3.Narrow but deep water channel / 4.No rock formation / 5.Clay soil / 6.No presence of expanding clay
choices: 1.Supported by vegetated watershed of large river
Located over fractured limestone or faulted bedrock
Situated on wide alluvial floodplains with deep silt
Surrounded by steep barren slopes with high erosion

choiceExplanations.1.Supported by vegetated watershed of la: Correct — A vegetated watershed sustains reliable river inflow while minimizing erosion and reservoir sedimentation, making it ideal for dams.
choiceExplanations.Located over fractured limestone or faul: Fractured or faulted foundations cause severe seepage losses and structural instability beneath dams.
choiceExplanations.Situated on wide alluvial floodplains wi: Wide, silty floodplains require excessively long embankments and provide weak foundations prone to settlement.
choiceExplanations.Surrounded by steep barren slopes with h: Barren eroding slopes rapidly silt up the reservoir and reduce storage capacity.

items.question: A kind of IC included as an important part of electronic instrument for gathering speed, velocity and discharge real-time data

choiceExplanations.Multiplexer: Selects and routes one of several input signals onto a single line rather than measuring time intervals.
choiceExplanations.Timer: Correct — A timer IC precisely measures elapsed intervals or pulse frequencies to compute real-time speed, velocity, and discharge.
choiceExplanations.Oscillator: Generates a continuous periodic clock waveform rather than directly counting intervals for velocity and discharge measurement.
choiceExplanations.Comparator: Compares two analog voltages to output a digital high or low state without timing pulses.

items.question: Type of precipitation associated with the movement of air masses from high pressure to low pressure region?

choiceExplanations.Advective Precipitation: Not a standard precipitation lifting mechanism; advection refers mainly to horizontal transport of air or moisture.
choiceExplanations.Convective Precipitation: Driven by local surface heating causing warm air parcels to rise vertically, not large-scale pressure-system convergence.
choiceExplanations.Orographic Precipitation: Caused by moist air forced upward over topographic barriers such as mountains.
choiceExplanations.Frontal/Cyclonic Precipitation: Correct — Cyclonic or frontal precipitation results from large-scale air mass movement from high-pressure to low-pressure centers and frontal lifting.

items.question: The amount of water withdrawn from irrigation and effective rainfall through evaporation from soil and water surfaces and transpiration from plants.he amount of water withdrawn from irrigation and effective rainfall through evaporation from soil and water surfaces and transpiration from plants.

choiceExplanations.Interception: Rainfall caught on plant leaves and stems before reaching the soil surface.
choiceExplanations.Infiltration: Downward entry of water through the soil surface into the root zone.
choiceExplanations.Percolation: Deep vertical movement of soil water below the root zone toward groundwater.
choiceExplanations.Evapotranspiration: Correct — Evapotranspiration combines water evaporated from soil and open water surfaces with water transpired by plants.

items.question: The hydrograph with a unit volume of direct runoff for a given duration?

choiceExplanations.Storm hydrograph: Represents total runoff (direct runoff plus baseflow) from a specific storm event of arbitrary volume.
choiceExplanations.Unit hydrograph: Correct — A unit hydrograph is the direct runoff hydrograph produced by one unit (e.g., 1 mm or 1 cm) of excess rainfall over a given duration.
choiceExplanations.Synthetic hydrograph: A hydrograph constructed from watershed physical characteristics when observed rainfall-runoff data are unavailable.
choiceExplanations.Dimensionless hydrograph: Expresses discharge and time as ratios to peak values rather than a unit runoff volume.

items.question: a geologic formation that will yield water to a well in sufficient quantities to make the production of water from this formation feasible for beneficial use; permeable layers of underground rock or sand that hold or transmit groundwater below the water table

choiceExplanations.Aquitard: A semi-permeable stratum that slows groundwater flow and cannot yield usable well quantities.
choiceExplanations.Aquifuge: An impermeable rock unit that neither stores nor transmits water.
choiceExplanations.Aquifer: Correct — An aquifer consists of permeable rock or sand that holds and transmits sufficient groundwater for beneficial well extraction.
choiceExplanations.Aquiclude: A very low-permeability layer that may hold water in pores but cannot transmit it usefully.

items.question: a subsurface water that occurs beneath a water table in soils and rocks, or in geological formations

choiceExplanations.Underflow: Subsurface water moving downstream through permeable alluvium directly beneath a surface stream bed.
choiceExplanations.Interflow: Shallow lateral subsurface flow through the unsaturated zone above the main water table.
choiceExplanations.Groundwater: Correct — Groundwater is subsurface water occupying saturated pores and fractures beneath the water table in soil or rock formations.
choiceExplanations.Baseflow: The portion of streamflow sustained by delayed groundwater discharge into a channel.

items.question: An aquifer or aquifer system in which groundwater is stored. The water may be placed in the aquifer by artificial or natural means.

choiceExplanations.Groundwater reservoir: Correct — A groundwater reservoir is an aquifer or aquifer system storing naturally or artificially recharged subsurface water.
choiceExplanations.Vadose zone: The unsaturated subsurface zone above the water table where pores contain both air and water.
choiceExplanations.Confining stratum: A low-permeability layer bounding an aquifer rather than the storage formation itself.
choiceExplanations.Recharge basin: A surface excavation constructed to infiltrate water into the ground rather than the underground aquifer system.

items.question: Natural pathway water follows as it changes between liquid, solid, and gaseous states. This biogeochemical cycle moves and recycles water in various forms through the ecosphere. (Also called the water cycle.)

choiceExplanations.Hydrologic cycle: Correct — The hydrologic (water) cycle describes the continuous movement and phase transitions of water across the ecosphere.
choiceExplanations.Nitrogen cycle: Biogeochemical circulation of nitrogen through atmospheric fixation, soils, organisms, and denitrification.
choiceExplanations.Phosphorus cycle: Slow biogeochemical movement of phosphorus through rocks, soils, water, and living organisms.
choiceExplanations.Carbon cycle: Biogeochemical exchange of carbon among the atmosphere, biosphere, oceans, and sediments.

items.question: All water which is open to the atmosphere and subject to surface runoff. Also defined as water that flows in streams and rivers and in natural lakes, in wetlands, and in reservoirs constructed by humans.

choiceExplanations.Vadose water: Water held in the unsaturated zone above the water table rather than on the land surface.
choiceExplanations.Subsurface water: All water occurring below the ground surface in the unsaturated and saturated zones.
choiceExplanations.Surface water: Correct — Surface water encompasses all water open to the atmosphere in streams, rivers, lakes, wetlands, and reservoirs.
choiceExplanations.Meteoric water: Water derived recently from atmospheric precipitation, regardless of whether it is on the surface or underground.

items.question: Upper level of a saturated formation where the water is at atmospheric pressure, or the upper surface of an unconfined aquifer.

choiceExplanations.Piezometric surface: Imaginary level to which water rises in wells tapping a confined aquifer under pressure.
choiceExplanations.Water table: Correct — The water table is the upper surface of an unconfined saturated zone where pore water pressure equals atmospheric pressure.
choiceExplanations.Capillary fringe: The moist zone just above the water table where water rises by surface tension under negative pressure.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic gradient: The slope of the water table or potentiometric surface driving groundwater flow, not the surface itself.

items.question: Free water surface in the well to the free water surface on the suction pipe is:

choiceExplanations.Friction head: Head loss caused by fluid resistance against pipe walls, fittings, and valves during flow.
choiceExplanations.Static head: Correct — Static suction lift/head is the vertical elevation difference between the free water level in the well and the pump suction level.
choiceExplanations.Dynamic head: Total head during pumping, combining static head, friction losses, and velocity head.
choiceExplanations.Velocity head: Kinetic energy per unit weight of flowing water, equal to V² / (2g).

items.question: the property of the soil to transmit water and air

choiceExplanations.Soil capillarity: Ability of fine soil pores to draw and retain water upward against gravity via surface tension.
choiceExplanations.Soil porosity: Fraction of total soil volume occupied by void spaces rather than flow transmission rate.
choiceExplanations.Soil plasticity: Property allowing moist clay-rich soils to deform without cracking rather than transmit fluids.
choiceExplanations.Soil permeability: Correct — Soil permeability is the property of a porous soil to transmit water and air through interconnected voids.

items.question: the ability of soils to transmit water through its entire saturated thickness

choiceExplanations.Soil-water storativity: Soil-water storativity measures the volume of water released from or taken into storage per unit area per unit head change.
choiceExplanations.Soil-water diffusivity: Soil-water diffusivity is the ratio of unsaturated hydraulic conductivity to differential water capacity.
choiceExplanations.Soil-water retention: Soil-water retention describes a soil's capacity to hold moisture against gravity or matric suction.
choiceExplanations.Soil-water transmissivity: Correct — Soil-water transmissivity equals hydraulic conductivity multiplied by saturated thickness, measuring water transmission across the entire saturated zone.

items.question: A quantitative measure of saturated soil’s ability to transmit water when subjected to a hydraulic gradient

choiceExplanations.Aquifer transmissivity: Aquifer transmissivity integrates hydraulic conductivity over the entire saturated thickness rather than per unit cross-section.
choiceExplanations.Specific yield: Specific yield is the ratio of drainable water volume to total bulk volume in an unconfined aquifer.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic conductivity: Correct — Hydraulic conductivity (K in Darcy's law) quantifies how readily a saturated porous medium transmits water under a unit hydraulic gradient.
choiceExplanations.Intrinsic permeability: Intrinsic permeability depends solely on pore geometry of the medium, independent of fluid viscosity and density.

items.question: poorly permeable underground layer that limits the flow of groundwater from one aquifer to another

choiceExplanations.Regolith: Regolith is the loose, unconsolidated layer of weathered rock and soil overlying solid bedrock.
choiceExplanations.Aquifuge: An aquifuge is a completely impermeable geologic formation that neither stores nor transmits groundwater.
choiceExplanations.Aquiclude: Correct — An aquiclude is a poorly permeable underground geologic layer that retards or limits groundwater movement between aquifers.
choiceExplanations.Aquifer: An aquifer is a permeable saturated geologic formation capable of yielding usable quantities of groundwater.

items.question: Difference in elevation between the groundwater table and the water surface at the well and pumping. Lowering of the water surface, water table, or piezometric surface resulting from the withdrawal of water from a well or drain.

choiceExplanations.Upconing: Upconing is the upward movement of underlying saline water toward a pumping well in coastal aquifers.
choiceExplanations.Recharge: Recharge is the downward addition of water into an aquifer from precipitation or surface water bodies.
choiceExplanations.Drawdown: Correct — Drawdown is the vertical drop between the static water table (or piezometric surface) and the pumping water level at a well.
choiceExplanations.Submergence: Submergence refers to the depth a pump intake or hydraulic structure sits below the water surface.

items.question: Method of measuring evapotranspiration that uses energy

choiceExplanations.Blaney criddle: Blaney-Criddle is an empirical temperature and daytime-percentage method that does not compute radiation energy balance.
choiceExplanations.Hamon equation: The Hamon equation estimates potential evapotranspiration solely from mean daily air temperature and daylight duration.
choiceExplanations.Jensen haise: Correct — The Jensen-Haise equation is a radiation-based method that estimates evapotranspiration using solar energy and mean air temperature.
choiceExplanations.Thornthwaite method: The Thornthwaite method estimates potential evapotranspiration strictly from monthly mean air temperature and latitude-adjusted day length.

items.question: no dry season with a very pronounced maximum rainfall from November to January

choiceExplanations.Type I: Type I under the Corona classification has two pronounced seasons: dry from November to April, wet the rest.
choiceExplanations.Type II: Correct — Type II in the Philippine Corona climate classification has no dry season with a very pronounced maximum rainfall from November to January.
choiceExplanations.Type III: Type III has unpronounced seasons, relatively dry from November to April and wet during the rest of the year.
choiceExplanations.Type IV: Type IV has rainfall more or less evenly distributed throughout the year without a distinct dry period.

items.question: seasons not very pronounced, relatively dry from November to april and wet during the rest of the year

choiceExplanations.Type IV: Type IV exhibits rainfall distributed relatively evenly throughout all months of the year.
choiceExplanations.Type II: Type II has no dry season and a very pronounced rainfall peak from November to January.
choiceExplanations.Type I: Type I features two distinct seasons, dry from November to April and wet from May to October.
choiceExplanations.Type III: Correct — Type III in the Corona classification has unpronounced seasons, being relatively dry from November to April and wet the rest of the year.

items.question: rainfall more or less evenly distributed throughout the year

choiceExplanations.Type I: Type I has two sharp seasons: dry from November to April and wet for the remaining months.
choiceExplanations.Type III: Type III has unpronounced seasons, relatively dry from November to April and wet the rest of the year.
choiceExplanations.Type IV: Correct — Type IV in the Corona climate classification features rainfall more or less evenly distributed throughout the year.
choiceExplanations.Type II: Type II lacks a dry season and experiences maximum rainfall between November and January.

items.question: temperature/day time

choiceExplanations.Jensen haise: Jensen-Haise estimates evapotranspiration primarily using solar radiation and mean air temperature rather than daytime percentage alone.
choiceExplanations.Priestley taylor: Priestley-Taylor is a simplified energy-balance method driven by net radiation and soil heat flux.
choiceExplanations.Penman monteith: Penman-Monteith is a physically based combination method requiring radiation, wind speed, humidity, and temperature.
choiceExplanations.Blaney criddle: Correct — The Blaney-Criddle method estimates consumptive use from mean temperature and monthly percentage of annual daytime hours.

items.question: water liquid to vaporize stage

choiceExplanations.Hargreaves: Hargreaves is an empirical temperature-range and extraterrestrial-radiation method for estimating reference evapotranspiration.
choiceExplanations.Thornthwaite: Thornthwaite estimates potential evapotranspiration using only monthly mean air temperature and daylight length.
choiceExplanations.Sharovs: Correct — Sharov's equation relates evaporation to the energy required to convert liquid water to vapor using temperature and saturation deficit.
choiceExplanations.Penman: Penman combines aerodynamic vapor transport and energy-balance terms rather than focusing on Sharov's phase-change formulation.

choiceExplanations.Q = CIA Where C is the runoff coefficien: Correct — The Rational Method computes peak runoff discharge as Q = CIA, combining runoff coefficient, rainfall intensity, and watershed drainage area.

choiceExplanations.Q = AV Where A is the cross-sectional fl: Q = AV is the continuity equation for channel discharge using cross-sectional area and velocity, not rainfall-runoff.

items.question: It is an equation which the most theoretically sound equation for estimating potential evapotranspiration (PET) PET).

choiceExplanations.Penman: Correct — The Penman equation combines energy-balance and aerodynamic mass-transfer principles, making it the most theoretically sound PET equation among the choices.
choiceExplanations.Thornthwaite: Thornthwaite is a purely empirical method relying only on mean monthly air temperature and day length.
choiceExplanations.Makkink: Makkink is a simplified empirical radiation-temperature equation calibrated mainly for humid grass conditions.
choiceExplanations.Hargreaves: Hargreaves is an empirical equation estimating reference evapotranspiration from temperature range and extraterrestrial radiation.

items.question: The passage of water into the soil surface

choiceExplanations.Infiltration: Correct — Infiltration is the downward entry or passage of water through the soil surface into the soil profile.
choiceExplanations.Seepage: Seepage is the slow lateral or vertical movement of water through porous soil, embankments, or canal walls.
choiceExplanations.Interception: Interception is the capture and retention of precipitation by plant canopies before it reaches the ground.
choiceExplanations.Percolation: Percolation is the downward movement of water deeper through the soil profile below the root zone.

items.question: Horton realized that infiltration rate is a decay type function whereby continuous infiltration and wetting of the soil will decrease infiltration due to decrease in soil profile storage potential, inwashing of fine soil particles into soil voids and swelling of soil colloids and closing of soil cracks. What is the Horton Equation?
items.rationale: Horton's infiltration equation models exponential decay from initial capacity fo to constant final capacity fc: f(t) = fc + (fo - fc)e^(-kt).

choiceExplanations.f = fc + (fo - fc)e^(-kt): Correct — Horton's infiltration equation models exponential decay from initial capacity f_o to constant final capacity f_c over time t.
choiceExplanations.f = fo + (fc - fo)e^(kt): A positive exponent e^(kt) grows unboundedly over time instead of decaying toward equilibrium capacity f_c.
choiceExplanations.f = fc - (fo + fc)e^(-kt): Subtracting (f_o + f_c)e^(-kt) yields a negative initial infiltration capacity at t = 0 rather than f_o.
choiceExplanations.f = (fo - fc)ln(kt): Horton's infiltration capacity decays exponentially with time, not logarithmically, and approaches f_c asymptotically.

items.question: Static water level is the level at which the water rests in a well before pumping. On the other hand, pumping water level is the level at which water stands in a well when pumping at any given rate. What do you call the difference between the two water levels?

choiceExplanations.Submergence: Submergence is the vertical distance a well screen or pump intake sits below the pumping water level.
choiceExplanations.Recovery: Recovery is the rise in water level back toward static equilibrium after well pumping stops.
choiceExplanations.Drawdown: Correct — Drawdown is the vertical difference between the static water level before pumping and the pumping water level.
choiceExplanations.Interference: Well interference is the additional drawdown caused in one well by pumping from nearby neighboring wells.

items.question: Method of calculating average areal precipitation involving the construction of lines of equal precipitation is called

choiceExplanations.Hypsometric method: The hypsometric method relates watershed elevation to area rather than constructing equal-rainfall contours.
choiceExplanations.Isohyetal method: Correct — The isohyetal method computes average areal rainfall by drawing contours of equal precipitation (isohyets) and weighting enclosed areas.
choiceExplanations.Arithmetic method: The arithmetic mean method simply averages point gage readings without drawing contours or area weights.
choiceExplanations.Thiessen method: The Thiessen polygon method weights station rainfall by perpendicular-bisector polygons rather than equal-depth contours.

items.question: The rate at which groundwater moves across the underground soil profile

choiceExplanations.Specific retention: Specific retention is the ratio of water retained against gravity to total rock or soil volume.
choiceExplanations.Storage coefficient: Storage coefficient measures water volume released from aquifer storage per unit area per unit head drop.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic conductivity: Correct — Hydraulic conductivity measures the rate at which groundwater moves through a unit cross-section of saturated soil under a unit hydraulic gradient.
choiceExplanations.Specific yield: Specific yield is the volume fraction of water that drains freely by gravity from an unconfined aquifer.

items.question: The soil reservoir is filled with flooding water on to the soil surface so that it can be absorbed by the soil. Absorbing water in this way is called:

choiceExplanations.Capillarity: Capillarity is the upward or lateral movement of soil water driven by surface tension in fine pores.
choiceExplanations.Percolation: Percolation refers to gravity-driven downward flow deeper within the soil profile after surface entry.
choiceExplanations.Seepage: Seepage is slow subsurface water movement out of or into channels, reservoirs, or soil boundaries.
choiceExplanations.Infiltration: Correct — Infiltration is the absorption and entry of surface water (such as floodwater) downward across the soil surface.

items.question: The rational method of determining runoff is applicable to

choiceExplanations.Watershed with high tidal influence: Tidal influence violates the Rational Method's assumption of gravity-driven rainfall-runoff from small upland basins.
choiceExplanations.Watershed with good vegetation: Correct — The Rational Method applies best to small, uniform watersheds (such as well-vegetated agricultural catchments) with negligible channel storage.
choiceExplanations.Watershed with barren steep slopes: Extremely steep barren basins produce flashy non-uniform flows and sediment transport poorly represented by constant C.
choiceExplanations.Watershed with large storage lakes: Significant reservoir or lake storage attenuates peak discharge, invalidating the Rational Method's no-storage assumption.

items.question: An instrument used to measure temperature and water in the atmosphere or surrounding is?

choiceExplanations.Pyranometer: A pyranometer measures global solar radiation intensity incident on a horizontal surface.
choiceExplanations.Anemometer: An anemometer measures wind speed or air velocity rather than temperature and atmospheric moisture.
choiceExplanations.Barometer: A barometer measures atmospheric air pressure rather than air temperature and humidity.
choiceExplanations.Psychrometer: Correct — A psychrometer uses dry-bulb and wet-bulb thermometers to measure air temperature and atmospheric humidity.

items.question: What instrument needed in measuring wind speed?

choiceExplanations.Psychrometer: A psychrometer measures dry-bulb and wet-bulb temperatures to determine atmospheric humidity.
choiceExplanations.Hygrometer: A hygrometer measures atmospheric humidity or moisture content, not wind speed.
choiceExplanations.Barometer: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure rather than horizontal wind velocity.
choiceExplanations.Anemometer: Correct — An anemometer is the standard meteorological instrument used to measure wind speed.

items.question: Type of Precipitation where a there is a lifting of warm air converging into a low pressure are.

choiceExplanations.Cyclonic precipitation: Correct — Cyclonic precipitation occurs when warm, moist air converges into a low-pressure center and is lifted, cooled, and condensed.
choiceExplanations.Convective precipitation: Convective precipitation forms when localized surface heating causes warm air parcels to rise buoyantly.
choiceExplanations.Orographic precipitation: Orographic precipitation results from moist air being forced upward over topographic barriers such as mountain ranges.
choiceExplanations.Advective precipitation: Advection describes horizontal air-mass transport rather than low-pressure convergent lifting.

items.question: An instrument used to measure the velocity of air

choiceExplanations.Tachometer: A tachometer measures rotational shaft speed in revolutions per minute, not air velocity.
choiceExplanations.Anemometer: Correct — An anemometer measures the velocity (speed) of moving air or wind.
choiceExplanations.Barometer: A barometer measures static atmospheric pressure rather than air movement speed.
choiceExplanations.Manometer: A manometer measures fluid pressure differences using a liquid column, not wind velocity directly.

items.question: The Green Ampt Equation is use for computing

choiceExplanations.Percolation rate and groundwater recharg: Green-Ampt models surface wetting-front entry, not deep percolation or aquifer recharge directly.
choiceExplanations.Evaporation rate and cumulative runoff: Green-Ampt predicts soil-water infiltration, whereas evaporation and runoff are separate hydrologic processes.
choiceExplanations.Baseflow recession and peak discharge: Baseflow recession and peak discharge describe stream-channel routing rather than soil-surface infiltration.
choiceExplanations.Infiltration rate and cumulative infiltr: Correct — The Green-Ampt equation physically models wetting-front advance to compute both instantaneous infiltration rate and cumulative infiltration depth.

items.question: A hydrograph of direct runoff for one unit depth

choiceExplanations.Synthetic hydrograph: A synthetic hydrograph is derived empirically from watershed characteristics when observed runoff records are lacking.
choiceExplanations.Storm hydrograph: A storm hydrograph shows total runoff from an actual storm of any excess depth, not unit depth.
choiceExplanations.Composite hydrograph: A composite hydrograph combines runoff contributions from multiple successive storms or sub-basins.
choiceExplanations.Unit hydrograph: Correct — A unit hydrograph represents the direct runoff hydrograph produced by one unit depth of excess rainfall uniformly distributed over a storm duration.

items.question: The hydrologic cycle by which water return to the atmosphere through plant tissues

choiceExplanations.Transpiration: Correct — Transpiration is the hydrologic process where water absorbed by roots moves through plant tissues and vaporizes to the atmosphere via stomata.
choiceExplanations.Interception: Interception is precipitation caught on external plant surfaces before reaching soil, not internal tissue transport.
choiceExplanations.Evaporation: Evaporation is the direct phase change of liquid water into vapor from soil or open water surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Condensation: Condensation is the phase change of atmospheric water vapor back into liquid droplets or ice crystals.

items.question: Darcy equation is used only to what type of flow?

choiceExplanations.Unsteady: Unsteady flow involves time-varying hydraulic heads, requiring transient storage equations beyond basic Darcy flow.
choiceExplanations.Transitional: Transitional flow exceeds the laminar Reynolds-number limit where Darcy's linear velocity-gradient relation breaks down.
choiceExplanations.Turbulent: Turbulent flow in coarse media exhibits nonlinear head-loss behavior that violates Darcy's linear law.
choiceExplanations.Steady: Correct — Darcy's law applies to steady, laminar flow through saturated porous media where hydraulic head does not change with time.

items.question: A method of measuring evaporation that uses energy

choiceExplanations.Thornthwaite: Thornthwaite relies solely on mean monthly air temperature and day length, not an explicit energy budget.
choiceExplanations.Hargreaves: Hargreaves estimates evapotranspiration from air temperature range and extraterrestrial radiation rather than a full energy balance.
choiceExplanations.Penman: Correct — The Penman method explicitly incorporates net radiation energy balance alongside aerodynamic vapor transport to estimate evaporation.
choiceExplanations.Dalton: Dalton's law is an aerodynamic mass-transfer formula driven by wind speed and vapor-pressure deficit without energy terms.

items.question: SFR total annual rainfall

choiceExplanations.above 1725mm: This threshold exceeds the Philippine standard annual rainfall criterion for Small Farm Reservoir (SFR) siting.
choiceExplanations.above 1620mm: This threshold exceeds the established 1500 mm annual rainfall requirement for Small Farm Reservoirs.
choiceExplanations.above 1320mm: This value falls below the minimum 1500 mm annual rainfall guideline for reliable SFR storage.
choiceExplanations.above 1500mm: Correct — Philippine agricultural engineering guidelines (PAES/DA-BSWM) recommend areas with annual rainfall above 1500 mm for Small Farm Reservoir (SFR) feasibility.

items.question: A thermometer that has a constriction above the bulb that permits the mercury to rise in the capillary tube but does not allow it to descend the capillary tube unless the thermometer is reset (PAGASA, 2022).

choiceExplanations.Minimum thermometer: A minimum thermometer uses alcohol and a movable glass index pin that stays at the lowest temperature.
choiceExplanations.Wet-bulb thermometer: A wet-bulb thermometer has a moistened muslin wick around its bulb to measure evaporative cooling.
choiceExplanations.Soil thermometer: A soil thermometer is designed to measure subsurface soil temperatures at specified depths.
choiceExplanations.Maximum thermometer: Correct — A maximum thermometer has a capillary constriction above the mercury bulb that holds the highest temperature reading until reset by shaking.

items.question: The science that encompasses the occurrence, distribution, movement and properties of the waters of the earth and their relationship with the environment (USGS, 2022).

choiceExplanations.Hydrogeology: Hydrogeology focuses specifically on the distribution and movement of subsurface groundwater within geologic formations.
choiceExplanations.Limnology: Limnology is the scientific study of inland freshwater ecosystems such as lakes, ponds, and rivers.
choiceExplanations.Hydrometeorology: Hydrometeorology deals specifically with water and energy exchange between land surfaces and the lower atmosphere.
choiceExplanations.Hydrology: Correct — Hydrology is the earth science covering the occurrence, distribution, movement, and properties of Earth's waters and their relationship with the environment.

items.question: A branch of meteorology and hydrology that studies the transfer of water and energy between the land surface and the lower atmosphere.

choiceExplanations.Hydrometeorology: Correct — Hydrometeorology bridges meteorology and hydrology by studying the transfer of water and energy between the land surface and the lower atmosphere.
choiceExplanations.Climatology: Climatology studies long-term atmospheric weather patterns and statistical climate averages over extended periods.
choiceExplanations.Hydrogeology: Hydrogeology investigates groundwater occurrence, flow, and aquifer properties beneath the Earth's surface.
choiceExplanations.Agrometeorology: Agrometeorology focuses on how weather and climate conditions affect agricultural crops, livestock, and farm operations.

items.question: Heavy rainfall or rain that accumulates at a rate of 3 tenths of an inch (0.3 inch or about 7.5 mm), or more, per hour (US National Weather Service, 2022).

choiceExplanations.Intermittent rain: Intermittent rain refers to precipitation that starts and stops over time, regardless of hourly intensity.
choiceExplanations.Light rain: Light rain is defined by low accumulation rates up to 2.5 mm (0.10 inch) per hour.
choiceExplanations.Torrential rain: Correct — Under NWS intensity terminology as cited, torrential (heavy) rain accumulates at a rate of 0.3 inch (about 7.5 mm) or more per hour.
choiceExplanations.Moderate rain: Moderate rain falls between 2.6 mm and 7.5 mm (0.11 to 0.30 inch) per hour.

items.question: Dominant form of precipitation in the Philippines.

choiceExplanations.Rainfall: Correct — Rainfall (liquid precipitation) is the dominant form of precipitation across the tropical climate of the Philippines.
choiceExplanations.Drizzle: Drizzle consists of tiny liquid droplets (< 0.5 mm) and contributes only a minor fraction of total precipitation.
choiceExplanations.Sleet: Sleet consists of frozen ice pellets formed in cold layers, absent in Philippine tropical lowlands.
choiceExplanations.Snowfall: Snowfall is frozen crystalline precipitation requiring sub-freezing atmospheric profiles absent in the Philippines.

items.question: Kind of thermometer with pin inside its tube which does not go with the expanding liquid when temperature increases.

choiceExplanations.Dry-bulb thermometer: A dry-bulb thermometer measures ambient air temperature without an internal minimum-index pin.
choiceExplanations.Maximum thermometer: A maximum thermometer uses mercury and a bulb constriction rather than an internal index pin.
choiceExplanations.Minimum thermometer: Correct — A minimum thermometer contains alcohol with an internal glass pin dragged down by the meniscus during cooling and left behind when warming.
choiceExplanations.Wet-bulb thermometer: A wet-bulb thermometer measures evaporative cooling temperature using a dampened cloth wick, not a minimum pin.

items.question: Method of areal rainfall determination done by computing the weighted average.

choiceExplanations.Normal ratio method: The normal ratio method estimates missing data at a single station, not areal average rainfall over a watershed.
choiceExplanations.Arithmetic method: Correct — Keyed as the arithmetic method (note: standard arithmetic mean averages gage depths equally, whereas Thiessen and isohyetal methods compute area-weighted averages).
choiceExplanations.Isohyetal method: The isohyetal method computes area-weighted rainfall by integrating areas between drawn contours of equal rainfall.
choiceExplanations.Thiessen method: The Thiessen polygon method weights station rainfall by polygon areas rather than simple arithmetic averaging.

items.question: An instrument to measure depth of rainfall.

choiceExplanations.Rain gage: Correct — A rain gage collects and measures the depth of liquid precipitation falling at a specific location.
choiceExplanations.Staff gage: A staff gage is a graduated vertical scale used to read water-surface stage in streams or reservoirs.
choiceExplanations.Current meter: A current meter measures flow velocity in open channels or streams, not rainfall depth.
choiceExplanations.Evaporation pan: An evaporation pan measures water loss rate to the atmosphere via evaporation, not rainfall depth.

items.question: Part of rainfall which runs off the soil as surface or subsurface flow.

choiceExplanations.Percolation: Percolation is deep downward water movement below the root zone toward the groundwater table.
choiceExplanations.Interception: Interception is precipitation caught and held on foliage or surfaces before reaching the ground.
choiceExplanations.Runoff: Correct — Runoff is the portion of precipitation that flows over the land surface or through shallow subsurface paths into drainage channels.
choiceExplanations.Infiltration: Infiltration is the vertical entry of water from the ground surface into the soil profile.

items.question: Ratio of runoff over rainfall.

choiceExplanations.Pan coefficient: A pan coefficient converts open-pan evaporation measurements into reference crop evapotranspiration.
choiceExplanations.Crop coefficient: A crop coefficient relates a specific crop's evapotranspiration to reference evapotranspiration.
choiceExplanations.Drainage coefficient: A drainage coefficient is the depth of excess water removed from an area within 24 hours.
choiceExplanations.Runoff coefficient: Correct — The runoff coefficient (C in Q = CIA) is the dimensionless ratio of runoff depth or rate to rainfall depth or intensity.

items.question: The part of rainfall that is stored in the root zone and can be used by the plants (FAO, 2022). This excludes rainfall that does not reach the soil and percolation below the root zone. For grassed soil surface, it is estimated that this rainfall is greater than 0.5 mm/day.

choiceExplanations.Effective rainfall: Correct — Effective rainfall is the fraction of total precipitation stored in the root zone and usable by plants, excluding surface runoff and deep percolation.
choiceExplanations.Dependable rainfall: Dependable rainfall is the rainfall amount expected to be equaled or exceeded at a given probability level.
choiceExplanations.Antecedent rainfall: Antecedent rainfall refers to precipitation occurring prior to a storm event that affects initial soil moisture.
choiceExplanations.Excess rainfall: Excess rainfall is the portion of storm rain that generates direct surface runoff rather than infiltrating.

items.question: The inverse of the probability of exceedance of a certain hydrologic event.

choiceExplanations.Hydrologic risk: Hydrologic risk is the probability that an event occurs at least once during a structure's design life.
choiceExplanations.Return period: Correct — Return period (recurrence interval T = 1/P) is the reciprocal of the exceedance probability of a hydrologic event.
choiceExplanations.Base period: Base period refers to the total duration of direct runoff in a hydrograph or irrigation cropping season.
choiceExplanations.Exceedance probability: Exceedance probability is the chance P an event is equaled or exceeded, not its inverse.

items.question: Indicates to what depth liquid precipitation would cover a horizontal surface in an observation period if nothing could drain, evaporate or percolate from this surface.

choiceExplanations.Storm duration: Storm duration is the elapsed time over which a precipitation event occurs, not water depth.
choiceExplanations.Precipitation depth: Correct — Precipitation depth measures the vertical thickness of water that would accumulate on a flat horizontal surface assuming no losses.
choiceExplanations.Rainfall intensity: Rainfall intensity is the rate of precipitation depth per unit time (e.g., mm/hr), not total depth.
choiceExplanations.Precipitation volume: Precipitation volume equals precipitation depth multiplied by catchment area, expressed in cubic meters or liters.

items.question: The precipitation depth that corresponds to a liquid quantity of 1 liter falling into a 1 square meter of ground area.
items.answer: 1 mm Precipitation = (1 li x 1,000,000 mm3/li)/(1 m2 x 1,000,000 mm2/m2)
items.rationale: 1 mm Precipitation = (1 li x 1,000,000 mm3/li)/(1 m2 x 1,000,000 mm2/m2) / = 1 mm
choices: 1 mm Precipitation = (1 li x 1,000,000 mm3/li)/(1 m2 x 1,000,000 mm2/m2)

choiceExplanations.100 mm: Spreading 1 liter over 1 square meter yields 1 mm depth; 100 mm requires 100 liters.
choiceExplanations.10 mm: A depth of 10 mm over 1 square meter corresponds to 10 liters of water, not 1 liter.
choiceExplanations.1 mm Precipitation = (1 li x 1,000,000 m: Correct — Dividing 1 liter (1,000,000 mm³) by 1 m² (1,000,000 mm²) yields a uniform precipitation depth of 1 mm.
choiceExplanations.0.1 mm: A depth of 0.1 mm over 1 square meter corresponds to only 0.1 liter (100 mL) of water.

items.question: Rainfall depths recorded were as follows: 8mm and 2mm for 8:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M., respectively on 7-7-2022 and 5 mm and 9 mm for 8:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M., respectively on 7-8-2022. What is the total rainfall depth on 7-7-2022?
items.answer: 7 mm The rainfall recorded at 8:00 AM of any day is counted as part of the total rainfall for the previous day.
items.rationale: 7 mm The rainfall recorded at 8:00 AM of any day is counted as part of the total rainfall for the previous day. / Rainfall on 7-7-2022 / = Rainfall at 2:00 P.M. on 7-7-2022 + Rainfall at 8:00 A.M. / on 7-8-2022 / = 2 mm + 5 mm / = 7 mm
choices: 7 mm The rainfall recorded at 8:00 AM of any day is counted as part of the total rainfall for the previous day.

choiceExplanations.15 mm: Adding 8 mm + 2 mm + 5 mm wrongly counts 7-7-2022's 8:00 AM reading, which belongs to 7-6-2022.
choiceExplanations.7 mm The rainfall recorded at 8:00 AM of: Correct — Under standard meteorological observation rules, the 8:00 AM reading belongs to the previous day, so 7-7-2022 total = 2 mm (2:00 PM on 7-7) + 5 mm (8:00 AM on 7-8) = 7 mm.
choiceExplanations.13 mm: Summing 8 mm + 5 mm wrongly pairs two 8:00 AM readings instead of 7-7-2022's afternoon and next-morning totals.
