items.question: Using a triangular hydrograph, estimate the runoff volume in cubic meters from a 10-hectare drainage basin if rainfall depth for 6 hours reached 60 mm and duration of runoff is about 3 hours. Use a typical runoff coefficient of 0.35.
items.rationale: Rainfall intensity is I = 60 mm / 6 hr = 10 mm/hr and peak runoff rate is q = 0.0028 × C × I × A = 0.0028 × 0.35 × 10 × 10 = 0.098 ≈ 0.1 m³/s, yielding a triangular hydrograph runoff volume of V = 0.5 × q × T = 0.5 × 0.1 m³/s × (3 hr × 3600 s/hr) = 540 m³.

choiceExplanations.540: Correct — using rational peak flow (≈ 0.10 m³/s) in a 3-hour triangular hydrograph gives V = 0.5 × 0.10 × 10,800 = 540 m³.
choiceExplanations.2020: Overestimates the triangular hydrograph volume by nearly four times the computed peak-flow integration.
choiceExplanations.1020: Nearly doubles the triangular hydrograph volume obtained from the 3-hour runoff duration.
choiceExplanations.450: Underestimates the triangular hydrograph volume for a 3-hour base time and 0.10 m³/s peak flow.

items.question: The three major processes of the water cycle are evaporation, precipitation, and __________.
items.rationale: Evaporation, condensation, and precipitation are the three primary physical processes driving the hydrologic (water) cycle.

choiceExplanations.Raindrop formation: Coalescence process within clouds rather than one of the three primary phase-change hydrologic cycle processes.
choiceExplanations.Runoff: Overland and channel flow returning water to oceans, not one of the three primary atmospheric processes.
choiceExplanations.Cloud formation: Visible result of vapor cooling, whereas condensation itself is the fundamental phase-change process.
choiceExplanations.Condensation: Correct — evaporation, condensation, and precipitation are the three primary processes driving the hydrologic cycle.

items.question: Estimate the net irrigation discharge requirement for 100 hectares of lowland rice.
items.rationale: Based on the FAO and NIA recommended irrigation discharge of 1.5 L/s per hectare for lowland rice, Q = 1.5 L/(s·ha) × 100 ha = 150 L/s.
choices: 1.Supported by vegetated watershed of large river

choiceExplanations.1.Supported by vegetated watershed of la: A qualitative watershed description from another option set, not a numerical discharge requirement.
choiceExplanations.15 l/s: Corresponds to only 0.15 L/s/ha, ten times below standard Philippine lowland rice water duty.
choiceExplanations.1,500 l/s: Corresponds to 15 L/s/ha, ten times higher than the standard 1.5 L/s/ha rice irrigation requirement.
choiceExplanations.150 l/s: Correct — multiplying 100 hectares by the standard 1.5 L/s/ha lowland rice water duty yields 150 L/s.

items.question: This stage begins before panicle initiation in late maturing varieties; it may occur during the later part of the tillering stage. While in short-duration varieties, this stage occurs almost simultaneously with panicle initiation. What rice growth stage is it?
items.rationale: Per the Philippine Rice Production Training Manual, stem elongation begins before panicle initiation (often during late tillering) in late-maturing rice varieties and occurs almost simultaneously with panicle initiation in short-duration varieties.

choiceExplanations.Heading: Reproductive stage when the rice panicle fully emerges from the flag leaf sheath.
choiceExplanations.Flowering: Anthesis stage after heading when spikelets open, shed pollen, and fertilization occurs.
choiceExplanations.Stem elongation: Correct — internode elongation begins before panicle initiation in late varieties and coincides with it in short-duration varieties.
choiceExplanations.Tillering: Early vegetative phase when secondary shoots develop from the main culm before panicle initiation.

items.question: A big watershed has 3 subsidiary watersheds inside it. The simultaneous peak runoffs at subsidiary outlets are 0.5, 1 and 1.5 cu.m/s. What is the corresponding peak runoff at the outlet of the main watershed? Neglect seepage loss and travel lag time along the river connecting the subsidiary watersheds.
items.rationale: Neglecting seepage losses and travel lag time, the simultaneous peak runoff at the main watershed outlet is the sum of the subsidiary peak runoffs: Q = 0.5 + 1 + 1.5 = 3 cu.m/s.

choiceExplanations.3: Correct — neglecting seepage and travel lag, simultaneous sub-watershed peak flows add directly: 0.5 + 1.0 + 1.5 = 3 m³/s.
choiceExplanations.2: Omits one of the tributary peak flows when summing the simultaneous sub-watershed discharges.
choiceExplanations.1: Represents only the middle sub-watershed's discharge rather than the combined main outlet peak flow.
choiceExplanations.2.5: Fails to include the 0.5 m³/s subsidiary outflow in the total main outlet sum.

items.question: Examine the flow in triangular weirs in relation to flows in rectangular weirs. What is the likely range of values of the coefficient of discharge?
items.rationale: For sharp-crested triangular (V-notch) weirs, the dimensionless coefficient of discharge Cd typically falls within 0.557 to 0.598 (around 0.58 for standard 90-degree V-notch weirs).

choiceExplanations.0.098 to 0.189: Too low for standard sharp-crested triangular V-notch weir discharge coefficients.
choiceExplanations.0.657 to 0.798: Exceeds the standard hydraulic contraction range for sharp-crested V-notch triangular weirs.
choiceExplanations.0.068 to 0.089: Represents empirical lumped coefficient values for rectangular weirs rather than V-notch weirs.
choiceExplanations.0.557 to 0.598: Correct — standard sharp-crested triangular (V-notch) weirs typically have discharge coefficients Cd ranging from 0.557 to 0.598.

items.question: If you need to determine the ground formation up to 5 meters below the soil surface for a water resource development project, what estimation method will you use?
items.rationale: The georesistivity (electrical resistivity) method measures subsurface electrical resistance to characterize shallow soil and rock formations below the ground surface for water resource exploration.

choiceExplanations.Aquifer profile estimation method: General conceptual term rather than a specific field geophysical survey technique for shallow strata.
choiceExplanations.Geotagging method: Assigns geographic coordinates to photos or records and cannot probe subsurface soil strata.
choiceExplanations.LiDAR method: Uses laser pulses to map surface topography and cannot penetrate 5 meters underground.
choiceExplanations.Georesistivity method: Correct — electrical resistivity surveying measures subsurface resistance to characterize shallow soil and aquifer layers.

items.question: The inverse of return period in hydrology.
items.rationale: In hydrologic frequency analysis, the probability of exceedance P (the annual probability that an event equals or exceeds a given magnitude) is the reciprocal of the return period T, i.e., P = 1/T.

choiceExplanations.Event probability: General probability of any occurrence, not specifically the annual probability of equaling or exceeding a magnitude.
choiceExplanations.Hydrologic probability: Broad descriptor rather than the exact reciprocal of return period T (P = 1/T).
choiceExplanations.Probability of exceedance: Correct — exceedance probability P equals 1/T, the inverse of the recurrence interval or return period T.
choiceExplanations.Return period: Average recurrence interval T in years between events, which is the inverse of exceedance probability.

items.question: The width of spillway shall be determined from the result of flood routing by allowing a maximum surcharge height of __ m.
items.rationale: According to PAES 609:2016 (Small Water Impounding System, Section 7.2.2), the spillway width shall be determined from flood routing by allowing a maximum surcharge height of 1 m.

choiceExplanations.1: Correct — PAES small farm reservoir design standards specify sizing spillway width with a 1.0 m maximum surcharge height.
choiceExplanations.1.5: Exceeds the 1.0 m maximum allowable surcharge head specified in small farm reservoir spillway design.
choiceExplanations.2: Excessive surcharge height that would require a taller embankment and higher freeboard than standard.
choiceExplanations.1.25: Above the standard 1.0 m maximum surcharge height limit used in flood routing for small spillways.

items.question: In evaluating the size of the drainage canal, what should be the design minimum discharge of the drainage canal?
items.rationale: In Philippine irrigation and drainage design criteria, the minimum design discharge of a drainage canal is taken as 10% (0.1) of the irrigation discharge.

choiceExplanations.0.2 of irrigation discharge: Double the standard minimum drainage canal design fraction of 10% of irrigation inflow.
choiceExplanations.0.1 of irrigation discharge: Correct — standard irrigation drainage design sets minimum drainage canal capacity at 0.1 (10%) of irrigation discharge.
choiceExplanations.0.15 of irrigation discharge: Exceeds the baseline 10% (0.1) minimum irrigation discharge fraction for drainage canal sizing.
choiceExplanations.0.25 of irrigation discharge: Two and a half times higher than the minimum 0.1 irrigation discharge criterion.

items.question: An area for catching water bounded by ridges and having one main outlet.
items.rationale: A watershed is a topographic land area bounded by ridges or drainage divides that collects precipitation and channels surface runoff to a single main outlet.

choiceExplanations.Rain forest: Biome characterized by high rainfall and dense canopy, not a topographically bounded drainage unit.
choiceExplanations.Basin: Broader regional drainage area often comprising multiple watersheds rather than a single ridge-bounded unit.
choiceExplanations.Watershed: Correct — a watershed is a topographically divided land area draining all precipitation to one main outlet.
choiceExplanations.Rain catchment: General term for any surface collecting rainwater, including roofs or cisterns, not specifically ridge-bounded terrain.

items.question: Which one of the following below is not part of the 7 steps in the water cycle?
items.rationale: In the standard seven-step hydrologic cycle classification, condensation (rather than "cloud formation" as a separate named step) represents vapor turning into droplets, alongside evaporation, transpiration, sublimation, precipitation, runoff, and infiltration.

choiceExplanations.Sublimation: One of the 7 standard hydrologic cycle steps, where ice or snow converts directly to vapor.
choiceExplanations.Transpiration: One of the 7 water cycle steps, releasing water vapor from plant leaves into the atmosphere.
choiceExplanations.Evaporation: One of the 7 water cycle steps, converting liquid surface water into atmospheric vapor.
choiceExplanations.Cloud formation: Correct — condensation is the named hydrologic step, whereas cloud formation is its visible result rather than a separate step.

items.question: What is the appropriate method of determining crop water consumptive use in a lysimeter?
items.rationale: Crop water consumptive use (evapotranspiration) in a standard lysimeter is determined using the inflow-outflow (water balance) method by subtracting drainage outflow and soil storage change from total irrigation and rainfall inflow.

choiceExplanations.Weighing method: Measures mass change in a weighing lysimeter, whereas drainage/percolation lysimeters track water volumes entering and leaving.
choiceExplanations.Inflow-outflow method: Correct — water-balance lysimeters determine crop consumptive use (ET) by accounting for all water inflows minus drainage outflows.
choiceExplanations.Inflow method: Measures only water added without accounting for deep percolation or surface drainage losses.
choiceExplanations.Outflow method: Tracks only drainage leaving the lysimeter and ignores irrigation and rainfall inputs.

items.question: In carrying out a small farm reservoir project, the main components to be included are catchment area, reservoir, embankment and __________.
items.rationale: Per PAES 610:2016 (Small Farm Reservoir, Figure 1), the main components of a small farm reservoir project are the catchment area, reservoir, embankment, and service area.

choiceExplanations.Length of rainy season: A climatic design parameter rather than a physical structural component of an SFR project.
choiceExplanations.Crops irrigated: Agricultural land-use factor used to estimate water demand, not a physical project component.
choiceExplanations.Service area: Correct — a small farm reservoir (SFR) comprises the catchment area, reservoir, embankment, spillway, and irrigated service area.
choiceExplanations.Watershed: Synonymous with the catchment area already listed among the four components.

items.question: The likely range of values of the coefficient of discharge in a rectangular weir.
items.rationale: Within the PRC ABELE reference range provided for weir discharge coefficients, 0.068 to 0.089 corresponds to the rectangular weir option (as distinguished from 0.557 to 0.598 for triangular weirs).

choiceExplanations.0.657 to 0.798: Exceeds the standard hydraulic discharge coefficient range for sharp-crested rectangular weirs.
choiceExplanations.0.557 to 0.598: Typical dimensionless Cd range for triangular V-notch weirs rather than this empirical rectangular weir range.
choiceExplanations.0.068 to 0.089: Correct — in standard ABE reviewer tables for rectangular weir flow formulas, this coefficient range is 0.068 to 0.089.
choiceExplanations.0.098 to 0.189: Higher than the empirical 0.068 to 0.089 coefficient range cited for rectangular weir flow.

items.question: Examine a big watershed. It is a big rain catchment composed of ___________.
items.rationale: A large watershed is a composite catchment made up of smaller tributary catchments called subsidiary watersheds that drain into the main river system.

choiceExplanations.Subsidiary watersheds: Correct — large watersheds are composed of interconnected subsidiary watersheds draining into the main river system.
choiceExplanations.Drainage basins: Usually synonymous with or larger than watersheds rather than their smaller internal subdivisions.
choiceExplanations.Small watersheds: Informal size descriptor rather than the standard hydrologic term for component sub-basins within a main watershed.
choiceExplanations.Forests: Vegetative land cover inside a watershed, not a hydrologic drainage subdivision.

items.question: areas open for public entry such as golf courses, public and private parks, playgrounds, schoolyards and playing fields, residential landscapes and industrial park landscapes

choiceExplanations.Service areas: Total arable land intended to receive water from an irrigation system.
choiceExplanations.Access areas: Correct — PAES defines access areas as landscaped and recreational grounds open for public entry.
choiceExplanations.Restricted areas: Zones where public entry is prohibited or tightly controlled for safety or sanitation.
choiceExplanations.Buffer areas: Protective strips separating irrigated or treated zones from sensitive boundaries or waterways.

items.question: volume of water stored in reservoir between the minimum water level and normal water level
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; GENERAL KNOWLEDGE part 1; recalled 2022

choiceExplanations.Active storage: Correct — active (live) storage is the usable reservoir volume between minimum and normal operating water levels.
choiceExplanations.Bank storage: Water absorbed into permeable reservoir banks during high stage and released when levels drop.
choiceExplanations.Surcharge storage: Temporary flood volume stored above the normal water level up to maximum flood level.
choiceExplanations.Dead storage: Unusable reservoir volume below the lowest outlet or intake reserved for sediment accumulation.

items.question: rise in maximum flood level from the original unobstructed flood level which result after an obstruction to the flow such as a dam, has been introduced

choiceExplanations.Afflux elevation: Correct — afflux is the maximum flood water level rise upstream caused by a dam or flow obstruction.
choiceExplanations.Tailwater elevation: Water surface elevation immediately downstream of a dam, spillway, or hydraulic structure.
choiceExplanations.Surcharge elevation: Maximum water level reached above normal pool during spillway flood routing.
choiceExplanations.Normal pool elevation: Design maximum operating water surface level maintained in a reservoir during normal conditions.

items.question: overgrowths of algae in water producing dangerous toxins in fresh or marine water

choiceExplanations.Saline intrusion: Movement of saltwater into freshwater aquifers or coastal surface waters.
choiceExplanations.Thermal turnover: Seasonal vertical mixing of lake water layers caused by surface cooling and density equalization.
choiceExplanations.Algal bloom: Correct — rapid algae overgrowth fueled by excess nutrients that depletes oxygen and can release dangerous toxins.
choiceExplanations.Organic loading: Rate of biodegradable organic matter discharged into a water body or wastewater treatment unit.

items.question: ratio of the average depth of irrigation water infiltrated and stored in the root zone to the average depth of irrigation water applied
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; RECALLED COMPRESS PART 2

choiceExplanations.Storage efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the root zone to the total water needed to refill it.
choiceExplanations.Application efficiency: Correct — PAES defines application efficiency as the ratio of root-zone stored water to total water applied to the field.
choiceExplanations.Conveyance efficiency: Ratio of water delivered at the field inlet to water diverted from the source.
choiceExplanations.Distribution efficiency: Measure of how uniformly irrigation water is spread across the entire irrigated field.

items.question: cross-sectional area of the flow which is measured perpendicular to the direction of flow

choiceExplanations.Topwidth: Horizontal width of the channel water surface measured perpendicular to flow.
choiceExplanations.Freeboard: Vertical safety margin from the maximum water surface to the top of the canal bank.
choiceExplanations.Area: Correct — cross-sectional flow area is the wetted area measured perpendicular to the flow direction.
choiceExplanations.Slope: Longitudinal inclination or elevation drop per unit length along a channel.

items.question: field that is level in all directions, encompassed by a dike to prevent runoff, and provides an undirected flow of water onto the field

choiceExplanations.Basin: Correct — PAES defines a basin as a level field enclosed by dikes that retains water without runoff.
choiceExplanations.Corrugation: Small closely spaced shallow channels used to guide surface water across sloping fields.
choiceExplanations.Terrace: Stepped earthen embankment constructed across hillslopes to slow runoff and control soil erosion.
choiceExplanations.Furrow: Small parallel trench excavated between crop rows to convey irrigation water down a slope.

items.question: type of surface irrigation where water is applied to the basin through a gap in the perimeter dike or adjacent ditch; water is retained until it infiltrates into the soil or the excess is drained off

choiceExplanations.Basin irrigation: Correct — basin irrigation floods diked level fields through dike gaps or ditches and retains water to infiltrate.
choiceExplanations.Corrugation irrigation: Applies water through small closely spaced rills down a slope for close-growing crops.
choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Guides sheet flow down gently sloping parallel strips bounded by low ridges.
choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Supplies water in small parallel channels between crop rows rather than flooding diked level plots.

items.question: maximum average contact pressure between the foundation and the soil which should not produce shear failure in the soil

choiceExplanations.Uplift pressure: Upward hydrostatic water pressure acting beneath a hydraulic structure's foundation.
choiceExplanations.Shear strength: Internal resistance of soil against sliding failure along a plane, not specifically foundation contact pressure.
choiceExplanations.Overburden pressure: Vertical stress exerted at depth by the weight of overlying soil and water.
choiceExplanations.Bearing capacity: Correct — PAES defines bearing capacity as the maximum contact pressure a foundation can transmit without soil shear failure.

items.question: method of irrigation which makes use of parallel strips where the water flows down the slope at a nearly uniform depth

choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Channels water into narrow trenches between crop rows rather than uniform sheet flow over strips.
choiceExplanations.Corrugation irrigation: Directs water through shallow closely spaced rills on irregular or steeper slopes.
choiceExplanations.Basin irrigation: Floods completely level diked plots rather than flowing uniformly down sloped parallel strips.
choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Correct — border irrigation advances a nearly uniform sheet of water down sloped strips bounded by ridges.

items.question: area of land bounded by two border ridges or dikes that guide the irrigation stream from the inlet point of application to the ends of the strip

choiceExplanations.Border strip: Correct — PAES defines a border strip as land bounded by two dikes guiding flow from inlet to end.
choiceExplanations.Level basin: Flat field enclosed on all four sides by dikes for ponded irrigation without slope.
choiceExplanations.Furrow channel: Narrow trench between crop ridges conveying small individual streams down a field.
choiceExplanations.Contour levee: Earthen bund built along terrain contours to impound water on sloping paddy fields.

items.question: inclination or elevation drop per unit length of the channel bottom

choiceExplanations.Energy grade slope: Rate of total head (elevation plus pressure plus velocity head) loss per unit channel length.
choiceExplanations.Channel bed slope: Correct — channel bed slope is the longitudinal inclination or elevation drop per unit length of channel bottom.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic grade slope: Slope of the piezometric or water surface line excluding velocity head.
choiceExplanations.Water surface slope: Longitudinal inclination of the free water surface, equal to bed slope only in uniform flow.

items.question: groundwater that is confined by relatively impermeable layer

choiceExplanations.Confined aquifer: Correct — a confined aquifer is bounded above and below by relatively impermeable strata under artesian pressure.
choiceExplanations.Perched aquifer: Localized unconfined groundwater body resting on an impermeable lens above the main water table.
choiceExplanations.Unconfined aquifer: Aquifer whose upper boundary is the open water table at atmospheric pressure.
choiceExplanations.Leaky aquifer: Aquifer bounded by semi-permeable aquitards that allow vertical seepage into or out of adjacent layers.

items.question: introduction of substances not found in the natural composition of water that make the water less desirable or unfit for intended use

choiceExplanations.Eutrophication: Excessive nutrient enrichment in water bodies causing dense algal growth and oxygen depletion.
choiceExplanations.Contamination: Correct — PAES defines contamination as introducing foreign substances that degrade water quality for its intended use.
choiceExplanations.Salinization: Accumulation of soluble salts in soil or water reducing agricultural suitability.
choiceExplanations.Sedimentation: Settling of suspended soil or mineral particles onto a channel or reservoir bed.

items.question: ratio between water received at the inlet for a block of fields to that released at the project's headwork

choiceExplanations.Distribution efficiency: Measures spatial uniformity of water application across an irrigated field.
choiceExplanations.Application efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the crop root zone to water delivered onto the field.
choiceExplanations.Conveyance efficiency: Correct — PAES defines conveyance efficiency as water received at the field block inlet divided by headwork release.
choiceExplanations.Storage efficiency: Ratio of water actually stored in the root zone to the total root-zone deficit.

items.question: loss of water from a channel during transport due to seepage and percolation
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; RECALLED COMPRESS; Tambong Subject B Part 1

choiceExplanations.Evaporation loss: Water vaporized directly into the air from open water surfaces or wetted soil.
choiceExplanations.Application loss: Water lost via runoff or deep percolation during actual field irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Conveyance loss: Correct — PAES defines conveyance loss as canal transport loss primarily from seepage and percolation.
choiceExplanations.Operational loss: Canal water wasted through gate mismanagement, spills, or unscheduled deliveries.

items.question: depth of water flow where the energy content is at minimum hence, no other backwater forces are involved
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 1; GENERAL KNOWLEDGE part 1

choiceExplanations.Alternate depth: Either of two flow depths (subcritical or supercritical) having the same specific energy.
choiceExplanations.Normal depth: Uniform flow depth where gravity force balances channel friction resistance.
choiceExplanations.Critical depth: Correct — critical depth occurs at minimum specific energy for a given discharge, where Froude number equals 1.
choiceExplanations.Conjugate depth: Paired subcritical and supercritical depths before and after a hydraulic jump with equal specific force.

items.question: ratio of the actual crop evapotranspiration to its potential evapotranspiration
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 1

choiceExplanations.Runoff coefficient: Dimensionless ratio of direct surface runoff to total rainfall in the rational formula.
choiceExplanations.Stress coefficient: Factor Ks (0 to 1) reducing crop evapotranspiration when soil moisture becomes limiting.
choiceExplanations.Pan coefficient: Empirical factor Kp converting Class A evaporation pan measurements to reference evapotranspiration.
choiceExplanations.Crop coefficient: Correct — crop coefficient (Kc) is the ratio of actual crop evapotranspiration (ETc) to reference/potential evapotranspiration (ETo).

items.question: sequence of different crops grown in regular order on any particular field or fields

choiceExplanations.Cropping intensity: Ratio of total harvested crop area per year to net physical cultivated area.
choiceExplanations.Cropping calendar: Time-based chart showing planting, management, and harvesting dates for crops in a year.
choiceExplanations.Planting schedule: Specific timetable specifying seeding or transplanting dates across irrigation blocks.
choiceExplanations.Cropping pattern: Correct — PAES defines cropping pattern as the yearly sequence and spatial arrangement of crops grown on a field.

items.question: amount of water used in producing crops which is the sum of evapotranspiration or consumptive use plus seepage and percolation losses

choiceExplanations.Field water requirements: Crop water requirement plus farm-level application losses incurred during irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Farm water requirements: Total water needed at the farm turnout, including field losses and farm ditch conveyance losses.
choiceExplanations.Crop water requirements: Correct — PAES defines crop water requirement for paddy crops as evapotranspiration plus seepage and percolation losses.
choiceExplanations.Gross water requirements: Total water diverted at the headworks, accounting for both farm and main canal losses.

items.question: any barrier constructed to store water

choiceExplanations.Flume: Open or elevated channel structure built to convey water across depressions or measure flow.
choiceExplanations.Dam: Correct — PAES defines a dam as any barrier constructed across a watercourse to impound and store water.
choiceExplanations.Weir: Overflow barrier built across a stream to measure discharge or raise upstream water level.
choiceExplanations.Spillway: Safety channel or structure designed to pass excess floodwater safely past a dam.

items.question: vertical distance from lowest point of the ground line to the dam crest

choiceExplanations.Freeboard height: Vertical distance between maximum flood water level and the top of the dam crest.
choiceExplanations.Dam height: Correct — PAES defines dam height as the vertical distance from the lowest ground line point to the dam crest.
choiceExplanations.Crest width: Horizontal top thickness of an embankment dam perpendicular to its axis.
choiceExplanations.Spillway height: Vertical elevation of the spillway crest above the riverbed or datum.

items.question: volume below the intake structure; sediment volume based on 25 years of accumulation in the reservoir

choiceExplanations.Flood storage: Dedicated reservoir space above normal level reserved to detain and attenuate flood peaks.
choiceExplanations.Surcharge storage: Temporary uncontrolled storage above the spillway crest during extreme flood inflows.
choiceExplanations.Active storage: Usable reservoir capacity between minimum operating level and normal pool level.
choiceExplanations.Dead storage: Correct — PAES defines dead storage as volume below the intake allocated for 25-year sediment accumulation.

items.question: depth of water in the channel cross-section

choiceExplanations.Area: Wetted cross-sectional area of the flowing stream perpendicular to flow.
choiceExplanations.Topwidth: Width of the free water surface across the top of an open channel.
choiceExplanations.Depth: Correct — flow depth is the vertical distance of water in the channel cross-section from bed to surface.
choiceExplanations.Freeboard: Safety height between the design water surface and the top of the channel lining or bank.

items.question: actual height of the embankment after settlement

choiceExplanations.Structural height: Vertical distance from the lowest foundation cutoff or excavation point to the dam crest.
choiceExplanations.Constructed height: Initial built height including extra settlement allowance before consolidation occurs.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic height: Vertical distance from the riverbed to the maximum water surface level.
choiceExplanations.Designed height: Correct — PAES defines designed height as the target embankment height achieved after full consolidation and settlement.

items.question: maximum area which an irrigation project can serve considering the extent of arable lands and the available water supply

choiceExplanations.Design irigable area: Correct — PAES defines design irrigable area as the maximum arable land an irrigation system can serve with available water.
choiceExplanations.Actual irrigated area: Land area that actually receives irrigation water during a given cropping season.
choiceExplanations.Operational service area: Portion of the project area currently equipped and actively managed for irrigation delivery.
choiceExplanations.Potential irrigable area: Total arable land physically suitable for irrigation regardless of current water supply limits.

items.question: numerical value on the uniformity of application for agricultural irrigation systems

choiceExplanations.Application efficiency: Application efficiency is the ratio of water stored in the root zone to total water applied to the field.
choiceExplanations.Water use efficiency: Water use efficiency is the ratio of crop yield or biomass produced to the amount of water consumed.
choiceExplanations.Distribution uniformity: Correct — Distribution uniformity quantifies how evenly irrigation water is applied across a field, typically comparing low-quarter to mean depth.
choiceExplanations.Storage efficiency: Storage efficiency is the ratio of water stored in the root zone during irrigation to the water needed before irrigation.

items.question: structure or weir provided across the river or creek to raise its water level and divert the water into the main canal to facilitate irrigation by gravity

choiceExplanations.Storage dam: Storage dam impounds a large volume of water in a reservoir for long-term supply, flood control, or power generation.
choiceExplanations.Check dam: Check dam is a small structure built across a gully or canal to reduce flow velocity, trap sediment, or raise head locally.
choiceExplanations.Diversion dam: Correct — A diversion dam or weir raises the water level across a river or creek to divert water by gravity into a main canal.
choiceExplanations.Detention dam: Detention dam temporarily holds flood runoff to reduce peak downstream discharge and releases it gradually.

items.question: the total quantity of water diverted from a stream, lake, or reservoir, or removed from the ground in order to irrigate a crop

choiceExplanations.Diversion water requirement: Correct — Diversion water requirement is the total water volume diverted from a surface source or pumped from groundwater to irrigate a crop.
choiceExplanations.Farm delivery requirement: Farm delivery requirement is the water delivered at the farm turnout, excluding main and lateral conveyance losses.
choiceExplanations.Net irrigation requirement: Net irrigation requirement is the depth of water needed in the root zone, excluding effective rainfall and all application losses.
choiceExplanations.Crop water requirement: Crop water requirement is the water needed by a crop to meet evapotranspiration losses for optimal growth under field conditions.

items.question: involves dripping water onto the soil at very low rates (2-20 litres/hour) from the emitters where water is applied close to plants so that only part of the soil in which the roots grow is wetted

choiceExplanations.Sprinkler irrigation: Sprinkler irrigation sprays water into the air through nozzles to fall over the entire crop area like rainfall.
choiceExplanations.Center-pivot irrigation: Center-pivot irrigation uses a mechanized rotating lateral supported on wheeled towers to sprinkle water over circular fields.
choiceExplanations.Drip irrigation/ trickle irrigation: Correct — Drip or trickle irrigation applies water slowly at 2–20 L/h near plants via emitters, wetting only the root zone soil.
choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Furrow irrigation applies water by gravity through small parallel channels excavated between crop rows.

items.question: in-line canal structure designed to convey canal water from a higher level to a lower level, duly dissipating the excess energy resulting from the drop in elevation

choiceExplanations.Siphon: Siphon conveys canal water under pressure over an obstruction or under a depression without dissipating elevation energy.
choiceExplanations.Flume: Flume is an artificial trough or chute supported above ground to carry canal water across depressions or unstable slopes.
choiceExplanations.Drop: Correct — A drop is an in-line canal structure that lowers water from a higher to a lower level while dissipating excess energy.
choiceExplanations.Turnout: Turnout is a gate or outlet structure that diverts controlled irrigation water from a supply canal into a farm ditch or field.

items.question: amount of rainwater that falls directly on the field and is used by the crop for growth and development excluding deep percolation, surface runoff and interception

choiceExplanations.Design rainfall: Design rainfall is a selected rainfall depth or intensity for a given return period used to size hydraulic or drainage structures.
choiceExplanations.Effective rainfall: Correct — Effective rainfall is the portion of direct rainfall retained in the root zone for crop growth, excluding runoff, deep percolation, and interception.
choiceExplanations.Gross rainfall: Gross rainfall is the total measured precipitation falling over an area before deducting any hydrological losses.
choiceExplanations.Excess rainfall: Excess rainfall is the fraction of storm rainfall that becomes direct surface runoff after subtracting infiltration and depression losses.

items.question: soil depth from which the bulk of the roots of the crop extracts most of the water needed for evapotranspiration

choiceExplanations.Effective rooting depth: Correct — Effective rooting depth is the soil depth from which the majority of crop roots extract most water for evapotranspiration.
choiceExplanations.Critical root zone: Critical root zone is not a standard irrigation design term for the primary water-extraction soil depth.
choiceExplanations.Allowable depletion depth: Allowable depletion depth is the fraction of available soil water permitted to be used before triggering the next irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Maximum rooting depth: Maximum rooting depth is the deepest extent any plant root reaches, which is deeper than the main water-extracting zone.

items.question: particle diameter corresponding to a 10% sieve passing

choiceExplanations.Median particle size: Median particle size (D50) is the grain diameter at which 50% of the soil sample by weight passes the sieve.
choiceExplanations.Modal grain size: Modal grain size is the most frequently occurring particle diameter class in a soil grain-size distribution.
choiceExplanations.Effective size: Correct — Effective size (D10) is defined in soil mechanics and filter design as the particle diameter corresponding to 10% sieve passing.
choiceExplanations.Mean grain diameter: Mean grain diameter is the arithmetic or geometric average particle size of a soil sample rather than the 10% passing percentile.

items.question: discharges from known sources which is passed into a body of water or land, or wastewater flowing out of a manufacturing plant, industrial plant including domestic, commercial and recreational facilities

choiceExplanations.Supernatant: Supernatant is the clear liquid layer lying above settled solids or sludge in a sedimentation tank or digester.
choiceExplanations.Effluent: Correct — Effluent refers to wastewater or liquid discharges flowing out of industrial, domestic, commercial, or treatment facilities into water or land.
choiceExplanations.Leachate: Leachate is liquid that has percolated through solid waste or soil, extracting dissolved or suspended materials.
choiceExplanations.Influent: Influent is raw wastewater or water flowing into a treatment plant, reservoir, or hydraulic structure.

items.question: any legal restriction or limitation on quantities, rates, and/or concentrations or any combination thereof, of physical, chemical or biological parameters of effluent which a person or point source is allowed to delivery into a body of water or land

choiceExplanations.Stream standard: Stream standard specifies allowable pollutant concentrations or quality criteria maintained within a receiving river or stream.
choiceExplanations.Ambient standard: Ambient standard sets maximum permissible pollutant levels in the surrounding natural environment such as air or receiving water bodies.
choiceExplanations.Influent limit: Influent limit restricts the strength or flow of wastewater entering a treatment plant rather than discharges leaving a facility.
choiceExplanations.Effluent standard: Correct — Under Philippine water quality regulations (RA 9275), an effluent standard sets legal limits on pollutants discharged into water or land.

items.question: water conveying conduit or trough which is supported on abutments by piers

choiceExplanations.Inverted siphon: Inverted siphon is a closed pressure conduit carrying canal water beneath roadways, railways, drainage channels, or depressions.
choiceExplanations.Elevated flume: Correct — An elevated flume is an above-ground water-conveying trough supported on abutments by piers across a depression or waterway.
choiceExplanations.Bench flume: Bench flume is a concrete or masonry channel built along a steep hillside bench rather than elevated on piers.
choiceExplanations.Box culvert: Box culvert is a closed rectangular conduit passing through an embankment to carry drainage or road-crossing flow.

items.question: spacing between emitters or emission points along a lateral line

choiceExplanations.Manifold spacing: Manifold spacing refers to the distance between submain or manifold pipes rather than between individual emitters.
choiceExplanations.Row spacing: Row spacing is the lateral distance between adjacent planted crop rows in the field.
choiceExplanations.Emitter spacing: Correct — Emitter spacing is the distance between adjacent emitters or emission points along a drip irrigation lateral line.
choiceExplanations.Lateral spacing: Lateral spacing is the distance between parallel irrigation lateral pipes across the irrigated block.

items.question: applicator used in drip, subsurface, or bubbler irrigation designed to disspate pressure and to discharge a small uniform flow or trickle of water at a constant rate that does not vary significantly because of minor differences in pressure

choiceExplanations.Diffusers: Diffusers are devices used to aerate wastewater or disperse air bubbles into a liquid tank.
choiceExplanations.Nozzles: Nozzles are orifices designed to break a pressurized water jet into droplets or a spray pattern for sprinkler irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Emitters: Correct — Emitters are micro-irrigation applicators engineered to dissipate pressure and discharge a small, nearly constant trickle of water.
choiceExplanations.Microsprinklers: Microsprinklers are low-pressure rotary or spray heads that throw fine water jets over a small radial area rather than dripping.

items.question: grade line of the water surface profile plus the velocity head in open channels
items.answer: Energy grade line/ specific energy line
choices: Energy grade line/ specific energy line

choiceExplanations.Hydraulic grade line: Hydraulic grade line represents the water surface profile in open channels without adding the velocity head.
choiceExplanations.Critical depth line: Critical depth line marks the elevation corresponding to minimum specific energy for a given discharge in an open channel.
choiceExplanations.Energy grade line/ specific energy line: Correct — The energy grade line (or total head line) equals the open-channel water surface elevation plus the velocity head (V²/2g).
choiceExplanations.Piezometric surface line: Piezometric surface line connects the levels to which water would rise in piezometer tubes, matching the hydraulic grade line.

items.question: provision for passing of equipment and small machinery

choiceExplanations.Cattle Crossing: Cattle crossing is a canal or stream structure built specifically to allow livestock to cross safely without damaging banks.
choiceExplanations.Turnout Structure: Turnout structure regulates and diverts irrigation water from a supply canal into a farm ditch or field.
choiceExplanations.Division Box: Division box splits incoming canal or ditch flow proportionally among two or more distribution channels.
choiceExplanations.Equipment Crossing: Correct — An equipment crossing is a bridge, culvert, or ramp structure provided across a canal for farm machinery and small equipment.

items.question: combination of water transpired from vegetation and evaporated from the soil, water, and plant surfaces.

choiceExplanations.Percolation: Percolation is the downward movement of water through saturated or near-saturated soil below the root zone toward groundwater.
choiceExplanations.Evapotranspiration: Correct — Evapotranspiration is the combined process of water loss through plant transpiration and direct evaporation from soil, water, and plant surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Infiltration: Infiltration is the downward entry of water through the soil surface into the soil profile.
choiceExplanations.Interception: Interception is rainfall caught and retained on plant foliage and stems that evaporates before reaching the soil surface.

items.question: channel which conveys irrigation water from the turnout to the paddy field

choiceExplanations.Main canal: Main canal is the primary conveyance channel that carries water from the headworks or diversion dam to lateral canals.
choiceExplanations.Drainage ditch: Drainage ditch collects and removes excess surface or subsurface runoff water from agricultural fields.
choiceExplanations.Farm ditch: Correct — A farm ditch is the small irrigation channel that conveys water from the canal turnout directly to the paddy field.
choiceExplanations.Lateral canal: Lateral canal branches off a main or submain canal to deliver water to farm turnouts across a service area.

items.question: dam component which prevents migration of small particles and screen off fine materials that flow with seepage water and prevent piping

choiceExplanations.Cutoff trench: Cutoff trench is an impermeable trench excavated beneath a dam foundation to block or lengthen the seepage path.
choiceExplanations.Filter drain: Correct — A filter drain intercepts seepage inside an embankment dam while screening out fine soil particles to prevent internal piping erosion.
choiceExplanations.Impervious core: Impervious core is a low-permeability clay or concrete central zone designed to minimize water seepage through the dam body.
choiceExplanations.Relief well: Relief well is a vertical well installed at the downstream toe of a dam to relieve excess hydrostatic uplift pressure.

items.question: height of the embankment to be attained during construction

choiceExplanations.Settled height: Settled height is the final elevation of the embankment after post-construction foundation and fill consolidation has occurred.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic height: Hydraulic height is the vertical distance from the lowest point of the original streambed to the maximum water surface elevation.
choiceExplanations.Structural height: Structural height is the vertical distance from the lowest foundation excavation point to the dam crest.
choiceExplanations.Finished height: Correct — Finished height is the constructed height of an earth embankment attained immediately upon completion, including settlement allowance.

items.question: amount of water to replenish the crop water requirement and losses less the effective rainfall

choiceExplanations.Farm water requirement: Correct — Farm water requirement equals crop water requirement plus farm application losses minus effective rainfall.
choiceExplanations.Diversion water requirement: Diversion water requirement includes main and lateral conveyance losses in addition to the farm water requirement.
choiceExplanations.Crop water requirement: Crop water requirement is the water needed for crop evapotranspiration without adjusting for farm losses or effective rainfall.
choiceExplanations.Net irrigation requirement: Net irrigation requirement excludes farm application and distribution losses, representing only the water stored in the root zone.

items.question: additional height of the dam provided as a safety factor to prevent overtopping by wave action or other causes

choiceExplanations.Freeboard: Correct — Freeboard is the vertical safety height between the maximum reservoir water level and the dam crest to prevent wave overtopping.
choiceExplanations.Camber: Camber is extra crown height built into the center of a dam crest to compensate for anticipated post-construction settlement.
choiceExplanations.Drawdown: Drawdown is the lowering of a reservoir water surface or groundwater table due to water withdrawal or release.
choiceExplanations.Surcharge: Surcharge is the temporary rise of reservoir water level above the normal spillway crest during flood routing.

items.question: small parallel channels, made to carry water in order to irrigate the crop

choiceExplanations.Borders: Borders are long, gently sloping field strips separated by low earth levees for surface sheet-flow irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Basins: Basins are level, diked field plots flooded completely with ponded water during irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Ridges: Ridges are raised soil beds formed between furrows on which row crops are planted.
choiceExplanations.Furrows: Correct — Furrows are small parallel channels excavated across a field to convey irrigation water along crop rows.

items.question: method of irrigation where water runs through small parallel channels as it moves down the slope of the field
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; recalled 2019; area 2 TERMINOLOGIES

choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Border irrigation floods gently sloping parallel strips bounded by levees as a thin sheet of water advances downslope.
choiceExplanations.Check irrigation: Check irrigation impounds water inside small level rectangular checks or basins surrounded by low dikes.
choiceExplanations.Basin irrigation: Basin irrigation applies water to level, diked areas until the entire surface is ponded to the desired depth.
choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Correct — Furrow irrigation directs water down the field slope through small parallel channels excavated between crop rows.

items.question: small channel along one part of a field that is used for distributing water in surface irrigation

choiceExplanations.Drainage ditch: Drainage ditch removes excess surface or subsurface water away from agricultural land rather than supplying irrigation water.
choiceExplanations.Tailwater ditch: Tailwater ditch collects excess surface runoff at the lower end of an irrigated field for disposal or reuse.
choiceExplanations.Head ditch/supply ditch: Correct — A head ditch (or supply ditch) runs along the upper edge of a field to distribute water into furrows or borders.
choiceExplanations.Collector ditch: Collector ditch gathers drainage outflow or tailwater from multiple field drains into a main outlet channel.

items.question: ratio of flow area to the wetted top width

choiceExplanations.Hydraulic depth: Correct — Hydraulic depth (D = A/T) is defined in open-channel hydraulics as the cross-sectional flow area divided by the water top width.
choiceExplanations.Normal depth: Normal depth is the uniform flow depth where gravity force equals channel boundary friction at a given slope and discharge.
choiceExplanations.Critical depth: Critical depth is the flow depth at which specific energy is minimum and the Froude number equals one.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic radius: Hydraulic radius (R = A/P) is the cross-sectional flow area divided by the wetted perimeter rather than the top width.

items.question: profile of the free water surface

choiceExplanations.Specific energy line: Specific energy line plots total head relative to the channel bed, equal to flow depth plus velocity head.
choiceExplanations.Critical depth line: Critical depth line connects elevations representing critical flow depth along a channel profile.
choiceExplanations.Energy grade line: Energy grade line plots the water surface elevation plus the velocity head along the channel.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic grade line/ hydraulic gradient: Correct — In open-channel flow, the hydraulic grade line (or hydraulic gradient) coincides with the free water surface profile.

items.question: occurs when a thin sheet of incoming flow moving at high velocity strikes water of sufficient depth

choiceExplanations.Hydraulic bore: Hydraulic bore is a moving surge wave advancing upstream or downstream due to rapid gate operation or tidal change.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic jump: Correct — A hydraulic jump occurs when high-velocity supercritical flow abruptly transitions to deeper, slower subcritical flow, dissipating energy.
choiceExplanations.Backwater curve: Backwater curve is a gradually varied water surface profile rising upstream behind a dam, weir, or constriction.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic drop: Hydraulic drop is a rapid transition from subcritical to supercritical flow over an abrupt lowering of the channel bed.

items.question: cross-sectional area of flow divided by the wetted perimeter

choiceExplanations.Hydraulic depth: Hydraulic depth is the cross-sectional flow area divided by the free-surface top width.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic radius: Correct — Hydraulic radius (R = A/P) is defined as the cross-sectional flow area divided by the wetted perimeter.
choiceExplanations.Wetted perimeter: Wetted perimeter is the length of the channel boundary in direct contact with the flowing water.
choiceExplanations.Section factor: Section factor is the product of flow area and square root of hydraulic depth (Z = A√D) used in critical flow calculations.

items.question: estimation of the chance or likelihood of occurrence of a given event by determining the frequency curves of best fit to samples of hydrologic data

choiceExplanations.Flow duration analysis: Flow duration analysis plots the percentage of time a given streamflow discharge is equaled or exceeded.
choiceExplanations.Double mass analysis: Double mass analysis tests the consistency of hydrologic records by comparing cumulative values of one station against nearby stations.
choiceExplanations.Flood routing analysis: Flood routing analysis tracks the attenuation and movement of a flood hydrograph through a reservoir or river reach.
choiceExplanations.Hydrologic frequency analysis: Correct — Hydrologic frequency analysis fits probability distributions to historical hydrologic data to estimate return periods and event likelihoods.

items.question: inside bottom or sill of the conduit
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Soffit: Soffit is the inside top surface (underside of the arch or roof) of a closed conduit or culvert.
choiceExplanations.Invert: Correct — The invert is the lowest inside bottom surface or sill of a pipe, culvert, or closed conduit.
choiceExplanations.Crown: Crown is the highest exterior or top point of an arch, pipe, or closed conduit cross-section.
choiceExplanations.Haunch: Haunch is the lower curved side portion of a pipe or arch conduit between the springline and the invert.

items.question: closed conduit designed to convey canal water in full and under pressure running condition, to convey canal water by gravity under roadways, railways, drainage channels and local depressions
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Box culvert: Box culvert is a short rectangular passage through an embankment typically flowing partially full as an open channel.
choiceExplanations.Elevated flume: Elevated flume carries canal water in an open trough supported above ground on piers rather than underground under pressure.
choiceExplanations.Inverted siphon: Correct — An inverted siphon is a pressurized closed conduit conveying canal water by gravity beneath roads, railways, drains, or depressions.
choiceExplanations.Pipe culvert: Pipe culvert conveys surface drainage water under a roadway or embankment rather than pressurized canal flow across depressions.

items.question: time required to cover an area with one application of water
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 1

choiceExplanations.Application time: Application time is the duration water is continuously applied to a single irrigation set or field plot.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation frequency: Irrigation frequency is how often irrigation is applied, expressed as the inverse of the irrigation interval.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation interval: Irrigation interval is the total number of days elapsed between the start of one irrigation and the start of the next.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation period: Correct — Irrigation period is the total time required to complete one full irrigation cycle across the entire target area.

items.question: geological formation shaped by the dissolution of a layer or layers of soluble bedrock, usually carbonate rocks such as limestone or dolomite
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Karst Topography: Correct — Karst topography forms through chemical dissolution of soluble carbonate bedrock such as limestone or dolomite, creating sinkholes and caves.
choiceExplanations.Deltaic Basin: Deltaic basin is a low-lying depositional landform built from river sediment at the mouth of a stream entering standing water.
choiceExplanations.Alluvial Plain: Alluvial plain is a flat landform created by the long-term deposition of river-borne sediments during flooding.
choiceExplanations.Fluvial Terrace: Fluvial terrace is a bench-like remnant of an old river floodplain left above the current valley floor by stream incision.

items.question: amount of water required in lowland rice production which includes water losses through evaporation, seepage and percolation and land soaking
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Crop Establishment water requirement: Crop establishment water requirement covers water needed after transplanting or seeding rather than the pre-planting land preparation phase.
choiceExplanations.Land Soaking water requirement: Land soaking water requirement covers only soil saturation and excludes puddling, evaporation, seepage, and percolation losses.
choiceExplanations.Deep Percolation water requirement: Deep percolation water requirement accounts solely for downward water loss below the root zone, not full land preparation.
choiceExplanations.Land Preparation water requirement: Correct — Land preparation water requirement in lowland rice includes land soaking plus evaporation, seepage, and percolation losses during preparation.

items.question: amount of water required in lowland rice production which is a function of the initial soil moisture and the physical properties of the soil
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; RECALLED COMPRESS; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Land soaking water requirement: Correct — Land soaking water requirement is the water needed to saturate paddy soil before puddling, depending on initial moisture and soil properties.
choiceExplanations.Net irrigation water requirement: Net irrigation water requirement is the total crop water deficit supplied to the root zone across the growing season.
choiceExplanations.Land preparation water requirement: Land preparation water requirement includes land soaking plus evaporation, seepage, and percolation throughout the preparation period.
choiceExplanations.Farm irrigation water requirement: Farm irrigation water requirement equals the crop water deficit plus on-farm application and distribution losses.

items.question: spacing between irrigation laterals
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Lateral spacing: Correct — Lateral spacing is the perpendicular distance between adjacent parallel irrigation lateral lines in sprinkler or drip systems.
choiceExplanations.Emitter spacing: Emitter spacing is the distance between consecutive emitters along a single drip lateral line.
choiceExplanations.Sprinkler spacing: Sprinkler spacing is the distance between individual sprinkler heads along a lateral pipe.
choiceExplanations.Manifold spacing: Manifold spacing is the distance between adjacent submain or manifold pipes supplying groups of laterals.

items.question: deep percolation of water beyond the root zone of plants, resulting in loss of salts or nutrients
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Infiltration: Infiltration is the entry of surface water into the top layer of soil rather than downward salt transport.
choiceExplanations.Leaching: Correct — Leaching is the deep percolation of water below the crop root zone that washes away dissolved salts or nutrients.
choiceExplanations.Percolation: Percolation is the general downward movement of water through soil layers without specifically referring to salt or nutrient removal.
choiceExplanations.Seepage: Seepage is the slow lateral or downward escape of water through porous soil, embankments, or unlined canal banks.

items.question: canals with impermeable material (usually concrete) for channel stabilization and/or reduced seepage

choiceExplanations.Natural waterway: Natural waterway is an unimproved natural stream or depression carrying surface runoff without artificial lining.
choiceExplanations.Unlined earth canal: Unlined earth canal is an excavated soil channel without an impermeable barrier, making it prone to seepage and erosion.
choiceExplanations.Subsurface conduit: Subsurface conduit is a buried pipe or closed drain carrying water underground rather than an open lined canal.
choiceExplanations.Lined channel/lined canals: Correct — Lined channels are open canals covered with impermeable materials like concrete to prevent seepage losses and stabilize banks.

items.question: portion of the pipe network between the mainline and the laterals
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Submain: Submain is a secondary supply pipe branching from the mainline that feeds one or more manifolds or directly feeds laterals.
choiceExplanations.Lateral: Lateral is the smallest distribution pipe along which sprinklers or drip emitters are mounted.
choiceExplanations.Mainline: Mainline is the primary large-diameter pipe conveying water from the pump or source to submains or manifolds.
choiceExplanations.Manifold: Correct — A manifold is the pipe header connecting the mainline or submain to multiple irrigation laterals.

items.question: measure of the variability of discharge of a random sample of a given make, model and size of emitter, as provided by the manufacturer and before any field operations or aging has taken place determined through a discharge test of a sample of 50 emitters under a set pressure at 20°C

choiceExplanations.Distribution uniformity coefficient: Distribution uniformity coefficient measures field-wide emitter discharge uniformity after installation, including pressure variations.
choiceExplanations.Manufacturer's coefficient of variation: Correct — Manufacturer's coefficient of variation measures inherent flow variability among 50 new emitters tested at constant pressure and 20°C.
choiceExplanations.Pressure variation coefficient: Pressure variation coefficient is not the standard index for factory emitter manufacturing variability.
choiceExplanations.Christiansen uniformity coefficient: Christiansen uniformity coefficient quantifies the spatial uniformity of water application across an irrigated field, commonly for sprinklers.

items.question: spillway which is not excavated such as natural draw, saddle or drainage way
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Ogee spillway: Ogee spillway is a constructed concrete overflow dam section shaped to match the lower nappe of a falling water jet.
choiceExplanations.Drop spillway: Drop spillway is a built concrete or masonry weir structure that drops excess flow vertically into a stilling basin.
choiceExplanations.Natural spillway: Correct — A natural spillway utilizes an unexcavated natural saddle, draw, or drainage way to pass excess reservoir floodwater safely.
choiceExplanations.Chute spillway: Chute spillway is an excavated, concrete-lined steep open channel built to convey floodwater down an embankment slope.

items.question: constant flow depth along a longitudinal section of a channel under a uniform flow condition
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Critical depth: Critical depth is the depth of minimum specific energy where the Froude number equals one.
choiceExplanations.Conjugate depth: Conjugate depth refers to the pre-jump or post-jump depth paired across a hydraulic jump in a horizontal rectangular channel.
choiceExplanations.Sequent depth: Sequent depth is the alternate depth after a hydraulic jump that has the same specific force as the initial depth.
choiceExplanations.Normal depth: Correct — Normal depth is the constant water depth maintained along a channel when flow is steady and uniform.

items.question: maximum elevation the water surface which can be attained by the dam or reservoir without flow in the spillway
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Maximum pool elevation: Maximum pool elevation is the highest reservoir water level reached during the design flood while the spillway is discharging.
choiceExplanations.Dead storage elevation: Dead storage elevation is the lowest outlet level below which stored water cannot be released by gravity.
choiceExplanations.Minimum operating elevation: Minimum operating elevation is the lowest water surface level required to sustain normal reservoir withdrawals or intakes.
choiceExplanations.Normal storage elevation: Correct — Normal storage elevation (or normal pool level) is the maximum reservoir water elevation attainable before water flows over the spillway.

items.question: water flow that is conveyed in such a manner that top surface is exposed to the atmosphere such as flow in canals, ditches, drainage channels, culverts, and pipes under partially full flow conditions

choiceExplanations.Open channel flow: Correct — Open channel flow occurs whenever water flows with a free surface exposed to atmospheric pressure, as in canals and partially full pipes.
choiceExplanations.Pressurized pipe flow: Pressurized pipe flow completely fills a closed conduit under pressure greater than atmospheric, with no free water surface.
choiceExplanations.Closed conduit flow: Closed conduit flow refers generally to water conveyed inside enclosed pipes or tunnels, typically running full under pressure.
choiceExplanations.Artesian aquifer flow: Artesian aquifer flow is confined groundwater movement under hydrostatic pressure between impermeable geologic strata.

items.question: drip emitter spacing which is 80% of the wetted diameter estimated from field tests
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; GENERAL KNOWLEDGE part 1

choiceExplanations.Minimum lateral spacing: Minimum lateral spacing is the smallest allowable distance between parallel drip lateral pipes, not between emitters.
choiceExplanations.Maximum wetted diameter: Maximum wetted diameter is the largest horizontal wet-bulb diameter observed beneath a single emitter, not a spacing ratio.
choiceExplanations.Nominal sprinkler spacing: Nominal sprinkler spacing refers to the design spacing between sprinkler heads, not drip emitters.
choiceExplanations.Optimal emitter spacing: Correct — Optimal emitter spacing is set at 80% of the field-tested wetted diameter to ensure continuous overlapping wetted strips along laterals.

items.question: method to determine the rate of flow under laminar flow conditions through a unit cross sectional are of soil under unit hydraulic gradient

choiceExplanations.Permeability test: Correct — A permeability test measures hydraulic conductivity—the laminar flow rate through a unit soil area under a unit hydraulic gradient.
choiceExplanations.Consolidation test: Consolidation test measures the rate and magnitude of soil settlement under applied vertical loads over time.
choiceExplanations.Infiltration test: Infiltration test measures the rate at which water enters the surface of unsaturated field soil, such as with a ring infiltrometer.
choiceExplanations.Hydrometer test: Hydrometer test determines the particle-size distribution of fine-grained silt and clay soils by sedimentation velocity.

items.question: sealed section formed between earth embankments where combined seepage and percolation will be measured

choiceExplanations.Lysimeter: Lysimeter is an isolated soil tank or container used to measure crop evapotranspiration and percolation water balance directly.
choiceExplanations.Pond: Correct — Under PAES irrigation standards, a pond is a sealed earth-embanked test section used to measure combined seepage and percolation rates.
choiceExplanations.Reservoir: Reservoir is a large impounding basin built to store surface runoff for irrigation, water supply, or flood control.
choiceExplanations.Infiltrometer: Infiltrometer is a metal ring or cylinder driven into the soil surface to measure vertical water infiltration rate.

items.question: area capable of being irrigated, principally as regards to availability of water, suitable soils, and topography of land

choiceExplanations.Gross command area: Gross command area is the total geographic area within a project boundary, including non-agricultural land, roads, and settlements.
choiceExplanations.Actual irrigated area: Actual irrigated area is the net land area that actually receives irrigation water during a given cropping season.
choiceExplanations.Developed service area: Developed service area is the land already equipped with irrigation canals and structures ready to receive water.
choiceExplanations.Potential irrigable area: Correct — Potential irrigable area is land suitable for irrigation based on water availability, soil suitability, and favorable topography.

items.question: part of the system that impounds the runoff

choiceExplanations.Catchment: Catchment is the drainage area or land surface that collects rainfall and directs runoff toward a stream or outlet.
choiceExplanations.Watershed: Watershed is the total upland area drained by a river system and bounded by topographic divides.
choiceExplanations.Reservoir: Correct — A reservoir is the engineered storage basin behind a dam that impounds surface runoff for later use.
choiceExplanations.Spillway: Spillway is the hydraulic safety structure that releases excess floodwater from a reservoir to prevent dam overtopping.

items.question: moisture left in the soil before the initial irrigation water delivery which describes the extent of water depletion from the soil when the water supply has been cut-off

choiceExplanations.Saturation moisture content: Saturation moisture content is the maximum water held in soil when all pore spaces are completely filled with water.
choiceExplanations.Residual moisture content: Correct — Residual moisture content is the moisture remaining in the soil after supply cutoff, just before initial irrigation water delivery.
choiceExplanations.Available moisture content: Available moisture content is the water held between field capacity and permanent wilting point that plants can extract.
choiceExplanations.Hygroscopic moisture content: Hygroscopic moisture content is thin water film tightly adsorbed to soil particles below the wilting point, unavailable to plants.

items.question: taking wastewater from one industry or process, treating it and then using it in another process or industry such as for irrigation, as liquid fertilizer and for aquaculture

choiceExplanations.Recycling: Refers to reprocessing wastewater back into the same industrial process or facility rather than another sector.
choiceExplanations.Reclamation: Refers to treating wastewater to restore its quality for safe discharge or beneficial purposes in general.
choiceExplanations.Recovery: Refers to extracting valuable materials, energy, or nutrients from waste streams during treatment processes.
choiceExplanations.Re-use: Correct — PAES defines re-use as treating wastewater from one industry or process for beneficial use in another, like irrigation or aquaculture.

items.question: conveys canal water under roads or railroads

choiceExplanations.Division box: A canal structure used to split and distribute flow proportionately among two or more branch channels.
choiceExplanations.Road crossing: Correct — A road crossing is a conveyance structure, such as a culvert or bridge, carrying canal water beneath roads or railroads.
choiceExplanations.Check structure: A gated or weir structure placed across a canal to raise upstream water level for diversion.
choiceExplanations.Drop structure: A hydraulic structure installed to convey water safely down steep canal slopes without causing erosion.

items.question: tube or shaft vertically set into the ground at a depth that is usually less than 15 m for the purpose of bringing groundwater into the soil surface whose pumps are set above the water level

choiceExplanations.Shallow tubewell: Correct — Under PAES 222, a shallow tubewell is a vertical shaft under 15 m deep using surface-mounted suction pumps.
choiceExplanations.Artesian well: A well tapping a confined aquifer where hydrostatic pressure pushes water upward without mechanical pumping.
choiceExplanations.Deep tubewell: A drilled well generally exceeding 15 m depth requiring submerged or turbine pumps set below water level.
choiceExplanations.Open well: A large-diameter dug well, usually lined with masonry or concrete, accessing shallow unconfined groundwater.

items.question: occurrence or frequency of earthquakes in a region

choiceExplanations.Stratigraphy: The geological study of layered rock and soil strata, their sequence, and depositional history.
choiceExplanations.Seismicity: Correct — Seismicity denotes the geographic and historical occurrence, frequency, and intensity of earthquakes within a given region.
choiceExplanations.Liquefaction: A phenomenon where saturated, loose soil temporarily loses strength and behaves like a liquid during shaking.
choiceExplanations.Subsidence: The gradual sinking or downward settling of the Earth's surface caused by groundwater extraction or compaction.

items.question: water escaping below or out from water conveyance facilities such as open ditches, canals, natural channels, and waterway

choiceExplanations.Infiltration: The downward entry of surface water into the soil through the ground surface.
choiceExplanations.Percolation: The downward movement of water through saturated or unsaturated soil below the root zone.
choiceExplanations.Evaporation: The phase change of liquid water into vapor directly from open water or wet soil surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Seepage: Correct — Seepage is water escaping laterally or downward out of conveyance facilities such as canals, ditches, and reservoirs.

items.question: line with no filter arrangements where seepage occurs

choiceExplanations.Hydraulic grade line: A plot representing the sum of pressure head and elevation head along a fluid conduit.
choiceExplanations.Equipotential line: A contour connecting points of equal hydraulic head within a porous medium flow net.
choiceExplanations.Capillary fringe line: The upper boundary of soil moisture drawn upward above the water table by surface tension.
choiceExplanations.Seepage line/phreatic line: Correct — The seepage or phreatic line marks the upper surface of saturation in an embankment where seepage emerges without filters.

items.question: distance from the perimeter of the irrigation area to the community or area of concern that is sensitive to contamination

choiceExplanations.Setback distance: Correct — PAES defines setback distance as the required separation between an irrigated area perimeter and sensitive communities or contamination receptors.
choiceExplanations.Buffer width: Generally describes a vegetated strip or zone along waterways meant to trap sediment and pollutants.
choiceExplanations.Border allowance: Refers to extra strip width or margin provided at field edges during land grading or border irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Clearance distance: Typically refers to vertical or horizontal physical spacing around machinery, pipelines, or overhead structures.

items.question: ratio of the horizontal to vertical dimension of the channel wall

choiceExplanations.Bed slope: The longitudinal inclination of the channel bottom along the direction of flow.
choiceExplanations.Friction slope: The rate of head loss due to friction per unit length of channel flow.
choiceExplanations.Side slope: Correct — Side slope is defined as the horizontal-to-vertical ratio (z:1) of an open channel's inclined bank walls.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic slope: The slope of the water surface or energy grade line along an open channel.

items.question: channel which releases surplus or flood water which cannot be contained in the active storage space of the reservoir

choiceExplanations.Sluiceway: A gated opening near a dam base used to flush accumulated sediment or release bottom water.
choiceExplanations.Penstock: A closed pressure conduit carrying water from a forebay or reservoir to hydraulic turbines.
choiceExplanations.Headworks: Diversion structures at a river intake designed to regulate water entry into a main irrigation canal.
choiceExplanations.Spillway: Correct — A spillway safely discharges excess floodwater that exceeds the active storage capacity of a reservoir.

items.question: method of applying irrigation water similar to natural rainfall where water is distributed through a system of pipes by pumping and then sprayed into the air through sprinklers so that it breaks up into small water drops which fall to the ground

choiceExplanations.Subsurface irrigation: Delivers water directly beneath the soil surface into the crop root zone via buried pipes or water table control.
choiceExplanations.Drip irrigation: Applies water slowly and directly near individual plant roots through low-pressure emitters or drippers.
choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Directs gravity-fed water down small parallel channels excavated between crop rows.
choiceExplanations.Sprinkler irrigation: Correct — Sprinkler irrigation pumps water through pipes and sprays it into the air through nozzles to simulate natural rainfall.

items.question: distance between two sprinkler heads along the lateral

choiceExplanations.Emitter spacing: The distance between adjacent drip emitters along a trickle or micro-irrigation lateral line.
choiceExplanations.Submain spacing: The distance between parallel submain pipes feeding multiple lateral lines in an irrigation layout.
choiceExplanations.Lateral spacing: The distance between adjacent parallel lateral pipelines along the main or submain line.
choiceExplanations.Sprinkler spacing: Correct — Sprinkler spacing is the measured distance between consecutive sprinkler heads mounted along a single lateral line.

items.question: total capacity at normal water surface elevation

choiceExplanations.Active capacity: The usable reservoir volume between the minimum operating level and normal water surface elevation.
choiceExplanations.Dead capacity: The reservoir volume below the lowest outlet sill that cannot be drained by gravity.
choiceExplanations.Storage capacity: Correct — Total storage capacity is the entire reservoir volume impounded up to the normal water surface elevation.
choiceExplanations.Surcharge capacity: The temporary flood storage volume situated between normal water surface elevation and maximum flood level.

items.question: ratio of the storage capacity to the total earth volume required for embankment construction which indicates the relative cost of the different types of reservoir

choiceExplanations.Runoff ratio: The fraction of total rainfall depth that becomes surface runoff over a watershed.
choiceExplanations.Embankment ratio: Not a standard PAES reservoir cost index; usually refers to embankment slope or fill proportion.
choiceExplanations.Drawdown ratio: Compares water level drop during pumping or reservoir release to initial water depth.
choiceExplanations.Storage ratio: Correct — Under PAES small water impounding guidelines, storage ratio equals reservoir storage capacity divided by embankment earth volume.

items.question: vertical distance measured from the top of the dam down to the bedrock
