choiceExplanations.Hydraulic height: The vertical distance from the lowest point of the original streambed to maximum water level.
choiceExplanations.Structural height: Correct — Structural height of a dam is measured vertically from the dam crest down to the lowest foundation bedrock.
choiceExplanations.Embankment height: Typically measured from the original ground surface or streambed to the crest of an earthfill dam.
choiceExplanations.Effective height: Represents the functional water-retaining height above tailwater or natural ground rather than bedrock depth.

items.question: application of water by gravity flow to the surface of the field. Either the entire field is flooded (basin irrigation) or the water is fed into small channels (furrows) or strips of land (borders)

choiceExplanations.Subsurface irrigation: Applies water below the ground surface directly to the root zone without wetting the topsoil.
choiceExplanations.Drip irrigation: Delivers frequent, low-volume water droplets directly to plants through pressurized tubing and emitters.
choiceExplanations.Surface irrigation: Correct — Surface irrigation distributes water over the field by gravity flow using basins, borders, or furrows.
choiceExplanations.Sprinkler irrigation: Pressurizes water through pipes and sprays droplets over crops like artificial rainfall.

items.question: width of the channel cross-section at the free surface

choiceExplanations.Bottom width: The horizontal width of a trapezoidal or rectangular channel measured along its bed.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic depth: The cross-sectional flow area divided by the top width of the free water surface.
choiceExplanations.Normal depth: The uniform flow depth occurring in a channel when gravity balances boundary friction.
choiceExplanations.Top width: Correct — Top width is the horizontal width of an open channel's water cross-section at the free surface.

items.question: ratio of the particle size at 60% pasing to that at 10% passing

choiceExplanations.Consolidation coefficient: Measures the rate at which saturated soil compresses and expels pore water under sustained load.
choiceExplanations.Gradation coefficient: A general informal phrase rather than the specific D60/D10 soil particle-size ratio.
choiceExplanations.Uniformity coefficient: Correct — Hazen's uniformity coefficient (Cu) equals D60 divided by D10, measuring the range of soil particle sizes.
choiceExplanations.Curvature coefficient: Defined as (D30)^2 / (D10 * D60) to describe the shape of a grain-size distribution curve.

items.question: occurs when flow has a constant water area, depth, discharge, and average velocity through a reach of channel

choiceExplanations.Varied flow: Open-channel flow whose depth, area, and velocity change along the length of the channel.
choiceExplanations.Uniform flow: Correct — Uniform flow maintains constant depth, cross-sectional area, discharge, and average velocity along a channel reach.
choiceExplanations.Steady flow: Flow whose velocity and depth at any fixed point remain constant over time.
choiceExplanations.Critical flow: Flow occurring at minimum specific energy for a given discharge, where Froude number equals one.

items.question: canals that are cut through the soil, in which the soil excavated from the bed are used to form the embankment

choiceExplanations.Elevated concrete flume: A raised reinforced-concrete trough supported on piers to carry water across depressions or valleys.
choiceExplanations.Masonry-lined channel: An earth channel armored with mortared stone or brick lining to reduce seepage and erosion.
choiceExplanations.Concrete-lined canal: An irrigation channel paved with cast-in-place or precast concrete slabs to minimize conveyance losses.
choiceExplanations.Unlined canal/unlined channel: Correct — An unlined canal is excavated directly in earth with its banks built from the excavated soil without artificial lining.

items.question: side of the embankment wetted by the impounded water

choiceExplanations.Upstream face: Correct — The upstream face is the sloping reservoir-side surface of an embankment directly in contact with impounded water.
choiceExplanations.Cutoff wall: A vertical impermeable barrier extending below a dam foundation to block under-seepage paths.
choiceExplanations.Embankment crest: The flat top surface of a dam providing freeboard above water and roadway access.
choiceExplanations.Downstream face: The dry outer slope of an embankment facing away from the impounded reservoir water.

items.question: accounting of water inflows, such as irrigation and rainfall, and outflows, such as evaporation, seepage and percolation

choiceExplanations.Water duty: The total volume or depth of irrigation water required to mature a given crop area.
choiceExplanations.Water demand: The total water requirement needed for crop evapotranspiration, conveyance losses, and agricultural operations.
choiceExplanations.Water yield: The total runoff volume produced by a watershed over a specified time period.
choiceExplanations.Water balance: Correct — Water balance systematically accounts for all water inflows (rainfall, irrigation) and outflows (evaporation, seepage, percolation) in a system.

items.question: area which contributes runoff or drains water into the reservoir

choiceExplanations.Recharge zone: A permeable land area where surface water infiltrates downward to replenish an underlying groundwater aquifer.
choiceExplanations.Water shed: Correct — A watershed is the land area whose topography drains all surface runoff into a reservoir or stream.
choiceExplanations.Flood plain: Low-lying land adjacent to a river channel subject to periodic inundation during high-flow events.
choiceExplanations.Water course: A natural or artificial channel along which surface water flows continuously or intermittently.

items.question: privilege granted by the government to use and appropriate water

choiceExplanations.Water permit: The formal document issued by NWRB evidencing the grant of a water right under the Water Code.
choiceExplanations.Water lease: A temporary contractual rental arrangement for using water allocated to another entity.
choiceExplanations.Water right: Correct — Under the Philippine Water Code (PD 1067), a water right is the government-granted privilege to appropriate and use water.
choiceExplanations.Water tariff: The fee or pricing rate charged to users for water supply and irrigation services.

items.question: reservoir where the upper reaches of the basin is shielded by high mountain barriers

choiceExplanations.Well-protected reservoir: Correct — Under reservoir wind-exposure classification, a well-protected reservoir has its upper basin shielded by surrounding high mountain barriers.
choiceExplanations.Open-valley reservoir: A reservoir situated in broad, flat terrain with minimal topographic shielding from wind.
choiceExplanations.Wind-exposed reservoir: A reservoir lacking surrounding terrain barriers, experiencing high wind fetch and evaporation losses.
choiceExplanations.Partially-sheltered reservoir: A reservoir bordered by moderate hills providing only limited protection against prevailing winds.

items.question: diameter of the circular area wetted by the sprinkler when operating at a given pressure and no wind

choiceExplanations.Wetted diameter: Correct — Wetted diameter is the full diameter of the circular ground area covered by a sprinkler operating without wind.
choiceExplanations.Effective spacing: The recommended distance between sprinklers or laterals to achieve uniform water distribution overlap.
choiceExplanations.Wetted radius: Half of the wetted diameter, measuring the maximum throw distance from the sprinkler head.
choiceExplanations.Nozzle diameter: The internal bore size of the sprinkler orifice controlling discharge rate and droplet breakup.

items.question: portion of the perimeter of the canal that is in contact with the flowing water

choiceExplanations.Bottom width: The horizontal dimension of the flat base of an open channel cross-section.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic depth: Flow cross-sectional area divided by the water surface top width.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic radius: Flow cross-sectional area divided by the wetted perimeter of the channel.
choiceExplanations.Wetted perimeter: Correct — Wetted perimeter is the total length of the channel cross-section boundary directly touching flowing water.

items.question: width of the strip that would be wetted by a row of emitters spaced at their optimal spacing along a single lateral line

choiceExplanations.Emitter spacings: The longitudinal distances between individual drip emitters installed along a lateral pipe.
choiceExplanations.Wetted depths: The vertical penetration distances of moisture below drip emitters into the soil profile.
choiceExplanations.Wetted radii: The lateral radial spread of moisture outward from a single point-source emitter.
choiceExplanations.Wetted widths: Correct — Wetted width is the lateral width of the continuous soil strip wetted by optimally spaced emitters along a lateral.

items.question: is one of the methods used to measure the seepage and percolation in open channels where a section of the channel shall be sealed at two ends by earth embankments lined with plastic sheet. This sealed section of the channel shall serve as a pond, in which the amount of water lost for a given time interval shall be measured

choiceExplanations.Dilution: Measures discharge by injecting a known tracer concentration and sampling its downstream dilution.
choiceExplanations.Tracing: Uses dyes, salts, or isotopes to track water flow paths and travel times.
choiceExplanations.Ponding: Correct — Under PAES 603, the ponding method isolates a canal reach with plastic-lined dikes to measure static water level drop.
choiceExplanations.Metering: Measures flow rates directly using mechanical, electromagnetic, or ultrasonic flow meters in conduits.

items.question: one of the methods used to measure the conveyance losses in open channels where a section of the selected channel shall be analyzed using the water balance approach

choiceExplanations.Area-velocity: Determines channel discharge at a single cross-section by multiplying flow area by average velocity.
choiceExplanations.Stage-discharge: Relates measured water surface elevation to discharge via a calibrated rating curve.
choiceExplanations.Inflow-outflow: Correct — The inflow-outflow method computes canal conveyance losses by subtracting outflow from inflow over a reach using water balance.
choiceExplanations.Salt-dilution: Estimates stream discharge by measuring electrical conductivity changes after injecting a salt tracer.

items.question: an overflow structure built perpendicular to an open channel axis to measure the rate of flow of water

choiceExplanations.Weir: Correct — A weir is an overflow barrier built perpendicular to a channel axis where head above the crest indicates flow rate.
choiceExplanations.Flume: An in-line open-channel constriction aligned with flow direction to measure discharge without ponding sediment.
choiceExplanations.Siphon: A closed inverted or bent conduit conveying water over an obstacle or beneath a roadway.
choiceExplanations.Orifice: A submerged sharp-edged opening in a wall through which flow discharges under upstream pressure head.

items.question: in-line structure with a geometrically specified constriction built in an open channel such that the center line coincides with the center line of the channel in which the flow is to be measured

choiceExplanations.Orifice: A sharp-edged submerged aperture in a plate or wall used to measure flow.
choiceExplanations.Venturi: A closed-conduit meter with a converging-diverging throat that measures pipe flow via pressure drop.
choiceExplanations.Flume: Correct — A measuring flume is a calibrated in-line channel constriction aligned with the channel centerline to measure open-channel flow.
choiceExplanations.Weir: A perpendicular overflow crest wall across an open channel that backs up upstream water.

items.question: measuring device with a well-defined, sharp-edged opening in a wall through which flow occurs such that the upstream water level is always well above the top of this opening

choiceExplanations.Flume: An open-channel flow-measuring structure with a free water surface passing through a throat constriction.
choiceExplanations.Venturi: A closed-pipe constriction meter that relates differential pressure between inlet and throat to flow rate.
choiceExplanations.Weir: An open-channel overflow structure where water spills freely over a crest rather than a submerged opening.
choiceExplanations.Orifice: Correct — An orifice is a sharp-edged opening placed well below the upstream water surface to measure flow from head difference.

items.question: water applied to an individual basin and all of that applied water is allowed to infiltrate. Each basin in the irrigation block is hydraulically independent. Water advances from the inflow point towards the downstream end of the basin in a regular pattern, which may be distorted by surface irregularities. Inflow is normally shutoff before the water reaches the downstream end of the basin

choiceExplanations.Closed Single Basin: Correct — In a closed single basin, water enters an isolated, bunded basin and infiltrates completely without draining downstream.
choiceExplanations.Cascade Flow Basin: Water overflows from an upper terrace or basin sequentially into adjacent lower-elevation basins.
choiceExplanations.Multiple Supply Basin: Basins fed simultaneously or sequentially via shared supply channels rather than completely independent infiltration.
choiceExplanations.Open Single Basin: A single basin with drainage outlets allowing excess applied water to leave the lower end.

items.question: each basin is irrigated separately by a supply channel running along the boundary with a number of adjacent basins. In each basin, the water level in the supply channel controls the water application. When a basin is irrigated, the water level in the channel is raised higher than the soil surface elevation and overflows onto the basin. When the irrigation is completed, the water level in the channel is lowered below the soil surface elevation of the basin and supply is diverted to the next basin. The excess water from the first basin drains back to the supply channel. The next basin is irrigated with the supply discharge plus the drainage water from the upstream basin (or basins)

choiceExplanations.Cascade Terrace Basin: Irrigates tiered hillside plots by allowing water to spill directly from higher terraces to lower ones.
choiceExplanations.Multiple/ Sequential Basin: Correct — In multiple/sequential basin irrigation, a shared boundary supply channel raises levels to flood each basin and reuses drained excess downstream.
choiceExplanations.Closed Single Basin: Irrigates one hydraulically isolated basin where all applied water infiltrates without draining back to a channel.
choiceExplanations.Open Single Basin: Applies water to a single basin equipped with a free-draining outlet rather than sequential channel reuse.

items.question: irrigation water is led directly from the field channel into the basin through siphons, spiles or bundbreaks.

choiceExplanations.Direct method: Correct — In the direct basin irrigation method, water enters each basin directly from a field channel via siphons, spiles, or bund breaks.
choiceExplanations.Series method: Routes irrigation water sequentially through multiple connected plots rather than feeding each from a field channel.
choiceExplanations.Controlled method: A generic term for regulated water delivery rather than the specific field-channel-to-basin intake method.
choiceExplanations.Cascade method: Passes irrigation water from the uppermost terrace downward by gravity through successive lower terraces.

items.question: irrigation water is supplied to the highest terrace, and then allowed to flow to a lower terrace and so on.

choiceExplanations.Intermittent method: Delivers irrigation water in alternating on-and-off cycles rather than continuous terrace-to-terrace overflow.
choiceExplanations.Cascade method: Correct — The cascade method supplies water to the highest terrace and lets excess flow downward into successive lower terraces.
choiceExplanations.Parallel method: Feeds multiple terraces or basins independently at the same time from a distribution canal.
choiceExplanations.Direct method: Supplies each basin individually from an adjacent field ditch using siphons, spiles, or bund breaks.

items.question: this is usually applied to large borders where the end borders are provided with openings to accommodate free flow of water for drainage

choiceExplanations.Contour-strip border system: Border strips laid out along land contours on sloping terrain rather than straight down-slope.
choiceExplanations.Blocked-end border system: Uses closed downstream dikes to impound all applied water within small, nearly level border strips.
choiceExplanations.Dead-level border system: Zero-slope basins enclosed on all sides where water spreads rapidly and ponds until infiltrated.
choiceExplanations.Open-end border system: Correct — An open-end border system leaves openings at the downstream end of large borders to allow free excess drainage.

items.question: this is usually applied to small borders where the end borders restrict the further downward flow of water.

choiceExplanations.Contour-strip border system: Arranges border strips along topographic contours across gentle slopes to limit erosion.
choiceExplanations.Graded-slope border system: Refers to borders constructed with a uniform longitudinal slope down the field rather than closed ends.
choiceExplanations.Open-end border system: Provides downstream openings on large borders to discharge excess runoff freely into a drain.
choiceExplanations.Blocked-end border system: Correct — A blocked-end border system closes the downstream end of small borders to retain water and prevent tailwater runoff.

items.question: the water flows down the slope in small furrows called corrugations or rills which is used for germinating drill-seeded on broadcasted crops. No raised beds are used for crops

choiceExplanations.Surge irrigation: Applies water intermittently in timed pulses down furrows or borders to improve advance uniformity.
choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Floods wide strips of land bounded by parallel low earthen dikes without small rills.
choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Uses larger excavated channels spaced between raised beds for row crops.
choiceExplanations.Corrugation irrigation: Correct — Corrugation irrigation guides water down small shallow rills without raised beds, ideal for germinating close-grown or broadcast crops.

items.question: this type of furrow irrigation shall increase the length that the water must travel to reach the end of irrigation run thus, reducing the average slope and velocity of the water. This can be formed down and across the slope by machines.

choiceExplanations.Straight furrows: Parallel linear channels running directly down or across gentle slopes without winding paths.
choiceExplanations.Zigzag furrows: Correct — Zigzag furrows wind back and forth to lengthen the flow path, thereby reducing effective slope and water velocity.
choiceExplanations.Alternate furrows: Irrigates only every second furrow during a given application to conserve water and promote root aeration.
choiceExplanations.Contour furrows: Curved channels laid out nearly perpendicular to steep field slopes along elevation contours.

items.question: average sprinkler pressure of a lateral

choiceExplanations.Design pressure: The total pump head required to overcome elevation, friction losses, and supply nominal nozzle pressure.
choiceExplanations.Residual pressure: The remaining pressure available at the far end of a pipeline after all losses.
choiceExplanations.Average pressure: Correct — Average pressure refers to the mean operating water pressure measured across all sprinklers along a lateral line.
choiceExplanations.Static pressure: The water pressure measured inside a closed pipe system when no water is flowing.

items.question: pressure required to overcome the elevation difference between the water source and the sprinkler nozzle, to counteract friction losses and to provide adequate pressure at the nozzle for good water distribution

choiceExplanations.Average pressure: The mean pressure experienced across all operating sprinklers along a lateral pipe.
choiceExplanations.Static pressure: The pressure exerted by stationary water in a pipe system when valves are closed.
choiceExplanations.Design pressure: Correct — Design pressure accounts for elevation lift, pipe friction losses, and the required nozzle operating pressure for uniform distribution.
choiceExplanations.Residual pressure: The leftover pressure remaining at a downstream point after friction and elevation losses occur.

items.question: delivers water from the source to the pipe system at an adequate capacity

choiceExplanations.Pump unit: Correct — The pump unit draws water from the source and supplies pressurized flow into the pipe network at required capacity.
choiceExplanations.Surge tank: A pressure-relief vessel installed to dampen water hammer transients in pipelines.
choiceExplanations.Control unit: Consists of valves, gauges, and timers that regulate system pressure, flow rate, and scheduling.
choiceExplanations.Filter unit: Removes suspended sediment and organic debris before water enters sprinklers or emitters.

items.question: consists of screen openings considerably lower than the nozzle diameter to prevent nozzles from clogging

choiceExplanations.Filtration system: Correct — A filtration system uses screen or media openings much smaller than nozzle diameters to trap debris and prevent clogging.
choiceExplanations.Injection system: Introduces dissolved fertilizers or chemicals into pressurized irrigation water for chemigation.
choiceExplanations.Pumping system: Generates the hydraulic head and flow rate needed to move water from source to field.
choiceExplanations.Distribution system: The network of mainlines, submains, and laterals conveying water to application points.

items.question: device of various nozzle sizes which sprays water over the ground or crop.

choiceExplanations.Risers: Short vertical pipes connecting underground or surface laterals up to the sprinkler heads.
choiceExplanations.Laterals: Branch pipes running across the irrigated field to feed individual sprinklers or emitters.
choiceExplanations.Sprinklers: Correct — Sprinklers are fitted with nozzles of various sizes to break pressurized water into droplets sprayed over crops.
choiceExplanations.Emitters: Low-discharge micro-irrigation outlets that drip or trickle water directly at the soil surface.

items.question: pipes which convey water from the pump to the laterals

choiceExplanations.Headers and Manifolds: Short connecting pipe sections that distribute flow into multiple parallel drip tapes or laterals.
choiceExplanations.Laterals and Risers: Small-diameter field pipes and vertical standpipes that directly carry sprinklers or emitters.
choiceExplanations.Mainlines and SubMainlines: Correct — Mainlines and submainlines form the primary trunk pipelines transporting pumped water to the field laterals.
choiceExplanations.Branches and Feeders: Informal plumbing terms not used in PAES pressurized irrigation pipe hierarchy.

items.question: areas with limited entry such as freeway landscape, highway medians and other similar areas

choiceExplanations.Buffer areas: Protective transition strips separating agricultural zones from waterways or neighboring properties.
choiceExplanations.Exposed areas: Open sites subject to direct sun, wind, or public contact rather than limited entry.
choiceExplanations.Restricted areas: Correct — Under wastewater reuse and landscape irrigation standards, restricted areas are low-access sites like highway medians and freeway landscapes.
choiceExplanations.Sloped areas: Steeply graded lands prone to surface runoff and soil erosion during irrigation.

items.question: temporary water storage that adds kinetic energy to facilitate water distribution. This is also known as a water tank

choiceExplanations.Reservoir: Correct — In PAES solar irrigation terminology, a reservoir or water tank temporarily stores water and adds potential/kinetic energy for distribution.
choiceExplanations.Standpipe: A tall vertical open-topped pipe used in water networks to maintain head and absorb surges.
choiceExplanations.Penstock: A pressurized intake conduit delivering water from a reservoir directly into a hydro turbine.
choiceExplanations.Forebay: A small regulating basin immediately upstream of a pump intake or hydroelectric penstock.

items.question: amount of solar energy received by or projected onto a surface, expressed in Watts per square meter(W/m2)

choiceExplanations.Solar Constant: The average solar irradiance received outside Earth's atmosphere at one astronomical unit (~1361 W/m2).
choiceExplanations.Solar Emittance: The radiant flux emitted per unit area by a surface, rather than incoming solar power.
choiceExplanations.Solar Insolation: Total cumulative solar energy received per unit area over time, expressed in kWh/m2 or J/m2.
choiceExplanations.Solar Irradiance: Correct — Under PAES solar pump standards, solar irradiance is instantaneous solar power incident per unit area, measured in W/m2.

items.question: irrigation system powered by solar energy, using PV technology, which converts solar energy into electrical energy to run a DC or AC motor-based water pump. It consists of solar PV modules, pump set, electronic controls to operate the pump, the required hardware, and in some cases other items like inverters and batteries

choiceExplanations.Diesel Driven irrigation system: Uses an internal combustion diesel engine to drive the irrigation water pump.
choiceExplanations.Solar Powered irrigation system: Correct — A solar-powered irrigation system (SPIS) uses PV modules and electronic controls to convert sunlight into electricity driving a water pump.
choiceExplanations.Wind Powered irrigation system: Harnesses wind turbine rotor blades to mechanically or electrically pump groundwater.
choiceExplanations.Hydro Powered irrigation system: Uses flowing stream energy, such as a hydraulic ram or waterwheel, to lift irrigation water.

items.question: the vertical distance from the free suction water level to the center line of the pump suction

choiceExplanations.Suction head: Refers to positive pressure head when the free water level is above the pump suction centerline.
choiceExplanations.Suction lift: Correct — PAES defines suction lift as the vertical distance from the free suction water level up to the pump centerline.
choiceExplanations.Discharge lift: Not a standard pump head term; discharge elevation is measured as static discharge head.
choiceExplanations.Static head: Represents the total vertical distance between the suction water level and the discharge water level.

items.question: ratio of the output power of the pump set and the total solar input power

choiceExplanations.Array efficiency: Measures only how effectively the photovoltaic array converts incident solar irradiance into DC electrical power.
choiceExplanations.Pump efficiency: Measures only the ratio of hydraulic water power output to mechanical shaft power input.
choiceExplanations.System efficiency: Correct — In solar-powered irrigation systems (PAES), system efficiency is the pump output power divided by total solar input power.
choiceExplanations.Motor efficiency: Measures only how effectively the electric motor converts electrical input power into mechanical shaft power.

items.question: measure of energy increase imparted to the water by the pump and expressed by the algebraic difference between the total discharge head and total suction head, expressed in meters (m)

choiceExplanations.Net suction head: Refers only to pressure conditions on the suction side, not the total energy imparted by the pump.
choiceExplanations.Static discharge head: Measures only the vertical elevation from the pump centerline to the free discharge water level.
choiceExplanations.Total dynamic head/total head: Correct — Total dynamic head is the net energy per unit weight added to water, equal to total discharge minus suction head.
choiceExplanations.Friction loss head: Accounts only for head lost to pipe and fitting friction, not the pump's total energy increase.

items.question: combine the structure and guidance system of a centerpivot lateral with a traveling water-feed system similar to a travelling sprinkler

choiceExplanations.Side-Roll: Uses a rigid lateral pipe serving as the axle of large wheels rolled sideways between set positions.
choiceExplanations.Traveling-Gun: Uses a single high-capacity gun sprinkler mounted on a wheeled cart pulled across the field.
choiceExplanations.Center-Pivot: Rotates a self-propelled lateral continuously around one fixed central pivot point to irrigate a circle.
choiceExplanations.Linear-Move: Correct — A linear-move system pairs a center-pivot-style lateral and guidance system with a traveling water-feed mechanism.

items.question: sprinkles water from a continuously moving lateral pipeline. The self-propelled lateral is fixed at one end and rotates to irrigate a large cicular area. The fixed end of the lateral, called the pivot point is connected to the water supply.

choiceExplanations.Center pivot: Correct — A center pivot rotates a self-propelled lateral continuously around a fixed pivot supply point to water a circular field.
choiceExplanations.Linear move: Moves continuously in a straight rectangular path rather than rotating around a fixed pivot point.
choiceExplanations.Traveling gun: Pulls a single large gun sprinkler across the field using a flexible hose or cable.
choiceExplanations.Side roll: Uses a wheel-mounted lateral pipe periodically rolled sideways rather than continuously rotating around a pivot.

items.question: sprinklers operate while moving in either a circular or straight path

choiceExplanations.Solid set system: Uses stationary sprinklers arranged across the entire field so laterals never move during irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Hand move system: Consists of portable laterals manually disconnected, carried, and reconnected between stationary irrigation sets.
choiceExplanations.Periodic move system: Operates stationary sprinklers during each set and moves them between positions after irrigation stops.
choiceExplanations.Continuous move system: Correct — Continuous move systems (like center-pivot and linear-move) apply water while traveling steadily along a circular or straight path.

items.question: sprinkler systems not requiring to be moved during the course of irrigation

choiceExplanations.Portable system: Uses movable pipes and sprinklers relocated across the field during the irrigation season.
choiceExplanations.Fixed system: Correct — A fixed (solid-set or permanent) sprinkler system remains stationary and requires no moving during irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Periodic move system: Requires shifting laterals or sprinklers from one stationary irrigation set to the next.
choiceExplanations.Continuous move system: Operates sprinklers mounted on self-propelled laterals or carts that travel continuously while irrigating.

items.question: type of mechanical-move system where nozzles are attached to long discharge tubes and rotated by means of a rocker arm drive

choiceExplanations.Linear-move sprinkler system: Uses a self-propelled lateral moving straight across rectangular fields with multiple small sprinklers.
choiceExplanations.Center-pivot sprinkler system: Uses a self-propelled lateral rotating continuously around a fixed central supply point.
choiceExplanations.Side-roll lateral sprinkler system: Supports a rigid lateral on large wheels rolled sideways between stationary irrigation sets.
choiceExplanations.Gun and Boom sprinkler system: Correct — Boom sprinklers use nozzles on long rotating discharge tubes driven by a rocker arm or jet reaction.

items.question: type of mechanical-move system where it consists of rigidly coupled lateral pipe connected to a buried mainline positioned in the center of the field. Laterals are towed lengthwise over the mainline from one side to the other in an "s" form

choiceExplanations.End-tow lateral system: Correct — End-tow laterals are rigidly coupled and towed lengthwise in an S-path across a central buried mainline.
choiceExplanations.Side-roll lateral system: Moves the lateral sideways on large axle-mounted wheels rather than towing it lengthwise.
choiceExplanations.Center-pivot lateral system: Rotates continuously around a fixed central water supply rather than being towed across a mainline.
choiceExplanations.Linear-move lateral system: Advances continuously in a straight line using self-propelled towers and guidance controls.

items.question: type of mechanical-move system where the lateral pipes are rigidly coupled and each joint of pipe is supported by a large wheel where the lateral line forms the axle for the wheels. This is mechanically moved by an engine mounted at the center of the line.

choiceExplanations.Linear-move lateral system: Travels continuously in a straight line via powered A-frame towers rather than wheel-axle rolling.
choiceExplanations.End-tow lateral system: Consists of rigidly coupled pipes towed lengthwise across a central mainline in an S-pattern.
choiceExplanations.Side-roll lateral system: Correct — A side-roll (wheel-move) system uses the lateral pipe as an axle for large wheels driven by a center engine.
choiceExplanations.Center-pivot lateral system: Rotates continuously around a stationary central pivot point on powered wheeled towers.

items.question: composed of portable or buried pipe with valve outlets at intervals for attaching the portable laterals.

choiceExplanations.Side-roll lateral system: Uses large wheels and a central engine to roll the rigid lateral laterally.
choiceExplanations.Hose-pull lateral system: Uses flexible hoses with attached sprinklers dragged manually between positions rather than rigid portable pipe.
choiceExplanations.Hand-move lateral system: Correct — Hand-move systems use portable or buried mainlines with valve outlets where lightweight portable laterals attach manually.
choiceExplanations.End-tow lateral system: Uses rigidly coupled laterals towed lengthwise by tractor across a central buried mainline.

items.question: sprinklers that must be moved manually through a series of positions during the course of irrigation

choiceExplanations.Automated permanent system: Remains fixed underground or above ground with automatic valves, requiring no manual relocation.
choiceExplanations.Continuous move system: Irrigates while moving steadily rather than stopping in discrete manual positions.
choiceExplanations.Fixed sprinkler system: Stays stationary across the entire field without needing relocation during irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Periodic move system: Correct — Periodic move systems operate stationary sprinklers at each set and are moved manually between irrigation positions.

items.question: operate with sprinklers set in a fixed position

choiceExplanations.Linear-move system: Irrigates while moving continuously in a straight path across a rectangular field.
choiceExplanations.Continuous-move system: Applies water while the lateral or gun steadily travels across the field.
choiceExplanations.Travelling system: Uses a self-propelled cart and flexible hose moving continuously while spraying water.
choiceExplanations.Set system: Correct — A set system operates sprinklers while they remain in a fixed, stationary position during application.

items.question: deliver water from the mainlines or submainlines to the sprinklers

choiceExplanations.Headers: Pipe sections that collect or distribute flow among parallel pipes rather than carrying field sprinklers.
choiceExplanations.Laterals: Correct — Laterals are the branch pipelines that convey water from mainlines or submainlines directly to sprinklers or emitters.
choiceExplanations.Manifolds: Sub-headers that feed multiple lateral lines or group control valves, not the lines holding sprinklers.
choiceExplanations.Risers: Short vertical pipes connecting a lateral line upward to an individual sprinkler head.

items.question: the water both from the sprinkler inlet and through the flow controller reaches the silicon tube, setting the tube in motion and water is spread on the field.

choiceExplanations.Oscillating sprinklers: Sweep a perforated spray bar back and forth to water rectangular areas.
choiceExplanations.Stationary sprinklers: Correct — Per PAES trickle/micro-sprinkler classification, water enters a flexible silicon tube whose motion disperses droplets uniformly.
choiceExplanations.Gear-driven sprinklers: Rotate a turret smoothly using an internal water-powered turbine and gear reduction assembly.
choiceExplanations.Impact sprinklers: Rotate intermittently by a spring-loaded arm striking the sprinkler body.

items.question: water coming out of the nozzle is directed into an offset channel on the rotor plate, which creates a reactionary drive force that turns the sprinkler

choiceExplanations.Rotor and gear rotating sprinkler: Correct — Rotor/gear sprinklers direct water through an offset channel on a rotor plate, creating reaction torque to rotate.
choiceExplanations.Spring-arm impact rotating sprinkler: Rotates via a spoon-deflected spring arm repeatedly impacting the sprinkler bridge.
choiceExplanations.Pop-up fixed-head spray sprinkler: Emits a fixed fan or full-circle mist pattern without rotating parts.
choiceExplanations.Stationary nozzle spray sprinkler: Sprays water continuously through fixed orifices without any rotating rotor mechanism.

items.question: water coming out of the nozzle is directed by the spoon at a 90- degree angle, forcing the arm away from the impact bridge. The arm spring, after absorbing this energy, returns the arm to its original position, which hits the bridge and causes the body to rotate

choiceExplanations.Gear-driven sprinkler: Turns smoothly via an internal water turbine and gear train without a hitting arm.
choiceExplanations.Oscillating sprinkler: Uses a swinging spray tube oscillating back and forth rather than a spring impact arm.
choiceExplanations.Impact sprinkler: Correct — An impact sprinkler uses a nozzle-deflecting spoon and spring arm that rebounds to strike the bridge and rotate.
choiceExplanations.Stationary sprinkler: Releases water through fixed nozzles or a static deflector with no rotating drive mechanism.

items.question: high capacity sprinkler fed with water through a flexible hose which is mounted on a self-powered chassis and travels along a straight line while watering

choiceExplanations.Center-pivot: Rotates a long multi-tower lateral around a fixed central pivot rather than traveling straight with a hose.
choiceExplanations.Side-roll: Rolls a wheel-mounted rigid lateral sideways between fixed irrigation sets.
choiceExplanations.Hand-move: Requires manual lifting and moving of portable lateral pipes between stationary sets.
choiceExplanations.Travelling: Correct — A travelling sprinkler mounts a high-capacity gun on a self-propelled chassis fed by a flexible hose along a straight path.

items.question: consists of valves to control the discharge and pressure in the entire system which may have filters and a a fertilizer or nutrient tank.

choiceExplanations.Submain line: Conveys pressurized water from the mainline to individual field lateral lines.
choiceExplanations.Control head: Correct — In drip/trickle irrigation (PAES), the control head houses main valves, filters, pressure regulators, and fertigation tanks.
choiceExplanations.Pumping station: Houses the pump and prime mover supplying pressure, before filtration and fertigation controls.
choiceExplanations.Distribution manifold: Splits flow from a submain into multiple laterals in a field zone.

items.question: supply water from the control head into the fields which are usually made from PVC or polyethylene hose and should be buried below ground because they easily degrade when exposed to direct solar radiation

choiceExplanations.Main, submain lines and laterals: Correct — PVC or PE main, submain, and lateral pipes convey water from the control head and degrade under UV exposure.
choiceExplanations.Hydrants, couplers and sprinklers: Above-ground connection hardware and application heads rather than the buried supply pipe network.
choiceExplanations.Valves, regulators and filters: Flow-control and filtration components typically grouped at the control head or manifold.
choiceExplanations.Risers, manifolds and emitters: Short vertical pipes, sub-headers, and discharge outlets rather than the entire buried delivery network.

items.question: removes particle to prevent emitter clogging where its net diameter is smaller than one-tenth to one-fouth of the emitter opening diameter.

choiceExplanations.Filter: Correct — A drip filter removes suspended particles using screen or media openings smaller than one-tenth to one-fourth of the emitter orifice.
choiceExplanations.Manifold: Distributes filtered water from a submain to multiple lateral lines.
choiceExplanations.Regulator: Controls downstream water pressure or flow rate rather than straining particulates.
choiceExplanations.Injector: Introduces fertilizers or chemicals into the irrigation line rather than removing solid particles.

items.question: contains filters, pressure regulators, air and/or vacuum relief valves

choiceExplanations.Manifold: Correct — In PAES micro-irrigation standards, a manifold assembly contains secondary filters, pressure regulators, and air/vacuum relief valves.
choiceExplanations.Lateral: The small-diameter polyethylene pipe along crop rows carrying emitters.
choiceExplanations.Riser: A short vertical pipe connecting a buried pipe to an above-ground outlet or sprinkler.
choiceExplanations.Submain: The supply pipeline branching off the mainline to feed field manifolds.

items.question: water is routed through a long, narrow passage at laminar flow to reduce the water pressure and to create a more uniform flow; flow areas: 1 mm2 to 4.5 mm2.

choiceExplanations.Long-path: Correct — Long-path emitters route water through a narrow laminar channel (1–4.5 mm²) to dissipate pressure evenly.
choiceExplanations.Short-path: Uses a much shorter laminar flow channel suited specifically for very low operating pressures.
choiceExplanations.Vortex: Dissipates pressure through swirling rotational motion inside a circular chamber rather than a straight narrow channel.
choiceExplanations.Tortuous: Uses a longer, zigzagging larger-section channel generating turbulent flow to reduce pressure.

items.question: have relatively long flow paths with larger path cross-section with turbulent flow regime

choiceExplanations.Tortuous: Correct — Tortuous-path emitters feature long zigzagging channels with larger cross-sections that induce turbulent flow to resist clogging.
choiceExplanations.Vortex: Creates a circular swirling vortex inside a round cell to dissipate pressure.
choiceExplanations.Orifice: Relies on a small sharp-edged opening that emits water as a turbulent jet broken into drops.
choiceExplanations.Diaphragm: Uses a flexible elastomeric membrane that deforms with pressure changes to regulate discharge.

items.question: This type of dam shall be considered if sufficient quantities of both pervious and impervious materials are available.

choiceExplanations.Homogeneous type: Built almost entirely of a single uniform low-permeability soil when pervious material is scarce.
choiceExplanations.Diaphragm type: Uses a thin central cutoff wall of concrete, steel, or clay within pervious embankment fill.
choiceExplanations.Rockfill type: Relies primarily on dumped or compacted rock fragments with an upstream or internal impervious membrane.
choiceExplanations.Zoned type: Correct — A zoned embankment dam uses an impervious core flanked by pervious outer shells when both materials are abundant.

items.question: This type of dam shall be considered if the supply of materials of low permeability such as sandy or silty clay and other clayey material is abundant. The embankment material must be sufficiently impervious to provide adequate water barrier.

choiceExplanations.Dumped Rockfill Membrane Type: Relies on rockfill for stability and an artificial or clay membrane rather than uniform clayey earth.
choiceExplanations.Homogeneous/Modified Homogeneous Type: Correct — A homogeneous dam is chosen when low-permeability clayey soils are abundant enough to form the entire water-retaining body.
choiceExplanations.Impervious Diaphragm Core Type: Uses a thin impervious barrier inside predominantly pervious embankment fill.
choiceExplanations.Zoned Embankment Core Type: Combines an impervious central core with large quantities of pervious shell materials.

items.question: Suited to an area with an undulating topography. A dam is built across a valley and water is impounded on the upstream side of the dam

choiceExplanations.Rectangular balance excavation: Balances cut and fill on gently sloping land rather than damming across a valley.
choiceExplanations.Dugout pond: Excavates storage completely below flat ground level, requiring pumping to extract water.
choiceExplanations.Straight embankment: Correct — A straight embankment dam spans across a valley in undulating terrain to impound runoff upstream.
choiceExplanations.Semicircular embankment: Curves along contours on gently sloping terrain rather than spanning straight across a valley.

items.question: On slightly sloping land, the excavated earth can be used to impound some water above ground level. On higher slopes, it can be designed so that all water is stored above service level

choiceExplanations.Straight valley embankment: Built straight across a valley floor in undulating topography to impound water upstream.
choiceExplanations.Semicircular contour embankment: Follows a curved contour line on sloping land without balanced rectangular cut-and-fill walls.
choiceExplanations.Rectangular balance excavation: Correct — Rectangular balance excavation uses excavated earth on sloping land to form embankments storing water partly or wholly above ground.
choiceExplanations.Excavated dugout pond: Stores water wholly below ground level on flat terrain, requiring pumping for extraction.

items.question: The only designed suited to flat areas. A reservoir is constructed by excavating the earth leaving storage space that can be filled with water. Water is stored below the ground level and pumping is required to draw out water.

choiceExplanations.Straight embankment: Requires undulating valley topography to dam runoff behind a straight wall.
choiceExplanations.Dugout pond: Correct — A dugout pond is suited to flat land, storing water below ground in an excavated pit requiring pumping.
choiceExplanations.Semicircular embankment: Used on gently sloping terrain to impound runoff along a curved earth berm.
choiceExplanations.Rectangular balance excavation: Uses sloped ground so excavated earth forms embankments holding water above service level.

items.question: intended for installation between laterals

choiceExplanations.End-line: Installed only at the terminal end of a lateral or spaghetti tube.
choiceExplanations.In-line: Correct — In-line emitters are spliced or molded directly between sections of the irrigation lateral pipe.
choiceExplanations.On-line: Punched directly into or attached onto the outer wall of the lateral pipe.
choiceExplanations.Off-line: Not a standard PAES lateral emitter mounting classification.

items.question: intended for direct or indirect installation in the wall of the irrigation lateral

choiceExplanations.End-line: Placed at the outlet end of a micro-tube rather than in the lateral wall.
choiceExplanations.In-line: Spliced between cut segments of the lateral pipe rather than inserted into its wall.
choiceExplanations.On-line: Correct — On-line emitters are inserted directly into punched holes along the wall of the lateral pipe.
choiceExplanations.Off-line: Not a recognized PAES classification for emitter installation on irrigation laterals.

items.question: eject large particles during operation since this type has relatively large-diameter flexible orifices in series to dissipate pressure

choiceExplanations.Continuous flushing: Correct — Continuous-flushing emitters use large flexible orifices in series that flex to expel particles continuously during operation.
choiceExplanations.Manual flushing: Requires an operator to open lateral end caps or valves by hand to clear debris.
choiceExplanations.Periodic flushing: Flushes debris only briefly during system start-up or shut-down rather than continuously while operating.
choiceExplanations.Pressure compensating: Regulates uniform flow across varying inlet pressures using an internal flexible diaphragm.

items.question: its flow path is a round cell that causes circular flow. The fast rotational motion creates a _____ which results to higher head losses that allow for larger openings

choiceExplanations.Siphon: Conveys water over an elevated crest by atmospheric pressure and gravity, not emitter swirling.
choiceExplanations.Vortex: Correct — A vortex emitter forces water tangentially into a circular chamber, creating a spinning vortex that increases head loss.
choiceExplanations.Vacuum: Refers to sub-atmospheric pressure conditions, typically prevented by vacuum relief valves in drip lines.
choiceExplanations.Venturi: Uses a constricted throat to create suction for injecting fertilizer, not for emitter pressure dissipation.

items.question: the fully turbulent jet emitted at the outlet of the emitter is broken and converted into drop by drop flow; flow area: 0.2 mm2 to 0.35mm2

choiceExplanations.Orifice: Correct — Orifice emitters discharge water through a tiny 0.2–0.35 mm² opening, breaking a turbulent jet into drops.
choiceExplanations.Vortex: Dissipates pressure through rotational swirling inside a circular chamber rather than a simple small orifice.
choiceExplanations.Tortuous: Reduces pressure along a long zigzagging turbulent path rather than a single small orifice.
choiceExplanations.Diaphragm: Uses a flexible membrane to maintain constant discharge under fluctuating line pressures.

items.question: almost similar with long-path emitters but with shorter water path; ideal for use in very low pressure systems

choiceExplanations.Vortex: Uses a circular spinning chamber to generate high head loss at standard pressures.
choiceExplanations.Orifice: Uses a single tiny hole to convert a turbulent jet into dripping flow.
choiceExplanations.Short-path: Correct — Short-path emitters resemble long-path emitters but have a shorter laminar channel suited for very low pressures.
choiceExplanations.Diaphragm: Relies on a pressure-sensitive flexible diaphragm to regulate emitter flow rate.

items.question: the angle with which a ray of sunlight strikes the surface of the PV module, measured with respect to a line perpendicular to said surface

choiceExplanations.Angle of elevation: Vertical angle of the sun measured above the horizontal ground plane, not relative to module normal.
choiceExplanations.Angle of declination: Angular distance of the sun north or south of the Earth's equatorial plane.
choiceExplanations.Angle of azimuth: Horizontal compass bearing of the sun measured from north or south.
choiceExplanations.Ray of incidence: Correct — Under PAES solar pump standards, ray (angle) of incidence is the angle between incoming sunlight and the PV surface normal.

items.question: ratio of the input solar power to the PV module and the output power of the inverter/controller

choiceExplanations.PV conversion efficiency: Measures the ratio of electrical power output from a cell or module to incident solar power.
choiceExplanations.PV capacity factor: Compares actual energy generated over a period to the maximum possible output at rated capacity.
choiceExplanations.PV performance ratio: Correct — Per PAES solar pump terminology, PV performance ratio relates PV solar input power to inverter/controller output power.
choiceExplanations.PV array utilization: Refers to how much of the array's available capacity is used by the load.

items.question: assembly of photovoltaic cells mounted in a frame that uses sunlight as a source of energy to generate a DC electricity

choiceExplanations.PV string inverter: Converts DC electricity from a series string of PV modules into AC power.
choiceExplanations.PV charge controller: Regulates battery charging current and voltage between a PV array and battery bank.
choiceExplanations.PV module/ solar panel: Correct — A PV module (solar panel) is a framed assembly of photovoltaic cells converting sunlight into DC electricity.
choiceExplanations.Solar thermal collector: Absorbs sunlight to heat water or air rather than generating DC electricity.

items.question: pump designed to operate above water surface

choiceExplanations.Submersible pump: Operates fully submerged below the water surface inside a well or sump.
choiceExplanations.Surface pump: Correct — A surface pump is installed and operates above the water surface, drawing water via suction pipe.
choiceExplanations.Semi-submersible pump: Has its wet end submerged in water while its drive motor remains above the surface.
choiceExplanations.Deep-well cylinder pump: Places its reciprocating plunger cylinder submerged deep inside the well casing.

items.question: pump designed to operate fully submerged in the water source

choiceExplanations.Submersible pump: Correct — A submersible pump has a hermetically sealed motor-pump unit designed to operate fully submerged in water.
choiceExplanations.Dry-pit pump: Installed in a dry chamber adjacent to a wet well rather than submerged in water.
choiceExplanations.Surface pump: Mounted above the water source and relies on suction lift to draw water.
choiceExplanations.Suction-lift pump: Operates above water level, limited by atmospheric pressure and cavitation.

items.question: agricultural machinery that is used to lift or transfer water from one source to another

choiceExplanations.Pump: Correct — A pump is agricultural machinery that adds hydraulic energy to lift or transfer water between sources.
choiceExplanations.Blower: Moves large volumes of air or gas at relatively low pressure increases.
choiceExplanations.Turbine: Extracts mechanical work from flowing fluid rather than imparting energy to lift water.
choiceExplanations.Compressor: Increases the pressure of compressible gases by reducing their volume.

items.question: composed of PV modules connected in combination of series and parallel connections, which convert energy from the sun into electrical energy

choiceExplanations.Photovoltaic Controller: Regulates electrical power transfer between the solar array, battery, or pump motor.
choiceExplanations.Photovoltaic Cell: The smallest single semiconductor unit that converts sunlight directly into electricity.
choiceExplanations.Photovoltaic Array: Correct — A photovoltaic array consists of multiple PV modules wired in series and parallel to generate higher power.
choiceExplanations.Photovoltaic Inverter: Converts DC electricity produced by PV modules into alternating current (AC).

items.question: converts direct current (DC) from PV module to alternating current

choiceExplanations.Invrter: Correct — An inverter (spelled "Invrter" in the source key) converts direct current (DC) from PV modules into alternating current (AC).
choiceExplanations.Transformer: Steps alternating current voltage up or down via electromagnetic induction without converting DC to AC.
choiceExplanations.Rectifier: Performs the opposite function, converting alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC).
choiceExplanations.Converter: Generally changes DC voltage levels (DC-to-DC) rather than specifically inverting DC to AC.

items.question: monitors the charging and discharging of the battery connected to the PV array

choiceExplanations.Surge arrester: Protects electrical equipment from sudden high-voltage lightning or switching transients.
choiceExplanations.Voltage regulator: Maintains a constant output voltage level without specifically managing battery charge/discharge cycles.
choiceExplanations.Charge controller: Correct — A charge controller regulates battery charging and prevents overcharging or deep discharging in PV systems.
choiceExplanations.Power inverter: Converts direct current (DC) power into alternating current (AC) for AC loads.

items.question: link between motor pump and solar generator that regulates the operation of PV array to pump and is classified into two types: inverter (directly connected to pump set) and charge controller (with batteries)

choiceExplanations.Controller: Correct — Under PAES solar pump standards, the controller links the PV generator and motor pump via an inverter or charge controller.
choiceExplanations.Transformer: Alters AC voltage levels through magnetic induction without regulating solar-to-pump operation.
choiceExplanations.Rectifier: Converts AC to DC, whereas solar PV modules already output direct current.
choiceExplanations.Combiner: Merges electrical outputs from multiple PV strings into one main feed without active pump regulation.

items.question: consists of a well-graded mixture of hard and durable particles, and slightly weathered to fresh rock to secure the stability of dam body

choiceExplanations.Filter zone or transition zone: Uses graded sand and gravel to prevent fine core particles from migrating into coarse rockfill.
choiceExplanations.Impervious zone or core zone: Uses compacted cohesive clay or silt to block water seepage through the dam.
choiceExplanations.Blanket zone or toe drain: Collects and safely discharges seepage water exiting at the downstream dam toe or foundation.
choiceExplanations.Rockfill zone or pervious zone: Correct — The rockfill (pervious) zone uses well-graded, hard, durable rock to provide structural stability for the dam body.

items.question: composed of semi-pervious materials

choiceExplanations.Rockfill zone: Composed of coarse, highly pervious durable rock providing structural weight and stability.
choiceExplanations.Filter zone: Correct — A filter (transition) zone uses semi-pervious graded materials between the impervious core and coarse rockfill to prevent piping.
choiceExplanations.Impervious zone: Built from low-permeability clay or silty soils to block seepage through the dam.
choiceExplanations.Riprap zone: Consists of large armor stones placed on the upstream slope to resist wave erosion.

items.question: composed of impervious blanket usually made of cohesive soil or non-cohesive silt and is covered for protection. Materials shall have the required coefficient of permeability with a smaller compressibility after compaction, shall be easy to be compacted, and shall not contain organic substances.

choiceExplanations.Impervious zone: Correct — The impervious zone uses compactable, organic-free cohesive soil or silt with low permeability to prevent water seepage.
choiceExplanations.Transition zone: Uses intermediate-sized materials separating fine filter layers from coarse rockfill shells.
choiceExplanations.Rockfill zone: Uses coarse, durable, free-draining rock fragments to stabilize the dam body.
choiceExplanations.Filter zone: Uses semi-pervious sand and gravel to stop soil particles migrating out of the core.

items.question: The interior section of a rockfill dam is typically divided into zones depending on the range of variation in the character and gradation of the available material.

choiceExplanations.Zoning: Correct — Zoning divides a dam's interior section into distinct material zones based on gradation, permeability, and availability.
choiceExplanations.Compaction: Densifies placed soil or rock layers mechanically to increase shear strength and reduce settlement.
choiceExplanations.Benching: Cuts stepped horizontal ledges into steep abutments or slopes to bond embankment fill safely.
choiceExplanations.Grouting: Injects cement or chemical slurry into foundation rock fissures to seal seepage paths.

items.question: dam that relies on rock, either dumped in lifts or compacted in layers, as a major structural element where an impervious membrane is used as the water barrier and can be placed either within the embankment or on the upstream slope

choiceExplanations.Buttress dam: Uses a thin watertight upstream face supported by concrete or masonry buttress walls.
choiceExplanations.Earthfill dam: Constructed primarily of compacted soil materials (clay, silt, sand, gravel) rather than rockfill.
choiceExplanations.Gravity dam: Relies on the massive weight of concrete or masonry alone to resist water pressure.
choiceExplanations.Rockfill dam: Correct — A rockfill dam uses dumped or compacted rock for structural stability with an internal or upstream impervious membrane.

items.question: a widened, unobstructed shoulder area, about 30 meters long, that may be used for emergency purposes or allow slow-moving vehicles to pull out of the carriageway to give passing opportunity to following or incoming vehicles

choiceExplanations.Tangent section: A straight roadway alignment segment between curves, not a widened passing shoulder.
choiceExplanations.Turnout section: Correct — PAES defines a turnout section as a ~30 m widened shoulder for emergency stops or slow-vehicle pullouts.
choiceExplanations.Transition section: A roadway or canal segment where cross-sectional geometry gradually changes between two different sections.
choiceExplanations.Approach section: The roadway segment immediately preceding an intersection, bridge, or hydraulic structure.

items.question: raised structure of soil, soil aggregate, sand or rock

choiceExplanations.Roadway shoulder: The strip adjacent to the carriageway providing lateral support and emergency stopping space.
choiceExplanations.Roadway subbase: A compacted granular layer placed between the subgrade and base course for load distribution.
choiceExplanations.Roadway subgrade: The prepared native soil or foundation surface supporting the pavement structure.
choiceExplanations.Roadway embankment: Correct — PAES defines a roadway embankment as a raised structure composed of soil, aggregate, sand, or rock.

items.question: product resulting from the mechanical crushing of gravel, with substantially all fragments having at least one face resulting from fracture

choiceExplanations.Bank-run gravel: Natural unscreened gravel excavated directly from a pit or riverbed without crushing.
choiceExplanations.Screened gravel: Natural gravel separated by size using screens without mechanical fracture of particles.
choiceExplanations.Crushed gravel: Correct — PAES defines crushed gravel as mechanically crushed gravel with substantially all fragments having at least one fractured face.
choiceExplanations.Washed gravel: Natural gravel cleaned with water to remove silt, clay, and organic impurities.

items.question: stones wrapped in wire fence meshes for added stability and strength

choiceExplanations.Riprap: Loose, unenclosed rocks or stones placed on slopes or banks to prevent erosion.
choiceExplanations.Revetment: A facing of stone, concrete, or other material built to protect an embankment or shoreline.
choiceExplanations.Bulkhead: A vertical retaining wall structure built along a waterfront to hold back earth.
choiceExplanations.Gabion: Correct — A gabion consists of stones enclosed in wire mesh baskets to provide structural stability and erosion protection.

items.question: small barrier built across the direction of water flow on shallow rivers and streams intended to convey runoff during peak flow and to slow and hold surface water long enough for the water to deposit sediment it is carrying; facilitates irrigation by using the upstream bay of the dam as pump sump

choiceExplanations.Detention basin: An excavated or embanked storage area that temporarily detains stormwater runoff to reduce peak flows.
choiceExplanations.Drop spillway: A weir structure that safely conveys water from a higher channel elevation to a lower one.
choiceExplanations.Diversion dam: A barrier across a river primarily built to raise water level and divert flow into a canal.
choiceExplanations.Check dam: Correct — A check dam is a small barrier across shallow streams that slows flow, traps sediment, and forms an upstream pump sump.

items.question: a weir wherein the upper curve of the ogee is made to conform to the shape of the lower nappe of a ventilated sheet of water falling from a sharp-crested weir; has a high discharge efficiency

choiceExplanations.Broad-crested: A flat-crested weir with substantial crest length where flow lines become parallel above the crest.
choiceExplanations.Cipolletti: A trapezoidal sharp-crested weir with 1:4 side slopes that compensate for end contractions.
choiceExplanations.Triangular: A V-notch sharp-crested weir suited for accurately measuring low discharges.
choiceExplanations.Ogee: Correct — An ogee weir follows the lower nappe profile of a ventilated sharp-crested weir for high discharge efficiency.

items.question: Composite parts of the irrigation system that divert water from natural bodies of water such as rivers, streams and lakes.
items.source: GENERAL KNOWLEDGE part 1; Recalled 2012; area 2 TERMINOLOGIES; recalled 2022

choiceExplanations.Headworks: Correct — Headworks are the composite structures at an intake that divert water from natural rivers, streams, or lakes into canals.
choiceExplanations.Aqueducts: Elevated or bridged conduits designed to carry irrigation water across depressions, roads, or streams.
choiceExplanations.Turnouts: Small outlet structures that deliver water from a supply canal into farm ditches or laterals.
choiceExplanations.Spillways: Overflow structures that safely discharge excess floodwater from reservoirs or canals.

items.question: The type of surveying that takes into account the true shape of the earth. These surveys are of high precision and extend over large areas.

choiceExplanations.Geodetic surveying: Correct — Geodetic surveying accounts for the Earth's curvature and true shape for high-precision surveys over large areas.
choiceExplanations.Plane surveying: Surveying that assumes the Earth's surface is flat, suitable only for relatively small areas.
choiceExplanations.Cadastral surveying: Surveying focused on establishing and mapping legal property boundaries and land parcels.
choiceExplanations.Topographic surveying: Surveying conducted to determine natural and artificial ground features and elevation contours.

items.question: Type of roadside ditch that is intended to reduce the risk of erosion for a lower water velocity.

choiceExplanations.Roadside triangular ditch: A V-shaped ditch that concentrates low flows and carries higher erosion risk on erodible soils.
choiceExplanations.Roadside trapezoidal ditch: Correct — A trapezoidal roadside ditch has a flat bottom and sloped sides that lower water velocity and reduce erosion risk.
choiceExplanations.Roadside rectangular ditch: A vertical-walled ditch usually requiring concrete lining due to high flow velocities and wall instability.
choiceExplanations.Roadside parabolic ditch: A dish-shaped ditch designed mainly for grassed waterways rather than standard trapezoidal roadside drainage.

items.question: The allowable limits of / NEMATODE(MPN/100mL) in irrigation waters (reuse)

choiceExplanations.9 MPN/100ML: Exceeds the zero-tolerance Philippine/PAES reuse limit for nematodes in irrigation water.
choiceExplanations.11 MPN/100ML: Exceeds the strict zero-nematode standard required for safe agricultural wastewater reuse.
choiceExplanations.0 MPN/100ML: Correct — Under PAES/DENR guidelines for irrigation reuse, the allowable nematode limit is 0 MPN/100 mL to protect public health.
choiceExplanations.8 MPN/100ML: Exceeds the mandatory zero-nematode threshold for treated wastewater used in irrigation.

items.question: Type of irrigation where the field is level in all direction,encompassed by a dike to prevent runoff, and provides an undirected flow of water into the field.

choiceExplanations.Basin irrigation: Correct — Basin irrigation floods level fields surrounded by dikes to hold water without runoff.
choiceExplanations.Corrugation irrigation: Surface irrigation using small, closely spaced shallow channels to guide water down a sloped field.
choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Surface irrigation dividing sloped land into parallel strips bounded by ridges to guide sheet flow.
choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Surface irrigation applying water into small parallel trenches between crop rows.

items.question: In surveying, what do you measure when using coordinate method

choiceExplanations.Area: Correct — The coordinate method computes the enclosed horizontal area of a closed traverse from vertex coordinates.
choiceExplanations.Bearing: Measured as the horizontal angle of a line from a north-south meridian, not computed via the coordinate method.
choiceExplanations.Volume: Determined using end-area, prismoidal, or borrow-pit methods rather than the 2D coordinate area method.
choiceExplanations.Elevation: Determined by leveling or trigonometric methods rather than horizontal traverse coordinates.

items.question: Farming practice where plowing and harrowing are done along the contour
items.source: RECALLED COMPRESS PART 2; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Contouring: Correct — Contouring performs plowing, harrowing, and planting along contour lines across the slope to reduce runoff and erosion.
choiceExplanations.Mulching: Covering the soil surface with crop residues or plastic sheets to conserve moisture and suppress weeds.
choiceExplanations.Strip cropping: Alternating bands of row crops and close-growing cover crops along slopes to slow runoff.
choiceExplanations.Terracing: Constructing earthen embankments or stepped benches across slopes to intercept runoff and shorten slope length.

items.question: Mechanical device used to force on system

choiceExplanations.Compressor: A mechanical device that increases the pressure of compressible gases rather than forcing liquids through a system.
choiceExplanations.Pump: Correct — A pump is a mechanical device that adds energy to force liquid flow through a piping or irrigation system.
choiceExplanations.Valve: A flow-control fitting used to regulate, direct, or shut off fluid flow without adding mechanical energy.
choiceExplanations.Turbine: A rotary machine that extracts energy from moving fluid rather than imparting energy to it.

items.question: Standard thickness of rectangular ditch (PAES)
items.source: RECALLED COMPRESS PART 2; area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.0.15m: Correct — PAES specifies 0.15 m (150 mm) as the standard wall/lining thickness for a rectangular open canal/ditch.
choiceExplanations.0.14m: Non-standard thickness below the 0.15 m PAES specification for rectangular ditches.
choiceExplanations.0.12m: Thinner than the standard 0.15 m rectangular ditch thickness specified in PAES.
choiceExplanations.0.16m: Exceeds the standard 0.15 m rectangular ditch thickness listed in PAES.

items.question: A hydraulic jump is a classic example of this type of flow

choiceExplanations.Unsteady uniform flow: Flow where depth varies with time but remains constant along the channel, rarely occurring in practice.
choiceExplanations.Steady uniform flow: Flow where depth and velocity stay constant with both time and distance along the channel.
choiceExplanations.Gradually varied flow: Steady flow where depth changes slowly over a long channel distance, such as backwater curves.
choiceExplanations.Rapidly varied flow: Correct — A hydraulic jump exhibits an abrupt change in flow depth over a short distance, defining rapidly varied flow.

items.question: Water flowing at a constant rate through a conical pipe, what type of flow?

choiceExplanations.Steady Uniform: Flow with constant discharge and constant velocity along the conduit, impossible in a conical pipe.
choiceExplanations.Unsteady Uniform: Flow whose velocity changes with time while remaining identical along the pipe length.
choiceExplanations.Unsteady Non-uniform: Flow where velocity varies with both time and spatial position along the conduit.
choiceExplanations.Steady Non-uniform: Correct — Constant flow rate keeps flow steady in time, while changing diameter in a conical pipe varies velocity spatially.

items.question: What type of drainage system uses the natural contour of the ground?

choiceExplanations.Gridiron: Correct — In standard ABELE board review items, gridiron (parallel) layout drains uniform slopes following the natural ground contour toward one submain.
choiceExplanations.Interceptor: A single drain placed at the base of a slope to cut off seepage before it reaches wet lowland.
choiceExplanations.Herringbone: A drainage layout where parallel laterals enter a central main from both sides at acute angles in a depression.
choiceExplanations.Random: An irregular drainage pattern connecting isolated scattered wet spots rather than following uniform natural ground contours.

items.question: What is the angle of sprinkler at a maximum throw above the ground?

choiceExplanations.12-25 degrees: Low-angle sprinkler trajectories intended to minimize wind drift rather than maximize throw distance.
choiceExplanations.25-38 degrees: Correct — Standard irrigation sprinklers use nozzle angles of 25–38 degrees (typically ~30°) to achieve maximum horizontal throw.
choiceExplanations.51-64 degrees: Excessively steep trajectory that reduces horizontal throw distance and increases wind distortion.
choiceExplanations.38-51 degrees: Angles steeper than optimal for maximum throw, causing higher trajectory arc and shorter horizontal reach.

items.question: It is most commonly used method in surveying work. A vertical distance with respect to a horizontal line is used to determine the relative difference in elevation between two adjacent points

choiceExplanations.Reciprocal leveling: A specialized leveling procedure used to determine elevation differences across wide obstacles like rivers or valleys.
choiceExplanations.Trigonometric leveling: Determining elevation differences indirectly using measured vertical angles and slope or horizontal distances.
choiceExplanations.Barometric leveling: Estimating relative elevations using atmospheric pressure differences measured by a barometer or altimeter.
choiceExplanations.Direct leveling: Correct — Direct (spirit) leveling uses a horizontal line of sight from a level to a rod to measure vertical differences directly.

items.question: In open channel design, which side slope ratio (horizontal:vertical) represents the "flattest" canal

choiceExplanations.4:1: Correct — Keyed as the flattest standard PAES canal side slope (4:1 H:V, flatter than 3:1 and 6:2) for very unstable soils.
choiceExplanations.6:2: Equivalent to a 3:1 side slope (6 horizontal to 2 vertical), which is steeper than 4:1.
choiceExplanations.3:1: Represents 3 horizontal to 1 vertical, which is steeper than a 4:1 side slope.
choiceExplanations.5:1: Geometrically flatter than 4:1 (5 horizontal to 1 vertical), though not a standard PAES canal side-slope ratio.

items.question: For an 10m x 10m sprinkler spacing, what is the design sprinkler throw for a 50% overlap?
items.answer: 7.5 m Solution: Radius of sprinkler + radius of sprinkler (% overlap) = sprinkler throw
items.rationale: 7.5 m Solution: Radius of sprinkler + radius of sprinkler (% overlap) = sprinkler throw / 10/2 + 10/2(0.50) = 7.5 m
choices: 7.5 m Solution: Radius of sprinkler + radius of sprinkler (% overlap) = sprinkler throw

choiceExplanations.10.0 m: Corresponds to 100% overlap (radius equals full 10 m spacing) rather than 50% overlap.
choiceExplanations.15.0 m: Twice the required 7.5 m throw, corresponding to excessive overlap or a 20 m spacing.
choiceExplanations.7.5 m Solution: Radius of sprinkler + ra: Correct — With 10 m spacing (5 m half-spacing) and 50% overlap, design throw is 5 + 5(0.50) = 7.5 m.
choiceExplanations.5.0 m: Represents the half-spacing (0% overlap) without adding the required 50% overlap distance.

items.question: If the most efficient trapezoidal open channel will be used to carry 100 m3/s at a water velocity of 5 m/s, what is its bottom width?
items.rationale: A = Q/V = 100/5 = 20 m². For the most efficient trapezoidal section (θ = 60°), A = √3·d² → d = √(20/1.732) = 3.40 m; bottom width b = (2/√3)·d = 3.92 m.

choiceExplanations.3.40 m: Corresponds to the optimal flow depth d = √(A/√3) ≈ 3.40 m, not the bottom width b.
choiceExplanations.3.92 m: Correct — With A = 100/5 = 20 m², optimal depth is 3.40 m and bottom width b = 2d/√3 ≈ 3.92 m.
choiceExplanations.4.45 m: Exceeds the 3.92 m bottom width required for a hydraulically most efficient 20 m² half-hexagon section.
choiceExplanations.5.10 m: Too wide for the most efficient trapezoidal section, increasing wetted perimeter and reducing hydraulic efficiency.

items.question: Most common structure used in open channel

choiceExplanations.Weir: Correct — A weir is the simplest and most widely used open-channel structure for flow measurement and water-level control.
choiceExplanations.Flume: A specially shaped open-channel constriction used where minimal head loss or sediment passage is needed.
choiceExplanations.Culvert: A closed conduit structure designed to convey open-channel flow underneath a road, railway, or embankment.
choiceExplanations.Orifice: A submerged opening in a wall or plate used for flow measurement, less common than weirs in open canals.

items.question: Any structure at the head or diversion point of a waterway. It is smaller than a barrage and is used to divert water from a river into a canal or from a large canal into a smaller canal.
items.rationale: Headworks are diversion structures built at the intake or head of a waterway to regulate and divert flow from a river into a main canal or from a larger canal into a smaller canal.

choiceExplanations.Turnouts: Farm-level or lateral outlet structures delivering water from a canal directly into smaller field ditches.
choiceExplanations.Checkgate: A control gate placed across a canal to raise upstream water level rather than divert from a river.
choiceExplanations.Headworks: Correct — Headworks are diversion structures located at the head of a canal to intake water from a river or larger canal.
choiceExplanations.Endgate: A terminal gate at the downstream end of a canal used to close off or spill remaining flow.

items.question: It is a structure used to maintain or increase water level in an open channel.
items.rationale: A checkgate is a flow-control structure placed across an open channel to maintain or raise the upstream water surface elevation for diversion or delivery.

choiceExplanations.Endgate: A gate at the end of a canal reach used to regulate or stop terminal outflow.
choiceExplanations.Checkgate: Correct — A checkgate (check structure) obstructs canal flow to raise and maintain upstream water levels for diversion.
choiceExplanations.Headworks: Intake structures located at a water source to divert flow into the main irrigation canal.
