choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Surface irrigation applying water through small channels cut between crop rows.
choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Surface irrigation flooding gently sloping strips bounded by low earth dikes.
choiceExplanations.Sub-irrigation: Correct — Sub-irrigation supplies water beneath the soil surface into the root zone, keeping the surface dry.
choiceExplanations.Sprinkler irrigation: Pressurized overhead irrigation spraying water droplets onto crops and the soil surface.

items.question: An internal condition of a seed or bud that prevents its prompt germinating or sprouting under normal growth conditions:

choiceExplanations.Quiescence: Growth arrest caused purely by unfavorable external conditions rather than internal blocks.
choiceExplanations.Senescence: Natural physiological aging process leading to tissue deterioration or organ death.
choiceExplanations.Dormancy: Correct — Dormancy is an internal condition preventing germination or sprouting despite favorable growth conditions.
choiceExplanations.Vernalization: Chilling exposure required by certain plants to induce flowering.

items.question: It involves controlled flooding from field ditches along the contour of the land, which allows the water to flood down the slope between field ditches without employing dikes or other means that guide or restrict its movement

choiceExplanations.Check-basin irrigation: Floods level plots enclosed by low dikes or ridges to impound water.
choiceExplanations.Corrugation irrigation: Uses closely spaced small rills downslope to guide water over close-growing crops.
choiceExplanations.Border-strip irrigation: Directs sheet flow downslope between parallel border dikes or ridges.
choiceExplanations.Contour-ditch irrigation: Correct — Contour-ditch irrigation releases water from contour ditches downslope without guiding dikes or levees.

items.question: Similar to that of tertiary canals, the main systems (main and secondary canals) also incur losses termed as conveyance losses. Seepage and percolation losses and evaporation along the conveyance canals comprise the conveyance losses

choiceExplanations.Crop Water Requirement (CWR): Water required by crops to satisfy evapotranspiration for optimal growth.
choiceExplanations.Net Irrigation Requirement (NIR): Irrigation water needed in the root zone after subtracting effective rainfall.
choiceExplanations.Diversion Water Requirement (DWR): Correct — Diversion Water Requirement adds main- and secondary-canal conveyance losses to the farm water requirement.
choiceExplanations.Farm Water Requirement (FWR): Water required at the farm turnout, excluding main and secondary canal conveyance losses.

items.question: The ability of the stream to provide water determines the extent of the total service area of a national irrigation system

choiceExplanations.Drainage modulus: Depth of excess water removed from a drainage area over 24 hours.
choiceExplanations.Water duty: Area of land that a unit continuous flow rate of water can irrigate.
choiceExplanations.Canal capacity: Correct — Canal capacity sets the maximum flow rate deliverable to determine the irrigable service area.
choiceExplanations.Channel slope: Longitudinal grade of the canal bed that drives gravity flow velocity.

items.question: The common name for Anser domesticus:

choiceExplanations.Quail: Common name for small game birds in the genus Coturnix.
choiceExplanations.Turkey: Common name for Meleagris gallopavo, a large domestic poultry bird.
choiceExplanations.Goose: Correct — Anser domesticus refers to the domesticated goose.
choiceExplanations.Duck: Common name for waterfowl such as Anas platyrhynchos or Cairina moschata.

items.question: The ratio of the weight of water to the dry weight of the soil

choiceExplanations.Bulk volume basis: Expresses soil moisture as water volume divided by total bulk soil volume.
choiceExplanations.Wet weight basis: Expresses moisture as water weight divided by total wet soil weight.
choiceExplanations.Total weight basis: Divides water weight by combined solid-plus-water weight, same as wet weight basis.
choiceExplanations.Dry weight basis: Correct — Dry weight basis defines gravimetric moisture content as water weight divided by dry soil weight.

items.question: Water is supplied to level plots surrounded by dikes or levees. This method is particularly useful on fine-textured soils with low permeability, it is necessary to hold the water on the surface to secure adequate penetration.

choiceExplanations.Furrow or corrugation irrigation: Channels water in narrow furrows or rills rather than ponding on diked level plots.
choiceExplanations.Level-border or basin irrigation: Correct — Level-border or basin irrigation ponds water in diked level plots for adequate infiltration in fine soils.
choiceExplanations.Graded-border or strip irrigation: Moves sheet flow down sloped strips rather than holding water on level plots.
choiceExplanations.Contour-ditch or wild flooding: Releases water from contour ditches without enclosing dikes or levees.

items.question: The fraction of the irrigation water that must be leached through the root zone to control soil salinity at specified level.

choiceExplanations.Leaching Requirement (LR): Correct — Leaching Requirement is the fraction of applied irrigation water needed to percolate past the root zone to control salinity.
choiceExplanations.Sodium Adsorption Ratio (SAR): Index comparing sodium to calcium and magnesium concentrations to evaluate sodicity hazard.
choiceExplanations.Exchangeable Sodium Percentage (ESP): Percentage of soil cation exchange capacity occupied by exchangeable sodium ions.
choiceExplanations.Drainage Requirement (DR): Total excess water rate or volume that must be removed by a drainage system.

items.question: Water horsepower divided by pump efficiency, in decimal.

choiceExplanations.Drawbar horsepower: Usable pulling power available at a tractor's drawbar for towing implements.
choiceExplanations.Indicated horsepower: Theoretical power developed inside engine cylinders from combustion pressure before friction losses.
choiceExplanations.Friction horsepower: Power lost internally to mechanical friction within an engine or machine.
choiceExplanations.Brake horsepower: Correct — Brake horsepower is the shaft input power required, equal to water horsepower divided by pump efficiency.

items.question: Any open or close ground or surface for the passage of water.

choiceExplanations.Water way: Correct — A waterway is any natural or artificial open or closed channel for conveying water.
choiceExplanations.Drainage ditch: Specifically an excavated open channel built to remove excess water from land.
choiceExplanations.Catch basin: Sump structure built to collect storm runoff and trap sediment before discharge.
choiceExplanations.Diversion canal: Channel built specifically to intercept and redirect water away from a protected area.

items.question: Soil productivity is the ability of the soil
items.answer: To produce the desired amount of plant yield
choices: To supply essential nutrients in adequate proportions
To produce the desired amount of plant yield
To retain moisture against the pull of gravity
To resist erosion caused by wind and water

choiceExplanations.To supply essential nutrients in adequat: Defines soil fertility, which is only one factor contributing to overall soil productivity.
choiceExplanations.To produce the desired amount of plant y: Correct — Soil productivity is the soil's overall ability to produce desired crop yields under specified management.
choiceExplanations.To retain moisture against the pull of g: Describes soil water retention or field capacity rather than crop-yielding ability.
choiceExplanations.To resist erosion caused by wind and wat: Refers to soil erosion resistance rather than capacity to produce plant yields.

items.question: The soil type largely influences the width of bed to be used. The furrows drain to collection ditches.

choiceExplanations.Bedding system: Correct — A bedding system uses raised beds sized by soil type, draining furrows into collection ditches.
choiceExplanations.Cross-slope system: Terraced ditches laid across slopes to intercept surface runoff and prevent erosion.
choiceExplanations.Random ditch system: Irregular ditches connecting scattered wet depressions or potholes to an outlet.
choiceExplanations.Parallel ditch system: Uniformly spaced parallel ditches suited to flat fields with regular topography.

items.question: The scientific name for pigeon:

choiceExplanations.Coturnix coturnix: Scientific name of the common quail.
choiceExplanations.Meleagris gallopavo: Scientific name of the domestic or wild turkey.
choiceExplanations.Anas platyrhynchos: Scientific name of the mallard duck.
choiceExplanations.Columbia livia: Correct — Columba livia (spelled Columbia livia here) is the scientific name of the pigeon.

items.question: Irrigation systems that have relatively large service areas and are managed by government agencies

choiceExplanations.Small Water Impounding Systems (SWIS): Small earth-dam reservoirs built for localized upland runoff harvesting and irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Private Irrigation Systems (PIS): Small irrigation systems constructed, owned, and operated by private individuals or entities.
choiceExplanations.National Irrigation Systems (NIS): Correct — National Irrigation Systems (NIS) are large government-managed irrigation systems operated by NIA.
choiceExplanations.Communal Irrigation Systems (CIS): Smaller irrigation systems turned over to and managed by Irrigators' Associations.

items.question: Type of flow wherein the depth of flow in a prismatic channel is constant at any point in the channel

choiceExplanations.Unsteady flow: Flow whose depth and velocity at a given channel point change over time.
choiceExplanations.Steady flow: Correct — Steady flow keeps hydraulic depth and velocity constant over time at a channel point.
choiceExplanations.Turbulent flow: Chaotic, eddying flow regime occurring above the critical Reynolds number.
choiceExplanations.Varied flow: Flow whose depth varies along the channel length due to slope or section changes.

items.question: The unit of heredity, variation, sex determination and related phenomena:

choiceExplanations.Gene: Correct — A gene is the basic functional unit of heredity, variation, and sex determination.
choiceExplanations.Chromosome: Thread-like DNA-protein structure carrying numerous genes inside the cell nucleus.
choiceExplanations.Allele: Alternative variant form of a specific gene at a given chromosomal locus.
choiceExplanations.Genome: Complete set of all genetic material possessed by an organism.

items.question: Lands serviced by natural irrigation or irrigation facilities. These include land where water is not readily available as existing irrigation facilities need rehabilitation or upgrading or where irrigation water is not available year-round

choiceExplanations.Rainfed Lands: Agricultural land relying entirely on natural rainfall without irrigation facilities.
choiceExplanations.Irrigated Lands: Correct — Irrigated lands are areas served by natural or constructed irrigation, including systems needing rehabilitation or seasonal supply.
choiceExplanations.Irrigable Lands: Land physically suitable for irrigation that currently lacks irrigation facilities.
choiceExplanations.Serviceable Lands: Area commanded by an irrigation system network, distinct from actual irrigated status.

items.question: The ratio of water beneficially used on the project, farm or field to the amount of water delivered to the farm expressed in percent.

choiceExplanations.Water application efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the root zone to water delivered into the field.
choiceExplanations.Water conveyance efficiency: Ratio of water delivered at the farm turnout to water diverted from the source.
choiceExplanations.Water used efficiency: Correct — Water use efficiency is the percentage of delivered water that is beneficially used on the project or farm.
choiceExplanations.Water storage efficiency: Ratio of water stored during irrigation to the root-zone water needed beforehand.

items.question: include seepage and percolation losses.

choiceExplanations.Non-consumtive: Correct — Seepage and percolation are non-consumptive losses because water leaves via subsurface flow rather than evaporation or transpiration.
choiceExplanations.Irrecoverable: Losses permanently unavailable for downstream reuse, whereas seepage often recharges groundwater or return flows.
choiceExplanations.Beneficial: Water portions directly supporting crop growth, leaching, or microclimate cooling.
choiceExplanations.Consumptive: Water removed from the system by evaporation, transpiration, or plant tissue incorporation.

items.question: Governed by chance; time dependent

choiceExplanations.Deterministic process: Process whose future outcomes are completely fixed by initial conditions with no randomness.
choiceExplanations.Empirical process: Relationship derived purely from observed data rather than physical or probabilistic laws.
choiceExplanations.Stochastic process: Correct — A stochastic process is time-dependent and governed by probability or chance.
choiceExplanations.Conceptual process: Simplified representation of physical watershed storages and fluxes.

items.question: Interval between corresponding points on successive terraces

choiceExplanations.Horizontal interval: Correct — Horizontal interval is the horizontal distance between corresponding points on successive terraces.
choiceExplanations.Slope interval: Distance measured along the inclined ground slope rather than horizontally.
choiceExplanations.Contour interval: Constant vertical elevation difference between adjacent contour lines on a map.
choiceExplanations.Vertical interval: Difference in elevation between corresponding points on two successive terraces.

items.question: It is a variation of the furrow method and it uses small rills or corrugations for irrigating closely spaced crops, such as small grains and pastures.

choiceExplanations.Corrugation irrigation: Correct — Corrugation irrigation uses small shallow rills to irrigate close-growing small grains and pastures.
choiceExplanations.Surge irrigation: Applies water intermittently in pulses down furrows to improve uniformity and limit percolation.
choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Floods sloping strips bounded by parallel dikes rather than using small rills.
choiceExplanations.Basin irrigation: Impounds water within level, dike-enclosed plots until infiltration completes.

items.question: The scientific name of strawberry:

choiceExplanations.Rubus idaeus: Scientific name of the red raspberry.
choiceExplanations.Vaccinium corymbosum: Scientific name of the northern highbush blueberry.
choiceExplanations.Fragaria vesca: Correct — Fragaria vesca (woodland strawberry) is the scientific name for strawberry.

items.question: (Crop rotation) planting different crops, one after the other each season

choiceExplanations.Ratoon cropping: Harvesting a second crop from stubble regrowth after the first harvest.
choiceExplanations.Strip cropping: Growing different crops in alternating strips across a field to control erosion.
choiceExplanations.Alley cropping: Planting annual crops between rows of perennial trees or shrubs.
choiceExplanations.Relay cropping: Correct — Relay cropping sequentially plants different crops one after another across seasons.

items.question: The name for seasonal winds (derived from Arabic mausim, a season)

choiceExplanations.Monsoon winds: Correct — Monsoon winds (from Arabic mausim, season) are seasonal prevailing winds that reverse direction each season.
choiceExplanations.Trade winds: Steady year-round tropical easterlies blowing toward the equator.
choiceExplanations.Katabatic winds: Local downslope winds formed by cold dense air draining downhill at night.
choiceExplanations.Westerly winds: Prevailing mid-latitude winds blowing year-round from west to east.

items.question: The Philippine Agricultural Engineering law of 1998.

choiceExplanations.RA 6847: A 1990 Philippine Republic Act unrelated to agricultural engineering regulation.
choiceExplanations.RA 7532: A 1992 Philippine Republic Act unrelated to the 1998 Agricultural Engineering Law.
choiceExplanations.RA 8559: Correct — RA 8559 is the Philippine Agricultural Engineering Act of 1998.
choiceExplanations.RA 9244: A 2004 Philippine Republic Act unrelated to agricultural engineering licensure or practice.

items.question: A notch of regular form through which the irrigation stream is made to flow and built as either portable or stationary structure.

choiceExplanations.Orifice: A submerged or free-discharging opening in a wall or plate, not an open top notch.
choiceExplanations.Culvert: A closed conduit carrying drainage or irrigation flow beneath a road or embankment.
choiceExplanations.Weir: Correct — a weir is a calibrated notch over which irrigation water flows for discharge measurement.
choiceExplanations.Flume: An open channel section with a narrowed throat or raised floor for measuring flow without a notch.

items.question: The mass per unit volume of the soil particle is:

choiceExplanations.Soil porosity: Ratio of total pore space volume to total bulk soil volume, expressed as a fraction or percent.
choiceExplanations.Dry density: Mass of oven-dry soil solids divided by total bulk soil volume including pore spaces.
choiceExplanations.Bulk density: Mass of dry soil per unit bulk volume that includes both solids and pore spaces.
choiceExplanations.Soil density: Correct — soil particle density is the mass per unit volume of the solid soil particles alone.

items.question: Composite facilities that permit entry of water to paddy areas and consist of farm ditches and turnouts

choiceExplanations.Main Conveyance Canal Facilities: Primary canals transporting large diverted flows from headworks to lateral distribution networks.
choiceExplanations.Headworks Diversion Irrigation Facilitie: Dams, intake gates, and regulators that divert water from a river or reservoir into the main canal.
choiceExplanations.On-Farm Irrigation Facilities: Correct — PAES/NIA defines on-farm irrigation facilities as farm ditches and turnouts delivering water to paddy areas.
choiceExplanations.Secondary Distribution Network Facilitie: Lateral and sub-lateral canals conveying water from main canals toward turnout service areas.

items.question: The ____ is the amount of water to be applied to the field as irrigation.

choiceExplanations.Crop Water Requirement (CWR): Total depth of water needed by a crop for evapotranspiration and metabolic use regardless of source.
choiceExplanations.Net Irrigation Requirement (NIR): Crop water need minus effective rainfall and groundwater contribution, excluding application losses.
choiceExplanations.Diversion Water Requirement (DWR): Total water volume diverted at the headworks, including conveyance, distribution, and farm application losses.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation Water Requirement (IWR): Correct — irrigation water requirement is the amount of water that must be applied to the field as irrigation.

items.question: That portion of the available moisture that is most easily extracted by plants; this is approximately 75% of the available moisture.

choiceExplanations.Available water capacity (AWC): Total water held between field capacity and permanent wilting point within a given soil depth.
choiceExplanations.Management allowed depletion (MAD): Maximum fraction of available water a grower permits to be depleted before triggering irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Readily available moisture (RAM): Correct — readily available moisture is the easily extracted fraction, approximately 75% of total available moisture.
choiceExplanations.Total available moisture (TAM): Entire moisture range between field capacity and permanent wilting point, not just the easily extracted fraction.

items.question: One liter per second is equal to. ____gpm

choiceExplanations.14.58 gpm: Underestimates 1 L/s because 60 L/min divided by 3.7854 L/gal exceeds 15 gpm.
choiceExplanations.15.85 gpm: Correct — converting 1 L/s (60 L/min) using 3.7854 liters per US gallon equals 15.85 gpm.
choiceExplanations.17.12 gpm: Overestimates 1 L/s since 60 divided by 3.7854 yields 15.85, not 17.12 gpm.
choiceExplanations.19.34 gpm: Overstates the flow rate by roughly 22% above the exact 1 L/s to US gpm conversion.

items.question: Lands which display marked characteristics justifying the operation of an irrigation system

choiceExplanations.Arable Lands: Lands suited for plowing and crop production regardless of irrigation feasibility.
choiceExplanations.Serviceable Lands: Lands physically reachable by a canal network, though not necessarily soil-suited or economically viable for irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Irrigated Lands: Lands currently receiving artificial water applications from an existing irrigation system.
choiceExplanations.Irrigable Lands: Correct — irrigable lands exhibit soil, topographic, and economic characteristics justifying an irrigation system.

items.question: A method of asexual propagation involving the transfer of aerial parts of one plant (scion) to the root or trunk material (stock) of another plant:

choiceExplanations.Marcotting: Air layering where roots are induced on an intact aerial stem before detaching it from the parent plant.
choiceExplanations.Grafting: Correct — grafting joins an aerial scion shoot from one plant onto the rootstock or trunk of another.
choiceExplanations.Layering: Rooting an attached branch in soil or media before severing it from the parent plant.
choiceExplanations.Budding: A specialized graft using only a single detached bud rather than a multi-bud scion stem.

items.question: The ratio of the normal consumptive use of water to the net amount of water depleted from the root zone soil.

choiceExplanations.Consumptive use efficiency: Correct — consumptive use efficiency is the ratio of normal consumptive use to net water depleted from the root zone.
choiceExplanations.Water storage efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the root zone during irrigation to water needed prior to irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Water application efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the root zone to total water delivered at the farm turnout.
choiceExplanations.Water distribution efficiency: Uniformity index measuring how evenly infiltrated irrigation depth is distributed across the field.

items.question: The ratio between water stored in the soil root zone during irrigation and the water delivered to the farm expressed in percent.

choiceExplanations.Water distribution efficiency: Measures uniformity of water depth infiltrated across different parts of an irrigated field.
choiceExplanations.Water application efficiency: Correct — water application efficiency is the percentage ratio of root-zone stored water to water delivered to the farm.
choiceExplanations.Water storage efficiency: Ratio of water actually stored in the root zone to total moisture needed before irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Water conveyance efficiency: Ratio of water delivered at the farm turnout to water diverted from the river or reservoir.

items.question: Time for surface and interflow to recede; duration of flooding

choiceExplanations.Concentration time: Time required for runoff from the hydrologically most remote point to reach the watershed outlet.
choiceExplanations.Recession time: Correct — recession time is the duration during which surface runoff and interflow recede after peak flow or flooding.
choiceExplanations.Base time: Total duration of direct runoff from the start of the rising limb until flow returns to baseflow.
choiceExplanations.Lag time: Time interval from the centroid of rainfall excess to the peak or centroid of direct runoff.

items.question: If the depth changes abruptly over a comparatively short distance such as in a hydraulic jump

choiceExplanations.Steady uniform flow: Open-channel flow where depth and velocity remain constant over both time and distance.
choiceExplanations.Gradually varied flow: Steady non-uniform flow in which water depth changes smoothly over a long channel reach.
choiceExplanations.Rapidly varied flow: Correct — rapidly varied flow involves abrupt depth changes over a short distance, such as in a hydraulic jump.
choiceExplanations.Spatially varied flow: Open-channel flow whose discharge varies along the channel due to lateral inflow or outflow.

items.question: Which wets the entire land surface

choiceExplanations.By dripping: Applies water slowly at discrete emitter points near plant roots rather than wetting the whole surface.
choiceExplanations.By sprinkling: Applies water overhead like rain droplets rather than submerging the entire land surface.
choiceExplanations.By flooding: Correct — flooding spreads a continuous sheet of water that wets the entire land surface.
choiceExplanations.By furrowing: Channels water through small parallel grooves between crop ridges, wetting only part of the surface.

items.question: The channel where diverted water from a source flows to the intended area to be irrigated

choiceExplanations.Secondary canal: A branching distribution channel fed by the main canal to serve smaller sub-areas.
choiceExplanations.Drainage canal: A channel designed to collect and remove excess surface or subsurface water from agricultural fields.
choiceExplanations.Main canal: Correct — the main canal conveys diverted water directly from the headworks source to the area to be irrigated.
choiceExplanations.Lateral canal: A secondary or tertiary branch off a main canal serving localized farm turnouts.

items.question: The percentage of moisture on dry weight basis that is held against the pull of gravity, after drainage has ceased in a soil that has been saturated:

choiceExplanations.Saturation capacity: Moisture content when all soil pores are completely filled with water just before gravity drainage.
choiceExplanations.Permanent wilting point: Lower moisture limit at which plants can no longer extract water and permanently wilt.
choiceExplanations.Field capacity: Correct — field capacity is the moisture held against gravity after drainage of a saturated soil ceases.
choiceExplanations.Hygroscopic coefficient: Thin water film tightly adsorbed on soil particles from humid air, unavailable to plant roots.

items.question: Plants living more than one year but in some cases, producing seed in the first year and every season thereafter:

choiceExplanations.Ephemeral: Short-lived plants completing their entire life cycle within a few weeks after rain.
choiceExplanations.Perennial: Correct — perennial plants live more than one year and typically produce seed in the first year and every season thereafter.
choiceExplanations.Biennial: Plants requiring two growing seasons to complete vegetative growth, flowering, seeding, and death.
choiceExplanations.Annual: Plants completing germination, seeding, and death within a single growing year or season.

items.question: It is the simplest piece of overhead irrigation equipment and is commonly used in small-scale upland farming

choiceExplanations.Drip emitter: A pressurized trickle device releasing water dropwise directly at the root zone, not overhead.
choiceExplanations.Perforated pipe: A low-pressure sprinkler lateral with drilled holes spraying jets along a pipe length.
choiceExplanations.Watering can: Correct — a handheld watering can is the simplest overhead irrigation equipment commonly used in small-scale upland farming.
choiceExplanations.Garden hose: A flexible conduit delivering pressurized water, typically paired with a nozzle rather than being a standalone overhead tool.

items.question: An imaginary line of constant elevation on the surface of the ground.

choiceExplanations.Grade line: A sloped line representing uniform rise or fall along a canal, road, or hydraulic profile.
choiceExplanations.Contour line: Correct — a contour line is an imaginary line connecting points of constant elevation on the ground surface.
choiceExplanations.Datum line: A fixed horizontal reference elevation plane, such as mean sea level, used for vertical measurements.
choiceExplanations.Traverse line: A series of connected survey lines with measured lengths and bearings used for horizontal control.

items.question: The ratio of the volume of water to the total soil volume

choiceExplanations.Volume basis or volumetric MC: Correct — volumetric moisture content is the ratio of the volume of water to the total bulk soil volume.
choiceExplanations.Weight basis or gravimetric MC: Mass of water divided by oven-dry mass of soil solids, not total soil volume.
choiceExplanations.Depth basis or equivalent MC: Moisture expressed as equivalent water depth per unit soil depth, derived from volumetric content.
choiceExplanations.Saturation basis or relative MC: Ratio of actual soil water volume to total pore space volume at full saturation.

items.question: The Scientific name for onion:

choiceExplanations.Allium sativum: Botanical name for common garlic, distinct from bulb onion.
choiceExplanations.Allium porrum: Botanical name for leek, a mild-flavored Allium grown for its blanched pseudostem.
choiceExplanations.Allium schoenoprasum: Botanical name for chives, grown primarily for slender hollow leaves.
choiceExplanations.Allium sepa: Correct — Allium cepa (given here as Allium sepa) is the scientific name for common onion.

items.question: An association of farmers within a contiguous area served by a national irrigation system or communal irrigation system

choiceExplanations.Planters’ Federation: A broad commodity or growers' organization not specific to managing an irrigation service area.
choiceExplanations.Farmers’ Cooperative: A member-owned enterprise focused on credit, inputs, or marketing rather than canal system operation.
choiceExplanations.Irrigators’ Association: Correct — an Irrigators' Association unites farmers in a contiguous area served by a national or communal irrigation system.
choiceExplanations.Watershed Association: A multi-stakeholder group protecting an entire river basin rather than operating farm irrigation turnouts.

items.question: The ratio between the water delivered to the farm and the water diverted from a river or reservoir expressed in percent

choiceExplanations.Water application efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the crop root zone to water delivered at the farm.
choiceExplanations.Water distribution efficiency: Measures spatial uniformity of infiltrated water depth across an irrigated field.
choiceExplanations.Water storage efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the root zone to water needed before irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Water conveyance efficiency: Correct — water conveyance efficiency compares water delivered to the farm against water diverted from the river or reservoir.

items.question: Consists of carrying out agricultural operations very nearly on the contour. It reduces the velocity of overland flow and retards soil erosion

choiceExplanations.Contour cultivation: Correct — contour cultivation performs tillage and planting along contour lines, slowing overland flow and retarding soil erosion.
choiceExplanations.Minimum tillage: Reduced soil disturbance leaving crop residue on the surface, independent of slope contour alignment.
choiceExplanations.Bench terracing: Earthmoving practice cutting steep slopes into flat, step-like horizontal benches supported by risers.
choiceExplanations.Strip cropping: Alternating bands of close-grown and row crops across a slope, distinct from general contour tillage.

items.question: An irrigation system that is managed by a bonafide irrigators’ / association

choiceExplanations.Private irrigation system: An irrigation facility owned, constructed, and operated individually or by a private entity.
choiceExplanations.Communal irrigation system: Correct — a communal irrigation system is operated and maintained by a bona fide irrigators' association.
choiceExplanations.National irrigation system: Large irrigation system constructed, owned, and jointly managed by the National Irrigation Administration.
choiceExplanations.Pump irrigation system: Any system lifting water mechanically by pump regardless of whether ownership is private, communal, or national.

items.question: Record the pressure required to maintain a small flow of gas from an orifice submerged in the stream

choiceExplanations.Wire-weight gage: A manual bridge-mounted reel lowering a weight to touch the water surface for stage readings.
choiceExplanations.Bubbler gage: Correct — a bubbler gage records the pressure needed to maintain a small gas flow from a submerged orifice.
choiceExplanations.Float gage: A stilling-well device tracking water stage via a buoyant float linked to a pulley or recorder.
choiceExplanations.Crest-stage gage: A passive tube containing cork dust that records only the maximum flood peak elevation.

items.question: Planting different crops simultaneously in the same field at the same cropping season.

choiceExplanations.Sequential cropping or double cropping: Growing two or more crops one after another in the same field within one year.
choiceExplanations.Multi cropping or mixed cropping: Correct — mixed or multi cropping plants different crops simultaneously on the same field during the same cropping season.
choiceExplanations.Relay cropping or overlap cropping: Planting a second crop into a standing first crop before harvest, overlapping only part of their cycles.
choiceExplanations.Ratoon cropping or stubble cropping: Cultivating regrowth from stubble left after harvesting the first crop, such as sugarcane or rice.

items.question: The scientific name for sheep:

choiceExplanations.Capra hircus: Scientific name for the domestic goat.
choiceExplanations.Bos taurus: Scientific name for European humpless domestic cattle.
choiceExplanations.Sus scrofa: Scientific name for wild boar and domestic swine.
choiceExplanations.Ovis aries: Correct — Ovis aries is the binomial scientific name for domestic sheep.

items.question: The water right based on the concept first time, first in right:

choiceExplanations.Appropriation Act: Correct — the prior appropriation doctrine grants water rights based on "first in time, first in right" priority.
choiceExplanations.Water Code: Presidential Decree No. 1067 governing comprehensive water ownership, permits, and administration in the Philippines.
choiceExplanations.Correlative Doctrine: Groundwater rule allocating shared aquifers proportionally among overlying landowners based on acreage or reasonable use.
choiceExplanations.Riparian Doctrine: Common-law rule granting water use rights solely to owners of land bordering a natural watercourse.

items.question: The lateral movement of water in the soil:

choiceExplanations.Infiltration: Downward entry of water through the soil surface into the upper soil profile.
choiceExplanations.Seepage: Correct — seepage is the slow lateral movement of water through porous soil or canal embankments.
choiceExplanations.Leaching: Downward washing of dissolved salts or nutrients out of the root zone by excess percolating water.
choiceExplanations.Percolation: Vertical downward movement of water through soil layers below the root zone.

items.question: It is the sheet of water which overflows a weir:

choiceExplanations.Crest: The top horizontal edge or sill of a weir over which water flows.
choiceExplanations.Apron: A protective concrete or masonry floor placed downstream of a structure to prevent scour.
choiceExplanations.Napped: Correct — the nappe (spelled "Napped" here) is the sheet of water overflowing a weir crest.
choiceExplanations.Contraction: Narrowing of the flow cross-section caused by weir end projections or piers.

items.question: Sprinkler type with operating pressure from 20-40 psi:

choiceExplanations.Very low pressure: Micro-sprinklers and drip systems typically operating below 15 to 20 psi.
choiceExplanations.High pressure: Large-gun or volume sprinklers requiring operating pressures typically above 60 to 80 psi.
choiceExplanations.Low pressure: Correct — low-pressure sprinklers operate within the 20 to 40 psi pressure range.
choiceExplanations.Medium pressure: Standard agricultural impact sprinklers generally operating between 40 and 60 psi.

items.question: Barrier constructed to hold water back and raise its level.

choiceExplanations.Spillway: An overflow structure designed to safely pass excess floodwater past a dam.
choiceExplanations.Sluice: A gated passage or conduit used to release controlled flow or flush sediment.
choiceExplanations.Levee: An embankment built parallel to a river channel to prevent floodwater overflow onto adjacent land.
choiceExplanations.Dam: Correct — a dam is a barrier constructed across a waterway to hold water back and raise its level.

items.question: The channel connected to the main canal which distributes irrigation to specific areas

choiceExplanations.Secondary canal: Correct — a secondary canal connects to the main canal and distributes irrigation water to specific service areas.
choiceExplanations.Drainage canal: An open channel built to remove surplus runoff or subsurface water from agricultural fields.
choiceExplanations.Primary canal: Synonym for the main canal that carries diverted water from the headworks before branching.
choiceExplanations.Tertiary canal: Small sub-lateral or farm ditch branching from a secondary canal to feed individual farm turnouts.

items.question: Vigna radiata is commonly known as:

choiceExplanations.Chickpea: Cicer arietinum, a cool-season pulse crop unrelated to Vigna radiata.
choiceExplanations.Mungbean: Correct — Vigna radiata is the scientific name for mungbean (mungo), a major Philippine legume crop.
choiceExplanations.Cowpea: Vigna unguiculata, a related legume species distinct from mungbean.
choiceExplanations.Soybean: Glycine max, an oilseed legume belonging to a different genus.

items.question: A conveyance structure used to turn conduits of varying sizes and shapes

choiceExplanations.Chute: A steep open-channel spillway or drop carrying water rapidly down a steep grade.
choiceExplanations.Flume: An elevated open channel supported on trestles to carry water across depressions or streams.
choiceExplanations.Transition: Correct — a transition connects conduits or channels of varying cross-sectional sizes and shapes.
choiceExplanations.Culvert: A closed pipe or box conduit conveying water beneath an embankment, road, or railroad.

items.question: Surface irrigation method where a much smaller area is enclosed by levees

choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Applies water in small parallel channels cut between crop rows rather than ponding an enclosed plot.
choiceExplanations.Wild flooding: Releases water uncontrolled over ungraded land without guiding levees or borders.
choiceExplanations.Border flooding: Divides sloped land into parallel strips bounded by low dikes so water advances downslope as a sheet.
choiceExplanations.Basin flooding: Correct — basin flooding ponds water inside small, level areas completely enclosed by levees or bunds.

items.question: This refer to the additional height or depth of hydraulic structures

choiceExplanations.Hydraulic depth: Flow cross-sectional area divided by the top water surface width.
choiceExplanations.Free board: Correct — freeboard is the additional safety height added above maximum design water level in hydraulic structures.
choiceExplanations.Critical depth: Flow depth at which specific energy is minimum and the Froude number equals unity.
choiceExplanations.Normal depth: Uniform flow depth calculated from Manning's equation for a given discharge, slope, and roughness.

items.question: Refers to the number of days between irrigation periods without rainfall

choiceExplanations.Irrigation period: Number of days allowed to complete one irrigation cycle over the design area during peak demand.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation depth: Volume of water applied per unit field area, expressed as an equivalent depth in millimeters or inches.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation duration: Hours or time required for a single irrigation set to apply the target depth.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation frequency: Correct — irrigation frequency is the number of days between consecutive irrigations without rainfall.

items.question: One in which a definite law of certainty exists

choiceExplanations.Stochastic process: Time-dependent hydrologic process governed by random variables and probability distributions rather than fixed certainty.
choiceExplanations.Stationary process: A random process whose statistical properties like mean and variance remain invariant over time.
choiceExplanations.Probabilistic process: Process modeled through likelihoods and chance outcomes rather than exact cause-and-effect laws.
choiceExplanations.Deterministic process: Correct — a deterministic process follows a definite law of certainty with zero randomness in its outcome.

items.question: A storm type occuring at the boundaries of warm moist air and dry cold air.

choiceExplanations.Orographic storm: Precipitation triggered when moist air is forced upward over mountain barriers and cools adiabatically.
choiceExplanations.Convective storm: Localized rainfall caused by intense solar surface heating driving unstable warm air upward.
choiceExplanations.Frontal storm: Correct — a frontal storm forms at boundaries where warm moist air meets and rises over cold dry air.
choiceExplanations.Cyclonic storm: Large-scale rotating low-pressure system driven by horizontal convergence around a storm center.

items.question: The no. of days allowed for operating irrigation to a given design area during the peak consumptive period of the crop being irrigated

choiceExplanations.Irrigation period: Correct — irrigation period is the days allowed to irrigate a design area during peak crop consumptive use.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation frequency: Days elapsed between successive irrigations at a given field without rainfall.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation cycle: Repeated sequence of irrigation events over a season rather than the peak operating window.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation interval: Synonym for irrigation frequency, representing the time elapsed between two consecutive waterings.

items.question: A notch of regular form through which the irrigation stream is made to flow and flow built as either portable or stationary structures is called:

choiceExplanations.Turnout: An outlet gate delivering water from a supply canal into a farm ditch rather than a measuring notch.
choiceExplanations.Orifice: A submerged opening through a wall or plate rather than an open-top notch.
choiceExplanations.Weir: Correct — a weir is a regular-shaped notch built as a portable or stationary structure to measure irrigation flow.
choiceExplanations.Flume: A specially shaped open channel throat measuring discharge without using a notch.

items.question: For the most efficient circular cross-section, semi-circle the hydraulic radius is equal to:

choiceExplanations.¼ its diameter: Correct — for a semi-circular section, flow area divided by wetted perimeter equals R/2, or one-fourth its diameter.
choiceExplanations.⅓ its diameter: Exceeds the true hydraulic radius of a semi-circular open channel, which is exactly D/4.
choiceExplanations.½ its diameter: Equals the circle's geometric radius (maximum flow depth), not its hydraulic radius R/2.
choiceExplanations.¾ its diameter: Larger than both the geometric radius and hydraulic radius of a semi-circular channel.

items.question: A hydraulic structure that serves as an outlet of water in irrigation canals whereby water passes through and discharges into the main farm ditch of service area is called

choiceExplanations.Check: A canal cross-regulator placed across a channel to raise upstream water level into laterals.
choiceExplanations.Headgate: Main intake control gate at the canal headworks regulating flow entering the main canal from a river.
choiceExplanations.Turnout: Correct — a turnout is an outlet structure discharging canal water into the main farm ditch of a service area.
choiceExplanations.Spillway: An overflow safety structure discharging excess floodwater from a reservoir or canal.

items.question: In drainage, open channel is often referred to as:

choiceExplanations.Culverts: Closed underground pipes or boxes conveying water beneath roads or embankments, not standard open channels.
choiceExplanations.Canals: Correct — open drainage channels excavated in earth or lined are commonly referred to as canals.
choiceExplanations.Flumes: Elevated artificial troughs carrying water across valleys or depressions rather than general drainage channels.
choiceExplanations.Conduits: General term typically referring to closed pipes or covered waterways under pressure or partial flow.

items.question: The direct attraction of similar molecules between similar molecules

choiceExplanations.Cohesion: Correct — cohesion is the direct intermolecular attraction holding similar molecules together.
choiceExplanations.Adsorption: Surface retention of water molecules or ions onto solid soil particle surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Capillarity: Rise or retention of water in small soil pores driven jointly by adhesion and surface tension.
choiceExplanations.Adhesion: Attraction between dissimilar molecules, such as water clinging to solid soil surfaces.

items.question: A temporary method of drainage artificially produced in the subsoil with digging a trench from the surface.

choiceExplanations.Pipe drain: Subsurface perforated plastic or corrugated tubing installed inside an excavated trench.
choiceExplanations.Tile drain: Short clay or concrete pipe sections laid end-to-end inside a dug trench.
choiceExplanations.Mole drain: Correct — a mole drain is a temporary unlined subsoil channel pulled by a mole plow without digging a surface trench.
choiceExplanations.French drain: A dug trench backfilled with gravel around a perforated pipe to intercept groundwater.

items.question: The depth of water in mm or inches to be removed in 24 hr period from the drainage area.

choiceExplanations.Drainage porosity: Volume fraction of soil pores that drains freely under gravity, also called drainable porosity.
choiceExplanations.Drainage density: Total length of stream or drainage channels per unit watershed area.
choiceExplanations.Drainage coefficient: Correct — the drainage coefficient is the depth of water in mm or inches to be removed in a 24-hour period.
choiceExplanations.Runoff coefficient: Dimensionless ratio of surface runoff volume to total rainfall volume in the Rational Method.

items.question: Other terms for drip irrigation are __________ irrigation and __________ irrigation. This type of overhead irrigation operates at low pressure.

choiceExplanations.Border – furrow: Surface irrigation methods applying water by gravity flow over land strips or channels.
choiceExplanations.Trickle – micro: Correct — drip irrigation is also called trickle or micro-irrigation and operates at low pressure.
choiceExplanations.Surge – pulse: Intermittent surface-furrow watering cycles, not the standard synonyms for drip irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Bubbler – spray: Specific emitter types within micro-irrigation rather than the two general names for drip irrigation.

items.question: In open channel, the term A/P is:

choiceExplanations.Wetted perimeter: Length of the channel boundary in contact with flowing water, denoted by P alone.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic depth: Flow area A divided by the top water surface width T, not wetted perimeter P.
choiceExplanations.Section factor: Product of flow area and square root of hydraulic depth used in critical flow computations.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic radius: Correct — hydraulic radius in open-channel flow is defined as cross-sectional flow area A divided by wetted perimeter P.

items.question: These are usually rural traders or barrio buyers who do accumulation of the produce of individual farmers and bulk these for storage or for distribution to wholesalers

choiceExplanations.Jobbers: Middlemen who buy from wholesalers or manufacturers and sell in smaller quantities to retailers.
choiceExplanations.Assemblers: Correct — assemblers are rural buyers who gather individual farmers' produce and bulk it for storage or wholesalers.
choiceExplanations.Brokers: Agents who negotiate transactions between buyers and sellers for a fee without taking ownership of goods.
choiceExplanations.Speculators: Traders who hold commodities expecting price increases rather than performing bulking and distribution services.

items.question: It is used to divide and distribute the flow of water at desired direction usually placed or built in main farm ditch to divert water to supplementary farm ditches.

choiceExplanations.Stilling basin: An energy-dissipating basin built below spillways or drops to reduce high-velocity flow turbulence.
choiceExplanations.Drop structure: A hydraulic structure that conveys canal water abruptly from a higher elevation to a lower one.
choiceExplanations.Division box: Correct — a division box splits and diverts water from a main farm ditch into supplementary farm ditches.
choiceExplanations.Check structure: A structure placed across a canal to raise the upstream water level for diversion or flow measurement.

items.question: In designing an open channel, it is necessary to know what the material firming the channel bed is to know the value of:

choiceExplanations.Roughness coefficient: Correct — Manning's roughness coefficient (n) depends directly on the material forming the channel bed and sides.
choiceExplanations.Discharge coefficient: A dimensionless factor relating actual discharge to theoretical flow through orifices, weirs, or meters.
choiceExplanations.Contraction coefficient: The ratio of cross-sectional flow area at the vena contracta to the opening area.
choiceExplanations.Runoff coefficient: The ratio of surface runoff volume to total rainfall volume used in the Rational Method.

items.question: This refers to wants for specific satisfiers backed up by an ability and willingness to buy them.

choiceExplanations.Need: A basic state of felt deprivation for fundamental requirements like food, water, or shelter.
choiceExplanations.Supply: The total quantity of a good producers are willing and able to offer at given prices.
choiceExplanations.Want: A desire shaped by culture and personality for specific satisfiers without requiring purchasing power.
choiceExplanations.Demand: Correct — demand refers to human wants backed by both the ability and willingness to buy.

items.question: An irrigation method formed by building longitudinal levees approximately parallel to the contour and connecting them at a desirable places with levees at right angle.

choiceExplanations.Border strip: An irrigation method using parallel dikes down a gentle slope to guide a flowing sheet of water.
choiceExplanations.Level border: A flat, diked rectangular plot flooded rapidly to uniform depth with zero land slope.
choiceExplanations.Check contour: Correct — contour-check irrigation uses longitudinal levees along contours connected by perpendicular cross levees.
choiceExplanations.Contour furrow: Small parallel channels excavated along land contours to convey irrigation water across sloping fields.

items.question: A device used to control the flow of water to or from a pipeline.

choiceExplanations.Weir: An overflow barrier or notch placed across an open channel to measure or raise water levels.
choiceExplanations.Riser: A vertical pipe extending from a buried mainline to supply water to the ground surface or sprinklers.
choiceExplanations.Flume: An open artificial trough used to carry water across depressions or measure channel flow.
choiceExplanations.Gate: Correct — a gate or valve regulates, opens, or shuts off water flow into or from a pipeline.

items.question: A closed conduit usually circular, square or rectangular in cross section, used for conveying water across and under an elevated roadway, embankment and dikes.

choiceExplanations.Aqueduct: An elevated conduit or bridge-like channel carrying water across a valley or low-lying area.
choiceExplanations.Chute: A steep lined open canal designed to convey water safely down sharp elevation drops.
choiceExplanations.Flume: An open channel supported above ground to carry water across ravines or existing waterways.
choiceExplanations.Culvert: Correct — a culvert is a closed conduit carrying water underneath roadways, embankments, or dikes.

items.question: This is a marketing function which facilitates transfer of ownership

choiceExplanations.Advertising: Paid non-personal communication informing prospective buyers about products to stimulate demand.
choiceExplanations.Financing: Providing capital or credit needed to fund production, inventory holding, and marketing operations.
choiceExplanations.Negotiation: Correct — negotiation establishes price and sale terms that directly facilitate the transfer of product ownership.
choiceExplanations.Standardization: Establishing uniform product grades, weights, and specifications to simplify buying and selling.

items.question: It is natural or artificial channel that shortens a meandering stream.

choiceExplanations.Oxbow lake: A U-shaped standing water body formed after a river meander bend becomes isolated from the main stream.
choiceExplanations.Flood plain: Flat alluvial land bordering a river channel that is subject to periodic overflow during floods.
choiceExplanations.Bypass channel: An auxiliary floodway constructed to divert excess peak floodwaters around vulnerable areas.
choiceExplanations.Cut off: Correct — a cutoff is a natural or artificial shortcut channel that shortens a meandering stream.

items.question: A concept used to evaluate the losses of water during irrigation from the time it leaves that source to the point of use.

choiceExplanations.Storage efficiency: The ratio of water stored in the root zone to the water needed there prior to irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Application efficiency: The ratio of water stored in the root zone to the total water delivered at the field.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation efficiency: Correct — irrigation efficiency evaluates cumulative water losses from the diversion source to the point of crop use.
choiceExplanations.Conveyance efficiency: The ratio of water delivered to the farm turnout to the water diverted from the source.

items.question: This is oftentimes not considered a marketing activity, but it is a marketing function. This is because agricultural products must pass through some levels of transformation before being made available to the users. This marketing function increases marketability of products by changing product forms.

choiceExplanations.Packaging: Enclosing products in containers to protect quality, simplify handling, and aid retail marketing.
choiceExplanations.Processing: Correct — processing transforms agricultural products into new usable forms, increasing their overall marketability.
choiceExplanations.Grading: Sorting products into uniform lots based on established standards of size, weight, and quality.
choiceExplanations.Storage: Holding agricultural products over time to preserve quality and balance supply with market demand.

items.question: The most simple form of open channel flow computation is:

choiceExplanations.Steady varied: Flow with constant discharge over time while depth and velocity vary along the channel length.
choiceExplanations.Steady uniform: Correct — steady uniform flow has constant depth and velocity in time and space, simplifying calculations via Manning's equation.
choiceExplanations.Unsteady uniform: A theoretical condition where depth changes over time equally across all channel sections.
choiceExplanations.Unsteady varied: Complex flow where depth and velocity vary with both time and distance, requiring unsteady flow equations.

items.question: These are intermediaries who deal directly with the end-users or the consumers. They are the wholesalers’ partners in distribution activities

choiceExplanations.Assemblers: Rural buyers who gather small farm lots and bulk them for storage or distribution to wholesalers.
choiceExplanations.Retailers: Correct — retailers partner with wholesalers to sell goods directly to end-users or final consumers.
choiceExplanations.Brokers: Agents who match buyers and sellers for a fee without taking ownership of the goods.
choiceExplanations.Jobbers: Small-scale wholesalers who buy in bulk and resell to retail stores rather than end consumers.

items.question: Methods of supplying water in the basin

choiceExplanations.Series supply and parallel supply: Terms describing hydraulic pipe networks or pump configurations rather than paddy basin water supply methods.
choiceExplanations.Direct supply and cascade supply: Correct — basin irrigation supplies water either directly from a ditch or by cascading across adjacent basins.
choiceExplanations.Gravity supply and pumped supply: Classifications based on the energy source delivering water rather than basin-to-basin layout.
choiceExplanations.Continuous supply and rotational supply: Scheduling methods describing timing of water delivery rather than physical basin supply paths.

items.question: It is anything offered for sale, attention, and acquisition

choiceExplanations.Place: Distribution channels and logistics used to make goods available to target customers.
choiceExplanations.Promotion: Marketing communications that inform and persuade target buyers to purchase a product.
choiceExplanations.Price: The monetary value charged to customers in exchange for a good or service.
choiceExplanations.Product: Correct — a product is anything offered to a market for attention, acquisition, use, or sale.

items.question: Which is not part of the macro-environment?

choiceExplanations.Suppliers of raw materials: Correct — suppliers belong to the firm's immediate microenvironment alongside customers, competitors, and intermediaries.
choiceExplanations.Political and legal factors: Laws, regulations, and government policies that form part of the external macro-environment.
choiceExplanations.Technological and natural forces: Industry-wide innovations and environmental conditions belonging to the broader macro-environment.
choiceExplanations.Demographic and cultural forces: Population traits and societal values that are key components of the macro-environment.

items.question: A geologic formation that contains water but do not have the capacity to transmit it.

choiceExplanations.Aquitard: A low-permeability geologic layer that stores water and transmits it slowly without completely blocking flow.
choiceExplanations.Phreatic zone: The saturated subsurface zone below the water table where all pores are filled with water.
choiceExplanations.Aquifer: A permeable water-bearing geologic formation capable of storing and transmitting significant groundwater quantities.
choiceExplanations.Aquifuge: Correct — an aquifuge is an impermeable geologic formation that may hold water but cannot transmit it.

items.question: Farm water requirement minus the application losses is the_______

choiceExplanations.Crop water requirement: Total water needed by a crop for evapotranspiration and leaching, met by rainfall and irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Farm irrigation requirement: Correct — subtracting field application losses from the farm water requirement gives the farm irrigation requirement.
choiceExplanations.Net irrigation requirement: Water needed directly in the root zone excluding effective rainfall, conveyance losses, and application losses.
choiceExplanations.Gross irrigation requirement: Total water diverted at the headworks, including net requirement plus conveyance and application losses.

items.question: In furrow irrigation, the rate of water application should be __________ the intake rate of the soil.

choiceExplanations.Proportional to: States only a linear ratio without specifying whether application stays below soil infiltration capacity.
choiceExplanations.Less than: Correct — applying water slower than the soil intake rate prevents furrow overtopping, surface runoff, and erosion.
choiceExplanations.Equal to: Matching the exact intake rate leaves no safety margin for spatial soil infiltration variability.
choiceExplanations.Greater than: Exceeding the soil intake rate causes excessive tailwater runoff and erosion along furrows.

items.question: Irrigation method used fore row crops wherein only a part of the surface is wetted

choiceExplanations.Wild flooding: An uncontrolled method letting water spread freely over the entire field surface without levees.
choiceExplanations.Basin irrigation: Flooding flat diked plots uniformly, which wets the entire soil surface.
choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Correct — furrow irrigation delivers water along channels between row crops, wetting only part of the surface.
choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Applying water between parallel ridges as a continuous sheet covering the full strip width.

items.question: Run-off is the difference between the gross depth of irrigation water and the____.

choiceExplanations.Depth that infiltrated: Correct — by field water balance, surface runoff equals gross applied depth minus the depth that infiltrated.
choiceExplanations.Depth of percolation: Water draining below the root zone after infiltration, constituting a subsurface loss rather than runoff.
choiceExplanations.Net depth required: The target root-zone moisture deficit to replenish, which equals infiltrated depth minus deep percolation.
choiceExplanations.Depth of evaporation: Moisture lost directly to air, typically negligible relative to infiltration and runoff during surface irrigation.

items.question: It is the type of sprinkler irrigation system where the number of laterals installed is equal to the total number of lateral positions

choiceExplanations.Set system: Correct — a set (solid-set) sprinkler system has enough laterals installed to cover all positions without moving pipes.
choiceExplanations.Continuous move: A mechanized sprinkler system that travels continuously across the field while applying water.
choiceExplanations.Center pivot: A lateral rotating continuously around a central pivot point to irrigate circular field areas.
choiceExplanations.Periodic move: A sprinkler system with fewer laterals that are moved manually or mechanically between fixed irrigation sets.

items.question: It is a surface irrigation system where the area is subdivided by dikes and water flows over these dikes from one subdivision to another.

choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Directs water down sloping strips bounded by parallel ridges without cascading across dikes.
choiceExplanations.Corrugation irrigation: Uses small shallow channels to guide water across close-growing crops on sloping land.
choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Applies water along narrow channels excavated between raised crop rows rather than over diked plots.
choiceExplanations.Basin irrigation: Correct — basin irrigation subdivides fields with dikes where water may spill from one basin to another.

items.question: Governed by chance; time series INDEPENDENT

choiceExplanations.Stationary process: A stochastic process whose statistical properties like mean and variance remain constant over time.
choiceExplanations.Deterministic process: A process governed by exact physical laws with zero randomness and identical outputs for identical inputs.
choiceExplanations.Probabilistic process: Correct — a probabilistic process is governed by chance with outcomes that are independent across time.
choiceExplanations.Stochastic process: A chance-governed process whose random variables form a time-dependent sequential series.

items.question: In surface irrigation, the ratio between the gross amount of irrigation water and the net requirement of the crop is the _____

choiceExplanations.Distribution efficiency: Measures how uniformly applied irrigation water is distributed across the irrigated field.
choiceExplanations.Storage efficiency: The ratio of water stored in the root zone to the water needed prior to irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Application efficiency: Correct — application efficiency compares the crop's net irrigation requirement to the gross water applied to the field.
choiceExplanations.Conveyance efficiency: The ratio of water delivered at the farm or field turnout to the water diverted at the source.

items.question: It is an orderly sequence of planting crop in an area for a 365-day period.

choiceExplanations.Cropping pattern: Correct — a cropping pattern specifies the orderly yearly (365-day) sequence of planting crops in an area.
choiceExplanations.Cropping intensity: The ratio of total annual harvested crop area to physical farm area, expressed in percent.
choiceExplanations.Crop rotation: Growing different crops sequentially across seasons or years primarily to manage pests and soil fertility.
choiceExplanations.Cropping calendar: A timetable detailing exact planting, management, and harvesting dates for individual crops.

items.question: In the furrow irrigation, it is the difference between the depth of water that infiltrated and the net depth requirement is the

choiceExplanations.Deep percolation: Correct — water infiltrating beyond the net root-zone requirement drains downward below the roots as deep percolation.
choiceExplanations.Evaporation loss: Water vaporizing directly from the soil or water surface before reaching the root zone.
choiceExplanations.Surface runoff: Excess applied water flowing off the field end without infiltrating into the soil.
choiceExplanations.Conveyance loss: Seepage, leakage, and evaporation occurring in canals or pipes before water reaches the field.

items.question: The sum total of head above the vapor pressure of the liquid being pumped at a given pumping temperature.

choiceExplanations.Total static head: Vertical elevation difference between supply and discharge water surfaces under zero-flow conditions.
choiceExplanations.Static discharge head: Vertical height from the pump centerline up to the free discharge water surface.
choiceExplanations.Total dynamic head: Correct — keyed as total dynamic head in the reviewer, representing total static, friction, and pressure head above suction vapor limits.
choiceExplanations.Static suction head: Vertical height of the supply water surface above the pump centerline in flooded suction.

items.question: The recommended pressure head variation in the lateral between the first and the last sprinkler

choiceExplanations.24%: Exceeds the standard 20% lateral pressure limit, causing excessive discharge variation along the lateral.
choiceExplanations.20%: Correct — standard sprinkler lateral design limits pressure head variation between first and last sprinklers to 20%.
choiceExplanations.22%: Exceeds the standard 20% allowable pressure variation needed to maintain uniform sprinkler output.
choiceExplanations.18%: More restrictive than the standard 20% design limit, requiring unnecessarily larger lateral pipe diameters.

items.question: If the suction lift is 6 m, the suited type of pump is

choiceExplanations.Submersible: Placed fully underwater in deep wells where pumping lifts exceed surface suction limits.
choiceExplanations.Centrifugal: Correct — surface centrifugal pumps handle practical suction lifts up to about 6 m reliably.
choiceExplanations.Turbine: Deep-well pumps with submerged impellers designed for pumping lifts much greater than 6 m.
choiceExplanations.Propeller: Axial-flow pumps suited for very low heads (under 3–4 m) and very high flow rates.

items.question: The common name for Camelus dromedaries:

choiceExplanations.Camel: Correct — Camelus dromedarius is the scientific name of the single-humped dromedary camel.
choiceExplanations.Llama: Lama glama, a domesticated South American camelid that lacks humps.
choiceExplanations.Donkey: Equus asinus, a domesticated equine species closely related to horses.
choiceExplanations.Alpaca: Vicugna pacos, a smaller South American camelid raised primarily for its fine fleece.

items.question: What is the term for water that penetrates into the soil and flows laterally in the surface soil to a stream channel?

choiceExplanations.Baseflow: Groundwater discharge from the saturated zone that sustains stream flow during dry weather.
choiceExplanations.Infiltration: The downward entry of surface water into the top soil layer.
choiceExplanations.Percolation: The downward movement of water through soil pores under gravity toward the water table.
choiceExplanations.Interflow: Correct — interflow is infiltrated water flowing laterally through upper soil layers into a stream channel.

items.question: The amount of moisture content that is left from the soil 2-3 days after heavy application of rain or irrigation water

choiceExplanations.Hygroscopic Coefficient: Moisture tightly bound to soil particles by adsorption and completely unavailable to plant roots.
choiceExplanations.Saturation Capacity: Soil state right after wetting when all soil pores are completely filled with water.
choiceExplanations.Field Capacity: Correct — field capacity is the moisture remaining 2–3 days after heavy wetting once free drainage stops.
choiceExplanations.Permanent Wilting Point: Lower soil moisture limit at which plants wilt permanently and cannot recover in humid air.

items.question: Soil less agriculture.

choiceExplanations.Geoponics: Traditional crop cultivation practiced directly in natural soil rather than nutrient solutions.
choiceExplanations.Aquaculture: Farming of aquatic organisms like fish and crustaceans in controlled water environments.
choiceExplanations.Hydrophonic: Correct — hydroponics (spelled "hydrophonic" here) is soilless agriculture growing plants in mineral nutrient solutions.
choiceExplanations.Vermiculture: Cultivation of earthworms to convert organic waste into nutrient-rich vermicompost.

items.question: Characterize by irregular path of particle movements which keep of crossing and re-crossing

choiceExplanations.Turbulent flow: Correct — turbulent flow exhibits irregular, chaotic particle paths that constantly cross and re-cross.
choiceExplanations.Unsteady flow: Flow whose velocity or depth at a fixed point varies over time regardless of path regularity.
choiceExplanations.Transitional flow: Intermediate flow regime between laminar and turbulent where eddies begin appearing intermittently.
choiceExplanations.Laminar flow: Smooth, orderly flow where fluid particles move along parallel layers without crossing paths.

items.question: Constructed along the channel or waterway to control the velocity of flowing water and encourage deposition of sediments carried by water

choiceExplanations.Culverts or siphons: Closed conduits carrying water underneath roadways, embankments, or intersecting channels.
choiceExplanations.Check dams or weirs: Correct — check dams and weirs slow channel velocity to trap sediment and stabilize gully beds.
choiceExplanations.Flumes or aqueducts: Open or elevated conduits designed to carry water across valleys or depressions.
choiceExplanations.Spillways or chutes: Structures built to discharge excess floodwaters or carry water down steep slopes at high velocity.

items.question: This system is used in rolling topography where drainage is necessary only in small valleys.

choiceExplanations.Parallel system: Subsurface drainage with equally spaced parallel laterals suited for flat, uniformly wet fields.
choiceExplanations.Natural system: Correct — the natural drainage system follows winding depressions and small valleys in rolling topography.
choiceExplanations.Herringbone system: Drainage layout with parallel laterals joining a central main from both sides at acute angles.
choiceExplanations.Gridiron system: Subsurface layout using parallel laterals entering one side of a main drain on flat terrain.

items.question: The key objectives of each of the 3 Cs of marketing must be attained to be considered

choiceExplanations.Sales-oriented: Focuses on aggressive selling of existing goods rather than balancing customer, company, and competitor objectives.
choiceExplanations.Production-oriented: Prioritizes high output and low unit cost over tailored customer-driven marketing goals.
choiceExplanations.Product-oriented: Concentrates on product technical features without aligning customer, company, and competitor goals.
choiceExplanations.Marketing-oriented: Correct — a marketing-oriented firm achieves key objectives across the 3 Cs: Customers, Company, and Competitors.

items.question: This is the set of tools a firm uses to pursue the marketing objectives for the target market

choiceExplanations.Marketing plan: The written document detailing marketing budgets, schedules, and tactical execution programs.
choiceExplanations.Marketing strategy: The overarching game plan for selecting target markets and positioning the brand.
choiceExplanations.Marketing channel: The network of intermediaries moving goods from producers to final buyers.
choiceExplanations.Marketing mix: Correct — the marketing mix (4 Ps) is the set of controllable tools used to reach target-market objectives.

items.question: This is an indispensable component of a firm to continuously satisfy customers. It comes from having excess of sales over cost and expenses

choiceExplanations.Capital: Financial assets or resources invested to start and operate a business enterprise.
choiceExplanations.Revenue: Total gross income generated from sales before deducting operating costs and expenses.
choiceExplanations.Profit: Correct — profit is the financial surplus left when sales revenue exceeds total costs and expenses.
choiceExplanations.Equity: The owners' residual claim on business assets after subtracting all liabilities.

items.question: _____ are products that underwent secondary or the second level of transformation. These are in the forms which are for use by other industries and processors but may not be consumed

choiceExplanations.Fully-processed products: Finished goods ready for direct final consumption without further industrial processing.
choiceExplanations.Semi-processed products: Correct — semi-processed products undergo secondary transformation as intermediate inputs for other processors and industries.
choiceExplanations.Primary-processed products: Commodities undergoing only initial postharvest handling such as cleaning, shelling, drying, or milling.
choiceExplanations.Unprocessed raw products: Freshly harvested produce sold in natural form without mechanical or chemical transformation.

items.question: A field is divided into a series of strips by borders or ridges running down the predominant slope or on the contour.

choiceExplanations.Check-basin flooding: Divides fields into level plots surrounded by dikes on all four sides.
choiceExplanations.Contour-levee flooding: Uses closely spaced levees following land contours to impound water on sloping terrain.
choiceExplanations.Free-wild flooding: Allows water to flow freely over ungraded fields without guiding levees or borders.
choiceExplanations.Border-strip flooding: Correct — border-strip flooding divides a field into strips using parallel ridges down the slope or contour.

items.question: This is a continuous function of marketing. The objective of this function is to inform prospective buyers of product availability and also to increase sales.

choiceExplanations.Pricing: Setting the monetary amount charged to buyers in exchange for a product or service.
choiceExplanations.Packaging: Designing and producing containers to protect, store, and present a product.
choiceExplanations.Promotion: Correct — promotion continuously informs prospective buyers of product availability and persuades them to increase sales.
choiceExplanations.Distribution: Managing logistics and channels to move products physically to target markets.

items.question: built along a supplementary farm ditch at the head of the internal farm ditch to control and regulate the flow.

choiceExplanations.Offtake: Correct — an offtake is built at the head of an internal farm ditch along a supplementary farm ditch to regulate flow.
choiceExplanations.Aqueduct: An elevated conduit carrying irrigation water across depressions, streams, or roadways.
choiceExplanations.Checkgate: A gate across a ditch or canal used to raise upstream water level for diversion.
choiceExplanations.Turnout: A diversion structure along a main or lateral canal that supplies water into a main farm ditch.

items.question: PAES 421:2009 FMR. Type of Roadside ditch that easily be constructed and requires less right-of-way shall be determined by considering the intended purpose, terrain, flow velocity and quantity of flow to be conveyed and intended primarily for low flow conditions such as in median and roadside ditches

choiceExplanations.Trapezoidal Ditch: Standard flat-bottomed ditch with sloped sides designed for conveying larger drainage flows.
choiceExplanations.Rectangular Ditch: Vertical-walled concrete or masonry ditch used mainly where space is severely constrained.
choiceExplanations.Triangular V-Ditch: Correct — PAES 421:2009 specifies the triangular V-ditch for easy construction, minimal right-of-way, and low median or roadside flows.
choiceExplanations.Parabolic Ditch: Smoothly curved ditch cross-section mimicking natural waterways, harder to excavate than a V-ditch.

items.question: Operating pressure classification of sprinkler (kpa)
items.answer: Low - less than 150 kPa Medium - 150 kPa to 350 kPa High >350 kPa
choices: Low - less than 100 kPa Medium - 100 kPa to 250 kPa High >250 kPa
Low - less than 250 kPa Medium - 250 kPa to 500 kPa High >500 kPa
Low - less than 150 kPa Medium - 150 kPa to 350 kPa High >350 kPa
Low - less than 200 kPa Medium - 200 kPa to 400 kPa High >400 kPa

choiceExplanations.Low - less than 100 kPa Medium - 100 kPa: Understates standard sprinkler pressure thresholds, placing medium-pressure sprinklers into the high category.
choiceExplanations.Low - less than 250 kPa Medium - 250 kPa: Overstates standard low and medium pressure thresholds for agricultural sprinkler classification.
choiceExplanations.Low - less than 150 kPa Medium - 150 kPa: Correct — standard classification defines sprinkler operating pressure as low (<150 kPa), medium (150–350 kPa), and high (>350 kPa).
choiceExplanations.Low - less than 200 kPa Medium - 200 kPa: Shifts standard pressure thresholds higher than the 150 kPa and 350 kPa classification cutoffs.

items.question: Radius of throw classification of sprinkler (m)

choiceExplanations.Small 50 m: Correct — standard sprinkler classification sets 50 m as the small/medium radius of throw boundary.
choiceExplanations.Small 45 m: Incorrect threshold value below the standard 50 m sprinkler radius of throw classification.
choiceExplanations.Small 55 m: Exceeds the standard 50 m radius of throw benchmark used in sprinkler classification.
choiceExplanations.Small 40 m: Understates the 50 m cutoff defined in the sprinkler radius of throw classification.

items.question: Application rate classification of sprinkler

choiceExplanations.Low 13mm/hr: Understates the standard 15 mm/hr upper limit for low sprinkler application rates.
choiceExplanations.Low 17mm/hr: Exceeds the standard 15 mm/hr cutoff separating low and medium sprinkler application rates.
