choiceExplanations.Low 19mm/hr: Overstates the low application rate classification threshold of 15 mm/hr.
choiceExplanations.Low 15mm/hr: Correct — standard sprinkler classification defines a low application rate as up to 15 mm/hr.

items.question: The ratio of water stored in the root zone during the irrigation to the water needed in the root zone prior to irrigation, expressed in percent.

choiceExplanations.Water application efficiency: Ratio of water stored in the root zone to total irrigation water delivered to the field.
choiceExplanations.Water conveyance efficiency: Ratio of water delivered to the farm or field turnout to water diverted from the source.
choiceExplanations.Water storage efficiency: Correct — water storage efficiency is the percentage of pre-irrigation root-zone water need stored during irrigation.
choiceExplanations.Water distribution efficiency: Measure of how uniformly infiltrated irrigation water is distributed across the entire field.

items.question: The survey of bodies of water made for the purpose of navigation, water supply, or sub-aqueous construction

choiceExplanations.Cadastral surveying: Surveying performed to establish, subdivide, and register legal land property boundaries.
choiceExplanations.Geodetic surveying: Large-scale surveying that accounts for Earth's curvature to establish precise geodetic control.
choiceExplanations.Hydrographic surveying: Correct — hydrographic surveying maps water bodies for navigation, water supply, and sub-aqueous construction.
choiceExplanations.Topographic surveying: Surveying land surfaces to map elevations, contours, and natural or man-made terrain features.

items.question: Flow in pipe

choiceExplanations.Unsteady-uniform: Velocity remains constant along the pipe length at any instant, while discharge changes over time.
choiceExplanations.Unsteady-varied: Flow depth or velocity changes both with time and along the conduit length, as in surge waves.
choiceExplanations.Steady-varied: Discharge is constant over time, while velocity or cross-section changes along the flow path.
choiceExplanations.Steady-uniform: Correct — flow in a constant-diameter pipe under constant head maintains unchanging velocity across both time and distance.

items.question: The minimum trajectory angle for sprinkler.

choiceExplanations.55-70 degrees: Exceedingly steep angles increase wind drift and evaporation losses rather than providing low-trajectory clearance.
choiceExplanations.10-25 degrees: Correct — low-angle sprinklers use 10 to 25 degrees to clear low foliage and minimize wind distortion.
choiceExplanations.25-40 degrees: Standard-angle impact sprinklers typically operate around 25 to 30 degrees, above the minimum low-angle range.
choiceExplanations.40-55 degrees: High trajectory angles cause excessive droplet drift in wind and are not used as minimum sprinkler angles.

items.question: Basic irrigation method for lowland farming

choiceExplanations.Basin irrigation: Correct — level diked basins pond water uniformly, making it the basic method for lowland rice farming.
choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Uses small parallel channels between crop ridges, suited for upland row crops rather than ponded lowlands.
choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Applies water as a sheet down sloped strips between dikes, requiring graded fields rather than flat lowlands.
choiceExplanations.Sprinkler irrigation: Pressurized overhead spraying suits undulating upland soils but is uneconomical for flooded lowland paddy fields.

items.question: Irrigation method with high cost but low operation cost

choiceExplanations.Basin irrigation: Has low initial installation cost for land leveling and dikes but higher labor demand during water application.
choiceExplanations.Surface irrigation: Gravity-fed surface systems require minimal equipment cost but higher field labor and water management effort.
choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Inexpensive to establish on graded land, though it demands continuous labor to regulate furrow streams.
choiceExplanations.Overhead irrigation: Correct — pressurized sprinkler or overhead systems require high capital investment yet run with low labor and operation costs.

items.question: Laterals enter the submain from one side only to minimize the double drainage that occurs near the submain

choiceExplanations.Herringbone: Laterals enter the submain at angles from both sides, causing double drainage near the submain.
choiceExplanations.Gridiron: Correct — parallel laterals enter the submain from one side only, minimizing double drainage along the submain.
choiceExplanations.Random: Irregularly placed drains follow isolated wet depressions rather than a parallel one-sided lateral layout.
choiceExplanations.Interceptor: A single cutoff drain placed across a slope to intercept subsurface seepage from higher ground.

items.question: Flow greater than the critical flow.

choiceExplanations.Uniform flow: Flow whose depth and velocity remain constant along the channel length, independent of Froude number.
choiceExplanations.Laminar flow: Viscous-dominated flow at low Reynolds numbers where fluid particles move in smooth parallel layers.
choiceExplanations.Subcritical flow: Tranquil flow slower than critical velocity, having a Froude number less than one.
choiceExplanations.Supercritical flow: Correct — rapid flow exceeding critical velocity has a Froude number greater than one and shallower depth.

items.question: Irrigation components, related to flow and head.

choiceExplanations.Head gates: Correct — head gates are installed at canal intakes to regulate both water head and inflow discharge.
choiceExplanations.Tail gates: End-check or wasteway structures located at ditch ends to safely discharge excess water into drains.
choiceExplanations.Drop structures: Vertical or inclined drops that dissipate excess kinetic energy when lowering water across steep terrain.
choiceExplanations.Division boxes: Junction structures that proportion and split canal flow among multiple branching farm ditches.

items.question: The type of surveying in which the surface of the earth is considered as a plane, or in which its spheroidal shape is neglected, with regard to horizontal distances and directions.

choiceExplanations.Photogrammetric surveying: Uses overlapping aerial or terrestrial photographs to measure ground features and map terrain.
choiceExplanations.Plane surveying: Correct — assumes the Earth's surface is flat over limited areas, neglecting curvature for horizontal measurements.
choiceExplanations.Topographic surveying: Determines horizontal positions and elevations to represent natural and man-made terrain relief on maps.
choiceExplanations.Geodetic surveying: Accounts for the Earth's true spheroidal curvature when measuring large areas with high precision.

items.question: Most commonly used type for domestic and irrigation purposes. Consists of an impeller inside an involute casing.

choiceExplanations.Reciprocating: Positive-displacement pump using a piston or plunger inside a cylinder rather than a rotating impeller.
choiceExplanations.Turbine: Vertical multi-stage pump designed for deep wells using bowl diffusers rather than a single involute casing.
choiceExplanations.Centrifugal: Correct — uses a rotating impeller inside a volute casing, making it standard for domestic and irrigation pumping.
choiceExplanations.Propeller: Axial-flow pump moving high volumes at very low heads using propeller blades inside a straight tube.

items.question: A small trench for the drainage of animal waste

choiceExplanations.Lagoon: A large earthen impoundment used for biological treatment and long-term storage of livestock wastewater.
choiceExplanations.Pit: Correct — a small trench or shallow excavation beneath or beside animal housing that collects and drains waste.
choiceExplanations.Sump: A collection chamber or well where liquid accumulates before being lifted out by a pump.
choiceExplanations.Basin: A broad shallow holding structure or diked area, larger than a small waste-drainage trench.

items.question: The minimum trajectory angle for sprinkler

choiceExplanations.Very low = 5 deg 15 deg < 20 deg: Understates the standard low-trajectory sprinkler classification range used in irrigation design.
choiceExplanations.Very low = 10 deg 25 deg < 28 deg: Correct — standard irrigation classification lists very low sprinkler trajectory angles starting around 10 to 25 degrees, below 28 degrees.
choiceExplanations.Very low = 15 deg 30 deg < 35 deg: Shifts the trajectory thresholds upward into standard-angle sprinkler territory above 28 degrees.
choiceExplanations.Very low = 20 deg 32 deg < 40 deg: Represents moderate-to-high trajectory angles rather than the minimum low-angle sprinkler class.

items.question: installed at the head of the main canal, lateral and main farm ditch to admit and regulate the flow into the canal

choiceExplanations.Headgate head regulator intake structure: Correct — headgates or head regulators are placed at canal heads to admit and control incoming discharge.
choiceExplanations.Checkgate cross regulator check structur: Placed across a canal downstream of a junction to raise upstream water level for diversion.
choiceExplanations.Turnout farm outlet intake gate: Specifically delivers water from a supply canal into a farm ditch or individual service area.
choiceExplanations.Tailgate end check wasteway structure: Located at the downstream end of a ditch to release excess water safely into drainage.

items.question: installed immediately downstream of the junction of an irrigation canal to raise the water level upstream in order to facilitate its diversion into the branching canal

choiceExplanations.Drop structure or chute: Lowers water elevation along steep grades while dissipating excess kinetic energy.
choiceExplanations.Checkgate or cross regulator: Correct — installed downstream of a canal junction to back up water and raise upstream head for diversion.
choiceExplanations.Headgate or intake structure: Placed at the entrance of a branching canal to admit and meter inflow rather than raise main canal head.
choiceExplanations.Turnout or farm outlet: Small outlet structure delivering water from a lateral or sub-lateral into a farm ditch.

items.question: special intake structure that serves as an outlet of irrigation water into the main farm ditch or service area

choiceExplanations.Headgate: Regulates water entering major canals at the source or main lateral junctions rather than farm-level service areas.
choiceExplanations.Turnout: Correct — a turnout is an outlet structure discharging irrigation water from a canal into a main farm ditch or service area.
choiceExplanations.Wasteway: A spillway or escape channel discharging surplus canal water into natural drainage ways.
choiceExplanations.Checkgate: Controls upstream water elevation in a canal rather than acting as a farm-ditch outlet.

items.question: hydraulic structure that splits the flow from parent canal by at least 25%. Below 25% is called turnout.

choiceExplanations.Cross regulator: Controls upstream canal water surface elevation rather than splitting discharge by a fixed percentage.
choiceExplanations.Head regulator: Controls the volume admitted into a secondary or lateral canal at its intake gate.
choiceExplanations.Flow divisor: Correct — splits flow from a parent canal when at least 25% of discharge is diverted into a branch.
choiceExplanations.Division box: Small farm-level box splitting flow among supplementary farm ditches rather than parent canals.

items.question: diverts the flow into one or more supplementary farm ditches

choiceExplanations.Check structure: Raises upstream water level in a canal or ditch without itself dividing flow into multiple ditches.
choiceExplanations.Flow divisor: Splits major parent canal discharge where diverted branch flow is at least 25 percent.
choiceExplanations.Division box: Correct — a division box distributes and diverts irrigation water from a main farm ditch into supplementary farm ditches.
choiceExplanations.Drop structure: Transitions canal flow from a higher elevation to a lower elevation safely.

items.question: structure built at the tail end of the farm ditch to allow the safe entry of excess irrigation water into the drainage canals

choiceExplanations.Cross regulator check gate: Placed mid-canal downstream of junctions to raise water level for upstream diversion.
choiceExplanations.End check tail gate: Correct — an end check or tail gate sits at the ditch terminus to spill excess water safely into drains.
choiceExplanations.Farm ditch division box: Splits irrigation flow among supplementary farm ditches rather than discharging waste at the tail end.
choiceExplanations.Head gate intake structure: Admits and regulates incoming flow at the head of a canal or farm ditch.

items.question: discharge measurement structure that constricts the flow by narrowing the width of the channel section. The most common is the parshall flume – bridge for water irrigation

choiceExplanations.Weir: Correct — in standard ABELE review classifications, open-channel discharge measurement structures like weirs and flumes constrict flow to measure discharge.
choiceExplanations.Culvert: A closed conduit conveying water underneath a road, embankment, or railway rather than measuring open-channel flow.
choiceExplanations.Orifice: A submerged or free-flowing opening in a plate or wall rather than a channel-width constriction structure.
choiceExplanations.Siphon: A closed pipe using atmospheric pressure or inverted grade to carry water over ridges or under obstructions.

items.question: structure that conveys water across and above natural depressions such as creeks or rivers

choiceExplanations.Bench flume: Correct — an elevated open channel or aqueduct supported above ground to carry irrigation water across creeks or depressions.
choiceExplanations.Inverted siphon: A pressurized closed conduit carrying canal water underneath a depression, road, or stream instead of above it.
choiceExplanations.Drop structure: Conveys water down a steep slope between two canal elevations rather than bridging a depression.
choiceExplanations.Road culvert: Passes drainage or canal water beneath a roadway embankment rather than spanning above a river.

items.question: also known as tertiary canal
items.answer: Main farm ditch primary canal - main canal secondary canal - lateral quaternary canal - supplementary farm ditch
items.rationale: Main farm ditch primary canal - main canal secondary canal - lateral quaternary canal - supplementary farm ditch / 5th canal - internal farm ditch
choices: Supplementary farm ditch primary canal - main canal secondary canal - lateral quaternary canal - main farm ditch
Lateral canal primary canal - main canal secondary canal - main farm ditch quaternary canal - supplementary farm ditch
Main farm ditch primary canal - main canal secondary canal - lateral quaternary canal - supplementary farm ditch
Sub-lateral canal primary canal - main canal secondary canal - lateral quaternary canal - main farm ditch

choiceExplanations.Supplementary farm ditch primary canal -: Mislabels the supplementary farm ditch as tertiary; it is actually the quaternary canal.
choiceExplanations.Lateral canal primary canal - main canal: Mislabels the lateral canal as tertiary; laterals and sub-laterals are secondary canals.
choiceExplanations.Main farm ditch primary canal - main can: Correct — under NIA canal hierarchy, the main farm ditch is the tertiary canal between secondary laterals and quaternary supplementary ditches.
choiceExplanations.Sub-lateral canal primary canal - main c: Sub-laterals remain part of the secondary canal network, not the tertiary farm-level ditch.

items.question: Abnormal growth of plant which occur in barks, center, etc.

choiceExplanations.Checks: Lengthwise surface cracks in lumber caused by uneven shrinkage during seasoning, not plant growth.
choiceExplanations.Shakes: Separation of wood fibers along or between annual growth rings due to stress in standing trees or felling.
choiceExplanations.Knots: Correct — knots are embedded branch bases or abnormal woody growths formed within the tree trunk and bark.
choiceExplanations.Splits: Lengthwise cracks extending completely through a timber piece from one face to the opposite face.

items.question: Surveying instrument used for measuring horizontal and vertical angles, its telescope tube rest in a Y-shaped supports. The telescope with the attached bubble?

choiceExplanations.Dumpy level: Has a telescope rigidly attached to the leveling bar and uprights rather than removable Y-shaped supports.
choiceExplanations.Automatic level: Uses an internal gravity-activated pendulum compensator to level the line of sight automatically without Y-supports.
choiceExplanations.Tilting level: Features a telescope mounted on a pivot that is tilted slightly with a micrometer screw before each reading.
choiceExplanations.Wye level: Correct — a wye (Y) level holds a detachable telescope with an attached bubble tube inside Y-shaped bearing supports.

items.question: Pump used on shallow tube well

choiceExplanations.Propeller: Suited for very low-head, high-discharge surface pumping in open canals rather than tube wells.
choiceExplanations.Centrifugal: Correct — surface-mounted centrifugal pumps efficiently draw water from shallow tube wells where suction lift is under 7 meters.
choiceExplanations.Submersible: Deep-well multi-stage pump submerged below the water table, primarily used when lift exceeds suction limits.
choiceExplanations.Turbine: Vertical multi-stage shaft-driven pump designed for deep tube wells rather than shallow suction wells.

items.question: Flow of water to the propeller of the propeller pump

choiceExplanations.Mixed: Combines both axial and radial discharge components, characteristic of mixed-flow pumps rather than pure propeller pumps.
choiceExplanations.Tangential: Describes peripheral fluid velocity around a casing, not the primary through-flow direction of a propeller pump.
choiceExplanations.Radial: Water leaves the impeller perpendicular to the pump shaft, typical of centrifugal pumps.
choiceExplanations.Axial: Correct — water enters and exits a propeller pump parallel to the rotating shaft in an axial direction.

items.question: Critical Flow
items.rationale: Fr = 1 / SUBCIRITCAL, Fr1

choiceExplanations.Fr = 1: Correct — critical open-channel flow occurs when inertial and gravitational forces balance, giving a Froude number equal to 1.
choiceExplanations.Fr = 4: Represents strongly supercritical rapid flow well above the critical threshold.
choiceExplanations.Fr = 3: Indicates supercritical flow where flow velocity is three times the shallow-water wave celerity.
choiceExplanations.Fr = 2: Indicates supercritical flow exceeding critical velocity, not the critical state itself.

items.question: Is a special type of furrow irrigation, used for broadcast crops. Corrugations are small hills pressed into the soil surface. The application of this method is limited

choiceExplanations.Flood irrigation: Applies water uncontrolled over the entire land surface without small pressed channels or ridges.
choiceExplanations.Basin irrigation: Ponds water inside level diked areas rather than guiding flow through small pressed channels.
choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Guides water as a sheet down sloped strips bounded by low earth ridges.
choiceExplanations.Corrugated irrigation: Correct — corrugation (corrugated) irrigation uses closely spaced shallow furrows pressed into soil for broadcast or close-growing crops.

items.question: method of irrigation which makes use of parallel border strips where the water flows down the slope at a nearly uniform depth

choiceExplanations.Border irrigation: Correct — divides the field into parallel sloped strips bounded by dikes so water advances evenly as a sheet.
choiceExplanations.Furrow irrigation: Channels water through narrow parallel trenches between planted crop rows rather than wide strips.
choiceExplanations.Basin irrigation: Floods flat, level diked compartments where water stands without flowing down a slope.
choiceExplanations.Corrugation irrigation: Uses very small closely spaced rills to guide water across broadcast-seeded or forage fields.

items.question: facility withdrawing water from irrigation sources to the main canal in the volume and time required for irrigation in accordance with the relevant water use schedule.

choiceExplanations.Turnouts: Outlet structures transferring water from distribution canals into farm ditches, not from the primary river source.
choiceExplanations.Headworks: Correct — headworks (diversion dam, intake, and sluices) withdraw and regulate water from the river or source into the main canal.
choiceExplanations.Wasteways: Escape structures discharging excess canal water safely back to natural drainage channels.
choiceExplanations.Headgates: Individual gate components at canal inlets rather than the entire river diversion and intake facility.

items.question: Application rate at 15 mm/ha of sprinkler categorize as

choiceExplanations.Medium: Correct — in standard sprinkler application-rate classification, 10 to 20 mm/hr (around 15) falls in the medium range.
choiceExplanations.High: High sprinkler application rates generally exceed 20 mm/hr for coarse, high-infiltration soils.
choiceExplanations.Low: Low application rates are typically below 10 mm/hr to match fine-textured, slow-infiltrating soils.
choiceExplanations.Very high: Very high rates far exceed 25 mm/hr and risk severe surface runoff and erosion on most agricultural soils.

items.question: the lateral pipes are rigidly coupled and each joint of pipe is supported by a large wheel where the lateral line forms the axle for the wheels. This is mechanically moved by an engine mounted at the center of the line

choiceExplanations.Hand move system: Portable aluminum laterals uncoupled and carried manually from one set position to the next.
choiceExplanations.Side roll system: Correct — uses rigid lateral pipe acting as the axle of large wheels driven across the field by a center engine.
choiceExplanations.Center pivot system: Rotates a suspended lateral line continuously in a circle around a fixed central water supply pivot.
choiceExplanations.Linear move system: Self-propelled overhead towers move laterally in a straight line across rectangular fields without using the pipe as an axle.

items.question: Type of flow which is the same at every section of the prismatic channel

choiceExplanations.Varied flow: Flow whose depth, cross-sectional area, and velocity change from section to section along the channel.
choiceExplanations.Uniform flow: Correct — uniform flow maintains identical depth, cross-sectional area, and velocity at every section of a prismatic channel.
choiceExplanations.Laminar flow: Characterizes smooth, non-turbulent fluid motion at low Reynolds numbers regardless of spatial uniformity.
choiceExplanations.Steady flow: Means flow properties at a fixed point do not change with time, though they may vary spatially.

items.question: This is usually applied to large borders where the end borders are provided with openings to accommodate free flow of water for drainage

choiceExplanations.Open-ended: Correct — open-ended borders leave openings at the downstream dike so excess runoff drains freely into a tail ditch.
choiceExplanations.Dead-level: Level borders built with zero slope so water ponds uniformly without longitudinal drainage outflow.
choiceExplanations.Ponded-end: Closed downstream borders that retain tailwater in a ponded zone to maximize infiltration at the lower end.
choiceExplanations.Closed-ended: Borders blocked by a downstream levee to prevent surface runoff and retain all applied water.

items.question: IRRIGATION: Propeller pump’s impeller flows in a _____ manner

choiceExplanations.Tangential: Flows along the perimeter of the casing rather than straight along the propeller shaft axis.
choiceExplanations.Axial: Correct — propeller pump impellers discharge water parallel to the drive shaft in an axial flow path.
choiceExplanations.Radial: Fluid exits perpendicular to the impeller shaft, typical of standard centrifugal volute pumps.
choiceExplanations.Mixed: Combines axial intake with angled outward discharge, characteristic of mixed-flow turbine pumps.

items.question: DRAINAGE: A system of Drainage across contour.

choiceExplanations.Intercepting or cross slope: Correct — cross-slope or interceptor drains run across the contour to cut off seepage and surface runoff moving downslope.
choiceExplanations.Herringbone or chevron: A herringbone layout places angled laterals entering a central main from both sides in flat or depressed land.
choiceExplanations.Gridiron or parallel: Uses parallel uniformly spaced laterals discharging from one side into a submain on flat fields.
choiceExplanations.Natural or random: Follows scattered natural depressions irregularly without following a systematic cross-contour alignment.

items.question: A type of indirect leveling in which differences of elevation are determined from differences of atmospheric pressure observed with altimeters or barometers.

choiceExplanations.Trigonometric levelling: Computes elevation differences from measured vertical angles and horizontal or slope distances.
choiceExplanations.Differential levelling: Determines elevation differences directly by reading horizontal sight lines on graduated leveling rods.
choiceExplanations.Barometric levelling: Correct — uses barometers or altimeters to estimate elevation differences from changes in atmospheric air pressure.
choiceExplanations.Reciprocal levelling: Takes simultaneous forward and backward sights across wide obstacles like rivers to cancel curvature and refraction errors.

items.question: When the water level in an orifice drops below the upper edge of the orifice, the flow becomes

choiceExplanations.Pressurized pipe flow: Requires the conduit to flow completely full under internal hydraulic pressure above atmospheric.
choiceExplanations.Closed conduit flow: Occurs when water fills the entire opening with no free air-water surface inside the structure.
choiceExplanations.Submerged orifice flow: Occurs when both upstream and downstream water levels remain above the top edge of the orifice.
choiceExplanations.Open channel flow: Correct — dropping below the top edge exposes a free water surface to atmospheric pressure, creating open-channel flow.

items.question: DRAINAGE: Artificially produced in the subsoil by digging a trench from the surface.

choiceExplanations.French drain: A gravel-filled trench wrapped or lined to convey subsurface water rather than an unlined subsoil channel.
choiceExplanations.Mole drain: Correct — in classic board-review keys, a mole drain is an unlined subsoil channel formed artificially to drain excess water.
choiceExplanations.Blind drain: A subsurface trench backfilled with permeable stones or brush and covered with soil without open pipes.
choiceExplanations.Tile drain: Uses rigid clay, concrete, or perforated plastic pipes laid inside an excavated trench.

items.question: SURVEYING: A sign by extending both arms horizontally and moves up or down.

choiceExplanations.Move Left: Signaled by extending one arm out toward the left side of the instrumentman.
choiceExplanations.All Right: Correct — extending both arms horizontally and waving them up and down is the standard surveying signal for "all right."
choiceExplanations.Move Right: Signaled by extending one arm horizontally toward the right direction.
choiceExplanations.Plumb Rod: Signaled by holding one arm vertically overhead and tilting it toward the side the rod leans.

items.question: IRRIGATION: Irrigation enclosed by dikes

choiceExplanations.Border: Uses parallel low dikes down a slope with an open or regulated lower end rather than a fully enclosed compartment.
choiceExplanations.Furrow: Channels water in small parallel trenches between crop rows without enclosing dikes.
choiceExplanations.Corrugation: Uses shallow pressed rills on sloped land rather than enclosing dikes.
choiceExplanations.Basin: Correct — basin irrigation ponds water within a level field completely enclosed on all sides by earthen dikes.

items.question: it occurs in fast-moving open flows when the flow becomes unstable

choiceExplanations.Hydraulic bore: A moving abrupt wavefront advancing upstream or downstream in a channel due to sudden flow changes.
choiceExplanations.Backwater curve: A gradual rise in water surface profile upstream of an obstruction in subcritical flow.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic jump: Correct — an abrupt, turbulent transition from unstable fast supercritical flow to slower, deeper subcritical flow.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic drop: A rapid decrease in water depth as flow accelerates from subcritical over a free overfall or steep transition.

items.question: PROCESSING: Centrifugal Fan was producing air at _________
items.answer: High pressure and low air flow
choices: Low pressure and high air flow
Low pressure and low air flow
High pressure and low air flow
High pressure and high air flow

choiceExplanations.Low pressure and high air flow: Characteristic of axial or propeller fans moving large air volumes against low static resistance.
choiceExplanations.Low pressure and low air flow: Indicates an undersized or throttled fan rather than standard centrifugal fan characteristics.
choiceExplanations.High pressure and low air flow: Correct — centrifugal fans develop higher static pressures against grain-bed resistance at comparatively lower airflow rates than axial fans.
choiceExplanations.High pressure and high air flow: Exceeds normal single-stage centrifugal fan characteristics, which trade volume flow for static pressure.

items.question: When contour line from a closed figure with the highest elevation in the center, the topographic map indicates

choiceExplanations.Saddle: A low point between two adjacent peaks where contour lines form an hourglass or figure-eight pattern.
choiceExplanations.Mound: Correct — closed concentric contour lines increasing in elevation toward the center represent a hill or mound.
choiceExplanations.Depression: Closed contour lines whose elevation decreases toward the center, typically marked with hachures.
choiceExplanations.Valley: Indicated by V- or U-shaped contour lines pointing upstream toward higher elevations.

items.question: The process of determining the difference in elevation between two points

choiceExplanations.Profile leveling: Determines elevations along a continuous centerline alignment to plot ground longitudinal profiles.
choiceExplanations.Contour leveling: Locates ground points of equal elevation to draw topographic contour lines.
choiceExplanations.Differential leveling: Correct — measures vertical rod readings from a level line of sight to find the elevation difference between two points.
choiceExplanations.Check leveling: Repeats leveling back to a starting benchmark solely to verify the accuracy of a closed circuit.

items.question: A fixed point of reference whose elevation is either known or assumed.

choiceExplanations.Benchmark: Correct — a benchmark is a permanent or fixed physical reference point with a known or assumed elevation.
choiceExplanations.Foresight: A rod reading taken on a point of unknown elevation to determine its height.
choiceExplanations.Backsight: A rod reading taken on a point of known elevation to establish the height of instrument.
choiceExplanations.Datum: The horizontal reference surface, such as mean sea level, from which elevations are measured.

items.question: refers to a surface crack within the board, usually running lengthwise

choiceExplanations.Check: Correct — a check is a lengthwise separation of wood fibers extending across growth rings on a board's surface from drying.
choiceExplanations.Shake: A lengthwise separation occurring between or along the annual growth rings rather than across them on the surface.
choiceExplanations.Split: A lengthwise crack extending completely through a piece of lumber from one surface to another.
choiceExplanations.Wane: The presence of bark or lack of wood along the edge or corner of a sawn board.

items.question: Part of the roadway next to the travelled way or auxiliary lanes that provide lateral support of base and surface courses and is an emergency stopping area for vehicles

choiceExplanations.Road shoulder: Correct — the road shoulder borders the traveled way to laterally support pavement layers and provide emergency vehicle stopping space.
choiceExplanations.Roadway ditch: An excavated longitudinal channel alongside the roadbed built to collect and carry surface runoff.
choiceExplanations.Base course: The compacted aggregate structural layer placed directly beneath the pavement surface course.
choiceExplanations.Side slope: The inclined embankment or cut face sloping downward from the road shoulder to the roadside ditch.

items.question: This system is adapted to areas that have depressions that are too deep or too large to fill by land leveling. The ditches meander from one low spot to another, collecting the water and carrying it to an outlet ditch

choiceExplanations.Random ditch system: Correct — meandering random ditches link scattered deep depressions to convey ponded surface water to an outlet ditch.
choiceExplanations.Parallel ditch system: Uses evenly spaced straight parallel field ditches suited for flat, uniformly sloped land.
choiceExplanations.Cross-slope ditch system: Places shallow ditches across field slopes to intercept surface runoff and carry it along contour grades.
choiceExplanations.Diversion ditch system: Intercepts upland runoff at the field boundary before it flows onto lower agricultural land.

items.question: A point of fixed location which can be used as a reference point.

choiceExplanations.Benchmark: Correct — a benchmark is a fixed physical station of known elevation used as a survey reference point.
choiceExplanations.Waypoint: A temporary coordinate location recorded during GPS navigation rather than a fixed elevation reference monument.
choiceExplanations.Datum: A reference plane or surface, such as mean sea level, rather than a physical ground point.
choiceExplanations.Backsight: A leveling rod reading taken on an already established point to determine instrument height.

items.question: Structures that convey water across and above natural depressions such as creeks and rivers.

choiceExplanations.Check structure: Controls upstream canal water surface elevation rather than spanning across a stream depression.
choiceExplanations.Bench flume: Correct — an elevated open flume structure supported across valleys, creeks, or rivers to carry irrigation water above depressions.
choiceExplanations.Drop structure: Lowers canal water safely from a higher elevation to a lower one along steep terrain.
choiceExplanations.Inverted siphon: A pressurized closed conduit running underneath creeks or roads rather than above them.

items.question: The lateral movement of percolating water when encounters an impervious layer is

choiceExplanations.Interflow: Correct — interflow is the lateral subsurface movement of water above an impervious layer toward streams or drains.
choiceExplanations.Percolation: The downward vertical movement of water through soil pores below the root zone toward the water table.
choiceExplanations.Baseflow: Sustained groundwater discharge entering streams from the deeper saturated aquifer zone.
choiceExplanations.Infiltration: The initial entry of surface water downward into the top soil surface.

items.question: What inclined drop structure will you carry out to have a series of steps or levels that reduce the water velocity?
items.rationale: A stepped cascade is an inclined hydraulic drop structure built with a series of steps that dissipate kinetic energy and reduce flow velocity along steep terrain.

choiceExplanations.Stepped cascade: Correct — A stepped cascade is an inclined drop structure using a series of steps to dissipate energy and reduce water velocity.
choiceExplanations.Vertical drops: Vertical drops lower water abruptly over a single vertical wall rather than a series of inclined steps.
choiceExplanations.Flume series: Flumes convey water across depressions or obstacles via elevated channels rather than stepping down to reduce velocity.
choiceExplanations.Canal fall: A canal fall is the general category of drop structures, not specifically an inclined multi-stepped cascade.

items.question: The estimated fry survival rate, from newly hatched larvae until 3 weeks, of African catfish (Clarias gariepinus).
items.rationale: Under standard hatchery conditions for African catfish (Clarias gariepinus), the typical survival rate from newly hatched larvae to 3 weeks of age is about 50%.

choiceExplanations.25%: Under normal hatchery nursery care, 25% underestimates typical 3-week survival of African catfish fry.
choiceExplanations.80%: Reaching 80% survival by 3 weeks is unrealistically high due to cannibalism and early larval mortality.
choiceExplanations.50%: Correct — Standard aquaculture benchmarks estimate about 50% survival for African catfish fry from hatching through the 3-week nursery period.
choiceExplanations.75%: A 75% survival rate is higher than expected for Clarias gariepinus larvae during the vulnerable first 3 weeks.

items.question: What should be the total depth of your trapezoidal drainage canal if the design water depth is 2 meters and freeboard is 15%?
items.rationale: Total canal depth is the design water depth plus the 15% freeboard allowance: D = 1.15 × 2 m = 2.3 m.

choiceExplanations.3.2 m: A depth of 3.2 m implies a 60% freeboard allowance, far exceeding the specified 15%.
choiceExplanations.2.3 m: Correct — Total canal depth equals design water depth plus 15% freeboard: 2 m + (0.15 × 2 m) = 2.3 m.
choiceExplanations.2.6 m: A 2.6 m depth corresponds to a 30% freeboard rather than the given 15% freeboard.
choiceExplanations.1.8 m: A 1.8 m total depth is less than the 2 m design water depth and would cause overflow.

items.question: A spillway shall be hydraulically and structurally adequate and shall provide sufficient capacity. A spillway longitudinal cross-section is composed of the approach channel, discharge channel and ________.
items.rationale: Per PAES 609:2016 (Small Water Impounding System, Figure 6), the longitudinal cross-section of a spillway comprises the approach channel, discharge channel, and terminal structure.

choiceExplanations.Terminal: Correct — Under PAES spillway design standards, the longitudinal profile comprises the approach channel, discharge channel (chute), and terminal structure.
choiceExplanations.Apron: An apron is only one component of an energy-dissipating stilling basin, not the general longitudinal section term.
choiceExplanations.Tail race: A tail race is the outlet channel discharging water from a hydropower turbine, not a standard spillway section.
choiceExplanations.Water exit: Water exit is a generic descriptive phrase, not the recognized hydraulic engineering term for a spillway's end section.

items.question: Which laboratory method is commonly used in the Philippines to determine soil texture by particle size analysis?
items.rationale: The Bouyoucos hydrometer method is the standard laboratory technique commonly used in the Philippines for particle-size analysis to classify soil texture based on settling rates.

choiceExplanations.Pipette method: The pipette method is more precise for research, but is less routine in Philippine labs due to higher cost and effort.
choiceExplanations.Feel: The feel method is a rapid field technique for estimating soil texture, not a quantitative laboratory analysis.
choiceExplanations.Percolation method: The percolation method measures vertical water movement rate through soil rather than particle size distribution.
choiceExplanations.Hydrometer method: Correct — The Bouyoucos hydrometer method is the standard, practical laboratory test commonly used in Philippine soil labs to determine soil texture.

items.question: Applying minimization of maintenance cost, which kind of canal is less costly to maintain?
items.rationale: A concrete trapezoidal canal resists bank erosion, sloughing, and weed growth, resulting in lower recurring maintenance costs compared to unlined canals or grassed waterways.

choiceExplanations.Concrete trapezoidal canal: Correct — Concrete lining prevents erosion, seepage, and weed growth, while the trapezoidal section resists bank collapse, minimizing maintenance costs.
choiceExplanations.Grassed waterway: Grassed waterways require periodic mowing, reseeding, and sediment removal to maintain channel capacity and prevent gullies.
choiceExplanations.Unlined triangular canal: Unlined earthen triangular canals easily silt up, erode, and grow weeds, demanding frequent desilting and reshaping.
choiceExplanations.Unlined rectangular canal: Vertical earthen walls in unlined rectangular canals readily cave in and erode, resulting in high maintenance costs.

items.question: Given the data set: 27, 18, 46, 22, 14, 3, 52, 27, 5, 35, 9, 35, 10, 30, 46, 27. What is the range of the given data set?
items.rationale: The range of a data set is the difference between its highest and lowest values: Range = 52 − 3 = 49.

choiceExplanations.46: Forty-six is the second-largest value in the dataset, not the difference between maximum and minimum.
choiceExplanations.27: Twenty-seven is the mode (most frequent value) and median area, not the statistical range.
choiceExplanations.3: Three is the minimum value of the dataset, not the spread between extremes.
choiceExplanations.49: Correct — The range is the maximum value minus the minimum value: 52 − 3 = 49.

items.question: When constructing an irrigation canal on steep slopes, what drop structure will you provide when the natural slope of the ground is steeper than the designed gentle bed slope of the canal?
items.rationale: A canal fall is provided when the natural ground slope exceeds the designed canal bed slope so that the water level is stepped down safely without causing excessive flow velocities and erosion.

choiceExplanations.Chute: A chute is a steep sloped concrete channel used to convey water down a long steep grade rather than a stepped drop.
choiceExplanations.Aqueduct: An aqueduct is an elevated bridge-like structure carrying a canal over a depression, road, or natural drainage channel.
choiceExplanations.Flume: A flume is an artificial open channel supported above ground to cross depressions or unstable terrain, not to drop bed grade.
choiceExplanations.Canal fall: Correct — A canal fall (drop structure) lowers the canal bed elevation to reconcile a steep natural ground slope with a gentle design slope.

items.question: If you are to carry out a land survey for determining the path of a main irrigation channel, what type of survey will you employ?
items.rationale: A route survey is performed to establish the alignment, profile, and right-of-way along narrow corridors for linear engineering works such as main irrigation canals.

choiceExplanations.Cadastral survey: A cadastral survey establishes legal property boundaries and land parcel ownership rather than canal alignment.
choiceExplanations.Route survey: Correct — A route survey determines the optimal horizontal and vertical alignment of linear infrastructures like canals, roads, and pipelines.
choiceExplanations.Path survey: Path survey is not a standard surveying classification in Philippine engineering practice.
choiceExplanations.Construction survey: A construction survey sets out stakes and grades after design alignment is already chosen via route surveying.

items.question: You are tasked to evaluate pumps for use in the automation of water pumping in a greenhouse. Which kind of pump will you use?
items.rationale: Electric pumps are standard for automated greenhouse water pumping because they can be easily controlled by timers, pressure switches, and sensors without manual starting or exhaust emissions indoors.

choiceExplanations.Piston pump: Piston pumps are positive-displacement mechanisms classified by pumping action and usually produce pulsating flow unless dampened.
choiceExplanations.Diesel pump: Diesel engine pumps emit exhaust fumes, run noisily, and are difficult to automate inside enclosed greenhouses.
choiceExplanations.Electric pump: Correct — Electric pumps easily integrate with timers, moisture sensors, and relay controllers for clean, quiet greenhouse automation.
choiceExplanations.Gasoline pump: Gasoline engine pumps produce toxic exhaust inside greenhouses and lack straightforward automatic start-stop control.

items.question: A farmer will receive Php 200,000 in 5 years. If the interest rate is 8% per year, what is the present worth of that amount?
items.rationale: Using the single-payment present worth formula P = F / (1 + i)^n = Php 200,000 / (1 + 0.08)^5 = Php 200,000 / 1.469328 = Php 136,116.64.

choiceExplanations.Php 140,116.64: Php 140,116.64 overestimates the present worth by under-discounting the future sum at 8% over 5 years.
choiceExplanations.Php 130,116.64: Php 130,116.64 underestimates the present worth by applying a higher effective discount than 8% compounded over 5 years.
choiceExplanations.Php 138,116.64: Php 138,116.64 does not satisfy the compound discounting formula P = F / (1 + i)^n at i = 8%, n = 5.
choiceExplanations.Php 136,116.64: Correct — Discounting Php 200,000 at 8% for 5 years gives P = 200,000 / (1.08)^5 = Php 136,116.64.

items.question: A small refrigeration unit is used to store harvested vegetables. The unit absorbs 5 kW of heat from the refrigerated space and requires 2 kW of electrical power to operate. Calculate the Coefficient of Performance (COP) of the refrigerator. The electrical cost is Php 10 per kWh.
items.rationale: The Coefficient of Performance of a refrigerator is COP = Q_L / W_in = 5 kW / 2 kW = 2.5 (the electricity rate is extraneous information).

choiceExplanations.2: A value of 2 equals the input electrical power in kW, not the ratio of heat absorbed to work input.
choiceExplanations.4.5: A value of 4.5 does not result from dividing 5 kW of cooling load by 2 kW power input.
choiceExplanations.2.5: Correct — Coefficient of Performance is cooling effect divided by power input: COP = 5 kW / 2 kW = 2.5.
choiceExplanations.3.3: A COP of 3.3 would require roughly 6.6 kW of cooling for 2 kW of input power.

items.question: What drop structure will you implement to slow down the water flow and dissipate energy as the water passes over it?
items.rationale: Baffle chute drops use rows of baffle blocks along the sloped chute face to continuously slow down flow velocity and dissipate hydraulic energy as water descends.

choiceExplanations.Vertical drops: Vertical drops rely mainly on a downstream stilling pool rather than blocks along the slope to slow flow.
choiceExplanations.Baffle chute drops: Correct — Baffle chute drops use rows of concrete baffle blocks on a sloped apron to continuously decelerate flow and dissipate energy.
choiceExplanations.Canal fall: Canal fall is a broad term for any drop structure and does not specify energy-dissipating baffles along the chute.
choiceExplanations.Piped drops: Piped drops convey water through an inclined buried conduit rather than dissipating energy over a baffled open chute.

items.question: Determine the number of laterals needed for 103 m by 53 m field. The laterals are laid out across the shorter side of the field. Sprinkling diameter is 20 m. Use 50 % sprinkling overlap.
items.rationale: With 50% overlap on a 20 m sprinkling diameter, lateral spacing along the 103 m side is 0.50 × 20 m = 10 m; dividing 103 m / 10 m = 10.3, which rounds up to 11 laterals.

choiceExplanations.15: Fifteen laterals corresponds to a tighter spacing of about 7 m rather than the 10 m spacing from 50% overlap.
choiceExplanations.12: Twelve laterals overestimates the count needed along the 103 m side at 10 m lateral spacing.
choiceExplanations.11: Correct — With 50% overlap of a 20 m diameter, lateral spacing is 10 m along the 103 m side, requiring ⌈103 / 10⌉ = 11 laterals.
choiceExplanations.10: Ten laterals at 10 m spacing cover only 100 m, leaving part of the 103 m length uncovered.

items.question: In a concrete trapezoidal primary irrigation canal, what should be the spacing of 10 mm reinforcing bars?
items.rationale: Under Philippine irrigation canal design standards (PAES / NIA), temperature and shrinkage reinforcement for concrete-lined primary trapezoidal canals uses 10 mm reinforcing bars spaced at 20 cm × 20 cm on centers.

choiceExplanations.25 cm x 25 cm: A 25 cm × 25 cm grid exceeds the standard 20 cm maximum spacing for 10 mm bars in primary canals.
choiceExplanations.30 cm x 30 cm: Spacing bars at 30 cm × 30 cm provides insufficient crack and temperature control for concrete canal walls.
choiceExplanations.20 cm x 20 cm: Correct — PAES and NIA design standards specify 10 mm reinforcing bars spaced at 20 cm × 20 cm for concrete primary irrigation canals.
choiceExplanations.15 cm x 15 cm: A 15 cm × 15 cm grid is denser and costlier than the standard 20 cm spacing for 10 mm bars.

items.question: Evaluate which criteria is suitable for designing a concrete trapezoidal canal with 60 degrees side angle.
items.rationale: A trapezoidal canal with 60° side slopes forms half of a regular hexagon, minimizing the wetted perimeter for a given cross-sectional area and defining the most efficient trapezoidal canal section.

choiceExplanations.Moderately efficient canal: Moderately efficient canal is not the standard hydraulic design criterion for an optimal 60° trapezoidal section.
choiceExplanations.Most efficient canal: Correct — A trapezoidal canal with 60° side slopes forms a half-hexagon, which is the most efficient hydraulic cross-section minimizing wetted perimeter.
choiceExplanations.Good hydraulic cross-section: Good hydraulic cross-section is a vague label, whereas 60° side slopes specifically achieve maximum hydraulic efficiency.
choiceExplanations.Best hydraulic cross-section: While conceptually related, Philippine ABELE board references designate the 60° half-hexagon design specifically as the most efficient canal.

items.question: When two species compete for the same limited resource, what ecological interaction is occurring?
items.rationale: Competition is the ecological interaction in which two or more species contend for the same limited resource (such as food, water, light, or space), negatively affecting both.

choiceExplanations.Competition: Correct — Competition occurs when two or more species vie for the same limited resource such as water, nutrients, light, or space.
choiceExplanations.Mutualism: Mutualism is a symbiotic relationship where both interacting species derive mutual benefit.
choiceExplanations.Predation: Predation is an interaction in which one organism hunts, kills, and consumes another organism.
choiceExplanations.Commensalism: Commensalism is a relationship where one species benefits while the other is neither helped nor harmed.

items.question: In Wenner method of georesistivity measurement, the method is performed by placing four pins at equal distance, injecting a known current on the outermost electrodes and recording the _______ between the interior electrodes.
items.rationale: In the Wenner four-electrode configuration, a known current (I) is injected through the outer electrodes while the potential difference or voltage (V) is measured between the inner electrodes to compute apparent resistivity (ρ = 2πa·V/I).

choiceExplanations.Voltage: Correct — In the Wenner four-electrode array, current is injected through the outer electrodes while potential difference (voltage) is measured across the inner two.
choiceExplanations.Conductance: Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance and is calculated afterward rather than directly recorded by the voltmeter.
choiceExplanations.Resistivity: Apparent resistivity is computed from current, voltage, and electrode spacing using ρ = 2πa(V/I), not directly measured.
choiceExplanations.Resistance: Resistance is derived by dividing the measured voltage by the injected current (V/I), not directly sensed alone.

items.question: Analyze which of the following pumps is best for pumping water with algae from a 3-cubic meter hatchery tank into larval rearing tanks.
items.rationale: A submersible pump sits directly inside the 3-m³ hatchery tank without priming issues and efficiently transfers algae-laden water into larval rearing tanks.

choiceExplanations.Centrifugal pump: Standard surface centrifugal pumps require priming and suction piping, making small-tank hatchery transfers less convenient.
choiceExplanations.Diaphragm pump: Diaphragm pumps deliver low, pulsating flow suited for dosing or slurry rather than rapid hatchery water transfer.
choiceExplanations.Piston pump: Piston pumps have tight-fitting valves and seals that easily clog or wear from algae and suspended solids.
choiceExplanations.Submersible pump: Correct — A submersible pump sits directly in the hatchery tank without priming and handles suspended algae smoothly during water transfer.

items.question: You are requested to serve as a consultant of a large centrifugal irrigation pump 30-meter above an unconfined aquifer. The pump exhibits gassing when turned on and cannot produce water. The pump elevation is 550 meters above mean sea level. What is your recommendation to make pumping operational?
items.answer: Replace pump with a submersible one
items.rationale: A surface centrifugal pump cannot lift water across a 30 m suction head (theoretical maximum atmospheric suction lift is ~10.3 m at sea level and lower at 550 m elevation), causing cavitation; replacing it with a submersible pump placed in the water eliminates suction lift.
choices: Use artificial recharge to fill aquifer with water
Replace pump with a submersible one

choiceExplanations.Use artificial recharge to fill aquifer: Artificial recharge cannot quickly raise a regional water table enough to overcome a 30-meter suction lift limit.
choiceExplanations.Replace pump with a submersible one: Correct — Atmospheric pressure limits centrifugal suction lift to under 10.3 m (even lower at 550 m), so a submersible pump below water level is needed.
choiceExplanations.Use large diesel pump instead: Changing the prime mover to diesel still cannot overcome the physical suction-lift cavitation limit of a surface pump.
choiceExplanations.Relocate pump to lower elevation: Lowering the surface pump slightly at 550 m amsl will not solve a 30 m depth unless placed near water level.

items.question: A 2,000-kg tractor accelerates uniformly from rest to 6 m/s in 10 s. Find the tractive force.
items.rationale: The acceleration is a = Δv / t = 6 m/s / 10 s = 0.6 m/s², so the tractive force is F = m·a = 2,000 kg × 0.6 m/s² = 1200 N.

choiceExplanations.2000 N: A force of 2000 N would produce an acceleration of 1 m/s² rather than 0.6 m/s².
choiceExplanations.1200 N: Correct — Acceleration is a = (6 − 0) / 10 = 0.6 m/s², so tractive force F = ma = 2,000 kg × 0.6 m/s² = 1,200 N.
choiceExplanations.1400 N: A force of 1400 N would accelerate a 2,000 kg tractor at 0.7 m/s² instead of 0.6 m/s².
choiceExplanations.1000 N: A force of 1000 N yields only 0.5 m/s² acceleration, reaching 5 m/s in 10 seconds.

items.question: In applying the design criteria for the horizontal drain of a rockfill dam, the acceptable leakage volume is ______% of the storage capacity.
items.rationale: Per PAES 612:2016 (Section 14.2) on rockfill dam horizontal drain design criteria, the acceptable leakage volume is 0.05% of the storage capacity.

choiceExplanations.5: Allowing 5% leakage per day would rapidly drain the reservoir and risk piping failure in the embankment.
choiceExplanations.0.05: Correct — Standard dam horizontal-drain design criteria limit acceptable seepage or leakage volume to 0.05% of the reservoir's storage capacity.
choiceExplanations.0.03: A 0.03% limit is stricter than the standard 0.05% design threshold for rockfill dam horizontal drains.
choiceExplanations.0.5: A 0.5% leakage allowance is ten times higher than the accepted 0.05% engineering criterion.

items.question: In evaluating a rockfill dam design, what is not part of the design criteria?
items.answer: The velocity of flow at dam face shall be within 3 m/s to 5 m/s with reliable protection measures against scouring.
items.rationale: Rockfill dam design criteria prohibit overtopping, minimize seepage to prevent piping, and require adequate crest height for settlement and freeboard; allowing flow velocities of 3 m/s to 5 m/s along the dam face is not part of the design criteria.
choices: The velocity of flow at dam face shall be within 3 m/s to 5 m/s with reliable protection measures against scouring.
The dam crest shall be high enough allowing for rockfill embankment and foundation settlements and sufficient freeboard.
Seepage shall be kept at minimum to avoid piping of material.

choiceExplanations.The velocity of flow at dam face shall b: Correct — Rockfill dams are non-overflow structures designed against overtopping, so specifying 3–5 m/s overflow velocity at the dam face is not a rockfill dam criterion.
choiceExplanations.There shall be no overtopping: Preventing overtopping is a mandatory design criterion because overflow quickly erodes and breaches rockfill embankments.
choiceExplanations.The dam crest shall be high enough allow: Providing adequate crest height for embankment settlement and freeboard is essential to prevent overtopping.
choiceExplanations.Seepage shall be kept at minimum to avoi: Controlling seepage to prevent internal erosion (piping) is a core stability criterion for rockfill dams.

items.question: Determine the number of sprinklers per lateral needed for 103 m by 53 m field. The laterals are laid out across the shorter side of the field. Sprinkling diameter is 20 m. Use 50 % sprinkling overlap.
items.rationale: Each lateral spans the 53 m shorter side with sprinkler spacing = 50% × 20 m = 10 m, so 53 m / 10 m = 5.3, which rounds up to 6 sprinklers per lateral.

choiceExplanations.6: Correct — At 50% overlap of a 20 m diameter, sprinkler spacing is 10 m along the 53 m lateral, requiring ⌈53 / 10⌉ = 6 sprinklers.
choiceExplanations.3: Three sprinklers spaced at 10 m cover only 30 m, falling well short of the 53 m lateral length.
choiceExplanations.8: Eight sprinklers at 10 m spacing correspond to an 80 m lateral rather than 53 m.
choiceExplanations.5: Five sprinklers cover only 50 m at 10 m spacing, leaving 3 m of the lateral unreached.

items.question: You are working as a research assistant right after your graduation. One day, you are tasked to take a soil sample from a cultivation plot and analyze it in the laboratory. After the analysis, one of its particle fractions have an average diameter of 12 microns (µm). Based on USDA particle size classification, which of the following is the correct classification of the soil fraction?
items.rationale: Converting 12 µm to millimeters yields 0.012 mm, which falls within the USDA silt fraction range (0.002 mm to 0.05 mm; clay is < 0.002 mm and sand is 0.05–2.0 mm).

choiceExplanations.Clay: Under USDA classification, clay particles are smaller than 2 µm (0.002 mm), whereas 12 µm is larger.
choiceExplanations.Silt: Correct — Under USDA soil texture classification, silt particles range from 2 to 50 µm (0.002 to 0.05 mm), which includes 12 µm.
choiceExplanations.Loam: Loam is a textural class representing a balanced mixture of sand, silt, and clay, not a single particle size fraction.
choiceExplanations.Sand: Under USDA classification, sand particles range from 50 to 2,000 µm (0.05 to 2.0 mm), larger than 12 µm.

items.question: Design a drainage channel for a rice area supplied with 10 cubic m/s. What is the discharge of the drainage channel in cubic m/s?
items.rationale: Using the recommended ratio of drainage discharge to irrigation supply of 0.1 (10%), Q_drainage = 0.1 × 10 m³/s = 1 m³/s.

choiceExplanations.0.5: A discharge of 0.5 m³/s uses a 5% ratio, under-sizing the drain relative to the standard 10% design factor.
choiceExplanations.2: A discharge of 2 m³/s uses a 20% ratio, doubling the standard 10% irrigation-to-drainage design factor.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct — Using the standard 10% (0.1) ratio of drainage discharge to irrigation supply gives Q_drain = 0.1 × 10 m³/s = 1 m³/s.
choiceExplanations.1.5: A discharge of 1.5 m³/s corresponds to a 15% ratio rather than the recommended 10% ratio.

items.question: Which of the following is a bio-invasive species and has an allelopathic effect on the environment?
items.rationale: Big-leaf mahogany (Swietenia macrophylla) is an introduced bio-invasive tree species in the Philippines known for its allelopathic leaf litter that suppresses native understory plant growth.

choiceExplanations.Molave: Molave (Vitex parviflora) is a native Philippine hardwood species rather than an invasive alien tree.
choiceExplanations.Cocos nucifera: Coconut (Cocos nucifera) is a widely cultivated tropical palm not classified as an allelopathic bio-invasive species.
choiceExplanations.Big-leaf mahogany: Correct — Big-leaf mahogany (Swietenia macrophylla) is an introduced tree in the Philippines known for invasive spread and allelopathic suppression of native understory plants.
choiceExplanations.Narra: Narra (Pterocarpus indicus) is the native national tree of the Philippines, not a bio-invasive species.

items.question: Appropriate surveying instrument for determining the location of the center of the crest of a spillway?
items.rationale: A hand-held GPS directly records the geographic coordinates (location) of a point feature such as the center of a spillway crest during field inspection or mapping, whereas levels and transits measure elevations and angles.

choiceExplanations.Real-time kinematic (RTK) positioning GP: RTK GPS provides centimeter-level survey coordinates for detailed construction staking, which is unnecessarily complex for general spillway location referencing.
choiceExplanations.Hand-held GPS: Correct — A hand-held GPS quickly determines the geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude) locating the spillway crest center during field surveys.
choiceExplanations.Transit: A transit measures horizontal and vertical angles and distances rather than directly providing global geographic coordinates.
choiceExplanations.Dumpy level: A dumpy level measures elevation differences and horizontal sightlines, not horizontal geographic coordinates.

items.question: Design an unlined trapezoidal drainage channel to serve a 1.84 meters deep large main irrigation canal conveying 100 cu.m/s of irrigation water. Drainage discharge is limited to 1 m/s. Use side angle of 26.57 degrees. Use the 0.1 recommended ratio of drainage discharge to irrigation discharge. What is the base of the canal in meters?
items.rationale: Drainage discharge is Q = 0.1 × 100 m³/s = 10 m³/s, and with limiting velocity V = 1 m/s the cross-sectional area is A = 10 / 1 = 10 m²; using d = 1.84 m and θ = 26.57° (side slope z = cot 26.57° ≈ 2), b = A/d − z·d = 10/1.84 − 2(1.84) ≈ 1.75 m (or b = 4d·tan(26.57°/2) = 1.737 m), matching 1.7 m.

choiceExplanations.1.7: Correct — With Q = 0.1 × 100 = 10 m³/s, v = 1 m/s (A = 10 m²), d = 1.84 m, and z = cot(26.57°) ≈ 2, A = (b + zd)d yields b ≈ 1.7 m.
choiceExplanations.Mole drain: A mole drain is an unlined subsurface soil tunnel, not a dimension for a trapezoidal canal base.
choiceExplanations.7.1: A 7.1 m base width gives an area over 19 m², nearly double the required 10 m² cross-section.
choiceExplanations.6.8: A 6.8 m base width yields an area near 19.3 m², far larger than the 10 m² needed.

items.question: Determine the total number of drippers needed for 1,000 m x 1,000 m banana plantation. Planting distance is 2 m between hills x 2 m between rows.
items.rationale: Total plantation area is 1,000 m × 1,000 m = 1,000,000 m², and each dripper covers 2 m × 2 m = 4 m², so 1,000,000 / 4 = 250,000 drippers are required.

choiceExplanations.52000: 52,000 drippers covers only about one-fifth of the 1,000,000 m² plantation at 2 m × 2 m spacing.
choiceExplanations.520000: A count of 520,000 exceeds the 250,000 planting hills calculated for a 2 m × 2 m grid.
choiceExplanations.500000: A count of 500,000 would apply if there were 2 drippers per hill or 2 m × 1 m spacing.
choiceExplanations.250000: Correct — Dividing the 1,000,000 m² plantation area by 4 m² per plant (2 m × 2 m) gives 250,000 hills and drippers.

items.question: Determine the total number of sprinklers needed for 103 m by 53 m field. The number of laterals is 11 and the number of sprinklers per lateral is 6.
items.rationale: Total sprinklers = (number of laterals) × (number of sprinklers per lateral) = 11 × 6 = 66.

choiceExplanations.66: Correct — Multiplying 11 laterals by 6 sprinklers per lateral gives 11 × 6 = 66 total sprinklers.
choiceExplanations.60: Sixty sprinklers corresponds to only 10 laterals with 6 sprinklers each, rather than 11 laterals.
choiceExplanations.50: Fifty sprinklers is insufficient for 11 laterals carrying 6 sprinklers each.
choiceExplanations.55: Fifty-five sprinklers corresponds to 11 laterals with 5 sprinklers each instead of 6.

items.question: What is the most general level of classification in the USDA system of soil taxonomy?
items.rationale: In USDA Soil Taxonomy, the six hierarchical levels from broadest to most specific are Order, Suborder, Great Group, Subgroup, Family, and Series, so Soil order is the most general level.

choiceExplanations.Soil family: Soil family is the fifth and second-most specific category in USDA Soil Taxonomy, below subgroup.
choiceExplanations.Soil order: Correct — Soil order is the highest and most general taxonomic level in the USDA Soil Taxonomy system (12 orders).
choiceExplanations.Soil series: Soil series is the lowest and most specific category in USDA Soil Taxonomy.
choiceExplanations.Soil group: Great group is an intermediate level below suborder, whereas soil group is not the highest USDA category.

items.question: A technique for determining the existence of aquifers and kind of materials beneath the soil surface without digging the soil and without using soundwaves.
items.rationale: Georesistivity measurement injects electrical current into the ground and measures potential differences to identify subsurface strata and aquifers without excavation or seismic sound waves.

choiceExplanations.Pedonology: Pedology (soil science) studies soil formation and morphology, typically requiring physical sampling or pit excavation.
choiceExplanations.Seismology: Seismic surveys rely on propagating acoustic/sound waves through earth strata rather than electrical resistance.
choiceExplanations.Soil profiling: Soil profiling involves digging test pits or augering cores to directly inspect soil horizons.
choiceExplanations.Georesistivity measurement: Correct — Georesistivity (electrical resistivity) surveying injects electrical current into the ground to infer subsurface strata and aquifers non-invasively without soundwaves.

items.question: Apply hydraulics principles in an irrigation water flow over small dike. It resembles a flow over a __________.
items.rationale: Because a dike has a relatively wide flat top compared to the overflow head, water passes over it with critical flow established on the crest, resembling a broad-crested weir.
choices: Free-fall at the end of a spillway

choiceExplanations.Sharp-crested weir: A sharp-crested weir has a thin edge where the nappe springs clear, unlike a wide earthen dike top.
choiceExplanations.Ogee spillway: An ogee spillway has a curved S-shaped concrete profile matched to the lower nappe of a falling jet.
choiceExplanations.Broad-crested weir: Correct — A dike has a flat, wide crest over which flow lines become parallel near critical depth, behaving hydraulically like a broad-crested weir.
choiceExplanations.Free-fall at the end of a spillway: A free overfall drops abruptly from a channel end without the horizontal crest length of a dike.

items.question: You are to irrigate a 50 hectare lowland rice. What is the appropriate irrigation system?
items.rationale: Lowland rice is cultivated in bunded paddies requiring submerged or ponded soil conditions, making flooding irrigation the appropriate system.

choiceExplanations.Drip irrigation: Drip irrigation delivers water slowly to individual root zones and is impractical for ponded 50 ha lowland paddy rice.
choiceExplanations.Flooding irrigation: Correct — Basin/flooding irrigation maintains the shallow standing water layer required for lowland paddy rice cultivation across large areas.
choiceExplanations.Sprinkler Irrigation: Sprinkler irrigation suits upland crops and uneven terrain, not submerged lowland rice paddies over 50 hectares.
choiceExplanations.Mist irrigation: Mist irrigation supplies fine droplets for greenhouse propagation or cooling, not field-scale rice irrigation.

items.question: When water is limited to supply a rice growing area, what irrigation supply scheme is appropriate?
items.rationale: Rotational irrigation distributes limited water in scheduled turns among farm sections or turnouts, ensuring equitable allocation and minimizing conveyance losses.

choiceExplanations.Continuous: Continuous irrigation keeps water flowing to all fields simultaneously, requiring abundant supply and causing high losses when water is scarce.
choiceExplanations.Rotational: Correct — Rotational irrigation delivers water to different canal sections or farms in scheduled turns, ensuring equitable distribution under limited water supply.
choiceExplanations.As water need arises: Delivering water whenever requested is unscheduled and infeasible when total supply cannot meet simultaneous demand.
choiceExplanations.Irrigation on demand: Demand-based delivery requires surplus canal capacity and storage, making it unsuitable during water scarcity.

items.question: Find for the maximum rectangular area that 400 meters of fence can enclose.
items.rationale: With perimeter P = 2(L + W) = 400 m (so L + W = 200 m), maximum rectangular area occurs when the rectangle is a square with L = W = 100 m, giving A = 100 m × 100 m = 10,000 sq. m.

choiceExplanations.1000 sq. m: An area of 1,000 m² uses far less than the maximum area a 400 m perimeter can enclose.
choiceExplanations.5000 sq. m: An area of 5,000 m² corresponds to a narrow rectangle (e.g., 170.7 m × 29.3 m), not the maximum.
choiceExplanations.10000 sq. m: Correct — A rectangle maximizes area when it is a square: side s = 400 / 4 = 100 m, giving Area = 100² = 10,000 m².
choiceExplanations.50000 sq. m: Enclosing 50,000 m² requires at least 894 m of fencing, exceeding the 400 m available.

items.question: A greenhouse wall is 3 m², thickness 0.1 m, k = 1.5 W/m·K, inside temperature 35 °C, outside 25 °C. Heat loss per second?
items.rationale: By Fourier's law of conduction, Q = k·A·ΔT / Δx = (1.5 W/m·K)(3 m²)(35 °C − 25 °C) / 0.1 m = 450 W (J/s).

choiceExplanations.400 W: Four hundred watts underestimates the conductive heat transfer rate through the 3 m² wall.
choiceExplanations.450 W: Correct — By Fourier's law, Q = kAΔT / L = 1.5 × 3 × (35 − 25) / 0.1 = 450 W.
choiceExplanations.435 W: A value of 435 W does not follow from kAΔT / L with the given parameters.
choiceExplanations.520 W: Five hundred twenty watts overestimates the steady-state conduction loss across the 0.1 m wall.

items.question: If a pump delivers water to an elevation of 15 m, find the pressure head.
items.rationale: The pressure corresponding to 15 m of water head is P = ρ·g·h = (1000 kg/m³)(9.81 m/s²)(15 m) = 147,150 Pa = 147.15 kPa.

choiceExplanations.147.20 Pa: A pressure of 147.20 Pa is about 1,000 times too small, corresponding to only 1.5 cm of water.
choiceExplanations.147.15 kPa: Correct — Hydrostatic pressure is P = ρgh = 1,000 kg/m³ × 9.81 m/s² × 15 m = 147,150 Pa = 147.15 kPa.
choiceExplanations.145.28 kPa: A value of 145.28 kPa corresponds to about 14.81 m of head rather than 15 m.
choiceExplanations.145.57 Pa: A pressure of 145.57 Pa is roughly 1,000 times smaller than the hydrostatic pressure of 15 m of water.

items.question: Find the area bounded by the curve y = 9 - x², x = -2, x = 2, and the x-axis.
items.rationale: Integrating y = 9 - x² from x = -2 to x = 2 gives 2 × [9x - x³/3] from 0 to 2 = 2 × (18 - 8/3) = 2 × (46/3) = 92/3 square units.

choiceExplanations.92/4: Dividing 92 by 4 gives 23, which miscalculates the denominator of the integrated x³ term.
choiceExplanations.31/3: Integrating only from 0 to 2 gives 46/3, and 31/3 does not match the definite integral.
choiceExplanations.92/3: Correct — Integrating y = 9 − x² from x = −2 to 2 gives 2[9x − x³/3]₀² = 2(18 − 8/3) = 92/3.
choiceExplanations.31/4: A value of 31/4 neither integrates 9 − x² properly nor matches the symmetric interval [−2, 2].

items.question: Compare pumps you know. Which pump is best for pumping muddy water from a 20-square meter fish pond?
items.rationale: A reciprocating positive-displacement pump (such as a diaphragm mud pump) is self-priming and handles muddy or viscous water at low flow rates without losing prime, whereas standard centrifugal and clean-water submersible pumps lose prime or clog more readily.

choiceExplanations.Reciprocating pump: Correct — Positive-displacement reciprocating pumps (such as diaphragm or mud-handling piston pumps) maintain self-priming suction and move thick muddy water without losing prime.
choiceExplanations.Submersible pump: Standard clean-water submersible pumps quickly clog or suffer impeller abrasion when pumping heavy mud from pond bottoms.
choiceExplanations.Centrifugal pump: Standard centrifugal pumps lose prime easily and suffer rapid impeller wear and clogging in thick muddy water.
choiceExplanations.Centripetal pump: Centripetal pump is not a standard pump classification used for agricultural or aquaculture drainage.

items.question: In constructing a rockfill dam, the major components are filter zone, rockfill, and _________.
items.rationale: Per PAES 612:2016 (Rockfill Dam), the three major embankment components of a rockfill dam are the rockfill zone, filter zone, and impervious membrane to prevent seepage.

choiceExplanations.Gate: A gate is an appurtenant control valve on an outlet or spillway, not part of the dam embankment body.
choiceExplanations.Outlet: An outlet works conveys controlled releases through or around the dam rather than forming the dam embankment itself.
choiceExplanations.Spillway: A spillway is an appurtenant flood-discharge structure separate from the three basic embankment zones of a rockfill dam.
choiceExplanations.Impervious membrane: Correct — A rockfill dam embankment consists of a structural rockfill zone, transition filter zones, and an impervious membrane (core or facing) to block seepage.

items.question: If you invest Php 150,000 today at 10% annual interest for 7 years, what is the future worth?

choiceExplanations.Php 283,307.57: Php 283,307.57 underestimates the future value obtained from compounding Php 150,000 at 10% over 7 years.
choiceExplanations.Php 292,907.57: Php 292,907.57 exceeds the exact compound future value by Php 600.
choiceExplanations.Php 292,307.57: Correct — Compounding Php 150,000 at 10% for 7 years gives F = 150,000 × (1.10)^7 = Php 292,307.57.
choiceExplanations.Php 299,307.57: Php 299,307.57 overstates the compounded future worth at 10% annual interest for 7 years.

items.question: In carrying out georesistivity measurements for underground profiling, what field data are needed to be gathered?
items.rationale: Georesistivity surveying injects known electric current (amperage, I) through outer current electrodes and measures the resulting potential difference (voltage, V) across inner potential electrodes to compute apparent subsurface resistivity.

choiceExplanations.Amperage and resistance: Resistance is calculated from measured voltage and current rather than recorded directly as primary field data.
choiceExplanations.Voltage and amperage: Correct — Georesistivity field surveys inject a known current (amperage) via outer electrodes and measure the resulting potential drop (voltage) across inner electrodes.
choiceExplanations.Voltage and conductance: Conductance is a derived reciprocal of resistance and is not directly read in standard resistivity field instruments.
choiceExplanations.Resistance and voltage: Resistance is derived by Ohm's law (V/I) from voltage and amperage, not gathered alongside voltage directly.

items.question: A trapezoidal concrete open channel has a wetted cross-sectional area of 50 sq. meters. Determine the hydraulic radius of the channel.
items.rationale: Assuming the most efficient trapezoidal section (A = 1.732 d²), depth d = √(50 / 1.732) = 5.37 m (≈ 5.4 m), and hydraulic radius R = d / 2 = 5.37 / 2 ≈ 2.7 m.

choiceExplanations.6.2 m: A hydraulic radius of 6.2 m implies a wetted perimeter of only 8.1 m, geometrically impossible for 50 m².
choiceExplanations.2.7 m: Correct — For a most efficient (half-hexagon) trapezoidal section, A = √3 d² = 50 m² gives d ≈ 5.37 m and hydraulic radius R = d/2 ≈ 2.7 m.
choiceExplanations.7.2 m: A hydraulic radius of 7.2 m would require a wetted perimeter smaller than any rectangle or trapezoid of 50 m² area.
choiceExplanations.14.6 m: A hydraulic radius of 14.6 m corresponds to a wetted perimeter of 3.4 m, which cannot enclose 50 m².

items.question: In an 8-inch standard raingage, the funnel is __ times bigger in area than the inner cylinder.
items.rationale: An 8-inch standard rain gauge uses a 10:1 cross-sectional area ratio between the collector funnel and the inner measuring cylinder, magnifying rainfall depth tenfold for precise measurement.

choiceExplanations.5: A 5:1 area ratio is half the standard amplification used in 8-inch rain gauges.
choiceExplanations.2: A 2:1 ratio provides insufficient magnification to read light rainfall depths accurately on the measuring stick.
choiceExplanations.10: Correct — In a standard 8-inch rain gauge, the receiver funnel has 10 times the area of the inner measuring tube to magnify rainfall depth tenfold.
choiceExplanations.1: A 1:1 area ratio gives no depth magnification, making small rainfall measurements imprecise.

items.question: Apply the principles of hydraulics in weirs. What weir is likely to have a higher coefficient of discharge?
items.rationale: In standard ABELE hydraulics references, a sharp-crested triangular (V-notch) weir avoids crest friction losses of flat- or broad-crested weirs and side-wall end-contraction effects of contracted rectangular weirs, giving a higher and more consistent discharge coefficient.

choiceExplanations.Triangular weir: Correct — In board review hydraulics references, a triangular (V-notch) weir exhibits less end-contraction interference at low flows and is keyed as having the higher discharge coefficient.
choiceExplanations.Broad-crested weir: Broad-crested weirs have higher friction losses across their long flat crest, resulting in lower discharge coefficients.
choiceExplanations.Rectangular weir: Rectangular weirs experience side contraction losses along the vertical edges unless fully suppressed.
choiceExplanations.Flat-crested weir: Flat-crested (broad-crested) weirs suffer greater head loss over the wide crest surface, lowering discharge efficiency.
