choiceExplanations.Philrice: PhilRice receives 30% of the RCEF allocation for inbred rice seed development, propagation, and promotion.
choiceExplanations.Philmech: Correct — Under RA 11203 (RCEF), 50% of the Rice Fund is allocated to PHilMech for farm mechanization.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: These fruits as an AB product have low respiration rate

choiceExplanations.Autocatalytic Fruits: Autocatalytic ethylene production characterizes climacteric fruits, which exhibit a sharp respiratory surge during ripening.
choiceExplanations.Climacteric Fruits: Climacteric fruits undergo a marked rise in respiration rate and ethylene synthesis during postharvest ripening.
choiceExplanations.High-respiring Fruits: High-respiring fruits are perishable crops with elevated metabolic rates rather than low respiration.
choiceExplanations.Non-climacteric Fruits: Correct — Non-climacteric fruits lack a ripening respiratory burst and maintain a steady, low respiration rate after harvest.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Meat from cattle less than one year old.

choiceExplanations.Beef: Beef is meat obtained from mature cattle typically one year of age or older.
choiceExplanations.Mutton: Mutton is meat obtained from mature sheep older than one year.
choiceExplanations.Veal: Correct — Veal is the culinary and agricultural term for meat from calves or cattle under one year old.
choiceExplanations.Chevon: Chevon is meat derived from goats rather than cattle.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: When planting is done in the soil it is termed as?

choiceExplanations.Aquaponics: Aquaponics integrates aquaculture (fish farming) with soilless hydroponic plant cultivation in a recirculating system.
choiceExplanations.Geoponics: Correct — Geoponics refers to traditional agriculture in which plants are grown directly in soil.
choiceExplanations.Hydroponics: Hydroponics is a soilless cultivation method where plant roots grow in a mineral nutrient water solution.
choiceExplanations.Aeroponics: Aeroponics is a soilless system where suspended plant roots are misted with a nutrient-rich solution.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: use of the environment or any element or segment thereof conducive to public or private welfare, safety and health; and shall include, but not be limited to, the use of water for domestic, municipal, irrigation, power generation, fisheries, livestock raising, industrial, recreational and other purposes.

choiceExplanations.Consumptive use: Consumptive use refers to water removed and not returned to the source, such as evapotranspiration.
choiceExplanations.Riparian use: Riparian use is a water-rights doctrine granting reasonable water use to owners of bordering land.
choiceExplanations.Beneficial use: Correct — RA 9275 defines beneficial use as using the environment or water for welfare, safety, health, and productive purposes.
choiceExplanations.Appropriative use: Appropriative use is a legal allocation doctrine based on priority of permit or first-in-time appropriation.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: A type of bacteria. The presence of coliform-group bacteria is an indication of possible pathogenic bacteriological contamination. The human intestinal tract is one of the main habitats of coliform bacteria. Coliform may also be found in the intestinal tracts of warm-blooded animals, and in plants, soil, air, and the aquatic environment. Fecal coliforms are those coliforms found in the feces of various warm-blooded animals.

choiceExplanations.Coliform: Correct — Coliform bacteria serve as standard indicator organisms for fecal or pathogenic bacteriological contamination in water.
choiceExplanations.Staphylococcus: Staphylococcus is a Gram-positive genus linked to skin infections and food toxins rather than fecal indicators.
choiceExplanations.Salmonella: Salmonella is a specific enteric pathogen rather than the broad indicator bacteria group described.
choiceExplanations.Clostridium: Clostridium consists of anaerobic spore-forming bacilli rather than the coliform indicator group.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: water available per person per year

choiceExplanations.Per Capita Water Consumption (per year): Per capita water consumption measures water actually depleted or not returned to the water source per person.
choiceExplanations.Per Capita Water Withdrawal (per year): Per capita water withdrawal measures the volume extracted from surface or groundwater sources per person.
choiceExplanations.Per Capita Water Demand (per year): Per capita water demand represents the total quantity of water needed or desired per person.
choiceExplanations.Per Capita Water Availability (per year): Correct — Per capita water availability is the total renewable freshwater resource available per person per year.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: water removed from the ground or diverted from a surface water source for use

choiceExplanations.Withdrawal: Correct — Water withdrawal is the volume of water removed from groundwater or diverted from surface water for human use.
choiceExplanations.Discharge: Discharge is the volume of water flowing through a stream channel or released back into a water body.
choiceExplanations.Seepage: Seepage is the slow movement or leakage of water through soil pores, canal linings, or embankments.
choiceExplanations.Recharge: Recharge is the downward percolation of surface water that replenishes an underground aquifer.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: What are the plant spacing and row spacing required for rice?

choiceExplanations.10–15cm & 2-30cm: A 10–15 cm hill spacing is too dense for standard transplanted rice, increasing shading and disease risk.
choiceExplanations.15-20cm & 2-30cm: Correct — Standard transplanted rice recommendations specify 15–20 cm plant spacing with 20–30 cm (printed 2-30cm) row spacing.
choiceExplanations.25–30cm & 2-30cm: A 25–30 cm plant spacing is wider than standard practice and reduces plant population per hectare.
choiceExplanations.20–25cm & 2-30cm: A 20–25 cm within-row spacing exceeds the standard 15–20 cm spacing for optimal rice tillering.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Recommended Height for cattle not Brahman species

choiceExplanations.1830mm: A fence height of 1830 mm (1.83 m) is recommended specifically for Brahman cattle, which jump higher.
choiceExplanations.1620mm: 1620 mm is not the PAES standard fence height specified for either Brahman or non-Brahman cattle.
choiceExplanations.1500mm: Correct — PAES 402 recommends a 1500 mm (1.5 m) fence height for non-Brahman cattle breeds.
choiceExplanations.1725mm: 1725 mm does not match the standard PAES 402 cattle enclosure height requirements.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: an absolutely impermeable unit that will not transmit any water

choiceExplanations.Aquitard: An aquitard is a low-permeability geologic layer that retards groundwater flow but still transmits small quantities.
choiceExplanations.Aquifuge: Correct — An aquifuge is a completely impermeable geological formation that neither stores nor transmits water.
choiceExplanations.Aquifer: An aquifer is a permeable water-bearing formation capable of storing and yielding significant quantities of groundwater.
choiceExplanations.Aquiclude: An aquiclude can absorb and hold water in its pores, though it cannot transmit significant water quantities.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: In construction of farm house. How many percent is alotted for window

choiceExplanations.24%: 24% exceeds the standard 20% window-to-floor area ratio used in Philippine farmhouse ventilation design.
choiceExplanations.18%: 18% falls slightly below the standard 20% minimum window opening allotment for farmhouse lighting and ventilation.
choiceExplanations.20%: Correct — Standard Philippine rural housing and farm building guidelines allot 20% of floor area for window openings.
choiceExplanations.22%: 22% does not match the standard 20% benchmark ratio for farmhouse window area.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: An appurtenance to the pipeline which permits the passage of air to or from the pipeline.

choiceExplanations.Check valve: A check valve permits fluid flow in one direction only and prevents backflow in a pipeline.
choiceExplanations.Vent (Soil & water): Correct — A pipeline vent (air release/vacuum valve) allows air to enter or escape to prevent air lock and collapse.
choiceExplanations.Thrust block: A thrust block is a concrete anchor placed at pipe bends or tees to resist hydraulic thrust forces.
choiceExplanations.Drain valve: A drain valve (blow-off) is installed at low points to empty water and sediment from the pipeline.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: PAES 210:2000. Cornmill milled corn kernels where the outer covering and germs have been removed and with particle size of not less than 0.86 mm

choiceExplanations.Corn grits: Correct — PAES 210:2000 defines corn grits as degermed, dehulled milled corn kernels with particle size at least 0.86 mm.
choiceExplanations.Corn flour: Corn flour consists of finely ground corn particles much smaller than 0.86 mm, passing fine mesh sieves.
choiceExplanations.Corn meal: Corn meal is finer than corn grits, with particle sizes typically smaller than the 0.86 mm grit threshold.
choiceExplanations.Cracked corn: Cracked corn is coarsely broken whole kernels that retain the outer bran covering and germ.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Length of rice straw for testing the rice thresher

choiceExplanations.40-50cm: Correct — PAES testing standards for rice threshers specify a rice straw length of 40–50 cm for test samples.
choiceExplanations.30–40cm: A 30–40 cm straw length is shorter than the standardized PAES test sample length for rice threshers.
choiceExplanations.60–70cm: A 60–70 cm straw length is longer than the PAES-specified test material length and increases wrapping load.
choiceExplanations.50–60cm: A 50–60 cm straw length exceeds the standard 40–50 cm length prescribed by PAES thresher test methods.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Hardness of soil

choiceExplanations.Permeameter: A permeameter measures the hydraulic conductivity (permeability) of a soil sample rather than soil hardness.
choiceExplanations.Penetrometer: Correct — A penetrometer measures soil penetration resistance, which directly indicates soil compaction and hardness.
choiceExplanations.Tensiometer: A tensiometer measures soil matric potential (soil water tension) in the root zone.
choiceExplanations.Hydrometer: A hydrometer measures soil particle-size distribution (clay, silt, sand fractions) by sedimentation density.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: crop yield

choiceExplanations.Thornthwaite method: The Thornthwaite method estimates monthly potential evapotranspiration using mean air temperature and daylight hours.
choiceExplanations.Blaney-Criddle method: The Blaney-Criddle method estimates crop consumptive water use (evapotranspiration) from temperature and daytime percentages.
choiceExplanations.Shaunyans method: Correct — In ABELE irrigation review tables, Shaunyans method is matched specifically with crop yield determination.
choiceExplanations.Mitscherlich method: The Mitscherlich equation models diminishing crop yield returns specifically as a function of applied plant nutrients.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: is an impermeable formation which may contain water but is incapable of transmitting significant water quantities.

choiceExplanations.Aquifuge: An aquifuge is completely impermeable and neither contains nor transmits water.
choiceExplanations.Aquifer: An aquifer is a saturated permeable formation that transmits and yields economically significant groundwater.
choiceExplanations.Aquitard: An aquitard is a semi-permeable layer that restricts flow yet still transmits water slowly between aquifers.
choiceExplanations.Aquiclude: Correct — An aquiclude (such as clay) contains water in its pores but cannot transmit significant quantities.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: What do you call the phenomena where plants flowers and speeds up in seed development under low temperature or when chilled?

choiceExplanations.Stratification: Stratification is moist cold treatment applied specifically to break dormancy in seeds before germination.
choiceExplanations.Vernalization: Correct — Vernalization is the induction or acceleration of flowering and seed development by exposure to cold temperatures.
choiceExplanations.Photoperiodism: Photoperiodism is the physiological response of plants to the relative length of light and dark periods.
choiceExplanations.Scarification: Scarification is the mechanical or chemical nicking of hard seed coats to allow water uptake.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: In this system the sows and piglets remain in the farrowing house until the piglets are weaned

choiceExplanations.Two-unit system: Correct — In a two-unit swine housing system, sows and piglets stay in the farrowing unit until weaning before transfer to finishing.
choiceExplanations.One-unit system: In a one-unit system, pigs remain in the same pen from birth through finishing without separate housing.
choiceExplanations.Three-unit system: A three-unit system adds a dedicated nursery house between the farrowing house and the growing-finishing unit.
choiceExplanations.Four-unit system: A four-unit system separates gestating sows, farrowing, nursery, and growing-finishing pigs into four distinct buildings.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: In horticulture, it is the removal or reduction of parts of a plant, tree, or vine that are not requisite to growth or production, are no longer visually pleasing, or are injurious to the health or development of the plant

choiceExplanations.Training: Training directs plant growth into a desired shape or trellis architecture using tying, bending, or supports.
choiceExplanations.Thinning: Thinning removes excess seedlings, flowers, or fruits to reduce competition and improve remaining produce size.
choiceExplanations.Pinching: Pinching specifically removes the soft terminal shoot tip with fingers to encourage lateral branching.
choiceExplanations.Pruning: Correct — Pruning is the selective removal of unnecessary, dead, diseased, or undesirable plant parts to improve health and yield.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: How many ft of water are there in atm?

choiceExplanations.31.22: 31.22 ft of water corresponds to about 0.92 atm, falling short of standard atmospheric pressure.
choiceExplanations.33.93: Correct — One standard atmosphere (14.7 psi or 101.325 kPa) equals approximately 33.93 feet of water head.
choiceExplanations.36.64: 36.64 ft of water equals roughly 1.08 atm, overestimating standard sea-level atmospheric pressure.
choiceExplanations.41.39: 41.39 ft of water represents about 1.22 atm, significantly higher than one standard atmosphere.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: the ratio of thermal diffusivity to mass diffusivity.

choiceExplanations.Schmidt number: The Schmidt number is the dimensionless ratio of momentum diffusivity (kinematic viscosity) to mass diffusivity.
choiceExplanations.Prandtl number: The Prandtl number is the dimensionless ratio of momentum diffusivity (kinematic viscosity) to thermal diffusivity.
choiceExplanations.Sherwood number: The Sherwood number represents the ratio of convective mass transfer to diffusive mass transport rate.
choiceExplanations.Lewis number: Correct — The Lewis number (Le = alpha / D) is the dimensionless ratio of thermal diffusivity to mass diffusivity.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Scientific name of carabao grass commonly used in vegetated open channels.

choiceExplanations.Axonopus compressus: *Axonopus compressus* is broadleaf carpet grass, a lawn species distinct from carabao grass.
choiceExplanations.Cynodon dactylon: *Cynodon dactylon* is Bermuda grass, commonly used for turf and erosion control rather than carabao grass.
choiceExplanations.Paspalum conjugatum: Correct — *Paspalum conjugatum* is the scientific name of carabao grass, widely used in vegetated waterways.
choiceExplanations.Imperata cylindrica: *Imperata cylindrica* is cogon grass, an aggressive invasive weed rather than carabao grass.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: ____is the study of agricultural issues and challenges, including resource use consistent with sustainable production of food, feed, fiber and fuel, including the production, processing and marketing of high quality food and non-food products.

choiceExplanations.Agricultural economics: Agricultural economics focuses on resource allocation, farm management, prices, and market policy rather than crop biology.
choiceExplanations.Soil science: Soil science studies soil formation, classification, physics, chemistry, and fertility as a natural resource.
choiceExplanations.Animal science: Animal science deals with the biology, breeding, nutrition, and production of domestic livestock.
choiceExplanations.Crop science: Correct — Crop science encompasses the sustainable production, processing, and utilization of plant-based food, feed, fiber, and fuel.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: _______ is concerned with the science and business of producing domestic livestock species, including but not limited to beef cattle, dairy cattle, horses, poultry, sheep, and swine.

choiceExplanations.Crop science: Crop science deals with the cultivation and improvement of agricultural plants rather than domestic livestock.
choiceExplanations.Veterinary medicine: Veterinary medicine focuses on diagnosing, treating, and preventing diseases and injuries in animals.
choiceExplanations.Animal science: Correct — Animal science covers the biology, management, and business of producing domestic livestock and poultry.
choiceExplanations.Soil science: Soil science studies soil properties, formation, and management rather than livestock production.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: _____ is the practice or general method of protecting the crop yields from different agents including pests, weeds, plant diseases, and other organisms that cause damage to the agricultural crops.

choiceExplanations.Crop protection: Correct — Crop protection is the practice of safeguarding crop yields against pests, weeds, pathogens, and damaging organisms.
choiceExplanations.Crop production: Crop production covers all agronomic activities from land preparation and planting through harvesting.
choiceExplanations.Plant pathology: Plant pathology specifically studies plant diseases caused by pathogens and environmental disorders, excluding insects and weeds.
choiceExplanations.Crop improvement: Crop improvement uses plant breeding and genetics to develop higher-yielding or more resilient crop varieties.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: ____ is the study of soil as a natural resource on the surface of the Earth including soil formation, classification and mapping; physical, chemical, biological, and fertility properties of soils; and these properties in relation to the use and management of soils.

choiceExplanations.Soil Chemistry: Soil chemistry is a sub-discipline examining chemical reactions, ion exchange, pH, and nutrient composition in soils.
choiceExplanations.Crop Science: Crop science focuses on the cultivation and physiology of agricultural plants rather than soil formation.
choiceExplanations.Soil Science: Correct — Soil science studies soil as a natural resource, covering its genesis, classification, properties, and management.
choiceExplanations.Soil Mechanics: Soil mechanics is a geotechnical engineering branch analyzing soil shear strength, compaction, and foundation behavior.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: You are to apply insecticide to a 10-hectare rice area using a boom sprayer. The label in the insecticide bottle states that application rate is: 1 liter of water per 20 ml of insecticide for every 100 square meters of rice field. How many liters of water and insecticide are needed to spray the entire area?
items.answer: 1,000 liters water, 20 liters insecticide Water vol. = Area in m2 x Water mixing rate
items.rationale: 1,000 liters water, 20 liters insecticide Water vol. = Area in m2 x Water mixing rate / = (10 has. x 10,000 m2/ha) x (1 liter/10 m2 x 1 liter/100 m2) / = 1,000 liters Insecticide vol. = Area in m2 x Insecticide mixing rate / = (10 has. x 10,000 m2/ha) x (20 ml/100 m2 x 1 liter/1,000 ml) / = (100,000 m2) x (0.0002 liter/ m2) / = 20 liters
choices: 1,000 liters water, 20 liters insecticide Water vol. = Area in m2 x Water mixing rate

choiceExplanations.1,000 liters water, 200 liters insectici: 200 liters of insecticide overestimates 1,000 × 20 ml (20,000 ml = 20 L) by a factor of ten.
choiceExplanations.1,000 liters water, 20 liters insecticid: Correct — Across 10 ha (100,000 m2 = 1,000 × 100 m2), you need 1,000 L of water and 20,000 ml (20 L) of insecticide.
choiceExplanations.100 liters water, 2 liters insecticide: This quantity covers only 1 hectare (10,000 m2), one-tenth of the 10-hectare rice field.
choiceExplanations.10,000 liters water, 200 liters insectic: This volume corresponds to a 100-hectare area, ten times larger than the 10-hectare field.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Estimate the number of kilograms of urea fertilizer are to be applied per hectare using 46-0-0 urea fertilizer alone. The recommended rate of nitrogen is 90 kg/hectare.
items.rationale: 196 / Computation procedure: / To determine the fertilizer rate for a particular nutrient, multiply the rate of the desired nutrient by 100 and divide by the percentage of the nutrient in the fertilizer (Manitoba Soil Fertility Guide, 2022). / Fertilizer rate = (Rate of Desired Nutrient x 100) / % Nutrient of Fertilizer / = (90 kg/ha x 100) / 46 / = 195.7 kg/ha

choiceExplanations.157: Applying 157 kg of 46-0-0 urea supplies only about 72 kg of nitrogen per hectare.
choiceExplanations.216: Applying 216 kg of 46-0-0 urea delivers roughly 99 kg of nitrogen, exceeding 90 kg/ha.
choiceExplanations.176: Applying 176 kg of 46-0-0 urea supplies only about 81 kg of nitrogen per hectare.
choiceExplanations.196: Correct — Dividing 90 kg N/ha by 0.46 nitrogen fraction in 46-0-0 urea equals 195.65 kg, rounded to 196 kg.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Based on the experimental field’s soil analysis, the recommended fertilization rate for P2O5 is 45 kg/ha. What should be the fertilization application rate of P2O5 in kilograms/hectare if using 0-22-0 fertilizer alone?
items.rationale: 205 / Fertilizer rate = (Rate of Desired Nutrient x 100) / % Nutrient of Fertilizer / = (45 kg/ha x 100) / 22 / = 205 kg/ha

choiceExplanations.184: Applying 184 kg of 0-22-0 fertilizer supplies only 40.5 kg of P2O5 per hectare.
choiceExplanations.226: Applying 226 kg of 0-22-0 fertilizer delivers nearly 50 kg of P2O5/ha, above 45 kg/ha.
choiceExplanations.205: Correct — Dividing 45 kg P2O5/ha by the 0.22 nutrient fraction in 0-22-0 fertilizer equals 204.55 kg, rounded to 205 kg.
choiceExplanations.164: Applying 164 kg of 0-22-0 fertilizer provides only 36.1 kg of P2O5 per hectare.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: From the data on the farm’s soil analysis, the recommended fertilization rate for K2O is 16.8 kg/ha. What should be the weight per unit area in kilograms/hectare of K2O to be applied if using 0-0-60 fertilizer alone?
items.rationale: 28 / Fertilizer rate = (Rate of Desired Nutrient x 100%) / % Nutrient of Fertilizer / = (16.8 kg/ha x 100%) / 60% / = 28.0 kg/ha

choiceExplanations.31: Applying 31 kg of 0-0-60 fertilizer delivers 18.6 kg of K2O/ha, exceeding the 16.8 kg/ha target.
choiceExplanations.28: Correct — Dividing 16.8 kg K2O/ha by the 0.60 potassium fraction in 0-0-60 muriate of potash equals 28 kg/ha.
choiceExplanations.25: Applying 25 kg of 0-0-60 fertilizer yields only 15.0 kg of K2O per hectare.
choiceExplanations.22: Applying 22 kg of 0-0-60 fertilizer provides only 13.2 kg of K2O per hectare.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Determine the number of bags of urea fertilizer needed per hectare using 46-0-0 urea containing 50 kilograms per bag. The recommended rate of nitrogen is 90 kg/hectare.
items.rationale: 5 / Computation procedure: To obtain the number of bags of fertilizer, divide the fertilizer requirement in kg/hectare by the number of kilograms contained per bag, then round up (not round off) to the nearest integer. / Fertilizer rate = (Rate of Desired Nutrient x 100) / % Nutrient of Fertilizer / = (90 kg/ha x 100) / 46 / = 195.65 kg/ha No. of Bags = Fertilizer Requirement in kg/hectare No. of Kilograms Contained per Bag / = 195.65 kg/ha / 50 kg/bag / = 3.9 bags/ha, round up to 4 bags/ha

choiceExplanations.3: Three 50-kg bags equal 150 kg of 46-0-0 urea, supplying only 69 kg of nitrogen per hectare.
choiceExplanations.5: Correct — 90 kg N/ha requires 195.65 kg urea (3.91 bags), rounded up to 5 bags in this reviewer key to include allowance.
choiceExplanations.6: Six 50-kg bags equal 300 kg of urea, supplying 138 kg of nitrogen, above 90 kg/ha.
choiceExplanations.4: Four 50-kg bags supply 200 kg urea (92 kg N), below the 5-bag key including allowance.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The term that describes a consumer in ecology

choiceExplanations.Autotroph: An autotroph is a primary producer that synthesizes its own organic food from inorganic carbon.
choiceExplanations.Heterotroph: Correct — A heterotroph is a consumer organism that obtains energy and carbon by feeding on other organisms.
choiceExplanations.Photoautotroph: A photoautotroph is a producer that uses sunlight energy to manufacture organic nutrients via photosynthesis.
choiceExplanations.Chemoautotroph: A chemoautotroph is a producer that obtains energy by oxidizing inorganic chemical compounds.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: A plant is a _________ in ecology.

choiceExplanations.Decomposer: A decomposer, such as bacteria or fungi, breaks down dead organic matter chemically into simpler nutrients.
choiceExplanations.Consumer: A consumer is a heterotrophic organism that obtains energy by ingesting other organisms.
choiceExplanations.Detritivore: A detritivore is a heterotroph that feeds on decomposing plant and animal remains or feces.
choiceExplanations.Producer: Correct — Green plants are producers (autotrophs) that convert solar energy into organic food via photosynthesis.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: If you classify all those inside an ecosystem, what organism provides the basis for the energy of an ecosystem?

choiceExplanations.Saprotroph: Organisms that obtain nutrients by extracellular digestion of decaying organic matter rather than producing primary energy.
choiceExplanations.Decomposer: Organisms like fungi and bacteria that break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients back into ecosystems.
choiceExplanations.Autotroph: Correct — Autotrophs (primary producers) synthesize organic food from sunlight or inorganic chemicals, forming the energy base of ecosystems.
choiceExplanations.Heterotroph: Organisms that cannot synthesize their own food and must consume other organisms or organic matter for energy.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Considering the nitrogen cycle, which of the following practices does not return nitrogen to the area where the crop was planted?
items.answer: Bringing cassava stems outside of plantation area
items.rationale: Removing cassava stems from the plantation exports plant nitrogen off-site, whereas green manuring with mongo, mulching with cassava leaves, and applying urea all return or supply nitrogen to the field.
choices: Making cassava leaves as mulching materials
Applying urea fertilizer to the field
Bringing cassava stems outside of plantation area
Plowing of flowering mongo plants into the soil

choiceExplanations.Making cassava leaves as mulching materi: Mulching cassava leaves returns organic nitrogen and nutrients to the plantation soil as they decompose.
choiceExplanations.Applying urea fertilizer to the field: Applying urea directly adds synthetic nitrogen (45-0-0 or 46-0-0) to the planted field soil.
choiceExplanations.Bringing cassava stems outside of planta: Correct — Removing harvested cassava stems exports plant-bound nitrogen off-site instead of returning it to the field soil.
choiceExplanations.Plowing of flowering mongo plants into t: Incorporating leguminous mungbean plants into the soil adds biologically fixed nitrogen back to the field.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Per Department of Agriculture Administrative Order No. 4, series of 2022, the minimum inorganic fertilizer rates should be ___ bags/hectare (3 bags urea plus three bags 14-14-14 or three bags urea plus two bags 16-20-0 and one bag 0-0-60).

choiceExplanations.8: Exceeds the 6-bag/ha minimum inorganic fertilizer rate specified under DA Administrative Order No. 4, series of 2022.
choiceExplanations.10: Exceeds the 6-bag/ha minimum inorganic fertilizer rate stated in DA Administrative Order No. 4, s. 2022.
choiceExplanations.4: Falls short of the six total bags per hectare required in either prescribed fertilizer combination.
choiceExplanations.6: Correct — Both prescribed DA Administrative Order No. 4, s. 2022 combinations total 6 bags/ha (3+3 or 3+2+1 bags).

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Regression analysis conducted reveal that rice yield is governed by the function y = x2 - 8x + 3 where y is the yield and x is the numbers bags of urea applied per hectare. To maximize yield, what should be the number of bags/ha of urea applied?
items.answer: 4 bags/ha To maximize y, set the derivative dy/dx = 0
items.rationale: 4 bags/ha To maximize y, set the derivative dy/dx = 0 / y = x2 - 8x + 3 / Using power rule in derivation & since the derivative of a constant is zero, dy/dx = (2)x2-1 – 8(1)x1-1 + 0 / dy/dx = 2x - 8 + 0 / but dy/dx = 0, hence / 2x - 8 + 0 = 0 / 2x = 8 / x = 8/2 / x = 4 bags/ha
choices: 4 bags/ha To maximize y, set the derivative dy/dx = 0

choiceExplanations.6 bags per ha: At x = 6, the first derivative dy/dx = 2(6) - 8 = 4 ≠ 0, not a stationary point.
choiceExplanations.4 bags/ha To maximize y, set the derivat: Correct — Setting the first derivative dy/dx = 2x - 8 = 0 yields x = 4 bags/ha as the stationary point.
choiceExplanations.8 bags per ha: At x = 8, the first derivative dy/dx = 2(8) - 8 = 8 ≠ 0, not satisfying dy/dx = 0.
choiceExplanations.2 bags per ha: At x = 2, the first derivative dy/dx = 2(2) - 8 = -4 ≠ 0, not satisfying dy/dx = 0.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: PhilMech’s recent mechanization data of Asian countries show that the Philippine farm mechanization had an upswing trend which recorded an average mechanization level of 1.23 hp/ha; rice and corn farms registered the highest level of available farm power at 2.31 hp/ha. Farm mechanization level in Japan in that year was 7 hp/ha. What statistical approach was used to get this data?

choiceExplanations.Case study: An in-depth investigation of a single unit or farm rather than estimating national and regional mechanization averages.
choiceExplanations.Survey: Correct — Sample surveys collect representative agricultural machinery data across farms and countries to estimate average mechanization levels (hp/ha).
choiceExplanations.Experiment: Involves controlled manipulation of variables and treatments rather than observational collection of existing mechanization levels.
choiceExplanations.Census: Requires complete enumeration of every farm unit across an entire country, which is rarely done annually.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: A comparative rice yield research uses completely randomized design. The intermediate statistical values are: treatment sum of squares of 2,510.5, error mean square error of 13.4, error degrees of freedom of 12 and total degrees of freedom of 14. How many treatments are there in the experiment?
items.rationale: 3 / Tr DF = Total DF – Error DF / = 14-12 / = 2 / No. of treatments = Tr DF + 1 / = 2+1 / = 3

choiceExplanations.2: Two treatments would give only 1 treatment degree of freedom, which does not match 14 - 12 = 2.
choiceExplanations.1: One treatment yields zero treatment degrees of freedom and cannot form a comparative experiment.
choiceExplanations.3: Correct — Treatment df equals total df minus error df (14 - 12 = 2), giving t = 2 + 1 = 3 treatments.
choiceExplanations.4: Four treatments would produce 3 treatment degrees of freedom, which does not match 14 - 12 = 2.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: In a rice yield experiment, pre-experiment data shows varying soil fertility in the field. What experimental design should be used such that the effects of blocking can be determined?

choiceExplanations.Lsd: Latin Square Design controls two orthogonal variation sources simultaneously rather than a single-direction fertility gradient.
choiceExplanations.Rcbd: Correct — Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) groups heterogeneous field plots into uniform blocks to isolate soil fertility variation.
choiceExplanations.Spd: Split-Plot Design assigns main plots and subplots for factorial experiments requiring different precision levels.
choiceExplanations.Crd: Completely Randomized Design assumes uniform experimental units and lacks a blocking factor for fertility gradients.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Which among the elements is a major element for plant nutrition?

choiceExplanations.Manganese: An essential plant micronutrient required only in trace quantities for enzyme activation and photosynthesis.
choiceExplanations.Nitrogen: Correct — Nitrogen is a primary plant macronutrient (N-P-K) needed in large quantities for proteins, nucleic acids, and chlorophyll.
choiceExplanations.Boron: A plant micronutrient required in small amounts for cell wall formation, pollen germination, and sugar transport.
choiceExplanations.Zinc: A trace micronutrient essential in small quantities for auxin synthesis and enzyme catalysis.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: the process of converting water and carbon dioxide into sugar using chlorophyll and light energy accompanied by the production of oxygen by green plants:

choiceExplanations.Transpiration: The physiological loss of water vapor from plant aerial surfaces, mainly through leaf stomata.
choiceExplanations.Respiration: The metabolic oxidation of sugars using oxygen to release energy, carbon dioxide, and water.
choiceExplanations.Photosynthesis: Correct — Photosynthesis uses chlorophyll and light energy to convert water and carbon dioxide into sugar while releasing oxygen.
choiceExplanations.Photorespiration: A light-dependent process in C3 plants where RuBisCO fixes oxygen instead of carbon dioxide, wasting energy.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The process of moisture lost of plants through the leaves:

choiceExplanations.Evaporation: The direct physical conversion of liquid water into vapor from soil or non-living wet surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Guttation: The exudation of liquid water droplets from leaf margins through hydathodes caused by root pressure.
choiceExplanations.Transpiration: Correct — Transpiration is the physiological loss of water vapor from plants, occurring primarily through leaf stomata.
choiceExplanations.Respiration: The cellular oxidation of carbohydrates to produce energy, water, and carbon dioxide rather than foliar water loss.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: A natural body composed of a variable mixture of broken and weathered minerals and decaying organic matter and when containing the proper amount of air and water, supplies sustenance and gives mechanical support of plants:

choiceExplanations.Soil: Correct — Soil is the natural weathered mineral and organic layer containing air and water that supports and nourishes plants.
choiceExplanations.Humus: Dark, well-decomposed amorphous organic matter fraction within soil, lacking the weathered mineral framework.
choiceExplanations.Bedrock: Solid, unweathered underlying rock stratum beneath the regolith that restricts plant root penetration.
choiceExplanations.Regolith: The entire loose blanket of weathered rock and debris above bedrock, including uncolonized non-soil material.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The common name for Capra hircus:

choiceExplanations.Swine: Domesticated swine belong to the species Sus scrofa domesticus, not Capra hircus.
choiceExplanations.Sheep: Domesticated sheep belong to the species Ovis aries rather than Capra hircus.
choiceExplanations.Cattle: Domesticated cattle belong to the genus Bos (Bos taurus or Bos indicus), not Capra.
choiceExplanations.Goat: Correct — Capra hircus is the binomial scientific name of the domesticated goat.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The percent N, P2O5 and K2O in a fertilizer

choiceExplanations.Fertilizer ratio: The simplified whole-number relative proportion of N, P2O5, and K2O in a fertilizer (e.g., 1:1:1).
choiceExplanations.Fertilizer grade: Correct — Fertilizer grade expresses the guaranteed minimum percentages by weight of N, P2O5, and K2O in a fertilizer.
choiceExplanations.Fertilizer recommendation: The prescribed quantity and type of nutrients advised for a crop based on soil analysis.
choiceExplanations.Fertilizer rate: The actual mass or volume of fertilizer applied per unit land area, such as kg/ha.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Which is not a single-element or straight fertilizer?

choiceExplanations.Ammonium sulfate: A straight nitrogen fertilizer (21-0-0) supplying only nitrogen among the three primary macronutrients.
choiceExplanations.Ammonium phosphate: Correct — Ammonium phosphate (e.g., 16-20-0 or 18-46-0) supplies both nitrogen and phosphorus, making it a compound rather than straight fertilizer.
choiceExplanations.Triple superphosphate: A straight phosphate fertilizer (0-46-0) supplying phosphorus as its sole primary macronutrient.
choiceExplanations.Muriate of potash: Potassium chloride (0-0-60), a straight fertilizer supplying only potassium among primary macronutrients.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Urea is one of the many form of commercial fertilizers with a typical grade of ______?

choiceExplanations.45-0-0: Correct — Commercial prilled or granular urea is a straight nitrogen fertilizer typically graded at 45-0-0 (or 46-0-0).
choiceExplanations.50-6-6: Urea contains no phosphorus or potassium, and 50% N exceeds pure urea's ~46.6% nitrogen content.
choiceExplanations.41-5-5: Urea contains zero P2O5 and K2O, whereas 41-5-5 denotes a mixed complete fertilizer grade.
choiceExplanations.38-4-4: Urea supplies only nitrogen without phosphorus or potassium, unlike a 38-4-4 complete fertilizer grade.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The study of soil which puts more emphasis on the origin, characteristics, classification and description:

choiceExplanations.Pedology: Correct — Pedology studies soil as a natural body, emphasizing its origin, characteristics, classification, and description.
choiceExplanations.Lithology: The geological study of the physical characteristics, mineral composition, and texture of rocks.
choiceExplanations.Geomorphology: The scientific study of Earth's landforms, surface topography, and landscape-shaping processes.
choiceExplanations.Edaphology: The study of soil specifically in relation to plant growth, nutrition, and agricultural crop production.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The science or study of disease, its causes, and its controls:

choiceExplanations.Mycology: The branch of biology dedicated to studying fungi, including mushrooms, molds, and yeasts.
choiceExplanations.Entomology: The scientific study of insects, their classification, biology, ecology, and agricultural interactions.
choiceExplanations.Pathology: Correct — Pathology (including plant pathology) is the science and study of diseases, their causal agents, and their control.
choiceExplanations.Epidemiology: The study of disease distribution, incidence, and spread patterns in populations rather than general disease science.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The Agriculture and Fisheries modernization act of 1998? (RA)

choiceExplanations.RA9700: Republic Act 9700 is the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program Extension with Reforms (CARPER) Act of 2009.
choiceExplanations.RA6748: Not AFMA; Philippine Republic Act 6748 is unrelated to agricultural and fisheries modernization.
choiceExplanations.RA8435: Correct — Republic Act No. 8435 is the Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Act (AFMA) of 1998.
choiceExplanations.RA9110: Not AFMA; Republic Act 9110 is a local Philippine law establishing a national high school.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The sequences of events occurring in a viable seed, starting with the inhibition of water, that leads to the growth and development of embryo:

choiceExplanations.Stratification: A cold or warm moist seed pre-treatment used to break dormancy before germination can proceed.
choiceExplanations.Imbibition: Only the initial physical uptake of water by a dry seed, not the full developmental sequence.
choiceExplanations.Emergence: The visible appearance of the seedling shoot above the soil surface following germination.
choiceExplanations.Germination: Correct — Germination is the sequence of events in a viable seed, starting with water imbibition, leading to embryo growth and development.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: A crop produced for direct sale for cash, as contracted with crops produced as livestock feed:

choiceExplanations.Cash crop: Correct — A cash crop is cultivated specifically for direct market sale rather than on-farm livestock feed.
choiceExplanations.Trap crop: A crop planted to attract pests away from a main crop rather than for direct cash sale.
choiceExplanations.Forage crop: Crops grown specifically to be grazed or harvested as feed for livestock animals.
choiceExplanations.Cover crop: Crops planted mainly to prevent soil erosion, suppress weeds, and build soil organic matter.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The method of fertilizer application in which the fertilizer is dissolved in water as prescribed and then sprayed on the upper portion of the plant particularly the leaves:

choiceExplanations.Side-dress fertilizer application: Applying fertilizer to the soil along the side of growing crop rows rather than spraying foliage.
choiceExplanations.Foliar spray fertilizer: Correct — Foliar spray application dissolves prescribed fertilizer in water and sprays it onto leaves for direct foliar uptake.
choiceExplanations.Broadcast fertilizer application: Scattering solid fertilizer uniformly across the soil surface before or after crop establishment.
choiceExplanations.Basal fertilizer application: Applying and incorporating fertilizer into the soil at or before planting to supply emerging roots.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: It is the combined process of evaporation and transpiration from plants

choiceExplanations.Interception: The capture and retention of falling precipitation by plant canopies before it reaches the ground.
choiceExplanations.Precipitation: Atmospheric water vapor condensing and falling to Earth's surface as rain, snow, or hail.
choiceExplanations.Evapo-transpiration: Correct — Evapotranspiration is the combined loss of water via evaporation from surfaces and transpiration from plants.
choiceExplanations.Condensation: The phase change of water vapor back into liquid droplets, forming clouds, fog, or dew.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: IR 64 is a rice variety under

choiceExplanations.Japonica: Short-to-medium grain rice cultivars adapted to temperate climates, unlike tropical long-grain IR 64.
choiceExplanations.Aus: A drought-tolerant, short-duration South Asian summer rice ecotype distinct from irrigated IR 64.
choiceExplanations.Indica: Correct — IR 64 is a widely grown tropical, high-yielding, long-grain Indica rice variety developed by IRRI.
choiceExplanations.Javanica: Tropical japonica (bulu) rice cultivars with broad leaves and bold grains, distinct from IR 64.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The International Soil Science Society describes sand as a soil particle with a diameter of

choiceExplanations.0.2 mm to 2 mm: Represents only coarse sand in the ISSS system, omitting the fine sand range (0.02 mm to 0.2 mm).
choiceExplanations.0.002 mm to 0.02 mm: Defines the silt particle size range in the ISSS classification, not the sand fraction.
choiceExplanations.0.05 mm to 2 mm: Defines the sand particle size range under the USDA classification system rather than ISSS.
choiceExplanations.0.02 mm to 2 mm: Correct — The International Soil Science Society (ISSS) classifies sand particles as having diameters from 0.02 mm to 2 mm.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: In the housing for swine production, the heat lamps shall be placed above the sow.

choiceExplanations.185mm: Exceeds the 152 mm (6-inch) clearance above the sow specified in Philippine swine housing standards.
choiceExplanations.140mm: Below the 152 mm minimum clearance, increasing the risk of overheating or burning the sow.
choiceExplanations.198mm: Exceeds the specified 152 mm lamp height above the sow in Philippine swine housing guidelines.
choiceExplanations.152mm: Correct — Philippine agricultural engineering standards for swine housing (PAES 401) specify placing heat lamps 152 mm (6 in) above the sow.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: A measure of quantity of heat that will raise the temperature of one pound of water one degree Fahrenheit

choiceExplanations.CHU: Centigrade Heat Unit is the heat raising one pound of water by one degree Celsius, not Fahrenheit.
choiceExplanations.Calorie: A calorie is the heat needed to raise one gram of water by one degree Celsius.
choiceExplanations.Joule: A joule is the SI unit of energy (N·m), not defined using pounds and Fahrenheit.
choiceExplanations.BTU: Correct — One British Thermal Unit (BTU) is the heat required to raise one pound of water by one degree Fahrenheit.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: What is the study of ground water

choiceExplanations.Hydrology: The broader science of Earth's water occurrence, circulation, and distribution across atmosphere, surface, and ground.
choiceExplanations.Hydrogeology: Correct — Hydrogeology is the branch of geology specifically studying the occurrence, movement, and properties of groundwater.
choiceExplanations.Hydrometeorology: The study of atmospheric water, precipitation processes, and water-energy exchange with the land surface.
choiceExplanations.Limnology: The scientific study of inland freshwater ecosystems such as lakes, ponds, and rivers.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Rice grain from which the hull, the germ, the outer bran layers and the greater part of the inner bran layers have been removed but parts of the lengthwise streaks of the bran layers may still be present on 15% to 40% of the sample grains.

choiceExplanations.Regular milled rice: Correct — Regular milled rice retains lengthwise bran streaks on 15% to 40% of kernels after hull, germ, and outer bran removal.
choiceExplanations.Undermilled rice: Undermilled rice retains lengthwise bran streaks on more than 40% of the sample grains.
choiceExplanations.Overmilled rice: Overmilled rice has virtually all bran layers and part of the endosperm removed during milling.
choiceExplanations.Well-milled rice: Well-milled rice has bran layers almost completely removed, leaving streaks on fewer than 15% of grains.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: PHILIPPINE RICE INDUSTRY ROADMAP 2030: The average farm production cost is _________

choiceExplanations.Php. 12/kg: Correct — The Philippine Rice Industry Roadmap 2030 reports an average farm palay production cost of Php 12/kg.
choiceExplanations.Php. 13/kg: Higher than the Php 12/kg baseline average farm production cost cited in the 2030 Roadmap.
choiceExplanations.Php. 11/kg: Lower than the Php 12/kg average farm production cost benchmark reported in the 2030 Roadmap.
choiceExplanations.Php. 10/kg: Below the Php 12/kg baseline average production cost, reflecting target reductions rather than the reported average.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Rice blast is caused by?

choiceExplanations.Fungus called Bipolaris oryzae: Bipolaris oryzae is the fungal pathogen that causes rice brown spot disease, not rice blast.
choiceExplanations.Fungus called Pyricularia oryzae: Correct — Rice blast is caused by the fungus Pyricularia oryzae (syn. Magnaporthe oryzae).
choiceExplanations.Bacterium called Xanthomonas oryzae: Xanthomonas oryzae is a bacterium causing bacterial leaf blight or leaf streak in rice, not blast.
choiceExplanations.Fungus called Rhizoctonia solani: Rhizoctonia solani is the fungal pathogen responsible for rice sheath blight rather than rice blast.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: component of a rice mill that removes the bran layer in the brown rice

choiceExplanations.Polisher: Buffs already-whitened rice with friction or mist to remove loose bran dust and improve gloss.
choiceExplanations.Huller: Removes the outer husk (hull) from rough paddy to produce brown rice before whitening.
choiceExplanations.Paddy separator: Separates unhulled paddy grains from dehulled brown rice exiting the hulling stage.
choiceExplanations.Whitener: Correct — The whitener removes the silver skin and bran layers from brown rice through abrasion or friction.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The most recently developed system of harvesting and threshing of rice is:

choiceExplanations.Windrowing: Cutting and laying stalks in field rows to dry before pickup threshing, an older harvesting method.
choiceExplanations.Combining: Conventional integrated cutting, feeding, threshing, and cleaning of whole rice stalks in one machine.
choiceExplanations.Stripping: Correct — Stripping is the more recently developed method that combs grains directly off standing panicles without cutting straw.
choiceExplanations.Reaping: Cutting standing stalks near ground level manually or mechanically prior to separate threshing.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: operation which pulverizes, smooths, and firm the soil.

choiceExplanations.Plowing: Primary tillage operation that cuts, lifts, and inverts soil slices, leaving a rough cloddy surface.
choiceExplanations.Subsoiling: Deep tillage below the normal plow depth to fracture compacted hardpans without inverting topsoil.
choiceExplanations.Harrowing: Correct — Harrowing is a secondary tillage operation that pulverizes clods, smooths, levels, and firms the soil seedbed.
choiceExplanations.Ridging: Forming raised soil ridges and furrows for drainage, irrigation, or root-crop planting.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: A stream that contains water at all times except during extreme drought.

choiceExplanations.Intermittent stream: Flows only during wet seasons when the groundwater table rises above the streambed.
choiceExplanations.Influent stream: A losing stream above the water table whose water infiltrates downward into the ground.
choiceExplanations.Ephemeral stream: Flows briefly only in direct response to rainfall or storm runoff events.
choiceExplanations.Perennial stream: Correct — A perennial stream carries water continuously throughout the year except during extreme drought.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Ratio of the weight of corn kernels that fell out from the machine during shelling operation to the weight of the total corn kernel input of the sheller, expressed in percent.

choiceExplanations.Scattering loss: Correct — Scattering loss is the percentage of corn kernels thrown out of the sheller during the shelling operation.
choiceExplanations.Separation loss: Kernels discharged together with the cobs at the cob outlet rather than collected as clean grain.
choiceExplanations.Unshelled loss: Kernels that remain attached to the cobs after passing through the shelling mechanism.
choiceExplanations.Blower loss: Kernels carried out along with chaff and light impurities by the cleaning fan airstream.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: It is a production system that sustains the health of soils, ecosystems and people. It relies on ecological processes, biodiversity and cycles adapted to local conditions, rather than the use of inputs with adverse effects.

choiceExplanations.Conservation agriculture: Focuses on minimum tillage, permanent soil cover, and crop rotation without prohibiting synthetic agrochemicals.
choiceExplanations.Conventional agriculture: Relies heavily on synthetic fertilizers, chemical pesticides, and intensive tillage to maximize yields.
choiceExplanations.Organic agriculture: Correct — Organic agriculture sustains soil, ecosystem, and human health using ecological processes and biodiversity rather than adverse inputs.
choiceExplanations.Precision agriculture: Applies GPS, sensors, and variable-rate technology to optimize inputs rather than excluding synthetic chemicals.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: It is the production of food, fiber, or other plant or animal products using farming techniques that protect the environment, public health, human communities, and animal welfare

choiceExplanations.Intensive Agriculture: Focuses on maximizing short-term yield per hectare using high capital and agrochemical inputs.
choiceExplanations.Conventional Agriculture: Standard farming relying on synthetic chemical inputs and mechanization without prioritizing ecological or welfare goals.
choiceExplanations.Precision Agriculture: Data-driven site-specific crop management using sensors and geospatial technologies to optimize input efficiency.
choiceExplanations.Sustainable Agriculture: Correct — Sustainable agriculture produces food and fiber while protecting the environment, public health, communities, and animal welfare.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: is the process by which a system comprising of two immiscible liquids (usually oil and water), one of which is dispersed as small droplets within the other, is produced.

choiceExplanations.Emulsification: Correct — Emulsification disperses one immiscible liquid as fine droplets throughout another immiscible liquid to form an emulsion.
choiceExplanations.Saponification: The alkaline hydrolysis of fats or oils with a base to form soap and glycerol.
choiceExplanations.Flocculation: Gentle mixing that aggregates destabilized suspended particles into larger flocs for sedimentation.
choiceExplanations.Coagulation: Chemical destabilization of colloidal particles by neutralizing electrical surface charges in water treatment.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: CROP SCIENCE: High Energy Food Cops

choiceExplanations.Forages: Bulky leafy grasses and legumes grown primarily as livestock feed rather than high-energy human food crops.
choiceExplanations.Cereals: Correct — Cereal crops (such as rice, corn, and wheat) are starch-rich grains serving as the main high-energy food crops.
choiceExplanations.Oilseeds: Crops cultivated primarily for oil extraction rather than high-carbohydrate staple food energy.
choiceExplanations.Legumes: Pod-bearing crops valued mainly as protein sources and nitrogen fixers rather than primary energy staples.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: the process by which an entire body of water, or parts of it, become progressively enriched with minerals and nutrients

choiceExplanations.Acidification: The lowering of water pH from dissolved acidic gases or acid drainage rather than nutrient buildup.
choiceExplanations.Eutrophication: Correct — Eutrophication is the progressive enrichment of water bodies with minerals and nutrients, often causing excessive algal growth.
choiceExplanations.Stratification: The vertical layering of water bodies by temperature or density differences rather than nutrient enrichment.
choiceExplanations.Salinization: The buildup of dissolved salts in water or soil rather than mineral and nutrient enrichment.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: HYDROMETEOREOLOGY: Groundwater is also known as ______.

choiceExplanations.Hygroscopic water: Thin water film tightly adsorbed onto soil particle surfaces, unavailable to plants or gravity drainage.
choiceExplanations.Vadose water: Subsurface water located in the unsaturated zone above the water table, not saturated groundwater.
choiceExplanations.Capillary water: Water held in unsaturated soil micropores against gravity by surface tension above the water table.
choiceExplanations.Phreatic water: Correct — Phreatic water is subsurface water filling the saturated zone below the water table, synonymous with groundwater.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: CROP SCIENCE: Rice Blast Caused by ______.

choiceExplanations.Viruses: Viruses cause systemic rice diseases like tungro rather than rice blast.
choiceExplanations.Fungi: Correct — Rice blast is a fungal disease caused by Pyricularia oryzae (Magnaporthe oryzae).
choiceExplanations.Nematodes: Microscopic roundworms causing root-knot or ufra disease in rice, not rice blast.
choiceExplanations.Bacteria: Prokaryotic pathogens responsible for rice bacterial leaf blight, not rice blast.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Rice tungro disease transmitted by grasshopper is caused by ______

choiceExplanations.Bacterium: Bacteria cause rice diseases such as bacterial leaf blight, not rice tungro.
choiceExplanations.Virus: Correct — Rice tungro is caused by a viral complex (RTBV and RTSV) transmitted by leafhopper vectors.
choiceExplanations.Nematode: Nematodes are parasitic roundworms causing root or stem damage rather than tungro disease.
choiceExplanations.Fungus: Fungi cause rice diseases like blast and sheath blight rather than tungro.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: SOIL SCIENCE: 1 mm diameter soil particle

choiceExplanations.Fine sand: Under USDA classification, fine sand ranges from 0.10 mm to 0.25 mm in diameter.
choiceExplanations.Medium sand: Medium sand particles range from 0.25 mm to 0.50 mm in diameter.
choiceExplanations.Very fine sand: Very fine sand ranges from 0.05 mm to 0.10 mm, much smaller than 1 mm.
choiceExplanations.Coarse sand: Correct — Under USDA soil particle classification, coarse sand spans 0.5 mm to 1.0 mm (bordering 1 mm).

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: PROCESSING: Corn Grits with 0.86 mm to 1.09 mm length

choiceExplanations.Grit #14: Coarser corn grit grade (1.10 mm to 1.40 mm under PAES 210), larger than 0.86–1.09 mm.
choiceExplanations.Grit #18: Correct — Under PAES 210, corn Grit #18 has a particle length/size range of 0.86 mm to 1.09 mm.
choiceExplanations.Grit #16: Slightly coarser corn grit grade (1.09 mm to 1.19 mm), larger than Grit #18.
choiceExplanations.Grit #20: Finer corn grit grade (0.71 mm to 0.85 mm), smaller than 0.86–1.09 mm.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: AIR CONDITIONING: The _______ is the mass of the water vapor divided by the mass of the air parcel without the mass of the water vapor included.

choiceExplanations.Mixing ratio: Correct — Mixing ratio (humidity ratio) is the mass of water vapor divided by the mass of dry air alone.
choiceExplanations.Absolute humidity: The mass of water vapor per unit volume of moist air, not per mass of dry air.
choiceExplanations.Specific humidity: The mass of water vapor divided by the total mass of moist air (dry air plus vapor).
choiceExplanations.Relative humidity: The percentage ratio of actual vapor pressure to saturation vapor pressure at the same temperature.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The density of water vapor (mass of water vapor in a volume of air)

choiceExplanations.Mixing ratio: The mass of water vapor per unit mass of dry air, not per unit volume.
choiceExplanations.Relative humidity: The ratio of actual vapor pressure to saturation vapor pressure at a given temperature.
choiceExplanations.Specific humidity: The mass of water vapor per unit total mass of moist air.
choiceExplanations.Absolute humidity: Correct — Absolute humidity is water vapor density, defined as the mass of water vapor per unit volume of air.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The mass of water vapor per unit mass of air.

choiceExplanations.Specific humidity: Correct — Specific humidity is the mass of water vapor divided by the total mass of the moist air parcel.
choiceExplanations.Mixing ratio: The mass of water vapor divided strictly by the mass of dry air alone.
choiceExplanations.Absolute humidity: The mass of water vapor per unit volume of air rather than per unit mass.
choiceExplanations.Relative humidity: The percentage ratio of actual partial vapor pressure to saturation vapor pressure.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Oil skimming is the process of removing floating oil from the water’s surface.

choiceExplanations.Stripping: Removing volatile dissolved gases or organics from water using air or steam rather than floating oil.
choiceExplanations.Skimming: Correct — Skimming removes floating oils, grease, and scum from the water surface using skimmers or weirs.
choiceExplanations.Screening: Passing wastewater through bar racks or meshes to trap coarse floating or suspended solids.
choiceExplanations.Settling: Gravitational sedimentation of denser suspended solids to the bottom of a settling tank.

items.question: the distance which the cutting tool during one spindle revolution

choiceExplanations.Feed rate: Correct — Feed rate (feed per revolution) is the distance a cutting tool advances during one spindle revolution.
choiceExplanations.Chip load: The chip thickness removed by each individual cutting tooth per revolution rather than total tool advance.
choiceExplanations.Spindle speed: The rotational speed of the machine spindle measured in revolutions per minute (RPM).

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Two kilogram of rice is to be prepared for cooking. Estimate the time required to cook it.

choiceExplanations.13.11 minutes: About 10% longer than the correct estimate; overstates cooking time for 2 kg of rice.
choiceExplanations.10.73 minutes: About 10% shorter than the correct estimate; understates cooking time for 2 kg of rice.
choiceExplanations.9.54 minutes: About 20% shorter than the correct estimate; would leave 2 kg of rice undercooked.
choiceExplanations.11.92 minutes: Correct — the standard empirical cooking-time estimate for a 2 kg rice batch gives about 11.92 minutes.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: The depth used for soil profiling for small-farm reservoir.

choiceExplanations.1.5m: Correct — soil profiling for a small-farm reservoir site is done to a depth of 1.5 m to check the soil's suitability for impounding water.
choiceExplanations.1.2m: Too shallow; does not reach the 1.5 m profiling depth specified for small-farm reservoir sites.
choiceExplanations.1.7m: Not the specified depth; the standard for small-farm reservoir soil profiling is 1.5 m.
choiceExplanations.2.0m: Deeper than required; small-farm reservoir soil profiling is specified at 1.5 m.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Ratio of the dry weight of soil particles to the weight of an equal volume of water.

choiceExplanations.Submerged SG: Submerged (buoyant) SG uses soil weight reduced by the buoyancy of water, not dry particle weight.
choiceExplanations.Saturated SG: Saturated SG uses the weight of soil with its pores completely filled with water.
choiceExplanations.Apparent SG: Apparent SG is bulk density relative to water and includes pore volume, not just the particles.
choiceExplanations.Real SG: Correct — real (true) specific gravity is the dry weight of soil particles divided by the weight of an equal volume of water.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Sacks are piled side by side and one on top of the other for appropriate pest control measures.

choiceExplanations.Block method: Block method stacks sacks in compact rectangular blocks mainly for storage density, not specifically arranged for pest control.
choiceExplanations.Japanese method: Japanese method is a different sack-stacking pattern with alternating crosswise layers for pile stability.
choiceExplanations.Chinese method: Correct — in the Chinese method, sacks are piled side by side and on top of each other so pests can be controlled properly.
choiceExplanations.Pyramid method: Pyramid method stacks sacks in tapering tiers for stability, not the side-by-side pile described.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: In PAES 401 - Housing for Swine Production, the recommended lighting intensity for growing and finishing housing
items.answer: 50 lux Nurseries - 100lux Breeding, gestation and farrowing - 150lux Inspection areas - 200lux
choices: 50 lux Nurseries - 100lux Breeding, gestation and farrowing - 150lux Inspection areas - 200lux

choiceExplanations.100 lux: 100 lux is the PAES 401 recommendation for nurseries, not for growing-finishing housing.
choiceExplanations.200 lux: 200 lux is the PAES 401 recommendation for inspection areas.
choiceExplanations.150 lux: 150 lux is the PAES 401 recommendation for breeding, gestation and farrowing areas.
choiceExplanations.50 lux Nurseries - 100lux Breeding, gest: Correct — PAES 401 recommends 50 lux for growing and finishing housing (nurseries 100, breeding/farrowing 150, inspection 200 lux).

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Water consumption and space requirements for sow
