choices: 5 to 8 gal per day Pigs 0.5 to 1.5 gal per day Fattening hogs 1.5 to 3 gal per day Boars 2 to 4 gal per day

choiceExplanations.0.5 to 1.5 gal per day: 0.5–1.5 gal/day is the water requirement for young pigs, not sows.
choiceExplanations.1.5 to 3 gal per day: 1.5–3 gal/day is the water requirement for fattening hogs.
choiceExplanations.5 to 8 gal per day Pigs 0.5 to 1.5 gal p: Correct — a sow needs about 5–8 gal of water per day, more than other swine classes because of gestation and lactation.
choiceExplanations.2 to 4 gal per day: 2–4 gal/day is the water requirement for boars.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: How many times greater is the power of a carabao over man?

choiceExplanations.9 times: Underestimates; a carabao (about 1 hp) is commonly rated about ten times a man (about 0.1 hp).
choiceExplanations.10 times: Correct — a man produces about 0.1 hp of sustained work while a carabao produces about 1 hp, so about 10 times more.
choiceExplanations.11 times: Overestimates the usual farm-power ratio of about 10:1 between carabao and man.
choiceExplanations.8 times: Underestimates the usual farm-power ratio of about 10:1 between carabao and man.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Period of heat and greatest receptivity to male, rapture of ovarian follicles in most farm animals

choiceExplanations.Metestrus: Metestrus follows estrus; the corpus luteum forms and the female no longer accepts the male.
choiceExplanations.Estrus: Correct — estrus is the heat period when the female is most receptive to the male and ovulation (follicle rupture) occurs.
choiceExplanations.Proestrus: Proestrus comes before estrus; follicles grow under FSH, but the female is not yet receptive.
choiceExplanations.Diestrus: Diestrus is the luteal phase dominated by progesterone, with no sexual receptivity.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Zone planning can be a useful tool, but it is most effective when planning a new farmstead. The farmstead is divided into different zones of 10 to 30 meters wide by concentric circles. The livestock building area is placed under

choiceExplanations.Zone 3: Zone 3 is nearer the residence and holds service areas such as machinery and storage, not livestock buildings.
choiceExplanations.Zone 4: Correct — in farmstead zone planning, livestock buildings go in Zone 4, away from the residence, to reduce odor, noise and disease risk.
choiceExplanations.Zone 2: Zone 2 is close to the residence and is used for gardens, lawns and light activity areas.
choiceExplanations.Zone 5: Zone 5 is the outermost zone, used for manure handling, expansion and other areas needing isolation.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Which organisms primarily carry out decomposition, aiding nutrient recycling back to the ecosystem?
items.rationale: Fungi and bacteria are the primary decomposers (saprotrophs) that break down dead organic matter and mineralize nutrients back into the ecosystem.

choiceExplanations.Fungi and bacteria: Correct — fungi and bacteria are the main decomposers, breaking down organic matter and returning nutrients to the soil.
choiceExplanations.Amphibians and reptiles: Amphibians and reptiles are consumers or predators, not primary decomposers.
choiceExplanations.Autotrophs and herbivores: Autotrophs are producers and herbivores are primary consumers; neither mainly decomposes organic matter.
choiceExplanations.Birds and insects: Birds and insects are mostly consumers or pollinators; only some insects help break down material.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: It is the growth stage of the rice plant that starts when the panicle emerges from the flagleaf sheath and ends when it completely protrudes from the sheath.
items.rationale: Per the Philippine Rice Production Training Manual, heading begins when the panicle starts emerging from the flagleaf sheath and ends once it fully protrudes.

choiceExplanations.Heading: Correct — heading is the stage from the panicle's first emergence out of the flag-leaf sheath until it fully protrudes.
choiceExplanations.Flowering: Flowering (anthesis) is when spikelets open and pollination occurs, usually right after heading.
choiceExplanations.Tillering: Tillering is the vegetative stage when side shoots develop from the main culm.
choiceExplanations.Panicle initiation: Panicle initiation is when the panicle primordium starts forming inside the stem, well before it emerges.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: This term refers to a young female cattle between two to three years of age which has not given birth.
items.rationale: A heifer is a young female cattle that has not yet given birth (calved), whereas a calf is a young bovine of either sex, a ewe is a female sheep, and a doe is a female goat.

choiceExplanations.Heifer: Correct — a heifer is a young female cow that has not yet calved.
choiceExplanations.Doe: A doe is a female goat, rabbit or deer, not cattle.
choiceExplanations.Calf: A calf is a young bovine of either sex, usually under one year old.
choiceExplanations.Ewe: A ewe is a mature female sheep.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: A rice mill flywheel (I = 12 kg·m²) spins at 300 rpm. Find the kinetic energy stored.
items.rationale: Angular velocity ω = 2π(300) / 60 = 10π ≈ 31.416 rad/s; stored kinetic energy KE = 0.5 × I × ω² = 0.5 × 12 × (31.416)² = 5,921.8 J ≈ 5.9 kJ.

choiceExplanations.7.6 kJ: Too high; KE = ½(12)(31.42 rad/s)² ≈ 5.9 kJ.
choiceExplanations.4.7 kJ: Too low; check the rpm-to-rad/s conversion (300 rpm = 31.42 rad/s).
choiceExplanations.8.5 kJ: Too high; does not match ½Iω² with I = 12 kg·m² and ω = 31.42 rad/s.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Rice blast is one of the destructive diseases of rice, causing as much as 50% crop loss in areas where severe outbreaks occur. Rice blast is caused by _____.
items.rationale: Rice blast is a fungal disease caused by Magnaporthe oryzae (Pyricularia oryzae), responsible for severe yield losses during outbreaks.

choiceExplanations.Fungus: Correct — rice blast is caused by the fungus Magnaporthe oryzae (Pyricularia oryzae).
choiceExplanations.Bacteria: Bacteria cause other rice diseases, such as bacterial leaf blight (Xanthomonas oryzae), not blast.
choiceExplanations.Virus: Viruses cause diseases such as tungro and grassy stunt, not blast.
choiceExplanations.Insects: Insects are pests or disease vectors, not the causal agent of rice blast.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: Rice tungro disease is caused by ______.
items.rationale: Rice tungro disease is caused by a combination of two viruses—Rice tungro bacilliform virus (RTBV) and Rice tungro spherical virus (RTSV)—transmitted by green leafhoppers.

choiceExplanations.Viruses: Correct — tungro is caused by two viruses together (RTBV and RTSV), spread by the green leafhopper.
choiceExplanations.Fungus: Fungi cause diseases such as blast and sheath blight, not tungro.
choiceExplanations.Pollution: Pollution is an abiotic stress, not the cause of the infectious tungro disease.
choiceExplanations.Bacteria: Bacteria cause bacterial leaf blight and leaf streak, not tungro.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: You purchased 12.0 MT of commercial feed for your aquaculture farm. Laboratory analysis shows that the batch has a moisture content (wet basis) of 12%. Compute the dry weight and the dry basis moisture content of the commercial fish feed delivered to your farm.
items.rationale: Total mass = 12,000 kg; water weight = 0.12 × 12,000 = 1,440 kg, so dry weight = 12,000 - 1,440 = 10,560 kg. Dry-basis moisture content = (1,440 / 10,560) × 100% = 13.64% ≈ 13.6%.

choiceExplanations.10560 kg and 10.7%: Dry weight is right, but dry-basis MC = 1,440/10,560 = 13.6%, not 10.7%.
choiceExplanations.1,440 kg and 16.3%: 1,440 kg is the water weight, not the dry weight, and 16.3% is the wrong dry-basis MC.
choiceExplanations.1,440 kg and 13.6%: 1,440 kg is the water content (12% of 12,000 kg), not the dry weight.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: A rice mill costs Php 600,000, has an estimated salvage value of Php 60,000, and has a useful life of 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
items.rationale: Using the straight-line depreciation formula D = (C - S) / n, D = (Php 600,000 - Php 60,000) / 8 = Php 540,000 / 8 = Php 67,500 per year.

choiceExplanations.Php 60,500 per year: Wrong; does not match (P − S)/n for these values.
choiceExplanations.Php 67,500 per year: Correct — straight-line depreciation = (600,000 − 60,000)/8 = Php 67,500 per year.
choiceExplanations.Php 55,500 per year: Wrong; understates the depreciable amount of Php 540,000 spread over 8 years.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: A rice thresher drum (I = 5 kg·m²) accelerates from rest to 600 rpm in 5 s. Find the torque required.
items.rationale: Final angular velocity is ω = 2π(600) / 60 = 62.83 rad/s, giving angular acceleration α = 62.83 / 5 = 12.57 rad/s²; the required torque is T = Iα = 5 × 12.57 = 62.85 N-m.

choiceExplanations.62.85 N-m: Correct — α = (62.83 rad/s)/5 s = 12.57 rad/s², so T = Iα = 5×12.57 ≈ 62.8 N·m.
choiceExplanations.60.00 N-m: Too low; uses a rounded value instead of the exact 600 rpm = 62.83 rad/s.
choiceExplanations.57.43 N-m: Too low; does not match T = I·Δω/Δt.
choiceExplanations.45.21 N-m: Too low; does not match T = 5×12.57 N·m.

items.subtopic: 2.5 Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences
items.question: It is the study of the relationships between living organisms, including humans, and their physical environment.
items.rationale: Ecology is the branch of biology concerned with the relationships and interactions between living organisms, including humans, and their physical environment.

choiceExplanations.Sociology: Sociology studies human society, social relationships and institutions.
choiceExplanations.Anthology: An anthology is a collection of literary works, not a science.
choiceExplanations.Ecology: Correct — ecology is the study of how organisms, including humans, interact with their physical environment.
choiceExplanations.Anthropology: Anthropology studies human origins, cultures and biological development.

items.question: slope of the upstream face of the embankment
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 1

choiceExplanations.Outside slope: Outside slope is the downstream (dry-side) face of the embankment.
choiceExplanations.Side slope: Side slope is a general term for any embankment face slope, not specifically the upstream face.
choiceExplanations.Crest slope: Crest refers to the top of the embankment, not a face slope.
choiceExplanations.Inside slope: Correct — the inside slope is the upstream face of the embankment, in contact with the stored water.

items.question: allowable pollutant-loading limit per unit of time, which the wastewater generator is permitted to discharge into any receiving body of water or land.
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Assimilative capacity: Assimilative capacity is how much pollutant a water body can absorb without violating water-quality standards.
choiceExplanations.Ambient standard: Ambient standard sets the water-quality levels required in the receiving water body itself.
choiceExplanations.Loading limit: Correct — loading limit is the allowable pollutant load per unit time that a wastewater generator may discharge.
choiceExplanations.Effluent standard: Effluent standard limits pollutant concentration in the discharge, not the load per unit time.

items.question: slope at the downstream face of the embankment
items.source: Area 2 IRRIGATION STRUCTURES; Tambong Subject B Part 2

choiceExplanations.Inside slope: Inside slope is the upstream face of the embankment, against the impounded water.
choiceExplanations.Outside slope: Correct — the outside slope is the downstream face of the embankment.
choiceExplanations.Crest slope: Crest is the top width of the embankment, not a face slope.
choiceExplanations.Side slope: Side slope is a general term for embankment face inclination, not specifically downstream.

items.question: The angle between the idler rolls and the horizontal in conveyor.

choiceExplanations.Wrap Angle: Wrap angle is the arc of contact between the belt and a pulley.
choiceExplanations.Surcharge Angle: Surcharge angle is the slope of the material's surface while being carried on a moving belt.
choiceExplanations.Repose Angle: Repose angle is the natural slope of bulk material when piled at rest.
Correct — troughing angle is the angle of the inclined side idler rolls from the horizontal.

items.question: Is a non-probability sampling technique where subjects are selected because of their convenient accessibility and proximity to the researcher.

choiceExplanations.Purposive sampling: Purposive sampling picks subjects based on the researcher's judgment of specific traits they need.
choiceExplanations.Quota sampling: Quota sampling picks non-randomly until set quotas for each subgroup are filled.
choiceExplanations.Snowball sampling: Snowball sampling recruits subjects through referrals from earlier participants.
choiceExplanations.Convenience sampling: Correct — convenience sampling picks subjects simply because they are easy to reach and close to the researcher.

items.question: Two cubic meters per hour of water are cooled from 30°C to 4°C. What is the rate of heat transfer in kilowatts?
items.answer: Calculate m Calculate Heat Transfer Rate Q
choices: Calculate m Calculate Heat Transfer Rate Q

choiceExplanations.Calculate m Calculate Heat Transfer Rate: Correct — the method is to find mass flow ṁ = 2000/3600 = 0.556 kg/s, then Q = ṁcpΔT = 0.556×4.187×26 ≈ 60.5 kW.
choiceExplanations.54.22 kW: Does not match ṁcpΔT; the correct value is about 60.5 kW.

items.question: Two infinite black planes at 800°C and 300°C exchange heat by radiation. The heat transfer rate per unit area (kW/m2) is
items.rationale: formula constant / =69,049 w/m2 or 6.9kw/m2

choiceExplanations.58.2 kW/m2: Does not match σ(T1⁴ − T2⁴) with absolute temperatures 1073 K and 573 K (about 69 kW/m²).
choiceExplanations.formula constant: Correct — use q = σ(T1⁴ − T2⁴) with σ = 5.67×10⁻⁸ W/m²·K⁴ and Kelvin temperatures, giving about 69 kW/m².

items.question: The ratio of convection heat transfer to fluid conduction heat transfer under the same conditions
items.source: RECALLED COMPRESS PART 2; area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled; recalled 2018

choiceExplanations.Nusselt number: Correct — Nusselt number (hL/k) is the ratio of convective to conductive heat transfer in the fluid.
choiceExplanations.Biot number: Biot number compares internal conduction resistance of a solid with surface convection resistance.
choiceExplanations.Prandtl number: Prandtl number is the ratio of momentum diffusivity to thermal diffusivity.
choiceExplanations.Grashof number: Grashof number is the ratio of buoyancy forces to viscous forces in natural convection.

items.question: The ratio between the buoyancy force due to spatial variation I fluid density (cause by temperature differences) to the retraining force due to the viscosity of fluid

choiceExplanations.Grashof number: Correct — Grashof number is the ratio of buoyancy forces (from temperature-driven density differences) to viscous forces.
choiceExplanations.Reynolds number: Reynolds number is the ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces.
choiceExplanations.Prandtl number: Prandtl number is the ratio of momentum diffusivity to thermal diffusivity.
choiceExplanations.Rayleigh number: Rayleigh number is the Grashof number multiplied by the Prandtl number; it indicates when natural convection starts.

items.question: The ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces. A dimension less number use to categorize the fluids system in which the effect of viscosity is important in controlling the velocities or the flow patern of fluid

choiceExplanations.Mach number: Mach number is the ratio of flow velocity to the speed of sound.
choiceExplanations.Weber number: Weber number is the ratio of inertial forces to surface-tension forces.
choiceExplanations.Reynolds number: Correct — Reynolds number is the ratio of inertial to viscous forces and classifies flow as laminar or turbulent.
choiceExplanations.Froude number: Froude number is the ratio of inertial forces to gravity forces, used for open-channel flow.

items.question: What is the study of the free convection of a fluid caused by a hot body

choiceExplanations.Grassof Number: Correct — the Grashof number governs free (natural) convection caused by buoyancy around a hot body.
choiceExplanations.Peclet Number: Peclet number is the ratio of advective to diffusive transport (Re×Pr).
choiceExplanations.Prandtl Number: Prandtl number compares momentum diffusivity with thermal diffusivity of a fluid.
choiceExplanations.Nusselt Number: Nusselt number measures how much convection increases heat transfer compared with conduction alone.

items.question: Pitot tube is an instrument used in measuring, what characteristics of fluid?

choiceExplanations.Dynamic viscosity: Dynamic viscosity is measured with viscometers, not Pitot tubes.
choiceExplanations.Mass flow: Mass flow needs flow meters such as Coriolis meters; a Pitot tube gives only point velocity.
choiceExplanations.Static velocity: Correct (as keyed) — a Pitot tube compares stagnation and static pressure to find flow velocity.
choiceExplanations.Fluid density: Fluid density is measured with hydrometers or pycnometers, not Pitot tubes.

items.question: Best Cycle for vapor power?

choiceExplanations.Otto: Otto is the ideal gas cycle for spark-ignition engines, not a vapor power cycle.
choiceExplanations.Diesel: Diesel is the ideal gas cycle for compression-ignition engines.
choiceExplanations.Carnot: Correct — the Carnot cycle has the highest possible efficiency between two temperature limits, so it is the ideal benchmark.
choiceExplanations.Brayton: Brayton is the ideal gas-turbine cycle, which uses gas rather than vapor.

items.question: Using the float method in determining the velocity of water in a channel, the float velocity in relation the average water velocity is
items.answer: Greater than the average water velocity
choices: Greater than the average water velocity
Independent of the average water velocity
Equal to the average water velocity
Less than the average water velocity

choiceExplanations.Greater than the average water velocity: Correct — surface floats move faster than the average velocity; mean velocity is about 0.8–0.85 times the float velocity.
choiceExplanations.Independent of the average water velocit: Wrong; float velocity is directly related to mean velocity through a correction coefficient.
choiceExplanations.Equal to the average water velocity: Wrong; surface velocity is higher than the average because of friction at the bed and banks.
choiceExplanations.Less than the average water velocity: Wrong; the slowest water is near the bed, while the surface is near the maximum velocity.

items.question: The basic form of energy loss in flow equation stating that the energy loss is directly proportional to some friction factor, the length of the system and the kinetic energy level and inversely proportional to the diameter of the conductor.

choiceExplanations.Manning equation: Manning equation is an empirical velocity formula using roughness n, hydraulic radius and slope.
choiceExplanations.Hazen-Williams equation: Hazen-Williams is an empirical pipe-flow formula using coefficient C, mainly for water.
choiceExplanations.Darcy equation: Correct — Darcy-Weisbach: hf = f(L/D)(V²/2g), proportional to f, L and kinetic energy and inversely to D.
choiceExplanations.Chezy equation: Chezy equation gives V = C√(RS) for open-channel velocity.

items.question: What is the base of the most efficient trapezoidal concrete open channel if discharge is 100 m3/s and velocity is 2 m/s?

choiceExplanations.8.75 m: Does not match; with A = 50 m², the best section (b = 2y/√3, A = √3y²) gives b ≈ 6.2 m.
choiceExplanations.Q = A V A = Q/V: Correct — the first step is A = Q/V = 50 m², then apply the best-hydraulic-section relations to get b ≈ 6.2 m.
choiceExplanations.2.50 m: Too small; it would not give the required 50 m² flow area for the half-hexagon section.
choiceExplanations.10.40 m: Too large; inconsistent with the most efficient trapezoid for A = 50 m².

items.question: Given velocity 2.5 m/s, what is the height?

choiceExplanations.V= √2𝐺𝐻: Correct — Torricelli's relation V = √(2gH) gives H = V²/2g = 2.5²/19.62 ≈ 0.32 m.
choiceExplanations.V= √3𝐺𝐻: Wrong; there is no factor of 3 in the velocity-head relation.
choiceExplanations.V= √1𝐺𝐻: Wrong; omits the factor 2 in the kinetic-energy (velocity head) relation.
choiceExplanations.V= √4𝐺𝐻: Wrong; the factor 4 is not part of the free-fall velocity relation.

items.question: What is the depth of water in a trapezoidal channel with a side slope of 2 and carrying a 2.5 cu.m water flow? The channel’s bottom width is 1.5 meters and the flowing water has a velocity of 0.8 m/s. (Exact values)

choiceExplanations.0.65 m: Too shallow; A = (1.5 + 2y)y must equal Q/V = 3.125 m², giving y ≈ 0.93 m.
choiceExplanations.1.25 m: Too deep; it gives an area well above the required 3.125 m².
choiceExplanations.1.50 m: Too deep; inconsistent with the required flow area of 3.125 m².

items.question: The principal law that serve as basis of the heat transfer by radiation
items.answer: Stefan-Boltzmann Conduction - Fourier’ Law Convection - Newton’s Law of Cooling
choices: Stefan-Boltzmann Conduction - Fourier’ Law Convection - Newton’s Law of Cooling

choiceExplanations.Stefan-Boltzmann Conduction - Fourier’ L: Correct — radiation is governed by the Stefan-Boltzmann law (q = εσT⁴); conduction follows Fourier's law and convection Newton's law of cooling.
choiceExplanations.Fourier’s Law: Fourier's law governs conduction heat transfer, not radiation.
choiceExplanations.Fick’s Law: Fick's law governs mass diffusion, not heat radiation.
choiceExplanations.Newton’s Law of Cooling: Newton's law of cooling governs convection heat transfer.

items.question: In AUTOCAD cutting the edge of a square smoothly to become a circle is called

choiceExplanations.Fillet: Correct — Fillet rounds corners with an arc; a radius of half the side turns a square into a circle.
choiceExplanations.Trim: Trim cuts objects back to a cutting edge without rounding.
choiceExplanations.Extend: Extend lengthens objects to meet a boundary edge.
choiceExplanations.Chamfer: Chamfer bevels corners with straight angled lines, not arcs.

items.question: slope of Small farm Reservoir
items.answer: The inside slope (IS) shall be equal to 3
items.rationale: The inside slope (IS) shall be equal to 3:1 (H:V) while the outside slope (OS) shall be equal to 2:1.
choices: The inside slope (IS) shall be equal to 3
The inside slope (IS) shall be equal to 2
The inside slope (IS) shall be equal to 4
The inside slope (IS) shall be equal to 1

choiceExplanations.The inside slope (IS) shall be equal to: Correct — the inside (upstream) slope of a small-farm reservoir embankment is set at 3:1 to resist wave action and saturation.
2:1 is too steep for the wetted inside face; it is more typical of outside slopes.
4:1 is flatter than the specified 3:1 inside slope and needs more fill.
1:1 is far too steep and unstable for a water-retaining earth embankment.

items.question: Land with a slope of not more than 58% shall be used

choiceExplanations.Cropland slope: Cropland is limited to gentle slopes (generally ≤18%) to control erosion from tillage.
choiceExplanations.Orchard slope: Orchards are allowed on moderate slopes, but the 58% limit refers to ranch use.
choiceExplanations.Forest slope: Forest classification applies to the steepest lands, usually above the limits for agricultural uses.
choiceExplanations.Ranch slope: Correct — land with slopes up to 58% may be used as ranch or pasture land.

items.question: In the discharged state, both the positive and negative plates of a lead-acid battery transform into this substance as the electrolyte loses much of its dissolved sulfuric acid and becomes primarily water.
items.rationale: During discharge, both the lead dioxide positive plate and spongy lead negative plate react with sulfuric acid to form lead sulfate (PbSO₄), leaving primarily water in the electrolyte.

choiceExplanations.16/52: Correct — P = 13/52 + 4/52 − 1/52 = 16/52, subtracting the queen of hearts counted twice.
