choiceExplanations.Emergency slaughter: Correct — emergency slaughter is the immediate killing of injured or downer animals to end their suffering.
choiceExplanations.Scheduled slaughter: Scheduled slaughter is routine, planned slaughter after normal lairage and ante-mortem inspection.

items.question: "uppermost surface of a floor once construction has been completed"

choiceExplanations.Subgrade elevation line: The subgrade elevation is the level of the prepared soil beneath the slab or fill.
choiceExplanations.Structural slab line: The structural slab line is the top of the bare slab before finishes or toppings are applied.
choiceExplanations.Finished floor line: Correct — the finished floor line is the uppermost floor surface after all construction and finishes are done.
choiceExplanations.Natural grade line: The natural grade line is the original ground surface before any excavation or construction.

items.question: "designated compartment in the lairage used to separate sick and injured animal identified at the unloading area and ante mortem inspection"

choiceExplanations.Sorting pen: A sorting pen is used to classify or group animals by size, sex, or ownership.
choiceExplanations.Holding pen: A holding pen is where healthy animals are kept while waiting for slaughter.
choiceExplanations.Receiving pen: A receiving pen is where animals are first unloaded and checked on arrival.
choiceExplanations.Isolation pen: Correct — an isolation pen separates sick or injured animals found at unloading or during ante-mortem inspection.

items.question: "place where the animals can rest prior to slaughter"

choiceExplanations.Abattoir: An abattoir is the whole slaughter facility, not specifically the area where animals rest.
choiceExplanations.Feedlot: A feedlot is a confinement area for fattening livestock before marketing.
choiceExplanations.Chute: A chute is the passageway that moves animals from the lairage to the slaughter area.
choiceExplanations.Lairage: Correct — the lairage is the area of pens where animals rest before slaughter.

items.question: "weight of the live animal prior to slaughter"

choiceExplanations.Carcass weight: Carcass weight is the weight after slaughter and dressing, not the weight of the live animal.
choiceExplanations.Dressed weight: Dressed weight is the carcass weight after the hide, head, viscera, and offal are removed.
choiceExplanations.Chilled weight: Chilled weight is the carcass weight after cooling, which reflects shrink losses.
choiceExplanations.Live weight: Correct — live weight is the weight of the animal before it is slaughtered.

items.question: "means of transporting animals, including but not limited to trucks, tractors, trailers, or utility vehicles"

choiceExplanations.Restraint chute: A restraint chute holds an animal still for stunning, treatment, or inspection.
choiceExplanations.Hauling crate: A hauling crate is a container for carrying animals, not the vehicle that moves it.
choiceExplanations.Loading ramp: A loading ramp is an inclined structure for moving animals onto or off vehicles.
choiceExplanations.Transport vehicle: Correct — a transport vehicle is any truck, tractor, trailer, or utility vehicle used to move animals.

items.question: "premises that are approved and registered by the controlling authority in which food animals are slaughtered for human consumption"

choiceExplanations.Meat cutting plant: A meat cutting plant breaks down carcasses into cuts but does not slaughter animals.
choiceExplanations.Slaughterhouse/ abattoir: Correct — a slaughterhouse or abattoir is approved, registered premises where food animals are slaughtered for human consumption.
choiceExplanations.Rendering plant: A rendering plant processes inedible animal by-products into fats, meals, and similar products.
choiceExplanations.Cold storage plant: A cold storage plant stores chilled or frozen meat but does not slaughter.

items.question: "any animal presented for slaughter showing physical or physiological abnormalities that may lead the authority to pass or condemn until final judgement can be ascertained and therefore requiring further inspection and/or examination"

choiceExplanations.Reactor animal: A reactor animal has tested positive in a specific diagnostic test.
choiceExplanations.Condemned animal: A condemned animal has already been judged unfit for human consumption.
choiceExplanations.Downer animal: A downer animal is one that cannot stand or move.
choiceExplanations.Suspected animal: Correct — a suspected animal shows abnormalities and is held for further examination before being passed or condemned.

items.question: "general term for hogs, pigs, native pigs, and shoats"

choiceExplanations.Poultry: Poultry refers to domesticated birds such as chickens, ducks, and turkeys.
choiceExplanations.Swine: Correct — swine is the general term for hogs, pigs, native pigs, and shoats.
choiceExplanations.Equine: Equine refers to horses, donkeys, and mules.
choiceExplanations.Cattle: Cattle refers to bovine animals such as cows, bulls, and steers.

items.question: "refers to sheep, goat, and deer"

choiceExplanations.Large ruminant: Large ruminants are cattle and carabao (water buffalo).
choiceExplanations.Monogastric animal: Monogastric animals, such as pigs and poultry, have a single-compartment stomach.
choiceExplanations.Small ruminant: Correct — small ruminants include sheep, goats, and deer.
choiceExplanations.Pseudo ruminant: Pseudo-ruminants, such as camelids, have a three-compartment stomach.

items.question: "provides access inside the silo which may be located at the roof or at the wall"

choiceExplanations.Roof ventilator: A roof ventilator releases moist air and heat from the silo headspace.
choiceExplanations.Aeration duct: An aeration duct carries fan air through the stored grain mass.
choiceExplanations.Discharge spout: A discharge spout is the outlet that releases grain from the silo.
choiceExplanations.Access door: Correct — the access door lets people enter the silo and may be located in the roof or wall.

items.question: "angle of the material when the grains held starts to move"

choiceExplanations.Angle of surcharge: The angle of surcharge is the slope of the grain peak above the eave line of a filled silo.
choiceExplanations.Angle of rupture: The angle of rupture is the angle of the failure plane behind a retaining wall.
choiceExplanations.Angle of repose: The angle of repose is the slope angle of a free-standing pile of grain at rest.
choiceExplanations.Angle of friction: Correct — the angle of friction is the angle at which grain resting on a surface begins to slide.

items.question: "floor located at the basement of flat bottom silos"

choiceExplanations.Base flooring: Correct — the base flooring is the floor located at the basement of a flat-bottom silo.
choiceExplanations.Plenum flooring: A plenum floor is a raised perforated floor that forms an air chamber for aeration or drying.
choiceExplanations.Aeration flooring: Aeration flooring is a perforated floor that distributes fan air through the grain.
choiceExplanations.Subgrade flooring: The subgrade is the compacted soil layer under the foundation, not the silo floor.

items.question: "panel where all the controls are located, with or without mimic board"

choiceExplanations.Control panel: Correct — the control panel houses all system controls, with or without a mimic board.
choiceExplanations.Switchgear panel: A switchgear panel holds circuit breakers and disconnects for power distribution and protection.
choiceExplanations.Instrument panel: An instrument panel displays gauges and meter readings rather than housing all controls.
choiceExplanations.Distribution panel: A distribution panel divides electrical supply into branch circuits.

items.question: "height of the vertical-walled segment of silo"

choiceExplanations.Clearance height: Clearance height is the free vertical space available above or below a structure.
choiceExplanations.Ridge height: Ridge or peak height is measured to the top of the roof, not just the vertical wall.
choiceExplanations.Eave height: Correct — eave height is the height of the vertical-walled segment of the silo.
choiceExplanations.Effective height: Effective height is a design parameter, not the height of the silo's vertical wall.

items.question: "mechanism that facilitates vertical movement of grains"

choiceExplanations.Elevator: Correct — an elevator, such as a bucket elevator, moves grain vertically.
choiceExplanations.Feeder: A feeder meters grain at a controlled rate into equipment.
choiceExplanations.Spreader: A spreader distributes grain evenly over the bin surface during filling.
choiceExplanations.Conveyor: A conveyor such as a belt, chain, or screw conveyor generally moves grain horizontally or on a slight incline.

items.question: "equipment for receiving grains at the bottom of a bucket elevator"

choiceExplanations.Elevator boot: Correct — the boot is the bottom section of a bucket elevator, where grain is received.
choiceExplanations.Elevator leg: The elevator leg is the vertical casing that encloses the moving buckets and belt.
choiceExplanations.Elevator hood: The elevator hood is the top cover over the head pulley.
choiceExplanations.Elevator head: The elevator head is the top section, where grain is discharged.

items.question: "height of grains at level condition"

choiceExplanations.Surcharge height: Surcharge height is the height of the grain cone above the level fill line.
choiceExplanations.Equivalent height: Correct — the equivalent height is the height of the stored grain when its surface is leveled.
choiceExplanations.Nominal height: Nominal height is a rated or catalog dimension, not the leveled grain height.
choiceExplanations.Effective height: Effective height is a design height used in structural calculations, not the leveled grain level.

items.question: "action of releasing a toxic chemical in the gaseous state to control a targeted pest"

choiceExplanations.Dusting: Dusting applies a pesticide as a dry powder.
choiceExplanations.Misting: Misting sprays fine liquid droplets, not a gas.
choiceExplanations.Fumigation: Correct — fumigation releases a toxic chemical as a gas to kill target pests.
choiceExplanations.Fogging: Fogging disperses tiny liquid aerosol droplets, not a true gas.

items.question: "milled or unmilled, seeds or fruits of various food plants more specifically the cereal grasses."

choiceExplanations.Pulse: Pulses are the dry edible seeds of legumes such as mungbean and lentils.
choiceExplanations.Grain: Correct — grain means the milled or unmilled seeds or fruits of food plants, especially cereal grasses.
choiceExplanations.Forage: Forage is plant material such as grasses and legumes fed to livestock.
choiceExplanations.Kernel: A kernel is a single seed of a grain, not the general term.

items.question: "grain receiving area which may consist of elevator and other accessories such as weighing and cleaning machines."

choiceExplanations.Dryer house: A dryer house shelters the grain drying equipment.
choiceExplanations.Bagging house: A bagging house is where grain is packed into sacks.
choiceExplanations.Headhouse/ dumping house/ intake house: Correct — the headhouse, also called the dumping or intake house, receives grain and holds elevators, scales, and cleaners.
choiceExplanations.Scale house: A scale house holds the truck weighbridge for weighing vehicles.

items.question: "sloping, walled structure for discharging grains"

choiceExplanations.Hopper: Correct — a hopper is a sloping, walled structure that discharges grain by gravity.
choiceExplanations.Trough: A trough is an open, elongated channel, such as the housing of a screw conveyor.
choiceExplanations.Sump: A sump is a low pit that collects material or liquid.
choiceExplanations.Chute: A chute is an inclined channel that carries grain by gravity, not a walled discharge vessel.

items.question: "structure above the silo bins that houses conveyor systems for grain distribution"

choiceExplanations.Dust collection system: A dust collection system captures airborne dust using cyclones or bag filters.
choiceExplanations.Load distribution system: Correct — the load distribution system is the structure above the bins that houses conveyors distributing grain.
choiceExplanations.Bin aeration system: A bin aeration system uses fans and ducts to cool and condition the stored grain.
choiceExplanations.Grain transfer system: Grain transfer system is a general term for moving grain between units, not a defined silo part.

items.question: "board where the flow of grains at different points of the system at any time will be reflected"

choiceExplanations.Mimic board: Correct — a mimic board shows the real-time grain flow at different points of the system.
choiceExplanations.Annunciator board: An annunciator board shows alarm or status lights, not a diagram of the grain flow.
choiceExplanations.Distribution board: A distribution board divides electrical power into branch circuits.
choiceExplanations.Terminal board: A terminal board is where wiring connections are terminated.

items.question: "overall height of the silo structure from the topmost structure of the roof to the ground"

choiceExplanations.Eave height: Eave height covers only the vertical-wall segment, not the full height to the top of the roof.
choiceExplanations.Clearance height: Clearance height is the free space available, not the overall height of the structure.
choiceExplanations.Effective height: Effective height is a design parameter, not the overall height from ground to roof peak.
choiceExplanations.Peak height: Correct — peak height is the overall height from the ground to the topmost part of the silo roof.

items.question: "unit consisting of upright containers used for storage and handling of grains in bulk and provided with necessary equipment and accessories"

choiceExplanations.Silo: Correct — a silo is a unit of upright containers, with equipment, for storing and handling grain in bulk.
choiceExplanations.Granary: A granary is a general storehouse for grain, often for bagged grain or small-scale storage.
choiceExplanations.Bunker: A bunker is a horizontal, ground-level bulk storage structure.
choiceExplanations.Warehouse: A warehouse is a flat building for storing bagged or packaged goods.

items.question: "inside diameter of the largest inscribed circle within the silo cross-section"

choiceExplanations.Silo diameter: Correct — the silo diameter is the inside diameter of the largest circle that fits within the silo cross-section.
choiceExplanations.Effective diameter: Effective diameter is a derived design value, not the defined inscribed inside diameter.
choiceExplanations.Equivalent diameter: Equivalent diameter converts a non-circular section into an equivalent circular one.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic diameter: Hydraulic diameter equals 4A/P and is used for fluid flow in ducts.

items.question: "surface at the bottom of the silo where the grains lie"

choiceExplanations.Silo flooring: Correct — the silo flooring is the bottom surface of the silo on which the grain rests.
choiceExplanations.Base flooring: Base flooring refers specifically to the basement floor of flat-bottom silos.
choiceExplanations.Perforated flooring: Perforated flooring is a type of aeration floor with holes for airflow.
choiceExplanations.Plenum flooring: Plenum flooring is a raised floor above an air chamber used for aeration.

items.question: "ratio of the equivalent height (h) to the silo diameter (d), (h:d)"

choiceExplanations.Void ratio: Void ratio is the volume of voids divided by the volume of solids in a granular mass.
choiceExplanations.Compactness ratio: Compactness ratio is not the standard term for the silo height-to-diameter ratio.
choiceExplanations.Slenderness/ aspect ratio: Correct — the slenderness or aspect ratio is the equivalent height divided by the silo diameter (h:d).
choiceExplanations.Fineness ratio: Fineness ratio is the length-to-diameter ratio of streamlined bodies in aerodynamics.

items.question: "passageway of grains to be loaded into the silo"

choiceExplanations.Chute: A chute is a general inclined gravity channel, not specifically the loading passage into the silo.
choiceExplanations.Duct: A duct is an air passage, such as for aeration or ventilation.
choiceExplanations.Flume: A flume is an open channel that carries water or water-borne material.
choiceExplanations.Spout: Correct — the spout is the passage through which grain is loaded into the silo.

items.question: "vertical frame fastened to the silo walls which carries the loads"

choiceExplanations.Stiffener: Correct — stiffeners are vertical members fastened to the silo walls that carry the loads.
choiceExplanations.Purlin: Purlins are horizontal roof members that support the roof sheeting.
choiceExplanations.Girt: Girts are horizontal wall members that support the wall cladding.
choiceExplanations.Strut: A strut is a general compression member, not specifically a vertical wall frame.

items.question: "portion of the silo where grains are stored"

choiceExplanations.Aeration zone: The aeration zone is the region through which air passes, not the defined storage portion.
choiceExplanations.Holding chamber: Holding chamber is not the standard term for the grain-storage portion of a silo.
choiceExplanations.Discharge section: The discharge section is the hopper or outlet area used for unloading.
choiceExplanations.Storage block: Correct — the storage block is the portion of the silo where grain is stored.

items.question: "intersection of the hopper and the vertical wall, for hopper bottom type silos"

choiceExplanations.Shoulder: Shoulder is not the standard term for the junction between the hopper and the wall.
choiceExplanations.Collar: A collar is a ring-shaped fitting or opening frame, not the hopper-wall junction.
choiceExplanations.Transition: Correct — the transition is where the hopper meets the vertical wall in hopper-bottom silos.
choiceExplanations.Flange: A flange is a projecting rim used to connect parts together.

items.question: "structure below or at ground level that houses the collection equipment"

choiceExplanations.Intake system: The intake system receives incoming grain at the headhouse.
choiceExplanations.Distribution system: The distribution system sits above the bins and spreads grain into them.
choiceExplanations.Unloading system: Correct — the unloading system is the structure below or at ground level that houses the grain collection equipment.
choiceExplanations.Conveying system: Conveying system is a general term for grain-moving equipment, not this defined below-grade structure.

items.question: "volume contained in the cylindrical portion only of the silo or the volume contained in both the cylindrical portion and the conical section within the roof space"

choiceExplanations.Rated capacity: Rated capacity is usually the manufacturer's stated capacity in tonnes.
choiceExplanations.Nominal capacity: Nominal capacity is an approximate designation, not the defined cylinder-plus-cone volume.
choiceExplanations.Volumetric capacity: Correct — volumetric capacity is the volume of the cylindrical part, with or without the conical roof space.
choiceExplanations.Effective capacity: Effective capacity is the usable storage after allowing for unfillable spaces.

items.question: "one level of the storage block of silo"

choiceExplanations.Wall ring: Correct — a wall ring is one level, or tier, of the silo storage block.
choiceExplanations.Tension ring: A tension ring is a structural ring that resists hoop tension, such as at the eave.
choiceExplanations.Base ring: A base ring is the bottom anchoring ring at the foundation.
choiceExplanations.Compression ring: A compression ring is at the roof apex or hopper transition and resists compressive forces.

items.question: "process of sealing the connections between sheets and other parts such as caulking"

choiceExplanations.Rust proofing: Rust proofing protects metal from corrosion with coatings or galvanizing.
choiceExplanations.Weather proofing: Correct — weatherproofing seals the joints between sheets and other parts, for example by caulking.
choiceExplanations.Vapor sealing: Vapor sealing uses barriers to stop water vapor from moving through walls.
choiceExplanations.Damp proofing: Damp proofing keeps ground moisture from rising into foundations and walls.

items.question: "connected to the sidewall stiffeners to provide continuous circular reinforcement around the silo"

choiceExplanations.Wind rings: Correct — wind rings attach to the sidewall stiffeners and form continuous circular reinforcement around the silo.
choiceExplanations.Wall rings: Wall rings are the stacked tiers of wall sheets that make up the storage block.
choiceExplanations.Compression rings: Compression rings resist compressive forces at the roof apex or hopper junction.
choiceExplanations.Tension rings: Tension rings resist hoop tension at the eave or hopper transition.

items.question: "A silo that has an aspect ratio less than or equal to 0.4 (h/d\le0.4) with a flat bottom"

choiceExplanations.Retaining: Correct — a flat-bottom silo with h/d ≤ 0.4 is classified as retaining.
choiceExplanations.Intermediate: Intermediate silos have aspect ratios with 1.0 < h/d < 2.0.
choiceExplanations.Squat: Squat silos have 0.4 < h/d ≤ 1.0, or h/d ≤ 0.4 if they have a hopper.
choiceExplanations.Slender: Slender silos have aspect ratios of h/d ≥ 2.0.

items.question: "A silo that has an aspect ratio greater than 0.4 and less than or equal to 1 (0.4<h/d\le1.0). If the silo has an aspect ratio less than or equal to 0.4 (h/d\le0.4) and has a hopper, it is also classified as squat."

choiceExplanations.Squat: Correct — squat silos have 0.4 < h/d ≤ 1.0, or h/d ≤ 0.4 if they have a hopper.
choiceExplanations.Retaining: Retaining silos have h/d ≤ 0.4 and a flat bottom.
choiceExplanations.Slender: Slender silos have aspect ratios of h/d ≥ 2.0.
choiceExplanations.Intermediate: Intermediate silos have aspect ratios with 1.0 < h/d < 2.0.

items.question: "A silo that has an aspect ratio greater than 1.0 and less than 2.0. (1.0<h/d<2.0)

choiceExplanations.Intermediate: Correct — intermediate silos have aspect ratios with 1.0 < h/d < 2.0.
choiceExplanations.Retaining: Retaining silos have h/d ≤ 0.4 and a flat bottom.
choiceExplanations.Slender: Slender silos have aspect ratios of h/d ≥ 2.0.
choiceExplanations.Squat: Squat silos have aspect ratios with 0.4 < h/d ≤ 1.0.

items.question: "A silo that has an aspect ratio greater than or equal to 2.0(h/d\ge2.0)"

choiceExplanations.Retaining: Retaining silos have h/d ≤ 0.4 and a flat bottom.
choiceExplanations.Intermediate: Intermediate silos have aspect ratios with 1.0 < h/d < 2.0.
choiceExplanations.Squat: Squat silos have aspect ratios with 0.4 < h/d ≤ 1.0.
choiceExplanations.Slender: Correct — slender silos have aspect ratios of h/d ≥ 2.0.

items.question: "consist of a flat continuous belt in tension that is positioned between rollers driven by pulleys with intermittently spaced idlers for support."

choiceExplanations.Screw conveyors: Screw conveyors move grain with a rotating helical flight inside a trough or tube.
choiceExplanations.Chain conveyors: Chain conveyors move material with attachments on a continuous chain loop running over sprockets.
choiceExplanations.Belt conveyors: Correct — belt conveyors use a continuous belt under tension, run between pulleys and supported by spaced idlers.
choiceExplanations.Roller conveyors: Roller conveyors move packages over a series of rollers, not a continuous belt.

items.question: "consist of a continuous loop of chains between two sprockets. A take-up device which is connected to the sprocket opposite to the drive sprocket is responsible for proper tensioning of the chain. The materials are conveyed using some type of attachment such as pans."

choiceExplanations.Chain conveyors: Correct — chain conveyors use a continuous chain loop over sprockets with a take-up and attachments such as pans.
choiceExplanations.Roller conveyors: Roller conveyors use a series of rollers and have no chain loop with attachments.
choiceExplanations.Screw conveyors: Screw conveyors use a rotating helical flight, not chains and sprockets.
choiceExplanations.Belt conveyors: Belt conveyors use a continuous belt over pulleys and idlers, not chains with attachments.

items.question: "use high pressure air to transport grains in a totally enclosed system. It consists of the high pressure air source, a feed device, a conveying pipeline, and a receptacle for release of transported material and carrier gas."

choiceExplanations.Vibratory conveyors: Vibratory conveyors move material by oscillating a trough, not by high-pressure air in an enclosed pipeline.
choiceExplanations.Screw conveyors: Screw conveyors move grain with a rotating helical flight inside a trough or tube.
choiceExplanations.Pneumatic conveyors: Correct — pneumatic conveyors carry grain in an enclosed pipeline using an air source, a feeder, the pipeline, and a receiver.
choiceExplanations.Chain conveyors: Chain conveyors drag material along a trough with chain-mounted paddles or flights.

items.question: "are ideally used for the vertical conveyance of loose grains. It consists of several buckets that are carried by either belt or chain elevators."

choiceExplanations.Screw conveyors: Screw conveyors are mostly horizontal or inclined helical conveyors and are not built from buckets.
choiceExplanations.Bucket elevators: Correct — bucket elevators lift loose grain vertically in buckets attached to a belt or chain.
choiceExplanations.Flight conveyors: Flight conveyors drag material along a trough with flights on a chain, mostly horizontally or on inclines.
choiceExplanations.Auger elevators: Auger elevators lift grain with a helical screw inside a tube, with no buckets.

items.question: "slope located at the side of the road carriageway that provides entrance from lower ground levels"

choiceExplanations.Access ramp: Correct — an access ramp is a slope beside the carriageway that gives entry from lower ground.
choiceExplanations.Side slope: A side slope is the inclined face of a cut or fill beside the roadway, not an entrance.
choiceExplanations.Embankment slope: An embankment slope is the inclined face of a raised fill section.
choiceExplanations.Road shoulder: A road shoulder is the strip next to the travelled way for stopped vehicles and lateral support.

items.question: "granular material of mineral composition such as sand, gravel, shell, crushed and uncrushed stone or lightweight materials"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); Tambong Subject C part 1; RECALLED COMPRESS PART 2

choiceExplanations.Fillers: Fillers are fine mineral powders added to mixes to fill voids, not graded sand, gravel, or stone.
choiceExplanations.Aggregates: Correct — aggregates are granular mineral materials such as sand, gravel, shell, and crushed or uncrushed stone.
choiceExplanations.Binders: Binders such as cement or bitumen hold aggregate particles together.
choiceExplanations.Admixtures: Admixtures are chemicals added to concrete to change properties such as setting time or workability.

items.question: "production of crops, livestock, and aquatic flora and fauna"

choiceExplanations.Horticulture and forestry: Horticulture covers garden crops and forestry covers tree stands; neither includes livestock and aquatic production.
choiceExplanations.Agribusiness and forestry: Agribusiness is the commercial and trade side of farming, not the production of crops, livestock, and aquatic life.
choiceExplanations.Agroforestry and aquaculture: Agroforestry combines trees with crops and aquaculture is fish farming; together they are narrower than the definition.
choiceExplanations.Agriculture and fisheries: Correct — under AFMA, agriculture and fisheries means producing crops, livestock, and aquatic flora and fauna.

items.question: "suitable materials such as gravel, sand, and earth used to refill excavated materials during construction"

choiceExplanations.Backfill: Correct — backfill is suitable gravel, sand, or earth used to refill excavations during construction.
choiceExplanations.Borrow: Borrow is suitable material taken from another site, mainly to build embankments.
choiceExplanations.Spoil: Spoil is excavated material that is unsuitable or surplus and is hauled away for disposal.
choiceExplanations.Subbase: Subbase is a designed pavement layer between the subgrade and the base course.

items.question: "the act of refilling suitable materials or replacing unsuitable materials removed during construction"

choiceExplanations.Backfilling: Correct — backfilling is refilling excavations with suitable material or replacing unsuitable material that was removed.
choiceExplanations.Grading: Grading is shaping the subgrade to the required line and elevation.
choiceExplanations.Trenching: Trenching is digging narrow, long excavations for pipes, cables, or drains.
choiceExplanations.Grubbing: Grubbing is removing stumps and roots below the ground surface.

items.question: "layer of aggregate, soil-treated aggregate, treated soil, or soil aggregate of designed thickness that rests upon the Subbase or if no Subbase, upon the sub-grade, to support a surface course."

choiceExplanations.Leveling course: A leveling course is a thin layer placed to correct an uneven surface before an overlay.
choiceExplanations.Base course: Correct — the base course rests on the subbase (or the subgrade if there is none) and supports the surface course.
choiceExplanations.Binder course: A binder course is an intermediate asphalt layer directly under the wearing course.
choiceExplanations.Wearing course: The wearing course is the top pavement surface that carries traffic directly.

items.question: "suitable material used for embankments"

choiceExplanations.Subbase: Subbase is a pavement layer above the subgrade, not material for building embankments.
choiceExplanations.Spoil: Spoil is unsuitable or surplus excavated material that is disposed of.
choiceExplanations.Borrow: Correct — borrow is suitable material, usually from borrow pits, used to build embankments.
choiceExplanations.Backfill: Backfill is material used to refill excavations, not specifically to build embankments.

items.question: "ratio between a test load and an arbitrarily defined standard load, expressed as a percentage"

choiceExplanations.Unconfined Compressive Strength (UCS): UCS is the axial stress at which an unconfined cylindrical specimen fails.
choiceExplanations.Aggregate Impact Value (AIV): AIV measures how well aggregate resists sudden impact loading.
choiceExplanations.California Bearing Ratio (CBR): Correct — CBR is the test load divided by a standard crushed-stone load at the same penetration, expressed as a percentage.
choiceExplanations.Aggregate Crushing Value (ACV): ACV measures how well aggregate resists crushing under a gradually applied compressive load.

items.question: "removal and disposal of trees, vegetation or other unwanted materials from the ground surface"

choiceExplanations.Grading: Grading is shaping the ground to the required line and elevation.
choiceExplanations.Clearing: Correct — clearing removes and disposes of trees, vegetation, and debris on the ground surface.
choiceExplanations.Stripping: Stripping is removing the topsoil layer.
choiceExplanations.Grubbing: Grubbing removes stumps, roots, and buried material below the ground surface.

items.question: "string made of coconut coir strands twisted together"

choiceExplanations.Coco coir fiber: Coco coir fiber is the raw strand taken from the husk, before it is twisted.
choiceExplanations.Coco coir twine: Correct — coco coir twine is string made by twisting coconut coir strands together.
choiceExplanations.Coco coir peat: Coco coir peat is the fine pith residue used as a soil conditioner.
choiceExplanations.Coco coir mesh: Coco coir mesh is a woven net or blanket made from coir twine.

items.question: "natural and residual materials from coconut coir which serves as soil conditioner"

choiceExplanations.Coco coir peat: Correct — coco coir peat is the residual pith from coir processing and is used as a soil conditioner.
choiceExplanations.Coco coir fiber: Coco coir fiber is the long strand used for twine and nets, not a soil conditioner.
choiceExplanations.Coco coir twine: Coco coir twine is string made of twisted coir strands.
choiceExplanations.Coco coir mesh: Coco coir mesh is a woven coir net used for erosion control.

items.question: "tubular structure of coconut coir fiber blankets of different diameter filled with coco coir, and/or coco peat"

choiceExplanations.Coco-log: Correct — a coco-log is a tube of coir fiber blanket filled with coir and/or coco peat.
choiceExplanations.Coco-mat: A coco-mat is a flat mat of coir fiber, not a filled tube.
choiceExplanations.Coco-blanket: A coco-blanket is a flat rolled coir erosion-control blanket.
choiceExplanations.Coco-mesh: A coco-mesh is an open woven coir net laid flat on slopes.

items.question: "handspun coconut coir fiber twine woven into blankets of different density"

choiceExplanations.Geogrid: A geogrid is a polymer grid used to reinforce soil.
choiceExplanations.Geotextile: A geotextile is a permeable synthetic fabric used for separation, filtration, and drainage.
choiceExplanations.Coconet: Correct — a coconet is handspun coir twine woven into blankets of different density.
choiceExplanations.Cocopeat: Cocopeat is coir pith residue used as a soil conditioner, not a woven blanket.

items.question: "any coconut coir fiber-based material such as coconets, coco-logs, coco peat, placed in sloping lands and embankments to hold the vulnerable soil and permit vegetative growth to control surface erosion and conserve the productivity of the soil"

choiceExplanations.Coconut geogrid: A geogrid is a reinforcing grid; this term is not the collective name for coir erosion-control materials.
choiceExplanations.Jute geonet: A jute geonet is made from jute fiber, not coconut coir.
choiceExplanations.Coconut geonet: Correct — coconut geonet is the general term for coir products such as coconets, coco-logs, and coco peat used for slope erosion control.
choiceExplanations.Woven geotextile: Woven geotextile is a synthetic fabric, not a natural coir product.

items.question: "application of pressure to soil materials to result in a dense mass free of excessive voids; minimizes settlement, decreases permeability and increases strength"

choiceExplanations.Cementation: Cementation is the binding of soil particles by cementing agents.
choiceExplanations.Stabilization: Stabilization is improving soil properties, often by adding lime, cement, or other materials.
choiceExplanations.Consolidation: Consolidation is slow volume reduction of saturated soil as pore water drains out under a sustained load.
choiceExplanations.Compaction: Correct — compaction applies mechanical pressure to densify soil, which reduces voids, settlement, and permeability and increases strength.

items.question: "hardened mixture of fine and coarse aggregate, water, cement, and admixtures"

choiceExplanations.Grout: Grout is a fluid mix of cement, water, and sometimes fine sand used to fill voids.
choiceExplanations.Concrete: Correct — concrete is a hardened mix of fine and coarse aggregate, cement, water, and admixtures.
choiceExplanations.Mortar: Mortar is cement, sand, and water with no coarse aggregate, used to bond masonry.
choiceExplanations.Asphalt: Asphalt concrete uses bitumen as its binder, not cement.

items.question: "entity having a Contract with a procurement agency and accredited by the Philippine Constructors Accreditation Board (PCAB)"

choiceExplanations.Contractor: Correct — a contractor holds a contract with the procuring entity and must be licensed by PCAB.
choiceExplanations.Supplier: A supplier provides goods or materials and does not need PCAB construction accreditation.
choiceExplanations.Consultant: A consultant provides professional services such as design or supervision, not construction.
choiceExplanations.Subcontractor: A subcontractor works under the main contractor and has no direct contract with the procuring agency.

items.question: "structural component of specified thickness; it may consist of one layer or more"

choiceExplanations.Overlay: An overlay is a new layer placed over an existing pavement to restore or strengthen it.
choiceExplanations.Course: Correct — a course is a structural pavement layer of specified thickness, made of one or more layers.
choiceExplanations.Subbase: Subbase is one specific course, between the subgrade and the base.
choiceExplanations.Pavement: Pavement is the whole layered structure, not a single component course.

items.question: "transverse slope that helps the carriageway to drain properly"

choiceExplanations.Crossfall/ cross slope: Correct — crossfall or cross slope is the transverse slope that drains water off the carriageway.
choiceExplanations.Side slope: A side slope is the inclined face of a cut or fill beyond the shoulder.
choiceExplanations.Shoulder rollover: Shoulder rollover is the difference in slope between the travel lane and the shoulder.
choiceExplanations.Longitudinal grade: Longitudinal grade is the slope along the length of the road.

items.question: "drainage structure that may or may not, directly support and that extends across and beneath a highway street, driveway, alley, arterial, or other public way"

choiceExplanations.Culvert: Correct — a culvert is a drainage structure that runs across and beneath a road or other public way.
choiceExplanations.Flume: A flume is an open elevated channel that carries water, usually above ground.
choiceExplanations.Siphon: An inverted siphon is a closed conduit that carries water under an obstruction by gravity and pressure.
choiceExplanations.Headwall: A headwall is the retaining wall at a culvert's inlet or outlet, not the conduit itself.

items.question: "removal of water from the road area by the use of culverts, ditches, channels and other several structures"

choiceExplanations.Diversion: Diversion redirects flow from its natural course into another channel.
choiceExplanations.Impoundment: Impoundment stores water behind a dam or embankment.
choiceExplanations.Drainage: Correct — drainage removes water from the road area through culverts, ditches, channels, and similar structures.
choiceExplanations.Dewatering: Dewatering removes groundwater or standing water from excavations during construction.

items.question: "operations connected with excavating and placing embankments with soil, earth or rock"

choiceExplanations.Dredging: Dredging is excavating material from underwater beds.
choiceExplanations.Quarrying: Quarrying is extracting rock or stone from a quarry.
choiceExplanations.Backfilling: Backfilling only refills excavations and does not cover the full cycle of excavation and embankment.
choiceExplanations.Earthwork: Correct — earthwork covers all operations of excavating and placing soil, earth, or rock in embankments.

items.question: "construction, usually of earth or stone, to raise the ground or formation level above the natural surface"

choiceExplanations.Revetment: A revetment is a facing of stone or concrete that protects a slope or bank from erosion.
choiceExplanations.Causeway: A causeway is a raised road built across water or wetland, which is a specific type of embankment.
choiceExplanations.Abutment: An abutment is the end support of a bridge that retains the approach fill.
choiceExplanations.Embankment: Correct — an embankment is an earth or stone fill that raises the formation level above natural ground.

items.question: "load from the conversion of an expected axle load into an equivalent number of 18-kip single axle load"

choiceExplanations.Maximum Dry Density (MDD): MDD is the highest dry density a soil reaches in a Proctor compaction test.
choiceExplanations.California Bearing Ratio (CBR): CBR is a penetration test of the strength of subgrade or base material.
choiceExplanations.Equivalent Single Axle Load (ESAL): Correct — ESAL converts mixed axle loads into an equivalent number of 18-kip (80 kN) single axle loads.
choiceExplanations.Average Annual Daily Traffic (AADT): AADT is the total yearly traffic volume divided by 365 days.

items.question: "protection of soil from disclosing by water, wind, or other agent"

choiceExplanations.Erosion control: Correct — erosion control protects soil from being detached and carried away by water, wind, or other agents.
choiceExplanations.Slope stabilization: Slope stabilization prevents mass movement such as landslides, not only surface erosion.
choiceExplanations.Sediment control: Sediment control traps soil that has already eroded before it leaves the site.
choiceExplanations.Soil compaction: Soil compaction densifies soil mechanically; it is not a protection measure against erosive agents.

items.question: "act of cutting, digging, or scooping to remove material"

choiceExplanations.Grading: Grading shapes the surface to the required line and elevation.
choiceExplanations.Compaction: Compaction densifies soil by applying pressure.
choiceExplanations.Backfilling: Backfilling refills excavated spaces with suitable material.
choiceExplanations.Excavation: Correct — excavation is cutting, digging, or scooping to remove material.

items.question: "road within the agriculture and fisheries production areas, coastal landing points, and postharvest or processing facilities that links to local roads, national highways, and markets."

choiceExplanations.National Secondary Roads (NSR): National secondary roads connect cities and municipalities that national primary roads do not serve.
choiceExplanations.National Tertiary Roads (NTR): National tertiary roads are other public roads under DPWH that serve local national functions.
choiceExplanations.National Primary Roads (NPR): National primary roads connect major cities and form the main national road network.
choiceExplanations.Farm-to-Market Roads (FMR): Correct — farm-to-market roads link farms, fishery landings, and postharvest facilities to markets and highways.

items.question: "determination of the degree of compaction of the soil"

choiceExplanations.Standard Proctor Test (SPT): The Proctor test is a lab test that finds the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content.
choiceExplanations.Field Density Test (FDT): Correct — the field density test (e.g., sand cone) finds in-place density to check the degree of compaction.
choiceExplanations.Unconfined Compression Test (UCT): The unconfined compression test measures the compressive strength of cohesive soil.
choiceExplanations.California Bearing Ratio (CBR): CBR measures the bearing strength of a material, not the degree of compaction achieved.

items.question: "suitable embankment materials placed above natural ground line"

choiceExplanations.Fill: Correct — fill is suitable embankment material placed above the natural ground line.
choiceExplanations.Subbase: Subbase is a designed pavement layer above the subgrade.
choiceExplanations.Ballast: Ballast is coarse stone used under railway ties or for drainage.
choiceExplanations.Borrow: Borrow is the source material taken from pits; fill is that material once placed above ground.

items.question: "fabrics used in subsurface drainage, hydraulic filter, erosion control, sediment control, pavement structures and used as waterproofing and stress relieving membrane, and as a permeable separator to prevent mixing of dissimilar materials such as foundations and select fill materials"

choiceExplanations.Geonet: A geonet is a net-like polymer core used for in-plane drainage.
choiceExplanations.Geogrid: A geogrid is an open polymer grid used mainly to reinforce soil.
choiceExplanations.Geomembrane: A geomembrane is an impermeable liner that blocks fluids, not a permeable fabric.
choiceExplanations.Geotextile: Correct — a geotextile is a permeable fabric used for filtration, drainage, separation, and erosion control.

items.question: "slope of a roadway, channel, or natural ground"

choiceExplanations.Alignment: Alignment is the horizontal and vertical path of a road's centerline.
choiceExplanations.Grade: Correct — grade is the slope of a roadway, channel, or natural ground.
choiceExplanations.Camber: Camber is the convex crown of a road surface that sheds water sideways.
choiceExplanations.Contour: A contour is a line joining points of equal elevation.

items.question: "property of a soil which describes the distribution of size groups"

choiceExplanations.Porosity: Porosity is the ratio of void volume to the total volume of soil.
choiceExplanations.Gradation: Correct — gradation describes how soil particles are distributed among size groups.
choiceExplanations.Consistency: Consistency is how firm or soft a cohesive soil is at different moisture contents.
choiceExplanations.Plasticity: Plasticity is the ability of soil to deform without cracking within a moisture range.

items.question: "rate of increase or decrease in the level of the land, the slope expressed in percentage"

choiceExplanations.Relief: Relief is the difference between the highest and lowest elevations in an area.
choiceExplanations.Contour: A contour is a line joining points of equal elevation.
choiceExplanations.Elevation: Elevation is the vertical height of a point above a datum.
choiceExplanations.Gradient: Correct — gradient is the rate of rise or fall of the land, expressed as a percentage slope.

items.question: "preparation of the sub-grade, in line and elevation, for application of pavement materials including base and surfacing materials"

choiceExplanations.Scarifying: Scarifying loosens or breaks up the surface before reshaping or recompacting.
choiceExplanations.Compacting: Compacting densifies material but does not set line and elevation.
choiceExplanations.Grading: Correct — grading prepares the subgrade to the required line and elevation for pavement layers.
choiceExplanations.Paving: Paving is placing the surface course after the subgrade has been prepared.

items.question: "removal and disposal of trees, and other unwanted materials below the ground surface"
items.rationale: Grubbing (below ground) / clearing (surface)

choiceExplanations.Clearing (above ground): Clearing removes trees and vegetation on the ground surface, not below it.
choiceExplanations.Grubbing (below ground): Correct — grubbing removes stumps, roots, and buried material below the ground surface.
choiceExplanations.Stripping (topsoil layer): Stripping removes the organic topsoil layer, not buried roots and stumps.
choiceExplanations.Scalping (surface vegetation): Scalping removes surface vegetation and thin sod, not material below ground.

items.question: "general area where two or more roads, within which are included the roadway and roadside facilities for traffic movements in that area"

choiceExplanations.Intersection: Correct — an intersection is the area where two or more roads meet, including the roadway and roadside traffic facilities.
choiceExplanations.Interchange: An interchange is a grade-separated junction connected by ramps.
choiceExplanations.Median: A median separates opposing traffic lanes.
choiceExplanations.Roundabout: A roundabout is a circular type of intersection where traffic flows around a central island.

items.question: "roadway with single, two, or more clearly marked lanes for vehicular traffic"

choiceExplanations.Service road: A service road runs parallel to a main road and serves adjacent property.
choiceExplanations.Lane roadway: Correct — a lane roadway has one, two, or more clearly marked lanes for vehicles.
choiceExplanations.Divided highway: A divided highway has opposing lanes separated by a median.
choiceExplanations.Access road: An access road connects a particular site to the main road network.

items.question: "road that predominantly carries through traffic from one area to another, forming principal avenues of travel for traffic movements which include provincial, municipal, city, and barangay roads"

choiceExplanations.Local roads: Correct — in this definition, local roads include provincial, municipal, city, and barangay roads.
choiceExplanations.Arterial roads: In general classification, arterial roads carry high-volume through traffic; this definition specifically names provincial, municipal, city, and barangay roads.
choiceExplanations.Collector streets: Collector streets gather traffic from local streets and carry it to arterials.
choiceExplanations.National highways: National highways are under DPWH, not provincial, municipal, city, or barangay governments.

items.question: "a place, building, or structure where buyers and sellers meet for the sale or purchase of agriculture and fisheries products"

choiceExplanations.Market: Correct — a market is a place where buyers and sellers meet to trade agriculture and fisheries products.
choiceExplanations.Terminal: A terminal is a transport hub for loading, unloading, and transferring goods or passengers.
choiceExplanations.Warehouse: A warehouse is a building used to store goods, not to trade them.
choiceExplanations.Depot: A depot is a facility for storing goods or vehicles, or for distributing them.

items.question: "form of stone, brick, concrete block, concrete, or other similar building materials that have been bonded together with mortar to form a structure"

choiceExplanations.Masonry: Correct — masonry is stone, brick, block, or concrete units bonded together with mortar.
choiceExplanations.Shotcrete: Shotcrete is concrete sprayed pneumatically onto a surface.
choiceExplanations.Riprap: Riprap is loose, graded stone placed without mortar to resist erosion.
choiceExplanations.Gabion: A gabion is a wire basket filled with stone, with no mortar.

items.question: "concrete roadway, with clearly marked single or one lane for vehicular traffic"

choiceExplanations.One-lane asphalt road: A one-lane asphalt road is surfaced with bituminous material, not concrete.
choiceExplanations.Single-lane gravel road: A single-lane gravel road has an unpaved aggregate surface.
choiceExplanations.One-lane concrete road: Correct — a one-lane concrete road is a concrete roadway with a single clearly marked lane.
choiceExplanations.Two-lane concrete road: A two-lane concrete road has two marked lanes, not one.

items.question: "the contract drawings which show the locations, character, and dimension of the prescribed work, including layouts, profiles, cross sections, and other details"

choiceExplanations.Plans: Correct — plans are the contract drawings showing the location, character, dimensions, layouts, profiles, and cross sections of the work.
choiceExplanations.Specifications: Specifications are written requirements for materials, workmanship, and methods.
choiceExplanations.Estimates: Estimates are computed quantities and costs of the work.
choiceExplanations.Schedules: Schedules are timelines showing the sequence and duration of activities.

items.question: "a part or the entirety of the property, site, or location with defined physical boundaries used or required by a government project"

choiceExplanations.Scope of Work (SOW): The scope of work is the description of tasks and deliverables, not the land itself.
choiceExplanations.Right of Way (ROW): Correct — the right of way is the property or site with defined boundaries that a government project needs.
choiceExplanations.Limits of Construction (LOC): Limits of construction mark the physical extent of construction activity on site.
choiceExplanations.Zone of Influence (ZOI): A zone of influence is the area affected by stresses from a load or excavation.

items.question: "quarried stone especially selected, graded and placed to prevent erosion and thereby preserve the shape of a surface, slope, or underlying structure"

choiceExplanations.Revetment: A revetment is any protective facing on a slope, which may be riprap, concrete, or other materials.
choiceExplanations.Ballast: Ballast is coarse stone used under railway track or for weight and drainage.
choiceExplanations.Gabion: A gabion is a wire basket filled with stone, not loose placed stone.
choiceExplanations.Riprap: Correct — riprap is selected, graded quarried stone placed to protect surfaces and slopes from erosion.

items.question: "portion of a road intended for the movement of vehicles, exclusive of shoulders"

choiceExplanations.Road median: A road median is the strip that separates opposing traffic.
choiceExplanations.Road carriageway: Correct — the carriageway is the part of the road for moving vehicles, not including shoulders.
choiceExplanations.Road prism: The road prism is the whole cross-section of cut, fill, and roadway.
choiceExplanations.Road shoulder: A road shoulder lies next to the carriageway and is used for stopped vehicles and lateral support.

items.question: "lateral design width for one lane or two lanes strip of roadway"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Road prism width: Road prism width covers the full cross-section, including cuts and fills.
choiceExplanations.Road median width: Road median width is the width of the separating strip between opposing lanes.
choiceExplanations.Road shoulder width: Road shoulder width is the width of the shoulder strip beside the travelled way.
choiceExplanations.Road carriageway width: Correct — carriageway width is the design width of the one- or two-lane traffic strip.

items.question: "portion of the roadway contiguous with the travelled way for accommodation of stopped vehicles, for emergency use, and for lateral support of base and surface courses"

choiceExplanations.Road shoulder: Correct — the shoulder lies next to the travelled way and serves stopped vehicles, emergencies, and lateral support of the pavement layers.
choiceExplanations.Road verge: A road verge is the unpaved, often grassed, strip beyond the shoulder.
choiceExplanations.Road median: A road median separates opposing traffic lanes.
choiceExplanations.Road carriageway: The road carriageway is the travelled way itself, not the strip next to it.

items.question: "civil works covering removal, replacement, widening of pavement, and/or increase of thickness of pavement to ensure road safety and easier road safety"

choiceExplanations.Road resurfacing: Road resurfacing places a new surface layer without widening or replacing the pavement.
choiceExplanations.Road upgrading: Correct — road upgrading involves removing, replacing, widening, or thickening the pavement to improve the road's standard and safety.
choiceExplanations.Road rehabilitation: Road rehabilitation restores a deteriorated road to its original condition without raising its standard.
choiceExplanations.Road maintenance: Road maintenance is routine or periodic upkeep that keeps an existing road serviceable.

items.question: "graded portion of a road between top and side slopes, prepared as a foundation for the pavement structure and shoulders"

choiceExplanations.Carriageway: Carriageway is the road portion used for vehicle movement, excluding shoulders, not the graded foundation.
choiceExplanations.Subbase: Subbase is a pavement layer placed above the subgrade and below the base course.
choiceExplanations.Roadbed: Correct — the roadbed is the graded portion between top and side slopes that serves as the foundation for the pavement and shoulders.
choiceExplanations.Embankment: Embankment is a raised earth fill placed above natural ground to bring the road up to grade.

items.question: "space, location, or site intended to employ traffic consideration, preferably for the transport of agricultural and fisheries products"

choiceExplanations.Roadbed: Roadbed is the graded foundation for the pavement and shoulders, not the whole traffic space.
choiceExplanations.Carriageway: Carriageway is only the travelled part of the road used by vehicles.
choiceExplanations.Turnout: Turnout is a widened shoulder area for emergencies or for slow vehicles to pull out.
choiceExplanations.Roadway: Correct — the roadway is the space or site meant for traffic, including transport of agricultural and fisheries products.

items.question: "saving of different existing materials from the projects which are removed and intended to be used in other construction"

choiceExplanations.Select materials: Select materials are materials of specified quality, such as gradation or plasticity, used for subgrade or backfill.
choiceExplanations.Surplus materials: Surplus materials are excavated materials left over after fill needs are met.
choiceExplanations.Salvage materials: Correct — salvage materials are existing materials removed from a project and saved for use in other construction.
choiceExplanations.Borrow materials: Borrow materials are dug from pits outside the roadway to supply embankment fill.

items.question: "portion of the roadway primarily constructed for the use of pedestrians"

choiceExplanations.Median: Median is the strip separating opposing traffic lanes.
choiceExplanations.Crosswalk: Crosswalk is a marked path across the road for pedestrians to cross, not to walk along.
choiceExplanations.Sidewalk: Correct — a sidewalk is the part of the roadway built mainly for pedestrians.
choiceExplanations.Shoulder: Shoulder is the strip beside the carriageway for stopped vehicles and lateral support of the pavement.

items.question: "distance at which a driver of a vehicle can see an object of specified height on the road ahead, assuming adequate sight and visual acuity and clear atmospheric conditions"

choiceExplanations.Sight distance: Correct — sight distance is how far ahead a driver can see an object of specified height on the road.
choiceExplanations.Reaction distance: Reaction distance is the distance travelled during the driver's perception-reaction time, before braking starts.
choiceExplanations.Braking distance: Braking distance is the distance needed to stop the vehicle once the brakes are applied.
choiceExplanations.Clearance distance: Clearance distance is the lateral or vertical gap from an obstruction, not a visibility length.

items.question: "difference in crossfall between the pavement and its adjacent shoulder"

choiceExplanations.Lane transition: Lane transition is a tapered section where the number or width of lanes changes.
choiceExplanations.Shoulder rollover: Correct — shoulder rollover is the difference in crossfall between the pavement and its adjacent shoulder.
choiceExplanations.Pavement crown: Pavement crown is the high point of the cross-section, from which the pavement slopes down for drainage.
choiceExplanations.Curve widening: Curve widening is extra pavement width added on horizontal curves to allow for vehicle off-tracking.

items.question: "written technical description of materials, equipment, construction systems, standards, and workmanship that, in conjunction with the drawings, detail the requirements for acceptable completion of the work"

choiceExplanations.Schedules: Schedules are time programs of work activities or tables of items such as doors and finishes.
choiceExplanations.Addenda: Addenda are written changes to the bid documents issued before bids are opened.
choiceExplanations.Estimates: Estimates are computed quantities and costs of the work.
choiceExplanations.Specifications: Correct — specifications are the written technical requirements that, together with the drawings, define acceptable completion of the work.

items.question: "bridges, culverts, wall, buildings, foundations, water tanks, transmission towers, cribbing, caissons or coffer dams, other similar features which may be encountered in the work and are classified as _______"

choiceExplanations.Structures: Correct — bridges, culverts, walls, foundations, caissons and similar features met in the work are classified as structures.
choiceExplanations.Facilities: Facilities is a general term for installations serving a function, not this contract classification.
choiceExplanations.Utilities: Utilities are public service lines such as water, power and telecommunications.
choiceExplanations.Appurtenances: Appurtenances are accessory items attached to a main work, such as guardrails and signs.

items.question: "layer of the specified or selected materials, treated or untreated, of designated thickness in a pavement structure immediately above the sub-grade and below the pavement"

choiceExplanations.Binder layer: Binder layer is the middle asphalt course between the base and the surface course.
choiceExplanations.Base layer: Base layer sits on the subbase and directly supports the surface course.
choiceExplanations.Subbase layer: Correct — the subbase layer lies immediately above the subgrade, below the base and surface layers.
choiceExplanations.Surface layer: Surface layer is the topmost wearing course that carries traffic.

items.question: "top surface of the roadbed upon which the pavement structure is placed"

choiceExplanations.Subgrade: Correct — the subgrade is the top surface of the roadbed on which the pavement structure is placed.
choiceExplanations.Basecourse: Basecourse is a pavement layer placed above the subbase.
choiceExplanations.Roadbed: Roadbed is the whole graded foundation including shoulders; the subgrade is its top surface.
choiceExplanations.Subbase: Subbase is the pavement layer placed on top of the subgrade.

items.question: "material which is acceptable in accordance with the contract and which can be compacted"

choiceExplanations.Borrow materials: Borrow materials are fill taken from pits outside the roadway; the term refers to source, not acceptability.
choiceExplanations.Suitable materials: Correct — suitable materials meet the contract requirements and can be properly compacted.
choiceExplanations.Salvage materials: Salvage materials are existing materials recovered from removed works for reuse.
choiceExplanations.Unsuitable materials: Unsuitable materials, such as garbage, organics or muck, are not acceptable for fill.

items.question: "cross slope of the pavement at a horizontal curve, provided to partially counterbalance the centrifugal force on a vehicle going around that curve."

choiceExplanations.Superelevation: Correct — superelevation is the banking of the pavement on a curve that partly counteracts centrifugal force.
choiceExplanations.Crossfall: Crossfall is the general sideways slope of the pavement on straight sections, provided for drainage.
choiceExplanations.Gradient: Gradient is the slope of the road along its length.
choiceExplanations.Camber: Camber is the convex cross slope (crown) on straight sections that drains water off.

items.question: "a widened, unobstructed shoulder area that may be used for emergency purposes or allow slow-moving vehicles to pull out of the carriageway to give passing opportunity to following or incoming vehicles"

choiceExplanations.Shoulder: Shoulder is the regular strip beside the carriageway, not a specially widened pull-out area.
choiceExplanations.Ramp: Ramp is a connecting roadway between highways at interchanges.
choiceExplanations.Turnout: Correct — a turnout is a widened, unobstructed shoulder area used for emergencies or for slow vehicles to pull out.
choiceExplanations.Median: Median is the strip separating opposing traffic flows.

items.question: "materials not appropriate and safe for backfill and borrow which include garbage etc."

choiceExplanations.Salvage materials: Salvage materials are recovered materials reused in other construction.
choiceExplanations.Unsuitable materials: Correct — unsuitable materials, such as garbage and organic matter, are unsafe and inappropriate for backfill and borrow.
choiceExplanations.Select materials: Select materials are high-quality materials meeting specified gradation and plasticity.
choiceExplanations.Suitable materials: Suitable materials meet the contract requirements and can be compacted.

items.question: "an opening provided during construction in retaining walls, aprons, canal linings, foundation, etc., to permit drainage of water collecting behind and beneath such structures to reduce hydrostatic head."

choiceExplanations.Relief well: Relief well is a vertical well that relieves uplift pressure beneath dams or levees.
choiceExplanations.Catch basin: Catch basin is an inlet chamber with a sump that collects surface runoff.
choiceExplanations.French drain: French drain is a gravel-filled trench, with or without a pipe, for subsurface drainage.
choiceExplanations.Weep hole: Correct — weep holes are openings in walls and linings that drain water trapped behind them and reduce hydrostatic head.

items.question: "refers to a male breeding swine which is at least 8 months old"

choiceExplanations.Gilt: Gilt is a young female swine that has not yet farrowed.
choiceExplanations.Barrow: Barrow is a male swine castrated before sexual maturity.
choiceExplanations.Boar: Correct — a boar is a male breeding swine at least 8 months old.
choiceExplanations.Sow: Sow is a female swine that has farrowed.

items.question: "place for piglets inside the farrowing pen"

choiceExplanations.Weaning area: Weaning area houses piglets after they are separated from the sow.
choiceExplanations.Loafing area: Loafing area is a resting or exercise area, usually for cattle.
choiceExplanations.Creep area: Correct — the creep area is the protected, often heated space for piglets inside the farrowing pen.

items.question: "rate of removing undesirable or unproductive animals within the herd"

choiceExplanations.Mortality rate: Mortality rate is the proportion of animals that die in a given period.
choiceExplanations.Replacement rate: Replacement rate is the rate at which new breeders are brought in to replace removed animals.
choiceExplanations.Conception rate: Conception rate is the proportion of bred females that become pregnant.
choiceExplanations.Culling rate: Correct — culling rate is the rate at which undesirable or unproductive animals are removed from the herd.

items.question: "unbred sows which have just been weaned; non-pregnant sows"

choiceExplanations.Bred sows: Bred sows have already been mated and may be pregnant.
choiceExplanations.Dry sows: Correct — dry sows are newly weaned, unbred, non-pregnant sows.

items.question: "act of giving birth in swine"

choiceExplanations.Farrowing: Correct — farrowing is the act of giving birth in swine.
choiceExplanations.Lambing: Lambing is giving birth in sheep.
choiceExplanations.Calving: Calving is giving birth in cattle and carabao.
choiceExplanations.Kidding: Kidding is giving birth in goats.

items.question: "area in which a sow is confined during farrowing and lactation periods, but in which the sow can turn around"

choiceExplanations.Gestation pen: Gestation pen houses pregnant sows before farrowing.
choiceExplanations.Weaning pen: Weaning pen houses piglets after separation from the sow.
choiceExplanations.Finishing pen: Finishing pen houses market hogs in their final growth stage.
choiceExplanations.Farrowing pen: Correct — a farrowing pen confines the sow during farrowing and lactation but lets her turn around.

items.question: "device in which a sow is confined during farrowing and lactation periods and which prevents sow from turning around"

choiceExplanations.Boar stall: Boar stall is an individual enclosure for a breeding boar.
choiceExplanations.Farrowing stall/ farrowing crate: Correct — a farrowing stall or crate confines the sow during farrowing and lactation and stops her from turning around.
choiceExplanations.Breeding crate: Breeding crate is a device that supports the animals during mating.
choiceExplanations.Gestation stall: Gestation stall confines a pregnant sow individually, not during farrowing or lactation.

items.question: "swine raised for meat production usually starts at 15 kg"

choiceExplanations.Finisher: Finisher refers specifically to swine weighing 66 kg and up.
choiceExplanations.Grower: Grower refers specifically to swine weighing 40–65 kg.
choiceExplanations.Suckling: Suckling is a piglet that is still nursing from the sow.
choiceExplanations.Fattener: Correct — a fattener is swine raised for meat, usually starting at about 15 kg.

items.question: "swine which are 66 kg and up"

choiceExplanations.Finisher: Correct — finishers are swine weighing 66 kg and up.
choiceExplanations.Grower: Grower refers to swine weighing 40–65 kg.
choiceExplanations.Weaner: Weaner is a piglet recently separated from its mother.
choiceExplanations.Starter: Starter is a young post-weaning pig fed a starter ration, below grower weight.

items.question: "female swine that has not farrowed"

choiceExplanations.Gilt: Correct — a gilt is a female swine that has not farrowed.
choiceExplanations.Sow: Sow is a female swine that has already farrowed.
choiceExplanations.Boar: Boar is an intact male breeding swine.
choiceExplanations.Barrow: Barrow is a castrated male swine.

items.question: "swine from 40 to 65 kg"

choiceExplanations.Finisher: Finisher refers to swine weighing 66 kg and up.
choiceExplanations.Starter: Starter is a young post-weaning pig lighter than grower weight.
choiceExplanations.Grower: Correct — growers are swine weighing 40 to 65 kg.

items.question: "piglets born in one farrowing"

choiceExplanations.Clutch: Clutch is a set of eggs laid by a bird.
choiceExplanations.Litter: Correct — a litter is the group of piglets born in one farrowing.
choiceExplanations.Brood: Brood is a group of young birds hatched and raised together.
choiceExplanations.Herd: Herd is a group of animals kept together, not one birth group.

items.question: "average number of farrowings of one sow per year"

choiceExplanations.Litter index/farrowing index: Correct — the litter or farrowing index is the average number of farrowings per sow per year.
choiceExplanations.Parity index: Parity is the total number of times a sow has farrowed, not a yearly rate.
choiceExplanations.Fertility index: Fertility index measures reproductive ability, such as conception success.
choiceExplanations.Weaning index: Weaning index relates to piglets weaned, not the number of farrowings per year.

items.question: "number of days an animal stays in a pen"

choiceExplanations.Turnover: Turnover is the number of batches passing through a facility in a period.
choiceExplanations.Occupancy: Correct — occupancy is the number of days an animal stays in a pen.
choiceExplanations.Rotation: Rotation is the cyclic movement of animals between pens or pastures.
choiceExplanations.Downtime: Downtime is the period a pen stays empty for cleaning and disinfection.

items.question: "any breeding female pig that has farrowed"

choiceExplanations.Gilt: Gilt is a female that has not yet farrowed.
choiceExplanations.Barrow: Barrow is a castrated male swine.
choiceExplanations.Boar: Boar is an intact male breeding swine.
choiceExplanations.Sow: Correct — a sow is any breeding female pig that has farrowed.

items.question: "piglet that has been recently separated from its mother"

choiceExplanations.Suckling: Suckling is a piglet still nursing from its mother.
choiceExplanations.Finisher: Finisher refers to swine weighing 66 kg and above.
choiceExplanations.Weaner/ weanling: Correct — a weaner or weanling is a piglet recently separated from its mother.
choiceExplanations.Grower: Grower refers to swine weighing 40–65 kg.

items.question: "materials that are placed around the brooder stoves to prevent the chicks from straying too far away from the heat supply until they learn the source of heat"

choiceExplanations.Brooder hover: Brooder hover is a canopy over the heat source that holds warm air above the chicks.
choiceExplanations.Chick divider: Chick divider is a partition that separates groups of chicks within a house.
choiceExplanations.Brooder curtain: Brooder curtain is a side curtain that controls drafts and temperature in the house.
choiceExplanations.Brooder guard: Correct — a brooder guard encircles the heat source so chicks stay near it until they learn where the heat is.

items.question: "process of supplying heat to the chicks after hatching up to the time that their natural heat regulatory mechanisms becomes fully functional"

choiceExplanations.Rearing: Rearing is raising birds from the end of brooding until maturity.
choiceExplanations.Brooding: Correct — brooding supplies heat to chicks until their own temperature regulation is fully working.
choiceExplanations.Hatching: Hatching is the chick emerging from the egg.
choiceExplanations.Incubation: Incubation keeps eggs under controlled conditions so the embryos develop.

items.question: "material used as bedding for animals"

choiceExplanations.Mulch: Mulch is a soil-cover material used to conserve moisture and control weeds.
choiceExplanations.Roughage: Roughage is high-fiber feed such as hay or straw.
choiceExplanations.Litter: Correct — litter is the bedding material, such as rice hull or shavings, spread for animals.
choiceExplanations.Silage: Silage is high-moisture forage preserved by fermentation for feed.

items.question: "long and narrow type of houses wherein at least one-half of the front and the back of the house are open"

choiceExplanations.Enclosed housing: Enclosed housing is fully walled, with mechanical ventilation and lighting.
choiceExplanations.Monitor-type housing: Monitor-type refers to a roof with a raised ridge section for ventilation, not the open-wall layout.
choiceExplanations.Open-sided housing: Correct — open-sided houses are long and narrow, with at least half of the front and back open.
choiceExplanations.Semi-enclosed housing: Semi-enclosed housing is partly walled, with less open area than open-sided houses.

items.question: "house wherein inside conditions are maintained as near as possible to the bird's optimum requirements with the use of mechanical ventilation and artificial lighting"

choiceExplanations.Enclosed housing: Correct — enclosed housing keeps conditions near the birds' optimum using mechanical ventilation and artificial lighting.
choiceExplanations.Open-sided housing: Open-sided housing relies on natural ventilation through open walls.
choiceExplanations.Natural-ventilated housing: Natural-ventilated housing relies on wind and stack effect, not mechanical control.
choiceExplanations.Semi-confinement housing: Semi-confinement housing gives animals part-time access to outdoor range.

items.question: "type of flooring utilizing the most commonly available materials such as rice hull and rice straw and wood shavings over the cemented floor"

choiceExplanations.Litter type: Correct — litter-type flooring spreads rice hull, straw or wood shavings over a cement floor.
choiceExplanations.Slotted type: Slotted flooring has openings so droppings fall through.
choiceExplanations.Slot-litter type: Slot-litter flooring combines about 60% slots and 40% litter.
choiceExplanations.Wire-mesh type: Wire-mesh flooring uses elevated welded wire that lets droppings pass through.

items.question: "type of flooring with openings to facilitate cleaning of the droppings"

choiceExplanations.Slot-litter type: Slot-litter flooring combines slotted and litter sections.
choiceExplanations.Slotted type: Correct — slotted flooring has openings that make removing droppings easier.
choiceExplanations.Concrete type: Concrete-type flooring is a solid cement floor without openings.
choiceExplanations.Litter type: Litter-type flooring uses bedding over a cement floor, without openings.

items.question: "combination of slotted and litter type flooring wherein slots cover 60% of the total floor area and 40% is covered with litter."

choiceExplanations.Slot-litter type: Correct — slot-litter flooring has slots over 60% of the floor area and litter over 40%.
choiceExplanations.Slotted type: Slotted flooring is entirely slats or openings, with no litter section.
choiceExplanations.Elevated-wire type: Elevated-wire flooring is a raised wire-mesh floor without litter.
choiceExplanations.Litter type: Litter-type flooring is entirely bedding over cement, with no slots.

items.question: "large nesting boxes for 3-___ layers"

choiceExplanations.Community nest: Correct — community nests are large nesting boxes shared by several layers.
choiceExplanations.Individual nest: Individual nest is a single compartment used by one hen at a time.
choiceExplanations.Rollaway nest: Rollaway nest has a sloped floor that rolls eggs to a collection area.
choiceExplanations.Trap nest: Trap nest has a door that traps the hen so individual egg production can be recorded.

items.question: "mature male goat"

choiceExplanations.Buck: Correct — a buck is a mature male goat.
choiceExplanations.Kid: Kid is a young goat under six months old.
choiceExplanations.Doe: Doe is a mature female goat.
choiceExplanations.Wether: Wether is a castrated male goat or sheep.

items.question: "mature female goat that has kidded"

choiceExplanations.Doe: Correct — a doe is a mature female goat that has kidded.
choiceExplanations.Doeling: Doeling is a young female goat that has not yet kidded.
choiceExplanations.Wether: Wether is a castrated male goat.
choiceExplanations.Buck: Buck is a mature male goat.

items.question: "doe without milk"

choiceExplanations.Kidding doe: Kidding doe is a doe that is giving birth or about to.
choiceExplanations.Bred doe: Bred doe is a doe that has been mated and may be pregnant.
choiceExplanations.Dry doe: Correct — a dry doe is a doe that is not producing milk.
choiceExplanations.Lactating doe: Lactating doe is a doe currently producing milk.

items.question: "young goat under six months old of either sex"

choiceExplanations.Lamb: Lamb is a young sheep, not a goat.
choiceExplanations.Doeling: Doeling is specifically a young female goat, not either sex.
choiceExplanations.Kid: Correct — a kid is a young goat of either sex under six months old.

items.question: "mature female sheep that has already lambed"

choiceExplanations.Doe: Doe is a mature female goat, not a sheep.
choiceExplanations.Wether: Wether is a castrated male sheep or goat.
choiceExplanations.Ewe: Correct — a ewe is a mature female sheep that has lambed.
choiceExplanations.Ram: Ram is a mature male sheep.

items.question: "sheep under six months of age"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Kid: Kid is a young goat, not a sheep.
choiceExplanations.Hogget: Hogget is a young sheep of about one year, past the lamb stage.
choiceExplanations.Wether: Wether is a castrated male sheep.
choiceExplanations.Lamb: Correct — a lamb is a sheep under six months of age.

items.question: "mature male sheep"

choiceExplanations.Ram: Correct — a ram is a mature male sheep.
choiceExplanations.Buck: Buck is a mature male goat.
choiceExplanations.Wether: Wether is a castrated male sheep.
choiceExplanations.Boar: Boar is a male breeding swine.

items.question: "area with its physical facilities used for cattle fattening"

choiceExplanations.Paddock: Paddock is a small fenced grazing enclosure.
choiceExplanations.Feedlot: Correct — a feedlot is the area and facilities used to fatten cattle on concentrated feeding.
choiceExplanations.Corral: Corral is an enclosure for holding, sorting and handling cattle.
choiceExplanations.Pasture: Pasture is grassland used for grazing.

items.question: "breeding male bovine of any age"

choiceExplanations.Ox: Ox is a castrated mature bovine used for draft work.
choiceExplanations.Calf: Calf is a young bovine under one year old.
choiceExplanations.Steer: Steer is a male bovine castrated before sexual maturity, raised for beef.
