choiceExplanations.Bull: Correct — a bull is a breeding male bovine of any age.

items.question: "young male or female bovine under one year of age"

choiceExplanations.Steer: Steer is a castrated male bovine raised for beef.
choiceExplanations.Yearling: Yearling is a bovine about one to two years old.
choiceExplanations.Calf: Correct — a calf is a young male or female bovine under one year old.
choiceExplanations.Heifer: Heifer is a young female bovine that has not yet calved.

items.question: "mature female bovine that has already calved"

choiceExplanations.Bull: A bull is an uncastrated mature male bovine used for breeding.
choiceExplanations.Heifer: A heifer is a young female bovine that has not yet calved.
choiceExplanations.Steer: A steer is a male bovine castrated before sexual maturity, usually raised for beef.
choiceExplanations.Cow: Correct — a cow is a mature female bovine that has already given birth to at least one calf.

items.question: "female bovine between two to three years of age which has not given birth"

choiceExplanations.Calf: A calf is a young bovine of either sex, usually under one year old.
choiceExplanations.Steer: A steer is a castrated male bovine, not a female.
choiceExplanations.Cow: A cow is a mature female bovine that has already calved.
choiceExplanations.Heifer: Correct — a heifer is a young female bovine, about two to three years old, that has not yet given birth.

items.question: "enclosure for confining and handling livestock"

choiceExplanations.Feedlot: A feedlot is a confined area for intensive feeding and finishing of cattle before slaughter.
choiceExplanations.Paddock: A paddock is a fenced subdivision of pasture used for rotational grazing.
choiceExplanations.Pasture: A pasture is land with forage plants used for grazing livestock.
choiceExplanations.Corral: Correct — a corral is an enclosure for confining, sorting and handling livestock.

items.question: "pen for confining animals from the pasture"

choiceExplanations.Crowding pen: A crowding pen funnels cattle into the working chute.
choiceExplanations.Hospital pen: A hospital pen isolates sick or injured animals for treatment.
choiceExplanations.Sorting pen: A sorting pen is used to separate animals into groups.
choiceExplanations.Holding pen: Correct — a holding pen confines animals brought in from pasture until they are handled.

items.question: "pen used to funnel cattle into the working chute"

choiceExplanations.Sorting pen: A sorting pen separates animals into groups by class or treatment.
choiceExplanations.Holding pen: A holding pen confines animals brought in from pasture before handling.
choiceExplanations.Loading pen: A loading pen holds animals waiting to go up the loading chute onto vehicles.
choiceExplanations.Crowding pen: Correct — a crowding pen, often circular or funnel-shaped, forces cattle into the working chute.

items.question: "chute leading the cattle from the crowding pen to the holding chute/squeeze"

choiceExplanations.Loading chute: A loading chute is a ramp for moving cattle onto a vehicle.
choiceExplanations.Sorting chute: A sorting chute uses gates to divert animals into different pens.
choiceExplanations.Holding chute: A holding chute or squeeze restrains one animal for treatment.
choiceExplanations.Working chute: Correct — a working chute is the single-file alley leading cattle from the crowding pen to the holding chute or squeeze.

items.question: "use to restrain animals"

choiceExplanations.Working chute: A working chute is a single-file alley that moves cattle along; it does not fully restrain them.
choiceExplanations.Weighing chute: A weighing chute is fitted with a scale for weighing animals.
choiceExplanations.Holding chute/ squeeze: Correct — a holding chute or squeeze restrains an animal for vaccination, treatment or inspection.
choiceExplanations.Loading chute: A loading chute is a ramp for loading cattle onto a vehicle.

items.question: "chute used to load cattle from working chute or crowding pen to a vehicle"

choiceExplanations.Loading chute: Correct — a loading chute is a ramp that moves cattle from the working chute or crowding pen onto a vehicle.
choiceExplanations.Holding chute: A holding chute restrains individual animals for treatment.
choiceExplanations.Sorting chute: A sorting chute diverts animals into separate pens.
choiceExplanations.Working chute: A working chute leads cattle from the crowding pen to the squeeze.

items.question: "animals are free to move between resting, feeding and watering areas"

choiceExplanations.Conventional housing: Conventional housing confines animals in individual stalls or stanchions.
choiceExplanations.Stanchion housing: Stanchion housing locks each animal by the neck at a fixed stall position.
choiceExplanations.Tie-stall housing: Tie-stall housing tethers each animal in its own stall.
choiceExplanations.Loose housing: Correct — in loose housing, animals move freely between resting, feeding and watering areas.

items.question: "one to two year old cattle of either sex"

choiceExplanations.Heifer: A heifer is a young female that has not calved; the term does not cover males.
choiceExplanations.Calf: A calf is a young bovine under one year old.
choiceExplanations.Weanling: A weanling is a young animal just weaned from its dam, usually under one year.
choiceExplanations.Yearling: Correct — a yearling is cattle of either sex aged about one to two years.

items.question: "act of giving birth"

choiceExplanations.Conception: Conception is the fertilization of an ovum that begins pregnancy.
choiceExplanations.Parturition: Correct — parturition is the act of giving birth.
choiceExplanations.Gestation: Gestation is the length of pregnancy, from conception to birth.
choiceExplanations.Lactation: Lactation is the period during which a female secretes milk after giving birth.

items.question: "Philippine water buffalo or swamp buffalo"

choiceExplanations.Zebu: Zebu (Bos indicus) is humped tropical cattle, not a buffalo.
choiceExplanations.Murrah: Murrah is an Indian riverine dairy buffalo breed, not the swamp type.
choiceExplanations.Carabao: Correct — the carabao is the Philippine swamp-type water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis).
choiceExplanations.Banteng: Banteng (Bos javanicus) is wild Southeast Asian cattle, not a water buffalo.

items.question: "building or a portion of building where milking occurs but where no animals are housed"

choiceExplanations.Milking parlor: Correct — a milking parlor is a building or area used only for milking, with no animals housed there.
choiceExplanations.Loafing barn: A loafing barn is a shelter where animals rest freely in loose housing.
choiceExplanations.Holding area: A holding area keeps animals waiting before milking.
choiceExplanations.Milk room: A milk room is used for cooling, storing and handling milk and equipment, not for milking.

items.question: "area provided to accommodate animals before milking"

choiceExplanations.Feeding area: A feeding area is where animals receive feed and forage.
choiceExplanations.Holding area: Correct — a holding area keeps animals waiting just before they enter the milking parlor.
choiceExplanations.Milking area: A milking area is where animals are actually milked.
choiceExplanations.Loafing area: A loafing area is an open resting or exercise space in loose housing.

items.question: "type of stall where animals must back up to exit the stall"

choiceExplanations.Herringbone stall: Herringbone stalls angle animals diagonally in rows, and they exit forward as a group.
choiceExplanations.Rotary stall: Rotary stalls sit on a revolving platform, and animals leave at the exit point.
choiceExplanations.Back-out stall: Correct — in a back-out stall, the animal must back out to leave.
choiceExplanations.Walk-through stall: In a walk-through stall, animals exit forward after milking.

items.question: "type of stalls that allows the animals to proceed directly forward after milking is completed"

choiceExplanations.Herringbone: Herringbone stalls are angled parlor stalls where animals stand in echelon in groups.
choiceExplanations.Walk-through: Correct — walk-through stalls let animals walk straight forward out of the stall after milking.
choiceExplanations.Back-out: Back-out stalls require the animal to back up to exit.
choiceExplanations.Side-opening: Side-opening stalls have side gates and let animals exit sideways, not straight forward.

items.question: "any building or place used for killing of animals where the flesh is intended for human consumption"

choiceExplanations.Hatchery: A hatchery is a facility for incubating eggs and hatching chicks.
choiceExplanations.Tannery: A tannery processes animal hides into leather.
choiceExplanations.Creamery: A creamery processes milk into cream, butter and cheese.
choiceExplanations.Slaughterhouse: Correct — a slaughterhouse is any building or place where animals are killed for meat for human consumption.

items.question: "compartment which is suitable for confining only one animal at a time while it is being stunned and which is so constructed as to confine, without discomfort, to prevent any substantial movement of the animal forward, backward or sideway"

choiceExplanations.Stunning pen: Correct — a stunning pen holds one animal at a time and limits its movement while it is stunned.
choiceExplanations.Isolation pen: An isolation pen separates sick or suspect animals from the herd.
choiceExplanations.Quarantine pen: A quarantine pen holds newly arrived animals for disease observation.
choiceExplanations.Holding pen: A holding pen keeps groups of animals before processing.

items.question: "renders an animal insensible before it is killed"

choiceExplanations.Pithing: Pithing destroys the brain and spinal cord after stunning to stop reflex movements.
choiceExplanations.Sticking: Sticking cuts the major neck blood vessels to bleed the animal.
choiceExplanations.Shackling: Shackling chains or hooks the animal's legs to hoist it.
choiceExplanations.Stunning: Correct — stunning makes an animal insensible before it is killed.

items.question: "insertion of a rod or coiled wire through the hole in the skull of cattle made by the captive blot to destroy the brain and spinal cord to prevent reflex muscular action and possible injury to operatives"

choiceExplanations.Bleeding: Bleeding drains blood from the carcass after sticking.
choiceExplanations.Pithing: Correct — pithing inserts a rod through the captive-bolt hole to destroy the brain and spinal cord.
choiceExplanations.Stunning: Stunning makes the animal insensible before it is killed.
choiceExplanations.Sticking: Sticking cuts the major blood vessels with a knife.

items.question: "severance of the major blood vessels in the neck or immediately anterior to the heart by means of a knife and ""stuck"" shall be construed accordingly."

choiceExplanations.Pithing: Pithing destroys the brain and spinal cord with a rod through the skull.
choiceExplanations.Flaying: Flaying is removing the hide or skin from a carcass.
choiceExplanations.Bleeding: Bleeding is draining blood, which follows sticking.
choiceExplanations.Sticking: Correct — sticking is cutting the major blood vessels in the neck or near the heart with a knife.

items.question: "remove as much blood from the carcass as possible before further handling"

choiceExplanations.Washing: Washing removes dirt, blood and contaminants from the carcass surface.
choiceExplanations.Bleeding: Correct — bleeding (exsanguination) removes as much blood as possible from the carcass before further handling.
choiceExplanations.Scalding: Scalding uses hot water or steam to loosen hair or feathers.
choiceExplanations.Sticking: Sticking is the knife cut that starts bleeding; it is not the draining itself.

items.question: "lowering of animal into steam to prepare skin for dehairing"

choiceExplanations.Scalding: Correct — scalding exposes the carcass to steam or hot water to loosen the hair for dehairing.
choiceExplanations.Singeing: Singeing burns off remaining hair with a flame.
choiceExplanations.Scraping: Scraping mechanically removes loosened hair and scurf.
choiceExplanations.Dehairing: Dehairing is the actual removal of hair after scalding.

items.question: "removal of the hair of the carcass"

choiceExplanations.Scalding: Scalding only loosens the hair; it does not remove it.
choiceExplanations.Singeing: Singeing burns off residual hair; it is one specific method.
choiceExplanations.Flaying: Flaying removes the whole hide, not just the hair.
choiceExplanations.Dehairing: Correct — dehairing is the removal of hair from the carcass.

items.question: "suspending the carcass for particular operation"

choiceExplanations.Splitting: Splitting divides the carcass into halves or parts.
choiceExplanations.Shackling: Shackling chains the live animal's legs for hoisting before bleeding.
choiceExplanations.Gambrelling: Correct — gambrelling hangs the carcass on a gambrel by the hind legs for later operations.
choiceExplanations.Trimming: Trimming removes defects, bruises and excess fat from the carcass.

items.question: "cleaning the carcass by burning the hair"

choiceExplanations.Flaying: Flaying removes the hide from the carcass.
choiceExplanations.Dehairing: Dehairing is general hair removal, often by scraping after scalding.
choiceExplanations.Singeing: Correct — singeing cleans the carcass by burning off hair with a flame.
choiceExplanations.Scalding: Scalding loosens hair with hot water or steam.

items.question: "process of removing the internal organs in the abdominal and thoracic cavities"

choiceExplanations.Evisceration: Correct — evisceration removes the internal organs from the abdominal and thoracic cavities.
choiceExplanations.Depilation: Depilation is the removal of hair.
choiceExplanations.Decapitation: Decapitation is the removal of the head.
choiceExplanations.Exsanguination: Exsanguination is the removal of blood (bleeding).

items.question: "preparation of carcass after evisceration, ready for storage or sale"

choiceExplanations.Chilling: Chilling cools the carcass to slow microbial growth.
choiceExplanations.Splitting: Splitting divides the carcass into parts.
choiceExplanations.Dressing: Correct — dressing prepares the carcass after evisceration so it is ready for storage or sale.
choiceExplanations.Trimming: Trimming removes defects and excess fat; it is only part of the preparation.

items.question: "dividing carcass into parts"

choiceExplanations.Splitting: Correct — splitting divides the carcass into parts, such as sides.
choiceExplanations.Dressing: Dressing prepares the whole carcass for storage or sale.
choiceExplanations.Boning: Boning removes bones from the meat cuts.
choiceExplanations.Trimming: Trimming removes defects and excess fat.

items.question: "all parts including viscera of slaughtered cattle, sheep, goats or swine that may be used for human consumption"

choiceExplanations.Carcass: Correct — under the meat code definition, carcass means all parts, including viscera, of slaughtered animals that may be used for human consumption.
choiceExplanations.Meat: Meat refers only to the edible muscle part.
choiceExplanations.Offal: Offal refers only to the internal organs.
choiceExplanations.Viscera: Viscera are only the internal organs of the body cavities.

items.question: "edible part of the muscle of cattle, sheep, goats or swine"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Carcass: A carcass includes all usable parts, including viscera, not just muscle.
choiceExplanations.Meat: Correct — meat is the edible muscle part of cattle, sheep, goats or swine.
choiceExplanations.Tripe: Tripe is the edible stomach lining of ruminants.
choiceExplanations.Offal: Offal refers to the internal organs.

items.question: "part of internal organs of a slaughtered animal"

choiceExplanations.Meat: Meat is the edible muscle tissue.
choiceExplanations.Giblet: Giblets are edible poultry organs: heart, liver and gizzard.
choiceExplanations.Offal: Correct — offal is the internal organs of a slaughtered animal.
choiceExplanations.Carcass: A carcass is the whole slaughtered body, including its parts.

items.question: "digestive tract of ruminants such as the stomach, or the intestines which still contain fecal matter"

choiceExplanations.Green offal: Correct — green offal is the ruminant digestive tract (stomach, intestines) still holding fecal matter.
choiceExplanations.Black offal: Black offal refers to the swine digestive tract.
choiceExplanations.Red offal: Red offal is edible organs such as heart, liver, lungs and spleen.
choiceExplanations.White offal: White offal is not a standard term for the ruminant digestive tract with contents.

items.question: "digestive tract of swine such as the stomach, or the intestines which still contain fecal matter"

choiceExplanations.Green offal: Green offal refers to the ruminant digestive tract.
choiceExplanations.Black offal: Correct — black offal is the swine digestive tract still holding fecal matter.
choiceExplanations.White offal: White offal is not the standard term for the swine digestive tract with contents.
choiceExplanations.Red offal: Red offal is edible organs such as heart, liver and lungs.

items.question: "meat requiring further examination as declared by a veterinary inspector after veterinary examination"

choiceExplanations.Contaminated meat: Contaminated meat has been exposed to harmful substances or filth; the term does not mean held for re-examination.
choiceExplanations.Passed meat: Passed meat has been inspected and approved as fit for human consumption.
choiceExplanations.Condemned meat: Condemned meat has been declared unfit for human consumption.
choiceExplanations.Detained meat: Correct — detained meat is held for further examination as declared by a veterinary inspector.

items.question: "meat which is unfit for human consumption as declared by a veterinary inspector after veterinary examination"

choiceExplanations.Passed meat: Passed meat has been approved as fit for human consumption.
choiceExplanations.Detained meat: Detained meat is held for further examination.
choiceExplanations.Condemned meat: Correct — condemned meat has been declared unfit for human consumption by a veterinary inspector.
choiceExplanations.Contaminated meat: Contaminated meat describes exposure to contaminants, not an inspector's final ruling.

items.question: "black or green offal"

choiceExplanations.Gut and tripe: Correct — gut and tripe means black or green offal, the digestive tract of swine or ruminants.
choiceExplanations.Heart and liver: Heart and liver are red (edible organ) offal.
choiceExplanations.Lungs and spleen: Lungs and spleen are red offal, not digestive tract.
choiceExplanations.Head and feet: Head and feet are carcass extremities, not digestive offal.

items.question: "process of removing feathers from the skin of the poultry animal after scalding to prepare its meat for food"

choiceExplanations.Slitting and bleeding: Slitting and bleeding cut the neck vessels and drain blood before scalding.
choiceExplanations.Chilling and draining: Chilling and draining cool the dressed bird and remove excess water.
choiceExplanations.Defeathering/ plucking: Correct — defeathering, or plucking, removes feathers from the scalded bird's skin.
choiceExplanations.Eviscerating and washing: Eviscerating and washing remove the viscera and clean the carcass.

items.question: "process composed of stunning, slitting and bleeding, defeathering, eviscerating from which head, shanks, crop, oil gland and other inedible parts are removed"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Carcass fabrication: Carcass fabrication cuts dressed carcasses into retail or wholesale cuts.
choiceExplanations.Dressing/ slaughtering: Correct — dressing or slaughtering covers stunning, bleeding, defeathering, evisceration and removal of inedible parts.
choiceExplanations.Further processing: Further processing turns poultry meat into products such as sausages or nuggets.
choiceExplanations.Primary processing: Primary processing is a broad term and is not the defined name for this sequence.

items.question: "edible offals"

choiceExplanations.Tripe: Tripe is the edible stomach lining of ruminants.
choiceExplanations.Giblet: Correct — giblets are the edible offal, such as the heart, liver and gizzard.
choiceExplanations.Viscera: Viscera are all internal organs, edible or not.
choiceExplanations.Carcass: A carcass is the whole dressed body.

items.question: "group of animals that are mostly domesticated for their eggs, meat and/or feathers (e.g. chicken, geese, turkeys, ducks and ostriches)"

choiceExplanations.Poultry: Correct — poultry are domesticated birds raised for eggs, meat or feathers, such as chickens, ducks and turkeys.
choiceExplanations.Ruminants: Ruminants are cud-chewing mammals with multi-chambered stomachs, such as cattle and goats.
choiceExplanations.Livestock: Livestock usually means farm mammals such as cattle, swine and goats.

items.question: "any premises and building established for poultry dressing/slaughtering which include cut up processes to prepare poultry meat, parts, and products for human consumption"

choiceExplanations.Poultry dressing/slaughtering plant: Correct — a poultry dressing/slaughtering plant is premises for slaughtering and cutting up poultry for human consumption.
choiceExplanations.Poultry cold storage facility: A poultry cold storage facility only chills or freezes poultry products.
choiceExplanations.Meat cutting and packing plant: A meat cutting and packing plant fabricates and packs meat cuts but does not slaughter.
choiceExplanations.Poultry rendering and feed plant: A poultry rendering and feed plant processes by-products into feed or fat, not food.

items.question: "subjecting poultry into steam or hot water to loosen feathers from its skin prior to defeathering"

choiceExplanations.Shackling: Shackling hangs birds by the legs before slitting.
choiceExplanations.Singeing: Singeing burns off hair-like filoplumes after plucking.
choiceExplanations.Scalding: Correct — scalding dips poultry in hot water or steam to loosen feathers before defeathering.
choiceExplanations.Chilling: Chilling cools the eviscerated carcass to control microbial growth.

items.question: "animal species regarded as pests"

choiceExplanations.Pathogens: Pathogens are disease-causing microorganisms such as bacteria and viruses.
choiceExplanations.Parasites: Parasites are organisms living on or in a host at its expense.
choiceExplanations.Vermin: Correct — vermin are animal species regarded as pests, such as rats, mice and cockroaches.
choiceExplanations.Predators: Predators are animals that hunt and kill other animals for food.

items.question: "process of restraining birds prior to slitting"

choiceExplanations.Shackling: Correct — shackling restrains birds by hanging them by the legs before slitting.
choiceExplanations.Bleeding: Bleeding drains blood after the neck is slit.
choiceExplanations.Stunning: Stunning makes birds unconscious; it is not the act of restraining them.
choiceExplanations.Scalding: Scalding loosens feathers with hot water.

items.question: "digester and gas chamber form separate units"

choiceExplanations.Single-unit plant: A single-unit plant combines the digester and gas storage in one structure.
choiceExplanations.Integrated-type plant: An integrated-type plant has the gas chamber built into the digester.
choiceExplanations.Split-type plant: Correct — in a split-type plant, the digester and gas chamber are separate units.
choiceExplanations.Multi-digester plant: A multi-digester plant uses several digesters in series.

items.question: "plant with series of digesters"

choiceExplanations.Multi-digester plant: Correct — a multi-digester plant has a series of digesters, often used for staged digestion.
choiceExplanations.Integrated-type plant: An integrated-type plant has the digester and gasholder built as one unit.
choiceExplanations.Single-stage plant: A single-stage plant carries out digestion in only one digester.
choiceExplanations.Split-type plant: A split-type plant separates the digester from the gas chamber.

items.question: "closed digester with an immovable, rigid gas chamber and a displacement pit"

choiceExplanations.Balloon type: A balloon type uses a flexible plastic or rubber bag as both digester and gasholder.
choiceExplanations.Floating type: A floating type has a movable drum gasholder that rises and falls with gas volume.
choiceExplanations.Split type: A split type has a separate digester and gas chamber.
choiceExplanations.Fixed type: Correct — a fixed-dome type has an immovable rigid gas chamber, with slurry pushed into a displacement pit.

items.question: "plant consisting of a heat-sealed plastic or rubber bag (balloon), combining digester and gasholder"

choiceExplanations.Floating type: A floating type uses a movable steel drum gasholder on the digester.
choiceExplanations.Balloon type: Correct — a balloon type is a heat-sealed plastic or rubber bag that serves as both digester and gasholder.
choiceExplanations.Fixed type: A fixed type has a rigid, immovable dome and a displacement pit.
choiceExplanations.Split type: A split type has a separate digester and gas chamber.

items.question: "space inside or outside the digester for the collection and storage of biogas"

choiceExplanations.Mixing tank: A mixing tank is where substrate and water are mixed before feeding the digester.
choiceExplanations.Displacement pit: A displacement pit receives slurry pushed out by gas pressure in fixed-dome plants.
choiceExplanations.Gas chamber: Correct — the gas chamber is the space inside or outside the digester where biogas collects and is stored.
choiceExplanations.Sludge tank: A sludge tank stores digested effluent (slurry) discharged from the digester.

items.question: "cantilever beam that holds the movable cover in position at the desired biogas pressure"

choiceExplanations.Gasholder retainer: Correct — the gasholder retainer is the cantilever beam that holds the movable cover at the desired biogas pressure.
choiceExplanations.Counterweight frame: A counterweight frame carries weights that balance a floating gasholder; it is not the cantilevered retaining beam.
choiceExplanations.Pressure regulator: A pressure regulator is a valve that keeps gas line pressure steady; it is not a structural beam.
choiceExplanations.Gasholder guide: A gasholder guide is the frame or pipe that keeps a floating drum moving vertically.

items.question: "organic material used to produce biogas"

choiceExplanations.Effluent: Effluent is the digested slurry leaving the digester, not the raw organic feed.
choiceExplanations.Inoculum: Inoculum is seed sludge rich in active microbes, added to start or speed up digestion.
choiceExplanations.Substrate: Correct — substrate is the organic material, such as manure or crop residue, that is fed in and converted to biogas.
choiceExplanations.Slurry: Slurry is the mix of substrate and water inside the digester, not specifically the gas-producing material.

items.question: "difference in height between the digester wall and the filling line"

choiceExplanations.Headspace: Headspace is the gas-collection volume above the slurry, not a height difference defined by the filling line.
choiceExplanations.Drawdown: Drawdown is the drop in liquid level as a tank or pond is emptied.
choiceExplanations.Clearance: Clearance is a general term for spacing between parts; it is not the defined digester term.
choiceExplanations.Freeboard: Correct — freeboard is the height between the top of the digester wall and the filling line.

items.question: "level of slurry when the digesters is at full load"

choiceExplanations.Overflow level: The overflow level is where excess liquid spills out through the outlet, not the defined full-load slurry level.
choiceExplanations.Scum line: The scum line marks the top of the floating fibrous layer, not the design slurry level.
choiceExplanations.Filling line: Correct — the filling line is the slurry level when the digester is at full load.
choiceExplanations.Sludge line: The sludge line marks the top of the settled solids at the digester bottom.

items.question: "materials that inhibit the normal growth of pathogens in the digester such as mineral ions, heavy metals and detergents"

choiceExplanations.Inert materials: Inert materials such as sand or grit do not break down and do not chemically inhibit microbes.
choiceExplanations.Volatile solids: Volatile solids are the biodegradable organic part of the feed that is converted to biogas.
choiceExplanations.Fibrous materials: Fibrous materials such as straw degrade slowly and form scum, but they are not inhibitors.
choiceExplanations.Toxic materials: Correct — toxic materials such as mineral ions, heavy metals and detergents inhibit normal microbial growth in the digester.

items.question: "various processes that take place among the methanogens, non-methanogens and substrates fed into the digester as inputs"

choiceExplanations.Digestion: Correct — digestion covers all the processes among methanogens, non-methanogens and the substrates fed into the digester.
choiceExplanations.Methanization: Methanization is only the final stage, in which methanogens convert acids into methane.
choiceExplanations.Hydrolysis: Hydrolysis is only the first stage, in which enzymes break complex organics into soluble compounds.
choiceExplanations.Acidification: Acidification is only the middle stage, in which acid formers ferment monomers into organic acids.

items.question: "temperature range of 20 o C-40 o C where mesophilic bacteria operates"

choiceExplanations.Psychrophilic temperature range: The psychrophilic range is below about 20 °C, where cold-loving bacteria work slowly.
choiceExplanations.Ambient temperature range: Ambient temperature is the surrounding air temperature, not a defined bacterial operating range.
choiceExplanations.Thermophilic temperature range: The thermophilic range is about 45–60 °C, where heat-loving bacteria operate.
choiceExplanations.Mesophilic temperature range: Correct — mesophilic bacteria operate in the 20 °C–40 °C range.

items.question: "layer of floating material (mainly fibrous) on the slurry"

choiceExplanations.Scum: Correct — scum is the floating, mainly fibrous layer on top of the slurry.
choiceExplanations.Sediment: Sediment is heavy material that settles to the bottom, not material that floats.
choiceExplanations.Supernatant: Supernatant is the clarified liquid layer between the scum and the settled sludge.
choiceExplanations.Sludge: Sludge is the settled, solids-rich layer at the bottom of the digester.

items.question: "The waste materials of plant and animals origins, which consist mainly of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and inorganic materials are solubilized into simpler ones with the help of extracellular enzyme released by the bacteria."

choiceExplanations.Hydrolysis: Correct — in hydrolysis, extracellular enzymes break carbohydrates, lipids and proteins into simpler soluble compounds.
choiceExplanations.Acidification: Acidification is the second stage, in which monomers are fermented into volatile fatty acids.
choiceExplanations.Acetogenesis: Acetogenesis converts longer-chain acids into acetate, hydrogen and CO₂.
choiceExplanations.Methanization: Methanization is the final stage, in which methanogens turn acids into methane.

items.question: "The monomer such as glucose, which is produced in Stage 1, is fermented under anaerobic condition into various acids with the help of enzymes produced by the acid forming bacteria. At this stage, the acid-forming bacteria break down molecules of six atoms of carbon into molecules of less atoms of carbon which are in more reduced state. The principal acids produced in this process are acetic acid, propionic acid, butyric acid and ethanol."

choiceExplanations.Methanization: Methanization is the third stage, in which methanogens convert the acids into methane.
choiceExplanations.Acidification: Correct — in acidification, acid formers ferment glucose into acetic, propionic and butyric acids and ethanol.
choiceExplanations.Hydrolysis: Hydrolysis is the first stage, which produces the monomers that this stage then ferments.
choiceExplanations.Denitrification: Denitrification is the microbial reduction of nitrate to nitrogen gas, which is unrelated to biogas stages.

items.question: "The principal acids produce in stage 2 are processed by methanogenic bacteria to produce methane."

choiceExplanations.Methanization: Correct — in methanization, methanogenic bacteria convert the stage-2 acids into methane.
choiceExplanations.Gasification: Gasification is the high-temperature thermochemical conversion of biomass into syngas, not a biological process.
choiceExplanations.Acidification: Acidification is stage 2, which produces the acids rather than methane.
choiceExplanations.Hydrolysis: Hydrolysis is stage 1, in which complex organics are solubilized.

items.question: "requires free oxygen"

choiceExplanations.Anaerobic: Anaerobic processes take place without free oxygen.
choiceExplanations.Anoxic: Anoxic conditions lack free oxygen but contain bound oxygen, such as nitrate.
choiceExplanations.Facultative: Facultative organisms can live with or without oxygen, so they do not strictly require it.
choiceExplanations.Aerobic: Correct — aerobic processes require free oxygen.

items.question: "consist of liquid waste and slurry resulting from the production of livestock and poultry; and processing of crops, livestock and poultry"

choiceExplanations.Agricultural solid waste: Agricultural solid waste is non-liquid residue such as crop stalks or dry manure.
choiceExplanations.Animal manure slurry: Animal manure slurry is only one part of the category and excludes crop-processing wastewater.
choiceExplanations.Agricultural liquid waste: Correct — agricultural liquid waste covers liquids and slurries from livestock and poultry production and from crop and animal processing.
choiceExplanations.Domestic wastewater effluent: Domestic wastewater comes from households, not from agricultural production or processing.

items.question: "presence of free oxygen is not required"

choiceExplanations.Anoxic: Anoxic conditions have no free oxygen but do have bound oxygen such as nitrate; the term is not the general opposite of aerobic.
choiceExplanations.Anaerobic: Correct — anaerobic means free oxygen is not required.
choiceExplanations.Aerobic: Aerobic means free oxygen is required.
choiceExplanations.Facultative: Facultative describes organisms that can switch between aerobic and anaerobic metabolism.

items.question: "runoff not contaminated with manure such as runoff from roofs, grassed areas, drives and other areas which are not animal alleys"

choiceExplanations.Feedlot runoff: Feedlot runoff is rainfall that has run over manure-covered lots and is contaminated.
choiceExplanations.Surface runoff: Surface runoff is any overland flow, whether clean or contaminated.
choiceExplanations.Clean runoff: Correct — clean runoff comes from roofs, grassed areas and drives that are not contaminated with manure.
choiceExplanations.Contaminated runoff: Contaminated runoff is runoff that has picked up manure or other pollutants.

items.question: "process of killing all pathogenic microorganisms"

choiceExplanations.Sanitization: Sanitization only reduces microbes to safe levels and does not kill all pathogens.
choiceExplanations.Pasteurization: Pasteurization is moderate heating that kills most pathogens, mainly in food and milk.
choiceExplanations.Sterilization: Sterilization destroys all microorganisms, including non-pathogens and spores, not just pathogens.
choiceExplanations.Disinfection: Correct — disinfection is defined as the process of killing all pathogenic microorganisms.

items.question: "part of total solids passing through the filter in a filtration procedure"

choiceExplanations.Volatile solids: Volatile solids are the solids lost on ignition at 600 °C, a measure of organic content.
choiceExplanations.Dissolved solids: Correct — dissolved solids are the part of total solids that passes through the filter.
choiceExplanations.Settleable solids: Settleable solids are the solids that settle in an Imhoff cone within a set time.
choiceExplanations.Suspended solids: Suspended solids are the solids retained on the filter.

items.question: "part of total solids remaining after volatile gases driven off at 6000 C"

choiceExplanations.Dissolved solids: Dissolved solids are the filterable fraction, determined by filtration rather than ignition.
choiceExplanations.Volatile solids: Volatile solids are the fraction driven off as gas at 600 °C.
choiceExplanations.Fixed solids: Correct — fixed solids are the residue left after volatile matter is driven off at 600 °C.
choiceExplanations.Suspended solids: Suspended solids are the fraction retained on a filter.

items.question: "non-biodegradable component of liquid waste composed of sand, gravel, cinders or other heavy solid materials"

choiceExplanations.Grit: Correct — grit is the heavy, non-biodegradable sand, gravel and cinders in liquid waste.
choiceExplanations.Screenings: Screenings are coarse debris such as rags and sticks caught on bar screens.
choiceExplanations.Scum: Scum is light floating material such as grease and fibers.
choiceExplanations.Sludge: Sludge is the settled, largely organic solids from treatment.

items.question: "storage where liquid waste is stored before final disposal"

choiceExplanations.Oxidation pond: An oxidation pond treats waste through algal and bacterial aerobic action, not just storage.
choiceExplanations.Settling basin: A settling basin removes settleable solids by sedimentation.
choiceExplanations.Holding pond: Correct — a holding pond stores liquid waste before final disposal.
choiceExplanations.Anaerobic lagoon: An anaerobic lagoon is a deep pond that biologically treats waste without oxygen.

items.question: "liquid that flows into a containing space"

choiceExplanations.Leachate: Leachate is liquid that has percolated through waste or soil and carries dissolved contaminants.
choiceExplanations.Effluent: Effluent is liquid flowing out of a tank or treatment unit.
choiceExplanations.Supernatant: Supernatant is the clarified liquid above settled solids.
choiceExplanations.Influent: Correct — influent is liquid flowing into a containing space.

items.question: "system of clay layers and/or geosynthetic membranes used to contain leachate and reduce or prevent contaminant flow to groundwater"

choiceExplanations.Liners: Correct — liners are clay or geosynthetic barriers that contain leachate and protect groundwater.
choiceExplanations.Berms: Berms are raised earthen banks that direct or hold back surface flow.
choiceExplanations.Baffles: Baffles are walls inside a tank or pond that redirect flow to prevent short-circuiting.
choiceExplanations.Dikes: Dikes are embankments that hold or exclude water above ground.

items.question: "rainfall containing animal manure"

choiceExplanations.Wash water: Wash water is water used to clean barns or equipment, not rainfall.
choiceExplanations.Silage leachate: Silage leachate is acidic liquid seeping from ensiled forage.
choiceExplanations.Lot runoff: Correct — lot runoff is rainfall that has become mixed with animal manure on open lots.
choiceExplanations.Roof runoff: Roof runoff is clean rainwater from roofs, which is not contaminated with manure.

items.question: "accumulated moist animal excrement that does not undergo decomposition or drying; it include feces and urine which may be mixed with bedding material, spilled feed or soil"

choiceExplanations.Slurry: Slurry is manure mixed with water into a pumpable liquid.
choiceExplanations.Compost: Compost is organic matter that has already decomposed under controlled conditions.
choiceExplanations.Manure: Correct — manure is accumulated moist feces and urine, possibly mixed with bedding, feed or soil, that has not decomposed.
choiceExplanations.Biosolids: Biosolids are treated sewage sludge suitable for land application.

items.question: "treatment that causes substances in liquid waste to readily settle or float"

choiceExplanations.Secondary treatment: Secondary treatment uses biological processes to convert dissolved and suspended organics.
choiceExplanations.Primary treatment: Correct — primary treatment makes substances readily settle or float so they can be removed.
choiceExplanations.Tertiary treatment: Tertiary treatment is advanced polishing that removes nutrients, pathogens or residual solids.
choiceExplanations.Preliminary treatment: Preliminary treatment removes coarse debris and grit before primary treatment.

items.question: "treatment used to convert dissolved or suspended materials into a form more readily separated from the liquid waste being treated"

choiceExplanations.Secondary treatment: Correct — secondary treatment converts dissolved or suspended matter into a form that separates more easily, usually biologically.
choiceExplanations.Primary treatment: Primary treatment only lets existing solids settle or float out by physical means.
choiceExplanations.Tertiary treatment: Tertiary treatment is advanced final polishing after secondary treatment.
choiceExplanations.Preliminary treatment: Preliminary treatment screens out coarse solids and grit.

items.question: "solids removed by filtration"

choiceExplanations.Settleable solids: Settleable solids are measured by gravity settling in an Imhoff cone, not by filtration.
choiceExplanations.Volatile solids: Volatile solids are measured by ignition loss at 600 °C.
choiceExplanations.Suspended solids: Correct — suspended solids are the solids retained, or removed, by filtration.
choiceExplanations.Dissolved solids: Dissolved solids pass through the filter.

items.question: "residue remaining after water is removed from waste material by evaporation"

choiceExplanations.Fixed solids: Fixed solids are the residue left after ignition at 600 °C, not after evaporation alone.
choiceExplanations.Volatile solids: Volatile solids are the portion of total solids lost on ignition.
choiceExplanations.Total solids: Correct — total solids are the residue left after water is evaporated from the waste.
choiceExplanations.Suspended solids: Suspended solids are only the fraction retained on a filter.

items.question: "part of total solids driven off as volatile gases when heated to 6000 С"

choiceExplanations.Fixed solids: Fixed solids are the residue that remains after heating to 600 °C.
choiceExplanations.Suspended solids: Suspended solids are determined by filtration, not ignition.
choiceExplanations.Volatile solids: Correct — volatile solids are the part of total solids driven off as gas at 600 °C.
choiceExplanations.Dissolved solids: Dissolved solids are the fraction that passes through a filter.

items.question: "quantity of oxygen needed to satisfy biochemical oxidation of organic matter in waste sample in 5 days at 200 C"

choiceExplanations.Ultimate Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BODu: Ultimate BOD is the total oxygen demand once biodegradation is complete, typically measured over 20 days or more.
choiceExplanations.5-day Bio-Chemical Oxygen Demand (BOD5): Correct — BOD5 is the oxygen consumed in the biochemical oxidation of organics over 5 days at 20 °C.
choiceExplanations.Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD): COD measures oxygen demand from oxidation with a strong chemical oxidant, not microbes.
choiceExplanations.Theoretical Oxygen Demand (ThOD): ThOD is the oxygen demand calculated from stoichiometry for complete oxidation.

items.question: "any item used to improve the compost structure and to increase porosity to allow internal air movement"

choiceExplanations.Bulking agent: Correct — a bulking agent improves compost structure and porosity so that air can move through the pile.
choiceExplanations.Carbon source: A carbon source supplies carbon to balance the C:N ratio; it does not specifically provide structure.
choiceExplanations.Microbial inoculant: A microbial inoculant adds microorganisms to start or speed up decomposition.
choiceExplanations.Nitrogen source: A nitrogen source supplies nitrogen, such as manure, to lower a high C:N ratio.

items.question: Weight ratio of carbon to nitrogen

choiceExplanations.N:P ratio: The N:P ratio is the nitrogen-to-phosphorus ratio, used for nutrient balance.
choiceExplanations.C:P ratio: The C:P ratio is the carbon-to-phosphorus ratio.
choiceExplanations.N:K ratio: The N:K ratio is the nitrogen-to-potassium ratio, used in fertilizer formulation.
choiceExplanations.C:N ratio: Correct — the C:N ratio is the weight ratio of carbon to nitrogen, ideally about 25–30:1 for composting.

items.question: "controlled decomposition of organic matter by micro-organisms, mainly bacteria and fungi, into a humus-like product"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Digestion: Digestion usually means anaerobic breakdown that produces biogas and digestate.
choiceExplanations.Pyrolysis: Pyrolysis is thermal decomposition without oxygen that produces char, oil and gas.
choiceExplanations.Fermentation: Fermentation is anaerobic microbial conversion of sugars into acids, alcohols or gases.
choiceExplanations.Composting: Correct — composting is controlled decomposition of organic matter by bacteria and fungi into a humus-like product.

items.question: "process where fungi digest the carbons not degraded during composting and further stabilize the nutrients"

choiceExplanations.Curing: Correct — curing is the final stage, in which fungi degrade the remaining carbon and stabilize the nutrients.
choiceExplanations.Turning: Turning mixes and aerates the pile during active composting.
choiceExplanations.Shredding: Shredding reduces particle size before composting.
choiceExplanations.Screening: Screening sieves finished compost to remove oversized particles.

items.question: "site where solid waste is finally discharged and deposited"

choiceExplanations.Collection point: A collection point is where waste is gathered for pickup, not where it is finally deposited.
choiceExplanations.Disposal site: Correct — a disposal site is where solid waste is finally discharged and deposited.
choiceExplanations.Transfer station: A transfer station is an intermediate facility where waste is moved to larger vehicles.
choiceExplanations.Recovery facility: A recovery facility sorts and recovers recyclables from waste.

items.question: "interim containment of solid waste after generation and prior to collection for ultimate recovery or disposal"

choiceExplanations.Storage: Correct — storage is the interim containment of waste after it is generated and before it is collected.
choiceExplanations.Disposal: Disposal is the final placement of waste, not interim holding.
choiceExplanations.Collection: Collection is gathering waste and hauling it from the points of generation.
choiceExplanations.Transfer: Transfer is moving waste from collection vehicles to larger transport units.

items.question: "structure that provide a reliable enclosure within which an environment favorable to plant growth can be attained"

choiceExplanations.Screenhouse: A screenhouse is enclosed with insect-proof netting and offers only limited control of the environment.
choiceExplanations.Shadehouse: A shadehouse uses shade cloth to reduce sunlight but is not a fully controlled enclosure.
choiceExplanations.Headhouse: A headhouse is the service building attached to a greenhouse for work and storage.
choiceExplanations.Greenhouse: Correct — a greenhouse is an enclosure in which an environment favorable to plant growth can be maintained.

items.question: "method of greenhouse construction where modular roof units are connected at the eave by a common gutter"
items.answer: Ridge and furrow greenhouse/ gutter connected
choices: Ridge and furrow greenhouse/ gutter connected

choiceExplanations.Sawtooth naturally ventilated greenhouse: A sawtooth greenhouse has vertical vents along each roof step for natural ventilation.
choiceExplanations.Uneven span hillside greenhouse: An uneven-span greenhouse has roof slopes of unequal length to suit hillside sites.
choiceExplanations.Even span gable roof greenhouse: An even-span greenhouse is a single freestanding unit with equal roof slopes.
choiceExplanations.Ridge and furrow greenhouse/ gutter conn: Correct — a ridge-and-furrow greenhouse links modular roof units at the eaves with a shared gutter.

items.question: "removal of heat from the interior of the greenhouse"

choiceExplanations.Shading: Shading reduces incoming solar radiation rather than directly removing heat.
choiceExplanations.Ventilation: Ventilation exchanges inside and outside air; it is one method of cooling, not the definition.
choiceExplanations.Heating: Heating adds heat to the greenhouse.
choiceExplanations.Cooling: Correct — cooling is the removal of heat from the greenhouse interior.

items.question: "addition of heat to the interior of the greenhouse from any energy source including the sun"

choiceExplanations.Ventilation: Ventilation exchanges inside and outside air.
choiceExplanations.Humidification: Humidification adds moisture to the greenhouse air.
choiceExplanations.Heating: Correct — heating is adding heat to the greenhouse from any energy source, including the sun.
choiceExplanations.Cooling: Cooling removes heat from the greenhouse.

items.question: "prevents excess solar radiation in the greenhouse"

choiceExplanations.Shading: Correct — shading prevents excess solar radiation from entering the greenhouse.
choiceExplanations.Misting: Misting sprays fine water droplets for evaporative cooling and humidity.
choiceExplanations.Ventilation: Ventilation exchanges air to control temperature, humidity and gas levels.
choiceExplanations.Cooling: Cooling removes heat in general rather than blocking radiation.

items.question: "process of exchanging air inside the greenhouse with outside air to control temperature, humidity, oxygen or carbon dioxide levels"

choiceExplanations.Ventilation: Correct — ventilation exchanges inside and outside air to control temperature, humidity, O₂ and CO₂.
choiceExplanations.Recirculation: Recirculation moves internal air around without exchanging it with outside air.
choiceExplanations.Humidification: Humidification adds water vapor to the air.
choiceExplanations.Infiltration: Infiltration is uncontrolled air leakage through cracks and gaps.

items.question: "ventilation of greenhouse using fans"

choiceExplanations.Gravity ventilation: Gravity ventilation relies on buoyancy (the stack effect), not fans.
choiceExplanations.Convective ventilation: Convective ventilation is driven by natural thermal convection.
choiceExplanations.Mechanical ventilation: Correct — mechanical ventilation uses fans to move air through the greenhouse.
choiceExplanations.Natural ventilation: Natural ventilation uses wind and thermal pressure differences through vents.

items.question: "ventilation of greenhouse which occurs through controlled openings due to natural pressure variations inside and outside the greenhouse"

choiceExplanations.Natural ventilation: Correct — natural ventilation moves air through controlled openings because of natural pressure differences.
choiceExplanations.Mechanical ventilation: Mechanical ventilation uses fans instead of natural pressure variations.
choiceExplanations.Exhaust ventilation: Exhaust ventilation uses fans to pull air out of the greenhouse.
choiceExplanations.Forced ventilation: Forced ventilation uses fans to push air through the greenhouse.

items.question: "growth of protoplasts, cells, tissues, shoot tips, roots, anthers, embryos, flowers and meristems in a laboratory medium"

choiceExplanations.Tissue culture: Correct — tissue culture grows protoplasts, cells, tissues and organs on a laboratory medium.
choiceExplanations.Sand culture: Sand culture grows whole plants in sand irrigated with nutrient solution.
choiceExplanations.Hydroponic culture: Hydroponic culture grows whole plants in nutrient solution without soil.
choiceExplanations.Aeroponic culture: Aeroponic culture grows plants with their roots suspended in air and misted with nutrients.

items.question: "any nutrient material prepared for the growth and cultivation plant tissue"

choiceExplanations.Solidifying agent: A solidifying agent such as agar gels the medium but is only one ingredient.
choiceExplanations.Culture medium: Correct — a culture medium is any nutrient preparation used to grow plant tissue.
choiceExplanations.Stock solution: A stock solution is a concentrated mix of ingredients diluted later to make the medium.
choiceExplanations.Growth regulator: A growth regulator is a hormone, such as an auxin or cytokinin, added to direct growth.

items.question: "condition that describes the freedom of plant materials, culture medium, confines of the culture vessel from contaminating microorganisms"

choiceExplanations.Asepsis: Correct — asepsis is the condition in which plant material, medium and vessel are free of contaminating microorganisms.
choiceExplanations.Incubation: Incubation is keeping cultures under conditions that favor growth.
choiceExplanations.Inoculation: Inoculation is transferring explants onto the culture medium.
choiceExplanations.Acclimatization: Acclimatization is gradually adapting plantlets grown in vitro to outside conditions.

items.question: "subjecting of cultures to conditions favorable to the growth of the plant tissue"

choiceExplanations.Inoculation: Inoculation is placing explants onto the medium, which happens before incubation.
choiceExplanations.Sterilization: Sterilization eliminates microorganisms from the media, tools and explants.
choiceExplanations.Incubation: Correct — incubation is keeping cultures under conditions that favor tissue growth.
choiceExplanations.Acclimatization: Acclimatization is hardening plantlets for transfer to ex vitro conditions.

items.question: "flow air currents in which air currents do not intermingle"

choiceExplanations.Laminar flow: Correct — in laminar flow, air moves in parallel layers that do not intermingle, as in laminar flow hoods.
choiceExplanations.Turbulent flow: Turbulent flow has chaotic, mixing eddies.
choiceExplanations.Transitional flow: Transitional flow lies between the laminar and turbulent regimes.
choiceExplanations.Convective flow: Convective flow is air motion driven by temperature differences.

items.question: "storage in an artificial atmosphere in which the proportion of carbon dioxide and/or oxygen is precisely controlled"

choiceExplanations.Modified atmosphere storage: Modified atmosphere storage changes gas levels, for example through packaging, without precise continuous control.
choiceExplanations.Refrigerated air storage: Refrigerated air storage only lowers the temperature in normal air.
choiceExplanations.Hypobaric pressure storage: Hypobaric storage holds produce under reduced pressure.
choiceExplanations.Controlled atmosphere storage: Correct — controlled atmosphere storage precisely regulates O₂ and/or CO₂ levels in the storage room.

items.question: "produce is piled in room-sized bins, which exerts forces that must be resisted by the building walls"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Rack storage: Rack storage holds containers on shelves or frames, not loose produce piled against walls.
choiceExplanations.Bag storage: Bag storage keeps produce in sacks stacked in piles, not loose in room-sized bins.
choiceExplanations.Bulk storage: Correct — Bulk storage piles produce loose in large bins or rooms; the pile's weight pushes on the walls, so walls must be built strong.
choiceExplanations.Crate storage: Crate storage uses stackable boxes; the load is carried by the crates, not poured against walls.

items.question: "produce is placed in boxes or pallet bins which in turn are stacked in storage room"

choiceExplanations.Pallet bin storage: Correct — Pallet bin storage puts produce in boxes or pallet bins and stacks them in the storage room, usually handled by forklift.
choiceExplanations.Bagged floor storage: Bagged floor storage stacks sacks on the floor; the question describes boxes or pallet bins.
choiceExplanations.Silo bin storage: Silo bin storage is for loose grain in tall bins, not stacked boxes in a room.
choiceExplanations.Bulk room storage: Bulk room storage piles produce loose in a room, not in boxes or pallet bins.

items.question: "low portable platform made of wood or metal or plastic or in combination to facilitate handling, storage, or transport of materials as a unit load using a forklift"

choiceExplanations.Pallet: Correct — A pallet is a low portable platform that lets a forklift move and store materials as one unit load.
choiceExplanations.Crate: A crate is a box or frame container for produce; it is stacked on pallets, not a forklift platform.
choiceExplanations.Carton: A carton is a paperboard box for packing products; it is not a handling platform.
choiceExplanations.Hamper: A hamper is a large basket for produce or laundry; it is not a forklift platform.

items.question: "storage structure with continuously wetted walls"

choiceExplanations.Ice cooler: An ice cooler uses ice to chill produce, not continuously wetted walls.
choiceExplanations.Drip cooler: Correct — A drip cooler keeps the storage walls continuously wetted, so evaporation cools the air inside.
choiceExplanations.Vacuum cooler: A vacuum cooler lowers air pressure so water evaporates from produce; walls are not wetted.
choiceExplanations.Spray cooler: A spray cooler sprays water on the produce, not on the storage walls.

items.question: "coarse cloth made of jute, flax or hemp"

choiceExplanations.Burlap: Correct — Burlap is a coarse, strong cloth woven from jute, flax or hemp, widely used for sacks.
choiceExplanations.Muslin: Muslin is a fine, lightweight cotton cloth, not coarse jute, flax or hemp.
choiceExplanations.Canvas: Canvas is a heavy cloth, typically of cotton or linen, not the coarse jute fabric described.
choiceExplanations.Cheesecloth: Cheesecloth is a loose, light cotton gauze, not coarse jute, flax or hemp.

items.question: "storage provided with good ventilation"

choiceExplanations.Ice cooled: Ice cooled storage cools with ice, not ventilation.
choiceExplanations.Water cooled: Water cooled storage uses water as the cooling medium, not ventilation.
choiceExplanations.Vacuum cooled: Vacuum cooled storage removes heat by reducing pressure, not by ventilation.
choiceExplanations.Air cooled: Correct — Air cooled storage relies on good ventilation to move air through the produce and carry heat away.

items.question: "materials used to prevent migration of moisture into a storage area"

choiceExplanations.Radiant barrier: A radiant barrier reflects radiant heat, such as sun heat; it does not block moisture.
choiceExplanations.Vapor barrier: Correct — A vapor barrier is a material, such as plastic sheet or foil, that stops moisture vapor from moving into a storage area.
choiceExplanations.Thermal insulator: A thermal insulator slows heat flow; it does not by itself stop moisture migration.
choiceExplanations.Air curtain: An air curtain is a stream of air across a doorway to limit air exchange, not a moisture-blocking material.

items.question: "individual divisions in a carton formed by fiberboard dividers, each cell to contain one fruit"

choiceExplanations.Cell pack: Correct — A cell pack uses fiberboard dividers to form cells in a carton, each holding one fruit to prevent bruising.
choiceExplanations.Bulk pack: Bulk pack puts fruits loose in the container without individual divisions.
choiceExplanations.Jumble pack: Jumble pack places fruits randomly in the container, with no cells.
choiceExplanations.Tray pack: Tray pack lays fruits on trays in layers; it is not individual cells in a carton.

items.question: "cartons in which the cover is separate and fits snugly over the bottom part"

choiceExplanations.Collapsible cartons: Collapsible cartons fold flat when not in use; they are not defined by a separate fitted cover.
choiceExplanations.Telescopic cartons: Correct — Telescopic cartons have a separate cover that fits snugly over the bottom part, like a lid sliding over a box.
choiceExplanations.Slotted cartons: Slotted cartons are one-piece boxes with slots forming flaps; the cover is not separate.
choiceExplanations.Folding cartons: Folding cartons are one-piece paperboard cartons folded flat; they lack a separate fitted cover.

items.question: "product handling which include steps to make a harvested commodity more suitable for manufacturers or consumers"

choiceExplanations.Primary processing: Correct — Primary processing makes a harvested commodity more suitable for manufacturers or consumers, e.g. cleaning, sorting, drying.
choiceExplanations.Minimal processing: Minimal processing is light treatment, such as washing and cutting fresh produce; it is not the general step described.
choiceExplanations.Tertiary processing: Tertiary processing makes highly processed, ready-to-eat products; it is beyond the first step described.
choiceExplanations.Secondary processing: Secondary processing turns primary products into other food products, e.g. milling into flour; it comes after the step described.

items.question: "process of classifying into groups according to a set of recognized criteria of quality and size, each group bearing an accepted name and size grouping"

choiceExplanations.Grading: Correct — Grading classifies produce into groups by recognized quality and size standards, each group with an accepted name.
choiceExplanations.Sizing: Sizing groups by size only, and its criteria need not be recognized by the industry.
choiceExplanations.Trimming: Trimming removes unwanted parts such as stalks or damaged portions; it does not classify groups.
choiceExplanations.Sorting: Sorting uses criteria set by the person sorting, not recognized standards.

items.question: "process of classifying into sizes according to criteria that may or may not be recognized or accepted by the industry"

choiceExplanations.Sizing: Correct — Sizing classifies produce by size, using criteria that may or may not be recognized by the industry.
choiceExplanations.Weighing: Weighing only measures mass; it does not classify into size groups.
choiceExplanations.Sorting: Sorting groups by whatever criteria the sorter chooses, not necessarily size.
choiceExplanations.Grading: Grading uses recognized quality and size standards; the question says criteria may not be recognized.

items.question: "Process of classifying into groups designated by the person classifying the produce either according to a set of criteria or whatever criteria he may set"

choiceExplanations.Culling: Culling removes unacceptable or damaged produce; it does not group by chosen criteria.
choiceExplanations.Sizing: Sizing classifies by size specifically, not by any criteria the person sets.
choiceExplanations.Sorting: Correct — Sorting groups produce by criteria chosen by the person doing it, with no required standard.
choiceExplanations.Grading: Grading uses recognized quality and size standards with accepted names.

items.question: "ratio of the volume of air that enters a room to the volume of air of the empty room"

choiceExplanations.Air change ratio: Correct — Air change ratio is the volume of air entering a room divided by the volume of the empty room.
choiceExplanations.Void space ratio: Void space ratio compares empty space between stored items to total volume; it is not about air entering.
choiceExplanations.Pressure drop ratio: Pressure drop ratio compares pressure loss across a bed or duct; it is not a ratio of air volumes entering.
choiceExplanations.Infiltration rate: Infiltration rate is the leakage of outside air through cracks, usually per time; it is not defined against room volume as here.

items.question: "process of determining whether the grade standards have been interpreted or enforced properly by inspecting random samples usually of predetermined amount large enough to give an indication of the correctness of the grading procedure"

choiceExplanations.Inspection: Correct — Inspection checks random samples to find out whether grade standards were interpreted and enforced correctly.
choiceExplanations.Grading: Grading is the classifying itself; inspection is what verifies the grading was done correctly.
choiceExplanations.Certification: Certification is the official statement that produce meets a standard; it is not the checking of samples.
choiceExplanations.Sampling: Sampling is only taking the samples; inspection is the checking that uses them.

items.question: "process to ensure adequate protection and safe delivery of a product from the producer to the ultimate consumer"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Labeling: Labeling gives product information; it does not itself protect the product.
choiceExplanations.Packaging: Correct — Packaging protects a product and ensures it is delivered safely from producer to final consumer.
choiceExplanations.Palletizing: Palletizing stacks packages on pallets for handling; it is only one part of delivery.
choiceExplanations.Warehousing: Warehousing is storing goods; it does not protect during delivery.

items.question: "storing of paddy, milled rice, corn, and other grains in bags usually made of jute, polyethylene, and other packaging materials."

choiceExplanations.Bulk type storage: Bulk type storage keeps loose grain in piles or bins, not in bags.
choiceExplanations.Bag type storage: Correct — Bag type storage keeps paddy, milled rice, corn and other grains in jute, polyethylene or similar bags.
choiceExplanations.Silo type storage: Silo type storage keeps loose grain in tall cylindrical structures, not bags.
choiceExplanations.Bin type storage: Bin type storage keeps loose grain in bins, not bags.

items.question: "wooden or plastic (food grade) frames used on concrete floors for stacking bags to prevent direct contact between the grains and the floor"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); Crop Production and Processing

choiceExplanations.Perforated false floor: A perforated false floor is a built-in aerated floor for drying or aeration, not a frame for stacking bags.
choiceExplanations.Dunnage/ pallet/ \"\"tarima\"\"\": Correct — Dunnage (pallet or tarima) is a wooden or plastic frame on the floor that keeps bags off direct contact with concrete.
choiceExplanations.Moisture barrier mat: A moisture barrier mat is a sheet that blocks moisture; it is not the wooden or plastic stacking frame.
choiceExplanations.Timber floor decking: Timber floor decking is a permanent floor finish, not a movable frame for stacking bags.

items.question: "process of using chemicals to control insects in grains in a form of fumes"

choiceExplanations.Fogging: Fogging disperses fine liquid droplets as a mist, not a fumigant gas.
choiceExplanations.Dusting: Dusting applies chemical powder, not fumes.
choiceExplanations.Fumigation: Correct — Fumigation uses chemicals in gas or fume form to kill insects in stored grain.
choiceExplanations.Spraying: Spraying applies liquid droplets to surfaces, not fumes.

items.question: "building used for storing paddy, milled rice and other grains in bags"

choiceExplanations.Crib: A crib is a ventilated slatted structure for ear corn, not bagged grain.
choiceExplanations.Silo: A silo is a tall structure for loose bulk grain, not bags.
choiceExplanations.Warehouse: Correct — A warehouse is a building for storing paddy, milled rice and other grains in bags.
choiceExplanations.Barn: A barn is a farm building for livestock, hay or implements, not mainly bagged grain.

items.question: "building for fabrication, repair and maintenance of tools, implements, equipments and parts of structures and provides a place where tools, supplies and spare parts are stored"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Warehouse: A warehouse stores goods and produce; it is not for fabrication and repair.
choiceExplanations.Workshop: Correct — A workshop is the farm building for making and repairing tools and equipment and keeping supplies and spare parts.
choiceExplanations.Garage: A garage shelters vehicles; it is not mainly for fabricating and repairing tools.
choiceExplanations.Toolroom: A toolroom only stores tools; it lacks fabrication and repair work.

items.question: "area to protect machinery from weather, theft, vandalism and to allow easy maintenance and adjustment of machines"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Storage warehouse: A storage warehouse stores produce or goods, not machinery maintenance.
choiceExplanations.Machinery shed: Correct — A machinery shed protects machines from weather, theft and vandalism and allows easy maintenance and adjustment.
choiceExplanations.Repair workshop: A repair workshop is for fabrication and repair work, not mainly for protecting machines from weather and theft.
choiceExplanations.Equipment yard: An equipment yard is open space, so it does not protect machines from weather or theft.

items.question: "substances on farms that are highly flammable or poisonous such as engine fuels and oils such as gasoline, diesel, kerosene and lubricating oils; gases such as butane, propane and acetylene; paints containing flammable solvents, cellulose thinner or alcohol; herbicides, insecticides, rat poison; acids and alkalies such as detergents, cleaning liquids, lye and quicklime (CaO); and wood preservatives and corrosion inhibiting paints."

choiceExplanations.Corrosive substance: A corrosive substance covers only acids and alkalies, a part of the list given.
choiceExplanations.Combustible material: A combustible material covers only things that burn, not poisons such as pesticides.
choiceExplanations.Hazardous material: Correct — Hazardous materials are flammable, poisonous or harmful substances like fuels, gases, solvents, pesticides, acids and alkalies.
choiceExplanations.Biohazard material: A biohazard material is biological, such as pathogens; fuels and chemicals are not biohazards.

items.question: the sows are removed when the piglets reach weaning age. The pigs remain in the same building from farrowing until they reach the desired weight for slaughtering.

choiceExplanations.Four-Unit System: Four-Unit System uses separate farrowing, nursery, growing and finishing buildings.
choiceExplanations.Two-Unit System: Two-Unit System moves weaners to a separate growing-finishing house.
choiceExplanations.Three-Unit System: Three-Unit System moves weaners to a nursery and then to a growing-finishing house.
choiceExplanations.One-Unit System: Correct — One-Unit System: sows leave at weaning and the pigs stay in the same building from farrowing to slaughter weight.

items.question: The sows and piglets remain in the farrowing house until the piglets are weaned. The weanlings are transferred to a growing-finishing house.

choiceExplanations.Two-unit System: Correct — Two-unit System: sows and piglets stay in the farrowing house until weaning, then weanlings go to a growing-finishing house.
choiceExplanations.Four-unit System: Four-unit System uses separate nursery, growing and finishing houses after farrowing.
choiceExplanations.Three-unit System: Three-unit System adds a separate nursery house between farrowing and growing-finishing.
choiceExplanations.One-unit System: One-unit System keeps pigs in one building from farrowing to slaughter; no transfer happens.

items.question: The sows and piglets remain in the farrowing house until weaning. The weanlings are moved to a nursery house and finally to a growing-finishing unit where they stay until they are ready for slaughter.

choiceExplanations.One-unit System: One-unit System keeps pigs in one building throughout.
choiceExplanations.Two-unit System: Two-unit System has only farrowing and growing-finishing houses, no nursery.
choiceExplanations.Four-unit System: Four-unit System splits growing and finishing into two separate houses.
choiceExplanations.Three-unit System: Correct — Three-unit System: farrowing house until weaning, then a nursery house, then a growing-finishing unit until slaughter.

items.question: The sows and piglets remain in the farrowing house until weaning. After weaning, piglets are moved to a nursery house, then to a growing house and finally to a finishing house until they are ready for slaughter.

choiceExplanations.Two-unit System: Two-unit System has only farrowing and growing-finishing houses.
choiceExplanations.Three-unit System: Three-unit System combines growing and finishing in one house.
choiceExplanations.Four-unit System: Correct — Four-unit System: farrowing, then nursery, then growing, then finishing house, each a separate unit until slaughter.
choiceExplanations.One-unit System: One-unit System keeps pigs in one building throughout.

items.question: The types of roofs for swine housing are

choiceExplanations.Monitor, gable, mansard, sawtooth and ar: Includes gable, mansard, sawtooth and arch, which are not the swine-housing roof types of the standard.

items.question: Recommended width of concrete strips to be laid around warehouse to prevent rain from eroding the base of the walls below the damp course.

choiceExplanations.2m: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 1m.
choiceExplanations.3m: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 1m.

choiceExplanations.4m: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 1m.

items.question: Min dimension of roof truss span for warehouse

choiceExplanations.16.0 meters: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 14.5 meters.
choiceExplanations.14.5 meters: Correct — The recommended minimum roof truss span for a warehouse is 14.5 meters.
choiceExplanations.11.6 meters: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 14.5 meters.
choiceExplanations.13.1 meters: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 14.5 meters.

items.question: Maximum height of stacks for warehouse using jute sacks

choiceExplanations.4 meters: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 6 meters.

items.question: You are undergoing a test to determine the suitability of a 12-cm thick steel material as part of your drying chamber wall. choiceExplanations.0.016 m2: Does not match the worked solution; the correct result is 0.018 m2.

choiceExplanations.0.014 m2: Does not match the worked solution; the correct result is 0.018 m2.

choiceExplanations.Threshold maximum absolute value of soil: Maximum soil tension means the soil is dry; that signals starting irrigation, not stopping.
