choiceExplanations.Stilling basin: Correct — A stilling basin holds a pool of water to cushion falling water from a weir, chute or drop and slow its flow.
choiceExplanations.Headwall: A headwall is a wall at a culvert end, not a water-cushion pool.

items.question: This is the most common type of farmstead where buildings are located sufficiently far apart to allow adequate room for road drives and yards, reasonable fire safety and sanitation, yet sufficiently close together to be effective for farm operation.

choiceExplanations.Centralized type: Centralized type groups buildings tightly around one center.
choiceExplanations.Linear type: Linear type arranges buildings in a row along a road or line.
choiceExplanations.Concentrated type: Concentrated type packs buildings close together, which gives less fire safety.
choiceExplanations.Distributed type: Correct — The distributed type is the most common farmstead layout: buildings are spaced for safety and sanitation but close enough for efficient work.

items.question: Upper portion of material which act as foundation subbase course

choiceExplanations.Base course (Gravel Road): Base course is a constructed layer above the subbase, not the foundation soil.
choiceExplanations.Subgrade (Gravel Road): Correct — Subgrade is the upper part of the natural or compacted soil that serves as the foundation for the subbase course.
choiceExplanations.Surface course (Gravel Road): Surface course is the top wearing layer.
choiceExplanations.Roadbed (Gravel Road): Roadbed is the whole graded road section, not specifically the foundation material under the subbase.

items.question: Travel way or crown portion of the roadway intended for the movement of vehicles, exclusive of shoulders

choiceExplanations.Road Embankment: Road embankment is raised fill supporting the road.
choiceExplanations.Road Carriageway: Correct — The road carriageway is the part of the roadway for moving vehicles, excluding shoulders.
choiceExplanations.Road Subgrade: Road subgrade is the foundation soil under the pavement.
choiceExplanations.Road Shoulder: Road shoulder is the strip beside the carriageway, which the question excludes.

items.question: Also called as milking parlor, it is a room where the cows are milked but not housed.

choiceExplanations.Calving pen: A calving pen is where cows give birth.
choiceExplanations.Feed room: A feed room is for storing and preparing feed.
choiceExplanations.Holding pen: A holding pen is where cows wait before milking, not where they are milked.
choiceExplanations.Milking room: Correct — A milking room (milking parlor) is where cows are milked but not housed.

items.question: Compared to bag storage, the following are the characteristics of bulk storage, except:
items.rationale: Compared to bag storage, bulk storage involves higher capital costs, lower labor requirements, and lower handling costs, while being less (not more) susceptible to rodent infestation.

choiceExplanations.Higher capital costs: Bulk storage has higher capital costs for structures and equipment, so this is a true characteristic.
choiceExplanations.Lower handling costs: Bulk storage has lower handling costs because grain moves by machine, so this is a true characteristic.
choiceExplanations.More susceptible to rodent infestation: Correct — Bulk storage is generally less exposed to rodents than bagged storage, so 'more susceptible' is not a characteristic of bulk storage.
choiceExplanations.Not labor intensive: Bulk storage is not labor intensive because it is mechanized, so this is a true characteristic.

items.question: Materials that are usually very corrosion resistant and are used mostly for food handling equipments.

choiceExplanations.Carbon steel: Carbon steel rusts and is not corrosion resistant.
choiceExplanations.Galvanized iron: Galvanized iron is zinc coated and corrodes once the coating wears off.
choiceExplanations.Mild steel: Mild steel rusts easily and is not corrosion resistant.
choiceExplanations.Stainless steel: Correct — Stainless steel is highly corrosion resistant and is used mostly for food handling equipment.

items.question: it is the temporary structure of wooden poles and planks providing platform for working men to stand on while erecting or repairinga building

choiceExplanations.Scaffolding: Correct — Scaffolding is the temporary structure of poles and planks that gives workers a platform while building or repairing.
choiceExplanations.Formwork: Formwork is the mold that holds fresh concrete in shape.
choiceExplanations.Shoring: Shoring is temporary support that holds up a structure or excavation, not a work platform.
choiceExplanations.Falsework: Falsework is temporary support for a structure under construction, not primarily a worker platform.

items.question: Cut nails, duplex nails, cement nails and all kinds of nails and staples are all classified as _________.

choiceExplanations.Temporary fasteners: Temporary fasteners, such as clamps, hold only briefly and are removed easily.
choiceExplanations.Permanent fasteners: Permanent fasteners, such as welds and rivets, cannot be removed without destroying the joint.
choiceExplanations.Semi-permanent fasteners: Correct — Nails and staples can be removed with some damage, so they are classed as semi-permanent fasteners.
choiceExplanations.Removable fasteners: Removable fasteners are not the class used here; nails and staples are semi-permanent.

items.question: A list of all the different pieces of materials needed for a job. It is also called a “finish-stock list”.

choiceExplanations.Specification sheet: A specification sheet describes quality and technical requirements, not a materials list.
choiceExplanations.Bill of quantities: A bill of quantities gives measured work items and quantities with prices, not the finish-stock list.
choiceExplanations.Bill of materials: Correct — A bill of materials lists all the pieces of material needed for a job, also called a finish-stock list.
choiceExplanations.Cost estimate: A cost estimate gives expected cost, not a list of pieces.

items.question: Metal sheets that are freshly galvanized and are kept hot for a few minutes to allow zinc to alloy with the steel.

choiceExplanations.Aluminized sheets: Aluminized sheets are coated with aluminum, not zinc.
choiceExplanations.Galvanized sheets: Galvanized sheets are zinc-coated but not heated to alloy with the steel.
choiceExplanations.Terneplate sheets: Terneplate sheets are coated with a lead-tin alloy, not zinc.
choiceExplanations.Galvanealed sheets: Correct — Galvannealed sheets are freshly galvanized sheets heated so the zinc alloys with the steel, giving a paint-ready surface.

items.question: Flaw in lumber which characterized by separation along the lengthwise grain. These are present even before the tree is cut.

choiceExplanations.Wane: Wane is missing wood or bark on the edge of a board.
choiceExplanations.Shake: Correct — A shake is a lengthwise separation along the grain, often between growth rings, that exists in the standing tree.
choiceExplanations.Split: A split is a lengthwise crack through the piece caused by drying, not present in the live tree.
choiceExplanations.Check: A check is a lengthwise crack that develops during drying, not before cutting.

items.question: The daily water requirement of boar and of sow at normal ambient temperature.

choiceExplanations.35-55 liters per day-animal: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 10-30 liters per day-animal.
choiceExplanations.3-8 liters per day-animal: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 10-30 liters per day-animal.
choiceExplanations.60-80 liters per day-animal: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 10-30 liters per day-animal.
choiceExplanations.10-30 liters per day-animal: Correct — Boars and sows need about 10 to 30 liters of water per animal per day at normal temperatures.

items.question: A factor of this value in watts per square meter must be used for all floor area excluding porches, garages, basements or unused or unfinished spaces not adaptable for future use.

choiceExplanations.26 va per square meter: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 32 va per square meter.
choiceExplanations.29 va per square meter: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 32 va per square meter.
choiceExplanations.32 va per square meter: Correct — The keyed general lighting load is 32 VA per square meter of floor area, excluding porches, garages and unused spaces.
choiceExplanations.35 va per square meter: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 32 va per square meter.

items.question: The weight of a steel roof truss W in pounds per square foot of the horizontal surface as a function of span L in feet can be determined by an empirical equation ___.

choiceExplanations.W = 0.4 + 0.037 L: Slope coefficient 0.037 does not match the standard equation 0.4 + 0.040 L.
choiceExplanations.W = 0.4 + 0.044 L: Slope coefficient 0.044 does not match the standard equation 0.4 + 0.040 L.
choiceExplanations.W = 0.3 + 0.034 L: Constant 0.3 and slope 0.034 do not match the standard equation 0.4 + 0.040 L.
choiceExplanations.W = 0.4 + 0.040 L: Correct — The empirical equation for steel roof truss weight is W = 0.4 + 0.040 L (psf of horizontal surface, L in feet).

items.question: Based on PAES 411:2000 Slaughterhouse for Swine; Small and Large Animals: What is the minimum elevation of the site from the ground?

choiceExplanations.648 mm: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 600 mm.
choiceExplanations.552 mm: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 600 mm.
choiceExplanations.600 mm: Correct — PAES 411:2000 requires a minimum site elevation of 600 mm above the ground.
choiceExplanations.780 mm: Not the standard value for this question; the correct figure is 600 mm.

items.question: This stonework is made from squared stones, with thin mortar joints.

choiceExplanations.Rubble: Rubble is rough, irregular stone laid without squaring.
choiceExplanations.Ashlar: Correct — Ashlar is stonework of squared, cut stones laid with thin mortar joints.
choiceExplanations.Riprap: Riprap is loose rock placed to protect slopes from erosion, not laid with mortar joints.
choiceExplanations.Flagstone: Flagstone is flat stone slab used for paving, not squared wall stone.

items.question: Dehulled palay (husk/hull removed) with the bran layer still intact?

choiceExplanations.Brown rice: Correct — Brown rice is dehulled palay with the bran layer still on.
choiceExplanations.Polished rice: Polished rice has had bran and germ removed and been polished.
choiceExplanations.Parboiled rice: Parboiled rice is paddy soaked and steamed before milling, not defined by bran retention.
choiceExplanations.Milled rice: Milled rice has the bran removed.

items.question: Floor slope requirement for cattle pen.

choiceExplanations.Not less than 6 degrees: Not less than 6 degrees is steeper than the standard minimum of 3 degrees.
choiceExplanations.Not less than 10 degrees: Not less than 10 degrees is far steeper than the standard minimum of 3 degrees.
choiceExplanations.Not less than 1 degree: Not less than 1 degree is flatter than the minimum of 3 degrees and drains poorly.
choiceExplanations.Not less than 3 degrees: Correct — The floor of a cattle pen must slope not less than 3 degrees so water and waste drain away.

items.question: Wood obtained from log after slicing into various sizes.

choiceExplanations.Rough lumber: Correct — Rough lumber is wood sawn from the log into sizes but not yet planed or smoothed.
choiceExplanations.Dressed lumber: Dressed lumber is lumber already surfaced by planing; it is a later stage, not the first sawn product.
choiceExplanations.Planed lumber: Planed lumber has been smoothed by a planer, so it is further processed than just sliced from a log.
choiceExplanations.Seasoned lumber: Seasoned lumber is lumber dried to reduce moisture; it describes drying, not slicing a log.

items.question: Surface of the plywood showing veneer of higher grade than that of the back side

choiceExplanations.Face: Correct — The face is the plywood surface carrying the higher-grade veneer; the back side has a lower grade.
choiceExplanations.Back: The back is the lower-grade side, the opposite of what the question describes.
choiceExplanations.Crossband: Crossband is the veneer layer laid at right angles to the face next to the core, not an outer surface.
choiceExplanations.Core: The core is the center layer of the plywood, not a visible surface.

items.question: Recommended concrete mixing proportion for reinforced concrete.

choiceExplanations.1 : 2 : 4 or class A: Correct — The standard Class A mix for reinforced concrete is 1 cement : 2 sand : 4 gravel.
choiceExplanations.1 : 2 : 3 or class A: 1:2:3 is a richer mix than the standard Class A proportion for reinforced concrete.
choiceExplanations.1 : 1 : 3 or class A: 1:1:3 is a very rich mix, not the standard Class A proportion.
choiceExplanations.1 : 2 : 5 or class A: 1:2:5 is leaner than Class A and is not the recommended reinforced concrete mix.

items.question: Recommended concrete mixing proportion for machinery foundation

choiceExplanations.1 : 3 : 6 class c: Correct — Class C, 1 : 3 : 6, is the recommended mix for machinery foundations and other massive, lightly stressed work.
choiceExplanations.1 : 2 : 5 class c: 1:2:5 is a richer ratio than the Class C mix used for machinery foundations.
choiceExplanations.1 : 3 : 7 class c: 1:3:7 is not a standard concrete class proportion for machinery foundations.
choiceExplanations.1 : 3 : 5 class c: 1:3:5 is not the standard Class C proportion; Class C uses 6 parts gravel.

items.question: It is an aggregate for concrete with particles passing through a 5 mm sieve

choiceExplanations.All-in aggregate: All-in aggregate is an unscreened mix of fine and coarse particles, not just those passing a 5 mm sieve.
choiceExplanations.Coarse aggregate: Coarse aggregate is retained on the 5 mm sieve, the opposite of this description.
choiceExplanations.Fine aggregate: Correct — Fine aggregate (sand) is aggregate that passes the 5 mm sieve.
choiceExplanations.Lightweight aggregate: Lightweight aggregate is defined by low density (e.g., pumice), not by sieve size.

items.question: Part of structure that supports the floor joist

choiceExplanations.Purlin: A purlin is a roof member that spans between trusses to carry roof covering, not floor joists.
choiceExplanations.Girder: Correct — A girder is the main horizontal beam that supports the floor joists.
choiceExplanations.Rafter: A rafter is a sloping roof member that supports roofing, not the floor.
choiceExplanations.Lintel: A lintel is a beam over a door or window opening carrying the wall above.

items.question: It is a structural member supporting the traverse load with each end resting on a support.

choiceExplanations.Pier: A pier is a vertical support or footing element, not a member spanning between two supports.
choiceExplanations.Strut: A strut is a member carrying axial compression, usually in a truss, not transverse load.
choiceExplanations.Column: A column is a vertical member carrying axial compression, not a transverse load across a span.
choiceExplanations.Beam: Correct — A beam is a horizontal member that carries transverse loads with its ends resting on supports.

items.question: It is the effect of external forces that acts upon the structure causing the adjacent section of a member to slip from each other.

choiceExplanations.Tension: Tension is a pulling force that stretches a member, not a sliding of adjacent sections.
choiceExplanations.Compression: Compression is a pushing force that shortens a member, not a sliding action.
choiceExplanations.Shear: Correct — Shear is the force that makes adjacent sections of a member slide past each other.
choiceExplanations.Torsion: Torsion is a twisting effect about the member's axis, not a sliding of sections.

items.question: PAES recommended slope for window ledges of milking parlor to prevent accumulation of dirt, water or debris.

choiceExplanations.45 deg: Correct — PAES specifies a 45-degree slope for milking parlor window ledges so dirt, water and debris cannot collect.
choiceExplanations.50 deg: 50 degrees is not the PAES slope for window ledges; the standard is 45 degrees.
choiceExplanations.36 deg: 36 degrees is not the PAES-specified slope; the standard is 45 degrees.
choiceExplanations.40 deg: 40 degrees is not the PAES-specified slope; the standard is 45 degrees.

items.question: Minimum floor slope requirement for poultry dressing plant

choiceExplanations.4–6 %: 4–6 % is steeper than the required minimum slope for a poultry dressing plant floor.
choiceExplanations.6–8 %: 6–8 % is too steep; it is not the required floor slope for this plant.
choiceExplanations.3–5 %: 3–5 % is not the stated requirement; the standard range is 2 to 4 %.
choiceExplanations.2 to 4 %: Correct — Poultry dressing plant floors need a slope of 2 to 4 % so wash water drains to the drains.

items.question: It is an aggregate for concrete with particles retained on a 5-mm sieve.

choiceExplanations.Coarse aggregate: Correct — Coarse aggregate (gravel or crushed stone) is the part retained on the 5 mm sieve.
choiceExplanations.Lightweight aggregate: Lightweight aggregate is classified by low density, not by being retained on a 5 mm sieve.
choiceExplanations.Fine aggregate: Fine aggregate passes the 5 mm sieve, the opposite of this description.
choiceExplanations.All-in aggregate: All-in aggregate is an unseparated mix of fine and coarse particles.

items.question: A temporary boarding, sheathing, or pan used to produce the desired shape and size of concrete.

choiceExplanations.Scaffold: Scaffold is a temporary platform for workers, not a mold that shapes concrete.
choiceExplanations.Form: Correct — A form (formwork) is the temporary mold that gives fresh concrete its shape and size.
choiceExplanations.Lath: Lath is a thin strip used as a base for plaster, not a mold for concrete.
choiceExplanations.Shore: Shore is a temporary prop supporting loads, not the mold that shapes concrete.

items.question: It is a more substantial framework progressively buildup as building rises up.

choiceExplanations.Staging: Correct — Staging is the stronger framework built up progressively as the building rises (keyed answer).
choiceExplanations.Scaffolding: Scaffolding is the lighter temporary platform for workers; here it is not the keyed term for the substantial framework.
choiceExplanations.Shoring: Shoring is temporary propping to support structures or excavations, not a framework built up with the building.
choiceExplanations.Formwork: Formwork is the mold for concrete, not a framework built up as the building rises.

items.question: Standard pitch for screw conveyor.
items.answer: Pitch is equal to the diameter
choices: Pitch is equal to the diameter

choiceExplanations.Pitch is half the diameter: A pitch of half the diameter is a close-pitch conveyor, not the standard.
choiceExplanations.Pitch is equal to the diameter: Correct — A standard screw conveyor has a pitch equal to the screw diameter.
choiceExplanations.Pitch is one-third the diameter: A pitch of one-third the diameter is a short pitch used for inclined or controlled feeding, not standard.
choiceExplanations.Pitch is twice the diameter: A pitch of twice the diameter is a long pitch used for special fluid materials, not the standard.

items.question: Minimum temperature requirement in cold storage compartment of slaughterhouse.

choiceExplanations.3 C and below: 3 C is not the stated limit; slaughterhouse cold storage must be 2 C or below.
choiceExplanations.1 C and below: 1 C is lower than the stated minimum requirement, which is 2 C and below.
choiceExplanations.2 C and below: Correct — Slaughterhouse cold storage compartments must be kept at 2 C and below to keep meat safe.
choiceExplanations.4 C and below: 4 C is above the required limit; the standard is 2 C and below.

items.question: Recommended orientation of swine house
items.source: area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled; recalled 2019

choiceExplanations.Northeast-southwest direction: Northeast-southwest places a long wall to sun at an angle; it is not the recommended swine house orientation.
choiceExplanations.Northwest-southeast direction: Northwest-southeast is not the recommended orientation for a swine house.
choiceExplanations.East-west direction: Correct — Swine houses are oriented east-west so the long sides avoid direct sun and the roof can shade pens.
choiceExplanations.North-south direction: North-south puts a long side toward the afternoon sun, so it is not the recommended orientation.

items.question: The recommended dimension for warehouse with 100,000 cavans capacity

choiceExplanations.28 m x 86 m: Not the recommended value; the standard for 100,000 cavans is 25 m x 78 m.
choiceExplanations.23 m x 72 m: Not the recommended value; the standard for 100,000 cavans is 25 m x 78 m.
choiceExplanations.21 m x 66 m: Not the recommended value; that size is too small; the standard for 100,000 cavans is 25 m x 78 m.
choiceExplanations.25 m x 78 m: Correct — The recommended size for a 100,000-cavan warehouse is 25 m x 78 m.

items.question: Linear feeder space requirement for broiler 4 weeks and below

choiceExplanations.4 cm per bird or 4m/100birds: Correct — Broilers 4 weeks and below need 4 cm of linear feeder space per bird, or 4 m per 100 birds.
choiceExplanations.10 cm per bird or 10m/100birds: 10 cm per bird is more than required for young broilers.
choiceExplanations.8 cm per bird or 8m/100birds: 8 cm per bird is more than the standard for broilers 4 weeks and below.
choiceExplanations.2 cm per bird or 2m/100birds: 2 cm per bird is too little; the standard is 4 cm per bird.

items.question: Lairage: For large animals, the space requirement for loose type should be ______ per animal and ______ animal for tie-up type.

choiceExplanations.1.90 m2 and 2.80 m2: 1.90 m2 and 2.80 m2 are not the required lairage areas; the standard is 2.23 and 3.30 m2.
choiceExplanations.2.05 m2 and 3.04 m2: 2.05 m2 and 3.04 m2 are not the required lairage areas; the standard is 2.23 and 3.30 m2.
choiceExplanations.2.45 m2 and 3.63 m2: 2.45 m2 and 3.63 m2 are larger than the standard lairage areas of 2.23 and 3.30 m2.
choiceExplanations.2.23 m2 and 3.30 m2: Correct — Lairage for large animals needs 2.23 m2 for loose type and 3.30 m2 for tie-up type.

items.question: Lairage: For swine, the space requirement should be _____ per animal (if the weight is more than 100 kg) and _____ per animal (if the weight is less than 100kg).

choiceExplanations.0.6 m² and 8.6m²: 0.6 m² with 8.6 m² is not valid; the second value is far too large for a swine pen space per animal.
choiceExplanations.0.6 m² and 9.6m²: 0.6 m² with 9.6 m² is not valid; the second value is far too large for space per animal.
choiceExplanations.0.7 m² and 0.6m²: Correct — Lairage for swine needs 0.7 m² per animal above 100 kg and 0.6 m² per animal below 100 kg.
choiceExplanations.0.8 m² and 11.6m²: 0.8 m² with 11.6 m² is not valid; 11.6 m² per animal is unrealistic for swine lairage.

items.question: For workshop and machinery shed the minimum dimension of a doorway shall be ____ high and ____ wide. For bigger equipment, a clearance of 0.6 m on both sides shall be added.

choiceExplanations.3 m and 4.1 m: 4.1 m width is not the minimum doorway; the standard is 3 m high and 3.7 m wide.
choiceExplanations.3 m and 3.4 m: 3.4 m width is narrower than the specified 3.7 m minimum.
choiceExplanations.3 m and 3.7 m: Correct — A workshop or machinery shed doorway must be at least 3 m high and 3.7 m wide.
choiceExplanations.3 m and 3.1 m: 3.1 m width is narrower than the specified 3.7 m minimum.

items.question: PAES 419 Warehouse for Bagged Storage of Grains the standard pallet size should be ______

choiceExplanations.140 cm x 56 cm: 140 cm x 56 cm is not the standard pallet size in PAES 419.
choiceExplanations.129 cm x 52 cm: 129 cm x 52 cm is not the standard pallet size in PAES 419.
choiceExplanations.167 cm x 67 cm: 167 cm x 67 cm is larger than the PAES 419 standard pallet.
choiceExplanations.152 cm x 61 cm: Correct — PAES 419 specifies a standard pallet of 152 cm x 61 cm for bagged grain storage.

items.question: PAES 419 Warehouse for Bagged Storage of Grains the Optimum recommended stack heights for paddy:

choiceExplanations.18 layers at 4.57 m 12bags/m³: 18 layers at 4.57 m, 12 bags/m² is the recommended stack for wheat, barley and maize, not paddy.
choiceExplanations.20 layers at 6.5 m 18bags/m³: 20 layers at 6.5 m and 18 bags/m² is not a PAES 419 recommended paddy stack.
choiceExplanations.14 layers at 4.0 m 10bags/m³: 14 layers at 4.0 m and 10 bags/m² is not the PAES 419 optimum for paddy.
choiceExplanations.16 layers at 5.5 m 15bags/m³: Correct — PAES 419 recommends paddy stacks of 16 layers at 5.5 m height, 15 bags/m².

items.question: PAES 419 warehouse for bagged storage of grains the optimum recommended stack heights for wheat, barley and maize:

choiceExplanations.18 layers at 4.57 m 12bags/m³: Correct — For wheat, barley and maize, the optimum stack is 18 layers, 4.57 m high, 12 bags/m².
choiceExplanations.14 layers at 3.8 m 10bags/m³: 14 layers at 3.8 m is not the PAES 419 optimum for wheat, barley or maize.
choiceExplanations.20 layers at 6.0 m 16bags/m³: 20 layers at 6.0 m is not the PAES 419 optimum for these grains.
choiceExplanations.16 layers at 5.5 m 15bags/m³: 16 layers at 5.5 m, 15 bags/m² is the recommended stack for paddy, not wheat, barley or maize.

items.question: Warehouse for Bagged Storage of Grains: Space between piles shall be wide.

choiceExplanations.0.6 meter wide: Correct — Piles in a bagged-grain warehouse need a 0.6 m wide space between them for access and inspection.
choiceExplanations.0.7 meter wide: 0.7 m is not the specified width between piles; the standard is 0.6 m.
choiceExplanations.0.5 meter wide: 0.5 m is narrower than the required 0.6 m between piles.
choiceExplanations.0.4 meter wide: 0.4 m is narrower than the required 0.6 m between piles.

items.question: According to PAES 402:2001 (Agricultural Structures – Housing for Broiler Production), the width of the pen shall be about _______.
items.rationale: Under PAES 402:2001 (Housing for Broiler Production), the recommended width of a naturally ventilated broiler pen is about 10 m to 12 m to ensure adequate cross-ventilation.

choiceExplanations.10 m - 12 m: Correct — PAES 402:2001 says a broiler pen should be about 10 m to 12 m wide for good ventilation.
choiceExplanations.6 m - 8 m: 6–8 m is narrower than the PAES 402 recommended broiler pen width.
choiceExplanations.20 m - 25 m: 20–25 m is too wide for natural ventilation and is not the PAES 402 value.
choiceExplanations.15 m - 18 m: 15–18 m is wider than the PAES 402 recommended broiler pen width.

items.question: PAES 405:2001 / Agricultural Structures – Cattle Feedlot Structural requirement Concrete floors shall be skid resistant. The minimum floor thickness shall be _____ mm with 2 - 4% slope towards the drainage.

choiceExplanations.67 mm: 67 mm is not the PAES 405 minimum floor thickness for cattle feedlot floors.
choiceExplanations.76 mm: Correct — PAES 405 requires skid-resistant feedlot concrete floors at least 76 mm thick, sloped 2–4 % to drains.
choiceExplanations.99 mm: 99 mm is not the stated minimum; the standard minimum is 76 mm.
choiceExplanations.61 mm: 61 mm is thinner than the stated minimum of 76 mm.

items.question: PAES 415:2001 / Agricultural Structures - Greenhouses Walkways. If the walkway will be used only as a place to stand while servicing the benches, a minimum of ___x___ aisle shall be used for determinate crops and a minimum of ___y___ aisle for indeterminate crops.

choiceExplanations.x=0.30 m; y=0.80 m: Correct — PAES 415 requires at least 0.30 m aisle for determinate crops and 0.80 m for indeterminate crops.
choiceExplanations.x=0.28 m; y=0.74 m: x=0.28 m; y=0.74 m does not match the PAES 415 minimum aisle widths.
choiceExplanations.x=0.26 m; y=0.68 m: x=0.26 m; y=0.68 m does not match the PAES 415 minimum aisle widths.

items.question: Temperature for weaner (PAES)?

choiceExplanations.35°C: 35 C is too hot for weaners; the recommended temperature is 30 C.
choiceExplanations.20°C: 20 C is too cool for weaners; the recommended temperature is 30 C.
choiceExplanations.30°C: Correct — Weaner pigs are kept at about 30 C per PAES recommendations.
choiceExplanations.25°C: 25 C is cooler than the recommended 30 C for weaners.

items.question: Part of old farmstead where vehicles park

choiceExplanations.Apron: An apron is a paved area in front of a structure, not the keyed term for the vehicle parking part of an old farmstead.
choiceExplanations.Court: A court is an open yard area, not the keyed term for where vehicles park.
choiceExplanations.Alley: Correct — The alley is the part of the old farmstead where vehicles are parked.
choiceExplanations.Lane: A lane is a narrow path or road, not the keyed parking part of the farmstead.

items.question: Measures air in concrete and mortar

choiceExplanations.Kelly ball: A Kelly ball tests the consistency of fresh concrete by penetration, not air content.
choiceExplanations.Slump cone: A slump cone measures workability (slump) of fresh concrete, not air content.
choiceExplanations.Vicat apparatus: A Vicat apparatus measures setting time of cement, not air content.
choiceExplanations.Air meter: Correct — An air meter measures the air content of fresh concrete and mortar.

items.question: Measurement of alley for vehicles in cattle feedlot

choiceExplanations.3m: Correct — The vehicle alley in a cattle feedlot is 3 m wide.
choiceExplanations.5m: 5 m is wider than the specified feedlot vehicle alley width of 3 m.
choiceExplanations.4m: 4 m is wider than the specified feedlot vehicle alley width of 3 m.
choiceExplanations.2m: 2 m is too narrow for vehicles; the specified alley width is 3 m.

items.question: For concrete road the maximum slope of road shoulder shall be ___ from the edge of the road carriageway.

choiceExplanations.1.5%: Correct — The shoulder of a concrete road slopes at a maximum of 1.5 % away from the carriageway edge.

choiceExplanations.7 YEARS: 7 years is more than the minimum experience required of a CPES evaluator.
choiceExplanations.6 YEARS: 6 years is more than the minimum experience required of a CPES evaluator.
choiceExplanations.5 YEARS: Correct — A CPES evaluator needs at least 5 years of experience in actual project implementation.
choiceExplanations.4 YEARS: 4 years is less than the required minimum of 5 years.

items.question: (PAES: Farm to Market Road) Part of roadway next to travelled way or auxiliary lanes that provide lateral support of base and surface courses and is an emergency stopping for vehicles.

choiceExplanations.Road shoulder: Correct — The road shoulder is the strip beside the travelled way that supports the courses and serves for emergency stops.
choiceExplanations.Pavement crown: The pavement crown is the raised center of the road for drainage, not the side strip.
choiceExplanations.Roadside ditch: A roadside ditch is a drain channel along the road, not a vehicle stopping area.
choiceExplanations.Side slope: The side slope is the embankment or cut slope beyond the shoulder, not a stopping area.

items.question: (PAES 414-1: Waste Management Structure) Liquid waste storage ponds and structures shall be sized to hold all the manure, bedding, and liquid waste from animal housing, animal and crop processing plants, and contaminated runoff that can be expected during the storage period. Account for a freeboard of _____.

choiceExplanations.0.3m: Correct — PAES 414-1 requires a freeboard of 0.3 m for liquid waste storage ponds.
choiceExplanations.0.4m: 0.4 m is greater than the stated freeboard of 0.3 m.
choiceExplanations.0.5m: 0.5 m is greater than the stated freeboard of 0.3 m.
choiceExplanations.0.2m: 0.2 m is less than the stated freeboard of 0.3 m.

items.question: A term used to describe the shape of the beam having a negative bending moment.

choiceExplanations.Hogging sagging - positive bending momen: Correct — Hogging is the shape of a beam under negative bending moment; sagging is positive bending moment.
choiceExplanations.Cambering sagging - neutral bending mome: Cambering is an upward pre-curve, and sagging is positive moment, not neutral.
choiceExplanations.Sagging hogging - negative bending momen: This reverses the terms: sagging is positive bending, hogging is negative.
choiceExplanations.Buckling warping - torsional shear momen: Buckling and warping are not bending moment shapes; torsional shear moment is unrelated.

items.question: Zone planning can be a useful tool, but it is most effective when planning a new farmstead. The farmstead is divided into different zones of 10 to 30 meters wide by concentric circles. Implement and machinery storage, farm workshop is placed under

choiceExplanations.Zone 3: Zone 3 is a different zone of the farmstead, not the keyed zone for machinery storage and workshop.
choiceExplanations.Zone 4: Zone 4 is a different zone of the farmstead, not the keyed zone for machinery storage and workshop.
choiceExplanations.Zone 1: Zone 1 is the innermost zone, closest to the house, not machinery storage.
choiceExplanations.Zone 2: Correct — Per the keyed zone plan, implement and machinery storage and the farm workshop are in Zone 2.

items.question: Zone planning can be a useful tool, but it is most effective when planning a new farmstead. The farmstead is divided into different zones of 10 to 30 meters wide by concentric circles. The farm access road and courtyard area are placed under

choiceExplanations.Zone 3: Zone 3 is not the keyed zone for the access road and courtyard.
choiceExplanations.Zone 6: Zone 6 is not the keyed zone for the access road and courtyard.
choiceExplanations.Zone 5: Correct — Per the keyed zone plan, the farm access road and courtyard fall in Zone 5.
choiceExplanations.Zone 4: Zone 4 is not the keyed zone for the access road and courtyard.

items.question: (PAES 415: Agricultural Structures Greenhouse) The height of the greenhouse should be sufficient for the operation of machinery and the comfort of the workers. Gutter heights of ___ are recommended for multi-span houses to allow machines to move freely.

choiceExplanations.2.8m-3.0m: Correct — PAES 415 recommends gutter heights of 2.8–3.0 m for multi-span greenhouses so machines can move freely.
choiceExplanations.2.8m-2.0m: 2.8–2.0 m is not a valid range, since the upper value is less than the lower.
choiceExplanations.3.8m-4.0m: 3.8–4.0 m is taller than the recommended gutter height range.
choiceExplanations.2.8m-4.0m: 2.8–4.0 m is too wide a range and is not the PAES-recommended gutter height.

items.question: PAES 420: Farm workshop and Machinery Shed, states that the minimum clear height from the floor to the truss shall be at least 3 meters. For machines higher than 3 meters, the height shall be the sum of the machine height plus

choiceExplanations.0.4m: 0.4 m is not the PAES 420 added clearance above machine height.
choiceExplanations.0.5m: 0.5 m is not the PAES 420 added clearance above machine height.
choiceExplanations.0.2m: 0.2 m is less than the PAES 420 added clearance of 0.3 m.
choiceExplanations.0.3m: Correct — For machines taller than 3 m, the clear height is machine height plus 0.3 m.

items.question: In the National Building Code of the Philippines, Agricultural Structure belongs to what group?

choiceExplanations.Group i: Group I covers institutional occupancies, not agricultural structures.
choiceExplanations.Group h: Group H covers assembly occupancies such as theaters, not agricultural structures.
choiceExplanations.Group j: Correct — Agricultural structures such as barns and silos belong to Group J in the National Building Code.
choiceExplanations.Group f: Group F covers industrial occupancies, not agricultural structures.

items.question: A concrete column of an agricultural building has 35 cm × 30 cm side dimensions. It uses 16 mm longitudinal bars and 10 mm lateral ties. What should be the maximum lateral tie spacing based on vertical bar diameter complying with the American Concrete Institute (ACI) standard?
items.rationale: Under the ACI Code, lateral tie spacing must not exceed the least of 16 × vertical bar diameter (16 × 1.6 cm = 25.6 cm), 48 × tie diameter (48 cm), or the least column dimension (30 cm), so 25.6 cm governs.

choiceExplanations.20.6 cm: 20.6 cm does not equal 16 times the 16 mm bar diameter.
choiceExplanations.26.5 cm: 26.5 cm does not equal 16 times the 16 mm bar diameter.
choiceExplanations.30.5 cm: 30.5 cm is not 16 times the bar diameter; it is not the limit from the vertical bars.
choiceExplanations.25.6 cm: Correct — ACI limits tie spacing to 16 times the longitudinal bar diameter: 16 × 16 mm = 256 mm = 25.6 cm.

items.question: Compare 1-lane and 2-lane regular farm-to-market roads (FMRs). If the carriageway and 1-side shoulder for a 1-lane road are 2.5 m and 0.75 m, respectively, how wide are the minimum carriageway and 1-side shoulder for a regular 2-lane road, respectively?
items.rationale: According to Philippine farm-to-market road design standards (PAES 421), a regular 2-lane FMR requires a minimum carriageway width of 5.0 m and a 1-side shoulder width of 1.5 m.

choiceExplanations.5.0 and 1.5 m: Correct — A regular 2-lane FMR has a 5.0 m carriageway (2 × 2.5 m) and 1.5 m shoulders per side as keyed.
choiceExplanations.3.0 and 1.0 m: 3.0 m and 1.0 m are too narrow to carry two lanes.
choiceExplanations.3.0 and 0.75 m: A 3.0 m carriageway is too narrow for two lanes, and the shoulder is not 0.75 m.
choiceExplanations.2.5 and 0.75 m: 2.5 m and 0.75 m are the 1-lane values given, not the 2-lane values.

items.question: What device should be installed in the water pipeline in both marine and freshwater fish hatcheries if water for placement in the algal laboratory needs to be disinfected?
items.rationale: A UV water sterilizer is installed in fish hatchery water pipelines to effectively disinfect water entering the algal laboratory without introducing chemical residues harmful to algal cultures.

choiceExplanations.Sand filter: A sand filter removes particles but does not disinfect water.
choiceExplanations.Sand and charcoal filter: A sand and charcoal filter removes particles and some chemicals but does not kill microbes.
choiceExplanations.Electric water sterilizer: An electric water sterilizer is not the standard disinfection device named for algal lab water.
choiceExplanations.UV water sterilizer: Correct — A UV water sterilizer disinfects water by killing microorganisms with ultraviolet light.

items.question: A group of student immersion workers is assisting you at the municipal agricultural office where you work as an AB engineer. One day, one of the students asks what the minimum space requirement is for a boar pen because his father plans to build one for three boars. What should your answer be?
items.rationale: Based on PAES 401:2001 (Housing for Swine Production), the minimum space requirement for a boar pen is 7.50 m²/animal, so three boars require 7.50 m²/boar × 3 boars = 22.5 sq. m.

choiceExplanations.22.5 sq. m: Correct — A boar pen needs 7.5 m² per boar, so 3 boars need 22.5 m².
choiceExplanations.2.50 m: 2.50 m is a length, not a floor area, and does not fit three boars.
choiceExplanations.7.5 sq. m: 7.5 sq. m is the space for one boar, not three.
choiceExplanations.7.50 m: 7.50 m is a length, not an area.

items.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the standard specifications of the general and structural requirements of a slaughterhouse for ruminants?
items.answer: The slaughterhouse shall be located at least 100 m away from the river bank.
items.rationale: Based on PNS/BAFS PABES 306:2020 (Slaughterhouse for Ruminants), the slaughterhouse shall be located at least 10 m (not 100 m) away from the river bank, whereas the 28 sq. m slaughtering area, 20 sq. m offal cleaning area, and 200 m setback from habitation and highways are standard specifications.
choices: The slaughterhouse shall be located at least 100 m away from the river bank.
The minimum size of the offal cleaning area for small and large ruminants is 20 sq. meters.
The minimum size of the slaughtering area for small and large ruminants is 28 sq. meters.
The slaughterhouse shall be located at least 200 m away from any building used for human habitation, national highway, public or commercial buildings/places, and any animal production facilities.

choiceExplanations.The slaughterhouse shall be located at l: Correct — This statement is NOT true, since the keyed standard distance from a river bank is not 100 m.
choiceExplanations.The minimum size of the offal cleaning a: This is true: the offal cleaning area minimum for ruminants is 20 sq. m, so it cannot be the NOT-true statement.
choiceExplanations.The minimum size of the slaughtering are: This is true: the slaughtering area minimum for ruminants is 28 sq. m.
choiceExplanations.The slaughterhouse shall be located at l: This is true: the slaughterhouse is at least 200 m from habitation, highways and public places.

items.question: A company assigned you as the safety engineer in a grain processing plant. A round steel bar having a cross-sectional area of 25 square mm and design working tensile stress of 403 MPa is suspending a 4.905 kN wheat grain while the silo for its storage is being opened. Applying your knowledge in strength of materials, what is the factor of safety and is it safe from breakage?
items.rationale: Actual tensile stress is P / A = 4,905 N / 25 mm² = 196.2 MPa, giving a factor of safety FS = 403 MPa / 196.2 MPa = 2.05. Since FS > 1.0, the steel bar is safe from breakage.

choiceExplanations.1.05, unsafe: 1.05 is wrong; the stress is 196.2 MPa, so FS is 2.05, not 1.05.
choiceExplanations.2.25, safe: 2.25 is miscalculated; FS = 403 divided by 196.2 gives 2.05.
choiceExplanations.2.05, safe: Correct — Stress = 4905 N ÷ 25 mm² = 196.2 MPa; FS = 403 ÷ 196.2 = 2.05, which is greater than 1, so safe.
choiceExplanations.1.09, unsafe: 1.09 and unsafe are wrong; FS is above 1, so the bar is safe.

items.question: If you are to design a primary processing plant for fresh fruit and vegetable strictly based on standards, how will you design the floor intersection with the wall?
items.rationale: Based on PAES 418:2002 (Primary Processing Plant for Fresh Fruit and Vegetable), the floor intersection with the wall shall be coved with a 50 mm - 60 mm radius to allow easy cleaning and prevent dirt buildup.

choiceExplanations.Cornered with 40 mm - 50 mm radius: A cornered junction is hard to clean; the standard requires a coved one.
choiceExplanations.Coved with 40 mm - 50 mm radius: Coved is correct, but a 40–50 mm radius is not the standard value.
choiceExplanations.Cornered with 50 mm - 60 mm radius: A cornered junction is hard to clean and not the standard.
choiceExplanations.Coved with 50 mm - 60 mm radius: Correct — Floor-wall junctions in food plants are coved with a 50–60 mm radius so they are easy to clean.

items.question: Based on the standard of the American Concrete Institute, the minimum lateral ties spacing based on vertical bar diameter can be simply paraphrased as equal to the vertical bar diameter multiplied by ___.
items.rationale: Under American Concrete Institute (ACI 318) standards for tied columns, maximum lateral tie spacing shall not exceed 16 times the longitudinal (vertical) bar diameter, 48 times the tie bar diameter, or the least dimension of the column.

choiceExplanations.16: Correct — ACI sets maximum tie spacing as 16 times the vertical bar diameter.
choiceExplanations.32: 32 is not the ACI multiplier for vertical bar diameter; it is not the tie spacing rule.
choiceExplanations.36: 36 is not the ACI multiplier for vertical bar diameter.
choiceExplanations.48: 48 applies to the tie bar diameter (48 × tie diameter), not the vertical bar diameter.

items.question: In building a primary processing plant for fresh vegetable, how far must the windowsill be from the finish floor line?
items.rationale: Based on PAES 418:2002 (Primary Processing Plant for Fresh Fruit and Vegetable), the windowsill shall be located at least 1 m above the finish floor line.

choiceExplanations.1 m: 1 m is the keyed minimum, but it is stated here without the phrase 'at least'; the keyed answer is the longer option.
choiceExplanations.At least 1.5 m: The windowsill must be at least 1 m high, not 1.5 m.
choiceExplanations.At least 1.25 m: The windowsill must be at least 1 m high, not 1.25 m.
choiceExplanations.At least 1 m: Correct — The windowsill must be at least 1 m above the finished floor line.

items.question: You are assigned to implement a sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) silo project for bioprocessing. During peak production months, a maximum of 10 tonnes of dried shelled grain needs to be stored in a cylindrical silo. What should be the silo volume in cubic meters if dried grain samples electronically registered an average bulk density of 536 kg/cu.m. at 9.7% moisture content wet basis?
items.rationale: Converting 10 tonnes to 10,000 kg and dividing by the bulk density yields V = mass / bulk density = 10,000 kg / 536 kg/m³ = 18.66 m³ ≈ 18.7 m³.

choiceExplanations.18.7: Correct — Volume = mass ÷ bulk density = 10,000 kg ÷ 536 kg/m³ = 18.7 m³.
choiceExplanations.8.7: 8.7 m³ is wrong arithmetic; 10,000 divided by 536 is about 18.7.
choiceExplanations.17.8: 17.8 m³ is a transposed digit error of the correct 18.7 m³.
choiceExplanations.7.8: 7.8 m³ is wrong arithmetic; the volume is 18.7 m³.

items.question: Based on PAES, what is the recommended maximum length of a greenhouse?
items.rationale: Based on PAES 415:2001 (Agricultural Structures – Greenhouses), the length of a greenhouse should not exceed 50 m to maintain proper ventilation and environmental control.

choiceExplanations.80 m: 80 m exceeds the PAES recommended maximum greenhouse length.
choiceExplanations.30 m: 30 m is shorter than the PAES maximum; the recommended limit is 50 m.
choiceExplanations.60 m: 60 m exceeds the PAES recommended maximum greenhouse length of 50 m.
choiceExplanations.50 m: Correct — PAES recommends a maximum greenhouse length of 50 m.

items.question: A simply supported beam, 4-meter long, weighs 250 kg per meter. The maximum live load it carries is 200 half sacks of milled rice. Each full sack weighs 50 kg. What is the weight that is supported by each of the 2 columns at both ends?
items.rationale: Total load equals Dead load (4 m × 250 kg/m = 1,000 kg) plus Live load (200 half sacks × 25 kg/half sack = 5,000 kg) = 6,000 kg. Divided equally between the 2 end columns, each column supports 6,000 kg / 2 = 3,000 kg.

choiceExplanations.3,000 kg: Correct — Total load = beam 4 × 250 = 1,000 kg + live 200 × 25 kg = 5,000 kg = 6,000 kg; each column carries half, 3,000 kg.
choiceExplanations.150 kg: 150 kg is far too low; it ignores most of the beam and live load.
choiceExplanations.30,000 kg: 30,000 kg is ten times too high; it is a decimal error.
choiceExplanations.1,500 kg: 1,500 kg is too low; it would be half of only 3,000 kg of load.

items.question: If PERT means Project Evaluation and Review Technique, CPES means ________________.
items.rationale: In Philippine construction project management and government procurement guidelines (CIAP/GPPB), CPES stands for Constructors' Performance Evaluation System.

choiceExplanations.Construction Performance Evaluation Syst: CPES is for Constructors, not 'Construction', so this wording is wrong.
choiceExplanations.Constructor’s Performance Evaluation Sys: This is the same name as the keyed answer but with a different apostrophe spelling; the keyed form is the plural possessive Constructors'.
choiceExplanations.Constructors' Performance Evaluation Sys: Correct — CPES stands for Constructors' Performance Evaluation System, which rates contractors' performance.
choiceExplanations.Construction Project Evaluation System: CPES does not stand for Construction Project Evaluation System.

items.question: As a registered AB Engineer, you are tasked to carry out the design of a large-capacity food storage. What food storage material will you use such that the food storage chamber is durable, stain-resistant and eco-friendly?
items.rationale: Food-grade stainless steel is non-reactive, highly durable, stain- and corrosion-resistant, hygienic for large-capacity food storage, and fully recyclable.

choiceExplanations.PVC: PVC is a plastic that can leach chemicals and stain, so it is not the best durable, stain-resistant, eco-friendly choice.
choiceExplanations.Glass: Glass is stain-resistant but brittle and heavy, so it is not best for large-capacity storage.
choiceExplanations.HDPE: HDPE is a plastic that scratches and can absorb stains or odors, and is less durable than steel.
choiceExplanations.Stainless steel: Correct — Stainless steel is durable, resists stains and corrosion and is recyclable, so it suits large food storage.

items.question: Applying mechanics, determine the moment exerted at the supported end of a 3-meter cantilever beam weighing 1.96 kN per meter. The design maximum live load it will carry is approximately 4.9 kN of grains lifted by a pulley at the unsupported end of the beam.
items.rationale: Dead-load moment is wL²/2 = 1.96 kN/m × (3 m)² / 2 = 8.82 kN·m, and live-load moment is P × L = 4.9 kN × 3 m = 14.7 kN·m. Total fixed-end moment is 8.82 + 14.7 = 23.52 kN·m (listed as 23.5 kN in the choices).

choiceExplanations.53.2 kN: 53.2 kN overstates the moment; it is not the sum of the correct terms.
choiceExplanations.23.5 kN: Correct — M = (1.96 × 3)(3/2) + 4.9 × 3 = 8.82 + 14.7 = 23.5 kN·m at the fixed support.
choiceExplanations.16 mm: 16 mm is a length unit, not a moment in kN.
choiceExplanations.25.3 kN: 25.3 kN does not match the calculation; the correct moment is 23.5 kN·m.

items.question: When evaluating a grain silo for compliance with PNS/BAFS PABES 270:2019, you are required to verify its volumetric capacity. Based on the standard, which document must you consult to determine the correct method for calculating this capacity?
items.rationale: PNS/BAFS PABES 270:2019 specifies that the volumetric capacity of a cylindrical grain silo shall be determined using the method stated in ASAE S413.1:1997.

choiceExplanations.ASAE S412.1:1997: ASAE S412.1:1997 is a different ASAE standard and is not the one for grain bin capacity calculation.
choiceExplanations.PNS/PAES 419:2015: PNS/PAES 419:2015 covers warehouses for bagged grain, not silo volume calculation.
choiceExplanations.ASAE S413.1:1997: Correct — The silo standard refers to ASAE S413.1:1997 for the method of computing bin volumetric capacity.
choiceExplanations.PNS/BAFS 193:2017: PNS/BAFS 193:2017 is a different Philippine standard, not the one cited for silo capacity method.

items.question: You are commissioned to design a machinery shed to house a pickup truck (W = 2.3 m, H = 2.1 m, L = 6 m) and a two-plow tractor (W = 2.3 m, H = 1.5 m, L = 3.7 m). Given the space requirements of the truck and tractor, what is the total required area for the machinery shed?
items.rationale: Per PAES 420:2002 (Farm Workshop and Machinery Shed), add 0.6 m clearance to each machine's width and length: tractor area = (2.3 + 0.6) × (3.7 + 0.6) = 12.47 m² and pickup truck area = (2.3 + 0.6) × (6.0 + 0.6) = 19.14 m², for a total of 12.47 + 19.14 = 31.61 sq. m.

choiceExplanations.28.61 sq. m: 28.61 sq. m does not match the keyed total space requirement.
choiceExplanations.22.31 sq. m: 22.31 sq. m is only the footprint of the two machines (13.8 + 8.51) without clearance allowances.
choiceExplanations.31.61 sq. m: Correct — The keyed total of 31.61 sq. m is the machine areas plus the required clearances and space allowance.
choiceExplanations.34.31 sq. m: 34.31 sq. m is more than the keyed total required area.

items.question: A poultry house requires stable temperatures between 24–28 C. You must select a control method that automatically adjusts ventilation fans based on measured temperature. Which control strategy would best meet this requirement?
items.answer: PID controller with variable-speed fan drive (VFD)
items.rationale: A PID controller with a variable-frequency drive (VFD) continuously modulates fan speed based on real-time temperature feedback, maintaining tight thermal stability inside the 24–28 °C band without the abrupt swings of on–off or timer controls.
choices: Manual fan switches operated by staff
Timers that switch fans at fixed intervals
PID controller with variable-speed fan drive (VFD)

choiceExplanations.Manual fan switches operated by staff: Manual switches are not automatic and depend on staff attention.
choiceExplanations.Timers that switch fans at fixed interva: Timers switch fans on a schedule, not according to measured temperature.
choiceExplanations.On–off thermostat controlling single-spe: An on-off thermostat reacts to temperature but causes larger swings than smooth speed control.
choiceExplanations.PID controller with variable-speed fan d: Correct — A PID controller with a variable-speed drive adjusts fan speed smoothly to hold temperature steady.

items.question: Explain thermal conductivity by completing the following sentence: Thermal conductivity strongly depends on the _______ of the bioprocessed material.
items.rationale: Thermal conductivity of agricultural and biological materials depends strongly on moisture content (water conducts heat better than air), temperature, and material structure/porosity.

choiceExplanations.Moisture, temperature and material struc: Correct — Thermal conductivity of bioprocessed materials depends on moisture, temperature and material structure together.
choiceExplanations.Material structure: Material structure alone is incomplete; moisture and temperature also matter.
choiceExplanations.Temperature: Temperature alone is incomplete; moisture and structure also affect conductivity.
choiceExplanations.Moisture: Moisture alone is incomplete; temperature and structure also affect conductivity.

items.question: You are assigned to carry out the design of a farm-to-market road applying the PAES 289:2009 standard. In your design, what should be the minimum carriageway and shoulder widths, respectively, for a one-lane regular concrete farm-to-market road?
items.rationale: Under PAES 289:2009 (Farm-to-Market Roads), the minimum carriageway width for a one-lane regular concrete farm-to-market road is 2.5 m with a minimum shoulder width of 0.75 m.

choiceExplanations.3.0 and 1.0 m: 3.0 and 1.0 m are wider than the minimum for a one-lane regular concrete FMR.
choiceExplanations.2 and 1 m: 2 and 1 m are not the PAES minimums; the carriageway is narrower than required.
choiceExplanations.3.0 and 0.75 m: 3.0 and 0.75 m use the wrong carriageway width for a one-lane regular road.
choiceExplanations.2.5 and 0.75 m: Correct — A one-lane regular concrete FMR has a 2.5 m carriageway and 0.75 m shoulder per side.

items.question: You are the head of a project management team assigned to organize the construction of all structures of a marine fish hatchery project. What method will you use to minimize construction time?
items.rationale: PERT-CPM integrates probabilistic activity time estimation (PERT) with critical path scheduling and crashing analysis (CPM) to optimize schedules and minimize total construction duration.

choiceExplanations.CPES: CPES is a contractor performance rating system, not a method to minimize construction time.
choiceExplanations.PERT: PERT alone estimates project time using probabilities but does not optimize cost-time trade-off.
choiceExplanations.PERT-CPM: Correct — PERT-CPM combines time estimation and critical path analysis to plan and shorten construction time.
choiceExplanations.CPM: CPM alone finds the critical path but lacks PERT's probabilistic time estimates in the keyed answer.

items.question: You are tasked to evaluate an existing vermicomposting project. Its cages are sized 0.8 m x 0.8 m each. The cage walls are made of banana stems. Each cage is hidden from direct and indirect sunlight. What cage improvement is needed?
items.answer: Cage walls should not be edible to vermi worms
items.rationale: Banana stems are organic and edible to vermi worms, which will eat away the enclosure walls; cage walls should instead be made of non-edible, durable materials while keeping the bed shaded from sunlight.
choices: Cage walls should not be edible to vermi worms
Cage should be exposed to sunlight
Cage walls should be coconut fronds
Cage size should be 1 m x 1 m

choiceExplanations.Cage walls should not be edible to vermi: Correct — Banana stems are edible to worms, so the cage walls should be made of material the worms cannot eat.
choiceExplanations.Cage should be exposed to sunlight: Worms avoid sunlight; the cage should stay shaded, so exposing it would harm them.
choiceExplanations.Cage walls should be coconut fronds: Coconut fronds are not named as the needed improvement; the issue is edible walls, not the frond type.
choiceExplanations.Cage size should be 1 m x 1 m: A 1 m x 1 m size is not the issue; the 0.8 m cage size is acceptable.

items.question: Determine the laboratory area in square meters required for a bioprocessing plant with 6 laboratory employees based on existing ABE standards.
items.rationale: Using the standard laboratory space requirement of 20 m² per employee, the total required area is 20 m²/employee × 6 employees = 120 m².

choiceExplanations.20: 20 sq. m is too small for the keyed standard for a bioprocessing lab with 6 employees.
choiceExplanations.50: 50 sq. m is below the keyed standard for 6 lab employees.
choiceExplanations.150: 150 sq. m is more than the keyed standard for 6 lab employees.
choiceExplanations.120: Correct — Based on the keyed ABE standard, a lab for 6 employees needs 120 sq. m (20 sq. m per employee).

items.question: You are consulted in designing a cylindrical grain bin or silo. What is the bin diameter if the target level full volume is 700 standard US bushels and the eave height is 5 meters?
items.rationale: Converting 700 US bushels to volume (700 bu × 0.03524 m³/bu = 24.67 m³) and using V = (π/4)D²h with h = 5 m gives D = √(4 × 24.67 / (π × 5)) = 2.51 m ≈ 2.5 m.

choiceExplanations.3.0 m: 3.0 m would give a volume larger than 700 bushels at 5 m height.
choiceExplanations.1.5 m: 1.5 m would give a volume much smaller than 700 bushels.
choiceExplanations.2.5 m: Correct — 700 US bushels is about 24.7 m³; with a 5 m height, diameter ≈ 2.5 m (area 4.9 m² × 5 m).
choiceExplanations.2.0 m: 2.0 m would give only about 15.7 m³, below 700 bushels.

items.question: Examine the different review and evaluation methods in project management. Which one is effective for construction projects?
items.rationale: Combining PERT (for uncertain activity durations) and CPM (for critical path identification and time-cost optimization) provides the most effective planning and control framework for construction projects.

choiceExplanations.CPM: CPM alone does not capture time uncertainty; the keyed answer is the combination.
choiceExplanations.CPES: CPES rates contractor performance; it is not a scheduling method.
choiceExplanations.Combination of PERT and CPM: Correct — The combined PERT-CPM method is effective for construction projects, giving both time estimates and critical path.
choiceExplanations.PERT: PERT alone handles time uncertainty but lacks the critical path cost control of CPM.

items.question: Ampere capacity of AWG no. 12 wire

choiceExplanations.18 amperes: 18 amperes is not the rated capacity of AWG no. 12 wire.
choiceExplanations.20 amperes: Correct — AWG no. 12 copper wire has an ampacity of about 20 amperes.
choiceExplanations.16 amperes: 16 amperes is not the rated capacity of AWG no. 12 wire.
choiceExplanations.22 amperes: 22 amperes is not the rated capacity of AWG no. 12 wire.

items.question: The ability of the wire or conductor to carry the current without overheating

choiceExplanations.Resistivity: Resistivity is a material's opposition to current flow, not its current-carrying limit.
choiceExplanations.Impedance: Impedance is total opposition to AC current, not the heat-safe current limit.
choiceExplanations.Ampacity: Correct — Ampacity is the maximum current a conductor can carry without overheating.
choiceExplanations.Conductivity: Conductivity is how well a material passes current, not the safe current limit.

items.question: It is the internal resistance per unit area that results from external force

choiceExplanations.Shear modulus: Shear modulus is a material constant relating shear stress to strain, not internal resistance per unit area.
choiceExplanations.Elastic limit: Elastic limit is the maximum stress before permanent deformation, not the stress itself.
choiceExplanations.Unit strain: Unit strain is deformation per unit length, not resistance per unit area.
choiceExplanations.Unit stress: Correct — Unit stress is the internal resisting force per unit area caused by an external force.

items.question: Stresses tending to cause two contiguous parts of a body to slide, relative to each other in a direction parallel to the plane of contact

choiceExplanations.Shearing stress: Correct — Shearing stress acts parallel to the contact plane and tends to make parts slide past each other.
choiceExplanations.Compressive stress: Compressive stress pushes parts together, perpendicular to the plane.
choiceExplanations.Tensile stress: Tensile stress pulls parts apart, perpendicular to the plane.
choiceExplanations.Bearing stress: Bearing stress is the contact pressure between two surfaces, not a sliding stress.

items.question: Recommended size of branch circuit for general-purpose circuit

choiceExplanations.16 amp branch circuit: 16 amp is not a standard branch circuit rating.
choiceExplanations.15 amp branch circuit: Correct — The recommended general-purpose branch circuit is 15 amperes.
choiceExplanations.14 amp branch circuit: 14 amp is not a standard branch circuit rating.

items.question: Recommended size of branch circuit for small appliance circuit

choiceExplanations.16 amp branch circuit: 16 amp is not a standard branch circuit rating.
choiceExplanations.22 amp branch circuit: 22 amp is not a standard branch circuit rating.

choiceExplanations.18 amp branch circuit: 18 amp is not a standard branch circuit rating.

items.question: Chair of the current Board of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering:

items.question: A type of fault that occurs when there is an erratic flow of current in the conductors

choiceExplanations.Line Fault: A line fault is a short or open in a line conductor, not an erratic arcing current.
choiceExplanations.Ground Fault: A ground fault is current leaking to ground, not an erratic arcing flow.
choiceExplanations.Bolted Fault: A bolted fault is a solid short circuit with very low impedance, not an erratic flow.
choiceExplanations.Arc Fault: Correct — An arc fault is an unintended, erratic arcing discharge of current in the conductors.

items.question: It is a device that opens a circuit whenever it detects a ground fault.

choiceExplanations.Mccb: An MCCB is a molded case circuit breaker for overcurrent, not specifically ground-fault sensing.
choiceExplanations.Ocpd: An OCPD is any overcurrent protection device, not one that senses ground fault.
choiceExplanations.Gcfi: Correct — A GFCI trips the circuit when it senses current leaking to ground.
choiceExplanations.Afci: An AFCI detects arc faults, not ground faults.

items.question: How much is the maximum allowable resistance of a grounding electrode?

choiceExplanations.20 ohms: 20 ohms is not the code limit; the maximum allowed is 25 ohms.
choiceExplanations.28 ohms: 28 ohms is above the maximum allowed of 25 ohms.
choiceExplanations.22 ohms: 22 ohms is not the code limit; the maximum allowed is 25 ohms.

items.question: Electric motors can ____the power factor in a system.
items.rationale: Induction motors, the most common motors on farms and plants, draw lagging magnetizing current and lower (decrease) the system power factor, especially when lightly loaded.

choiceExplanations.Eliminate: Wrong — motors do not eliminate power factor; every AC load has one.
choiceExplanations.Increase: Wrong — only over-excited synchronous motors raise power factor; ordinary induction motors lower it.
choiceExplanations.Reverse: Wrong — motors do not reverse power factor; they make it more lagging.
choiceExplanations.Decrease: Correct — induction motors draw lagging magnetizing current, which decreases the system power factor.

items.question: Majority of the energy consumed by incandescent light bulbs is converted into

choiceExplanations.Chemical and magnetic energy: Incandescent bulbs do not convert energy mainly to chemical or magnetic energy.
choiceExplanations.Heat and infrared radiation: Correct — Most incandescent bulb energy becomes heat and infrared radiation, with little visible light.
choiceExplanations.Acoustic and mechanical vibration: Acoustic and mechanical vibration is negligible in a bulb.
choiceExplanations.Visible and ultraviolet radiation: Visible light is only a small share; most energy is not visible and UV.

items.question: Which is an assumption that should be considered when solving problems using the OHM's LAW?
items.answer: Resistors have constant resistance (at constant temperature); in simple circuit problems, connecting conductors are also assumed to have negligible resistance.
items.rationale: [Merged & Verified both assumptions]
choices: Resistors have constant resistance (at constant temperature); in simple circuit problems, connecting conductors are also assumed to have negligible resistance.
Inductors have zero impedance (at constant current); in simple circuit problems, connecting conductors are considered t
Capacitors have constant reactance (at constant frequency); in simple circuit problems, connecting conductors are also i
Resistors have variable resistance (at varying voltage); in simple circuit problems, connecting conductors are treated a

choiceExplanations.Resistors have constant resistance (at c: Correct — Ohm's law assumes constant resistance at constant temperature and negligible resistance in connecting wires.
choiceExplanations.Inductors have zero impedance (at consta: Inductors do not have zero impedance; they oppose AC current, so this is not an Ohm's law assumption.
choiceExplanations.Capacitors have constant reactance (at c: Capacitors' reactance varies with frequency and is not an Ohm's law assumption for resistive circuits.
choiceExplanations.Resistors have variable resistance (at v: Ohm's law requires constant, not variable, resistance.

items.question: A moisture meter that determines the moisture content of the product based on the ability of current to pass through the material.

choiceExplanations.Dielectric type meter: A dielectric type meter measures the material's dielectric properties, not current flow.
choiceExplanations.Resistance type meter: Correct — A resistance type meter reads moisture from how easily electric current passes through the material.
choiceExplanations.Capacitance type meter: A capacitance type meter measures the material's capacitance, not current passing through it.
choiceExplanations.Infrared type meter: An infrared type meter uses light absorption, not electric current.

items.question: An electricity-operated device commonly used for automatic bagging of grains or feeds

choiceExplanations.Pressure switch: A pressure switch senses fluid or air pressure, not weight for bagging.
choiceExplanations.Proximity sensor: A proximity sensor detects an object nearby, not the weight of bagged product.
choiceExplanations.Limit switch: A limit switch detects position or travel, not weight.
choiceExplanations.Load cell: Correct — A load cell converts weight into an electrical signal, so it controls automatic bagging by weight.

items.question: It is the electrical pressure of a circuit

choiceExplanations.Resistance: Resistance opposes current flow; it is not the electrical pressure.
choiceExplanations.Voltage: Correct — Voltage is the electrical pressure (potential difference) that drives current in a circuit.
choiceExplanations.Capacitance: Capacitance is the ability to store charge, not electrical pressure.
choiceExplanations.Current: Current is the flow of charge, not the pressure that causes it.

items.question: A method of determining the properties of air which measures the electrical resistance of a film of moisture- / absorbing materials exposed to the gas

choiceExplanations.Dew-point hygrometer: A dew-point hygrometer cools a surface to find the dew point, not resistance of a film.
choiceExplanations.Hair hygrometer: A hair hygrometer uses hair length change, not electrical resistance.
choiceExplanations.Electric hygrometer: Correct — An electric hygrometer senses humidity from the electrical resistance of a moisture-absorbing film.
choiceExplanations.Sling psychrometer: A sling psychrometer uses wet and dry bulb thermometers, not resistance.

items.question: The siemens or mhos is a measure of what property of / AB material.

choiceExplanations.Electrical Conductance: Correct — The siemens (mho) is the unit of electrical conductance, the inverse of resistance.
choiceExplanations.Electrical Capacitance: Capacitance is measured in farads, not siemens.
choiceExplanations.Electrical Inductance: Inductance is measured in henrys, not siemens.
choiceExplanations.Electrical Resistance: Resistance is measured in ohms; the siemens is its reciprocal.

items.question: Reduced voltage in certain areas which may result in flickering of lights and/or damage to equipment appliance.

choiceExplanations.Blackout: A blackout is a total loss of power, not a reduced voltage.
choiceExplanations.Underfrequency: Underfrequency is low system frequency, not low voltage.
choiceExplanations.Brownout: Correct — A brownout is a drop in voltage that makes lights flicker and can damage equipment.
choiceExplanations.Overvoltage: Overvoltage is voltage that is too high, the opposite of reduced voltage.

items.question: Coverts DC to AC

choiceExplanations.Transformer: A transformer changes voltage level of AC, not DC to AC.

choiceExplanations.Alternator: An alternator generates AC from mechanical motion, not by converting DC.

choiceExplanations.Inertia: Inertia is resistance to a change in motion, not a force produced by a motor.

choiceExplanations.Exciter: An exciter supplies field current, not the part that generates the power.

choiceExplanations.Stator: The stator is the stationary part of the generator and is not the keyed part.

choiceExplanations.Balance of payments: Balance of payments records all international transactions, not a ratio.

items.question: Part of planter that is always present in all planters regardless of types and cropping system.

choiceExplanations.Press wheel: A press wheel firms the soil but is not present in every planter.

items.question: How many sprinklers with spacing of 7 m x 7 m are needed to irrigate a rectangular piece of land 125 m x 190 m if the laterals are set parallel to the longer side of the field?

items.question: A crop which is planted in short duration before the crop is to be harvested

choiceExplanations.Catch crop: A catch crop is a fast-growing crop planted between main crops, not planted before harvest.
choiceExplanations.Relay crop: Correct — A relay crop is planted shortly before the standing crop is harvested.
choiceExplanations.Ratoon crop: A ratoon crop regrows from the stubble after harvest, not planted.
choiceExplanations.Cover crop: A cover crop protects soil and is not defined by planting before harvest.

items.question: It is the unit of power equivalent to that of raising a mass of 75 kilograms against the earth’s gravitational force over a distance of one meter in one second.

items.question: In measuring distance between two points with an obstruction, what should be the method/s to be used?

choiceExplanations.Sway: Sway is not a method for measuring distance.

items.question: is a variation of the three-phase induction motor, designed to provide high starting torque for loads with high inertia, while requiring very low current.

items.question: You are evaluating a functional processing machine based on Kick’s law. From a series of tests, an average of 3 kWh was required to reduce a material from 5 mm to 2 mm diameter. Using Kick’s law, what is the expected energy consumption if the diameter of the same material is to be reduced from 5 mm to 0.5 mm?

choiceExplanations.7 kWh: 7 kWh is too low; Kick's law E = C ln(d1/d2) gives about 7.5 kWh, which rounds to 8.
choiceExplanations.9 kWh: 9 kWh is too high; the Kick's law result is about 7.5 kWh.
choiceExplanations.6 kWh: 6 kWh is too low; it ignores the larger size reduction ratio of 10.
choiceExplanations.8 kWh: Correct — Kick's law: 3 = C ln(5/2), so C = 3.27; E = 3.27 ln(5/0.5) = 7.5, about 8 kWh.

items.question: You are to implement the optimization of a meat cold storage facility which has a current utilization coefficient of 0.43. If the utilization coefficient is increased to 0.53, what is the effect in operating cost?

choiceExplanations.Fluctuate: Cost does not fluctuate randomly; a higher utilization coefficient raises the load, so cost changes in one direction.
choiceExplanations.Increase: Correct — A higher utilization coefficient means more refrigeration load and running time, so operating cost increases.
choiceExplanations.Decrease: Operating cost does not fall when the facility is used more heavily.
choiceExplanations.Remain constant: Cost does not stay the same when utilization rises from 0.43 to 0.53.

items.question: How many tonnes of biomass is needed annually to optimally operate a 27-ampere 9-kw vermi cast production shredder having a capacity of 0.27 tonne of waste per hour? It optimally operates 16 hours daily during the 3-month peak sunny months and 8 h/day at 26 days/month for the rest of the year.
items.rationale:
[0.27 tonne/h][(16h/d x30d/mo x3mo/yr)+ (8h/d x26d/mo x9mos/yr)] / = 894 tonnes /yr

Notes: 894 / Wt = Input Rate x (Peak Operating Time + Lean Operating Time) / =

choiceExplanations.894: Correct — Hours/yr: 3 months at 16 h/day (about 1,440 h) plus the rest at 8 h × 26 d × 9 months (1,872 h) = 3,312 h; × 0.27 t/h ≈ 894 t.
choiceExplanations.715: 715 tonnes comes from using fewer operating hours than the problem states.

items.question: What does a larger D-value indicate regarding the time required to kill or inactivate microorganisms and their resistance to heat?

items.question: A certain farmstead has 3 separate circuit breakers having ampacities of 60 A, 30 A and 15 A. Determine the ampacity of the main circuit breaker.

choiceExplanations.50 A: 50 A is not the keyed main breaker ampacity.

items.question: An egg incubator operates at 240 volts. It uses a pair of 25-meter AWG 10 copper wire having a resistance of 3.87x10-3 ohm per linear meter at 65 °C. The heating load of the incubator is composed of twelve 100-watt heating coils. Determine the amperage of the main wire.
items.rationale: Heating coils are connected in parallel across 240 V. Total load = 12 × 100 W = 1,200 W, so I = P/V = 1,200/240 = 5.0 A. Line drop: 2 × 25 m × 3.87×10⁻³ Ω/m = 0.19 Ω, which is negligible.

choiceExplanations.5.00 A: Correct — the coils run in parallel: I = 12 × 100 W / 240 V = 5.0 A (the 0.19 Ω line resistance is negligible).
choiceExplanations.0.03 A: Wrong — 0.03 A assumes all twelve coils in series, where each would get only 20 V and give almost no heat.
choiceExplanations.0.30 A: Wrong — 0.30 A does not match P = VI for a 1,200 W load at 240 V.
choiceExplanations.0.05 A: Wrong — 0.05 A is far too small; a 1,200 W load at 240 V draws 5 A.
