choiceExplanations.143 Watts: 143 W is more than the electrical input of 117 W, so it cannot be an output.
choiceExplanations.117 Watts: 117 W is the input power (12 × 9.77), not the output after efficiency.

items.question: Determine the power input of a 24-volt DC motor system having a total amperage of 20 Amperes. Use 82% system efficiency.
items.answer: 585 Watts Form the theoretical formula P = VI, divide VI by efficiency to get input Power input = Voltage x Amperage System efficiency
items.rationale: 585 Watts Form the theoretical formula P = VI, divide VI by efficiency to get input Power input = Voltage x Amperage System efficiency / = 24 V x 20 A / 0.82 / = 585.37 Watt
choices: 585 Watts Form the theoretical formula P = VI, divide VI by efficiency to get input Power input = Voltage x Amperage System efficiency

choiceExplanations.566 Watts: 566 W does not equal 480 divided by 0.82.
choiceExplanations.394 Watts: 394 W multiplies by 0.82 instead of dividing, giving output, not input.
choiceExplanations.585 Watts Form the theoretical formula P: Correct — Input = V × I ÷ efficiency = 24 × 20 ÷ 0.82 = 585 W.
choiceExplanations.480 Watts: 480 W is the output (24 × 20) before accounting for losses.

items.question: Quantify the surge current of a 24-volt DC motor if it is supplying current to a 528-Watt, 24-Vdc sprinkler. Surge current is assumed at 25%.
items.rationale: 27.5 A P = VI I = P/V / = 528/24 / = 22 Amp Since surge current is approximately 25% / Surge Current = (1+ Surge current in ratio) x Load amperage / = (1 + 0.25) x (22 Amp) / = 27.5 Amp

choiceExplanations.27.5 A P = VI I = P/V: Correct — Running current = 528 ÷ 24 = 22 A; adding 25 % surge gives 27.5 A.
choiceExplanations.22.0 A P = VI I = P/V: 22.0 A is the normal running current without the surge allowance.
choiceExplanations.24.8 A P = VI I = P/V: 24.8 A does not equal 22 A plus 25 %.

items.question: You need to do the planning of an automated control for the switching on and off of the electricity supply of an AC powered rain gun type sprinkler system. What is the appropriate central controller of your system?

choiceExplanations.Comparator: A comparator compares two voltages; it cannot act as the central controller of a system.
choiceExplanations.Amplifier: An amplifier boosts signal strength, not a controller.
choiceExplanations.Rectifier: A rectifier converts AC to DC, not a controller.
choiceExplanations.Microcontroller: Correct — A microcontroller is the programmable central brain that switches the sprinkler power on and off.

items.question: What electronic control switch will you use to automate the switching on and off of a high current and high power electrical circuits like that of a bioprocessing plant?

choiceExplanations.Junction field-effect transistor (JFET): A JFET is for low-power switching and amplification, not for high-current loads.
choiceExplanations.Unijunction transistor (UJT): A UJT is used mainly for timing and triggering pulses, not for high power switching.
choiceExplanations.Operational amplifier (Op-Amp): An op-amp is an amplifier for signals, not a power switch.
choiceExplanations.Metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect t: Correct — A MOSFET switches high currents and power efficiently, so it suits automatic control of large loads.

items.question: Evaluate and recommend the most appropriate sensor to be used in a microcontroller for automating the turning on and off of farmstead street lighting system based on the presence of daylight. What sensor do you recommend?

choiceExplanations.Thermistor: A thermistor senses temperature, not daylight.
choiceExplanations.Photosensor: Correct — A photosensor (photoresistor/LDR) detects daylight, so it can switch the lights on at dusk.
choiceExplanations.Thermocouple: A thermocouple measures temperature, not light.
choiceExplanations.Accelerometer: An accelerometer measures acceleration or tilt, not light.

items.question: States that the voltage or potential difference between two points is directly proportional to the current or electricity passing through the resistance and directly proportional to the resistance of the circuit.

choiceExplanations.Ohm's law: Correct — Ohm's law states V = IR: voltage is proportional to current and resistance.
choiceExplanations.Faraday's law: Faraday's law relates a changing magnetic field to induced voltage.
choiceExplanations.Joule's law: Joule's law relates heat produced to current, resistance and time.
choiceExplanations.Kirchhoff's law: Kirchhoff's laws give current and voltage rules for circuit junctions and loops.

items.question: Based on the 2009 Philippine Electrical Code, what is the minimum conductor size in mm2 for a voltage rating of 0-2,000 volts when using copper wire?

choiceExplanations.3: 3 mm² is larger than the keyed minimum of 2 mm².
choiceExplanations.1: 1 mm² is smaller than the keyed minimum of 2 mm².
choiceExplanations.2: Correct — The 2009 PEC sets 2 mm² as the minimum copper conductor size for 0–2,000 V.
choiceExplanations.4: 4 mm² is larger than the keyed minimum of 2 mm².

items.question: A farmhouse requires a minimum conductor size of 2 mm2 which is equivalent to AWG ____.
items.rationale: 14 / AWG 14 has 2.08 mm2 conductor size, AWG 16 should not be used in houses. / Except for the drop wire, the common household wires are AWG nos. 10, 12 & 14.

choiceExplanations.14: Correct — A conductor of 2 mm² is about AWG 14.
choiceExplanations.11: AWG 11 is about 4 mm², larger than 2 mm².
choiceExplanations.13: AWG 13 is not a standard size for 2 mm².

items.question: Which electrical wire in the list below has the biggest cross-sectional area?
items.rationale: In the American Wire Gauge (AWG) system, a smaller gauge number indicates a thicker wire with a larger cross-sectional area; thus AWG 8 has the largest area among the choices.

choiceExplanations.AWG 8: Correct — The smaller the AWG number, the thicker the wire, so AWG 8 is the biggest in cross-section.
choiceExplanations.AWG 12: AWG 12 is thinner than AWG 8 and AWG 10.
choiceExplanations.AWG 14: AWG 14 is the thinnest of the choices.

items.question: Which type of electrical wire has a maximum operating temperature of 90 oC?

choiceExplanations.Thw: THW is rated 75 C, not 90 C.
choiceExplanations.Thhn: Correct — THHN is rated for 90 C in dry locations.
choiceExplanations.Thwn: THWN is rated 75 C, not 90 C.

items.question: Based on the Phil. Electrical Code, what is the minimum conductor size in mm2 for a voltage rating of 2,001-8,000 volts when using copper, aluminum or copper-clad aluminum wire?

choiceExplanations.12: 12 mm² is larger than the keyed minimum of 8 mm².
choiceExplanations.10: 10 mm² is larger than the keyed minimum of 8 mm².
choiceExplanations.8: Correct — For 2,001–8,000 V, the minimum conductor size is 8 mm².
choiceExplanations.6: 6 mm² is smaller than the keyed minimum of 8 mm².

items.question: If V is voltage, I is current and P is power, according to Ohm's law, V is equal to _____.

choiceExplanations.PI: PI is not voltage; V = P/I, not P × I.
choiceExplanations.PR: PR is not voltage; it has no relation in Ohm's law.
choiceExplanations.IR: Correct — Ohm's law: voltage equals current times resistance (V = IR).

items.question: Ohm's law is applicable to _____.

choiceExplanations.DC circuits only: Ohm's law is not limited to DC; it also applies to AC with impedance.
choiceExplanations.Both DC and AC: Correct — Ohm's law applies to both DC and AC circuits.
choiceExplanations.Three-phase AC only: It is not restricted to three-phase AC.
choiceExplanations.AC circuits only: It is not restricted to AC; it also works for DC.

items.question: Ohm's law applies to both AC and DC circuits as long as mutual _________ of the circuit is considered.

choiceExplanations.Inductance: Correct — In AC circuits, mutual inductance (and its reactance) must be considered for Ohm's law to hold.
choiceExplanations.Capacitance: Capacitance is not the mutual quantity in the keyed statement.
choiceExplanations.Reluctance: Reluctance belongs to magnetic circuits, not electrical Ohm's law.
choiceExplanations.Conductance: Conductance is the inverse of resistance, not a mutual circuit effect.

items.question: The resistivity of annealed copper in ohm meters at 20oC.

choiceExplanations.1.72 x 10-8: Correct — Annealed copper has a resistivity of 1.72 × 10⁻⁸ ohm-meter at 20 C.
choiceExplanations.1.55 x 9-7: 1.55 × 9⁻⁷ is not a valid value for the resistivity of copper.
choiceExplanations.1.38 x 8-6: 1.38 × 8⁻⁶ is not a valid value for the resistivity of copper.
choiceExplanations.1.89 x 11-9: 1.89 × 11⁻⁹ is not a valid value for the resistivity of copper.

items.question: The resistance of a certain length of wire can be obtained by multiplying its ________ with its length and dividing the resulting product by the cross-sectional area of the wire.

choiceExplanations.Conductivity: Conductivity is the inverse of resistivity; multiplying it would give the wrong result.
choiceExplanations.Permittivity: Permittivity relates to electric fields in dielectrics, not wire resistance.
choiceExplanations.Permeability: Permeability relates to magnetic fields, not wire resistance.
choiceExplanations.Resistivity: Correct — Resistance R = resistivity × length ÷ area.

items.question: A farmstead has its farthest load located 350 linear meters from a single phase power source. What length of the wire in meters should be used in the voltage loss computation?

choiceExplanations.805: 805 m does not equal twice the 350 m distance.
choiceExplanations.644: 644 m does not equal twice the 350 m distance.
choiceExplanations.700: Correct — Single phase needs a go-and-return path, so use 2 × 350 m = 700 m.
choiceExplanations.854: 854 m does not equal twice the 350 m distance.

items.question: In connecting electricity from a post to a farmhouse, a ______ wire is needed.

choiceExplanations.Feeder: A feeder runs from the main panel to sub-panels, not from the post to the house.
choiceExplanations.Ground: A ground wire is a safety conductor, not the supply line from a post.
choiceExplanations.Riser: A riser carries power vertically within a building, not from a post.
choiceExplanations.Drop: Correct — A drop wire carries electricity from the utility post to the house.

items.question: The minimum wire size for a farmhouse drop wire.

choiceExplanations.AWG 5: AWG 5 is not the keyed minimum drop wire size.

choiceExplanations.AWG 6: Correct — The minimum wire size for a farmhouse drop wire is AWG 6.

items.question: Based on PAES 418:2002, the recommended lighting intensity in lux (lumen/m2) for fruit and vegetable processing plant are: 100 for outside the building, 200 for general indoor locations, and ___ for working tables.

choiceExplanations.650: 650 lux is higher than the PAES 418 value.
choiceExplanations.440: 440 lux is not the PAES 418 level for working tables.

items.question: A poultry layer area requires a brightness of 1,600 lumens. What incandescent-equivalent wattage rating should the daylight-color LED bulb have?
items.rationale: A 1,600-lumen LED bulb is sold as a 100 W incandescent equivalent, though it actually draws only about 14–20 W.

choiceExplanations.80: Wrong — an 80 W equivalent gives only about 1,100–1,300 lm.

choiceExplanations.100: Correct — 1,600 lm is the standard 100 W incandescent-equivalent rating (actual LED draw is about 14–20 W).

items.question: What is the voltage needed to light a 1-ampere LED bulb having a resistance of 220 ohms?
items.answer: 220 volts Applying the formula V=IR in the third quadrant of the formula wheel, V = IxR

choiceExplanations.220 volts Applying the formula V=IR in t: Correct — V = I × R = 1 A × 220 ohms = 220 volts.

items.question: How many amperes will pass through a circuit having ten 22-watt LED bulbs if the source is 220 volts?
items.answer: 1 Amp Applying the formula I=P/V in the fourth quadrant of the formula wheel, I = P/V

choices: 1 Amp Applying the formula I=P/V in the fourth quadrant of the formula wheel, I = P/V

choiceExplanations.1 Amp Applying the formula I=P/V in the: Correct — Total power 10 × 22 = 220 W; I = P/V = 220 ÷ 220 = 1 A.
choiceExplanations.10 Amp: 10 A is too high; the total current is 1 A.

items.question: What is the electrical energy consumption of a 15-kw vermi cast production shredder plugged in a 220-volt source if it requires 2 hours to shred 1.5 tonnes of farm waste?

items.question: Solid annealed copper has a resistivity of 1.72 x 10-8 ohm-meter at 20 oC. What is the resistance in ohm-meter per linear meter of AWG 10 solid annealed copper wire having a diameter of 2.588 mm?
items.answer: 3.27x10-3 ohms Determining the cross-sectional area of the wire in square meters, A = 3.1416 x (Diameter)2
items.rationale: 3.27x10-3 ohms Determining the cross-sectional area of the wire in square meters, A = 3.1416 x (Diameter)2 / 4 / = 3.1416 x (2.588 mm x 1 m/1000 mm)2 / 4 / = 5.26 x 10-6 m2 / Determining the resistance of AWG 10 solid annealed copper wire per linear meter, R = Resistivity x Length Cross-sectional area / = (1.72 x 10-8 ohm-m) x (1 m) / (5.26 x 10-6 m2) / = 3.27 x 10-3 ohms
choices: 3.27x10-3 ohms Determining the cross-sectional area of the wire in square meters, A = 3.1416 x (Diameter)2

choiceExplanations.3.27x10-4 ohms: 3.27 × 10⁻⁴ ohm is ten times too small.
choiceExplanations.8.17x10-4 ohms: 8.17 × 10⁻⁴ ohm does not match the area and resistivity computation.

items.question: A 240-volt industrial incubator uses a pair of 25-m 7-strand AWG 10 copper wire having a resistance of 3.87x10-3 ohm per linear meter at 65 oC. The heating load of the incubator is composed of twelve 100-watt heating coils. What is the expected current in the main wire?
items.rationale: Heating coils are connected in parallel across 240 V. Total load = 12 × 100 W = 1,200 W, so I = P/V = 1,200/240 = 5.0 A. Line drop: 2 × 25 m × 3.87×10⁻³ Ω/m = 0.19 Ω, which is negligible.

choiceExplanations.5.00 A: Correct — the coils run in parallel: I = 12 × 100 W / 240 V = 5.0 A (the 0.19 Ω line resistance is negligible).
choiceExplanations.0.03 A: Wrong — 0.03 A assumes all twelve coils in series, where each would get only 20 V and give almost no heat.
choiceExplanations.0.30 A: Wrong — 0.30 A does not match P = VI for a 1,200 W load at 240 V.
choiceExplanations.0.05 A: Wrong — 0.05 A is far too small; a 1,200 W load at 240 V draws 5 A.

items.question: In off-grid farmhouse electrification, which one has the lowest operation and maintenance cost?

choiceExplanations.Diesel generator: A diesel generator has high fuel and maintenance cost.
choiceExplanations.Hydro power plant: A hydro plant needs periodic upkeep of civil works and turbine, more than solar.
choiceExplanations.Solar Home System: Correct — A solar home system has no fuel and few moving parts, so it has the lowest O&M cost.
choiceExplanations.Grid extension: Grid extension carries line maintenance and energy charges, more than solar.

items.question: Which one has the highest operation and maintenance cost?
items.rationale: A diesel generator has the highest ongoing operation and maintenance cost because it continuously requires diesel fuel purchases, lubricants, and regular mechanical engine servicing.

choiceExplanations.Hydro power plant: A hydro plant needs maintenance but has no fuel cost.
choiceExplanations.Grid extension: Grid extension has line maintenance, but no fuel cost like diesel.
choiceExplanations.Diesel generator: Correct — A diesel generator needs fuel, oil and frequent repairs, so it has the highest O&M cost.
choiceExplanations.Solar Home System: A solar home system has the lowest O&M cost.

items.question: In off-grid barangay electrification located 3 kilometers from the electricity grid, which one is recommended?
items.rationale: For an entire barangay located only 3 km from an existing utility line, grid extension is typically more cost-effective and provides greater, more reliable power capacity than standalone off-grid options.

choiceExplanations.Grid extension: Correct — At only 3 km from the grid, extending the grid line is the most practical and economical choice.
choiceExplanations.Hydro power plant: A hydro plant needs a water source and is costly for a site this close to the grid.
choiceExplanations.Diesel generator: A diesel generator has high fuel cost and emissions, so it is not preferred near the grid.
choiceExplanations.Solar Home System: A solar home system suits remote households, not a site just 3 km from the grid.

items.question: Which electricity source has no greenhouse gas emission?
items.rationale: A Solar Home System generates electricity directly from solar radiation using photovoltaic panels with zero operational greenhouse gas emissions.

choiceExplanations.Grid extension: Grid electricity comes largely from fossil plants, so it is not emission-free.
choiceExplanations.Hydro power plant: Hydropower has very low emissions but reservoirs can release some gases; the keyed answer is solar.
choiceExplanations.Diesel generator: A diesel generator burns fuel and emits greenhouse gas.
choiceExplanations.Solar Home System: Correct — A solar home system produces electricity with no greenhouse gas emission during operation.

items.question: Which electricity source has the highest greenhouse gas emission?
items.rationale: Diesel generators combust fossil diesel fuel directly, yielding the highest greenhouse gas emissions per kilowatt-hour among the listed electricity sources.

choiceExplanations.Diesel generator: Correct — A diesel generator burns fossil fuel and gives the highest greenhouse gas emission.
choiceExplanations.Grid extension: Grid extension emits less per unit than a small diesel set when powered by a mixed grid.
choiceExplanations.Solar Home System: A solar home system has no operating emission.

items.question: To minimize power loss, which equipment is needed to transform DC electricity from a centralized solar power plant into AC electricity before transmitting it to distributed 220-volt farmstead electrical devices?

choiceExplanations.Transformer: A transformer changes AC voltage levels; it cannot convert DC to AC.
choiceExplanations.Rectifier: A rectifier converts AC to DC, the opposite direction.
choiceExplanations.Converter: A converter is a general term and not the specific device that makes AC from DC.
choiceExplanations.Inverter: Correct — An inverter changes DC from solar panels to AC, so it can be transmitted at high voltage with less loss.

items.question: A 950-kW cassava flour processing plant is to be powered using hydro. Which electricity source will you recommend?
items.answer: Minihydro Under the Philippine classification, minihydro is over 100 kW up to 10 MW
choices: Minihydro Under the Philippine classification, minihydro is over 100 kW up to 10 MW

choiceExplanations.Minihydro Under the Philippine classific: Correct — Under Philippine classification, minihydro is over 100 kW up to 10 MW, so 950 kW is minihydro.
choiceExplanations.Macrohydro: Macrohydro is for plants far larger than 950 kW.
choiceExplanations.Microhydro: Microhydro is up to 100 kW, too small for 950 kW.
choiceExplanations.Picohydro: Picohydro is below about 5 kW, far too small.

items.question: A 3-hectare hillside farm is to be energized. It is 20 meters below a river having a dependable summer discharge of 50 liters/second. Which electricity source will you recommend?
items.answer: Microhydro Picohydro is up to 5 kW only while mini and regular hydros are oversized
choices: Microhydro Picohydro is up to 5 kW only while mini and regular hydros are oversized

choiceExplanations.Minihydro: Minihydro is over 100 kW, far larger than a 3-hectare farm needs; it would be oversized.
choiceExplanations.Macrohydro: Macrohydro is for very large plants and is far oversized for a hillside farm.
choiceExplanations.Microhydro Picohydro is up to 5 kW only: Correct — P = 9.81 × 0.05 m³/s × 20 m ≈ 9.8 kW theoretical, so microhydro (above 5 kW up to 100 kW) fits.
choiceExplanations.Picohydro: Picohydro is up to about 5 kW only, so it is too small for the available power.

items.question: The 1-kW lighting of a farmstead is to be energized using hydropower. It is 10 meters below a creek having a dependable summer discharge of 5 liters/second. Which hydropower will you recommend for development?
items.answer: Picohydro Since power requirement is less than 5 kw, picohydro is recommended.
choices: Picohydro Since power requirement is less than 5 kw, picohydro is recommended.

choiceExplanations.Microhydro: Microhydro is for roughly 5 to 100 kW, larger than this 1 kW load needs.
choiceExplanations.Minihydro: Minihydro is over 100 kW, far oversized for a 1 kW lighting load.
choiceExplanations.Picohydro Since power requirement is les: Correct — The power needed is below 5 kW, so picohydro is the right size.
choiceExplanations.Macrohydro: Macrohydro is for very large plants, far oversized for 1 kW.

items.question: A battery bank of a centralized solar power generator needs to store energy in a 48-volt DC system to power a cassava processing plant. If each battery is 12 volts, how many batteries are there in series?
items.rationale: 4 / No. of batteries in series / = System voltage Battery nominal voltage / = 48 volts / 12 volts / = 4 batteries in series

choiceExplanations.3: Three 12-V batteries in series give only 36 V.
choiceExplanations.2: Two 12-V batteries in series give only 24 V.
choiceExplanations.4: Correct — Series voltages add: 48 V ÷ 12 V = 4 batteries in series.
choiceExplanations.5: Five 12-V batteries in series give 60 V, not 48 V.

items.question: An off-grid tomato processing plant has 48-volt output battery bank composed of 60 units of 12-volt automotive batteries. How many batteries are there in parallel?
items.rationale: 15 / No. of batteries in series / = System voltage Battery nominal voltage / = 48 volts / 12 volts / = 4 batteries in series No. of batteries in parallel / = Total number of batteries No. of batteries in series / = 60 total batteries / 4 batteries in series / = 15 batteries in parallel

choiceExplanations.12: 12 in parallel would require 5 in series (12 × 4 ≠ 60), so the bank would not give 48 V.
choiceExplanations.16: 16 in parallel would need 3.75 in series, which is not possible.
choiceExplanations.14: 14 in parallel would need about 4.3 in series, which is not possible.
choiceExplanations.15: Correct — 48 V ÷ 12 V = 4 in series; 60 batteries ÷ 4 = 15 strings in parallel.

items.question: A centralized solar power plant with DC to AC inverter is used to electrify a farmstead using 75 watt-peak solar modules of the same brand. choiceExplanations.26: 26 kWh is lower than the calculated output.

items.question: Find the dependable power output of a 12-volt DC motor if it is rated at 10 Amperes. Assume a system efficiency of 80%.

choices: 600 Watts Form the theoretical formula P = VI, divide VI by efficiency to get input Power input = Voltage x Amperage System efficiency

items.question: Evaluate and quantify the surge current of a 24-volt DC motor if it is supplying current to a 528-Watt, 24-Vdc water pump. Surge current is estimated at 25%.

choices: 27.5 A Since Surge Current is about 25%

items.question: Applying the principles of electronics, what control switch will you use to automate the switching on and off of a high current and high power electrical circuits like that of a farmstead?

choiceExplanations.Metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect t: Correct — A MOSFET can switch high currents and power efficiently, so it suits automatic control of large loads.
choiceExplanations.Bipolar junction transistor (BJT): A BJT is current-controlled and wastes more power, so it is less suitable than a MOSFET here.
choiceExplanations.Junction field-effect transistor (JFET): A JFET is a low-power device, not for switching high power.
choiceExplanations.Unijunction transistor (UJT): A UJT is used for timing and triggering, not for high-power switching.

items.question: If you are to carry out the planning of an automated control for the switching on and off of the electricity supply of an AC powered central pivot sprinkler system, what should be the central controller of your system?

choiceExplanations.Multiplexer: A multiplexer selects between signals; it does not run a control program.
choiceExplanations.Microprocessor: A microprocessor needs external memory and parts; a microcontroller has these built in for control tasks.
choiceExplanations.Comparator: A comparator only compares two voltages and cannot act as a central controller.
choiceExplanations.Microcontroller: Correct — A microcontroller is a single programmable chip that controls on-off switching of the system.

items.question: You are to evaluate and recommend the most appropriate sensor to be used in a microcontroller for automating the turning on and off of the lighting system of a farmstead based on the presence of sunlight. What sensor will you recommend?

choiceExplanations.Thermistor: A thermistor senses temperature, not sunlight.
choiceExplanations.Photosensor: Correct — A photosensor detects light level, so it can switch the lights on and off with daylight.
choiceExplanations.Thermocouple: A thermocouple measures temperature, not light.
choiceExplanations.Accelerometer: An accelerometer measures acceleration or tilt, not light.

items.question: The electronic board which is able to read inputs like light on a sensor, temperature reading, a finger on a button, or a social media message and can turn these inputs into outputs like activating a motor, turning on an LED, turning on a solenoid valve, or publishing something online.

choiceExplanations.Microprocessor: A microprocessor is the processing chip alone and needs extra parts to read inputs and drive outputs.
choiceExplanations.Oscillator: An oscillator produces a repeating signal and does not process inputs.
choiceExplanations.Motherboard: A motherboard is a computer's main circuit board, not a small input-output control board.
choiceExplanations.Microcontroller: Correct — A microcontroller reads inputs and turns them into outputs such as running a motor or an LED.

items.question: An electronic part of solar module needed such that solar charging is continuous at slower rate when the solar modules are partially shaded by trees.

choiceExplanations.Blocking diode: A blocking diode prevents reverse current, e.g., from battery to panel at night, not shading.
choiceExplanations.Tunnel diode: A tunnel diode is a high-speed device not used for solar shading protection.
choiceExplanations.Bypass diode: Correct — A bypass diode lets current flow around shaded cells so charging continues at a lower rate.
choiceExplanations.Zener diode: A Zener diode regulates voltage, not shading.

items.question: A diode needed as protection against lightning in solar panels.

choiceExplanations.Varactor diode: A varactor diode acts as a voltage-variable capacitor for tuning, not surge protection.
choiceExplanations.Bypass diode: A bypass diode routes current around shaded cells, not for lightning protection.
choiceExplanations.Blocking diode: Correct — Keyed answer: the blocking diode (it stops reverse current; true surge protection needs a TVS or arrester).
choiceExplanations.Zener diode: A Zener diode regulates voltage but is not the keyed answer.

items.question: An integrated circuit (IC) that is included as an important part of electronic instrumentation for gathering time and time-based data like velocity, speed, discharge and acceleration.

choiceExplanations.Timer: Correct — A timer IC gives time-base signals for measuring time-based data like speed and discharge.
choiceExplanations.Amplifier: An amplifier boosts a signal level and does not measure time.
choiceExplanations.Comparator: A comparator compares two voltages and does not keep time.
choiceExplanations.Multiplexer: A multiplexer selects among inputs and does not keep time.

items.question: Which one is a single timer integrated circuit that is appropriate in simple instrumentation and control?

choiceExplanations.IC 610: IC 610 is not a standard timer IC.
choiceExplanations.IC 444: IC 444 is not a standard timer IC.
choiceExplanations.IC 555: Correct — The IC 555 is the popular single timer chip for simple instrumentation and control.
choiceExplanations.IC 500: IC 500 is not the common single timer IC.

items.question: Which one is an obsolete timer integrated circuit that should not be used in your new instrumentation and control projects?

choiceExplanations.IC 502: IC 502 is not the timer IC named as obsolete.
choiceExplanations.IC 558: Correct — The keyed answer names IC 558 as the obsolete timer IC not to be used in new projects.
choiceExplanations.IC 614: IC 614 is not the timer IC named as obsolete.
choiceExplanations.IC 446: IC 446 is not the timer IC named as obsolete.

items.question: What voltage is appropriate in remote instrumentation and control?

choiceExplanations.9, 7, and 5 Vdc: Correct — Remote instrumentation commonly uses low voltages of 9, 7 and 5 Vdc to save power.
choiceExplanations.10, 8, and 6 Vdc: 10, 8 and 6 Vdc is not the standard set given.
choiceExplanations.8, 6, and 4 Vdc: 8, 6 and 4 Vdc is not the standard set given.
choiceExplanations.7, 6, and 4 Vdc: 7, 6 and 4 Vdc is not the standard set given.

items.question: Switch for automatic pump motor control of sealed water tanks in drip irrigation systems.

choiceExplanations.Pressure switch: Correct — A pressure switch turns the pump on and off based on pressure in a sealed tank.
choiceExplanations.Limit switch: A limit switch detects position of a moving part, not tank pressure.
choiceExplanations.Flow switch: A flow switch senses water flow in a pipe, not tank pressure.
choiceExplanations.Float switch: A float switch senses level in an open tank, not in a sealed pressurized tank.

items.question: A device to convert biogas to electricity.

choiceExplanations.Biogas scrubber: A biogas scrubber removes impurities like H2S from biogas, not converts to electricity.
choiceExplanations.Biogas digester: A biogas digester produces the gas from waste, not electricity.
choiceExplanations.Biogas generator: Correct — A biogas generator burns biogas in an engine to produce electricity.
choiceExplanations.Biogas compressor: A biogas compressor raises gas pressure for storage and does not make electricity.

items.question: Part of aerogenerators in wind farms that converts rotational movement to AC electricity.

choiceExplanations.Dynamo: A dynamo produces DC, not AC electricity.
choiceExplanations.Inverter: An inverter converts DC to AC; it does not convert rotation to electricity.
choiceExplanations.Rectifier: A rectifier converts AC to DC, not rotation to electricity.
choiceExplanations.Alternator: Correct — An alternator converts the turbine's rotary motion into AC electricity.

items.question: Expression of relationship among current, resistance and voltage or electromotive force.

choiceExplanations.Joule’s law: Joule's law gives heat produced by current in a resistance.
choiceExplanations.Kirchhoff’s law: Kirchhoff's laws give circuit junction and loop rules.
choiceExplanations.Ohm’s law: Correct — Ohm's law relates current, resistance and voltage: V = IR.
choiceExplanations.Faraday’s law: Faraday's law relates changing magnetic flux to induced voltage.

items.question: The application of electricity in rural areas including the home, farm and farmstead.

choiceExplanations.Rural electrification: Correct — Rural electrification is bringing electricity to homes, farms and farmsteads in rural areas.
choiceExplanations.Energy auditing: Energy auditing assesses energy use, not supplying electricity.
choiceExplanations.Power distribution: Power distribution is delivering electricity from substations to users, not specific to rural use.
choiceExplanations.Load management: Load management controls electricity demand, not bringing power to rural areas.

items.question: The current rating of American Wire Gage (AWG) No. 10 wire.

choiceExplanations.33 amp: 33 amp is not the current rating of AWG no. 10.
choiceExplanations.27 amp: 27 amp is not the current rating of AWG no. 10.
choiceExplanations.30 amp: Correct — AWG no. 10 copper wire is rated about 30 amperes.
choiceExplanations.24 amp: 24 amp is not the current rating of AWG no. 10.

items.question: The standard size of drop wire (post to building wire) for farmhouses and households.

choiceExplanations.4.4 sq. mm: 4.4 sq. mm is not the standard drop wire size.
choiceExplanations.5.5 sq. mm: Correct — The standard drop wire for farmhouses and households is 5.5 sq. mm.
choiceExplanations.5.0 sq. mm: 5.0 sq. mm is not the standard drop wire size.
choiceExplanations.6.1 sq. mm: 6.1 sq. mm is not the standard drop wire size.

items.question: How many square millimeters is AWG No. 10 wire?

choiceExplanations.4.8: 4.8 sq. mm is not the cross-section of AWG no. 10.
choiceExplanations.5.5: Correct — AWG no. 10 wire has a cross-section of about 5.5 sq. mm (exact value 5.26).
choiceExplanations.6.3: 6.3 sq. mm is larger than AWG no. 10.
choiceExplanations.7.2: 7.2 sq. mm is larger than AWG no. 10.

items.question: Solar irradiance at the Earth surface.

choiceExplanations.1,000 watt/m^2: Correct — Standard solar irradiance at the Earth's surface is taken as 1,000 W/m².
choiceExplanations.800 watt/m^2: 800 W/m² is below the standard value.
choiceExplanations.1,100 watt/m^2: 1,100 W/m² is above the standard value.
choiceExplanations.900 watt/m^2: 900 W/m² is below the standard value.

items.question: The reciprocal of resistance

choiceExplanations.Inductance: Inductance is a property of coils that opposes current change.
choiceExplanations.Capacitance: Capacitance is the ability to store charge, not the reciprocal of resistance.
choiceExplanations.Conductance: Correct — Conductance (G = 1/R) is the reciprocal of resistance.
choiceExplanations.Reactance: Reactance is opposition from inductors or capacitors to AC, not the reciprocal of resistance.

items.question: If the unit of resistance is ohms, what is the unit of conductance?

choiceExplanations.Mhos: Correct — Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance, so its unit is the mho (siemens).
choiceExplanations.Henrys: The henry is the unit of inductance.
choiceExplanations.Farads: The farad is the unit of capacitance.
choiceExplanations.Webers: The weber is the unit of magnetic flux.

items.question: Unit for battery

choiceExplanations.Amp-hr: Correct — A battery's charge capacity is rated in ampere-hours.
choiceExplanations.Amp-turn: Ampere-turn is a unit of magnetomotive force, not battery capacity.
choiceExplanations.Volt-amp: Volt-ampere is a unit of apparent power, not battery capacity.
choiceExplanations.Watt-hr: Watt-hour is an energy unit; batteries are normally rated in amp-hours.

items.question: It is a basic electrical element which prevents the current from changing instantly

choiceExplanations.Capacitor: A capacitor opposes sudden changes in voltage, not current.
choiceExplanations.Diode: A diode allows current in one direction only.
choiceExplanations.Resistor: A resistor limits current but does not oppose changes in it over time.
choiceExplanations.Inductor: Correct — An inductor resists any sudden change in current through it.

items.question: Unit for alternating current (AC)

choiceExplanations.Hertz (Hz): Hertz is the unit of frequency, not current.
choiceExplanations.Watt (W): Watt is the unit of power.
choiceExplanations.Amp (A): Correct — Current, including AC, is measured in amperes.
choiceExplanations.Volt (V): Volt is the unit of voltage.

items.question: Unit for AC with capacitor

choiceExplanations.Kwh: Kwh is a unit of energy, not reactive effect of a capacitor.
choiceExplanations.Kw: Kw is real power, not capacitor-related power.
choiceExplanations.Kvar: Correct — A capacitor supplies reactive power, measured in kvar.

items.question: Unit for reactive power (Q)

choiceExplanations.Volt Amp-Reactive (VAR): Correct — Reactive power Q is measured in volt-amperes reactive (VAR).
choiceExplanations.Ampere-Turn (At): Ampere-turn is a unit of magnetomotive force.
choiceExplanations.Volt-Ampere (VA): Volt-ampere is the unit of apparent power.
choiceExplanations.Watt-Hour (Wh): Watt-hour is a unit of energy.

items.question: When the resistance of a certain circuit is zero or almost zero, the circuit is called

choiceExplanations.Shorted: Correct — A circuit with zero or near-zero resistance is shorted.
choiceExplanations.Isolated: Isolated means disconnected from the source, not zero resistance.
choiceExplanations.Overloaded: Overloaded means drawing more than rated current, not zero resistance.
choiceExplanations.Grounded: Grounded means connected to earth, not necessarily zero resistance.

items.question: Unit for illuminance

choiceExplanations.Nit: The nit is a unit of luminance, not illuminance.
choiceExplanations.Candela: The candela is the unit of luminous intensity.
choiceExplanations.Lumen: The lumen is the unit of luminous flux; illuminance is lumen per square meter.
choiceExplanations.Lux: Correct — Illuminance is measured in lux (lumen per m²).

items.question: Type of electric current where electricity flows in one direction only.

choiceExplanations.Direct current: Correct — Direct current flows in one direction only.
choiceExplanations.Induced current: Induced current is produced by a changing magnetic field, not defined by direction.
choiceExplanations.Eddy current: Eddy currents are circulating currents in conductors from changing magnetic fields.

items.question: 200 lux is equivalent to how many ft candle
items.rationale: 1 foot-candle = 10.764 lux, so 200 lux ÷ 10.764 = 18.6 fc.

choiceExplanations.22 Ft Candle: Wrong — 22 fc would be about 237 lux.
choiceExplanations.24 Ft Candle: Wrong — 24 fc would be about 258 lux.
choiceExplanations.20 Ft Candle: Wrong — 20 fc comes from the rough 1 fc ≈ 10 lux shortcut; the exact value is 18.6 fc.

items.question: Unit for magnetomotive force (mmf)

choiceExplanations.Volt amperes (VA): Volt-ampere is a unit of apparent power.
choiceExplanations.Ampere hours (Ah): Ampere-hour is a unit of charge capacity.
choiceExplanations.Ampere turns (At): Correct — Magnetomotive force is measured in ampere-turns (At).
choiceExplanations.Watt hours (Wh): Watt-hour is a unit of energy.

items.question: This happens when the electric field in a material is large enough, in which conducting paths suddenly appear in the material. Electrons flow along one or more conducting paths, creating electrical sparks.

choiceExplanations.Dielectric polarization: Dielectric polarization is the shifting of charges in an insulator without conduction.
choiceExplanations.Thermal runaway: Thermal runaway is rising temperature causing more current and heat, not sudden sparks through a field.
choiceExplanations.Magnetic saturation: Magnetic saturation is a limit on magnetic flux, not an electric spark.
choiceExplanations.Electrical breakdown: Correct — Electrical breakdown happens when a strong field creates conducting paths and sparks.

items.question: Unit for electrical energy

choiceExplanations.Kw-hr: Correct — Electrical energy is measured in kilowatt-hours.
choiceExplanations.Amp-hr: Ampere-hour measures charge capacity, not energy.
choiceExplanations.Kvar-hr: Kvar-hour is reactive energy, not the unit for electrical energy.

items.question: Unit for current (I)

choiceExplanations.Watt (W): Watt is the unit of power.
choiceExplanations.Amp (A): Correct — Current is measured in amperes.
choiceExplanations.Volt (V): Volt is the unit of voltage.
choiceExplanations.Coulomb (C): Coulomb is the unit of charge; one ampere is one coulomb per second.

items.question: Unit for impedance (Z)

choiceExplanations.Ohm: Correct — Impedance is measured in ohms, like resistance.
choiceExplanations.Mho: Mho is the unit of conductance, the reciprocal of ohm.
choiceExplanations.Henry: Henry is the unit of inductance.
choiceExplanations.Farad: Farad is the unit of capacitance.

items.question: Unit for generator

choiceExplanations.KWh or Wh: KWh or Wh are energy units, not generator ratings.
choiceExplanations.KVAR or VAR: KVAR or VAR are reactive power units, not the usual generator rating.
choiceExplanations.KW or W: Correct — Generators are rated in kilowatts or watts (real power output).
choiceExplanations.KVA or VA: KVA or VA is apparent power, often used for transformers and alternators, but the keyed answer is KW or W.

items.question: Unit for quantity of electricity

choiceExplanations.Farad (F): Farad is the unit of capacitance.
choiceExplanations.Coulomb (C): Correct — The quantity of electricity (charge) is measured in coulombs.
choiceExplanations.Ampere (A): Ampere is the unit of current, charge per second.
choiceExplanations.Joule (J): Joule is a unit of energy.

items.question: Unit for apparent power (S)

choiceExplanations.Volt-amp (VA): Correct — Apparent power S is measured in volt-amperes (VA).
choiceExplanations.Amp-hour (Ah): Ampere-hour is a unit of charge capacity.
choiceExplanations.Volt-amp reactive (VAR): VAR is the unit of reactive power, not apparent power.
choiceExplanations.Watt-hour (Wh): Watt-hour is a unit of energy.

items.question: When AWG #12 wire is replaced with AWG #14, the ampere capacity will:

choiceExplanations.Increase: Replacing AWG 12 with AWG 14 means a thinner wire, so ampacity cannot increase.
choiceExplanations.Decrease: Correct — AWG 14 is thinner than AWG 12, so it carries less current safely.
choiceExplanations.Fluctuate: Ampacity is fixed by wire size; it does not fluctuate.
choiceExplanations.Double: Ampacity does not double with a thinner wire.

items.question: This type of control is operated by electricity but it is used to control the flow of water, oil or gas.

choiceExplanations.Float valve: A float valve is operated by liquid level, not electricity.
choiceExplanations.Solenoid valve: Correct — A solenoid valve uses an electric coil to open or close and control flow of water, oil or gas.
choiceExplanations.Relief valve: A relief valve opens by pressure to release excess, not by electricity.
choiceExplanations.Check valve: A check valve allows flow one way automatically, not by electricity.

items.question: Classification of AC motors according to principles and characteristics of operation that runs at an exact speed for all loads up to the pull-out point.

choiceExplanations.Repulsion: Repulsion motors vary speed with load.
choiceExplanations.Induction: Induction motors slip under load, so speed is not exact.
choiceExplanations.Synchronous: Correct — Synchronous motors run at exact synchronous speed for all loads up to the pull-out point.
choiceExplanations.Universal: Universal motors vary speed with load.

items.question: A process in which two pieces of metal are joined by passing current between electrodes positioned on opposite sides of the pieces to be welded. There is no arc with this process.

choiceExplanations.Plasma arc welding: Plasma arc welding uses an arc of ionized gas.
choiceExplanations.Submerged arc welding: Submerged arc welding uses an arc under flux.
choiceExplanations.Friction stir welding: Friction stir welding joins metals by frictional heat, not electric current between electrodes.
choiceExplanations.Resistance spot welding: Correct — Resistance spot welding joins metal with current passing between electrodes, with no arc.

items.question: It is the amount of electrical pressure used not to advantage

choiceExplanations.Load factor: Load factor is average load divided by peak load. It measures steady use, not lost electrical pressure.
choiceExplanations.Phase shift: Phase shift is the angle between voltage and current waves. It is not a loss of electrical pressure.
choiceExplanations.Voltage drop: Correct — Voltage drop is the loss of electrical pressure along a conductor because of its resistance, so it is not used to advantage.
choiceExplanations.Power factor: Power factor is true power divided by apparent power. It does not describe lost electrical pressure.

items.question: According to Philippine Electrical Code, a receptacle is rated _____VA.

choiceExplanations.194: 194 is not the PEC rating. A receptacle outlet is counted at 180 VA.
choiceExplanations.180: Correct — 180 is the load the PEC assigns to each receptacle outlet when computing branch-circuit loads.
choiceExplanations.158: 158 is not the PEC rating. A receptacle outlet is counted at 180 VA.
choiceExplanations.166: 166 is not the PEC rating. A receptacle outlet is counted at 180 VA.

items.question: The ratio of the average load to the maximum demand of a system.

choiceExplanations.Power factor: Power factor is true power over apparent power. It does not compare average load with maximum demand.
choiceExplanations.Diversity factor: Diversity factor is the sum of individual maximum demands over the system's maximum demand, not average over maximum.
choiceExplanations.Demand factor: Correct — Demand factor is the term this item keys for the ratio of average load to maximum demand.
choiceExplanations.Utilization factor: Utilization factor is maximum demand over rated capacity of the system, not average load over maximum demand.

items.question: Refers to tools that are driven by electric motor, hydraulics, air, gas engine, or forces other than, or in addition to human power. They are generally STATIONARY and are usually FIXED in the shop.

choiceExplanations.Power tools: Power tools are portable tools held in the hand. The item describes stationary tools fixed in the shop.
choiceExplanations.Power machines: Correct — Power machines are stationary and fixed in the shop, driven by motor, hydraulics, air or engine, like a lathe or drill press.
choiceExplanations.Precision tools: Precision tools are measuring and layout tools such as calipers. They are not defined by their power source.
choiceExplanations.Hand tools: Hand tools use human power only, so they do not fit tools driven by motors or engines.

items.question: Which of the following electrical installations is not covered by the Philippine Electrical Code?
items.rationale: Under Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) Part 1, Section 1.0.1.2 (Scope), electrical installations in aircraft, railway rolling stock, and automotive vehicles are excluded, whereas watercraft, airfields, and trailers are covered.

choiceExplanations.Trailers: Trailers such as mobile homes are covered by the PEC, so they are not the exception.
choiceExplanations.Aircraft: Correct — Aircraft installations are excluded from the PEC scope, so they are not covered by the Code.
choiceExplanations.Airfield: Airfield lighting and ground installations are on land and fall under the PEC. Only the aircraft itself is excluded.
choiceExplanations.Watercraft: Watercraft is also excluded in the full Code, but the keyed exception here is aircraft.

items.question: The property of an electric circuit that enables it to store an electric charge

choiceExplanations.Resistance: Resistance opposes current flow. It does not store charge.
choiceExplanations.Inductance: Inductance opposes a change in current by storing energy in a magnetic field, not by storing charge.
choiceExplanations.Reactance: Reactance is the opposition to AC from inductors or capacitors. It is not the charge-storing property itself.
choiceExplanations.Capacitance: Correct — Capacitance is the ability of a circuit or component, like a capacitor, to store electric charge.

items.question: An arc cutting process which severs metal by using a constricted arc to melt a small area of the work. This process can cut all metals that conduct electricity.

choiceExplanations.Water jet cutting: Water jet cutting cuts with a high-pressure water stream, not an electric arc.
choiceExplanations.Plasma arc cutting: Correct — Plasma arc cutting uses a constricted arc to melt a small area of the work. It can cut any metal that conducts electricity.
choiceExplanations.Laser beam cutting: Laser beam cutting melts or vaporizes metal with a focused light beam, not a constricted arc.
choiceExplanations.Carbon arc cutting: Carbon arc cutting uses an arc between a carbon electrode and the work. It is not a constricted-arc process.

items.question: According to PEC, for a dwelling unit having a floor area not more than 50m², it shall be permitted to have a single 20-ampere 2-wire branch circuit provided that the total load does not exceed _______ VA.

choiceExplanations.4490: 4490 is not the PEC limit. A single 20 A, 2-wire circuit is allowed up to 3680 VA.
choiceExplanations.3974: 3974 is not the PEC limit. The permitted load is 3680 VA.
choiceExplanations.3680: Correct — 3680 is 230 V x 16 A, the load permitted on a single 20 A 2-wire branch circuit in a small dwelling.
choiceExplanations.4784: 4784 is not the PEC limit. The permitted load is 3680 VA.

items.question: The instrument used to measure the speed of the electric motor is:

choiceExplanations.Anemometer: Anemometer measures wind or air speed, not motor speed.
choiceExplanations.Wattmeter: Wattmeter measures electrical power in watts, not speed.
choiceExplanations.Tachometer: Correct — Tachometer measures rotational speed in rpm, so it is used to check motor speed.
choiceExplanations.Dynamometer: Dynamometer measures torque or power output of a motor, not its speed directly.

items.question: A wire installation that supplies current to lights and convenience outlets.

choiceExplanations.Circuit: Correct — Circuit is the wire installation that carries current to lights and convenience outlets.
choiceExplanations.Busbar: Busbar is a metal bar in a panel that distributes current. It is not the wiring to lights and outlets.
choiceExplanations.Conduit: Conduit is the pipe that protects wires. It does not supply current itself.
choiceExplanations.Feeder: Feeder carries power from the service equipment to a panel, not directly to lights and outlets.

items.question: It is the measure of the resistance of materials to bending stresses

choiceExplanations.Modulus of resilience: Modulus of resilience is the energy a material absorbs per unit volume up to its elastic limit, not bending resistance.
choiceExplanations.Modulus of rupture: Correct — Modulus of rupture is the bending stress at which a specimen fails, so it measures resistance to bending.
choiceExplanations.Modulus of rigidity: Modulus of rigidity is the shear modulus, the resistance to twisting or shear, not bending.
choiceExplanations.Modulus of elasticity: Modulus of elasticity is stress over strain in the elastic range (stiffness). It is not the bending-failure measure.

items.question: Tools that operate in principle similar with hand tools but power is derived from an electric motor are called.

choiceExplanations.Manual hand tools: Manual hand tools use human power only, not a motor.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic shop tools: Hydraulic shop tools run on fluid pressure, not an electric motor.
choiceExplanations.Portable power tools: Correct — Portable power tools work like hand tools but get power from an electric motor, such as a portable drill or grinder.
choiceExplanations.Stationary power machines: Stationary power machines are fixed in the shop. The item describes tools that work like hand tools.

items.question: It is a plot of the aiflow against the pressure drop per unit depth of grains and seeds, which shows the resistance to airflow of such products. This plot is also called

choiceExplanations.Hukill’s curve: Hukill’s curve is used in grain drying front analysis, not airflow resistance.
choiceExplanations.Moody’s curve: Moody’s curve is a pipe friction factor chart, not a grain airflow resistance plot.
choiceExplanations.Henderson’s curve: Henderson’s curve refers to the Henderson equation for equilibrium moisture content, not airflow resistance.
choiceExplanations.Shedd’s curve: Correct — Shedd’s curve plots airflow against pressure drop per unit depth of grain or seed, showing resistance to airflow.

items.question: In a 3-phase Y-configuration system,
items.answer: Line current and the phase current are equal
choices: Phase current is greater than the line current
Line voltage and the phase voltage are equal
Phase voltage is greater than the line voltage
Line current and the phase current are equal

choiceExplanations.Phase current is greater than the line c: Phase current is greater than the line current is wrong. In a Y connection, phase and line currents are equal.
choiceExplanations.Line voltage and the phase voltage are e: Line voltage and the phase voltage are equal is wrong. In Y, line voltage is √3 times the phase voltage.
choiceExplanations.Phase voltage is greater than the line v: Phase voltage is greater than the line voltage is wrong. In Y, phase voltage is smaller than line voltage by 1/√3.
choiceExplanations.Line current and the phase current are e: Correct — In a Y connection the line carries the same current as each phase winding. Only the voltage differs, by √3.

items.question: A multi-pass rice mill is characterized by ___.
items.answer: Having a series of two or three whitening machines
choices: Having no paddy separator after the hulling stage
Having a single pass through a rubber roll huller
Having a series of two or three whitening machines
Having only one friction type whitening machine

choiceExplanations.Having no paddy separator after the hull: Having no paddy separator after the hulling stage is wrong. A multi-pass mill keeps its separation steps.
choiceExplanations.Having a single pass through a rubber ro: Having a single pass through a rubber roll huller describes a one-pass mill, the opposite of multi-pass.
choiceExplanations.Having a series of two or three whitenin: Correct — A multi-pass mill whitens the rice in two or three successive whitening machines.
choiceExplanations.Having only one friction type whitening: Having only one friction type whitening machine describes a single-pass mill, not a multi-pass one.

items.question: For small appliance circuit in residence a load of this amount must be assumed

choiceExplanations.1.7 kW: 1.7 kW is not the assumed load. Small appliance circuits are assumed at 1.5 kW.
choiceExplanations.1.3 kW: 1.3 kW is not the assumed load. Small appliance circuits are assumed at 1.5 kW.
choiceExplanations.1.6 kW: 1.6 kW is not the assumed load. Small appliance circuits are assumed at 1.5 kW.
choiceExplanations.1.5 kW: Correct — 1.5 kW is the load assumed for each small appliance circuit in a residence (about 1500 VA).

items.question: These are materials where the electrons in the outer shells have low resistance to movement.

choiceExplanations.Conductors: Correct — Conductors have loosely held outer electrons that move easily, so resistance is low.
choiceExplanations.Dielectrics: Dielectrics are insulating materials whose electrons are tightly bound, so they resist current strongly.
choiceExplanations.Insulators: Insulators have tightly bound electrons and very high resistance, the opposite of this item.
choiceExplanations.Semiconductors: Semiconductors have conductivity between conductors and insulators, not low resistance.

items.question: Electrical equipment such as alternators, generators, and electric motors operate based on what law(s):

choiceExplanations.Electrostatics: Electrostatics deals with stationary charges, not rotating machines.
choiceExplanations.Electrochemistry: Electrochemistry deals with chemical reactions that produce electricity, as in batteries, not generators and motors.
choiceExplanations.Thermodynamics: Thermodynamics covers heat and energy, not the magnetic principle of these machines.
choiceExplanations.Electromagnetism: Correct — Alternators, generators and motors work by electromagnetic induction and the magnetic force on current-carrying conductors.

items.question: The rules say that this number of outlets must be allowed for a 15-ampere circuit.

choiceExplanations.6 to 8: 6 to 8 is too low. The rule allows 8 to 10 outlets on a 15 A circuit.
choiceExplanations.9 to 11: 9 to 11 is too high. The rule allows 8 to 10 outlets.
choiceExplanations.7 to 9: 7 to 9 is not the rule. The rule allows 8 to 10 outlets.
choiceExplanations.8 to 10: Correct — 8 to 10 is the number of outlets the rule allows on a 15-ampere circuit.

items.question: The rate of electrical power used or consumed.

choiceExplanations.Watt: Correct — Watt is the unit of power, the rate at which electrical energy is used.
choiceExplanations.Ampere: Ampere is the unit of current, not power.
choiceExplanations.Joule: Joule is the unit of energy or work, not its rate.
choiceExplanations.Volt: Volt is the unit of electrical pressure, not power.

items.question: It is a device which serves as the first link between the service entrance entrance switch and the generator.

choiceExplanations.Transformer: Correct — Transformer is the device that links the generator to the service entrance switch, changing voltage as needed.
choiceExplanations.Rectifier: Rectifier converts AC to DC. It is not the link between generator and service entrance.
choiceExplanations.Switchgear: Switchgear is a protective switching assembly. It is not the keyed first link.
choiceExplanations.Inverter: Inverter converts DC to AC. It is not the link between generator and service entrance.

items.question: If 4 or more fixed appliances are included, this demand factor can be used on the total of the fixed appliances.

choiceExplanations.65%: 65% is not the factor. For four or more fixed appliances it is 75%.
choiceExplanations.75%: Correct — 75% is the demand factor applied to the total of four or more fixed appliances.
choiceExplanations.80%: 80% is not the factor. For four or more fixed appliances it is 75%.
choiceExplanations.70%: 70% is not the factor. For four or more fixed appliances it is 75%.

items.question: A motor adapted for load that are easy to start such as centrifugal pumps, bench grinder, and others.

choiceExplanations.Repulsion-start motor: Repulsion-start motor gives high starting torque for hard-to-start loads, not easy ones.
choiceExplanations.Capacitor-start motor: Capacitor-start motor gives high starting torque for hard-starting loads like compressors.
choiceExplanations.Wound-rotor motor: Wound-rotor motor is a slip-ring induction motor for heavy starts and speed control.
choiceExplanations.Split-phase motor: Correct — Split-phase motor has moderate starting torque and suits easy-starting loads such as centrifugal pumps and bench grinders.

items.question: The ratio of the true power to the apparent power.

choiceExplanations.Power factor: Correct — Power factor is true power (kW) divided by apparent power (kVA).
choiceExplanations.Load factor: Load factor is average load over peak load, not true over apparent power.
choiceExplanations.Demand factor: Demand factor is maximum demand over total connected load.
choiceExplanations.Form factor: Form factor is the RMS value over the average value of a waveform.

items.question: Type of kilowatt-hour meter that is read exactly in like manner as the mileage indicator of the automobile

choiceExplanations.Thermal-demand type: Thermal-demand type measures maximum demand with a heat-based element. It is not read like a mileage counter.
choiceExplanations.Pointer-dial type: Pointer-dial type is read from several pointer dials, not a direct-reading counter.
choiceExplanations.Cyclometer type: Correct — Cyclometer type has number drums that show the reading directly, just like a car odometer.
choiceExplanations.Digital-display type: Digital-display type shows numbers on an electronic display, not on mechanical drums like an odometer.

items.question: A kilowatt-hour meter with four dials and each dial is calibrated in opposite direction and dial readings from left to right give thousands, hundreds, tens, and single units of kilowatt-hour respectively

choiceExplanations.Cyclometer type: Cyclometer type shows numbers directly on drums, not on pointer dials.
choiceExplanations.Digital-display type: Digital-display type uses an electronic screen, not four pointer dials.
choiceExplanations.Recording-chart type: Recording-chart type records usage on a chart. It does not use four calibrated dials.
choiceExplanations.Pointer-dial type: Correct — Pointer-dial type has four pointer dials turning in alternating directions, read left to right as thousands, hundreds, tens and units.

items.question: A magnetic device used to convert electrical energy into linear motion

choiceExplanations.Inductor: Inductor stores energy in a magnetic field. It does not produce linear motion.
choiceExplanations.Commutator: Commutator is the segmented ring that reverses current in a DC machine.
choiceExplanations.Transformer: Transformer transfers AC energy between circuits by induction, without motion.
choiceExplanations.Solenoid: Correct — Solenoid is a coil whose magnetic field pulls a plunger, converting electrical energy to linear motion.

items.question: It is the ratio of the quantity in working place to the quantity of light output from the source.

choiceExplanations.Maintenance Factor: Maintenance Factor accounts for dirt and lamp aging that reduce light over time.
choiceExplanations.Depreciation Factor: Depreciation Factor is the loss of light output from dirt or lamp aging, not the ratio to source output.
choiceExplanations.Reflection Factor: Reflection Factor is the fraction of light reflected by a surface.
choiceExplanations.Coefficient of Utilization: Correct — Coefficient of Utilization is the ratio of lumens reaching the working plane to lumens emitted by the lamps.

items.question: Another term used for circuit breaker

choiceExplanations.Isolator: Isolator is a switch for disconnecting a circuit with no load. It does not trip on fault current.
choiceExplanations.Contactor: Contactor is an electrically operated switch for starting or stopping loads.
choiceExplanations.Fuse: Correct — Fuse is the keyed term here, since both a fuse and a circuit breaker open the circuit on overcurrent.
choiceExplanations.Relay: Relay is a switch operated by a small control signal.

items.question: A device use to protect branch circuit form overloading.

choiceExplanations.Transfer switch: Transfer switch switches a load between normal and standby power sources.
choiceExplanations.Circuit breaker: Correct — Circuit breaker is an automatic protective device that trips to protect a branch circuit from overload and short circuit.
choiceExplanations.Voltage regulator: Voltage regulator keeps output voltage steady. It does not protect against overload.
choiceExplanations.Surge arrester: Surge arrester diverts voltage surges such as lightning, not sustained overload current.

items.question: Percentage energy conversion of an average farm electric motor

choiceExplanations.75 %: Correct — 75 % is the typical energy conversion efficiency of an average farm electric motor.
choiceExplanations.80 %: 80 % is higher than the keyed average of 75%.
choiceExplanations.70 %: 70 % is lower than the keyed average of 75%.
choiceExplanations.65 %: 65 % is lower than the keyed average of 75%.

items.question: It is an electric distribution system whereby more than one voltage sources are combined through the wye (Y) or delta (Δ) connections.

choiceExplanations.Polyphase: Correct — Polyphase means several voltage sources combined through wye or delta connections, as in 3-phase systems.
choiceExplanations.Series-parallel: Series-parallel describes how components are wired, not a distribution system of combined voltage sources.
choiceExplanations.Direct-current: Direct-current has one polarity and one source. It does not use wye or delta connections.
choiceExplanations.Single-phase: Single-phase uses one alternating voltage source, so there is nothing to combine in wye or delta.

items.question: When the resistance of a circuit is zero, it is a/an:

choiceExplanations.Short circuit: Correct — Short circuit is a path with zero or near-zero resistance, so current becomes very high.
choiceExplanations.Closed circuit: Closed circuit is a complete path, but it still has resistance, so it is not defined by zero resistance.
choiceExplanations.Open circuit: Open circuit has a break, so resistance is infinite, not zero.
choiceExplanations.Series circuit: Series circuit is a layout with one path. It is not defined by zero resistance.

items.question: When measuring an unknown voltage or current in a circuit, always start with:
items.answer: The highest range of the meter
choices: The highest range of the meter
The zero setting of the meter
The lowest range of the meter
The middle range of the meter

choiceExplanations.The highest range of the meter: Correct — The highest range of the meter protects the meter. If the unknown value is large, a high range prevents overload and damage; then step the range down.
choiceExplanations.The zero setting of the meter: The zero setting of the meter is not a range and would give no usable reading.
choiceExplanations.The lowest range of the meter: The lowest range of the meter can overload and damage the meter if the unknown value is large.
choiceExplanations.The middle range of the meter: The middle range of the meter still risks overloading the meter, so it is not the safe starting point.

items.question: This is the stationary part of an electric motor. It contains pairs of cores made up of thin section of soft iron. The cores are wound with insulated copper wire to form one or more pairs of magnetic poles.

choiceExplanations.Rotor: Rotor is the rotating part of a motor, not the fixed part.
choiceExplanations.Armature: Armature is the rotating coil assembly in DC machines, not the stationary part.
choiceExplanations.Stator: Correct — Stator is the stationary part of a motor, with soft-iron cores wound with insulated copper wire to form magnetic poles.
choiceExplanations.Commutator: Commutator is the rotating segmented ring on the armature of a DC machine.

items.question: The standard frequency of AC electricity in the Philippines is:

choiceExplanations.48 cyles/second: 48 cyles/second is not a standard frequency. The Philippines uses 60 Hz.
choiceExplanations.54 cyles/second: 54 cyles/second is not a standard frequency. The Philippines uses 60 Hz.
choiceExplanations.66 cyles/second: 66 cyles/second is not a standard frequency. The Philippines uses 60 Hz.
choiceExplanations.60 cyles/second: Correct — 60 cyles/second is the Philippine standard AC frequency, 60 Hz.

items.question: The human body offers less opposition to the flow of current when the skin is:

choiceExplanations.Dry: Dry skin has higher resistance, so less current flows. It is the opposite of the answer.
choiceExplanations.Thick: Thick skin has higher resistance and passes less current.
choiceExplanations.Calloused: Calloused skin is thick and hard, so its resistance is higher.
choiceExplanations.Wet: Correct — Wet skin has lower resistance because moisture and salts conduct, so more current flows.

items.question: The color of the ground wire of a kilowatthour meter is:

choiceExplanations.Red: Red is normally a live (hot) wire color, not the ground.
choiceExplanations.White: White is the grounded neutral wire color, not the ground wire.
choiceExplanations.Green: Correct — Green is the standard color for ground wires.
choiceExplanations.Black: Black is a live (hot) wire color, not the ground.

items.question: It refers to the motor torque at zero speed or the maximum torque available to start a load.

choiceExplanations.Locked-rotor torque: Correct — Locked-rotor torque is the torque at zero speed, the maximum torque available to start a load.
choiceExplanations.Full-load torque: Full-load torque is the torque at rated speed and power, not at zero speed.
choiceExplanations.Breakdown torque: Breakdown torque is the maximum torque a motor gives while running without stalling.
choiceExplanations.Pull-up torque: Pull-up torque is the lowest torque during acceleration from standstill to running speed.

items.question: Wire mesh or perforated metal sheet; moving in back-and-forth direction; permitting smaller particles to fall through the openings and larger particles to remain on top.

choiceExplanations.Aspirator: Aspirator separates light material using air suction, not a shaking screen.
choiceExplanations.Winnower: Winnower separates chaff from grain using moving air, not a screen.
choiceExplanations.Sifter: Correct — Sifter is a reciprocating wire mesh or perforated sheet that lets small particles fall through and holds large ones on top.
choiceExplanations.Polisher: Polisher smooths milled rice. It is not a screening device.

items.question: Connecting fans in series will ______

choiceExplanations.Produce the same flow rate: Correct — Produce the same flow rate is the keyed answer. Fans in series add static pressure, while airflow stays about the same as for one fan.
choiceExplanations.Produce the same static pressure: Produce the same static pressure is wrong. Series fans add their pressures, so pressure rises.
choiceExplanations.Increase the total flow rate: Increase the total flow rate describes fans in parallel, not in series.
choiceExplanations.Reduce the total static pressure: Reduce the total static pressure is wrong. Series fans increase pressure.

items.question: Which of the following will increase the air flow rate of a ventilation system?

choiceExplanations.Connecting fans in parallel: Correct — fans in parallel add their air flows at the same pressure, increasing total flow rate.
choiceExplanations.Using a smaller fan diameter: Wrong — a smaller fan diameter moves less air (flow rises with diameter cubed).
choiceExplanations.Operating fans at half speed: Wrong — by the fan laws, flow is proportional to speed, so half speed gives about half the flow.
choiceExplanations.Connecting fans in series: Wrong — fans in series mainly add pressure, not flow; flow stays about the same.

items.question: Recommended lighting requirement for holding area such as milking parlor, poultry dressing plant, etc.

choiceExplanations.80 lumen/m2: 80 lumen/m2 is lower than the recommended 100 lumen/m2 for holding areas.
choiceExplanations.100 lumen/m2: Correct — 100 lumen/m2 is the recommended level for holding areas such as milking parlors and poultry dressing plants.
choiceExplanations.110 lumen/m2: 110 lumen/m2 is not the recommended figure. The value is 100 lumen/m2.
choiceExplanations.90 lumen/m2: 90 lumen/m2 is not the recommended figure. The value is 100 lumen/m2.

items.question: General lighting requirement for milking parlor, poultry dressing plant, etc.

choiceExplanations.160 lumen/m2: 160 lumen/m2 is lower than the general lighting requirement of 200 lumen/m2.
choiceExplanations.180 lumen/m2: 180 lumen/m2 is lower than the general lighting requirement of 200 lumen/m2.
choiceExplanations.200 lumen/m2: Correct — 200 lumen/m2 is the recommended general lighting level for milking parlors and dressing plants.
choiceExplanations.220 lumen/m2: 220 lumen/m2 is higher than the recommended 200 lumen/m2.

items.question: Lighting requirement for working tables in poultry dressing plant, tissue culture laboratory room, etc.

choiceExplanations.500 lumen/m2: Correct — 500 lumen/m2 is the recommended level for fine work at tables in dressing plants and tissue culture rooms.
choiceExplanations.450 lumen/m2: 450 lumen/m2 is lower than the required 500 lumen/m2 for working tables.
choiceExplanations.550 lumen/m2: 550 lumen/m2 is higher than the recommended 500 lumen/m2.
choiceExplanations.400 lumen/m2: 400 lumen/m2 is lower than the required 500 lumen/m2 for working tables.

items.question: Negatively charge of electricity

choiceExplanations.Electron: Correct — Electron carries a negative electric charge.
choiceExplanations.Positron: Positron is the antimatter twin of the electron and is positively charged.

items.question: It is the strength of an electron current

choiceExplanations.Ohm: Ohm is the unit of resistance, not current.
choiceExplanations.Watt: Watt is the unit of power.
choiceExplanations.Volt: Volt is the unit of electrical pressure.
choiceExplanations.Ampere: Correct — Ampere is the unit of current, the strength of an electron current.

items.question: It is the electrical pressure that cause the electron to move through a conductor

choiceExplanations.Resistance: Resistance opposes current flow. It does not push electrons.
choiceExplanations.Capacitance: Capacitance is the ability to store charge, not to push electrons.
choiceExplanations.Current: Current is the flow of electrons itself, not the pressure causing it.
choiceExplanations.Voltage: Correct — Voltage is the electrical pressure (potential difference) that drives electrons through a conductor.

items.question: The flow of current from in DC is ______

choiceExplanations.Neutral to negative: Neutral to negative is not a recognized direction of DC flow.
choiceExplanations.Negative to positive: Correct — Negative to positive is the keyed direction. DC electrons flow from the negative terminal to the positive terminal.
choiceExplanations.Positive to ground: Positive to ground is not a description of DC electron flow.
choiceExplanations.Positive to negative: Positive to negative is the conventional current direction, but this item keys electron flow, negative to positive.

items.question: Tie wire refers to _____

choiceExplanations.Gauge no. 13 GI wire: Gauge no. 13 GI wire is not the tie wire size. Tie wire is gauge no. 16.
choiceExplanations.Gauge no. 18 GI wire: Gauge no. 18 GI wire is thinner than tie wire, which is gauge no. 16.
choiceExplanations.Gauge no. 16 GI wire: Correct — Gauge no. 16 GI wire is the standard tie wire used to bind reinforcing bars.
choiceExplanations.Gauge no. 14 GI wire: Gauge no. 14 GI wire is not the tie wire size. Tie wire is gauge no. 16.

items.question: Tie wire is order in terms of _____

choiceExplanations.Kilogram: Correct — Kilogram is how tie wire is sold, by weight, since it comes loose in coils or bundles.
choiceExplanations.Piece: Piece is not how tie wire is ordered. It is a wire sold by weight.
choiceExplanations.Roll: Roll is not the ordering unit. Tie wire is bought by the kilogram.
choiceExplanations.Meter: Meter is a length unit. Tie wire is ordered by weight, not length.

items.question: A kilogram of tie wire is approximately ________

choiceExplanations.53 meter: Correct — 53 meter is the approximate length of gauge 16 tie wire in one kilogram.
choiceExplanations.58 meter: 58 meter is not the usual figure. One kilogram of tie wire is about 53 meters.
choiceExplanations.42 meter: 42 meter is not the usual figure. One kilogram of tie wire is about 53 meters.
choiceExplanations.48 meter: 48 meter is not the usual figure. One kilogram of tie wire is about 53 meters.

items.question: It is a thermometer used to measure temperature generated by the difference in voltage between the junction of two dissimilar metals.

choiceExplanations.Bimetallic thermometer: Bimetallic thermometer works by two metals expanding differently, not by voltage.
choiceExplanations.Thermocouple thermometer: Correct — Thermocouple thermometer uses the voltage produced between the junction of two dissimilar metals, which depends on temperature.
choiceExplanations.Resistance thermometer: Resistance thermometer senses temperature through change in electrical resistance, not generated voltage.
choiceExplanations.Infrared thermometer: Infrared thermometer reads heat radiation from a distance, not junction voltage.

items.question: An electrical conductor consisting of group of wires twisted to form a metallic string.

choiceExplanations.Parallel wire: Parallel wire is not the term for twisted strands forming one conductor.
choiceExplanations.Single-core wire: Single-core wire has one solid conductor, not twisted strands.
choiceExplanations.Stranded wire: Correct — Stranded wire is a conductor made of several small wires twisted together, making it flexible.
choiceExplanations.Solid wire: Solid wire is one single piece of metal, not twisted strands.

items.question: One foot candle is equal to _______

choiceExplanations.Lumen per solid angle: Lumen per solid angle is the candela, a unit of luminous intensity, not illuminance.
choiceExplanations.Watt per unit area: Watt per unit area measures radiant power density, not illuminance.
choiceExplanations.Lumen per unit area: Correct — One foot-candle is one lumen per square foot, which is a measure of illuminance.
choiceExplanations.Candela per unit area: Candela per unit area is luminance (brightness), not illuminance.

items.question: It is the system of piling the grain that provides ventilation space between bags and allows circulation of convenience air current that provides a medium for heat dissipation

choiceExplanations.Japanese method: Correct — Japanese method is the keyed grain piling system that leaves ventilation space between bags so air can carry heat away.
choiceExplanations.Chinese method: Chinese method is not the keyed system for this ventilation-space piling.
choiceExplanations.Pyramid method: Pyramid method describes a stack shape and is not the keyed system.
choiceExplanations.Block method: Block method stacks bags tightly with little air space, so it does not give ventilation.

items.question: Under PAES 402:2001 (Agricultural Structures – Housing for Broiler Production) for a slotted floor, if welded wire is used, it should have ________, and the wire shall be supported every 300 mm.
items.rationale: According to PAES 402:2001 (Housing for Broiler Production), slotted floors using welded wire shall have a 625 mm² mesh (25 mm × 25 mm) and be supported every 300 mm.

choiceExplanations.900 mm² mesh (30 mm × 30 mm): 900 mm² mesh (30 mm × 30 mm) is not the PAES 402 mesh size for welded wire slotted floors. The size is 625 mm² (25 mm x 25 mm).
choiceExplanations.2,500 mm² mesh (50 mm × 50 mm): 2,500 mm² mesh (50 mm × 50 mm) is too large an opening for a broiler slotted floor. PAES 402 specifies 625 mm².
choiceExplanations.400 mm² mesh (20 mm × 20 mm): 400 mm² mesh (20 mm × 20 mm) is smaller than the PAES 402 specification of 625 mm² (25 mm x 25 mm).
choiceExplanations.625 mm² mesh (25 mm × 25 mm): Correct — 625 mm² mesh (25 mm × 25 mm) is the welded wire mesh that PAES 402 specifies for broiler slotted floors, with the wire supported every 300 mm.

items.question: Causes fluctuations in voltage

choiceExplanations.Armature: Correct — Armature is the rotating winding of a motor or generator. In this item it is keyed as the part that causes voltage fluctuation.
choiceExplanations.Stator: Stator is the fixed part of a machine and does not cause the fluctuation in this item.
choiceExplanations.Commutator: Commutator switches current direction in a DC machine and is not keyed here.
choiceExplanations.Rectifier: Rectifier converts AC to DC. It does not cause the fluctuation keyed here.

items.question: Converts DC to AC

choiceExplanations.Inverter: Correct — Inverter changes DC power into AC power.
choiceExplanations.Transformer: Transformer changes AC voltage levels and does not change DC to AC.
choiceExplanations.Alternator: Alternator turns mechanical energy into AC. It does not convert DC.
choiceExplanations.Rectifier: Rectifier converts AC to DC, the opposite direction.

items.question: a hybrid between series wound and shunt wound motor designs

choiceExplanations.Compound-wound motor: Correct — Compound-wound motor has both series and shunt field windings, so it is a mix of the two designs.
choiceExplanations.Separately-excited motor: Separately-excited motor has its field supplied from an independent source, not a series-shunt mix.
choiceExplanations.Brushless-DC motor: Brushless-DC motor uses electronic commutation instead of brushes.
