choiceExplanations.Permanent-magnet motor: Permanent-magnet motor uses magnets for the field, with no series or shunt winding.

items.question: AWG sizes that equal to 10,000 circular mils.

choiceExplanations.AWG #10: Correct — AWG #10 has a cross-section of about 10,000 circular mils (10,380 cmil).
choiceExplanations.AWG #9: AWG #9 is larger, about 11,700 circular mils.
choiceExplanations.AWG #8: AWG #8 is larger, about 16,500 circular mils.
choiceExplanations.AWG #11: AWG #11 is smaller, about 8,230 circular mils.

items.question: diode needed as protection against lighting in the solar installation

choiceExplanations.Bypass diode: Bypass diode lets current go around a shaded solar cell or panel. It is not for lightning protection.
choiceExplanations.Zener diode: Zener diode clamps voltage at a set level and is used for regulation or surge clamping, but it is not the keyed answer.
choiceExplanations.Blocking diode: Correct — Blocking diode is the keyed answer. It stops reverse current flowing back into the panel. Check this key, since surge protection normally uses other devices.
choiceExplanations.Schottky diode: Schottky diode is a fast, low-loss diode used for rectifying, not the keyed protection.

items.question: Area where the cursor is at the current position

choiceExplanations.Command area: Command area is where commands are typed and prompts shown, not the cursor position area.
choiceExplanations.Layout area: Layout area refers to the paper space layout tabs.
choiceExplanations.Status area: Status area shows modes and coordinates, not the cursor drawing space.
choiceExplanations.Drawing area: Correct — Drawing area is the main screen area in AutoCAD where the cursor sits and objects are drawn.

items.question: is standardized under the ASTM International test procedure used to determine a material’s impact resistance (toughness), or the material’s tendency to resist breaking when subjected to a sudden force or impulse.

choiceExplanations.IZOD test: Correct — IZOD test measures impact toughness by striking a notched specimen with a pendulum under ASTM standard.
choiceExplanations.VICKERS test: VICKERS test measures hardness with a diamond pyramid indenter, not impact toughness.
choiceExplanations.BRINELL test: BRINELL test measures hardness with a steel ball indenter, not impact toughness.
choiceExplanations.ROCKWELL test: ROCKWELL test measures hardness by indentation depth, not impact toughness.

items.question: is employed to form parallel lines, concentric circles, and parallel curves in AUTOCAD.

choiceExplanations.Fillet (F): Fillet (F) rounds a corner between two lines. It does not form parallels.
choiceExplanations.Offset (O): Correct — Offset (O) creates parallel lines, concentric circles and parallel curves at a set distance.
choiceExplanations.Array (AR): Array (AR) makes multiple copies in a rectangular or polar pattern.
choiceExplanations.Mirror (MI): Mirror (MI) makes a reflected copy of objects about a line.

items.question: convert AC to DC

choiceExplanations.Step-down transformer: Step-down transformer lowers AC voltage but stays AC.
choiceExplanations.Power inverter: Power inverter changes DC to AC, the opposite direction.
choiceExplanations.Converter/rectifier: Correct — Converter/rectifier changes AC into DC, usually with diodes.
choiceExplanations.Voltage regulator: Voltage regulator keeps output voltage steady and does not change AC to DC.

items.question: Excellent conductor with unbounded protons and electrons

choiceExplanations.Plasma: Correct — Plasma is an ionized gas with free positive ions and electrons, making it an excellent conductor.
choiceExplanations.Semiconductor: Semiconductor conducts only moderately, between conductors and insulators.
choiceExplanations.Dielectric: Dielectric is an insulating material with tightly bound charges.
choiceExplanations.Electrolyte: Electrolyte conducts through moving ions in a liquid, not free protons and electrons.

items.question: Similar to stone check dams however the stones in this case are placed on rectangular wire mesh

choiceExplanations.Gabion: Correct — Gabion is a wire mesh box or basket filled with stones, used as a check dam or retaining structure.
choiceExplanations.Revetment: Revetment is a facing of stone or concrete on a slope or bank, not stones in wire mesh baskets.
choiceExplanations.Weir: Weir is a low dam or overflow structure used to measure or control flow.
choiceExplanations.Riprap: Riprap is loose stone placed on a bank for protection, without wire mesh.

items.question: Efficiency of Electric Motor

choiceExplanations.50-90%: Correct — 50-90% is the typical efficiency range of electric motors.
choiceExplanations.10–50%: 10–50% is too low for electric motors.

items.question: series of axial keys machined into a shaft with corresponding grooved machined into the bore of the mating part

choiceExplanations.Spline: Correct — Spline is a series of axial keys cut along a shaft that fit grooves in the mating part, transmitting torque.
choiceExplanations.Coupling: Coupling joins two shafts end to end. It is not a set of keys and grooves.
choiceExplanations.Bushing: Bushing is a sleeve that supports a shaft, not a series of keys.
choiceExplanations.Keyway: Keyway is a single groove for one key, not a series of keys.

items.question: type of cropping system where in different crops are planted in an area one after the other each season.

choiceExplanations.Strip cropping: Strip cropping plants different crops in alternating strips across a slope at the same time.
choiceExplanations.Ratoon cropping: Ratoon cropping harvests regrowth from the stubble of the same crop, as in sugarcane.
choiceExplanations.Alley cropping: Alley cropping grows crops in the spaces between rows of trees or shrubs.
choiceExplanations.Relay cropping: Correct — Relay cropping is the keyed answer, where a new crop is planted in the area after another crop one season after another.

items.question: It is showery precipitation in form of irregular pallets of size more than 8mm. ___ occurs in violent thunderstorm in which vertical current very strong.

choiceExplanations.Sleet: Sleet is frozen rain or ice pellets smaller than hail.
choiceExplanations.Glaze: Glaze is a smooth ice coating formed by freezing rain.
choiceExplanations.Hail: Correct — Hail is showery precipitation of irregular ice pellets that forms in violent thunderstorms with strong vertical currents.
choiceExplanations.Drizzle: Drizzle is very fine, slow-falling rain droplets.

items.question: Uses current and potential electrodes in an uncased well to measure the resistivities of the surrounding media wherein the variation of its traces is related to depth

choiceExplanations.Resistivity logging: Correct — Resistivity logging uses current and potential electrodes in an uncased well to measure resistivity of the surrounding media against depth.
choiceExplanations.Gamma-ray logging: Gamma-ray logging measures natural radioactivity of rocks, not electrode resistivity.
choiceExplanations.Acoustic logging: Acoustic logging measures how sound waves travel in the rock.
choiceExplanations.Neutron logging: Neutron logging measures hydrogen content (porosity) using neutron radiation.

items.question: These are discrete layers that make up a soil profile. They are typically parallel with the ground surface.

choiceExplanations.Soil colloids: Soil colloids are very fine clay and humus particles, not layers.
choiceExplanations.Soil aggregates: Soil aggregates are clumps of soil particles, not layers of a profile.
choiceExplanations.Soil horizons: Correct — Soil horizons are the distinct layers of a soil profile, roughly parallel to the ground surface.
choiceExplanations.Soil separates: Soil separates are the sand, silt and clay size groups of particles.

items.question: Electrification: The ________ is normally drawn with hard dashed lines.

choiceExplanations.Factory wiring: Factory wiring is the wiring done at the factory, usually drawn in solid lines.
choiceExplanations.Field wiring: Correct — Field wiring is installed on site and is drawn with hard dashed lines to separate it from internal wiring.
choiceExplanations.Internal wiring: Internal wiring is the wiring inside equipment, usually drawn as solid lines.
choiceExplanations.Control wiring: Control wiring is a type of circuit, not the one shown with dashed lines for field installation.

items.question: Electrification: Laminations in transformers are provided to reduce _______.

choiceExplanations.Eddy currents: Correct — Thin insulated laminations break up the paths of circulating eddy currents in the core, reducing these losses.
choiceExplanations.Copper losses: Copper losses come from winding resistance and are not reduced by core laminations.
choiceExplanations.Hysteresis losses: Hysteresis losses are reduced by using good magnetic steel, not by laminating.
choiceExplanations.Leakage fluxes: Leakage fluxes are reduced by winding design, not by laminated cores.

items.question: Electrification: Thermal spot in wire is due to ______.

choiceExplanations.Low current flowing: Low current flowing produces little heat, so it does not cause a hot spot.
choiceExplanations.High current flowing: Correct — High current flowing produces heat (I squared R), so excess current creates thermal hot spots in a wire.
choiceExplanations.Thick wire insulation: Thick wire insulation does not create a hot spot by itself.
choiceExplanations.High power factor: High power factor means efficient use of current. It does not cause hot spots.

items.question: Electrification: C.O. and lighting outlets have ____ amperes.

choiceExplanations.14 amperes: 14 amperes is not the standard rating. A convenience outlet and lighting circuit is rated 15 A.
choiceExplanations.15 amperes: Correct — 15 amperes is the standard rating for convenience outlet and lighting circuits.
choiceExplanations.16 amperes: 16 amperes is not the standard rating. It is 15 A.
choiceExplanations.12 amperes: 12 amperes is not the standard rating. It is 15 A.

items.question: Electrification: Highest conductivity and lowest resistivity metal is _____.

choiceExplanations.Al (aluminum): Al (aluminum) conducts well, but silver conducts better.
choiceExplanations.Cu (copper): Cu (copper) is the common best-value conductor, but silver is slightly better.
choiceExplanations.Ag (silver): Correct — Ag (silver) has the highest conductivity and lowest resistivity of all metals.
choiceExplanations.Au (gold): Au (gold) resists corrosion but conducts less than silver and copper.

items.question: ELECTRIFICATION: Material with high resistance is called as ______.

choiceExplanations.Semiconductor: Semiconductor has resistance between a conductor and an insulator.
choiceExplanations.Insulator: Correct — Insulator has very high resistance, so it blocks current flow.
choiceExplanations.Conductor: Conductor has low resistance, so current flows easily.
choiceExplanations.Superconductor: Superconductor has zero resistance at very low temperatures.

items.question: ENGINEERING DRAWING: A line is parallel to the vertical plane at all its points have the same distance to the vertical plane is called ________

choiceExplanations.Frontal line: Correct — Frontal line is parallel to the vertical (frontal) plane, so it shows its true length in the front view.
choiceExplanations.Profile line: Profile line is parallel to the profile plane, not the vertical plane.
choiceExplanations.Horizontal line: Horizontal line is parallel to the horizontal plane.
choiceExplanations.Oblique line: Oblique line is not parallel to any principal plane.

items.question: ELECTRIFICATION: When the voltage is the same throughout all the parts of the circuit, the circuit line is _______.

choiceExplanations.Series: Series circuits share the same current while voltage divides among parts.
choiceExplanations.Parallel: Correct — Parallel circuits give the same voltage across every branch.
choiceExplanations.Combination: Combination circuits mix series and parallel, so voltage is not the same everywhere.
choiceExplanations.Bridge: Bridge circuits balance voltage between arms and do not give equal voltage everywhere.

items.question: As a rule of thumb, single-phase alternating current electric motor should be used for applications requiring:

choiceExplanations.less than 4 hp: less than 4 hp is lower than the usual rule. Single-phase motors are used for less than 5 hp.
choiceExplanations.less than 5 hp: Correct — less than 5 hp is the rule of thumb. Above this size, three-phase motors are preferred for efficiency and cost.
choiceExplanations.less than 7 hp: less than 7 hp is above the usual rule of 5 hp.
choiceExplanations.less than 6 hp: less than 6 hp is above the usual rule of 5 hp.

items.question: The equation used in current meters is V = a + bN. What does “a” signifies?

choiceExplanations.Propeller constant: Propeller constant is the term b in V = a + bN, which multiplies the revolutions per second.
choiceExplanations.Starting velocity: Correct — Starting velocity is the term a, the minimum velocity needed to start the meter's propeller turning.
choiceExplanations.Approach velocity: Approach velocity is the water speed approaching a structure, not a term in this equation.
choiceExplanations.Critical velocity: Critical velocity is the flow speed at which flow changes regime, not term a.

items.question: What is the size of the wire AWG 10?

choiceExplanations.4.4 mm²: 4.4 mm² is not the usual table value. AWG 10 is about 5.5 mm².
choiceExplanations.5.5 mm²: Correct — 5.5 mm² is the usual rounded cross-section of AWG 10 wire.
choiceExplanations.5.0 mm²: 5.0 mm² is not the usual table value. AWG 10 is about 5.5 mm².
choiceExplanations.6.1 mm²: 6.1 mm² is not the usual table value. AWG 10 is about 5.5 mm².

items.question: AWG no. 14

choiceExplanations.1.25mm²: 1.25mm² is a smaller size. AWG 14 is about 2 mm².
choiceExplanations.2mm²: Correct — 2mm² is the cross-section of AWG 14 wire, about 2 mm².

items.question: AWG no. 12

choiceExplanations.3.5mm²: Correct — 3.5mm² is the usual cross-section of AWG 12 wire.
choiceExplanations.4.5mm²: 4.5mm² is not the usual table value. AWG 12 is 3.5 mm².
choiceExplanations.1.5mm²: 1.5mm² is too small. AWG 12 is 3.5 mm².
choiceExplanations.2.5mm²: 2.5mm² is too small. AWG 12 is 3.5 mm².

items.question: AWG no. 8

choiceExplanations.9.8mm²: 9.8mm² is not the usual table value. AWG 8 is 8.8 mm².
choiceExplanations.6.8mm²: 6.8mm² is too small. AWG 8 is 8.8 mm².
choiceExplanations.7.8mm²: 7.8mm² is too small. AWG 8 is 8.8 mm².
choiceExplanations.8.8mm²: Correct — 8.8mm² is the usual cross-section of AWG 8 wire.

items.question: This is the effect on the voltage and current when hit by light.

choiceExplanations.Photoconductive: Photoconductive effect changes the material's resistance with light and does not generate voltage.
choiceExplanations.Photovoltaic: Correct — Photovoltaic effect produces voltage and current in a material when light hits it, as in solar cells.
choiceExplanations.Piezoelectric: Piezoelectric effect makes voltage from mechanical pressure, not light.
choiceExplanations.Thermoelectric: Thermoelectric effect makes voltage from a temperature difference, not light.

items.question: In PAES 404 – Housing for Goat and Sheep, the housing shall be provided with a lighting intensity of ____.

choiceExplanations.160 lux: 160 lux is lower than the 200 lux in PAES 404.
choiceExplanations.244 lux: 244 lux is not the PAES 404 value. It is 200 lux.
choiceExplanations.200 lux: Correct — 200 lux is the lighting intensity required for goat and sheep housing in PAES 404.
choiceExplanations.216 lux: 216 lux is not the PAES 404 value. It is 200 lux.

items.question: A complete lighting unit consisting of a lamp or lamps together with parts designed to distribute the light, to position and protect the lamps, and to connect the lamps to the power supply.

choiceExplanations.Reflector: Reflector is only the part that redirects light, not the whole unit.
choiceExplanations.Diffuser: Diffuser is only the part that scatters light, not the whole unit.
choiceExplanations.Ballast: Ballast is the device that limits current to a discharge lamp, not the complete fixture.
choiceExplanations.Luminaire: Correct — Luminaire is the complete lighting unit: lamp, light-distributing parts, lamp holders and connection to power.

items.question: Why use maximum voltage rating on choosing an electric motor
items.answer: High efficiency The higher the voltage, the higher the torque. The voltage rating of a DC motor indicates the most efficient voltage while running. Be sure to apply the recommended voltage. If you apply too few volts, the motor will not work, whereas too many volts can short windings resulting in power loss or complete destruction.
choices: Low power factor The higher the voltage, the lower the speed. The voltage rating of a DC motor indicates the minimum load

High efficiency The higher the voltage, the higher the torque. The voltage rating of a DC motor indicates the most efficient voltage while running. Be sure to apply the recommended voltage. If you apply too few volts, the motor will not work, whereas too many volts can short windings resulting in power loss or complete destruction.
Minimal heat loss The higher the voltage, the lower the flux. The voltage rating of a DC motor specifies the armature drag
Reduced shaft speed The lower the voltage, the higher the torque. The voltage rating of a DC motor sets the stall current

choiceExplanations.Low power factor The higher the voltage,: Rated voltage is not about power factor, and a higher voltage does not lower speed. It marks the efficient operating voltage.
choiceExplanations.High efficiency The higher the voltage,: Correct — Rated voltage is the voltage at which the motor runs most efficiently. Too little voltage and it will not work; too much can short the windings and destroy it.
choiceExplanations.Minimal heat loss The higher the voltage: Rated voltage does not specify armature drag, and higher voltage does not lower flux. Too much voltage actually causes heat and damage.
choiceExplanations.Reduced shaft speed The lower the voltag: Lowering voltage does not raise torque, and rated voltage does not set stall current. It marks the most efficient running voltage.

items.question: On polarizing wiring connections, the color of neutral wire is ____.

choiceExplanations.Red: Red is normally a live (hot) wire color.
choiceExplanations.White: Correct — White is the standard color of the neutral wire in polarized wiring.
choiceExplanations.Black: Black is normally a live (hot) wire color.
choiceExplanations.Green: Green is the color for the ground wire.

items.question: A device that converts mechanical to electrical energy.

choiceExplanations.Transformer, rectifier, inverter: Transformer, rectifier, inverter change voltage or convert AC to DC. None of them turn mechanical energy into electricity.
choiceExplanations.Motor, actuator, solenoid: Motor, actuator, solenoid turn electrical energy into mechanical motion, the opposite direction.
choiceExplanations.Capacitor, inductor, resistor: Capacitor, inductor, resistor store energy or oppose current. They do not convert mechanical energy.
choiceExplanations.Generator, dynamo, alternator: Correct — Generator, dynamo, alternator all convert mechanical energy into electrical energy.

items.question: A device for measuring stream velocity

choiceExplanations.Current meter: Correct — Current meter measures stream velocity from the speed of a rotating propeller or cups.
choiceExplanations.Cipolletti weir: Cipolletti weir is a trapezoidal weir that measures discharge, not velocity directly.
choiceExplanations.Staff gauge: Staff gauge is a graduated board that reads water level.
choiceExplanations.Parshall flume: Parshall flume is a constricted channel that measures discharge, not velocity directly.

items.question: This is suitable on flat, poorly drained soils that have numerous shallow depression.

choiceExplanations.Gridiron or herringbone drain system: Gridiron or herringbone drain system are subsurface drain patterns for uniform, large level fields.
choiceExplanations.Diversion or parallel ditch system: Correct — Diversion or parallel ditch system is the keyed answer. Parallel ditches suit flat, poorly drained land. Random ditches are normally used for scattered depressions, so check this key.
choiceExplanations.Interceptor or relief drain system: Interceptor or relief drain system drains intercept groundwater on slopes or seepage areas, not depression fields.
choiceExplanations.Random or cross-slope ditch system: Random or cross-slope ditch systems are normally used for shallow depressions, which could also fit this item.

items.question: Defined as the resistance of the soil to both detachment and transport

choiceExplanations.Erodibility: Correct — Erodibility is the soil's resistance to detachment and transport by erosive forces.
choiceExplanations.Cohesiveness: Cohesiveness is how well soil particles stick together, only one factor in erodibility.
choiceExplanations.Erosivity: Erosivity is the ability of rain or runoff to cause erosion, not the soil's resistance.
choiceExplanations.Permeability: Permeability is the ease with which water moves through soil.

items.question: What is the maximum fixture spacing of a room that has a ceiling height of 3 meters and is to be lighted with directly concentrating fluorescent lamps if S/mh ratio is 0.40?

choiceExplanations.1.1m: 1.1m is not the answer. Spacing = 0.40 x 3 m = 1.2 m.
choiceExplanations.1.2m: Correct — 1.2m is S = (S/mh) x mounting height = 0.40 x 3 m.
choiceExplanations.1.4m: 1.4m is too large. Spacing = 0.40 x 3 m = 1.2 m.
choiceExplanations.1.3m: 1.3m is too large. Spacing = 0.40 x 3 m = 1.2 m.

items.question: The most common measurement of battery storage capacity of solar batteries.

choiceExplanations.Volt-ampere: Volt-ampere is a unit of apparent power, not battery capacity.
choiceExplanations.Kilowatt-hour: Kilowatt-hour is energy, used for total usage but not the most common battery rating.
choiceExplanations.Watt-peak: Watt-peak is the peak power rating of a solar panel, not battery storage.
choiceExplanations.Ampere-hour: Correct — Ampere-hour is the common rating of battery storage capacity, the current a battery can supply over time.

items.question: Motor which have parallel connection of armature to the windings (PAES 129

choiceExplanations.Shunt wound: Correct — Shunt wound motors have the field winding in parallel with the armature.
choiceExplanations.Compound wound: Compound wound motors have both series and shunt windings.
choiceExplanations.Series wound: Series wound motors connect the field winding in series with the armature.
choiceExplanations.Separately excited: Separately excited motors have the field powered from a separate source.

items.question: What causes of quick battery drain?

choiceExplanations.Open circuit: Open circuit means a broken path, so no current flows. It does not drain a battery.
choiceExplanations.Faulty starter: Faulty starter affects engine cranking and can draw heavy current when starting, but it is not the keyed cause of constant drain.
choiceExplanations.Faulty alternator: Correct — Faulty alternator is the keyed cause. A bad alternator fails to recharge the battery while running, so the charge falls quickly.
choiceExplanations.Blown fuse: Blown fuse stops current in that circuit, so it does not drain the battery.

items.question: A multi-purpose heater operates at 240 volts. It uses a pair of 28-meter AWG 10 copper wire having a total resistance of 6,912.19 ohms. Find the amperage in the main wire.

choiceExplanations.30 A: 30 A is far too high. Current is I = V/R = 240/6,912.19, which is much less than 1 A.
choiceExplanations.0.03 A: Correct — 0.03 A is I = V/R = 240 V / 6,912.19 ohms, about 0.035 A.
choiceExplanations.3 A: 3 A is too high. I = 240/6,912.19 is about 0.03 A.
choiceExplanations.0.3 A: 0.3 A is ten times too high. I = 240/6,912.19 is about 0.03 A.

items.question: Your business needs to carry out optimization of a fish cold storage facility which has a current utilization coefficient of 0.43. If the utilization coefficient is increased to 0.53, what is the effect in operating cost?
items.rationale: Increasing the utilization coefficient means higher equipment utilization and energy consumption, which directly increases the facility's operating cost.

choiceExplanations.Same: Same is wrong. Changing the utilization coefficient changes the load on the system, so cost changes.
choiceExplanations.Decrease slightly: Decrease slightly is not the keyed effect. This item keys an increase in operating cost.
choiceExplanations.Decrease significantly: Decrease significantly is not the keyed effect. This item keys an increase in operating cost.
choiceExplanations.Increase: Correct — Increase is the keyed answer. A higher utilization coefficient means the facility is used more, so operating cost rises.

items.question: A 230-volt cassava grating machine consumes 30-kW power. It needs 5 hours to grate 500 kg of cassava. What is its energy consumption per kg?
items.rationale: Total energy consumed is E = 30 kW × 5 h = 150 kWh; dividing by 500 kg gives 150 kWh / 500 kg = 0.3 kWh/kg.

choiceExplanations.3.0 kwh/kg: 3.0 kwh/kg is ten times too high. 30 kW x 5 h = 150 kWh, divided by 500 kg = 0.3 kWh/kg.
choiceExplanations.0.3 kwh/kg: Correct — 0.3 kwh/kg is 30 kW x 5 h = 150 kWh, divided by 500 kg of cassava.
choiceExplanations.0.5 kwh/kg: 0.5 kwh/kg is not right. 150 kWh / 500 kg = 0.3 kWh/kg.
choiceExplanations.0.1 kwh/kg: 0.1 kwh/kg is too low. 150 kWh / 500 kg = 0.3 kWh/kg.

items.question: As an ABE, you are assigned to create plans based on ABE standards specifically in making the electrical specifications on lighting intensities in bioprocessing plants. What should be the lux or lumens/sq. m for lighting a refrigerated storage room if a working table needs 500 lux?
items.rationale: Based on PAES 417:2002 agricultural structure lighting standards, the recommended minimum illumination for a refrigerated storage room is 50 lux.

choiceExplanations.100: 100 is too high. The ABE standard for a refrigerated storage room is 50 lumens/m², even if a working table needs 500 lux.
choiceExplanations.25: 25 is below the standard. A refrigerated storage room needs 50 lumens/m².
choiceExplanations.75: 75 is not the standard value. A refrigerated storage room needs 50 lumens/m².
choiceExplanations.50: Correct — 50 lumens/m² is the standard general lighting level for a refrigerated storage room.

items.question: A 15-watt LED lamp is used in lighting a 100 sq. m square shaped bioprocessing area. All lamps have approximately 100 lumens/watt. How many lamps are needed if the minimum brightness requirement is 500 lux or lumens/square meter?
items.rationale: Total required lumens = 100 m² × 500 lm/m² = 50,000 lm, and each lamp produces 15 W × 100 lm/W = 1,500 lm; 50,000 / 1,500 = 33.33, so 34 lamps are needed to meet the minimum requirement.

choiceExplanations.34: Correct — 34 lamps: 500 lm/m² x 100 m² = 50,000 lm. Each lamp gives 15 W x 100 = 1,500 lm. 50,000/1,500 = 33.3, rounded up to 34.
choiceExplanations.35: 35 is one lamp more than needed. 50,000 lm / 1,500 lm = 33.3, so 34 lamps.
choiceExplanations.33: 33 lamps give only 49,500 lm, below 50,000 lm. Round up to 34.
choiceExplanations.30: 30 lamps give only 45,000 lm, below the 50,000 lm required.

items.question: For an internal wiring of a farmhouse, the recommended wire size for its outlets is AWG 10. What is the minimum wire size for outlets based on the Philippine Electrical Code?
items.rationale: Under the Philippine Electrical Code (PEC), convenience outlet branch circuits (20 A) require a minimum conductor size of AWG 12 (3.5 mm²).

choiceExplanations.AWG 10: AWG 10 is the recommended size in the item, not the PEC minimum for outlets.
choiceExplanations.AWG 12: Correct — AWG 12 is the minimum wire size for outlet circuits under the Philippine Electrical Code.
choiceExplanations.AWG 8: AWG 8 is thicker than the minimum, so it is not the minimum size.
choiceExplanations.AWG 14: AWG 14 is thinner than the PEC minimum for outlets, so it is not allowed there.

items.question: What kind of lighting should be installed in a bioprocessing chamber if the chamber needs light and heating at the same time?
items.rationale: Incandescent lamps emit substantial infrared heat along with visible light, making them suitable when both illumination and heating are desired.

choiceExplanations.Fluorescent: Fluorescent gives light with little heat.
choiceExplanations.Ultraviolet (UV): Ultraviolet (UV) lamps are for disinfection, not for ordinary lighting and heating.
choiceExplanations.Incandescent: Correct — Incandescent lamps give off a lot of heat along with light, so they serve both purposes.
choiceExplanations.LED: LED lamps give light with very little heat.

items.question: What kind of lighting should be installed in a working area inside a bioprocessing facility such that it is economical?
items.rationale: LED lamps offer the highest luminous efficacy and longest lifespan, consuming less electricity for the same brightness and lowering operating costs.

choiceExplanations.Ultraviolet (UV): Ultraviolet (UV) lamps are for disinfection, not general work lighting.
choiceExplanations.LED: Correct — LED lamps give high light output per watt and long life, so they are the most economical.
choiceExplanations.Incandescent: Incandescent lamps waste most energy as heat, so they cost more to run.
choiceExplanations.Fluorescent: Fluorescent lamps are efficient, but LEDs are more economical overall in this item.

items.question: You are tasked to carry out biosecurity in a bioprocessing laboratory which needs the disinfecting of surfaces. To effect disinfecting, which of these lighting should be installed?
items.rationale: Ultraviolet (UV) germicidal lighting inactivates microorganisms on surfaces, making it effective for laboratory biosecurity disinfection.

choiceExplanations.Incandescent: Incandescent lamps give light and heat, not disinfection.
choiceExplanations.LED: LED lamps give visible light and do not kill germs on surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Ultraviolet (UV): Correct — Ultraviolet (UV) light damages microbial DNA, so it disinfects surfaces.
choiceExplanations.Fluorescent: Fluorescent lamps give ordinary light and do not disinfect.

items.question: Given a 25 hp, three-phase, 230-volt, squirrel cage induction motor that has a full-load current of 68 Amperes at 230 volts. Evaluate which wire should be used. The ambient temperature of the place of installation is 40 degrees C.
items.answer: 50 sq. mm TW copper wire with 98.4 ampacity at 40 deg. C ambient temperature
items.rationale: Per PEC Article 4.30 and PAES 129:2002, branch-circuit conductors for a continuous-duty motor must have an ampacity of at least 125% of full-load current (68 A × 1.25 = 85 A), so only the 50 sq. mm TW copper wire (98.4 A at 40°C) meets this requirement.
choices: 50 sq. mm TW copper wire with 98.4 ampacity at 40 deg. C ambient temperature
22 sq. mm THHW copper wire with 74.8 ampacity at 40 deg. C ambient temperature
30 sq. mm THWN copper wire with 82.5 ampacity at 50 deg. C ambient temperature
38 sq. mm TW copper wire with 82 ampacity at 40 deg. C ambient temperature

choiceExplanations.50 sq. mm TW copper wire with 98.4 ampac: Correct — 50 sq. mm TW copper wire with 98.4 ampacity at 40 deg. C ambient temperature 50 sq. mm TW copper wire has 98.4 A ampacity at 40 °C, above 125% of 68 A (85 A), so it is suitable.
choiceExplanations.22 sq. mm THHW copper wire with 74.8 amp: 22 sq. mm THHW copper wire with 74.8 ampacity at 40 deg. C ambient temperature 22 sq. mm THHW has 74.8 A, below the required 85 A (125% of 68 A).
choiceExplanations.30 sq. mm THWN copper wire with 82.5 amp: 30 sq. mm THWN copper wire with 82.5 ampacity at 50 deg. C ambient temperature 30 sq. mm THWN is rated at 82.5 A at 50 °C, not 40 °C, and it is still below 85 A.
choiceExplanations.38 sq. mm TW copper wire with 82 ampacit: 38 sq. mm TW copper wire with 82 ampacity at 40 deg. C ambient temperature 38 sq. mm TW has 82 A, which is below the required 85 A (125% of 68 A).

items.question: Considering that surge current is estimated at 25% higher than regular current, evaluate and determine the surge current of a 24-volt DC motor if it is supplying current to a 528-Watt 24-Vdc water pump.
items.rationale: Regular load current is I = P / V = 528 W / 24 V = 22 A; with a 25% surge allowance, surge current = 22 A × (1 + 0.25) = 27.5 A.

choiceExplanations.29.74 foot-candle: 29.74 foot-candle is a lighting unit, not a current, so it cannot be the surge current.
choiceExplanations.27.5 A: Correct — 27.5 A is the normal current 528 W / 24 V = 22 A, plus 25% surge, 22 x 1.25 = 27.5 A.
choiceExplanations.25.7 A: 25.7 A is not right. Normal current is 22 A, and 22 x 1.25 = 27.5 A.
choiceExplanations.0.28 A: 0.28 A is far too low. Normal current alone is 528/24 = 22 A.

items.question: What is the minimum wire size of a drop wire for a farmhouse?
items.rationale: Under Philippine Electrical Code and rural electrification standards for agricultural structures, AWG 6 is the standard minimum conductor size for a farmhouse service drop wire.

choiceExplanations.AWG 8: AWG 8 is smaller than the minimum drop wire for a farmhouse, which is AWG 6.
choiceExplanations.AWG 4: AWG 4 is thicker than the minimum, so it is not the minimum size.
choiceExplanations.AWG 6: Correct — AWG 6 is the minimum size for a service drop wire to a farmhouse.
choiceExplanations.AWG 2: AWG 2 is much thicker than the minimum, so it is not the minimum size.

items.question: Determine the power output of a 12-volt DC motor if it is rated at 10 Amperes. Assume a system efficiency of 80%.
items.rationale: Input electrical power is P_in = V × I = 12 V × 10 A = 120 W; multiplying by the 80% efficiency yields P_out = 120 W × 0.80 = 96 W.

choiceExplanations.960 W: 960 W is ten times too high. Input is 12 V x 10 A = 120 W, and output at 80% is 96 W.
choiceExplanations.8 kWh: 8 kWh is a unit of energy, not power, so it cannot be a power output.
choiceExplanations.96 W: Correct — 96 W is the output: input 12 V x 10 A = 120 W, times 0.80 efficiency.
choiceExplanations.6.9 W: 6.9 W is far too low. Output is 120 W x 0.80 = 96 W.

items.question: Your bioprocessing plant has 3 separate circuit breakers having ampacities of 15 A, 30 A and 60 A. What should be the ampacity of the main circuit breaker?
items.rationale: The main circuit breaker must have an ampacity at least equal to the largest branch circuit breaker (60 A) to prevent nuisance tripping; among the given choices, 60 A is the only adequate rating.

choiceExplanations.45 A: 45 A is not the keyed answer. This item keys the largest branch breaker rating, 60 A.
choiceExplanations.60 A: Correct — 60 A is the keyed answer, the highest rating among the branch breakers. Note that the sum (105 A) would normally set a main breaker.
choiceExplanations.15 A: 15 A is the smallest branch breaker and cannot cover the 30 A and 60 A branches.
choiceExplanations.30 A: 30 A cannot protect the 60 A branch, so it is too small for a main breaker.

items.question: A COP of 3 means that for every 1 unit of energy which is likely the electricity used, the system moves ___ units of heat out of the cold space.
items.rationale: Coefficient of Performance (COP) equals heat removed divided by work input (COP = Q_L / W); a COP of 3 means 3 units of heat are removed per 1 unit of electrical energy consumed.

choiceExplanations.0.3: 0.3 is wrong. COP is heat moved per unit of energy used, so COP 3 means 3 units.
choiceExplanations.3: Correct — A COP of 3 means the system moves 3 units of heat for each 1 unit of electrical energy used.
choiceExplanations.3.3: 3.3 is not the value. COP 3 means exactly 3 units of heat moved.
choiceExplanations.0.03: 0.03 is not the value. COP 3 means 3 units of heat moved per 1 unit of energy.

items.question: "plant used to process animal wastes or manure to produce biogas and sludge consisting of an inlet/mixing tank, digester, gas chamber and outlet/sludge tank"

choiceExplanations.Compost plant: Compost plant makes compost aerobically and has no digester or gas chamber.
choiceExplanations.Incineration plant: Incineration plant burns waste and does not make biogas and sludge.
choiceExplanations.Biogas plant: Correct — Biogas plant digests manure anaerobically to produce biogas and sludge, with inlet tank, digester, gas chamber and outlet tank.
choiceExplanations.Gasification plant: Gasification plant turns solid fuel into syngas by heat, not by biological digestion.

items.question: "biogas plant where the digester and gas chamber form one unit"

choiceExplanations.Batch-type plant: Batch-type plant is loaded all at once and emptied after digestion, a different operating mode.
choiceExplanations.Integrated plant: Correct — Integrated plant has the digester and gas chamber built together as one unit.
choiceExplanations.Multi-stage plant: Multi-stage plant uses several digesters in sequence, not one combined unit.
choiceExplanations.Split-type plant: Split-type plant has the digester and gas chamber as separate units.

items.question: "plant consisting of digester and a moving, floating gasholder that either float directly in the fermenting slurry or in a separate water jacket"

choiceExplanations.Floating type: Correct — Floating type has a moving gasholder that floats on the slurry or in a water jacket, rising and falling with the gas stored.
choiceExplanations.Fixed-dome type: Fixed-dome type has a fixed, non-moving gas chamber, so the gasholder does not float.
choiceExplanations.Balloon type: Balloon type uses a flexible bag as digester and gas storage, not a rigid floating holder.
choiceExplanations.Plug-flow type: Plug-flow type describes how slurry moves through a long tank, not a floating gasholder.

items.question: "chamber where manure and water are collected, stored and separated from heavy and nonbiodegradable materials before feeding them into the digester"

choiceExplanations.Storage and effluent tank: Storage and effluent tank holds digested material, not the incoming manure.
choiceExplanations.Collecting tank/ holding tank: Correct — Collecting tank/ holding tank is where manure and water are collected and separated from heavy and non-biodegradable materials before feeding the digester.
choiceExplanations.Sludge and outlet tank: Sludge and outlet tank receives digested slurry after the digester.
choiceExplanations.Mixing and blending tank: Mixing and blending tank mixes the manure with water for feeding, but does not do the first collection and separation.

items.question: "serves as conveyor of the manure-water mixture or slurry from the mixing tank to the digester"

choiceExplanations.Inlet pipe: Correct — Inlet pipe carries the manure-water slurry from the mixing tank into the digester.
choiceExplanations.Drain pipe: Drain pipe removes liquid for drainage, not feed slurry.
choiceExplanations.Outlet pipe: Outlet pipe takes digested slurry out of the digester.
choiceExplanations.Overflow pipe: Overflow pipe carries off excess liquid, not feed slurry.

items.question: "any water and air tight container designed for the process of anaerobic microbiological degradation of organic matter into which the slurry is introduced for digestion and methanization"
choices: Primary settling basin and sludge thickener
Aerobic compost chamber and aeration basin
Facultative oxidation pond and stabilization lagoon

choiceExplanations.Primary settling basin and sludge thicke: Primary settling basin and sludge thickener are for settling solids, not anaerobic digestion.
choiceExplanations.Digester/ biodigester/bio-reactor/ anaer: Correct — Digester/ biodigester/bio-reactor/ anaerobic reactor / biodigester / bio-reactor is the airtight, watertight container where slurry undergoes anaerobic digestion and produces methane.
choiceExplanations.Aerobic compost chamber and aeration bas: Aerobic compost chamber and aeration basin use oxygen, but the item describes an airtight (anaerobic) container.
choiceExplanations.Facultative oxidation pond and stabiliza: Facultative oxidation pond and stabilization lagoon are open ponds, not water and air tight containers.

items.question: "division in the digester that prevent the slurry from premature exit into the sludge/outlet tank"

choiceExplanations.Retention wall: Retention wall holds back soil or fill and is not a division inside a digester.
choiceExplanations.Baffle board: Correct — Baffle board is a partition in the digester that stops slurry from exiting early to the outlet tank.
choiceExplanations.Scum breaker: Scum breaker breaks the crust floating on top of the slurry, not a division.
choiceExplanations.Weir plate: Weir plate controls overflow level, not a division that blocks premature exit.

items.question: "mechanical device inside the digester used to stir the slurry"

choiceExplanations.Submersible slurry pump: Submersible slurry pump moves slurry from place to place, not stir it inside the digester.
choiceExplanations.Stirrer/mixer/agitator: Correct — Stirrer/mixer/agitator / mixer / agitator is the mechanical device inside the digester used to stir the slurry.
choiceExplanations.Mechanical grit scraper: Mechanical grit scraper removes settled grit from the bottom of a tank.
choiceExplanations.Rotary scum breaker: Rotary scum breaker breaks the surface crust, not stir the full slurry.

items.question: "serves as conveyor where the effluent or the slurry is forced out"

choiceExplanations.Outlet pipe: Correct — Outlet pipe is where the effluent or digested slurry is forced out of the digester.
choiceExplanations.Overflow pipe: Overflow pipe carries away excess liquid when level is too high, not the normal effluent flow.
choiceExplanations.Drainage pipe: Drainage pipe is for draining liquid, not the normal slurry exit.
choiceExplanations.Inlet pipe: Inlet pipe brings fresh slurry in, the opposite direction.

items.question: "amount of slurry fed per unit volume of digester capacity per day"

choiceExplanations.Digestion rate: Digestion rate is how fast organic matter breaks down, not how much is fed.
choiceExplanations.Loading rate: Correct — Loading rate is the amount of slurry fed per unit volume of digester per day.
choiceExplanations.Feeding frequency: Feeding frequency is how often the digester is fed, not the amount per volume.
choiceExplanations.Dilution rate: Dilution rate is the water-to-manure ratio, not the feed per digester volume.

items.question: "adding or introducing anaerobic bacteria to the digester"

choiceExplanations.Seeding: Correct — Seeding is adding anaerobic bacteria (such as old slurry) to the digester to start digestion.
choiceExplanations.Aerating: Aerating adds air, which is bad for anaerobic bacteria.
choiceExplanations.Flushing: Flushing is washing out material with water.
choiceExplanations.Buffering: Buffering is controlling pH changes, not adding bacteria.

items.question: "mixture of manure and water"

choiceExplanations.Sludge: Sludge is the settled mud-like solid, not the fresh manure-water mix.
choiceExplanations.Effluent: Effluent is the digested material coming out of the digester.
choiceExplanations.Leachate: Leachate is liquid that drains through decomposing waste.
choiceExplanations.Slurry: Correct — Slurry is the mixture of manure and water fed into the digester.

items.question: "average period that a given quantity of slurry is retained in the digester for digestion"

choiceExplanations.Retention time: Correct — Retention time is the average time a quantity of slurry stays in the digester.
choiceExplanations.Mixing cycle: Mixing cycle is how often or how long the slurry is stirred.
choiceExplanations.Startup period: Startup period is the time to get a new digester working.
choiceExplanations.Curing period: Curing period is the time for compost to mature, not slurry stay in a digester.

items.question: "anaerobic bacteria that act upon organic materials and in the process, produce biogas"

choiceExplanations.Acidogens: Acidogens make organic acids earlier in digestion, not the methane.
choiceExplanations.Actinomycetes: Actinomycetes are bacteria important in composting, not the biogas producers.
choiceExplanations.Methanogens: Correct — Methanogens are the anaerobic bacteria that produce methane, the main part of biogas.
choiceExplanations.Acetogens: Acetogens make acetate and hydrogen, which methanogens then turn into methane.

items.question: "amount of biogas produced per day per cubic meter of slurry"

choiceExplanations.Biogas consumption rate: Biogas consumption rate is how much gas is used, not made.
choiceExplanations.Gas production rate: Correct — Gas production rate is the biogas produced per day per cubic meter of slurry.
choiceExplanations.Volumetric loading rate: Volumetric loading rate is feed per digester volume, not gas output.
choiceExplanations.Methane yield ratio: Methane yield ratio is methane produced per unit of material, not per day per cubic meter of slurry.

items.question: "mixture of gas (composed of 50 to 70 percent methane and 30 to 40 percent carbon dioxide) produced by methanogenic bacteria"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Syngas: Syngas is made by gasification, mostly carbon monoxide and hydrogen.
choiceExplanations.Propane: Propane is a petroleum gas, not made by methanogens.
choiceExplanations.Butane: Butane is a petroleum gas, not made by methanogens.
choiceExplanations.Biogas: Correct — Biogas is the gas mixture of 50-70% methane and carbon dioxide produced by methanogenic bacteria.

items.question: "settled portion or precipitate of the slurry; a mud-like, semi-solid mass"

choiceExplanations.Scum: Scum is the crust that floats on top of the slurry.
choiceExplanations.Supernatant: Supernatant is the clear liquid above the settled solids.
choiceExplanations.Sludge: Correct — Sludge is the settled, mud-like, semi-solid portion of the slurry.
choiceExplanations.Effluent: Effluent is the liquid output leaving the digester.

items.question: "residue that comes out at the outlet after the substrate is digested/processed inside the digester"

choiceExplanations.Scum: Scum is floating crust, not the output.
choiceExplanations.Sludge: Sludge is the settled solid part, not the whole output residue.
choiceExplanations.Influent: Influent is the material going into the digester, the opposite of output.
choiceExplanations.Effluent: Correct — Effluent is the residue that leaves at the outlet after digestion.

items.question: "lagoons that can function as aerobic or anaerobic depending on the environment"

choiceExplanations.Facultative lagoons: Correct — Facultative lagoons work aerobically near the surface and anaerobically at the bottom, depending on conditions.
choiceExplanations.Anaerobic lagoons: Anaerobic lagoons work without oxygen only.
choiceExplanations.Aerated lagoons: Aerated lagoons use mechanical aeration to stay aerobic.
choiceExplanations.Aerobic lagoons: Aerobic lagoons work with oxygen only.

items.question: "pit in the ground where liquid waste is stored to produce a higher quality effluent"

choiceExplanations.Cistern: Cistern is a tank storing water, not for waste treatment.
choiceExplanations.Cesspool: Cesspool is a pit for sewage that lets liquid soak into the ground, not for producing a better effluent.
choiceExplanations.Digester: Digester is a closed container, not a pit in the ground.
choiceExplanations.Lagoon: Correct — Lagoon is a pit or pond in the ground where liquid waste is stored and treated to give a higher quality effluent.

items.question: "mixture of an organic waste with amendment(s) or bulking agent(s) in the proper proportions to promote aerobic microbial activity and growth and to achieve optimum temperatures"

choiceExplanations.Compost mix: Correct — Compost mix is the organic waste mixed with amendments or bulking agents in the right proportions to support aerobic microbes.
choiceExplanations.Compost amendment: Compost amendment is an item added to change moisture, C:N ratio or pH, not the whole mix.
choiceExplanations.Bulking agent: Bulking agent is a material added to give structure and air space, only one part of the mix.
choiceExplanations.Digester slurry: Digester slurry is for anaerobic digestion, not aerobic composting.

items.question: "any item added to the compost mixture that alters the moisture content, C:N ratio, or pH"

choiceExplanations.Compost mix: Compost mix is the whole combination, not one added item.
choiceExplanations.Microbial inoculant: Microbial inoculant adds microbes, but it does not alter moisture, C:N ratio or pH.
choiceExplanations.Bulking agent: Bulking agent adds structure and air space and is one kind of amendment, but the general term is amendment.
choiceExplanations.Composting amendment: Correct — Composting amendment is any item added to the compost mixture to change moisture, C:N ratio or pH.

items.question: "shall refer to the liquid produced when waste undergo decomposition, and when water percolate through solid waste undergoing decomposition; contaminated liquid that contains dissolved and suspended materials"

choiceExplanations.Supernatant: Supernatant is the clear liquid above settled solids.
choiceExplanations.Effluent: Effluent is the liquid output from a treatment process.
choiceExplanations.Leachate: Correct — Leachate is the contaminated liquid from decomposing waste, carrying dissolved and suspended materials.

items.question: "involves the arrangement of compost mix in long, narrow piles or windrows that are periodically turned to maintain aerobic conditions"
items.source: AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURES (area3); area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.In-vessel composting: In-vessel composting takes place inside a closed container or reactor.
choiceExplanations.Trench composting: Trench composting buries compost in trenches.
choiceExplanations.Windrow composting: Correct — Windrow composting arranges the mix in long, narrow piles that are turned to keep aerobic conditions.
choiceExplanations.Static-pile composting: Static-pile composting does not turn the pile and uses forced aeration instead.

items.question: A method of separating fine duct by allowing it to pass through a mist of water

choiceExplanations.Cyclone separator: Cyclone separator uses centrifugal force to separate dust, not water mist.
choiceExplanations.Electrostatic precipitator: Electrostatic precipitator uses an electric charge to collect dust.
choiceExplanations.Baghouse filter: Baghouse filter uses fabric bags to filter dust.
choiceExplanations.Water scrubber: Correct — Water scrubber passes dust-laden air through a water spray or mist that traps fine dust.

items.question: A dark carbonaceous residue resulting from aerobic decomposition of organic matter

choiceExplanations.Biochar: Biochar is charcoal made by pyrolysis without oxygen, not aerobic decomposition.
choiceExplanations.Mulch: Mulch is a covering material put on soil, not a decomposed residue.
choiceExplanations.Peat: Peat is partly decayed plant matter formed in waterlogged, low-oxygen conditions.
choiceExplanations.Humus: Correct — Humus is the dark, stable carbon-rich residue left from aerobic decomposition of organic matter.

items.question: It is a biological waste water treatment process in which the mixture of waste water and biological solids is agitated and aerated

choiceExplanations.Activated sludge process: Correct — Activated sludge process agitates and aerates wastewater mixed with biological solids so microbes break down the waste.
choiceExplanations.Anaerobic digestion process: Anaerobic digestion process works without oxygen, so it has no aeration.
choiceExplanations.Trickling filter process: Trickling filter process passes wastewater over a fixed media bed, not a stirred mixture.
choiceExplanations.Rotating biological contactor: Rotating biological contactor uses rotating discs with microbial film, not an aerated mixture of solids.

items.question: It is an earthen facility for biological treatment of wastewater

choiceExplanations.Clarifier: Clarifier is a tank for settling solids, not an earthen basin.
choiceExplanations.Lagoon: Correct — Lagoon is an earthen basin used for biological treatment of wastewater.
choiceExplanations.Digester: Digester is a closed tank, not an earthen facility.
choiceExplanations.Biofilter: Biofilter uses media with microbes to treat air or water, not an earthen basin.

items.question: Particles that ultimately settle after the wastewater losses velocity

choiceExplanations.Colloids: Colloids are very fine particles that stay suspended and do not easily settle.
choiceExplanations.Solutes: Solutes are dissolved substances that do not settle.
choiceExplanations.Surfactants: Surfactants are detergent-like chemicals that stay dissolved or suspended.
choiceExplanations.Sediments: Correct — Sediments are particles that settle out once wastewater slows down.

items.question: The precipitate or settled solids from treatment, coagulation or sedimentation of wastewater

choiceExplanations.Effluent: Effluent is the treated liquid that flows out, not the settled solids.
choiceExplanations.Supernatant: Supernatant is the clear liquid above the settled solids.
choiceExplanations.Sludge: Correct — Sludge is the settled solids from treatment, coagulation or sedimentation of wastewater.
choiceExplanations.Scum: Scum is the material floating on top, not settled.

items.question: Refers to the application of engineering science and designs to the processes and systems involved in the sustainable production, post production and processing of safe food, feed, fiber, timber and other agricultural and biological materials and the efficient utilization, conservation, and management of natural and renewable resources in order to enhance human health in harmony with the environment

choiceExplanations.Environmental and Sanitary Engineering: Environmental and Sanitary Engineering deals with water, waste and public health, not the full production-to-processing scope given.
choiceExplanations.Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering: Correct — Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering is the application of engineering to sustainable production, post-production and processing of food, feed, fiber, timber and bio-resources, and management of natural resources.
choiceExplanations.Biological and Ecological Engineering: Biological and Ecological Engineering focuses on biological systems and ecosystems, not the specific scope listed.
choiceExplanations.Food and Bioprocess Engineering: Food and Bioprocess Engineering covers food and bio-processing only, narrower than the full scope.

items.question: A piece of lumber having a minimum smallest dimension of 5 inches or 13cm

choiceExplanations.Plank: Plank is a thin, wide piece, thinner than timber.
choiceExplanations.Timber: Correct — Timber is lumber with a smallest dimension of at least 5 inches (13 cm).
choiceExplanations.Board: Board is thin lumber less than 2 inches thick.
choiceExplanations.Scantling: Scantling is a small piece of lumber with a thickness and width under 5 inches.

items.question: Method of reducing the moisture of timber using artificial heat on a heated chamber

choiceExplanations.Solar drying: Solar drying uses the sun's heat, not a heated chamber.
choiceExplanations.Air drying: Air drying lets timber dry naturally in open air.
choiceExplanations.Chemical seasoning: Chemical seasoning uses chemicals to draw out moisture, not heat.
choiceExplanations.Kiln drying: Correct — Kiln drying uses artificial heat in a heated chamber to reduce timber moisture.

items.question: PAES 401(housing for swine Production: It shall be constructed to allow manure and urine to pass through

choiceExplanations.Solid floor: Solid floor does not let manure and urine pass through.
choiceExplanations.Slotted floor: Correct — Slotted floor has openings that let manure and urine drop through to a pit below.
choiceExplanations.Bedded floor: Bedded floor is covered with bedding that absorbs waste, not lets it pass.
choiceExplanations.Concrete floor: Concrete floor is a solid surface material, and by itself does not let waste pass through.

items.question: Which gas is produced during anaerobic fermentation of agricultural wastes?

choiceExplanations.Propane: Propane is a petroleum or natural gas fuel, not made by anaerobic fermentation of wastes.
choiceExplanations.Syngas: Syngas is made by heating solid fuel in gasification, not by fermentation.
choiceExplanations.Acetylene: Acetylene is made from calcium carbide and water, not from fermentation of wastes.
choiceExplanations.Biogas: Correct — Biogas is the methane and carbon dioxide mixture produced when microbes digest wastes without oxygen.

items.question: chamber where manure and water are collected, stored and separated from heavy and non-biodegradable materials before feeding them into the digester

choiceExplanations.Outlet tank: Outlet tank receives digested slurry leaving the digester.
choiceExplanations.Sludge tank: Sludge tank holds the settled digested solids.
choiceExplanations.Collecting tank: Correct — Collecting tank is where manure and water are collected, stored and cleared of heavy and non-biodegradable materials before the digester.
choiceExplanations.Mixing tank: Mixing tank mixes manure with water, but does not do the first collecting and separating.

items.question: space inside or outside the digester for the collection and storage of biogas

choiceExplanations.Outlet chamber: Outlet chamber takes out digested slurry, not store gas.
choiceExplanations.Inlet chamber: Inlet chamber takes in fresh slurry, not store gas.
choiceExplanations.Gas chamber: Correct — Gas chamber is the space inside or outside the digester where biogas is collected and stored.
choiceExplanations.Digester chamber: Digester chamber is where digestion takes place, not the gas storage space.

items.question: Heating of earth

choiceExplanations.Ozone depletion: Ozone depletion is thinning of the ozone layer, not heating of the Earth.
choiceExplanations.Global warming: Correct — Global warming is the rise in Earth's average temperature caused by trapped heat from greenhouse gases.
choiceExplanations.Ocean acidification: Ocean acidification is the drop in ocean pH due to absorbed CO2, not heating.
choiceExplanations.Thermal inversion: Thermal inversion is a warm air layer over cooler air, a local weather effect, not Earth's heating.

items.question: microorganisms, such as coliforms, whose presence is indicative of pollution or of more harmful microorganisms

choiceExplanations.Methanogenic organisms: Methanogenic organisms produce methane in digesters and do not signal pollution.
choiceExplanations.Saprophytic organisms: Saprophytic organisms feed on dead organic matter and are not pollution indicators.
choiceExplanations.Pathogenic organisms: Pathogenic organisms are the actual disease-causing microbes, not the signal organisms like coliforms.
choiceExplanations.Indicator organisms: Correct — Indicator organisms such as coliforms show that pollution or harmful microbes may be present.

items.question: any source of pollution not identifiable as point source to include, but not be limited to, runoff from irrigation or rainwater which picks up pollutants from farms and urban areas

choiceExplanations.Mobile emission source: Mobile emission source covers moving sources like vehicles, not runoff.
choiceExplanations.Domestic sewage source: Domestic sewage source is a point discharge from households through pipes.
choiceExplanations.Stationary point source: Stationary point source is a single identifiable place like a factory pipe, the opposite of the item.
choiceExplanations.Non point source: Correct — Non point source is pollution that cannot be traced to one place, such as farm and urban runoff.

items.question: a river, stream, lake, ocean, or other surface of groundwater into which treated or untreated wastewater is discharged

choiceExplanations.Percolation Pond: Percolation Pond lets water seep into the ground, not receive discharged wastewater.
choiceExplanations.Receiving Water: Correct — Receiving Water is the river, stream, lake, ocean or groundwater that receives treated or untreated wastewater.
choiceExplanations.Retention Basin: Retention Basin holds water for a time to reduce flooding or settle solids, not the body receiving discharge.

items.question: it removes gaseous pollutants and solid particles while cooling the gas at the same time

choiceExplanations.Scrubber/wet scrubber: Correct — Scrubber/wet scrubber uses water spray to remove gases and particles while it cools the gas.
choiceExplanations.Cyclone separator: Cyclone separator removes particles by spinning the gas, not gases, and does not cool it.
choiceExplanations.Baghouse filter: Baghouse filter traps dust in fabric bags and does not remove gases or cool well.
choiceExplanations.Electrostatic precipitator: Electrostatic precipitator removes particles by electric charge and does not remove gases or cool.

items.question: pH value of biogas
items.rationale: [Verified & Corrected from '7-8.5']

choiceExplanations.5.0–5.5: 5.0–5.5 is too acidic. Methane-forming microbes need near-neutral pH.
choiceExplanations.4.0–4.5: 4.0–4.5 is far too acidic for methanogens, which would be inhibited.
choiceExplanations.7.0–7.5 (optimal methanogenesis range; 6: Correct — 7.0–7.5 (optimal methanogenesis range; 6.0–8.0 overall) to 7.5 is the optimum pH for methanogenesis, with 6.0 to 8.0 workable overall.
choiceExplanations.8.5–9.0: 8.5–9.0 is too alkaline and would inhibit the methane-forming microbes.

items.question: Dry ice is the solid form of what compound?

choiceExplanations.Nitrogen dioxide: Nitrogen dioxide is a brown toxic gas, not dry ice.
choiceExplanations.Sulfur dioxide: Sulfur dioxide is a toxic gas from burning sulfur, not dry ice.
choiceExplanations.Carbon monoxide: Carbon monoxide is a toxic gas from incomplete burning, not dry ice.
choiceExplanations.Carbon dioxide or CO2: Correct — Carbon dioxide or CO2 frozen solid is dry ice, which sublimes directly into gas.

items.question: PABES 016 Vol. X: For crop irrigation, the threshold of BOD for wastewater quality is

choiceExplanations.<172 mg/L: <172 mg/L is not the PABES 016 limit. The threshold for crop irrigation is below 150 mg/L.

choiceExplanations.<132 mg/L: <132 mg/L is not the limit. The threshold is below 150 mg/L.
choiceExplanations.<150 mg/L: Correct — <150 mg/L is the BOD threshold for wastewater used for crop irrigation in PABES 016.

items.question: From Dr. Tambong: CDM stands for?

choiceExplanations.Climate Disaster Mitigation: Climate Disaster Mitigation is not the name of the Kyoto Protocol scheme.
choiceExplanations.Certified Development Market: Certified Development Market is not the name of the Kyoto Protocol scheme.
choiceExplanations.Carbon Development Mechanism: Carbon Development Mechanism is a wrong word order and name. The scheme is the Clean Development Mechanism.
choiceExplanations.Clean Development Mechanism: Correct — Clean Development Mechanism is the Kyoto Protocol scheme that gives carbon credits for emission reduction projects in developing countries.

items.question: Greenhouse gases are those that can absorb and emit infrared radiation. This process fundamentally causes the greenhouse effect. Which of the gases below is not considered a greenhouse gas?
items.rationale: Nitrogen (N₂) is a symmetric diatomic molecule that does not absorb or emit infrared radiation, whereas water vapor, carbon dioxide, and ozone are greenhouse gases.

choiceExplanations.Nitrogen: Correct — Nitrogen (N2) makes up most of the air but does not absorb infrared radiation, so it is not a greenhouse gas.
choiceExplanations.Water vapor: Water vapor absorbs and emits infrared radiation and is a major greenhouse gas.
choiceExplanations.Ozone: Ozone absorbs infrared radiation and is a greenhouse gas.
choiceExplanations.Carbon dioxide: Carbon dioxide absorbs infrared radiation and is a main greenhouse gas.

items.question: A division in the biogas digester that prevents slurry from premature exit into sludge/outlet tank.

choiceExplanations.Scum breaker: Scum breaker breaks up the crust floating on the slurry, not a division.
choiceExplanations.Baffle board: Correct — Baffle board is the division inside the digester that stops slurry from leaving early to the outlet tank.
choiceExplanations.Overflow pipe: Overflow pipe carries away excess liquid, not a division inside the digester.
choiceExplanations.Weir plate: Weir plate controls overflow level, not block early exit of slurry.

items.question: Your agency needs to organize a project management team for the 6-month construction of a large covered lagoon biodigester for the waste management of 30,000 heads of layers and for biogas generation. To minimize construction duration, what method your agency should employ in the project management?

choiceExplanations.Pert-cpm: Correct — Pert-cpm schedules tasks and finds the critical path, so it helps cut total construction time.
choiceExplanations.Decision tree: Decision tree compares choices under uncertainty, not construction scheduling.
choiceExplanations.Gantt chart: Gantt chart displays a schedule but does not find the critical path to shorten duration.
choiceExplanations.Break-even analysis: Break-even analysis finds where income equals cost, not how to cut construction time.

items.question: In a continuous-fed floating-type biogas digester, the upper end of the outlet pipe should be ______ with in the upper end on the inlet pipe.

choiceExplanations.Level: Correct — The upper ends of the inlet and outlet pipes are at the same level, so the slurry level in the digester stays steady as feed flows in and out.
choiceExplanations.Sloped: Sloped is not a position of the pipe ends that keeps constant slurry level.
choiceExplanations.Lower: Lower would make slurry level fall as it overflows the outlet before the digester is full.
choiceExplanations.Higher: Higher would make the inlet side overflow or the digester fill beyond the set level.

items.question: Determine which of the following floating-type rectangular biogas digesters with integrated digester and gasholder follows the standard height/length ratio for optimum design based on PAES 413:2001?
items.answer: Length is twice the side, height side ratio of 0.34

choices: Length is thrice the side, height side ratio of 0.34
Length is twice the side, height side ratio of 0.50
Length is equal to side, height side ratio of 0.68

choiceExplanations.Length is equal to side, height side rat: Length is equal to side, height side ratio of 0.68 to the side with 0.68 ratio is not the PAES 413 optimum proportion.
