items.question: You are tasked to evaluate the effluent of a rice mill. In addition to high concentration of organic and inorganic substances leading to significant source of pollution, its effluent is also high in __________.

choiceExplanations.TH, SAR and RSC: TH, SAR and RSC describe water hardness and irrigation suitability, not rice mill effluent strength.
choiceExplanations.BOD, COD and TDS: Correct — BOD, COD and TDS are high in rice mill effluent, from organic matter and dissolved solids.
choiceExplanations.DO, ORP and pH: DO, ORP and pH are general water readings, and DO is low rather than high in polluted water.
choiceExplanations.PAH, PCB and VOC: PAH, PCB and VOC are toxic organic chemicals not typical of rice mill effluent.

items.question: A medium-size floating-type biogas digester accommodates manure from 551 heads of porkers of mixed ages and retains manure inside the digester for 30 days. The mean daily manure production of porkers is 2.2 kg/head while the specific gas production for 30-day manure retention period is 0.063 m3/kg. Water:manure ratio is 1:1. What is the daily biogas production?
items.rationale: 76 m3/day P = NMG where: / P = biogas production potential N = No. of heads M = manure production G = Specific gas production of the manure for a specific retention period P = (551 heads)(2.2 kg/head)(0.063 m3/kg for the entire retention period) / = 76.37 m3/day

choiceExplanations.92 m3 per day: 92 m3 per day is too high. P = N x M x G = 551 x 2.2 x 0.063 is about 76 m3/day.
choiceExplanations.76 m3/day P = NMG where:: Correct — 76 m3/day P = NMG where: m3/day. P = N x M x G = 551 heads x 2.2 kg x 0.063 m3/kg = 76.4 m3/day.
choiceExplanations.115 m3 per day: 115 m3 per day is too high. P = 551 x 2.2 x 0.063 is about 76 m3/day.
choiceExplanations.54 m3 per day: 54 m3 per day is too low. P = 551 x 2.2 x 0.063 is about 76 m3/day.

items.question: Feedlot cattle are used as source of manure to generate 50.1 m3 of biogas daily. Retention period is 25 days and the water-manure ratio is 1:1. The mean daily manure production of feedlot cattle is 13 kg/head while its specific gas production for 25-day manure retention period is half of that of chicken dung. Find the number of animal heads required.
items.rationale:
[(13 kg/head)(0.03 m3/kg)] / = 128.46 heads, to avoid gas shortage round up to 129 heads

Notes: 129 / N = P/(MG) / where N = No. of heads C = biogas production M = manure production, G = Half of specific gas production of chicken dung / = 1/2 x 0.06 m3/kg or 0.03 m3/kg N = (50.1 m3)/

choiceExplanations.103: 103 heads is too few. N = 50.1 / (13 x 0.03) is about 129.
choiceExplanations.142: 142 heads is too many. N = 50.1 / (13 x 0.03) is about 129.
choiceExplanations.129: Correct — 129 heads. Specific gas production is half of chicken dung, about 0.03 m3/kg, so N = 50.1 / (13 x 0.03).
choiceExplanations.116: 116 heads is too few. N = 50.1 / (13 x 0.03) is about 129.

items.question: You are assigned to plan a biogas project in the southern Philippines. The prevailing daytime temperature in the project site is more or less 30°C. What type of biogas digester is appropriate?
items.rationale: Floating type Since ambient temperature in the likelihood of 30°C which favors floating type digester. / Reference: Biogas Plant Design by Arthur Tambong, 1992

choiceExplanations.Fixed dome: Fixed dome digesters are underground and keep stable temperature, which is not the keyed choice for a warm 30°C site.
choiceExplanations.Balloon type: Balloon type is a flexible bag digester, not the keyed choice for this site.
choiceExplanations.Floating type: Correct — Floating type digester is the keyed choice, since a warm site near 30°C favors it.
choiceExplanations.Plug flow: Plug flow digesters suit specific solids content, not the keyed choice for this site.

items.question: The quick method of farm composting that uses live earthworms and plant biomass.

choiceExplanations.Windrowing: Windrowing is composting in long turned piles without earthworms.
choiceExplanations.Mulching: Mulching is covering soil with organic material, not composting.
choiceExplanations.Vermicomposting: Correct — Vermicomposting is a quick composting method using live earthworms to eat plant biomass and make castings.
choiceExplanations.Bokashi: Bokashi is fermentation of waste using microbes, not earthworms.

items.question: Giant bamboo is a fast-growing environment friendly tall grass that neutralizes greenhouse gas emissions in the atmosphere. Give the scientific name of a giant bamboo variety that is suited in the Philippines.

choiceExplanations.Gigantochloa levis: Gigantochloa levis a different bamboo species (bolo), not the giant bamboo meant here.
choiceExplanations.Bambusa vulgaris: Bambusa vulgaris common bamboo (kawayan dilaw), smaller than giant bamboo.
choiceExplanations.Dendrocalamus asper: Correct — Dendrocalamus asper is the scientific name of giant bamboo (giant bamboo, 'giant bamboo' in the Philippines).
choiceExplanations.Bambusa blumeana: Bambusa blumeana is spiny bamboo (kawayan tinik), not the giant variety.

items.question: The toxic component of biogas

choiceExplanations.Carbon dioxide: Carbon dioxide is a non-flammable gas in biogas, but it is not toxic in the usual sense of the item.
choiceExplanations.Nitrogen gas: Nitrogen gas is harmless and makes up most of air.
choiceExplanations.Water vapor: Water vapor is harmless moisture in the gas.
choiceExplanations.Hydrogen sulfide: Correct — Hydrogen sulfide is a poisonous, corrosive gas in biogas that smells like rotten eggs.

items.question: The by-product of biogas production commonly used as soil conditioner after air drying.

choiceExplanations.Scum: Scum is the floating crust, not the digested solid used on soil.
choiceExplanations.Slurry: Slurry is the raw manure-water mix before digestion.
choiceExplanations.Effluent: Effluent is the liquid output of the digester.
choiceExplanations.Sludge: Correct — Sludge is the settled digested solids, which are air-dried and used as soil conditioner.

items.question: The amount paid to project owners from CDM fund for carbon emission reduction projects.

choiceExplanations.Carbon tax rate: Carbon tax rate is a charge on emissions, which is paid by emitters, not to project owners.
choiceExplanations.Carbon credit value: Correct — Carbon credit value is the amount paid to project owners from the CDM fund for emission reductions.
choiceExplanations.Marginal abatement cost: Marginal abatement cost is the cost of cutting one more unit of emissions, not a payment.
choiceExplanations.Emission abatement cost: Emission abatement cost is the cost of reducing emissions, not the payment the owner receives.

items.question: The acronym of IPCC

choiceExplanations.Inter-Governmental Program on Climate Ch: Inter-Governmental Program on Climate Change is a wrong name. IPCC is a Panel.
choiceExplanations.Inter-Governmental Panel for Climate Cha: Correct — Inter-Governmental Panel for Climate Change is the keyed expansion of IPCC, the UN body that assesses climate science.
choiceExplanations.Inter-Governmental Policy on Climate Cha: Inter-Governmental Policy on Climate Change is a wrong name. IPCC is a Panel.
choiceExplanations.International Panel for Climate Control: International Panel for Climate Control is a wrong name. IPCC is not about climate control.

items.question: Best kind of biogas plant for large animal farms having effluents with low solid content.

choiceExplanations.Floating drum: Floating drum suits small to medium farms using solid-rich manure, not large farms with watery effluent.
choiceExplanations.Fixed dome: Fixed dome suits small household scale, not large farms.
choiceExplanations.Balloon type: Balloon type is a small plastic bag digester, not for large farms.
choiceExplanations.Covered lagoon: Correct — Covered lagoon is a big lined pond with a gas-tight cover, best for large farms with watery, low-solid effluent.

items.question: Plastic sheet for constructing balloon and bed lining in covered lagoon biogas plants.
items.source: Tambong Subject C part 2; area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Polyvinyl chloride (PVC): Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is a rigid or flexible plastic used for pipes, not the standard lagoon liner.
choiceExplanations.Linear low density polyethylene (LLDPE): Linear low density polyethylene (LLDPE) polyethylene is flexible but not the keyed liner material.
choiceExplanations.Low density polyethylene (LDPE): Low density polyethylene (LDPE) is thin and less durable, not the keyed lagoon liner.
choiceExplanations.High density polyethylene (HDPE): Correct — High density polyethylene (HDPE) is the tough, chemical-resistant plastic used for balloons and covered-lagoon liners.

items.question: By how many times is methane destructive to the environment than carbon dioxide?
items.source: Tambong Subject C part 2; area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.17 times: 17 times is not the commonly used figure. Methane is taken as 21 times CO2 in warming effect.
choiceExplanations.23 times: 23 times is not the keyed figure. The item uses 21.
choiceExplanations.19 times: 19 times is not the keyed figure. The item uses 21.
choiceExplanations.21 times: Correct — 21 times is the commonly used global warming potential of methane relative to CO2.

items.question: When using covered lagoon biodigester, what is approximate methane content in biogas?

choiceExplanations.75%: 75% is too high for a covered lagoon, which gives about 70% methane.
choiceExplanations.65%: 65% is lower than the keyed 70% for a covered lagoon.
choiceExplanations.70%: Correct — 70% is the approximate methane content in biogas from a covered lagoon digester.
choiceExplanations.60%: 60% is lower than the keyed 70% for a covered lagoon.

items.question: What is the minimum methane content of biogas in order to operate biogas-fueled generators?

choiceExplanations.70%: 70% is higher than needed. Generators run on biogas from about 65% methane.
choiceExplanations.65%: Correct — 65% is the minimum methane content for biogas to run generators properly.
choiceExplanations.60%: 60% is below the minimum for biogas generators.
choiceExplanations.55%: 55% is below the minimum for biogas generators.

items.question: When using 1:1 water-manure ratio, what is the approximate methane content of biogas?

choiceExplanations.50%: 50% is lower than the typical methane content at a 1:1 ratio.
choiceExplanations.60%: Correct — 60% is the approximate methane content of biogas produced with a 1:1 water-manure ratio.
choiceExplanations.65%: 65% is higher than the keyed 60% for this ratio.
choiceExplanations.55%: 55% is lower than the keyed 60% for this ratio.

items.question: A board constructed across the bottom of the biogas digester to prevent early exit of slurry.

choiceExplanations.Weir plate: Weir plate controls overflow level, not a board across the digester bottom.
choiceExplanations.Scum breaker: Scum breaker breaks up floating crust, not a board across the bottom.
choiceExplanations.Diversion gate: Diversion gate redirects flow in channels, not inside a digester.
choiceExplanations.Baffle board: Correct — Baffle board is a board across the bottom of the digester that stops slurry from leaving early.

items.question: You are tasked to implement a biogas project for a poultry having 5,000 heads of layers. The prevailing daytime temperature in the project site is 30°C. Which of the biogas digesters below will you use?

choiceExplanations.Balloon type: Balloon type is a small plastic bag digester, not suited for 5,000 layers.
choiceExplanations.Fixed dome: Fixed dome is a household-size underground digester, not the keyed choice.
choiceExplanations.Covered lagoon: Covered lagoon suits very large farms with watery effluent, not the keyed choice here.
choiceExplanations.Floating type: Correct — Floating type digester is the keyed choice, since a warm site near 30°C favors it (Tambong, 1992).

items.question: Covered lagoon biodigester, minihydro and solar energy projects are evaluated for financial feasibility. Only one feasible project can be funded. Each of them requires PHP 20,000,000 investment. The financial internal rates of return are 8%, 9% and 10%, respectively. Annual discount plus inflation rate is 11%. Which project shall be implemented?
items.answer: None Since all their IRRs are less than the discount plus inflation rate
choices: None Since all their IRRs are less than the discount plus inflation rate

choiceExplanations.Minihydro: Minihydro has IRR of 9%, below the 11% discount plus inflation rate, so it should not be funded.
choiceExplanations.Solar energy: Solar energy has the best IRR at 10%, but 10% is still below the 11% required rate.
choiceExplanations.None Since all their IRRs are less than: Correct — None Since all their IRRs are less than the discount plus inflation rate is correct since all three IRRs (8%, 9%, 10%) are below the 11% discount plus inflation rate, so none is feasible.
choiceExplanations.Covered lagoon biodigester: Covered lagoon biodigester has IRR of 8%, below the 11% required rate, so it is not feasible.

items.question: In the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), how much will the project owner of a new covered lagoon biodigester receive annually from CDM fund for the first 10 years if his biodigester produces 8,000 tonnes of methane and 3,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide per year. Assume that the current carbon credit costs US$8 per tonne of carbon equivalent.
items.rationale:
[(tonnes carbon/year + 21 (tonnes of methane/year)] / = US$ 8/tonne [3,000 tonnes + 21(8,000 tonnes)] / = US$ 1,368,000/year

Notes: US$ 1,368,000 / Considering that methane is 21 times more destructive than carbon, Amount / = Carbon cost x

choiceExplanations.US$ 1,094,400: US$ 1,094,400 is too low. Methane is 8,000 t x 21 = 168,000 t CO2e, plus 3,000 t, then x $8.
choiceExplanations.US$ 1,368,000: Correct — US$ 1,368,000 is (8,000 x 21 + 3,000) tonnes CO2e x US$8 = 171,000 x 8, using methane as 21 times CO2.
choiceExplanations.US$ 1,504,800: US$ 1,504,800 is too high. The total is 171,000 tonnes CO2e x US$8 = US$1,368,000.
choiceExplanations.US$ 1,231,200: US$ 1,231,200 is too low. The total is 171,000 tonnes CO2e x US$8 = US$1,368,000.

items.question: What is the daily biogas consumption in cubic meters of an industrial boiler using 12 units of 50-cm gas burner 8 hours a day? The consumption of each gas burner is 1.3 cu.m./hour.
items.rationale: 125 / C = NBT where C= Consumption, N = No. of units, B = biogas consumption of device, T = Time C = (12 units)( 1.3 m3/hr)(8 hrs) / = 124.8 m3

choiceExplanations.138: 138 m3 is too high. Consumption = 12 x 1.3 x 8 = 124.8 m3 per day.
choiceExplanations.100: 100 m3 is too low. Consumption = 12 x 1.3 x 8 = 124.8 m3 per day.
choiceExplanations.125: Correct — 125 m3 per day is 12 burners x 1.3 m3/hr x 8 hr = 124.8, rounded.
choiceExplanations.112: 112 m3 is too low. Consumption = 12 x 1.3 x 8 = 124.8 m3 per day.

items.question: Estimate the biogas production in cubic meters per day from a large balloon type digester using 1:1 water-manure ratio. The source farm has 1,100 heads of porkers of mixed ages. Use a retention period of 30 days. The mean daily manure production of porkers is 2.2 kg/head while the specific gas production for 30-day manure retention period is 0.063 m3/kg.
items.rationale: 153 / P = NMG where P = biogas production potential, N = Number of heads, M = manure production, G = Specific gas production of the manure for a specific retention period P = (1,100 heads)(2.2 kg/head)(0.063 m3/kg) / = 152.46 m3

choiceExplanations.153: Correct — 153 m3 per day is P = N x M x G = 1,100 x 2.2 x 0.063 = 152.5, rounded.

items.question: How many heads of breeding cattle are needed as source of manure to generate 80 m3 of biogas a day if the retention period is 25 days and water-manure ratio is 1:1. The mean daily manure production of breeding cattle is 13 kg/head while its specific gas production for 25-day manure retention period is half of that of chicken dung.
items.rationale:
[(13 kg/head)(0.03 m3/kg)] / = 205.13 heads, to avoid gas shortage round up to 206

Notes: 206 / N = P/(MG) / where N = No. of heads, C = biogas production, M = manure production G = Half of specific gas production of chicken dung / = 1/2 x 0.06 m3/kg or 0.03 m3/kg N = (80 m3)/

choiceExplanations.227: 227 heads is too many. N = 80 / (13 x 0.03) is about 206.
choiceExplanations.185: 185 heads is too few. N = 80 / (13 x 0.03) is about 206.
choiceExplanations.165: 165 heads is too few. N = 80 / (13 x 0.03) is about 206.
choiceExplanations.206: Correct — 206 heads. Specific gas production is half of chicken dung (about 0.03 m3/kg), so N = 80 / (13 x 0.03).

items.question: The biggest biogas digester type in terms of volume that is appropriate for large animal farms.

choiceExplanations.Floating drum biodigester: Floating drum biodigester digesters are small to medium, far smaller than a lagoon.
choiceExplanations.Covered lagoon biodigester: Correct — Covered lagoon biodigester is a large lined pond with a gas-tight cover, the biggest in volume for large farms.
choiceExplanations.Plug flow biodigester: Plug flow biodigester digesters are long narrow tanks, smaller than lagoons.
choiceExplanations.Fixed dome biodigester: Fixed dome biodigester digesters are underground masonry tanks, limited in size.

items.question: The recommended biogas digester type for most Philippine households.

choiceExplanations.Plug flow digester: Plug flow digesters suit farms, not households.
choiceExplanations.Covered lagoon digester: Covered lagoon digesters are for large farms, not households.
choiceExplanations.Fixed dome digester: Fixed dome digesters are common in other countries but not the keyed choice for Philippine households.
choiceExplanations.Floating type digester: Correct — Floating type digester is the keyed recommendation for most Philippine households.

items.question: Power system that utilizes more than one energy sources such as solar, wind and biogas.

choiceExplanations.Cogeneration: Cogeneration makes heat and power together from one fuel, not several energy sources.
choiceExplanations.Hybrid: Correct — Hybrid power systems combine more than one energy source, such as solar, wind and biogas.
choiceExplanations.Standalone: Standalone means it works off-grid, not necessarily with several sources.
choiceExplanations.Grid-tied: Grid-tied means it is connected to the utility grid, not using several sources.

items.question: The acronym of the Inter-Governmental Panel for Climate Change.

choiceExplanations.Igcc: Igcc stands for Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle, a power plant type, not the climate panel.
choiceExplanations.Ipcc: Correct — Ipcc is the acronym of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change.
choiceExplanations.Iccc: Iccc is not the recognized acronym of the climate panel.
choiceExplanations.Ipcp: Ipcp is not the recognized acronym of the climate panel.

items.question: Best type of biogas plant for large animal farms having effluents with low volatile solids.

choiceExplanations.Floating drum: Floating drum suits small to medium farms, not large farms with watery effluent.
choiceExplanations.Covered lagoon: Correct — Covered lagoon is best for large farms with effluent low in volatile solids.
choiceExplanations.Plug flow: Plug flow needs high solids content, so it does not suit low-solid effluent.
choiceExplanations.Fixed dome: Fixed dome is a small, household-scale design.

items.question: Energy system consisting of the digester, gasholder, mixing tank and sludge tank.

choiceExplanations.Pyrolysis plant: Pyrolysis plant heats biomass without oxygen to make char and oil, with no digester.
choiceExplanations.Biogas plant: Correct — Biogas plant is the energy system with digester, gasholder, mixing tank and sludge tank.
choiceExplanations.Bioethanol plant: Bioethanol plant ferments sugars to ethanol using fermenters, not a digester and gasholder.
choiceExplanations.Gasification plant: Gasification plant makes syngas from solid fuel with a gasifier, not a digester.

items.question: The non-flammable component of biogas occupying significant volume.

choiceExplanations.Carbon monoxide: Carbon monoxide is a flammable, toxic gas and is not a major part of biogas.
choiceExplanations.Carbon dioxide: Correct — Carbon dioxide makes up about 30 to 40% of biogas and does not burn.
choiceExplanations.Nitrous oxide: Nitrous oxide is a minor greenhouse gas, not a large part of biogas.
choiceExplanations.Hydrogen sulfide: Hydrogen sulfide is flammable and present only in small amounts.

items.question: Watery mixture of insoluble solid.

choiceExplanations.Sludge: Sludge is settled, mud-like solids, thicker than a watery mixture.
choiceExplanations.Slurry: Correct — Slurry is a watery mixture of insoluble solids, like manure mixed with water.
choiceExplanations.Solution: Solution has dissolved substances, not insoluble solids.
choiceExplanations.Emulsion: Emulsion is a mix of two liquids that don't blend, not solids in water.

items.question: Color of biogas flame during daytime in outdoor areas.

choiceExplanations.Colorless: Correct — Biogas burns with a pale blue flame that is hardly visible in daylight, so it looks colorless outdoors.
choiceExplanations.Yellow: Yellow flames come from incomplete burning, which is not typical for clean biogas.
choiceExplanations.Orange: Orange flames come from incomplete burning or impurities, not clean biogas.
choiceExplanations.Red: Red flames suggest poor combustion and are not how biogas normally burns.

items.question: Estimated biogas produced per kg cow manure for 25-day hydraulic retention time.

choiceExplanations.0.12 m³ per kg: 0.12 m³ per kg is too high. The figure for cow manure at 25-day retention is about 0.03 m³/kg.
choiceExplanations.0.03 m³/kg: Correct — 0.03 m³/kg is the estimated biogas yield per kg of cow manure at 25-day retention.
choiceExplanations.0.09 m³ per kg: 0.09 m³ per kg is too high. The figure for cow manure is about 0.03 m³/kg.
choiceExplanations.0.06 m³ per kg: 0.06 m³ per kg is too high. The figure for cow manure is about 0.03 m³/kg.

items.question: Recommended manure-water ratio by volume for economical biogas production.

choiceExplanations.1:1: Correct — 1:1 means equal volumes of manure and water. It gives slurry that flows and digests well without needing too much water.
choiceExplanations.1:3: 1:3 adds too much water, which dilutes the slurry and wastes digester volume.
choiceExplanations.1:2: 1:2 adds more water than needed, lowering gas per unit digester volume.
choiceExplanations.2:1: 2:1 is too thick for easy flow and mixing in the digester.

items.question: The metal-corrosive component of biogas in small amount which smells like a rotten egg

choiceExplanations.Hydrogen sulfide: Correct — Hydrogen sulfide is the corrosive gas in biogas that smells like rotten eggs, even in small amounts.
choiceExplanations.Carbon monoxide: Carbon monoxide is odorless, and it is not a biogas component that corrodes metals.
choiceExplanations.Ammonia gas: Ammonia gas has a sharp pungent smell, not a rotten egg smell.
choiceExplanations.Sulfur dioxide: Sulfur dioxide has a sharp burnt-sulfur smell and forms from burning sulfur, not in raw biogas.

items.question: Main cause of air pollution as a result of combustion of fuel.

choiceExplanations.Nitrogen dioxide: Nitrogen dioxide is a pollutant from combustion, but it is not the main product here.
choiceExplanations.Sulfur dioxide: Sulfur dioxide comes from burning sulfur-containing fuel, a smaller share.
choiceExplanations.Carbon dioxide: Correct — Carbon dioxide is the main product when fuel burns completely, so it is keyed as the main pollutant.
choiceExplanations.Carbon monoxide: Carbon monoxide comes from incomplete combustion, and is toxic, but less in quantity than CO2.

items.question: Chemical formula for ozone

choiceExplanations.O2: O2 is ordinary oxygen with two atoms.
choiceExplanations.O3: Correct — O3 is ozone, three oxygen atoms bonded together.
choiceExplanations.N2O: N2O is nitrous oxide, a greenhouse gas.

items.question: Which statement is not true?
items.answer: Lowland rice is never grown in bunded fields.
items.rationale: Lowland (paddy) rice is typically cultivated in leveled, bunded fields built to impound irrigation or rainwater and maintain saturated soil conditions.
choices: Lowland rice is never grown in bunded fields.
Lowland rice is also called as “paddy rice”.
Lowland rice fields have saturated (anaerobic) soil conditions.
Rice is the only cereal that can grow in wetland conditions.

choiceExplanations.Lowland rice is also called as “paddy ri: Lowland rice is also called as “paddy rice”. paddy rice is a true statement.
choiceExplanations.Lowland rice fields have saturated (anae: Lowland rice fields have saturated (anaerobic) soil conditions. soil with anaerobic conditions is a true statement.
choiceExplanations.Rice is the only cereal that can grow in: Rice is the only cereal that can grow in wetland conditions. that can grow in wetland conditions is accepted as true in this item.

items.question: The normal atmosphere for storage is 21% oxygen, 0.03% carbon dioxide, and 79% nitrogen. In controlled atmosphere storage, the ___(X)___ is reduced and the ___(Y)___ level is increased.

choiceExplanations.X = oxygen; Y = nitrogen: X = oxygen; Y = nitrogen is wrong. In controlled atmosphere storage nitrogen is not the gas raised.
choiceExplanations.X = carbon dioxide; Y = oxygen: X = carbon dioxide; Y = oxygen reduced and oxygen increased is the reverse of controlled atmosphere storage.
choiceExplanations.X = nitrogen; Y = oxygen: X = nitrogen; Y = oxygen reduced and oxygen increased is wrong. Oxygen is the one lowered.
choiceExplanations.X = oxygen; Y = carbon dioxide: Correct — Lower oxygen and higher carbon dioxide slow respiration and ripening of stored produce.

items.question: Which of the following gases is principally produced during aerobic degradation of manure?

choiceExplanations.NH3: NH3 (ammonia) is produced mainly during anaerobic decay or by urea breakdown.
choiceExplanations.CH4: CH4 (methane) is produced in anaerobic degradation.
choiceExplanations.CO2: Correct — CO2 is the main gas produced when microbes break down manure with oxygen present.
choiceExplanations.H2S: H2S is produced in anaerobic conditions.

items.question: It refers to feces and urine prior to any changes due to addition of water, drying, volatilization and other processes.

choiceExplanations.Stabilized manure sludge: Stabilized manure sludge is already treated, so it is not raw excreta.
choiceExplanations.Raw manure slurry: Raw manure slurry has had water added, so it has changed from the original.
choiceExplanations.As excreted manure: Correct — As excreted manure is feces and urine before any change from water addition, drying or volatilization.
choiceExplanations.Fresh manure solids: Fresh manure solids describes only the solid part, not feces and urine together.

items.question: This parameter indicates the organic strength or load of a waste.

choiceExplanations.Biochemical Oxygen Demand: Correct — Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) is the oxygen microbes need to break down organic matter, so it shows organic strength.
choiceExplanations.Total Suspended Solids: Total Suspended Solids measures solid particles in water, not organic strength.
choiceExplanations.Total Kjeldahl Nitrogen: Total Kjeldahl Nitrogen measures organic plus ammonia nitrogen only.
choiceExplanations.Total Dissolved Solids: Total Dissolved Solids measures dissolved salts and minerals.

items.question: This process involves heating up of manure at high temperature in the complete absence of oxygen producing combustible gas, oil, and charcoal.

choiceExplanations.Combustion: Combustion burns with oxygen, so it is not oxygen-free.
choiceExplanations.Gasification: Gasification uses limited oxygen or steam to make syngas, not in complete absence of oxygen.
choiceExplanations.Incineration: Incineration burns waste with oxygen to ash.
choiceExplanations.Pyrolysis: Correct — Pyrolysis heating without oxygen, producing combustible gas, oil and charcoal.

items.question: Stage of aerobic composting which involves rapid increase in material temperature and uptake of soluble sugars and starches

choiceExplanations.1st mesophilic stage: Correct — 1st mesophilic stage is the initial stage where temperature rises quickly as microbes use soluble sugars and starches.
choiceExplanations.2nd mesophilic stage: 2nd mesophilic stage comes after the hot phase as the pile cools.
choiceExplanations.1st thermophilic stage: 1st thermophilic stage is the hot phase, after the first mesophilic stage.
choiceExplanations.Final curing stage: Final curing stage is the last stage where the compost matures.

items.question: Which of the following compost material is high in nitrogen content?
items.rationale: Chicken manure is a nitrogen-rich ('green') composting material with a low C:N ratio, whereas wood chips, rice straw, and newspaper are carbon-rich ('brown') materials.

choiceExplanations.Newspaper: Newspaper is carbon-rich and low in nitrogen.
choiceExplanations.Rice straw: Rice straw is carbon-rich with high C:N ratio.
choiceExplanations.Wood chips: Wood chips are very high in carbon and low in nitrogen.
choiceExplanations.Chicken manure: Correct — Chicken manure is high in nitrogen, so it balances carbon-rich materials.

items.question: The amount of volatile solids fed daily per unit working volume of digester.

choiceExplanations.Volatile solids fraction: Volatile solids fraction is the share of solids that is organic, not a feed rate.
choiceExplanations.Organic loading rate: Correct — Organic loading rate is the volatile solids fed per day per unit working volume of digester.
choiceExplanations.Solids retention time: Solids retention time is how long solids stay in the digester.
choiceExplanations.Hydraulic retention time: Hydraulic retention time is how long liquid stays in the digester.

items.question: This commercial anaerobic digester uses a high density polyethylene (HDPE) material as lagoon liner and cover to completely seal and contain the wastewater and biogas generated.

choiceExplanations.Upflow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB): Upflow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB) is a tank reactor with granular sludge, not a lined lagoon.
choiceExplanations.Expanded granular sludge bed (EGSB): Expanded granular sludge bed (EGSB) is a tall tank reactor, not a lagoon.
choiceExplanations.Covered in ground anaerobic reactor (CIG: Correct — Covered in ground anaerobic reactor (CIGAR) is a lagoon sealed with an HDPE liner and cover to hold wastewater and biogas.
choiceExplanations.Continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR): Continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR) is a mixed tank, not a lined lagoon.

items.question: The recommended distance of a septic tank from a well is:

choiceExplanations.16 meters or more: 16 meters or more is not the standard. The recommended distance is 15 m or more.
choiceExplanations.12 meters or more: 12 meters or more is less than the recommended distance of 15 m.
choiceExplanations.15 meters or more: Correct — 15 meters or more is the recommended distance of a septic tank from a well to protect water.
choiceExplanations.14 meters or more: 14 meters or more is less than the recommended distance of 15 m.

items.question: Cyclone efficiency increases for ___.

choiceExplanations.Fine particles: Fine particles are hard to separate in a cyclone, so efficiency falls.
choiceExplanations.Light particles: Light particles follow the gas stream and are hard to separate.
choiceExplanations.Small particles: Small particles carry less centrifugal force, so efficiency drops.
choiceExplanations.Large particles: Correct — Large particles have more centrifugal force and are thrown to the wall, so cyclone efficiency increases.

items.question: The biological decomposition of nitrogenous organic matter producing a foul-smelling product associated with the anaerobic degradation of proteins.

choiceExplanations.Ammonification: Ammonification is the release of ammonia from organic nitrogen, not the foul-smelling protein decay.
choiceExplanations.Fermentation: Fermentation is breakdown of sugars by microbes without oxygen, not specifically protein decay.
choiceExplanations.Putrefaction: Correct — Putrefaction is anaerobic decay of proteins that gives foul-smelling products.
choiceExplanations.Nitrification: Nitrification is oxidation of ammonia to nitrate with oxygen.

items.question: discharges from known sources which is passed into a body of water or land; or wastewater flowing out of a manufacturing plant; industrial plant including domestic; commercial; and recreational activities.

choiceExplanations.Septage: Septage is material pumped from septic tanks.
choiceExplanations.Leachate: Leachate is liquid that drains through decomposing waste.
choiceExplanations.Effluent: Correct — Effluent is wastewater discharged from a known source, such as a plant or household, into water or land.
choiceExplanations.Influent: Influent is wastewater flowing into a treatment plant.

items.question: PAES 414-2:2002 Waste Management Structures Part 2: Agricultural solid waste Composting: What is the typical composting time for windrow method?

choiceExplanations.3 months: 3 months is shorter than the typical windrow time of 4 months in PAES 414-2.
choiceExplanations.5 months: 5 months is longer than the typical windrow time of 4 months.
choiceExplanations.4 months: Correct — 4 months is the typical composting time for the windrow method in PAES 414-2:2002.
choiceExplanations.2 months: 2 months is shorter than the typical windrow time of 4 months.

items.question: PAES 414-2:2002 Waste Management Structures Part 2: Agricultural solid waste Composting: What is the typical composting time for aerated static in pile?

choiceExplanations.4 weeks: Correct — 4 weeks is the typical composting time for the aerated static pile method.
choiceExplanations.3 weeks: 3 weeks is not the typical time. The aerated static pile takes about 4 weeks.
choiceExplanations.2 weeks: 2 weeks is shorter than the typical 4 weeks.
choiceExplanations.5 weeks: 5 weeks is longer than the typical 4 weeks.

items.question: Typical composting time for In-vessel composting method

choiceExplanations.4 month: 4 month is too long. In-vessel composting is fast, about 1 month.
choiceExplanations.2 month: 2 month is longer than the typical 1 month for in-vessel composting.

choiceExplanations.Nonmetallic cable: Nonmetallic cable (Romex) has a plastic sheath with no metal enclosure.
choiceExplanations.Armored cable: Correct — Armored cable (BX) has insulated conductors inside a flexible interlocked metal sheath, used for exposed and concealed work.

items.question: It is a wiring accessories or channels designed for holding wires cables or busbars w/c are either made of metal plastic or any insulating materials

choiceExplanations.Panelboards: Panelboards are distribution boxes with breakers or fuses, not channels for holding wires.
choiceExplanations.Raceways: Correct — Raceways are channels (conduit, wireways, ducts) of metal, plastic or insulating material that hold wires, cables or busbars.
choiceExplanations.Cabinets: Cabinets are enclosures that house panelboards; they are not wire channels.
choiceExplanations.Switchboards: Switchboards are large panels for controlling and distributing power, not channels for wires.

items.question: Maximum stock height for grains stored in woven polypropylene bags

choiceExplanations.4m: 4 m is higher than the allowed stack height for woven polypropylene bags.
choiceExplanations.2m: 2 m is lower than the standard maximum stack height.
choiceExplanations.3m: Correct — Bags of woven polypropylene may be stacked to a maximum of 3 m under the grain storage standard.
choiceExplanations.5m: 5 m is too high; such stacks would be unstable.

items.question: In flocculation process, it is necesarry that the water being treated must be

choiceExplanations.Filtered: Filtering comes after flocculation and sedimentation; it is not what flocs need during flocculation.
choiceExplanations.Aerated: Aeration adds oxygen to remove gases and iron; it is not the flocculation requirement.
choiceExplanations.Chlorinated: Chlorination is disinfection, done after clarification, not during flocculation.
choiceExplanations.Agitated: Correct — Flocculation needs gentle agitation so fine particles collide and form larger flocs that settle.

items.question: Lesser amount of chlorine is needed for water being treated if the turbidity of water is

choiceExplanations.Low: Correct — Low turbidity means few particles shielding microbes, so less chlorine is consumed and needed.
choiceExplanations.Variable: Variable turbidity does not by itself lower chlorine demand.
choiceExplanations.High: High turbidity shields microbes and consumes chlorine, so more chlorine is needed.
choiceExplanations.Moderate: Moderate turbidity needs more chlorine than low turbidity.

items.question: A partially lined or unlined underground pit into which raw animal or household waste water is discharged

choiceExplanations.Cesspool: Correct — A cesspool is a partially lined or unlined pit that receives raw wastewater and lets it seep into the soil.
choiceExplanations.Oxidation pond: An oxidation pond is a shallow lagoon for biological treatment, not an underground pit.
choiceExplanations.Imhoff tank: An Imhoff tank is a two-story settling and digestion tank, not a seepage pit.
choiceExplanations.Septic tank: A septic tank is a watertight tank with an outlet to a drain field, not an unlined pit.

items.question: A film produced during slow filtration responsible for the bacteriological purification effect on water

choiceExplanations.Scum layer: Scum layer is floating material on a settling tank, not the filter's purification film.
choiceExplanations.Sludge blanket: Sludge blanket is settled solids in a clarifier, not a film on a slow sand filter.
choiceExplanations.Filter cake: Filter cake is solids built up on pressure or vacuum filters, not the slow filtration film.
choiceExplanations.Filter skin: Correct — The filter skin (schmutzdecke) is a biological film on top of a slow sand filter that removes bacteria.

items.question: The water-carried waste from households or industry

choiceExplanations.Effluent: Effluent is the liquid flowing out of a treatment unit, not the waste itself.
choiceExplanations.Sewage: Correct — Sewage is water-carried waste from households or industry.
choiceExplanations.Sludge: Sludge is the settled solid portion of waste, not the water-carried waste.
choiceExplanations.Sullage: Sullage is wastewater from bathing and washing without toilet waste; it is only part of sewage.

items.question: The average time wherein waste is subjected to stabilization process or held in storage

choiceExplanations.Contact time: Contact time is how long disinfectant touches water, not waste stabilization time.
choiceExplanations.Settling time: Settling time is the time for solids to settle, not the average holding time.
choiceExplanations.Detention time: Correct — Detention time is the average time waste is held in a tank or pond for stabilization.
choiceExplanations.Reaction time: Reaction time refers to a chemical reaction, not the holding time of waste.

items.question: 1 psi = ____ inches of water

choiceExplanations.35.9: 35.9 is not the right conversion for 1 psi.
choiceExplanations.24.3: 24.3 is not the right conversion for 1 psi.
choiceExplanations.29.8: 29.8 is roughly inches of mercury for 1 atm, not inches of water per psi.
choiceExplanations.27.6: Correct — 1 psi equals about 27.6 inches of water column.

items.question: A unit of deformation as a result of change in the form produced by stress

choiceExplanations.Strain: Correct — Strain is the deformation per unit length that results from stress.
choiceExplanations.Shear: Shear is a type of stress acting parallel to a surface, not the deformation unit.
choiceExplanations.Creep: Creep is slow deformation under constant load over time.
choiceExplanations.Deflection: Deflection is the displacement of a member, not deformation per unit length.

items.question: It is the amount of stress that produce failure by increasing the unit stress until breakage or rupture occurs

choiceExplanations.Allowable stress: Allowable stress is the safe working stress, well below failure.
choiceExplanations.Ultimate strength: Correct — Ultimate strength is the stress at which the material breaks or ruptures.
choiceExplanations.Yield strength: Yield strength is where permanent deformation starts, not breakage.
choiceExplanations.Elastic limit: Elastic limit is the stress up to which the material returns to shape, not breakage.

items.question: Ratio of the ultimate strength to the working stress

choiceExplanations.Factor of safety: Correct — Factor of safety = ultimate strength divided by working stress.
choiceExplanations.Margin of safety: Margin of safety is a related quantity (factor of safety minus 1), not the ratio itself.
choiceExplanations.Modulus of toughness: Modulus of toughness is the area under the whole stress-strain curve, the energy to fracture.
choiceExplanations.Modulus of resilience: Modulus of resilience is the energy absorbed up to the elastic limit.

items.question: It refers to the stress in a material tending to cause deformation along a plane or planes perpendicular to the imposed force

choiceExplanations.Bending stress: Bending stress comes from moments and causes bending, not deformation along planes perpendicular to the force.
choiceExplanations.Shear stress: Shear stress acts parallel to the plane, not perpendicular to it.
choiceExplanations.Normal stress: Correct — Normal stress acts perpendicular to the plane (tension or compression), as the question describes.
choiceExplanations.Bearing stress: Bearing stress is contact pressure between two surfaces, not the stress described.

items.question: Given the thermodynamic identity dU = TdS - PdV, an adiabatic process assumes a constant
items.rationale: For a reversible adiabatic process dQ = TdS = 0, so entropy S stays constant (isentropic).

choiceExplanations.V , volume: Wrong — constant volume is an isochoric process, not adiabatic.
choiceExplanations.S , entropy: Correct — in dU = TdS − PdV, no heat flow means TdS = 0, so entropy S is constant (isentropic).
choiceExplanations.T , temperature: Wrong — constant temperature is an isothermal process; an adiabatic process usually changes temperature.
choiceExplanations.P , pressure: Wrong — constant pressure is an isobaric process, not adiabatic.

items.question: The highest pressure drop in the refrigeration cycle occurs at the

choiceExplanations.Evaporator coil: The evaporator has only a small friction pressure drop in its coils.
choiceExplanations.Expansion device: Correct — The expansion device (valve or capillary) drops pressure sharply from condenser to evaporator pressure.
choiceExplanations.Condenser coil: The condenser has only small friction pressure loss at high pressure.
choiceExplanations.Compressor unit: The compressor raises pressure; it does not cause the biggest drop.

items.question: In a throttling device, the enthalpy in the direction of flow

choiceExplanations.Remains constant: Correct — Throttling is isenthalpic: no work or heat transfer, so enthalpy stays constant while pressure drops.
choiceExplanations.Drops sharply: Enthalpy does not drop sharply in throttling; it is constant.
choiceExplanations.Decreases steadily: Enthalpy does not decrease in throttling; pressure and temperature may change but enthalpy does not.
choiceExplanations.Increases rapidly: Enthalpy does not increase in throttling; it stays constant.

items.question: Fresh fruits and vegetables respire and release heat during storage. This heat produced by respiration varies with the product and its temperature. As the product temperature decreases,

choiceExplanations.Heat of respiration increases exponentia: Respiration heat does not rise as temperature falls; it falls.
choiceExplanations.Heat of respiration remains constant: Heat of respiration changes with temperature, so it does not stay constant.
choiceExplanations.Heat of respiration decreases linearly: Respiration rate follows an exponential-type temperature relation, not a straight-line one.
choiceExplanations.Heat of respiration decreases exponentia: Correct — Respiration is enzyme-driven, so lowering temperature reduces heat of respiration exponentially.

items.question: All life-forms require water for growth. Water activity refers to the availability of water within a food system and is defined at a given temperature as
items.answer: Vapor pressure of water in the food over the vapor pressure of pure water
items.rationale: Water activity aw = p / p₀: the vapor pressure of water in the food divided by that of pure water at the same temperature (0 to 1).
choices: Vapor pressure of solution over the vapor pressure of solute
Vapor pressure of pure solvent over the vapor pressure of solution
Osmotic pressure of solute over the osmotic pressure of solution
Vapor pressure of water in the food over the vapor pressure of pure water

choiceExplanations.Vapor pressure of solution over the vapo: Wrong — water activity compares the food's vapor pressure to pure water, not to the solute.
choiceExplanations.Vapor pressure of pure solvent over the: Wrong — this is inverted (p₀/p) and would give values above 1.
choiceExplanations.Osmotic pressure of solute over the osmo: Wrong — water activity is defined by vapor pressure, not osmotic pressure.
choiceExplanations.Vapor pressure of water in the food over: Correct — aw = p/p₀, the vapor pressure of water in the food over that of pure water at the same temperature.

items.question: In a flat bed dryer, as the airflow rate (m3/s.m2) is increased exponentially, the pressure drop per meter depth

choiceExplanations.Fluctuates: Pressure drop does not fluctuate randomly; it rises steadily with airflow.
choiceExplanations.Increases: Correct — Pressure drop through a grain bed rises with airflow rate, faster than linearly.
choiceExplanations.Stabilizes: Pressure drop does not stabilize; more air through the same bed means higher resistance.
choiceExplanations.Decreases: Pressure drop does not decrease with more air; it increases.

items.question: The protection of inventions by RPABE registered as patents and utility models

choiceExplanations.Intellectual property: Correct — Patents and utility models registered by RPABE-type inventors are protected as intellectual property.
choiceExplanations.Trade secret: A trade secret is protected by confidentiality, not by registration as patents or utility models.
choiceExplanations.Industrial design: Industrial design protects the look of a product, not patents or utility models.
choiceExplanations.Copyright protection: Copyright protects creative works like writings, not inventions.

items.question: The agency mandated to develop standards for agriculture and fishery machinery, tools and equipment.

choiceExplanations.Philmech: PHilMech does research, development and extension on postharvest and mechanization, not standards.
choiceExplanations.Bafs: Correct — BAFS (Bureau of Agriculture and Fisheries Standards) develops standards for agri-fishery machinery, tools and equipment.
choiceExplanations.Bafe: BAFE is not the agency that sets these standards.
choiceExplanations.Amtec: AMTEC tests and evaluates machinery; it does not develop the standards.

items.question: Items indicated in the documents signed, used, or issued by a PABE in connection with the practice of the profession, except:
items.rationale: Under Philippine ABE professional practice regulations (RA 10915), a PABE must indicate the professional license number, Professional Tax Receipt (PTR) number, and duration of validity on signed or issued documents; the registration date of the license is not required.

choiceExplanations.Professional license number: The professional license number must be indicated on documents signed or issued by the PABE.
choiceExplanations.Registration date of license: Correct — The date of registration of the license is not among the items required on documents the PABE signs.
choiceExplanations.Professional tax receipt: The professional tax receipt number is required on documents the PABE signs.
choiceExplanations.Duration of validity: The validity period of the license is required on documents the PABE signs.

items.question: Part of the BAC that purpose is to enhance transparency of the government procurement process.

choiceExplanations.Secretariat: The Secretariat handles BAC paperwork and support, not transparency monitoring.
choiceExplanations.Auditors: Auditors review after the fact; they are not the BAC part meant to ensure transparency.
choiceExplanations.Consultants: Consultants give technical advice, not transparency oversight.
choiceExplanations.Observers: Correct — Observers (such as civil society and COA representatives) watch BAC proceedings to boost transparency in procurement.

items.question: Republic Act No. 9367 is also known as:

choiceExplanations.Renewable energy act: The Renewable Energy Act is RA 9513, not 9367.
choiceExplanations.Biofuels act: Correct — RA 9367 is the Biofuels Act of 2006, promoting biodiesel and bioethanol use.
choiceExplanations.Clean water act: The Clean Water Act is RA 9275, not 9367.
choiceExplanations.Clean air act: The Clean Air Act is RA 8749, not 9367.

items.question: The code that deals with minimum standards and requirements for all buildings and structures:
items.answer: RA 6541 or national bulding code PD 1096
choices: RA 6541 or national bulding code PD 1096
RA 9275 or clean water code PD 984
RA 9514 or revised fire code PD 1185

choiceExplanations.RA 6541 or national bulding code PD 1096: Correct — The National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096) sets minimum standards for all buildings and structures.
choiceExplanations.RA 1364 or sanitation code PD 856: The Sanitation Code is PD 856, which covers health and sanitation, not building standards.
choiceExplanations.RA 9275 or clean water code PD 984: This pairs the Clean Water Act with a wrong PD number; it is not the building code.
choiceExplanations.RA 9514 or revised fire code PD 1185: The Fire Code is for fire safety, not general minimum building standards.

items.question: The agency mandated in the testing and evaluation of agricultural and fisheries machinery and equipment to be sold in the market.

choiceExplanations.Bafs: BAFS develops standards but is not the agency that tests machinery for sale.
choiceExplanations.Amtec: Correct — AMTEC (Agricultural Machinery Testing and Evaluation Center) tests and evaluates agri-fishery machinery for the market.
choiceExplanations.Philmech: PHilMech does postharvest R&D and extension, not the official testing for sale.
choiceExplanations.Bafe: BAFE is not the agency that tests and evaluates machinery.

items.question: Majority of electric power in the Philippines is produced using this.

choiceExplanations.Photovoltaics: Photovoltaics turns sunlight into electricity and supplies a small share of Philippine power.
choiceExplanations.Piezoelectricity: Piezoelectricity makes tiny power from pressure and is not used for bulk power.
choiceExplanations.Magnetism: Correct — Most power plants (coal, hydro, geothermal, diesel) spin generators using electromagnetic induction, which is based on magnetism.
choiceExplanations.Electrochemistry: Electrochemistry (batteries) is not how grid power is mainly produced.

items.question: A dryer in w/c the material being dried moves through the drying chamber is substantially continuous stream w/out being recirculated

choiceExplanations.Recirculating-type dryer: A recirculating dryer returns grain to be dried repeatedly, unlike this description.
choiceExplanations.Batch-type dryer: A batch dryer holds a fixed load until dry, not a continuous stream.
choiceExplanations.Continuous-flow type dryer: Correct — A continuous-flow dryer moves grain through the drying chamber in a steady stream without recirculation.
choiceExplanations.Fluidized-bed type dryer: A fluidized-bed dryer suspends grain in air; it is not defined by a single continuous pass.

items.question: An air moving device to force heated air through the mass of grain at a desired air-flow rate and pressure

choiceExplanations.Aspirator: An aspirator is a suction device to remove dust or light material, not a main air supply.
choiceExplanations.Compressor: A compressor raises gas pressure to high levels, far more than drying needs.
choiceExplanations.Exhauster: An exhauster pulls air out of a space; it does not push heated air through grain.
choiceExplanations.Blower: Correct — A blower forces heated air through a grain mass at the needed airflow and pressure.

items.question: Warranty period for mechanical grain dryers

choiceExplanations.4 months: 4 months is shorter than the standard warranty.
choiceExplanations.7 months: 7 months is longer than the standard warranty.
choiceExplanations.6 months: Correct — The standard warranty for mechanical grain dryers is 6 months.
choiceExplanations.5 months: 5 months is shorter than the standard warranty.

items.question: Pressure build up in plenum chamber to maintain uniform distribution of air flow through the grain mass

choiceExplanations.Differential pressure: Differential pressure is a difference between two points, not the pressure in the plenum.
choiceExplanations.Static pressure: Correct — Static pressure builds in the plenum chamber, and this keeps airflow uniform through the grain mass.
choiceExplanations.Velocity pressure: Velocity pressure comes from air movement, not pressure buildup in the plenum.
choiceExplanations.Total pressure: Total pressure is static plus velocity; the plenum buildup is static pressure.

items.question: Moisture that can be found at the surface of the material

choiceExplanations.Hygroscopic moisture: Hygroscopic moisture is held inside the material in equilibrium with humid air, not on the surface.
choiceExplanations.Free moisture: Correct — Free moisture is on the surface and in large pores, and is easily removed.
choiceExplanations.Bound moisture: Bound moisture is held within the material by physical or chemical forces, not on the surface.
choiceExplanations.Equilibrium moisture: Equilibrium moisture is the moisture reached with surrounding air, not surface moisture.

items.question: The recommended depth of grain in a shallow bed dryer is

choiceExplanations.Up to 20 inches: 20 inches is deeper than the recommended shallow-bed depth.
choiceExplanations.Up to 18 inches: Correct — A shallow bed dryer keeps the grain layer thin, up to about 18 inches, so air dries it evenly.
choiceExplanations.Up to 14 inches: 14 inches is thinner than the maximum recommended depth.
choiceExplanations.Up to 16 inches: 16 inches is thinner than the maximum recommended depth.

items.question: Manufacturers prescribed peripheral velocity of a disk huller is:

choiceExplanations.18m/s: 18 m/s is faster than the manufacturer's prescribed disk huller speed.
choiceExplanations.14m/s: Correct — Manufacturers prescribe a peripheral velocity of about 14 m/s for a disk huller.
choiceExplanations.12m/s: 12 m/s is slower than the prescribed speed.
choiceExplanations.16m/s: 16 m/s is faster than the prescribed speed.

items.question: Manufacturers recommendation for the speed of cone in a vertical abrasive whitening cone must not exceed

choiceExplanations.13m/s: Correct — The cone of a vertical abrasive whitener should not exceed 13 m/s peripheral speed, to avoid grain breakage.
choiceExplanations.11m/s: 11 m/s is below the stated maximum limit.
choiceExplanations.15m/s: 15 m/s is above the recommended maximum.
choiceExplanations.17m/s: 17 m/s is above the recommended maximum.

items.question: Manufacturers recommendation for the speed of a horizontal abrasive whitener

choiceExplanations.1000 rpm: Correct — Manufacturers recommend about 1000 rpm for a horizontal abrasive whitener.
choiceExplanations.800 rpm: 800 rpm is below the recommended speed.
choiceExplanations.880 rpm: 880 rpm is below the recommended speed.
choiceExplanations.1150 rpm: 1150 rpm is above the recommended speed.

items.question: Recommended stacking density per cubic meter of space for palay

choiceExplanations.12 bags: 12 bags per m3 is more than the recommended density for palay.
choiceExplanations.8 bags: 8 bags per m3 is less than the recommended density.
choiceExplanations.10 bags: Correct — Palay is stacked at about 10 bags per cubic meter of storage space.
choiceExplanations.14 bags: 14 bags per m3 is more than the recommended density for palay.

items.question: Recommended stacking density per cubic meter of space for corn

choiceExplanations.14 bags: 14 bags per m3 is more than the recommended density for corn.
choiceExplanations.10 bags: 10 bags per m3 is the figure for palay, not corn.
choiceExplanations.16 bags: 16 bags per m3 is more than the recommended density for corn.
choiceExplanations.12 bags: Correct — Corn is stacked at about 12 bags per cubic meter, being denser than palay.

items.question: A process of separating lower density materials from grains

choiceExplanations.Scalping: Scalping removes large trash and oversize material, not lighter particles.
choiceExplanations.Sieving: Sieving separates by particle size using screens, not by density.
choiceExplanations.Aspiration: Correct — Aspiration uses an air stream to carry away lighter material like chaff and dust from grain.
choiceExplanations.Polishing: Polishing is a final milling step that smooths rice; it does not separate light matter.

items.question: A hydrothermal treatment of paddy before miling

choiceExplanations.Steaming: Steaming is only a part of parboiling; the complete process also includes soaking and drying.
choiceExplanations.Blanching: Blanching is a short heat treatment for vegetables, not a paddy process.
choiceExplanations.Tempering: Tempering is resting grain for moisture equalization, not a heat-soak treatment.
choiceExplanations.Parboiling: Correct — Parboiling soaks, steams and dries paddy before milling, which hardens the grain and reduces breakage.

items.question: In a disk huller, the stationary disk is located at

choiceExplanations.Side of the huller: The stationary disk is not on the side; the rotating disk faces it across a gap.
choiceExplanations.Center of the huller: The center holds the feed opening or shaft, not the stationary disk.
choiceExplanations.Bottom of the huller: The bottom is where the rotating disk is placed in this design.
choiceExplanations.Top of the huller: Correct — In a disk huller the stationary disk sits on top while the rotating disk is beneath, with the clearance between them.

items.question: The capacity of a compartment type separator is

choiceExplanations.40-60 kg brown rice per hour: Correct — A compartment type separator handles about 40-60 kg brown rice per hour.
choiceExplanations.120-150 kg brown rice per hour: 120-150 kg/h is higher than the typical capacity.
choiceExplanations.80-100 kg brown rice per hour: 80-100 kg/h is higher than the typical capacity.
choiceExplanations.10-20 kg brown rice per hour: 10-20 kg/h is lower than the typical capacity.

items.question: A small meta probe for taking samples of paddy

choiceExplanations.Scoop: A scoop is a shovel-like tool, not a probe for sampling inside a bag.
choiceExplanations.Divider: A divider splits a sample into equal parts; it does not take samples from bags.
choiceExplanations.Trier: Correct — A trier is a small metal probe pushed into a bag or pile to take grain samples.
choiceExplanations.Auger: An auger is a screw-type device, not the small probe used for sampling paddy.

items.question: The coefficient of friction of rice to a steel material is 0.41 what is the minimum angle of hopper required for the system

choiceExplanations.18 deg: 18 deg is smaller than the angle needed; hopper slope must exceed the friction angle.
choiceExplanations.20 deg: 20 deg is smaller than the friction angle of about 22 deg.
choiceExplanations.24 deg: 24 deg is more than the minimum needed.
choiceExplanations.22 deg: Correct — Minimum hopper angle equals the friction angle: arctan(0.41) = about 22 degrees.

items.question: One ton of coconut will produce approximately ____kg of oil

choiceExplanations.528kg: 528 kg is lower than the typical oil yield figure.
choiceExplanations.552kg: 552 kg is lower than the typical oil yield figure.
choiceExplanations.600kg: Correct — One ton of coconut (copra basis) yields approximately 600 kg of oil by the reference figure.
choiceExplanations.732kg: 732 kg is higher than possible oil yield.

items.question: The density of pig and poultry feed is approx.

choiceExplanations.396kg/m³: 396 kg/m3 is not the standard density used for pig and poultry feed.
choiceExplanations.549kg/m³: 549 kg/m3 is higher than the typical feed density.
choiceExplanations.450kg/m³: Correct — Pig and poultry feed has a bulk density of about 450 kg/m3.
choiceExplanations.518kg/m³: 518 kg/m3 is higher than the typical feed density.

items.question: A type of bearing used for tightening bucket elevator belts

choiceExplanations.Pillow block units: Pillow block units are bearing housings that support shafts, not the tensioning device.
choiceExplanations.Flange block units: Flange block units are bolted bearing mounts, not belt tighteners.
choiceExplanations.Take-up units: Correct — Take-up units are bearing units on adjustable slides that tighten the bucket elevator belt.
choiceExplanations.Cartridge bearing units: A cartridge bearing unit is a sealed bearing assembly, not the tension adjuster.

items.question: Recommended size of scalper for paddy cleaning

choiceExplanations.2.2-2.2m²/ton: 2.2 m2/ton is far larger than the recommended scalper size.
choiceExplanations.0.2-0.25m²/ton: Correct — A scalper for paddy cleaning is sized at about 0.2-0.25 m2 per ton of capacity.
choiceExplanations.4.2-4.2m²/ton: 4.2 m2/ton is far larger than recommended.
choiceExplanations.6.2-6.2m²/ton: 6.2 m2/ton is far larger than recommended.

items.question: An air moving device w/c produces high airflow but low head
items.source: Area 3 objectives; area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Fan: Correct — A fan moves large volumes of air at low pressure (low head).
choiceExplanations.Exhauster: An exhauster is for pulling air at higher suction pressure than fans.
choiceExplanations.Compressor: A compressor produces high pressure at low flow.
choiceExplanations.Blower: A blower gives higher pressure than a fan, with lower airflow.

items.question: A device that is used to moved oil

choiceExplanations.Blower: A blower moves air or gas, not oil.
choiceExplanations.Pump: Correct — A pump is the device used to move liquids such as oil.
choiceExplanations.Ejector: An ejector uses a jet of fluid to draw in another fluid; it is not the standard oil mover.
choiceExplanations.Compressor: A compressor raises gas pressure and does not move oil.

items.question: Reccomended for conveying product with less damage

choiceExplanations.Bucket elevator: Bucket elevators lift material and drop it, which can bruise product.
choiceExplanations.Belt conveyor: Correct — A belt conveyor carries product gently on a smooth belt, causing the least damage.
choiceExplanations.Screw conveyor: Screw conveyors rub and crush product against the trough.
choiceExplanations.Pneumatic conveyor: Pneumatic conveyors move product by fast air, causing impact damage.

items.question: A machine that is used to removed the bran from the brown rice

choiceExplanations.Whitener: Correct — A whitener (rice mill) removes the bran layer from brown rice to give white rice.
choiceExplanations.Huller: A huller removes the hull from paddy to give brown rice, not bran.
choiceExplanations.Separator: A separator separates paddy from brown rice.
choiceExplanations.Destoner: A destoner removes stones from grain, not bran.

items.question: A type of whitener consisting of a fluted roller rotating inside the hexagonal chamber with slot-type perforations

choiceExplanations.Abrasive-type whitener: An abrasive whitener uses stone or emery rollers rather than a fluted roller.
choiceExplanations.Vertical-cone whitener: A vertical cone whitener has a cone-shaped abrasive, not a fluted roller in a hex chamber.
choiceExplanations.Horizontal-stone whitener: A horizontal stone whitener uses abrasive stones rather than a fluted roller.
choiceExplanations.Frictional-type whitener: Correct — A frictional whitener uses a fluted roller turning in a slotted hexagonal chamber to remove bran by friction.

items.question: The husking ratio of the rubber roll huller is about

choiceExplanations.90–100%: 90-100% is above the husking ratio rubber roll hullers achieve.
choiceExplanations.70–80%: 70-80% is lower than the typical husking ratio.
choiceExplanations.80-90%: Correct — A rubber roll huller husks about 80-90% of paddy per pass.
choiceExplanations.100–110%: 100-110% is impossible; a ratio cannot exceed 100%.

items.question: The usual depth of grain in deep bed batch dryer is

choiceExplanations.12–14 ft: 12-14 ft is deeper than the usual deep bed batch dryer depth.
choiceExplanations.10–12 ft: 10-12 ft is deeper than the usual deep bed batch dryer depth.
choiceExplanations.8-10 ft: Correct — A deep bed batch dryer holds grain usually 8-10 ft deep.
choiceExplanations.6–8 ft: 6-8 ft is shallower than the usual depth.

items.question: Average velocity of a hammer tip of a hammer mill

choiceExplanations.100m/s: Correct — A hammer mill tip speed averages about 100 m/s to shatter grain.
choiceExplanations.105m/s: 105 m/s is above the average hammer tip speed.
choiceExplanations.95m/s: 95 m/s is below the average hammer tip speed.
choiceExplanations.90m/s: 90 m/s is below the average hammer tip speed.

items.question: Optimum mixing time of vertical-type feed mixer

choiceExplanations.35mins: 35 mins is much longer than needed for a vertical feed mixer.
choiceExplanations.15mins: Correct — The optimum mixing time for a vertical feed mixer is about 15 minutes.
choiceExplanations.25mins: 25 mins is longer than the optimum.
choiceExplanations.45mins: 45 mins is much longer than the optimum.

items.question: Approx. Speed of horizontal type feed mixer

choiceExplanations.15rpm: 15 rpm is slower than the usual speed of a horizontal mixer.
choiceExplanations.25rpm: Correct — A horizontal feed mixer runs at about 25 rpm.
choiceExplanations.30rpm: 30 rpm is faster than the usual speed.
choiceExplanations.20rpm: 20 rpm is slower than the usual speed.

items.question: Required mixing time for horizontal feed mixer

choiceExplanations.15mins: 15 mins is the longer time typical of vertical mixers.
choiceExplanations.5mins: Correct — A horizontal mixer is fast, needing only about 5 minutes of mixing.

items.question: Cooling meat, fruits, and vegetables are examples of heat transmission by

choiceExplanations.Crumbling: Correct — Crumbling grinds pellets into coarse granular form.

choiceExplanations.Blanching: Blanching is brief heating of vegetables to inactivate enzymes.
choiceExplanations.Sterilization: Sterilization kills all organisms, not just many.

items.question: Rapid removal of moisture of the product usually to a very low level.

choiceExplanations.Pasteurizing: Pasteurizing kills many microbes but is not a preparation step like this.

items.question: It is the heat added or removed from a substance causing a change in its state without changing its temperature.

items.question: It is the simplest method of separating solid particles from air by allowing air to pass through a large chamber to cause the solid material to fall due to its weight.

items.question: A pretreatment method for fruits and vegetables to retard spoilage and darkening of fruits.

choiceExplanations.Coconut flour: Coconut flour is a food product milled from dried meat.

items.question: A broken piece of glass in a manufactured food is considered as _______hazard.

choiceExplanations.Allergenic: Allergenic hazards come from allergens such as nuts or milk.

choiceExplanations.Biological: Biological hazards are microbes such as bacteria or viruses.

items.question: REFRIGERATION: The line from evaporator to compressor

choiceExplanations.Liquid Line: The liquid line carries liquid from the condenser to the expansion device.

choiceExplanations.Suction Line: Correct — The suction line carries low-pressure vapor from the evaporator to the compressor.
choiceExplanations.Hot Gas Line: The hot gas line carries hot vapor from the compressor, for example for defrost.

items.question: It is a ratio of total heat utilized by the fuel to the heat supplied to the burner.

choiceExplanations.Drying Efficiency: Correct — Drying efficiency is the heat used for drying divided by the heat supplied to the burner.
choiceExplanations.Burner Efficiency: Burner efficiency is how well the burner converts fuel to heat.
choiceExplanations.Thermal Efficiency: Thermal efficiency is a general ratio of output to input energy.
choiceExplanations.Heat Utilization Efficiency: Heat utilization efficiency is a related general term, not the keyed one.

items.question: The percentage equivalent of the ratio of the weight of water (WW) to the total weight of the material (Wt)

choiceExplanations.Equilibrium moisture content: Equilibrium moisture content is moisture in balance with the air.
choiceExplanations.Critical moisture content: Critical moisture content is where the drying rate changes.
choiceExplanations.Moisture content wet basis: Correct — Moisture content wet basis = weight of water / total weight of material x 100.
choiceExplanations.Moisture content dry basis: Moisture content dry basis uses the weight of dry matter, not total weight.

items.question: Moisture content of air remains constant so specific humidity is constant, temperature increases as it flows over a heating coil.

choiceExplanations.Sensible heat: Correct — Heating with constant moisture raises temperature only, which is sensible heat change.
choiceExplanations.Evaporative cooling: Evaporative cooling adds moisture to air.
choiceExplanations.Sensible cooling: Sensible cooling lowers temperature, not raises.
choiceExplanations.Latent heat: Latent heat involves moisture change, not constant humidity.

items.question: Moisture content of air remains constant so specific humidity is constant, but its temperature decreases as it flows over a cooling coil.

choiceExplanations.Evaporative cooling: Evaporative cooling adds moisture to air.
choiceExplanations.Adiabatic cooling: Adiabatic cooling is cooling by evaporation with no heat exchange.
choiceExplanations.Sensible heating: Sensible heating raises temperature, not lowers.
choiceExplanations.Sensible cooling: Correct — Cooling at constant specific humidity is sensible cooling.

items.question: An energy absorbed or released by a substance during a change in its physical state (phase) that occurs without changing its temperature.

choiceExplanations.Latent heat: Correct — Latent heat is energy absorbed or released during a phase change at constant temperature.
choiceExplanations.Radiant heat: Radiant heat is transferred by radiation.
choiceExplanations.Sensible heat: Sensible heat changes temperature, not phase.
choiceExplanations.Specific heat: Specific heat is the heat per degree per unit mass.

items.question: Water at 0.06 kg/s enters a boiler at 90°C (enthalpy 379.9 kJ/kg) and leaves as steam at 100°C (enthalpy 2,676 kJ/kg). What is the rate of heat transfer added in the boiler?
items.rationale: For a steady-flow boiler with no work, Q = m(h2 − h1) = 0.06 × (2,676 − 379.9) = 137.8 kW.

choiceExplanations.160.6 kW: Wrong — 160.6 kW uses only the exit enthalpy (0.06 × 2,676) and forgets to subtract the inlet enthalpy.
choiceExplanations.22.8 kW: Wrong — 22.8 kW is only the inlet enthalpy flow (0.06 × 379.9).
choiceExplanations.183.4 kW: Wrong — 183.4 kW adds the two enthalpies instead of taking their difference.

items.question: Air flowing at the rate of 2.5 kg/s is heated in a heat exchanger from -10°C to 30°C. What is the rate of heat transfer?

choiceExplanations.Q = 90kj/s or 90kw: 90 kW is below the computed value.
choiceExplanations.Q = 100kj/s or 100kw: Correct — Q = m cp dT = 2.5 kg/s x 1.0 kJ/kg-K x 40 K = 100 kW.
choiceExplanations.Q = 110kj/s or 110kw: 110 kW is above the computed value.
choiceExplanations.Q = 80kj/s or 80kw: 80 kW is below the computed value.

items.question: Water at the rate 68 kg/min is heated from 35°C to 75°C by an oil having a specific heat of 1.9 kJ/kg-°C. The fluids are used in counterflow double-pipe heat exchanger, and the refrigerant enters the heat exchanger at 110°C and leaves at 75°C. The overall heat-transfer coefficient is 320 W/m2 -°C. The total heat transfer, in kW, from the energy absorbed by the water is

choiceExplanations.152.4 kW: 152.4 kW does not match 1.133 kg/s x 4.187 x 40.
choiceExplanations.174.6 kW: 174.6 kW does not match the energy absorbed by the water.
choiceExplanations.189.8 kW: Correct — Q = m cp dT = (68/60) kg/s x 4.187 kJ/kg-C x 40 C = 189.8 kW absorbed by the water.
choiceExplanations.215.2 kW: 215.2 kW is higher than the energy absorbed by the water.

items.question: Air chamber under pressure usually converted to one or more distributing ducts in a drying or aeration system

items.question: instrument that measures relative humidity

items.question: Heat utilized over heat supplied

choiceExplanations.Heating efficiency: Heating efficiency is not the keyed term.

choiceExplanations.Burner efficiency: Burner efficiency compares heat from burner to fuel energy.
choiceExplanations.Combustion efficiency: Combustion efficiency is how completely the fuel burns.

items.question: an opening into a cooling or holding tank for maintaining atmospheric pressure during filing,emptying and cleaning.

choiceExplanations.Overflow pipe (Machinery): An overflow pipe removes excess liquid.

choiceExplanations.Manhole (Machinery): A manhole is an access opening for entry or cleaning.

choiceExplanations.Jensen Haise: Jensen-Haise estimates evapotranspiration from radiation and temperature.
choiceExplanations.Penman Monteith: Penman-Monteith estimates evapotranspiration from energy and aerodynamic terms.

items.question: The air requirement for gasification of agricultural waste ranged from
items.rationale: 30-40% of stoichiometric air / 10-20% for pyrolysis

choiceExplanations.50-60% of stoichiometric air: 50-60% of stoichiometric air is too much and leads to combustion.
choiceExplanations.80-90% of stoichiometric air: 80-90% would burn the fuel, making combustion instead of gasification.
choiceExplanations.30-40% of stoichiometric air: Correct — Gasification uses only 30-40% of the stoichiometric air, so fuel is partially oxidized into producer gas.
choiceExplanations.10-20% of stoichiometric air: 10-20% is too little air to keep gasification going.

items.question: When the dry bulb and wet bulb temp. are equal
items.answer: the air is 100% saturated with moisture, or has 100% relative humidity
choices: the air contains no water vapor, or has 0% relative humidity
the air is 100% saturated with moisture, or has 100% relative humidity
the air is partially saturated with moisture, or has 50% relative humidity
the air has reached its maximum enthalpy, or has zero latent heat

choiceExplanations.the air contains no water vapor, or has: At 0% relative humidity there is no vapor, and wet bulb would be lower than dry bulb.
choiceExplanations.the air is 100% saturated with moisture,: Correct — When wet and dry bulb are equal, no evaporation occurs because the air is saturated at 100% relative humidity.
choiceExplanations.the air is partially saturated with mois: At 50% relative humidity the wet bulb is lower than the dry bulb.
choiceExplanations.the air has reached its maximum enthalpy: Equal bulbs relate to saturation, not maximum enthalpy or zero latent heat.

items.question: Which one below is not a function of a lubricant?
items.rationale: Engine lubricants perform lubricating (friction/wear reduction), sealing (filling piston-ring clearances), cooling (heat transfer), and cleaning functions, so none of the listed functions is an exception.

choiceExplanations.None of the above: Correct — Sealing, lubricating and cooling are all lubricant functions, so none of the choices is the exception.
choiceExplanations.Sealing function: Sealing is a lubricant function, so it is not the exception.
choiceExplanations.Lubricating function: Lubricating is the main function, so it is not the exception.
choiceExplanations.Cooling function: Cooling is a lubricant function by carrying heat away.

items.question: continuous flow dryer wherein the product being dried moves in the same direction as drying air

Crossflow has air moving across the product path.
Counterflow has air moving opposite to the product.

items.question: In rubber for rice mill, the rubber shall have a minimum thickness

items.question: A vegetable processing plant uses a built-type slightly inclined conveyor having a conveying capacity of 10.28 kg per linear meter which moves at a speed of 0.63 m/s. Determine how many tonnes of vegetables can it convey for an 8-hour shift of work. Assume that the whole length of the conveyor is full when time recording starts.
items.rationale: 187 / Weight conveyed = conveying capacity x time x speed / = 10.28 kg/m x (8 hrs x 3,600 s/hr) x 0.63 m/s / = 186,52 kgs x 1 tonne/1,000 kg, converted to tonnes / = 186.52 tonnes

choiceExplanations.150: 150 tonnes is lower than the computed value.
choiceExplanations.168: 168 tonnes is lower than the computed value.
choiceExplanations.187: Correct — Rate = 10.28 kg/m x 0.63 m/s = 6.48 kg/s; over 8 h (28,800 s) this is about 187 tonnes.
choiceExplanations.206: 206 tonnes is higher than the computed value.

items.question: In a fruit processing plant, a 30-meter slightly inclined built-type conveyor carrying washed fruits has a conveying capacity of 10.28 kg per linear meter. At what speed the conveyor should move to convey a total of 186.52 tonnes of fruits in an 8-hour work shift? The whole length of the conveyor is full when time recording starts.
items.rationale: Length of fruit conveyed = 186,520 kg / 10.28 kg/m = 18,144 m. Speed = 18,144 m / (8 × 3,600 s) = 0.63 m/s.

choiceExplanations.0.63 m/s: Correct — Speed = weight conveyed / (capacity per meter x time) = 186,520 / (10.28 x 28,800) = 0.63 m/s.
choiceExplanations.0.84 m/s: 0.84 m/s would convey more than 186.52 tonnes.
choiceExplanations.1.26 m/s: 1.26 m/s would convey about twice the required amount.
choiceExplanations.0.42 m/s: 0.42 m/s would convey less than the required amount.

items.question: Give the appropriate standard to comply in setting limits for Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) of pesticide residues in rice?

choiceExplanations.PNS 193:2017: PNS 193:2017 is another food standard; it does not set pesticide residue limits for rice.
