items.question: It is the extra value created over and above the original value of a product as a result of subjecting the product to bioprocess engineering.

choiceExplanations.Gross profit: Gross profit is sales minus cost of goods; it is not the extra value created by processing.
choiceExplanations.Salvage value: Salvage value is the worth of an asset at the end of its life, not value gained from processing.
choiceExplanations.Value added: Correct — Value added is the extra value over the original value of a product created by bioprocess engineering or processing.
choiceExplanations.Market price: Market price is what buyers pay; it is not the extra value created by processing itself.

items.question: A value-added food product is a pre-processed or raw commodity whose value has been increased through the addition of _________ or processes that make it more attractive to the buyer and/or more readily usable by the consumer.

choiceExplanations.Ingredients: Correct — A value-added food product has its value increased by adding ingredients or by processes that make it more attractive or usable.
choiceExplanations.Stabilizers: Stabilizers are only one kind of additive; the general term used in the definition is ingredients.
choiceExplanations.Preservatives: Preservatives are one specific additive type, too narrow for the general definition of value-added.
choiceExplanations.Emulsifiers: Emulsifiers are one specific additive type, not the general word used in the definition.

items.question: You are estimating the energy consumption of a bioprocessing machine. If 3 kWh was recorded in reducing a processing material from 5 mm to 2 mm diameter, using Rittinger's law, how much energy is required if the same material is to be reduced from 5 mm to 0.5 mm diameter?

choiceExplanations.16 kWh: Too low. Rittinger's law gives 3 x (1/0.5 - 1/5)/(1/2 - 1/5) = 18 kWh, not 16.
choiceExplanations.14 kWh: Too low. Energy is proportional to (1/d2 - 1/d1); the ratio 1.8/0.3 = 6 gives 18 kWh, not 14.
choiceExplanations.18 kWh: Correct — Rittinger: E is proportional to (1/d2 - 1/d1). 5 to 2 mm gives 0.3 for 3 kWh; 5 to 0.5 mm gives 1.8, so 18 kWh.
choiceExplanations.20 kWh: Too high. The surface-area ratio 1.8/0.3 = 6 times 3 kWh equals 18 kWh, not 20.

items.question: You are designing an evaporative condenser type cooling tower. Hot water is to be cooled from 50 °C through the tower which has an expected efficiency of 65%. The temperature of the surrounding air is 30 °C dry bulb and 26.5 °C wet bulb. Determine the cold temperature of the water at the receptacle vat.

choiceExplanations.27.78 °C: Too low; that is close to the wet-bulb temperature, which cannot be reached at 65% efficiency.
choiceExplanations.34.73 °C: Correct — Tcold = Thot - eff x (Thot - Twb) = 50 - 0.65 x (50 - 26.5) = 34.73 °C.
choiceExplanations.31.95 °C: Does not follow from the formula; applying 65% efficiency to the 23.5 °C range gives 34.73 °C.
choiceExplanations.42.37 °C: Too high. It would imply only about 32% efficiency; 65% efficiency cools the water to 34.73 °C.

items.question: A grain or piece of a grain of milled rice with its length equal to or longer than three-fourths of the average length of the whole kernels.

choiceExplanations.Brown rice: Brown rice is unmilled rice with the bran layer still on; it is not defined by kernel length.
choiceExplanations.Head rice: Correct — Head rice is a whole or part grain of milled rice whose length is at least three-fourths of the average whole kernel length.
choiceExplanations.Brewers rice: Brewers rice is a very small broken fraction used for brewing, much shorter than head rice.

items.question: Compare Rittinger's law and Kick's law.
items.answer: Both concern the estimation of energy for crushing a material
choices: Both apply exclusively to fine grinding of brittle solids
Both concern the estimation of energy for crushing a material
Both state that crushing energy varies with particle mass
Both relate crushing energy directly to new surface area

choiceExplanations.Both apply exclusively to fine grinding: Wrong. They apply to coarse and intermediate crushing, not only fine grinding, and Kick's law suits coarse sizes.
choiceExplanations.Both concern the estimation of energy fo: Correct — Rittinger's and Kick's laws are both empirical rules for estimating the energy needed to crush a material.
choiceExplanations.Both state that crushing energy varies w: Wrong. Kick's law relates energy to the size reduction ratio and Rittinger's to new surface area, not mass.
choiceExplanations.Both relate crushing energy directly to: Wrong. Only Rittinger's law relates energy to new surface area; Kick's law relates it to the log of the size ratio.

items.question: Amount of energy required to effect the reduction in particle size of a solid is directly proportional to the increase in surface area. What law is this?

choiceExplanations.Bond's law: Bond's law says energy is proportional to the new crack length, between Rittinger's and Kick's; it is not directly about surface area.
choiceExplanations.Hukki's law: Hukki's law is a combined relation joining the three crushing laws over different size ranges.
choiceExplanations.Kick's law: Kick's law relates energy to the logarithm of the size reduction ratio, not to surface area.
choiceExplanations.Rittinger's law: Correct — Rittinger's law: crushing energy is directly proportional to the new surface area produced.

items.question: The _______ states that the energy required to crush a material is proportional to the logarithm of the ratio of the initial and final diameters of the material.

choiceExplanations.Bond's law: Bond's law relates energy to the square root of the size ratio, not the logarithm.
choiceExplanations.Kick's law: Correct — Kick's law: crushing energy is proportional to ln(d1/d2), the log of the initial to final diameter ratio.
choiceExplanations.Hukki's law: Hukki's law combines the three laws over size ranges; it is not the pure logarithmic rule.
choiceExplanations.Rittinger's law: Rittinger's law relates energy to new surface area (1/d2 - 1/d1), not the log of diameters.

items.question: The Kick's Law is a reasonable approximation for coarse grinding. It applies best to particles that are greater than ___ centimeters in size.

choiceExplanations.0.4: Not the limit. Kick's law is applied to coarse particles larger than 0.5 cm.
choiceExplanations.0.5: Correct — Kick's law is a reasonable approximation for coarse grinding of particles larger than about 0.5 cm.
choiceExplanations.0.7: Not the accepted limit; the stated threshold for coarse grinding is 0.5 cm.
choiceExplanations.0.6: Not the accepted limit; the stated threshold for coarse grinding is 0.5 cm.

items.question: What is the thermal conductivity range of tomato paste?

choiceExplanations.0.86–1.06 W m−1 K−1: Too high; this range is above that of tomato paste and approaches the value of pure water.
choiceExplanations.0.66–0.86 W m−1 K−1: Too high for tomato paste; its conductivity falls in the 0.46-0.66 W/m-K range.
choiceExplanations.0.26–0.46 W m−1 K−1: Too low for a water-rich food such as tomato paste; its conductivity is 0.46-0.66 W/m-K.

items.question: How can you reduce the specific heat of meat?

choiceExplanations.By blanching: Blanching heats food briefly in hot water; it does not lower specific heat.
choiceExplanations.By freezing: Correct — Freezing turns water into ice, which has a lower specific heat (about 2.1 kJ/kg-K) than liquid water, so the meat's specific heat drops.
choiceExplanations.By thawing: Thawing turns ice back into water, which raises specific heat, not lowers it.
choiceExplanations.By scalding: Scalding uses hot water or steam on the surface; it does not reduce specific heat.

items.question: How can you greatly reduce the specific heat of a liquid bioprocessing material?

choiceExplanations.By supercooling: Supercooling lowers temperature below freezing without freezing; the material stays liquid with high specific heat.
choiceExplanations.By condensing: Condensing turns vapor into liquid, which raises specific heat (water vapor 2.0 vs liquid 4.2 kJ/kg-K).
choiceExplanations.By vaporizing: Correct — Vaporizing converts liquid to vapor, which has a much lower specific heat (about 2.0 vs 4.18 kJ/kg-K for water).
choiceExplanations.By diluting: Diluting with water makes the material's specific heat closer to water's, so it increases rather than decreases.

items.question: If the specific heat capacity of water is 4.187 kJ/kgK, what is the specific heat capacity of ice?

choiceExplanations.2.108 kJ/kgK: Correct — The specific heat of ice is about 2.108 kJ/kg-K, roughly half that of liquid water.
choiceExplanations.2.740 kJ/kgK: Too high. Ice is about 2.108 kJ/kg-K, not 2.740.
choiceExplanations.2.277 kJ/kgK: Too high. Ice is about 2.108 kJ/kg-K, not 2.277.

items.question: If the specific heat capacity of ice is 2.108 kJ/kgK, what is the specific heat capacity of water vapor?

choiceExplanations.2.435 kJ/kgK: Too high. Water vapor's specific heat is about 1.996 kJ/kg-K, not 2.435.
choiceExplanations.1.996 kJ/kgK: Correct — Water vapor (steam) has a specific heat of about 1.996 kJ/kg-K.

items.question: Heat required to change a solid into a liquid or vapor, or a liquid into a vapor, without change in temperature.

choiceExplanations.Latent heat: Correct — Latent heat is the heat absorbed or released during a phase change (solid, liquid, vapor) at constant temperature.
choiceExplanations.Specific heat: Specific heat is heat needed to raise 1 kg by 1 degree; it involves a temperature change.
choiceExplanations.Sensible heat: Sensible heat changes temperature without a phase change, the opposite of this definition.
choiceExplanations.Radiant heat: Radiant heat is energy transferred by electromagnetic waves; it is not defined by phase change.

items.question: Heat released or absorbed when a solid is changing to liquid at atmospheric pressure and at its melting point.

choiceExplanations.Latent heat of sublimation: Latent heat of sublimation is for solid directly to vapor, not solid to liquid.
choiceExplanations.Latent heat of condensation: Latent heat of condensation is released when vapor becomes liquid.
choiceExplanations.Latent heat of fusion: Correct — Latent heat of fusion is the heat absorbed or released when a solid melts to liquid at its melting point.
choiceExplanations.Latent heat of vaporization: Latent heat of vaporization is for liquid to vapor at its boiling point.

items.question: Latent heat of fusion is the heat energy released or absorbed when a ____ changes to liquid at atmospheric pressure and at its melting point.

choiceExplanations.Solid: Correct — Latent heat of fusion is the heat absorbed or released when a solid changes to liquid at its melting point.
choiceExplanations.Vapor: Vapor changing to liquid involves latent heat of condensation, not fusion.
choiceExplanations.Plasma: Plasma is an ionized gas state and is not involved in fusion (melting).
choiceExplanations.Gas: Gas changing to liquid is condensation, not fusion.

items.question: Heat that must be supplied to a liquid in order to facilitate a phase change and for the conversion of the liquid into a solid.

choiceExplanations.Heat of sublimation: Heat of sublimation is for solid going directly to vapor.
choiceExplanations.Heat of solidification: Correct — Heat of solidification is the heat that must be removed from a liquid to change it to a solid, the reverse of fusion.
choiceExplanations.Heat of vaporization: Heat of vaporization is for liquid changing to vapor.
choiceExplanations.Heat of condensation: Heat of condensation is for vapor changing to liquid.

items.question: Find the cooling energy load of a 150 kg carabeef if it is to be frozen from 28°C to -20°C. The specific heats of carabeef above and below freezing are 3.5 kJ/kg-°C and 1.75 kJ/kg-°C, respectively. The freezing point is -2.2 °C and the specific latent heat of carabeef is 250 kJ/kg.

[28 - (-2.2)°C] + 150kg (250 kJ/kg) + 150kg (1.75 kJ/kg-°C) [-2.2 – (-20)°C] / Qt = 58,027.5 kJ

Notes: 58,027.5 kJ Total energy = Energy to cool + Energy to change phase + Energy to freeze Qt = m Ca (Te - Tf) + mL + m Cb (Tf - Ts) / where: / Qt = Energy total, kJ m = Mass, kg Ca = Specific heat above freezing, kJ/kg-0C Cb = Specific heat below freezing, kJ/kg-0C L = Specific latent heat of carabeef, kJ/kg Te = Temperature at entry Tf = Temperature at freezing Ts = Temperature at storage Qt = 150kg (3.5kJ/kg-°C)

choiceExplanations.53,355.0 kJ: Too low; the three terms sum to 58,027.5 kJ, not 53,355.

items.question: What is the opposite of latent heat of fusion?

choiceExplanations.Heat of solidification: Correct — Heat of solidification (freezing) is the reverse of heat of fusion: heat removed when liquid changes to solid.
choiceExplanations.Heat of condensation: Heat of condensation is the reverse of vaporization, not fusion.
choiceExplanations.Heat of sublimation: Heat of sublimation is solid to vapor; its reverse is deposition.
choiceExplanations.Heat of vaporization: Heat of vaporization is liquid to vapor, not the opposite of fusion.

items.question: Find the apparent air velocity in a 1,000-kg capacity flat-bed dryer with 2.5m x 2.9m dimension square bin. The specific airflow rate of the dryer is 50 m3 per minute of air per m3 of grain. The density of grain is 500kg/m3.

items.question: Hot air flows by natural or forced convection inside an oven while heat is distributed from the heating element through ________.

choiceExplanations.Evaporation: Evaporation is a phase change of water; it is not how the element distributes heat.

choiceExplanations.Conveyor: Correct — A vertical feed mixer uses a hopper, a vertical screw (auger) and a discharge chute; a conveyor is not one of its parts.

items.question: A feed mixer tested to have mixing coefficient of variation of 10-15% is rated as _____.

choiceExplanations.Fair: Fair is a poorer rating than the 10-15% band; it applies to higher coefficients of variation.
choiceExplanations.Good: Correct — A mixing coefficient of variation of 10-15% is rated Good; lower CV means more uniform mixing.
choiceExplanations.Excellent: Excellent is for a lower coefficient of variation than 10-15%.
choiceExplanations.Poor: Poor is for a much higher coefficient of variation than 10-15%.

items.question: As a standard, stripping efficiency of the mechanized stripping machine shall be at least

choiceExplanations.70%: Too low. The standard requires a stripping efficiency of at least 80%.

items.question: What is the percent moisture content in dry basis of a rice sample having 100 grams and 82 grams wet and dry weights?
items.rationale: 22 / MCdb = 100% x (Wet weight – Dry weight) / Dry weight / = 100% x (100 gm – 82 gm) / 82 gm / = 21.95%

choiceExplanations.22: Correct — MCdb = (100 - 82)/82 x 100 = 22% dry basis, using dry weight as the divisor.
choiceExplanations.20: Wrong calculation; 18 g of water over 82 g dry matter is 22%, not 20%.
choiceExplanations.18: 18 is the wet basis value (18/100); the question asks for dry basis, which is 22%.

items.question: What is the percent moisture content in wet basis of a corn sample having 100 grams and 82 grams wet and dry weights?

items.question: A dried palay sample was milled using a rubber roller laboratory rice mill. After milling, the weight of whole milled grains, broken milled grains, and hull were 25 g, 305 g and 170 g, respectively. The milled rice was classified as Class A. Determine the percent head rice.

choiceExplanations.Apron conveyor: An apron conveyor is a conveying machine, not a head rice formula.

items.question: A 21-tonne capacity coconut oil expeller was loaded full with grated copra. It produced 9,000 kg of crude oil in 12 hours. What is the copra cake production rate of the machine at 97% cake collection efficiency?

choiceExplanations.1067 kg/h Pcake=: Too high; this would be about 100% of the cake without the efficiency loss.
choiceExplanations.873 kg/h Pcake=: Too low; 12,000 kg x 0.97 / 12 h is 970 kg/h, not 873.

items.question: What device allows for controlled and efficient heating using steam while sterilizing a product without adversely changing its quality, typically functioning as a closed system except for steam injection?

choiceExplanations.Cooling Tower: A cooling tower removes heat from water by evaporation; it does not heat or sterilize with steam.
choiceExplanations.Vacuum Evaporator: A vacuum evaporator removes water from liquids under reduced pressure to concentrate them, not for sterilizing.
choiceExplanations.Spray Dryer: A spray dryer turns liquid into powder with hot air, not a steam-heating sterilizer.
choiceExplanations.Heat Exchanger: Correct — A heat exchanger transfers heat from steam to the product for controlled heating and sterilizing without changing quality.

items.question: Acid foods have pH range below ___.

choiceExplanations.4.0: Too low; the limit between acid and low acid foods is pH 4.6.
choiceExplanations.4.6: Correct — Foods with pH below 4.6 are classed as acid foods; above that they are low acid.

choiceExplanations.5.1 to 7.7: Range does not match the standard 4.6 to 7.0.
choiceExplanations.4.1 to 6.3: Range does not match the standard 4.6 to 7.0.

items.question: What is the name of the potent toxin produced by the bacterium that forms spores?

choiceExplanations.Choleragen: Choleragen is the toxin of Vibrio cholerae, which does not form spores.
choiceExplanations.Botulin: Correct — Botulin (botulinum toxin) is produced by Clostridium botulinum, a spore-forming bacterium, and is highly potent.
choiceExplanations.Aflatoxin: Aflatoxin is produced by Aspergillus molds, not by spore-forming bacteria.
choiceExplanations.Shigatoxin: Shiga toxin is produced by Shigella and some E. coli, which do not form spores.

items.question: It is the process if reducing and maintaining the temperature of the space or material below the temperature of the surrounding.

choiceExplanations.Refrigeration: Correct — Refrigeration is reducing and maintaining the temperature of a space or material below its surroundings.
choiceExplanations.Pasteurization: Pasteurization is mild heat treatment to kill microbes, not cooling.
choiceExplanations.Ventilation: Ventilation is moving air in or out of a space, not lowering temperature below ambient.
choiceExplanations.Dehumidification: Dehumidification removes moisture from air; it is not defined by cooling below surroundings.

items.question: The separation of solids from suspension in liquid by gravity alone is called as

choiceExplanations.Flocculation: Flocculation clumps fine particles together using chemicals; it is not settling by gravity alone.
choiceExplanations.Centrifugation: Centrifugation uses spinning force, not gravity alone.
choiceExplanations.Sedimentation: Correct — Sedimentation separates solids from a liquid suspension using gravity alone.
choiceExplanations.Filtration: Filtration uses a porous medium to hold back solids, not gravity settling.

items.question: What is the value of Nusselt number in conduction from a sphere droplet to the surrounding fluid film?

choiceExplanations.4: Not the value; Nusselt number for conduction to a sphere in a still fluid is 2.
choiceExplanations.3: Not the value; Nu = 2 for a sphere in a stagnant fluid.
choiceExplanations.1: Not the value; Nu = 2 for a sphere in a stagnant fluid.
choiceExplanations.2: Correct — For pure conduction from a sphere to a stagnant surrounding fluid, the Nusselt number is 2.

items.question: Which of the following is employed to measure pressure in ammonia reactor?

choiceExplanations.Bellows gage: A bellows gage measures low to moderate pressure with an elastic bellows, not the usual choice for high-pressure ammonia reactors.
choiceExplanations.McLeod gage: A McLeod gage measures very low vacuum pressures, not reactor pressure.
choiceExplanations.Diaphragm gage: A diaphragm gage measures low pressures with a flexible diaphragm, not the typical choice for high pressures.
choiceExplanations.Bourdon gage: Correct — A Bourdon gage uses a curved tube to measure medium to high pressures and suits ammonia reactors.

items.question: The work required for crushing material is proportional to the natural logarithm of the ratio between initial and final diameters. This is the _______ statement.

choiceExplanations.Kick’s Law: Correct — Kick's law: work of crushing is proportional to ln(d1/d2).
choiceExplanations.Hukki’s Law: Hukki's law combines Kick's, Bond's and Rittinger's laws over size ranges.
choiceExplanations.Bond’s Law: Bond's law relates energy to the square root of the size ratio, not the logarithm.
choiceExplanations.Rittinger’s Law: Rittinger's law relates energy to new surface area, not the logarithm.

items.question: A refrigeration system function on a reversed Carnot cycle. The minimum and maximum temperature are -30 °C and 75 °C, respectively. If the system rejects 6500 kJ/min at the condenser, determine the power input required.

choiceExplanations.1961.2 kJ/min: Correct — COP = TL/(TH - TL) = 243/105; heat rejected = W(1 + COP), so W = 6500/3.314 = 1961.2 kJ/min.
choiceExplanations.2392.7 kJ/min: Too high; the work equals the rejected heat divided by (1 + COP), which gives 1961.2.
choiceExplanations.2549.6 kJ/min: Too high; dividing 6500 by 3.314 gives 1961.2 kJ/min.

items.question: A certain refrigeration system function on a reversed Carnot cycle. The minimum and maximum temperature are -30°C and 75°C, respectively. If the system rejects 6500 kJ/min at the condenser, find the tons of refrigeration developed.

choiceExplanations.19.36 TR: Too low. Refrigerating effect = 6500 - 1961.2 = 4538.8 kJ/min = 21.51 TR.
choiceExplanations.23.66 TR: Too high. 4538.8 kJ/min / 211 kJ/min per TR is 21.51 TR.
choiceExplanations.21.51 TR: Correct — Refrigerating effect = 6500 - 1961.2 = 4538.8 kJ/min; divided by 211 kJ/min per TR gives 21.51 TR.

choiceExplanations.1.073 W/m2K: Wrong — 1.073 does not satisfy the overall-coefficient equation based on the inside area.

items.question: A refrigerant is a working fluid used in cooling, heating or _____ of air conditioning systems and heat pumps where they undergo a repeated phase transition from a liquid to a gas and back again.

choiceExplanations.Reverse cooling and heating: Correct — A refrigerant serves in cooling, heating or reverse cooling and heating of air conditioning systems and heat pumps.
choiceExplanations.Forced air heating and exhaust: Forced air heating and exhaust describes air handling, not a refrigerant's function in cycles.
choiceExplanations.Direct expansion and drying: Direct expansion and drying are not the heat pump functions listed in the definition.
choiceExplanations.Thermal storage and recovery: Thermal storage and recovery are not the usual functions named in this definition.

items.question: In refrigeration, what is the most promising refrigerant in terms of environment friendliness?

choiceExplanations.CF2Cl2 (R12): R-12 (CF2Cl2) is a CFC that depletes the ozone layer, so it is not environmentally friendly.
choiceExplanations.C3H8 (R290): R-290 (propane) has low global warming potential but is flammable; CO2 is considered more promising here.
choiceExplanations.CO2 (R744): Correct — CO2 (R744) has zero ozone depletion and a global warming potential of 1, making it the most environment-friendly choice.
choiceExplanations.NH3 (R717): NH3 (R717) has zero ODP and GWP but is toxic and flammable, so it is not the most promising.

items.question: Water force of 981 kN is exerted against a 1-meter central section of a diversion dam weighing 9,810 kN. Height of water from the dam base is 30 meters. Applying mechanics, what is the total moment at the base of the dam where the line of gravity passes? Neglect uplift force due to seepage.

choiceExplanations.9,810 kN: Correct — Overturning moment = water force x lever arm = 981 kN x (30/3) m = 9,810 (kN-m); the water force acts at one-third of the depth.
choiceExplanations.11,968 kN: Does not match the moment of the 981 kN water force acting at one-third of the 30 m height.
choiceExplanations.8,633 kN: Does not match the moment of the 981 kN water force acting at one-third of the 30 m height.
choiceExplanations.12,753 kN: Does not match the moment of the 981 kN water force acting at one-third of the 30 m height.

items.question: What rice dryer will you use for a rice processing center having a capacity of 15 tonnes paddy rice per hour? It is operating whole year round during both sunny and rainy days and all levels of relative humidity.

choiceExplanations.Recirculating dryer: Correct — A recirculating dryer handles large capacity (15 t/h) and works all year in any weather.
choiceExplanations.Flatbed dryer: A flatbed dryer suits small batches and is not suited to 15 t/h continuous capacity.
choiceExplanations.Solar tunnel dryer: A solar tunnel dryer depends on sunshine and cannot work on rainy days.
choiceExplanations.Fluidized bed dryer: A fluidized bed dryer is for small granular or powder materials, not 15 t/h paddy.

items.question: For a good structural design, the following criteria in gravity dam design are followed, except ___________.
items.answer: Factor of safety against dam break is 2 or more
items.rationale: Gravity dam stability checks require the resultant force to fall within the middle third of the base and minimum factors of safety against overturning and sliding; there is no structural criterion called "factor of safety against dam break."
choices: Factor of safety against overturning is 2 or more
Center of gravity acts within the middle third of the base
Factor of safety against dam break is 2 or more
Factor of safety against sliding is 2 or more

choiceExplanations.Factor of safety against overturning is: This is a real criterion; overturning needs a factor of safety of 2 or more.
choiceExplanations.Center of gravity acts within the middle: This is a real criterion; the resultant should lie in the middle third of the base to avoid tension.
choiceExplanations.Factor of safety against dam break is 2: Correct — Dam break is not a design factor-of-safety criterion; the checks are overturning, sliding and stresses.
choiceExplanations.Factor of safety against sliding is 2 or: This is a genuine gravity dam design check against sliding, so it is not the exception.

items.question: The most crucial design criterion in gravity dam design.
items.answer: Center of gravity acts within the middle third of the base
choices: Factor of safety against sliding is 1.5 or more
Center of gravity acts within the middle third of the base
Factor of safety against overturning is 2 or more
Maximum compressive stress stays within safe limits

choiceExplanations.Factor of safety against sliding is 1.5: Sliding safety factor is an important check but not the most crucial criterion.
choiceExplanations.Center of gravity acts within the middle: Correct — The resultant must pass within the middle third of the base so there is no tension and no overturning.
choiceExplanations.Factor of safety against overturning is: Overturning safety is important, but it is covered by the middle-third rule.
choiceExplanations.Maximum compressive stress stays within: Stress limits are important but not the single most crucial criterion.

items.question: The name given to a set of codes for a commonly used microcontroller program which serve as instructions to the microcontroller.

items.question: Data transmission to a remote and line-of-sight point in an unelectrified place is best done through ___.

choiceExplanations.Optical fiber: Optical fiber needs a physical cable, not suitable for a remote line-of-sight point.
choiceExplanations.Infrared signal: Infrared signals work over short ranges and are blocked by sunlight and objects.

choiceExplanations.Ultrasonic wave: Ultrasonic waves have short range and are affected by air conditions; they are not suited to long distances.

items.question: In automatic control of irrigation dam gates, what switch is useful in the instrumentation?

choiceExplanations.Manual transfer switch (MTS): A manual transfer switch needs a person to operate, so it does not allow automatic control.

choices: Less bulk density of milled rice

choiceExplanations.Less bulk density of milled rice: Correct — Parboiling does not reduce the bulk density of milled rice; it makes the grain denser and harder, so this statement is the untrue one.
choiceExplanations.Sterilization of grain: True of parboiling: the heat treatment helps sterilize the grain.
choiceExplanations.Increase in milling recovery: True of parboiling: it raises milling recovery by reducing breakage.
choiceExplanations.Food value increase: True of parboiling: nutrients move into the endosperm, raising food value.

items.question: It shall consist of the excavation and disposal of all materials regardless of its nature, not classified and included in the Bill of / Quantities under other pay items.

choiceExplanations.Structure Excavation: Structure excavation is for foundations of structures and is paid under its own item.
choiceExplanations.Common Excavation: Common excavation covers ordinary soil and is a separate pay item.
choiceExplanations.Rock Excavation: Rock excavation covers hard rock and is paid under its own item.
choiceExplanations.Unclassified Excavation: Correct — Unclassified excavation covers all materials regardless of nature that are not in other pay items.

items.question: The angle of road intersection, if possible, shall be at right angles (90 degrees). However, intersecting angles in the range of _____ are acceptable. Intersections at angles of _____ may be used in special situations, while intersections at angles of less than _____ are strongly discouraged.
items.rationale: Under PAES 421:2009 (Farm-to-Market Roads), intersections should ideally be 90°, angles of 45–60° are acceptable (including in special situations), and angles below 45° are strongly discouraged for safety and visibility reasons.

choiceExplanations.50–75 degrees; 40–50 degrees; 40 degrees: Not the specified angles; the acceptable range is 45-60 degrees, with less than 45 degrees strongly discouraged.
choiceExplanations.45–60 degrees; 45–60 degrees; 45 degrees: Correct — Angles of 45-60 degrees are acceptable, and intersections under 45 degrees are strongly discouraged.
choiceExplanations.30–60 degrees; 30–45 degrees; 30 degrees: Does not match the specified ranges.
choiceExplanations.60–90 degrees; 30–45 degrees; 30 degrees: Does not match the specified ranges.

items.question: Unit for luminous discharge

choiceExplanations.Ionization: Ionization is the formation of ions, not a unit of luminous discharge.
choiceExplanations.Arcing: Arcing is a continuous electrical spark, not a luminous discharge in air.
choiceExplanations.Flashover: Flashover is a sudden full breakdown across an insulator, not a luminous glow.
choiceExplanations.Corona: Correct — Corona is the luminous discharge from ionized air around a high-voltage conductor.

items.question: It is the refrigerant suitable for large industrial low-temperature installations.

choiceExplanations.Ammonia: Correct — Ammonia is the refrigerant used in large industrial low-temperature installations because of its high efficiency.
choiceExplanations.Ethane: Ethane is a flammable hydrocarbon used only in some very low temperature systems.
choiceExplanations.Isobutane: Isobutane is mainly used in small domestic refrigerators.
choiceExplanations.Propane: Propane is a flammable hydrocarbon used in small systems; ammonia is the standard for large industrial plants.

items.question: correct drying process?

choiceExplanations.Heating → evaporation → tempering → cool: Correct — Drying heats the grain, moisture evaporates, the grain is tempered to let moisture move to the surface, then cooled.
choiceExplanations.Tempering → heating → evaporation → cool: Tempering comes after evaporation, not before heating.
choiceExplanations.Evaporation → heating → cooling → temper: Heating must come first; evaporation cannot start before the grain is heated.
choiceExplanations.Heating → tempering → evaporation → cool: Tempering follows evaporation to equalize moisture; it is not done before evaporation.

items.question: Unit for susceptance (S)

choiceExplanations.Henry: Henry is the unit of inductance.
choiceExplanations.Ohm: Ohm is the unit of resistance, not susceptance.
choiceExplanations.Siemens: Correct — Susceptance is measured in siemens (S), the reciprocal of reactance.
choiceExplanations.Farad: Farad is the unit of capacitance.

items.question: Unit for conductance (G)

choiceExplanations.Coulomb: Coulomb is the unit of electric charge.
choiceExplanations.Ohm: Ohm is the unit of resistance, the inverse of conductance.
choiceExplanations.Siemens: Correct — Conductance (G) is measured in siemens (S), the inverse of resistance.
choiceExplanations.Weber: Weber is the unit of magnetic flux.

items.question: Feed materials are mixed purposely to:
items.answer: Obtain homogeneous feed to ensure that animals are given the same proportions of nutrients
choices: Eliminate moisture content from raw ingredients to prevent mold growth during prolonged warehouse storage
Increase bulk density of raw rations to maximize hopper capacity during pneumatic bin conveying
Obtain homogeneous feed to ensure that animals are given the same proportions of nutrients
Reduce particle size of grains to improve digestibility and feed conversion efficiency in livestock

choiceExplanations.Eliminate moisture content from raw ingr: Eliminating moisture is drying, not mixing.
choiceExplanations.Increase bulk density of raw rations to: Mixing does not increase bulk density for hopper capacity.
choiceExplanations.Obtain homogeneous feed to ensure that a: Correct — Mixing makes feed uniform so every animal gets the same nutrient proportions.
choiceExplanations.Reduce particle size of grains to improv: Reducing particle size is grinding, not mixing.

items.question: Which is not a good ethic of an engineer?
items.answer: He will supplant another engineer in particular employment after becoming aware that definite steps have been taken toward the other's employment.
items.rationale: Under the Code of Ethics for Agricultural and Biosystems Engineers, an engineer must not attempt to supplant another engineer in particular employment after becoming aware that definite steps have been taken toward the latter's employment.
choices: He will not use the advantage of a salaried position to compete with engineers who do not conform to ethical practices.
He will practice due restraint in criticizing another engineer's work in public.
If he considers that an engineer is guilty of unethical, illegal, or unfair practice, he will present the information to the proper authority for action.
He will supplant another engineer in particular employment after becoming aware that definite steps have been taken toward the other's employment.

choiceExplanations.He will not use the advantage of a salar: This is an ethical practice: engineers must not use a salaried position to compete unfairly.
choiceExplanations.He will practice due restraint in critic: This is an ethical practice: restraint in criticizing a colleague's work.
choiceExplanations.If he considers that an engineer is guil: This is an ethical practice: unethical practice is reported to proper authority.
choiceExplanations.He will supplant another engineer in par: Correct — Supplanting another engineer once definite steps toward his employment have been taken is unethical.

items.question: Swine housing should have sufficient warmth. Yet, hogs must also be protected from excessive heat. What is the effect of extreme temperature to swine?

choiceExplanations.Faster muscle growth: Heat stress does not speed muscle growth; it lowers it.
choiceExplanations.Slower weight gain: Correct — Extreme heat or cold makes pigs divert energy to cope, resulting in slower weight gain.
choiceExplanations.Increased milk yield: Milk yield is not a swine growth outcome of extreme temperature.
choiceExplanations.Higher feed intake: Hogs eat less in extreme heat, not more.

items.question: In a building, which may be a source of latent heat?

choiceExplanations.Temperature difference: Temperature difference creates sensible heat, not latent heat.
choiceExplanations.Moisture difference: Correct — Latent heat in a building comes from moisture (water vapor) differences, such as people breathing and wet processes.
choiceExplanations.Wall conduction: Wall conduction is a sensible heat gain.
choiceExplanations.Solar radiation: Solar radiation is a sensible heat source.

items.question: For oil seeds, which is the most suited handling method?

choiceExplanations.Screw conveyor: Correct — A screw conveyor handles oilseeds well since it is enclosed and handles sticky or oily material.
choiceExplanations.Pneumatic conveyor: Pneumatic conveyors can crush oily seeds and are less suited.
choiceExplanations.Bucket elevator: A bucket elevator is for vertical lifting, not general handling of oilseeds.
choiceExplanations.Belt conveyor: Belt conveyors can spill oilseeds on inclines.

items.question: Grains, a hygroscopic material, will gain moisture when vapor pressure of the ___(X)___ is greater than the vapor pressure of the ___(Y)___.

choiceExplanations.X = air; Y = grain: Correct — A hygroscopic grain absorbs moisture when the vapor pressure of the surrounding air is greater than that of the grain.
choiceExplanations.X = dryer; Y = grain: A dryer is a machine, not the humid-air source in this vapor pressure comparison.
choiceExplanations.X = grain; Y = air: This reverses the rule; grain loses moisture when its vapor pressure is higher than air.
choiceExplanations.X = kernel; Y = hull: A kernel and hull belong to the same grain and are not an air-grain comparison.

items.question: The difference in pressure between any two points in a homogeneous fluid at rest is equal to the product of the ___(X)___ of the fluid to the ___(Y)___ distance between the points.

choiceExplanations.X = unit weight; Y = vertical: Correct — Pressure difference equals unit weight of fluid times the vertical distance between the points (P = gamma x h).
choiceExplanations.X = specific gravity; Y = vertical: Specific gravity is a ratio and does not directly give pressure difference.
choiceExplanations.X = mass density; Y = horizontal: Mass density times horizontal distance does not give a pressure difference.
choiceExplanations.X = unit weight; Y = horizontal: Horizontal distance does not change pressure in a fluid at rest.

items.question: When a substance undergoes allotropic transformation, it changes phases from:

choiceExplanations.Solid directly to gas: Solid directly to gas is sublimation.
choiceExplanations.Solid directly to liquid: Solid directly to liquid is melting.
choiceExplanations.Liquid directly to solid: Liquid directly to solid is freezing.
choiceExplanations.Solid to another solid: Correct — An allotropic transformation is a change from one solid crystal form to another solid form.

items.question: It is the point when additional heat transfer (or reduction) results in a change of phase.

choiceExplanations.Equilibrium: Equilibrium means balance of properties, not the onset of phase change.
choiceExplanations.Saturation: Correct — Saturation is the state where any heat added or removed starts a phase change.
choiceExplanations.Superheat: Superheat is temperature above saturation of a vapor.
choiceExplanations.Subcooling: Subcooling is a liquid cooled below its saturation temperature.

items.question: The elements of a heat engine are: working substance, hot body, heat sink, and engine. Which element is the source of heat?

choiceExplanations.Heat sink: Heat sink is where heat is rejected.
choiceExplanations.Engine: Engine is the device that converts heat to work.
choiceExplanations.Working substance: Working substance is the fluid that carries energy through the cycle.
choiceExplanations.Hot body: Correct — The hot body (source) supplies heat to the working substance of a heat engine.

items.question: The process of mixing two or more different products together, such as grains and supplements, to obtain desired food ratios, or the process of mixing different quantities of the same product with different size of kernels to obtain the desired quality grade is called

choiceExplanations.Tempering: Tempering is holding grain to equalize moisture.
choiceExplanations.Pelleting: Pelleting is compressing feed into pellets.
choiceExplanations.Conditioning: Conditioning is treating material with steam or moisture before pelleting or milling.
choiceExplanations.Blending: Correct — Blending is mixing different products or lots of different kernel sizes to get the desired ratio or grade.

items.question: Materials that are quite brittle but are used for machine parts like engine blocks.

choiceExplanations.Carbon steel: Carbon steel is tough and ductile, not brittle.
choiceExplanations.Cast iron: Correct — Cast iron is hard and brittle but strong in compression and good for casting engine blocks.
choiceExplanations.Wrought iron: Wrought iron is tough and ductile, not brittle.
choiceExplanations.Stainless steel: Stainless steel is corrosion-resistant and tough, not brittle.

items.question: Part of total solids remaining after volatile gases driven off at 600C.

choiceExplanations.Fixed solids: Correct — Fixed solids are the portion that remains as ash after volatile solids burn off at about 550-600 °C.
choiceExplanations.Suspended solids: Suspended solids are particles carried in the water, not defined by burning.
choiceExplanations.Volatile solids: Volatile solids are the portion that is burned off, not the remainder.
choiceExplanations.Dissolved solids: Dissolved solids are those passing through a filter, not defined by burning.

items.question: In construction sites, shops and other work places, which should come first?

choiceExplanations.Efficiency: Efficiency matters but safety comes before it.
choiceExplanations.Quality: Quality matters but safety comes before it.
choiceExplanations.Productivity: Productivity matters but safety comes before it.
choiceExplanations.Safety: Correct — Safety comes first in any work place to protect lives.

items.question: It is an electrically-controlled switch for regulating the flow of liquid or of gas

choiceExplanations.Float valve: A float valve controls liquid level by a float, not electrically.
choiceExplanations.Butterfly valve: A butterfly valve is a rotating disc valve, usually manual.
choiceExplanations.Solinoid valve: Correct — A solenoid valve is an electrically controlled valve for liquid or gas flow.
choiceExplanations.Relief valve: A relief valve opens automatically at a set pressure for safety, not electrically controlled.

items.question: Artificial method of seasoning wood include;
items.answer: Radio frequency dielectric drying, forced air drying, kiln drying
choices: Solar air drying, cold water soaking, shade curing
Radio frequency dielectric drying, forced air drying, kiln drying
Air drying, water seasoning, open shed drying
Natural air seasoning, river immersion, pressure creosoting

choiceExplanations.Solar air drying, cold water soaking, sh: These are natural or low-technology methods, not artificial seasoning.
choiceExplanations.Radio frequency dielectric drying, force: Correct — Artificial seasoning includes radio frequency dielectric drying, forced air drying and kiln drying.
choiceExplanations.Air drying, water seasoning, open shed d: Air drying and open shed drying are natural methods.
choiceExplanations.Natural air seasoning, river immersion,: Natural seasoning, river immersion and creosoting are not artificial drying methods.

items.question: What is a physical factor related to the evaporative potential of air and which causes a product to shrivel called?

choiceExplanations.Water loss: Correct — Evaporative potential of air (low humidity) draws moisture from produce, causing water loss and shriveling.
choiceExplanations.Vapor pressure: Vapor pressure is a property of air or water, not the physical loss that shrivels.
choiceExplanations.Chilling injury: Chilling injury is damage from low temperature, not dryness.
choiceExplanations.Respiration rate: Respiration rate is the metabolic rate of produce, not shriveling.

items.question: A republic act providing for the development and promotion of organic agriculture in the Philippines.

choiceExplanations.RA13088: RA 13088 is a different law, not the Organic Agriculture Act.
choiceExplanations.RA11578: RA 11578 is a different law, not the Organic Agriculture Act.
choiceExplanations.RA8054: RA 8054 is a different law, not the Organic Agriculture Act.
choiceExplanations.RA10068: Correct — RA 10068 is the Organic Agriculture Act of 2010.

items.question: They are machines with rotating knives that are used to straighten and smoothen edges of boards.

choiceExplanations.Routers: A router cuts grooves and profiles with a spinning bit.
choiceExplanations.Jointers: Correct — A jointer has rotating knives that straighten and smooth board edges.
choiceExplanations.Shapers: A shaper cuts decorative profiles on edges.
choiceExplanations.Planers: A planer smooths faces to uniform thickness, not mainly edges.

items.question: An item commonly referred to as convenient outlet

choiceExplanations.Receptacle: Correct — A receptacle is the convenient outlet where plugs are connected.
choiceExplanations.Connector: A connector joins wires or cables, not the outlet.
choiceExplanations.Switch: A switch opens or closes a circuit.
choiceExplanations.Plug: A plug fits into the outlet, but it is not the outlet.

items.question: The angle measured from the horizontal at which product will start to move downwards over a smooth surface with gravity discharging the product is called

choiceExplanations.Angle of repose: Angle of repose is the slope of a pile of material.
choiceExplanations.Angle of shear: Angle of shear refers to the failure plane in shear.
choiceExplanations.Angle of friction: Correct — The angle of friction is the angle from horizontal at which product begins to slide down a smooth surface.
choiceExplanations.Angle of inclination: Angle of inclination is a general term, not the specific property.

items.question: It is the soluble form of nitrogen and is easily leached beyond the root zone of plants. The principal sources of this form of nitrogen from agricultural activities are animal waste and commercial fertilizer.

choiceExplanations.Ammonium: Ammonium is the positive ion that binds to soil and is less easily leached.
choiceExplanations.Nitrate: Correct — Nitrate is the soluble form of nitrogen that is easily leached beyond the root zone.
choiceExplanations.Nitrite: Nitrite is an unstable intermediate and usually does not accumulate.
choiceExplanations.Ammonia: Ammonia is a gas or its dissolved form, and it is not the leached form.

items.question: It is the meat obtained from hogs

choiceExplanations.Pork: Correct — Pork is meat from hogs.

items.question: Ground beef can be stored at -18°C within a period of

choiceExplanations.2 to 3 months: Shorter than the recommended period of 3 to 4 months.
choiceExplanations.4 to 5 months: Longer than the recommended 3 to 4 months.
choiceExplanations.4 to 6 months: Longer than the recommended 3 to 4 months.
choiceExplanations.3 to 4 months: Correct — Ground beef keeps good quality for 3 to 4 months at -18 °C.

items.question: A type of switch having contacts that is operated by magnetism.

choiceExplanations.Transistors: Transistors are semiconductor switches with no moving contacts.
choiceExplanations.Breakers: Breakers protect circuits by tripping on overload.
choiceExplanations.Relays: Correct — A relay is a switch whose contacts are operated by an electromagnet.
choiceExplanations.Thyristors: Thyristors are semiconductor switches without contacts.

items.question: It refers to a ferrous metal that is malleable, corrosion resistant, and is relatively tough. Often used for decorative material.

choiceExplanations.Wrought iron: Correct — Wrought iron is malleable, corrosion resistant and tough, and is used for decorative work.
choiceExplanations.Cast iron: Cast iron is brittle, not malleable.
choiceExplanations.Pig iron: Pig iron is crude brittle iron that needs refining.
choiceExplanations.Mild steel: Mild steel is not as corrosion resistant.

items.question: Lumber defects as separation from the lengthwise grain. It occurs due to too rapid and uneven drying.

choiceExplanations.Knot: A knot is the base of a branch in the wood.
choiceExplanations.Check: Correct — A check is a lengthwise grain separation caused by rapid, uneven drying.
choiceExplanations.Shake: A shake is a separation between growth rings, not caused by drying.
choiceExplanations.Wane: Wane is bark or missing wood at the edge.

items.question: Clamps, pliers are all examples of _______.

choiceExplanations.Driving tools: Driving tools such as hammers and screwdrivers force fasteners.
choiceExplanations.Holding tools: Correct — Clamps and pliers hold work or objects, so they are holding tools.
choiceExplanations.Cutting tools: Cutting tools like saws and chisels remove material.
choiceExplanations.Measuring tools: Measuring tools like rulers and calipers measure size.

items.question: It is a method of freezing the surface of poultry meat using mist of liquid prior to storage in an air blast freezer or cold storage room

choiceExplanations.Fluidized bed freezing: Fluidized bed freezing suspends food in cold air; it is not a mist.
choiceExplanations.Air blast freezing: Air blast freezing uses cold air only, not a liquid mist.
choiceExplanations.Plate contact freezing: Plate contact freezing uses cold plates.
choiceExplanations.Liquid spray freezing: Correct — Liquid spray freezing freezes the surface of poultry using a liquid mist before air blast freezer storage.

items.question: It represents the portion of light which reaches the work area

choiceExplanations.Mounting height: Mounting height is the distance of luminaires above the work plane.
choiceExplanations.Spacing ratio: Spacing ratio is the spacing between luminaires relative to mounting height.
choiceExplanations.Maintenance factor: Maintenance factor accounts for light loss due to dirt and lamp aging.
choiceExplanations.Cavity ratio: Correct — The cavity ratio is the keyed term for the portion of light reaching the work area.

items.question: Pipe with higher schedule:

choiceExplanations.Thinner: A lower schedule has thinner walls.
choiceExplanations.Thicker: Correct — A higher pipe schedule number means thicker walls, which handle higher pressure.
choiceExplanations.Lighter: Schedule does not make a pipe lighter.
choiceExplanations.Wider: Schedule describes wall thickness, not the pipe's width.

items.question: On what plane is the Mollier diagram plotted?

choiceExplanations.P-v: P-v diagram is a pressure-volume plot.
choiceExplanations.P-h: P-h is the pressure-enthalpy diagram used in refrigeration.
choiceExplanations.H-s: Correct — The Mollier diagram plots enthalpy against entropy (h-s).

items.question: This thermostat makes use of two unlike metals that do not expand in the same amount.

choiceExplanations.Bellows thermostat: A bellows thermostat uses a gas-filled bellows.
choiceExplanations.Bimetallic thermostat: Correct — A bimetallic thermostat uses two metals with different expansion rates to bend and switch.
choiceExplanations.Capillary thermostat: A capillary thermostat uses a liquid-filled tube.

items.question: The unit used when specifying the intensity of light needed for various seeing task

choiceExplanations.Lumen-hours: Lumen-hours is not a unit of illumination intensity.
choiceExplanations.Candelas: Candelas measure luminous intensity of a source.
choiceExplanations.Foot-candles: Correct — Foot-candles measure illuminance, which sets the light level for seeing tasks.
choiceExplanations.Foot-lamberts: Foot-lamberts measure luminance of a surface.

items.question: The sacks for milled rice are usually labeled with the following information, except:
items.rationale: Milled rice sack labeling standards require product type, grade, milling degree, date of milling, net weight, and name/address of the miller, whereas storage measures are not required on the sack label.

choiceExplanations.Name and address of miller: Name and address of the miller are shown on sacks.
choiceExplanations.Date of milling: Date of milling is shown on sacks.
choiceExplanations.Storage measures: Correct — Storage measures are not labeled on rice sacks.
choiceExplanations.Type, grade, and milling degree: Type, grade and milling degree are shown on sacks.

items.question: If a poultry products is stored at a temperature of 35-40°F, the product quality can be maintained within

choiceExplanations.1 to 2 days: Correct — Poultry stored at 35-40 °F keeps quality only for about 1 to 2 days.
choiceExplanations.2–3 days: Longer than the safe 1 to 2 days.
choiceExplanations.3–4 days: Longer than the safe 1 to 2 days.

items.question: Changes in the flavor of meat, fish, or poultry during freezing is due to the

choiceExplanations.Crystallization of water: Crystallization of water affects texture and drip, not flavor.
choiceExplanations.Sublimation of ice: Sublimation of ice causes freezer burn, not flavor change.
choiceExplanations.Oxidation of fats: Correct — Oxidation of fats causes rancid flavor changes in frozen meat, fish and poultry.
choiceExplanations.Denaturation of proteins: Denaturation of proteins affects texture, not flavor.

items.question: The recommended time for storing beet cuts at -18°C is

choiceExplanations.6 to 12 months: Correct — Frozen beef cuts keep quality for 6 to 12 months at -18 °C.
choiceExplanations.5 to 10 months: Shorter than the recommended period of 6 to 12 months.

items.question: Power tool with saw teeth on a continuous blade or band.

choiceExplanations.Scrollsaw: A scroll saw cuts fine curves with a thin reciprocating blade, not a continuous band.
choiceExplanations.Bandsaw: Correct — A bandsaw has saw teeth on a continuous blade loop running over wheels.
choiceExplanations.Jigsaw: A jigsaw uses a short reciprocating blade, not a continuous band.
choiceExplanations.Chainsaw: A chainsaw has teeth on a chain, not a band blade.

items.question: Freezer burn in meat product is a result of
items.answer: Storing meat product without plastic sheet at low relative humidity
choices: Storing meat product inside vacuum-sealed bags at high relative humidity
Freezing meat product rapidly using cryogenic nitrogen at very low temperature
Storing meat product without plastic sheet at low relative humidity
Thawing meat product slowly inside chiller rooms at moderate air velocity

choiceExplanations.Storing meat product inside vacuum-seale: Vacuum-sealed bags at high humidity prevent surface drying and so do not cause freezer burn.
choiceExplanations.Freezing meat product rapidly using cryo: Rapid cryogenic freezing preserves quality and does not cause freezer burn.
choiceExplanations.Storing meat product without plastic she: Correct — Unwrapped meat in dry freezer air loses surface moisture by sublimation, causing freezer burn.
choiceExplanations.Thawing meat product slowly inside chill: Slow thawing in a chiller does not cause freezer burn.

items.question: Which operation could not be accomplished with a welding machine?

choiceExplanations.Gouge: Gouging is done with an arc or torch and can be done with a welding machine.
choiceExplanations.Braze: Brazing is done with a torch or arc and can be done with welding equipment.
choiceExplanations.Thread: Correct — Threading cuts screw threads using a tap or die and cannot be done with a welding machine.
choiceExplanations.Cut: Cutting can be done with a plasma, arc or oxy-fuel setup.

items.question: The continuity equation is applicable to

choiceExplanations.Conservation of energy: Conservation of energy is described by the energy equation (Bernoulli), not continuity.
choiceExplanations.Conservation of momentum: Conservation of momentum is described by the momentum equation.
choiceExplanations.Conservation of charge: Conservation of charge is for electrical systems.
choiceExplanations.Conservation of mass: Correct — The continuity equation (A1V1 = A2V2) expresses conservation of mass in fluid flow.

items.question: GPEP stands for ___.

choiceExplanations.Grain Production Enhancement Program: Correct — GPEP stands for Grain Production Enhancement Program.
choiceExplanations.Grains Processing Enhancement Project: Not the correct expansion of GPEP.
choiceExplanations.Grain Productivity Extension Program: Not the correct expansion of GPEP.
choiceExplanations.Grain Postharvest Equipment Program: Not the correct expansion of GPEP.

items.question: What condition exists in an adiabatic throttling process?

choiceExplanations.Pressure is constant: Pressure drops across a throttling device.
choiceExplanations.Entropy is constant: Entropy increases in a throttling process, so it is not constant.
choiceExplanations.Temperature is constant: Temperature usually changes in throttling, like the cooling in a refrigerator expansion valve.
choiceExplanations.Enthalpy is constant: Correct — In an adiabatic throttling process, enthalpy stays constant (h1 = h2).

items.question: It is the meat from rabbit

choiceExplanations.Lapan: Correct — Lapan is the Filipino term for rabbit meat.

items.question: If mixing is needed during conveying, the suitable conveyor to use is ___ type.

choiceExplanations.Screw: Correct — A screw conveyor mixes the material as it moves it along.
choiceExplanations.Belt: A belt conveyor carries material without mixing.
choiceExplanations.Bucket: Bucket elevators lift material without mixing it.
choiceExplanations.Pneumatic: Pneumatic conveyors move material by air and do not mix much.

items.question: The amount of heat transferred per unit temperature per unit length.

choiceExplanations.Thermal conductivity: Correct — Thermal conductivity is the rate of heat flow per unit temperature gradient and per unit length (W/m-K).
choiceExplanations.Thermal resistance: Thermal resistance is the opposition to heat flow, the inverse idea.
choiceExplanations.Thermal diffusivity: Thermal diffusivity is conductivity divided by density and specific heat.
choiceExplanations.Thermal resistivity: Thermal resistivity is the reciprocal of thermal conductivity.

items.question: The major component of a corn mill that reduces corn kernels into grits.

choiceExplanations.Impact hammer mill: An impact hammer mill smashes material with hammers instead of rolling it into grits.
choiceExplanations.Disk attrition mill: A disk attrition mill grinds between plates and is used for flour or feed.
choiceExplanations.Stone burr mill: A stone burr mill grinds between stones, producing flour.
choiceExplanations.Steel roller mill: Correct — A steel roller mill crushes corn between steel rolls to make grits.

items.question: It is a meat of less than one-year old cattle.

choiceExplanations.Veal: Correct — Veal is meat from cattle under one year old.
choiceExplanations.Beef: Beef is meat from mature cattle.

items.question: When a product is termed as frozen, it is ___.

choiceExplanations.Stored between 55F to 65F: 55-65 °F is above room temperature range, not frozen storage.
choiceExplanations.Stored between –10F to 10F: Correct — Frozen products are stored between -10 °F and 10 °F.

1.0% of the project cost, with a minimum of Php 150.00 per 1 Million pesos of project cost.

choiceExplanations.1.0% of the project cost, with a minimum: Correct — The minimum fee for review, signing and sealing of project proposals is 1.0% of project cost, minimum Php 150 per million.

items.question: The recommended minimum width for doorways of slaughter houses.

choiceExplanations.1.4 meters wide: Too narrow; the recommended minimum doorway width is 1.5 m.
choiceExplanations.1.2 meters wide: Too narrow; the recommended minimum doorway width is 1.5 m.
choiceExplanations.1.5 meters wide: Correct — The recommended minimum width for slaughterhouse doorways is 1.5 m.
