choiceExplanations.40 lumen/m2: 40 lumen/m2 is not the recommended standard value for a machine shed.

items.question: Storage method of fruits and vegetables where the produce are placed in boxes which in turn are stacked in storage room.

choiceExplanations.Clamp storage: Clamp storage piles produce in the field and covers it with straw and soil, not boxes in a room.
choiceExplanations.Bin storage: Bin storage holds produce loosely in bins, not in stacked boxes.
choiceExplanations.Bulk storage: Bulk storage piles loose produce in large heaps, not in boxes.
choiceExplanations.Pallet storage: Correct — Pallet storage places produce in boxes on pallets, which are then stacked in the storage room.

items.question: It is a method of storage of product in an artificial condition in which the proportion of carbon dioxide and/or oxygen is precisely limited.

choiceExplanations.Modified atmosphere storage: Modified atmosphere storage changes gas levels only once and does not keep them precisely controlled.
choiceExplanations.Refrigerated cold storage: Refrigerated cold storage controls temperature only, not carbon dioxide and oxygen proportions.
choiceExplanations.Controlled atmosphere storage: Correct — Controlled atmosphere storage holds CO2 and/or O2 at precisely limited levels to slow ripening and spoilage.
choiceExplanations.Hypobaric pressure storage: Hypobaric storage lowers the air pressure to reduce oxygen; it does not control gas proportions precisely.

items.question: The percentage weight of milled rice whose length remain is ¾ of the original length over the weight of milled rice.

choiceExplanations.Brown rice recovery: Brown rice recovery is the weight of dehulled rice per paddy; it does not involve kernel length.
choiceExplanations.Head rice recovery: Correct — Head rice recovery is the percent weight of milled rice kernels that remain at least three-fourths of their original length.
choiceExplanations.Total milling recovery: Total milling recovery counts all milled rice, whole and broken, so kernel length is not considered.
choiceExplanations.Broken kernel recovery: Broken kernel recovery is the share of shorter, broken pieces, the opposite of the long kernels in the definition.

items.question: Based on PAES 406:2001 Cattle Ranch: What is the minimum fence height?

choiceExplanations.1.6 m: 1.6 m is higher than the minimum fence height in PAES 406:2001.
choiceExplanations.1.2 m: 1.2 m is lower than the minimum fence height required by PAES 406:2001.
choiceExplanations.1.7 m: 1.7 m is higher than the minimum fence height in PAES 406:2001.
choiceExplanations.1.5 m: Correct — PAES 406:2001 for cattle ranch sets the minimum fence height at 1.5 m.

items.question: It is a size-reducing machine that reduces the size of the material by pressing or squeezing until the material breaks.

choiceExplanations.Crusher: Correct — A crusher reduces size by pressing or squeezing the material until it breaks.
choiceExplanations.Cutter: A cutter reduces size by cutting with knives, not by squeezing until breaking.
choiceExplanations.Shredder: A shredder tears material apart with rotating teeth or knives, not by pressing.
choiceExplanations.Grinder: A grinder reduces size by impact, attrition or shear into fine particles, not by pressing.

items.question: A type of rice mill that is characterized by low milling recovery.

choiceExplanations.Cono type rice mill: A cono-type rice mill is a whitening mill with cone-shaped rollers; it is not noted for the lowest recovery.
choiceExplanations.Rubber roll rice mill: A rubber roll mill hulls gently and gives good recovery with few broken grains.
choiceExplanations.Stone disc rice mill: A stone disc mill hulls paddy with stone discs; it is not the type known for low recovery.
choiceExplanations.Steel flueted rice mill: Correct — A steel fluted rice mill hulls and mills roughly, causing many broken grains and low milling recovery.

items.question: A paddy separator is usually placed in a rice mill ________

choiceExplanations.After the polishing machine: After polishing the rice is finished, so separating paddy then would be too late.
choiceExplanations.Before the husking machine: Before husking, the grain is still all paddy, so there is nothing to separate yet.
choiceExplanations.After the whitening machine: After whitening, unhulled grain should already have been removed.
choiceExplanations.Before the whitening machine: Correct — The paddy separator sits after hulling and before the whitening machine, removing unhulled paddy from brown rice.

items.question: A size reduction equipment suitable for reducing shelled corn particles for feed grains

choiceExplanations.Rod mill: A rod mill grinds ore with steel rods in a rotating drum; it is not used for feed grains.
choiceExplanations.Roller mill: Correct — A roller mill crushes shelled corn between rolls and is suitable for size reduction of feed grains.
choiceExplanations.Colloid mill: A colloid mill makes fine suspensions or emulsions of liquids, not feed grain particles.
choiceExplanations.Ball mill: A ball mill grinds with tumbling balls, mostly for minerals and fine powders, not feed grains.

items.question: A size reduction equipment suitable for moist product

choiceExplanations.Roller mill: A roller mill is suitable for dry grain; moist material would stick to the rolls.
choiceExplanations.Hammer mill: A hammer mill needs dry material; moisture clogs the screens.
choiceExplanations.Attrition mill: Correct — An attrition mill grinds by rubbing between plates and can handle moist product.
choiceExplanations.Burr mill: A burr mill is used for dry grain; moist product tends to clog it.

items.question: Recommended temperature for incubating poultry eggs.

choiceExplanations.43.1 C: 43.1 C is too high and would cook or kill the embryos.
choiceExplanations.37.5 C: Correct — The recommended incubation temperature for poultry eggs is 37.5 C.
choiceExplanations.40.5 C: 40.5 C is too high for the recommended incubation of poultry eggs.
choiceExplanations.45.8 C: 45.8 C is far too high and would kill the embryos.

items.question: Incubation period for chicken eggs.

choiceExplanations.19 days: 19 days is too short for chicken eggs to hatch.
choiceExplanations.26 days: 26 days is too long for chicken eggs.
choiceExplanations.24 days: 24 days is too long for chicken eggs.
choiceExplanations.21 days: Correct — Chicken eggs hatch after 21 days of incubation.

items.question: Incubation period for duck eggs.
items.rationale: Common (Mallard-derived) duck eggs, including the Pateros duck, hatch in about 28 days. Muscovy duck eggs take about 35 days.

choiceExplanations.28 days: Correct — common duck eggs (e.g. Pateros duck) hatch in about 28 days.
choiceExplanations.20 days: Wrong — about 21 days is the incubation period of chicken eggs, not ducks.
choiceExplanations.35 days: Wrong — 35 days is for Muscovy duck eggs, not common ducks.
choiceExplanations.25 days: Wrong — 25 days is too short; common duck eggs need about 28 days.

items.question: Incubation period for quail eggs.

choiceExplanations.18 days: 18 days is longer than the 16-day quail incubation period in the key.
choiceExplanations.14 days: 14 days is too short for quail eggs.
choiceExplanations.16 days: Correct — Quail eggs are incubated for about 16 days before hatching.
choiceExplanations.20 days: 20 days is too long for quail eggs.

items.question: A wood chips exploded into fibers under high pressure steam.

choiceExplanations.Hardboard: Correct — Hardboard is made by exploding wood chips into fibers with high-pressure steam and pressing them into dense board.
choiceExplanations.Chipboard: Chipboard is made from wood chips glued and pressed, not exploded into fibers by steam.
choiceExplanations.Plywood: Plywood is made of thin wood veneers glued crosswise, not from fibers.
choiceExplanations.Blockboard: Blockboard has a core of wood strips between veneers, not steam-exploded fibers.

items.question: Board principally made from wood chips and formed by hot press process with adhesive.

choiceExplanations.Particle board: Correct — Particle board is made from wood chips mixed with adhesive and formed by a hot press.
choiceExplanations.Block board: Block board has a core of wood strips covered by veneers, not made from chips.
choiceExplanations.Veneer board: Veneer board is made from thin wood sheets, not wood chips.
choiceExplanations.Fiber board: Fiber board is made from wood fibers, not from chips pressed with adhesive.

items.question: It is the tendency of a force to cause rotation about a certain point of axis

choiceExplanations.Momentum: Momentum is mass times velocity; it is not a turning tendency of a force.
choiceExplanations.Moment: Correct — A moment is the tendency of a force to cause rotation about a point or axis (force times perpendicular distance).
choiceExplanations.Impulse: Impulse is force times time, which changes momentum, not rotation.
choiceExplanations.Inertia: Inertia is resistance to change in motion; it is not the turning effect of a force.

items.question: Known as silent-type centrifugal blower

choiceExplanations.Backward curve centrifugal blower: A backward curve blower is high-efficiency and non-overloading, not the quiet type.
choiceExplanations.Airfoil blade centrifugal blower: An airfoil blade blower is the most efficient and also fairly quiet, but the silent type is forward-curved.
choiceExplanations.Forward curve centrifugal blower: Correct — The forward curve centrifugal blower runs at low speed and is known as the silent type.
choiceExplanations.Radial blade centrifugal blower: A radial blade blower handles dusty or dirty air and is noisier than the forward curve type.

items.question: An example of rotary pump.
items.answer: Gear pump Lobe pump Vane pump
choices: Gear pump Lobe pump Vane pump
Volute pump Diffuser pump Turbine pump
Jet pump Airlift pump Axial pump
Piston pump Plunger pump Diaphragm pump

choiceExplanations.Gear pump Lobe pump Vane pump: Correct — Gear, lobe and vane pumps are all rotary pumps, moving fluid by rotating parts.
choiceExplanations.Volute pump Diffuser pump Turbine pump: Volute, diffuser and turbine pumps are centrifugal types, not rotary positive-displacement pumps.
choiceExplanations.Jet pump Airlift pump Axial pump: Jet, airlift and axial pumps are not rotary positive-displacement pumps.
choiceExplanations.Piston pump Plunger pump Diaphragm pump: Piston, plunger and diaphragm pumps are reciprocating pumps, not rotary.

items.question: A pump well adapted for high pressure pumping of fluid.

choiceExplanations.Propeller: A propeller pump moves large flows at low head, not high pressure.
choiceExplanations.Centrifugal: A centrifugal pump suits large flows at moderate pressure, not high pressure.
choiceExplanations.Reciprocating: Correct — A reciprocating pump forces fluid with a piston and is well adapted to high-pressure pumping.
choiceExplanations.Airlift: An airlift pump uses air bubbles to lift water and gives low pressure.

items.question: A conveying element that serves as mixing device for a vertical-type feed mixer.

choiceExplanations.Bucket: A bucket is a conveying element in elevators, not a mixing device inside a vertical feed mixer.
choiceExplanations.Auger: Correct — A vertical feed mixer uses a vertical auger that lifts and tumbles feed, acting as the mixing element.
choiceExplanations.Ribbon: A ribbon is the mixing element of horizontal mixers, not vertical ones.
choiceExplanations.Paddle: A paddle is used in horizontal paddle mixers, not vertical-type mixers.

items.question: Operating speed of attrition mill.

choiceExplanations.less than 1560 rpm: Less than 1560 rpm is not the specified operating speed of an attrition mill.
choiceExplanations.less than 1296 rpm: Less than 1296 rpm is not the specified operating speed of an attrition mill.
choiceExplanations.less than 1200 rpm: Correct — An attrition mill runs slowly, at less than 1200 rpm.
choiceExplanations.less than 1380 rpm: Less than 1380 rpm is not the specified operating speed of an attrition mill.

items.question: Operating speed of hammer mill.

choiceExplanations.1500 to 4000 rpm: Correct — A hammer mill operates at about 1500 to 4000 rpm.
choiceExplanations.2750–5250 rpm: 2750 to 5250 rpm is not the standard hammer mill speed range.
choiceExplanations.6500–9000 rpm: 6500 to 9000 rpm is far above hammer mill speeds, more like a pin or fine impact mill.
choiceExplanations.4000–6500 rpm: 4000 to 6500 rpm is above the standard hammer mill speed range.

items.question: Device use for grinding which is a result of the impact between the particles and hammers; which are mounted on a shaft rotating along a horizontal axis.

choiceExplanations.Attrition mill: An attrition mill grinds by rubbing between plates, not by hammer impact.
choiceExplanations.Roller mill: A roller mill crushes grain between rolls, not by hammers on a shaft.
choiceExplanations.Ball mill: A ball mill grinds with tumbling balls in a drum, not hammers on a shaft.
choiceExplanations.Hammer mill: Correct — A hammer mill grinds by impact between particles and hammers mounted on a horizontally rotating shaft.

items.question: A type of fruit washer suitable for removing sandy or loamy soil as well as spray residue.

choiceExplanations.Brush washer: Correct — A brush washer scrubs fruit with rotating brushes under water or spray, removing sandy or loamy soil and spray residue.
choiceExplanations.Flotation washer: A flotation washer soaks and floats produce in a water tank; it suits delicate or light produce and is weak on caked soil.
choiceExplanations.Spray washer: A spray washer rinses with water jets and cannot scrub off sticky sandy or loamy soil by itself.
choiceExplanations.Drum washer: A drum washer tumbles produce in a rotating drum with water; it suits root crops, not spray residue removal.

items.question: It is a device that separates dissimilar particles in a liquid.

choiceExplanations.Homogenizer: A homogenizer breaks up and blends particles in a liquid, such as fat globules in milk; it does not separate them.
choiceExplanations.Aspirator: An aspirator uses suction or an air stream to move or clean material; it does not separate particles in a liquid.
choiceExplanations.Centrifuge: Correct — A centrifuge spins a liquid so that denser particles are thrown outward and separated from the lighter ones.
choiceExplanations.Evaporator: An evaporator removes liquid by boiling it off to concentrate a solution; it does not separate particles.

items.question: Maximum inclination for installation of horizontal screw conveyors.

choiceExplanations.Up to 22 degrees: Up to 22 degrees is steeper than the accepted limit for horizontal screw conveyors.
choiceExplanations.Up to 20 degrees: Correct — Horizontal-type screw conveyors are installed at an inclination of up to 20 degrees; steeper slopes reduce capacity.
choiceExplanations.Up to 18 degrees: Up to 18 degrees is below the accepted limit of 20 degrees.
choiceExplanations.Up to 16 degrees: Up to 16 degrees is below the accepted limit of 20 degrees.

items.question: Standard width if Corrugated GI Sheet.

choiceExplanations.85 cm: 85 cm is not the standard width of corrugated GI sheet.
choiceExplanations.75 cm: 75 cm is not the standard width of corrugated GI sheet.
choiceExplanations.80 cm: Correct — The standard width of corrugated GI sheet is 80 cm.
choiceExplanations.70 cm: 70 cm is not the standard width of corrugated GI sheet.

items.question: Standard length of Corrugated GI Sheet.

choiceExplanations.390 cm: 390 cm is not the standard length of corrugated GI sheet.
choiceExplanations.324 cm: 324 cm is not the standard length of corrugated GI sheet.
choiceExplanations.300 cm: Correct — The standard length of corrugated GI sheet is 300 cm.
choiceExplanations.345 cm: 345 cm is not the standard length of corrugated GI sheet.

items.question: A type of dryer used to remove water from a solutions or suspensions and dry the resulting powder to a moisture content that approaches equilibrium with the exhaust drying air.

choiceExplanations.Spray drying: Correct — Spray drying atomizes a solution or suspension into hot air so the droplets dry into powder near equilibrium moisture.
choiceExplanations.Drum drying: Drum drying dries a thin film on a heated rotating drum and gives flakes or sheets, not a spray-dried powder.
choiceExplanations.Tray drying: Tray drying dries solid pieces on trays in a hot air flow; it is not used for solutions.
choiceExplanations.Freeze drying: Freeze drying removes ice by sublimation under vacuum; it does not use hot exhaust air.

items.question: A thermometer with a gauze-covered bulb that permit to determine the relative humidity of the air.

choiceExplanations.Dew point thermometer: A dew point thermometer finds the temperature at which moisture condenses; it has no gauze-covered bulb.
choiceExplanations.Black bulb thermometer: A black bulb thermometer measures radiant heat; it is not used for humidity.
choiceExplanations.Dry bulb thermometer: A dry bulb thermometer reads plain air temperature and has no wet gauze.
choiceExplanations.Wet bulb thermometer: Correct — A wet bulb thermometer has a wet gauze-covered bulb; evaporative cooling, compared with dry bulb reading, gives relative humidity.

items.question: Radiant energy from perfect emitter is known as __________

choiceExplanations.Gray body: A gray body emits less radiation than a perfect emitter, at a fixed fraction of it.
choiceExplanations.White body: A white body reflects radiation and is a poor emitter, the opposite of a perfect emitter.
choiceExplanations.Black body: Correct — A black body is the perfect emitter (and absorber) of radiant energy at every wavelength.
choiceExplanations.Opaque body: An opaque body only blocks transmission of radiation; it is not a perfect emitter by definition.

items.question: It is the ratio of the coefficient of thermal capacity of a material to that of water.

choiceExplanations.Specific heat: Correct — Specific heat is the ratio of a material's thermal capacity to that of water, per unit mass.
choiceExplanations.Latent heat: Latent heat is heat absorbed or released in a phase change at constant temperature, not a ratio to water.
choiceExplanations.Sensible heat: Sensible heat is heat that changes temperature; it is energy, not a ratio to water.
choiceExplanations.Thermal conductivity: Thermal conductivity is how fast heat flows through a material; it is not compared with water's heat capacity.

items.question: What is the size in square millimeter of the cable 250 MCM?

choiceExplanations.126.7 mm2: Correct — A 250 MCM (thousand circular mils) cable has a cross section of about 126.7 mm2.
choiceExplanations.139.4 mm2: 139.4 mm2 is the area of a different size, about 275 MCM, not 250 MCM.
choiceExplanations.101.4 mm2: 101.4 mm2 is the area of a smaller cable, about 200 MCM.
choiceExplanations.114.0 mm2: 114.0 mm2 is the area of a smaller cable, about 225 MCM.

items.question: It is the intensity of light per unit area.

choiceExplanations.Emittance: Emittance is the light or radiation given off by a surface, not the light received.
choiceExplanations.Illumination: Correct — Illumination is the amount of light falling on a surface per unit area, measured in lux or lumens per m2.
choiceExplanations.Luminance: Luminance is the brightness of a surface seen in a direction, not light received per area.
choiceExplanations.Reflectance: Reflectance is the fraction of light that a surface reflects.

items.question: Which of the following size reducing equipment that reduces the size of particle by crushing and shearing?

choiceExplanations.Hammer mill: A hammer mill reduces size mainly by impact, not crushing and shearing.
choiceExplanations.Roller mill: A roller mill crushes by compression between rolls; shearing is secondary to grinding by rubbing.
choiceExplanations.Attrition mill: Correct — An attrition mill reduces size by crushing and shearing between rubbing plates or discs.
choiceExplanations.Pin mill: A pin mill uses impact from high-speed pins, not crushing and shearing.

items.question: It is conveyor usually used in meat processing plant which conveys the product as they are being hanged.
items.rationale: Carcasses are hung on hooks or shackles that run along an overhead rail, i.e. an overhead trolley conveyor.

choiceExplanations.Belt conveyor: Wrong — a belt conveyor carries products lying on a moving belt, not hanging.
choiceExplanations.Screw conveyor: Wrong — a screw conveyor pushes bulk material through a trough with a rotating auger.
choiceExplanations.Apron conveyor: Wrong — an apron conveyor carries heavy items on overlapping plates, not hanging.
choiceExplanations.Overhead trolley conveyor: Correct — hanging carcasses move on hooks along an overhead trolley conveyor rail.

items.question: A type of chain conveyor that is used for granular and non-abrasive materials

choiceExplanations.Scraper conveyor: Correct — A scraper conveyor drags granular, non-abrasive materials along a trough using scrapers attached to a chain.
choiceExplanations.Trolley conveyor: A trolley conveyor carries hanging loads on an overhead track, not granular material.
choiceExplanations.Apron conveyor: An apron conveyor is a moving platform of plates for heavy or lumpy loads, not mainly granular material.
choiceExplanations.Slat conveyor: A slat conveyor carries unit loads on slats attached to chains; it is not for loose granular material.

items.question: It is a moving platform type chain conveyor.

choiceExplanations.Flight conveyor: A flight conveyor pushes bulk material with flights through a trough; it does not have a platform.
choiceExplanations.Apron conveyor: Correct — An apron conveyor is a chain conveyor with overlapping plates forming a moving platform.
choiceExplanations.Trolley conveyor: A trolley conveyor moves hanging loads on an overhead track, not on a platform.
choiceExplanations.Scraper conveyor: A scraper conveyor drags material in a trough with scrapers, not on a moving platform.

items.question: A device used mostly in larger cooling units to cool the water that absorbs the heat from the condenser.

choiceExplanations.Air handler: An air handler moves and conditions air; it does not cool condenser water.
choiceExplanations.Heat exchanger: A heat exchanger transfers heat between two fluids; it is not the device that cools condenser water using air.
choiceExplanations.Cooling tower: Correct — A cooling tower cools the water that carries heat from the condenser, by evaporation to air.
choiceExplanations.Liquid receiver: A liquid receiver stores liquid refrigerant after the condenser; it does not cool water.

items.question: A slaughter house with required facilities and operational procedures to serve local market community

choiceExplanations.B slaughter house: B slaughterhouse is a lower class that serves smaller or limited operations.
choiceExplanations.A slaughter house: Correct — Class A slaughterhouse has the required facilities and procedures to serve the local market community (keyed answer).
choiceExplanations.AA slaughter house: AA slaughterhouse is a higher class with more facilities, serving wider markets.
choiceExplanations.AAA slaughter house: AAA slaughterhouse is the highest class, with full facilities for export and large-scale operations.

items.question: Any tag, brand, mark, pictorial or other descriptive matter, written, printed, marked, embossed or impressed on or attached to a container of food.

choiceExplanations.Seal: A seal closes or secures a container; it is not descriptive matter written on it.
choiceExplanations.Wrapper: A wrapper is packaging material wrapped around food; it is not the descriptive matter itself.
choiceExplanations.Label: Correct — A label is any tag, brand, mark, picture or descriptive matter written, printed or attached to a food container.
choiceExplanations.Package: A package is the container itself, not the descriptive matter on it.

items.question: Under PAES 118:2001 (Agricultural Machinery - Four-Wheel Tractor - Specifications), all tractors powered by ______ engines or higher shall be equipped with ROPS and seat belts.
items.rationale: PAES 118:2001 specifies that all four-wheel agricultural tractors powered by 15 kW engines or higher must be equipped with a Roll-Over Protective Structure (ROPS) and seat belts.

choiceExplanations.20 kW: 20 kW is not the power level stated in PAES 118:2001 for requiring ROPS and seat belts.
choiceExplanations.25 kW: 25 kW is not the power level stated in PAES 118:2001 for requiring ROPS and seat belts.
choiceExplanations.10 kW: 10 kW is below the level in PAES 118:2001 at which ROPS and seat belts are required.
choiceExplanations.15 kW: Correct — PAES 118:2001 requires tractors with engines of 15 kW or higher to have ROPS and seat belts.

items.question: Under PAES 118:2001 (Agricultural Machinery - Four-Wheel Tractor - Specifications), the tractor shall be able to pull field implements up to ______.
items.rationale: PAES 118:2001 specifies that four-wheel agricultural tractors must be capable of pulling field implements at speeds up to 8 km/h.

choiceExplanations.5 km/h: 5 km/h is below the speed stated in PAES 118:2001 for pulling field implements.
choiceExplanations.12 km/h: 12 km/h is above the speed stated in PAES 118:2001 for pulling field implements.
choiceExplanations.15 km/h: 15 km/h is above the speed stated in PAES 118:2001 for pulling field implements.
choiceExplanations.8 km/h: Correct — PAES 118:2001 requires the tractor to pull field implements at speeds up to 8 km/h.

items.question: Under PAES 141:2005 (Agricultural Machinery - Weeder - Specifications), when tested under PAES 142, the weeding efficiency shall be at least (x) and the percentage of plant damage shall not exceed (y).
items.rationale: PAES 141:2005 performance requirements for weeders tested under PAES 142 specify a minimum weeding efficiency of 80% and a maximum plant damage of 6%.

choiceExplanations.x = 85%; y = 5%: x = 85%; y = 5% is not the pair stated in PAES 141:2005.
choiceExplanations.x = 80%; y = 6%: Correct — PAES 141:2005 requires weeding efficiency of at least 80% and plant damage of not more than 6%.
choiceExplanations.x = 75%; y = 10%: x = 75%; y = 10% is not the pair stated in PAES 141:2005.
choiceExplanations.x = 90%; y = 3%: x = 90%; y = 3% is stricter than the pair stated in PAES 141:2005.

items.question: PAES 415:2001 Agricultural Structures - Greenhouses: It should be durable as well as economical and should withstand heavy loads like wind gusts of ______

choiceExplanations.150kph: Correct — PAES 415:2001 says a greenhouse should withstand wind gusts of 150 kph.
choiceExplanations.162kph: 162 kph is not the wind gust value stated in PAES 415:2001.
choiceExplanations.138kph: 138 kph is not the wind gust value stated in PAES 415:2001.
choiceExplanations.120kph: 120 kph is lower than the wind gust value stated in PAES 415:2001.

items.question: Based on PAES 204:2000 mechanical rice thresher: What is the maximum mechanically damaged grain?

choiceExplanations.4%: 4% is above the maximum mechanically damaged grain allowed in PAES 204:2000.
choiceExplanations.1%: 1% is below the allowed value; the standard sets the maximum at 2%.
choiceExplanations.3%: 3% is above the maximum mechanically damaged grain allowed in PAES 204:2000.
choiceExplanations.2%: Correct — PAES 204:2000 limits mechanically damaged grain in a rice thresher to a maximum of 2%.

items.question: Dries quickly for interior walls, woods, used with thinner

choiceExplanations.Acrylic latex paint: Acrylic latex paint is water-based and thinned with water, not a thinner-based quick drying paint.
choiceExplanations.Flat wall enamel: Flat wall enamel is a matte finish for walls and is not known for quick drying with thinner.
choiceExplanations.Quick drying enamel: Correct — Quick drying enamel is a thinner-based paint that dries fast and is used on interior walls and wood.
choiceExplanations.Epoxy primer paint: Epoxy primer paint is a two-part protective primer for metal, not a quick drying wall and wood enamel.

items.question: Used in agriculture where things are sustained

choiceExplanations.Precision Agriculture: Precision agriculture uses sensors and GPS to apply inputs exactly; it does not specifically mean sustaining resources.
choiceExplanations.Conventional Agriculture: Conventional agriculture relies on heavy chemical inputs and does not focus on sustaining resources.
choiceExplanations.Sustainable Agriculture: Correct — Sustainable agriculture farms in ways that sustain resources, environment and productivity over time.
choiceExplanations.Conservation Agriculture: Conservation agriculture protects soil with minimal tillage and cover, but the word 'sustained' points to sustainable agriculture.

items.question: Length between trusses
items.rationale: The distance between adjacent trusses (or frames) is the bay length or truss spacing. Clear span is the width a truss covers between supports.

choiceExplanations.Clear span: Wrong — clear span is the width a single truss covers between its supports, not the spacing between trusses.
choiceExplanations.Ridge height: Wrong — ridge height is the vertical height from floor to the roof's peak.
choiceExplanations.Eave height: Wrong — eave height is the height from floor to the lower edge of the roof.
choiceExplanations.Bay length: Correct — the distance between neighboring trusses is the bay length (truss spacing).

items.question: How to increase entropy?

choiceExplanations.Crystallizing sugar from water: Crystallizing sugar from water makes the particles more ordered, which lowers entropy.
choiceExplanations.Dissolving salt in water: Correct — Dissolving salt in water spreads ions through the liquid, increasing disorder and so entropy.
choiceExplanations.Freezing water into ice: Freezing water into ice makes molecules more ordered, which lowers entropy.
choiceExplanations.Condensing steam into water: Condensing steam into water makes molecules less free, which lowers entropy.

items.question: Constant enthalpy

choiceExplanations.Isenthalpic: Correct — Isenthalpic means constant enthalpy, as in throttling through an expansion valve.

items.question: Which should be done first in wind projects

choiceExplanations.Grid interconnection setup: Grid interconnection comes late, after the project design is settled.
choiceExplanations.Turbine foundation design: Turbine foundation design depends on site and wind data, so it cannot come first.
choiceExplanations.Power curve testing: Power curve testing is done on an installed turbine, so it comes late.
choiceExplanations.Wind velocity measurement: Correct — Wind velocity measurement is done first to confirm the site has enough wind for the project.

items.question: Percent purity in sampling method

choiceExplanations.120%: 120% is not possible; purity cannot exceed 100%.
choiceExplanations.113%: 113% is not possible; purity cannot exceed 100%.
choiceExplanations.98%: Correct — Keyed answer is 98% purity; the other choices are impossible as purity cannot exceed 100%.
choiceExplanations.106%: 106% is not possible; purity cannot exceed 100%.

items.question: Used to hold purins and rafters

choiceExplanations.Chords: Chords are the top and bottom members of a truss, not the pieces that hold purlins and rafters.
choiceExplanations.Girts: Girts are horizontal wall members that support siding, not purlins and rafters.
choiceExplanations.Cleats: Correct — Cleats are small pieces fastened to trusses or rafters to hold purlins and rafters in place.
choiceExplanations.Struts: Struts are compression members that brace parts of a frame, not the holders of purlins.

items.question: With perforated cylinder (PAES)

choiceExplanations.Rubber roll huller: A rubber roll huller removes hulls between two rubber rolls; it has no perforated cylinder.
choiceExplanations.Impeller type huller: An impeller type huller throws paddy against a wall; it has no perforated cylinder.
choiceExplanations.Friction type whitener: Correct — A friction type whitener uses a rotor inside a perforated cylinder to remove bran by friction.
choiceExplanations.Disc type sheller: A disc type sheller shells grain between discs; it has no perforated cylinder.

items.question: Used to record real time data

choiceExplanations.Counter: A counter counts events or pulses; it does not record time-based data.
choiceExplanations.Transducer: A transducer converts a physical quantity into an electrical signal; it senses data, not records it in real time.

items.question: PAES 201:2000 Heated Air Mechanical Grain Dryer: batch type dryer wherein a fixed volume of grain is held stationary in a vertical grain holding bin

choiceExplanations.Flatbed batch type: A flatbed batch dryer holds grain in a shallow horizontal bed, not a vertical bin.

items.question: PAES 201:2000 Heated Air Mechanical Grain Dryer: ratio of the total heat utilized to vaporize moisture in the material, to the amount of heat added to the drying air, expressed in percent

Air Heating efficiency or furnace efficiency
Thermal Generation efficiency or burner efficiency
Combustion Energy efficiency or fan efficiency

choiceExplanations.Air Heating efficiency or furnace effici: Air heating or furnace efficiency compares heat delivered to the air with fuel energy, not heat used to vaporize moisture.
choiceExplanations.Thermal Generation efficiency or burner: Thermal generation or burner efficiency measures how well fuel is turned to heat, not heat used for evaporation.
choiceExplanations.Combustion Energy efficiency or fan effi: Combustion energy or fan efficiency are not the PAES term for heat used in drying moisture.

items.question: When the dry bulb and wet bulb temp. are equal

items.question: What do you call the mountain side, with reference to the wind direction in which the air masses passing through it is cold and dry.

items.question: The ratio of the actual partial pressure exerted by the water vapor in any volume of air to the partial pressure that would be exerted by the water vapor if the water vapor in the air is saturated at the temperature of the air or simply actual water vapor pressure/saturation water vapor pressure

choiceExplanations.Physical and thermal properties: Correct — A psychrometric chart shows physical properties (volume, humidity) and thermal properties (temperature, enthalpy) of moist air.
choiceExplanations.Chemical and physical properties: Chemical properties are not shown on a psychrometric chart.

items.question: For PAES 414-1 Part 1, account for a freeboard of _____ for liquid waste storage ponds.
items.rationale: 0.3 m (storage ponds) / 0.2 m (storage tank)

choiceExplanations.0.5 m (storage ponds): 0.5 m is more than the freeboard stated for storage ponds in PAES 414-1.
choiceExplanations.0.3 m (storage ponds): Correct — PAES 414-1 requires a freeboard of 0.3 m for liquid waste storage ponds.
choiceExplanations.1.0 m (storage ponds): 1.0 m is more than the freeboard stated for storage ponds in PAES 414-1.
choiceExplanations.0.6 m (storage ponds): 0.6 m is more than the freeboard stated for storage ponds in PAES 414-1.

items.question: An air stream at a specified temperature and relative humidity undergoes evaporative cooling by spraying water into it at the same temperature. The lowest temperature the air stream can be cooled to is:
items.answer: Wet bulb temperature at the given state
choices: Wet bulb temperature at the given state
Dry bulb temperature at the given state
Critical temperature at the given state
Dew point temperature at the given state

choiceExplanations.Wet bulb temperature at the given state: Correct — Evaporative cooling at constant enthalpy can cool air only down to its wet bulb temperature.
choiceExplanations.Dry bulb temperature at the given state: The dry bulb temperature is the starting temperature; evaporation cools below it.
choiceExplanations.Critical temperature at the given state: Critical temperature is a fluid property for liquefying gas, not a limit of evaporative cooling.
choiceExplanations.Dew point temperature at the given state: Dew point is lower than wet bulb temperature and cannot be reached by adding water at the same temperature.

items.question: The ratio of the amount of water vapor actually present in the air to the greatest amount possible at the same temperature.

choiceExplanations.Specific humidity: Specific humidity is the mass of vapor per mass of moist air, not a ratio to the maximum.
choiceExplanations.Relative humidity: Correct — Relative humidity is the amount of vapor present divided by the most the air can hold at that temperature.
choiceExplanations.Absolute humidity: Absolute humidity is vapor mass per volume of air, not a ratio to the maximum.
choiceExplanations.Humidity ratio: Humidity ratio is vapor mass per mass of dry air, not a ratio to the maximum.

items.question: This is a process of heat treating and then subjected to cooling

choiceExplanations.Annealing: Correct — Annealing heats a metal and then cools it slowly to soften it and relieve stress.
choiceExplanations.Electroplating: Electroplating coats a metal with another metal using electric current; it is not heat treatment.
choiceExplanations.Shot peening: Shot peening bombards a surface with small balls to strengthen it, without heating.
choiceExplanations.Cold rolling: Cold rolling shapes metal at room temperature, not by heating.

items.question: A fruit cold storage facility has a utilization coefficient of 0.43 and an investment cost of Php 2 million. If the utilization coefficient is increased to 0.53, what is the percent increase in the investment cost of the facility?
items.rationale: Increasing the utilization coefficient reflects higher operational use of existing storage space rather than adding physical capacity, so the facility's investment cost increases by 0%.

choiceExplanations.5%: 5% is not correct because the question gives no basis for any change in cost.
choiceExplanations.20%: 20% is not correct because the question gives no basis for any change in cost.
choiceExplanations.0%: Correct — Utilization coefficient describes how the space is used; the keyed answer is 0% increase in investment cost.
choiceExplanations.10%: 10% is not correct because the question gives no basis for any change in cost.

items.question: What is the opposite of latent heat of fusion?
items.rationale: Latent heat of fusion is the thermal energy absorbed when a solid melts into a liquid, while the heat of solidification (or freezing) is the equal energy released during the reverse transition from liquid to solid.

choiceExplanations.Specific latent heat: Specific latent heat is heat per unit mass for any phase change, not the opposite of fusion.
choiceExplanations.Latent heat of fusion: Latent heat of fusion is the same process in the melting direction, not its opposite.
choiceExplanations.Latent heat: Latent heat is a general term for any phase change heat, not specifically the opposite of fusion.
choiceExplanations.Heat of solidification: Correct — Heat of solidification is the heat released when liquid freezes, the reverse of the latent heat of fusion.

items.question: The Coefficient of Performance (COP) is a measure of a system's efficiency, defined as the ratio of the cooling effect (heat extracted) to the energy input. In a refrigeration system, which component performs the work or receives the energy input?
items.rationale: In a vapor-compression refrigeration system, the compressor takes in mechanical work to raise refrigerant pressure and temperature, representing the energy input term in COP = Q_L / W_in.

choiceExplanations.Condenser: The condenser rejects heat; it receives no work input.
choiceExplanations.Compressor: Correct — The compressor receives the work input that raises refrigerant pressure and circulates it through the system.
choiceExplanations.Cooling chamber: The cooling chamber is the space being cooled, where the cooling effect occurs.
choiceExplanations.Motor: The motor drives the compressor; the work is done on the refrigerant by the compressor.

items.question: In order to reduce the specific heat of meat, what should you do to it?
items.rationale: Freezing meat converts its high-specific-heat liquid water (~4.18 kJ/kg·K) into ice (~2.10 kJ/kg·K), substantially reducing the overall specific heat of the meat.

choiceExplanations.Chop: Chopping changes size, not specific heat.
choiceExplanations.Heat up: Heating raises temperature and does not reduce the specific heat of meat.
choiceExplanations.Place in a cooler: Placing in a cooler lowers temperature but meat stays unfrozen with high specific heat.
choiceExplanations.Freeze: Correct — Freezing turns water in meat to ice, which has a lower specific heat than liquid water, so meat's specific heat drops.

items.question: As the lead engineer in a greenhouse vegetable production team, what sensor input data should trigger the solenoid valve to start overhead mist sprinkling?
items.rationale: Overhead misting in greenhouses is activated for evaporative cooling when air temperature reaches a maximum threshold; soil tension triggers root irrigation, whereas high relative humidity would inhibit misting.
choices: Threshold maximum absolute value of soil tension

choiceExplanations.Threshold maximum temperature: Correct — Misting is used to cool the greenhouse, so a maximum temperature threshold should trigger the solenoid valve.
choiceExplanations.Threshold maximum absolute value of soil: Soil tension relates to irrigation of the root zone, not overhead misting.
choiceExplanations.Threshold maximum relative humidity: Misting raises humidity; a maximum relative humidity would stop misting rather than start it.
choiceExplanations.Threshold maximum atmospheric pressure: Atmospheric pressure does not control misting.

items.question: In applying both Kick's law and Rittinger's law, which statement is correct?
items.answer: Both concern the estimation of energy for crushing a material
items.rationale: Both Kick's law (energy proportional to volume reduction ratio) and Rittinger's law (energy proportional to newly created surface area) are comminution laws used to estimate the energy required to crush or grind materials.
choices: Both concern the estimation of energy for crushing a material
Kick's law concerns energy, Rittinger's law concerns power
Both concern the volume estimation of bioprocess material
Kick's law is about volume, Rittinger's law is about density

choiceExplanations.Both concern the estimation of energy fo: Correct — Both laws estimate energy for crushing and grinding; Kick relates it to size ratio, Rittinger to new surface area.
choiceExplanations.Kick's law concerns energy, Rittinger's: Both laws give energy; Rittinger's law is not about power.
choiceExplanations.Both concern the volume estimation of bi: Neither law estimates volume of bioprocess material.
choiceExplanations.Kick's law is about volume, Rittinger's: Neither law is about volume or density; both give crushing energy.

items.question: In refrigeration, ________ is a measure of efficiency that indicates how much cooling is delivered for each unit of energy consumed.
items.rationale: The Coefficient of Performance (COP) is defined as the ratio of cooling delivered (heat removed) to the energy consumed (work input) by the refrigeration system.

choiceExplanations.Coefficient of Performance (COP): Correct — COP is the cooling delivered per unit of energy input.
choiceExplanations.Coefficient of Freezing: Coefficient of freezing is not a standard refrigeration term.
choiceExplanations.Coefficient of Refrigeration: Coefficient of refrigeration is not the standard term for this measure.
choiceExplanations.Coefficient of Cooling: Coefficient of cooling is not the standard term for this measure.

items.question: A supplier proposes using low-cost, uncalibrated soil moisture sensors for an automated irrigation project. As the project engineer, how would you judge the suitability of these sensors for long-term field use?
items.answer: Suitable only if calibrated, validated, and used with redundancy/quality checks
items.rationale: Low-cost sensors can only provide reliable long-term irrigation control if they are properly calibrated for the site's soil, validated against reference readings, and paired with redundancy and ongoing quality checks.
choices: Fully suitable, savings on cost justify use
Suitable without calibration if placed in many locations
Always unsuitable, it's just a bunch of disposable sensors
Suitable only if calibrated, validated, and used with redundancy/quality checks

choiceExplanations.Fully suitable, savings on cost justify: Low cost alone does not make a sensor reliable; wrong readings would waste water or harm crops.
choiceExplanations.Suitable without calibration if placed i: Placing many uncalibrated sensors does not remove their systematic errors; readings can all be wrong in the same way.
choiceExplanations.Always unsuitable, it's just a bunch of: Cheap sensors are not always unsuitable; with calibration and checks they can give acceptable data.
choiceExplanations.Suitable only if calibrated, validated,: Correct — Low-cost sensors can be used only if calibrated, validated and backed by redundancy and quality checks to ensure reliable readings.

items.question: Applying the PAES 289:2009 standard, what should be your design superelevation when the travelling speed is 30 kph?
items.rationale: Under the PAES geometric design specifications for farm-to-market roads, a design speed of 30 kph requires a design superelevation in the range of 5.0–6.4%.

choiceExplanations.6.8–7.6%: 6.8-7.6% is higher than the PAES 289:2009 superelevation range for 30 kph.
choiceExplanations.5.0–6.4%: Correct — PAES 289:2009 gives a design superelevation of 5.0 to 6.4% for a travelling speed of 30 kph.
choiceExplanations.6.6–7.5%: 6.6-7.5% is higher than the PAES 289:2009 range for 30 kph.
choiceExplanations.7.8–8.0%: 7.8-8.0% is near the maximum, used for much higher speeds, not 30 kph.

items.question: A vegetable processing plant gets 1,000 tonnes daily of its raw materials from Locality 1, a municipality in Mindanao. The finished product is 28% of the total raw materials. Applying the Material Index as the basis for plant location, where should the processing plant be placed?
items.rationale: Material Index MI = (raw material weight) / (finished product weight) = 1,000 / (0.28 × 1,000) = 3.57; because MI > 1 (a weight-losing process), the plant should be located near the raw material source (Locality 1).

choiceExplanations.Near the product distributors: Material Index is 1000/280 = 3.6, above 1, so a plant near distributors is not indicated.
choiceExplanations.Near the mother company: The mother company's location does not enter the Material Index decision.
choiceExplanations.Near the market: A Material Index above 1 means raw materials lose weight in processing, so the market is not the best site.
choiceExplanations.Near Locality 1: Correct — Material Index = weight of raw materials / weight of finished product = 1000/280 = 3.6, more than 1, so locate near the raw material source.

items.question: Value adding on farm products is carried out to increase market value, extend shelf life, and reduce the _________ of farm harvests.
items.rationale: Value-adding operations process perishable farm commodities into more stable products, increasing market value, extending shelf life, and reducing post-harvest losses.

choiceExplanations.Processing cost: Value adding does not mainly aim to reduce processing cost; it often adds cost.
choiceExplanations.Processing time: Value adding does not aim at cutting processing time.
choiceExplanations.Post-harvest losses: Correct — Value adding increases market value and shelf life and reduces post-harvest losses of farm harvests.
choiceExplanations.Non-marketable components: Non-marketable components are not the main target; value adding turns produce into marketable products.

items.question: Your agency is experimenting on the effect of microclimate in the production of red bell pepper inside an automated greenhouse. What important microclimatic data should be measured inside the greenhouse?
items.answer: Temperature, relative humidity, and soil temperature
items.rationale: Air temperature, relative humidity, and soil temperature are the essential greenhouse microclimatic parameters governing crop transpiration, fruit set, and root-zone activity (whereas rainfall depth is excluded inside a covered greenhouse).
choices: Temperature, relative humidity, and soil temperature

choiceExplanations.Soil moisture and soil temperature: Soil moisture and soil temperature leave out air temperature and humidity, which are key microclimate data.
choiceExplanations.Rainfall depth and relative humidity: Rainfall does not occur inside a greenhouse, so it is not a microclimate measure there.
choiceExplanations.Maximum and instantaneous air temperatur: Maximum and instantaneous air temperatures alone leave out humidity and soil temperature.
choiceExplanations.Temperature, relative humidity, and soil: Correct — Greenhouse microclimate includes air temperature, relative humidity and soil temperature, the keyed data to measure.

items.question: A chiller provides 400 kWh of cooling for 1 hour and uses 100 kWh of electricity for the same duration. Determine the COP.
items.rationale: COP = Cooling Output / Energy Input = 400 kWh / 100 kWh = 4.

choiceExplanations.1: COP of 1 would mean cooling equal to the electricity used, but 400/100 is higher.
choiceExplanations.5: COP of 5 is not the result; 400 divided by 100 is 4.
choiceExplanations.10: COP of 10 is not the result; 400 divided by 100 is 4.
choiceExplanations.4: Correct — COP = cooling effect / energy input = 400 kWh / 100 kWh = 4.

items.question: Applying the Material Index as the location basis for a fruit processing plant, if the raw materials are sourced from 5 municipalities and the heaviest daily raw material from any single municipality is less than the daily weight of the finished goods, the processing plant should be placed near the _______.
items.rationale: When the finished product weighs more than the raw material transported from any single source municipality (MI < 1 per source), total transport cost is minimized by locating the plant near the market.

choiceExplanations.Mother company: The mother company's location is not a Material Index criterion.
choiceExplanations.Market: Correct — If the heaviest raw material from any one source is less than the finished goods weight, the plant is placed near the market.
choiceExplanations.Product distributors: Product distributors are not the Material Index choice for this case.
choiceExplanations.Source of raw materials: Locating at the raw material source is for when raw materials are heavier than the finished goods.

items.question: What is a piece of milled rice grain whose length is equal to or greater than 3/4 of the mean length of the whole kernels?
items.rationale: By definition in rice milling standards, head rice consists of whole kernels and milled kernels whose length is at least 3/4 (75%) of the average length of the whole kernels.

choiceExplanations.Polished rice: Polished rice is milled rice with the bran polished off; it does not describe kernel length.
choiceExplanations.Broken rice: Broken rice is kernels shorter than 3/4 of the whole kernel length, the opposite.
choiceExplanations.Milled rice: Milled rice is any rice with hull and bran removed, whole or broken.
choiceExplanations.Head rice: Correct — Head rice is milled rice whose kernel length is at least 3/4 of the average whole kernel length.

items.question: Compute the apparent air velocity in a 1.2-tonne capacity flat-bed dryer with a 2.9 m × 2.5 m rectangular bin if the airflow rate is 100 m³/min.
items.rationale: Apparent air velocity V = Q / A = (100 m³/min) / (2.9 m × 2.5 m) = 100 / 7.25 = 13.79 m/min ≈ 13.8 m/min.

choiceExplanations.14.3 m/min: 14.3 m/min does not match the airflow divided by bin area.
choiceExplanations.13.8 m/min: Correct — Apparent air velocity = airflow / bin area = 100 / (2.9 x 2.5) = 13.8 m/min.
choiceExplanations.15.3 m/min: 15.3 m/min does not match the airflow divided by bin area.
choiceExplanations.13.5 m/min: 13.5 m/min does not match the airflow divided by bin area.

items.question: A gravity dam has a water height of 30 m from its base. A 981 kN horizontal water force is exerted against the 100-cm central section of the dam, which weighs 9,810 kN. Neglecting uplift force due to seepage, what is the total moment at the base of the dam where the line of gravity passes?
items.rationale: The hydrostatic force acts at 1/3 of the water depth above the base (30 m / 3 = 10 m), while the dam's weight acts through the line of gravity (moment arm = 0 m); thus M = (981 kN × 10 m) + (9,810 kN × 0 m) = 9,810 kN·m.

choiceExplanations.9,810 kN·m: Correct — The water force acts at H/3 = 10 m, giving 981 x 10 = 9,810 kN-m; the weight acts through the reference line and gives no moment.
choiceExplanations.981 kN·m: 981 kN-m would result from using an arm of 1 m, not the 10 m at one-third of the height.
choiceExplanations.981,000 kN·m: 981,000 kN-m is far too large; it is not 981 times 10 times 100.
choiceExplanations.98,100 kN·m: 98,100 kN-m would use a 100 m arm; the correct arm is 10 m.

items.question: A few months after taking oath as a licensed AB engineer, you are entrusted to design a primary processing plant for fresh vegetable in your locality. What must be the minimum width of the doors, based on Philippine agricultural engineering standards?
items.rationale: Based on PAES 418:2002 (Primary Processing Plant for Fresh Fruit and Vegetable), doors shall have a minimum width of 1.5 m to allow unimpeded movement of personnel, carts, and produce.

choiceExplanations.2 m: 2 m is wider than the minimum required in the standard.
choiceExplanations.2.5 m: 2.5 m is wider than the minimum required in the standard.
choiceExplanations.1 m: 1 m is narrower than the minimum door width in the standard.
choiceExplanations.1.5 m: Correct — The standard (PAES 418) requires a minimum door width of 1.5 m in a primary processing plant for fresh produce.

items.question: If you are tasked of evaluating plans on the methods of waste disposal from an agricultural processing plant, the waste disposal plans should be based on what law or laws?
items.rationale: Agricultural processing plants produce solid wastes, wastewater, and air emissions, so waste disposal plans must comply with RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act), RA 9275 (Philippine Clean Water Act), and RA 8749 (Philippine Clean Air Act).
choices: 300 kg/h Pcake = Weight of resulting cake produced Total time

choiceExplanations.RA 8749: RA 8749 is the Clean Air Act only, so it covers just air pollution.
choiceExplanations.RA 9003, RA 9275, and RA 8749: Correct — Waste disposal plans must follow RA 9003 (solid waste), RA 9275 (clean water) and RA 8749 (clean air).
choiceExplanations.300 kg/h Pcake = Weight of resulting cak: This choice is a stray formula text for cake output, not a law.
choiceExplanations.RA 9275: RA 9275 is the Clean Water Act only, so it covers just water pollution.

items.question: For a refrigerator, COP is the ratio of heat removed from the _________ to the work input in doing the cooling process.
items.rationale: By thermodynamic definition, a refrigerator's Coefficient of Performance is COP = Q_L / W_in, the ratio of heat removed from the cold reservoir (refrigerated space) to the net work input.

choiceExplanations.Condenser: The condenser is where heat is rejected, not where heat is removed.
choiceExplanations.Material being refrigerated: The material being refrigerated is the load; the heat is removed from the cold space or reservoir in the COP definition.
choiceExplanations.Cold reservoir: Correct — COP of a refrigerator is the heat removed from the cold reservoir divided by the work input.
choiceExplanations.Refrigerant: The refrigerant carries the heat; it is not the reservoir that heat is removed from.

items.question: Your business needs to implement optimization of a vegetable cold storage facility which has a current utilization coefficient of 0.41. Charge is based on the volume and duration of storage. If the utilization coefficient is increased to 0.52, what is the effect in revenue?
items.rationale: Increasing the utilization coefficient from 0.41 to 0.52 allows a greater volume of vegetables to be stored per unit time within the same facility, which directly increases volume-and-duration-based revenue.

choiceExplanations.Same: Revenue does not stay the same, since more space is used.
choiceExplanations.Decrease significantly: Revenue does not fall, because a higher utilization means more stored volume billed.
choiceExplanations.Decrease slightly: Revenue does not fall, because a higher utilization means more stored volume billed.
choiceExplanations.Increase: Correct — Charges depend on volume and storage time; higher utilization means more volume stored, so revenue increases.

items.question: As an ABE, you are to tasked by your company to implement a fruit cold storage project. Based on your judgement, what is the appropriate range of storage utilization coefficient for your cold storage project?
items.rationale: In cold storage design, an appropriate storage utilization coefficient is 0.4 to 0.6 (40% to 60%) to provide sufficient space for aisles, pallet clearances, and proper cold-air circulation.

choiceExplanations.0.7 to 0.8: 0.7-0.8 is higher than the usual range for a fruit cold store.
choiceExplanations.0.4 to 0.6: Correct — The appropriate storage utilization coefficient for a cold storage is about 0.4 to 0.6.
choiceExplanations.0.2 to 0.3: 0.2-0.3 is too low for a good design.
choiceExplanations.0.8 to 0.9: 0.8-0.9 is higher than the usual range for a fruit cold store.

items.question: If the refrigeration effect is 1,150 kW and the electricity input is 225 kW, applying the COP formula, determine the Coefficient of Performance of the refrigeration system.
items.rationale: Applying COP = Refrigeration effect / Electrical input gives 1,150 kW / 225 kW = 5.11, or approximately 5.1.

choiceExplanations.0.015: 0.015 is wrong; it does not result from dividing 1,150 by 225.
choiceExplanations.0.051: 0.051 is wrong; it is not 1,150 divided by 225.
choiceExplanations.5.1: Correct — COP = refrigeration effect / work input = 1,150 / 225 = 5.1.
choiceExplanations.1.5: 1.5 is wrong; 1,150 divided by 225 is about 5.1.

items.question: In order to greatly reduce the specific heat of a bioprocessing liquid material, what will you do to the liquid material?
items.rationale: Vaporizing a liquid into its vapor/gas phase eliminates strong intermolecular liquid interactions (such as hydrogen bonding in water), greatly reducing its specific heat (e.g., from ~4.18 kJ/kg·°C for liquid water to ~2.0 kJ/kg·°C for steam).

choiceExplanations.Vaporize: Correct — Vaporizing the liquid into steam greatly lowers specific heat (steam about 2 kJ/kg-K versus water 4.18).
choiceExplanations.Freeze: Freezing lowers specific heat only partly (ice about 2.1) and is not the keyed answer for a liquid.
choiceExplanations.Heat up: Heating up does not reduce the specific heat of a liquid.
choiceExplanations.Place in a cooler: Cooling in a cooler does not greatly reduce specific heat.

items.question: You are to design a primary processing plant for fresh fruit in your locality. The window ledges must be sloped at what angle to prevent the accumulation of dirt, water, or debris based on standards?
items.rationale: Under PAES 418:2002 (Primary Processing Plant for Fresh Fruit and Vegetable), window ledges must be sloped at about 45 degrees to prevent the accumulation of dirt, water, or debris.

choiceExplanations.About 50 degrees: About 50 degrees is not the standard slope for window ledges.
choiceExplanations.About 65 degrees: About 65 degrees is not the standard slope for window ledges.
choiceExplanations.About 30 degrees: About 30 degrees is not steep enough, per the standard.
choiceExplanations.About 45 degrees: Correct — Window ledges are sloped about 45 degrees to prevent dirt, water or debris from accumulating.

items.question: In proper sequence, summarize the process of producing engineered bamboo. The engineered bamboo manufacturing process requires these steps: (1) splitting the bamboo culms into strips or crushing them into fibers, (2) treating them with ___________, and (3) hot-pressing them under high pressure to create dense, uniform panels or beams.
items.rationale: After splitting or crushing bamboo into strips or fibers, the material is treated with adhesives (resins) so it can be bonded under high temperature and pressure during hot-pressing; preservative treatment is carried out prior to or separately from the bonding step.

choiceExplanations.Pesticides: Pesticides protect against pests but do not bond strips into panels.
choiceExplanations.Preservatives: Preservatives protect against decay but do not bond strips into panels.
choiceExplanations.Adhesives: Correct — Bamboo strips or fibers are treated with adhesives (resin) and then hot-pressed to form dense panels or beams.
choiceExplanations.Borax: Borax is a preservative against insects and fungi, not the bonding agent.

items.question: Apply the calculated Material Index in selecting the location of a certain fruit processing plant. If the raw materials are sourced in a single locality and are heavier than the finished goods daily, the processing plant should be placed near the ___________ .
items.rationale: When localized raw materials outweigh finished products (Material Index > 1, a weight-losing process), locating the plant near the source of raw materials minimizes total transport weight and cost.

choiceExplanations.Source of raw materials: Correct — If raw materials are sourced from one locality and are heavier than finished goods, place the plant near the raw material source.
choiceExplanations.Product distributors: Product distributors are not the Material Index choice here.
choiceExplanations.Mother company: The mother company's location is not a Material Index criterion.
choiceExplanations.Market: Near the market is for cases where finished goods weigh more than the raw materials.

items.question: Implementing a Rice Processing Center (RPC) was assigned to you for carrying out immediately. The RPC will have a capacity of 15 tonnes paddy rice per hour, operating whole year round during both sunny and rainy days at all levels of relative humidity outside the processing center. What rice dryer will you use?
items.rationale: A 15 tonnes/hour, year-round, all-weather Rice Processing Center requires mechanical recirculating dryers to deliver high-throughput, uniform drying regardless of rain or ambient relative humidity.

choiceExplanations.Recirculating dryer: Correct — A recirculating dryer handles large tonnages continuously, works in all weather and humidity, so it fits a 15 t/h plant year-round.
choiceExplanations.Biomass-kerosene fired dryer: A biomass-kerosene fired dryer names a fuel type, not a dryer suited to 15 t/h continuous year-round use.
choiceExplanations.Sun dryer: A sun dryer depends on sunshine and cannot work on rainy days or at 15 t/h.
choiceExplanations.Batch dryer: A batch dryer holds a fixed load and is too small and slow for 15 t/h.

items.question: "microorganism capable of causing diseases"

choiceExplanations.Probiotic microorganism: A probiotic microorganism is beneficial to health, not disease-causing.
choiceExplanations.Thermophilic microorganism: A thermophilic microorganism grows at high temperatures; it says nothing about causing disease.
choiceExplanations.Saprophytic microorganism: A saprophytic microorganism feeds on dead matter and generally does not cause disease.
choiceExplanations.Pathogenic microorganism: Correct — A pathogenic microorganism is capable of causing disease.

items.question: "process of making any material entirely free from living microorganism"

choiceExplanations.Sanitization: Sanitization reduces microbes to safe levels but does not remove all of them.
choiceExplanations.Sterilization: Correct — Sterilization makes a material completely free of all living microorganisms.
choiceExplanations.Pasteurization: Pasteurization kills disease-causing microbes with mild heat but not all microorganisms.
choiceExplanations.Blanching: Blanching is brief heating to stop enzymes; it does not make material free of microorganisms.

items.question: Microorganisms are capable of growth over a wide range of temperatures. / Temperature is used to categorized microorganisms. Those capable of growth at 5°C, some are able to grow at temperature as slow as -5°C and are the primary cause of spoilage of perishable foods are called

choiceExplanations.Psychrotrops: Correct — Psychrotrophs grow at 5 C and even down to about -5 C, and are the main spoilers of refrigerated foods.
choiceExplanations.Hyperthermophiles: Hyperthermophiles grow at extremely high temperatures, not in the cold.
choiceExplanations.Thermophiles: Thermophiles grow at high temperatures (about 45-70 C), not in the cold.
choiceExplanations.Mesophiles: Mesophiles grow best at moderate temperatures (about 20-45 C), not at refrigerator temperatures.

items.question: A storage method wherein the gas concentration in storage atmosphere is changed

choiceExplanations.Modified atmosphere: Correct — Modified atmosphere storage changes the gas concentration (more CO2, less O2) around the stored product.
choiceExplanations.Evaporative cooling: Evaporative cooling cools by evaporating water and does not change the gas composition.
choiceExplanations.Ambient storage: Ambient storage uses the surrounding conditions with no change in gases.

items.question: A process of segregating alcohol, sugar, and some soluble materials with use of water

choiceExplanations.Distillation: Distillation separates liquids by boiling point, not by dissolving with water.
choiceExplanations.Sedimentation: Sedimentation settles solids out of a liquid by gravity.
choiceExplanations.Leaching: Correct — Leaching uses water to dissolve and separate soluble materials like sugar and alcohol from a solid.
choiceExplanations.Centrifugation: Centrifugation separates by spinning, not by dissolving soluble parts in water.

items.question: Pump commonly used in food processing industry

choiceExplanations.Axial flow pump: An axial flow pump moves large volumes at low head, but is not the common food processing pump.
choiceExplanations.Reciprocating piston pump: A reciprocating piston pump pulses and is harder to clean, so it is less common in food plants.
choiceExplanations.Jet ejector pump: A jet ejector pump uses a fluid jet, mainly for utility use, not typical food product pumping.
choiceExplanations.Rotary displacement pump: Correct — Rotary displacement pumps (lobe, gear) give gentle, smooth, sanitary flow, so they are common in food processing.

items.question: It is the process of decomposition of carbohydrates by microorganism or enzyme
items.source: Area 3 objectives; area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Putrefaction: Putrefaction is the breakdown of proteins by microbes, not carbohydrates.
choiceExplanations.Caramelization: Caramelization is browning of sugar by heat, with no microorganisms or enzymes.
choiceExplanations.Rancidification: Rancidification is the breakdown of fats and oils, not carbohydrates.
choiceExplanations.Fermentation: Correct — Fermentation is the decomposition of carbohydrates by microorganisms or enzymes, giving alcohol or acids.

items.question: Substances used to prevent food by retarding deterioration, rancidity, or discoloration due to oxidation

choiceExplanations.Emulsifiers: Emulsifiers help oil and water mix; they do not stop oxidation.
choiceExplanations.Stabilizers: Stabilizers keep texture and consistency; they do not stop oxidation.
choiceExplanations.Antioxidants: Correct — Antioxidants slow deterioration, rancidity and discoloration caused by oxidation.
choiceExplanations.Humectants: Humectants hold moisture in food; they do not prevent oxidation.

items.question: Substances that modify surface tension in the component phase of an emulsion to establish a uniform dispersion

choiceExplanations.Emulsifiers: Correct — Emulsifiers lower surface tension between phases of an emulsion so they stay evenly dispersed.
choiceExplanations.Antioxidants: Antioxidants prevent oxidation and do not modify surface tension.
choiceExplanations.Humectants: Humectants hold moisture and do not modify surface tension.
choiceExplanations.Preservatives: Preservatives stop spoilage by microbes and do not stabilize emulsions.

items.question: Canning temp. For fruits, tomatoes, and pickles in water bath canner

choiceExplanations.110 deg C: 110 deg C is above the boiling point of water at normal pressure, so a water bath cannot reach it.
choiceExplanations.100 deg C: Correct — A water bath canner works at boiling water temperature, 100 deg C, enough for high-acid foods like fruit and pickles.
choiceExplanations.90 deg C: 90 deg C is below the boiling point reached in a water bath canner.
choiceExplanations.80 deg C: 80 deg C is below the boiling point reached in a water bath canner.

items.question: Canning temp. For low-acid vegetables, meat and poultry in pressure canner

choiceExplanations.115 deg C: Correct — Low-acid foods are processed in a pressure canner at about 115 deg C (about 10 psi) to destroy spores.
choiceExplanations.104 deg C: 104 deg C is too low for low-acid foods; it is not hot enough for sterilization.
choiceExplanations.92 deg C: 92 deg C is too low for low-acid foods.
choiceExplanations.127 deg C: 127 deg C is higher than the keyed pressure canning temperature.

items.question: Freezing point of milk

choiceExplanations.-.501 C: -0.501 C is not the standard freezing point of milk.
choiceExplanations.-.463 C: -0.463 C is not the standard freezing point of milk.
choiceExplanations.-.545 C: Correct — The freezing point of milk is about -0.545 C, slightly below that of water because of dissolved solids.
choiceExplanations.-.600 C: -0.600 C is not the standard freezing point of milk.

items.question: It is the process which is the result of diffusion from region of high concentration to region of low concentration.

choiceExplanations.Momentum transfer: Momentum transfer moves momentum through viscous action, not by concentration difference.
choiceExplanations.Mass transfer: Correct — Mass transfer is movement of a substance by diffusion from high concentration to low concentration.
choiceExplanations.Heat transfer: Heat transfer moves energy due to temperature difference, not concentration.
choiceExplanations.Energy transfer: Energy transfer is a general term and does not describe diffusion of matter by concentration.

items.question: AE Road Map: one of the objective of AE Road Map is to produce _________ new registered and licensed agricultural engineers in the next 8 years.

choiceExplanations.12,200: 12,200 is not the AE Roadmap target number.
choiceExplanations.8,800: 8,800 is not the AE Roadmap target number.
choiceExplanations.10,000: Correct — The AE Road Map targets 10,000 new registered and licensed agricultural engineers in 8 years.
choiceExplanations.10,800: 10,800 is not the AE Roadmap target number.

items.question: Organization established to create standards on food and founded on 1963
items.answer: FDA (Food and Drug Administration or Bureau of Food and Drugs by Rep. Act. 3720)
choices: BAFS (Bureau of Agriculture and Fisheries Standards under Rep. Act. 8435)
FNRI (Food and Nutrition Research Institute under Exec. Order 128)
NFA (National Food Authority created under Presidential Decree No. 4)
FDA (Food and Drug Administration or Bureau of Food and Drugs by Rep. Act. 3720)

choiceExplanations.BAFS (Bureau of Agriculture and Fisherie: BAFS develops agricultural and fishery product standards under RA 8435 and was not founded in 1963.
choiceExplanations.FNRI (Food and Nutrition Research Instit: FNRI does nutrition research under EO 128; it does not set food standards.
choiceExplanations.NFA (National Food Authority created und: NFA handles rice and grain stocks and price; it is not a food standards body.
choiceExplanations.FDA (Food and Drug Administration or Bur: Correct — The FDA (formerly Bureau of Food and Drugs) was created by RA 3720 in 1963 to set food standards.

items.question: Location of the rain gages are plotted on the map of the area and stations are connected by straight lines?

choiceExplanations.Hypsometric method: The hypsometric method relates area and elevation, not rain gage station lines.
choiceExplanations.Arithmetic mean: Arithmetic mean averages gage readings without plotting polygons.
choiceExplanations.Thiessen polygon: Correct — The Thiessen polygon method connects stations by straight lines and draws perpendicular bisectors, forming polygons for weighted rainfall.
choiceExplanations.Isohyetal method: The isohyetal method draws lines of equal rainfall, not lines between stations.

items.question: Food preservation technique without the use of heat
items.source: RECALLED COMPRESS; area 3 non problem solving CPU,recalled

choiceExplanations.Retort canning: Retort canning uses high heat to sterilize.
choiceExplanations.Cold pasteurization: Correct — Cold pasteurization, such as high pressure or irradiation, preserves food without using heat.
choiceExplanations.Hot blanching: Hot blanching uses hot water or steam.
choiceExplanations.Thermal sterilization: Thermal sterilization uses heat by definition.

items.question: A method of measuring evaporation that uses climatological data

choiceExplanations.Blaney-Cridle: Correct — The Blaney-Criddle method estimates evaporation or evapotranspiration from climatological data such as temperature and daylight.
choiceExplanations.Evaporation pan: An evaporation pan measures evaporation directly in the field, not by climate data.
choiceExplanations.Weighing lysimeter: A weighing lysimeter measures water loss directly by weight change.
choiceExplanations.Water balance: The water balance method computes evaporation from inflow, outflow and storage change, not climate data.

items.question: What is meant by HACCP
items.answer: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point
choices: Health Analysis and Critical Contamination Point
Hazard Assessment and Critical Control Plan
Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point
Hazard Awareness and Critical Control Procedure

choiceExplanations.Health Analysis and Critical Contaminati: HACCP does not stand for Health Analysis and Critical Contamination Point.
choiceExplanations.Hazard Assessment and Critical Control P: HACCP does not stand for Hazard Assessment and Critical Control Plan.
choiceExplanations.Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Poi: Correct — HACCP means Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point, a food safety system.
choiceExplanations.Hazard Awareness and Critical Control Pr: HACCP does not stand for Hazard Awareness and Critical Control Procedure.

items.question: To produce safe and best quality food products, aside from Sanitation Standard Operating Procedures (SSOP) which of the following theories and principles will you employ in all aspects of food production, handling and distribution?

choiceExplanations.GMP, EMP and HACCP: Correct — Good Manufacturing Practice, Environmental Management Plan and HACCP are the principles applied in food production, handling and distribution.
choiceExplanations.GHP, JIT and LIFO: GHP, JIT and LIFO include inventory methods that are not food safety principles.
choiceExplanations.TQM, ERP and FIFO: TQM, ERP and FIFO include business and inventory tools that are not food safety principles.
choiceExplanations.GAP, MRP and CPM: GAP, MRP and CPM include planning tools that are not food safety principles.

items.question: The audits for Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) are carried out by ________.

choiceExplanations.Retail consumer association: A retail consumer association is not an authorized HACCP auditor.
choiceExplanations.Internal production supervisor: An internal production supervisor is not independent enough for HACCP certification audits.
choiceExplanations.Third-party audit organization: Correct — HACCP audits are carried out by an independent third-party audit organization.
choiceExplanations.Raw material supplier: A raw material supplier is not an independent auditor and has an interest in the result.

items.question: The seven principles of HACCP are: (1) hazard analysis, (2) critical control point identification, (3) establishment of critical limits, (4) monitoring procedures, (5) corrective actions, (6) _____________, and (7) record keeping and documentation.

choiceExplanations.Verification procedures: Correct — The sixth HACCP principle is establishing verification procedures to confirm the system works.
choiceExplanations.Sanitation procedures: Sanitation procedures belong to prerequisite programs, not the seven HACCP principles.
choiceExplanations.Calibration procedures: Calibration procedures are not one of the seven HACCP principles.
choiceExplanations.Recall procedures: Recall procedures are not one of the seven HACCP principles.

items.question: The thermal conductivity of bioprocessed material is _________ with increasing solids concentration and increasing as the temperature is raised from 30 C to 50 C.

choiceExplanations.Fluctuating: Fluctuating does not describe the steady trend of thermal conductivity with solids.
choiceExplanations.Increasing: Increasing is wrong; thermal conductivity increases with temperature but falls as solids rise.
choiceExplanations.Decreasing: Correct — Thermal conductivity decreases with increasing solids, since water, a better conductor, is replaced by solids.
choiceExplanations.Stabilizing: Stabilizing is not the trend; it falls with more solids.

items.question: The temperature effect on the thermal conductivity of bioprocessed material is less pronounced at higher ______.

choiceExplanations.Solids concentration: Correct — The effect of temperature on thermal conductivity is less pronounced at higher solids concentration.
choiceExplanations.Moisture content: Moisture content is the opposite of solids; the effect is stronger at high moisture.
choiceExplanations.Specific volume: Specific volume is not the factor linked to this effect.
choiceExplanations.Thermal diffusivity: Thermal diffusivity is not the factor linked to this effect.

items.question: The temperature effect on the __________ of bioprocessed material is less pronounced at higher solids concentration.

choiceExplanations.Bulk density: Bulk density is not the property in this statement.
choiceExplanations.Specific gravity: Specific gravity is not the property in this statement.
choiceExplanations.Thermal expansion: Thermal expansion is not the property in this statement.
choiceExplanations.Thermal conductivity: Correct — Temperature affects thermal conductivity less at higher solids concentration.

items.question: Heat can also be transferred by conduction from the ____ to the baked product during the baking process.

choiceExplanations.Baking metal container: Correct — Heat moves by conduction from the hot metal baking container (pan) to the product in contact with it.
choiceExplanations.Circulating hot air: Circulating hot air transfers heat by convection, not conduction.
choiceExplanations.Oven heating element: The oven heating element heats the product by radiation and convection.
