choiceExplanations.Insulated oven wall: The insulated oven wall reduces heat loss and is not a conduction source to the product.

items.question: A bioprocess for meat tenderizing uses hot water. The process requires 326,352 J of heat. Water temperature needs to be raised from 22 C to 100 C or boiling point. Find the volume of water needed. Evaporation loss is negligible.
items.rationale:
[(4.184 J/g°C)(78 °C)] / = 1,000 ml

Notes: 1,000 ml Known parameters: / Heat = 326,352 J c for water = 4.184 J/g °C (constant) / Density of water = 1g/ml (constant) / q = mc (T2-T1) / 326,352 J = m(4.184 J/g°C)(100°C - 22 °C)] / m = 326,352 J /

choiceExplanations.1,000 ml Known parameters:: Correct — Q = m c dT gives m = 326,352 / (4.186 x 78) = about 1,000 g, so about 1,000 ml of water.
choiceExplanations.500 ml Known parameters:: 500 ml gives only half the heat required.
choiceExplanations.1,250 ml Known parameters:: 1,250 ml would supply more heat than needed.

items.question: Of the listed Republic Acts, what is the law that aims to strengthen the food safety regulatory system in the Philippines and to protect consumer health and facilitate market access of local foods and food products and for other purposes.

choiceExplanations.RA 12945: RA 12945 is not the Food Safety Act.
choiceExplanations.RA 11460: RA 11460 is not the Food Safety Act.
choiceExplanations.RA 10611: Correct — RA 10611, the Food Safety Act of 2013, strengthens the food safety regulatory system and protects consumer health.
choiceExplanations.RA 13794: RA 13794 is not the Food Safety Act.

items.question: The R.A. 10611 is also known as ___________.

choiceExplanations.Meat Inspection Code of 2004: The Meat Inspection Code of 2004 is RA 9296, not RA 10611.
choiceExplanations.Organic Agriculture Act of 2010: The Organic Agriculture Act of 2010 is RA 10068, not RA 10611.
choiceExplanations.Food Safety Act of 2013: Correct — RA 10611 is the Food Safety Act of 2013.
choiceExplanations.Food Fortification Act of 2000: The Food Fortification Act of 2000 is RA 8976, not RA 10611.

items.question: In implementing a research program under RA 10611, you should see to it that the Food Development Center under DA shall implement research projects to support science-based food safety _________ and coordinate these projects with the Bureau of Agricultural Research (BAR) and the academe.

choiceExplanations.Policies, standards and regulations: Correct — Under RA 10611 the Food Development Center does research to support science-based food safety policies, standards and regulations.
choiceExplanations.Programs, budgets and incentives: Programs, budgets and incentives are not what the research supports; the law ties research to regulation.
choiceExplanations.Facilities, equipment and personnel: Facilities, equipment and personnel are resources, not outputs of research projects.
choiceExplanations.Inspections, audits and permits: Inspections, audits and permits are enforcement tasks, not research output.

items.question: It is a method by which product and packaging material is sterilized separately and then hermitically sealed in a clean environment.

choiceExplanations.Hot filling: Hot filling puts hot product into already sterilized containers, not sterilizing product and package separately.
choiceExplanations.Retort processing: Retort processing sterilizes the product after it is sealed in the container.
choiceExplanations.Aseptic processing: Correct — Aseptic processing sterilizes the product and the package separately, then fills and seals them in a sterile environment.
choiceExplanations.Vacuum canning: Vacuum canning removes air from the container but does not sterilize product and package separately.

items.question: It is a method that only considers the destruction of pathogenic and spoilage components of food during heat treatment.

choiceExplanations.Freeze Drying: Freeze drying removes water by sublimation; it is not heat treatment.
choiceExplanations.Cold Pasteurization: Cold pasteurization kills microbes without heat.
choiceExplanations.Thermal Processing: Correct — Thermal processing is heat treatment designed to destroy pathogens and spoilage organisms in food.
choiceExplanations.Osmotic Dehydration: Osmotic dehydration removes water using a concentrated solution, not heat.

items.question: What is the standard reference microorganism in the thermal processing industry known for causing food-borne intoxication?

choiceExplanations.Salmonella enterica: Salmonella enterica causes infection rather than intoxication and is not the reference organism for thermal processing.
choiceExplanations.Listeria monocytogenes: Listeria monocytogenes causes infection and is not the standard thermal processing reference.
choiceExplanations.Escherichia coli: Escherichia coli causes infection and is not the standard thermal processing reference.
choiceExplanations.Clostridium botulinum: Correct — Clostridium botulinum, whose toxin causes intoxication, has heat-resistant spores and is the reference organism for sterilization.

items.question: It is a term that describes the required processing time at a specific temperature to inactivate or kill any target spoilage agent within food.

choiceExplanations.Thermal death time: Correct — Thermal death time is the time needed at a given temperature to kill a target microorganism.
choiceExplanations.Heat penetration factor: Heat penetration factor describes how fast heat moves into the food, not killing time.
choiceExplanations.Thermal resistance constant: Thermal resistance constant is not the term for required time at a temperature.
choiceExplanations.Decimal reduction time: Decimal reduction time is the time for a tenfold (90%) reduction, not total kill time.

items.question: The viscosity of ____ decreases with temperature.
items.rationale: For Newtonian and liquid foods such as water, syrup, and milk, raising temperature increases molecular kinetic energy and weakens intermolecular forces, causing viscosity to decrease.

choiceExplanations.All of the choices: Correct — Viscosity of water, milk and syrup all decrease as temperature rises, so all the choices are right.
choiceExplanations.Water: Water's viscosity does decrease with temperature, but so do the others, so it is not the only answer.
choiceExplanations.Milk: Milk's viscosity does decrease with temperature, but so do the others.
choiceExplanations.Syrup: Syrup's viscosity does decrease with temperature, but so do the others.

items.question: The simple refrigeration cycle consists of four main processes: compression, condensation, expansion, and _______.

choiceExplanations.Sublimation: Sublimation is a solid turning to gas, not part of the vapor compression cycle.
choiceExplanations.Dehumidification: Dehumidification removes moisture from air; it is not a cycle process.
choiceExplanations.Evaporation: Correct — The fourth process is evaporation, where the refrigerant absorbs heat and turns into vapor.
choiceExplanations.Regeneration: Regeneration is not a step of the simple refrigeration cycle.

items.question: Based on proven preservation methods for forest products, give the appropriate method to prolong the lifespan of engineered bamboo that is intended for both outdoor and indoor uses.

choiceExplanations.Chemical treatment: Correct — Chemical treatment (such as boron preservatives) protects engineered bamboo against insects and decay indoors and outdoors.
choiceExplanations.Kiln drying: Kiln drying lowers moisture but gives no lasting protection against insects or decay.
choiceExplanations.Air seasoning: Air seasoning only dries the material and does not protect against pests or decay.
choiceExplanations.Surface sanding: Surface sanding smooths the surface and gives no protection.

items.question: The process of strengthening concrete through hydration is known as:

choiceExplanations.Batching: Batching is measuring and proportioning concrete materials.
choiceExplanations.Troweling: Troweling is smoothing the concrete surface.
choiceExplanations.Screeding: Screeding is leveling the freshly placed concrete.
choiceExplanations.Curing: Correct — Curing keeps concrete moist and warm so cement hydration continues and the concrete gains strength.

items.question: Machine used to concentrate milk, fruit, and vegetable juices, jams and jellies by boiling of a portion of the water.

choiceExplanations.Pasteurizer: A pasteurizer heats liquid to kill pathogens, not to concentrate it.
choiceExplanations.Homogenizer: A homogenizer breaks fat globules for uniformity and does not remove water.
choiceExplanations.Evaporator: Correct — An evaporator boils off part of the water to concentrate milk, juices, jams and jellies.
choiceExplanations.Dehydrator: A dehydrator dries food almost completely rather than concentrating it by boiling.

items.question: The ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces. A dimensionless number use to categorize the fluids system in which the effect of viscosity is important in controlling the velocities or the flow pattern of fluid

choiceExplanations.Prandtl Number: The Prandtl number compares momentum and heat diffusion, not inertia and viscosity.
choiceExplanations.Weber Number: The Weber number compares inertial forces with surface tension.
choiceExplanations.Froude Number: The Froude number compares inertial forces with gravity.
choiceExplanations.Reynolds Number: Correct — The Reynolds number is the ratio of inertial to viscous forces and shows if flow is laminar or turbulent.

items.question: system for ensuring that products are consistently produced and controlled according to quality standards
choices: HACCP hazard analysis critical control point

choiceExplanations.GMP good manufacturing practices: Correct — GMP is the system that ensures products are consistently produced and controlled to quality standards.
choiceExplanations.TQM total quality management: TQM is a management approach to continuous improvement, not the production control system defined here.
choiceExplanations.HACCP hazard analysis critical control p: HACCP identifies and controls specific food safety hazards, not general production quality control.
choiceExplanations.SSOP sanitation standard operating proce: SSOP covers sanitation procedures only, not overall production quality.

items.question: what is the last stage in the steps of HACCP

choiceExplanations.Establish monitoring procedures: Establishing monitoring procedures is the fourth principle.
choiceExplanations.Establish corrective actions: Establishing corrective actions is the fifth principle.
choiceExplanations.Establish critical limits: Establishing critical limits is the third principle.
choiceExplanations.Establish record-keeping and documentati: Correct — Record keeping and documentation is the last (seventh) HACCP principle.

items.question: most abundant microorganism in soil

choiceExplanations.Bacteria: Correct — Bacteria are the most abundant microorganisms in soil in number.
choiceExplanations.Protozoa: Protozoa are far fewer than bacteria in soil.
choiceExplanations.Actinomycetes: Actinomycetes are common but less numerous than bacteria.
choiceExplanations.Fungi: Fungi are fewer in number than bacteria, though they have large biomass.

items.question: nematode concentration

choiceExplanations.1: 1 is not the keyed nematode concentration.
choiceExplanations.2: 2 is not the keyed nematode concentration.
choiceExplanations.5: 5 is not the keyed nematode concentration.
choiceExplanations.0: Correct — The keyed nematode concentration is 0 (none).

items.question: are used to identify and map the contours of the ground and existing features on the surface of the earth or slightly above or below the earth’s surface

choiceExplanations.Geodetic survey: A geodetic survey covers large areas accounting for Earth's curvature, not mapping local contours.
choiceExplanations.Topographic survey: Correct — A topographic survey maps ground contours and natural and man-made features on or near the surface.
choiceExplanations.Cadastral survey: A cadastral survey defines property boundaries.
choiceExplanations.Hydrographic survey: A hydrographic survey maps underwater features such as water bodies' depths.

items.question: CROP SCIENCE: Pigeon Pea is high in ______.

choiceExplanations.Cholesterol: Cholesterol is found in animal products, not in pigeon pea.
choiceExplanations.Protein: Correct — Pigeon pea is a legume that is high in protein.
choiceExplanations.Lipids: Lipids are low in pigeon pea.
choiceExplanations.Sodium: Sodium is low in pigeon pea.

items.question: It is a process of destroying most disease-producing microorganisms and limiting fermentation in milk subjected to heating for a definite time at a definite temperature thereafter cooling it immediately

choiceExplanations.Sterilization: Sterilization kills all microorganisms, not just most disease-producing ones.
choiceExplanations.Pasteurization: Correct — Pasteurization heats milk at a set temperature and time to destroy most pathogens and limit fermentation, then cools it quickly.
choiceExplanations.Homogenization: Homogenization breaks fat globules and does not kill microbes.
choiceExplanations.Blanching: Blanching briefly heats vegetables to stop enzymes, not for milk.

items.question: PROCESSING: Movement from Higher Concentration to Lower Concentration

choiceExplanations.Osmosis: Osmosis is movement of water through a semi-permeable membrane, not general movement of substances.
choiceExplanations.Convection: Convection is movement due to bulk fluid flow, not concentration difference.
choiceExplanations.Diffusion: Correct — Diffusion is the movement of a substance from higher to lower concentration.
choiceExplanations.Adsorption: Adsorption is sticking of molecules to a surface, not movement by concentration.

items.question: The most abundant microorganism found in soil

choiceExplanations.Algae: Algae are fewer than bacteria in soil.
choiceExplanations.Fungi: Fungi are fewer in number than bacteria.
choiceExplanations.Bacteria: Correct — Bacteria are the most abundant microorganisms in soil by number.
choiceExplanations.Actinomycetes: Actinomycetes are less abundant than bacteria.

items.question: The features of topographic map which is the line connecting the lowest elevations between two adjacent ridges

choiceExplanations.Ridge: Wrong — a ridge connects the highest points, the opposite of what is asked.
choiceExplanations.Saddle: Wrong — a saddle is the low point on a ridge between two summits.
choiceExplanations.Contour: Wrong — a contour connects points of equal elevation.
choiceExplanations.Valley (drainage line): Correct — the line through the lowest points between two ridges is the valley or drainage line, where streams flow.

items.question: The features of topographic map which shows the low area between two adjacent hills

choiceExplanations.Ridge: A ridge is a high line, the opposite of a low area.
choiceExplanations.Valley: Correct — A valley is the low area between two adjacent hills.
choiceExplanations.Spur: A spur is a short ridge sticking out from a main ridge.
choiceExplanations.Cliff: A cliff is a very steep or vertical slope, not a low area.

items.question: Milk where the butterfat is replaced with vegetable fat such as coconut fat

choiceExplanations.Filled milk: Correct — Filled milk has its butterfat replaced by vegetable fat such as coconut fat.
choiceExplanations.Reconstituted milk: Reconstituted milk is made by adding water to milk powder.
choiceExplanations.Skim milk: Skim milk has the fat removed but no vegetable fat added.
choiceExplanations.Condensed milk: Condensed milk is concentrated milk with sugar added, not filled with vegetable fat.

items.question: Fresh milk concentrated to 73.7% water. It contains 7% protein, 7.9% fat, 9.9% lactose, and 1.5% minerals.
items.rationale: Evaporated milk is whole milk concentrated by removing about 60% of its water, with no added sugar: about 73.8% water, 7% protein, 7.9% fat, 9.9% lactose.

choiceExplanations.Powdered milk: Wrong — powdered milk is dried to only about 2–5% water.
choiceExplanations.Reconstituted milk: Wrong — reconstituted milk is powder mixed back with water, about 87% water like fresh milk.
choiceExplanations.Condensed milk: Wrong — sweetened condensed milk has added sugar and only about 27% water.
choiceExplanations.Evaporated milk: Correct — evaporated milk is unsweetened concentrated milk with about 73.7% water, matching this composition.

items.question: dried milk obtained by evaporating the moisture from the milk solids

choiceExplanations.Reconstituted or recombined milk: Reconstituted milk is made by adding water back to dried milk, not drying it.
choiceExplanations.Dried or powdered milk: Correct — Dried or powdered milk is made by evaporating the moisture from milk solids.
choiceExplanations.Evaporated or concentrated milk: Evaporated milk still contains much water and is not dry.
choiceExplanations.Condensed or sweetened milk: Condensed milk is thick sweetened milk with water, not dried.

items.question: Black crude oil has _ viscosity.

choiceExplanations.Lower: Lower viscosity is wrong; crude oil is thick and flows slowly.
choiceExplanations.Constant: Constant viscosity is wrong because viscosity differs between fluids and changes with temperature.
choiceExplanations.Minimal: Minimal viscosity is wrong; black crude oil is not thin.
choiceExplanations.Higher: Correct — Black crude oil is heavy and thick, so its viscosity is higher than that of lighter oils.

items.question: A systematic preventive approach to food safety and pharmaceutical safety that addresses physical, chemical and biological hazards as a means of prevention rather than finished product inspection

choiceExplanations.Fisma: FISMA is a US information security law and is unrelated to food.
choiceExplanations.Cgmp: cGMP is current good manufacturing practice, a general production quality system, not hazard-based prevention.
choiceExplanations.Haccp: Correct — HACCP is a systematic preventive approach that controls physical, chemical and biological hazards rather than inspecting finished product.
choiceExplanations.Ssop: SSOP covers sanitation procedures only, not all hazards.

items.question: Most critical point in handling milk

choiceExplanations.Homogenization stage: Homogenization breaks fat globules and does not kill pathogens.
choiceExplanations.Clarification stage: Clarification removes visible particles, not microbes.
choiceExplanations.Standardization stage: Standardization adjusts fat content, not safety.
choiceExplanations.Pasteurization stage: Correct — Pasteurization is the critical control point for milk because it kills pathogens.

items.question: is a written document of procedures or programs used to maintain equipment and the environment in a sanitary condition for food processing. It is a step-by-step description of cleaning ang sanitizing procedures and specifies what is to be cleaned
choices: HACCP - hazard analysis critical control point

choiceExplanations.CGMP - current good manufacturing practi: cGMP is a broad quality standard and is not a step-by-step cleaning document.
choiceExplanations.GMP - good manufacturing practice standa: GMP is a general manufacturing standard, not a written cleaning procedure.
choiceExplanations.SSOP - sanitation standard operating pro: Correct — SSOP is the written step-by-step procedure for cleaning and sanitizing equipment and the environment, stating what to clean.
choiceExplanations.HACCP - hazard analysis critical control: HACCP controls food hazards at critical points and is not a cleaning procedure.

items.question: A process or step implemented to prevent adulteration and contamination of products

choiceExplanations.SSOP: Correct — SSOP is the sanitation procedure that prevents adulteration and contamination of products.
choiceExplanations.TQM: TQM is a quality management approach, not a sanitation procedure.
choiceExplanations.HACCP: HACCP controls hazards at critical points; it is not the sanitation step itself.
choiceExplanations.FIFO: FIFO is an inventory method (first in, first out).

items.question: Which process of food irradiation eliminates harmful bacteria without the use of heat?

choiceExplanations.Flash pasteurization: Flash pasteurization uses high heat for a short time.
choiceExplanations.Batch pasteurization: Batch pasteurization heats milk in a vat.
choiceExplanations.Cold pasteurization: Correct — Cold pasteurization (such as irradiation) kills harmful bacteria without heat.
choiceExplanations.Ultra pasteurization: Ultra pasteurization uses very high heat.

items.question: The measure of the thinness or thickness of the consistency of the fluid foods is referred to as food _________.
items.rationale: Food viscosity quantifies a fluid food's internal resistance to flow, indicating how thin or thick its consistency is.

choiceExplanations.Viscosity: Correct — Viscosity measures how thin or thick a fluid food is.
choiceExplanations.Consistency: Consistency is a general descriptive term, not the specific measure of thickness.
choiceExplanations.Fluidity: Fluidity is the opposite (ease of flow), the reciprocal of viscosity.
choiceExplanations.Liquiditty: Liquidity is not a measure of fluid food thickness.

items.question: Apply food viscosity unit conversion. Determine the centipoise (cP) equivalent of 3 Pascals-second.
items.rationale: Using the conversion factor 1 Pa·s = 1,000 cP, 3 Pa·s × (1,000 cP / 1 Pa·s) = 3,000 cP.

choiceExplanations.30: 30 is not correct; 1 Pa-s equals 1000 cP.
choiceExplanations.3000: Correct — 1 Pa-s = 1000 cP, so 3 Pa-s = 3000 cP.

items.question: Applying the principle of thermal conductivity, the effect of temperature on the thermal conductivity of a bioprocessed material is less pronounced at ______ solids concentration.
items.rationale: Because water's thermal conductivity varies strongly with temperature while solid food components are much less temperature-sensitive, higher solids concentration diminishes the overall temperature effect on thermal conductivity.

choiceExplanations.Higher: Correct — The effect of temperature on thermal conductivity is less pronounced at higher solids concentration.
choiceExplanations.Much lower: Much lower solids concentration gives a stronger temperature effect, not weaker.
choiceExplanations.Lower: Lower solids concentration gives a stronger temperature effect, not weaker.
choiceExplanations.Constant: Constant is not a concentration level.

items.question: In a meat tenderizing process that uses hot water, the heat required is 326,352 J. Water temperature is to be raised from 22 C to boiling or 100 C. How many ml of water is needed? Specific heat of water is 4.184 J/g C (constant) and its density is 1 g/ml (constant). Neglect evaporation loss.
items.rationale: From q = m c (T2 - T1), m = 326,352 J / [4.184 J/(g·°C) × (100 - 22) °C] = 326,352 / 326.352 = 1,000 g; at a density of 1 g/mL, the required water volume is 1,000 mL.

choiceExplanations.500: 500 ml supplies only half the heat required.
choiceExplanations.750: 750 ml would supply less than 326,352 J.
choiceExplanations.1000: Correct — m = Q/(c dT) = 326,352 / (4.184 x 78) = 1000 g, so 1000 ml of water.
choiceExplanations.850: 850 ml would supply less than 326,352 J.

items.question: It is a systematic, preventative approach to food safety that identifies and controls biological, chemical, and physical hazards from production to consumption using 7 guiding principles. What is it?
items.answer: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points
items.rationale: HACCP stands for Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points, a preventive food safety management system built on seven core principles to control biological, chemical, and physical hazards.
choices: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points
Hazard Automation and Critical Control Presetting
Hazard Analysis and Critical Central Points
Hazard Analysis and Crucial Control Points

choiceExplanations.Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Poi: Correct — HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) is the preventive food safety system with 7 principles.
choiceExplanations.Hazard Automation and Critical Control P: Hazard Automation and Critical Control Presetting is not the real name of the system.
choiceExplanations.Hazard Analysis and Critical Central Poi: Hazard Analysis and Critical Central Points is not the real name of the system.
choiceExplanations.Hazard Analysis and Crucial Control Poin: Hazard Analysis and Crucial Control Points is not the real name of the system.

items.question: The commonly used unit of food viscosity.
items.rationale: Centipoise (cP), equal to 1 mPa·s (roughly the viscosity of water at 20 °C), is the standard practical unit for measuring food viscosity.

choiceExplanations.Pascal-meter (Pa-m): Pascal-meter is not a unit of viscosity.
choiceExplanations.Centipoise-second (cP-s): Centipoise-second is not a viscosity unit.
choiceExplanations.Centipoise (cP): Correct — The centipoise (cP) is the commonly used unit of food viscosity (1 cP = 0.001 Pa-s).
choiceExplanations.KiloPascal-meter (kPa-m): Kilopascal-meter is not a unit of viscosity.

items.question: Which one below does not describe Sanitation Standard Operating Procedures (SSOP)?
items.answer: Prevents contamination and ensures work safety
items.rationale: SSOPs are specific, written, step-by-step sanitation instructions intended to prevent contamination and ensure food safety, not occupational/work safety.
choices: Prevents contamination and ensures work safety

choiceExplanations.Specific: SSOP is specific, so this describes it.
choiceExplanations.Step-by-step procedures: SSOP is a set of step-by-step procedures, so this describes it.
choiceExplanations.Written instructions: SSOP is written instructions, so this describes it.
choiceExplanations.Prevents contamination and ensures work: Correct — This is the keyed answer, though SSOP does aim to prevent contamination; the keyed item is the choice that does not fit the question's list.

items.question: Value adding to raw or fresh vegetables can be attained by ________ them into a variety of products such as pickles and pre-cooked vegetables.
items.rationale: Processing is the broad transformation of raw vegetables into value-added products like pickles and pre-cooked items, whereas canning, bottling, and bioprocessing refer to narrower techniques.

choiceExplanations.Processing: Correct — Processing vegetables into products such as pickles and pre-cooked vegetables adds value.
choiceExplanations.Canning: Canning is only one specific processing method.
choiceExplanations.Bioprocessing: Bioprocessing uses biological agents and is narrower than the general term.
choiceExplanations.Bottling: Bottling is only a packaging step.

items.question: In your understanding of the 3 principles of food preservation, what is the primary principle?
items.rationale: The three principles of food preservation are preventing or delaying microbial growth/decomposition, preventing self-decomposition, and preventing damage from external factors, with preventing microbial growth being the primary principle.

choiceExplanations.Preventing microbial growth: Correct — The primary principle of food preservation is preventing the growth of microorganisms.
choiceExplanations.Preventing self-decomposition: Preventing self-decomposition (enzymes) is a secondary principle.
choiceExplanations.Minimizing spoilage: Minimizing spoilage is a general goal, not a principle by itself.
choiceExplanations.Preventing damage from external factors: Preventing damage from external factors is a secondary principle.

items.question: Inside the baking chamber, the hot air flows by forced or natural convection and the heat is distributed from the heating elements through ________.
items.rationale: While air circulates inside the baking chamber by convection, high-temperature heating elements radiate thermal energy directly to the baking product and chamber surfaces.

choiceExplanations.Radiation: Correct — Inside the baking chamber, heat from the heating elements is distributed by radiation, while air movement is by convection.
choiceExplanations.Conduction: Conduction needs direct contact, but heating elements do not touch the product.
choiceExplanations.Diffusion: Diffusion is movement of substances by concentration difference, not heat distribution.
choiceExplanations.Convection: Convection is already named in the question as the way hot air flows.

items.question: Find out which one below is not a critical limit in HACCP.
items.answer: Bread that is held hot before serving must be warm
items.rationale: A HACCP critical limit must be an objective, measurable criterion (such as specific temperature or time values), whereas stating that bread "must be warm" is subjective and unmeasurable.
choices: Vegetable must be heated to an internal temperature of at least 75 deg. C for 30 seconds to kill Salmonella
Bread that is held hot before serving must be warm
Cooked meat must cool down from 60 to 21 deg. C or below within 2 hours
Meat must be kept at or below 4 deg. C to prevent pathogen growth

choiceExplanations.Vegetable must be heated to an internal: A temperature of 75 C for 30 seconds is a measurable critical limit to kill Salmonella.
choiceExplanations.Bread that is held hot before serving mu: Correct — 'Warm' is vague and unmeasurable, so it cannot be a critical limit.
choiceExplanations.Cooked meat must cool down from 60 to 21: Cooling from 60 to 21 C within 2 hours is a measurable critical limit.
choiceExplanations.Meat must be kept at or below 4 deg. C t: Keeping meat at or below 4 C is a measurable critical limit.

items.question: The term ______ refers to the science that studies the flow and deformation of solids and fluids in foods under the influence of mechanical forces.
items.rationale: Food rheology specifically studies how liquid and solid food materials flow and deform when subjected to mechanical stresses and forces.

choiceExplanations.Food Engineering: Food engineering is the broad field of engineering for food, not the flow study.
choiceExplanations.Food Transfer: Food transfer is not the name of the science.
choiceExplanations.Food Rheology: Correct — Food rheology studies the flow and deformation of foods under mechanical forces.
choiceExplanations.Food Processing: Food processing is the series of operations on food, not a science.

items.question: Compare the toxic and non-toxic environmental effects of forest product preservatives. What solution is non-toxic for the preservation of engineered bamboo if the purposes are for indoor use and construction projects?
items.rationale: Boron-based solutions (such as borax and boric acid) have very low toxicity to humans and are safe, effective preservatives for indoor and construction-grade engineered bamboo.

choiceExplanations.Bamboocides: Bamboocides are not a recognized non-toxic preservative.
choiceExplanations.Mild acid-based solutions: Mild acid-based solutions are not the standard non-toxic preservatives for engineered bamboo.
choiceExplanations.Boron-based solutions: Correct — Boron-based solutions (borax and boric acid) have low toxicity and suit indoor and construction use.
choiceExplanations.Organic pesticides: Organic pesticides are toxic to people and the environment.

items.question: You need to apply preservation technique for engineered bamboos to protect them against insects and decay. What main chemical will you use as preservative?
items.rationale: A combined borax and boric acid aqueous solution is the standard chemical preservative used to protect engineered bamboo against boring insects, termites, and fungal decay.

choiceExplanations.Borax: Borax alone is only part of the preservative.
choiceExplanations.Insecticide: An insecticide is toxic and not the standard preservative for engineered bamboo.
choiceExplanations.Boric acid: Boric acid alone is only part of the preservative.
choiceExplanations.Borax and boric acid solution: Correct — A mixture of borax and boric acid protects bamboo against insects and decay.

items.question: Which one is not a primary food processing?
items.rationale: Oil extraction, grain milling, and milk pasteurization are primary processing steps that turn raw commodities into basic staples or ingredients, whereas cheese-making uses fermentation and coagulation to create a complex secondary food product.

choiceExplanations.Milling grains into flour: Milling grains into flour is a primary process that cleans or cuts raw material.
choiceExplanations.Pasteurizing milk: Pasteurizing milk is a primary process of making raw food safe and fit.
choiceExplanations.Making cheese from milk: Correct — Making cheese is secondary processing because it turns an ingredient into a new product.
choiceExplanations.Extracting oils: Extracting oils from seeds is a primary process.

items.question: Meat processing uses 1 liter of hot water having 1,000 g mass. Calculate the amount of heat in kJ required to raise the temperature of 1 liter of water from 22 deg. C to boiling or 100 deg. C. Specific heat of water is 4.184 J/g deg. C.

choiceExplanations.236.4: 236.4 kJ is wrong; it does not match 1000 x 4.184 x 78.
choiceExplanations.623.4: 623.4 kJ is wrong; it does not match 1000 x 4.184 x 78.
choiceExplanations.324.6: 324.6 kJ is wrong; it does not match 1000 x 4.184 x 78.

items.question: Find the viscosity of a liquid food in centipoise (cP), given that 1,000 cP equals 1 Pa·s. The applied shear stress is 36 Pa and the measured shear rate is 3,000 s⁻¹.

choiceExplanations.1.2 cP: Wrong — 1.2 cP is ten times too small; 36/3,000 = 0.012 Pa·s.
choiceExplanations.120 cP: Wrong — 120 cP is ten times too big; 0.012 Pa·s × 1,000 = 12 cP.
choiceExplanations.12,000 cP: Wrong — 12,000 cP results from using a shear rate of 3 s⁻¹ instead of 3,000 s⁻¹.
choiceExplanations.12 cP: Correct — μ = shear stress / shear rate = 36/3,000 = 0.012 Pa·s = 12 cP.

items.question: Secondary food processing is done by converting raw ingredients into more complex, ready-to-eat or semi-finished products through methods like mixing, cooking, and fermentation. Using the information in the preceding statement, identify which of these processes is not a secondary food processing.
items.rationale: Grinding raw meat is a primary processing step (mechanical size reduction), whereas making cheese, fermenting/seasoning wine, and baking bread from flour are strictly secondary food processing operations.
choices: Converting juice into wine and seasoning wine

choiceExplanations.Making cheese from milk: Wrong — cheese making uses fermentation and coagulation, a secondary process.
choiceExplanations.Grinding raw meat: Correct — grinding raw meat is only size reduction, a primary process; turning it into sausage would be secondary.
choiceExplanations.Converting juice into wine and seasoning: Wrong — fermenting juice into wine is a secondary process.
choiceExplanations.Baking bread from flour: Wrong — baking bread involves mixing, fermenting and cooking, a secondary process.

items.question: Applying thermal conductivity in a baking process, the heat also transfers through conduction from the _________ to the baked product.
items.rationale: Conduction transfers heat through direct molecular contact between solids; in a baking oven, the baking metal container (pan or tray) directly contacts the product to conduct heat into it. The fire, burner, and radiator transfer heat to the oven chamber and container primarily by radiation and convection rather than direct conduction to the baked product.

choiceExplanations.Fire: Fire is the heat source and does not touch the product.
choiceExplanations.Radiator: A radiator emits heat by radiation and convection, not by contact with the product.
choiceExplanations.Baking metal container: Correct — Heat conducts from the hot baking metal container (pan) to the product it touches.
choiceExplanations.Burner: A burner is the heat source and does not touch the product.

items.question: A wall of 25-cm thickness and 10 m² surface area is to be constructed from a material which has an average thermal conductivity of 0.5 W/m·K. The average inner and outer fluid temperatures are 20°C and -20°C, and the corresponding heat transfer coefficients are 8 W/m²·K and 23 W/m²·K, respectively. The rate of heat loss through the wall can be calculated to be
Type of soil composed of 86% sand, 10% clay and 4% loam.
items.rationale: Given: Sand = 86%, Clay = 10%, Silt (printed as loam) = 4%. Under the USDA Soil Texture Triangle, Loamy sand has 70% <= Sand < 90%, 0% <= Clay < 15%, Silt + 1.5(Clay) >= 15% (4 + 15 = 19% >= 15%), and Silt + 2(Clay) < 30% (4 + 20 = 24% < 30%). (Sandy clay loam requires 20%-35% clay.) Answer = Loamy sand

items.question: You are to implement a sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) silo project as a bioprocessing structure. During peak production months, maximum of 10 tonnes of dried shelled grain needs to be stored in a cylindrical silo. Find the silo volume in cubic meters. Dried grain samples electronically registered an average bulk density of 535 kg/m³ at 9.9% moisture wet basis.
items.rationale: Given: Mass m = 10 tonnes = 10,000 kg; bulk density ρ = 535 kg/m³. Formula: V = m / ρ = 10,000 kg / 535 kg/m³ = 18.6916 m³ ≈ 18.69 m³. Answer = 18.69 m³

items.question: You are undergoing a test to determine the suitability of a 12-cm thick steel material as part of your drying chamber wall. The allowed energy lost per second through the steel slab is 60 W. Temperature difference is 9 K. Find the suitable area of the steel slab. Steel thermal conductivity is 45 W/mK.

A 10 m long pipe has an inside radius of 70 mm, an outside radius of 80 mm, and is made of stainless steel (k = 15 W/m °C). Its inside is held at 150 °C, while its outside surface is at 30°C. There is no heat generation and steady-state conditions hold. Compute the rate at which heat is being transferred across the pipe wall.

A 5-meter simply supported beam weighs 200 kg per meter. The maximum live load it supports is 100 standard sacks of milled rice. What is the weight that is supported by each of the 2 columns at both ends of the beam?
items.rationale: Given: Beam weight = 5 m × 200 kg/m = 1,000 kg. Live load = 100 sacks × 50 kg/sack (standard Philippine milled rice sack) = 5,000 kg. Total load = 1,000 + 5,000 = 6,000 kg. For 2 symmetrically loaded end columns, load per column = 6,000 / 2 = 3,000 kg. Answer = 3,000 kg

items.question: A cantilever beam of 3-meter length is weighing 1.96 kN per linear meter. The maximum live load it carries is approximately 4.9 kN of fresh fruits lifted by a pulley at its unsupported end. Find the moment exerted at the supported end.
items.rationale: Given: L = 3 m, distributed weight w = 1.96 kN/m, point load at free end P = 4.9 kN. Formula: M = wL²/2 + PL = 1.96(3)²/2 + 4.9(3) = 8.82 + 14.70 = 23.52 kN·m. Answer = 23.52 kN·m

items.question: As safety engineer in a grain processing plant, you need to ensure the safety of grain transfer operation. A round steel bar having a cross-sectional area of 25 mm² and design tensile stress of 405 MPa is suspending a 4.928 kN wheat grain while the storage silo is being opened. Applying your knowledge in strength of materials, what is the factor of safety and is it safe from breakage?
items.rationale: Given: A = 25 mm², σ_design = 405 MPa, F = 4.928 kN = 4,928 N. Step 1: Actual tensile stress σ_actual = F / A = 4,928 N / 25 mm² = 197.12 MPa. Step 2: Factor of safety FS = σ_design / σ_actual = 405 / 197.12 = 2.055 ≈ 2.05. Since FS = 2.05 > 1.0, it is safe from breakage. Answer = 2.05, safe

items.question: A round tensile steel rod having a design working tensile stress of 405 MPa is carrying a 4.928 kN corn grain into a silo. Applying engineering mechanics, determine the cross-sectional area of the rod to have safety factor of 2.
items.rationale: Given: σ_design = 405 MPa, F = 4.928 kN = 4,928 N, FS = 2. Step 1: Allowable stress σ_allow = σ_design / FS = 405 / 2 = 202.5 MPa (N/mm²). Step 2: Required area A = F / σ_allow = 4,928 N / 202.5 N/mm² = 24.34 mm² ≈ 24.3 mm². Answer = 24.3 mm²

items.question: As provided in the Building Code, when curing concrete made from ordinary portland cement, the concrete shall be maintained above 10 degrees Celsius and in moist condition for the first how many days at least?
items.rationale: Per ACI 318 / National Structural Code of the Philippines (NSCP) curing provisions, concrete made with ordinary Portland cement (other than high-early-strength) shall be maintained above 10°C and in a moist condition for at least the first 7 days after placement. Answer = 7

items.question: To attain about 3,000 psi compressive strength in non-air entrained concrete, how many liters of water should be added per bag of cement?
items.rationale: Per standard concrete mix proportioning guidelines (ACI 211 / Philippine construction standards for 3,000 psi non-air-entrained concrete without trial mixes), the required mixing water is approximately 6.5 US gallons per bag of cement: 6.5 gal × 3.785 L/gal = 24.6 L ≈ 25 liters per bag of cement. Answer = 25

items.question: Based on ACI Code, what is the minimum diameter of lateral ties in a tied concrete column for 32 mm or smaller longitudinal bars?
items.rationale: Per ACI 318 / NSCP column reinforcement provisions, lateral ties shall be at least 10 mm (#3) in diameter for longitudinal bars 32 mm (#10) or smaller. Answer = 10 mm

items.question: Based on ACI Code, what is the minimum diameter of lateral ties in a tied concrete column for 36 to 57 mm and bundled longitudinal bars?
items.rationale: Per ACI 318 / NSCP column reinforcement provisions, lateral ties shall be at least 12 mm (#4) in diameter for 36 mm (#11), 43 mm (#14), 57 mm (#18), and bundled longitudinal bars. Answer = 12 mm

items.question: Determine the lateral ties spacing for a concrete column of a farmhouse having 36 cm × 40 cm side dimension. It uses 22 mm longitudinal bars and 10 mm lateral ties.
items.rationale: Given: Column = 36 cm × 40 cm, db = 22 mm = 2.2 cm, dt = 10 mm = 1.0 cm. Per ACI 318 / NSCP, maximum tie spacing s is the smallest of: (1) 16·db = 16(2.2 cm) = 35.2 cm; (2) 48·dt = 48(1.0 cm) = 48.0 cm; (3) least column dimension = 36.0 cm. Minimum value = 35.2 cm. Answer = 35.2 cm

items.question: In constructing trapezoidal concrete open channels, how many 900-gm packs of water proofing compound are needed per cubic meter of Class A (1:2:4) concrete mix?
items.rationale: Given: Class A (1:2:4) concrete requires 9 bags (40-kg) of Portland cement per cubic meter. Standard integral waterproofing compound dosage is one 900-gm pack per bag of cement (1:1 ratio). Packs needed = 9 bags × 1 pack/bag = 9 packs. Answer = 9 packs

items.question: In concrete canal construction, how many 40-kg bags of cement are needed for a 20-km lateral channel if it requires 0.6 cubic meter concrete per linear meter? Use 5% safety factor.
items.rationale: Given: Length L = 20 km = 20,000 m; Concrete per linear meter = 0.6 m³/m; Safety factor = 1.05; Standard 40-kg cement factor = 9 bags/m³. Formula: Bags = Safety factor × Cement factor × Concrete volume = 1.05 × 9 bags/m³ × (0.6 m³/m × 20,000 m) = 1.05 × 9 × 12,000 = 113,400 bags. Answer = 113,400 bags.

items.question: How many truck loads of sand are needed for 30-km main irrigation canal requiring 3.5 cubic meters concrete per linear meter? 1 truck load is 2.5 cubic meters. Use 5% safety factor.
items.rationale: Given: L = 30 km = 30,000 m; Concrete rate = 3.5 m³/m; Standard sand factor = 0.5 m³ sand/m³ concrete; Truck capacity = 2.5 m³/truck load; Safety factor = 1.05. Formula: Truck loads = (Safety factor × Sand factor × Concrete volume) / Truck capacity = (1.05 × 0.5 × 3.5 m³/m × 30,000 m) / 2.5 m³ = 55,125 / 2.5 = 22,050 truck loads. Answer = 22,050 truck loads.

items.question: Determine the cement budget for 36-km irrigation canal if it requires half cubic meter concrete per linear meter and cement costs Php200/bag? Use 5% safety factor.
items.rationale: Given: L = 36 km = 36,000 m; Concrete rate = 0.5 m³/m; Cement factor = 9 bags/m³; Unit cost = Php 200/bag; Safety factor = 1.05. Formula: Budget = Safety factor × Cement factor × Concrete volume × Unit cost = 1.05 × 9 bags/m³ × (0.5 m³/m × 36,000 m) × Php 200/bag = 170,100 bags × Php 200 = Php 34,020,000. Answer = Php 34,020,000.

items.question: The number of 10-mm horizontal reinforcing bars in a 3.2-meter tall trapezoidal canal wall is 2,836 pieces. Following the standard bar spacing 20 cm × 20 cm, how many vertical reinforcing bars are needed?
items.rationale: Given: Number of horizontal bars = 2,836 bars; Bar grid spacing = 20 cm × 20 cm. Because the horizontal and vertical reinforcing bar spacings are equal (20 cm in both directions), the number of vertical reinforcing bars equals the number of horizontal bars = 2,836 bars. Answer = 2,836 bars.

items.question: What is the cement budget for 18-km canal requiring 2/3 cubic meter concrete per linear meter? Cement costs Php200/bag while transport costs Php 10/bag. Use 5% safety factor.
items.rationale: Given: L = 18 km = 18,000 m; Concrete rate = 2/3 m³/m ≈ 0.667 m³/m; Cement factor = 9 bags/m³; Total unit cost = Php 200 + Php 10 = Php 210/bag; Safety factor = 1.05. Formula: Budget = 1.05 × 9 bags/m³ × (0.667 m³/m × 18,000 m) × Php 210/bag = 113,456.7 bags × Php 210 = Php 23,825,907. Answer = Php 23,825,907.

items.question: The middle concrete column of a bioprocessing building has a 35 cm × 30 cm side dimensions. It uses 18 mm longitudinal bars and 10 mm lateral ties. What should be the minimum lateral ties spacing based on the standard of the American Concrete Institute (ACI)?
items.rationale: Given: Column dimensions = 35 cm × 30 cm; Longitudinal bar diameter d_b = 18 mm = 1.8 cm; Lateral tie diameter d_t = 10 mm = 1.0 cm. Formula (ACI Code governing lateral tie spacing is the smallest of three limits): (1) 16 × d_b = 16 × 1.8 cm = 28.8 cm; (2) 48 × d_t = 48 × 1.0 cm = 48.0 cm; (3) Least column dimension = 30 cm. Controlling spacing = min(28.8, 48.0, 30) = 28.8 cm. Answer = 28.8 cm.

items.question: The weight of a steel roof truss W in pounds per square foot of the horizontal surface as a function of span L in feet can be determined by an empirical equation ___.
items.rationale: Standard Structural/ABE Formula (Fowler's empirical formula for light-load steel roof trusses): W = 0.4 + 0.040 L, where W is the truss weight in lb/ft² of horizontal projection and L is the truss span in ft. Answer = 0.4 + 0.040 L.

items.question: PAES 415:2001 Agricultural Structures - Greenhouses Walkways. If the walkway will be used only as a place to stand while servicing the benches, a minimum of ___x___ aisle shall be used for determinate crops and a minimum of ___y___ aisle for indeterminate crops.
items.rationale: Standard Reference: PAES 415:2001 (Agricultural Structures – Greenhouses) specifies that for walkways used only as a place to stand while servicing benches, the minimum aisle width is x = 0.30 m for determinate crops and y = 0.80 m for indeterminate crops. Answer = 0.30 m and 0.80 m.

items.question: Area covered by 1 gallon of acrylic paint for the first coating
items.rationale: Standard Construction Estimating Reference: One gallon of acrylic paint covers 20 m²/gal for the 1st coating (primer/first coat) and 25 m²/gal for the 2nd coating (whereas surface-texture estimating rates are 30 m²/gal for coarse-to-rough, 35 m²/gal for fine-to-coarse, and 40 m²/gal for smooth-to-fine). Answer = 20 m²/gal.

items.question: Minimum height of pen partition for swine under 25 kg
items.rationale: Standard Reference: PAES 401:2001 (Agricultural Structures – Housing for Swine Production) specifies minimum pen partition heights by swine weight/class: under 25 kg = 0.70 m (0.7 m); 25–100 kg = 0.90 m; sow = 1.00 m; boar = 1.20 m. Answer = 0.7 m.

items.question: A concrete column of an agricultural building has a 35 cm × 30 cm side dimensions. It uses 16 mm longitudinal bars and 10 mm lateral ties. What should be the minimum lateral ties spacing based on vertical bar diameter and complying with the standard of the American Concrete Institute?
items.rationale: Given: Column = 35 cm × 30 cm; Vertical (longitudinal) bar diameter d_b = 16 mm = 1.6 cm; Lateral tie diameter d_t = 10 mm = 1.0 cm. Formula (ACI Code): Spacing based on vertical bar diameter S_v = 16 × d_b = 16 × 1.6 cm = 25.6 cm (which is also smaller than 48 × 1.0 cm = 48 cm and the least column dimension of 30 cm). Answer = 25.6 cm.

items.question: Compare 1-lane and 2-lane regular farm-to-market roads (FMRs). If the carriageway and 1-side shoulder for a 1-lane road is 2.5 m and 0.75 m, respectively, how wide are the minimum carriageway and 1-side shoulder for a regular 2-lane road, respectively?
items.rationale: Given: 1-lane FMR carriageway = 2.5 m, 1-side shoulder = 0.75 m. Doubling the lane and corresponding shoulder allowance for a regular 2-lane road gives: Carriageway = 2 × 2.5 m = 5.0 m; 1-side shoulder = 2 × 0.75 m = 1.5 m. Answer = 5.0 and 1.5 m.

items.question: A group of student immersion workers is assisting you at the municipal agricultural office where you work as an AB engineer. One day, one of the students asks what the minimum space requirement is for a boar pen because his father plans to build one for three boars. What should your answer be?
items.rationale: Given: Number of boars = 3; PAES 401:2001 minimum space requirement for boar pens = 7.50 m²/animal. Formula: Total minimum area = 7.50 m²/boar × 3 boars = 22.5 m². Answer = 22.5 m².

items.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the standard specifications of the general and structural requirements of slaughterhouse for ruminants? The minimum size of the slaughtering area for small and large ruminants is 28 sq. meters. The slaughterhouse shall be located at least 200 m away from any building used for human habitation, national highway, public or commercial buildings/places, and any animal production facilities. The minimum size of the offal cleaning area for small and large ruminants is 20 sq. meters. The slaughterhouse shall be located at least 100 m away from the river bank.
items.answer: The slaughterhouse shall be located at least 100 m away from the river bank.
items.rationale: Standard Reference: Under PNS/BAFS/PABES 306:2020 (Slaughterhouse for Ruminants), the minimum slaughtering area for small and large ruminants is 28 m², the minimum offal cleaning area is 20 m², and the setback from residential/public buildings, highways, and animal production facilities is at least 200 m. However, the required distance from a river bank is at least 10 m (NOT 100 m). Therefore, the false statement is that it must be at least 100 m away from the river bank.
choices: The slaughterhouse shall be located at least 200 m away from any building used for human habitation, national highway, public or commercial buildings/places, and any animal production facilities.
The slaughterhouse shall be located at least 100 m away from the river bank.
The minimum size of the slaughtering area for small and large ruminants is 28 sq. meters.
The minimum size of the offal cleaning area for small and large ruminants is 20 sq. meters.

items.question: A company assigned you as the safety engineer in a grain processing plant. A round steel bar having a cross-sectional area of 25 square mm and design working tensile stress of 403 MPa is suspending a 4.905 kN wheat grain while the silo for its storage is being opened. Applying your knowledge in strength of materials, what is the factor of safety and is it safe from breakage?
items.rationale: Given: Load F = 4.905 kN = 4,905 N; Area A = 25 mm²; Design tensile stress σ_design = 403 MPa. Step 1: Actual stress σ_actual = F / A = 4,905 N / 25 mm² = 196.2 N/mm² = 196.2 MPa. Step 2: Factor of Safety FS = σ_design / σ_actual = 403 MPa / 196.2 MPa = 2.05. Since FS = 2.05 > 1.0, the bar is Safe. Answer = 2.05; Safe.

items.question: If you are to design a primary processing plant for fresh fruit and vegetable stricly based on standards, how will you design the floor intersection with the wall?
items.rationale: Standard Reference: PAES 418:2002 (Agricultural Structures – Primary Processing Plant for Fresh Fruit and Vegetables) specifies that the floor intersection with the wall shall be coved with a 50 mm - 60 mm radius to prevent dirt accumulation and facilitate cleaning. Answer = Coved with 50 mm - 60 mm radius.

items.question: In building a primary processing plant for fresh vegetable, how far must the windowsill be from the finish floor line?
items.rationale: Standard Reference: PAES 418:2002 (Agricultural Structures – Primary Processing Plant for Fresh Fruit and Vegetables) requires that windowsills be located at least 1 m above the finish floor line. Answer = 1 m.

items.question: You are assigned to implement a sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) silo project for bioprocessing. During peak production months, maximum of 10 tonnes dried shelled grain needs to be stored in a cylindrical silo. What should be the silo volume in cubic meters? Dried grain samples electronically registered an average bulk density of 536 kg/m³ at 9.7% moisture content wet basis.
items.rationale: Given: Mass m = 10 tonnes = 10,000 kg; Bulk density ρ = 536 kg/m³. Formula: V = m / ρ = 10,000 kg / 536 kg/m³ = 18.6567 m³ ≈ 18.66 m³. Answer = 18.66 m³.

items.question: Based on PAES, what is the recommended maximum length of greenhouse?
items.rationale: Standard Reference: PAES 415:2001 (Agricultural Structures – Greenhouses) specifies that the length of a greenhouse should not exceed 50 m to ensure effective ventilation and microclimate control. Answer = 50 m.

items.question: A simply supported beam, 4-meter long, weighs 250 kg per meter. The maximum live load it carries is 200 half sacks of milled rice. Each full sack weighs 50 kg. What is the weight that is supported by each of the 2 columns at both ends?
items.rationale: Given: L = 4 m; Beam weight = 250 kg/m; Live load = 200 half sacks × (50 kg / 2) = 200 × 25 kg = 5,000 kg. Dead load = 4 m × 250 kg/m = 1,000 kg. Formula: Load per column = (Live load + Dead load) / 2 = (5,000 kg + 1,000 kg) / 2 = 3,000 kg. Answer = 3,000 kg.

items.question: Applying mechanics, determine the moment exerted at the supported end of a 3-meter cantilever beam weighing 1.96 kN per meter. The design maximum live load it will carry is approximately 4.9 kN of grains lifted by a pulley at the unsupported end of the beam.
items.rationale: Given: Cantilever length L = 3 m; Uniform dead load w = 1.96 kN/m; Concentrated live load P = 4.9 kN at free end. Formula: M_dead = w L² / 2 = 1.96 × 3² / 2 = 8.82 kN·m; M_live = P × L = 4.9 × 3 = 14.70 kN·m. Total moment M = 8.82 + 14.70 = 23.52 kN·m ≈ 23.5 kN·m. Answer = 23.5 kN·m.

items.question: You are commissioned to design a machinery shed to house a pickup truck (width = 2.3 m, length = 6.0 m) and a two-plow tractor (width = 2.3 m, length = 3.7 m). Allowing a 0.6 m clearance on both width and length for each unit per PAES 420:2002, what is the total required area for the machinery shed?
items.rationale: Given (PAES 420:2002 Annex B standard dimensions with 0.6 m clearance on width and length): Two-plow tractor (W = 2.3 m, L = 3.7 m) → Area_1 = (2.3 + 0.6) × (3.7 + 0.6) = 2.9 × 4.3 = 12.47 m². Pickup truck (W = 2.3 m, L = 6.0 m) → Area_2 = (2.3 + 0.6) × (6.0 + 0.6) = 2.9 × 6.6 = 19.14 m². Formula: Total Area = 12.47 m² + 19.14 m² = 31.61 m². Answer = 31.61 m².

items.question: Determine the laboratory area in square meters required for a bioprocessing plant with 6 laboratory employees based on existing ABE standards.
items.rationale: Given: Number of laboratory employees = 6; Standard laboratory space requirement = 20 m²/employee. Formula: Area = 20 m²/employee × 6 employees = 120 m². Answer = 120 m².

items.question: You are consulted in designing a cylindrical grain bin or silo. What is the bin diameter if the target level full volume is 700 standard US bushels and the eave height is 5 meters?
items.rationale: Given: Volume = 700 US bushels; Eave height H = 5 m; Conversion: 1 US bushel = 1.2445 ft³ = 0.035239 m³. Step 1: V = 700 × 0.035239 m³ = 24.667 m³. Step 2: From cylinder volume V = (π / 4) D² H, solve for diameter D = √(4V / (π H)) = √(4 × 24.667 / (π × 5)) = √6.2815 = 2.506 m ≈ 2.51 m. Answer = 2.51 m.

items.question: Ten tons of shelled corn is to be stored in a cylindrical silo. Loading is from the bottom to the top of the cylindrical container, without considering the additional volume of the cone due to the effect of the angle of repose of the sample. If the silo requires a ratio of 2D = H, what would be the dimension of the silo? Assume a 45 lb/ft³ bulk density for shelled corn.
If 5000 bags of palay is to be piled 20-bags high, how many square meters of floor space is needed? (0.23 m/bag)
items.rationale: Given: Total bags = 5,000 bags; Stack height = 20 bags × 0.23 m/bag = 4.6 m; Standard stacking density = 10 bags/m³. Step 1: Volume of pile V = 5,000 bags / (10 bags/m³) = 500 m³. Step 2: Floor Area A = V / H = 500 m³ / 4.6 m = 108.695 m² ≈ 108.69 m². Answer = 108.69 m².

items.question: A sundrying floor made of concrete is to be constructed. The area of the floor will have a dimension of 20-ft wide × 40-ft long. The thickness of the floor is proposed to be 4 inches. If concrete mixture of 1:2:4 will be adopted for the construction, how many bags of cement will be needed? What is the estimated cubic meter of sand and gravel that will be needed?
items.answer: 59.3 bags cement, 3.33 m³ sand, 6.65 m³ gravel
items.rationale: Given: W = 20 ft, L = 40 ft, t = 4 in = 4/12 ft; 1:2:4 mix factors (7.84 bags/m³ cement, 0.44 m³/m³ sand, 0.88 m³/m³ gravel). Step 1: Volume V = 20 × 40 × (4/12) = 266.67 ft³ / (3.28 ft/m)³ = 7.56 m³. Step 2: Cement = 7.84 × 7.56 = 59.27 ≈ 59.3 bags; Sand = 0.44 × 7.56 = 3.33 m³; Gravel = 0.88 × 7.56 = 6.65 m³. Answer = 59.3 bags cement, 3.33 m³ sand, 6.65 m³ gravel.
choices: 70.2 bags cement, 3.94 m³ sand, 7.88 m³ gravel
64.5 bags cement, 3.62 m³ sand, 7.25 m³ gravel
52.4 bags cement, 2.95 m³ sand, 5.85 m³ gravel
59.3 bags cement, 3.33 m³ sand, 6.65 m³ gravel

items.question: Compute the volume of concrete required for the engine foundation of a rice mill. The engine is a Mitsubishi 4DR5 with 650 kg gross weight. Engine will be operated at a speed of 2000 rpm. Assume a concrete density of 2,406 kg/m³.
items.rationale: Given: Engine weight W_e = 650 kg; Speed N = 2,000 rpm; Concrete density ρ_c = 2,406 kg/m³. Step 1: Foundation weight W_f = 0.11 × W_e × N^0.5 = 0.11 × 650 × √2000 = 3,197.58 kg. Step 2: Volume V_f = W_f / ρ_c = 3,197.58 / 2,406 = 1.329 m³ (1.32 m³ per standard ABE reviewer key). Answer = 1.32 m³.

items.question: An engine concrete foundation requires a concrete volume of 1.32 m³. What will be the depth of the concrete foundation if the engine has a base width and length of 1.0 and 1.5 meters, respectively, considering an engine base allowance of 10%? If a concrete mixture of 1:3:6 (using 5.48 bags of cement, 0.44 m³ of sand, and 0.88 m³ of gravel per cubic meter of concrete) will be used for the foundation, determine the number of bags of cement and the volume of sand and gravel needed.
items.answer: 0.80 m depth, 7.23 bags cement, 0.58 m³ sand, 1.16 m³ gravel
items.rationale: Given: V_f = 1.32 m³ (from Problem 78 / A3-1932); Base width W_e = 1.0 m, length L_e = 1.5 m; Allowance = 10% (× 1.1); 1:3:6 mix factors (5.48 bags/m³ cement, 0.44 m³/m³ sand, 0.88 m³/m³ gravel). Step 1: Depth D_f = V_f / [(W_e × L_e) × 1.1] = 1.32 / (1.5 × 1.1) = 1.32 / 1.65 = 0.80 m. Step 2: Cement = 5.48 × 1.32 = 7.23 bags; Sand = 0.44 × 1.32 = 0.58 m³; Gravel = 0.88 × 1.32 = 1.16 m³. Answer = 0.80 m depth, 7.23 bags cement, 0.58 m³ sand, 1.16 m³ gravel.
choices: 0.92 m depth, 8.15 bags cement, 0.65 m³ sand, 1.30 m³ gravel
1.05 m depth, 9.02 bags cement, 0.72 m³ sand, 1.44 m³ gravel
0.68 m depth, 6.45 bags cement, 0.52 m³ sand, 1.04 m³ gravel
0.80 m depth, 7.23 bags cement, 0.58 m³ sand, 1.16 m³ gravel

items.question: A sundrying floor is to be constructed using concrete. The dimension is 10 cm thick by 20 m wide and 30 m long. The recommended mixing proportion is 1:2:4. Determine the number of bags of cement and the volume of sand and gravel needed for the construction.
items.answer: 470 bags cement, 26.4 m³ sand, 52.8 m³ gravel
items.rationale: Given: t = 10 cm = 0.10 m; W = 20 m; L = 30 m; 1:2:4 mix factors (7.84 bags/m³ cement, 0.44 m³/m³ sand, 0.88 m³/m³ gravel). Step 1: Volume V = 30 × 20 × 0.10 = 60 m³. Step 2: Cement = 7.84 × 60 = 470.4 ≈ 470 bags; Sand = 0.44 × 60 = 26.4 m³; Gravel = 0.88 × 60 = 52.8 m³. Answer = 470 bags cement, 26.4 m³ sand, 52.8 m³ gravel.
choices: 510 bags cement, 28.8 m³ sand, 57.6 m³ gravel
420 bags cement, 23.5 m³ sand, 46.5 m³ gravel
545 bags cement, 30.8 m³ sand, 60.7 m³ gravel
470 bags cement, 26.4 m³ sand, 52.8 m³ gravel

items.question: Determine the number of hollow blocks needed for a wall having a height of 3 m from the ground and a perimeter length of 100 meters. Every 10 meters is a concrete post having a dimension of 12 in × 12 inches. The wall is protruded below the ground with 3 layers of hollow blocks. Also compute the number of bags of cement and sand needed for the mortar using a mixing proportion of 1:3.
items.rationale:
Given: Perimeter = 100 m; Height above ground = 3 m; Post = 12 in × 12 in (0.30 m × 0.30 m) every 10 m; Foundation = 3 layers of CHB (0.20 m/layer); Mortar mix = 1:3.
Number of posts = 100 m / 10 m = 10 posts.
Length occupied by posts = 10 × 0.30 m = 3 m.
Net wall length = 100 m - 3 m = 97 m.
Total wall height = 3 m + (3 × 0.20 m) = 3.6 m.
Wall area = 97 m × 3.6 m = 349.2 m².
Number of CHB (at 12.5 CHB/m²) = 349.2 m² × 12.5 = 4,365 pcs (≈ 4,400 pcs with allowance; or 4,540 pcs at 13 CHB/m²).
Mortar volume (at ~0.001 m³/CHB with allowance) = 4,400 × 0.001 m³ = 4.40 m³.
For a 1:3 mortar mix (12 bags cement and 1.0 m³ sand per m³ mortar): Cement ≈ 53 bags, Volume of sand = 4.40 m³.
Answer = 4.40 m³ of sand

items.question: Compute the number of 4-in × 8-in × 16-in concrete-hollow blocks needed for a wall having a length of 50 m and a height of 3 m. The wall is provided with a 0.4-m foundation wall.
items.rationale:
Given: Length of wall (L) = 50 m; Height above ground = 3 m; Foundation height = 0.4 m; Factor = 13 CHB/m² (with allowance).
Formula: Total height = 3 m + 0.4 m = 3.4 m.
Area of wall = L × H = 50 m × 3.4 m = 170 m².
No. of CHB = 13 CHB/m² × 170 m² = 2,210 CHB.
Answer = 2,210 CHB

items.question: Compute the volume of 200 pieces mortar that can be contained in a 4-in × 8-in × 16-in concrete-hollow block.
items.rationale:
Given: CHB size = 4 in × 8 in × 16 in; Number of pieces = 200 pcs; Standard mortar volume per 4-in CHB = 0.001 m³/piece.
Formula: Volume of mortar = N × V_per_piece = 200 pcs × 0.001 m³/pc = 0.2 m³.
Answer = 0.2 m³

items.question: Compute the total cost of 50 pcs 2 × 3 × 12 lumber at P27/bd ft.
items.rationale:
Given: Quantity = 50 pcs; Lumber size = 2 in × 3 in × 12 ft; Unit price = P27/bd-ft.
Formula: bd-ft per piece = (T_in × W_in × L_ft) / 12 = (2 × 3 × 12) / 12 = 6 bd-ft/pc.
Total board feet = 50 pcs × 6 bd-ft/pc = 300 bd-ft.
Total cost = 300 bd-ft × P27/bd-ft = P8,100.
Answer = P8,100

items.question: A log has a 24-in diameter and an 18-ft length. What is the total number of board foot that can be obtained from the log?
items.rationale:
Given: Log diameter (D) = 24 in; Length (L) = 18 ft.
Formula (Doyle Log Rule): BF = [(D - 4)² × L] / 16.
Substitution: BF = [(24 - 4)² × 18] / 16 = (20² × 18) / 16 = (400 × 18) / 16 = 7,200 / 16 = 450 bd-ft.
Answer = 450 bd-ft

items.question: Determine the number of board foot of wood having the following dimension and number of stocks: (a) 40 pcs 2-in × 4-in × 10-ft; (b) 120 pcs 1-in × 2-in × 12-ft; (c) 500 pcs 2-in × 2-in × 8-ft; and (d) 20 pcs 1-in × 1-ft × 10-ft. Also compute the total cost of the stocks of wood if the cost per board foot is P30.00.

The temperature inside a rice hull furnace is maintained at 1500 °F by means of suitable control apparatus. The wall of the furnace is 9 in. in thickness and constructed from a material having a thermal conductivity of 0.18 Btu/hr-ft-°F. Calculate the heat loss for each square foot of wall surface per hour. Assume that the inside and outside wall temperatures are 1500 °F and 400 °F, respectively.
items.rationale:
Given: T_in = 1500 °F; T_out = 400 °F; Thickness (Δx) = 9 in = 9/12 ft = 0.75 ft; Thermal conductivity (k) = 0.18 BTU/hr-ft-°F.
Formula (Fourier's Law): q/A = k × ΔT / Δx.
Substitution: ΔT = 1500 °F - 400 °F = 1100 °F.
q/A = (0.18 × 1100) / 0.75 = 198 / 0.75 = 264 BTU/hr-ft².
Answer = 264 BTU/hr-ft²

items.question: Calculate the thermal conductivity of a 4’ × 8’ test panel, 1-in. thick if during a 3-hour test period it conducted 900 BTU of heat through the panel with a temperature differential of 15 °F between its surfaces.
items.rationale:
Given: Area (A) = 4 ft × 8 ft = 32 ft²; Thickness (Δx) = 1 in = 1/12 ft = 0.08333 ft; Heat (Q) = 900 BTU in t = 3 hr; ΔT = 15 °F.
Formula: Heat transfer rate q = Q / t = 900 BTU / 3 hr = 300 BTU/hr.
k = (q × Δx) / (A × ΔT).
Substitution: k = (300 × 1/12) / (32 × 15) = 25 / 480 = 0.0521 BTU/hr-ft-°F ≈ 0.052 BTU/hr-ft-°F.
Answer = 0.052 BTU/hr-ft-°F

items.question: The wall of a kiln is made up of 9-in fire bricks (k = 0.72 BTU/hr-ft-°F), 5-in insulating bricks (k = 0.08 BTU/hr-ft-°F), and 7.5-in red bricks (K = 0.5 BTU/hr-ft-°F). The inner (t1) and outer surface temperatures (t4) are 1500 °F and 150 °F, respectively. Neglecting the residences of the mortar joints, compute the temperatures t2 and t3 at the contact surface.

A biomass furnace with 1-in. horizontal-plate steel wall is covered by a 2-in. thick insulation. The temperature of the upper side of the steel wall is 450 °F while at the lower side of the insulation is 100 °F. If the k for steel is 29 BTU/hr-ft-°F and the k for the insulation is 0.5 BTU/hr-ft-°F, what is the temperature at the junction between the steel plate and the insulation?
items.rationale:
Given: Δx1 = 1/12 ft (k1 = 29 BTU/hr-ft-°F); Δx2 = 2/12 ft (k2 = 0.5 BTU/hr-ft-°F); T1 = 450 °F; T3 = 100 °F.
Thermal resistances (per ft²):
R1 = (1/12) / 29 = 0.002874 hr-ft²-°F/BTU
R2 = (2/12) / 0.5 = 0.333333 hr-ft²-°F/BTU
R_total = 0.336207 hr-ft²-°F/BTU.
Heat flux: q/A = (450 - 100) / 0.336207 = 1,041.03 BTU/hr-ft².
Junction temperature: T2 = T1 - (q/A)R1 = 450 - 1,041.03(0.002874) = 447.01 °F ≈ 447 °F.
Answer = 447 °F

items.question: A 12-inch diameter fan rotates at a speed of 1800 rpm. The fan blade has a pitch angle of 10 degrees. If the fan has 40% static efficiency, what is its flow rate?
items.rationale:
Given: Diameter (D) = 12 in = 1 ft (r = 6 in); Speed (N) = 1800 rpm; Pitch angle (θ) = 10°; Static efficiency (η) = 40% = 0.40.
Formula: Pitch = 2πr tan(θ) = 2π(6 in) tan(10°) = 6.65 in/rev = 0.554 ft/rev.
Cross-sectional area A = πD² / 4 = π(1 ft)² / 4 = 0.7854 ft².
Flow rate Q = Pitch × A × N × η = (6.65/12 ft) × 0.7854 ft² × 1800 rpm × 0.40 = 313.35 cfm.
Answer = 313.35 cfm

items.question: What is the rate of heat transfer from a concrete wall having a dimension of 9-ft high by 20-ft long. The temperature of the inside wall is 27 °C while that of the outside wall is 32 °C. The wall thickness is 4 inches with thermal conductivity of 10 BTU/hr-ft²-°F.
items.rationale:
Given: Area (A) = 9 ft × 20 ft = 180 ft²; T_in = 27 °C; T_out = 32 °C; Thickness (Δx) = 4 in = 4/12 ft = 1/3 ft; k = 10 BTU/hr-ft-°F.
Temperature difference: ΔT = (32 - 27) °C × (9/5) = 5 °C × 1.8 = 9 °F.
Formula (Conduction): Q = k × A × ΔT / Δx.
Substitution: Q = (10 × 180 × 9) / (4/12) = 16,200 × 3 = 48,600 BTU/hr.
Answer = 48,600 BTU/hr

items.question: What is the heat transfer rate by convection on a surface of a wooden wall having a dimension of 10-ft high by 20-ft long? The air temperature is 30 °C moving at a speed of 15 mph while the wall temperature is 27 °C. Assume a heat transfer coefficient of 6 BTU/hr-ft²-°F.
items.rationale:
Given: Area (A) = 10 ft × 20 ft = 200 ft²; T_air = 30 °C; T_wall = 27 °C; Convection coefficient (h) = 6 BTU/hr-ft²-°F.
Temperature difference: ΔT = (30 - 27) °C × (9/5) = 3 °C × 1.8 = 5.4 °F.
Formula (Newton's Law of Cooling): Q = h × A × ΔT.
Substitution: Q = 6 × 200 × 5.4 = 6,480 BTU/hr.
Answer = 6,480 BTU/hr

items.question: Calculate the energy transfer rate across a 6-in.-firebrick wall of a farm house with a temperature difference of 50 °C across the wall. The thermal conductivity of the firebrick is 0.65 BTU/hr-ft-°F.
items.rationale:
Given: Thickness (Δx) = 6 in = 6/12 ft = 0.5 ft; Temperature difference (ΔT) = 50 °C; k = 0.65 BTU/hr-ft-°F.
Convert temperature difference: ΔT = 50 °C × (9/5) = 90 °F.
Formula: q/A = k × ΔT / Δx.
Substitution: q/A = (0.65 × 90) / 0.5 = 58.5 / 0.5 = 117.0 BTU/hr-ft².
Answer = 117.0 BTU/hr-ft²

items.question: A 100,000-bag-capacity pile will be constructed to stack paddy in a warehouse using jute bags to a height of 20 ft. What will be the probable floor area of the stack if rectangular piles (2W = L) will be constructed? Assume a bag height of 0.23 m/bag and a stacking density of 10 bags per m³.
items.rationale:
Given: Capacity = 100,000 bags; Max height = 20 ft; Bag height = 0.23 m/bag; Stacking density = 10 bags/m³.
Volume required: V = 100,000 bags / (10 bags/m³) = 10,000 m³.
Maximum height in meters: H_max = 20 ft / 3.28 ft/m = 6.098 m.
Number of full layers = 6.098 m / 0.23 m/layer = 26.51 → 26 layers.
Actual pile height: H = 26 × 0.23 m = 5.98 m.
Floor area: A = V / H = 10,000 m³ / 5.98 m = 1,672.24 m² ≈ 1,672.2 m² (with W ≈ 28.9 m, L ≈ 57.8 m).
Answer = 1,672.2 m²

items.question: Two piles of shelled corn in bags will be stored in a warehouse having a dimension of 15-wide by 30-m long and 6-m high. How many bags of shelled corn could be contained per pile inside the warehouse?
items.rationale:
Given: Dimensions = 15 m × 30 m × 6 m; Standard shelled corn stacking density = 12 bags/m³.
Formula: Volume (V) = L × W × H = 30 m × 15 m × 6 m = 2,700 m³.
Number of bags = V × stacking density = 2,700 m³ × 12 bags/m³ = 32,400 bags.
Answer = 32,400 bags

items.question: Twenty (20) tons of shelled corn will be stored in a 6-meter-diameter silo in full load. If the corn has an average density of 450 kg/m³, what would be the probable height of the bin necessary for storage? Assume a maximum angle of fill of 20 degrees.
items.rationale:
Given: Mass (M) = 20 tons = 20,000 kg; Density (ρ) = 450 kg/m³; Diameter (D) = 6 m (r = 3 m); Angle of fill (θ) = 20°.
Total volume needed: V = M / ρ = 20,000 / 450 = 44.444 m³.
Cross-sectional area: A = πr² = π(3)² = 28.274 m².
Conical surcharge height: h_cone = r tan(20°) = 3 tan(20°) = 1.092 m.
Cone volume: V_cone = (1/3) A h_cone = (1/3)(28.274)(1.092) = 10.291 m³.
Cylindrical wall height: H = (V - V_cone) / A = (44.444 - 10.291) / 28.274 = 1.208 m ≈ 1.21 m (total peak height = 2.30 m).
Answer = 1.21 m

items.question: How many units of 1-hp air conditioning system is required to maintain the temperature of a farm house at 27 °C? The floor dimension of the house is 10-m wide × 30-m long. The height of ceiling of the room is 8 ft.
items.rationale:
Given: Floor area (A) = 10 m × 30 m = 300 m²; Ceiling height = 8 ft; Standard cooling coverage = 20 m² per 1-hp unit.
Formula: No. of units = Floor area / Coverage per 1-hp unit.
Substitution: No. of units = 300 m² / (20 m²/unit) = 15 units of 1-hp air conditioner.
Answer = 15 units of 1-hp air conditioner

items.question: A swine house, having a dimension of 20-ft wide by 60-ft long, requires an illumination of 200 lux. If a 25-watts fluorescent lamp with lighting intensity of 100 lumen is provided, how many bulbs will be needed for the structure?
items.rationale:
Given: Area (A) = 20 ft × 60 ft = 1,200 ft²; Illumination (E) = 200 lux (lumens/m²); Lamp output = 100 lumens/bulb.
Convert area to m²: A = 1,200 ft² / (3.28 ft/m)² = 111.54 m².
Total lumens needed = E × A = 200 lux × 111.54 m² = 22,308 lumens.
Number of bulbs = 22,308 lumens / 100 lumens/bulb = 223.08 ≈ 223 bulbs.
Answer = 223 bulbs

items.question: What is the heat loss per ft² of a 9-inch-thick brick-kiln wall made of a material with thermal conductivity of 0.18 BTU/hr-ft-°F? The outside and inside temperatures are 1500 °F and 400 °F, respectively.
items.rationale:
Given: k = 0.18 BTU/hr-ft-°F; To = 1500 °F; Ti = 400 °F; Thickness (Δx) = 9 in = 9/12 ft = 0.75 ft.
Formula (Fourier's Law): q/A = k × (To - Ti) / Δx.
Substitution: q/A = 0.18 × (1500 - 400) / 0.75 = (0.18 × 1100) / 0.75 = 264 BTU/hr-ft².
Answer = 264 BTU/hr-ft²

items.question: No. of outlets = (12 ft + 12 ft + 12 ft + 12 ft) duplex receptacle is needed for a 12 × 14 ft room?
items.rationale:
Given: Room dimensions = 12 ft × 14 ft; Maximum wall spacing per PEC/NEC for duplex convenience outlets = 12 ft.
Formula: Perimeter (P) = 12 ft + 14 ft + 12 ft + 14 ft = 52 ft.
Number of outlets = P / 12 ft = 52 ft / 12 ft = 4.33 → round up to 5 duplex receptacles.
Answer = 5 duplex receptacles

items.question: How many duplex receptacle is needed for a 12 × 14 ft room?
items.rationale:
Given: Room dimensions = 12 ft × 14 ft; Standard maximum wall spacing for duplex receptacles = 12 ft.
Formula: Perimeter (P) = 2(12 ft + 14 ft) = 52 ft.
Number of duplex receptacles = 52 ft / 12 ft = 4.33 → round up to 5 duplex receptacles.
Answer = 5 duplex receptacles

items.question: Determine the number of bags of cement (94 lbs), sand, and gravel of a proposed concrete sundrying pavement whose width and length are 100 meters × 200 meters. The thickness is 4 in.
items.rationale:
Given: Width = 100 m; Length = 200 m; Thickness ≈ 4 in = 0.10 m; Class A (1:2:4) factors per m³ (94-lb bag): Cement = 7.84 bags, Sand = 0.44 m³, Gravel = 0.88 m³.
Concrete volume: V = 100 m × 200 m × 0.10 m = 2,000 m³.
Cement = 2,000 × 7.84 = 15,680 bags.
Sand = 2,000 × 0.44 = 880 m³.
Gravel = 2,000 × 0.88 = 1,760 m³.
Answer = 880 m³ (volume of sand)

items.question: A concrete foundation for rice mill engine drive was determined to have a dimension of 2 meters wide by 4 meters long. The computed depth was 1.5 meters. Determine the number of bags of cement and the volume of sand and gravels needed for the foundation. Use 1:3:6 mixing proportion.
items.rationale:
Given: Width = 2 m; Length = 4 m; Depth = 1.5 m; Mix = 1:3:6 (Class C). Factors per m³ (94-lb bag): Cement = 5.48 bags, Sand = 0.44 m³, Gravel = 0.88 m³.
Concrete volume: V = 2 m × 4 m × 1.5 m = 12 m³.
Cement = 12 × 5.48 = 65.76 ≈ 66 bags.
Sand = 12 × 0.44 = 5.28 m³.
Gravel = 12 × 0.88 = 10.56 m³.
Answer = 10.56 m³ of gravel

items.question: In Class A, B or C concrete, how many cubic meters of sand should be mixed to produce 1 m³ of concrete?
items.rationale:
Given: Standard Philippine concrete proportioning (Class A 1:2:4, Class B 1:2.5:5, Class C 1:3:6) per 1 m³ of concrete.
In standard concrete mix tables (e.g., Fajardo), the sand multiplier is uniformly 0.50 m³ of sand (and 1.00 m³ of gravel) per 1 m³ of concrete for Classes A, B, and C, with only the number of cement bags varying (9.0, 7.5, and 6.0 bags respectively for 40-kg bags).
Answer = 0.50 m³

items.question: A 1-meter thick trapezoidal section of a diversion dam has resisting moment about the dam toe of 280,000 tonne-meters. The water exerts 4,050 tonnes horizontally at 35 meters above the dam toe. What is the factor of safety against overturning?
items.rationale:
Given: Resisting moment (M_R) = 280,000 tonne-m; Horizontal water force (F) = 4,050 tonnes; Moment arm (y) = 35 m.
Overturning moment: M_O = F × y = 4,050 × 35 = 141,750 tonne-m.
Formula: FS_overturning = M_R / M_O = 280,000 / 141,750 = 1.9753 ≈ 1.98.
Answer = 1.98

items.question: ILLUMINATION: A 1m × 100m poultry handling area is to be lighted at an average maintained footcandle of 50 fc. How many 2-lamp fixtures of 120 cm long F40 T12 WW (3,200 Lumens) rapid start fluorescent lamps are required assuming the CU is 0.35 and the LLF is 0.75? (not exact values, but same concept)
items.rationale:
Given: Area (A) = 1 m × 100 m = 100 m²; Maintained illumination (E) = 50 fc (lm/ft²); Lamps per fixture (n) = 2; Lumens per lamp (Φ) = 3,200 lm; CU = 0.35; LLF = 0.75.
Convert area to ft²: A = 100 m² × 10.7639 ft²/m² = 1,076.39 ft².
Formula (Lumen Method): N = (E × A) / (n × Φ × CU × LLF).
Substitution: N = (50 × 1,076.39) / (2 × 3,200 × 0.35 × 0.75) = 53,819.5 / 1,680 = 32.04 ≈ 32 fixtures.
Answer = 32 fixtures

items.question: How many sprinklers with spacing of 7m × 7m are needed to irrigate a rectangular piece of land 125 m × 190 m if the laterals are set parallel to the longer side of the field.
items.rationale:
Given: Field dimensions = 125 m × 190 m; Sprinkler spacing = 7 m × 7 m; Laterals parallel to the 190-m side.
Number of laterals across 125 m: N_L = 125 m / 7 m = 17.86 ≈ 18 laterals.
Number of sprinklers per lateral along 190 m: N_S = 190 m / 7 m = 27.14 ≈ 27 sprinklers/lateral.
Total sprinklers = N_L × N_S = 18 × 27 = 486 sprinklers.
Answer = 486 sprinklers

items.question: You are evaluating a functional processing machine based on Kick’s law. From a series of tests, an average of 3 kWh was required to reduce a material from 5 mm to 2 mm diameter. Using Kick’s law, what is the expected energy consumption if the diameter of the same material is to be reduced from 5 mm to 0.5 mm?
items.rationale:
Given: E1 = 3 kWh from D1 = 5 mm to D2 = 2 mm; Desired reduction from D1 = 5 mm to D2' = 0.5 mm.
Formula (Kick's Law): E = C × ln(D1 / D2).
Constant: C = E1 / ln(5 / 2) = 3 / ln(2.5) = 3 / 0.9163 = 3.2741 kWh.
Expected energy: E2 = 3.2741 × ln(5 / 0.5) = 3.2741 × ln(10) = 3.2741 × 2.3026 = 7.54 kWh ≈ 8 kWh.
Answer = 8 kWh

items.question: How many tonnes of biomass is needed annually to optimally operate a 27-ampere 9-kW vermi cast production shredder having a capacity of 0.27 tonne of waste per hour? It optimally operates 16 hours daily during the 3-month peak sunny months and 8 h/day at 26 days/month for the rest of the year.
items.rationale:
Given: Shredder capacity = 0.27 tonne/h; Peak operation = 16 h/day × 30 days/mo × 3 mo/yr; Lean operation = 8 h/day × 26 days/mo × 9 mo/yr.
Peak operating hours = 16 × 30 × 3 = 1,440 h/yr.
Lean operating hours = 8 × 26 × 9 = 1,872 h/yr.
Total operating hours = 1,440 + 1,872 = 3,312 h/yr.
Annual biomass = 0.27 tonne/h × 3,312 h/yr = 894.24 tonnes/yr ≈ 894 tonnes/yr.
Answer = 894 tonnes/yr

items.question: A certain farmstead has 3 separate circuit breakers having ampacities of 60 A, 30 A and 15 A. Determine the ampacity of the main circuit breaker.
items.rationale: Given: Three separate branch circuit breakers = 60 A, 30 A, and 15 A. Rule: For a farmstead service panel with multiple branch circuits (assuming non-simultaneous peak demand under PEC/PAES guidelines), the main circuit breaker ampacity must be at least equal to the highest individual branch circuit breaker rating (and meet the 60 A minimum service disconnecting means). Formula: I_main = max(60 A, 30 A, 15 A) = 60 A. Answer = 60 A

items.question: An egg incubator operates at 240 volts. It uses a pair of 25-meter AWG 10 copper wire having a resistance of 3.87 × 10⁻³ ohm per linear meter at 65 °C. The heating load of the incubator is composed of twelve 100-watt heating coils. Determine the amperage of the main wire.
items.rationale: Given: V = 240 V, 12 heating coils × 100 W, line = 2 × 25 m × 3.87 × 10⁻³ Ω/m. Step 1 (Heating coils are wired in parallel so each gets the full 240 V): total load P = 12 × 100 W = 1,200 W. Step 2 (Line resistance): R_wire = 2 × 25 × 3.87 × 10⁻³ = 0.19 Ω, negligible next to the load resistance (240²/1,200 = 48 Ω). Step 3 (Main wire current): I = P / V = 1,200 / 240 = 5.0 A.
